<meta>This page continues the author’s introductory remarks, shifting from the general obligation of ethical rebuke to a personal address to his family. He explains his motivation for writing these "pamphlets" as he prepares to depart for the Land of Israel, framing his work as a spiritual legacy for his children and students.</meta>

<page-num>2</page-num>
<header>The Generations of Man</header>

I speak words of understanding to bless the Lord: may my sons, my daughters, my sons-in-law, my daughters-in-law, my grandchildren, and their descendants forever be blessed. May the Lord increase you a thousandfold. I compose for you an ethical reproof <note>original: "תוכחת מוסר" (tochechat musar) — a traditional genre of moral and ethical instruction</note>, "as a man disciplines his son," for it is time for me to speak now that I am preparing to depart from them to find rest, with the help of God, in the Holy Land. It is mentioned in the chapter "These are Salted" <note>A section of the Talmud, Tractate Chullin 7b</note> that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] asked Rabbi Phinehas ben Jair: "Is Elijah the Prophet still alive?" He answered: "Since it is written, 'and he saw him no more,' [it means he lives] for his Creator." Regarding myself, I read this as a hint: "The reproofs of instruction are the way of life" <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>. This is the path toward the Lord, the "Land of the Living," for there the Lord commanded the blessing—life forevermore.

# Happy
are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the Lord. For behold, I have contemplated creating for every ethical teaching a connection to the words of Torah in length, breadth, and depth, so that it may enter more deeply into the heart. This way, one might fulfill the goal of "to learn and to teach, to observe and to perform." This aligns with the statement of our Sages: "One who departs from a friend should not depart except through words of Torah, for through this, he will remember him." Their intention was that one should say pleasant, straightforward words of Torah which are ethical teachings that penetrate the depths of the heart. This is why they were precise in saying *from within* the words of Torah, for I have already mentioned the obligation to engage in ethical words when parting. When the ethical lesson is adorned and illuminated by Torah, it enters the heart most effectively. Similarly, we say in the "Great Love" prayer: "put into our hearts to understand and to discern, to listen, to learn and to teach, to observe..." Then the Torah of his God is in his heart, and he fulfills "Your faithfulness is within my heart." These words of Torah, which are ethical instructions, bear fruit and leave an impression once they enter the heart. This study leads to action; thus, when an action comes to hand, one remembers the friend who taught it. This is why they concluded: "through this, he will remember him." Behold, they are remembered and performed—meaning one sees the action and remembers the Law (the simple Torah word) that testified to it. One then remembers the one who said it, which "brings redemption," as it is taught: "Whoever says a thing in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world." And if that person is deceased, then "his lips move in the grave." Thus, the remembrance happens in two ways: the action causes one to remember the Law (the Torah), and it causes one to remember his friend. Both together are good. This is hinted at in the verse "For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light" <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>; when it becomes a "way of life," and a departing person is seen off with ethical reproof, that reproof becomes "Torah light," and he merits the "lamp of the commandment," for study leads to action.

# And in order
to fulfill this verse, "For the commandment is a lamp," I thought of the imagery of our Sages who said: "To one who leaves over his fruits, we say: 'Finish them!'" <note>A metaphor for completing one's work/writings</note>. I did not want anything to be lacking, since my intention is to benefit you—my children (may their Rock and Redeemer protect them) and those joined with you—to merit the World to Come. I realized that it is impossible to reach the goal of *deveikut* <note>original: "דביקות" — spiritual attachment or "cleaving" to the Divine</note> except through the "lamp of the commandment" and "Torah light." By this, I mean to awaken you to the performance of commandments and to warn you about certain "thou shalts" and "thou shalt nots" that many are not careful about. This happens for several reasons. First, as our Sages said: "If a person commits a transgression and repeats it, it becomes permitted to him." This often stems from the "dust of greed" in which people have become mired, as the Sages testified regarding theft, forbidden sexual relations, and evil speech. Regarding sexual immorality and theft, and the "dust of greed," I will give a sign: there is no charge or decree that does not contain the "sin of A-N-L" <note>original: "ענ"ל" (A.N.L.) — an acronym for **A**rayot (sexual immorality), **G**ezel (theft/robbery), and **L**ashon Hara (evil speech)</note>. These are linked in the order of the *Vidui* <note>the Confession prayer</note>: "We have robbed (*Gazalnu*), we have spoken slander (*Dibarnu Dofi*), we have acted perversely..." The word "Sin" (*Avon*) hints at sexual immorality, as the *Rokeach* <note>Rabbi Eleazar of Worms, a 12th-13th century scholar</note> wrote in his secrets: the word *Avon* (עון) filled out <note>A Kabbalistic method where each letter's name is spelled out: Ayin-Vav-Nun</note> equals 48 (*M"CH*). This is because no transgression is performed with the sensation of all forty-eight limbs except for the act of intercourse. Thus, the Sages testified that these three are very grave sins found among many. The second reason is a lack of knowledge; certain commandments are not well-known to the masses or are not frequently discussed. Therefore, I took it upon myself to make them known, including some new legal insights that I have innovated with God's help, which were not mentioned by earlier authorities. All of this is included in the "Lamp of the Commandment."

# And Torah is Light
will be fulfilled through the knowledge of the reasons for the commandments and their secrets. Regarding this, it is said: "Happy is the man who does them and lives by them." "Doing them" refers to the physical performance of the commandment. "Living by them" refers to the *deveikut* (spiritual attachment) found in the hints of the commandment, which is the spiritual vitality of the deed. From this spirituality—which is the realm of thought—one achieves attachment to His Blessed Name, for the intention of the commandment is the secret of His Blessed Name. Without this, there is no attachment from the physicality of the action to the spirituality of the Creator, which is the ultimate spiritual goal.

# And also
the "service of our heart," which is Prayer, stands in place of the Sacrifice that brings us closer to Him. Prayer must be done with *kavanah* <note>original: "כוונה" — focused intention or heart-direction</note>; then it is like a body with a soul. The "inner" part of prayer is its order as established for us by our Sages. The "soul" is the intention of the secrets of prayer. Our Sages said: "Why do Israel pray and are not answered? Because they do not know how to pray with the [Divine] Name, as it is said: 'Because he has known My name, he shall call upon Me and I will answer him.'" I have already mentioned that study leads to action, and action leads to [spiritual] humility. This explains the phrasing in the "Great Love" blessing: first we ask for study ("put into our hearts to understand... to observe and perform"), then we ask "enlighten our eyes in Your Torah, and make our hearts cleave to Your commandments, and unite our hearts to love and fear Your name." This "enlightening of the eyes" refers to the secrets of the commandments, for which King David also prayed: "Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your law." Through this, we shall live attached to His Blessed Name in love and fear. It is explained in the Zohar and by the "Masters of Truth" <note>Kabbalists</note> that from the physical performance of commandments, Torah, and prayer (the action and the speech), "garments" for the soul are created in the Lower Garden of Eden. However, enlightenment and attachment in the Upper Garden of Eden—which are higher levels of spiritual refinement—come only from the secret intentions found in the knowledge of His Blessed Names. I will not expand further on this deep inquiry now, for "man is born to toil." I am merely presenting the main points of what is necessary. Know, my children, do not think that what I mention in these pamphlets regarding the secrets of commandments and prayers reaches the ultimate depth of the matter. It is not even a drop in the great ocean. To those secrets, there is no end or limit. Even if a man lives two thousand years, he would not reach the ultimate root of a single commandment, except for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions, who saw what those of "flesh and blood" do not see. They passed great knowledge to their students and their students' students who merited his great light. However, "not every mind can tolerate this." I have only come to reveal a small portion of what I received from the mouths of scribes and from books following the Zohar, especially the later holy and divine books: Rabbi Moses [Cordovero] (of blessed memory) and the later, holy man of God, the Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the father of modern Kabbalah</note> (of blessed memory). I will add a small touch of my own to explain the matters. It is known that holiness is like an "ever-flowing spring"—if a person sanctifies himself a little from below, he is sanctified greatly from above. May the Holy One grant us wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and then you shall merit to enter the innermost chambers through many thousands of levels toward the Place of the Blessed One.

# Behold
these pamphlets which I am bequeathing to you are a "threefold cord": **Ethical Reproof**, the **Lamp of Commandment**, and **Torah Light**. Their sign is the Hebrew word *MaNaT* <note>original: "מנ"ת" — meaning 'portion' or 'lot'</note>, standing for **M**usar (Ethics), **N**er (Lamp), and **T**orah.

# And because
students are also called "sons," and I have merited (thank God) to raise many students, I hereby command you: any student whose soul desires to copy these pamphlets, "do not withhold good from those to whom it is due." And you, my sons, "hear the instruction of your father," let it be a "reminder between your eyes," and "bequeath them to your children," for it is your life and the length of your days. Furthermore, my sons, be careful with extra holiness, purity, and attachment. I wrote this in haste as I was leaving for the designated journey to the Holy Land, to cleave to the Land of the Living. Therefore, I call these pamphlets:

# The Way of Life
based on the aforementioned verse, "For the commandment is a lamp... and the way of life [is the reproof of instruction]." This is the path to eternal life. Since the tread of a foot has three parts <note>A reference to the anatomy of an animal's leg in kosher laws</note>, I will arrange three chapters for the "upright foot" that treads the path of the Tree of Life: Chapter 1 is titled **The Ten Sayings**; Chapter 2 is titled **The Ten Commandments**; Chapter 3 is titled **The Ten Praises**. These three chapters bring a person—who is the purpose of creation—to his true purpose. Corresponding to these, the Men of the Great Assembly established [the liturgy] for Rosh Hashanah, the day the first man was created...

<meta>This page continues the author's introductory reflection. Having established his personal motivation to leave a spiritual legacy for his family before departing for the Land of Israel, he now turns to a rigorous legal and ethical analysis of the commandment of "Tochacha" (reproof or correction). He explores the Rabbinic debates regarding how far one must go when correcting others, balancing the duty to speak out with the practical reality of whether the message will be received.</meta>

# The Generations of Man

<margin>
Rabbi Yochanan said: only until a rebuff <note>original: "נזיפה" (nazifah) — a sharp scolding or social rebuff</note>.
</margin>
The Maharil <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Moses Moelin, a 14th-century German authority</note>, of blessed memory, held that even if a person has already encountered a rebuff or even a curse, and does not know for certain that the other will accept the correction, he is not exempt from the duty of reproof until it reaches the point of a physical blow. Maimonides <note>The text uses "המיומוני" (Ha-Miyumoni) to refer to Maimonides, likely referencing his legal code, the Mishneh Torah</note>, in the sixth chapter of the Laws of Character Traits, ruled according to the Sage Rav—even though the author of the *Smag* <note>The "Sefer Mitzvot Gadol," a 13th-century legal code by Rabbi Moses of Coucy</note> wondered at this, for the *Smag* ruled like Rabbi Yochanan. Usually, the law follows Rabbi Yochanan over Rav, and certainly so for Samuel in matters of prohibited actions. Nevertheless, the Maimonidean tradition records it thus: In the Midrash Tanchuma on the portion *Ki Tisa*, the language implies the words of Rabbi [Yochanan]. For it says that the Teacher of the World <note>God</note> said to him: "Master of the Universe, why are these different from those?" etc., until: "Nevertheless, they should have clarified the matter for the sake of the sanctification of Your Name and accepted blows from Israel upon themselves, just as the prophets suffered. For Jeremiah and Isaiah suffered many troubles from Israel, as it is written: 'I gave my back to those who strike me.'" Immediately, the Holy One, Blessed be He, relented and said to the angels of destruction: "[Strike] old and young, infants and women." This is the end of the Midrashic quote, and the end of Maimonides' reasoning. And even according to the words of the *Smag*, who ruled like Rabbi Yochanan only "until a rebuff" and no more, it is nonetheless proven from the Sages Rav and Samuel that even if one knows the other will not accept it, he is obligated to rebuke. For Samuel, who is more lenient than Rav, nonetheless holds that even after a rebuff—where one knows for certain it won't be accepted—he is still obligated to rebuke. And on this logic, Rabbi Yochanan does not actually disagree with Rav and Samuel. While he may hold that the one giving the correction does not need to suffer excessively or continue after a rebuff, he does not disagree that one was obligated to rebuke *before* the rebuff, even if it was already established in his mind that they would not accept the correction. Even if we say Rabbi Yochanan disagrees with them, and that this is his very reason for saying "until a rebuff" (because that is when it becomes clear the moral instruction won't be accepted), it would still not be appropriate to rule like Rabbi Yochanan, as he would be a lone voice in this logic against Rav and Samuel, who hold that the commandment of reproof applies even after a rebuff, at which point our knowledge is certain that it won't be accepted. Since the words of Rabbi Yochanan are weighed against both of them, it is proper to rule like Rav, for the law follows Rav in matters of prohibited actions. Perhaps this is the reason Maimonides ruled like Rav. Regarding the passage in Tractate Yevamot where Rabbi Ila'a says in the name of Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Simeon: "Just as it is a commandment for a person to say something that will be heard <note>i.e., accepted</note>, so it is a commandment *not* to say something that will not be heard"—Rabbi says it is an obligation, as it is said: "Do not rebuke a scoffer lest he hate you; rebuke a wise man and he will love you"—I do not say this is a separate matter, but rather it clarifies the words 

<margin>
Page 66.
And thus says the *Nimukei Yosef* <note>a commentary by Rabbi Joseph Habiba</note> at the end of the first chapter of Yevamot: He adds that one should only say something that is heard by one who accepts the commandment to "surely rebuke your neighbor." But many times, if he knows they won't accept the commandment, it is forbidden to rebuke. And he quoted exactly what we say in Tractate Arachin: one is obligated to rebuke until they strike him or curse him. This applies to a single individual, but for a group, we say in Tractate Shabbat that the Sages did not rebuke the Exilarch <note>the political head of the Jewish community in Babylon</note> because they knew he would not accept it from them. We also say in the name of Mar Ukva that there they were entirely wicked, and if he knew for certain they wouldn't listen, he was exempt. And his reasoning for refraining is based on the concern that there should not be a grievance against them; thus one is obligated to rebuke at least once. This ends his quote; it seems his words intend to reconcile the two views.
</margin>
that the sinners do not know that the act is forbidden and they mock the one rebuking them; in any case, they have transgressed. Therefore, it is better that they be unintentional sinners and not intentional ones <note>original: "מוטב שיהיו שוגגים ואל יהיו מזידים" (mutav she-yihyu shogegin...) — a famous legal principle suggesting that if people will definitely sin, it is better they do so without knowing it is a sin, so they are less culpable</note>. This is similar to what is found in Tractate Shabbat (chapter "The One Who Asks") and Tractate Beitzah (chapter "The One Who Brings") regarding the addition to the fast of Yom Kippur. We see people eating and drinking until dark, and we do not say a word to them, because of the principle: "It is better they be unintentional than intentional." Thus writes Maimonides in the fifth chapter of the Laws of Resting on the Tenth: "Women who eat and drink until dark, and do not know that it is a commandment to add from the secular day to the holy, we do not protest against them so that they do not come to act intentionally; for it is impossible to have a guard over every single person to warn them. Leave them to be unintentional rather than intentional, and so too for anything similar." And thus wrote the Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel, 13th-century German-Spanish authority</note> in Tractate Beitzah: "The author of the *Itur* wrote that this only applies to something derived from Midrashic interpretation, like the addition to Yom Kippur. But regarding something explicitly written in the Torah, we must protest and punish them until they desist." The reason is that since the prohibition is not clearly known to everyone, we fear they won't believe us and won't change; regarding this, there is an obligation *not* to say something that won't be heard, for the sake of them remaining unintentional. But regarding a matter whose prohibition is publicized and well-known, then "you shall surely rebuke," even a hundred times. Furthermore, one can explain the words of Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Simeon—that one should not say what will not be heard—as referring to rebuking a scoffer who mocks the words of the corrector and laughs at him. Even if they were sinners who did not listen to the voice of the prophets, that was not categorized as "scoffing," except when false prophets made them believe their own words were true. So too, one who rebukes a wise man, and the wise man responds to the correction saying "I didn't do that" or "I did it, but it was legally permitted"—in such a case, one is obligated to rebuke until a blow. However, if he laughs at the words of the corrector and mocks him, then the corrector is obligated *not* to speak. Rabbi Mordechai explained that if one wishes to be stringent with himself and rebuke beyond the required measure, to such a person we say: Do not do "good," and "good" do not say what won't be heard, because of the verse "Do not rebuke a scoffer." Look closely at this.

## And Because
of Maimonides' ruling "until a blow," it seems to me that his reasoning is sound: the corrector should be like an iron pillar, showing no favoritism even to the great. In the chapter "Helek," Jeroboam merited kingship because he rebuked Solomon, etc. And in the last chapter of Ketubot: "That Torah scholar whom the people of his city love—it is not because he is so superior, but because he does not rebuke them for matters of Heaven."

### And Behold,
Our Sages interpreted the verse "A man by his brother" to mean "by the sin of his brother"—that all Israel are responsible <note>original: "ערבין" (arvein) — guarantors or interconnected</note> for one another. But according to the commandment of reproof, one is exempt after two systems <note>referring to the stages of warning</note>.

## And Just As
there is a great commandment upon the corrector to rebuke, so too there is a great commandment upon the one being corrected to accept the reproof. In Tractate Tamid, first chapter, it is taught: Rabbi says, which is the straight path a person should choose for himself? He should love reproof, for as 

<column-break/>

long as reproof is in the world, contentment comes to the world, and goodness and blessing come to the world, and evil departs from the world, as it is said: "To those who rebuke, it shall be pleasant, and upon them shall come a blessing of good." And it says in Tractate Arachin: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said, "I call heaven and earth to witness that many times Akiva was lashed because of me, for I would complain about him before Rabban Shimon bar Rabbi, and all the more so did I increase my love for him, to fulfill that which is written: 'Do not rebuke a scoffer lest he hate you; rebuke a wise man and he will love you.'"

## And These
are the words which Moses, our teacher, spoke near his death, as he was going on the "way of life." Just as the master of prophets did, so too did the prophets who followed in his footsteps—rebuking Israel and urging them to come to God. Certainly, they did this near their departure from the world. So did Joshua his student, and so did Samuel. "And it was when Samuel was old..." And even earlier in Israel, Jacob our father, before his passing, called his sons, etc. This is the way of all the righteous: at the time of their passing, they occupy themselves with moral reproof with even greater intensity.

Thus, the lot of the commandment of reproof is clarified. Therefore, it is fitting for everyone to speak at length with words of correction as much as they are able. Even though all the matters mentioned above refer to rebuking a transgression that has already been committed, we also learn from this to stand and warn for the future—to make known the "good and straight path." One who fears Heaven and his two inclinations <note>the good and evil inclinations</note> knows that correction for the past and teaching ethics and conduct for the future are all of a piece. They are joined so that people may hear, learn, and be careful to perform all the words of the Torah. And so Moses our teacher did both: after he taught the Torah and the commandments to all Israel, when he was about to go on the path of eternal life near his death, he fulfilled "moral reproof." "These are the words"—words of reproof. He rebuked them for the past—how they had sinned since leaving Egypt—and taught them ethics for the future, both in the fulfillment of the Torah and its commandments (study and action) and in the cultivation of character traits, so as to reach "cleaving" <note>original: "דביקות" (deveikut) — spiritual communion with the Divine</note> to Him, blessed be He, and to walk in His ways and His attributes, as explained in many verses in the Book of Deuteronomy. And know, my children (may their Rock and Redeemer protect them), that all the ethical teachings that our Sages gave in the Talmud and Midrashim—and that which the authors of the books of Repentance, Character, and Ethics expanded upon later, as well as those who spoke according to the Secrets <note>i.e., Kabbalah</note>, the ethics of "cleaving," like the holy Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in the Zohar and Tikunim and those who followed him in early and later generations—the words of all of them are founded upon the ethical words of Moses our teacher. For whoever has eyes to see, or sees everything with the eye of the intellect, it is well-explained. Happy is the eye that has seen all these!

I know that my soul is not righteous enough to be counted among the "Tzaddikim" <note>righteous ones</note>; nonetheless, it is written: "Follow the tracks of the sheep and graze your kids." Therefore, I will follow the tracks of the early ones, to know the wisdom and ethics, and to understand the words of...

<meta>This page continues the author’s philosophical and kabbalistic introduction. # The Generations of Man

<margin>
The Reality of the Name
"And He called their name Adam"
</margin>
**Afterward**, it says, "On the day that [God] created," etc. This explains three things: "On the day God created man, in the likeness of God He made him." This is the explanation regarding the Name of the Lord, as I wrote above. We shall further explain at length the matter of the "instruments" of that Divinity through which the form and likeness of man became known and revealed.

This is the explanation of "The Generations of Man": ultimately, if he is attached to the One Above and makes himself similar to Him, may He be blessed, by walking in His ways, he is truly called **Adam**. This name is derived from the phrase "I will resemble [the Hebrew *adameh*] the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14) and "upon the throne was the likeness of the appearance of a man [*adam*]" (Ezekiel 1:26). But if he separates himself from this attachment, then he is called "Adam" only after the "ground" [*adamah*] from which he was taken—for he is dust and to dust he shall return. However, the name Adam which signifies "resembling the Most High" is the primary purpose, for evil was created only for the sake of good, as explained. Therefore, the essential name Adam has the same numerical value <note>Gematria: the numerical value of the letters. "Adam" (אדם) equals 45. The Name of God (Y-H-V-H) when spelled out in the specific "filling" of Yud-He-Vav-He (יו"ד ה"א וא"ו ה"א) also equals 45.</note> as His Great Name in its full spelling: Yod-He-Vav-He.

**And behold**, the three aforementioned roots require broad explanation to reach the depths of their meaning—to see the works of the great and awesome Lord, the Creator of man. These three have already been mentioned in the Zohar as well, regarding how they are connected and unified. It is a wondrous teaching, and we shall examine it, as the goodness of the Lord is upon us. After its explanation, we will find an open door to the three gates of wisdom, where in each and every gate we shall enter many chambers of knowledge.

The language of the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot) is as follows: "We have learned: there are three levels bound one to another: the Holy One Blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel. Each of these levels has a hidden aspect and a revealed aspect. The Holy One Blessed be He is level upon level, hidden and revealed. The Torah is hidden and revealed. Israel is level upon level, as it is written: 'He tells His words to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel' (Psalms 147:19). There are two levels, Jacob and Israel: one revealed and one hidden," etc.

The passage is long, and I have copied only what is necessary for our subject. We must examine a few points:
1. Why does it say "three levels are bound one to another," which implies three types of connections? If it were otherwise, it should have said "Israel is bound to the Torah, and the Torah to the Holy One."
2. What new insight does this teaching offer? Does not even a one-day-old schoolchild <note>original: "בר בי רב דחד יומא" — a common Talmudic idiom for a beginner student.</note> know that the Blessed Name is both revealed and hidden—hidden in His essence and revealed through His actions? And similarly, that the Torah has revealed and hidden layers?
3. Why the repetitive language "level upon level"? And why at the end does it mention "Jacob and Israel, one revealed and one hidden"? Certainly, these variations in language are not empty words but represent wondrous wisdom. Similarly, regarding the Torah, it says "hidden and revealed," but regarding Jacob and Israel, it says "one is hidden and one is revealed."

->Since this holy teaching is like a great and fortified city containing much in every word and utterance, I shall explain it<-
->at length and breadth, from the "depths of the well," moving from topic to topic until we reach the Mountain of the Lord where the light dwells.<-
->In this city, I shall build ten "Houses" with the help of the Mighty and Awesome God. For these Houses, there is a great gate called<-
->The Gate of Light. These are their names: The House of the Beloved; The House of Wisdom; The House of Israel; The House of the Sanctuary; The House of the Faithful;<-
->The Last House; The House of Choice; The House of the Walled City; The House of David; The Great House.<-
->**The House of the Beloved** shall remember the existence of the Blessed Name. **The House of Wisdom** shall speak of the Torah from Heaven. **The House of Israel** shall speak of the dominion of Israel and the excellence of man, for Israel is called "Adam."<-
->**The House of the Faithful** shall speak of the utterances of the Blessed Name, for they are faithful. **The House of the Sanctuary** shall speak of the excellence of the Holy Tongue and the matter of Divine Attributes.<-
->**The House of the Last** shall speak of the spiritual reward that comes at the end. **The House of Choice** shall speak of the inquiry into Free Will. **The House of the Walled City** shall speak of the inquiry<-
->into the Supreme Will, which is concealed and hidden. **The House of David** shall remember the matter of the Messiah. **The Great House** is the inquiry into the verse "And you shall write them"—it is the house that encompasses all other houses.<-

->It is the inquiry into Divine Service for "High Necessity" <note>original: "עבודה צורך גבוה" — a Kabbalistic concept suggesting that human performance of commandments sustains or affects the Divine realms.</note>. This is the gate of all the houses. And with that which we opened, we shall begin to speak of the existence of Existence,<-
->blessed and exalted be He. The reality of the Name is well known, for the Essential Name is the Name Y-H-V-H, and it famously makes known the essence of the Blessed God.<-

<margin>
The Man
</margin>

**Man** [Adam]: the essence of his existence is famous for his Choice and Will. From this, the first and second gates follow. The manner of the connection is that the Torah and Israel are also evaluated through the lens of "Will"—thus you have the connection of the three. This is the secret of Head, Middle, and End. The Head is the Holy One Blessed be He, who is first, and there is no beginning to His beginning. The Middle is the Torah, through which His Divinity is revealed via the performance of Torah and Commandments by Man. And Man is the "End"—the goal of creation. "The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God," etc. (Ecclesiastes 12:13), for this is the whole of Man. The Blessed Name is Head, Middle, and End: He was, He is, and He will be; He is Almighty and encompasses them all.

Now I shall explain, with God's help, one after another. Before my explanation, I will state the general principle of the teaching which says "hidden and revealed." It is known to every thinking person that the "revealed" is actually the "hidden" made manifest—that is, its revelation and expansion is the revealed part. Thus, the revealed *is* the hidden. Similarly, in the matter of the Torah, the revealed aspect is not a separate thing from the hidden aspect, as the common people understand it—as if the way of the hidden is one path and the way of the revealed is another. That is not so. Rather, the hidden was drawn down and revealed. This is the hint in the verse: "Apples of gold in settings of silver is a word spoken in its proper place" (Proverbs 25:11). That is, just as silver is brought close to be refined <note>meaning: silver acts as a beautiful casing that allows the more precious gold inside to be partially glimpsed</note>, though it is of a lower degree, so too is the revealed in relation to the hidden. This is close to the wisdom found in the *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>Maimonides' philosophical work</note>. He says: "The Sage said: 'Apples of gold in settings of silver.' Hear the explanation of this. 'Settings' [maskiyot] are bodies with decorative openings... through which the sight can pass... He says that a metaphor of golden apples in a network of silver with very fine holes is like a 'word spoken in its proper place.' See how wonderful this metaphor is. A thing with two faces—revealed and hidden—must have its revealed part be as good as silver, but its interior must be better than its exterior, such that the interior is to the exterior as gold is to silver. And the exterior must contain hints that point the observer to what is within." When seen from afar, one might think it is an apple of silver, but a person with sharp vision will realize it is gold. This is the correct view: the revealed part of the Torah hints at the hidden.

And after the inquiry into God has spurred us on, I shall come to the explanation of what I began:

<margin>
Beginning
</margin>
**The beginning** of the matter is the Essential Name Y-H-V-H. Afterward, it will be explained how the Torah and Israel reveal the Name of Yud-He-Vav-He. This is the language of the Divine [Scholar] the Ramak <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, 16th-century Kabbalist</note> in the book *Pardes Rimonim* (Gate 1, Chapter 1): "Let it not enter the mind of the reader that when we say 'Essential Name' we mean the actual Essence of the Emanator, the Infinite [*Ein Sof*]. Heaven forbid! For that is an improper thought, as we explained at length in the gate regarding the *Keter* [Crown]. Rather, our intention in saying 'Essential Name' is that it is the essence of the *Sefirot* <note>Divine emanations</note>. It is the Name that encompasses the whole essence of the *Sefirot*." It is known that the act of Emanation is the "Name" of the Infinite—meaning it indicates His essence. For example, the name "Isaac" identifies a specific man. If we did not attribute a name to Him, we could not speak of Him. Through the Emanation, we have a way to relate to Him. Therefore, the four-letter Name [Tetragrammaton] is a name that encompasses the whole of Emanation in general and in detail. But the Name is not to Him as names are to people. Human names are arbitrary conventions—Abraham decided to call his son Isaac for some reason. But His names all indicate the nature of the thing called by that name. Therefore, we say the Essential Name does not describe the Essence of the Emanator Himself, for nothing can limit His Essence or His Unity. Because this is true, the Sages of Israel and the Prophets agreed to describe Him with names that indicate His concealment from the hearts of men.

<meta>This page continues the author’s philosophical exploration of the human condition, specifically connecting the creation of Man to the structure of the Rosh Hashanah liturgy. It bridges the previous discussion of man's "likeness" to God with the practical theological "roots" of faith: God's existence, the Torah, and divine justice.</meta>

# The Generations of Man

His actions are in accordance with the one who holds <note>original: "כד"א דס"ל"</note> that the world was created on the 25th of Elul. Thus, Man—who is the "sum of all creation"—was created on the 28th, which was the sixth day. Consequently, the Men of the Great Assembly <note>An ancient legislative body of 120 sages during the early Second Temple period</note> instituted the recitation of ten verses each for *Kingship*, *Remembrances*, and *Shofar-blasts* <note>The three central themes of the Rosh Hashanah prayer service</note> corresponding to the aforementioned matters. As it is stated in the Talmud (Tractate Rosh Hashanah): "To what do these ten 'Kingship' verses correspond? Rabbi [Judah the Prince] says: To the ten praises said by King David in the Book of Psalms. Rav Joseph says: To the Ten Commandments spoken to Moses at Sinai. Rabbi Yochanan says: To the Ten Utterances <note>The ten times "And God said..." appears in the creation story in Genesis</note> by which the world was created."

Now, there appears to be a reversal of chronological order in the memory of the Sages, for they placed the words of Rav Joseph before those of Rabbi Yochanan, even though the latter lived long before him. In the book *Pardes* <note>The Orchard, a classic Kabbalistic work by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> (Gate 5, Chapter 9), this is resolved through secret, mystical means. However, according to the plain meaning, it seems to me that they are counted in order from bottom to top. That is: from top to bottom, the order was the Ten Utterances of Creation, then the Ten Commandments at the Giving of the Torah, and finally the ten praises in the Book of Psalms. Out of respect for "Rabbi" [Judah the Prince], he was placed first, and the order then proceeded from the bottom (Psalms) upward.

And if one should ask why they skipped and did not mention the hint from "above"—meaning, starting with the Ten Utterances—or why Rav Joseph chose the Commandments, you can tell him that each sage spoke according to his own spiritual attachment and character. This is similar to what is said in the Talmud (Tractate Sanhedrin, chapter *Chelek*) regarding the name of the Messiah: "The school of Rabbi Shila said: 'Shila' is his name. The school of Rabbi Yannai said: 'Yinnon' is his name. The school of Rabbi Hanina said: 'Hanina' is his name." Rashi <note>The preeminent medieval commentator</note> explains that each one interprets based on his own name.

So too here: each spoke according to his own spiritual path. Rav Joseph was considered a "Sinai" <note>A scholar with vast, encyclopedic knowledge of tradition</note>, as the Talmud says: "Rav Joseph is Sinai; Rabbah is a 'uprooter of mountains.'" Therefore, Rav Joseph associated the prayer with the Ten Commandments given at Sinai. Rabbi Yochanan, however, possessed a beauty that was a reflection <note>original: "שופרי דרבי יוחנן היה מגופלי' שופרי דאדם הראשון"</note> of the beauty of the first Man (Adam), who was the beginning of creation. Therefore, he associated it with the Ten Utterances of creation. The beauty of Rabbi Yochanan is praised in many places; the Talmud asks, "Was not the beauty of Rav Kahana a reflection of Rabbi Abbahu, and the beauty of Rabbi Abbahu a reflection of the Patriarch Jacob, and Jacob's beauty a reflection of Adam's?" Thus, Rabbi Yochanan's countenance was essentially a reflection of Adam’s beauty, which was so radiant that his very heel outshone the sun. This is the reason for the order of these three sages. But the simple chronological order is: Ten Utterances, Ten Commandments, Ten Praises. Therefore:
->I have called these three chapters by those names:<-

I have set it upon my heart to compose a preface to inform and reveal how awesome Man is: the nature of his creation, his form, his likeness, his Torah, and his ultimate end. For everything is chosen and hinted at, and as it is said, "This is the wise man, for his hand rules over all." He leaves an impression that ascends to the highest heights to cling to Him, blessed be He—and the opposite is also true, Heaven forbid. Then his heart will be inflamed to be "wholehearted with the Lord his God," to walk in His ways and to cling to Him with a bond of desire and longing, like a "Great Love" and an "Eternal Love." Then all words of moral rebuke and the "lamp of the commandment and the light of Torah" will enter his heart. "A wise man will hear and increase his learning." I hereby name this precious introduction:
### The Generations of Man
For in it will be revealed the occurrences of Man in this world and the next, and his time. Just as "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph" is interpreted to mean the *events* that befell them, so too the occurrences of Man will be recorded in this introduction. This includes the excellence of Man in particular, and then the collective—the Nation of Israel, who are called "Adam," as the Sages interpreted: "You are called 'Adam,' but the idol-worshipping nations are not called 'Adam.'" <note>A legal/spiritual distinction in the Talmud regarding ritual purity, often interpreted by later philosophers as a distinction in spiritual potential rather than biological humanity.</note>

->And I begin with the help of God, my Rock and my Redeemer:<-

---

## In the name of the Lord: "This is the book of the generations of Adam. On the day that God created man, in the likeness of God He made him; male and female He created them, and He blessed them and called their name Adam on the day they were created." (Genesis 5:1-2)

<margin>These three are the three roots: the root of the Existence of God, the root of the Torah of God, and the root of Attachment to God.</margin>
Man was made and created in the "Image of God" to know that "the Lord is God" and to strive to be "like God."

<margin>The Ramban <note>Nachmanides, 13th-century scholar</note> wrote in his commentary on the vision of Rav Sherira Gaon that they handed over to one another the "Book of Faces" and the secret of the lines [of the hand and forehead], which are hinted at in the order of the verses and the cantillation marks. He writes that all these are secrets of the Torah and mysteries, and without these "signs," one cannot truly grasp the depths. But we have not merited to fully understand them. (End of Ramban's words).</margin>

### Man
Who was made and created in the image of God, is a sign and a symbol for the existence of God. "Upon the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man" (Ezekiel 1:26), and it is said, "From my flesh I shall see God" (Job 19:26). I will explain all of this at length, if the God who is with us grants me life. And as for him being created "to know that the Lord is God"—this is achieved through the Torah of God, as it says regarding the giving of the Torah: "You have been shown to know that the Lord is God; there is none else beside Him." We will explain the nature of this "knowledge" at length.

His duty is to be "like God" through "cleaving" (attachment) to His name, as it says: "And you who cling to the Lord your God are all alive today." This is the true intelligence: to become like the Eternal God. Although this verse refers to man while he is still alive in this world—"today" meaning to do His commandments and emulate His attributes—nevertheless, this attachment is the essential cause for receiving a reward tomorrow, which is the attachment and life of the World to Come: eternal, spiritual life. This follows the secret that "the reward for a commandment is the commandment itself," for reward and punishment are not merely arbitrary agreements, but are intrinsic <note>original: "עצמיים" (essential/inherent)</note>. True life is rooted above. This also applies to the punishment for a transgression: the "thought of a transgression" is the transgression in the heart, meaning its evil root is like "poison and wormwood."

This matter will be explained at length, God willing, for everything depends on Man's choice. Indeed, God created Man for this purpose: that he should choose the attachment of life, as it says: "I have set life and death before you, the blessing and the curse; therefore choose life." Rashi explains: "I instruct you to choose the portion of life, like a man who says to his son, 'Choose a good portion in my inheritance.'" On this it is said, "The Lord is the portion of my inheritance... You maintain my lot." It is proper to take the good lot.

Good and evil both come from God's intention, but the "good" is intended for its own sake and flows essentially from God, whereas "evil" exists as a necessity of the material world. Or rather, everything is by His divine intention, for He "makes peace and creates evil." The reward for a commandment is essential to the commandment, and the punishment for a sin is essential to the sin. But "goods" are intended for themselves, while "evils" are intended for the sake of something else [to achieve a greater good]. When we look closely, we find that the ultimate purpose of "evil" is equal to the ultimate "good," for everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created was created only for His glory. Without "evil" [punishment/consequence], man would not fear God, and "from doing it not for its own sake, one comes to do it for its own sake." The Sages said: "The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the fear of Heaven."

It is written: "I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever... and God has done it so that men should fear before Him." This explains the whole discourse: just as He is sanctified through the righteous, He is sanctified through the wicked. "The Lord is known by the judgment He executes." The general rule is: "goods" are the purpose of Love for God, and "evils" are the purpose of Fear. However, God desires that we choose "Life," which is the ultimate goal. From the mouth of the Most High, "evils" do not proceed—only "Good"—meaning He desires the lot of choosing the Good. These matters will also be explained at length.

And these are the "Three Roots" upon which the author of *Sefer Ha-Ikkarim* <note>Rabbi Joseph Albo, 15th century</note> founded his book: The Existence of God, Torah from Heaven, and Reward and Punishment.

These three are hinted at in the verse I began with: "In the name of the Lord... this is the book..." Even though the phrase "In the name of the Lord" belongs to the preceding text, the Torah can be interpreted through hints, forward and backward, up and down. "In the name of the Lord" refers to the *Existence of God*. "This is the book" refers to the *Book of this Torah* (Torah from Heaven). He uses the word "This" <note>Hebrew: *zeh*</note> as if pointing with a finger. He could have said "These are the generations," but "This" hints that the Torah has "two faces": the Written Torah and the Oral Torah, hinted at by "male and female." Even though the whole Torah is written in the masculine, for the female is included in the male, there is a hint here: the letters *Vav* and *He* [of the Divine Name] are equal in their "small numerical value," indicating their unity. Thus it says "This [masculine] Book." And "Generations of Adam" means their developments and cycles until they reached the settlement of the Land of Israel—and in them, the events of Man until they reach the:
->Settlement of the Upper, eternal Land of Israel.<-

<meta>Continuity with previous page: The author continues the discussion of the divine structure, moving from the human correspondence to the ten verses of the Rosh Hashanah liturgy into a deep Kabbalistic analysis of the Divine Names and the nature of the Infinite (Ein Sof).</meta>

# Behold,
There are three elevations, one above the other: **1.** The unfolding of the Names, which are the *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers or attributes through which God interacts with the universe</term>, and their unity from the perspective of Cause and Effect. This is where the essence of this unfolding of *Atzilut* <term>Atzilut: the world of Emanation, the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term> descends. These are the words of the *Pardes* <note>original: "Pardes Rimmonim" by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. **2.** The secret of the Name <note>original: "Yod-Yod-He-He," a specific meditative spelling of the Tetragrammaton</note>, the "Simple Living Essence," which is without vowel points. Its branches and the vitality of the *Sefirot* serve as "garments" for them. This simple Being is the internal essence of the Emanation—the soul within the *Sefirot*—as described by the Maharam"a <note>Rabbi Menahem Azariah da Fano, a prominent 16th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> in the *Poteach HaRimon*. 

Behold, regarding this Name that includes the unfolding of Emanation, the "Exhaler of Breath" <note>God</note> said: "This is My Name forever" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. As the Sages taught: "Not as I am written am I read." I am not read with the letter *Aleph* <note>Adonai</note> but written with the letters of the Four-Letter Name. Yet, there is a level "high above the high," which is the Soul of the Emanation, the Simple Living Essence. In its branches, it is neither read nor written, but only contemplated in the meditation of the heart's intellect, following the secret of the "Backwards" <note>a specific Kabbalistic method of divine concealment</note>. 

The Tanna <term>Tanna: a sage from the era of the Mishnah</term> called these two levels—Vitality and Unfolding—"My Name." This is the secret of the Divine Beings, which is the Soul, and "His Name." This "His Name" refers to the revelation of the unfolding Names in the *Zohar* <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>. For it is written: "When I call out the Name of the Lord, ascribe greatness to our God" <note>Deuteronomy 32:3</note>. What is the "Name of the Lord"? Rabbi Simeon said: This refers to what is written, "ascribe greatness to our God," which is the attribute of *Gedulah* <note>Greatness/Kindness</note>. "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note> refers to the attribute of *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/Harmony</note>. "For all His ways are justice" refers to the attribute of *Mishpat* <note>Justice</note>. "A God of faithfulness" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note> refers to *Netzach* and *Hod* <note>Eternity and Splendor</note>. "Righteous and upright" refers to *Yesod* <note>Foundation</note>, and "Upright" refers to *Malchut* <note>Kingship/Sovereignty</note>. This is the general rule of the Holy Name.

As Rabbi Hiyya said: From this verse comes a teaching of High Wisdom. The end of the verse binds the "Bonds of Faith." It is written: "He is all, He is outside, He is one without separation." Though these attributes seem many, they return and are bound into One. He was, He is, and He will be—He is One, blessed be His Name forever and ever. The concept of "He" refers to the hidden level of the Soul that binds and connects everything.

We find the distinction of "He and His Name" in two aspects. However, above in the heights of the heavens, in the Root of all Roots, before the revelation of the Emanation, then "He and His Name are One." At that level, there are no "thoughts" of the Great Name, only the Will (*Ratzon*) within Him, through which He desires to do good and to be the object of intellect for all existences and Names. This Will is the source of all Vitality and Names. "He and His Name are One" because "He" is His Name and "His Name" is His Essence. As it is written: "He is the Lord... His Name is One." There, the Name is neither read nor written, nor even grasped in the contemplation of thought, even by Michael the Great Prince <note>the archangel Michael</note>. I have written about this in *Chesed L'Avraham* <note>by Rabbi Abraham Azulai</note>: that which we call "Will" is the secret of concealment. This is called the "Highest Hiddenness of all Hiddenness," for the word "His Name" <note>original: "Shemo"</note> has the same numerical value <term>Gematria: the system of assigning numerical value to Hebrew letters</term> as "Will" <note>original: "Ratzon," both equaling 346</note>. This hints at the supernal world that "rose in His thought" before the Blessed One.

Another interpretation: Sometimes the Four-Letter Name equals 176, and "Eight" equals "His Name." We find in the *Zohar* (portion of *Pekudei*) that when speaking of the "Cause of all Causes," it says it does not stand to be known, for it is the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). The *Pardes* (Gate of *Tzachtzachot*, Chapter 5) writes: "The Infinite is not subject to poverty..." 

The meaning is that the Will in the Creator, the Infinite, is One. If we were to say He "desires" something new, it would imply He changes from one will to another, which is impossible according to the laws of His Divinity. Therefore, the beginning of the expansion of Emanation is the "Will to Emanate." This Will is hidden; it is not a fully revealed Emanation, but rather a Will that "is pleased" to emanate. This Will is not the "Willer" Himself, but the Essence of the Infinite is the "Willer." He is called "Willer" through the medium of the "Will." This is explained in the *Gate of Essence and Vessels*, Chapter 4. In this way, we find the Will is closest to the Emanator because it is not yet "Emanation" but is Essence itself. However, it is the result of the Cause's Will to Emanate. Therefore, this Will is the "First Emanated" that came into being from the side of the Cause’s desire to emanate those who are emanated, as explained in the previous chapter. According to the Divine Honor, there is a chain of Will until it becomes a "Point of Unfolding." These Wills, in the secret of Essential Unity, are called His "Desires" <note>original: "Re'utav"</note>. Because of their hiddenness, the *Zohar* says: "The Infinite... does not stand for His desires."

He follows his own reasoning from the *Gate of Essence and Vessels* (Chapter 9): "The matter is that they attributed Knowledge to the Creator and said it is His Will... for regarding other descriptions, we cannot attribute them to Him... but I say, since we said above that the Creator is the Infinite, He is the Attribute of Wisdom itself, not possessing a wisdom external to Him... so we say that *Keter* <note>the highest Sefirah, "Crown"</note> is called Will, and the Creator 'wills' through it." He expanded on this in the *Gate of Tzachtzachot*. Similarly, "Power" is called a strength in the Creator, and He "knows" through *Da'at* <note>Knowledge</note>, meaning the attribute of *Da'at* is the Knowledge of the Creator. He knows through it and from within it. This is a necessity, as the verse says: "By His knowledge the depths were broken up" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. This does not contradict the idea that "He and His Wisdom are One." 

This applies to our human understanding before the Will rose to be revealed; then, the Infinite "did not stand to be known," being without end or beginning, for He is the Absolute Ancient One. Then, it was not even appropriate to use terms like "Essence" or "Root of Roots," for those only apply when the Will rises to be revealed. Then He is the "Root of Roots," and "He and His Name are One." Then we can say the Infinite "stands to be known," and from this His Name is called "The Beginning," to hint at His concealment. One might say "Infinite" because even though He is the Highest Concealment from the perspective of created beings, He has no end; but in the aspect of "not standing to be known"...

<meta>Catchword: expansion/extending</meta>

<column-break/>

**Gevurah** <note>Might/Severity</note>: The Name Y-H-W-H is vocalized entirely with the *Holam* vowel <note>the 'oh' sound</note>. **Netzach** <note>Victory/Eternity</note> also has the Name Y-H-W-H vocalized entirely with the *Hirik* vowel <note>the 'ee' sound</note>; this is the Name through which *Netzach* is revealed. **Hod** <note>Splendor</note> has the Name Y-H-W-H vocalized with the *Kibbutz* vowel <note>the 'oo' sound</note>. **Yesod** <note>Foundation</note> also has the Name Y-H-W-H vocalized entirely with the *Shurek* vowel <note>the 'oo' sound</note>. **Malchut** <note>Kingship</note> has the Name Y-H-W-H without any vowel points at all, simply the letters. According to the tradition received, so is the vocalization.

# There is 
However, a Simple Being without vocalization that includes the entire Emanation in its hidden subtlety. These ten Beings, with their specific vocalizations for each and every *Sefirah*, are the "branches" of the Simple Being. This is the meaning of the "expansion of the essence" understood by the Sages of Truth: that the essence and root of the unity of the Emanation in their source are contemplated through the grasp of the heart's intellect. It was without vocalization because it is the "Root of the Name," and the Being that is revealed in the unfolding of the Names—which are never erased—is where the Name includes them all, as we shall explain. This expansion of the Essence into ten Names is according to the excellence, level, subtlety, and closeness of each Name to the Emanator.

Before the Emanation, in absolute terms, there were no "vessels" or "boundaries." Everything was a simple, subtle, and unified light. When the Will arose to reveal His greatness and unity, the *Sefirot* existed within Him in total concealment, much like the flame is bound to the coal. This subtlety is beyond human description. Before the expansion into the various Names, the *Sefirot* were founded in His vitality, all unified in His essence and bound to Him in an ultimate bond. It is impossible to speak of "existence" regarding the *Sefirot* at this stage, for they were purely potential within His unity. Just as the soul is hidden within the body, so were the *Sefirot* hidden within the Infinite. We cannot even use the language of "vessels" to describe them yet. When it rose in His simple Will to arrange His powers, the *Sefirot* emerged from the absolute source like a soul emerging into a body. # The Generations of Adam

<margin>The principles of YHWH: for His emanation is His Name.</margin>

**The heart**—and this is His name by which they shall call Him in the heights of heaven, all the hosts above, arrayed rank against rank: "Where is the place of His glory?" <note>A reference to the Kedushah prayer, where angels ask where God's glory dwells.</note> to revere Him, for His place is not known and they cannot grasp Him with understanding. However, what is revealed to us of His Divinity and a fraction of His loftiness is from His emanations, according to the path of Truth <note>Kabbalah</note>, which teaches something of the hidden and concealed realms. The Essential Name—which is the Four-Letter Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>—indicates the essence of all His emanations, both in general and in detail, as was revealed through His merciful will for our merit to Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him. Regarding His existence within the emanations, many interpretations have been offered, as we shall explain in its own chapter with God's help.

***

**And the perfect sage**, the Ramak <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (1522–1570), a foundational systemizer of Kabbalah</note>, wrote in *Pardes Rimmonim* <note>The Pomegranate Orchard</note>, page 24a, that this is a name for the essence of the Emanation... not for the essence of the Emanator <note>the Infinite, or Ein Sof</note>, Heaven forbid, but rather for the inner aspect of the Emanation, which is the soul within the *Sefirot* <term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes or channels through which God interacts with the universe</term>. These *Sefirot* are to Him like "vessels" for the actions that flow from Him into the separated world below. And since that sage, peace be upon him, in his book *Gate 19, Chapter 1*, distanced the association of the Great Name even from the essence of the Emanation, I must direct the reader back, for it branches out from the One according to his system. Thus far his words. Behold, "these and those are the words of the Living God," <note>A Talmudic phrase meaning both opinions hold spiritual truth</note> for "one high official watches over another, and there are higher ones over them." <note>Ecclesiastes 5:7</note> This requires a broad explanation, and through our explanation, the teaching of Rabbi Elazar in his chapters will be clarified. The Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> cited it in their books: "Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name alone."

And Rabbi Yosef Hayyat wrote in *Ma'arekhet Ha-Shemot* <note>The Array of Names</note> that the letters from which the Name is built did not yet exist; for this reason, they are called *Otiyot* <note>Letters</note> from the language of *Atah* <note>You/Coming</note>, meaning they arrived after the Emanations were revealed. It says so explicitly in the *Ra'aya Meheimna* <note>The Faithful Shepherd, a later layer of the Zohar</note> in the portion of *Bo*: "To whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" <note>Isaiah 40:25</note>. Before the Holy One, Blessed be He, created any image in the world and formed any shape, He was alone, without shape or likeness. And for anyone who knew Him before creation—He who is beyond any image—it is forbidden to make for Him any shape or image in the world, not with the letter *Yod*, nor with the letter *He*, and not even with the Explicit Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>, nor with any letter or vowel point at all. This is the meaning of "For you saw no image" <note>Deuteronomy 4:15</note>—anything that has an image or likeness is not Him. But after He made this image of the **Celestial Adam** <term>Adam Kadmon/Elyon: the first spiritual manifestation of the Divine in the void</term>, He descended there and was called by that image "YHWH," so that He might be known through each and every attribute of His. He called Himself *El, Elohim, Shaddai, Tzevaot, Ehyeh*, so that they would recognize Him in every attribute: how the world is guided by Kindness (*Chesed*) and Judgment (*Din*) according to the deeds of humanity. For if His light did not spread over all creatures, how would they know Him? And how would the verse "The whole earth is full of His glory" be fulfilled? Thus far the language necessary for our subject. If so, I wonder: how could it be said "Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name"? Indeed, many are the interpretations and the commentators on these words of the aforementioned *Pirkei De-Rabbi Elazar*. However, I shall reveal to you what has become clear to me in this matter, built upon foundations I received from the mouths of scribes and from books, with the help of Him who grants knowledge to man.

<margin>
<note>Abbreviated kabbalistic formulas</note>
And there he gathers the nicknames of YHW as a key to our intention in the composition
**The Path of Life**
To grant you insight, to teach you
the way to reach *Devekut* <term>Devekut: "cleaving" or spiritual attachment to God</term> as
it is said: "And you who cleave to the Lord your God." May YHWH assist in his study

then you will understand what I wrote
in the introductory composition... which deals with this Name, and there is benefit
in understanding all that is hinted at regarding the secrets of the Name in this work.
</margin>

In this teaching of Rabbi Elazar, one must be very precise regarding the language, for he said, "Before the world was created" (*nivra*). The master grammarians have already noted: "You are He, our God, before the world was created," and so it is printed in all Ashkenazi prayer books. Yet others leave it as: "You are He, our God, before You created the world" (*barata*). For "was created" (*nivra*) might imply, Heaven forbid, as if the world was created by another and not by Him. Thus it appears in the Sephardic prayer books. However, to correct the text in *Pirkei De-Rabbi Elazar* seems difficult to me. In truth, the author of *Avodat Ha-Kodesh* and *Tola'at Ya'akov* wrote in these two books of his that some read in *Pirkei De-Rabbi Elazar* "before it was created" (*nivra*) and some read "before He created" (*bara*). However, in almost all the books of the Sages of Truth, the version is: "Before the world was created, there was He and His Name alone." Therefore, I say that this version is the true one, and likewise, in the Ashkenazi prayer books, one should not amend or change the established text. Indeed, the version "You are He... before the world was created" is found in the *Tosafot* <note>Medieval Talmudic commentaries</note> in the third chapter of *Berakhot*, and in the chapter *Arvei Pesachim*, and in the *Tur* code of law, section 46.

***

**And behold**, God has graced me with an explanation of Rabbi Elazar's words in two ways, and everything leads to one place—the secret of the Blessed Unity. One way will be analyzed precisely, and both are right.

<margin>
Analyze the word "Was" (*Hayah*) in the phrase "He and His Name were."
Analyze the word "He" (*Hu*) in the phrase "He and His Name were."
Together, and how their sign is the *Pataḥ* vowel.
</margin>

***

**All the Names of YHWH:** those who seek the hidden meanings of our Torah through Tradition <note>Kabbalah</note>—whether they be from the masters of Kabbalah, the masters of the literal meaning (*Peshat*), or the researchers of our holy Torah—all have agreed with one voice that this Name is: **The Essential Name** and the root of all other names; they are emanated from it and it includes them all. To the Sages initiated into the "Secret of the Lord," it is explained that there are three levels through which we perceive the matter of the Essential Name:

The names written in the Torah that may not be erased are ten: *Adonai, Yahu, YHWH* with the vowels of *Elohim, El, Elohim, YHWH* with the vowels of *Tzevaot, YHWH Tzevaot, Elohim Tzevaot, Shaddai, Adonai*. And these ten names are the Emanation (*Atzilut*) of the Ten Sefirot: *Keter* (Crown), *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), *Binah* (Understanding), etc. The *Sefirot* are the Names, and the Names are the *Sefirot*. For the spirituality of the *Sefirot* yearns for and shines upon the Names through the intention of the one who writes them or utters them with his lips in holiness and purity. Just as the Holy Temple is a palace and a place for the indwelling of the *Shekhinah* <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence</term>, so that the Divine light is concentrated between the two poles of the Ark, so too these ten Names are "palaces" for the spirituality of the *Sefirot* hinted at in the Name YHWH. For the *Yod* refers to *Chokhmah* and its tip hints at *Keter*; the first *He* is *Binah*; the *Waw* hints at *Tiferet* with its six extremities; and the final *He* is *Malchut* (Kingship). As we shall explain the matter further on for the one who understands well.

***

**And the spirituality** of the *Sefirot* serves as a "garment" for the inner spirituality hinted at by the Four-Letter Name within each and every *Sefirah*, as stated in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note>. They are distinguished by their vowel points: 

Higher Crown (*Keter Elyon*) is יְהוָֹה and its vowels are entirely the *Qamatz* <note>looks like a small 'T'</note>, indicating the Crown; its four letters indicate the ten Sefirot within it <insert>YHWH</insert> so that there is no separation, Heaven forbid. 
The Name of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is יְהוָֹה and its vowels are entirely the *Pataḥ* <note>a horizontal line</note>, and it is the Name through which Wisdom is revealed. 
Understanding (*Binah*) also has a Name <insert>YHWH</insert> and its vowels are entirely the *Tzere* <note>two dots side-by-side</note>, and it is the Name through which Understanding is revealed. 
Kindness (*Chesed*) also has a Name יְהוָֹה through which Kindness is revealed, and its vowels are entirely the *Segol* <note>three dots in a triangle</note>. 
Strength (*Gevurah*) also has a Name YHWH and its vowels are entirely the *Sheva* <note>two vertical dots</note>, and it is the Name through which Strength is revealed.
