# House 5

Because one must not investigate what lies between the Infinite <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*, the Boundless God prior to any self-manifestation</note> and the Crown <note>Hebrew: *Keter*, the first and highest of the ten Sefirot</note> at all, except to say that they are cleaved to the Infinite and emanate within the Crown, we call their existence a "revelation of thought." The subtlety within the Infinite draws a flow of influence to the delicate roots within the Crown. Thus, their existences were emanated from level to level. As long as they remain close to the Emanator, they are called "Faces" <note>Hebrew: *Panim*, representing the direct, revealed aspect of divinity</note>, and as they distance themselves, they are called "Backwards" <note>Hebrew: *Achoryaim*, representing a diminished or concealed divinity</note>. Therefore, there are many "Faces" to the awesome Face, and many "Backs" to the visible Backs. This ends the quote.

**Behold**, these matters are at their roots incomparably more sublime and eternal. If we were to say "before He created the world," it might imply that the world was an innovation <note>A change in God's perfect, unchanging nature</note>, Heaven forbid, even at the root level. But this is not so; for there is no change or innovation on His part, only from the perspective of the created beings that were formed and revealed now.

**And the holy man of God**, the Arizal <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria (1534–1572), the father of contemporary Kabbalah</note> of blessed memory, brought forth the four "fillings" <term>Miluim: a Kabbalistic method of expanding a name by spelling out its letters</term> of the Name YHWH: *Yod Yod He*, *Vav He*, *Yod He*, *Vav He*, *Yod He*, *Vav He*, *Yod He*, *Vav He*.

->Yod Yod He and Vav He Yod He Vav He Yod He Vav He<-
->Yod He and Vav He, 4, and it was revealed by the Arizal of blessed memory in the verse "Let there be<-
->light and there was light," which speaks of the lower realms, and the hint in the upper realms; he said the hint is "Goral" <note>Lot/Fate</note> or *Or* <note>Light</note> with a *Resh* in the third, and is the 7th at the end, which is the Light of the Lot without beginning:<-

And without end, may He be blessed and exalted. The word *Or* <note>Light</note> with a *Resh* equals 235 <note>Numerical value of Or (Light)</note> as the count of these four fillings. This is the secret of the Sages' statement: "And there was light"—meaning it *already* existed, for they were hidden within the Absolute Light.

**Furthermore**, we shall explain the words of Rabbi Eliezer the Great in another way regarding the precision of the word "Was" (*Hayah*), for he said, "He and His Name were alone." We shall first present the words of the book *Nagid U-Metzaveh* <note>A liturgical Kabbalistic work by Jacob Zemah</note> regarding the Name YHWH. *Hayah* <note>Was</note> is the Unique Name that hints at the ancient existence in its absolute "Necessary Existence" <term>Mechuyav Ha-Metziut: a philosophical term for a being that must exist by its very nature</term>. For this Name accounts for the fact that a being exists. Once there is "Existence" (*Havayah*), it is found. This refers to the Absolute that brings all existence into being. For if it were conceivable that He does not exist, no other being would have the possibility of existence or being. Since He is the truth of all existence, all beings depend on Him, and all beings would be nullified by His nullification, because He is the foundation of the truth of all being and existence.

However, He would not be nullified by the nullification of all beings, for He is the Truth of Existence and does not depend on anything else. Since this is so, observe the secret of His Unique Name: it is the Name of Existence <note>The Tetragrammaton YHWH is etymologically related to the Hebrew word for "to be" or "existence"</note> prior to any beings coming into existence. By the power of His existence, they exist. Without the Name of Existence, they would not emerge from being into the existence of life. Thus, when He is in the Name of Existence, it indicates that all life-forces are found through His life, and from His existence they were found. If it were conceivable that He does not exist, all existences would be nullified, for He is the cause of the truth of all life-forces. If they were all nullified, He is not nullified, for there is no Name of Existence other than Him that is drawn as a likeness to existences.

**And on this**, Rabbi Eliezer the Great hinted that "He and His Name [were alone]," as it is written: *Hayah* <note>Was</note>, meaning the "Necessary Existence." This is the meaning of "He and His Name." It does not mean the physical shape of the letters of the Name YHWH, Heaven forbid, but rather the Truth of Existence. However, when the world was innovated and the shapes of the letters were innovated, the "Existence" came to rest upon the shapes of the letters. For without the Name of Existence, there would be no shape to the letters. When the letters were innovated, all the other Names were innovated. Through the shape of the letters, the Divine Existence enters into the investigation of other Names, as they are drawn after the "Existence," but not from within the "Existence" itself, which does not dwell upon anything other than the truth of what was an existence like itself. Therefore, when the shapes of letters and the world were innovated, all the other Names drawn after Existence were innovated for Him. All this is from the words of *Nagid U-Metzaveh*. Thus, the words of Rabbi Eliezer the Great are correct and upright regarding the Name YHWH and its concealment, which is why it is not pronounced as written. There are two paths we have mentioned: the letters *He* and *Yod* indicate the Necessary Existence—He who was, is, and will be.

**And it is clear** from the proofs of the holy Zohar regarding the levels, "level upon level, hidden and revealed," that there are three ascents as explained above. The secret of Emanation (*Atzilut*) is in its place, and the high unites with the high... the reality of the chain of evolution is included in the Name YHWH, which is His essence in His emanation, as the *Pardes* wrote. Then the Name is written but not read, and this reality comes from the inner reality of the Simple Name YHWH, the secret of the expansion of the Essence, which is the soul of the Emanation. This is the secret of the Simple Existence which is neither read nor written, except in the aspect of its "extension" <note>The flow of divine energy downward</note>. The Essence in the Root of Roots is hidden in total concealment in the secret of "He and His Name are One," as explained. "He was, is, and will be" is correctly applied in the explanation of the Zohar, for as I have previously established, the revealed is a reflection of the hidden, and they are level upon level, three ascents.

**And now** I have come to explain the matter of the Name YHWH as it includes all of Emanation, which all the Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> have spoken of: the *Yod* hints at Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and its tip hints at the Crown (*Keter*). The first *He* hints at Understanding (*Binah*). The *Vav* hints at Beauty (*Tiferet*) with its "extremities," which are Kindness (*Chesed*), Might (*Gevurah*), Beauty (*Tiferet*), Victory (*Netzach*), Splendor (*Hod*), and Foundation (*Yesod*). The final *He* hints at Sovereignty (*Malkhut*).

It is not hidden from me that there are many wondrous and lofty matters regarding this. Nevertheless, I will reveal to you a portion of what God has graced me with from the mouths of scribes and books, being one who understands from his own mind in the Zohar, Portion Tazria, page 43a: Rabbi Abba opened, "How manifold are Your works, O Lord" <note>Psalm 104:24</note>. How many crowns are the crowns of the Holy King! All of them are hidden in Wisdom. All of them You made with Wisdom. All are included in Wisdom and do not go out except through known paths to Understanding (*Binah*). From there they were all made and all repaired, as it is said, "And with understanding it is established." Therefore, "You made them all with Wisdom." This is like the matter of the ocean, which is the Assembly of Israel <note>A term for the Sefirah of Malkhut</note>, for from there it is filled with everything, as it is said, "All the rivers go to the sea, yet the sea is not full." From the ocean, she brings them forth later. This is the meaning of "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created (*be-hibare'am*)"—He created them with the letter *He* and established them with the Son <note>A play on words involving the letters of the Name</note> from the matter of the ocean. This ends the quote.

Know that the Emanation was only revealed in order to reveal His Divinity through His governance—to lead the world with Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy. The governing attributes—Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy—are enacted through the seven Sefirot: *Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut*. This follows the secret of male and female: the six extremities <note>The six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> follow the secret of the Male who influences, and the six extremities follow the secret of the Female who receives and influences to govern the worlds through them.

The *Pardes* wrote: "The Order of Emanation is such that the primary governance of the lower beings is only through the five extremities... they are the governors of Judgment in the world for good or ill according to the will of their Creator. Behold, these six extremities are like a tree whose courtyard is planted and sown." The intention is that the primary first existence is hidden, through which the watering of this tree occurs. This is the metaphor of being "fixed" within Understanding (*Binah*). From there, the "river goes out of Eden" to water the Garden of Edens so that it may produce fruit of its kind, whose seed is in it upon the lower earth, which is *Malkhut*.

Thus, these six extremities have three necessary states: the state of "planting," which are the roots; the state of being "sown," which are the branches of the tree; and the state of the "fruits," which are the influence of the action below. Now, for the matter of the reality of Emanation, these matters were necessary. When it arose in His will for His planting to be in the Crown (*Keter*), it would not have endured. Likewise in Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), due to their proximity to their Source, as we explained, the life-force in them was in the power of Simple Mercy, and there was no visible vision in them as required for governance. Therefore, when the "extremities" reached Understanding (*Binah*), that was their first planting. There is the reality of their root, so that from there their influence is flowed to them through the roots hidden in *Binah*. And their root in *Binah* comes from their root in *Chokhmah*, and their root in *Chokhmah* from their root in *Keter*.

There in *Binah* is the first existence of the "extremities" in a reality revealed toward Judgment and Mercy. For in *Chokhmah*, even though there is also an existence there—as hinted in the statement that "He carved and engraved in it within the curtain"—that is their existence in *Chokhmah*, as we shall explain. But in *Binah*, their existence was revealed toward Judgment and Mercy, in the sense that it is Judgment and "judgments are awakened from her." But from *Chokhmah*, judgments are not awakened. Even in *Binah* itself there is no judgment, only that they are awakened from her to be revealed in their own place.

Afterward, from *Binah*, they were "sown" into their own essential places. This is the second existence of the "extremities"—their actual place where all six extremities shine and act in their world. They are like the body of the tree that sucks from its roots; so too the Sefirot suck from the roots hidden in *Binah*. This is the second existence of all the extremities. Afterward, the tree produces its fruits, which are the actions of the Sefirot enacted through *Malkhut*, as is known. These six extremities are doubled: six for Judgment and six for Mercy. These are the twelve "Existences" (YHWH-names) in *Tiferet*, which are the twelve boundaries. This ends the quote.

**And what** was explained in the verse "How manifold are Your works," etc., means: How great are Your works! For the totality of Your works are hidden in Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), where there is no grasp, only the "Is-ness" of Wisdom that exists. And even though there is no further grasp other than the existence of its reality, nevertheless "all of them"—meaning the totality of the ten Sefirot—are included within it. "You made them all with Wisdom" (*be-Chokhmah*)—the letter *Bet* [meaning "with" or "in"] indicates the place, like "a garden *in* Eden" or "a house *in* a field." So too, the meaning of the *Bet* is that they were all placed within the inner part of Wisdom and all hidden in its interior. Afterward, the verse says "You made," to indicate the system within Understanding (*Binah*), for there the "making" and repair of the Sefirot occurs, which is the repair of the reality of the roots of the "extremities" that were rooted there in the secret of planting. And afterward, the verse says...

### House of the Lord

<margin>
29
The cycle of the completion of Kingdom <note>Hebrew: *Malkhut*, the tenth and final Sefirah, associated with the physical world and divine sovereignty</note> is fixed, and regarding this year, what was and will be, one should not say it is flawed. Rather, anyone who merits even a small portion of intellect and asks about their essence and nature—behold, this will not be fulfilled in the aspect of the Emanator. In His aspect, there is "Nothing" <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*</note>, and they are hinted at by the acronym of the letters *Yod* of *Keter*, *Yod* of Wisdom, *Vav* of Understanding, as explained in the words of the Rashbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, see there in many places. And so it is explained in the "Gate of Names" <note>A section of the *Etz Chayim*, the primary text of Lurianic Kabbalah</note> etc., until their stature reaches the point of being designated as holy.
</margin>

The light spreads within it even if, Heaven forbid, His letters are not like [human] letters. Rather, He is the Root and the Beginning of all original existences in various "Faces," all of which are branches of the absolute Spark, called by a "Name" to benefit others. He is truly called the Infinite <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*</note>, for He is the Master of a simple Name that has no end, just as His life has no beginning. Therefore, Maimonides <note>The Rambam, 1135–1204</note> did not mention the aspect of God, may He be blessed, in his primary principles [regarding eternity], for it is obvious that He is eternal since He is primordial. It is known that everything primordial is eternal, though not everything eternal is primordial; for many created things will be eternal by the Will of the Creator. These matters are simple in themselves and are proven from their context, even if those who disagree with Maimonides did not descend to their depths—and not out of wisdom. Here too, His Name and His Will are the beginning; we need to inform that they have a beginning in terms of the "leaning of wills" and not in a temporal sense, but they have no end whatsoever. This ends his words. The general rule arising from our words previously:

---

In various places [it is written]: "He is the Sanctuary." Thus He is called the "circle of the world" in Scripture, and similarly by the name of the "Worlds" which indicates the hiddenness [of the divine]. And the "beginning of the hidden" is called "Being" <note>Hebrew: *Yesh*</note>, and this is the "Existing Being" <note>Hebrew: *Yesh mi-Ayin*, being from nothingness</note>, meaning Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*, the second Sefirah</note> from the Crown <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note>. And even though Wisdom is still the ultimate subtlety and simple light, it is designated for revelation through the Sefirot. Regarding their stature, they are referred to by the name "Thought," just as thought is the root [of action] and is not yet a concrete thing. So too is Wisdom; it is the root and the beginning of the letters that are in the Crown. Even though they are in the Crown, because they are called "Being" (*Yesh*), and there is the absolute hiddenness, it does not mean there is a tangible "substantiality" (*Yeshut*). However, the intention behind the word "Being" (*Yesh*) is as stated: between the "Nothing" (*Ayin*) and the "Being" (*Yesh*), there is no absolute substantiality at all, but rather that there is some beginning of existence. Even the term "Being" does not apply to "Thought" in relation to its own aspect, but only in relation to the aspect of the "Understanding" <note>Hebrew: *Binah*, the third Sefirah</note>. In this way, the explanation of "Being" is the letter *Yod* of Wisdom and the letter *He* of Understanding, as explained in the "Gate of Names." Therefore, although these two Sefirot are included in their root, the lower ones are not mentioned. This matter does not mean that the Sefirot cannot be included [in the root] at all; for everything is included in the "Source of Sources," all within the "Nothingness" and all within the "Thought." The entire matter is a hidden mystery.

---

...that the world was created in the aspect that "it arose in His Will" to be. Then He is the Root of the root of roots, and it is He and His Name alone—meaning, He is One and His Name is One.

And the existences and the Names were revealed in their place, which are two unifying aspects. But in the aspect of the Infinite <note>Ein Sof</note>, which is not subject to inquiry before the Will arose, it is not appropriate to say "Essence" or "Root," only—Heaven forbid—"He and His Name" and "He is He." Then His Will, His Knowledge, and His Power are His very Essence. When we say "His Will," "His Knowledge," and "His Power," it is not appropriate to call them by a name; we only do so because we cannot prevent our mouths from speaking of His absolute Holy Essence. In the aspect of His Will arising, then "He is One and His Name is One," and only in the aspect of "He and His Name are One." A hint to this is found in the verse "High above the high" and "The living creatures were above them"—"High above the high" refers to the aspect after revelation; then the secret of "HE" <note>Hebrew: *Hu*</note> is above the secret of "His Name." This is "High above the high." But in His hiddenness, before the world was created, we do not distinguish "high above high" between the secret of "He" and "His Name," for all is a simple unity of ultimate simplicity. Therefore it says "And the living creatures were above them." This is the foundation of the verse: "For He spoke and it was, He commanded and they were created." Nachmanides <note>The Ramban, 1194–1270</note> in the portion of Genesis explains that every instance of "And He said" means "desire and will." This is "HE spoke"—meaning, it arose in His Will to be revealed then. "And it was" refers to the secret of the Existences. "He commanded and they were created" refers to the secret of the revelation of the Names. Do not be surprised by the word "created," for we find "In the beginning God created," which the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> explained as referring to the secret of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds, where the divine light is most pure</term>.

<margin>
Translator's Note: I found in the writings of the scholar, may God protect him, Rabbi Joseph... [illegible name]... This was written at the time of the world's creation. What was written in our heart was to clarify that the beginning was the Will, may He be blessed. The intention of the Holy One was to make "Existences" within it, which are at the end of this desire. For what loss is there to His place in what was in His Will before? It would not return to be a helper... from the beginning... God is not like a man who regrets... as it is written: "For I, the Lord, have not changed." If so, how could the thought to create the world arise in His Will in its glory, and not before then? For therefore they said: "Better that I be answered by the ancients," who said the world is primordial [pre-existent] rather than saying He, may He be blessed, changed His mind... Heaven forbid that there should be a change in His Will... He is the One who leads... and He is the One who stood for us... He made the created beings by Will and not by necessity... One cannot give a reason for "Why," for there is no "reason" in the Will... You should not consider the beginning more than the end... for the "Knowledge" of the Beginning is more manifest than the "End"... and there is no reason for His Will... For wherever there is a reason, there is a branch above it... And if you should say, "Behold, all created things were made in their time," and He is the cause of their timing... The matter of primordiality is a holy matter, and He is the source of the creation of the world... And with this, it is said there is a reason... for there, the simple Will is not touched by anything else... for He alone knows His Name, and His Truth and Knowledge are His place... so one cannot grasp His Knowledge, for He is a Will without limit or reason... and the expansion [of light] was included in the "Many"... for everyone who reaches the gate of the "Highest Ancients"... which is the knowledge of His Essence, may He be blessed... there is no change in the souls nor in the Creator, may He be blessed... for there is no change... His Will never changes, and He knows why "then" and not before now, for His Knowledge is His place. End of quote.
</margin>

<margin>
And then
</margin>

...the matter of "before [the world] was created" will be clarified—and it does not say "before He created." We shall first provide a brief introduction from what is written in the *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero, 1522–1570</note>, Gate 1, "The Gate of Existence," as follows: "The matter is that the words of Holiness, Emanation, and Spirituality do not follow the ways of this lower world. The reason is that physical matters are of lesser value. When a man creates an action or a thing, his essence becomes physical. It is impossible for a man to perform a desired action unless the previous physical states of the body are first nullified, acting as vessels that transform into the desired thing. For example, when a man wants to produce a garment to wear, the wool or hair is shorn from the animal. In truth, the wool is called the 'first action,' and the animal is left stripped and naked, losing its former glory as its first state is battered to become another existence. Afterward, that wool is whitened, and after its whitening, its first existence (as it was on the body) does not remain, for the first physical state has passed away, and it has acquired a more beautiful existence than the first—the existence of pure, whitened wool. And when they spin that wool, it does not retain its first existence, for it has already been transformed into something more excellent: the thread. Then they might weave the garment, and the thread will not remain, for through the craft it has stripped off its first form and donned a more refined form. In this manner, as the crafts multiply, the forms are stripped away, nullified, and pass away as if they never were, and their first form and existence are no longer remembered.

"Behold, this is the case with physical accidents. But matters of Holiness, Spirituality, and Emanation are the opposite. These are not 'accidents.' Even when the types of emanations and spiritual beings spread out and don a more revealed form than they had before their expansion, their first existences are not nullified, Heaven forbid. Rather, on the contrary, things multiply without end, ascending without limit. Even if the spiritual subtlety changes into a more revealed existence, nevertheless, its first existence does not move from its place and its station is not missing. Furthermore, spirituality differs from physicality in this: in physicality, every new state is an 'elevation' over the previous one, particularly in human crafts... but on the contrary, as long as the previous existence is revealed, it is the essence and root for the renewed and emanated existence. The root draws from its root, and its root from its root, according to the multiplicity of existences, until this is dependent on that and that on this, all the way back to the one preceding them all. The higher they go, the more excellent they are, being closer to the Source and the True Root, which is the Root of all roots and the Source of all existence: the King of kings of kings." End of quote. Furthermore, he writes there: "When the Will arose before Him to emanate, there were formed the existences of the <term>Tzachtzachot: the 'Splendors' or 'Supernal Refulgences,' three hidden lights within/above Keter</term>, which are thin and hidden. From that subtle existence, the levels evolved until they reached the revelation of Thought, and there too were formed existences..."

Using an analogy from Cordovero's Pardes Rimonim, the text explains that unlike physical creation where the raw material is consumed, spiritual emanation allows the source to remain intact while producing new, revealed layers of existence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of Kabbalistic cosmology, specifically focusing on the structure of the Ten Sefirot (divine emanations) and how they emerge from the simple Will of the Infinite. It transitions from the hidden nature of the Crown (Keter) to the geometric and linguistic metaphors used to describe the four worlds of existence.</meta>

<page-num>6</page-num>
<header>The Fifth House</header>

Within it are the ten *Sefirot* <note>The ten creative powers or attributes through which the Divine interacts with the universe</note> one inside the other, and it is within these that they are hidden, each joined to the other. All of them are contained within the Crown (*Keter*), and to Him alone are they revealed. Within these *Sefirot* is the totality of everything, the essence where everything is revealed. He is the covering, and Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*) are in the "aperture" of the Crown. Through Wisdom, they are revealed from the totality of the "lines" revealed within it—five corresponding to the three lights which are thirty in the worlds. These are the Primordial Light (*Or Kadmon*), the Pure Light (*Or Tzach*), and the Refined Light (*Or Metzuchtzoach*). Just as they sparkle in the unity of the soul within it, they are within the three [higher Sefirot]. These are the *Sefirot* themselves, as I wrote in Chapter 29. And just as the hidden lines are in the *Sefirot* within it, all *Sefirot* are included in the three points. These are the three aspects I wrote about regarding the three Mercies, which are the three simple [aspects] taken from the words of the Rashbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> (may peace be upon him) in the "Book of the Name" regarding the secret of the Crown (*Keter*). And behold, in Wisdom, it was established within it, along with the three points that encompass all aspects. These are the three [letters] corresponding to the three Mercies, etc. Up to this point, I have copied from the words of "Moshe" <note>Referring to Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, known as the Ramak (1522–1570)</note>; see there at length for what pertains to this.

When "Moshe" desired to understand the secret of the simple [light], he established the line of Kindness (*Chesed*) to the right <note>original: "להימנו" - meaning the right side, associated with benevolence</note>, and the line of Judgment is not Strength (*Gevurah*) and Splendor (*Hod*). The secret of the line of Understanding (*Binah*) and the line of Mercy is Beauty (*Tiferet*), Foundation (*Yesod*), and Kingdom (*Malkhut*). This is the line of the Crown (*Keter*). These three lines comprise the "Glory," for it is the Body that connects its arms and pours out spirit to that Kingdom. These three lines are three, and this is "Behold" (*Hen*), "And They" (*Ve-hem*), "And there is" (*Ve-yesh*), and the letter *Yod*. These are worthy of the melody that enters from Kindness and above, and they are in the worlds in three. For the three roots mentioned above are established in the name of the "Three Yods." These *Yods* are the "legs" of the three lines, for the *Yod* is in the Crown, and in the "Mercies" which is the aspect of the Crown in its hiddenness. They have a *Yod* because Wisdom and Understanding in their root are filled within the Crown. Within the Crown, the aspect of the *Yod* is "empty" <note>unoccupied space for creation</note> in the aspect of Kindness. This is "He rode and went" <note>A reference to divine movement/manifestation</note>. The "One" is the root of the level of the three aspects in their place. In His body, in the Crown, on the "Day of Waters," and Understanding is in the Crown as I wrote. It is not that they become physical there, but only that points of Mercy are revealed there from the hiddenness, being refined and purified. These are the three points that become precious in that *Yod*—namely, Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding that are within the *Yod* of the Crown. The hiding of these physical things in the Crown, and the Wisdom and Understanding within the Crown, hides the "leg" of the *Yod* within, and that is the Kindness within it. The line of the letter *Vav* is the root of the level of Foundation (*Yesod*). It is called Primordial Light, Pure Light, and Refined Light. These two names are because He is the root of the Holy Spirit.

The "Fifth House" in its selection has two names for the three points, for they are the root of the three [letters] *He*, as mentioned. The root of the Holy [Spirit] is the "Shoulder and the Flank" <note>Anatomical metaphors for divine structures</note> which is the aspect of the completion of the "Garment" of the Kingdom (*Malkhut*). Know that the aspect of the "Mouth" exists in spirituality. These two names and the "Flank" hint at the aspect of the five [Sefirot]. The purpose of the *Sefirot* is for the sake of the ascent of His Will. He is the Root of the Root of the level of the roots that we divided into the roots of Primordial Light, Pure Light, and Refined Light. This is the reasoning for the "Throne of the Messiah" <note>original: "כרסי המשיח"</note>. This is what is meant by "ascent of His Will" to make it ready, for the word "His Will" (*Retzono*) shares the same root as the word "ascent." See how "ascent" exists in the cry, and in the worlds it returns. As is explained in the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of Intentions," the Will is to bequeath Will. For the Crown (*Keter*) is called "Will," and this Absolute Holy Will is of such a nature that one cannot call it by a name or say "Will" regarding it. Our intention in His thought is the Holy Will of the Ten *Sefirot*, for He created the world with a blessing. Even with vitality and strength, He established your lips.

## And Behold
The world is built on kindness <note>A reference to Psalm 89:3</note>, for we count from Kindness and below, where the secret of the three lines and the points and the expanse resides. Afterward, in the place of the level and in the Crown, three are emitted. The root of the "Sitting" and all these roots are the roots of Beauty (*Tiferet*). The root above is hidden until some revelation is revealed, and revelation follows revelation until the revelation in names and in the totality of Thought. Everything is Beauty (*Tiferet*), only that it is higher and higher than anything.

<sig>2 2</sig> <meta>catchword: The Excellences</meta>

<column-break/>

And the threads of the flame are inherited and stirred behind the desires. The light of Emanation (*Atzilut*) <note>The highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, closest to the Divine</note>, which is from the unattainable upper lights—these lights were revealed in the secret of "And God said, Let there be light, and there was light" <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. This "God" (*Elohim*) is the Attribute of Judgment included in our Will, the "contraction" (*Tzimtzum*) of His light so that it might spread. There is no change in the Emanator nor in the emanated in the secret of "and there was light," meaning the light that already existed, only it was hidden. While the world was in the root and the upper source as mentioned above, it was the secret of "God" (*Elohim*), for the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) is the "Soul of the Soul" of the *Sefirot*. They are the souls of everything that was formed afterward. The "Cause of all Causes" is the Soul to them in the secret of His Essence that spreads afterward.

The world of Emanation (*Atzilut*) spread through the Kingdom (*Malkhut*) by the contraction of their light, and the world of Emanation became the soul for the world of Creation (*Beriah*), just as the Infinite is to Emanation. Afterward, the world of Formation (*Yetzirah*) spread, which is the contraction of their light, and the world of Creation became the soul for the world of Formation. Afterward, the world of Formation spread by the contraction of its light and the world of Action (*Asiyah*) <note>The physical world</note> was formed. It is the soul for the aspect of the "Cause of all Causes" and "Reason of all Reasons," the Infinite, which is the power of Emanation. And Emanation is in the power of Creation, and Creation is in the power of Emanation—for the Infinite is their power. This Creation is the power of Formation, and Formation is in the power of Creation which is from the power of Emanation, which is from the power of the Infinite. This Formation is the power of Action. Only the light became hidden and "thickened" relative to the receiver.

This is the parable of Emanation: like a flame in a coal. The flame is revealed by the desire of the "fanning," yet it is attached and bound to the coal. Creation is like lighting a torch from a flame; the light of the torch does not remain attached and bound to the absolute "back" of the flame's light that lit it. Nevertheless, the torch has great status and great light, for its light is large and the light of the flame dwells within it. Formation is like lighting a candle from a torch, and this candle shines in a dark room. "And there was light"—behold, this entire chain of descent is one corresponding to the other in secret. It is revealed more, and it aids more. This is the secret of "light and dark" in the *Pardes*, Gate of Essence and Conduct, Chapter 11.

For the four elements exist in all worlds, only in the world of Action they are physical, but above in Formation they are spiritual. Namely: Michael is Water, Gabriel is Fire, Uriel is Air, Raphael is Earth. And above in the world of Creation, they are even more spiritual—namely, the Living Creatures (*Chayot*) that carry the Throne. Afterward, above, are the "legs" of the Throne until reaching the spirituality of Emanation, the ultimate spirituality: Kindness (*Chesed*) is Water, Strength (*Gevurah*) is Fire, Beauty (*Tiferet*) is Air, and Kingdom (*Malkhut*) is the Upper Earth. These are roots for those, and those for these. Therefore, everything that exists in the lower realms is a hint of the upper realms. We shall bring this hidden hint to the "Smith" <note>A metaphor for a scholar or craftsman of wisdom</note>. Every physical body has length, width, and depth. There is no physical thing in the world that does not have these three, for they are the boundaries of a body. If one were to imagine only two boundaries—length and width without depth—it would be called a "surface" <note>original: "שטח"</note>, which means like a "color" or the flat surface on a paper where length and width are applicable but depth cannot be imagined. Therefore it is so called. And when we imagine by way of the surface alone, meaning length without width, it is called a "line" <note>original: "קו"</note>, meaning the line of length devoid of width, and certainly devoid of depth. And when we imagine the absence of all three boundaries, the matter is a "point" <note>original: "נקודה"</note>. The point has neither length, nor width, nor depth. This is not because it can exist in physical reality, but it is called a "conceptual point," meaning a mental image of the absence of bodily boundaries, not that it exists [physically] in reality.

## And Behold
The ten *Sefirot*, the ninth and the seventh, in the filling of the letter *Yod*, hint at this Point, Line, and Surface. For the letter *Yod* <note>Written as a small dot</note> is nothing but a point. The letter *Vav* <note>Written as a vertical line</note> is a line. The letter *Dalet* <note>Written with a horizontal and vertical stroke</note> has length and width, which is a surface. Everything is included in the point of the *Yod* from the perspective that the *Yod* has three "flags" or concentrations. In the spreading of its "leg," it becomes a *Vav*. In the spreading of its "body," it becomes a *Dalet*. Its contraction hints at the Crown (*Keter*), where the hidden things are concealed. I have already proven that the Crown is "Nothingness" (*Ayin*); it is not attainable at all. All of Emanation is by way of conceptualization and a point. Only Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is the "Beginning" of a bit of revelation, hinted at by the point which is the *Yod*. The Crown is hinted at by the "tip" of the *Yod*, for there everything is so hidden that it is said to be "Nothing" (*Ayin*). "And Wisdom shall be found from Nothingness" <note>Job 28:12</note>, meaning the existence of "Is" (*Yesh*) from "Nothing" (*Ayin*), which is the Crown. Thus it is explained that the letter *Yod* hints at Wisdom.

## And Behold
The hidden part of the *Yod* in Wisdom—namely, the spelling out of the *Yod* [as *Yod-Vav-Dalet*] which equals 26—is where the concept of "existence" (*Yeshut*) begins to be acquired in the hidden secret of the "Two Faces," like the example of the hawk within the power of the father's brain. The *Vav*, which is the secret of the Line, is Beauty (*Tiferet*). For it is known that the three lines are the line of Kindness, the line of Judgment, and the line of Mercy. The line of Mercy is Beauty (*Tiferet*), and it is blended and includes all the lines. Therefore, Beauty includes the six "extremities" <note>The six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> and influences the Kingdom (*Malkhut*). Regarding this, the verse hints: "And a line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem" <note>Zechariah 1:16</note>. Jerusalem hints at the attribute of Kingdom (*Malkhut*), as is known, for the Holy Temple was there, in which the name *Y-H-W-D* of Beauty (called *Yod*) resides. Therefore, we should glow in the Holy Temple, for the Kingdom is the palace for the Lord (*Y-H-W-D*). Thus, the *Vav*, which is the line, is Beauty, and it is the "Great Line" that goes upward in the secret of Knowledge (*Da'at*) until the Crown, which is the height of excellences, in the secret of the "Inheritance of Jacob"—an inheritance without boundaries. As is known, Jacob is the "Chariot" for Beauty (*Tiferet*), unlike the line of Kindness, which only reaches up to Wisdom, and the line of Judgment, which only reaches up to Understanding.

### This is the *Dalet*
Which is the expansion in length and width; it is the Kingdom (*Malkhut*), for to that place all the influence of Emanation spreads. She is also the *Dalet* <note>The letter Dalet is the number 4</note> because she is the "fourth flag" in the Chariot. Also, *Dalet* in the "primordial numbering" is ten. For if you count up to four—namely, 1+2+3+4—it equals ten. This is because she is the tenth *Sefirah*. And also

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the internal structure of the Sefirot (divine emanations), moving from the general unity of the Crown (Keter) to the specific dynamics of Tiferet (the central "Beauty") and Malchut (the "Kingdom" or recipient). It emphasizes the boundary between what humans can contemplate and the hidden realms of the Divine Mind.</meta>

-># The Fifth House<-

...is full of elevations upon the system of Beauty (*Tiferet*), which fills and spreads its extremities from the hidden roots in the secret of "transplanting," until, due to its great and powerful fullness, it appears and reveals itself. Its edges overflow its banks until no part is found that does not include the six extremities, and no part is found that does not include all ten *Sefirot* <note>The ten fundamental divine attributes</note>. All of them are full of the abundance of "sated with favor" <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 33:23</note> to bestow upon the Kingdom (*Malchut*). Afterward, he elaborates on the matter of the elevations upon the system of the Kingdom, which receives this fullness in its own extremities, in the secret that she is the "Earth" and the place of "fruit" from the six extremities of Beauty, her husband, which are full of abundance to bestow, until she merits that abundance like a person who acquires a possession.

## And to understand
The matter well, one must know that even though there are Ten Utterances <note>The ten phrases by which the world was created in Genesis</note> in the secret of the emanation of the *Sefirot*, the root of the construction of this world stems from the side of the six *Partzufim* <note>term: Divine Personae; specific configurations of the Sefirot that interact like human personalities</note> which are Beauty and Kingdom. For "In six days the Lord made" refers to the six "Upper Days"—the six extremities which are the collective Beauty, encompassing six *Sefirot*. These are the "limbs" and the "body"—as it is written, "from my flesh I shall behold God" <note>Job 19:26; Kabbalists use the human body as a map of the divine structure</note>—just as the body includes its two arms, two legs, and the sign of the covenant <note>The reproductive organ, symbolizing the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation)</note>. He is the bestower to the *Sefirah* of Kingdom, the "Will of the Master" in the aspect of all His holiness; she is the "Palace" and "Dwelling" that receives the abundance. Afterward, it is poured downward to actually bring into existence the worlds of Creation (*Beriah*), Formation (*Yetzirah*), and Action (*Asiyah*).

For the first three—Crown (*Keter*), Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), and Understanding (*Binah*)—are hidden due to their extreme proximity to the Source regarding the governance of actions, such as leading the world with Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy and their branches. They are not graspable at all, in any way. They are the secret of His Thought and Wisdom (blessed be He), and through them, He protected the world and made it known. From the world, the six *Partzufim* were revealed in their emanation in their place. Metaphorically speaking, it is like one who thinks, calculates, understands, and decides how he will build a structure: the building remains hidden in his thought, and only afterward is it revealed. So it is regarding the holy and pure Emanation (*Atzilut*). Regarding this, it is said that in the first two, one cannot "linger" <note>Meaning, human intellect cannot remain or grasp these highest realms</note>; He comes to lead through them because they are beyond His "Building" and His world. Man has no permission to contemplate anything except his "World" and "Building," which is from the "Building" and below—meaning the Seven Days of Genesis. From there and above, the gate is closed. The Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> received that this is what was intended by the Sages in the tractate *Chagigah* in the chapter "One does not expound": "One might think a person may ask what was before the world was created? The Torah says: 'Since the day that God created man upon the earth.' One might think one should not ask about the six days of creation? The Torah says: 'Ask of the early days.' One might think one may ask what is above, what is below, what is before, and what is after? The Torah says: 'From one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens'—from one end of the heaven to the other you may ask, but you may not ask what is above, what is below, what is before, or what is after." Behold, they (of blessed memory) explained that man has no permission to ask or contemplate except from the "Building" and below, which is "from one end of heaven to the other," which is his world. But from there and above, you shall not know.

<margin>
<note>Note: This marginalia contains highly condensed technical notes, possibly from the "Pardes Rimmonim" by Moses Cordovero</note>
The matter of the "Deep, deep, who can find it" order... Blessing in the *Pardes* in its place... according to the clarity protected for man's knowledge... in his book like the ancient script... ten [levels of] Thought, Wisdom, and Knowledge... in the place of the writings of the one who builds a structure... this building was included in all his thought and strength and extension... just as in the structure in his thought, so he begins his possessions in the aspect of the Emanation of the world... the building thinks and speaks and is praised... the secret of the abundance of the building includes arms and legs and the sign of the flesh... just as the body has a head to think and understand, so, as it were, above the thought of Wisdom and Understanding... the thought to understand and calculate for the building to be in its place... the end of action was in the beginning of thought... "He spoke and it was" etc... in the script of the sanctuary of the building... only the ultimate purpose... in the details of the actions of the building from the thought of the building... all the attributes of Kindness and Judgment... this is included and the "rooting" of his will... the completion of the action of Beauty is called "Appointed Knowledge" which is in the Higher Thought... in portion *Pinhas* it says "and Knowledge was not," meaning it was hidden in Thought... "the world hidden from thought" refers to the world that exists always... the six days which are the six extremities... and afterward the seventh, and the highest encompassing head which is hidden is called "the world hidden from thought," namely Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding. And behold, it is written "and through Knowledge the rooms are filled," for the "rooms" are in Understanding, and the "rooms" are the six extremities... in Understanding, and they are the root of the six extremities of the building... they are the House, the Palace, and the Body... for Knowledge is the soul that lives... because Knowledge is the end of the connection of the extremities to Thought and above.
</margin>

## However,
The beginning of thought is the end of action. The root of the six extremities and the governance of the world's actions through the Kingdom (*Malchut*) is called in the Midrash of our Sages "the Architect" <note>original: "Ardiechal" - from the Greek 'architekton'</note> who brings to fruition the action of the Upper Days. This root is called above, in the first three [Sefirot], the "Secret of the Form," which is hidden from Beauty. When it arose in the absolute Primordial Will for all existence to be, it was then called the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) that "stands to make known"—to make known His absolute existence through His emanations. In the first three, which are considered as one, this "making known" was in the secret of: "He is the Knowledge, He is the Knower, and He is the Known." Afterward, the six *Partzufim* were revealed and known in their places, and they were called "Times," for they are the six Upper Days: Beauty and Kingdom, the "Attribute of Day" and the "Attribute of Night." From them, the concept of time and governance is drawn—sometimes with Judgment and sometimes with Mercy, all according to the matter. Regarding their hidden aspect, our Sages alluded in their Midrash: "'Let there be light' teaches that there was an order of times prior to this." This refers to the hidden aspect of "times" above, in the secret of Knowledge, Knower, and Known, where everything is a unified "One." Even so, the "hiddenness" is not equal: for the Crown (*Keter*) in its powers is completely hidden and is called "Nothingness" (*Ayin*), while Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is called "Being from Nothingness" (*Yesh me-Ayin*). Even though it is hidden, it is nonetheless called "Being" (*Yesh*) so that an aspect of "existence" may be discerned within it. This "existence" is revealed in a subtle reality through Understanding (*Binah*). This is why the Sages of Truth constructed terms to evaluate it: "Father" and "Mother" [for Wisdom and Understanding], and for Beauty and Kingdom, "Son" and "Daughter."

"From my flesh I shall behold God": the existence of the Son from the Father and Mother. Before the Son was revealed openly, he existed within the Father in great concealment—namely, in the seed that is drawn from the brain through the spinal cord. Afterward, he is revealed further in the "building" of the Mother during her pregnancy. Afterward, in his emergence from his mother's womb, he is in revelation alone. However, there is a concealment even greater than the aforementioned: the Will and the Thought to join together for a union. In this, it can be said that the power of the Son is embedded in great concealment. Afterward, it is drawn as the strength of the Father from the brain and bestows to the Mother. So too is the reality of the six *Partzufim* in the beginning of the "Secret of the Form"—the Thought within the secret of the Crown, which is called "Will," as explained in the *Pardes* in the "Gate of the Radiant Lights." This is the ultimate purpose of the worlds. Wisdom is the "Vision" of the revelation within the deep concealment. This first revelation is revealed through Understanding; then Understanding is "God" (*Yah*), Beauty is in its place, and its receptacle is Kingdom—"with me." For just as the emanation of the six extremities in Thought was through a bestower and a receiver (Wisdom and Understanding), so too is the unfolding of the six extremities above regarding action in the worlds of *Beriah, Yetzirah,* and *Asiyah*: Beauty bestows and Kingdom receives this abundance and brings it into action. Thus, "Son and Daughter" are in the likeness of "Father and Mother." Only "Father and Mother" concern the revelation of the emanation of the six extremities, whereas "Son and Daughter" concern the revelation of the Action.

## And after
this introduction, you will understand how "Beloved" (*Yedid*) includes the entire Emanation. Yet we still need one more introduction, and it is this: The Sages of Truth, particularly in the book *Pardes*, have already elaborated on the matter of the connection of the worlds—how the upper and lower are joined together. The upper bestows to the lower, and the lower is a "shadow" of the upper. Whatever exists in this one exists in that one, even though the lower is physical and the upper is spiritual. Everything is "one against the other." All of the Work of Creation speaks of the lower things but alludes to the upper things, for He (blessed be He) gives life to all the worlds, and all of them depend on His great Light. Although in this world the light is revealed in a more "thickened" way than the power of the [upper] world, this is due to the process of unfolding (*hishtalshelut*); nonetheless, everything is from His great Light. Take, for example, the light of the sun: from the power of its light, it is in the moon, and afterward the moon [reflects] with "returning light" to the world, and from there a light from the light of the world enters another room. Behold, the light has changed and become thicker due to the unfolding, yet it is all one light. So is the matter in the unfolding of the worlds of *Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah,* and *Asiyah*. The secret of the world of Emanation (*Atzilut*) is like "a flame bound to a coal"—it is not something outside of Him. For the flame is in the coal, and when the coal is blown upon, the flame is revealed, yet it is attached and bound to it. So is the Emanation...

<column-break/>

## And before
the explanation of the matter in its fullness, to sanctify the words of the *Pardes*, Gate 9, regarding the secret of the Kingdom, he says: "And after we have been awakened to the fact that with them are the extremities, for this reason it was necessary for the Kingdom by way of the Crown of its Wisdom... to choose the order of its emanation from Understanding and below, as it arose before Him to encompass the Crown at the time of its emanation, it was within it..."

<meta>This page transitions from the general structural description of the "House" (the Sefirotic system) to a specific, deep-dive analysis of the Divine Names. It focuses on the supremacy of the Tetragrammaton (the Four-Letter Name) over all other names, exploring its linguistic roots, its unique holiness, and its position within the "Tree" of divine emanations.</meta>

# The House of the Lord

It is called so because it interprets and reveals the existence and unity of the Unique Master, blessed be He. It is found, therefore, to be both the "interpreter" and the "interpreted" by virtue of its name; this is the uniqueness within its signs. This is the intent behind the calling of this Great Name the **Explicit Name** <note>Hebrew: *Shem HaMeforash*. The term refers to the Tetragrammaton (YHVH), the uniquely holy four-letter name of God</note>. They did not call it "the interpreter" simply to show that the world is one; rather, this name specifically indicates the **Beauty of Israel** <note>The Sefirah of *Tiferet*, which acts as the central harmonizing force of the divine attributes</note>, which is called "Torah." It is called so because it "teaches" <note>A wordplay on *Torah* and *Moreh* (teacher/indicator)</note> and reveals the power that was sealed. In the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>A reference to the *Zohar*, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>, may peace be upon him: "The Tree of Life is YHVH, and it is the supernal tree of blessing and strength; and the artisan is the Torah, because it teaches and reveals that which was hidden and unknown." Indeed, they called it the "Unique Name" because, in the construction of its letters, it unifies all of the Emanation <note>The *Atziluth*, the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, where the divine light is most pure</note> which is Divinity. For this reason, they said of it: "My name which is unique to Me."

**All** seekers of symbols in our holy Torah—whether they be masters of Kabbalah, masters of the plain meaning <note>*Pshat*, the literal or historical level of biblical interpretation</note>, or those who investigate the roots of our Torah—all agree with one voice that this Name is the Essential Name and no other. Its uniqueness among the other holy names (those which may not be erased) is such that they said even the name *Ehyeh* <note>Meaning "I Will Be," revealed to Moses at the burning bush</note>, despite being a very awesome name, does not equal this Name. In this Name are many secrets and the "vitality" of them all. This is because all other names that may not be erased eventually return to a partial action, except for the Four-Letter Name, whose letters do not necessitate any specific numerical action at all. 

For the name *Elohim*, *Eloah*, and *El* are derived from the language of "greatness," "strength," and "power," as in "and he took the *eilei* <note>mighty ones</note> of the land" (Ezekiel 17:13) or "Thy righteousness is like the *harrei-El* <note>mighty mountains</note>" (Psalm 36:7). The name *Shaddai* indicates that He "overpowers" <note>Hebrew: *shoded*</note> the celestial systems and delivers, and the word *dai* <note>enough</note> is within its letters. The name *Tzevaot* <note>Lord of Hosts</note> indicates being the Master of the hosts above and below, derived from the word for "army" (*tzava*). The name *Adonai* indicates "Lordship," as He is the Lord of all the earth. 

Which name indicates a present reality in the future tense, connecting "my existence" through the simple grammatical construction? As our Sages said: "I was with them in the redemption from Egypt, and I will be (*Ehyeh*) with them in the redemption from others..." (Talmud, Berakhot 9b). However, the Four-Letter Name is very awesome; who can contain it? It is explained that it has no explanation in any language. <margin>Secondly, all these other names can be used in a secular or common sense if we wish.</margin> This is not the case with the letters of the Four-Letter Name. The scriptures use the other names in a common sense for others, such as "mighty mountains" (*harrei-El*). Likewise, *Elohim* can refer to human judges, as in "provide for us *elohim* <note>leaders/gods</note> to go before us" or "you shall not curse the *elohim* <note>judges</note>" (Exodus 22:27). *Shaddai* can appear in a common context, as can *Tzevaot* (referring to the "hosts" of Israel leaving Egypt). Regarding *Adonai*, when Abraham speaks to the angels, some sages say he addressed the "greatest among them" <note>using the word as a secular title of respect</note>. Even though there are those who disagree and say it was holy, we see that for all of them, if one wishes to call a human lord "*adonai*" or the earth "*shaddai*," it can be used in a secular tongue. This is not so with these four holy letters, **YHVH**. Even though three of them can be found elsewhere, all four are never found together in a secular context. 

This brings us close to the "First Cause" <note>The ultimate source of all existence</note>. All names are pronounced as they are written, except for this holy Name, for it was never pronounced by its letters except by the sanctity of the Priestly Blessing and by the High Priest on Yom Kippur. The reason is that the other names "guide" the world through the clarity of their definitions, but the Four-Letter Name has no definition; its action is stripped bare across the world, unless it "clothes" itself in the other names. The other names may be expressed because their letters represent a spirituality like the human soul that clothes itself in reflected light to perform an action in the world. But the Four-Letter Name, due to its immense holiness, does not clothe itself in the light of the world, except in the Holy Temple. As it is written: "In every place where I mention My name, I will come to you and bless you" (Exodus 20:21). In that pure, clear place, it can be "clothed"; it clothes itself in the light of the Temple, which is the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence</note>, the name *Adonai*. This is the meaning of "The Lord (YHVH) is in His holy Temple."

The author of *Sefer HaOrah* <note>The Book of Light</note> wrote in his introduction: "Know that all His holy names mentioned in the Torah are all dependent on the Four-Letter Name... Know that the Four-Letter Name is like the body of the Tree, and the name *Ehyeh* is the root of the Tree, and from it its roots spread out, branching to every side. All other holy names are like branches and twigs extending from the body of the Tree, and each branch produces fruit after its kind." 

The explanation of his words is that all names that may not be erased are dependent on the Four-Letter Name; from it they spread and from it they are acquired. One might ask: why are they not dependent on the name *Ehyeh*, which corresponds to the **Crown** (*Keter*)—the ultimate root? A beautiful answer is given: *Ehyeh* is indeed the root, but the branches spread from the *trunk* (the body), not directly from the root itself. *Keter* is the hidden root from which the world does not directly branch; **Beauty** (*Tiferet*) is the "body" from which the branches extend. This is why *Tiferet* is related to the word for "branches" (*pe'erot*). 

# To indicate the most unique of names...
...among all names, you will find through the secret of **Gematria** <note>The Jewish system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters to find deeper meanings</note> that all ten names are hinted at within it. The name of the Crown (*Keter*) is hinted at... <note>The text begins a complex series of mathematical proofs showing how the Tetragrammaton (value 26) contains the "DNA" of the other divine names, such as Elohim (86) and Ehyeh (21)</note> ...the name of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is *Yah* (the first half of the Name)... the name of Understanding (*Binah*) is the Tetragrammaton vocalized as *Elohim*... the name of Kindness (*Chesed*) is *El*, which equals the Tetragrammaton when counting its letters and the "collective" value... 

->The Four-Letter Name is entirely "Holam" <note>A Hebrew vowel mark representing the "O" sound, here used mystically</note>, hidden within Beauty (*Tiferet*).<-

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the "House" of the Divine Name, moving from the general concept of the Tetragrammaton as a "teacher" to the specific anatomical and geometric symbolism of its letters. It transitions into a detailed explanation of how the divine light descends from the "Crown" through the "Understanding" into the lower "Building" of the world.</meta>

# The Fifth House
<note>Hebrew: *Beit Heh*. This likely refers to a chapter or section of the manuscript focused on the letter *Heh* or the fifth stage of emanation.</note>

The levels in the world are like the parable of a fruit: it has a source in the branch, the source in the branch has a source in the body of the tree, and the source in the body of the tree has its source in the root of the tree. I have already explained the existence of the "hidden fruits" which are the emanations <note>The *Sefirot*, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note>, rising level by level. As it is said, "Beauty" <note>*Tiferet*</note> is our "branch" and the root of the branch. This is the secret of the "World of Transition" which exists to make known His divinity to the "seeds and offspring" <note>Humanity/Created beings</note> who understand this world. This is a simple "Beauty," the end of the world and its purpose. It has no name other than "Beauty" which changes according to the "limbs and branches," meaning His actions through His branches. This is the secret of the "Will of Knowledge" and its likeness, which we call "Knowledge" <note>*Da'at*</note>. As it is written: "Hidden things belong to the Lord our God" <note>Deuteronomy 29:28</note>, referring to the "Crown" <note>*Keter*, the highest Sefirah</note> which is called the "Hidden Crown." Within it, the "Will" is equalized and hidden in a supernal concealment. It is not considered part of the "World of Manifestation" <note>*Atziluth*</note> because it is the beginning of the transition into "Wisdom" <note>*Chochmah*</note>. This is the secret of the "Supernal Name" [YHVH]. As explained in the *Pardes* <note>Referring to *Pardes Rimonim* by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, a central Kabbalistic text</note> regarding the three explanations: the "Hidden Writing," the "Visible Writing," and their "Place." The Supernal Name is our "Supernal Wisdom," which yearns for the lower aspect to manifest the hidden powers. Behold, the equalization of the light becomes a "vessel" so that the supernal aspect of Wisdom can be hidden within the "Crown" <note>Keter</note>. Afterward, the "branch" is revealed, showing a bit of the "hidden sweetness," until it reaches the place of "Beauty" <note>Tiferet</note>. For there is still a need to reveal the secret of the "Building" <note>The lower six Sefirot</note>. From the perspective of the "Above," it is the exact opposite; for afterward, in its place, the "Building" is revealed in its location, manifesting more than the "Three First Ones" <note>Keter, Chochmah, and Binah</note>. The Three First Ones are more revealed through the "Three Arms" <note>The Sefirot of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet</note>. This is why we rely on the "Three Colors" of the flesh: white, red, and green. From the perspective of the "Yod" [of the Name], there is a bit of revelation of Wisdom and Understanding <note>Chochmah and Binah</note> which are the "Beginning of the Revelation" of the "Unique Master." The "Three Branches" are hidden there in the secret of "Knowledge" <note>Da'at</note>. The root of Knowledge is the aspect that was equalized in the "Crown of the Crown."

<column-break/>

# The Letter Dalet (ד)
The term "Dalet" is used because it is the "Door" <note>Hebrew: *Delet*</note> to the Lord, through which the righteous shall enter. 
And behold, in the hand <note>Hebrew: *Yad*, spelled *Yod-Dalet*</note> is hinted a line, a surface, and a point. In the physical world, there is nothing that does not have a line, a surface, and height or depth. Here, "Depth" is hinted at in the "tip of the Yod," which is the highest point. Similarly, "Depth, depth, who can find it?" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>. This "Depth" indicates the chain of "Deep things" found in the Sefirot: the depth of the beginning, the depth of the end, the depth of good, the depth of evil, the depth of height, the depth of depth, the depth of east, the depth of west, the depth of north, and the depth of south. The "Unique Master, God, the Faithful King," rules over them all from His holy dwelling forever and ever. This is the end of his words. The meaning of saying "Depth" for each and every one individually is that even though the beginning, end, east, and other boundaries indicate a limit, they are nonetheless "Depth of depth, who can find it?" Providence over them is impossible for us because they are without limit. A lengthy explanation of this teaching can be found in the *Pardes*, in the gate "Is the Infinite (*Ein Sof*) the Crown (*Keter*)?" chapter 4; see there.

# And Behold 
This extension spreads into "Understanding" <note>*Binah*</note> like a father bestowing upon a son. There, it is revealed more fully, as if passing through, and the power is transformed from the letter *Dalet* (ד) to *Reish* (ר). In the secret of the union of these forms, they were joined as one. Just as the first Adam was below, initially in his "going out" and "breathing in," the *Vav* (ו) entered the *Dalet* (ד) and it became a *Heh* (ה). This is the secret of the first *Heh* of the Name [YHVH], which hints at "Understanding" (*Binah*). The letter *Yod* has three lines, which represent the expansion of Emanation into the "Seven Extremities" <note>The seven lower Sefirot</note>. In Understanding, they acquired their root in a somewhat revealed way, like a child in its mother's womb. The masters of the secret <note>The Kabbalists</note> said that the shape of this *Heh* is open at the bottom to flow into the world of Emanation, and open at the top (like an opening in a wall) to receive from the "Crown." It is wide at the bottom to provide flow for the entire expansion, for Understanding is called the "Supernal Mother" <note>*Ima Ila'ah*</note>, and from there the entire "Building" of Emanation was emanated.

# And Afterward 
Understanding emanated these seven or six "Personifications" <note>*Partzufim*, divine personas</note> to their places. That is to say, the *Vav* (ו) that was inside the *Heh* (ה) was emanated as "Beauty" (*Tiferet*) in its place, which includes the six extremities. It is the "Inclusive Line" that contains all lines. Therefore, the secret of the letter *Vav* in the Name hints at Beauty. Afterward, "Kingdom" <note>*Malchut*</note> was emanated in its place, which is the *Dalet* (ד) that remained from Understanding. The *Vav* also entered into the *Dalet*, because Kingdom is a "reception vessel" for the six extremities. The "Six are clothed in the Six," meaning Beauty with its six extremities is clothed in Kingdom, which is a "Palace" having six rooms to receive the six extremities. This *Vav* entering the *Dalet* becomes a *Heh*. Thus, Kingdom is the final *Heh* of the Name [YHVH]. The masters of the secret said this *Heh* is open at the bottom and wide to flow into the lower worlds <note>Beri'ah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah</note>, but narrow at the top to receive the Supernal Holiness. It is also wide at the bottom to receive all prayers and services and to elevate them through the "Thin Pillar" to the supernal heights.

# Also 
In the secret of the hidden union of Beauty and Kingdom, the "double Heh" (ה"ה) appears, indicating the female. In the *Zohar*, on the verse "My Name is not Y[H]" <note>original: *lit shemi l'yod-heh*</note>, it is said (Heaven forbid) that until the female aspect receives the male, it is called "Night" (*Layil*), but once it receives the male, it is called "Nighttime" (*Laylah*). See the wonders in the *Pardes*, section 2, regarding the order of Emanation.

# Also 
The final *Heh* elevates the first *Heh*. This is the secret of the "Three Lines." However, the first *Heh* is the secret of the emanation of the three lines, while the final *Heh* is the secret of bringing them into action.

# Thus 
The Name [YHVH] includes all of Emanation. All of Emanation is the "Beauty of the Building of the World" through "Kingdom," which is within its body (based on the secret "his wife is like his own body"). For Beauty consists of six extremities... these are the extremities that provide life to them, and the five boundaries... in the secret of the twelve permutations of the Name [YHVH]. Above, in the world, it is the secret of "Knowledge" (*Da'at*). Everything is "Beauty," but Knowledge is the hidden aspect of Beauty. However, since everything is Beauty, it is called by the Name [YHVH]. For every instance of the Name [YHVH] in the Torah [has various vocalizations]... This is Beauty because the Name includes Emanation, and the totality of Emanation is Beauty. Everything is the Name [YHVH] because it is the "Essential Name" <note>*Shem HaEtzem*</note>. Therefore, it is called the **Unique Name** <note>*Shem HaMeyuchad*</note>, for it unifies all of Emanation. It is also called the **Explicit Name** <note>*Shem HaMeforash*</note>. As the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>The *Service of the Holy*, by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> says in chapter 15: "The holy Name written with *Yod, Heh, Vav, Heh* is what is called the Explicit Name and the Unique Name." This is found in the words of the Sages in the *Sifrei* and in *Sotah*: "'Thus you shall bless [the people of Israel]'—with the Explicit Name. You say with the Explicit Name, or is it only with its substitute name? The verse says: 'And they shall put My name'—the Name unique to Me." The Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel</note>, of blessed memory, wrote in the *Book of Unity*: "These four letters are called the Explicit Name because they 'explain' <note>*mefaresh*</note> all the Sefirot, indicating the existence that the Creator, blessed be He, brought into being through the manifestation of His powers, encompassing all that was, is, and will be."

And the sage Rabbi Todros HaLevi <note>Todros ben Joseph Abulafia, 13th-century Kabbalist</note>, in his commentary on the legends in the tractate *Pesachim*, said: "Know that all the foundations of the true Kabbalah and all its cornerstones are founded upon this great and holy Name. Within it, the Perfect Unity is explained. Therefore, it is called the Explicit Name—meaning it is self-explanatory. Through its intent, the 'branches' are unified and joined in the essence of His holy and pure Unity." (It has already been explained that the emanated being exists in perfect unity with the Essence, and the Four-Letter Name is attributed to the Unique Master, for He and His Name are One and shall not be separated. It was also explained that the necessity of mentioning Emanation is to testify to the existence and unity of the Root of all Roots. Behold, this Explicit Name includes and unifies all of Emanation...

<column-break/>

...within it is hidden the hidden Wisdom, and it is in the "Crown of the Crown." For Knowledge is within the "Wisdom" that was equalized in the Crown. It is found, therefore, that this Knowledge is the aspect of the Crown. Afterward, the three lines are revealed in their place. This is modeled after "Wisdom in the Crown," hidden within hiddenness. So too, in the aspect of the "Seven," in their place in "Supernal Understanding," it is equalized in the "Lower Writing" of the Crown, and so too in Understanding. Afterward, Knowledge is clarified through Wisdom in a partial revelation, namely the *Vav* of the Name [YHVH]. For from the revelation of the *Vav*, [the letters] *Yod* and *Heh* [emerge]. As is known, *Yod* is the secret of the ten Personifications. The hidden filling of the letters is in Knowledge... for everything comes to a partial revelation in Understanding. This is the "Yod of Understanding"... the line and the leg expanded into three lines, which is the whole of the *Heh*. That is to say, the secret of the three lines is their inclusion in their place, like a drop that is contemplated from its source. All this is the degree of Knowledge. This is why they say "Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge" (*Chochmah, Binah, Da'at*) and not "Knowledge, Wisdom, and Understanding." These first three are called by the name "Knowledge," for they are called "The Knower, the Knowledge, and the Known," unified together, as explained in the *Pardes*, in the gate of "The Essence and the Vessels," chapter 3: "Knowledge is the Crown, Wisdom is the Root, Understanding is the Root." Observe this matter in the *Zohar*. Therefore, the three first ones are as one, and they are the "End of Knowledge."

# And 
Behold, the entire Emanation is "Beauty" (*Tiferet*), and the totality of the Kabbalah is in the secret of "Knowledge," which is the "Five Knowledges" in the secret of the one who contemplates them from the aspect of Understanding.
