<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Divine Name, moving from the abstract structures of the previous page to the specific connection between the Tetragrammaton, the Torah, and the human form. It bridges the gap between the "World of Emanation" and the creation of humanity.</meta>

<page-num>8</page-num>
<header>House of Israel</header>

The letters that serve the four letters of the Name—namely Y-H-V <note>The first three letters of the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H, the four-letter name of God</note>—are the letters *L* and *B* <note>Hebrew: *Lamed* and *Bet*, which spell *Lev*, meaning "heart"</note>, as when you say "to me," "to him," "to it," or "in her" and so on. Thus, the Torah is bound to the Name Y-V-D-D <note>original: "יוד"ד"; this represents a specific "filling" or expanded spelling of the Divine Name used in Kabbalistic meditation</note>. And as I wrote above, just as the letter *Yod* is hinted at in the expansion Y-V-D-D, and the hand <note>Hebrew: *Yad*, which sounds like the letter *Yod*</note> consists of fourteen joints <note>Hebrew: *Yod* (10) + *Dalet* (4) = 14</note>, so too the 613 commandments are hinted at in the Two Tablets. As the author wrote, the letter *Vav* is like an *Aleph* and so on, for they were spoken in a single utterance. Therefore, the Torah begins with the Ten Commandments starting with the letter *Aleph* <note>For the word *Anokhi*, "I am"</note>. Just as a point, a line, and a surface represent length and breadth, so too "the Torah is longer than the earth and wider than the sea" <note>Job 11:9</note>. It is also written, "Your commandment is exceedingly broad" <note>Psalm 119:96</note>. The matter is this: we can walk in the "length" through our measurements and in the "breadth" by fulfilling the commandments; however, in its secrets, the Torah is like a point. We cannot descend to its ultimate depth, as it is written: "Deep, deep, who can find it?" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>. This follows the path I wrote above regarding the secret of the letter *Yod*, which includes the expanded *Y-V-D*, and then from *Y-V-D* the letter *Aleph* is formed: a *Yod* above, a *Yod* in the middle, and a small *Dalet* below.

# House of Israel: The Human

Behold, the human soul comes from the expansion of the Name Y-V-D-D, and even the limbs of the body are marked and designated by this Name Y-V-D-D. Through this, we can clarify the matter of the "Image and Likeness" <note>Genesis 1:26</note> in which the human was created and made. This matter requires an extensive explanation. When understood, the heart of a person will be set aflame to live by "turning from evil and doing good" <note>Psalm 34:14</note> and to sanctify themselves. For it was for this purpose that the human was created, and the entire creation was for the sake of humanity. As we say in the prayers of Rosh Hashanah: "This day is the beginning of Your works" <note>A liturgical poem marking the New Year</note>. We say in Tractate Rosh Hashanah that we pray on the first of the month because Rabbi Eliezer holds that the world was created in the month of Tishrei. This presents a difficulty: does he not hold that the world was created on the 25th of Elul? Rather, when he said "the beginning of Your works," he meant the creation of Adam, who is the ultimate purpose of creation and was created on Rosh Hashanah. Similarly, the verse says, "How awesome is Your work" <note>Psalm 66:3</note>. The question is asked: why does it not say "works" in the plural? It is because all the works of creation are for a single purpose, which is the Human. The Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> have already expanded on this, striking the heads of the philosophers who walk in darkness and have no light; we shall elaborate on this matter further on.

# The Subject

Just as the simple Will and Desire emerged from the Infinite—the Root of all Roots, the *Ein Sof*—to emanate from His hidden light the Holy Emanation <note>The world of *Atziluth*, the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalistic cosmology</note> which testifies to His absolute, hidden existence, so too was it His Will to create one perfected and inclusive creature. This creature was made in the image and likeness of the pattern of the Supernal Holy Sanctuary, which is this Emanation called the "Supernal Adam," as we will explain later. Regarding this creation, it is said: "Let us make man in our image." 

And these are the words of the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>A 16th-century work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>: "In the Midrash, they asked: With whom did He consult? Rabbi Joshua said in the name of Rabbi Levi: He consulted with the works of Heaven and Earth. This is like a commoner who had two advisors <note>original: "סנקלטין" (*synkletos* in Greek)</note> and would do nothing without their knowledge. Rabbi Samuel bar Nahman said: He consulted with the work of each and every day. This is like a king who had a counselor <note>original: "סנקלריון"</note> and did nothing without his knowledge. Rabbi Ami said: He consulted with His own heart. This is like a king who built a palace through an architect; he saw it and it did not please him. Against whom should he complain? Not against the architect? Thus, 'He was grieved in His heart' <note>Genesis 6:6</note>."

And in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*, it says: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the Torah: 'Let us make man...'" All of these converge on a single intention. The Sages of Truth hinted to us that He did not consult with anything outside of Himself. For those who say He consulted "with the works of Heaven and Earth," they refer to the two foundations <note>The spiritual archetypes of heaven and earth</note>. Those who say "with the work of each and every day" refer to the six supernal days of creation <note>The six *Sefirot* from *Chesed* to *Yesod*</note>. 

And it was said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>: "The world was created in two colors, right and left, through six supernal days. These six days were made to radiate, as it is said: 'For in six days the Lord made the heavens...'" And the one who says "in His heart," the intention is the "Heart of Heaven," which is the Bride <note>The *Sefirah* of *Malchut* (Kingship)</note>, comprised of the thirty-two wondrous paths of Wisdom, which is the Torah. 

The secret of the matter is that the Human is comprised of all of them, made in the pattern of the whole, as will be explained with God's help. The hidden reason is so that he, too, may testify to the Unity of the Unique Name and to the expansion of His emanation in which he is included. Thus, the Human, made in image and likeness, is a sign that testifies to and publicizes Divinity. To reveal this and make it known, he was "created in the image of God." 

It says in Chapter 11 of the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer*: "He stood on his feet and was formed in the likeness of God. The creatures saw him and were afraid, thinking he was their Creator." For this secret reason, the human form is called a *Diyokan* <note>original: "דיוקן", from the Greek *eikon*, meaning image or portrait</note>, and all forms are named after the human form. As they said in the first chapter of Tractate Bava Kama: "We do not send money with a *Diyokan* <note>an image/seal</note>," because the human form is secondary only to its Maker, and no other form is like it. As it is written: "For in the image of God He made man." The secret is that the word *Partzufin* <note>Faces/Personas</note> is numerically equivalent to "acquired" <note>Hebrew: *Koneh*</note>, for he is in the likeness of his Maker <note>Hebrew: *Kono*</note>. He possesses this because he is comprised of the supernal powers which are included in the secret of the Great Name. 

In the chapter *Chazkat HaBattim*, they said: "You have looked upon my *Diyokan*; do not look upon the *Diyokan* itself." And in the chapter *V'elu Megalchin*: "I gave them a likeness of a *Diyokan*." Even the word "Image" (*Tzelem*) is translated [in Aramaic] as *Diyokna*. Thus, being comprised of these virtues and made in the pattern of the Sanctuary, he has the power and capacity to unify and repair the "Glory," for that was the intention... Thus far the words of the *Avodat HaKodesh*. I will add a touch of my own to explain the aforementioned Midrash Rabbah, and the matter of souls coming from the Name Y-V-D-D will be clarified.

# And Before

I speak, I must raise a strong difficulty: why is it that the Sages and the Sages of Truth always mention three levels of the soul—*Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah*? As it says in the Zohar: "Fortunate are the righteous who bind *Nefesh* to *Ruach*, *Ruach* to *Neshamah*, and *Neshamah* to the Holy One, blessed be He." Yet are there not five levels: *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, *Neshamah*, *Chayah*, and *Yechidah*? <note>Nefesh (Vitality), Ruach (Spirit), Neshamah (Breath/Soul), Chayah (Living Essence), and Yechidah (Singularity/Unity)</note>. One cannot say that *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* are always bound together and one cannot exist without the others, while *Chayah* and *Yechidah* are merely "extra" additions to the soul. For the Sages say in the Zohar on Leviticus: "There is one who merits a *Neshamah*, one who merits the awakening of *Ruach*, and one who merits only a *Nefesh*." See also the *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of the Soul," where it says some do not even merit a *Nefesh*, possessing only the "natural biological soul" which serves as a chariot for the "Divine *Nefesh*." If one merits, he receives the Divine *Nefesh*; if he merits further, they bestow upon him *Ruach*; and if further still, they bestow *Neshamah*.

<margin>If so, the question returns to its place <note>i.e., the original difficulty remains</note>.</margin>

# And Now

Listen, my children, that your souls may live: the soul is [drawn] from the radiance and glory of His honor, an emanation from the supernal lights. Just as I explained regarding the secret of the Name Y-V-D-D, there are four arrangements corresponding to the four letters: Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), Understanding (*Binah*), Beauty (*Tiferet*), and Kingship (*Malchut*). Their source is the hidden Fifth, hinted at in the "thorn" <note>the top point</note> of the letter *Yod*. So it is found in the existence of the soul. 

The Ramban <note>Nahmanides, 13th-century scholar</note> wrote in his commentary on Genesis regarding the verse "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life": "The Torah hints to us in this the virtue of the soul, its foundation and its secret. For it mentions the Full Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note> and says that *He* breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, to let us know that it did not come to him from the elements... nor did it come through a chain of evolution from the separate intellects. Rather, it is the spirit of the Great Name... for he who breathes into the nostrils of another gives of his own soul. This is what is meant by 'the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding' <note>Job 32:8</note>, for it is rooted in the foundation of Understanding (*Binah*) through the way of Truth and Faith." 

This is also their statement in the Sifri regarding oaths: "One who swears 'by the life of the King' [is distinct from] one who swears 'by the King himself.' Although there is no absolute proof for this, there is a hint: 'As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives' <note>1 Samuel 20:3</note>." And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKana <note>The *Bahir*</note>, it is asked: "What is the meaning of the verse 'and He rested' (*Vayinafash*)? It teaches that the Sabbath day sustains all souls (*Nefashot*)." From this, you can understand the matter of the "Oaths of God," and the wise will understand.

These are the words of the Ramban, which are hidden; nevertheless, they are clarified through the words of the Zohar brought by the divine author of the *Pardes* in the "Gate of Essence and Transformation," Chapter 22. From the very union of Beauty (*Tiferet*) and Kingship (*Malchut*)—which we call the "Secret of the Union" (*Zivug*)—souls are brought into being. 

In the Zohar, section *Vayikra*: "The 'Daughter of a Priest' is the holy soul, called the 'Daughter of the King,' for they have established that the holy soul emerges from the union of the King and the Matronita <note>The feminine aspect of the Divine</note>. Just as the body below is formed from male and female, so too is the soul above." 

He has thus shown that the Union is for the purpose of receiving souls. This is also clarified in the Zohar, section *Lech Lecha*: "The fruit is sweet to my palate—this refers to the Tree of the Souls of the righteous, which are all the 'fruit' of the Holy One, blessed be He... Come and see: all the souls in the world, which are the fruit of the actions of the Holy One, blessed be He, are all a single spirit, yet they divide into sixty parts... male and female. These male and female aspects are joined as one. Come and see: the desire of the female toward the male creates a 'Nefesh,' and the desire of the male toward the female creates a 'Nefesh.' For the desire of the male toward the female and his cleavage to her brings forth a soul... and the lower desire is included in the supernal desire, and they become a single will without separation. Then the female receives everything and becomes pregnant by the male, and the desires of both are woven together as one... and when the souls go forth, they go forth as male and female joined as one. When they descend to the world, they separate, this one to this side and that one to that side, and the Holy One, blessed be He, joins them together later... for only the Holy One, blessed be He, knows their proper pairing to join them as they were originally. If a person merits through his actions and walks in the path of truth, his 'Nefesh' is joined to its [original] 'Nefesh' as they were at the beginning... and this is a complete person as is fitting." This is why it is written, "his fruit is sweet to my palate"—this is the blessed arrangement to settle the worlds, for everything depends on the actions of the human being.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Divine Name from the previous page, specifically focusing on how the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter Name of God) serves as the architectural blueprint for the Torah, the Sefirot (Divine Emanations), and the very structure of the Hebrew alphabet.</meta>

<header>House of Wisdom</header>

The Name **Y-H-V-D** <note>original: "יהו"ד"; a pious substitution for the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H, to avoid writing the Name in full</note> of Hosts, God of Hosts. It has already been explained that **Y-H-V-D** is the name of the "Foundation" that existed before, and we have already mentioned that the Essential Name is **Y-H-V-D**, as it is written: "This is my Name forever" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. It is the essence of all names, and all other names are derived from it. It is also written: "I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty (*El Shaddai*), but by my Name **Y-H-V-H** I was not known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. However, when one joins the name **Y-H-V-D** with *Shaddai*, it reaches the numerical value <note>The Hebrew practice of *Gematria*, where letters have number values</note> of the phrase: "In His holy Temple; let all the earth keep silence before Him" <note>Habakkuk 2:20</note>. The Name *Adonai* (Lord) has the same numerical value (65) as the word *Heikhal* (Temple/Palace), for it is the "Palace" for the Essential Name **Y-H-V-H**. This is the hint found in the word "Silence" (*Has*), for the Name is not to be mentioned; as it is written: "This is my Name and this is my memorial"—it is not pronounced as it is written. How then is **Y-H-V-D** mentioned? It is said through the Name *Adonai*, which equals "Silence" (*Has*). Why is it mentioned specifically by this Name? Because it is the "Palace" of the Name **Y-H-V-D**, as it is written: "The Lord is in His holy Temple." Furthermore, there is another hint: **Y-H-V-D** is the essence, and its "replacement" is "Holy." In its cipher form, it is the name *K-V-Z-V* <note>original: "כוז"ו"; a cipher where each letter of the Name is replaced by the next letter in the alphabet: Y becomes K, H becomes V, V becomes Z, H becomes V</note>, which are the letters that follow the Name. This is hinted at in the verse: "Is it not **Y-H-V-D**..." The secret of *K-V-Z-V* is elevated above it. When you calculate the Name and its replacement—that is, **Y-H-V-D** and *K-V-Z-V*—the sum equals the value of *Adonai*. There is yet another hint: "My Name is within him," for the "filling" <note>The spelling out of each letter as a word</note> of the Name **Y-V-D** using the letter *Yod* results in the value of 72. This is found "within" the Name *Adonai*, referring to the middle letters of the spelled-out name *Adonai*, which equals 72. Thus, the Name **Y-H-V-D** is the "Unique One" that unifies all names; they all emerge from it and are hinted at in its blessing, existing in a single unity. It includes all of the *Atzilut* <note>The World of Emanation, the highest spiritual realm</note> through the secret of the letter *Yod*, which represents a point, a line, and a surface—all are one true unity. For the secret of the letters *Y-V* is the secret of the letter *Aleph*, which teaches us about unity. 

Indeed, the Sages of Truth said that the letter *Aleph* (א) points to the Unique Name **Y-H-V-D**. This is because an *Aleph* is composed of a *Yod* above, a *Yod* below, and a *Vav* in the middle, totaling 26 <note>The numerical value of the Tetragrammaton</note>. However, the tradition I have is that the bottom *Yod* is slightly larger than the top *Yod*, representing the "Small Vav" found above the middle *Vav*.

<margin>Folio 66</margin>
The letter *Dalet* below represents the "latter things," hinting at the Name **Y-H-V-D**. All its letters are true; they all emerge from Him and are hinted at in His blessing, existing in a single unity. Truly, these are the words of the Living God. Below, it is also seen as a small *Dalet* to hint at the "Brother" (*Ach*) <note>Possibly a reference to the unity of God expressed in the *Shema*</note>. Furthermore, he gave a great hint regarding the secret of the letter *Aleph*, which indicates the unity of the Unique Name: when you say it equals 26, the *Yod* above is like the full spelling of *Yod*, and the *Yod* below points to the "Foundation" (*Yesod*). When you say that the *Aleph* contains the letters *Y-V*, it also hints at the Name **Y-H-V-D** through their names. This is clarified in the secret of *Tiferet* (Beauty/Harmony), adding to what we explained above regarding the secret of the letter *Yod*. There is another hint regarding the roots of the shapes of the letters... at times they interpret the shape of the letter *Heh* as being a *Vav* and a *Dalet*, or a *Yod* and a *Dalet*, or two *Dalets*. <gloss>The face crowns the crown and does not diminish.</gloss> Sometimes they interpret the shape of the *Heh* as a *Dalet*... and the *Heh* is the shape of a *Dalet*... Now we shall hint at a deeper truth than what we wrote above: The first *Heh* of the Name hints at *Binah* (Understanding). Even though in our truth it is the secret of two *Yods*, it is actually a *Y-V-H*. This is a small *Yod* that is somewhat elevated into a *Y-D-V*. The final *Heh* hints at *Malkhut* (Kingship), or it is a *Dalet*. The matter is that the Emanation from *Chesed* (Kindness) downward is included in three lines: the Line of Kindness, the Line of Judgment, and the Line of Compassion. These three lines are hidden in their roots above—namely in *Keter* (Crown), *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), and *Binah* (Understanding). *Keter* is the root of the Line of Compassion, *Chokhmah* is the root of the Line of Kindness, and *Binah* is the root of the Line of Judgment. Because they are hidden, they are called "Three" in the secret of *A-B-G*. In their expansion, they become the letter *Vav*, which is a "Line," as explained at length in the book *Pardes Rimonim*. I also say: the first *Heh* in *Binah*, even though they intend it as the secret of *Y-D*, nevertheless the small *Yod* is somewhat elevated into the shape of a *Vav*. The final *Heh* in *Malkhut* is the secret of receiving the lines, and it is a point. After God has shown us this, He enlightened our eyes regarding the word *Y-V-D*. How so? The *Y-V* as it is, is the letter 22, leaving the *Dalet*. You can see this in the secret of the *Heh* becoming the letter *Dalet*... thus the Name will enlighten our eyes... calculate the letter *Yod* (which is *Yod-Vav-Dalet*)... it becomes three... count from 1 to 10 and it equals 55, then count the letters from 1 to 4 and it equals 10, plus 5 and 1, reaching 86—the numerical value of the Name *Elohim* (God).

### And It Is Found
This unity exists in the names *Adonai*, **Y-H-V-D**, and *Adonai*. They are the Head of Emanation, the Middle of Emanation, and the End of Emanation. How so? Take the first half of these names (A-H-H, Y-A, A-D) and it equals 27, the value of the spelled-out *Yod*. Take the latter half (Y-H, V-H, N-Y) and it equals 86, the value of *Elohim*. Everything is included in the Name **Y-H-V-D**. The value 79 is the name *Yabok* <note>The river where Jacob wrestled the angel; its name is a Kabbalistic cipher for prayer</note> which emerges from the initials of the verse: "May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble" <note>Psalm 20:2</note>. This is the same value as **Y-H-V-D** and *Elohim*, which equals the value of "Redeemer" (*Goel*). After the "Foundation" (*Yesod*), **Y-H-V-D** is the Essential Name. Furthermore, the letters of *Elohim* contain the letters *Y-H*... when you fill the letter *Heh* with the power of *Yod-Heh*, it equals 25... Furthermore, regarding the "fullness" of all the expansions of the Name **Y-H-V-D**, the sign for which is "This is my Name and this is my memorial"—namely the filling of the *Yod*, the *Heh*, and the *Vav*. He mentioned *Y-H* to hint at the filling with the letter *Yod*. Afterward, he said "Full" to point to our essence... the Name **Y-H-V-D** filled with the letter *Aleph* equals 45, the value of the word "Full" (*Maleh*).

### Let Us Return
To the explanation of the discourse: It is now explained that the secret of **Y-H-V-D** concerns the "Hidden Will" and the "Revealed Will." That is, **Y-H-V-D** includes the entire chain of Emanation. It is written but not pronounced as **Y-H-V-D**, for it includes the general inwardness of the Emanation... which is the secret of the freedom of the Essence. It is all *Kamatz* (a vowel), all *Patach* (a vowel), etc. **Y-H-V-D** in the secret of the Name is such that His Name is neither written nor pronounced even in thought. And he said that it "hangs" because even the Torah is sanctified by the Name **Y-H-V-D**.

## House of Wisdom - The Torah
"The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. This means the Torah is complete in its perfection, woven upon the Name **Y-H-V-D**. For the entire Torah consists of His Names, and it was given through the Name **Y-H-V-D**, which is the secret of *Tiferet* (Beauty), as it is written: "From the heavens He made you hear His voice, and upon the earth He showed you His great fire" <note>Deuteronomy 4:36</note>. It is well known that "Heaven and Earth" are the secret of the "Six Faces" (*Vav Partzufim*), which are the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. The entire Torah is spoken in the masculine tongue, which is the secret of *Tiferet* and the Name **Y-H-V-D**. The Oral Torah is the vision. Just as the Name **Y-H-V-D** (*Tiferet*) includes the ten *Sefirot*—the revealed ones along with the hidden secret of *Da'at* (Knowledge)—so too the Torah is included in the Ten Commandments, which correspond to the ten *Sefirot*. The Sages of Truth said as a hint that the Torah was given through the Name **Y-H-V-D**, noting that the word for "twenty-six" (*Esrim ve-Shishah*) has the same letters as "The Ten Commandments" (*Aseret HaDibrot*). Thus, the "Crown of Torah" (*Keter Torah*) was given. Moses received the Torah from Sinai and handed it down with the knowledge that his prophecy came from the side of *Tiferet*, which is called the "Shining Mirror." This is why they established in the liturgy: "A crown of beauty (*Tiferet*) You placed on his head... when he stood before You on Mount Sinai." When it says "Crown of Beauty," it could have simply said "Beauty You placed on his head," but this is a sublime hint to the letter *Aleph* mentioned in the *Tikunim* and brought in the book *Pardes* (Gate 1, Chapter 1). It says: "Jacob is certainly the image of the Central Pillar (*Tiferet*), and Moses was there, but this one is from the inner side and that one is from the outer side; this one is from the Body and that one is from the Soul." Jacob is the "Chariot" for *Tiferet* in its place, while Moses our Teacher is the "Chariot" for its hidden aspect, which is the secret of *Da'at* (Knowledge). This is the "Crown of Beauty," for *Da'at* is the crown of *Tiferet*. Herein lies the secret of the Name **Y-H-V-D**. It is further explained that the Torah is the secret of the four letters of His Name. The Written and Oral Torah given to us are the secret of the letters *V-H* of the Name, even though their root is in the secret of the Holy and Hidden Torah, which is the secret of the letters *Y-H* of His Name. The Written Torah, which is the letter *Vav* of the Name, is the root of "Ancient Wisdom," the secret of the *Yod*. Regarding this, the Sages of blessed memory hinted: "A fallen fruit of the Wisdom above is the Torah." And they hinted: "The Torah preceded the world by two thousand years," for every *Sefira* is called a "thousand" because each *Sefira* is composed of ten, and each of those ten is composed of ten... returning to the secret of the number "one thousand" which points to unity. The secret of the "two thousand years" refers to the twenty *Sefirot* that precede the building of the world, which is *Chesed* (Kindness), as it is written: "The world shall be built on kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>. These are *Chokhmah* and *Binah*, the six roots of the Written and Oral Torah. As we said: "The Torah is a fallen fruit of the Wisdom above." This thought is deep and is partially revealed in the secret of *Binah* through the "Gates"—the secret of the 49 faces of purity and 49 faces of impurity which Moses attained, though he did not attain the 50th Gate. The Oral Torah, which is the final *Heh* of the Name, is revealed from the first *Heh*. The Torah was given to Israel through Moses through the secret of: "And the Lord from the heavens made you hear... and upon the earth etc." Thus, "The Torah of the Lord is perfect," for its perfection is the Name **Y-H-V-D**. Therefore, the Torah begins with the letter *Bet* and ends with the letter *Lamed*, which together form the "32 Paths of Wisdom." This is a wondrous time, for there are no other letters...

# House of Israel

When the verse says, "And man became a living soul" <note>Genesis 2:7; original: "ויהי האדם לנפש חיה"</note>, it alludes to the secret of the level of *Chayah* <note>The fourth of the five levels of the soul, associated with the Divine attribute of Wisdom</note>. Even though the preceding part of the verse says, "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life," we have explained that "in his nostrils" refers to both the man and the woman, Eve <note>original: "חיה" (Chayah); the author is linking the word for "living" with the name "Eve" (Chavah)</note>. This "breath of life" is the third level of the soul. For the attribute of *Binah* <note>Understanding</note> in its highest aspect is also associated with the letter *Yod*, and the *Chayah* level is drawn close to it, for she is "the mother of all living." It is appropriate to call her *Chayah*, as she inclines toward Understanding in the secret of the root of the "Six Extremities" <note>The six emotional Divine attributes (Sefirot) from Mercy to Foundation</note>. Thus, the name Eve (*Chavah*) was derived from the name *Chayah* through the exchange of the letters *Yod* and *Vav*. This is as Rashi explains: "Chavah" is like "Chayah," just as one might say *Hivya* <note>Aramaic for snake</note> for *Chayah* <note>A play on words linking life, Eve, and the serpent</note>. Understand this. From this level of *Chayah* is drawn the "Life of the King," from which the breath of life originates. And when the verse says "Man became a living soul," it means that his physical being contained everything from the lowest *Nefesh* <note>The basic life force</note> up to the *Chayah*, including the female principle, Eve—namely, the levels of *Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah,* and *Chayah*.

By this, a difficulty is resolved that has troubled me for years regarding the verse: "And the Lord God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden" <note>Genesis 2:15</note>. Rashi explains that He "took him with pleasant words and persuaded him to enter." This is difficult: was not his entire purpose to enter the Garden of Eden? Happy is the one who merits it! Why would the First Man refuse to enter until the Holy One, blessed be He, persuaded him? Rather, the matter is that there is a Lower Garden of Eden and an Upper Garden of Eden. These have roots high above in the "Structure" from whose root the Tree of Life is evolved and formed, which is the Lower Garden. Higher than that "Structure" is the root of the Upper Garden. Because the First Man had already attained the level of *Chayah*, which evolves from the root of the Upper Garden, he thought he was meant to enter the Upper Garden immediately. Therefore, he required persuasion to enter the lower one first.

The verse alludes to this: "The Lord God said: Behold, the man has become like one of us" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>. This means he is unique among the lower beings just as I am unique among the upper beings. The matter is that he had reached the realms of *Chayah*, and he desired to ascend even further to utilize the level of *Keter* <note>The Crown; the highest Divine emanation</note> or *Yechidah* <note>The fifth and highest level of the soul, meaning 'Singularity'</note>—that is, the fiftieth level. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I shall prevent him, for I shall cast him out." Regarding the secret of the Tree of Life, we have already written that it speaks of the lower realms but alludes to the upper ones. The Tree of Life is the "Singular Tree" from which the reality of Wisdom emerges, which gives life. "Wisdom gives life to those who possess it" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:12</note>; this is the Wisdom of the "Life of the King." Understand this.

Rabbi Eliezer the Great said in his chapters <note>Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer, ch. 11</note> that God said to the Torah, "Let us make man." Rabbi Ami, in the aforementioned Midrash, said that God "took counsel with His own heart." These two views are consistent. They both allude to this aspect of Man reaching the realms of *Chayah* from the side of Wisdom. We have already mentioned above that the Torah preceded the world in the secret of Wisdom. Therefore, the Torah begins with the letter *Bet* and ends with *Lamed*—the secret of the Heart (*Lev*), and the secret of the thirty-two (*Lamed-Bet*) paths of Wisdom.

The Kabbalists have already written that "Kingdom" (*Malkhut*) is called "Glory" (*Kavod*) and "Heart" (*Lev*). "Glory" has the numerical value of 32. It is called this when it is filled with the flow descending from the thirty-two paths of Wisdom. Thus, both rabbis said the same thing. The hint lies in the realm of the human soul, the secret of *Chayah* from Wisdom, which emanates in the secret of "Six and Four" <note>Refers to the relationship between the emotional attributes and the feminine presence</note> when *Tiferet* (Beauty) and *Malkhut* (Kingdom) are above and emerge into action through Kingdom. Thus, there are four arrangements corresponding to the four letters of the Name: *Nefesh* from the final *Heh* of the Name, *Ruach* from the *Vav*, *Neshamah* from the first *Heh*, *Chayah* from the *Yod*, and *Yechidah* from the tip of the *Yod* in the secret of the Crown. Let us return to our subject: just as the Name descends through the four arrangements and the tip of the *Yod* in the world of Emanation, so it is with souls. Just as the hand includes ten fingers corresponding to the ten *Sefirot*, so too the soul. As stated in the *Ra'aya Mehemna* <note>The 'Faithful Shepherd,' a section of the Zohar</note>: "Masters of Torah, masters of measurements, these souls come from the side of the 'Holy Garment,' which is comprised of the ten *Sefirot*. Whoever inherits it merits the ten *Sefirot* without separation..." This passage is cited in the Zohar and the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moses Cordovero</note> in the first gate, where it is well explained.

In the Midrash Ruth, the holy Rabbi Isaac says: "The Name **Y-H-V-H** is engraved in man, for it is His holy Name." The "Soul of the Soul" is what is truly called "Man" (*Adam*). Its lights spread into nine lights, and it hangs from the letter *Yod*. It spreads into many lights, which are the *Yod* and the *Heh* without separation. Regarding this, it says, "God created man in His image." The letter *Vav* is called *Ruach* (Spirit), and it is called "Son." The letter *Heh* is called *Nefesh* (Soul), and it is called "Daughter." Thus, we have Father, Mother, Son, and Daughter <note>The four letters of the Tetragrammaton interpreted as a family unit</note>. The secret of the "Filled Name" (*Yod-He-Vav-He*) is called "Man," and its lights spread into forty-five lights, which is the numerical value of "Man" (*Adam* = 45) and the expansion of the Name called *Mah*. This is also the level of *Yechidah*. "Male and female He created them, and He called their name Adam." Even the Crown formed the body, as it says: "And the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground." What is the difference between one "Man" and the other? The letter *Yod* is called "Man," and the body is called "Man." What is the difference? One is created "in the image of God," which is a state of unity, while the one not called "in His image" is the physical body. According to what I have written, this statement is clear.

Now, the word "Man" (*Adam*) has a "small numerical value" of 9 <note>45 -> 4+5=9</note>. This is because "Man" did not reach the secret of *Yechidah* from the side of the Crown, which is the tenth and highest level. Thus, "One man in a thousand I have found" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:28</note>. Do not read it as *Eleph* (thousand), but as *Aluph* (Chieftain), for he was lacking it. Nevertheless, "Man" is a seal, for the word "Truth" (*Emet*) also equals nine in its small numerical value. Man was made with a seal, as they explained on the verse "God created man in His image." Likewise, the final letters of the phrase "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" <note>original: "ויפח באפיו נשמת חיים"</note> spell "Seal" (*Chotam*). At the end of the creation story, you will find the seal of Man and the seal of Truth: "God saw the man <note>An interpretive addition by the author</note> and behold, it was very good" (*Me'od*). The letters of *Me'od* (Very) are the letters of *Adam* (Man). They are the sum of creation. "Which God created to do" (*Asot*)—the final letters of the preceding words spell "Truth" (*Emet*). See the passage "Give truth to Jacob," for he is the chariot for *Tiferet*, the father of the evolution of souls with Kingdom, his wife, in his body.

The verse alludes to this: "For the Lord's portion is His people, Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. Do not read "His people" (*Ammo*) with a *Patah* vowel, but rather with a *Hiriq* <note>Changing the meaning from "His people" to "With Him"</note>. For the Torah is not punctuated in its essence so that it can be interpreted in many ways. They are literally "with Him," with the Name **Y-H-V-H**. The "lot" (*Hevel* - also meaning rope) refers to the chain of evolution through Jacob, as mentioned above.

### The connection of Man, from the side of his soul, to the Name **Y-H-V-H**, just as the Torah is connected to the Name.

This is the secret of "Let us make man in our image." It is alluded to in the word "Image" (*Tzelem*). The Kabbalists call the evolution of the Emanations "The Tree." This Tree is the Holy One, blessed be He; it is the true Tree of Life, the soul of all living things. In the spelling of the word "Tree" (*Etz*), the Name **Y-H-V-H** is alluded to through a process of multiplication <note>A complex calculation where letters are multiplied by each other to reach 160, the value of 'Etz'</note>. For example: *Yod* (10) times *Heh* (5) is 50; *Heh* (5) times *Vav* (6) is 30; this equals 80. Then the reverse... it equals 160, which is the value of "Tree" (*Etz*).

See also in the introduction on the verse "Is there a tree in it?" <note>Numbers 13:20</note>. If there is not, one should contemplate if the providence of the Name is upon it, for it is a land that the Lord seeks out. It is as if he were asking: "Is the Name **Y-H-V-H** in its midst or not?" Caleb said: "Their shadow (*Tzelem*) has departed from them, but the Lord is with us" <note>Numbers 14:9</note>. "Image/Shadow" (*Tzelem*) has the numerical value of "Tree" (*Etz*) [160]. For we sit in His hidden shadow, and that is why "The Lord is with us."

The Torah is called a "Tree" in every place, for it is a "Tree of Life to those who hold fast to it." Man is beloved because he was created in the "Image" (*Tzelem*), which also equals this same number. Thus, they are connected to the Name **Y-H-V-H**. Regarding this, the verse says: "Let us make man in our image." And when it says "after our likeness," this refers to the likeness of the human body. For the essential name of "Man" belongs to the inner body, which is the soul. The physical body is called the "flesh of man."

As seen in the Zohar, the body of a person is called the "Garment of Man." Similarly, even in the forces of impurity, the "flesh of a pig" is their garment, but their internal form, which comes from the spirit of impurity, is called "Pig." Thus the verse says regarding the soul's embodiment in the limbs: "You have clothed me in skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews" <note>Job 10:11</note>. If the skin and flesh are a "garment" for the man, we are forced to conclude that the inner spirit is what is called "Man," not the skin and flesh.

The Zohar states: "Every form that is included in the expansion of this realm is called 'Man,' as it is written: 'You are Man.' You are called Man, but the other nations are not called Man." The spirit of the holy side is called "Man"; its body is the "Garment of Man." Therefore, "You clothed me in skin and flesh"—the flesh is the garment of Man. Everywhere it says "the flesh of man," it means the flesh is the garment. Thus you see that the name "Man" applies to the Form, not the Matter. Therefore, the nations of the world are not called "Man" <note>In this specific Kabbalistic context, 'Man' refers to the specific spiritual structure of the Jewish soul linked to the Sefirot</note>, for their souls are from the spirit of impurity. However, the souls of Israel are from His holy spirit, as it is said: "From Me is your fruit found." His fruit is sweet to the palate. They are compared to the Tree called "All," from which the souls called "Man" fly forth. They are in the image of God. It is also said: "Its interior is paved with love from the daughters of Jerusalem." The souls of Israel are set apart from the souls of the nations, for the souls of the righteous do not mix with the souls of the wicked.

Nevertheless, there is some connection to the "likeness of the body" because it serves as a case for the soul, similar to the law that one saves the case of a Torah scroll along with the scroll itself. If you, my children, will pay attention to what I show you—what the essence of Man is inwardly and what he alludes to in his form—then you will surely not rouse yourselves to approach [sin] in argument, thought, or deed.

Regarding the body of the First Man, in the Zohar, Rabbi Shimon stood and said: "I have observed that when the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create Man, the upper and lower worlds trembled. On the day that the 'Splendor' was to be created, He ascended through the levels until the Supernal Will arose, and the beginning of all lights shone. He opened the Gate of the East, for from there the light emerges..." He signaled a spark of light that descends from the Head and is established in the East. The East strengthened the North, and the North awakened and spread, calling out with a great voice to the West to approach and spread with it. Then the West ascended into the North and was bound by its hand to the Crown. The South came and took hold of the West, and the North and South protected it—the secret of the fences of the Garden. Then the East approached the West, and the West dwelt in expansiveness and sought from all of them, saying: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness," for this was the intention in the four directions...

<header>House of Israel</header>

Whether one is worthy or not, Rabbi Hezekiah said: This is what I have heard regarding the verse, "From Me is your fruit found" <note>Hosea 14:9; original: "ממני פריך נמצא"</note>. It turns out that the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the Community of Israel: "From Me, your fruit is found." It does not say "found fruit," but "your fruit is found." This refers to the desire of the Female <note>The attribute of *Malchut* or the Shekhinah</note> which creates a soul and is included within the strength of the Male <note>The attribute of *Tiferet*</note>. Then, soul is included within soul, becoming a single unified vessel, as we have stated. Afterward, both are found in this world; through the power of the Male, the Female aspect is found. Another interpretation: through the desire of the Female, the Male aspect is found. For if there were no desire of the Female toward the Male, "fruits" <note>referring to souls</note> would never be produced for the world. This is the meaning of "From Me is your fruit found." This concludes the quote. From the general scope of this passage, it is explained that souls result from the union of *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/the Male principle</note> and *Malchut* <note>Kingship/the Female principle</note>. When we come to the world of their preparation, we see that the soul of the male and the soul of the female are unified and "twins" in a single conception. It is impossible to depict the female soul without the male, or the male soul without the female. The reason is that they are two powers from two unified *Sefirot* <note>Divine emanations</note>: from the power of the Female comes the female aspect, and from the power of the Male comes the male aspect. Thus, souls—whether male or female—are formed from the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut*.

## And the Rabbi
The author of the *Pardes* <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero’s "Pardes Rimonim," a foundational Kabbalistic text</note> raised a difficulty: many passages in the *Zohar* <note>The central work of Jewish mysticism</note> state that the *Neshamah* <note>the higher soul</note> comes from *Binah* <note>Understanding</note>. This is also explained in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei Zohar</note>: "The lamp of God is the soul of man" <note>Proverbs 20:27</note>. *Ne-Re* <note>the word 'lamp' or *Ner*</note> stands for *Nefesh* and *Ruach* <note>the lower soul and the spirit</note>, which are the emanations of the *Shekhinah* <note>Divine Presence</note> and the "Middle Pillar" <note>Tiferet</note> which includes six *Sefirot*. "The soul of man" <note>Neshamah</note> is the emanation of the "Supernal Mother" <note>Binah</note>. This concludes the quote. Afterward, the *Pardes* explains the matter briefly: the *Neshamah* flows from *Binah* in a hidden and clinging state to *Tiferet* and *Malchut*. Then *Tiferet* and *Malchut* unite, and only then does the *Neshamah* gain an actual existence. See there at length. The general principle is: *Nefesh* comes from the side of *Malchut*, *Ruach* from the side of *Tiferet*, and *Neshamah* from the side of *Binah*. It is formed through the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut*. This is the "Full Name" <note>The Tetragrammaton and Elohim</note> mentioned by Nachmanides: "And the Lord God formed man" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>. "The Lord God" refers to *Tiferet* and *Malchut*. It then says, "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life," which refers to *Binah*. The *Neshamah* dwells within the structure of *Tiferet*, which includes the "Six Extremities" <note>the six emotional Sefirot</note> along with *Malchut*. This is the secret of an "oath" <note>term: *Shevuah*</note>, from the word "seven" <note>term: *Sheva*</note>. From there, the negative and positive commandments are drawn. For *Tiferet* leans toward the right, toward *Chesed* <note>Kindness</note>, the secret of positive commandments; while *Malchut* leans toward *Gevurah* <note>Strength/Judgment</note>, which is the left, the secret of negative commandments. Therefore, one who swears an oath to cancel a commandment has done nothing. How could the power of an oath—whose source is in "Seven"—cancel a commandment whose source is also in "Seven"? For the commandment was already accepted at Mount Sinai with an oath. However, we must descend to its place in *Binah*, which is the "Tower flying in the air" above *Tiferet*. For *Tiferet* is called "He," and it is above *Tiferet*. *Ner* <note>lamp</note> hints at "two lamps," which are the fifty gates of *Binah* and the inner essence. Thus, the lamp applies to the commandment, and the one who swears an oath swears by the King Himself in His union with the Queen. One who vows "by the life of the King" is even more significant. Even if these are distinct aspects, everything is unified: the "Life of the King" and "Living Water." The verse says "Breath of Life," meaning the "Life of the King," which is *Binah*. This is the explanation of the *Ramaz* <note>Rabbi Moshe Zacuto</note>. And I have come to explain the end of the verse where it says, "And man became a living soul."

Before I explain this verse, I will provide a short introduction, through which the *Midrash Rabbah* <note>A classic collection of homiletic teachings on the Bible</note> will be understood in its breadth, depth, and height. It is this: I have already mentioned that souls are formed from the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut*—the *Nefesh* from *Malchut* and the *Ruach* from *Tiferet*. Even the *Neshamah*, which is from *Binah*, flows subtly and hiddenly into *Tiferet* and *Malchut* in their place. Through the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut*, the *Neshamah* becomes an actual "Living Soul" (*Chayah*). You must know that when we speak of the union of *Tiferet* with *Malchut*, it refers to the "Six Extremities," which are the arms, the legs, and the covenant of the flesh <note>referring to the Sefirot Chesed, Gevurah, Netzach, Hod, and Yesod</note> that belong to the union in the secret of the "Embrace," as discussed in the *Pardes* in the section on Essence and Conduct. Thus, the matter of *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* comes from the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut* in the context of the "Six Extremities" in their place. However, we have already mentioned above that the "Six Extremities" and *Malchut* have their root in *Binah*, which is the place of "planting." They acquired a somewhat revealed existence in this root, but there they are unified together in the secret of the "Four Faces" <note>term: *Partzufim*</note>, which are the secret of seventy "sevens" <note>original: "ע' שבועות"</note>, as discussed above at length. 

You must also know that the souls of Adam and Eve were emanated from *Tiferet* and *Malchut* in this secret of the "Four Faces"—that is, not from *Tiferet* and *Malchut* in their lower place, but in this higher root. And just as the "Faces" in *Binah* are the root of the "Six Extremities," so too is the soul of Adam the root of all souls. For from the soul of Adam, 600,000 souls spread out in every generation. This is the soul of Moses our Teacher, of whom the Sages said: "One woman gave birth to 600,000 at once." Through him came the hint: "Six hundred thousand [people] among whom I am" <note>Numbers 11:21</note>. For the nation came from him; they lived from his life, and from him they emerged. Since Adam's soul is the root of all souls and all souls spread from it, when death was decreed upon him, it was decreed upon all who come from him, for all were within his potential. As the *Midrash Rabbah* says on the portion of *Ki Tissa*: when Adam was still an unformed mass (*golem*), the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him every righteous person destined to descend from him. Some were hanging from Adam’s head, some from his hair, some from his forehead, some from his eyes, his nose, his mouth, his ears...

<margin>When he finished the verse, he gathered it together. The language of "gathering" or "collecting" refers to the beginning of the formation of the "Faces." And as mentioned above, the Four Faces are written here, but later they are in their place as seven levels. Each one is in the secret of the Four Faces...</margin>

Know that when Job sought to argue with the Holy One, blessed be He, he said: "O that I knew where I might find Him, that I might come even to His seat! I would order my cause before Him" <note>Job 23:3-4</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, replied: "You seek to argue with Me? Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?" <note>Job 38:4</note>. What is the meaning of "Where" (*Eifoh*)? Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "Job, tell me, your *Eifoh* <note>a play on the word for 'where' and a measure of capacity</note>—on which place was it hanging? On the head or the forehead or which limb? If you knew where your *Eifoh* was, you could argue with Me. But 'Where' (*Eifoh*) were you?" This concludes the quote. From this explanation, our intention is clarified without doubt. It says that while Adam was a *golem*—meaning after the formation and the plan were set, and the "plantings" were almost spread out—they did not yet have bodies to clothe themselves in. Regarding this soul that includes all souls, it can be said that the souls existed before the world was created. The intention is that the "Building" <note>the structure of the Sefirot</note> is called the "World of Thought" from *Chesed* <note>Kindness</note>, as it is written: "The world shall be built with kindness" <note>Psalms 89:3</note>. But the *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* that are formed from the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut* in their place are the secret of the "New Souls" prepared to be formed when the Holy One, blessed be He, renews His world in the future, as written in the *Pardes*, chapter 23.

Thus, it is explained that the souls of Adam and Eve are in the secret of the "Four" and in *Binah*. This is the meaning of the verse: "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life"—this is the "Life of the King" in *Binah*. This also explains the grammar of the word "in his nostrils" (*be-apav*), which is plural. It should have said "in his nostril" (*be-appo*). But because Man was in the secret of the "Four Faces" <note>containing both male and female</note>, it says "his nostrils," for there were two faces. And this is simple. Thus, the detail in the *Midrash Rabbah* is well explained: Rabbi Joshua in the name of Rabbi Levi said: Regarding the work of Heaven and Earth, He took counsel. "Heaven and earth and their hosts" refer to *Tiferet* and *Malchut*, hinting at the souls of Adam and Eve in the secret of the "Four" and in *Binah*. Rabbi Samuel bar Nachman said: He took counsel with the works of each day. These are *Tiferet* and *Malchut* in their lower place, in the secret of the "Six Extremities," which are the "renewed souls" formed from them.

In any case, the souls from the side of *Tiferet* and *Malchut* are either in their place (the Six Extremities) or in their root (in *Binah*), in the secret of the "Four" which is the root of the "Building," the secret of the letter *He* of *Binah*. It is known that the Six Extremities are the cause and reason for this world. The Sages said: "This world was created with the letter *He*." Even though this *He* resembles *Malchut*—the "Small *He*" in the word "when they were created" <note>Genesis 2:4; original: "בהבראם"</note>—nevertheless, this latter *He* that brings the influences of the Six Extremities into action comes from the "First *He*," meaning the aspect of *Binah*, which is the root of the Extremities. But above this, beyond the aspect of the "Three Lines" <note>the three columns of the Sefirotic tree</note>... namely *Chokhmah* <note>Wisdom</note> and *Binah* in the aspect of the "Three Supernal Extremities" and *Keter* <note>Crown</note> (the "tip of the *Yod*"). This is the cause of the World to Come, which was created with the letter *Yod*. Therefore, there is a "Soul of Souls," which is the root above the roots of the Building. Then an additional "Extra Soul" (*Neshamah Yeterah*) from the side of *Chokhmah* will ascend. This level is called *Chayah* <note>Living One</note>. This is the fourth rank of the soul's secret: *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* (from *Malchut*, *Tiferet*, and *Binah*), and *Chayah* from the side of *Chokhmah*. And in the "World of the Hidden" <note>term: *Olam ha-He’elam*</note>, in the secret of *Keter*, it is called *Yechidah* <note>Unique One</note>. Only these levels of *Chayah* and *Yechidah* are the secret of the "Extra Soul" for the World to Come—"No eye has seen it, O God, beside You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. They are from the aspect of the letter *Yod*. But the levels mentioned—*Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* in this world—are from the aspect of the letter *He*. 

This answers the question: why are only *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* usually mentioned, when there are also *Chayah* and *Yechidah*? It is because *Chayah* and *Yechidah* are the secret of the Extra Soul in the World to Come, while *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* are the secret of this world. Do not be troubled by what you find in the later Kabbalists regarding the secret of these five levels at different times: *Nefesh* on weekdays and during the Additional Prayer of the New Moon; *Ruach* on Festivals; *Neshamah* on the Day of Atonement; *Chayah* on the Sabbath; and *Yechidah* in the World to Come. They gave a mnemonic: *Chayah* <note>meaning 'living' but here used as a hint</note> — the five words ascend... it is that the spirit rests, and the level of the "Sabbath Spirit" is therefore expanded, as is written. This is a thin spark of them. It is as the Sages said: "The Sabbath is one-sixtieth of the World to Come." But essentially, *Chayah* and *Yechidah* belong to the World to Come, which is the letter *Yod* and the "Five" with its tip. 

Behold, they said in the *Tikunei Zohar*, and it was cited in the *Pardes* (in the section on Essence and Conduct), that Adam and Eve are *Chokhmah* and *Binah*. For even though they were in the aspect of the "Four Faces," nevertheless, Adam's status is superior. As it says in the chapter "The One Who Sees" <note>Berakhot 61a</note> regarding the "Four Faces": "Which of them went first? Rav Nachman bar Isaac said: It stands to reason that the man went first." Behold, the soul of Adam is *Chayah* from the side of *Chokhmah*, which is the level called *Chayah*. And this is what...

It explains that all human souls were originally contained within Adam and Eve, who were created as a unified, multi-faceted being.</summary>

<header>House of Israel</header>

### **And they** are impure and worthy in the book to the boundary of the Altar. In this matter, there is a wonder; it says there in this language: The "Forms of Israel" <note>original: "צורות ישראל"; referring to the spiritual archetypes or souls of the Jewish people</note> were meant to be distinct and set apart from the rest of humanity in their internal character and souls. However, the Law of the Sabbatical <note>original: "חק השמיטה"; in Kabbalah, this refers to cosmic cycles of time where different divine attributes dominate</note> and the difficulty of existence caused these groups to become mixed and rolled—transmigrating <note>original: "מתגלגלות"; referring to *Gilgul*, the reincarnation of souls</note>—into many different bodies. They return to their proper place through the sacrifices offered on the Altar for acceptance from the animals. This concludes his words. The explanation is: Therefore, it was necessary for the "Form of Israel" to be distinct from its companions, just as their souls and spiritual powers are distinct and set apart from them. Thus, it was fitting for their physical bodies to be distinct as well. However, the order of the Sabbatical cycles and the difficulty of existence do not allow for this path because the spiritual powers and souls, like the colors of the bodies, become mixed and transmigrate into one another. This means that the souls of Israel become mixed within the bodies of the nations. Those mixed within the bodies of animals are redeemed through the sacrifice offered for acceptance from the animal. But the bodies of the nations <note>original: "גופי הני'"; likely referring to the *Goyim* or non-Jewish nations</note> cannot have the soul redeemed from them until they undergo conversion. This is the hidden matter. But this difficulty was resolved by the Holy One <note>unclear abbreviation</note> in another manner; look in the *Book of Wonder* <note>original: "ספר הפליאה"; an influential 14th-century Kabbalistic text</note>, for there you will find it.

<margin>
This is what is said there.
</margin>

### **And I shall return** to the matter of Creation which I was discussing. I say that the attribute of *Malchut* <note>term: Malchut (Kingship). The final Sefirah, representing the physical world and the feminine Divine Presence</note> includes all forms. Within it are internal arrangements within internal ones, and external ones within external ones, as the Supreme Wisdom decreed. The forms are given through the angel Sandalphon <note>note: Sandalphon is traditionally the angel who weaves crowns for God and governs the formation of embryos</note>. The souls, which are the roots of the upper beings, provide every spiritual body <note>term: Geviyah Ruchanit. A subtle, spiritual body that bridges the physical body and the pure soul</note> that joins with the physical body with the form appropriate for it. The secret of the matter is that the Unique Name <note>referring to the Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> includes ten *Sefirot*, which are ten holy Names. These are vessels for His differentiated Knowledge, which cannot be grasped by thought, for they are the secret of the Essence. These names act as a "soul" to one another. Every single name among these has descriptive titles and "wings" <note>original: "כנפים"; metaphorical layers of divine manifestation</note> attached to the titles, and princes <note>angels</note> attached to the wings. All the princes have chariots and hosts. Thus, everything hangs and stands upon the Unique Name. He conducts His world with Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, the secret of the Explicit Name <note>term: Shem Ha-Meforash. The 72-letter name of God derived from Exodus 14:19-21</note>, in which the Unique Name clothes itself. This is engraved upon the Staff, which is a "Staff leaning toward Kindness" <note>original: "מטה כלפי חסד"</note> in the secret of His Palace, *Malchut*. These are like a spiritual body to receive the inner wisdoms, which are like "Forms" for them, while the "Husks" <note>term: Kelipot. The outer shells or forces of impurity</note> are like a case for them. Therefore, **"Let us make man in our image"** <note>Genesis 1:26</note>, for the combinations of his matter and the variety of his limbs are based on the Explicit Name engraved on the Staff. His form is also included in three levels, one before the other: Body, Spirit (*Ruach*), and Soul (*Neshamah*). They are bound in one strong knot and serve as a dwelling for one another, drawing from their root. The Vital Soul (*Nefesh*) draws from the Bride <note>Malchut</note> in the secret of "My soul (*Nafshi*) desires You in the night." The Spirit (*Ruach*) draws from the Groom <note>Tiferet</note> in the secret of "Indeed, my spirit (*Ruchi*) within me seeks You." The Higher Soul (*Neshamah*) draws from the Wedding Canopy <note>Binah</note>, the secret of "Let every soul (*Neshamah*) praise God." These forms also have the spiritual body mentioned above. It mediates between the Form and the physical body, shaped like the "Husk" mentioned in the discourse of the holy luminary, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>note: The traditional author of the Zohar</note>, peace be upon him: "I found in the Book of King Solomon that at the time of union below, the Holy One sends down a single likeness of a human face, marked and engraved in an image (*Tzelem*). If permission were given to the eye to see, a person would see upon their head an image of a human face, and in that image, the person is created. Until that image stands over him and is sent by his Master to be found upon his head, the person cannot be created. This is the meaning of 'And God created man in His image.' That image is ready before him until he emerges into the world. When he emerges, he grows with that image and walks with that image, as it is written, 'Surely man walks in an image' <note>Psalm 39:7</note>. This image comes from above. At the time of union, all spirits emerge from beneath it, and their appearance is set before the Holy King in the beautiful arrangements of the face that exists in this world, and in that likeness, it emerges to this world." This concludes the quote. This "body" is the mediator for the physical body because it shares a connection with both the body and the Form. It would be impossible to join two opposites except through a mediator that is the spiritual body. To this body was joined "Vitality" <note>original: "חיות"</note> hidden from the dust of the Holy Temple in Jerusalem. In the Midrash, they said: "From the earth," Rabbi Boreriya and Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Nachman, "Man was created from the place of his atonement <note>the site of the Altar</note>," as it is written, "An altar of earth you shall make for me." The Holy One said, "I am creating him from the place of his atonement; may he only endure." Man has 248 limbs, which are vessels for 248 powers that serve the soul. These are in the pattern of the Explicit Name in combination with the 32 Wondrous Paths of Wisdom through which all existence came into being. For the Explicit Name consists of 72 names, built from the verses "And he traveled," "And he came," "And he stretched" <note>Exodus 14:19-21</note>. The 72 names are tripled: right, left, and center. They result in 216 letters. These letters hint at the inner Wisdom included in the secret of the Hidden Name. When the 32 Paths of Wisdom are joined with the 216 letters of the Explicit Name, they total 248. When it arose in the Pure Thought to create man, He created and established him with 248 limbs, which are thrones for him and the fifteen powers of the soul that serve him. This concludes the words of the book *Avodat Ha-Kodesh* <note>term: Avodat Ha-Kodesh. "The Service of the Holy," a classic Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai (16th century)</note>.

## **Furthermore,** I have something to say regarding the spiritual and mediating body between the soul and the physical body. This involves the nullification of the form toward its Creator. The Sages of Truth have already said by way of metaphor and hint: The Infinite (*Ein Sof*) is the "Soul of Souls." This means we describe the World of Emanation (*Atzilut*) as the souls of all created beings, and the Infinite is the soul to those souls. For those souls are within Him. The world of Emanation is called "Man" in terms of governance, as it is written, "And upon the throne was the likeness of the appearance of a Man." We will explain this well later. Man is made in the "Image and Likeness" and is called "Small Man" <note>original: "אדם קטן"; Microcosm</note>. Just as there is a distinction between the Soul and the body, and as we explained above regarding the Infinite and the governance of Emanation—which is the "Stripping of Form" and the Essence—so too the spiritual body of man is the connection between the soul and the physical body, like the connection of a flame to a coal.
</insert>

<insert>
## **I will also** copy the words of our teacher Rabbi Matityahu Lantarqi <note>note: A 14th-century philosopher and commentator</note>, may the memory of the righteous be a blessing, regarding the unification of Emanation with the Infinite and the connection of the soul to the body. He says: First of all, God, blessed be He, is first and ancient to all, exalted above all. He is called the Cause of all Causes. Before the world was created, all things were hidden and concealed with Him; it was not known what was in His power. Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name alone. The ten *Sefirot* are considered His power within His Essence. He says nothing was known but He and His Name in its simplicity, not in its expansion. All the Divine Attributes were hidden and stored in the Infinite in His simple Unity until it arose in His thought to create a world and for His ways and actions to be known. He revealed Himself to each according to their capacity to perceive His truth. This He revealed through the *Sefirot*, which are the essence of His Glory and His attributes. Knowledge of God is through His attributes, just as the soul's truth is recognized through its powers and actions in the limbs of the body. Do not think this was a new development or a change in His will; these *Sefirot* are His powers that existed in Him potentially always, only they were hidden. They are descriptions of His actions which were revealed later. It was not a "new creation" but a revelation of the hidden truth to created beings through various levels. One can understand this from the actions of a man: how they emerge from the source of the soul which rules him through the organs of the body. In truth, the first expansion of the soul's power is in **Thought**; from Thought, it becomes **Wisdom** and intellect. Then from **Understanding** (*Binah*) it emerges into a beautiful vessel. These things are attributed to the **Brain** and are called **Neshamah** <note>Higher Soul</note>. Furthermore, from the **Heart** emerge the powers of feeling and the movement of all limbs through the "Spirit of Life" (*Ruach Chaim*). This awakens one to good, evil, or the middle ground. Sometimes it moves one to be a man of kindness, and sometimes, seeing a bad deed, it moves one to vengeance and anger. When it sees a good deed, it draws will and spirit from the brain (the spinal cord) to have mercy and do good with justice and charity. These powers are called the **Ruach** <note>Spirit</note>. Furthermore, from the **Liver** emerge the power of nourishment, growth, and desire. This power is called **Nefesh** <note>Vital Soul</note>. it tends toward physical things and sustains the body for its temporary time. We further observe the power that binds all these things and conducts them properly; this is the temperament and nature within every man according to his composition. It is known that all these actions are only from the power of the soul clinging to him; they are her powers flowing and revealed from her. Even though we call this one *Ruach* and that one *Nefesh*, it is only in terms of their closeness to physicality. But the soul is always indivisible and unseparated, a single essence whose nature is hidden from us; we only say it is spiritual...
</insert>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of how the human form is a microcosm of the Divine. It transitions from the general concept of the soul's mixing to the specific anatomical correspondences between the human body and the Divine Names.</meta>

<header>House of Israel</header>

Above and below, East and West, and He brought him forth. Regarding this, we have learned: the lower man <note>original: "אדם תתאה"; referring to earthly humanity</note> emerged from the site of the Holy Temple. Let the wise one upon whom the spirit shines contemplate this wondrous secret and understand the mystery of "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>, for it is not appropriate to explain more than this. However, just as his true existence was formed from the four celestial corners, so too was this vitality prepared from the four lower corners. This is what they said in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer the Great*: He began to gather the dust of the first man from the four corners of the earth—red, black, white, and green—and everything corresponds to its counterpart. And what is said here—that the lower man emerged from the site of the Holy Temple—corresponds to what is written in the Midrash: "From the earth" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>; Rabbi Berechiah and Rabbi Helbo said in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Nachman: He was created from the place of his atonement, as it says, "An altar of earth you shall make for Me" <note>Exodus 20:21</note>. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Behold, I am creating him from the place of his atonement; if only he may endure." And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, Rabbi Shimon said: This is what Rabbi Hezekiah said, that when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created man, he was created from the dust of the lower sanctuary, and from the dust of the upper sanctuary three celestial sides were conceived in him. For when he was created from the lower dust, the three foundations of the world <note>original: "תלת סטרין יסודי עלמא"</note> were conceived in him; likewise, when he was created from the upper dust, three celestial sides were conceived in him, and man was completed. Behold, the body is the sanctuary of Solomon <note>original: "מקדש שלמה"; a play on "completed sanctuary"</note> and the soul is the sanctuary above. The lower sanctuary is aligned against the upper one, meaning that the

->lower man, called a "small world" <note>microcosm</note>, is modeled after the construction of the "Great Man" <note>macrocosm</note>, which is the secret of the World of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divinity</term>.<-

**Also** in the levels of the body: just as Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge <note>Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at</note>—the three primary attributes—are considered as one, so the head of a man includes the brain, the skull, and the tongue, which correspond to these three. Greatness and Might <note>Gedulah and Gevurah</note> are likened to the arms. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The Sefer HaBahir</note>, they said in this language: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has seven holy forms, and all of them have a counterpart in man, as it is said, "For in the image of God He made man," and "male and female He created them." These are: the right and left leg, the right and left hand, the body and the sign of the covenant <note>circumcision</note>, and the head—behold, that is six. But you said seven? It includes his wife, as it is written: "and they shall become one flesh."

**Furthermore**, hinted there is the Name of God <note>original: "יוד"ד"; referring to the four-letter name Y-H-V-H</note> in the stature of man from top to bottom and bottom to top. How so? Behold, the head is in the likeness of the letter *Yud* (י), the expanse of the body is in the likeness of the letter *Vav* (ו), and the ten fingers of the hands—five against five—correspond to the two letters *Heh* (ה). Similarly, the ten toes of the feet—five against five—correspond to the two letters *Heh* (ה), totaling ten. <margin>The extension of the covenant of the organ is in the likeness of the letter *Vav* (ו)</margin> The crown <note>original: "עטרה"; the tip of the organ</note> is in the likeness of the letter *Yud* (י). Now, the author of *Haparat* <note>possibly referring to a specific Kabbalistic work</note> wrote at the beginning of his book that the toes of the feet are like a shadow to the fingers of the hands, hinting at the World of Creation <note>Beriah</note> which is a shadow to the World of Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>. I have come to make you understand his words, for his intent is not regarding Creation in its own place, but rather regarding the sources of Creation that sparkle within Kingship <note>Malchut</note>, which are still within the reality of Emanation.

->They are in Emanation; therefore, it is fitting that they are part of the "Repair of Man" <term>Tikkun Adam: the spiritual restoration of the human archetype</term> made in the image of God.<-

**Furthermore**, you will find in the features of the face: two eyes and a nose are in the likeness of two *Yuds* and a *Vav*, corresponding to the Name of God... <margin>The numerical value 63</margin> The great virtue in man is when he lowers his eyes or they remain in one connection, but when he is haughty of eye or the eyes distance themselves from the nose, then the Name of God is not present and He does not sit on the Throne of Mercy; rather, only the "nose" remains, and then there is "burning anger" in the world. But when <margin>In the book *Chisun Romi* on 2 Chronicles, section 10, page 27: The height of his stature corresponds to the Holy of Holies, and his spread [arms] correspond to the wings of the Cherubim...</margin> he lowers his eyes, then the attribute of Mercy, the Name of God, is present. And beneath the nose are the nostrils...

**Furthermore**, you will find the Name of God hinted at in the ten fingers of the hands, which are the number of the ten Sephirot <term>Sephirot: the ten divine attributes or channels through which God reveals Himself</term>. How so? In every finger there are three joints, except for the thumb which has two joints. "He who formed man with wisdom" <note>from the Asher Yatzar blessing</note> formed him with wonderful intent: the right hand hints at the letters *Yud-Heh* (יה) and the left hand hints at the letters *Vav-Heh* (וה). Take the letters *Yud-Heh* in their spelled-out form <note>gematria filling</note>—*Yud-Vav-Dalet* and *Heh-Aleph*—there are five letters, and they are the five fingers of the hand. And take these letters and fill them a second time... behold, in four fingers there are three joints each, and in the "Divine Heh" only two joints; so too in four fingers there are three joints and in the thumb <note>original: "אצבע מנורל"</note> there are two.

->Therefore, the hand is called "Yad" (יד) after the number of joints <note>Yad equals 14; 3+3+3+3+2 = 14</note>.<-

The left hand corresponds to the letters *Vav-Heh* (וה)... and in the twenty fingers <note>including toes</note>... and this is the matter of "and they went without strength <note>original: "כח"; numerical value 28</note> before the pursuer," for these two hands <note>14 + 14 = 28</note> are the "Strength" (Koach), and when Israel are righteous, they add strength to the Supernal Might.

**Also**, you will find in the hand a hint to the name *Shaddai* (שד"י). How so? Take the middle, ring, and pinky fingers—stretch them out like a *Shin* (ש), then bend a finger like a *Dalet* (ד), <margin>In the likeness of a *Shin*; and when the arm is circumcised they are marked</margin> then bend the thumb which is smaller, and it is in the likeness of a *Yud* (י). This is what the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed to Abraham with the name *El Shaddai*. This name is also hinted at in the form of the body: the head and two arms stretched upward look like the shape of a *Shin* (ש). When the left arm is straight and the right is at rest, it looks like a *Dalet* (ד), and the crown of the circumcision is like a *Yud* (י). Nations that are not circumcised... but when they are circumcised and guard the holy covenant, they are attached to the Name of God...

**Furthermore**, see in the *Pardes* <note>by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of the Soul" the wonders of the soul within the body, and you will find that Enoch, because of his movement, was worthy to be a dwelling for the soul.

**Behold**, the levels of the *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* <note>the three levels of the soul: Vitality, Spirit, and Higher Soul</note> dwell in the body within the Brain, Heart, and Liver <note>original: "מוח לב כבד"</note>, the acronym of which is *Melech* (King). The *Nefesh* part is in the Liver, which is the vital force, the natural power containing the nourishing power, the pulling power, the power that sustains the food, the expelling power, the reproductive power, and the sensing power (hearing, sight, taste, smell, and touch). All these are powers of the natural *Nefesh*. The *Ruach* part is in the Heart, which is the Will, and it leads all its powers according to its will, like a king leading his people... so the spirit of life in the heart provides for all the powers. The *Neshamah* part is in the Brain, and it is the intellectual thought that rules over them all. To make you understand this: know that before the Will in the heart desires to do something, it arises in the Thought of the brain... and after the thought in the brain agrees, it clothes itself in the Will of the heart... from this reason, the power in the heart is called *Ruach*, for *Ruach* means "will"... and the *Ruach* in the heart clothes itself in the powers that spread from the *Nefesh* in the liver and acts through them... thus all are united in complete unity. The *Nefesh* receives from the *Ruach* (the Will), and the Will acts only according to the agreement of the Thought in the Brain, and according to the Wisdom in the Brain they act.

### To show you
the sanctity of the body, I have copied what is written in the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>by Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, Chapter 18: "I have seen regarding this creation specifically awesome things in the deep treasures of wisdom; I bring them here to benefit those who wander seeking the word of the Lord. Behold, as has been explained, man is in the image of God... for to each one is given a dwelling according to his honor... through Sandalphon... and there is a soul that is emanated from the inner Sephirot, and there is one from the outer, and some from the 'wings'... and behold, the chosen nation... their soul is from the side of holiness and purity, though there are differences among them, for the soul of the righteous is not like the soul of the wicked... but the souls of the nations are from the side of impurity and they are..."
