<meta>This page transitions from the general concept of the human body as a microcosm to a specific Kabbalistic defense of anthropomorphism—the practice of describing God with human features like hands, eyes, and ears. It contrasts the rationalist view (that these are merely metaphors) with the mystical view (that the human body is a physical reflection of spiritual realities).</meta>

<page-num>11</page-num>
<header>A Faithful House</header>

<margin>And he said they are</margin>
He explained all the attributes and said they are "borrowed names" <note>original: "שמות מושאלי' כחשי'"; a term used by rationalist philosophers like Maimonides to argue that physical descriptions of God are merely metaphors used to help human understanding</note> and he explained each and every attribute and to what matter it is "borrowed," explaining them with good taste and knowledge according to the 
<margin>Master of</margin>
plain meaning. However, the Kabbalistic Rabbi, the author of *The Service of Holiness* <note>original: "עבודת הקודש" (Avodat HaKodesh) by Meir ibn Gabbai, 1531</note> in the section on "Emanations," disagreed with him and explained them according to the "Secret" <note>the mystical/esoteric level of interpretation</note> regarding what they signify. And these are the words of the book *The Gates of
<margin>Path</margin>
Light* <note>original: "שערי אורה" (Sha'arei Orah) by Joseph Gikatilla, 13th century</note>: Know that the truth of the Essence of the Creator, may He be blessed, is not attainable by anyone else, and among all the heavenly hosts there is none who knows His place, let alone the essence of His truth. Do you
not see that the heavenly angels say, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place," wherever He may be? And if the upper beings do not know, how much more so the lower beings? If so, all
those matters that we read in the Torah, such as "hand," "foot," "ears," and all other similar things—what are they? <margin>as mentioned above</margin> Know and believe that all those matters, even though
they point to and testify to His greatness and truth, no creature can know or contemplate the essence of that thing called "hand" or "foot" and the like. And if we
are made in the image and likeness, let it not enter your mind that an "eye" is in the shape of an eye or a "hand" in the shape of a hand; rather, they are internal matters, internal within the internal, in the true existence of God,
may He be blessed, from which the source and flow <note>original: "שפע" (Shefa); the divine emanation or life-force</note> goes out to all beings. But the essence of the [Divine] Hand is not like the essence of a [human] hand, nor is its form equal, as it is written: "To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" <note>Isaiah 40:25</note>.
Know and understand: we provide hints from the perspective of the Essence and the form. Rather, the intention of the form of the limbs within us is that they are made as a signpost for exalted, virtuous matters that human knowledge
cannot know, except as a reminder—much like one who writes "Reuven son of Jacob." For these letters are not the physical form of Reuven son of Jacob, nor his essence,
but a reminder; "Reuven son of Jacob" in writing is a sign corresponding to that known person called Reuven son of Jacob. Because the Lord, may He be blessed
and exalted, desired our benefit, He created within the human body various limbs, <margin>rather</margin> hidden and revealed, like a sign for the "Work of the Chariot" <note>original: "מעשה מרכב' " (Ma'aseh Merkavah); the highest level of Jewish mysticism concerning the throne of God</note>. If a person is worthy to purify one
of his limbs, that limb becomes like a throne for that exalted, internal thing called by that name—if an eye, an Eye; if a hand, a Hand; and so for all the rest. How so? For example, if a
man is careful and guards the sight of his eyes so that he does not look at or gaze upon something forbidden <note>literally "nakedness"</note> or anything shameful, but only at that which is holy to the Lord and His service,
then that eye becomes like a throne for that exalted thing called "Eye" above. And so for the hand, the foot, and all other limbs. And regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "The Patriarchs are the Chariot."
They did not say "each one of the Patriarchs is the Chariot," but "the Patriarchs" [together]. <margin>Isaac</margin> How so? Abraham our father, peace be upon him, took for his attribute the "right eye" and inherited the "Right Hand" of above,
which is the attribute of Kindness <note>original: "חסד" (Chesed)</note>. Regarding this, it is said: "And Abraham journeyed, going on still toward the South" <note>Genesis 12:9; South/Right represents Chesed</note>. And Isaac took as his attribute the "left side," which is Fear <note>original: "פחד" (Pachad); also called Gevurah/Strength</note>. Regarding this, it is said: "And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac" <note>Genesis 31:53</note>. And Jacob took the holy attribute of the middle line, and regarding this it is said: "Jacob was a simple man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>—between the tent of Abraham and the tent of
Isaac. Thus, the three Patriarchs are the throne for the Chariot. And so it is found in the Recanati <note>Menahem Recanati, 14th-century commentator</note> on the portion of *Vayechi*, and it is also brought in the book *The Service of Holiness*. However, the matter
requires us to be informed about the ways of the Creator and the words of the Sages of Truth <note>the Kabbalists</note> who speak of the matter of Emanation <note>original: "אצילות" (Atzilut)</note> using substantial terms, so to speak, such as Father and Mother, Son and Daughter, and things like
them. And they speak regarding the attribute of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> and Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note> using the language of "union" <note>zivug</note>, like a man with his wife, and the connection is the "Covenant of the Awakening" <note>a euphemism for the sexual organ/circumcision site</note>, the limb of special usage for complete unity,
"and a man shall cleave to his wife" <note>Genesis 2:24</note>. And the term "standing" <note>kima</note> is used for the foundation <note>Yesod</note>... <margin>Happy is</margin> "from my flesh I shall see God" <note>Job 19:26; a key prooftext for Kabbalists that human anatomy reveals divine truths</note>.
And he correctly mentioned the matter of hugging and kissing, also hinted at in the verse: "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me" <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>, and it is written: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth."
We must know and contemplate such things. And here I will copy the words of the *Orchard* <note>original: "פרדס" (Pardes Rimmonim) by Moses Cordovero, 1548</note> regarding what he wrote in the "Gate of Titles." He said that these <margin>words</margin>
are attributes of a hidden matter—sight and hearing are not attainable. There is no doubt that the eye was not called an "eye" and the ear an "ear" and the mouth a "mouth" in our Holy Tongue by chance
or deficiency or by convention like other languages. The proof of this is that our language is called the "Holy Tongue," and He certainly desired it to be a Divine invention and not like other
languages. There is no doubt that it is the language the Holy One, Blessed be He, invented when He invented His world, or certainly it preceded the world.
Furthermore, he said: when the light of Abraham shone, the Holy One, Blessed be He, divided the seventy nations to seventy princes and seventy languages, but He chose us, and speech became our portion—His "young bird," a holy bird, and the Holy Tongue and
Divine wisdom. Regarding the ear being called an "ear" and the mouth being called a "mouth," this is because of the wisdoms that are a "shadow over my head" <note>Psalm 140:8</note>; the limb is emanated from the supernal power that emanates
upon it. And now, according to the truth, the intention of "ear" is not the physical ear, but the action performed through the ear by the power of the flow emanating upon it. Regarding this power it is said:
"He who planted the ear, shall He not hear? He who formed the eye, shall He not see?" <note>Psalm 94:9</note>. Another explanation: after He created man, it was through the cycle of the holy Alphabet <note>original: "גלגל האלפ"א בי"ת" (Galgal Ha-Aleph-Bet)</note> that draws flow from the
supernal root-powers that are behind the root of Israel. Necessarily, within that [Hebrew] letter there is the power of the action performed by the limb so named. And so it is in the root that flows into that letter, and so on, higher and higher to the top. For from the actions, the powers are known. Since sight and hearing exist in them, there must be in the Root-Source a power of
hearing and a power of sight—not physical sight and hearing, but a spiritual thing. It is like people who, when they hear the sound of a word in their ears, examine
the matter they heard; so too the supernal power that receives that sound—by examining whether it is worthy to be received or not—this is called "Ear." Regarding this it is said: "For the ear tests words" <note>Job 34:3</note>. The same applies to angels, who do not have physical power like our mouths with which to speak this speech which is physical. Rather, when an angel looks at an angel, they understand
one another... <note>original: "ורז"ל בעצמות נרתיקי' " (The Sages, of blessed memory, [spoke] of the essence of the "cases" or "containers")</note> the letters that represent the desired matter; and when I recognize the desired thing, that is their speech. They do not have
eyes like the eyes of men with which they see; rather, they have a spiritual function that performs "seeing." Thus he understands and gazes even from afar, and it is more praiseworthy
than our sight, as the sight of the intellect is superior to the eye. For the eye sees only what is before it—and not even everything before it, but only physical things that the animalistic intellect
can contemplate. But the [pure] intellect sees even what is not before the eye, just as a person sees in his mind many things he saw years ago, or even things
he never saw, and similar things in his mind... so that the sight of the intellect is so fine that it sees subtle matters that the eye cannot behold.
From this you can understand the sight of the prophets, for prophecy is attained in the intellect through spiritual perception. According to the breadth of the intellect, so is the breadth of the attainment. Thus King Solomon said: "As water reflects a face, so does the heart of
man reflect man" <note>Proverbs 27:19</note>, for people understand themselves from within. Even though the heart is a physical limb, it has wisdom according to the flow of the soul that rests upon it. So too the intellect. Even so, <margin>man</margin>
because he is a distinguished thing, his attainment is limited according to the level of the prophet in the degrees of prophecy. From this matter we can ascend to the understanding of angels
of one another, and from there many more levels to knowing the existence of "seeing" and the functions that reside in the spiritual. Just as the prophet says, "I saw, and behold, a golden menorah" <note>Zechariah 4:2</note>,
and just as formerly in Israel a prophet was called a "Seer" <note>1 Samuel 9:9</note>—this was not a matter of physical limbs, nor was the term "seeing" merely a metaphor, but it is truly "seeing." So is the matter
above: "seeing" among the angels is that attainment. Matters differ in all these ways, and "seeing" exists in the upper beings, and the upper among the upper, until the Might
above, the High One who watches. This is not surprising, for even in these physical vessels within us, an "eye" is not called such because of the physical eye, but because of the "sight" which is truly called
the "eye." Likewise, a "hand" is not called a "hand" because of the bone, but the action extending from the hand is what is truly called a "hand." The proof for this is what our Sages said in the tractate *Gittin*, chapter *Ha-Megeresh*:
"Do 'hands' that are not explicit count as 'hands' or not?" <note>a legal debate about shorthand or ambiguous language in a bill of divorce</note>. This refers to the matter of "taking." Thus Rashi explained: "hands" are a handle for a thing, to take hold of it and to say
that it was done through it. So too regarding marriage and divorce: "A minor girl has no 'hand' [legal capacity], but a man has a 'hand'." The intention is not that she lacks a physical hand made of bone, but that she lacks the power and the capacity to receive
marriage or divorce. So too the common idiom: "The matter has 'feet'" <note>it has a leg to stand on/it is plausible</note> or "his foot," and "I am an old man, is it better for one who has 'feet' or one who has no 'feet'?" It is a metaphor—just as
the feet are the standing and support of a man, so when a matter has a basis and an existence necessitated by the intellect, it is said to have "feet." And when the matter <margin>that the feet are</margin>
is not settled, it is said to have no "feet." Likewise, that which is written in the Torah, "a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot... a hand for a burn," etc. <note>Exodus 21:24-25</note>, and from the power of complete examination, "a soul for a soul."
It is as if the tradition [says] that the intention is not that for one who cuts off a hand, his own hand should be cut off, and so for other things; rather, the intention is the value of the limb <note>Rabbinic law interprets "eye for an eye" as monetary compensation for the value of the organ</note>. And so for the other limbs—it is called "hand,"
"foot," and "eye" because it is an equivalence of the power of the eye, hand, and foot. So are these matters in the spiritual: the power that searches and seeks to oversee the world from the power of the Infinite <note>Ein Sof</note> is called
"Eyes." Thus, "These seven are the eyes of the Lord, which range through the whole earth" <note>Zechariah 4:10</note>. The Kabbalists explain that these are seven powers, and they are called "Oraphni," "Al-Tagar," "Al-Palmiya," "Amato," and "Paskal-Boel" <note>names of specific angels or divine forces</note>.
These are the ones who oversee the affairs of men. Because they have the power of oversight, they are called "Eyes"—not that they are physical eyes, but they have spiritual oversight as I explained above.
Through them, they testify to the inclinations of a man's deeds and his small actions, a man's thoughts and his schemes, and they bring those matters up and testify to them before the Judges.

<summary>This page presents a Kabbalistic defense of anthropomorphism, arguing that human limbs are physical "signposts" or "thrones" for spiritual realities. It cites major mystical texts to explain that the Hebrew language and the human form are divinely designed to reflect the inner workings of the Sephirot and the angelic realms.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the human form as a reflection of the Divine structure. While the previous page focused on the creation of man from the "dust of the Sanctuary" and the four corners of the world, this page moves into the philosophical and kabbalistic justification for using physical terms (like hands, eyes, and feet) to describe the incorporeal Creator.</meta>

### A Faithful House ###

He explained all the attributes and said that they are borrowed names <note>original: "שמות מושאלים"; metaphorical terms used to describe God</note> applied to the Blessed Name. He explained each and every attribute and the reason it is applied to the Blessed Name with great taste and wisdom according to the way of 
<margin>the literal meaning.</margin> However, the Rabbi, the Kabbalist, author of the work *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Meir ibn Gabbai (1480–1540), a significant Kabbalist in Turkey and Egypt</note>, in the section on "The Purpose," responded to him and explained them according to the Secret <note>original: "הסוד"; the mystical or kabbalistic interpretation</note>—to what purpose they are borrowed. And do I not have the book *Sha'arei 
<margin>Ora* <note>original: "שערי אורה" (Gates of Light) by Joseph Gikatilla, a fundamental text explaining the ten Sefirot (divine emanations) through their various names</note>?</margin> Know that the truth of the Creator's essence, may He be blessed, is not attainable by anyone else. Among all the heavenly hosts, none know His place, let alone His true essence. 
Do you not see what the heavenly angels say? "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note>—wherever that place may be. If it is so for those above, how much more so for those below! If so, what is the meaning of all those matters we read in the Torah, such as "hand," "foot," "ears," and all other such things? Know and believe that although all those matters point to and testify to His greatness and truth, no creature can truly know or contemplate the nature of that thing called "hand" or "foot" and the like. Even though we are made "in the image and likeness" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>, let it not enter your mind that an Eye is in the shape of an eye or a Hand in the shape of a hand. Rather, they are inner matters—innermost of the innermost—within the true existence of the Blessed Name, from which the source and the flow <note>term: "שפע" (Shefa) — the divine influence or energy that sustains the universe</note> emerge to all existing things. But the nature of the [Divine] Hand is not like the nature of a [human] hand, nor is it a similar structure, as it is written: "To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" <note>Isaiah 40:25</note>. 
Know and understand: there is no likeness in terms of essence or form. Rather, the intent is that the form of the limbs within us are made as "symbols" <note>original: "סימנים"; markers or placeholders</note> for essential, celestial matters that the mind cannot know. They are like the written memory of one who writes "Reuven son of Jacob." Surely these letters and this shape are not the actual person of Reuven son of Jacob—not his form, his structure, or his essence. Rather, they are a reminder that this is Reuven son of Jacob. The writing is a sign corresponding to that known essence and structure called Reuven son of Jacob. And because the Blessed and Exalted Name wished to grant us merit, He created in the human body many hidden and revealed limbs as a symbolic likeness to the "Work of the Chariot" <note>term: "מעשה מרכבה" (Ma'aseh Merkavah) — the earliest form of Jewish mysticism involving the vision of the Divine Throne-Chariot</note>. If a person merits to purify one of his limbs, that limb becomes like a "throne" for that inner celestial thing called by that name—if an eye, then an eye; if a hand, then a hand; and so with all the rest. For example, if a person is careful and guards the sight of his eyes so that he does not look at or gaze upon something forbidden <note>original: "דבר ערוה"; literally "nakedness," referring to sexual immorality</note> or anything shameful, but only at things that are holy to the Lord and His service, then that eye becomes like a throne for the thing called "Eye" above. The same applies to the hand, the foot, and all other limbs. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "The Patriarchs, they are the Chariot" <note>Genesis Rabbah 82:4</note>. And why did they say each of the Patriarchs is the Chariot? Specifically the Patriarchs? 
Because Abraham our father, peace be upon him, took in purity the "Right Eye" and the "Right Arm" of above, which is the attribute of Kindness <note>term: "חסד" (Hesed) — the Sefirah of mercy and expansive love</note>. Concerning this it is said, "And Abraham journeyed, going and journeying toward the South" <note>Genesis 12:9; the South represents the right side/Hesed</note>. And Isaac took in purity the attribute of the Left side, which is "Dread" <note>term: "פחד" (Pachad) — another name for the Sefirah of Gevurah (Strength/Judgment)</note>, as it is said, "And Jacob swore by the Dread of his father Isaac" <note>Genesis 31:53</note>. And Jacob took in purity the "Middle Line," and concerning this it is said, "And Jacob was a simple man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>—between the tent of Abraham and the tent of Isaac. Thus, the three Patriarchs were a throne for the Chariot. This is also found in Rekanati <note>Menahem Rekanati, 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note> on the portion of *Vayechi*, and it is also brought in the book *Avodat HaKodesh*. 
<margin>However, the matter</margin> requires us to make known the words of the Zohar and the words of the Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> who speak concerning the "Emanation" <note>term: "אצילות" (Atzilut) — the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, where the Sefirot manifest</note> using essential descriptions with nicknames like "Father and Mother," "Son and Daughter," and the like. They speak regarding the "Tiferet" <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> and "Malchut" <note>Kingship/Kingdom</note> using the language of "union" <note>term: "זיווג" (Zivug) — the mystical union of divine attributes</note> like a man with his wife, and "connection" through the "Covenant of the Member" <note>circumcision/the procreative organ</note>, which is the organ of intimacy designated for complete unity, "and a man shall cleave to his wife" <note>Genesis 2:24</note>. The difficulty <unclear>...</unclear> is the foundation of the Covenant of Circumcision. And they mentioned the language of "arising." 
<margin>As it were, "From my flesh I shall behold</margin> God" <note>Job 19:26; a prooftext used by Kabbalists to show that human anatomy mirrors divine structures</note>. And he mentioned <unclear>...</unclear> the matter of hugging and kissing, "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me" <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>, and it is written, "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>. 
<margin>Such things we need</margin> to know and understand. Behold, I shall copy the words of the *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* (Orchard of Pomegranates) by Moses Cordovero (1522–1570)</note>, what he wrote on this in the "Gate of Values and Nicknames." He said that these things are attributes of a hidden matter, not of physical touch, sight, or hearing. There is no doubt that the eye was not called "eye," nor the ear "ear," nor the mouth "mouth" in our Holy Tongue by way of accident, deficiency, or by mere convention like other languages. The proof for this is that our language is called the "Holy Tongue," and it was desired and seen that its source is Divine, unlike other languages. There is no doubt that it is the language the Holy One, Blessed be He, invented when He brought His world into existence, or surely it preceded the world. 
He further said: When the light of Abraham shone, the Holy One, Blessed be He, divided seventy nations to seventy princes with seventy languages, but He chose us, and speech was our portion—for He is "His portion," a holy lot. The Holy Tongue is Divine wisdom. Regarding the ear being called *Ozen* and the mouth called *Peh*, it is according to the wisdom of their names <unclear>...</unclear> the limb is emanated from the celestial power that emanates upon it. 
Now, according to the truth, the intent of "ear" is not the physical ear, but rather the action performed through the ear by the power of the flow that is influenced upon it. Concerning this power it is said, "He who plants the ear, shall He not hear? He who forms the eye, shall He not see?" <note>Psalms 94:9</note>. Another explanation: When He created man, it was through the cycle of the holy Alphabet, which draws flow from the root of the roots. It is necessary that in the letter <unclear>...</unclear> there is the power of the actor and the one acted upon through the limb so named. And so too in the root that flows into the ear, and so on, higher and higher, to the very top. For from the action, the powers are startled. And since sight and hearing are within them, it is alive and present when God desires the power of hearing and the power of sight—not physical sight or hearing, but rather a spiritual thing. 
It is a parable: just as when people hear the sound of something in their ears, they examine the matter they have heard, so too the celestial power receives that sound; by examining it, [it determines] whether it is appropriate to receive it or not—this is called an "ear." Regarding this it is said, "For the ear tests words" <note>Job 34:3</note>. This is also the case with the angels, who have no physical power like our mouth with which they speak this physical speech. Rather, when an angel looks at another angel, they understand one another, for they sharpen within their essential creations the letters required for the desired matter, and his companion understands the thing desired by him—and this is their "speech." They do not have eyes like human eyes with which they see; rather, they have the spiritual [version] of the action <unclear>...</unclear> thus they contemplate and see even from afar. This is more praiseworthy than our sight, just as intellectual sight is more praiseworthy than the eye. For the eye only sees what is in front of it—and not even everything in front of it, but only something physical that the physical mind can limit. But the intellect sees even what is not in front of the eye, just as a person sees in his intellect many things he saw years ago, or even things he never saw at all, by imagining in his mind that they were thus. Thus, the sight of the intellect is subtle, seeing subtle matters that the eye cannot behold. Upon this rises the sight of the Prophets, for the Prophet attains spiritual matters through the intellect. According to the breadth of the intellect, so is the breadth of attainment. Thus King Solomon, peace be upon him, said: "As face reflects face, so the heart of 
<margin>man</margin> to man" <note>Proverbs 27:19</note>. For man gazes from his essence to the essence [of another]. Though it is a physical limb, it has a connection to the matter of the flow of the soul that rests upon it, and so too the intellect. Even so, because it is a <note>unclear/lower?</note> thing, its attainment will be <note>unclear/lower?</note>. According to the level of the Prophet, there will be levels in prophecies. 
Similarly, from this matter we ascend to the understanding of the angels with one another. From there, we attain many, many levels to know the existence of sight and physical actions within spiritual ones. As the Prophet says, "I saw, and behold, a golden menorah" <note>Zechariah 4:2</note>. Formerly in Israel, a Prophet was called a "Seer" <note>1 Samuel 9:9</note>. The matter is not the sight of limbs, nor is the language of "sight" merely a parable; rather, it is truly "sight." This is how it is above—sight among the angels. That attainment through which they grasp matters is called "sight" in the upper worlds, from the highest to the "Power over the high that watches" <note>Ecclesiastes 5:7</note>. 
This is not an error, for even in these physical vessels within us, an "eye" is not called an eye because of the physical eye itself, but because of the sight, which is truly called "eye." Likewise, a "hand" is not called a hand because of the bone, but because of the action that extends from the hand—that is truly called a "hand." The proof for this is what our Sages said in the Talmud, Tractate *Gittin*, in the chapter "The Giver of a Divorce": "Hands that do not prove their purpose—are they 'hands' or not?" <note>Gittin 85b; "Hands" here refers to legal agency or the handle of a document—the power of grasping/taking</note>. That is, regarding the act of taking. Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "Hands" are a "place for grasping" a thing to hold it. And so too regarding betrothal and divorce: "A minor girl has no 'hand,' but a grown man has a 'hand.'" The intent is not that she lacks a physical hand, but that she lacks the legal power of "reception" <note>original: "כוח הקבלה"</note> to receive betrothal or divorce. 
Similarly, we find in the language of our Sages: "There are 'feet' to the matter" <note>original: "רגלים לדבר"; meaning there is a basis or evidence for the claim</note> or "it has no 'feet'." The intent is not whether it has physical feet, but a parable: just as 
<margin>the feet are</margin> the standing and support of a person, so too when a matter has a "dwelling" and an existence necessitated by the intellect, it is said that "it has feet." When the matter is not settled, it is said to "have no feet." 
Likewise, what is written in the Torah: "Hand for hand, foot for foot... creature for creature..." <note>Exodus 21:24</note> and regarding an animal "he shall pay for it, soul for soul." Tradition has come to teach that the intent is not that one who cuts off a hand should have his own hand cut off, but rather the liability of the full value of the hand. And so with the other limbs. It is called "hand," "foot," and "eye" because it is the equivalent of the power of the eye, hand, and foot. 
So too in spiritual matters: the power which searches for ways to attain [knowledge] of the world through human power is called "Eyes." Similarly, "Those seven are the eyes of the Lord, which range" <note>Zechariah 4:10</note>. The Kabbalists explained that these are seven powers called "Ophanim" <note>term: "אופנים" — a class of angels</note> <unclear>...</unclear> who oversee the affairs of men. Because they have the power of Providence <note>term: "השגחה" (Hashgacha) — Divine supervision/Providence</note>, they are called "eyes." It is not that they are literal eyes, but that they possess spiritual providence in the way explained above. Through them, they testify to the inclinations of a man's deeds, and concerning him [it is said], "the steps of a man are from the Lord." They ascend with those matters and testify to them before the Judges when...

<header>A Faithful House</header>
<sig>20</sig>
<meta>catchword: Certainly</meta>

<margin>The matter of the Throne of Glory, as explained by Maimonides</margin>
<margin>12 Tribes etc. This is the meaning of "thrones for the House of David"</margin>
It is appropriate that what emanates from Him should be found within Him, and vice-versa, and that actions are revealed through the aforementioned intermediaries. Thus, we can illustrate it through the metaphor of "emanation" <term>Atzilus: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divine light</term>, or "spreading out," or a "radiating spark"—calling it whatever we please—to show that He revealed the truth of His essence to His creatures. This divine power is attributed and described through these ten intermediaries which emerged into action, step by step, from emanation to emanation, from the perspective of the created beings, even though the entire process was beyond time and without division. In any case, its existence is established, and the Kabbalists received it and organized the Order of Emanation for us. They called them *Sephirot* <note>The word *Sephirot* shares a root with 'sapphire' (brightness) and 'cipher' (number/telling)</note> after their purity and clarity, derived from the phrase "like a brickwork of sapphire." Just as forms are seen through a sapphire stone, so too are the Sephirot the mold and form of all existing things. They are not an addition to His essence; just as objects seen through a sapphire do not add anything to the stone itself.

The sage Rabbi Azriel <note>Azriel of Gerona, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note> said that the Sephirot are a power equal to all things. The change lies in the appearance of physical things within the sapphire-like medium; similarly, the hidden existences in the depths of the "Nothingness" <term>Ayin: the Infinite God prior to self-manifestation</term> are revealed through them and elevated by them. They do not represent an addition or multiplicity in the Master, unlike our own human attributes. Just as all things are revealed and elevated in a sapphire-like object to the eye of the one looking through it without adding multiplicity to the stone, so it was permitted to describe the Blessed One with these qualities.

They said that when God wished to make His truth known and to create the world, a power of His lights sparked forth upon the creation. His relationship to it is like "Thought"—as a prophet might use a metaphor—like one who thinks and contemplates his building at the moment of its beginning. They called this **Keter Elyon** (Supreme Crown) because it crowns everything. Then, the "point of the letter *Yod*" from the Essential Name was revealed, and that light sparked into 620 sparks <note>original: "ת"ר"; the numerical value (gematria) of the word Keter is 620</note>. This did not stop from the Crown until a spark of **Chochmah** (Wisdom) sparked from it in stages, revealing the "thickness of the *Yod*," which also sparked into 32 sparks, called the "32 Paths of Wisdom." 

The power of these radiating sparks did not cease until the power of Wisdom also emanated into a level of a spark they called **Binah** (Understanding). From the effect of these sparks, 50 were formed, called the "50 Gates of Understanding," and the letter *Heh* was revealed. Similarly, from Understanding, a power sparked and emanated called **Chesed** (Kindness) <margin>72 Names</margin>, affecting 72 sparks... <note>The text here details the derivation of the 72-letter Name of God from the verses in Exodus 14</note>. And from Kindness came **Pachad** (Fear/Strength) <margin>The 42-letter Name</margin> with 42 sparks, called the well-known "42-letter Name" derived from the letters between the words *Bereishit* and *Bohu*. From this, **Tiferet** (Beauty) sparked into seventy, called the "70 Branches of the Tree." These are included in the seven [lower Sephirot]... and the Name in its cycle is 12 and in its combination is 72... This corresponds to the 12-letter Name derived from the verse "The Lord reigns, the Lord has reigned, the Lord will reign forever and ever" <note>original: "ה' מלך ה' מלך ה' ימלוך לעולם ועד"</note>... and from Beauty emerged **Netzach** (Victory), and from the Conqueror emerged **Hod** (Splendor), and from Splendor came **Yesod** (Foundation). Afterward emerged the power that binds all powers and guides everything, which they called **Malchut** (Sovereignty/Kingdom), and the final letter *Heh* of the Name was revealed. These are the words of the Ramai <note>likely referring to Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai</note> at the beginning, though he elaborated much further. The conclusion of all this is that there is some resemblance between the soul in the body and the secret of Emanation in the Emanator.

->**You**, children of my command: after God has made this known, let us vow to understand the depth of the matter—what we mean when we speak of the "ascents of the Great Man" <note>Adam Kadmon, the primordial spiritual man</note> as it is written:<-
->The verse: "And upon the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man." Then you will understand the matter of "Let us make man in our image." Your hearts will burn with love for God, to cleave<-
->to Him and to be a "branch of the Patriarchs," of whom our Sages said: "The Patriarchs, they are the Chariot."<-

### A Faithful House

<margin>A matter regarding Governance</margin>
Among the constant things in the ways of our Torah are phrases like "And under His feet," "Written with the finger of God," "The Hand of the Lord," "The eyes of the Lord," "The ears of the Lord," and similar words which are descriptions of a body. Such things do not apply to the Creator, for He is not a body nor a power within a body. Therefore, these physical matters do not apply even to His Sephirot; they are far removed from any physical depiction. Our Sages said that He is the "Soul to His Sephirot," and He is a power in His Wisdom... Heaven forbid [one should think otherwise]. Therefore, it is proper to distance the Sephirot from the limitations of the body, thinking of them instead as the power of Divine Governance from the essence of the Infinite (Ein Sof).

Not only are they far from physical limits, but even from the essence of an angel... <note>Reference to the *Shir ha-Yichud* (Song of Unity) or similar liturgical poems</note>. It means He has no physical likeness, nor even the likeness of something non-physical like an angel.

<margin>It is of four kinds</margin>
If so, we must contemplate the attributes mentioned regarding the Creator and what they intend. According to the "Plain Meaning" <term>Pshat</term>, some attributes are explained based on what is written in the book *Arugat HaBosem* <note>The Garden-Bed of Spices, a work on grammar and theology</note>. We find a division of actions into four kinds: 
1. An action intended for its own sake.
2. An action intended for a metaphorical use.
3. An action intended to publicize its subject.
4. An action that appears to be an action but is actually only the revelation of the actor's state.

The first kind includes phrases like "they left the city" or "every wise-hearted person did," where the action is literal to the one doing it. 
The second kind is illustrated by "He conceived mischief and brought forth iniquity" <note>Psalm 7:14</note>, where "conception" is a metaphor for thought and "birth" for deed. <margin>Type 1</margin> Similarly, "Look" and "Behold" are applied to His providence, and "Traveling" to His remaining in a specific place. From this comes "the smoke of God's nose" and "His anger flared," which according to the Kabbalists refers to the awakening of Judgment. Similarly, "Speech," "Saying," and the "Voice of God" are metaphors for the attainment of prophecy, for they descend from hidden sources through the levels to the ears of the prophets. "Saying" and "Speaking" are also applied to Will and Thought, as in "My soul said," and thus "And God said: Let there be light"—meaning He said it in His "heart." <margin>Type 2</margin> The "Call" is a metaphor for the flow of influence, as in "Deep calls unto deep," which the Targum translates as "one receives from another." The Sages' statement "From where do we know that the Holy One wears Tefillin?" is a metaphor for God being unified in His attributes to influence according to the awakening of those below when they wear Tefillin. Such metaphors are numerous... like the interpretation of "Let him kiss me" <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note> as "He shall provide for me, purify me, and make me cleave." 

<margin>Type 3</margin> The third kind is illustrated by "King Ahasuerus magnified [Haman]," meaning he publicized his greatness. Similarly, Isaac "grew very great," meaning his actions publicized his greatness so that people said, "The dung of Isaac's mules is better than the gold of others." This is the meaning of "God tested Abraham"—He publicized the matter of the trial so everyone would recognize his devotion. Similarly, "Now I know that you fear God"—meaning, I have publicized it to the world. Other examples include "Magnify the Lord with me," "Exalt His name," and "I am the Lord who sanctifies you." All of these refer to the publicity of the matter. The Sages' phrase "My children have defeated Me" means: they have publicized that I am Eternal (*Netzchi*) and unchanging.

<margin>Type 4</margin> The fourth kind is like the time from dawn until the stars come out. Even during the day, the stars radiate their light, but the sun's light prevents the eye from seeing them. By the setting of the sun, the light of the stars is revealed, and they appear as if they are "coming out." This explains "I am going out into the midst of Egypt"—through the plague of the firstborn, which was the test between a firstborn drop of seed and a non-firstborn, it seemed as if God was "going out" in Egypt. Similarly, "The Lord descended upon Mount Sinai," even though the whole earth is full of His glory. It means that through the great visions at that chosen stand, it appeared as if the Divine Presence descended there. This also applies to "Let me go down and see," "And the Lord went," "And behold, the Lord stood over him," and "Now I will arise, says the Lord." These do not mean moving from place to place, but the revelation of His light through something in one place that was hidden in another. This is also what the Sages meant by "The Holy One does nothing until He looks at the Heavenly Entourage"—it means that when we are worthy of reward or punishment through the levels of heavenly intermediaries, it appears as if He is contemplating and consulting them. This is also found in the *Guide for the Perplexed*, Part One.

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic process of divine emanation through the Sephirot and provides a rationalist/mystical framework for understanding biblical anthropomorphisms as metaphors for divine action and publicity.</summary>

The judgment is the end of all judgment; the "end of thought" was "first in thought." <note>This is a play on the philosophical and liturgical phrase "the end of action was first in thought," suggesting that the ultimate purpose of creation (judgment/refinement) was the original divine intent.</note> This means that because the likeness of the "end"—as the "end" takes from every side and corner—is a complete conclusion, you should know that the operation of death and the "miserable one" mentioned in their place is the intent of our youth, stemming from hidden individual forces that are not perceptible to the eye. All of them are from us, and even from hidden offspring, they are removed from the iron <note>original: miborzel</note> to receive them. Lack, missing, kindness, muzzling... <note>The author is likely playing with the phonetic roots of the Hebrew words for 'missing' (chaser) and 'kindness' (chesed)</note> the height of the refuse to the tender treasure. Therefore, the Torah was necessary to return the rest of the wise men. Also, the Roman reward <note>likely referring to Edom/Western philosophy</note> for the pleasant Divine Presence <note>term: Shekhinah</note> and its elevation. Through this, the action of the Angel of Death is voided and the repair of the "Name of the King" is awakened as explained. This is not known except through the revealed path. Thus, the reward of the spiritual ones is not a difficulty, for in the matter of spiritual purity of the soul, the soul can ascend to the level of the "Divine Chariot" <note>term: Ma’aseh Merkavah — the highest form of Jewish mysticism involving the vision of the divine throne</note>, for when it acts, it is outside to take shelter under the wings of God in its place. If the soul is what includes the authority and the result of the inheritance, it causes it to cleave to the "Throne" more than the holy place. This is not something outside of nature, for the soul is spiritual and all-encompassing, and the nature of the all-encompassing is to be drawn toward the whole without anything intervening. It should be buried in the "Understanding" <note>Binah</note> which strengthens the sweetness of our intellect by removing the garment from upon it. But for the power of sweetness to prevail through this activity—this is not necessitated by nature, but only by the power of the Holy King. And this is the Law of the World Above.

...God and His unity. If so, just as the prophet [reveals] the will of the Divine Torah—the existence of God—by saying "I am the Lord your God," which was well-known or also [evident], he should have brought the "Immortality of the Soul" <note>term: Hash’arat HaNefesh — the concept that the soul survives physical death</note> as well. But this is nothing [of a challenge], for even if the existence of God and His unity were well-known in the time of Abraham, they were not well-known at the time of the giving of the Torah. Israel, having grown up in Egypt, needed to hear this from the mouth of the "Almighty" <note>original: HaGevurah</note> because the Egyptians were deniers of these two principles. As they said in the Midrash (Exodus Rabbah): "Pharaoh said to them: 'At first, you are telling a lie, for I am the master of the world and I created myself and the Nile,' as it is said: 'The Nile is mine, and I have made it for myself.'" <note>Ezekiel 29:3</note> However, as for the immortality of the soul, they did not slacken their hands from [believing in] it. Furthermore, I say that the immortality of the soul is indeed mentioned in the Torah in various passages, except that it was hidden to provide proof for it from what the senses testify regarding the cleaving a person has [to God] even while still joined to that which prevents it <note>the physical body</note>. This is a matter of immortality by "a fortiori" <note>original: Kal VaChomer — a logical argument from a minor premise to a major one</note> reasoning that has no rebuttal. Wisdom saw this as better for what would follow from it, as the Ran <note>Rabbi Nissim of Gerona, 14th-century philosopher</note> wrote. But regarding the existence of God and His unity, there was nothing else to provide proof, so the Torah had to bring it. This is why it decrees "I am [the Lord]" and "You shall not have [other gods]," to verify God's existence and unity. However, if they did not come for this but only to influence us to believe generally that there is a Torah from Heaven and not for any other god—as the Maharal <note>Rabbi Judah Loew of Prague</note> wrote in his sermons—then there is no place for his thoughts on God's existence and unity. In truth, the Torah did not need to bring this explicitly, for from what they saw in Egypt and at the Sea, it was verified to them that there is no power in Pharaoh, aside from what they received through the Patriarchs. This is the measure of what I have seen fit to bring on this matter according to the meager amount our smallness has grasped from these Sages and their opinions. After bringing their words, I saw fit to clarify for my part the truth in these two "rewards" according to the Torah and as they were inscribed by the Supernal Wisdom, whose way is to illuminate the path of truth before the seeker. Most of his words follow the Rabbi, the author of *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Meir ibn Gabbai’s "Service of the Holy," a foundational 16th-century Kabbalistic text</note>, who copied the opinion of the Sages in this inquiry. This Rabbi, the author of *Avodat HaKodesh*, knew why spiritual rewards were not mentioned in the Torah, as we will explain later. And now the time has come to inform you of what I am... and the three inquiries I mentioned shall join together: "And a threefold cord is not quickly broken." <note>Ecclesiastes 4:12</note>

### Know
That the holy letters and the words are all based on spiritual and true roots. The Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note> say: the **Letters** are from **Understanding** (*Binah*), the **Vowels** are from **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*), and the **Musical Accents** are from the **Crown** (*Keter*). To understand this matter, I will copy from the book *Pardes Rimonim* <note>The "Orchard of Pomegranates" by Moshe Cordovero</note>, the first chapter of the "Gate of Letters": "Many have thought that these letters are conventional—meaning that the Sages agreed to make signs for the sources of speech. For example, they agreed that the sound produced by the lips—the letters M, B, P—should be given the forms of the *Bet*, the *Vav*, the *Mem*, and the *Pe*. Similarly, for the other vowels and other languages, they have signs for all their combinations. Just as the mathematicians invented signs to include all numbers according to different levels... it would follow that there is no difference between these letters and the signs of the nations for their languages, except that these were agreed upon by the Nation of Israel through the counsel of Moses from his prophetic mouth, while those are the agreements of any fool who invented them. According to this view, there is no essence in the printed script itself, but only a disclosure of the speaker's intent. Like a wise physician who writes his wisdom in a medical book—his intent is not that the book itself should be the medicine, but rather his intent is to present his knowledge or his desire regarding healing. When a person understands the essence of the wisdom written in the book, the book itself no longer provides any benefit. Similarly, they said to their students: 'My children, do not trust in the skins of the animals...' <note>A warning not to focus only on the physical parchment but on the living wisdom within</note>... If one does not understand the study of wisdom, it will not help him at all and he will not perfect his soul... rather, it will take up his time and provide no benefit... But this is a [wrong] thought, for certainly the letters of the Torah 'restore the soul' <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. The proof is that we are obligated to study the Torah: 'two portions of Scripture and one of Translation' <note>term: Shnayim Mikra ve-Echad Targum — the traditional way of reviewing the weekly Torah portion</note>, and even the crowns and the decorations on the letters. This indicates the perfection of the Torah, and that it has an inner dimension, a hiddenness, a spirituality, a vitality, and a power..." as Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] explained in the portion *Beha'alotcha*. He wrote there regarding Torah scrolls: "One who learns them with the mind of one reading a book of chronicles—this certainly will not help in study... but when a person comes to study Torah, his intent must be that he is studying the matter through the power of these Divine names, even though the inner essence is hidden from him. Through this, it will be pleasing in all the Torah that comes from before the Holy One, blessed be He... And not only for one who understands, but even for one who does not understand at all because he is not fluent in the language or its explanation, but merely busies himself with the reading alone—he too has a good reward for his toil. About these and those like them, it is said: 'But his delight is in the Torah of the Lord, and in His Torah he meditates day and night' <note>Psalm 1:2</note>. The Sages expounded: it does not say 'in the Torah' but 'in *his* Torah'—according to the measure of his knowledge. For even one who does not know how to join the words, if he busies himself with it day and night, his reward is with him..." He wrote further in the second chapter of the "Gate of Letters" that the letters of the Torah are not conventional. Rather, they are primary and necessary forms corresponding to the inner soul within them. This is why the Sages were so meticulous even in the literal explanation regarding the form of the letters, their "thorns" <note>original: kotzim — the small strokes on letters</note>, their "crowns" <note>original: tagin</note>, and their beauty, for they allude to known spiritualities and supernal Sephirot. Every single letter has a spiritual form and a glorious light emanated from the essence of the Sephirot, cascading from level to level... and this script prepares and aims for those spiritualities...

which turned toward it and awakened it from its attachment to the body, for that immortality and delight—there is in its mention only a redundancy and a complete interpretation. This is because since you do not mention the spiritual life—which is the essence of the reward—why would you mention the physical promises, which are not the essence of the reward? According to the opinion of those who say that the spiritual reward is for the body and soul as one, it is not a natural thing for the body to endure in it. But he <note>the opponent</note> will not believe this, for the philosophers held otherwise and forced us to believe the opposite... to prevent truth and justice from those who follow their own bad reasoning. Among them is the wise Rabbi Joseph ben Shem Tov <note>A 15th-century Spanish philosopher and commentator</note>, of blessed memory, in his commentary on the *Principles of Faith*, second treatise, who says: "Even if we agree with Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman, a major medieval authority who argued for bodily resurrection</note> in everything he posited and conditioned... how does he know that the existence of that tranquility and life of pleasure follows the commandments of the Torah? For even if we agree that the soul is naturally immortal and does not undergo destruction like the body—because it is not mixed with it, but rather drawn through it in the bond of existence—nonetheless, we would not agree that it naturally remains in the delight and joy belonging to it. As our Sages said, 'Eye has not seen it' <note>Isaiah 64:3; a common reference to the hidden nature of the afterlife</note>. But the remaining in delight follows the commandment according to his opinion, even though it is the truth in itself. The existence of this success after the commandments is not 'natural' to a human being, and this is very clear." I have already written above that Maimonides knows the secret of the service, for its nature is to bring out success for the body... for it is the essence... and it will be clarified that the existence of eternal success follows the Torah commandments by nature. If it is not a "human intellectual nature," it is a "Divine intellectual nature." With this, the doubts regarding him will be removed.

## The Knowledge

The language leaves no doubt that the beliefs in those times... and the matter was handled according to the future of the soul after its separation from the body. They were distant from awakening it, because since they did not follow the truth, they could not give a close or tangible sign. When our Torah came among those beliefs... it awakened the truth of them which they were unable to verify. Just as the foundation of the Torah was the matter of the Exodus from Egypt—through which they saw that the Divine matter cleaves to us, something the philosophers <note>original: hermonim/hitzonim</note> could not do—they intended through the great counsel of the "Wise Son" that this matter is unique to our Torah and no other could claim it. Similarly, the intention regarding the reward of the soul after death appears, and our Torah is equal in this... for after our Torah, everyone would deny a non-tangible thing. Each [religion] would be able to teach and say that the truth is with them. For this reason, the Torah did not need to continue its promises regarding the matters of the World to Come, but rather continued stories about matters that prove its truth beyond doubt. The wise Rabbi Joseph responded to him in the second treatise of the book *Deep Inquiry* <note>original: Ein Hakoreh</note>, saying that the speech mentioned was not intended to promise these goods, but the omission of the true ultimate purpose is not a reason at all, for it should have been mentioned. I am surprised that he only took from the Rabbi's [Maimonides] language what he could use to cast doubt, but omitted what would save him from the doubt. For the Rabbi, at the beginning of this issue, says: "It is revealed, then, that the body and its powers do not give existence and permanence to the soul, but rather they hinder and weaken it, until it is proper that when the hinderance is removed, the soul will then live more perfectly. All the Torah's promises that came in physical matters are because if it is visible to the senses that a person has a connection to the Divine matter while he stands in a state that hinders him from achieving it—namely, the body—there is no doubt that the connection will be complete as much as possible when the disturber and hinderer is removed." If the Divine matter cleaves and rests upon him while he is alive in a state of hinderance, this is the greatest evidence and proof of his cleaving to Him when he leaves that hinderance. Since the cleaving in this life is a powerful indication of the spiritual reward, there was no need to mention it in the Torah, for it would be entirely redundant. And the wise Rabbi Abraham ben Bibago <note>A 15th-century Spanish-Jewish philosopher</note>, of blessed memory, in his book *The Path of Faith*, second treatise, fifth gate, wrote: "This answer is also insufficient, for if the immortality of the soul were famous then, it should have been famous to our father Abraham..."

<column-break/>

<margin>
The intention is that the service encompasses all... it will be founded on the Great Name in His Glory... how this foundation is drawn and emerges from the secret of the Torah. We know that the benefit for us is the foundation of the world through the power of service and the preparation of the "vessels" and the instruments... to hear His voice and to cleave to Him... he wrote in the aforementioned introduction... the foundation of the world is formed and its light corrected with His people... the merit of the matter of the foundation is from the side of the service. He said that he placed this world before them... and the intention of the holy heart is to speak in the way of truth. Even though they merited the matter of the sacrifices and the service... I turned to see this world to support the Supernal Will... the secret of the decree and the secret of the finding... there is no action in this service without the instruments... the man will find it... he did not know what the action of God was from the beginning to the end. That is to say, man did not know and did not find the end through the foundation of the heart, which is the Great Name in His Glory... the foundation of the Name in His action in perfection... therefore he said "I knew that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good in his life." This does not mean to act in the lower realms, but to act in the supernal realms... the world upon their hearts in the place of intention. The matter is as it is in the "Good" and it is the foundation of the Name. These are the ones who fulfill the foundation... the correction of the Great Name in His Glory. This must be the "Right Side." He spoke of life according to the tradition received from our teachers... connected from above to below... and when we hear from below, we are heard above. But one who awakens the foundation of the Creator, male and female... this is the truth. Nevertheless, in this we understand the reason for the service... not like the awakening of the foundation of the Name... but we know that there is a secret in this matter. Most of the words are known, examine them carefully: "But the whole day he is a man of Judah..." this is a debt and this is a finding... and those who know their writing here will be able to understand the foundation of the Name... the foundation of the dust... and things will be clarified through examination. But in the thick of the matter... one should not fear their drawing near... and so for the soul of the person who moves from place to place, he is pressed... every hidden secret of the Name. This is called "The Benefit"... for the action of the commandments and their intention cause the foundation of the Name as the King in His Glory. When the Name is walked, then abundance is poured upon all the world... a spiritual rest and an internal rest... and perhaps through the hint of the verse "And You shall be my God," to be for the Name... man corrects the Great Name through action. This is the benefit, for the wine makes the matter mix... but He is the Truth... and close to this wrote the pious Rabbi in the book *The System of Divinity*: "I have found that Rabbi Azriel squeezed the Sephirot but for life..."
</margin>

also follows the Torah and its commandments by nature, and it is a *Kal V'Chomer* <note>term: Kal V'Chomer — an "all the more so" logical argument (a fortiori)</note>. If the Master of Reward, blessed be He, had explicitly promised the spiritual reward, it would be entirely redundant, since we can judge it through the *Kal V'Chomer* from the physical promises. Since the physical reward follows the commandments and their obligations by nature, we should not think poorly of the Rabbi [Maimonides]... but we judge the spiritual reward from the physical one. In mentioning the physical, the spiritual is also included, even more so what we have linked there in his saying "and his knot was untied as a whole." This is because since you do not mention the spiritual life—which is the essence of the reward—why would you mention the physical promises, which are not the essence of the reward? According to the opinion of those who say that the spiritual reward is for the body and soul as one, it is not a natural thing for the body to endure in it. This is the opinion of the Rabbi, and it is the truth. Such was the intention in the creation of the first Man, had he not sinned—and his sin brought death. When the world is renewed, it will return to its original nature, and after they live, both will stand together, for the intention will return to its place; therefore, there is no need to prove it. There is more length on this in the commentary on the *Midrash Rabbah*. But he will not believe this, for the philosophers held otherwise and forced us to believe the opposite... to prevent truth and justice from those who follow their own bad reasoning. Among them is the wise Rabbi Joseph ben Shem Tov in his commentary on the *Principles of Faith*, second treatise, who says: "Even if we agree with Nachmanides in everything he posited... how does he know that the existence of that tranquility and life of pleasure follows the commandments of the Torah? And if they are not a human intellectual nature, they are a Divine intellectual nature. With this, the doubts regarding him will be removed.

# House of Israel
Page 14 | Signature 4-B-2

The Master of Light and the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the **Lower Man** <note>Humanity</note>, placing within him signs reflecting the **Upper Man** <note>The divine structure or archetype</note> so that he might serve as a **Chariot** <term>Merkabah: a vehicle or throne for the Divine Presence</term> for the manifestation of His truth. There are matters and inner subjects, extremely subtle and spiritual, which are the "sections of the Chariot" from which light and abundance spread to sustain all existing things. He acts in His likeness. These are called "hands," "feet," "eyes," and "ears." This does not mean that He possesses a hand like a human hand or a form like a human form—God forbid! For it is written, *"To whom will you liken God?"* <note>Isaiah 40:18</note>. There is no comparison at all between Him and us in terms of essence or physical form. 

However, man was fashioned and made in this likeness to teach that if a person merits to purify one of their limbs and perfect it through the commandments associated with it, that limb becomes like a **Chariot** and a **Throne of Glory** for that supernal, inner reality called by that name—whether it be an "eye" for an eye, a "hand" for a hand, or a "foot" for a foot, and so with all other limbs. The Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> have a sign for this: they said, "A limb supports a limb." For the "Perfect Man"—the one who perfects himself for his Creator and is corrected in his deeds, his study of Torah, and the purity of his limbs—completes, corrects, and establishes all his limbs to resemble the structure of the **Great Man** <note>Adam Gadol: the cosmic divine structure</note>. Every limb perfected through its specific commandments becomes a reflection of that Supernal limb which was established in His likeness.

<margin>The intention here is the "Power of Planting" <note>original: koach ha-netiah</note>. Just as a plant draws from its root, the body draws from the soul's holiness. This is the secret of the soul.</margin>

# And This
was the wisdom of the **First Man** <note>Adam Ha-Rishon</note>, who called every thing by its name so that it might be recognized by that name. It is said that his level in this was even greater than the **Ministering Angels**. Through the **Holy Spirit** <note>Ruach Ha-Kodesh</note> that was upon him, he constructed specific letters and words based on the vitality, form, and essential root of the inner light within the lower world. This is the "Secret of the Upper Chariots." For every created being below has a root above; otherwise, how would the parts of this world be connected if the foundations had no root above? And if creatures had no root above, how would **Divine Providence** spread? Providence comes through these alignments. This is a wondrous wisdom, for he grasped the source and root of every thing and faced it with that specific name—and that is its true name.

# And in Truth
one might ask, based on a superficial reading of the path mentioned above, about the famous saying of our Sages: *"The Torah speaks in the language of man"* <note>original: dibra torah bi-lashon bnei adam</note>. This phrase is usually used to "appease the ear" <note>to explain away anthropomorphisms as mere metaphors</note>. However, the reality is the opposite: it is through God that the names are truly blessed, and the words in the "language of man" are actually used by us as "borrowed" terms. The explanation is this: The Torah speaks of His Divine attributes in human terms as if they were essentially human language, but in truth, they are not human language at all, but the **Holy Tongue** <note>Hebrew</note>. It was necessary to mention them in relation to man in another way, and to this they answered: "to appease the ear." 

I have another way to answer their statement, which is a wondrous hint. It is explained in the *Zohar* and expanded upon in the *Pardes* <note>referring to 'Pardes Rimonim' by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> regarding the subject of **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: the first of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divinity</term>. The **Infinite** <note>Ein Sof</note> emanated a structure referred to as the **Great Man**, as I have explained. This was "so that His Divinity might be known," for without this, it would be impossible to have any knowledge of Him at all due to His extreme hiddenness, which is the ultimate spirituality. He elevated Himself through a bit of revelation in His guidance and providence, which is the "Man who is close to Himself" <note>a play on the legal phrase 'a man is close to his own relative'</note>. When they said "The Torah speaks [in human language]," they meant that the very existence of this revelation was intended "to appease the ear" in the language of human beings, so they might understand and know His Divinity. Therefore, the **Emanation** was emanated—which is the "True Man"—and then the secret of His Divinity is revealed slightly through His guidance and providence, by the power of the "Cause of all Causes," to be known by man. The wise will understand.

# Behold
it is now explained why it is called the **Holy Tongue**, and the matter of the **Great Man** is clarified. *"Great is the Lord and much praised"* <note>Psalm 148:1</note>; He is the end of the Emanation that unites with the Essence of the **Infinite**, serving as the Soul within them. He hinted at the secret of Unity with the phrase common among the Sages: "A man is close to himself." Thus you have two aspects: he is close to himself, yet he is in another. So too, the **Upper Man** is close to His Essence and hidden, and all is one unique whole, *"like a flame bound to a coal."*

# And Then
the inquiry as to why spiritual matters are not mentioned explicitly in the Torah is also clarified. They *are* mentioned and mentioned again! They are mentioned essentially and not as borrowed metaphors. Take for example the first creation in the portion of *Bechukotai*: *"I will give your rains [Geshem] in their season."* The word *Geshem* <note>Rain/Physicality</note> is from the **Holy Tongue**. These "right-hand flows" that descend are not essentially named "rain" [Geshem]; rather, the power of influence that exists high above at its root is essentially called *Geshem*. Afterward, it descends and pierces through all the worlds, and is called "rain" by borrowing the term. It goes from level to level until it fulfills the verse, *"I will answer the heavens and they shall answer the earth,"* and these clouds are formed to water the earth, causing growth and bringing life to the world. The level above this is also called *Geshem*, and it is a more spiritual life, up to the highest heights where the name *Geshem* exists in its essence: the eternal spiritual vitality, which is the secret of the eternal delight of the **World to Come**. The same applies to all the promises in *Bechukotai*. Thus, it is clear that the spiritual reward is mentioned essentially, but while we are physical beings, the words appear to us as physical according to our current state. Everything is now well-explained. Examine it with your own knowledge, for He has led me on the path of truth. Blessed be the Giver of Knowledge.

### House of Israel
Grace comes both from the side of the soul and the side of the body's form. Regarding this it is said, *"Let us make man in our image [Tzelem] and after our likeness [Demut]."* The **Image** refers to the secret of the soul, and the **Likeness** to the secret of the body. The "Likeness" is revealed and supernal, as it says, *"from my flesh I shall behold God"* <note>Job 19:26</note>. The "Image" is the secret of the hidden soul. This is also said regarding the secret of the **Great Man** upon the Throne: *"the likeness of a man"* appearing from above. The secret of **Primordial Man** <term>Adam Kadmon: the first spiritual realm</term> is in **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>, where the limbs of man are hidden. Afterward, in **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, it is written *"like the beauty of a man to dwell in a house,"* for there he is revealed in his six directions. He is His likeness, uniting in absolute unity, for he is nothing but the revelation of the Hidden. This "Man" is male and female, and their name is "Adam"—that is, the qualities of Beauty and Sovereignty <note>Tiferet and Malkhut</note>. A hint to this: **Adam** [אדם] is the secret of the name **Y-V-D-V** <note>Yod-Vav-Dalet-Vav, a variant of the Tetragrammaton</note> in its full spelling. The "filling" of Adam is his wife, who was filled from him through the sign of "conception" <note>Ibur</note>. If you calculate the "filling" letters—Vav, Dalet, Aleph, Vav, Aleph—they equal the numerical value of **Eve** [Chavah]. Thus the lower reflects the upper; this is the matter of the Image and Likeness of man.

<margin>It is also possible that according to what the Tosafot wrote... the name "Adam" [Man] is used because there is no comparison, as it is written "To whom will you liken Me?"</margin>

...to the point that the **Ministering Angels** were mistaken by him and came to prostrate before him. Adam said to them: *"Come, let us bow down and kneel, let us bless the Lord our Maker,"* as seen in the Midrash. It is also found in the Midrash that "God cast a deep sleep": when the Holy One created the First Man, the angels were mistaken and sought to say "Holy" before him. This is like a king and a governor... and in the future, when the purpose of creation is fulfilled and man becomes like he was before he sinned (and even higher), our Sages said: "In the future, the righteous will have 'Holy' said before them just as it is said before the Holy One, Blessed be He." As it says, *"He who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy."* The essence of it all is that the cleaving [Dveikut] of man, when he is in his perfection, is a cleaving to the Name **Y-V-D-V**.

## And as I wrote above
the name **Y-V-D-V** is included in the letter **Yod**, and **Yod** is the letter **Aleph**. I have explained this regarding the "cleaving of the Torah." It is the same with man: from the side of his soul, it comes from the secret of the "two faces" <note>the male and female aspects of the divine</note>, and the secret of the "soul of the soul" comes from the secret of the **Yod** and its tip. The sign of this is "Life" [Chai], meaning the levels of *Chayah* and *Yechidah* <note>the two highest levels of the soul</note> from **Wisdom** and **Crown** <note>Chokhmah and Keter</note>. In truth, all is one, for the light of the soul is not divided except in relation to its recipient—just as with physical light, one person enjoys the light but cannot draw too close to its source, while another can. It all depends on the level of the recipient's understanding.

## And so
the form of this body reflects this. The body has the shape of the letters: the human body has a front and back, a right and left—this is the letter **Dalet** [ד], which corresponds to the four directions of the world. The head above the body is in the likeness of the **Yod** [י]. The legs below the body spread out like the letter **Vav** [ו]. Thus you have **Y-V-D-V**. These are the six directions: up, down, and the four directions. All is one body.

<margin>This also fits with what the Tosafot wrote in the chapter "How do we dance"... regarding the 14 days...</margin>
