<meta>This page continues the discussion on how physical forms reflect divine archetypes. While the previous page focused on the human body as a "Chariot" for the Divine, this page transitions into the mystical nature of the Hebrew alphabet and the concept of "Lashon HaKodesh" (the Holy Tongue), explaining that physical objects are merely "borrowed" names for higher spiritual realities.</meta>

# A Faithful House: The Temple and the House of Aaron

The spiritual awakening awakens, and all speech proceeds from it. The divine forms ascend and are bound to their root, which is the Root of **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divine light</term>. This applies not only to the spiritual realm but also to our reality—meaning that in the writing of the letters, a spiritual light dwells upon them. This is the reason for the holiness of a Torah Scroll. 

It is also the reason why the Sages said that the letters *Mem* and *Samekh* in the Tablets of the Covenant stood by a miracle <note>original: "מ"ם וסמ"ך שבלוחות בנס היו עומדים"; since these letters are closed loops, the centers would have fallen out if engraved through the stone</note>. This is because the spiritual reality sustains the physical. This also explains the breaking of the Tablets, which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained by saying that the letters "flew away." 

The Midrash states: "Moses looked at the Tablets and saw the writing upon them fly away. They then became heavy in his hands and fell and were broken." Furthermore, in the Jerusalem Talmud, Rabbi Azariah said in the name of Rabbi Yose: "The Tablets weighed nine **se’ah** <note>A biblical unit of volume</note>, but the writing supported them. Once the writing flew away, they became heavy, fell, and broke." So it is with everything: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, removes His **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah</term> from a thing, it can no longer endure.

This all relates to the spirituality of the letters. This is the reason for the different forms and crowns on the letters, even in their writing alone, and certainly in their reading and their meditative intention. The written letters are the "body" and "palace" for the letters spoken by the mouth. To use a parable: the written letters are the physical vessels, while those spoken by the mouth are the spiritual life-force. This is the meaning of the **Written Torah** and the **Oral Torah**. The Written Torah is spiritual in a high place and requires a "garment" to clothe its light in physical letters. However, the Oral Torah is itself the law and does not require such a thick garment at all. 

The written letters are the body and palace for the speech of the mouth, and that speech is physical compared to the thoughts in the heart. Those thoughts in the heart are the realm of Emanation, as explained in the *Pardes* <note>Moses Cordovero’s *Pardes Rimonim*, a foundational Kabbalistic text</note>. There is a spiritual grace to the letters, and one who perceives them will tremble before them.

The inner meaning of the letters and their hints are explained in *Sefer HaTemunah* <note>The Book of the Image, an early Kabbalistic work</note> and in the "Gate of Letters" in the *Pardes*. From there, the wise student will know that the joining of holy letters creates a "word," and the spiritual essence of that word is a great matter on high. Just as divine forms and Names are the secret of Emanation, and the Names are the expansion of vitality, so too are the "titles" and all the words of our **Holy Tongue** <term>Lashon HaKodesh: Hebrew</term>. Every word exists above. Everything that exists below in physicality is an expansion and a "chain-like descent" of the abundance from above.

<insert>
Furthermore, you find in the word **Ayin-Bet** <note>The number 72, referring to the 72-letter Name of God</note>, which is called "white light." You will find this in words like **Elohim**, which represents judgment. There is a "Face" and a "Back." Where the "Back" is shown, the flow of abundance is withheld, and this is called **Ra’av** <note>Hunger/Famine</note>. For the "back-part" numerical value of the Name is 272, which spells *Ra'av*. Conversely, the "Face" of the King is life and satiety. Each and every word has its own secret governances, as revealed in the secrets of *Sefer HaTemunah*.
</insert>

**Furthermore**, I say that the hand is called "our hand" because it reveals the attribute of Mercy. The hand has a measurement of 10 fingers, corresponding to the letter **Yod** <note>The 10th letter, often representing a point of divine energy</note>. There are many hidden crowns and mysteries on every stroke of the letters.

<column-break/>

<margin>
From our place, we begin with Genesis, Noah, Lech Lecha, etc. And afterwards, the names of the books like Joshua, Judges, Samuel, Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and all the rest. And afterwards, the names of the Six Orders of the Mishnah: Seeds, Festivals, Women, Damages, Holy Things, and Purities, with all their tractates and chapters. And afterwards, the names of the Midrashim of our Sages: Rabba, Tanchuma, Sifra, Sifrei, Mechilta, the Torat Kohanim, the Midrash on Psalms, Midrash Proverbs, the Yalkut, and many more. Also, the Midrashim that speak of traditions, laws, secrets, and corrections, the Zohar, the Bahir, and the works of the *Kannah* and *Binah*. Finally, one should bind their soul to these names and write them upon the tablet of their heart. One will thus merit the future world. I have seen distinguished people who, even if they cannot learn everything, read these names, and it is considered as if they had delved into and learned them all. I have written this according to my ability for our merit. May God hear and help us.
</margin>

...thousands upon thousands of descents until it becomes physical in this world. This thing we call by a name—that name is its true name above in its root. Our language is called the **Holy Tongue** because all names and words exist in their root in the place of Supernal Holiness. 

As the author of the *Pardes* wrote: when we speak of "Hands," they are only "borrowed" from the human hand <note>Meaning we use the human hand as a metaphor to understand a divine power, but the divine power is the "real" hand</note>. I say that the spiritual power of the human limb called a "hand" is not its essential name; the name is borrowed from the Supernal power. So it is with the "eye," which indicates the power of sight, and the "ear," which indicates the power of hearing. All names are borrowed: "hand for a hand," "eye for an eye," "foot for a foot." 

The language is holy. A "hand" is what it is called above in the Holy Place. Through the **chain-like descent** <term>Hishtalshelut: the process by which divine light evolves into material existence</term> through tens of thousands of levels, it eventually reaches the physical. This applies to the four elements: **Fire, Water, Air, and Earth**. The air and writing we see are descended from the **Supernal Chariot**: Kindness is Water, Strength is Fire, Beauty is Air, and Sovereignty is Earth. These words—Fire, Water, Air, Earth—are their essential names in the realm of Holiness. We only call the physical elements below by these names as a "borrowed" term. 

This descent continues through the classes of Angels: **Michael** is the foundation of Water, **Gabriel** is the foundation of Fire, **Uriel** is the foundation of Air, and **Raphael** is the foundation of Earth. Then it descends through the celestial spheres until it reaches the physical elements. In each stage of this descent, there are myriads of levels. Water beneath water, without end. 

For example, people in every generation are named Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. One named Abraham is named after his grandfather, who was named after his uncle, and so on, back to **Abraham our Forefather**, whose name was truly Abraham (meaning "Father of many nations"). All others named Abraham are "borrowed" names. 

**Thus**, we find that all descriptions used for the Blessed One—eye, ear, foot, hand—and even concepts like "union," "embrace," "kiss," "father and mother," "son and daughter"—all of these are the Holy Tongue. These are their essential names in the realm of Holiness. In the descent to the physical, these names are borrowed. It is understood that, on the contrary, all the limbs and parts of the Chariot are the "Upper Man," and the names of our own physical limbs are merely signs for what is above...

It also discusses the spiritual nature of the Hebrew letters, noting that they provide the life-force that sustains physical reality.</summary>

While the previous page discussed the physical world as a reflection of spiritual archetypes, this page delves into the moral and mystical purpose of creation, explaining why "suffering of love" exists and how the 613 commandments function as natural spiritual conduits rather than just arbitrary laws.</meta>

## House of Wisdom
<page-num>16</page-num>

...love. These are the trials that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings upon a person to refine them. Suffering that is not "of love" is that which consumes the wicked of the world. Regarding the war of Gog and Magog, it is written: *“I will magnify Myself and sanctify Myself, and I will make Myself known in the eyes of many nations; and they shall know that I am the Lord.”* <note>Ezekiel 38:23. The scribe uses the name "Yehuda" (Judah) as a substitution for the Tetragrammaton Y-H-V-H to avoid writing the holy Name in a common text.</note> Even in these events, the Name of the Lord is found, for evil consumes itself, and what follows is goodness for those who cling to the Lord, who are the ultimate purpose of creation.

I will first present the words of Rabbeinu Tam <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Meir (1100–1171), a leading French Tosafist and grandson of Rashi.</note> in his work *The Book of Uprightness* <note>original: *Sefer HaYashar*; a classic work of Jewish ethics</note> from the first gate: 

> "We should know and understand that the Creator did not create the world for the sake of the wicked or those who provoke Him, for reason would not mandate such a thing. Rather, He created it for the sake of the righteous who know His divinity and serve Him properly. His entire intention was to create the righteous; even the wicked were created through the natural power of creation. Just as a fruit has a shell, and the choice part is what is inside the shell, so too the righteous are the fruit of the world's creation, and the wicked are like the husks <term>Klipot: literally "shells" or "husks," representing the external forces of evil or concealment in Kabbalah</term>. We see that a sower intends to grow pure wheat, but the power of growth brings forth weeds with the wheat and thorns with the rose. So too, the Creator intended to create the righteous, but the power of creation brings forth the wicked alongside them." 

Thus, when the wicked fall, the inner part is consumed and the shell is cast away—this is the goal of creation. Then the inner essence remains pure, without dross or the mixture of the husk, entirely holy to the Lord. <image-desc>small circular floral ornament</image-desc> Then the truth of His Name is known, and the Lord alone is exalted. For "the Lord" <note>Hebrew: *Yehuda*</note> implies "Faithful," as I have explained. See also the Gaon’s explanation that it implies eternity—that which will never falter. This is the ultimate Truth. By clinging to Him, those worthy of eternity make the Lord known.

---

## Let us Return
to our subject. It is clear that the Torah and Israel are bound to the Holy One, Blessed be He, through the Name of the Lord. These are the three principles: the existence of God, the Torah from Heaven, and reward and punishment. 

Now we shall complete the explanation of the passage from the *Zohar*. Until now, we explained the first matter: the existence of the Blessed Name. His Name is famous, and it is evident that the Torah and Israel have a deep attachment to this Name. As mentioned above: "Three upon three." This means the Name is famous for God's existence—to which the Torah and Israel are bound; the Name is famous within the Torah—to which the Blessed One (as it were) and Israel are bound; and the Name is famous within Israel—to which the Blessed One and the Torah are bound. We will now explain the Name as it is revealed through the Torah:

## House of Wisdom
This refers to the 613 commandments. At the end of Tractate Makkot, Rabbi Simlai taught: "613 commandments were told to Moses—365 corresponding to the days of the solar year, and 248 corresponding to the limbs of the human body." Rav Hamnuna said: "What is the scriptural source? *'Moses commanded us the Torah as an inheritance.'* The numerical value <term>Gematria: a system where Hebrew letters represent numbers</term> of the word *Torah* is 611. The commandments *'I am the Lord'* and *'You shall have no other gods'* (the first two of the Ten Commandments) we heard directly from the mouth of the Almighty," <note>Totaling 613</note>.

Regarding the *Zohar’s* statement that "the Torah is both hidden and revealed," it does not merely come to tell us that the Torah has a plain meaning and a secret meaning. Even the common folk know that! Rather, this holy statement, which encompasses many matters, comes to teach us a new insight:

## And You
my children—may God protect and preserve you—hear these things. The 613 commandments that we were commanded in this world of action are given for us to perform and to be rewarded for. However, reward and punishment are not merely arbitrary "agreements" <note>meaning, a reward isn't just a gift given for a task; it is a natural spiritual result</note>. They are truly natural and spiritual, flowing from the essence of the deed itself. 

As we have learned: "The reward for a commandment is the commandment itself, and the recompense for a sin is the sin itself." The physical action of a commandment creates a spiritual reward. Look at what I wrote above: all the titles and words mentioned in the Torah have an essential root in the Holy Tongue. This means the Name exists in true holiness above, and only through a process of "chain-like descent" <term>Seder Hishtalshelut: the unfolding of spiritual worlds from the Infinite to the physical</term> is the physical object "borrowed" and called by that name. 

So it is with the performance of the commandments: there is no commandment, even a minor one, that does not have a great root above. That root is itself the reward where the soul clings. The opposite is true for sin (may God protect us), as the Sages of the Mishnah hinted: "Do not come into the hand of sin," for the sinner falls into the "hand" of the sin itself—which is the "husk" <term>Klipah</term>, the root of the sin. 

The Recanati <note>Rabbi Menahem Recanati (1250–1310), an early Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote at the beginning of the portion *Bechukotai*: 
> "*'If you walk in My statutes... I will give you your rains in their season.'* Know that the blessings and curses written in the Torah are not merely for the sake of reward and punishment; they are truly natural, like a sower who reaps. As it says, *'He who works his land will be satisfied with bread.'* The opposite is also true. For the Blessed Name, who is called 'Man' <note>referring to the divine anthropomorphic metaphor</note>, receives all types of abundance and emanation from the highest heights through the Great Name. Into Him flow the streams from the thirteen attributes of mercy, blessing the stream of Wisdom and Thought, the gates of Understanding, and the fifty bridges... all moving through the channels of 'Endurance' and 'Splendor' (*Netzach* and *Hod*) and uniting in the 'Well,' which is the Assembly of Israel. When all these flows are one—one God and His Name is one—peace is unified, and the entire world is blessed. The 'pipes' of Judgment are diminished and the 'pipes' of Kindness are increased through the merit of the pious and the righteous of Israel."

He continues: 
> "This is why all the blessings in the Torah are natural. However, when people sin, the channels of Kindness are diminished and the channels of Judgment are increased. Even though the world is filled with pain and lack... the upper channels are completely blocked, and energy is drawn from the 'external' channels—the evil forces and 'bad waters.' Then follows the destruction of the land and harsh exiles. This is the matter of the Admonitions written in the Torah." 

In the portion *Tetzaveh*, he expands further: 
> "Do not let it enter your mind that the punishments in the Torah are like a master’s anger at his servant. It is not so. It is a truly natural thing. One who neglects a commandment of the Torah prevents the goodness that would have flowed through the heavenly blessing. It is like someone who doesn't sow and therefore doesn't reap, or someone who doesn't wear clothes and his body becomes cold. The nature of the fire is to warm, and the nature of the good is to do good and satisfy. So is the nature of every single commandment—to produce the goodness stated in it, or the punishment stated for its neglect."

Not all sins are equal. Some sins affect the "Inner Palace," such as idolatry, forbidden relations, or murder. Others affect the "Outside of the Palace," such as eating forbidden foods. This is why the righteous are called *Tzaddikim* (Just)—because they keep things in their proper place and order. 

The *Zohar* opens with Rabbi Shimon saying: "*'It is time to act for the Lord; they have made void Your Torah.'* What does 'It is time to act for the Lord' mean? It is because they made the Torah void. If the Torah is neglected below, the Name of God (as it were) cannot be properly established above." Rabbi Yehuda said: "'It is time to act for the Lord' means to repair and perfect everything." 

This is what the Sages meant when they said: "Whoever performs a commandment, I account it to him as if he *made* Me" (as it were). This is why the pious are called "men of action" <note>original: *Anshei Ma’aseh*</note>. The opposite is also true: "for he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord." The Sages said: "You should have been My helper." They also said: "As I live, says the Lord, you have given Me life." 

This is the secret: "Listen, my son, and be wise." When Rabbi Ishmael blessed the Lord, he drew the flow of goodness from the Infinite. This is why "the blessing of an ordinary person should not be light in your eyes," for a covenant is made with the lips. 

Once we know that we have the power to repair the upper and lower worlds and to sanctify the Name of Heaven above—or, heaven forbid, to cause a "blemish" in the holy realms—we must clarify the path by which we cling to the Unique Name. When a person purifies his limbs and aligns them with the intention of creation, a spiritual counterpart of that limb is added from above, clinging to the Blessed One. As it says: *"A likeness as the appearance of a man upon it from above."* Study this and you will find that "limb supports limb." 

After clarifying these wisdoms—how to maintain the *Sefirot* (Divine emanations) through pure thought and action—the Blessed One, out of His great love for His children and the people of His faith, gave us the secret of the form of the Ten Sefirot in His Torah. He further explained that every *Sefirah* has a "repair," a form, and a way of connecting and "kissing" the neighboring *Sefirah*, until they all join as one, forming one singular Image. 

According to the depth of this perception, the entire Torah was given to us perfectly—from "In the beginning" until "in the eyes of all Israel." Behold, all the letters of the Torah—their shapes, their connections, their separations, the deep letters that are extra or missing, large or small, open or closed—all of them represent the form of the *Sefirot*. One who performs a specific commandment (as it were) influences the power above in the Supernal Form through the paths of the forms of thought. Through the merit of those below, the upper realms are blessed, and the Great Name is blessed and increased with abundance from the depths of the Infinite. 

The soul then becomes crowned and ascends through the merit of service performed out of love. Regarding this, it is said: *"He said to me, You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified."* This means: because of you, I receive an increase and addition of emanation from the Source. In the *Midrash Yelamdenu*, our Sages said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: 'I am sanctified through you,' as it says: *'When he sees his children...'* and likewise, *'Israel, in whom I will be glorified.'* And you are sanctified through Me, as it says: *'And you shall be holy.'*" These are the words of the Recanati.

To complete the explanation of this hidden matter, I will copy from the book *Service of the Holy* <note>original: *Avodat HaKodesh* by Meir ibn Gabbai (1480–1540)</note>, Part 5 of the Section on Service: 
"We have already made known in many places—and this is the truth—that the nature of worship (which is Unification) is to open the Source and draw blessing from the 'Head of Thought' <note>the highest Sefirah</note> to its end, and from there it spreads to those below who caused it..."

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the mystical significance of the People of Israel and their connection to the Divine. Having previously established the righteous as the "fruit" or purpose of the world, the text now explores how the structure of the Hebrew name for "Israel" and the concept of "Man" (Adam) are encoded within the different kabbalistic expansions of the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter Name of God).</meta>

House of Aaron

<margin>As stated in the [Talmudic] commentary on Zechariah: "For there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast" (Zechariah 8:10), etc. End of quote.</margin>

Thus, the Torah is interpreted through the four "cleavings" in the Name of the Lord <note>original: יוד"ד (Yud-Daled-Daled); a common scribal substitution for the Tetragrammaton Y-H-V-H to avoid writing the holy Name in a mundane context. It literally sums to 18, the value of "Chai" (Life).</note>:

# And the Torah

is interpreted through the General and the Particular. By this, I mean to discuss the mystery of the "Singular Man." Indeed, the nation of Israel as a whole is called "Man" <note>Hebrew: *Adam*. Based on the Talmudic dictum "You are called Adam" (Yevamot 61a).</note>, and there is nothing in the General that is not also in the Particular. For the collective is a great "cleaving" to the Name of the Lord, as it is written: *“But you who did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day”* (Deuteronomy 4:4). Now, the four "fillings" <term>Miluim: a kabbalistic method of calculating the numerical value of a name by spelling out its individual letters</term> of the Name Y-H-V-H are well known: 72, 63, 45, and 52.

*   **72 (AV):** spelled YOD-VAV-DALET, HE-YOD, VAV-YOD-VAV, HE-YOD.
*   **63 (SAG):** spelled YOD-VAV-DALET, HE-YOD, VAV-ALEPH-VAV, HE-YOD.
*   **45 (MAH):** spelled YOD-VAV-DALET, HE-ALEPH, VAV-ALEPH-VAV, HE-ALEPH. This filling sums to the value of **ADAM** (Man/45).
*   **52 (BAN):** spelled YOD-VAV-DALET, HE-HE, VAV-ALEPH-VAV, HE-HE.

Blessed be He, who called His great Name upon us through the aspect of the Name **72**. This is the inheritance of Israel... to give them a world of 310 [worlds]. The gift of the world is represented by the seven elders, as it says, *“Gather unto Me seventy men of the elders of Israel”* (Numbers 11:16). The sign for this is "Dread" <note>Hebrew: *Pachad*. The text is playing with gematria and acronyms here.</note>. 

*“And they shall put My Name upon the children of Israel”* (Numbers 6:27). The Hebrew phrase "Upon the children" <note>original: *Al Bnei*</note> has the initials that equal **72**. Furthermore, there is a great hint: when the Name 72 is added to the value of **Israel** (541), it totals **613**, corresponding to the 613 commandments of the Torah.

Regarding the Name **63**, its filling contains the mystery of *EL* (God), which is the "Seal of Israel" (*Yashar-El*—Straight to God). For "Your Name is within us" refers to what I explained above: His Name is in his midst... the middle letters of the name Israel sum to 72, hinting at the filling of the Name of the Lord.

Next is the aspect of the Name **45**, which equals **ADAM**, and **“Israel is called Adam.”** Also, the filling of Name 45 represents "One," for Israel is called "One," as we say in the prayers: *“You are One and Your Name is One, and who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?”* (from the Shabbat afternoon prayer). This is the meaning of the verse *“For the Lord will not forsake His people for His great Name’s sake”* (1 Samuel 12:22). When the Assembly of Israel connects to the Holy One, Blessed be He, in Unity, they rise to the value of the Great Name.

For He, may He be blessed, chooses His people Israel with Love (*Ahavah*). The word for **Love** equals **One** (13). The love of Israel for the Holy One begins when he is a "Son of One"—meaning thirteen years old, when he enters the covenant to fulfill the Torah. In response, the Holy One awakens the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. 

This is the aspect of **BAN** (52/Son). Israel are beloved, as they are called "Sons to the Place [God]." There is a mystery here: the Holy One said to the prophet Ezekiel: *“And you, Son of Man”* (*Ben Adam*). He always called him "Son of Man" and not just "Man," because the status of prophets rises and falls with the status of Israel. As the Sages said: "Did I give you greatness for any reason other than for the sake of Israel?"

Israel in their essence are called **Adam**, after the mystery of the "Image and Likeness" of the Supernal Man. However, one who finds refuge in the shadow of the branching "limbs" is called **Son of Man** (*Ben Adam*). This is the secret of the "Sons of Abraham," as he is called the "Father of a Multitude." We, the seed of Israel, are called by the name of Abraham... for Abraham is called "The Great Man," and Israel is called "Man" (Name 45). The mystery of the "Son" (Name 52) is the "Son of Man."

## Let us return
to our original words. Israel is known by the sign "Israel the Elder" <term>Israel Saba: a kabbalistic term for a specific level of Divine intellect</term>, corresponding to the attribute of **Beauty** (*Tiferet*). "Man" includes both male and female. The Name of the Lord is within His holy "H" <note>The letter Heh (ה)</note>, for it is the Name *Adonai* (Lord/Master) that dwells within the Tetragrammaton. The Name *Adonai* is the source of Israel, the vessel that receives the souls of Israel that flow from Beauty (*Tiferet*) to Sovereignty (*Malchut*). Just as the Name *Adonai* represents this, so too the House of Israel. Of them, it is said: *“For you are the fewest of all peoples”* (Deuteronomy 7:7). As Rashi explains, the "fewest" (the letter Heh/5) refers to the fact that Israel is only five families <note>This refers to a specific midrashic count of the families of Israel</note> compared to the seventy nations. There is also a mystery that the world was created with the letter "Heh" for the sake of Israel.

## And a hint
from our Sages of blessed memory: The initials of the Ten Sefirot—**K**eter (Crown), **Ch**ochmah (Wisdom), **B**inah (Understanding), **G**edulah (Greatness/Kindness), **G**evurah (Might), **T**iferet (Beauty), **N**etzach (Eternity), **H**od (Splendor), **Y**esod (Foundation), **M**alchut (Sovereignty)—sum to the numerical value of **Israel** (541). This is the meaning of "And the Lord is at their head," for "their head" <note>original: *Rosham*</note> also equals Israel.

The Rama MiFano <note>Rabbi Menachem Azariah da Fano (1548–1620), an Italian kabbalist</note> wrote in *Kefelach HaRimon* that the thought of Israel preceded everything... Rabbi Simeon taught that there are three crowns designated for Israel: the Priesthood, the Kingship, and the Torah. We are led by the Chosen Nation—the Prince (*Nasi*), the Deputy (*Sagan*), and the Head of the Court (*Av Beit Din*). Below them are three flocks: the singers of the Priesthood (lovers and pursuers of peace), the officers of the army who rule over the people, and the Sanhedrin who sit on the seats of judgment. All of them have their eyes and hearts toward the "Crown of a Good Name"—the Community of Jacob, which is the "Mother" of them all. End of quote.

*   The **Prince** (*Nasi*) is the **Crown** (*Keter*).
*   **Wisdom** (*Chochmah*) is the mystery of the "Great Offering" which has no fixed measure.
*   The "King of the World" is **Understanding** (*Binah*).
*   The **Deputy**, the **Second-in-Command**, and the **Head of the Court** correspond to **Kindness**, **Might**, and **Beauty**.
*   The army officers and the **Sanhedrin** are the branches of the Patriarchs, the "sons," which are **Eternity**, **Splendor**, and **Foundation**.
*   The **Crown of a Good Name** is the Community of Israel.

## Thus
the mystery of "Man" and the mystery of "Israel being called Man" are established. The General and the Particular are all within the secret of the Name of the Lord. The purpose of creation was a voluntary act of His great goodness, to do good for others so they might recognize His divinity and then cleave to Him eternally. This is the ultimate hoped-for reward. Punishment was not the primary intent; rather, it exists for the sake of the reward, so that "they shall fear before Him." Then, "according to the effort is the reward."

This is also hinted at in the Name of the Lord (Y-H-V-H). As Rashi explains at the beginning of the portion *Va’era*: "I am the Lord—faithful to pay reward to those who walk before Me in truth." It was not for nothing that I sent you to fulfill the words I spoke to the Patriarchs. We find this interpreted in many places: "I am the Lord" is faithful to exact punishment when said in the context of a transgression (like desecrating God's Name), and faithful to pay a good reward when said in the context of a commandment. 

Rashi later quotes Rabbi Baruch bar Eliezer: When the Holy One verifies His words, even for punishment, He makes it known that His Name is the Lord, and all the more so when He speaks for the sake of good. 

One might ask: Is not the Name Y-H-V-H associated with the Attribute of Mercy, and the Name *Elohim* with the Attribute of Judgment? How then can we say the Lord (Y-H-V-H) is faithful to punish? The matter is as I explained: the punishment is for the sake of the reward, for the "evil" is a cause for the "good." This is the meaning of "The Lord is God" (*Hashem Hu HaElokim*). This was told to Moses: "You complain that I have done evil to this people... know that I am the Lord." Even the Attribute of Judgment (*Elohim*) is for the sake of Mercy (*Y-H-V-H*). Just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you. Know that there are two types of suffering...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the spiritual mechanics of the Torah and the soul. Having established the expansion of the Divine Name in the previous page, the author now addresses why the performance of commandments leads to physical and spiritual rewards, arguing that these benefits are not merely "prizes" promised by God, but the natural, "biological" consequences of spiritual labor.</meta>

### House of Wisdom

That those good things fall upon the guardians of the Torah, we say that this was indeed because He promised them, and He is faithful to His covenant and stands by His word. However, it is not simply that the nature of maintaining the Torah and the commandments necessitates this. Since we know with true faith that the maintenance of the Torah and commandments is naturally structured so that all those good things follow them, we say that what appears in the Torah regarding these matters is a narrative, a story, and a "revelation of the eyes." For that which is naturally destined to follow and come by the nature of things, a promise of it is redundant and unnecessary. And how would we know by what means the "benefactors" cause good and straighten their paths, and how much evil the "corrupters" and those who pervert them cause? 

King Solomon, peace be upon him, hinted at all we have said when he stated: *“He who tills his land shall be satisfied with bread, but he who follows vanities shall be satisfied with poverty”* (Proverbs 12:11). Behold, the owner of a field manures it, hoes it, and sows it; the rain grows and sprouts it, and the earth by its nature brings forth its produce. Thus, the worker "shall be satisfied with bread" because this is a natural and necessary consequence of his labor. One who does not work it will certainly "be satisfied with poverty," for what will he eat? He did not prepare his land nor acquire anything. This is why it says, "he who follows vanities shall be satisfied with poverty." 

The secret of the "daughter" in this allegory was made known to us through his wisdom: the "Worker of the Upper Land" <note>This refers to the *Shekhinah*, the Divine Presence, often symbolized as "Earth" or "Land" in Kabbalah.</note> is the secret of the final *He* [of the Tetragrammaton]. It is called so because it was emanated from the "Supernal Adam" <term>Adam Kadmon: The primary primordial spiritual realm</term>. This refers to the repair achieved through the engagement in Torah and commandments, comparable to sowing a field after manuring and hoeing—which is a metaphor for the proper intention <term>Kavanah: directed meditative focus</term> in divine service. 

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, Rabbi Eleazar opened: *“A locked garden is my sister, my bride...”* (Song of Songs 4:12). A "locked garden" refers to the Community of Israel. Rabbi Eleazar said: Just as this garden requires a person to hoe, water, and dig, so too does the Community of Israel, as it is written: *“For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts...”* (Isaiah 5:7). Thus, they are repaired and pruned. When it is repaired through this path, the Supreme Luminary gazes down and brings down the rain of light and blessing upon this "land," and she gives her harvest. The worker eats of the good because the nature of that obligation follows and is naturally necessitated by his work. This is the secret of: *“If you walk in My statutes... then I will give your rains in their season...”* (Leviticus 26:3-4). 

As mentioned above, "one who follows vanities" is one who did not complete the supernal repair, remembering only "emptiness wherein there is no water," and thus "he shall be satisfied with poverty." For the repair of the Might <note>Gevurah</note>, which is the engagement in Torah and the fulfillment of commandments, is the cause of all good and blessing. Without his effort, no good or blessing comes to the world, for one is dependent on the other. 

The prophet Isaiah, peace be upon him, said in prophecy: *“Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness; let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the Lord have created it”* (Isaiah 45:8). The secret of the "daughter" is "Drop down, ye heavens," acting in such a way that the Upper Heavens receive—according to the secret of *“And You shall hear in the Heavens”*—the flow of light and blessing from above, from the Supreme Source. The "skies" <note>Hebrew: *Shchakim*</note> receive from the Heavens and "pour down righteousness." 

In the Talmud (Chagigah 12b), it says: "We do not investigate the *Shchakim* (skies), where millstones grind manna for the righteous." These are the "Righteous One" <term>Tzadik: the sefira of Yesod</term> and "Righteousness" <term>Tzedek: the sefira of Malchut</term>, for they are called the Righteous ones. This is the secret of the Skies—they are the "disciples of the Lord" who understand, and upon them are carved the "pillars of marble" that channel the light they receive from the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds." From there, it spreads to the lower realms, as it says: "Let the earth open and bring forth salvation." By saying "and let righteousness spring up together," he hints at the cause of all this good coming from above to below. He says it is because of the "repair" <term>Tikkun: spiritual rectification</term> established by their service in the Torah and the fulfillment of commandments, as in the secret of *“And it shall be righteousness unto us...”* (Deuteronomy 6:25). He says that the "Righteousness"—which is the merit in that repair—will "spring up together" the light and the flow in the upper worlds, and the goodness and salvation in the lower worlds. This is why he says "together, I the Lord have created it"—meaning, I have fixed and ordered that system of repair, and the one who repairs using them will find stability. 

This is hinted at in nature, and the prophets hinted at it by saying: *“There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help, and in His excellency on the skies”* (Deuteronomy 33:26). In Midrash Bereshit Rabbah (Section 77): "There is none like God—and who is like God? Jeshurun, the most pleasant and praised among you." This means that those who complete the intention in the supernal repair through their service—which is the "Unification" <term>Yichud: the meditative act of unifying divine names</term>—they are "like God," in the secret of *“And he called him 'God,' the God of Israel”* (Genesis 33:20). In the Talmud (Megillah 18a): "Who called him God? The God of Israel." And in Bereshit Rabbah it says: "You are a god in the lower worlds, and I am a God in the upper worlds." 

He explained this by saying "who rideth upon the heaven in thy help." This is the secret of the Unification that they cause through their service; it is the "help" hinted at in the phrase "in thy help." This is the supernal repair, which is the "repair of the Glory." This is the "Excellency" (pride) that He prides Himself on through them, as in the secret of *“Ascribe ye strength unto God; His excellency is over Israel”* (Psalms 68:35). Through Israel below, He is "excellent" above. By saying "Skies," he hints that the result and necessity of the preparation and the excellency caused by the workers is that the Supreme Place opens for them and flows upon the Heavens. From them, the Skies receive—those that "grind manna for the righteous"—meaning He prepares for them pure and refined sustenance <note>The "Manna" represents spiritualized physical sustenance</note>, the secret of the Skies, and flows through them all the goodness and blessings received from above. For this is necessitated by the nature of the Service. 

This is what we sought to prove in this chapter, at any rate. This is from the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>The "Work of the Holy" by Meir ibn Gabbai, 16th century</note>; I have copied the most useful parts of the entire chapter that pertain to the matter I am engaged in, excluding many other excellent points that emerge.

### House of Wisdom

And in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: "Rashbi"</note>, peace be upon him, they said: *“And I will exalt Him”* <note>Exodus 15:2</note>—this means to include anyone who knows how to unify the Holy Name, for that is the true service of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Furthermore, it is written there: *“The Lord is near to all who call Him... to all who call Him in truth”* <note>Psalm 145:18</note>. What does “in truth” mean? As we have established: *“You will give truth to Jacob”* <note>Micah 7:20</note>; it refers to one who knows how to unify the Holy Name as is fitting, and this is the service of the Holy Name. And whoever knows how to unify the Holy Name establishes unity in the world, as it is written: *“And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?”* <note>2 Samuel 7:23</note>. Because of this, they established that any priest <note>Kohen</note> who does not know how to unify the Holy Name as is fitting, his service is not considered true service, for everything depends on his hand—the upper service and the lower service—and he requires a purity of heart and will so that the upper and lower beings may be blessed.

This matter is repeated in the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, in many places. The intention in all of this is to root us in what we have already explained many times: that the labor of the Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments draw down light and the abundance of blessing from the Source of Existence to the upper and lower worlds. This is the cause of all good things in this life, for their very nature necessitates this. The Torah is literally the Great Name itself. According to the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, we have learned that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called "Torah," and "there is no water but Torah," and "there is no Torah but the Holy One, Blessed be He." Therefore, the Great Name is the source of all goodness and success, as He is the Absolute Good Himself. It is fitting, then, that the Torah which was engraved from Him should draw all good to itself. This is because, through the Torah, one awakens its Source. This is what the Sages <note>original: "Racham"e," likely referring to 'our Rabbis of blessed memory'</note> hinted at when saying: *“The testimony of the Lord is faithful”* <note>Psalm 19:8</note>; one who merits it, merits all its wealth and happiness through the Great Name itself. As written in Chapter 3 of the first part of this book—it should be consulted there, for it is a wonder. Because this is so, all good things and successes are drawn to the Torah and are necessitated by it. For so the King established its nature, and so He obligated it according to the Source from which it was quarried. For it is proper that the nature of the Source be found in that which is quarried from it, as I wrote in that chapter with Divine help.

Through this, we will easily understand the blessings that come in the Torah to those who walk in the Torah of the Lord. The hidden secret in this is that all those good things are not by way of a King’s promise, who promises his servants a reward for their actions to give them this or that in exchange for their labor. For a good that comes through a promise implies that it is not naturally drawn from the work itself and is not necessitated by its nature. This would be a flaw and a great deficiency in the status of the "Service." However, when the good is drawn from the labor and necessitated by its nature, it demonstrates the praise and honor of the quality of that service and the One being served. Since our Torah is honored with an infinitely high status, and is the Torah and Law of God—for this reason, it is called "The Torah of the Lord"—and our service to our God is a true service, chosen above all others, therefore the Supreme Wisdom saw fit to imprint it and establish it in such a way that all goods and successes are drawn to it and necessitated by it with absolute necessity.

The sign and proof of this is that Great Voice which did not cease, in which all future blessings to be renewed in every generation were included (as will be explained in Chapter 23, Part 2). In it, reward and punishment were stated for every single matter. They did not come as a mere decree, but to make known that the reward is drawn from and necessitated by the commandment. This is the teaching of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: every single word and being is filled with all those reasons, and all those words are decrees of rewards and punishments, judgments and secrets, like a looking glass <note>original: "aspaklaria"</note>. Therefore, all the goods and successes mentioned in the Torah for those who keep it are only by way of "telling and narration." That is to say: from the performance of this Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments, all those goods will necessarily be drawn and necessitated. This is because the Torah is the true and correct key to opening the Source of all good and happiness, since they were engraved from that Source and this was placed in their nature. 

When that Source—which is Blessing—is activated, the abundance of light and blessing emanates and is drawn from the "Head of Thought" (which is the Source) until its end. When it reaches there, it necessarily spreads from there to the lower beings who serve, for the nature of the Service necessitates this. I have already written that the Holy Emanation <note>term: Atzilut, the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing the divine realm of sefirot</note> is the vessel for the necessity of abundance and blessing to the world. Without it, it is impossible in any way, except through His will. All worlds are blessed through it, and proper Service necessitates this. When the Service ascends with the proper intention, it awakens the abundance toward them. As the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says on this verse: *“Like the good oil upon the head”* <note>Psalm 133:2</note>: “What is the 'good oil'? This is the oil of the holy anointing that flows and comes forth from the Ancient Holy One <note>term: Atika Kadisha, the most hidden aspect of God</note>, which is found in that upper river that nourishes the children to light the lamps. That oil flows to the 'Head of the King' and anoints the preciousness of the Holy Beard, and from there it flows to all those precious garments in which the King is clothed. This is what is written: 'that goes down upon the opening of his robes'—literally upon his 'attributes' <note>note: a play on the word 'middot' which means both robes/measures and divine attributes/Sefirot</note>. These are the crowns of the King of Heaven. Come and see: all hidden things and all the freedom of the world do not descend to bless except through those holy crowns which are the Name of the Holy King. And the structure is such that it 'goes down upon his attributes'... as it says 'by the word <note>literally "mouth"</note> of Aaron and his sons,' so by the 'mouth' of His attributes it descends and flows to all the worlds, to provide blessings for all. And come and see: this 'good oil' is not prepared until the time that the service from below ascends and awakens it. This is what is written: *‘Oil and incense gladden the heart’* <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>—oil from above and incense from below, then there is joy for all.”

Behold, they have explained all that we required. They said "Oil and incense gladden the heart"—this is the "Heart of Heaven," regarding which it is written: *“And the Lord said to His heart.”* The oil descends from the Source to the Head, and the incense is the secret of the Service ascending from below, which is called and gathered there, and they gladden that Heart. From there, joy and light spread to all the lower beings. If it did not reach there first, it would be impossible for the lower beings to "eat" of the good, for from there comes the sustenance and livelihood for all worlds, in the secret of: *“The eyes of all look hopefully to You, and You give them their food in its time”* <note>Psalm 145:15</note>. In the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai they said: “Who is ‘its time’? This is the 'Time of the Righteous' <note>original: "Eto de-Tzadik"</note>, which is Metatron <note>note: the primary archangel in Kabbalistic literature, often acting as the celestial mediator</note>... for all look to this 'Time.' All lower beings are nourished from this, and we have established this secret: *‘The eyes of all look hopefully to You’*... come and see, at the time that this 'All' <note>term: Kol, usually referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note> provides for 'Time,' all the worlds are blessed together, and peace is found in the upper and lower realms.”

And in the midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben ha-Kana <note>The Bahir</note>, Rabbi Rahumai said: “If not for the righteous and pious in Israel who raise Him above all the world through their merits, the Heart would not be nourished, and the milk <note>or 'fatness'</note> would not nourish them.” I have already written this: their great Torah is the study of Torah and fulfillment of commandments. Because this was so, the blessings and all the good came in the Torah by way of "telling and narration" and not as a promise at all. It is like one who reveals and says: "When you perform the Torah and commandments, this good will necessarily be drawn and necessitated from them, for this is the nature of the Service." 

Since this is so and there is no doubt in it, one should not ask: "Why, just as He promised us physical good, did He not promise spiritual good?" or "Since you do not mention the spiritual reward which is the essence of the reward, why mention the physical reward which is not the essence?" For it did not come as a "promise" at all, but rather to reveal and tell what is necessarily drawn and necessitated by the nature of the Service—that all goods and successes follow the commandments by a Divine nature imprinted in them. By way of this revelation and narration, He explained by saying: *“If you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments and do them”* <note>Leviticus 26:3</note>. "If you walk in My statutes" refers to the labor of Torah; "and keep My commandments" is the fulfillment of the Mitzvot; "and do them" <note>Hebrew: va-asitem otam</note> is the "fixing" of the upper realms—the fixing of the Glory <note>term: Kavod, referring to the Shekhinah</note>—which is rectified through Torah labor and fulfillment of commandments. Afterward, He explains what is drawn and necessitated from this, saying: *“I will give you your rains in their season”* and the rest of the worldly goods, the victory over enemies, and being fruitful and multiplying. 

In the midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai they said: “It is written 'And you shall make them' <note>note: the Hebrew 'otam' can also be read as 'it' or 'me'</note>. If you strive to do them, to rectify the Holy Name as is fitting, all those blessings from above will be found with you in their proper rectifications... ‘And I will give your rains,’ etc. Each and every force will be upon you. And who are they? That very 'rectification' that you made, which is the Holy Name.” It is written: *“And they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do righteousness and justice.”* Since it says “keep the way of the Lord,” why add “to do righteousness and justice”? Rather, whoever keeps the path of the Torah, it is as if—as it were—he "makes" righteousness and justice, which is the Holy One, Blessed be He.

And the Kabbalistic Rabbi Joseph ben Gikatilla, of blessed memory, wrote in the book *Gates of Light* <note>Sha'arei Orah</note> regarding the attribute of Understanding <note>Binah</note> in these words: “Know and believe that the Sefirah of Binah and the Sefirah of Malchut are both aligned one with the other. When the attribute of Malchut is rectified by the rectification of Israel through the fulfillment of the Torah and commandments, then the Sefirah of Binah shines to pour out all kinds of abundance and blessing through the channels <note>original: "tsinnorot"</note> until the Sefirah of Malchut is blessed and filled. Then all the inhabitants of the world find themselves in quiet and tranquility, and the blessing is sent into all kinds of sustenance, and the blessing is found clinging to the earth. This is the secret of the order of all the blessings: ‘If you walk in My statutes... then I will give your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its produce,’ and the whole portion.” 

This is what I said: the "rectification of the Glory" is through the fulfillment of the Torah and commandments, and all those goods drawn from that rectification follow them. This good does not come by way of a promise, for the good and the comfort from that place—their nature is to be drawn down, and it depends on the Service. There is no place or need for a "promise" regarding it, except to reveal by way of narration that this follows and is necessitated by the thing naturally. This is the case with the fulfillment of the Torah and commandments, which are the essential key to the source of all goods, for they depend on them, and they will necessarily be drawn forth by that "opening" which is their fulfillment. If this wonder were not in the nature of performing the commandments, we would necessarily say that since there is no relationship between the fulfillment of commandments and those goods, and they are not drawn upon them by nature, yet we see...

# House of Wisdom

It is written that the word "Light" appears five times <note>In the first chapter of Genesis, the word "Light" (Ohr) appears five times</note>, corresponding to the Five Books of the Torah, as explained there. In Tractate Sanhedrin, in the chapter "He Who Selects," it is said: *“He has placed me in dark places, like those long dead”* <note>Lamentations 3:6</note>—Rabbi Jeremiah said: "This refers to the Babylonian Talmud." At first glance, this is very puzzling. For the Talmud is light and illuminates our eyes! <insert>And also</insert> the Torah is our life and the length of our days; why then call its students "those who are <insert>long</insert> dead"? <insert>Also</insert>, consider the Midrash of Rabbi Simon, who explains the "Light" mentioned at the beginning of the Torah as referring to the Five Books of the Torah. It is written there: *“And God separated”*—meaning He hid it away. How can "hiding" be attributed to the Holy One, Blessed be He? Rather, the matter is all one: it is the cause for the hiding of the light of <insert>man</insert>, namely the "garments of light" spelled with the letter *Aleph* <note>original: "Kotnot Ohr" (כתנות אור). In Midrashic tradition, Adam originally wore garments of light (Ohr/אור), but after the sin, these became garments of skin (Ohr/עור), which are physical and opaque</note>, which I have elaborated on elsewhere. This is the hiding of the light of the Torah.

The simple meaning and the interpretation of Rabbi Simon are one. It is explained from what was mentioned above that the Oral Torah is essentially the Holy Tongue and the secret of the "Whole." Its essence and its actions, which return to "working and guarding" <note>A reference to the Garden of Eden in Genesis 2:15</note>, were all part of the "Work of the Chariot" <note>Ma’aseh Merkavah; the highest form of Jewish mysticism involving the vision of the divine throne</note>. At that time, the Torah was entirely a clear light. Only when <insert>man</insert> became physicalized and the light was removed—the secret of the garments of light (with an *Aleph*) becoming garments of skin (with an *Ayin*, which also suggests "blindness")—and the Tree of Life was withdrawn, causing death, did the Torah likewise become physicalized into the "working and guarding" of physical commandments. Nevertheless, it remains like "apples of gold in settings of silver" <note>Proverbs 25:11; a metaphor for a deep truth hidden within a beautiful exterior</note>. Therefore, you will find within the Torah secrets and hints, as those who interpret the "marked verses" <note>original: "Dorshei Reshumot"; an ancient school of allegorical interpreters</note> say regarding the chapter of the Red Heifer: "The word *Parah* <note>Heifer</note> has the numerical value of 288, hinting at the levels of interpretation: <term>Pshat<gloss>Plain meaning</gloss></term>, <term>Drush<gloss>Homiletic interpretation</gloss></term>, <term>Remez<gloss>Hint/Allusion</gloss></term>, and <term>Sod<gloss>Secret/Mysticism</gloss></term>."

The "Secret" is the Hidden Light that is now concealed from us. According to the view that the light of the "garments of light" was withdrawn, that light is the very essence of the Holy Tongue. The "Hint" refers to the physical actions of the commandments, since it remains, as explained, a hint to the Oral Torah within the Written Torah—such as the questions "From where do we derive this?" or "From where are these words?" <note>Common phrases in the Talmud used to link oral laws back to biblical verses</note>. There is nothing that is not hinted at in the Torah "very clearly," it is only that our intellect has become darkened compared to what it should have been. If "the earth were full of the knowledge of the Lord," our hearts would not be turned to evil. The Written Torah is not understood except after great toil, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "The words of Torah only endure in one who kills himself over them," as it is said: *“This is the Torah: when a man dies in a tent”* <note>Numbers 19:14; interpreted homiletically to mean one must labor in the "tents" of study as if dying to the physical world</note>. For this reason, the Written Torah requires explanation and commentary, which is the Talmud. If not for the state of our hearts, the laws would be self-evident.

As our eyes have seen in the generations after the ancients: they possessed a clear intellect and understood deep matters without commentary. Later, people did not even understand the Holy Tongue... <unclear>calculating the turn of the darkness of the mind</unclear>. Therefore, if <insert>man</insert> had not sinned, and the intellect of his generation were pure, he would have understood the Written Torah, and it would have been very sweet, and he would have known everything without needing the Oral Torah. It was only because he sinned and removed the light, bringing death to the world, that he required toil and the Oral Torah as a commentary, and to "kill himself" over it. Eventually, the Oral Torah had to be written down. Thus it is explained: *“He has placed me in dark places, like those long dead”*—this is the Babylonian Talmud. This means that the darkness and death brought to the world caused this necessity. If the <insert>soul</insert> were in its original state and the light were to grow stronger—as it will be in the future—then the Torah would be light and joy to the heart, not darkness and self-sacrifice.

This is the secret of the "two lights." It has already been written in the book *Kol Bochim* <note>A commentary on Lamentations</note> that the letters of the word for "lights" (*Ma'orot*) can be rearranged to spell "Light" (*Ohr*) and "Death" (*Mavet*). This is the meaning of "He has placed me in dark places like those long dead"—that death was made from the "lights." The light became darkness, darkness and not light. Yet it is also fitting that "the Torah is light" <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>. Originally it was one Torah, but now there are two Torahs <note>The Written and the Oral</note>. This relates to the sixty thousand... those things which are oral may not be said in writing, and those which are written may not be said orally. The matter is like what is found in the chapter "The One Who Injures" regarding those excellent things that the schoolchildren interpreted using the alphabet. They said: "Make signs [mnemonics] for the interpretations in a book of usage so that you do not forget." Behold, the Oral Torah is "longer than the earth and wider than the sea," and it is impossible to remember it all. However, everything is hinted at in the Written Torah, and one who understands it thoroughly remembers everything, for there is a sign for everything in the Written Torah... The Oral Torah should not be written because the main thing is to remember it all, and the Written Torah serves as the "signs" for it.

But because of our sins, we have become darkened until the "House" <note>likely the Temple or spiritual clarity</note> was destroyed, and the need for commentary increased. This is the darkness that necessitated the Babylonian Talmud and its being written down. This is the matter of the Hidden Light in the Five Books of the Torah... and we use "Hints," though even this is with great difficulty, each person according to his level and how much he guards his soul regarding the words of Torah.

A great hint is mentioned regarding Moses our Teacher: *“And the Lord turned to see”* <note>Exodus 3:4</note>. Moses saw perfectly; he was the secret of the "Illuminating Mirror" <note>Aspaklaria ha-Me’irah; a prophetic clarity unique to Moses</note>, for the skin of his face shone with light. The face of Moses was like the face of the Sun, which is "the Torah is light." When God gave <insert>man</insert> the Written Torah, there was no darkness before him; he had a clear intellect full of knowledge and understood the Oral Torah on his own. This is the secret of "Hints" in the words of Torah. This is the meaning of the Sages' teaching: *“He gave to Moses like his bride”* <note>A pun on "Kechaloto" (when He finished) and "Kechallato" (like his bride)</note>. It was handed over to him, and he understood the Oral Torah on his own, as I have elaborated elsewhere regarding the secret of the "Cushite woman" that Moses took, which is the secret of the Oral Torah, the secret of the "Bride."

It is further explained in Midrash Rabbah at the end of the portion *Ki Tisa*: "Write for yourself"—the ministering angels began to say before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Master of the Universe, are You giving permission to Moses to write whatever he wishes to say to Israel?" I gave you the Torah, I am the one who wrote it and gave it to you. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: "Heaven forbid that Moses would do such a thing! And even if he did, he is faithful, as it is said: 'Not so My servant Moses; in all My house he is faithful.'" This is clear for our purposes. Therefore, the Torah is called "The Torah of God" and it is also called "The Torah of Moses." Because Moses understood it on his own and attained the Oral Torah, it is called by his name.

(Note: Do not err in my words to say that the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not tell Moses the Oral Torah, heaven forbid! And the Holy One, Blessed be He, explained it very well to him in its fullness, with its flavors, nuances, and traditions, with the explanation: "Thus and thus shall you say to Israel." This is the meaning of: *“This is the Torah: when a man dies in a tent”* and it is written *“And this is the Torah which Moses set.”* For the "Torah of Moses"—which is the Talmud that he attained and directed toward the Law—is the Torah that a man "kills himself" over due to the many debates and the "walls" of the logical structures. ## Let us return
to the matter: the Written Torah is "Secret" and "Hint." The Secret is a great thing, like the "Work of Creation." The Hint is a small thing, like the "discussions of Abaye and Rava" <note>4th-century Babylonian scholars whose debates form the core of the Talmud</note>. The matter is as explained: "twice Scripture and once Translation." The Land of Israel is the Holy Tongue, and there is the Secret and the Hint. They are like the "Hint" regarding the Oral Torah and do not sharpen themselves so much with the dialectic of Babylon. # House of Wisdom

The Supernal Man <note>original: "Adam Ha-Elyon," referring to the primordial spiritual structure of the divine emanations</note> and his root are comprised of 248 letters. These consist of 213 <note>original: "Shasa"v" - a numerical representation</note> plus 3, and 32 paths of Wisdom, totaling 248. The root of all these 248 letters is the "Name of 72" <note>A sacred divine name composed of 72 triplets of letters</note> and other combinations. There are two perspectives: when you count the words, there are 72; but when you count the individual letters, there are 210. This is the secret of the verse, *“And the Lord passed before his face and called”* <note>Exodus 34:6</note>. The Kabbalists explain the secret of "and He passed" <note>original: "Vayaavor" (ויעבר), which can be permuted to represent the numbers 72 and 210</note> as the beauty of Man, the Name of 72. The general rule is 72 and the detail is 210, and the root of the detail is the general rule, which is the secret of "Kindness" <note>original: "Chesed" (חסד), which has a numerical value of 72</note>. Afterward, the general total of the 248 "limbs" <note>original: "Evarim" (אברים)</note> is the secret of Man expanding as a light to the 45 lights <note>The "Name of 45" is a spelling of the divine name YHVH that equals the numerical value of "Adam" (Man)</note>. I have already mentioned the secret of the 44 <note>original: "M"D"</note>, which is the beauty of Man leaning toward kindness. If you add these sources together—72 and 45—and join them to the 248, the total is 365. This is hinted at in the communal sacrifices: *“Two flawless lambs a day as a continual offering”* <note>Numbers 28:3</note>. The author of the *Ba'al Ha-Turim* <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, a famous 14th-century commentator</note> wrote that the initials of "Two flawless lambs a day" <note>original: "Temimim Shenayim Le-Yom"</note> spell "Tashal" (730), because 730 is twice 365. They would offer lambs continually in the morning and evening, totaling 730 annually. It is well known that the Positive and Negative Commandments correspond to the attributes of Day and Night; it is hinted here that even the Positive Commandments contain the secret of the number 365.
