# House of Wisdom

...which is called "Repentance" <note>original: "Teshuvah"</note>, within which are included the ten emanations <term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes through which God interacts with the world</term> known as the "Ten Days of Repentance." These are the root and source from which the year descends <note>original: "karpi'" - a technical kabbalistic reference to the order of emanations</note>. Every single year, with all its 365 days, returns to its source and root through the power of "Understanding" <term>Binah: the third Sefirah, associated with the "Supernal Mother" and the power of return or repentance</term>. This is the secret of Repentance: it is the returning of a thing to its origin and root, where the days may rest and cease in peace, quiet, and tranquility. After these ten days of repentance within the realm of *Binah*—that is, after all the days of the year have returned to their source and found rest there—a new year is renewed and descends from its source in the secret of *Binah*. This new year begins after the Day of Atonement <note>original: "Yom Kippur"</note>. Because of this, during these ten days of *Binah*, a person is able to repair whatever they have distorted throughout the entire year. At the conclusion of these ten days is the tenth day, which gathers and includes all the days of the year along with the nine preceding days of repentance. This is the Day of Atonement, which is *Binah* itself along with the nine *Sefirot* of Repentance within it. The Day of Atonement hints at this; it is the "seal" and source for the entire year, a designated day of cessation and rest, in which all the worlds that descended from it rest and are quiet, according to the secret of "World, Year, and Soul" <note>A central triad in the *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient kabbalistic text, describing the dimensions of space, time, and consciousness</note>. Therefore, every person, before coming before the Great Source and the face of the Master, the Lord of Hosts, must repair what they have distorted during the ten days of repentance. If they have not yet repaired it, God forbid, they must at least repair it on the Day of Atonement, for it is the seal and source of everything. Each of these ten days is a source for the next, and the closer a day is to the Day of Atonement, the more inclusive and "source-like" it becomes, until the Day of Atonement itself stands as the "Source of all Sources." If one does not repair their ways even on the Day of Atonement, there is, God forbid, no further remedy, for after the Day of Atonement, a new year descends. That year is like a branch emerging from the source; how can one repair the root by working on the branch? Therefore, one must repair things within *Binah*, which is the Day of Atonement. This is the secret of the year: the 365 days of the solar year descend from *Binah*, from which "judgments are aroused," as she is the root of the Line of Justice. This is unified in the secret of "Beauty" <term>Tiferet: the central Sefirah, often associated with the Sun and the balance between Mercy and Justice</term>, which is called the "Sun" that leans toward "Kindness" <note>original: "Chesed"</note>. And everything is—

->according to the secret of the four unities and the Divine Faces<- <term>Partzufim: "Divine Faces," complex configurations of the Sefirot that represent different aspects of God's persona</term>

Now, regarding the commandments: there is a general positive commandment <note>original: "Mitzvat Aseh" or M"E</note> to link the study of Torah with action. Regarding "Positive Commandments within Negative Commandments," Rashi explains this in the portion of *Mishpatim*: *“And in all things that I have said unto you, take heed”* <note>Exodus 23:13</note>. This teaches that every "taking heed" <note>original: "shmirah"</note> in the Torah is a warning, functioning as a negative commandment <note>original: "Lo Ta'aseh" or L"T</note>. Conversely, "Negative Commandments within Positive Commandments" is seen in the verse *“to observe and to do all the words of this Torah”*; here, "observing" (the negative aspect) is included within "doing" (the positive aspect). A hint to this is found in the Sabbath commands *“Remember”* and *“Observe,”* which were spoken in a single divine utterance <note>The Talmud teaches that God spoke both versions of the Fourth Commandment—"Remember" (Exodus) and "Observe" (Deuteronomy)—simultaneously</note>, for "Remember" represents positive commandments and "Observe" represents negative ones. The book *Holy Service* <note>original: "Avodat HaKodesh," a 16th-century kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> states in Chapter 25: "Behold, the positive and negative commandments are one Torah. The positive commandments are weighty, emerging from the quality of 'Remember,' and they ascend. The negative commandments emerge from the quality of 'Observe,' the secret of Awe <note>original: "Yirah"</note>, which points toward the secret of punishments. The entire Torah exists within the quality of Awe, as it says, *'The Lord your God you shall fear,'* which is a positive commandment that includes all negative ones. For one who refrains from committing a sin is acting out of the fear of His Name." Similarly, the positive is included in the negative in the command *“Do not add to it and do not subtract from it.”* One who neglects a positive commandment is "subtracting," and is thus liable for punishment. Conversely, one who sits and does not commit a sin is worthy of reward. As the Sages said in the first chapter of *Kiddushin*: "If a person sits and does not commit a transgression, they are given a reward as if they performed a commandment," specifically when a temptation comes to hand and they are saved from it, as it is said, *“They also do no unrighteousness; they walk in His ways.”* King Solomon explained this secret when he said, *“The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.”* By saying "fear God," he hinted that the positive commandments include the negative. By saying "keep His commandments," he hinted that the negative include the positive. He said "this is the whole of man" because man includes them all: the 248 limbs correspond to the 248 positive commandments, and the 365 sinews <term>Gidim: can mean tendons, sinews, or veins; here referring to the mystical anatomy of the body</term> correspond to the 365 negative commandments. Man is composed of "matter" and "form"; therefore, the fulfillment of negative commandments is primarily in the mind, while positive commandments involve the physical matter as well. These two parts of the commandments are the totality of man, and if one part were missing, he would not be a "man."

I will now explain the secret of this matter—the inclusion of the positive in the negative and vice versa. How are the positive within the negative? Every commandment a person performs must be done with an "awakening of the heart," not just as a "commandment of men learned by rote," but with fresh focus <note>original: "parnastoka chadata" - likely a corruption of a Greek or Latin term for 'new provision' or 'fresh perspective'</note>. One should do it for the sake of Heaven even if the physical body resists it or if it goes against bodily desires. One must break their desire and fulfill the commandment with care and alacrity. A person should think in their heart when a positive commandment comes their way: "From the perspective of my physical nature and desire, I would not do this thing; I am doing it only because the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded me." Thus, by thinking that they would not do it of their own accord but only because of God's command, a "negative" (restraint) has preceded the "positive" (action). This is the principle of *“loving God with both your inclinations”* <note>The "Good Inclination" and the "Evil Inclination"</note>. One should think: "Regarding my Evil Inclination, I will perform this positive commandment to unify my Father in Heaven because He decreed it upon me." We find the opposite in the case of negative commandments. It was taught that Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel said: "A person should not say, 'I have no desire for pork.' Rather, one should say, 'I do desire it, but what can I do? My Father in Heaven has decreed against it!'" Thus, in both positive and negative commandments, the positive is included in the negative and the negative in the positive, for in both, one serves God with both the Good and Evil Inclinations. In a positive commandment, the Evil Inclination is "negated" as one conquers it to act. In a negative commandment, the Evil Inclination is "positive" in its desire, but one conquers it to remain in a state of "not doing." Thus, the negative commandment is also an "action"—the secret of self-conquest—and this is the "awakening of the heart." Through this, the statement at the end of the tractate *Makkot* is explained: "Whoever sits and does not commit a transgression is given a reward as if they performed a commandment." This refers to this specific intention, for the thought is joined to the deed. Regarding this it is said, *“They also do no unrighteousness; they walk in His ways,”* meaning even when one "does no unrighteousness" (fulfilling a negative commandment), they are "walking in His ways"—meaning they are performing an act of conquering the Evil Inclination when they say, "I desire it, but what can I do?" With this, a well-known concept from the *Zohar* and all books of Kabbalah is clarified: that the 248 positive commandments correspond to the 248 limbs and the 365 negative commandments correspond to the 365 sinews. In our Talmud, at the end of *Makkot*, Rabbi Shimlai says that the 365 negative commandments correspond to the days of the solar year. I have already hinted that the solar days come from *Binah*, from which judgments are aroused, and these are the "red sinews." However, this can also be understood rationally, close to the plain meaning. I learned this from the words of the Kabbalist, the Rema MiFano <note>Rabbi Menahem Azariah da Fano, a prominent 16th-century Italian Kabbalist</note>, who wrote in his book *The Ten Treatises*, quoting the Ibn Ezra, that there are 365 "pulsating" sinews and 365 "resting" sinews in man. The pulsating ones correspond to the days, and the resting ones correspond to the nights, in which things rest and cease. Likewise, in the 365 days of the solar year, there is day and night; though we say "a day," it specifically contains a day and a night. For one who fulfills the 365 negative commandments without the aforementioned "awakening"—meaning they simply "refrain from doing"—this corresponds to the 365 nights. However, one who fulfills the negative commandments through the "inclusion of the positive"—meaning with awakening and the mindset of "I would do it, but what can I do?"—this corresponds to the 365 days. Then, a light shines for them: *“The commandment is a lamp.”* According to this, the words of our Sages in the Talmud and the words of the *Zohar* are one and the same; in fact, the Talmud explains it even further. The 613 commandments always correspond to the stature of a man: 248 limbs and 365 sinews. The Talmud clarifies: do not say they only correspond to the 365 sinews called "nights" (passive refraining), but rather to the days of the sun—the 365 "pulsating" sinews, which correspond to the verse *“The voice of my beloved knocks, 'Open to me...'”* All the words of our Sages are truth, and their Torah is truth.

->And everything goes to one place for those who understand their words<-

Let us return to the secret of the Name *Elohim* <term>Elohim: A Name of God associated with Justice and the natural order</term>, and the secret of "Remember" and "Observe" being in one utterance, where positive and negative commandments are unified. The matter of unifying action and refraining all leads to one place, for "God has made one opposite the other." Action (positive) is the secret of the "Chariots of Holiness." Negative commandments are a "fence" against the "Husks" <note>original: "Kelipot" - forces of impurity or evil that block holiness</note>, so that nothing impure enters the Sanctuary. This is the secret of the Sages saying "these declare it unfit and these declare it fit," "these purify and these defile," "these acquit and these convict"—yet "both these and those are the words of the living God." For some lean toward Kindness <note>Chesed</note> and some toward Severity <note>Gevurah</note>, but all are a single unity. The book *Pardes Rimonim* <note>By Rabbi Moses Cordovero</note> states in the second chapter of the "Gate of Deciders" regarding the saying "both these and those are the words of the living God": the phrase "Living God" refers to *Binah*, from which all Severity <note>Gevurah</note> flows. He says that those who defile, declare unfit, and convict—who lean toward the side of Severity and stringency to show that the "Husks" have a foothold there—and those who purify, declare fit, and acquit—who lean toward the side of Kindness and leniency to show that the "Husks" have no dominion there—all of them come from *Binah*. From *Binah*, the influence of both extremes flows. When the "hand" or influence that is clarified from one of the two sides prevails, then the law is established according to that side, to forbid or to permit. Therefore, both the one who purifies and the one who defiles are acting righteously. Sometimes the law follows the House of Shammai <note>A school of law known for its stringency</note> in cases of great difficulty, even though the majority of the time the leaning is toward the side of Kindness. This is like the Sages saying that the House of Hillel is for leniency and the House of Shammai is for stringency; one represents Kindness and the other Severity, as the measure of Justice is composed of a known numerical value. The reason for the exchange of roles is according to the principle of "Behold my children," for sometimes Kindness is on the side of Severity and Severity is on the side of Kindness—just as fire is included in water and water is included in fire.

If someone were to say: "How can positive and negative commandments be unified as 'one opposite the other' if they are not equal in number? These are 248 and those are 365!" My children, may God protect and live you, I will inform you of a secret from which I will begin. Know that the 248 positive commandments, when including their root, are actually 365. For the 248 limbs...

->## House of Israel<-

In His simple unity, even after He brought created beings into existence. "And who can turn Him back?" <note>Job 23:13</note>, meaning there is no one to challenge Him on this or to suggest even the possibility of multiplicity, composition, or physicality arising from the One. "For His soul desired it, and He did it," meaning that His will was such, not out of necessity, but because His soul <note>original: "nafsho"</note> desired to manifest and live according to His will. Afterward, he explains the verse, "and many such things are with Him" <note>Job 23:14</note>. This means: even though I told you that everything was made by His will, do not say that they are separate from Him, just because they were made by will without a [humanly understandable] reason. Do not say that. Rather, these attributes are "with Him," and He formed them with wisdom, for all of existence is like a chain of linked segments, one connected to the other and that one to the next, starting from the first point until the last—the world of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divinity</term> through the secret of cause and effect. From Emanation to Creation <term>Beriyah</term>, from Creation to Formation <term>Yetzirah</term>, and from Formation to Action <term>Asiyah</term>—to the world of the celestial spheres and then to the elements, down to the element of Earth, which is the lowest point of physicality. Everything stems from the Will as a gift, not out of necessity. And how wonderful it is that the first point of Emanation—the secret of the Will and the Crown <term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, often equated with the Divine Will</term>—is the Will, as mentioned above. And the last point, namely the Earth <note>original: "Eretz"</note>, is called *Eretz* because of the word for Will <note>original: "Ratzon"</note>, as explained in the Zohar on the portion of Genesis regarding the verse "And God called the dry land Earth": "That which was dry land became 'Earth' to produce fruits and crops and to plant trees. This is why it is written 'And God called the dry land Earth'—through that lower union, the earth becomes a 'perfect desire' <note>original: "re'uta shelima"</note> as is fitting. On this it says 'it was good' twice: once for the upper union and once for the lower union. Since it was united on both sides, from here on the Earth is ready to produce fruits and crops as is fitting." Thus far the Zohar. And regarding the liturgy "Because of our sins we were exiled from our land <note>Eretz</note> and distanced from our soil <note>Adamah</note>," Rabbi Isaac Luria <note>the Arizal, 16th-century mystic</term> wrote: "Kingdom" <term>Malchut: the final Sefirah, associated with the physical world and the feminine principle</term> is called *Eretz* from the language of *Ratzon* (Will/Desire), as in "satisfied with favor" <note>original: "sava ratzon"</note>. And it is called *Adamah* (Soil) from the language of "Redness" <note>original: "adumah"</note> when it receives Judgment. Even regarding that from which we were distanced, *Eretz* is from the language of Will. Although all the above alludes to the "Upper Earth," nevertheless, this physical "Lower Earth" is also called *Eretz* from the language of Will. Thus, the secret of the seal of Will spans from the first point to the very last.

<margin>Thus, the Will is within the Holy One, blessed be He. The Torah is linked to the Will, for "one who is coerced is exempt" <note>A legal principle: if one lacks free will/desire, the law applies differently</note>. Openings of wisdom. End.</margin>

# The Torah

For the Torah is not forced into only one perspective; rather, it is comprised of many "faces," as discussed in the first chapter of Eruvin: "Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel: For three years the School of Shammai and the School of Hillel argued. These said 'the law is like us' and those said 'the law is like us.' A Heavenly Voice <note>original: "Bat Kol"</note> went forth and said to them: 'Both these and those are the words of the Living God, but the law follows the School of Hillel.'" And in the first chapter of Chagigah: "'The masters of assemblies' <note>Ecclesiastes 12:11</note>—these are the Torah scholars who sit in groups and engage in Torah. These declare impure and those declare pure; these forbid and those permit; these disqualify and those validate. A person might ask: How then can I learn Torah? The verse continues: 'They are all given from one Shepherd.' All of them were given by one God, and one leader said them from the mouth of the Master of all works, blessed be He, as it says: 'And God spoke all these words, saying...' Even you, make your ear like a funnel and acquire a heart to hear the words of those who declare impure and those who declare pure, the words of those who forbid and those who permit, the words of those who disqualify and those who validate." The explanation of these passages does not belong here, but will be discussed later if the Creator grants us life. Nevertheless, our eyes see that the Torah is not absolutely forced into a single form, but follows the "wills" according to the desire of the attached supervisors.

# He Then Said

The author of the statement later says: "There are two levels: Jacob and Israel; one is hidden <note>original: "satim"</note> and one is revealed <note>original: "galya"</note>." Behold, what he said at the beginning regarding "Will" on a level, that refers to the matter of the soul <note>original: "neshamah"</note>, as explained. And what he says here, "one hidden and one revealed," refers to the aspect of the body. This resolves why he said "one hidden <note>feminine: *stima*</note> and one revealed <note>feminine: *galya*</note>" rather than "concealed and manifest" <note>masculine forms</note>. For regarding the body, there are two distinct matters, and one is not like the other, as I will explain. Our Sages said in their Midrash: In the Torah of Rabbi Meir, it was written: "And God made for Adam and his wife garments of light <note>original: "or" spelled with an Aleph</note> and clothed them." The Zohar in the portion of *Pekudei* says: "Come and see, the soul does not ascend to appear before the Holy King until it merits to be clothed in the garment of that world... she only ascends in that garment given to Adam the first man when he was in the Garden of Eden, for he was clothed in a celestial garment, a garment of supernal light. Once he was driven out of the Garden of Eden and needed the colors of this world, what is written? 'And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin' <note>original: "or" spelled with an Ayin</note>. Originally they were 'garments of light'—light from that supernal radiance that served him in the Garden of Eden... and if he had not first been clothed in that light, he could not have entered there. Once he was driven out, he needed another garment... for the good deeds that a person does in this world create a garment from the supernal light to prepare him for that world... and in that garment, he is destined to see through the 'shining mirror,' to behold the pleasantness of the Lord and visit His sanctuary. Happy is the soul that is clothed in both worlds to be complete in everything, in this lower world and the upper world." The matter of this inquiry is long and will be explained in its place. However, it is clear from this that the garment of the soul which man had before he sinned was a holy, refined, and pure body leaning toward the spiritual. So shall it be in the future, as it is said, "the earth shall be full of knowledge"—meaning even the "earthliness," which is the body, will be transformed into intellect and will, as it was for Adam before he sinned. But when he sinned, the garment of the soul became "skin" <note>a pun in Hebrew: *Or* (light) vs. *Or* (skin/leather)</note>, a dry covering which is the coarse physical body. Through this, the "image of man" was sustained in him; "Man sees with the eyes, but God looks at the heart." This means: when man followed the "sight of his eyes"—that is, "it was a delight to the eyes"—he became clothed in physicality, and intellect remained only in his heart, for the heart still understands. This is "God looks at the heart," for He sees no evil in the human body, only in his heart. This is the secret of **"I have set Jacob-God to his heart,"** meaning to the heart of man, in which nothing remained but the understanding heart. Behold, that refined body of the future (which will be explained at length later) is called "hidden." And the coarse body which is currently physical is called "revealed." Therefore, they said "one hidden and one revealed" equally; when one rises, the other falls. And regarding Jacob and Israel: Jacob—"and his hand holding the heel <note>original: *akev*</note> of Esau," who is the primordial serpent, as will be explained. And Israel represents sovereignty <note>original: *serarah*</note> and freedom from subjugation and from the Angel of Death.

### Thus Far and to Complete

The explanation of the passage from the Zohar: the "Opening" that links the Holy One, blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel. From this, the excellence of Man will be explained—how he is in the "image and likeness."
In this introduction, which I have titled *The Generations of Man* <note>original: "Toldot Adam"</note>, I must make known the matter of Man's free will, which includes both the upper and lower realms. When he ascends, he ascends to the very top, and when he descends, he descends to the very bottom. This is similar to what is said in Tractate Megillah: "This nation is compared to the stars and compared to the dust; when they rise, they rise to the stars, etc."

# The Matter

Know that "God has made one thing opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. Just as He emanated a holy emanation, the secret of Unity called "Supernal Man" <note>as it says: "And upon the throne was the likeness of the appearance of a man"</note>, so too He made the "Wicked Man" <note>original: *Adam Belial*</note>, who is like a monkey before a human. This is called the "World of Husks" <term>Klipot: the forces of impurity or "shells" that conceal divine light</term>. It contains emanations <note>Sefirot</note> and seven palaces. Just as there are seven "faces" in the attributes of Beauty and Sovereignty within the holy emanation, so too in the Husks there are Samael and Lilith (may we be preserved from them). Their names and matters are explained at length in the *Pardes* <note>a classic kabbalistic text by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> in the Gate of Substitutions. And if you ask: from where did the Husks emerge, and "who can produce a pure thing from an impure one?" <note>Job 14:4</note>, the *Pardes* already answered that the truth is that above, in the place of Emanation, no evil thing descends from Heaven. For above, things are refined to the ultimate degree of subtlety. However, through the thickening of things and their descent through the levels of emanation, this force allows for the possibility of impurity. Just as a human, who is the choice of all physical forms, has waste within him—it would be unfitting for him to exist without it, yet it exists as a byproduct. In that spiritual realm, through the movement from level to level, and from a high level to a lesser one, this occurs through the power of "Choice" <note>represented by the "donkey," *chamur*, which shares a root with *chomer*, matter</note>. Thus impurity is formed. Similarly, in the high Emanation, in its own place, there is nothing evil. However, in the "thought" below, from the combination of the pure and the holy, an impure thing is formed, which is the waste and the dross of the gold. See there in the *Pardes* where he elaborates. He also wrote: "And such is the law regarding waste and evil—even though it is uprooted from its place to emerge into the skin, since it did not sin, no impurity rests upon it." See there for a pure explanation of how it is emanated from its source.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the divine hierarchy and the nature of creation. It moves from the abstract concept of the Divine Will (Ratzon) and the Crown (Keter) discussed on the previous page to the practical consequences of creation: the inherent "deficiency" of created beings compared to their Creator, the origins of evil (the "shells"), and the cosmic significance of Adam's choice in Eden.</meta>

# House of Israel

Our tradition tells us in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman that the ministering angels were pushed away from the presence of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for 138 years because they were expelled from His inner circle. Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said this was because they became arrogant and said, "For we are about to destroy this place" <note>Genesis 19:13—referring to the angels sent to Sodom speaking as if they had the power to destroy, rather than God</note>. Furthermore, every created being is inherently deficient. Even if a being is perfect in its own right, it still possesses a slight deficiency because it was preceded by "nothingness" before it came into existence.

(I will now copy the language of the Kabbalist "the Tailor" <note>original: "HaChayyat," likely referring to Isaac ben Samuel of Acre or a similar medieval commentator</note> from the work *The Gate of the New Wine*, though not all of it is necessary now, it will be needed later in this composition, with God's help.)

He writes: "I received a tradition from my teacher, Rabbi Shmuel Abushraga, of blessed memory, that the serpent’s intention in tempting Adam was rooted in the fact that he and his cohorts were jealous of the Divine. They resided in the 'habitations of light' on the edge of the World of Shells <term>Kelipot: 'shells' or 'husks' that represent the forces of evil or impurity that conceal the divine light</term>. They required the body of the first human, which was created from both the 'shell' and the soul. This is hinted at in the verse, 'These were the potters, and those that dwelt among plants and hedges; there they dwelt with the king for his work' <note>1 Chronicles 4:23</note>. These matters are ancient..."

He continues: "...and 'these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites' <note>Genesis 36:31</note>. This teaches that in all things, 'absence' precedes 'existence.' As it says in the *Book of Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei HaZohar</note>: 'And the earth was without form and void' <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. Formlessness (*Tohu*), void (*Bohu*), darkness, and the deep—these are the four primary 'shells' of the walnut. Because of this, it says 'the earth *was*,' meaning it existed in this chaotic state from the very beginning. It is the way of the shells to precede the 'brain' <note>the fruit or essence</note>."

Behold, when the Infinite emanated the world, He allowed the shells to emerge first. Their existence stemmed from the deficiency inherent in anything "new" at the moment it is renewed and revealed after having been hidden. This deficiency must eventually ascend to its Root. This concept is hinted at in the teaching that God "was building worlds and destroying them" <note>A famous Midrashic concept explaining the "Kings of Edom" as failed proto-worlds</note>. These are the worlds from which deficiency and sorrow emerge, which are destined to be swallowed up, as it is written: "He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away tears from all faces" <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>. Everything found within the holy realm has a counterpart on the outside. If these external forces did not deviate from their intended place, they would be good, for "He did not create the world for chaos, He formed it to be inhabited" <note>Isaiah 45:18</note>.

It is known that the "shell" attaches itself through desire. Just as in the human body, the "shell" surrounds the heart—as Job said, "You have clothed me with skin and flesh" <note>Job 10:11</note>—so too in the higher realms, "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalms 12:9</note>. The fruit is protected and hidden inside its shell. The four shells of the walnut correspond to the "shining electricity" <note>original: "Chashmal," the vision of Ezekiel</note> as explained at length in the commentary on the *Decanteni*.

The serpent was jealous of the Divine because it was "cunning" <note>original: "arum," which also means "naked" in Hebrew</note>. This means it was on the outside, like a garment that surrounds the person wearing it. It was "naked," being the garment itself. Therefore, the forces of the serpent wanted to "overturn the dish" <note>a metaphor for subverting the natural order</note>. They wanted to bring the "shell and soul" of man into the innermost holy chambers. To do this, they caused man to eat the fruit, as the serpent is an expert in desire. The proof is that Adam and Eve felt shame after eating; one only feels shame for something disgraceful. They realized that this "disgrace" was now part of them because it came from the animalistic power.

Thus, when the animalistic power of desire—driven by the serpent—overcomes a person, it creates a lack in the spiritual counterpart above. The "dish is overturned," and the "absence" takes over, as we see today in our sins. This was the great evil done by "cutting the fruit from the tree" <term>a Kabbalistic metaphor for separating the Divine attributes or causing a rift in spiritual unity</term>.

Some of our Sages say the fruit was a Citron <note>original: "Etrog"</note>, as the verse says, "it was a delight to the eyes." In the Aramaic translation, this implies a desire to see. Regarding the Citron, they say that if its stem is removed, it is invalid for ritual use, because it must remain connected to the tree to draw life. By sinning, Adam caused a great evil. The "Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil" is named such to distinguish it from the "Two" mentioned earlier; it is a tree that indicates both good and evil. God's intention was for man to live in the light of the "Shining Mirror" <note>prophetic clarity</note>, never choosing evil, but rather having his light naturally incline toward the good. This is why God told him to eat from the Tree of Life—to keep him far from evil and death.

As long as man acted correctly below, he awakened unity above, and all forces were subjugated to their proper places in peace. But he did not do so. By his own choice, he sinned in thought and deed, following the "Female Tree" <note>associated here with the lower, physical world of change</note> which leads down to death and destruction. Immediately, he became subject to change and death.

In the *Zohar* it is taught: "And the woman saw that the tree was good for food... Come and see: when the Holy One created Adam, He honored him with supernal glory and asked him to cling to Him, so that he would be unique, with a single heart, in a place of unique attachment that never changes. This is the secret of the Tree of Life in the center of the garden. But afterward, they strayed from the path of faith and abandoned the unique Tree that is above all trees, clinging instead to the place that changes and turns. They left the High One who is One and never changes. As it is written: 'God made man straight, but they sought out many schemes' <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29</note>. Because of this, their hearts were turned to that side—sometimes to good, sometimes to evil, sometimes to mercy, sometimes to judgment. The Holy One said to him: 'You abandoned life and clung to death.' The Tree of Life is called 'Life,' and whoever grasps it never tastes death. But by clinging to the 'other side,' death is found. Thus it is written: 'Her feet go down to death' <note>Proverbs 5:5</note>, and 'I find more bitter than death the woman' <note>Ecclesiastes 7:26</note>."

If you ask: "If Adam sinned, why did the whole world sin?" or "Did all creatures eat from the tree?" The answer is: when Adam stood on his feet, all creatures saw him and feared him, following him like servants after a king. He said to them: "Come, let us bow down and kneel before God our Maker." They all followed him. But when they saw Adam bowing to this "other place" and clinging to it, they all were drawn after him. This brought death to him and to the whole world. Adam changed into many forms: sometimes good, sometimes evil, sometimes angry, sometimes calm. He no longer stood in his permanence. This is the meaning of the "ever-turning sword" <note>Genesis 3:24</note>—turning from side to side, from mercy to judgment, from peace to war.

The Supreme King warned his creation: "But from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, you shall not eat." But man did not listen; he followed the woman, and the woman caused death for all. But in the World to Come, it is written: "For as the days of a tree shall be the days of my people" <note>Isaiah 65:22</note>—referring to that specific Tree <note>the Tree of Life</note>. Then, "He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away tears from all faces."

From this discourse, it is clear that God’s intent was for humans to cling to Him—the True One—and stay far from "change." Perhaps this is what the verse means: "Behold, the man has become like one of us" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>. Originally, in God's mind, man was meant to be "as one," clinging to the Tree of Unity. But through his choice, he followed the Tree of Knowledge, which is subject to change. These are the words of "the Tailor."

## Let us return
to the explanation of the levels. There is level upon level. One level comes from the soul, which is the union of "Beauty" <term>Tiferet</term> and "Kingdom" <term>Malchut</term> through the secret of the "Six Extremities." Another level is from "Understanding" <term>Binah</term> and above, in the secret of the living soul <note>original: "Chayah, Yechidah"</note>, which refers to the World to Come. There, man will be at the highest level, in a world that is entirely good, where evil is hidden and everything returns to absolute good. The wise will understand. Thus, the secret of man and "level upon level" is explained.

## And behold,
Regarding the "Will," these three are linked: the Holy One (so to speak), the Torah, and Israel. The entire realm of Emanation contains opposites, just as the will of the soul assists what is above it in a hidden way. This Will is hidden and concealed. However, we know that everything was created by His "Good Will"—not by necessity, but as a gift. This resolves the question of the philosophers: "How can many come from One? How can complexity come from simplicity? How can the finite come from the infinite?" Even the wise of our own people investigated this and spoke much philosophy. But their investigations were based on "natural necessity." The truth is that the Creator created His world through His "Good Will," and the Will desires what it desires without being forced.

Nachmanides <note>original: "Ramban"</note> alluded to this in his commentary on Genesis: "Know that composition does not imply destruction except to those of little faith who think creation was by necessity. But according to the people of faith, who say the world was renewed by a simple Divine desire, its continued existence also depends entirely on that Desire forever. This is the truth." This is the hint in the verse: "But He is at one, and who can turn Him? And what His soul desires, even that He does" <note>Job 23:13</note>. He is in His unity.

It then introduces the dual nature of the human body (light vs. skin) and the concept of "holy" vs. "impure" structures in the universe.</meta>

<header>House of Israel</header>

In His simple unity—even after He brought all beings into existence—no one can "turn Him back." This means there is no one who can question or cast doubt even on the possibility of multiplicity and composition arising from His Oneness. Regarding souls, the verse says, "For His soul desired it, and He did it" <note>Job 23:13</note>, meaning that His will was such, not by any necessity; rather, His "soul" <note>original: "nafsho," here referring to the Divine Will</note> desired to bring things into being, and it was according to His will. 

Afterward, the text discusses the "folding" of the verse, "and he has many things with him" <note>likely referring to Job 23:14</note>. This means: even though I told you that everything was made by Will, do not say that they are separate from Him. Rather, they were made "without a reason" <note>meaning, beyond human logic</note> by His Will. Do not think otherwise. These many things are "with Him," and He formed them with Wisdom. Everything that emerges is like "connected joints," one linked to the other, from the first point to the last: from the <term>Atzilut|The World of Emanation, the highest level of divine reality</term> in the secret of "Cause and Effect," from Atzilut to <term>Beriah|The World of Creation</term>, from Beriah to <term>Yetzirah|The World of Formation</term>, and from Yetzirah to <term>Assiyah|The World of Action</term>, down to the world of the celestial spheres, and then to the elements, until the "element of Earth," which is the lowest point of physicality.

All of this is from the side of the Will, as mentioned, not out of necessity. How wondrous it is that the first point of Atzilut is the secret of the Will, and the <term>Keter|The Crown, the highest Sephirah</term> is the Will, as explained above. And the last point—namely, the Earth—is called *Eretz* because of the word *Ratzon* <note>The Hebrew word for Earth (Eretz) shares a root with Desire/Will (Ratzon)</note>, as explained in the Zohar on the portion of *Bereshit* <note>Genesis</note>. Regarding the verse "God called the dry land Earth," the Zohar says: "When it was dry land, it was made into Earth to produce fruits and crops and to plant trees. This is why it says 'God called the dry land Earth'—through that lower union, the earth became a 'complete desire' <note>original: "re’uta sheleima," a play on Eretz/Ratzon</note> as is fitting. Because of this, 'it was good' is written twice: once for the Upper Union and once for the Lower Union. Once it was united on two sides, from that point onward, the Earth was prepared to produce fruits and crops properly."

Furthermore, regarding the prayer text "Because of our sins we were exiled from our land," the holy Rabbi Isaac Luria <note>the Arizal, the famous 16th-century Kabbalist</note> wrote that <term>Malchut|Kingship/Sovereignty, the lowest Sephirah</term> is called *Eretz* (Land/Earth) from the language of *Ratzon* (Will), like the phrase "satisfied with favor" <note>Deuteronomy 33:23, where "favor" is "ratzon"</note>. It is also called *Adamah* (Ground) from the language of *Adumah* (Red), signifying its reception of "Judgment." Even from this level we were distanced. Thus, *Eretz* is from the language of *Ratzon*. Even though all the above hints at the "Upper Earth," nevertheless, the lower, physical Earth is also called *Eretz* from the language of *Ratzon*. Behold the secret of the Seal of Will from the first point to the last. This is the "Will in Wisdom" <note>original: "Ratzon be-Chochma"</note>. There is another great matter regarding the Will that will be explained later in this gate.

### **The Torah**
The Torah is linked to the Will, for "one who is coerced is exempt" <note>Anus Patur—a legal principle that one is not liable for actions done without will</note> before the Merciful One. Furthermore, the power of the matter of the Torah’s "Will" is this: the Torah is not forced into only one perspective; rather, it is comprised of many perspectives. This is similar to what they said in the first chapter of *Eruvin* <note>Talmudic tractate</note>: "Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel: For three years the School of Shammai and the School of Hillel argued. These said 'The law is according to us' and those said 'The law is according to us.' A Heavenly Voice emerged and said to them: 'Both these and those are the words of the living God, but the law is like the School of Hillel.'"

And in the first chapter of *Chagigah*: "The 'masters of assemblies' <note>Ecclesiastes 12:11</note>—these are the scholars who sit in assemblies and engage in Torah. These declare a matter impure and those declare it pure; these forbid and those permit; these disqualify and those validate. If so, how can I learn Torah now? The verse says: 'They are given from one Shepherd'—one God gave them, one provider spoke them from the mouth of the Master of all works, blessed be He, as it says: 'And God spoke all these words, saying...' <note>Exodus 20:1</note>. Even you, make your ear like a funnel and acquire a heart to hear the words of those who declare impure and the words of those who declare pure, the words of those who forbid and those who permit..." This is the end of the quote.

The explanation of these sayings does not belong here, but will be provided later, if the Creator grants us life. Nevertheless, our eyes see that the Torah is not absolutely forced into one single face, but rather follows the "Wills" according to the will of those who achieve cleaving <note>original: "deveikut," spiritual attachment</note> to it.

# It has been said

->Three things are linked by Will:<-

The author of the statement then says: "There are two levels: Jacob and Israel—one is hidden and one is revealed." Behold, what he said at the beginning regarding "Will" being on a level—this refers to the matter of the Soul, as I explained. And what he said from here, "He opened with two levels, one hidden and one revealed"—this refers to the aspect of the Body. This would answer why he said "hidden and revealed" <note>original: "satim ve-galya"</note> and did not say "clothed and naked." Because in the aspects of the Body, there are two distinct matters, as I will explain.

Our Sages said in their Midrash that in the Torah scroll of Rabbi Meir, it was written: "And God made for Adam and his wife garments of Light (*Ohr* with an Aleph) and clothed them" <note>Genesis 3:21 usually says "skin" (*ohr* with an Ayin). Rabbi Meir’s version suggests they were beings of light before the fall</note>.

Observe the Zohar on the portion of *Pekudei*: "Come and see: the soul does not ascend to appear before the Holy King until it is privileged to be clothed in the garment of that world... When the first man, Adam, was in the Garden of Eden, he was clothed in an upper garment, which was a garment of Upper Light. Once he was driven out of the Garden of Eden and needed the colors of this world, what is written? 'The Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of Skin (*Ohr* with an Ayin).' Previously, they were garments of Light (*Ohr* with an Aleph)—the light of that Upper Radiance that served him in the Garden of Eden... If he had not been clothed first in that light, he could not have entered there. Once he was driven out, he needed another garment... Just as the righteous dwell in that light in the Garden of Eden... the good deeds that a person does in this world are the threads woven from the Upper Light to create a garment... and with that garment, the soul sees through the 'Luminous Mirror' <term>Aspaklaria HaMeira|A prophetic or mystical vision of total clarity</term>... Through this, the soul is clothed in two worlds to be complete in everything: in this lower world and the upper world." This is the end of the quote.

The matter of this discourse is long and will be explained in its place. However, it is clear from this that the garment of the soul—which man had before he sinned—was a holy, refined, and pure body leaning toward the spiritual. So too it will be in the future, when it is said "the Earth shall be full of knowledge," meaning even the "dregs"—namely the body—will be entirely intellect and will, just as it was for Adam before he sinned.

But when he sinned, the garment of the soul became "skin" and physical. Therefore, regarding this thickened body, the verse was established: "Man looks at the eyes, but God looks at the heart" <note>1 Samuel 16:7</note>. This means: when man followed the "sight of his eyes" <note>referring to the temptation in Eden</note>, he became clothed in his materiality, and no intellect remained in him except in the heart, for the heart still understands. This is "God looks at the heart"—He sees no "Will" in the body of man, only in his heart.

This is why "God turned toward his heart"—meaning toward the heart of man, for nothing remained of him but the understanding heart. Now, the refined body called "Garments of Light" (with an Aleph) is called "Hidden" (*Satim*). And the thickened body, which is currently material, is called "Revealed" (*Galya*). Therefore they said, "One is hidden and one is revealed." These correspond to Jacob and Israel. "Jacob" refers to the level of the "heel" (*akev*) and the subjection to Esau, who is the Primeval Serpent, as will be explained. "Israel" refers to lordship (*serarah*) and freedom from subjugation and the Angel of Death.

## Until here, and to be completed:
->The explanation of the Zohar's statement regarding the connection between the Holy One, the Torah, and Israel, from which the greatness of Man will be clarified—how he is in the Image and Likeness.<-

My intention in this introduction, which I have titled **The Generations of Man** (*Toldot Adam*), is to make known the matter of human choice, which encompasses the upper and lower realms. When man ascends, he ascends to the very top; when he descends, he descends to the very bottom. This is an example of what is said in Tractate *Megillah*: "This nation is compared to stars and compared to dust—when they rise, they rise to the stars, etc."

## The Matter
Know that "God has made one opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. Just as He emanated the Holy Emanation, the secret of Unity called "Upper Man," as it is written "and upon the throne was the likeness of a Man," so too He made the "Worthless Man" <note>original: "Adam Belial"</note>, who is like a "monkey before a man." This is what is called the World of Shells (*Kelipot*). It contains ten Sephirot and seven chambers. And just as there are "Partzufim" <term>Partzufim|'Divine Personas' or configurations of the Sephirot</term> in the holy realm of Tiferet and Malchut, so too in the Shells there are Samael and Lilith (may we be protected from them). Their names and matters are explained at length in the work *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moses Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of Substitutions."

And if you ask: from where did the Shells emerge? "Who can produce a pure thing from an impure one?" <note>Job 14:4</note>. The *Pardes* has already written the answer: the truth is that Above, in the place of Atzilut, no evil thing descends from Heaven. Above, things are refined to the ultimate degree of refinement. However, through the "thickening" of things and their descent through the hidden levels of emanation, it was necessary for the matter to be separated—"food from within food"—and there, dross was formed.

Here is a pleasant and very fitting parable for this: the human seed, which is the finest thing formed in the human body, emerges from a refined essence. From that drop in the full womb, the veins and organs are formed. Some organs are formed from the waste products of the milk, etc. Would it enter one's mind that in the human seed itself—which is the choice part of the body—there is the existence of filth? Certainly not! If it were so, it would be foul in an instant. Rather, that filth is formed through the movement of the seed-drop from place to place and level to level. From the drop drawn from the best of the food, the child is born, and from the rest, the filth is formed.

So it is with the Emanation above: in its own place, there is no evil. However, in the downward extension, the "protection of the dross" and the "impure thing" are formed, which is the waste and the "dross of gold," etc. See the *Pardes* who elaborated on this. He further wrote: "Such is the law regarding the seed—even though it has been uprooted from its place to exit, as long as it has not exited, no impurity falls upon it." See there; it is pure. It does not become impure until it exits from the organ outward.

# House of Israel

We find a discussion regarding the words of Rabbi Samuel bar Nachman: the ministering angels, because they revealed the secrets of the Holy One, blessed be He, were banished from their celestial proximity for 138 years. Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said: This was because they became haughty and said, "For we are about to destroy this place" <note>Referring to the angels' statement in Genesis 19:13 regarding the destruction of Sodom, where they took credit for the act rather than attributing it to God</note>. This teaches that every created being is inherently lacking; even if it appears perfect, it still possesses a slight deficiency due to the "privation" <note>original: "ha'eder," a philosophical term for the state of non-existence that precedes being</note> that comes before existence.

(I will now transcribe the words of the Kabbalist known as **The Tailor** <note>original: "HaHayyat," likely referring to Rabbi Isaac ben Samuel of Acre or a similar contemporary commentator</note> from what he wrote in the "Gate of Strengthening," and although not all of it is strictly necessary now, it will be needed later in this composition, with the help of God.)

And these are his words: "I received from the mouth of my master, the Rabbi, Samuel Absharna, may he rest in peace, that the Serpent's intent in enticing Adam was because he and his faction were jealous of the divine nature. They dwelled in the 'residences of light' above the world of the <term>shells|Kelipot; the 'husks' or spiritual forces of impurity that conceal the divine light</term>. They required the body of Adam, who was created from both the shell and the soul." The intent of these shells is mentioned in the verse: "These were the potters, and those that dwelt among plants and hedges; there they dwelt with the king for his work" <note>1 Chronicles 4:23</note>—these are "ancient matters." And so it is written: "And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel" <note>Genesis 36:31</note>. This is because, in all things, "privation" precedes existence. In the Book of <term>Tikkunim|Tikkunei HaZohar; a central kabbalistic text</term>, it is written: "And the earth was without form and void" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>; they explained that this "chaos" existed from long ago. This is the way of things: the shells precede the "brain" <note>meaning the inner essence or the fruit</note>.

Thus, when the Emanator <note>God</note> shone forth, He emanated the shells first. Their existence stemmed from the deficiency inherent in a newly created thing at the moment of its emergence, having previously been hidden. He must elevate and refine it because it came from a state of non-being, and non-being precedes being. This is also hinted at in the saying of the Sages: "He was building worlds and destroying them" <note>Midrash Genesis Rabbah 3:7</note>. These are the worlds that come from the side of darkness and desolation, which are destined to be swallowed up in the future, as it is said: "He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces" <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>. Every "chariot" <note>spiritual structure</note> that exists on the inside has a corresponding one on the outside. If they had not changed their places, they would have been good, for "He created it not in vain, He formed it to be inhabited" <note>Isaiah 45:18</note>.

It is known that from the shells comes "desire." Just as the shell is entangled around the heart in the human body—as it is written in Job: "You have clothed me with skin and flesh" <note>Job 10:11</note>—so too in the realms above: "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:8</note>. For the fruit is guarded and hidden within its shell. The shells of a **nut**, which are four, hint at the four levels of impurity. This is why they were jealous of divinity; the Serpent was "shrewd" <note>Hebrew "arum," which also means "naked"</note>, meaning he was on the outside like a garment that surrounds the one wearing it. Thus, he was "naked" in the sense of being a garment without a wearer. They wanted to "snatch the plate" <note>a metaphor for taking control of the divine flow</note>, but this was impossible except through Adam, who possesses both the shell and the soul. Through him, they could enter the innermost chambers. For this reason, they caused him to eat the fruit, as it increases desire. The proof is that they "clothed themselves" after eating from it.

As it says in the Zohar: "And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day" <note>Genesis 3:8</note>. When the animalistic power of desire—which comes from the Serpent—overpowers a person, it creates a deficiency above. Then the "plate is overturned" and the "privation" takes over, as it is now in our sins. 

Some of our Sages said the forbidden fruit was an **etrog** <note>a citron fruit</note>, as it is written: "it was a delight to the eyes," which the Targum translates as "desirable to look upon." For this reason, they said regarding an etrog used for a commandment: "if its stem is removed, it is invalid," because one must leave a part of the wood in it. The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil means one should distance themselves from the "evil" side of the tree. The Holy One's intent was for Adam to live on earth like the "divine angels," not turning his choice toward evil, but being unified with the One. But he was forbidden from eating of the Tree of Life to distance him from death. As long as he acted correctly below, he would awaken harmony above, and the shells would be subjugated. But he did not do so; by his choice, he sinned in thought and deed. 

The Zohar teaches: "The woman saw that the tree was good for food... Come and see: humans do not know or observe that when the Holy One created Adam, He honored him with supernal honor. He asked him to cleave to Him, so that he would be unique and with a single heart, in a place of unique cleavage that never changes. This is the Tree of Life. But later, he strayed from the path of faith and abandoned the unique tree that is above all trees, and cleaved to the place that changes and turns. He left the One who never changes." 

The Sages said: "God made man upright, but they have sought out many inventions" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29</note>. Their hearts were turned to the "other side," which is sometimes good and sometimes evil, sometimes mercy and sometimes judgment. By cleaving to that, they sought "many inventions." The Holy One said to him: "You abandoned life and cleaved to death." For the Tree of Life gives eternal life, but this other place is death. Thus, death was decreed upon him and the whole world. You might ask: if he sinned, why did the whole world sin? It is because when Adam stood on his feet, all creatures saw him and feared him, following him like servants before a king. He told them: "Come, let us bow down and kneel before the Lord our Maker." But when they saw Adam bowing to this "other place" and cleaving to it, they all followed him. Thus he caused death for himself and all of them. This place is called the **"revolving sword"**, turning from side to side, from good to evil, from mercy to judgment. 

But in the world to come, it is written: "For as the days of a tree are the days of my people" <note>Isaiah 65:22</note>, referring to the Tree of Life. And "He will swallow up death forever." From this, it is clear that God’s intent was for them to cleave to Him—the True One—and to distance them from "change." Perhaps this is the meaning of: "Behold, the man has become as one" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>; originally, in God's thought, he was to be "as one," like the Tree that indicates Unity. 

# Returning 
To the explanation of the levels: there is "level upon level." One level is from the soul, from the union of Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> and Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term>. The level above that is from Understanding <term>Binah</term> and above, in the secret of the "Living" and "Unique" soul <note>original: "Chaya" and "Yechida," the highest levels of the soul</note>. This is the secret of the World to Come, where man will be in the first level and even higher—a world that is entirely good, where evil is hidden and returns to absolute good. The wise will understand. This explains the secret of "Man, level upon level."

# And behold,
Regarding the **Will** <note>original: "Ratzon"</note>, these three are linked: the Holy One (blessedly be He), the Torah, and the People. All of Emanation acts according to this Will. This Will is hidden and concealed. We know that everything was created through "Good Will," not by necessity, but as a gift. This resolves the question of the philosophers: "How can multiplicity emerge from Unity? How can composition come from the Simple? How can the finite come from the Infinite?" The scholars of our people also philosophized much on this, but their investigations were based on "natural necessity." The truth of the Torah is that the Creator brought His world into being through His Good Will. Will wants what it wants; there is no "necessity" in it. 

Nachmanides <term>Ramban</term> wrote similarly on the portion of Bereshit: "Know that composition does not imply destruction except to those of little faith who think creation is by necessity. But according to the people of faith, who say the world was renewed by the desire of a simple God, its continued existence also depends on that desire forever." This is hinted at in the verse: "But He is at one <note>or "in Unity"</note>, and who can turn Him? And what His soul desires, even that He does" <note>Job 23:13</note>.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the spiritual forces behind the destruction of Jerusalem and the origins of the "External Forces" (evil), linking the historical tragedy of the Temple's fall to the primordial fall of Adam and the nature of the Serpent.</meta>

# House of David

<margin>The Lord has purposed to destroy the wall, etc.</margin>
"The Lord has purposed to destroy the wall... her palaces" <note>quoting Lamentations 2:8</note> refers to the upper walls of Jerusalem. You placed the life-force of the guardians there, as it is written: "On your walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen" <note>Isaiah 62:6</note>, so that the <term>External Forces|Chitzonim; spiritual forces of impurity that exist outside the realm of holiness</term> would not enter them. At the hour of the Temple's destruction, He delivered the walls into the hand of the enemy—these are the powers and the dominion of the <term>Shell|Kelipah; the "husk" of evil that conceals divine light</term>. This is what is stated in the Zohar (Section *Bereshit*) in the study of the "Dwellings" in the first chapter, which explains that there are spiritual dwellings. It says: "The third dwelling is where the 'bound ones' lie... and there the curses against Israel are found... and Samael the wicked is found there." 

My master <note>likely referring to Isaac Luria or a similar authority</note>, of blessed memory, explained: He is not permanently fixed there, but rather he is found there when he ascends from the "Female of the Great Abyss" into this dwelling to accuse Israel. From there, he and his company cry out with the voice of accusation, saying, "Shall the Judge of all the earth not do justice?" <note>Genesis 18:25</note>. From there, the sound of their accusation rises above, and the King of Judgment must necessarily incline His ear to the sound of their accusation. This is the meaning of "They have made a noise in the house of the Lord" <note>Lamentations 2:7</note>—this refers to the sound of accusation, like the day the Golden Calf was made, when they were made and called "Heralds of the Void" <note>original: "Malkurin," likely a Hebrew corruption of a Greek term for ambassadors or messengers of doom</note>. 

"He has profaned the appointed feast"—the "appointed feast" refers to the times designated for union. And this occurred "as in the day of an appointed feast," meaning a time designated for the union [of divine forces] shall not return as it used to be. The voice they raised in the days of the destruction was like that day when the Tent of Meeting was made, for there the accusation was undoubtedly going and growing stronger. According to this, "The House of the Lord" refers to the "Dwellings," for they are a house and a dwelling for the <term>Kingdom of Holiness|Malchut; the lowest of the ten Sephirot, representing the physical world and divine immanence</term>. 

Along the way, the author of this lament hints at a sublime principle: Heaven forbid we think that the "Shells" (evil forces) enter into the realms of <term>Emanation|Atzilut</term>, <term>Creation|Beriah</term>, or <term>Formation|Yetzirah</term>. Rather, the secret of the "External Forces" entering the Holy Place means that within the "Dwellings" there is a certain "Female" called the "Female of the Great Abyss." From there emerge many "disciplinary officers" and "deputies" of these forces in the world. It is a closed opening, and they do not emerge from there unless the wicked increase in the world. Then that opening is opened, and from there many "officers of judgment" and "bands of strikers" emerge and spread through those Dwellings. They ascend to the Dwelling that corresponds to the "Palace of Strength" (*Gevurah*)—the Palace of Merit—from where Esau, the son of Isaac, takes hold. They also reach the Dwelling corresponding to the "Palace of Kindness" (*Hesed*)—the Palace of Love—from where Ishmael, the son of Abraham, takes hold. There they cry out with the voice of their accusation, and it enters further upward before the Upright King, and then the decree goes forth according to the time and the sin. Thus, we find that no "External Force" actually enters any of the holy places. This is what the lamenter hinted at by saying, "He delivered into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces"—according to the first explanation. And there, in the "House of the Lord"—meaning the Dwellings—"they gave a voice" of accusation, "as on a feast day," as explained.

# And Behold
<margin>The matter of the serpent’s deed with Eve</margin>
Our Sages of blessed memory warned that one should not eat from the fruit of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, because the root of evil is there. For while it remains in its root, the root of the "surplus" <note>physical matter or potential evil</note> lives in a state where it is a "guard" (*shomer*) and not yet a "shell" (*kelipah*). However, when one separates the fruit from the tree, he performs a "severing" <note>original: "kitzutz," a technical term for creating a separation in the divine unity</note> and awakens "two authorities." Then the guard becomes a "peeled shell" separated from the food, and "unclean, unclean, shall he call out," for the shell is cast out "outside the camp shall be his dwelling." 

This was caused by man and his wife when they followed the counsel of the Serpent. The root of the Serpent's thought came from the essence of the "Tree of the Outsiders," which is **Samael** <note>the primary accuser or "Satan" figure in Kabbalah</note> and his female partner. They enticed the couple, Adam and Eve. In the *Book of the Bahir* <note>one of the earliest Kabbalistic texts</note>, the students asked their master: "Tell us, how did the event happen?" He said to them: Samael the wicked conspired with all his heavenly hosts against his Master because the Holy One, blessed be He, had said [to man], "And rule over the fish of the sea." Samael said, "How can I cause him to sin and drive him away from before God?" He descended with all his legions and sought a companion on earth like himself, and he found the Serpent. It had the likeness of a camel, and he rode upon it. 

He went to the woman and said to her, "Did God really say, 'You shall not eat of every tree of the garden'?" He thought: "I will seek more and add to the command so that she will diminish it." She said, "We were only prevented from the Tree of Knowledge which is in the midst of the garden; God said 'You shall not eat of it, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.'" She added two things: she said "from the fruit of the tree" when He only said "from the tree," and she said "neither shall you touch it," which He had not commanded. What did Samael the wicked do? He went and touched the tree. The tree screamed and said, "Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked move me" <note>Psalm 36:12</note>, "Wicked one, do not touch me!" 

He then said to the woman, "Behold, I touched the tree and did not die; you too may touch it and you will not die." The woman went and touched the tree with force. She saw the Angel of Death coming toward her. She said, "Perhaps I am now going to die, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will make another woman for Adam. I will cause him to eat with me; if we die, we both die, and if we live, we both live." She took from the fruits of the tree and gave to her husband. The eyes of both were opened and his teeth "were set on edge" <note>a metaphor for suffering or corruption</note>. He said, "What is this you have fed me? Just as my teeth were set on edge, so shall the teeth of all creatures be set on edge." 

The creature is called a Serpent (*Nachash*) because from there come all the powers of impurity, such as divination (*nichush*) and sorcery. Also, the word *Nachash* (Serpent) combined with *Hamah* (Heat/Wrath) has the numerical value of **Satan**. There is a great hint here regarding the calculation with the word itself: through the "word," the Serpent/Satan caused this—meaning the "filling" of her lips and the utterance of a lie against her Creator. This caused the form of man to change; "man in glory shall not endure," and it caused death, and his face was changed. For the purpose of man's creation was eternal life, as I will explain later. 

"The end of the matter, all has been heard: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>. "The end of the matter" refers to man, who was created last, though he was first in thought. He was created at the end so that he might include everything in his image and likeness. We find that man possesses 248 limbs and 365 sinews, corresponding to the Positive and Negative Commandments. "Fear God"—this refers to the Negative Commandments. "Keep His commandments"—this refers to the Positive. This is why it says "for this is the whole of man," for the structure of man is made of his limbs and sinews. 

In the "Chapter of the Chariot," it is asked: What is the meaning of "for this is the whole of man"? Rabbi Eleazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said, "The entire world was created only for the sake of this one." Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: "This one is equal in weight to the entire world." Rabbi Simeon ben Azzai (and some say Rabbi Simeon ben Zoma) said: "The entire world was created only to serve as a companion to this one." 

These sages are hinting at the matter of the creation of the "Shells." Rabbi Eleazar’s view aligns with what Rabbeinu Tam wrote in *Sefer HaYashar*: The world was only created for the pious and those who serve God, not for the wicked. However, the wicked were created through the nature of creation, just as the "shell" is created for the sake of the fruit. When a sower intends to grow wheat alone, the power of growth also brings forth thorns with the wheat. So too, the Creator's intent was to create the pious, but the power of creation brings forth the wicked along with them. 

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana adds that there is even a benefit in their creation, as the Zohar says regarding the utility of the "Evil Inclination" (*Yetzer HaRa*): it exists to bring man to his true purpose. If he conquers his inclination, then "according to the pain is the reward." See the *Pardes* <note>by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of Substitutions," where this is explained at length. Even an "evil angel" will answer "Amen," for the Evil Inclination also acts for the honor of its Creator—so that man may be tested and stand in the trial. When he does so, man is equal to the whole world and tips the scale for everyone. Rabbi Simeon says it was only created to "serve as a companion"—meaning what I said above: that the lower forces should be submissive servants to him. This explains the teaching of Rabbi Joshua ben Menasiah: "Alas for a great servant who has been lost..." 

There is a great hint in the matter of **Sandalphon**, for the dwelling of the "Shells" is "around" the world—"The wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>. This is in the World of Action (*Asiyah*), whose root is Sandalphon. As is known: the letters *Yod-He-Vav-He* correspond to the four worlds: Akatriel (Emanation/Creation), Metatron (Formation), and Sandalphon (Action). And he...

# House of David
<margin>Explanation of the matter of the "pig" that is destined to be purified</margin>
->As our Sages of blessed memory said: "In the future, the pig (*chazir*) is destined to be purified." If the Shells were in the secret of the "guard," they would be purified in the future.<-

...is also aligned with Sandalphon. Currently, while they are "Shells," there is a distance, for the Side of Holiness is called the "Right Side" and the Side of Impurity is called the "Left Side," for "from the North shall evil break forth." But if everything were sanctified, it would all be holiness. The pious one sees "two Sandalphons"—one for the South and one for the North—for great good shall also come from the North, as everything will return to the Right. 

Regarding the phrase "Stones that surround," there is also a great hint. The author of *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation</note> calls the letters "stones." We see that from "two stones (letters) two houses (words) are built; from three, six; from four, twenty-four," and so on. All the reversals and permutations of words indicate different matters and their opposites. As it says in *Sefer Yetzirah*: "The opposite of *Oneg* (Delight) is *Nega* (Plague)." Here, the substitution is a thing and its opposite, for there is nothing higher than Delight and nothing lower than a Plague. In the future, all "stones" will be good; there will be no "opposite" of evil. 

As for what is said about "a strap under his tail," there is a secret in this too. The Sephirah of **Malchut** (Kingdom) is the last level of Emanation (*Atzilut*), but she is the "First" and the "Head" over all things created, formed, and made. Through her, all influence flows to the worlds, whether of grace or mercy. Consequently, this Sephirah is a "tail to the lions" <note>the higher Sephirot</note> and a "head to the foxes" <note>the lower worlds</note>. From this aspect of being a "tail"—the final Sephirah—influence is also drawn to the "Shells." This is her "descent," for "her feet go down to death," as mentioned above. 

The "Shells" are called the "Ancient Serpent." The secret of what will happen to the Serpent is that in the end, the Holy One, blessed be He, will grasp the Serpent by its tail, and it will be below. This is what I spoke of regarding the "sweetening" of the Shells when they approach the root of their nourishment. For above, in their root, everything is holiness. Then the Serpent becomes the "Staff of God." This is the meaning of "taking hold by the tail"—the secret of being a "tail to lions," which is the root of their influence. But through sin, on the side of man’s sin, the Staff becomes a Serpent through the power of accusation. The wise will understand. And when they are purified, then...
