### House of Israel

**K**now that even though man is created in the upper image and likeness, once he became clothed in the filth of the serpent <note>The "filth" or "venom" refers to the spiritual impurity introduced into humanity after the sin in the Garden of Eden</note> to know good and evil, if he chooses evil, his face is changed and he is "likened to the silenced beasts" <note>quoting Psalm 49:13</note>. He becomes like a monkey. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "No wild beast has power over a man unless he appears to it like an animal." The "evil beast" that devours is the **Shell** <term>Shell|Kelipah; the spiritual "husk" or "peel" that represents evil and concealment of divine light</term>. Therefore, within the height and loftiness of man, the "Exchanged One" is hinted at, for every flawed thing is woven into its flawed, impure exchange. And behold, it is written: "And man became a **living soul**" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>, which refers to the loftiness of his station, as I have elaborated above. However, if he changes his "taste" <note>his spiritual character or behavior</note>, then "man becomes a living beast" <note>a play on the Hebrew words "Nefesh Chayah," which can mean both "living soul" and "living beast"</note> such that the evil beast rules over him, God forbid.

This is the matter of the two inclinations in man: the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination, existing since he came to know good and evil. Our Sages also said that the Evil Inclination comes to a person before the Good Inclination, just as the peel of a fruit precedes the growth of the fruit itself. These are the words of the *Service of Holiness* <note>Avodat HaKodesh, a 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, Part 1 (The Unity), Chapter 8: "I have already written in the book *The Worm of Jacob* <note>Tola'at Ya'akov, also by ibn Gabbai</note> that there were ten fingers on the hands of man corresponding to the Upper Wisdoms, for the points <note>or "Yods"</note> in their fingers are the instruments of action to serve the soul. Likewise, the Ten Utterances <note>through which the world was created</note> are instruments of desire for the Unique Master. And the ten toes of his feet, which are the foundations of the body, correspond to the ten levels in the lowest realm. 

Furthermore, man is comprised of the lower substances that are close to holiness; his portion of these is the bones, which are the most excellent arrangement in the body, and of them it is said: 'He will strengthen your bones' <note>Isaiah 58:11</note>. He is also comprised of good and evil, and a tablet was given to him showing the way of life and the way of death—that is, the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination—corresponding to the good and evil of which he is comprised. Choice was given to him corresponding to the 'Point.' However, his portion from the side of evil is the flesh, which passes away and perishes; for this reason, that Inclination is called 'the end of all flesh' <note>Genesis 6:13</note>, because its dominion is only over its own portion. There are also those who are lacking <note>spiritual maturity</note> who are under its command; they are its legions over which it is the minister, and we give them their portion—these are the tendons and the veins. 

He is also comprised of the heavens and the earth; his portion from the heavens is the covering of the skin that covers everything, and from the earth, the four elements. This is the general principle of the Lower Man, who is called by the Sages a '**Small World**' <term>Small World|Olam Katan; the concept of the human being as a microcosm reflecting the entire universe</term>." Thus far are his words.

---

**B**ehold, the **Shell**, the "peel of the fruit," is called in the language of our Sages a **Guardian** <note>Hebrew: Shomer</note>, and this is a great concept. I have already written that the nature of the Shell is that it comes from the "surpluses" of the holy forces. If man had not sinned, the Shell would not have been an adversary, but only a guardian for the fruit, like a king who sits in the inner chambers while the servants guard him. But because of sin, bitterness was awakened in them and they became rebels. 

In Tractate Sanhedrin, in the chapter "Four Deaths," it is taught: "Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya said: 'Alas for a great servant that was lost from the world! For had the serpent not been corrupted, every single person of Israel would have had two good serpents available to him: one to send to the north and one to send to the south to bring him precious pearls and gems. Not only that, but they would tie a strap under its tail and it would carry out dirt for his garden and his ruins.'" <note>Sanhedrin 59b</note>. This statement hints at what has been said, and so it shall be in the future, that the Shells, which are currently evil, will return to being good, in the secret of "the evil angel answers Amen." This was hinted at by the prophets in several verses. Isaiah said: "The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid... and a little child shall lead them... and the nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra" <note>Isaiah 11:6-8</note>. All of this points to their eventual submission above, for "every knee shall bow," and then the Shells will be called "Guardian," for they will guard the fruit. 

This is what Cain hinted at when he "stole the Upper Knowledge." He said: "**Am I my brother's keeper?**" <note>Genesis 4:9</note>. It is known that Cain is from the "Nest of Impurity" <note>original: "Kinza de-masakuta"</note>, from the filth of the serpent that came upon Eve. Abel is from the side of holiness. Cain is the Shell, and Abel is the fruit of the Holy Tree of Life. Cain said, "Am I my brother's *guardian*?" This was a declarative question, like "Did I clearly reveal myself?" <note>referring to 1 Samuel 2:27</note>. He meant to say that he was a "Guardian" and not an adversarial Shell. For a Shell causes damage on the outside, as they said regarding the "candle of Rabbi Meir," where "the light was darkened for all, and its shell was thrown away" <note>a metaphorical reference to Rabbi Meir's ability to "eat the fruit and throw away the peel" of his teacher's heterodox wisdom</note>. The Shell strengthens itself and accuses, but Cain wanted to "steal the Upper Knowledge" by claiming he was the Guardian of the fruit, a faithful servant to his Master. And indeed, so it shall be in the future.

---

**I** shall now explain this statement from "Four Deaths" so that God may grant me merit, for several excellent matters concerning the "Generations of Adam" will emerge from this, through which a person may understand how to cleave to holiness. First, I will provide a preface regarding the matter of the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge. Recanati <note>Menahem Recanati, a 13th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote in the portion of *Bereshit*, and it is similarly written in the book *Service of Holiness*, that they had a single root below, even though they were two in their branches. Therefore, Onkelos translated regarding both of them: "in the midst of the garden" <note>Aramaic: "bimzi'at ginneta"</note>. It is impossible for two trees to both be in the "middle" unless they are grafted into one another and unified at a single root. Behold, the text speaks of lower things but hints at upper things. The secret of the matter lies in the secret of **Emanation** <term>Emanation|Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah</term>, the Upper Tree where there are no "ends" <note>limitations</note>. 

Regarding the explanation of the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge, and the fruit of the Tree of Knowledge in the upper realms, interpretations have multiplied. However, the most clarified is this: the secret of the Tree of Life is **Beauty** <term>Beauty|Tiferet; the sixth Sefirah, representing balance and harmony</term>, which is the tree "of life," meaning it stems from **Understanding** <term>Understanding|Binah; the third Sefirah</term>, which is called "The Living God." The root of Understanding is in **Wisdom** <term>Wisdom|Chokhmah; the second Sefirah</term>, which is the life of the upper beings. There is the root of *Tiferet* and its concealment, and in its place, it is a "spreading tree," as I have elaborated above. 

The Tree of Knowledge is **Foundation** <term>Foundation|Yesod; the ninth Sefirah, associated with connection and procreation</term>, as in "And Adam *knew* his wife," for it is the Covenant of the Organ that connects the six and five "countenances." The fruit of the Tree of Knowledge is **Kingship** <term>Kingship|Malchut; the tenth and final Sefirah, representing the physical world and divine sovereignty</term>, which leads the world with an upper power for good or for evil, according to those who awaken it—for the people of the world awaken it through their actions. 

Our Sages of blessed memory said: "The world stands upon a single pillar, and its name is **Righteous**" <note>Tzaddik</note>. It is known that "Righteous" is *Yesod*, the foundation of the world. For just as all rivers go to the sea, all the "pipes" or channels are for it, for *Yesod*. Between *Yesod* and *Malchut* there is one single channel, namely the channel that goes from *Yesod* to *Malchut*. *Malchut* is called "World" because it leads all the worlds of created, formed, and made beings. This unique channel is the "one pillar." 

Behold, the flow of the "six edges" <note>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>—whether for judgment or for mercy—all flow into *Yesod*, and from *Yesod* into *Malchut*. This is the secret of the "two channels." These are the words of the *Orchard of Pomegranates* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note>, in the fourth Gate of the "Gate of Channels": "Another channel extends from *Yesod* to *Malchut*, for it is the extension of the 'Great River' that goes out from the 'Delights of Understanding' to water the Garden. Through this channel, *Malchut* is grasped by her husband above. Through this channel, the 'guards' <note>forces of judgment</note> are drawn down due to sins." 

Regarding this channel, we have seen in the "Reasons for the Commandments" <note>Ta'amei HaMitzvot</note> by the Recanati (page 30, regarding the negative commandment not to drink 'libation wine'): "There are two orifices in the Upper Covenant. One of them is to bestow upon the **Divine Presence** <term>Divine Presence|Shekhinah; the immanent aspect of God, associated with Malchut</term>; those flows that emerge are called 'sweet waters,' and from there emerge many flavors of the Torah—waters that quench the life of every thirsty person... The second orifice bestows upon the forces of impurity and is called 'libation wine' <note>Yayin Nesech; wine used for idolatry</note>." End of quote. 

From his language, it is implied that these matters are vital traditions of **Kabbalah** <term>Kabbalah; the Jewish mystical tradition</term>. The matters prove themselves, as if one "beholds God from my flesh." In man, there are two orifices: one for procreation and bestowing to give birth to one like him, and the second for digestion and waste. Furthermore, he wrote there in the name of another Kabbalist: "The letter *Tzadi* <note>the letter צ, representing the Tzaddik/Yesod</note> has two heads... these are two holy springs. One pours and draws from the 'Holy Guard' and from there the upper and lower beings are blessed... and from this spring, holy kings and many holy souls are created. In the second spring, it pours to the 'Left Side' of the Holy One, blessed be He, and from there the 'Harlot Woman' <note>impurity</note> draws. If Israel is worthy, that spring is closed and the holy spring of the right is opened. If not, the spring that the 'strange woman' draws from is opened... and from that second spring, demons and spirits emerge."

This good and evil is revealed through *Malchut* below. This does not mean, God forbid, that there is an actual revelation of evil there, for "evil shall not dwell with You." Rather, "her feet go down to death." The "feet" of *Malchut* are the worlds that chain down: Creation, Formation, and Action. The Shells, which are evil, are in the World of Action, surrounding the World of Formation (which is called **Metatron**). Regarding this, it is said: "The wicked walk on every side." 

Whenever you find in the words of the Kabbalists the "overlapping of the Shell onto Holiness," you must understand the matter thus: when there are righteous and pious people, then *Malchut* raises the "scent" of the deeds of the righteous above—this is what is mentioned in the Zohar as **Feminine Waters** <term>Feminine Waters|Mayin Nukvin; the spiritual "arousal from below" caused by human righteousness</term>. Then the channel of flow and blessing is opened. If the opposite occurs, God forbid, then the power of Judgment is awakened through the "accusation of the Shells"—meaning the Shells cry out and accuse: "These people are idolaters, and those people are idolaters," and the like. This is called the "overlapping of the Shell onto Holiness." 

Then, the flow is channeled through the "waste" channel. The flow that was intended for life from the Right Side for those who are on the "right" of the Torah is instead channeled from the Left for those on the "left," for the "True Judge" has decreed it so. Concerning this, it was judged that the serpent came upon Eve and cast filth into her. The matter of her "becoming a menstruant" <note>spiritually impure</note>, God forbid, is not to be taken literally. Rather, the intention is that by allowing the voice of the Shell's accusation to enter above, the flow of Judgment is triggered. The pride of Israel is taken and given to the nations of the world... and then they are judged. Everywhere this is mentioned, it refers to the time of Exile. Even though in truth "I am the Lord, I have not changed," nevertheless, He "desires kindness" and wants everything to be from the side of absolute good, so that "Good shall come and receive Good." 

These matters of the "overlapping of the Shell" and the "menstruant" state—I have summarized their explanation here, but it is explained well in the *Orchard* <note>Pardes Rimonim</note>, in the Gate of "Exchanges." The reader must contemplate this well, for who could put his hand to such matters and finish them? These are the words of the book *Voice of the Weepers* <note>Kol Bokhim, a commentary on Lamentations by Abraham Galante</note> on the verse "He has delivered..."

It interprets the roles of Cain and Abel and the original purpose of the "Shell" (evil) as a guardian that became corrupted through sin.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the spiritual nature of humanity before and after the Fall. Having established that man's character can descend to an animalistic level through sin, the text now discusses the potential for physical immortality and the metaphysical changes to the human "garment" caused by the primordial serpent.</meta>

### House of Israel / House of David
**6 I**

It is said of the **acacia wood** <note>original: "Atzei Shittim"</note> that it "stands forever and ever." Our Rabbis taught in the *Pesiqta*: We may rescue the case of a Torah book along with the book itself from a fire. Even though the words of the Torah are not written on the case, because it is attached to the book, it merits being saved with it. So too, King Solomon said: "He who walks with wise men shall be wise" <note>Proverbs 13:20</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "The first man, Adam, listened to his wife and was banished; had he instead remained attached to and listened to the Lord like Me, then just as I am living and enduring, so would he be living and enduring." 

This provides a hint that the body is like the **Torah case** and the soul is like the **Torah scroll**. We rescue the body from death—which is compared to a fire—along with the soul, provided the body is attached to the soul and listens to it, causing no hindrance to it. In such a case, it is fitting that death should not rule over the body, just as it does not rule over the soul, and both should endure together. We find that the enemy had no power over the handiwork of the righteous; how much more so should it have been that death had no power over the righteous themselves were it not for sin. As it is said in the first chapter of *Sotah*: Rabbi Hanina bar Papa taught, "What is the meaning of 'Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous; praise is comely <note>Hebrew: 'Navah'</note> for the upright' <note>Psalm 33:1</note>? Do not read 'comely' (*Navah*), but rather 'the dwelling' (*Naveh*) of praise." This refers to Moses and David, whose enemies had no power over their handiwork. Of David it is written, "Her gates have sunk into the ground" <note>Lamentations 2:9</note>, and regarding Moses, the Master said that when the first Temple was destroyed, the Tent of Meeting, its planks, bolts, pillars, and sockets were hidden away. Where? Rav Hisda said in the name of Avimi: "Under the tunnels of the Sanctuary." If the handiwork of man can be preserved, how much more so is it unfitting for the "enemy"—which is death and decay—to rule over the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He <note>meaning the human body</note>.

**And** this matter is like the "Garment of Light" spelled with the letter *Aleph* <note>The Hebrew word for light, 'Or', begins with Aleph</note>. For even the "case" of the Torah scroll, which is the body, was once refined and subtle. In the Midrash on Proverbs, Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shimeon ben Menasya: "The ball of the heel of the first man, Adam, outshone the orb of the sun." Do not be surprised by this; in the way of the world, if a man makes two pairs of goggles <note>or "vessels"</note>, one for himself and one for a member of his household, which one does he make more beautiful? His own! So, Adam was created for the service of the Holy One, while the sun was created for the service of creatures; is it not certain that the heel of Adam should outshine the sun? And it is an established principle: if his heel outshone the sun, how much more so the radiance of his face!

<margin>Man is meant to reach his ultimate purpose—eternal life—immediately. Otherwise, he walks in darkness until the day of death when the soul departs and the "filth" of matter, brought by the serpent, takes hold. Alternatively, one remembers the Supernal Light called the **World to Come** <term>World to Come|Olam Ha-Ba; the spiritual realm of reward</term>, which comes to a man after death as a result of sin. But the original "Good" was intended for him at the moment of his creation: to remain attached to the Supernal Light eternally. His soul originated from the secret of the "Fifty Faces" in **Understanding** <term>Understanding|Binah; the third Sefirah, associated with the source of the soul and the World to Come</term>, the root of the Upper Garden of Eden, the Holy of Holies. His body was taken from the holy place of the altar below, which corresponds to the altar above. Body and soul were like the "Two Crowns" below, mirroring the "Ten Faces" above. They were meant to be "joined together as one" <note>Exodus 36:13</note>, body and soul, progressing from one level of attachment to another, from the lower to the higher, until reaching the state of being "taken" by God, like Enoch and Elijah. Then the physical matter would become eternal, light reflecting light. His "World to Come" was already inscribed in his "World of Action," and the transition would have been an ascent without death, a simple lifting up to the root in *Binah*. While in the Garden of Eden, his "work" was his "food"; he did not need to plow or sow. Everything came from Holiness, and there was no lack in creation. Divine abundance would flow through all worlds. This is the meaning of "The Lord says, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth." Everything was in perfection, with no "Satan" and no "evil occurrence." This is the nature of eternity: a constant, unending providence. This is the secret of the World to Come—"they go from strength to strength." If man had guarded his high status, he would have seen his world immediately, for the lower Garden of Eden is a reflection of the upper. The Torah would have been purely spiritual, and its commandments performed spiritually. See the *Pardes Rimonim*, Gate 3 of the "Gate of Souls." His Torah would be eternal and his work would be done by others.</margin>

**Furthermore**, my children, I will grant you insight into this "Garment of Light." What is this light? Just as light increases and spreads without limit from one flame to another, so you can take one candle and light a piece of wood, and that wood lights another, infinitely. In this way, the light grows stronger. Such was the creation.

**The** matter is as I have written above: punishment and reward are not arbitrary decrees but natural consequences. It is the nature of being "attached" to the higher realms to open the Source and draw blessing from the "Head of Thought" to its end, spreading to the lower beings. This Good was never meant to stop; it was to be eternal. Man would walk from one eternity to another, becoming wiser and wiser without end. This is the very "Good" that flows to him, for "the reward of a commandment is the commandment itself." This was the intention of creation when man was made in the Divine Image and Likeness. The Holy One commanded him not to eat from the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**. The "World of Emanation" is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy—the "Depth of Good" and "Depth of Evil" mentioned in the *Book of Formation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note>. This refers to the roots from which good and evil extend. Not that there is actual evil in God—"Evil shall not dwell with You"—but from the "excesses" of holiness, if a man arouses them, he creates that evil, which is the "husk" <note>Kelipah</note>. Man was created from the upper and lower Sanctuaries to be entirely good and live eternally in a world of total goodness. Those "excesses" were meant to be humble and nullified. He was commanded not to arouse their power. Then, just as his soul was high, his body—the "case" for the soul—would have been a "Garment of Light" (*Or* with an *Aleph*). But man followed the Serpent, who caused a separation from the "Chief." The Serpent is the "man of perversions" who stirs up strife and turned words against the Creator, saying "You shall not surely die."

The **Ari** of blessed memory explained: "They saw that they were naked," and they were given "Garments of Light" (*Or* with *Aleph*), but now, because of the Serpent, it is the "death of the world," for there is darkness and not light—only **"Garments of Skin"** <note>Hebrew: 'Or' spelled with the letter Ayin</note>. This is "Evil" <note>Hebrew: 'Ra'</note> that he had not seen before. He became physical, made of skin and flesh. Then he became subject to the laws of nature that the philosophers mention: "Everything that is a composite must eventually decompose," which is death. The punishment of death was not a decree, but a natural result; for "the reward of a transgression is the transgression itself." He cut himself off from the Source of Life. Afterward, he fathered generations from a "putrid drop" <note>a common rabbinic term for semen in the context of human mortality</note>, contaminated by the "filth of the serpent." Had there been no filth, the drop would have been holy, like a "plastered cistern that loses not a drop." 

The Serpent, through a "crooked lie," testified against its Creator. It claimed God ate from the Tree to create the world. It separated the *Aleph* from *Adam* and from *Emet* ("Truth"). How? As I hinted above: "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very <note>Hebrew: 'Me'od', an anagram of 'Adam'</note> good." The seal is "Truth" <note>Emet</note>. Everything was good, not evil, until the power of the Serpent—chosen by the angel **Samael** <term>Samael|The principal angel of death and accuser in Kabbalistic lore</term>—was given to Adam and Eve, bringing evil from potential into reality. Where man was meant to live in "Truth" (*Emet*), meaning eternally, now "absence" is attached to him. The *Aleph* is separated from *Adam*, leaving **Blood** <note>Hebrew: 'Dam'</note>, which signifies the intensity of Judgment. The *Aleph* is separated from *Emet* (Truth), leaving **Death** <note>Hebrew: 'Met'</note>. Thus, from "Likeness" (*Demut*), there became **Blood-Death** (*Dam-Met*). "Blood" from the side of Adam, and "Death" from the side of Eve, who brought death to the world.

In the *Zohar* on Lamentations, Rabbi Hagai said: The Holy One showed the Torah to Adam, as it is written, "Then He saw it and declared it; He prepared it and searched it out. And He said to man..." <note>Job 28:27-28</note>. All were praising him until Samael saw from heaven and was jealous. He descended from heaven in the form of a shadow upon a serpent. Only the shadow of the serpent was seen, but the shadow was his strength and power. That serpent approached the woman, for her mind is more easily swayed than a man's. From this we learn a woman is only enticed by another woman <note>a metaphorical reference to the serpent's approach</note>. He said to the woman, "Even though <note>Hebrew: 'Af'</note> God has said..." He opened with the word "Af" <note>which also means 'anger' or 'wrath'</note>, indicating that the sin was present from his first words. The Serpent took the letter *Samekh* from Samael—testing if she would receive it. She responded until she opened with the letter *Mem*, saying "Of the fruit of the tree of the garden we may eat" <note>Hebrew: 'Mi-pri'</note>. Immediately, the Serpent took that letter and placed it on his left arm, waiting for death <note>Hebrew: 'Mavet', starting with Mem</note> to be ready for them. He enticed her until "the woman saw," with great and powerful desire. The letters of the Holy Name departed and ascended to join the letter *Mem*. The letter *Mem* was rising and falling, not wanting to join them, until she was enticed and gave to her husband. Four times they surrounded the letter *Mem* from four sides, as it is written: "**A**nd she took of its fruit, **A**nd she ate, **A**nd she gave also to her husband with her, **A**nd he ate."

<summary>This page discusses the metaphysical transformation of humanity from a state of eternal light to one of mortal skin and blood due to the Serpent's influence. It uses linguistic analysis of the words Adam and Truth to explain how the removal of the Divine 'Aleph' leads to blood and death.</summary>

# House of God
**21**
<meta>catchword: came</meta>

->House of God<-

...and modesty beneath their tail to bring their dust to the garden. For if the first man, Adam, had not sinned, his dwelling would have remained in the Garden of Eden. The secret of the "dust" refers to the holy ground, corresponding to the "Supernal Dust" <note>original: "Afar HaElyon"</note> or the "Supernal Land," as it says: "And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever" <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>. Regarding the phrase "and for its destruction," it refers to how his time was extended because of our many iniquities. The ruin and the breach occur through the casting off of vows, "and we lay down in our shame" <note>Jeremiah 3:25</note>. But in the future, the ruin will be filled through building and sanctification. Ezekiel also spoke of this: "The desolate land shall be tilled, instead of being a waste" <note>Ezekiel 36:34</note>. And they shall say: "This land that was desolate has become like the Garden of Eden, and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are now inhabited and fortified." 

These are the words of Rabbi Galante <note>original: "HaAlante," likely referring to the Safed Kabbalist Rabbi Abraham Galante</note> regarding the verse: "Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom." He presents a premise I received from my master: The "Husks" <note>term: "Kelipot" — the shells or external forces of evil in Kabbalah</note> will not be entirely destroyed or nullified. Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, will uproot the bitter, harsh, and difficult side from the world, and the remaining portion—the good, sweet, and pleasant part—will be sweetened by Him. He will remove the bitterness of the "External Forces" <note>term: "Chitzonim" — spiritual forces outside the realm of holiness</note> until they enter into the inner Holiness. This is the secret of the verse: "The suckling child shall play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the adder’s den" <note>Isaiah 11:8</note>. For as you know, the secret of spiritual union and coupling is called "play" or "delight" <note>original: "sha'ashua"</note>. This delight descends until the "suckling child"—representing the spiritual level of a nursing infant—stretches out his hand, and the union is made through the right and left sides. This delight descends even to the "hole of the cobra," which is the "female" side of the primordial Serpent <note>note: a reference to the dwelling place of impurity</note>. Regarding the "adder’s den" <note>original: "me'orat tziph'oni"</note>, this refers to the female of the deaf adder. The word for "den" (*me'orat*) is written deficiently, hinting at a "curse" (*me'erat*). The "weaned child" refers to the angel Sandalphon, who is "weaned" from his mother's milk. All of this points to the secret of sweetening the external forces; their bitterness will be removed from the world, and they will remain without filth. 

This is also the secret of why the pig is called *Chazir* in Hebrew—because in the future it is destined to "return" (*L'hachazir*) to being permitted. Currently, it is forbidden to use the "Evil Inclination" <note>term: "Yetzer Hara"</note> except for a commandment, for by its nature, if a part of it is spared, the whole is spared. Therefore, currently, this "pig" is forbidden to be approached, as in: "do not come near the door of her house." But in the future, when it is sweetened, it will be permitted. This is the "pig" returning to its source, which is the place of prophecy and holiness. This is the meaning of: "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh" <note>Ezekiel 36:26</note>. It is the nature of stone that if one part is hot, the whole is hot; such is the Evil Inclination. But "I will give you a heart of flesh," where the side on the fire is roasted while the other side remains cool. This is the "heart of flesh." As explained in the *Zohar*, a "heart of flesh" is a heart made to "act as flesh"—meaning the Evil Inclination will not seek its degradation except during the time of union between a man and his wife. At that moment, a person will be warmed to "make flesh" alone, and not for any other purpose. 

This is also the secret mentioned in the *Zohar* (Portion *Phinehas*): In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will break the "foot of the Ape" <note>note: "Koph" (Ape/the letter Qoph) is used in Kabbalah to represent how evil mimics holiness, like an ape mimics a human</note> and only "Hannah" <note>note: a name representing grace/holiness</note> will remain. This refers to the side of the unholy forces that step "outside the line," imitating holiness like an ape mimics a man. Just as holiness has levels and seven palaces, the unholy side has them too: "God has made one corresponding to the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. In the future, God will break that "foot of the ape" and what remains will be an offering of grace (*Hannah*). This is the meaning of: "The first to Zion, behold, they are here" <note>Isaiah 41:27</note>. 

This is also the secret of "He will swallow up death forever" <note>Isaiah 25:8</note>. It does not say He will swallow the "Angel of Death," but rather "Death" itself—the swallowed death will be removed, and a holy angel will remain. Similarly, the name of the archangel Samael will be changed: the "poison" (*Sam*) will be removed and nullified, leaving only "God" (*El*), who is holy. This is the secret of the Serpent whose "scales" or "plumage" will be shed. The Sages hinted at this in the Talmud when they said: "Snake, snake, open your mouth and let the son enter the father." Your Evil Inclination will eventually become a muzzle to guard and serve you. Our Sages also said: "Alas for the great servant that was lost from the world!" For had Adam not sinned, he would have led the Serpent by its tail to take waste to the trash heap, and the Serpent would have brought him pearls from distant lands. This shows that had Samael not rebelled and become bitter, the world would have used him for benefit. He would have helped remove the "waste" of sins and kept man from doing evil, and his utility would have been to bring "pearls"—the performance of commandments. As it is said: "The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and keep it" <note>Genesis 2:15</note>—"to work it" refers to the positive commandments, and "to keep it" refers to the negative prohibitions. However, because of the sin, the Serpent rebelled and caused man to sin. 

This is also what is said in the *Chapters of Rabbi Ishmael*: "Until all the princes are silenced and cast down on high like the scapegoat of Yom Kippur." This refers to the secret of sweetening, where they will be sweetened and remain on high, entering into the inner Sanctuary. This is the secret of the blood of menstruation, which is sweetened and transformed from impure blood into pure milk—this is a sign of what is destined to occur. These are the words of Rabbi Galante.

<margin>Behold</margin> These transformations in their transcription bring them closer to their proper dwelling. Even though they were stirred into bitterness by Adam's sin, they will be purified at the time of the End.

<margin>And if you ask:</margin> Before the sin of man, from where did the bitterness come? For Samael had already spoken against his Creator, as seen in the discourse of the "Young Man" I cited above. 

<margin>Know</margin> that initially he sinned for the sake of a commandment, and only afterward not for its sake, eventually leading to a sin for its own sake. That is to say, Samael was a pure angel. The Kabbalists say he was among the Seraphim, which is hinted at by the fact that the Serpent is called "fiery" (*Saraph*). He "clothed himself in jealousy"—the envy of scribes—for he was jealous of the status of Adam and wanted to draw closer to the inner Sanctuary. "Envy of scribes increases wisdom" for the sake of utility, but nonetheless, there was a force of bitterness within him, as I hinted above. Every created being has some deficiency, even if it is not physical. It is possible for a sin to cause a descent, as shown by the "Fallen Angels" who took greatness upon themselves, though this is rare. Regardless, Samael perhaps had more of the "Transformation" principle hidden within him. In his jealousy of Adam, Adam was stirred against him, and both assisted in the transgression until Samael became the "Accuser" and the "Evil Inclination." Adam became prepared to sin because he leaned away from absolute good and clothed himself in the "knowledge of good and evil." Then man became a "possessor of images"—the image of Holiness (the Supernal Man) and the image of Belial (the Ape mimicking man). Choice was placed within him: "the life and the good, and the death and the evil" <note>Deuteronomy 30:15</note>. When he walks in the good path, he rides upon life—the secret of the Tree of Life. When he walks in the evil path, he clings to death and his image changes. 

How so? When he walks in the good path, he is hinted at in the secret of "Death" (*M-V-T*) being ridden over by "Spirit" (*Y-R-Ch*). As our Sages said: "And you who cling to the Lord" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>—one who clings to His attributes is called *Adam* (Man), from the language of *Adameh* ("I will resemble") the Most High. But when he is in the opposite state, his image changes and he becomes "Death" (*M-V-T*). Then he is called *Adam* from the language of *Adamah* ("Earth"), for "dust you are and to dust you shall return." The "Exalted" (*Ram*) side is from the Man, and "Death" (*Mavet*) is from the side of Eve, who caused death to the world. 

How so? Know that the "seal" of the work of creation is "Truth" (*Emet*). "And God saw all that He had made [and behold it was very good]"—the final letters of these words spell *Emet* (Truth), and there the word *Adam* is hinted at. The words "Very Good" (*Tov Me'od*) have the same letters as *Adam* <note>note: in Hebrew gematria, both equal 45</note>, for he is the purpose of all creation. He was created to be "Truth"—meaning eternal. For "Truth" implies a true, eternal existence that does not fail but endures without faltering; this was the purpose of his creation, to live an eternal life. This matter requires a broad explanation.

<margin>Know</margin> that the natural philosophers said that death is natural to man. Their reason is that everything that is "generated" must "perish." Since man is generated and composed of the four elements, it is necessary that he decompose. This view was followed by all those who are "enraptured by Greek wisdom" from among our own people, who "turn justice into wormwood" regarding the Torah's intent. But the People of the Torah, the possessors of true faith and the truly wise Sages, believe that death is *not* natural. They said: "Had he not sinned, he would never have died." The truly wise and faithful believer, our great master Nahmanides <note>original: "HaRamban"</note>, said in the Portion of *Genesis*: "Know that composition does not necessitate decomposition except in the view of those small in faith who think creation was a necessity. But according to the people of faith who say the world was renewed by the simple will of God, its existence will also be eternal for as long as He wills it. This is a clear truth." Certainly, the natural scientists walk in darkness, for clinging to God is above nature. His will is for man's attachment to be eternal. The concept of "necessity" belongs to nature and tends toward those who believe the world is primordial (uncreated), but we believe the truth—that everything exists by His will. His command was for man to be eternal if he remained in "clinging" (*Deveikut*). As it says in *Midrash Rabbah* (Portion *Naso*) and *Midrash Hazita* on the verse "You are beautiful, my love, like Tirzah": Rabbi Meir says, "Until now they [the items of the Tabernacle] exist; they did not sin, they did not age, and they did not decay, but they live and endure." This is an argument from minor to major: if the items that were attached to man for the work of the Tabernacle were given life and endure forever, how much more so should Israel, who are attached to the Life of the Worlds, endure! As it is said: "And you who cling..." And in *Midrash Tehillim* (Psalm 92), Rabbi Meir says that in the future, these things will be ready to collect payment from the wicked, for "At daybreak I will destroy all the wicked of the land." The intention of the Sages is that those animals and objects will testify against the wicked; because sin brings death and because the wicked distanced themselves from God through their iniquities, they must face judgment. But those animals that were not commanded in the mitzvot, yet were attached to man for the work of the Tabernacle, merited eternal existence and will testify against the wicked in the future. And in Tractate *Yoma*...

# House of Israel, House of David
**22**
<sig>ו 2</sig>
<meta>catchword: The Delight</meta>

...above the five days of creation in their place, that is, in their root above in Understanding <note>term: "Binah" — the third "Sefirah" or divine emanation, often associated with the source of the soul and the "World to Come"</note>. This is the "Guarded [Wine]" <note>original: "יין המשומר" (Yayin HaMeshumar); the OCR text has a likely typo "י"י". This refers to the wine kept in its grapes since the six days of creation for the righteous in the future</note>, which no stranger's touch can affect. The influence shall spread so that the Name shall be complete; "on that day the Lord shall be one and His name one" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. 

The secret of the "Throne" <note>term: "Kise" (כס) — refers to the divine throne of glory</note> is Man, who shall be a chariot for the Divine Presence <note>term: "Shekhinah"</note> and the bearer of the Divine Presence, for Man was made in the supernal image and likeness; therefore, he shall be a throne. The [letter] *Aleph* (א), which was missing due to the power of the "diminution" that "separates the Master" <note>a wordplay on "mafrid aluph" from Proverbs 16:28; here "aluph" refers to the letter Aleph or God as the Master of the world</note>, shall return, and the Throne <note>original: "Kise" (כס) + "Aleph" (א) = "Kisea" (כסא), the complete word for Throne</note> shall be entirely whole. The *Aleph* of "Light" <note>term: "Or" (אור)</note> shall return, and there will be essential light, containing no dross of darkness, but only clear light.

---

<margin>Let us return</margin>
**Let us return** to the explanation of the discourse in the book *The Holy Service* <note>original: "Avodat HaKodesh," a seminal 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, as follows: Those who say "It would have been better for man not to have been created" <note>A famous debate in the Talmud, Eruvin 13b</note> do so because his physical matter is narrow and the "Accountant" standing at his right hand <note>a metaphor for the Evil Inclination or the record of sins</note> is ready and prepared to incline him toward the opposite of what he was formed for. It would have been better for him to remain "there" <note>in the spiritual realm</note> and not be created to increase transgression and multiply guilt. Not only does he fail to complete the Unity <note>term: "Yichud" — the spiritual task of unifying the divine attributes through holy actions</note> for which he was formed, but he "cuts and separates" that which should be connected, which is the opposite of what was intended in his creation.

However, those who say "It is better that he was created" argue that even though the Evil Inclination <note>term: "Yetzer HaRa"</note> was created, along with its deficiencies to turn him from the path, the Torah was created for him as a "spice" or remedy <note>original: "tavlin"</note>. It counsels him to guard his health so he does not fall ill, and guides him on the straight path to find "pleasant words" to complete the intended purpose, which is the Unity and the perfection of the Divine Glory. 

The Sages finally "voted and concluded" that it would have been better for him not to have been created, because the possibility of him turning from the path is very close due to his physical matter and his Evil Inclination. But now that he *is* created, he should "search his deeds" <note>original: "yifashpesh"</note> and examine himself for the transgressions he has already committed and remove them <gloss>meaning: he should investigate and consider repentance</gloss>. By this, he will repair himself through Torah and Commandments and return to "health" after having strayed and fallen ill. Others say he should "scrutinize/feel his deeds" <note>original: "yimashmesh"</note>, meaning he should keep his eyes on his ways and never let his mind wander, constantly reviewing his actions. He should clarify and take to heart the intention of his creation: the Unity, the Service, and Perfection. 

From this matter, the Sages said: "A man is obligated to feel his phylacteries <note>term: "Tefillin"</note> at every hour." The reason is so that he does not distract his mind from them at all, so that he takes to heart that he is a "Throne of Glory" and a dwelling for the Divine Presence. He should be sanctified in his actions and meticulous in his thoughts, remaining "simple/whole" in his deeds. Through this "scrutinizing" of his deeds, he examines within himself whether "it was better for him to have been created"—this concludes the words of *The Holy Service*.

But I say there is a further hint in these terms "search" (*yifashpesh*) and "scrutinize" (*yimashmesh*). "Search" refers to "running away" from evil, while "scrutinize" means to "clutch" onto the good. As it says: "the righteous man shall hold to his way" <note>Job 17:9</note>. The "Light" <note>referring to the letter Aleph</note> that was missing from the "Skin" <note>term: "Or" (עור) — the physical garments of skin given to Adam after the fall</note> is returned to purify it until it becomes "Light" <note>term: "Or" (אור) — the original garments of light Adam had before the sin</note>. This light is greater than the light that existed before he sinned. It was because of this potential "advantage" that those who argued "it is better that man was created" held their position. 

The reason for the final conclusion—"it would have been better not to be created"—is because I have seen "the children of the upper chamber" <note>a term for the truly righteous</note> and they are few, while the transgressors who do not overcome their inclination are many. However, the Holy One's intention in creating the world for man's purpose was based on the fact that "God made man straight" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29</note> in "Garments of Light" (*Kotnot Or*), so that the entire world would be light. Even though He created the "Power of Exchange" <note>the ability to choose evil</note> within him as well, the Creator's wisdom saw that there are two paths to the good: either he remains in "Garments of Light" and fills everything with radiance, or, even if he falls into "Garments of Skin," the "refined and the choice portion" (though it be few) will result in an *increase* of light. This is because the "Garments of Skin" will also be refined, forcing light out of the darkness. 

If there were no possibility of this "Garments of Light" state from the beginning, the creation of man would not have been worthwhile if he were only a "vessel of evil" with no mixture of good. But those who said "it is better to be created" argued that even if there were only this difficult path of struggle, man should still be created, for "the righteous shall walk in them" <note>Hosea 14:10</note>, and we need not concern ourselves with the transgressors.

Based on this, the verse is well-explained: "Better than both of them is he who has not yet been" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:3</note>. Initially, the verse speaks of us, we who are all in "Garments of Skin." It says, "I praise the dead who are already dead," for the death of His pious ones is precious in the Lord's eyes, because this death is "very good" <note>as explained on the previous page</note>. However, those souls who are prepared to be created—the holy souls hidden above who have not yet been created—refer to those ready for the Days of the Messiah, when the world will return to "Garments of Light" and a Great Light. They are "better than both" the living and the dead of the past, for they shall live an eternal, spiritual life. Everyone agrees that they are better than anything that has come before, even the original state of "Garments of Light," because this future light will be without any dross.

This future light, which will be without dross because the "Husk" (*Kelipah*) will be shattered, also explains the Midrash on Ecclesiastes regarding the "974 generations." It is taught in the tractate *Chagigah* <note>Chagigah 13b</note> that 974 generations were decreed to be created before the Giving of the Torah, to fulfill the verse: "the word He commanded for a thousand generations" <note>Psalm 105:8</note>. The Torah should have been given after 1000 generations, but when God saw the world could not endure without Torah, He uprooted them and gave it after 26 generations <note>from Adam to Moses</note>. I found it written in a book of Kabbalah that the "Spreading of the Supernal Adam" was intended for 1000 generations, corresponding to the "Ten Utterances" <note>the ten commands with which the world was created</note>, where each utterance includes all ten (10x10=100), and then each of those includes the whole (100x10=1000). 

Similarly, the "Adam of Belial" <note>the shadow or impure counterpart to the holy Adam</note>—for "God has made one corresponding to the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>—also had a spreading of 974. Immediately when Adam sinned, the "nest of impurity" was released through Cain. It was appropriate for these to spread for 1000 generations, hiding the "Tree of Life" for that entire time. But God's mercy was awakened after the reincarnation and refinement of Adam through Seth, and the Tree of Life remained hidden for only 26 generations. 

The 974 generations instead "ruled" in the way of the "Husk" (*Kelipah*), God forbid. They were "planted" in every generation <note>as the "brazen-faced" people of each age</note>. Every wise-hearted person will understand that the Holy One's intention was to abolish the "Husk." He uprooted these 974 and planted them across all generations as the "brazen-faced," who are as nothing. He "placed them on their heads" <note>subjugated them</note> like those whose existence was wiped out. Through this, the Great Light of the future is caused to be revealed sooner, since the Holy One "depleted" the existence of those 974 generations of "Husks." This is how I explain the verse: "Better than both of them" are the new creations whose holiness stems from the abolition of the "Husk," which was greatly caused by these 974 generations who were "uprooted" and spread out to be consumed. Then, the deeds of the righteous who overcome their inclination will also draw near, and the world will quickly return in our days to Light—and the Light shall be even greater.

---

<margin>And then</margin>
**And then** the Lord shall rejoice in His works, for then the intention of creation—to be "Man in Garments of Light"—will be fulfilled. Knowledge will increase, and "their work will be done by others" <note>meaning life will be effortless</note>. The "tree of the field shall give its fruit," meaning even barren trees will be full of fruit. It says "the tree of the field" <note>using the singular 'tree'</note> because the taste of the wood will be like the taste of the fruit, as it was at the beginning of creation. The earth will produce "delicacies" <note>original: "gluskauot" — fine rolls or cakes</note> and "fine woolens" <note>original: "kilei milat"</note>. All the good promises in prophecy that have not yet been fulfilled will be realized, for "the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord" <note>Isaiah 11:9</note>. 

The "goods" will follow naturally, for the blessings and curses in the Torah are not merely arbitrary "promises" or "threats"; rather, they describe a natural narrative. By performing the Torah and Commandments, this "Good" necessarily follows and is compelled by them. This is the nature of the Service: all "goods" and successes are drawn after the Commandments by a Divine nature implanted within them, as explained at length above. 

This also answers a question from *The Holy Service* in the section on "The Service": Why were physical promises mentioned in the Torah while spiritual promises were not? He answers that the physical promises were not actually "promised" as rewards, but were revealed to tell what must necessarily follow from the nature of the Service. All physical success follows the Commandments by a Divine nature. This "Good" is not a "reward" but a consequence, just as a key is the essential tool to open a source of good. There is no need to "promise" it; one only needs to reveal that it is the natural result. We can then learn through an "a fortiori" argument <note>original: "Kal VaChomer"</note>: if even physical goods follow the Service, how much more so the spiritual? What causes this "clinging" and the Service is the attachment of the pure soul; she causes the benefit to the body because of her attachment to the Source. The soul is the cause of these goods, and she certainly remains in eternal pleasantness in the place to which she turned while still connected to the body...

# House of Israel, House of David

The numerical value of the word "Hannah" <note>original: "חנה" (Hannah); the text links this to a kabbalistic calculation involving the word "Death"</note> is four times the value of the letters *Vav* and *Tav* <note>original: "ו-ת" (406); four times this equals 1624, connecting to the word "Mavet" (Death)</note>. This teaches that they surrounded the letter *Mem* on four sides, with "Violence" <note>original: "חמס" (Chamas/Violence); a wordplay on the letters of Hannah</note> in the middle, representing death on all sides, as it is written: "For death has climbed into our windows" <note>Jeremiah 9:21</note>. This "window" refers to the spleen, which is one of the windows of the heavens. Therefore, it is said that a person is mortal and shall not see death <note>referring to a spiritual state</note>; immediately, it was completed within her, and from that point, the Holy One, Blessed be He, descended to see them, and "the man and his wife hid themselves" <note>Genesis 3:8</note>. Come and see: before they sinned, the crown of the Divine Presence <note>term: "Shekhinah" — the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> was upon their heads so that they might be over the world. Once they sinned, as it were, their strength weakened and the Presence departed, and they no longer ruled over the seventy facets of beauty. This is why it says "death has climbed into our windows," for the final letters of the phrase "she took of its fruit and ate and gave" <note>original: "ותקח מפריו ותאכל ותתן" (Genesis 3:6); the final letters are Chet, Vav, Lamed, Nun, which spell "Chalon," meaning window</note> spell "window."

The purpose of a window is to bring in light; however, now light only comes through the side of death. This is the meaning of "death has climbed into our windows," for man cannot now merit the light except by stripping off the "garments of skin and flesh" <note>Genesis 3:21; the Hebrew "Or" (skin) is spelled with an Ayin, replacing the original "Or" (light) spelled with an Aleph</note> which come from a "putrid drop" on the side of the serpent's filth. Instead, he must clothe his loins in garments of glory made from Torah study and the performance of commandments, the details of which we shall explain later with God’s help. Thus, the verse "And behold, it was very good" <note>Genesis 1:31</note> is overturned; as the Midrash <note>term: "Midrash" — ancient rabbinic homilies and interpretations</note> says: "'Behold, it was very good'—this refers to death." Elsewhere it says this refers to the "Angel of Death" or "Suffering." All these are one matter, a wondrous concept as I shall explain. First, I will investigate a question: The Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world for the sake of Man, and He made Man upright; nevertheless, He gave him the power to turn from the good path to awaken evil, as indeed happened. If so, how could He create the world for him since it would not be absolutely good? The purpose would seem to be negated.

However, all this will be clarified. I will first quote from Tractate Eruvin <note>term: "Eruvin" — a volume of the Talmud dealing with Sabbath boundaries</note>: Our Rabbis taught: For two and a half years, the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel <note>the two major competing schools of early rabbinic thought</note> disagreed. These said: "It would have been more comfortable for man not to have been created than to have been created," and those said: "It is more comfortable for man to have been created than not to have been created." They eventually voted and concluded: "It would have been more comfortable for man not to have been created, but now that he has been created, let him examine his past deeds (or, as some say, let him scrutinize his future actions)." 

One must ask those who said "it is better to have been created": is there not a clear verse in Ecclesiastes <note>original: "Megillat Deborah" (The Scroll of Deborah) — a likely scribal error or a specific local title for Ecclesiastes/Kohelet</note> that says: "And I praised the dead who have already died more than the living who are still alive; but better than both of them is the one who has not yet been" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2-3</note>? This clearly supports those who say it is better not to have been created. The Aramaic translation <note>term: "Targum" — the ancient Aramaic translation of the Bible</note> says: "Better is he who has not yet been and has not been created." Since this verse has come to us, let us look at it: how can one say "better than both is he who has not yet been"? If he was not alive, he would be nothingness and non-existence! How can "good" be attributed to something that does not exist? Ibn Ezra <note>term: "Ibn Ezra" — a famous 12th-century Spanish biblical commentator</note> wrote: "Many wondered how they could say 'better' for one who was not created... it is merely a shorthand or metaphorical way of speaking." 

Rashi <note>term: "Rashi" — the preeminent 11th-century French commentator</note> wrote regarding "the one who has not yet been": I saw in the Midrash on Ecclesiastes that this refers to the 974 generations that were "folded up" <note>term: "folded up" — intended to be created but held back because the world was not ready</note> to be created but were not created. According to this, it is resolved, for they did exist in some sense as they were "folded up" to be created. But it is a great wonder to me: how can it be said that these 974 generations are "better" than the living and the dead? Did not the Sages say in Tractate Chagigah: "From where does the River of Fire <note>original: "Nehar Dinur" (Aramaic)</note> flow? From the sweat of the holy creatures. And where does it pour? Onto the heads of the wicked in Gehenna." Rabbi Akiva bar Yaakov said it pours upon those who were "folded up," as it says, "who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a river" <note>Job 22:16</note>. It was taught: Rabbi Simon the Pious said these are the 974 generations that were intended to be created before the world was created but were not; the Holy One, Blessed be He, stood and planted them in every single generation, and they are the "brazen-faced" <note>referring to those with a difficult or rebellious nature</note> of each generation. Furthermore, how can it be said they were not created, when in truth they are created in every generation? And further, there is a difficulty with those who say "it is better not to have been created": they are, as it were, trying to be wiser than the Holy One, Blessed be He! If He created him, then surely it is good that he was created, and the verse testifies of all creation that "it was good."

**Now** I shall explain the matter. Know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world for the purpose of Man, and God made Man upright to be entirely good and to be light. In this aspect, if Man had not awakened evil and had remained entirely good, everyone would agree it is better that he was created. However, the disagreement arose after Man corrupted himself through his own choice, and the intention of creation was seemingly nullified. The question then is: after the corruption, is it better to have been created or not?

I will first provide another introduction. Currently, in man's corrupted state, the world is not yet aligned with the intention of creation until the corruption is repaired. You must know that when man is repaired, then the "garments of skin" (which are now skin/darkness and not light) will return to being "light," and it will be an even greater light than the light that existed before he sinned. This is the concept of "the advantage of light over darkness" <note>Ecclesiastes 2:13</note>, for from the power of the darkness, there will be a surplus of light. Our Sages said [the world is like] "a needle's thread" or "a cluster of grapes," and there is a great hint in this. 

As long as they are grapes, the "dregs" <note>original: "shmarim" (שמרים); the sediment or waste in wine production</note> are known to be there, but they are mixed in and not recognizable. Only when a person squeezes the cluster of grapes and wine is made do the dregs become separated from the wine. That which was initially "potential" dregs now becomes "actual" dregs as they are cast out. While there is a disadvantage for the dregs—for initially they were not recognized and were unified [with the fruit], and now they are revealed as evil dregs—there is a much greater advantage for the wine. It has become clear, with no refuse, entirely pure. The wine remains "guarded" <note>original: "meshumar" (משומר); meaning both guarded and separated from the dregs</note>, meaning it is removed from the dregs by a strainer, and it is more refined and bright than it was before the squeezing. 

So it is with Man. When he was in the state of being "entirely good light," he still had the potential power to awaken the "husk" <note>term: "Kelipah" (husk/shell) — the kabbalistic term for the forces of evil that conceal divine light</note> in a hidden way. But now, through his sin, the evil husk was actually brought out—this is the Satan, this is the Evil Inclination <note>term: "Yetzer Hara"</note>, etc. Nevertheless, one who conquers and subdues it, canceling it entirely, then the evil passes away, and the soul's good is pure, bright, and clear without dregs. This is the "Perfect Man" who conquers his inclination. The Sages used the word "conquers" rather than "kills." This hints that he does not kill it, but rather subdues it under him to be good, turning the "matter" into "joy." This is a great concept: he overpowers it and purifies it until the "evil angel" is transformed into good. For example, he takes traits that are naturally "evil"—like jealousy, lust, and hatred—and instead of canceling them, he subdues them for the sake of good. He uses jealousy for "the jealousy of scribes" <note>which increases wisdom</note>, lust for the hidden and stored Torah, and hatred for the "hatred of wickedness," as it is written: "I hate them with a perfect hatred" <note>Psalm 139:22</note>. 

Behold, this is "very good." This is what is meant by "'Good' refers to the Good Inclination; 'Very Good' refers to the Evil Inclination," because then the evil causes the greatest good. Not only is the evil transformed, it is turned into actual good. This will happen in the future, after the refinement, the smelting, the "garments" [of skin], and the troubles that people suffer, which awaken them to repentance and cause the husks to cease. In the future, the Angel of Death will be slaughtered, and evil will be sweetened through the merit of the righteous who conquered their inclination and took it for holy service. Then "garments of skin" <note>original: "Ohr" (עור) spelled with an Ayin</note>—which implies "narrowness" or "suffering"—will be transformed into an "Eye" <note>original: "Ayin" (עין) — the same letter as skin</note> that sees. Through the power of the [suffering] eye, the vision will be magnified, and there will be an "advantage of light from the darkness." 

Not only will the world return to the original intention of being "garments of light," but there will even be an addition of light, for "eye to eye they shall see when the Lord returns to Zion" <note>Isaiah 52:8</note>. The "evil eye" of the garments of skin will return to being a "good eye." There will be such a great light that it was never perceived even by the prophets, as it is written: "No eye has seen, O God, beside You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. Our Sages said: "This refers to the wine guarded in its grapes since the six days of creation." This is exactly what I have said: the wine is "guarded" because the dregs have been removed from it. Then, the "garments of light" in the future will be even brighter because there will be no mixture of refuse in that goodness, not even in a hidden way. 

The phrase "from the six days of creation" also hints at a wondrous thing: Our Sages said that in the future, neither the Name nor the Throne will be complete until the time of Redemption. This is because the letters *Yod* and *Heh* [of the Divine Name] are missing, and the letter *Aleph* is missing from the word "Throne" <note>referring to Exodus 17:16 where "Throne" (Kise) is spelled without the Aleph and the Name of God is only "Yah"</note>. The matter is this: when the "Building" <note>term: "Binyan" — the structure of the six lower Sefirot</note>—that is, the six extremities—is rooted in Understanding <note>Binah</note>, and certainly from Understanding and above (which is included in the letters *Yod-Heh*), there is no touch of evil there. There is no grasp for the roots of the "princes of the nations" <note>angelic representatives of non-Jewish nations</note> except from the Building and below, which is included in the letters *Vav-Heh*—the "Beauty" <note>Tiferet</note> with the six extremities and "Kingship" <note>Malkhut</note>. As explained at length above, there is a grasp for the roots of the supernal princes there: from the side of Kindness <note>Chesed</note>, which was the Chariot for Abraham, came Ishmael; from the side of Strength <note>Gevurah</note>, the Chariot for Isaac, came Esau. So too the seventy princes are to the "right" and "left" of the Lord. From them are drawn all matters of the "husks," which are drawn from the letters of their root in the "Building of the Six Extremities," which are the secret of the "Six Days of Creation," as I have elaborated above.

However, Understanding <note>Binah</note>, which is the "Great Sabbath," the secret of the "World to Come" that is entirely Sabbath—there the root of the "Building" exists without any touch of evil. There they have no grasp. Regarding this it is said to Israel: "You are called Man" <note>Ezekiel 34:31</note>, in the secret of the Soul, which hints at the four "Faces" <note>Partzufim</note> in Understanding. In the future, all souls will be renewed and will rise higher and higher. This is the secret of "And the serpent was cunning" <note>Genesis 3:1</note>; the serpent found a root of a grasp in the secret of the "World of the Letter *Heh*," causing a separation between the letters *Vav* and *Heh*—meaning between Beauty and Kingship. The intention of the serpent was to cause a separation below between Adam and Eve, so that Adam would die and he (the serpent) would marry Eve. This caused a separation above in the Divine Union. In the future, the "garments of light" will return, for the serpent and its filth will be canceled. The "Wine"—hinting at the flow of divine influence that brings joy—will be "guarded." This is the meaning of "from the six days of creation," meaning
