<meta>This page continues the philosophical and mystical defense of the physical resurrection of the dead, specifically addressing the nature of the "World to Come" and responding to Maimonides' more spiritualized interpretation. It draws heavily from the 16th-century Kabbalistic work "Avodat HaKodesh" by Meir ibn Gabbai.</meta>

# House of David

If a person falls and dies, where is the "length of days" promised to them? And where is the "goodness" of those days? Rather, it must be interpreted as: "that your days may be long" <note>Exodus 20:12</note> in a world that is entirely long, and "that it may go well with you" in a world that is entirely good. If this were said regarding the World to Come <term>Olam HaBa; the afterlife</term> immediately following death, it would be neither "long" nor "good," for there is a limit and a measure to its duration and its goodness <note>The author argues that the intermediate state of the soul after death is temporary until the resurrection</note>, and their reward is destined to arise again in the Resurrection of the Dead. In this context, that intermediate world is not truly "long," and since it has a cessation, it is not an absolute good. Because of this, we ask: "where is the length of days for this one?" Rather, it must refer to the World to Come that follows the Resurrection of the Dead, which has no cessation or measure to its length or its goodness. Its existence is necessary based on the sages' statement that the Resurrection of the Dead is not dependent on it. When they said "a world that is entirely long and entirely good," they meant that this world comes after the Resurrection and is dependent on it because it follows it; it is the final reward for the commandments, given to the body and soul together. It is said in the Midrash: "There is no reward for the Torah except in the 'Last Day,'" as it says, "And she laughs at the last day" <note>Proverbs 31:25</note>. The World to Come that a person enters immediately after death is not worthy of being called the "Last Day," for the World to Come that follows the Resurrection comes after it. According to the view of Maimonides <note>original: "Rambam"</note> of blessed memory and those who follow him—who believe that death is decreed even for those who are resurrected—they would admit that the World to Come following their second death would be worthy of the name "Last Day," not the one immediately following a person's death in this world. 

If so, when the scripture says, "The righteous shall inherit the land forever" <note>Psalm 37:29</note>, the intention is that they will inherit the "Land of the Living" (which is the World to Come) without cessation, where they will merit the reward of the Torah and commandments in both body and soul. By saying "the branch of My planting" <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>, the verse explains that God will grant permanence and eternity to the body and soul together in that world. The reason He decrees this permanence and eternity is because the human is a "branch of the supernal planting," the secret of the Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah</term>, according to the secret of "The trees of the Lord are satisfied, the cedars of Lebanon which He planted" <note>Psalm 104:16</note>. Man was made in His image and likeness, as explained in the first part of this book; he shall bloom and multiply and be sustained in his Root, and from it, the Lord will draw down and emanate eternity upon him. 

After this, one cannot argue: "Since the World to Come has no use for the functions of the body, yet you decree permanence and eternity for it, this would imply—God forbid—that it is for nothing!" There is no "useless action" in the works of God. These "vessels" <note>the body parts</term> are made according to the design of the Chariot <term>Merkavah; the Divine Throne-Chariot</term>, the "Chariot of Him who rides upon the highest heavens from of old," the secret of Emanation. Therefore, it is necessary that these vessels exist eternally, because they draw their existence from their Source and Root. Their existence does not depend on eating and drinking, but rather on their cleaving to their Root. 

One can understand from this the nature of prayer at that time, which is the time when the Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer HaRa</term> is abolished—the very thing that prevents that cleaving which causes permanence and eternity. Because the level of Resurrection is a sublime matter, it is necessary to decree permanence for the body to demonstrate its attachment to the Divine. If the body lived and then departed again, this would imply a weakness or a "diminishing of the Image," God forbid. To instill this deeply in the hearts of believers, it was hinted at in the common saying of the sage Rav: "The World to Come is not like this world. In the World to Come, there is no eating, no drinking, no procreation, no business, no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition; rather, the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term>, as it is said, 'And they beheld God, and they ate and drank'" <note>Exodus 24:11</note>. 

I call out to you, O men! Look and see: if the World to Come has no physical body or form, why would Rav leave us with such "useless" words by saying "not like this world... there is no eating, etc."? Who does not know that all these functions belong only to a body? If there were no body there, all its functions would naturally be cancelled; would he come to tell us such obvious, empty things? And why would this be a "common saying" in his mouth? But if we accept that there *is* a body and form there, then the innovation Rav comes to teach us is very great: that even though there is a body and form, there are no physical functions, because the body does not need eating and drinking for its existence, but only its cleaving to its Root. Then the Supernal Light will rest upon it and sustain it, according to the secret of "in the light of the King's countenance is life" <note>Proverbs 16:15</note>. This is what he meant by "the righteous sit"—this "sitting" refers to the permanence decreed for them. "And their crowns are on their heads"—this is the crown of glory that sustains them, which is the joy mentioned in the verse "and eternal joy shall be upon their heads" <note>Isaiah 35:10</note>, for they become like a mirror and a Throne of Glory, as the lower structure reflects the upper structure.

This is the permanence and "covering of the ship" <note>original: "כפרה את הספינה"; likely a metaphorical reference to protection or atonement</note>. In the chapter "Hannah" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 31a</note>, Rabbi Yochanan said: "In the future, the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said, 'Everyone who is called by My name, whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him'" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. The righteous man is the foundation of the world, called "All Glory" <note>original: "כל כבוד"</note>, for "All" (Kol) refers to the connection of heaven and earth. Those who cleave to Him are called "Righteous" <term>Tzadikim</term> after His name, because they are the connectors and they awaken heaven and earth. He says they are made in the likeness of the Supernal Glory, for the Supernal Glory contains "Creation, Formation, and Action" <term>Beriyah, Yetzirah, Asiyah; the three lower worlds</term>. So too, in the righteous person below, all these were created to rectify the Glory below. Behold, they are made according to the design of the Menorah <term>the seven-branched candelabra</term> which is included in the Name of God for those who know His secret. In the future to come, that Name will rest upon them and within them to sustain them eternally, and then they will truly be called by the Name of God. Just as permanence and eternity are necessary and mandatory for the Name of God, so it shall be for the righteous, because they testify to Him and He is publicized through them.

Furthermore, Rabbi Eleazar said: "In the future, 'Holy' will be said before the righteous just as it is said before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said, 'And it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion and he who remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy'" <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>. This refers to the permanence decreed for them, as the sages said in the chapter *Helek* <note>Talmud, Sanhedrin 92a</note>: "The righteous whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to resurrect shall not return to their dust, as it says, 'And it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion... shall be called holy.' Just as the Holy One is eternal, so they are eternal." And if you ask: what will they do during those thousand years in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to renew His world, as it is said, "And the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day" <note>Isaiah 2:11</note>? The Holy One, Blessed be He, makes them wings like eagles, and they fly over the face of the waters, as it is said, "Therefore we will not fear, though the earth be removed" <note>Psalm 46:2</note>. And should you say they will suffer, the scripture says, "But those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles" <note>Isaiah 40:31</note>. 

The intention is that in the World to Come following the Resurrection, the world will return to its original state and uprightness. The righteous will exist in body and soul and will never be separated before Him, for they will enjoy the Supernal Radiance and the Clear Light, and this light will sustain them. This is the meaning of "enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence"—this is the "eating," the true nourishment that provides eternal existence. We have already seen that even the soul is called "body" in the words of those empty of light <note>perhaps referring to those who misunderstand the spiritual nature of the soul or the physical nature of the resurrection</note>. He who is the purest of the pure and more spiritual is nourished by something even finer and purer. Material people were sustained by the Manna, which was absorbed into the limbs; it was a product of the Light and the Supernal Radiance that descended and became physical for their sake, to elevate their souls. And what "elevated their souls"? That which they perceived at the Sea, etc. Elijah and Enoch the prophets, who rose higher than the general category and were unique in their knowledge of their Creator, did not require the *product* of the light but were sustained by the light itself, which is the "Life of the Heavens." We too believe with a faithful faith, as members of the World to Come, that they will be sustained by that light eternally; it is the sustainment of the Supernal Will and His spirit within them. This is what Moses our Teacher hinted at when he said, "And He afflicted you, and suffered you to hunger, and fed you with manna... that He might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of the Lord" <note>Deuteronomy 8:3</note>. He explained that the Manna was not naturally designed to sustain them for such a long time by its own nature, but the purpose of that food was to teach them that even though bread seems to satisfy and nourish, the life and permanence do not come from it, but from the Will of God that cleaves to it and sustains them. To establish them in this faith, He fed them Manna, which is "that which proceeds from the mouth of the Lord," according to the secret of "Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you" <note>Exodus 16:4</note>. It became physical and they were nourished by it, as if they were nourished by the "mouth of the Lord" and sustained by His spirit. If they had been nourished by the light itself, from which that Manna was produced, they would have merited the elevation of their souls and cleaving to that light until they were sustained in body and soul eternally. The "Children of the World to Come" who merit to enjoy and be nourished by that light will acquire eternity and merit existence in body and soul. This is what the sages meant by "they do not return to their dust," for then they will truly be "His handiwork to be glorified" <note>Isaiah 60:21</note> because of the permanence decreed for them. This is the true glorification—that the works of His hands are not lost or destroyed, being the "branch of His planting." Regarding the "wings," our Great Teacher explained it as a parable for the soul's angelic state when it is clothed in the body, so that it is not abolished when the physical elements are abolished. It is clarified, then, that the World to Come mentioned by our Sages when they said "All Israel has a portion in the World to Come" refers to the World to Come that follows the Resurrection. Thus far are the words of *Avodat HaKodesh*.

## And regarding
the four times mentioned in the "Yotzer" prayer for Sabbath <note>a liturgical poem recited before the Shema</note>, which were brought as proof: Maimonides <note>Rambam</note> wrote as I brought above. Regarding this, the author of *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Meir ibn Gabbai</note> answered in the 41st chapter of the section on "Service" (Avoda): Let that arrangement not be difficult for our Great Teacher, for it agrees with his view and is against the view of Maimonides. There are several reasons for this: 
First, because the World to Come is the hope of all who hope in their service and the success of their deeds and Torah study in this world. The World to Come following the Resurrection is linked to *this* world because the former is the purpose of the latter. 
Second, just as the service was performed in both body and soul in this world, so the receiving of reward must be in both body and soul. This is not possible in the "World of Souls" <note>the intermediate state</note> but is possible in the World to Come following the Resurrection; therefore, the prayer links them together. There is no place to mention the Garden of Eden <term>Gan Eden</term> here.
Third, the intention of those who established the prayer was to include the times when the wonders of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are seen, such as the Resurrection. This wonder will be great and famous among the people of the World to Come following the Resurrection, as they will exist eternally in body and soul. This was the intention even for this world, were it not for the sin <note>of Adam</note>, and this "crown" is destined to return to its former glory in the world. Therefore, the prayer links them together to say that what was lacking in this world will be completed in that world.

And that pleasure is also naturally drawn from the Torah and its commandments, and so it truly is. If the Dispenser of Rewards <note>God</note> had explicitly designated the spiritual reward, it would have been double and more complete, as we would judge it by an "all the more so" logic <term>Kal VaChomer; a logical inference from a minor premise to a major one</term> from the physical promise, since both of these are drawn from the commandment and are naturally necessitated by grace. This is the path taken by the work *Holy Service* <note>original: *Avodat HaKodesh* by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> in answering this difficulty. The pious Rabbi Joseph Ya'avetz wrote similarly in his book *Foundation of the Faith*. I have already revealed my opinion above regarding this inquiry, and "the words of the Torah are like a hammer that shatters a rock" <note>a reference to Jeremiah 23:29, meaning the Torah can be interpreted in many ways</note>, and "these and those are the words of the living God." This is especially true because the wise man is happy <note>original: *ashrei*</note> when he contemplates and understands from his own knowledge that his words and the words of his predecessors approach a single root; and the wise person will understand.

<margin>I have revealed my opinion above regarding this inquiry, and "the words of the Torah are like a hammer that shatters rock," and "these and those are the words of the living God." This is especially true because the wise man is happy when he contemplates and understands from his own knowledge that his words and the words of his predecessors approach a single root; and the wise person will understand.</margin>

## Behold, these goods described in the portion *Bechukotai* <note>Leviticus 26:3–46, detailing blessings for following God’s laws</note>, which have not yet been fulfilled until the future time (may it come speedily in our days), you will find to be gradual levels in the matter of the increase of goodness. It begins with physical satiation, then the matter of peace, and then the greatest of all promises: "And I will set my Tabernacle among you" <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>. This is the secret of the Divine Presence dwelling among the lower beings, just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired at the beginning of creation—but "man in his glory does not endure" <note>Psalm 49:13</note>. However, in the future, it will be eternal, and it will fulfill the verse "and he shall live forever" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>, for the attachment will be to the Tree of Life. Then, "I will walk among you and I will be your God" <note>Leviticus 26:12</note> will be fulfilled, for we will essentially become the Chariot <term>Merkavah; the divine vehicle or throne</term>, reaching a level higher than that of the angels. At that time, it will be said of Jacob and Israel, "What has God wrought?" <note>Numbers 23:23</note>, for the eternal perfection will be in both the body and the soul, which are represented by the names Jacob and Israel.

## A great dispute has already fallen regarding the final eternal perfection: will it be for the soul alone, or for both the body and the soul? Maimonides <note>Rambam</note> and his followers believe it is for the soul alone. However, the Sages of Truth <term>Kabbalists</term> believe, like Nachmanides <note>Ramban</note>, that eternity is for both the body and the soul. Just as the service of God was performed, so shall the reward be received. The service was performed by both body and soul in this world; therefore, the receipt of reward will be by both body and soul. For this reason, there will be a great Resurrection of the Dead, where they will exist eternally as body and soul. This is called the "World to Come" <term>Olam HaBa</term> in the words of our Sages—a world that is entirely life, a world that is entirely good. Concerning this, it is said: "Happy is he who performs them, man shall live by them" <note>Leviticus 18:5</note>, which Onkelos translated <note>into Aramaic</note> as "he shall live by them for eternal life." This World to Come is the "World of Life," meaning eternal life in body and soul, ascending from level to level without interruption, but in eternity. These matters are discussed at length in the works of various authors, particularly in the book *Holy Service*. For the sake of brevity, I will copy a bit of their words. Maimonides (may his memory be a blessing) wrote in the eighth chapter of the *Laws of Repentance*:

<margin>Maimonides, of blessed memory, regarding the World to Come in the 8th chapter of the Laws of Repentance:</margin>

"The World to Come has no body or physical form, but only the souls of the righteous alone without a body, like the ministering angels. Since there is no physical form, there is no eating, no drinking, and none of the things that human bodies need in this world. Nor does any of the things that happen to bodies in this world occur there, such as sitting, standing, sleep, death, sadness, laughter, and the like. Thus the early Sages said: 'In the World to Come there is no eating, no drinking, and no procreation, but the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence.' Behold, it has been clarified to you that there is no body there because there is no eating or drinking. And that which was said, 'the righteous sit,' is a riddle, meaning that the souls of the righteous exist there without labor or weariness. Likewise, 'their crowns on their heads' means the knowledge they knew, because of which they merited the life of the World to Come, exists with them, and that is their crown—just as Solomon said, 'with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him.' And it says, 'everlasting joy shall be upon their heads,' yet joy is not a physical body that rests on a head; so too, the 'crown' mentioned by the Sages here is knowledge. And what is meant by 'enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence'? That they know and grasp the truth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which they did not know while in the dark and lowly body." These are his words there. One should believe that although the primary reward is for the soul alone, there is yet another physical reward in this world for the Days of the Messiah, and this occurs during the Resurrection of the Dead, when the completely righteous will live. The reason for this, in his opinion, is either to publicize the miracles of God and faith in Him in the world, or so that they may attain some physical pleasure then, similar to the days in which they suffered or more, as the Higher Wisdom decrees, or so that they may acquire more perfection than they acquired at first, when they could not reach the level appropriate for them due to the oppressors and the yoke of exile. However, in any case, according to his opinion—as he stated in the chapter *Helek* in his commentary on the Mishnah and as found in his *Treatise on the Resurrection of the Dead*—they will die after they live and return to their dust. Then their souls will merit a higher level in the World to Come than the secret state they were in before the resurrection, according to what they grasped of the truth of God in their second life. In his opinion, it is regarding this that they said "the World to Come has no eating, etc.," because there is no body or physical form. For if there were a body and physical form, the organs would be in vain, since they would not be used for fleshly functions like eating, drinking, and procreation. In the *Treatise on the Resurrection*, he said that one cannot bring proof from the wonders we find with Moses our teacher and Elijah, who stood for a long time without eating or drinking while in a body, to say that the miraculous resurrection in the World to Come will be a body that endures for an unmeasured or very long time. According to the "Center of Truth," the reason is that if the physical powers were suspended for them, it was only temporary, and thus the organs were not in vain, for they used those organs before the wonder and after it. But in the World to Come, where there is no eating or drinking or other bodily uses, to say that God would create a new thing where there would be bodies and their organs would be useless—this is impossible. For the Wise Creator does not do anything with His hand in vain, God forbid. Therefore, every intelligent person must believe that in the World to Come there is no body or physical form, but only souls alone. This is the summary of his opinion and what emerges from his words.

<margin>The Ra'avad has already critiqued him.</margin>

The Ra'avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David</note> has already critiqued him and wrote concerning this: "The words of this man in my eyes are close to those who say there is no resurrection of the dead for bodies, but only for souls. By my life! This was not the opinion of the Sages of the Talmud, for they said: 'In the future, the righteous are destined to stand in their garments,' using an 'all the more so' logic from a grain of wheat. They also used to command their children: 'Do not bury me in white clothes lest I do not merit... nor in black lest I merit...' and the righteous said that the righteous do not return to dust but stand in their physical forms. They also said they rise with their blemishes and are then healed. All these prove that they stand in their physical forms. But it is possible that the Creator will make their bodies strong and healthy like the bodies of angels or the body of Elijah, and the crowns will be according to their literal and plain meaning, not a metaphor." These are his words. Thus, Maimonides believes perfection is for the soul—whether now at the death of the righteous when their souls merit the Garden of Eden, or after the Resurrection of the Dead, when they will live to acquire more perfection, then die, and their souls will reach a higher level of eternity. Those who critique Maimonides also sought to support their view from the version of the *Yotzer* prayer for the Sabbath. They mentioned four expressions regarding the change in receiving reward, which seem to be four types of reward. It says: "There is none to be compared to You, and there is none beside You; there is nothing but You, and who is like You?" They explained these four expressions as referring to four distinct times for the recipients of reward. "There is none to be compared to You, O Lord our God, in this world; and there is none beside You, our King, for the life of the World to Come." These are the two general times for receiving reward. Even so, he chose the reward of this world to mention first. Then it says, "There is nothing but You, our Redeemer, for the Days of the Messiah," and afterward the choice reward of the World to Come after death, which is the Resurrection of the Dead. He mentioned "the life of the World to Come" after "this world" because it comes immediately after death for each individual before the Days of the Messiah and the Resurrection. This supports Maimonides' view more, for if it were according to Nachmanides, he should have mentioned the Garden of Eden after this world, as that is the level that follows this world, and not "the life of the World to Come," which is the final level according to him. But since he did not mention the Garden of Eden at all, it appears that the term "World to Come" includes all levels that come to a person after death, and he mentioned "the life of the World to Come" as the most chosen of them all.

<margin>And the opinion of Nachmanides, with the agreement of the Sages of Truth, is:</margin>

## And the opinion of Nachmanides, with the agreement of the Sages of Truth, is that the world that comes to a person now after death is truly the "World of Souls." For the body, which comes from a "putrid drop" <note>a common rabbinic term for semen/physical origin</note> and the filth of the Serpent, is consumed. The "World to Come" after death now is called the World of Souls. However, after the Resurrection of the Dead, when they will be in body and soul, and the body is refined and purified until it becomes entirely light, then the resurrection will be an eternal world in body and soul. To strengthen the words of Nachmanides and refute the proofs of Maimonides, I will copy the words of the *Holy Service* from Chapter 42 of the "Laws of Service." It says there: "We have learned: All Israel has a portion in the World to Come, as it is said, 'And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.'" The "World to Come" mentioned here is the one that follows the Resurrection of the Dead, not the one that comes to a person immediately after death. A proof for this is the verse they cited, "they shall inherit the land forever," meaning forever without interruption, for there is no measure to the length of days and the goodness in that world. In the tractates *Kiddushin* (Chapter 1) and *Chullin* (the chapter on "Sending the Nest"), it is taught: Rabbi Jacob says, "There is no single commandment in the Torah whose reward is specified at its side that does not depend on the Resurrection of the Dead. Regarding honoring one's father and mother, it is written: 'that your days may be long and that it may go well with you.' Regarding sending away the mother bird, it is written: 'that it may go well with you and that you may prolong your days.' Behold, a case where a father told his son: 'Go up to the loft and bring me young birds.' He went up, sent away the mother, and took the young. On his return, he fell

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the nature of the "World to Come" and the Messianic era, shifting from the reward of the soul to the cosmic cycles of time (Shmita and Jubilee) and the specific laws that will apply in the future, such as sacrifices and the cities of refuge.</meta>

->## House of David<-

The restoration of the world <note>original: "Tikkun HaOlam"</note>. Regarding why the years of the Sabbatical cycle <term>Shmita; the seventh year in a seven-year agricultural cycle</term> are called "one world" in contrast to the world of the Jubilee <term>Yovel; the fiftieth year following seven Sabbatical cycles</term>, which lasts forty-nine thousand years. For in forty-nine [thousand], the entire world [cycle] is completed. The word "Jubilee" hints at the result, and the cause hints at the secret... these are the words of the author of *The System* <note>original: "Baal HaMaarechet," referring to the book *Ma'arekhet Ha-Elohut*, a 14th-century Kabbalistic text</note>. And these are the words of the Rabbi... The table, etc. and the seven days of the weeks hint at the Sabbatical cycle in the creation... The explanation is that the hint refers to being within the forty-nine years in general of all the Sabbatical cycles... The matter of the Sabbatical cycle hints at what will be, for the Sabbatical cycle hints at what will be consumed from the years of the cycles...

The six years hint at the seven spheres <term>Sefirot; the ten divine attributes or emanations in Kabbalah</term>. For regarding the matter of the degree... long... from the essence... The intention is that it is appropriate that the workers should rest from their labor. The essence of the intention... that the Sabbatical cycle is like the Sabbath of the seventh year; so too the workers [rest] from the thousands [of years]... and we see that "a thousand years in Your eyes are like a passing yesterday" <note>Psalm 90:4</note>. Also, our Rabbi Saadia <note>Saadia Gaon, a 10th-century philosopher</note> of blessed memory... and its benefit... and the essence... his actions in the whole world... and since all of them... the world will return to its arrangement and its foundation as it was before its existence. And behold, just as they said regarding the work of the days, that there were seven days of creation, so too it was shown to us that its existence would be for seventy thousand [years], a Sabbath... as it is said regarding the Sabbath of Creation, so too regarding the seventh, a "Sabbath to the Lord." For it is a day of rest, and the "End of Worlds" <note>original: "Sof HaOlamim"</note> is judged upon it. The scripture says: "It shall be one day which is known to the Lord, neither day nor night" <note>Zechariah 14:7</note>. Afterward, there is a seventh day of the world, and the reason is that in all the work of creation, it says of each day "and there was evening and there was morning," but regarding the Sabbath, it does not say "evening and morning." This is the secret of the... called "Sabbath," where the souls and the spiritual ones are gathered from above... this will be after the years are completed... and also in the scriptures, it is proven without doubt... as it is written: "Woe to his day, and who can live from his wrath?" If there were voices called without prayer... for there was no first morning, there would be no second one. And it is written: "They shall be dismayed, they shall fail, they shall melt away..." and they shall hope for the world to stand. And so "they shall stand before Me forever," meaning for the "world" of the Jubilee. And when it says "for the length of days" without the knowledge of the end, it means they have no end, like "the days of his life," the King David forever. And "forever" <note>original: "Le-olam"</note> is said regarding a time that has no after or end, as in "He shall reign forever and ever." This is the foundation... established the earth on its foundations, it shall not falter forever and ever. Also, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Every place where it says 'forever and ever' <note>original: *Sela*, *Va'ed*</note> has no interruption." One can interpret that "it shall not falter" refers to His glory... but all the time of the world's existence, even though according to the opinion of our Sages, every mention of "forever and ever" refers to the length of time... but "forever and ever" is a name for the sanctuary of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which is called "forever and ever"... just as the Lord God is "forever and ever." And this is the intention: that the verse says the Holy One, Blessed be He, established the earth on its foundations so that the Name called "forever and ever" shall not falter, as it were. It was not called by the name of glory, but rather the righteous ones who were chosen, and by the glory they shall stand. And it called the upper land "ever" <note>original: *Va'ed*</note>... therefore, one must believe that the existence of the world is from its Sustainer... but every end is like the first... and there is no doubt that the one who returns to its foundation, which returns and precedes... and the time of the gathering of the days and the division of the foundations shall establish it quickly.

<column-break/>

The first man <note>Adam</note> was changed in his nature, and he will return to his old self in the days of the King Messiah, for then the Supernal Intention will be completed. These are the words of the Rabbi, the author of *The Holy Service* <note>Meir ibn Gabbai</note>. But it seems more likely to me the way I wrote above... for it is possible that "Simeon" does not come in the sixth millennium, and this is what [Rabbi] Yohanan was discussing afterward. This will be the answer to a difficulty that has been hard for me for years regarding the Torah portion of *Shoftim* <term>Deuteronomy 16:18–21:9</term>, where it says: "And if the Lord your God enlarges your border... then you shall add three more cities" <note>Deuteronomy 19:8-9, referring to the Cities of Refuge for accidental killers</note>. Rashi explains: "Behold, there are nine: three on the other side of the Jordan, three in the land of Canaan, and three for the future to come." And it is a wonder! For when perfection comes, surely no evil will happen, as evil will be eliminated from the world and there will be only absolute good. One can bring proof for this from the Midrash on Psalms <note>original: *Midrash Tehillim*</note> regarding the "Psalm of Thanksgiving": Rabbi Yohanan said in the name of Rabbi Menachem of Gallia: "All prayers will be nullified in the time to come, but the Thanksgiving prayers will not be nullified. All sacrifices will be nullified in the time to come, but the Thanksgiving offering <note>original: *Korban Todah*</note> will not be nullified." The student of Jacob wrote in *The Secrets of the Festival of Weeks*: "You already know that sin causes the distancing of the Land, and therefore sacrifices were needed to sweeten the world and to draw from the Source to bestow influence, to bring the attributes closer and to suppress every evil thing. But in the future to come, the time when the evil inclination <note>original: *Yetzer HaRa*</note> is nullified and 'sinners shall cease from the earth' <note>Psalm 104:35</note>, there will be no need for a sacrifice, for the attribute of Wrath will be elevated into Mercy. On that day, the Lord shall be one and His name one. The Thanksgiving offering is not nullified because it does not come because of a sin or a need, but as an example of the world to come." But there will be peace in everything, for "there will no longer be a trader in the house of the Lord of Hosts," and "the kingdom shall be the Lord's," and "the Lord shall be King." Those who delve deep into wisdom said that the reason the Thanksgiving offering is not nullified is that it is needed to guide the souls when they leave their exile of judgment and ascend in beauty to the place of freedom and the place of thanksgiving. This is like the four types of people who must give thanks <note>Psalm 107; those who survived sea travel, the desert, illness, or imprisonment</note> when they arrive home in peace, saying "Let them give thanks to the Lord for His goodness and His wonders to the children of men," for they have come in peace to the world of souls... and from there "their return is to the Heights." So it is written in *The Holy Service* in the section on Service, chapter 43: "In the World to Come after the Resurrection, there is no sin, no death, and no funeral; there are no sin offerings or guilt offerings. No sacrifice [will exist] in the future except for the Daily Offerings <note>original: *Tamid*</note>, the Additional Offerings <note>original: *Musaf*</note>, and the Thanksgiving Offering, which will never be nullified. For sin and guilt offerings come because of sin, and obviously, where there is no sin, why would they come?" And in the *Midrash Shocher Tov*: "Enter His gates with thanksgiving... Rabbi Phineas said in the name of Rabbi Levi: All sacrifices are nullified, but the Thanksgiving offering is never nullified... as it says, 'I will pay my thanksgivings to You'—two: one corresponding to prayer and one corresponding to sacrifice... and it says, 'The voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of those who say: Give thanks to the Lord'—these are the eighteen prayers of thanksgiving—'and they bring the thanksgiving to the house of the Lord'—this is the Thanksgiving offering." The secret of the matter is that sin is what causes the distancing of the Supernal Land and the "cutting" and separation of the Unity. For this, sacrifices were needed to sweeten the world and open the Source to shine its light, to bring those who are far close, and to distance every evil and impure thing from the Sanctuary. In the future to come, when the evil inclination is eradicated, behold, 'sinners and sins shall cease from the land,' and there will be no more need for a sacrifice, for His attribute of Judgment will be elevated through Mercy, and 'the Lord shall be King.' On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one. See there. I have a difficulty with the aforementioned verse: "And you shall add three more cities." Rabbi Doroni explained "Keni, Kenizi, and Kadmoni" <note>the lands of these three tribes promised to Abraham but not yet fully possessed</note> which are Ammon, Moab, and Edom. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, promised ten nations to our father Abraham, but He only gave seven, and in the future, He will give three more. Will there be a boundary to the matter? Is it not written: "He shall rule from sea to sea"? For certainly the Messiah will rule from one end of the world to the other, and it is illogical to say that only these three nations include all the nations of the world. It is possible to say that the Messiah will rule from sea to sea, meaning all will be under him and pay him tribute, but the ten nations are his entirely. However, even this is forced—that there would remain any kingdom or authority among the nations. Therefore, it seems that all the great successes will not happen immediately upon the arrival of the Redeemer, but only over time as knowledge increases in Israel and they reach the level of "Garments of Light." Then the "husk" <term>Kelipah; the Kabbalistic term for the forces of evil or impurity</term> will be nullified entirely, and "He shall rule from sea to sea" will be fulfilled. Then all sacrifices will be nullified except for thanksgiving, and then they will not need cities of refuge. I found in the Jerusalem Talmud <note>original: *Yerushalmi*</note>, tractate *Ma'aser Sheni*, in the Mishnah: "A condition was made: whenever the Temple is rebuilt, the matter will return to how it was." It says there: Rabbi Aha said: "This means that the Holy Temple is destined to be built before the Kingdom of the House of David." With this, we answer why they needed a condition—let the Court <note>original: *Beit Din*</note> make a regulation as they wish when the Temple is built! Or perhaps they worried there might not be a "Son of David" <note>the Messiah</note> who was as great in wisdom and number as they were to nullify their words. Because it is difficult... the Court of the Messiah will not be greater than them. Therefore, they had to say that the Temple would be built while the "Son of David" had not yet come. This might happen in the time of the Messiah son of Joseph <term>Mashiach ben Yosef; a precursor to the final Messiah who undergoes suffering</term>. Now we can say that these things and their like are said regarding the time before the arrival of the Messiah son of David, and Blessed is He who knows. With this, a great difficulty is also answered: the building of the Third Temple. It mentions there sin offerings and guilt offerings, which is difficult according to the aforementioned Midrash that all sacrifices will be nullified except for the Daily Offering. Also there, in Ezekiel, the "impurity of the dead" <note>ritual impurity from a corpse</note> is mentioned for a father and mother, yet is it not written: "He will swallow up death forever"? Therefore, it seems right to explain everything as speaking of the time of the Messiah son of Joseph, while the great promises are for the time of the Messiah son of David. And Blessed is He who knows. After I wrote this, I found in the *Notes on the Holy Writings* of the Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, 16th-century Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, that he was also aroused by the matter of the three cities of refuge in the future. He answered in another way, and I will copy his language: "'And if the Lord enlarges your border... you shall add three more cities.' What is the difficulty? After our Messiah comes, it is appropriate that there should be no murderers, as it is written 'Nation shall not lift up sword against nation,' so how can it say 'And you shall add'?"

# And regarding
this matter, I must inform you that although we said that when our righteous Messiah comes, the world will return to its proper state and become eternal, nevertheless, it is hinted that there will be progressions within that eternity from one level of existence <term>Olam; literally "world" or "eon"</term> to another. This follows the secret of the saying: "The world exists for six thousand years, and for one thousand it is desolate" <note>Talmud, Sanhedrin 97a</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory said in the chapter *Helek*: just as the Sabbatical year <term>Shmita</term> waives debts and lets the land rest one year in seven, so too the world rests for one thousand years out of seven thousand. It is well known what the Kabbalists have written regarding the secret of the Sabbatical cycles and the Jubilee: six Sabbatical cycles followed by the Jubilee, which corresponds to the secret of "Understanding" <term>Binah; the third Sefirah, associated with the divine womb and liberation</term>. This is what the Zohar hinted at regarding the fifty years of the Jubilee—corresponding to fifty thousand generations in which the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to restore the spirit, and so on. Indeed, in each of these Sabbatical cycles, there is an addition of goodness beyond what existed in the one before it.

# And this
is what the Sages of blessed memory said: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan that all the prophets only prophesied regarding the days of the Messiah; but as for the World to Come <term>Olam Ha-Ba</term>, "no eye has seen it, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. This differs from the view of Samuel, who said: "There is no difference between this world and the days of the Messiah except for the end of subjugation to foreign kingdoms," as it is written, "For the poor shall never cease out of the land" <note>Deuteronomy 15:11</note>. Behold, the World to Come, which is the time of the Great Resurrection of the Dead occurring in this Jubilee year, is when "every man shall return to his ancestral possession" <note>Leviticus 25:13</note>. This seventh cycle possesses a superior level of spiritual eternity even greater than the days of the Messiah. Nonetheless, both eras involve the union of body and soul.

# Now
it appears from Samuel’s opinion that nothing new will be created in the days of the King Messiah beyond how the world functions today. Maimonides <note>original: "Rambam"</note>, of blessed memory, leaned toward this view in several places in the *Laws of Kings and Their Wars*, where he wrote: "Let it not enter your mind that in the days of the Messiah any part of the natural order of the world will be nullified, or that there will be some innovation in the work of Creation; rather, the world follows its natural course." However, I say with fear, trembling, and awe: it is possible that Samuel's intention only applied until the completion of these six thousand years. But afterward, Samuel would agree with everything we have said. Or perhaps even within the sixth millennium, Samuel would agree with our words regarding the revelations from the coming of the Messiah onward—that the righteous will merit "new souls." He was speaking only of those souls born before the Messiah’s arrival, who still possess the desires of this world until the Great Resurrection. However, the spiritual revelations of holiness will not be governed by the "wrath of the adversary" <note>a reference to the Evil Inclination or the forces of chaos</note>. Thus it is written, "Happy is he who waits and reaches" <note>Daniel 12:12</note>; happy are those who merit to live through the transition from death to eternal life, remaining alive and enduring. Thus, Samuel and Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba each spoke of a different stage and do not actually disagree. Though the Talmud says they differ, there is a distinction, as each speaks of a different matter.

The author of *The Holy Service* <note>original: "Avodat HaKodesh," a 16th-century work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> explained Samuel’s words differently in the section "The Purpose of Service." He suggests we can resolve this by saying Samuel meant God would not innovate anything *outside* of nature, but rather things will return to their natural perfection as they were at the beginning of their existence and creation. It is known that at the start of Creation, the world was perfectly satisfied for man’s benefit and pleasure. Life was intended to be eternal, but man's sin caused the nature of the world to change for him and all who followed, leading to death. As the scripture testifies: "And now, lest he put forth his hand and take also of the Tree of Life, and eat, and live forever" <note>Genesis 3:22</note>. Our Sages said that once man sinned, the Holy One diminished him. It appears from all this that man originally had the potential for all perfection. Just as man and his wife were punished, so too the earth was punished, as it says: "Cursed is the ground for your sake; in sorrow shall you eat of it... thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to you" <note>Genesis 3:17-18</note>. The earth was punished and no longer gave its full strength as was implanted in it at the start of Creation. The prophets testify that in the future, these qualities and perfections will return to their original nature and completeness which existed before they were diminished by sin. This is what they meant by saying the King desires "the fruit of desire"—to give to the earth as it was at the start of Creation, and "the earth shall yield its increase and the heavens shall give their dew." Because of man's sin, these were limited; but they will be restored to settle and order all things back to their freshness and repair. Emerging from their ruin caused by sin, they will return to their fullness as the Creator intended. 

Hanina said: "Sing, O heavens, for the Lord has done it" <note>Isaiah 44:23</note>. This refers to the restoration of the luminaries which were dimmed because of sin. "Shout, you lower parts of the earth" refers to the fruits of the earth and the trees, and the curse of the ground. He continues: "Break forth into singing, you mountains, O forest, and every tree therein," explaining the reason: "For the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and glorified Himself in Israel." At that time, all things will return to their repair, and all deficiencies will be filled. This happens when the sin that caused it all is wiped away, as preceded in the text: "I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions." For the ancient sin caused the corruption of both the upper and lower worlds. When they return to their original state as intended by the Higher Wisdom, that perfection is their "song" and "joy." All the words of the prophets and those who spoke with the Holy Spirit regarding this matter carry this same meaning. Doubtless, Samuel agrees that the world does not function the same after the sin as it did before, for sin brings death and world corruption. He believes the ultimate divine intention for Creation has not yet been fulfilled, but it must eventually be achieved.

**In** any case, this has not arrived yet, and will not until the one who holds the right of judgment is revealed. Then the original dominion—the dominion of the Higher Will and Desire—will be restored. This settles the statement of Rabbi Yochanan: the good things the prophets foretold are indeed "new" in the sense that they have not been seen since before Adam sinned. Samuel’s view is that these "new" things are simply the world returning to its original nature and custom as it was at the beginning of Creation, before the sin. And when...

Thus, it is given to the diligent, for according to the hint to the transcriber of the words of the *System of Divinity*... and in order that they may live through it... The words of the author of *The System* <note>original: "Baal HaMaarechet"</note> regarding the festival of Sukkot <term>The Feast of Tabernacles</term>: for the dimensions of the hints of Sukkot appear because the Sukkah <term>ritual booth</term> is like a protective covering... "Behold I create new heavens and a new earth" <note>Isaiah 65:17</note>... the "Crown" will be established as the "Head of Understanding" <term>Rosh Binah</term>... this is hinted at in the beginning of Genesis... the seven circuits... every day one circuit, and on the seventh day seven circuits... the seven days of creation... and the seventh circuit is the Sabbath to the Lord... the day that is entirely Sabbath and rest for eternal life... the dominion of the Great Jubilee... and regarding this Great Sabbath, the prophet said: "The light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of the seven days" <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>... meaning the attributes will be hidden in the "Crown" <term>Keter</term>... on the seventh day... the great foundations... they will be like the light... this is the matter of what we say in the Blessing of the New Moon: "A crown of beauty to those who are borne [from the womb]"... for she [the moon/nation] is the unique one... in the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will renew His world... since the Torah was given with seven [voices]... the Torah writes to count seven years seven times, which is forty-nine years, corresponding to the seven circuits.

### House of God, House of Wisdom

He is the Creator of the heavens and those who dwell in them. In every single matter, there must be some hint to the power of a single word that can be used in two ways. For example, why did the Sages not choose a clearer language that refers to the past? <note>The author is questioning why many blessings use the present tense participle "Borei" (Creates) instead of the past tense "Bara" (Created).</note>

<margin>House of God: And since</margin>
And since this has come to my hand, I will tell the reason for this matter: why we bless "Who **creates** <note>Hebrew: *Borei*</note> the illuminations of the fire" and not "**created**" <note>Hebrew: *Bara*</note>, which would be more linguistically clear. The *Tosafot* <note>Medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> wrote there in the tractate of *Berakhot* that this follows the language of the Bible. But I say there is a secret in this matter. Behold, it is stated there that the Schools of Shammai and Hillel disagree regarding "illumination" <note>singular: *ma'or*</note> and "illuminations" <note>plural: *meorei*</note>. The School of Shammai believes there is only one light in the fire, while the School of Hillel believes there are many lights in the fire. Rashi explains this refers to the red, white, and greenish flames. One might ask: did Shammai not see that there are many colors in the fire's illuminations? Furthermore, there is a great matter regarding "created" versus "creates," about which they do not disagree. Nevertheless, we see the version of Shammai was "Who **created** the **illumination** of the fire," while Hillel's version was "Who **creates** the **illuminations** of the fire." "Both these and those are the words of the Living God." <note>A famous Talmudic phrase indicating that multiple opposing views can both hold divine truth.</note>

It is known that "Emanation" <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah</term> is like a flame bound to a coal, and it is all a secret of unique unity. Even the white, the red, and the green—which represent the Line of Kindness, the Line of Judgment, and the Line of Mercy—are all a unique unity in their place. It is only through the "chain of descent" <term>hishtalshelut; the process by which divine light evolves into the material world</term>—from the perspective of the actions enacted in this world which is drawn from Emanation—that Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy are enacted below. In the realm of Emanation, in its own place, it is appropriate to say "created the illumination of the fire," for everything is one unique light and is already "made"—meaning the emanated being is complete. In this aspect, Shammai hints at "created the illumination of fire." But Hillel hints at the actions that are constantly renewed and drawn from them, which are many and are renewed at every moment; thus, He "**creates** the **illuminations** of the fire."

Why Shammai speaks from one perspective and Hillel from another is a secret already explained in the *Zohar*: that "illumination" was from the side of Strength <term>Gevurah; associated with Shammai</term> and "praise" was from the side of Kindness <term>Chesed; associated with Hillel</term>. Therefore, Shammai always needed to bring in and elevate the quality of Strength upward to its root and source, so that it would be sweetened and not destroy the world. But Hillel, who was from the side of Kindness, focused on the spreading of Kindness. 

To complete this matter through the hints of the fire's illuminations, I will copy the language of the *Zohar* from the portions of *Bereshit* and *Terumah*: 
<note>The following is a translation of a lengthy Aramaic passage from the Zohar regarding the mystical nature of fire.</note>
"Come and see: 'For the Lord your God is a consuming fire.' <note>Deuteronomy 4:24</note> This matter was said by the companions: there is a fire that consumes fire. There is a fire that is stronger than another fire. But come and see: one who wishes to know the wisdom of the holy unity should look at the flame rising from a coal or a burning lamp. For the flame only rises when it is grasped by a coarse substance. Come and see: in the rising flame there are lights—one white light and one light that holds black or blue. That white light is above and rises in a straight path. Beneath it is that blue or black light, which is a throne for that white light. And that white light rests upon it. To the eye, they appear as one. This black light, the color of consumption and beginning, is the throne of glory for the white. This is the secret of the blue thread <note>Tekhelet</note> in the fringes. This throne—blue or black—is grasped by another thing below to be lit, which arouses it to grasp that white. Sometimes this blue or black turns red. But that white light above it never changes; it is always white. But this blue changes to these colors: sometimes blue or black, and sometimes red. This blue is grasped on two sides: it is grasped above by that white light, and it is grasped below by that which is beneath it, which prepares it to shine. This blue consumes and destroys continually whatever is placed beneath it, for it is the nature of the blue to destroy and consume everything, for upon it hangs the destruction and death of all. Therefore, it consumes everything that clings to it below. But that white light that rests upon it neither eats nor destroys, and its light never changes. Regarding this, Moses said, 'For the Lord your God is a consuming fire'—He certainly consumes and destroys everything that rests beneath Him. Therefore, he said 'your God' <note>singular/personal</note> and not 'our God,' because Moses represented the aspect of the higher white light that does not consume or destroy. 

Come and see: there is no arousal for this blue light to grasp the white light except through Israel, who cling beneath it. Come and see: although it is the nature of this blue and black light to destroy everything that clings beneath it, Israel clings beneath it and remains standing in existence. 'But you who cling to the Lord your God are all alive today.' <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note> It does not say 'our God' regarding that blue-black light that consumes and destroys, but says 'You cling to *this* and are alive today.' And above the white light rests a hidden light that encompasses all. Everything is bound together in the rising flame." 

Rabbi Phineas came and kissed him, saying: "Blessed be the Merciful One that I happened upon this." Rabbi Shimon said to the companions: "This which we have said is the secret of wisdom regarding the holy unity. Therefore, the final 'He' of the Holy Name <note>The last letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the Shekhinah</note> is the blue-black light in which the white light is grasped." 

This is the secret of unity: when the flame has different colors, and the colors are distinct, yet the upper one never changes and does not burn—so too the quality of Mercy is above, never changes, and never burns or enacts judgment. The white fire hints at the "Beauty of Israel" <term>Tiferet Israel; a divine emotive attribute</term>, and the black fire hints at the "Assembly of Israel" <term>Knesset Yisrael; the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</term>. When Israel unifies the Name and clings to the Divine Presence, then God is truly with His Presence, like a flame and its glow, all becoming one secret. This is the secret of "when the flame is bound to the coal," for when the flame is bound to the coal, the white light and the black light are found and unified as one flame. Understand this: if there were no coal, the flame would not be ignited, and the white and black lights would not be connected. So too, were it not for Israel—who are the "coal"—the Divine Presence would not be clinging to the Holy One, blessed be He, and would not receive the higher flow of abundance. Thus, the matter of the fire's illuminations is explained.

Also, in the wording of the three blessings mentioned above, we must find a hint. I found it in the book *Hadrat Kodesh* regarding the laying of *Tefillin* <note>phylacteries</note>: "I have bound their speech... the giving of the Torah began with the blessing 'Who chose us' and 'gave us the Torah'." In the book *Nehar Shalom*, he wrote there that the giving of the Torah is "today," for the honored abundance descends every day and always, as it says in the verse, "Like the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountains of Zion, for there the Lord commanded the blessing, life forever." <note>Psalm 133:3</note> This is the secret of the "four cubits of Law" which the Holy One, blessed be He, has in His world. The Torah is like the signature of the blessing of the illuminations, "Who renews in His goodness every day, continually, the work of creation," which also seals the blessing of the Creator of the Illuminations. This secret also seals the blessing "Who chooses His people Israel with love," for every day He chooses from the individuals and the remnants whom the Lord calls. 

I will expand upon this with the "good hand of the Lord upon me" <note>Nehemiah 2:8</note> to explain these three blessings according to the matters I have elaborated on above. The general rule is: "Creates," "Gave," and "Chooses" refer to the holy increase that flows from the Source due to the "arousal from below" <term>it'aruta d'letata; human action stimulating divine response</term> which adds strength above.

<margin>House of Wisdom</margin>
# House of David

The matter of "He chooses Israel" means He chooses more than what He originally chose. That is to say: if man had remained in the "garment of light" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* with an Aleph</note> as was chosen at the beginning of creation, he would not shine with as great a light as he will when the "garment of skin" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* with an Ayin</note> returns to being "light." Then, "no eye has seen it, O God, besides You," as I have elaborated on this matter above. For the advantage of light comes from the darkness; through the power of the increase of darkness, the transmigrations, and the compositions, the light will be greater in the future. "He chose"—it is found that He is *always* "choosing" Israel.

This matter is a secret, and this memory requires a broad explanation. The verse says: "These words the Lord spoke to all your assembly at the mountain out of the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a great voice, and it did not cease" <note>Deuteronomy 5:19</note>. Rashi explains: "'and it did not cease'—we translate this as 'it did not stop,' for His voice is strong and exists forever." Another explanation: "'and it did not cease'—He did not add to appear in that public manner again." 

There is a secret in this matter, as both explanations are true. The aspect of "He did not add" refers to the Rabbinic commandments, their stringencies, and their safeguards; these were not yet commanded directly from the mouth of the Almighty. The aspect of "it did not stop" means that even these Rabbinic laws did not stop from that voice, for they were included in that voice in potential. However, the time and moment had not yet arrived for them to move from potential to action. For the matter depended on the "arousal of those below," according to their essence and quality, and according to the levels of the souls in every generation. Then the Sages added to arouse the higher power, and it emerged into action in its proper time and according to its knowledge. God forbid that the Sages innovated from their own minds; rather, it was through the "Higher Mind" and their souls that stood at Mount Sinai. For all souls were at that standing; they received it then in the aspect of their souls and their generation. Thus, the matter is rectified and accepted, and it is "from the mouth of the Almighty." A hint to this is that the word *Ha-Raban* <note>The Rabbi</note> has the same numerical value as *Gevurah* <note>Strength/Might</note>. 

In *Exodus Rabbah* and in the *Midrash Yelammedenu*, it is said: "'And God spoke all these words, saying...' Rabbi Isaac said: Whatever the prophets were destined to prophesy in every generation, they received from Mount Sinai. For so Moses said to Israel: 'With him who is standing here with us today... and with him who is not here with us today.' <note>Deuteronomy 29:14</note> It does not say 'is not standing with us today,' but simply 'is not here with us today.' These are the souls destined to be created, who had no physical substance, so 'standing' is not mentioned regarding them. Even though they were not there that day, they were created; nevertheless, each and every one received his portion. And so it says, 'The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachi.' <note>Malachi 1:1</note> It does not say 'in the days of Malachi,' but 'by the hand of Malachi,' for the prophecy was already in his hand from Mount Sinai, but until that hour, he was not given permission to prophesy. And so Isaiah said, 'From the time it was, there am I...'" Isaiah said: "From the day—"

# House of the Interior
## 31

"And you shall add three more cities" <note>Referring to the biblical Cities of Refuge in Deuteronomy 19:9, which are promised for the future Messianic era.</note> besides the first ones. But know that all the descendants and desires of **Abel** were liable for death, and therefore **Cain** killed them. However, **Moses** killed the Egyptian before his time in order to elevate him through the **Name of 72** <note>The *Shem Ha-Mephorash*, a mystical 72-letter name of God used in Kabbalistic practice.</note>, and he erred in this and was sentenced to exile. This is the secret of the verse, "I will appoint for you a place where he may flee" <note>Exodus 21:13</note>, for the Hebrew letters of the word "there" (*Sham*) are the same as **Moses** (*Moshe*). 

And behold, because **Abel** sinned in his thoughts regarding the realm of *Imma* <note>The Divine Mother or the attribute of Understanding/Binah</note>, through the names *EL* and *Y-W* and the letter *Dalet* from the name *ADNY* <note>The name of Lordship, *Adonai*</note>, which were the secret of the phrase "Where is Abel your brother?" <note>Genesis 4:9</note>, he and all his desires became liable for death. This is the secret of "The voice of your brother's bloods" <note>Genesis 4:10</note>—the word "bloods" (*damei*) in plural refers to his blood and his future desires. 

The rectification (*Tikkun*) of **Abel** occurs when he is killed, elevating him to the realm of *Binah* (Understanding) through three gates. Therefore, the secret of the "husk" <term>Klippah: An outer shell of impurity that conceals divine sparks</term> of Abel is **Balaam** <note>The non-Israelite prophet from the Book of Numbers</note>. As explained elsewhere, when Balaam was killed, that spark of holiness within him was separated from the impurity and ascended to the secret of *Binah*. This is why **Abel** (*Hevel*) and the fool **Nabal** (*Naval*) share the same letters, except the letter *He* of Abel is replaced by the *Nun* of Nabal, hinting that he began to rectify the secret of *Binah* in which he had sinned. 

This is the secret of the death of **Abner** <note>The general of Saul's army</note>, who was also from the soul-root of Abel and was killed to be elevated to *Binah*, just like Nabal; this is sufficient for the one who understands. This applies to all others killed from the line of Abel. 

Behold, there are two potential "ends" or times for the redemption: "I will hasten it" <note>If the generation is worthy</note> or "in its time" <note>If they are not</note>. If the end comes "in its time," all his desires will certainly be rectified. But even if they are worthy and the end is hastened before the rectification of **Abel** is complete, the verse says, "If [God] enlarges your border... then you shall add three more cities." This means if it happens through their merit because they fulfilled the commandments, three more cities are added to complete the desires of Abel. However, it will not be through intentional sin, but through "unintentional" killing <note>The purpose of the Cities of Refuge</note>. This is the meaning of the phrase "for he is also flesh" (*bashagam*) <note>Genesis 6:3; the word *bashagam* has the same numerical value as Moses</note>, for then I will remove the spirit of impurity from the earth. Thus, the killers will only be liable for exile. Therefore, it is necessary to add a third set of cities to complete these spiritual desires as a great gift. This is the language I found in the name of the **Ari, of blessed memory** <term>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foremost 16th-century Kabbalist</term>.

**Abel** (*Hevel*) will then rise above all his masters, and death will be swallowed up forever. There will be no more death, and **Abel** will become eternal life. The verse "they shall not labor in vain" will be fulfilled, for their work will be done by others. The Land of Israel will be eternal, and as long as they exist, they will increase in wisdom and "go from strength to strength" without end or limit. The beginning will be the ultimate satisfaction, where work is done by others, and the Land of Israel will bring forth **fine rolls and silk garments** <note>A famous Talmudic depiction of the material abundance in the Messianic era</note>. Afterward, there will be peace in the land, and "I will rid the land of evil beasts," which is the secret of the *Klippah*. 

The bitterness will be removed from the *Klippah*, and it will be humbled and "guard the opening," as mentioned earlier. I will restore you and make you stand upright like a standing *Mezuzah*, like Adam before he sinned. "And I will set my sanctuary among you... and I will walk among you." This whole matter is eternity itself, for these blessings are part of the beginning of eternal life. There is no difficulty in mentioning eternity here; it is only mentioned to show those who think the good will cease that it will not. Even if people "die" after the resurrection of the dead, it is merely the shedding of one form for a higher one. The question remains: why did the Torah not explicitly mention this? But according to your wisdom, O Sages of Truth, eternity exists in both body and soul. It does not cease, but rather collects more light, rising grade after grade forever. This is how I have weighed the opinion of the author of *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai, a 16th-century Kabbalist</note>, who explained at length that the Torah does not explicitly mention these spiritual rewards because they are eternal and beyond physical description. Man will be eternal in body and soul, clinging to the Divine, ascending like Enoch and Elijah, and a thousand times more so, without end. I have already written that even though I explained it another way elsewhere, it is all truth and one complete system for the one who understands.

**Behold**, the matter of the **garments of light** has been explained. Through Adam’s sin, the "garments of light" (*Kotnot Or* with an *Aleph*) became **garments of skin** (*Kotnot Or* with an *Ayin*). In the future, they will return to being garments of light, and "the Lord shall rejoice in His works." The word "rejoices" (*Samach*) is not written in the past tense because the world has not yet...

<column-break/>

Ecclesiastes said "it is near." And according to the words of the Rabbi <note>the Ari</note>, he said that the stature of the spiritual world is like a horn... and it is a hint toward repentance. This distinguishes between this world and the next. There are seven cycles (*Shmitot*), corresponding to the seven wisdoms... hinting that he will strengthen the soul... in every death. And Abel will have an addition of bounty and the flow of blessing from the seven... and it is said that due to the many souls returning to their source... it will be a new world... like the secret of the holy rolls of bread... and here the **Name of 42** (*Mem-Tet*) itself is hinted at... and the language of "Nabal" is related to the word "wither" (*Naval*).

Regarding when he will be able to complete the cycle... the Rabbi answered us... that his portion is in the new creation. But in the merit of the night, it is written "strength for the world."

My intention is to find and write for the sake of merit, hinting that every person... should be prepared for this time, which is the time of repentance and the end of death... and therefore one needs to look with the spirit of holiness...

And this is the meaning of "a child shall die a hundred years old" <note>Isaiah 65:20</note>.

According to this calculation, in the sixth millennium, death will cease and they will live... and in the seventh millennium the interruption of death will be complete, and there will be no more "new" souls in the world. The righteous will be fasting to receive pure, new souls. After the interruption, they will return to the state of the world of the Messiah... until the end of the seven millennia. And concerning the Sabbath, it is hinted in the verse "to the Lord alone on 그 day"... for the word of the Lord shall stand forever. This knowledge will not be understood by everyone... but only by those who delve into the secret of the seven cycles. These are the words of the Rabbi.
