# House of Hashem, House of Wisdom
## 25

Is it not the "Creator of the heavens who stretched them out" <note>original: *Borei ha-shamayim ve-notaihem*</note>? In every matter and context, there is some hint as to why the Sages connected them in "two houses" <note>Referring to the two phrasing options or schools of thought</note>, or why the Sages did not choose a more explicit language in the past tense.

->**House of Hashem**<-

And since this has come to my hand, I will provide a reason for why we bless God as the "Creator of the lights of the fire" <note>original: *Borei meorei ha-esh* — the blessing said during the Havdalah ceremony at the end of the Sabbath</note> and not "He who created the light," which would be more linguistically clear. The *Tosafot* commentary on the tractate of *Berakhot* wrote: "Our language follows the scriptural verse," but I say there is a secret in this matter.

<margin>
A secret in the matter
</margin>

Behold, it is taught there that the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel disagree over "light" versus "lights." The House of Shammai holds that one should say "Who created the light of the fire" <note>original: *Bara ma'or ha-esh*</note> because there is one primary light in the fire. The House of Hillel holds we say "lights" <note>plural: *meorei*</note> because there are many colors of light within the fire.

<margin>
Rashi's commentary explains: You have extended the matter and were precise... Shammai did not see that there are many hues in the illuminating fire. There is also a great matter concerning the terms "Created" <note>past tense: *Bara*</note> and "Creates" <note>present/continuous: *Borei*</note>. Everyone agrees on this, yet the version of the House of Shammai taught "Created the light of the fire" and the version of the House of Hillel taught "Creates the lights of the fire." Both are the "words of the living God." It is known that the *Atzilut* <term>Atzilut: The highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing the realm of pure Divine Emanation</term> is like a flame bound to a coal, and it is all the secret of a singular unity. Even the recycling of the red, the green—which represent the Line of Kindness, the Line of Judgment, and the Line of Mercy—everything is in its place a singular unity. It is only in the "chain of descent" <term>Hishtalshelut: The process by which Divine light descends and becomes more physical</term>, from the perspective of the actions performed in this world that are drawn from the *Atzilut* (or performed below), that Kindness, Judgment, and Mercy appear. In the realm of *Atzilut* itself, it is appropriate to say "He created the light of the fire," for everything is one unified light and has already been created. I mean to say, it is the "Emanated." From this perspective, the House of Shammai hints at "Created the light of the fire." But the House of Hillel hints at the actions that are constantly renewed and drawn from them, which are many and renewed at every moment—and this is "Who creates the lights of the fire." As for why Shammai speaks from one perspective and Hillel from another, the secret of the matter is already explained in the *Zohar*: that Shammai represents the side of *Gevurah* <term>Gevurah: The Divine attribute of Strength, Restraint, and Judgment</term>, which is sweetened by the attribute of Kindness (*Chesed*). Therefore, the "Light" always needed to be brought in.
</margin>

...and to elevate his attribute, which is *Gevurah*, upward to its root and source, so that it may be sweetened and not destroy the world. But Hillel, who was from the side of Kindness (*Chesed*), held that "the world is built through Kindness." For the completion of the matter regarding the "lights of the fire," I will copy the language of the *Zohar* (Portions *Bereishit* and *Terumah*): "Behold, it is said: 'For Hashem your God is a consuming fire.' <note>Deuteronomy 4:24</note> It has been said that there is a fire that consumes fire; it consumes and destroys it because there is a fire stronger than fire. But come and see: one who wishes to know the wisdom of the Holy Unity should gaze at the flame rising from a coal or from a burning lamp. For the flame does not rise unless it is attached to a coarse substance. Come and see: in the rising flame there are two lights: one white and one light that holds onto it, which is black or blue. The white light is above and rises in a straight path, and beneath it is the blue or black light, which is a throne for the level of the white light that rests upon it. They are joined together to become one. This black light, the blue hue which is below, is the Throne of Glory for the white. This blue-black light is attached to another substance to be ignited from below, and it is aroused to join the white light. This blue-black light sometimes turns red, while the white light above never changes, for the white is constant. But when this blue light changes colors—sometimes blue or black and sometimes red—it is attached to two sides: it is attached above to that white light, and attached below to that which is beneath it, which is prepared for it to illuminate. And this [lower light] consumes constantly and destroys that which is left beneath it. For whatever sticks to it from below, the blue light joins and consumes it, for it is its way to consume and destroy all, as upon it depends the destruction of all and the death of all. Therefore it consumes whatever sticks to it below. But that white light which rests upon it never eats or consumes, and its light never changes. Regarding this Moses said, 'For Hashem your God is a consuming fire'—He certainly consumes and destroys whatever rests beneath Him. Therefore he said 'Your God' and not 'Our God,' because Moses was in that upper white light that does not consume or destroy. Come and see: the blue light has no arousal to attach to the white light... except through the people of Israel who attach themselves beneath it... it is written: 'And you who cling to Hashem your God are all alive today.' <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note> He did not say 'Our God' regarding that blue-black light that consumes and destroys all that clings beneath it, for they cling to *This* [the white light] and thus 'are all alive today.' And upon the white light always rests the blue light... and this is found in the rising flame and the wisdom of the upper beings." Rabbi Phineas approached and kissed him, saying, "Blessed be the Merciful One that I have trembled here." Rabbi Phineas and three hundred went with him. Rabbi Simeon said: "This which we have said is the secret of wisdom regarding the Holy Unity. Therefore, Hashem is in the holy light; it is the blue-black light that the white light is always attached to." Thus far [the Zohar].

<margin>
Hashem is One and His Name is One
</margin>

Behold, the secret of the Unity is like the flame with its hues; and our hues change but He never changes. Our light burns from the attribute of Mercy which is above, and it never changes and never burns nor performs judgment. The white fire hints at the "Tiferet of Israel" <term>Tiferet: The Divine attribute of Beauty/Harmony, often associated with the masculine principle or God as King</term>, and the black fire hints at the "Assembly of Israel" <term>Knesset Yisrael: The collective soul of the Jewish people, associated with the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</term>. When Israel unifies the Name and clings to the *Shekhinah*, then it is a complete constant: Hashem in the Name of 72, the *Shekhinah* of His strength. Just as the white and black of the flame are all one flame, this returns to the secret of "the flame bound to the coal." For when the flame is bound to the coal, then the white light and the black light are found and unified in one flare and one flame. Understand that if it were not for the coal and the burning, the flame would not be seen, and the white and black lights would not be unified. So too, were it not for Israel who are the "action," the *Shekhinah* would not cling to the Holy One, Blessed be He, and would not receive the upper emanation.

<margin>
Hashem is One and His Name is One
</margin>

Thus the matter of the "lights of the fire" is explained. Also, in the wording of the three blessings mentioned above, we must find a hint. I found in the conduct of the "Prayer of the Glory of Holiness" <note>likely a reference to a specific prayer manual or *Siddur* commentary</note> as follows: "And they hardened their two... gave and Torah," just as the blessing begins "Who chose us... and gave us," that you are a servant and taken until your signature "Giver of the Torah" <note>original: *Noten ha-Torah*</note>, which is in the present tense. For the precious emanation descends every day constantly, as hinted in the verse "Like the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountains of Zion, for there Hashem commanded the blessing, life forever." <note>Psalm 133:3</note> This is the secret of the "four cubits of Law" which are the Holy Language... and His signature is shown within all the later blessings that He "renews every morning in His goodness, constantly, the work of Creation." Thus he also signs, "Blessed is He who chooses His people Israel with love," for every day He chooses from the individuals and the remnants whom the Lord calls. Thus far his words. I will expand the discussion as the good hand of Hashem is upon me, to explain the first of the three blessings according to the matters I have detailed above. The general point is that the "Giver" is within the preceding blessing... the detail of the arousal that adds strength above.

House of David

### House of David

The matter of the "Choosing of Israel": He chooses more than He has already chosen. I mean to say, if the signature had remained in the aspect of light as it was chosen at the beginning of Creation, it would not illuminate as greatly as it will illuminate through the extension of the "garment of skin" <note>referring to the physical human state post-Eden</note>, and they will give it back to be "the light that no eye has seen, O God, besides Yours," <note>Isaiah 64:3</note> as I have elaborated on this matter above. Through the "advantage of light over darkness" <note>Ecclesiastes 2:13</note>, from the power of the swords of darkness and the transmigrations (*Gilgulim*) and the refinements, the light will increase in the future. "The Chosen One" is found always "choosing" Israel.

->**House of Wisdom**<-

And the matter of "Giver of the Torah": In truth, the Blessed One already gave it, but He is still the "Giver of the Torah" and it does not stop. This matter needs broad explanation. The verse says: "These words Hashem spoke to all your assembly at the mountain from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, a great voice, and it did not cease" <note>Deuteronomy 5:19</note>. Rashi explains: "'And it did not cease'—we translate this as 'and it did not stop,' for His voice is strong and exists forever. Another explanation: 'And it did not cease'—He did not add to appear in that public display again." Thus far his words. There is a hidden secret in this matter, and both explanations are true. The matter of "He did not add" refers to the Rabbinic commandments, their stringencies, and their fences—these were not yet commanded from the mouth of the Almighty. But the matter of "It did not stop" means that even these did not stop from that voice, for they were included in that voice in potential. However, for every time and season, the time had not yet arrived for them to go from potential to action. For the matter depended on the arousal of those below, and according to their thoughts and according to the levels of the souls in every generation. Then the Sages added to arouse the upper power, and it emerged into action in its time and according to its logic. God forbid that the Sages permitted things from their own minds; rather, they established the upper logic and their souls that stood at Mount Sinai. For all souls in their entirety were at that standing, each one receiving the aspect of their soul... then that matter is rectified and accepted, and it is "from the mouth of the Almighty." A hint to this is that "Mordecai the Great ascended by the mouth of the Almighty" <note>Wordplay on the name Mordecai and the source of his authority</note>. And in *Exodus Rabbah* and the *Tanhuma* Midrash it says: "'And God spoke all these words, saying'—Rabbi Isaac said: Whatever the prophets were destined to prophesy in every generation, they received from Mount Sinai. For thus Moses said to Israel: 'With him who is here standing with us today... and with him who is not here with us today.' <note>Deut 29:14</note> 'Is not standing' is not written here, but 'with us today'—these are the souls destined to be created... for even though they were not at that standing, each one received his portion. And so it says, 'The burden of the word of Hashem to Israel by the hand of Malachi.' It does not say 'In the days of Malachi,' but 'By the hand of Malachi,' for the prophecy was already in his hand from Mount Sinai, but until that hour, permission was not given to him to prophesy. And so Isaiah said, 'From the time it was, there am I' <note>Isaiah 48:16</note>... Isaiah said:

<header>House of David</header>

"And you shall add three more cities besides the first ones" <note>Referring to the Cities of Refuge mentioned in Deuteronomy 19:9.</note>. But know that all the "limbs" of Abel <note>original: *yeda'o* / *nizozot*, referring to the sparks of his soul</note> were liable for death, and that is why Cain killed him. However, Moses killed the Egyptian <note>The taskmaster Moses slew in Exodus 2:12.</note> before his time in order to elevate him through the **Name of 72** <term>The *Shem Ayin-Bet*, a 72-letter divine name used in Kabbalistic tradition to perform miracles or spiritual rectifications</term>. Moses sinned in this and thus became liable for exile; this is the secret behind the verse, "I will appoint for you a place where he may flee," where the Hebrew word for "there" (*Shammah*) contains the same letters as the name **Moses** (*Moshe*). 

Behold, because Abel sinned in his thoughts regarding the "Mother" <note>The Sephirah of *Binah* (Understanding)</note>, he and all his "thoughts" <note>likely referring to his soul-sparks</note> were liable for death. This is the secret of "the voice of your brother’s bloods" <note>Genesis 4:10</note>, which refers to his various sparks and thoughts. The rectification of Abel occurs when he is killed, allowing him to ascend to *Binah*, which corresponds to the **Fifty Gates** <note>The 50 Gates of Understanding</note>. Therefore, the "husk" <term>*Klippah*—the spiritual shell or impurity that clings to holiness</term> of Abel is **Balaam**; he was separated from Moses. When those holy sparks within him are struck and killed, they ascend into the secret of *Binah*. Thus, the names **Abel** (*Hevel*) and **Nabal** contain the same letters, except the *He* (ה) of Abel is replaced with the *Nun* (נ) of Nabal, hinting that he began to rectify the secret of *Binah* (represented by the letter *Nun*, numerical value 50) where he had sinned. This is the secret of the verse "Should Nabal die as a churl dies?" <note>2 Samuel 3:33</note>, for Abner was also a spark of Abel, and he was killed to be elevated to *Binah*, just like Nabal. This is sufficient for those who understand. The same applies to all others killed from the root of Abel.

There are two potential "Ends of Days": "I will hasten it" or "in its time" <note>Based on Isaiah 60:22. The Sages taught that if the generation is worthy, the redemption is hastened; if not, it comes at its set time.</note>. If the "End" comes in its time, it is certain that all his thoughts are rectified. If they are worthy and hasten the End, his rectification might not yet be complete. This is the meaning of "If [the Lord] enlarges [your borders]... if you keep all these commandments." This means that through their merit, He will "add three more [cities]" to complete the rectification of Abel’s thoughts. Then, one will not die intentionally, but only by error, for the spirit of impurity will have passed from the earth. There will still be "cities of refuge" for those who kill accidentally, and we must add three more cities to complete his thoughts in his great territory. This is the language I found in the name of the **Arizal** <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century father of modern Kabbalah.</note>, may his memory be a blessing.

**The General Principle** that emerges from all our words is that once death is swallowed up, death will no longer exist. Abel will be an eternal and enduring life-force. "I will set My Tabernacle among you," and their work will be done by others <note>A Talmudic concept where, in the future, the righteous will not need to labor.</note>. The Land of Israel will be eternal. As people age, they will increase in wisdom, going "from strength to strength" without end or limit. The beginning will be the height of satisfaction without toil, for the Land of Israel will produce "finished cakes and silk garments" <note>A classic Talmudic description (Ketubot 111b) of the supernatural bounty in the messianic age.</note>. Afterward, there will be peace in the land; "I will cause evil beasts to cease"—this is the secret of the *Klippah* (the husk), as the bitterness will be removed from the husk and it will be subdued. As mentioned above: "I will make you fruitful and multiply you" in an upright stature, like Adam before he sinned. "I will set My Tabernacle... and I will walk among you." This entire matter is itself eternity, for as soon as those blessings take hold, eternity begins. There is no difficulty in the Torah mentioning eternity only through hints.

**The Sages**—the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note>—maintain that eternity exists in both body and soul, and the longing to rise higher and higher will never cease, forever and without end. Then Abel will reach his proper place. This elevation is the promise mentioned by the author of *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai, a famous 16th-century Kabbalist.</note>, who explained at length that man will be eternal in body and soul. Death will be no more, only eternal cleavage to God. One will rise higher and higher in this eternal attachment until they merit the level of **Enoch** and **Elijah**, and a thousand times more than them, without end. I have already written that Abel returns to his place—this is for the wise.

**Behold**, the matter of the "Garments of Light" has been explained. At the morning light, they became "Garments of Skin" <note>A famous wordplay: *Ohr* (Light, spelled with an Aleph) became *Or* (Skin, spelled with an Ayin) after the sin of Adam.</note>. In the future, the "Garments of Light" will return, and "the Lord will rejoice in His works." The word "rejoiced" (past tense) is not written, but rather "will rejoice" (future tense), because currently...

Behold, in the seventh millennium, there are no "offspring," for the souls have already finished [their time] in the body. The human body will gather other spirits and souls to give to Israel below. There will be a new world, producing offspring without any filth or dross. According to this, the Messiah will come in the sixth millennium after the souls finish in the body, and in the seventh millennium, there will be an additional outpouring of souls. There will be no "new" souls in the world during that entire millennium, for the attribute of the Sabbath ascends to receive new, pure souls. This is the secret of the "Fifty [Gates]," until the completion of the verse of the Jubilee. Regarding the Sabbath of the Jubilee, it is written: "The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof," meaning the higher beings will be for Israel. Corresponding to the five thousand years... then it is written: "Splendor will come," for the husks will have no power to cut, and "the word of our God shall stand forever"—this refers to the "forever" of the Jubilee. According to this view, there will not be seven cycles [of 7,000 years each], for the first Sabbatical cycle will be extended to ten. These are the words of the Rabbi... and what Rabbi Chaim [Vital] wrote according to the view that there are not seven cycles—this matter should not be revealed to one's thoughts to believe, for most of the words of the Sages of Truth, and primarily the famous **Zohar**, maintain the matter of the six cycles.

The world was not yet in its full goodness, which is why it says "The Lord *will* rejoice" (future tense), referring to what is to come with the arrival of our righteous Messiah. The word "Will Rejoice" (*Yismach*) contains the same letters as **Messiah** (*Mashiach*). Then it will be fulfilled that "light will dwell with him" as "light like darkness," for from the "curtain of darkness"—which is the refining and the filth of the "Garments of Skin"—the light will increase. Then it will be said to Jacob and Israel: "What has God wrought?" These are the two aspects mentioned in the **Zohar** in the passage we are discussing, which says that Jacob and Israel are "one hidden and one revealed."

**And then** they shall sing together, bound in a strong bond: the Holy One, Blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel, as mentioned in this passage of the Zohar.

**Regarding** the "increase of light" that we hinted at, the wording of the conclusion of the three blessings is clarified: "Creator of the lights," "Giver of the Torah," and "Who chooses His people Israel with love." All are phrased in the present tense, but they hint at the future: "He [will] create the lights," "He [will] choose His people Israel." Even though in the tractate of *Berakhot*, in the chapter "These are the matters," the conclusion regarding the blessing "Who creates the lights of the fire" uses the term *Borei* (Creator)... the verse "Who forms light and creates darkness" and "Who forms mountains and creates..."

### **House of God, House of David**

The "wise of heart" explained that the **great voice that did not cease** <note>original: *v'ha-kol ha-gadol asher lo yasuf* - a reference to Deuteronomy 5:19, often interpreted as the ongoing nature of Revelation</note> is drawn from the Source and comes from it. It is included in all the changing facets of reality, for there is no lack in it. Through the greatness and strength of that voice, all things lived and shifted from side to side, one corresponding to another. Every prophet and sage received their specific portion: one received the left side <note>Severity/Judgment</note>, and another received the aspect of purity, each according to their standing and their capacity to receive. Yet, everything comes from one place and returns to one place.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, it is taught: "There is no word spoken by the companions—even when one says this and another says that regarding the Torah—that does not all travel to a single place and gather at a single spring." As the verse says, "All the rivers run into the sea" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:7</note>, and it is written, "All go to one place" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:20</note>. The meaning is that all things emerged from the Source—the "Head of the Supreme Thought"—and they spread and travel until their end, which is the "Final Sea" <note>the Sephirah of *Malchut* or Sovereignty</note>. This is the "one place" where everything is unified, and within it, the Divine Unity is completed.

For this reason, it is said that the teachings were "given from one Shepherd" <note>Ecclesiastes 12:11</note>, and the Sages said: "They were all given by one God." This is to teach us that contradictions and variations did not come from different divine powers, but rather everything came from one unique Place, even though that Source itself contains no change or substitution.

To indicate this wonderful secret, every sage maintains their own opinion and brings proof from the Torah for their reasoning. Since the Divine Unity is not completed without all these diverse views—just as the "repair" <term>*Tikkun* — the process of fixing or balancing the spiritual realms</term> occurs above through all these facets—so too must we act to bring "repair" and make the Divine Name whole below. Therefore, the Sages said: "Make your ear like a funnel and acquire for yourself a heart to hear the words of those who declare impure and the words of those who declare pure" <note>Tosefta Sotah 7:12</note>. This is the path of restoration and perfection for the sake of God.

In this way, it is said: **"Both these and those are the words of the Living God."** <note>A famous Talmudic principle regarding legal disputes between the House of Hillel and the House of Shammai</note>. However, because "that which is far off and exceeding deep, who can find it?" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:24</note>, this matter depends on "Thought" (meaning, the Sephirah of Wisdom/*Chokhmah*), which is impossible to fully grasp. Even the **Fiftieth Gate** <note>The final level of Understanding</note> was hidden even from our teacher Moses. All these matters appear to contradict and differ from one another only from our perspective, because we do not have the authority or power to fully comprehend them. Therefore, it is impossible for us to uphold two contradictory sides at once in practice, and so the law (*Halakhah*) is fixed according to one of the two opinions. Yet, even so, they did not stop saying "both these and those are the words of the Living God." Everything is one from the side of the Giver, blessed be He, but from our side, they are different things. The law follows the House of Hillel alone. These are the words of the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>A work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>.

The words of the *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Moses Cordovero</note> at the end of Chapter 2 of the "Gate of the Decisive" are similar: "In the dispute between Hillel and Shammai: Hillel was a man of **Kindness** <term>*Chesed* — the attribute of expansive love and mercy</term> and Shammai was a man of **Might** <term>*Gevurah* — the attribute of judgment, severity, and restriction</term>. Their attributes were recognizable in them. God forbid Shammai ever felt anger that would cause a spiritual blemish; rather, he was 'impatient' only because his divine attribute caused it. The core of their dispute was 'for the sake of Heaven' to receive the divine decision, and therefore their words endured. Furthermore, one must understand why the House of Hillel merited having the law fixed according to them: it was because of their humility. They were attached to the side of Kindness through humility and lowliness. Since they leaned toward Kindness, the Law—which is the *Shekhinah* <term>the Divine Presence in the world</term>—followed them, for her tendency is toward the side of Kindness." This is like the matter of Esther, where the sages noted that "a thread of kindness was drawn over her."

The phrase **"both these and those are the words of the Living God"** refers to *Binah* (Understanding), which is called "Living God," for from there, understanding flows. He said that between those who declare impure or unfit and those who declare pure or fit—those on the side of Might (*Gevurah*)—they show that there is "permission" for the "husks" <term>*Klippot* — forces of impurity</term> and spiritual damages to exist. Therefore, Shammai often declares things unfit. On the other hand, those who declare pure and fit lean toward the side of Kindness (*Chesed*) and leniency, showing that the "husks" have no authority or dominion there. Therefore, things are "pure." Everything comes from *Binah*, where the influence of both "extremes" originates. When the "Hand" and the influence of the Divine Chariot become clear through one of the two sides, then the law follows that side to forbid or permit. Therefore, both the pure and the impure are "righteous" in their source. Sometimes the law even follows the House of Shammai in pressing circumstances, though the majority of the leaning is toward Kindness. Note that the House of Hillel leans toward leniency and Shammai toward stringency; this corresponds to Kindness and Might. This is the reason for the variation, as it is explained that sometimes Kindness is within Might and Might is within Kindness, "his head included in water and the water included in fire," as explained in the "Gate of Attributes and Conduct," Chapter 6, regarding the Binding of Isaac. These are the words of the *Pardes*.

---

# **And I**
I will add my own contribution to the explanation of the teaching in the *Yalkut* on the Torah portion *Vayechi*: Rabbi Acha said in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Hanina: When Moses ascended to the heights, he heard the voice of the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and engaging with the laws of the **Red Heifer** <term>*Parah Adumah* — a ritual used for purification from death-impurity</term>. God was saying: "My son Eliezer says: A heifer must be two years old, and a calf one year old." 

Moses said before the Holy One: "Master of the Universe! The upper and lower worlds are under Your authority, yet You sit and recite a law in the name of flesh and blood?" 

The Holy One replied: "Moses, a certain righteous man is destined to arise in My world and begin the Tractate of *Parah* first. Rabbi Eliezer says: A heifer must be two years old..." 

Moses said: "Master of the Universe! May it be Your will that he emerges from my loins." 

The Holy One said to him: "By your life, he shall emerge from your loins!" Thus it is written: "And the name of the first was Eliezer" <note>Exodus 18:4</note>—referring to that specific Eliezer.

This is difficult: Is the law not fixed *against* Rabbi Eliezer? He says the heifer is two years old, but the Sages say it must be three years or older! Furthermore, why did Moses ask, "The upper and lower worlds are under Your authority"? And what did God see in him? And why does it matter that he would *begin* the Tractate of *Parah*?

Regarding the principle that **"both these and those are the words of the Living God,"** it seems to me the explanation is as follows: It is like the story in the Talmud <note>Baba Metzia 59b, the "Oven of Achnai"</note> regarding the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Joshua, where it is said: "It is not in Heaven." I explained earlier that every single commandment has a root above, and a root above that root, up to the Root of Roots. According to one's spiritual "attachment" (*Dveikut*) above, so is the commandment and the action below. However, there are levels one above the other; one person enters and attaches themselves higher than another. Therefore, the commandments "live" according to one's attachment above. One sage speaks according to his level of attachment, and the law is decided according to the majority because when many agree, the influence on the *Malchut* (Sovereignty) is stronger. Even though the "Kindness" might be leaning toward "Might," the law follows the "lower awakening." 

Take for example the dispute over Tefillin <note>Phylacteries</note> between Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam regarding the order of the scrolls. Heaven forbid we should think one of them is not holy! Rather, each one is attached to a different root above. 

Now we can explain the teaching: God spoke about the Red Heifer in the name of Rabbi Eliezer. Moses understood that Rabbi Eliezer would innovate something new that had never been—heaven forbid—a "new source." Moses asked: "The upper and lower worlds are Yours; how can flesh and blood innovate something that did not exist?" 

The Holy One answered him: It is not that he creates something "new" from nothing, but that Rabbi Eliezer's spiritual level will be so high, and his attachment to the root of the commandment of the Red Heifer—which is exceedingly deep—will be so profound that he will enter into its root until the very "Secret of the Beginning." For the Beginning is the root of all roots, and from the Beginning, branches and offsets spread. This is why he "starts" the tractate. The law is not like those who are at a different level of attachment. If everyone were at this specific high level, the law would follow him. But Rabbi Eliezer is a "unique one," representing the highest level of Might (*Gevurah*), just as Moses was set apart above all the insights of the Sages of Israel. Therefore, it was necessary for Rabbi Eliezer to be a descendant of Moses.

# **And in the aspects**
And the insights and levels go up and up until the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). The "great voice did not cease"—it never stopped, nor did it add, for everything is the secret of the Unique Unity, and the detail is found within the general whole. Thus, it is explained: He gave the Torah and He continues to give the Torah.

# **The Matter**
Regarding the blessing "Who forms the luminaries" (*Yotzer HaMe'orot*): the custom in Ashkenaz is to conclude the blessing with the words "As it is said: To Him who made the great lights... a new light will shine upon Zion, and may we all speedily merit its light. Blessed are You... who forms the luminaries." This is found in the *Tur*, Laws of Daily Prayer, Section 51. 

The Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel</note> wrote in a responsa that the conclusion of the blessing must reflect its opening. The "light" mentioned at the start of the blessing refers to the light God created during the six days of Creation, which the world was not yet worthy to use, so God **hid it for the righteous** in the world to come. About this light, it is said: "And nations shall walk by your light." This is the "new light"—the light from the beginning of Creation which the Holy One will renew for us. 

Behold, the secret of the **Hidden Light** <term>*Or HaGanuz* — the primordial light of Creation stored away for the future Messianic age</term> is hinted at in the verse "To Him who made the great lights," and afterward it mentions "the sun and the moon." Thus, the "great lights" are the spiritual essence of the sun and moon—the hidden part. This hidden light is within the "treasury of treasuries," the secret of the great luminaries which are Beauty (*Tiferet*) and Sovereignty (*Malchut*). The original intention was for this light to shine for Man if he had not sinned, and he would have worn "garments of light." 

The root is the "Lower Garden of Eden," which is the clean place of birth of the Tree of Knowledge. It is the secret of the letters *Vav* and *Heh*, from which they descend. The letters *Yud* and *Heh* are from where they descend... for He is the "Rock of Worlds." The "building" of the world was formed through the letters *Yud* and *Heh* (Wisdom and Understanding). Every Sephirah includes the "days of the world" in the secret of the Sabbatical and Jubilee years. The letters *Yud* and *Chet* <note>numerical value 18, *Chai*/Life</note> are the roots from the root of the "Upper Garden of Eden." The purpose of the "Rock of Worlds" was for Man "to work it and guard it." However, when he corrupted his ways and drew impurity upon himself, he damaged the letters...

## **House of Wisdom**

From the day the Torah was given at Sinai, I was there and received this prophecy; but "now the Lord God has sent me, and His Spirit" <note>original: Isaiah 48:16</note>. Until now, permission was not granted to me to prophesy. It was not just the prophets alone who received their prophecy from Sinai, but also the sages who stand in every single generation—each one received his own portion from Sinai. Thus it says: "These words the Lord spoke to all your assembly... a great voice that did not cease" <note>original: Deuteronomy 5:19</note>. This implies that everything the prophets were destined to say in all generations, they received at Sinai from that very voice.

This was not according to their own human intellect or investigation. Because this is the truth, we were commanded in His Torah, through His faithful prophet <note>Moses</note>: "According to the Torah they teach you and the judgment they tell you, you shall do; you shall not turn from the matter they tell you, right or left" <note>original: Deuteronomy 17:11</note>. One who does not listen to them is liable for death, because their voice is that same **great voice that did not cease**. It is said: "And the man who acts willfully, not listening to the priest... or to the judge, that man shall die" <note>original: Deuteronomy 17:12</note>. In the Jerusalem Talmud (Tractate Peah), they said: "Even what a diligent student is destined to teach before his teacher was already said to Moses at Sinai." From this, it is clear that all the words of the sages in every generation—what they innovate and all their analytical arguments—are from Sinai. It is not merely human intellect, but Divine intellect, which they have simply brought from **potential into actual**.

In the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Service of the Holy, a 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, in Part 2, Chapter 24, it is explained: Since the source of "external wisdoms" <note>secular philosophy</note> comes from the side of evil within the Tree of Knowledge, and we have distanced ourselves from that side and were joined to be a "nation of inheritance"—as it is written, "I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine"—it follows that it is forbidden for us to weigh any matter of the paths of the Torah with our own minds or to follow intellectual speculation to investigate its secrets and reasons.

The holy supreme sages illuminated our eyes on this in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note>. On the verse "You shall not make for yourself a graven image," Rabbi Isaac opened: "Do not let <margin>24</margin> your mouth cause your flesh to sin." How careful a person must be with the words of the Torah! How careful one must be not to err in them or to deviate from the path because he does not know or cannot grasp them. Regarding this it is written, "You shall not make for yourself a graven image or any likeness," for he is destined to be punished for it in the World to Come. When the time comes for the soul to enter its place, they push it outside and it is destroyed from that place...

Rabbi Judah said: As we have learned, why should God be angry at your voice? This refers to the soul of man... It is written: "For I the Lord your God am a jealous God." Why? Because His Name is "Jealous" <note>Kanno</note>. If it is because of the "Faces" <note>Divine attributes</note> that belong to His Name, it is because one lies against His Name. And if it is because of the Torah—we have learned that the entire Torah is the Holy Name of God. There is not a word in the Torah that is not included in the Holy Name. Because of this, one must not err in His Name or lie about it. One who lies against the King cannot enter the King's palaces and is punished in the World to Come. Rabbi Abba said: It is written, "You shall not make for yourself a graven image," and it is written regarding the Tablets, "Carve <note>Psol</note> for yourself two stone tablets." This means: Do not make for yourself another Torah that you do not know and that your teacher did not tell you. Why? "For I the Lord your God am a jealous God"—I am the one destined to take payment from you in the World to Come when the soul seeks to enter before Him; I will uproot it and cast it into Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>.

The Kabbalist Rabbi Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov wrote on this: Behold, your eyes see the words of the Fathers of the World, the holy ones on high. See how they feared the generation of error and the weighing of "images and likenesses." He explained that those who make "images" intend to receive power from the higher forces... but there is no permission to make such forms except as Bezalel and Solomon did, who knew how to combine the letters <note>Tziruf Otiyot</note> with which heaven and earth were created. They made them by the power of the Name, and these forms became prepared and designated for the glory of the God of Israel... but when another person thinks to make a likeness of those forms, they are not sanctified or prepared for His glory at all... the distance between them is like the distance between the Creator and the created. <margin>25</margin> Through a hidden counsel, such a form becomes prepared for an "external force," called the "Force of Impurity," for it lies outside the camp of the Divine Presence... Therefore, the one who errs in this is uprooted from the world, for he replaces the King with a servant and exchanges good for evil.

So it is in this parable regarding the letters of the Torah. Even if they are physical, they hint at the Divine Names and the Throne emanating from His light. Their interpretation must agree with the hidden meaning within them, so that the "matter" <note>the literal text</note> becomes a vessel for the "form" <note>the spiritual essence</note>. When someone explains them in another way, that spiritual form is not prepared to dwell upon the matter. His Torah is then found to be "thorny," and his wisdom is without God—a flawed and invalid wisdom, no different from a maker of idols.

**This** is the meaning of what they said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said, "The Torah is placed in the lap of the Sages." Regarding this, some explain our request "and give us our portion in Your Torah"—meaning, may we merit that a teaching be illuminated in our name within the treasure of the Sages. Our Sages of blessed memory interpreted: "Is it from the power of analytical debate?" No, everything was within the power of the aforementioned "Voice," and the time arrived for them to bring it from **potential to actual** through their contemplation. Truly, the "wisdom is great and the power is vast, His understanding is beyond number," for the potential power never ceases... it is a constant renewal according to the source of souls in every generation. The Holy One gave the Torah, and He *continues* to give the Torah at every moment. The "Flowing Spring" never stops, and that which is hidden in the potential is revealed from the gift He gave.

**Furthermore**, I will explain this matter essentially. We see in every generation that innovations spread. In the days of Moses, only what was explicitly received at Sinai was forbidden. Yet, some decrees were made for specific needs. So too with the Prophets, the Tannaim <note>Sages of the Mishnah</note>, and every generation and its leaders. The observer will note that as the "venom of the snake" <note>spiritual impurity</note> spreads, more "fences" and "boundaries" are needed so that the snake does not bite. The "External Force" <note>Sitra Achra</note> must not be allowed to awaken the snake's walls. If these conditions had existed at the time the Torah was given, they would have been written in the Torah then. But it was all included in the command: "Make a safeguard for My safeguard" <note>original: Sifra on Leviticus 18:30</note>. Everything is according to the needs of the generation to block the material of impurity. Since the venom of the snake spreads and emerges from potential to actual, the Holy One, blessed be He, who "created the Evil Inclination, created the Torah as its antidote." We must then draw down light from the potential to the actual until the future, when we will be enlightened by the Supreme Source.

**I have yet** to reveal secrets close to this matter to understand how all the words of the Sages are "the words of the living God." Consider the statement in Tractate Eruvin: Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rabbi Samuel: For three years the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel argued. These said "the law is like us" and those said "the law is like us." A Heavenly Voice <note>Bat Kol</note> went forth and said to them: "**These and those are the words of the living God**, but the law follows the House of Hillel." The Ritva <note>Rabbi Yom Tov Asevilli, 13th-century commentator</note> wrote in his novellae: "Our rabbis of France asked: How is it possible for both to be the words of the living God when one forbids and one permits?" They answered that when Moses went up to the heights to receive the Torah, he was shown 49 facets to forbid and 49 facets to permit for every single matter. He asked God about this, and God said this would be handed over to the Sages of Truth in Israel in every generation, and the decision would be according to them. This is correct according to the homiletical approach, and according to the "Path of Truth" <note>Kabbalah</note> there is a specific reason for this.

I say that "these and those" can be upheld even when they seem contradictory. This is justified in the case of the "Concubine in Gibeah" in Tractate Gittin: "My son Abiathar says thus, and my son Jonathan says thus." A sage asked, "Is there doubt before the Holy One?" He answered, "These and those are the words of the living God," for it was possible to uphold both their descriptions of what happened. But when one forbids and the other permits, how can both be upheld? If the decision only goes one way, does the other opinion "fall to the ground"? The opinion of the French rabbis is not sufficient here; one must rest on the secret reason according to the tradition. As the Sages said: "Masters of Assemblies"—these are the scholars who sit in groups and engage in Torah. These declare impure and those declare pure; these forbid and those permit. Lest a person say, "How can I learn Torah now?" The verse says: "They were given from one Shepherd" <note>original: Ecclesiastes 12:11</note>. One God gave them; one leader spoke them from the mouth of the Master of all works... Even you, "make your ear like a hopper and acquire a heart to hear the words of those who declare impure and the words of those who declare pure."

The Sages have thus alerted us that all differences of opinion and contradictory logic were given by one Shepherd. This thing is very far from human intellect; it is impossible unless one has a paved way to the Lord, dwelling in the light of Truth. In the book *Avodat HaKodesh*, Chapter 24, it is written: "He is the Force of that Source which flows constantly... and is the foundation for changes and opposites... changing from impure to pure, from forbidden to permitted, from invalid to valid."

### House of the Walled City

The prophet Elijah, of blessed memory, stated in the *Zohar* on the Song of Songs: "Just as an awakening in joy is required to stir the realms from this world toward the world above, so too is it necessary to stir joy and freedom from the world of witness toward the Supernal world. Because the worlds exist in a state of potential 'wrongs' <note>original: "רוגזא" - often referring to the attribute of Strict Judgment or tension between worlds</note>, the awakening only ascends from below to above."

This teaches that the Supernal Union <term>Yichud; the unification of Divine attributes</term>—specifically the awakening of *Binah* <term>the attribute of Understanding</term>—requires an impulse from *Malchut* <term>the attribute of Kingship or the physical world</term>. See the *Pardes* <note>The "Orchard of Pomegranates" by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note>, Chapter 4 of the "Gate of Essence and Conduct," and Chapter 6 of the "Gate of Radiance," regarding the awakening of the union between *Tiferet* <term>Beauty/the masculine principle</term> and *Malchut* <term>Kingship/the feminine principle/the Divine Presence</term>. The Jerusalem of below awakens the union of *Chokhmah* <term>Wisdom</term> and *Binah* <term>Understanding</term>, which is the Jerusalem of above.

The Jerusalem built here below in this world is aligned exactly with the spiritual Jerusalem hinted at above. Indeed, Shem, the son of Noah, was the first to go and establish power in Jerusalem. As the saying goes, "The end of the action was first in thought." This means his name <note>Shem literally means "Name" in Hebrew</note> hints at the state of the Divine Name when it is complete, specifically the unification of the letters *Yod* and *Heh* <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>. This was the initial thought during the creation of light <note>Genesis 1:3: "Let there be light"</note>, which was then hidden and did not fully manifest in action. Nevertheless, the first person to take hold of this Jerusalem below bore a name that hinted at this potential, and he was called the "King of *Salem*" <note>Malki-Tzedek/Shem; Salem means 'complete' or 'peace'</note>.

"Salem" refers to the secret of the Complete Name <note>original: "שם שלם"</note>, the Jerusalem of Above. Afterward, the Land of Israel was given as a promise to our forefather Abraham, when the Lord said: "Go forth from your land... to the land I will show you." It is well known that our Sages said: "These are the generations of heaven and earth when they were created (*be-hibaram*)"—the letters of *be-hibaram* can be rearranged to spell *be-Abraham* ("for Abraham"). Everything was created for Abraham, for he is the foundation of the world's structure, representing *Chesed* <term>Loving-kindness</term>. As it is written: "A world of kindness shall be built."

Thus, the verse "Go forth" (*Lech Lecha*) hints at the secret of the Tetragrammaton. At that time, the Light did not yet fully manifest, even during the establishment of the Land of Israel, but only the letters *Yod-Heh*. Abraham's life represented the repair of Adam's sin involving the Tree of Knowledge. Abraham said, "Lean under the tree," and we have already explained that this "Tree" was partial, and Abraham represented its "living" <note>original: "חי" - Chai, meaning life/18</note> repair.

In the future, Shem’s hint regarding the "Hidden Thought" will be realized, but Abraham's kindness is the force that builds the world through the repair of the Name. This is also hinted at by the numerical value <term>Gematria</term> of 72 <note>The "Name of 72" associated with Chesed</note>, which equals the word for "One" (*Chad*) when the Name is expanded. Abraham also called the place "Fear" (*Yireh*), which shares the same letters as "Lion" (*Aryeh*), the animal that channels kindness. This is the secret behind the commandment to appear in the Temple three times a year—the word "Shall appear" (*Yera'eh*) also relates to the number 72.

To return to the matter: Abraham preceded the hint of the Name that represents the "Initial Thought" <note>Shem</note>, even though that thought will only be fully realized in the "Final Action" of the future. Abraham acted in the realm of the Temple. This is why the Midrash places Abraham before Shem in the naming of Jerusalem. Jerusalem was first called *Salem* (associated with Shem and the Hidden Thought) and then *Yireh* (associated with Abraham and the revealed service). The final name, *Yerushalayim*, combines both.

<margin>
This is explained in the *Zohar* and in the *Pardes* (Chapter 7 on Essence and Chapter 20 on the Singing Kingship). We merit to awaken the union of Wisdom and Understanding through our awakening below. Just as the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) awakens us from below, we awaken the union of Beauty and Kingship. This is the secret of the prayer mentioned where the Holy One, Blessed be He, "prays" in the *Sukkah*: "May it be My will that I see the building of My house." This is the awakening rising from the secret of the *Sukkah*, where the Kingship sings to the higher realms, for a house is built with Wisdom and Understanding.
</margin>

**And** this also explains the statement of Rabbi Berechiah regarding how the Holy One, Blessed be He, "changed" the world. The **Sukkah** is known to represent the secret of the number 26 <note>The value of the Tetragrammaton</note> and the union of the Names of God. This represents the union we merited in the Temple.

**Let us return** to our topic: through the cessation of the "husks" <term>Kelipot; forces of impurity</term> and the daily refinement of our actions, a "New light will shine upon Zion." This is the secret of the blessing "Creator of the Lights." It does not say "He who created" (past tense), because that light was hidden. However, every single day we get closer to that light. The Name of God will eventually be complete, and the "Form" will be perfectly aligned. May the Blessed Name forgive me for speaking at such length to reveal these hints.

**Thus**, the structure of the blessings—"Creator of the Lights," "Giver of the Torah," and "Who chooses His people Israel with love"—is clarified. These are the three things that bind the Holy One, the Torah, and Israel together. "The Lord's portion is His people, Jacob is the lot <note>original: "chevel" - literally a rope</note> of His inheritance." Like a rope tied above, when one who holds it below shakes it, the movement travels to the top. If one ties himself to impurity, God forbid, the holiness does not descend. If one connects to the "Left Side" <note>The Side of Impurity</note>, he brings impurity upon himself and causes himself harm.

Then, the "rope of his inheritance" becomes a "rope of mourning." As I cited above, "Woe for the great sun" <note>A metaphor for a great soul lost</note>, for man is made in the Supernal image and likeness. Man also contains a side of evil, for "God made one corresponding to the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note>. The "Side of Impurity" is like an ape before a human, which was awakened by Adam’s sin. Choice is in man's hand to lean toward whichever side he desires. "To one who comes to be purified, they assist; to one who comes to be defiled, they open the door."

Reward and punishment are essential and natural consequences of the deed itself. They are not like the arbitrary decrees of a human king who could have chosen to punish or reward differently. In the commandments of God, the "reward for a commandment is the commandment itself"—it is the person's cleaving to the Divine. The "reward for a transgression is the transgression itself," for it brings the person to the root of that sin, which is the "husk" (*Kelipah*). I have already elaborated on this matter previously.

<margin>
The counselor is praised... in my youth in my pamphlet... regarding the verse... from the two paths of our secret...
</margin>

**From this**, we can properly understand what is hidden from the eyes of the philosophers who investigate the "change of Divine Will."

House, City, Wall <note>Metaphors for spiritual protection</note>. They think that the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees a decree and then, through repentance, prayer, and charity, He "changes" His mind for the better. They walk in darkness, for there is no "change" in Him, Heaven forbid. Rather, it is all a matter of the person grasping a different aspect of the Divine Will. If reward and punishment were merely arbitrary agreements, it would look like a change of heart in God. But "Will" is the secret of the revelation of the Emanations <term>Atzilut</term>, which include all opposites according to the awakening of those below. If a person sanctifies himself below, he is naturally sanctified from above.

If he then awakens and casts off his sins and clings to holiness, he is naturally sanctified, and the Supernal Will has not changed. On the contrary, this is the very "shadow" of the Will. "Everything is foreseen, yet permission is granted." Even His humility, of which the Sages said, "Wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility"—this is just human language. In reality, it is essential: as the person is, so is the Divine response awakened. The anger or "burning wrath" mentioned in verses is not an emotional change in God, but the person bringing that specific boundary or judgment upon themselves.

The author of *Maarekhet Elokut* wrote in the "Book of Kingship": Everything is part of the thought... not separate... He is simple and unique in all parts of His names and attributes... only from the perspective of the receivers...
</insert>

# House of the Lord, House of David

<margin>Understanding</margin> <note>Hebrew: *Binah*, the third of the ten Divine emanations, often associated with the Divine Mother</note> Through its letters, it extended the letter *Pe* <note>The letter P, which also means "mouth"</note> in such a way that it brought into action the "touching" mentioned above in that encompassing circle. This is not the case for what is above Understanding, where there is no such contact, as I explained at length earlier. At that time, it was clothed in "garments of skin" <note>original: *kotnot or* (כתנות עור) - referring to the physical state of humanity after the Fall in Genesis</note>. Then, the Name was not "whole," for the letters *Yod-Heh* <note>the first two letters of the four-letter Name of God, Y-H-V-H</note> are, as it were, affected by a blemish, in the manner we will explain later. Thus, the letters *Yod-Heh* do not currently have their full elevation. However, when the world returns to its primordial state of "garments of light" <note>original: *kotnot or* (כתנות אור) - a pun on "skin" vs "light" based on nearly identical Hebrew pronunciation</note>, then the Name will be whole. I have already explained above that the "advantage of light comes from darkness." In the future, goodness will be absolute, and there will never be a blemish again, for the concept of "going away" will cease. The letters *Yod-Heh* will then be like the letters <margin>And You</margin> *Vav-Heh*, meaning there will be no grasp for any blemish. They will constantly ascend to their root in Wisdom and Understanding. "The son will ascend to the father"—meaning the *Vav* into the *Yod*—and "the daughter will ascend to her mother"—meaning the final *Heh* into the first *Heh*. In this state, the letters *Yod-Heh*, according to their root, will also be *Vav-Heh*. Then the secret of the Name, which is *Yod*, will become the name *Y-H-H* <note>original: יה"ה</note>. This is what I understood from the Godly Kabbalah of the Arizal <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century mystic of Safed</note>. The order of the levels will be as follows: first, the Name will be whole, namely *Yod*, and "His great Name will be magnified and sanctified" to reveal <margin>And You</margin> the secret of the "hidden of hiddens." The *Yod* will be the secret of *Y-H-H*, and the verse "And the Lord shall be King" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> hints at this. On that day "The Lord shall be One and His name One." First, the Name is magnified and sanctified; these are the letters *V-H-H*, which are the letters of *Yod* when the Name is whole and the Throne is whole. These are the letters of *V-H-A* <note>original: והא</note>, and the letter *Heh* is His dwelling place. This is "The Lord shall be King... on that day." Afterward, the Great Presence ascends higher and higher to *Y-H-Y-H* <note>original: יה"יה</note>. The letters *Y-D Y-D* <note>original: יד' יד</note> will return to being the letters *Y-H-H*. <margin>And You</margin> Then He is One and His Name is One, symbolized by "Two kings using one crown" <note>A Talmudic reference to the sun and moon, here used to describe the perfect balance of Divine attributes</note> above in their root in Understanding. Now, it is *Y-D Y-D* and His Name is One in His holy palace, in the secret of the "great luminary" and the "lesser luminary" <note>The sun and moon / Masculine and Feminine principles</note>. But in the aspect of the highest elevations, they are "two great luminaries" in the secret of the "crown of beauty." To understand this matter clearly, God has granted me knowledge of three things. First, the True Light is He, as it says: "The Lord is my light," "Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you." This exists <margin>And You</margin> in three matters, as I will explain. But first, I will introduce the verse: "Let there be light, and there was light." We also find three letters of the Name together in a place where sin falls, which is *Y-H-H*. These are the letters *Y-D Y-D*, for the final *Heh* is doubled. Behold, the light hidden in the "hiddens of hiddens" is represented by the letters *Y-H-H* in place of *Y-H-V*, for then the Name is *Y-H-H* instead of *Y-D Y-D*. This is a hint that *Y-H-V* was the light that was hidden, becoming *Y-H-Y-H*. When the *Vav-Nun* <note>The letters representing the physical/temporary world</note> is removed from them, it returns to being *Y-H-H*. That is, after six thousand years, it will return to being "Light." This is what is meant by "Let there be light [future] and there was light [past]"—it already was. This is the secret of "Let there be light and there was light."

---

## **Then**

You will be able to explain the interpretation of the Name, which people explain as "He was, He is, and He will be." One might ask: how are the letters *Y-H-H* hinted at in the letters of the Name? Only according to the way I have written does it work well. God forbid one should think otherwise of what is written: "That which was, is that which shall be" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:9</note>. For "He was" is the Name that was hidden, and in the future, the Name will return to being "He will be" (*Yihyeh*). Even now, when the Name is in its full spelling, it is in the secret of *Y-H-V*. This is the hint in "What is man (*Adam*)?" <note>A play on the numerical value of the Name</note>, for the name *Y-D Y-D* in its full spelling—*Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Aleph, Vav-Aleph-Vav, Heh-Aleph*—has the numerical value of 45, which is the same as *Adam*. From the time of Adam’s corruption, even though they later achieved some rectification—such as at the receiving of the Torah and later during the building of the Temple when the moon was at its full—the Name did not return to the state of "He will be" (*Yihyeh*), only to *V-H-H*. This is because the world was not fully rectified; only at the coming of the Messiah will it be rectified and the Hidden Light revealed. This is the hint: "In the place where the sin falls"—which is the tree from which the first man ate—there shall be *Y-H-H*. Even in rectification and corruption, it will not yet be in the state of "He will be" until the future. Then it will be clearly seen that "He who was, will be." Now, the Name is in the state of "He is" (*Hoveh*). At the time of corruption, such as during the destruction of the Temple, the Name is not at all whole; the letters *Vav-Heh* are missing. This is the secret of "woe upon woe" <note>original: *hoveh al hoveh* - a pun on "is" and "calamity"</note>. It is not just that the letters of "Being" (*Hoveh*) are missing, but because of our sins, the Name is not whole even in these letters. The three states are: 1) "He was/He will be," which is the secret of the Hidden Light; 2) The aspect of the four-letter Name during the time of the Temple; 3) The aspect where the Name is completely whole, when a spirit from on high is poured out in the future, and "The Lord shall be King" as *Y-H-H*. This is the secret of why the "Mother of all living" is called *Chavah* (Eve), though she should have been called *Chayah* (Living). Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki, the premier medieval commentator</note> wrote that *Chavah* is like *Chayah*. This is why *Chavah* is like *M-Y-H* <note>unclear numerical or mystical substitution</note>. One who has the eyes of the intellect will understand what I have written about the "missing" letter; for even during the time of rectification, it becomes *Y-H-V* from that which was hidden. This is the hint in the verse "bitter was..." and in the future, when the letters return to their root in the secret of "the mother of all living," which is Understanding in union with Wisdom, then the letters *Vav-Heh* will return to being *Yod-Heh*. This is the secret of why "Songs" <note>referring to the Song of the Sea or the Temple songs</note> are sometimes referred to in the feminine and in the future in the masculine. Even at the time of the song during the building of the Temple, it was in the secret of "Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad." The Sages said "Let the heavens rejoice" is masculine, and "Let the earth be glad" is feminine. However, in the future, the letters *Vav-Heh* will also return to being *Yod-Heh*—everything will be masculine, which has the numerical value of "Blessing" (*Berakhah*).

---

## **And according to**

What I have written, we can explain the *Midrash Rabbah* on the portion of *Vayeira*. The text reads: "Abraham called the place 'Yireh' (He will see), as it is said, 'And Abraham called the name of that place: The Lord will see (*Yireh*)' [Gen 22:14]. Shem <note>The son of Noah, traditionally identified as Melchizedek, the king of Shalem</note> called it 'Shalem' (Whole/Peace), as it is said, 'And Melchizedek, king of Shalem' [Gen 14:18]. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: 'If I call it *Yireh* as Abraham did, the righteous Shem will be aggrieved. If I call it *Shalem*, the righteous Abraham will be aggrieved. Rather, I will call it *Yerushalayim* (Jerusalem), combining both names: *Yireh-Shalem*.'" Rabbi Berakhia said in the name of Rabbi Helbo: "While it was still called *Shalem*, the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a sukkah <note>tabernacle/booth</note> for Himself and would pray in it, as it is said, 'And His sukkah was in Shalem' [Psalm 76:3]." What did He say? "May it be My will that I see the building of My house." Another interpretation: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed Abraham the Temple destroyed, built, destroyed, and built. "Built"—as it says, "The Lord will see." "Destroyed"—as it says, "On this day in the mountain of the Lord, it shall be seen/destroyed" <note>The Midrash plays on the word *Yera'eh*</note>. "Built and perfected in the future"—as it is said, "For the Lord has built Zion, He has appeared in His glory" [Psalm 102:17].

One must ask of this passage: why does it mention Abraham before Shem twice? First: "Abraham called it *Yireh*... Shem called it..." and later in God's speech: "If I call it *Yireh*... if I call it *Shalem*..." but in the third instance, the name *Jerusalem* is a consensus. On a literal level, we can answer why God did not say "as Shem called it" in the second part, but only "as Abraham called it." The matter is that Shem did not actually "innovate" a name; the city had always been called *Shalem*. He simply called it by its existing name. But the name *Yireh* was an innovation by Abraham. Therefore, since Abraham was more "essential" in the naming, he has precedence. However, we must delve deeper: what honor does Shem receive if the name *Shalem* remains, even though he didn't invent it? We can say that since he was called "Melchizedek, King of Shalem," if the name *Shalem* had been changed, we would not know his greatness. No one would know he reigned over the Holy Land—the land which God seeks out—because in later generations, the identity of *Shalem* would be forgotten. People might think it was some foreign land. This is the literal explanation of the Midrash.

However, we must look deeper into why God didn't just call it *Yireh-Shalem* instead of *Yerushalayim*. Abraham called it *Yireh*, not *Yeru*. The words of Rabbi Berakhia also need explanation regarding the nature of God's "prayer." Many commentators have "dived into mighty waters" <note>an idiom for tackling difficult texts</note> and come up with nothing. We only have the words of the Living God and the foundations laid by the Sages of Truth <note>the Kabbalists</note>, for "the secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him." My teacher, Rabbi Z. <note>likely a reference to a specific mentor or author</note>, noted the phrase "destroyed and built, destroyed and built." I have seen some books that correct this to just "destroyed" once, but if we can justify the existing version, it is "good and pleasant." Furthermore, I have come to give a reason why *Yerushalayim* is written "missing" <note>without the letter *Yod* before the final *Mem*</note> but pronounced *Yerushalayim* <note>as if the *Yod* were there</note>. This is related to the idea that the "Jerusalem of Below" corresponds to the "Jerusalem of Above." Our Sages said: "I will not enter the Jerusalem of Above until I enter the Jerusalem of Below." The simple meaning is that the physical Jerusalem here in the Holy Land corresponds to the spiritual Jerusalem, the "Land of Desire," the "Palace of the Lord." But there is a deeper power here: the "Jerusalem of Below" is the secret of the union of the Divine Names *Y-H-V-H* and *Adonai*, the union of the lower realms. The "Jerusalem of Above" is the union of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*), the supernal union. This is explained in the *Zohar*, the *Tikunim*, and the *Pardes* [by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero].

It distinguishes between the physical Jerusalem and its supernal counterpart, emphasizing that the complete unification of Divine attributes will only occur in the messianic future.</summary>
