<header>The House of Choice</header>

# The House of Choice

->The House of Choice<-

The awakening of the "Good Abundance" <note>original: *Shefa HaTov* — the flow of Divine energy into the world</note> through this good deed occurs because the Holy Will includes opposites. Every "great voice that did not cease" <note>A reference to the revelation at Sinai (Deuteronomy 5:19). In Jewish tradition, this voice continues to echo eternally.</note> in the aspect of the revelation of the world of Emanation <note>original: *Atzilut* — the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, closest to the Divine source</note> was likewise a voice comprised of the forty-nine facets of the "impure and pure," the "forbidden and permitted," and the "liable and innocent," as I have explained at length above.

<margin>
Your sign for the letter *Bet*: 164. He wrote "in His mercy" and "in the beginning" in "World, Year, and Soul." <note>These are the three dimensions of reality—space, time, and spirit—found in the *Sefer Yetzirah* (The Book of Formation).</note> See the "Right Hand in the Soul" in section 7. Your sign for the letter *Gimel*: 169. He wrote "Crown," "and they added this to that," and "so it was fixed in the World." See "Right Hand in the Soul," etc. There are one hundred items in the rest of the matters and the rest of the letters through which the letters are constructed, their combinations, their repairs, and their crowns. In the beginning, He created every member found in human beings—all the limbs, tendons, and veins—through these twenty-two letters. When a person is joined in the "Book of the World," that covenant and knot that binds the limbs together is made of the letters through which the limbs were created. They are divided individually and then return to move and rest, saturating the light and the flow of the spirits that thicken within the person through the awakening of the King, in order to bind the companions and the veins. So it is found in His words.
</margin>

**Based on** the matter I have written, I shall now build, in awe and fear, in law and knowledge, a gateway to the **House of Choice**. By **"House of Choice,"** I mean the subject of knowledge and free choice which the early and later scholars investigated, following the path of Maimonides <note>original: *HaRambam* — Rabbi Moses ben Maimon (1138–1204), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher</note> in the *Book of Knowledge*, specifically in the *Laws of Repentance* and in the eighth of his *Eight Chapters* <note>The introductory chapters to Maimonides' commentary on *Ethics of the Fathers*</note>. There they investigate the following premise: "Lest you say: Does the Holy One, Blessed be He, not know everything that will be before it happens? Does He know if this person will be righteous or wicked, or does He not know? If He knows they will be righteous, it is impossible for them not to be righteous. And if you say He knows they will be righteous but it is possible for them to be wicked, then He does not know the matter clearly." These are his words, and Maimonides ascended there...

The intention of God regarding the "Beginning of Choice" <note>original: *Reshit HaBechirah*</note> was to bind the "dead deed." Its lightness was within the letters engraved in it, not at the moment of its movement. He explained to them that this is why Elisha <note>The prophet Elisha, who revived the son of the Shunammite woman (2 Kings 4)</note> lay upon the boy, putting "his mouth upon his mouth, his eyes upon his eyes, and his palms upon his palms," in order to return and engrave within the "House of Choice" <note>here meaning the body</note> those letters that were engraved in the boy’s limbs. He sought to re-engrave them from above, so that every limb would receive its vitality according to its specific "engraved law" <note>original: *chok*</note>. Therefore, the word for "Resurrection" <note>original: *HaTechiya*</note> has the same numerical value as the phrases "and He did," "and He looked," and "the Hand." Thus, the one who "engraved the Torah" is called "Rabbi Meir" <note>A pun on *Meir* (illuminator) and the counting of the letters</note>... and when joined with the "six," they represent the two aspects in which the sun is harsh, reaching 248 matters of law.

From now on, all matters will be included: the general principle that Man was created with the consent of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who placed within him a "letter of simple light." This light is suspended within the composite nature of the good. This light precedes the spiritual nature of the Torah and its deeds; it is the secret of the "consent" mentioned in the preface. This is what draws itself from above into the place of our repair. My physical body is a "receptacle" <note>term: *beit kibul* — a vessel meant to contain or receive spiritual light</note> for the mystical "Orchard" <note>term: *Pardes* — the four levels of Torah interpretation, often referring to the mystical realm</note>, as mentioned in the second preface regarding the "Mistress of Ethics." Man's vessels are elongated there... and they are bound together. If a person delays receiving his spiritual pleasure, his whole body eventually becomes a vessel prepared to receive a light greater than that of an angel, because he possesses a Soul. 

(At first glance, this is difficult: shouldn't one who has a more material composition be more prepared for the light while in the Orchard? That is, from the "tithe of folly"? If God were to send the limb to the light that is "harsh in the sun," the person who is most "composed" would turn away and would not be ready or "ripened" in every vessel of the "Mistress of Ethics" through the process of spiritual descent. Even as we enter the imagery of the "husks" <note>term: *Klipot* — spiritual shells or peels that conceal Divine light and represent evil or impurity</note>, he would not have the primary protection for the benefit of the soul.)

Corresponding to this, God made the spiritual descent of the "husks" to oppose the holy integration. This too is done with wisdom; see the *Pardes* <note>Referring to *Pardes Rimonim* by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Last Gate." 

(A person who is withdrawn and drawn from the beginning toward the heights—leaving the physical world as it is—is naturally led by his "glory" <note>meaning his soul's nature</note> into the imagery and likeness of the "husks," whether in his body or his soul. This is because the source of his soul causes the "Simple Light" to pass through the "pipe" <note>original: *tzinor* — a channel of Divine flow</note> of his soul, leading his soul into the husks, which are the cause of "thickness" and the cause of "good.") 

(And this is exactly what it means: "Do not watch over every person who comes into the world." In the "Holy World," his heart is directed toward God. It is also by chance; this is why we compare our words to glass, for there they adhere.)

The "Simple Light," blessed be He, does not change. Rather, He placed it upon Himself with knowledge and strength. In His clarity, He drew the light to the "flowing place." For one who can perceive it, it is not by chance. There is a great secret here... it is all within the body of the "Name of Man." There are unique "visions." He was not closed off from everything else. 

Consider the "Gate of Choice": God made a large "window" <note>A metaphor for spiritual perception</note> to face the spirit, and the light of the sun would enter it. There are those who also make a window, but it is not so large, and so the light enters only partially. There are those who did not open a window toward their "portion" at all—such as the Nazirite <note>A person who takes a vow of abstinence</note>—even though wisdom enters him because he opened a "pipe" or channel. Even if his choice stops the light from his "portion," it is almost nullified in its significance. And there is one who builds in a "corner," not a "House of Rest" <note>original: *Beit HaShabbat*</note> but a place of "dwelling." He has a window, and he is blessed with pleasure from the light...

The one who goes to make a "doorway" in the "House of Dwelling" <note>original: *Beit HaMeshuvat*</note> allows the light to enter. He brings the light in, even if that was not his intention. This is "merit," for he did not learn from the "transgressors." Your eyes see how the "Chosen One" changes according to the light of the heavens—this one has a great view, this one a small one, and this one is weak. The matter is limited by the person and by our consent; God, blessed be He, does not change. This is the "Thought of Understanding."

Conversely, there is "merit" for the one who "poisons" this. For one who opens a window draws a great light to himself, and he is chosen and blessed. But if he sinks away from the right path, he returns to life through "choice." The "darkness" that comes from the light is caused by the person himself. This is discussed in the *Pardes*, Gate 15, Chapter 5. 

When a person draws from this, it comes with the "thickness" of a delay. There is a "Great Voice" and a "Second Voice." There are "sources" and "refined sources" in the imagery that the Holy One, Blessed be He, spoke of when He founded everything with a "Great Crown." 

Now, if one source is missing, the "connection of the black source" occurs. They are like a spring. The "Great Spring" is the "Darkness of Expansion" found in the world. The "refined firstborns" <note>The initial spiritual flows</note> accompany the human soul in its imagery and reincarnations. Through the soul, the person can be bound to the spirit. But when diligence is lacking and a person transgresses, one of the "voices" is sent away. Though there is "greatness" above and "greatness" below, the "repair" and the "vision" made through the "pipe" of his soul will be lessened. He will be "closed in the black" and tested. 

Who can receive the "Black Light" <note>A paradoxical mystical term for a light so intense it appears as darkness, or a degraded form of light</note>? This was the "refined firstborn" within the "thickness." Who can repair it? They will endure with strength and return. For now, there are "five kingdoms" which were included in five "garments." Every individual's speech was "included in the secret." Each one is a "master of five." 

This is the meaning of "All Israel." There is a spirit. We said there is a "pipe," but that does not mean all "images" are equal. There are many divisions in human wisdom. One who draws from the power of "Kindness" <note>term: *Chesed* — the attribute of mercy and expansion</note> according to the measure of the commandment and recognition will have abundance flow into it. The "pipe" will grow, thicken, and its light will increase. When a person makes "his Torah his primary craft," the greatness of the "reversal" will never cease. 

Returning to the ancient parable: the worker's deed covers him. In the deed of transgression, there is a slight difference. In the parable of the "Black Ointment" in the "Place of Dwelling," the dwelling is not recognized as great because the opening in the "House of Dwelling" is small. The light does not return to him. So it is with the "Tax Collector" in the parable: he did not commit a transgression, but he drew the "light of visions" against his will. That light passes through the "shadows." 

The "Will" and the "Reason" behind the "Oral Torah" <note>original: *Torah she-be'al peh*</note> can overcome this. Man is the one who "measures" everything. He is the knot in everything that is awakened. The "reward" and the "response" are "essential" and not "accidental." Everything depends on the choice of the receiver. 

The "Simple Light" does not change. "The ways of the Lord are straight; the righteous walk in them, but the transgressors stumble in them" <note>Hosea 14:10</note>. This helps us understand the difference between different types of "Penitents" <note>term: *Ba'al Teshuvah* — one who returns to the path of God</note>. There is a Penitent who is lower than a perfectly righteous person, and there is a Penitent who is superior to a perfectly righteous person. 

From the "Ancient Copying" <note>a reference to an earlier manuscript source</note>: On the subject of Yom Kippur <note>The Day of Atonement</note>, it is said that "Great is repentance, for intentional sins are counted as unintentional errors" <note>original: *sh'gagot*</note>. This is when one returns out of fear. But "Great is repentance, for intentional sins are counted as merits" <note>original: *zakhiyot*</note>—this is when one returns out of love. As it says: "When the wicked man turns away from his wickedness... he shall surely live" <note>Ezekiel 18:27</note>. See the *Book of Principles* <note>original: *Sefer Ha-Ikkarim* by Joseph Albo</note>, Part 3, Chapter 16.

According to the parable above, the person’s portion had equal power. Through the "punishment" of God, the water of "Repentance" was poured upon him. His spiritual body was not revealed, nor was his "thickness." There was no lack in God's poverty. The matter is the "Pipe of God," so that the "husks" do not rule over him. These "husks" were the cause of the "punishment," as I wrote. The "Tablet" is the power of the "Kingship" <note>term: *Malchut* — the final Sefirah, associated with the physical world and the feminine Divine</note>. He "opened his mouth with wisdom" <note>Proverbs 31:26</note>. This is actual "Life." The "Integration" meant to "cut off" <note>original: *karet* — spiritual excision</note> is in the "Thought of Light" within the "husks." This is the "House of Dwelling" in the parable. 

This is the "Straight Path," not the "Crooked" or the "Calculated" one. One cannot understand this without it. "Do not let him live." Even with the "wrath" of a "Great and Sweet Repentance," as it was with the "Name" <note>Y-H-V-H</note>. A statement made out of fear does not absorb "blackness" into the light. This "blackness" pushes against the "lowliness." It stands against the secret of "Kindness." Blackness will not spread in the "House of Dwelling" because he acted so...

All of these are the aspects of the Vitality <note>original: *Chiyut* — the divine life-force that sustains existence</note> from the living soul that came into being through the "clothing" of its life-force; for only the Torah <note>original: *Oraita* — the Aramaic term for Torah often used in Kabbalah to denote its mystical essence</note> is, as it were, like a good thing enclosed in His word, may He be blessed. When He removes His way and source, it creates and becomes a living thing. By way of an analogy, the twenty-four <note>referring to the twenty-four books of the Bible or perhaps a specific division of laws</note> who sang of the "four deaths" <note>the four types of capital punishment in Jewish law: stoning, burning, beheading, and strangulation</note> did not do so out of hatred or rage, God forbid, but rather because the person distanced themselves from the source, causing the "evil cutter" <note>original: *Katov Kanzor* — likely a corrupted transcription of a term for a destructive angel or force of judgment</note> to take effect. This is because every recipient experiences the opposite of the source according to their own state. Thus, judgment was permitted for the sake of the person's repair; thus far <note>original: *Knesset HaGedolah* — referencing a halakhic or kabbalistic authority</note>. And so, regarding the matter of blessing and "I will give..." etc., the Divine does not change, as mentioned. His word, may He be blessed, is for you a King, may He be blessed, over both evil and good.

->Only an Awakening<-

Abundance descends from the "Good One" because He is "Simple" <note>original: *Pashut* — in medieval philosophy, this means non-composite, indivisible, and unchanging</note> and unchanging. The change occurs only in the recipient. To use the language of our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: *Hazal*</note>: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will remove the sun from its sheath. The righteous transform the Attribute of Judgment into the Attribute of Mercy <note>original: *Middat HaRachamim*</note>, and the wicked transform the Attribute of Mercy into the Attribute of Justice <note>original: *Middat HaDin*</note>. This is to sweeten the judgment; for the righteousness of the righteous is kindness, mercy, and blessing for him, his children, and his generation. But the wickedness of the wicked is judgment, law, and a curse for him, his children, and his generation, for "the reward of his hands shall be done to him," as the Sages said.

And Rabbi Judah K_y_z <note>likely a reference to a specific commentator or a variant spelling of a known sage like the Maharal</note> wrote as follows: He who breaks his integrity and the foundation of the matter of his connection... his soul is prepared to receive both good and evil. For the praised preparation within it is a "One" that performs opposite things according to the preparation of the recipient. And this is to say—as explained elsewhere—the secret of the verse: "For the Lord God is a sun and a shield" (Psalm 84:12). This means these two attributes are one thing; the performer of kindness also performs and brings the judgment. This is like the sun, which is both "sun and shield." When the sun itself comes, it punishes the wicked and benefits the righteous. As it is said: "Behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace..." <note>Malachi 3:19</note>, and that very same sun that punishes the wicked heals the righteous, as it is said: "The sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in its wings" (Malachi 3:20).

There is also a beautiful parable for this whole matter: food. Food is good for the healthy and bad for the sick. Because of the lightness of the food, it turns into something praised and good for the body; thus far his words. And so wrote all the Kabbalists regarding this change coming from the recipients. It is also mentioned in the words of the Philosophers: In an "uprooted city" <note>unclear reference, possibly a philosophical text title</note>, it says there is a type of "sweetness of holiness" that includes all directions. The Godly essence, may He be blessed, is equally Simple. As it is said regarding "Blessed be He" and others: He is Unique without any specific "matter." Just as with the sun—the sun rises simply without any composition, and when it reaches a strong shield, the difference in effects is due to the accidental changes in the recipient, not a change in the sun at all. The *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>the famous work by Maimonides</note>, Part Five, states that there is no change in Him, for He is Simple in the ultimate simplicity. He is the Absolute Good. Any change or difference is taken from the recipient; if the recipient was wicked and experienced "evil for him," it is because he turned the good into its opposite.

Behold, everything is good in its nature, but that which is drawn from Him—the "seeing" of it—is determined by the person's state. If he "breaks himself," then it is "evil for himself." It is as if the Word itself changed, as it says: "They shall be terrified before Him" <note>referring to the wicked</note>, while "The righteous shall rejoice and exult before God." This is the meaning of "The Lord God is a shield." The wicked man is in rage because the kindness of the righteous man shines upon him as a burden. This is one Simple law before Him, may He be blessed. The Philosophers clarified that no multiplicity or change arises in Him; all change is in the recipient. The Sages attributed this to the Attribute of Good, sometimes to the "Right" and sometimes to the "Left," or to His place. This is the secret of "His right hand is strong."

The intention further is that in all our structures, He, may He be blessed, acts. Sometimes we stand at His "Right" like sons who are close to Him, and sometimes at His "Left" like servants who are distant. One might ask: "Is there not difficulty in this? Is He not a God in whom there is no change, and no 'Right Hand' in a physical sense?" Heaven forbid. Thus far the words of the Sages. And behold, the words of the Sages, the Godly men, and the Philosophers are sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. From there, the matters are deep and hinted at within the essence of the thing itself.

And at the beginning, he presented three precious preliminaries. With these, the first matter will be explained—that which is famous among all who fear heaven: "Good and Evil," and "No evil descends from above," etc. And the verse says:

>And this is to say the opposite: "Out of the mouth of the Most High, there proceeds not evil" (Lamentations 3:38). See the page on the "Unity of Prayer." It will further be explained according to the Kabbalists who said that the thing and its opposite come from Him.<

These are not the "Sun-worshippers" as I have explained elsewhere.

### Preliminary A

The human being, who was created in the "Image of God" in all matters and developments, both physical and bodily, has spirituality within them. In truth, this was the spirituality of the Torah and the Commandments <note>original: *Mitzvot*</note>. *Reshit Chochmah* <note>The "Beginning of Wisdom," a 16th-century kabbalistic ethical work by Eliyahu de Vidas</note> says at the end of Chapter 4: "Wisdom is at the head." The matter of the Torah's commandments is that they were written after the "Way of God." Wisdom in the human body is the entry point for what the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared between the "Hand of Will." For above, Wisdom and the Heavens cannot contain Him, and there is no change in Him. But His understanding can descend and clothe itself below. This is why the Torah and Commandments are called "Life," for they are the "Upper One" clinging to the "Tree of Water." This is the secret of the *Tikkunim* <note>referring to the *Tikkunei Zohar*</note> and the Torah of Adam Kadmon <note>the "Primordial Man," the first manifestation of light in Lurianic Kabbalah</note>. Even though one now engages in the commandments in a physical way, they are rooted in the Upper Emanations. The "Small Man" <note>the human being</note> corresponds to the "Great Man" <note>the Divine structure of the universe</note>. The letters of the body and the four or five elements of the world's building depend on this. Thus, when a person performs a commandment now, even if it seems like a small thing in their eyes, it is a great light before God. By performing a physical act, one awakens its spiritual root above. Therefore, the reward for a person's deed is measureless. As the Rashba <note>Rabbi Shlomo ben Aderet, a major medieval scholar</note> explained, the seven chambers of holiness are affected by the "Upper Spirit" through these small "vessels" or limbs. One angel cannot contain the Upper Light, but the spiritual structure of a commandment can.

### Preliminary B

The excellence of the body, its form, and its wisdom according to our Sages. It was brought by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: *Rashbi* — the traditional author of the Zohar</note> that the body is a "servant" and "throne" for the Holy One, blessed be He. He placed a "judgment" on every limb. The intention is that we are made, as it were, in His "image and likeness," which is an Upper Mold. This is discussed in the *Zohar*, the *Tikkunim*, and all the books of the Kabbalists, and in the *Pardes* <note>referring to *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note>, gate 9. They wrote how the human eye and the kingdom's foundation are a "bond" of the soul with the body. The soul is "borrowed" from the body's events, yet it is a "Crown." The connection of the soul to the body is a fundamental concept, as will be explained in the "Gate of the Soul." See there, and in the *Tikkunim*, how the Divine is present in every single limb. See also *Reshit Chochmah* on the "Gate of Awe" and "Gate of Wisdom," and the "Gate of Holiness." The 248 limbs correspond to the 248 positive commandments, and the 365 sinews to the 365 negative commandments. Furthermore, the human form hints at several Divine Names, as I have lengthened elsewhere. The body is a "mold" for everything.

### Preliminary C

The aspect of the body and soul in the "Secret of Life." These are spiritual matters, such as Adam was before the eating <note>from the Tree of Knowledge</note>, and as he will be in the future. As I have lengthened in my discourse elsewhere, the connection and the "partnership" between body and soul is a state of "drawing close." The book *Hod Tov* says on the verse "The face of the Lord..." that the body has 248 limbs just as the soul has 248 limbs. No one can truly count the "limbs" of the soul—they are the 22 letters of the Torah. Just as the limbs of the body are bound together, the letters bind the 248 limbs of the soul. You must know that the "weaving" of the human structure and its intention was done through the twenty-two letters, as is explained in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, the earliest extant book on Jewish esotericism</note>.

# House of Choice
### Page 29

Apparently, with proper contemplation, everything will be settled correctly with the help of God. In the chapter "With What May One Light" <note>original: *Bameh Madlikin*; Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 32a</note>, the school of Rabbi Ishmael taught: *“If the faller falls from it”* <note>Deuteronomy 22:8, regarding the law of building a parapet on a roof</note>—this person was destined <note>original: *ra'ui*, meaning "fit" or "worthy"</note> to fall from the six days of creation, for he has not yet fallen, yet the verse already calls him a "faller." However, merit is brought about through the meritorious, and liability through the liable. 

Rashi explains: "From the six days of creation," as it is written, "He calls the generations from the beginning," meaning the generations and their deeds were revealed before Him, as well as their punishments; for when the Torah was given, this person had not yet fallen, yet the Torah called him a "faller." Thus far his words. This explicitly states that everything was already known before it was done, including reward and punishment. 

Rashi also notes on the portion *V'Zot HaBerachah* <note>Deuteronomy 34:1</note>, based on the words of our Sages: *"And the Lord showed him all the land."* He showed Moses the land in its tranquility and the oppressors destined to be oppressors. Until Dan—He showed him the children of Dan practicing idolatry, as it says, "And the children of Dan set up the graven image for themselves." He also showed him Samson, who was destined to arise from Dan as a savior. And all of Naphtali—He showed him his land in its tranquility and its destruction, and He showed him Deborah and Barak from Kedesh-Naphtali fighting with Sisera and his armies. And the land of Ephraim and Manasseh—He showed him their land in its tranquility and its destruction, and He showed him Joshua fighting the kings of Canaan who came from Ephraim, and Gideon who came from Manasseh fighting Midian and Amalek. And all the land of Judah—in its tranquility and its destruction, showing him the Kingdom of the House of David and its victory. Until the "hindmost sea" <note>original: *ha-yam ha-acharon*</note>—the western land in its tranquility and its destruction. Do not read it as "the hindmost sea," but "until the final day" <note>original: *ha-yom ha-acharon*</note>—all the events destined to happen to Israel until the resurrection of the dead. And the plain—He showed him Solomon casting the vessels of the Holy Temple, as it says, "In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground." Thus far his words.

Behold, at first glance, this knowledge appears to be absolute and decreed. If so, whatever happened afterward was by necessity and not by choice! Similarly, our Sages said that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed Adam "every generation and its seekers, every generation and its sages, every generation and its leaders." It follows that these preachers, sages, and leaders were already decreed and existed by necessity. Likewise, they showed Moses... <note>reference to Moses seeing Rabbi Akiva in a vision</note> until Elijah raises Rabbi Eliezer... and Moses prayed that he might descend from his loins and was comforted. There are many such sayings of our Sages. 

Furthermore, in the Book of Kings, a man of God said: "Behold, a son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name; and he shall sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places..." This was a long time before Josiah was even born! It would seem Jeroboam and the priests of the high places were forced, Heaven forbid, to maintain this altar so that Josiah would be forced to perform this good deed.

<margin>
See above at the end of the book. I am copying the language of the *Sefer Reshit Chokhmah* <note>a 16th-century kabbalistic ethical work by Eliyahu de Vidas</note> regarding the chapter... tractate Nazir. His language is: "He arranged the order of the verses to be placed in the nature of the possessor of virtue and not the possessor of deficiency..."
</margin>

**And now**, listen to me and let your soul live: Knowledge is Will, and Will is Knowledge. For the matter of "Will" is what He desires to do, and Will is the root of the entire unfolding chain of existence <term>Hishtalshelut: the kabbalistic concept of the process by which the infinite Divine Light descends into finite reality</term> from the greatest to the smallest, and there is nothing else. "Whatever the Lord pleased, He has done." This is itself "Knowledge"—by knowing Himself, He knows His Will. He is the Will and He is the Knowledge, and He knows everything from Himself. 

I must elaborate for my benefit, for the Will includes opposite paths. All paths and their counterparts were given to man to awaken whichever force he desires. "God made man upright," and commanded him not to choose the force of evil. Through his sin, "Good and Evil" were mixed. From this follows reward and punishment, which are not arbitrary; rather, the reward for a commandment is the root of the commandment itself in the upper realms, and the reward for a transgression is the transgression itself. 

All of this is rooted in the concept of Will as one, for the Will includes all paths and their transformations. Similarly, the Torah, which is drawn from the "Brain of the Will," includes forty-nine facets of "impure" and forty-nine facets of "pure," "forbidden" and "permitted," "liable" and "exempt." These are the words of the Living God. Everything exists in the power of the "Great Voice that did not cease," but it manifests only according to the awakening of those below. This "awakening" is the tilt that brings a potential into action. However it turns out, nothing is separate from God, Heaven forbid; it is merely the extraction of one of the paths from the singular power of the Actor.

Behold, before a person does anything—whether good or evil—these paths were prepared. The proof is that the verse says: "See, I set before you today..." <note>Deuteronomy 11:26</note> and "I have placed before you life and death... therefore choose life." This means the path of the righteous and the path of the wicked both exist, and the root of them all is the Supreme Will, which is the "Knowledge"—the knowledge of the essence of His Will at the root of the entire unfolding. Whatever people do, they do through the Supernal power, but the righteous person chooses to walk uprightly.

The Torah is like a hammer that shatters a rock; the attachment and indwelling of everything depends on the awakening of the lower being. If man had remained upright and had not awakened the force of evil, then all his descendants for generations would have been fit to exist in that same state. The soul is a source that would have spread and divided from expansion to expansion, branch to branch. But after he sinned and opened the "Source" in a different, defiled, and evil way, the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed Adam "each generation and its seekers" according to the state of the Source that was now opened—how the expansions and branches were now likely to be.

The truth is that in this composition, they are not "forced." For whoever wants to overcome and walk away from that expansion, and wants to open another of the sources and draw down according to his will, has the power of Choice in his hand to overcome. The Holy One, Blessed be He, only showed Adam—according to the opening of the Source *as it was then*—how the expansion was *fit* to be. There are thousands and tens of thousands of matters that were "fit" to be according to the opening of the source at that time, but they were changed through the power of Choice. Many things remained as they were "fit" to be, like Samuel who was prophesied to be a sage... and these are such matters. Had Samuel wished not to study Torah at all, Heaven forbid, he could have chosen that. But because he walked the good path, he fulfilled the potential. 

Many things are changed through the power of Choice and become attached to a different source. But everything is within the Will, for the source and root of all paths are there. This settles the difficulty in the language of the chapter "With What May One Light" mentioned above: "It was *fit* <note>original: *ra'ui*</note> for this one to fall." There is a difference between "fit/potential" and "established/actual" <note>original: *muchzak*</note>. We learn that a field is "fallen" for two years to be considered "established," not just "fit." This is to say that according to the opening of the Supernal source, it is "fit" for the expansion to be such, but it is not yet "established" until Choice arrives. The power of Choice is not known "above" in the sense of being a recorded decree, but rather through the "Knowledge of the Essence of His Will." It is "known" and "not known" <note>a classic paradox in Kabbalah: God knows the outcome, yet the human has choice</note>; a mark is only made above when one actually walks in darkness and causes a blemish to awaken the force of Judgment, or when one walks in light and illuminates above. Then everything returns from below to above to the Supernal source. 

This is the meaning of the verse: *"Now I know that you are a God-fearing man"* <note>Genesis 22:12, after the Binding of Isaac</note>. The word "Now" means exactly that—literally *now* I know. It implies "I knew already," but the matter is: *Now* it is "established/actual" what I already knew as "fit/potential."

After writing this, God merit me to find hidden words in the Ramban <note>Nachmanides</note> that incline toward my words. In the portion *Vayelech* <note>Deuteronomy 31:21</note>: "For I know their inclination which they are doing today"—this is like "For now I know that you fear God." It was a knowledge in action, for knowledge of the future is "in potential." Had they not sinned, their inclination would not have been known in action... But now that their evil inclination is known to them as well... He tells them all that will happen to them. Thus far his words.

And the Ramban's words in the tractate... Israel was not "fit" to perform that act [the Golden Calf]... but only so that if an individual sins, he may return... or if many sin... The point is that from the side of being "fit"—meaning according to the Source that was opened for Israel—they were not "fit" for that expansion of sin. On the contrary, it should have been the opposite. When Israel received the Torah, they opened the Supernal Source of Good. However, it was changed into an "established" reality through the strength of the choice they made. But it was "fit" that they should not have come to this sin. 

They said, "Unless many sin..." etc. The explanation of their words is: they were not "fit" for the sin, but they were "fit" for the *Repentance* <note>Teshuvah</note> that follows the sin. For even in the strength of their choice, when they departed from their straightness, there remained a "Good Path" inclined toward the "Fit/Potential." 

All the visions that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed to Adam and to Moses were according to what was "Fit"—meaning according to the Wisdom prepared based on how the Source was opened. In this choice, He "calls the generations from the beginning." But the Choice is given as a power to overcome, whether for good or for evil. Many matters were changed from the Wisdom that was prepared according to the "Fit" because the power of Choice did not overcome it, and many attached things were changed by the power of Choice to open another source. But everything is in the Supernal Source, in the root of the Will. And the Will is the Knowledge, for the Knowledge is not outside of Him.

Understand the matter of what the Sages said, cited by Rashi in the portion *Vayera* <note>Genesis 21:17</note> on the verse *"In the place where he is"*: "He is judged according to what he is now, and not according to what he is destined to do." For the ministering angels were accusing and saying: "Master of the Universe! For one who is destined to kill Your children with thirst, You are bringing up a well?" He replied: "What is he now, righteous or wicked?" They said: "Righteous." He said: "According to his current deeds I judge him." This is "In the place where he is." And how did Ishmael [and his descendants] "kill with thirst"? When Nebuchadnezzar exiled them... they were leading them near the Arabians, and the Israelites said to the captors: "We beg of you, lead us to the children of...

<meta>This page begins a new section titled "The Great Gate," focusing on the Kabbalistic principle of "Arousal from Below"—the idea that human actions on earth trigger corresponding movements in the Divine realms.</meta>

# The Great Gate

<margin>The secret of the "Feminine Waters" <note>original: *Mayin Nukvin*; a Kabbalistic term for the human initiative or prayer that ascends to "fertilize" the Divine realm</note> is related to the acts of the pious. It is connected to the mystery of the Menorah as mentioned, and the mystery of the Feminine Waters is found in the deeds of the righteous. Our Sages, of blessed memory, spoke of "Wine of the Worlds" <note>the hidden wine of creation</note> and the establishing of the bowl. For more, see the *Pardes* <note>The classic Kabbalistic work *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> Chapter 10 and the section on the Place of Ma'aser.</margin>

Regarding the verse, "He who blesses himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of Truth" <note>Isaiah 65:16; "God of Truth" is *Elohei Amen* in Hebrew</note>, it is said that the cause of being blessed on earth is due to one first causing the blessing in the "God of Truth." For one who worships with the proper intention <term>kavanah; focused meditative intent during prayer</term> unifies the Name at its beginning, and thereby "gives strength and power" to Him. This is the secret of the verse "Through God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalm 60:14</note> and the secret of "Ascribe strength to God" <note>Psalm 68:35</note>. 

The matter is this: the Supreme Wisdom saw fit to repair the lower form in the likeness of the Higher Form. As the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> received in the chapters on Man: the limbs of a human are arranged according to the pattern of the parts of the Divine Chariot <term>Merkavah; the visionary Chariot of Ezekiel representing the Divine administration of the universe</term>. From this, a person can understand that his own structure is a reflection of the Supernal Structure. It is explained, therefore, that this lower form has a relationship and similarity to the High Form, in whose "image and likeness" we were made. 

It follows from this that one must believe that when this lower form moves through its actions, the High Form moves toward it, hearing and answering. It can be imagined that through the awakening we initiate below in our service, the supernal things are awakened above. For the Torah and the Commandments <term>Mitzvot</term>, which are the intermediaries, were given this power in their very nature—having been emanated and engraved from the Source of Existence and the Supernal Light—to be the key to open that Source from which they flowed. Through their perfect performance, they ascend as a "rectification" via the lower form, which is built in the likeness of the Higher. This is because all "structures" correspond to one another, as has been explained. 

In the chapter "He who Carries" <note>Talmud, Tractate Ketubot 104a</note>, at the time of the passing of Rabbi <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century editor of the Mishnah</note>, he raised his ten fingers toward heaven and said: "Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that I have labored with my ten fingers in the Torah, and I have not derived personal benefit even with my smallest finger." Through this, he made known at his passing that all his days he was a "True Unifier," raising all the branches and unifying them in their Root. He demonstrated this by raising his ten fingers. He showed that in all his Torah study and service, he never asked or intended anything for himself; rather, his entire intention was for the "Divine Necessity" <term>Tzorech Gavoah; the idea that human deeds complete or affect the Divine realm</term> and nothing else. This is the meaning of his saying, "I labored... and did not benefit." Because his unification was truly for the Divine and not for himself, wealth and honor followed him beyond all the sages of his generation.

As it says in a Midrash <note>originally in Aramaic/Hebrew</note>: The Holy One said to Moses, "Go tell Israel: My Name is *I Am That I Am* (*Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh*)." What does this mean? Simply: "Just as you are [present] with Me, so I am [present] with you." Likewise, David said: "The Lord is your shadow at your right hand" <note>Psalm 121:5</note>. What does "The Lord is your shadow" mean? Like a shadow: if you smile at it, it smiles back; if you weep toward it, it weeps in response; if you show it a frowning face or a welcoming one, it gives you the same. So too, the Holy One is your "shadow"—just as you are with Him, so He is with you. 

Thus, the supernal beings are awakened according to the awakening of the lower beings. For this reason, the supernal beings are compared to the lower ones as a shadow is to a form, because they are related and appraised one against the other. Therefore, the shadow moves according to how the form moves. Thus, according to the actions that the lower ones initiate, the upper ones are awakened, whether for good or, God forbid, for ill. This is what they meant by "If you show a frowning face..." and "Just as you are with Him." This is due to the relationship and likeness between them. Therefore, the supernal ones hear and answer the lower ones; the Supernal Source is opened, and the flow of blessing and light descends. 

This is the meaning of the future event mentioned by the Prophet: for then this relationship and likeness will be preserved in perfection. As it says: "And it shall come to pass in that day, I will answer, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth; and the earth shall answer the corn, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall answer Jezreel" <note>Hosea 2:23-24</note>. The verse repeats the word "I will answer" twice. It should have simply said, "In that day, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens..." But it comes to hint that the awakening rising from the lower form awakens the High One and opens the Source, and the Supernal Heads are blessed. This is the "Will" <term>Ratzon; the highest level of Divine desire</term> referred to in the first "I will answer"—to say that the Source of Existence answers the awakening rising from below first. From there, the flow and light come to the "Supernal Heavens," the secret of His Great Name. 

As it says in the *Sefer HaBahir* <note>An early, foundational Kabbalistic text</note>: "How do we know that the 'Heavens' are the Holy One, blessed be He? As it is written: 'And You shall hear [from] the heavens' <note>1 Kings 8:32</note>." This is the meaning of "I will answer the heavens." From there, the light and blessing spread and come to the "Supernal Earth," the Land of Life, the secret of the final letter *He* [of the Name YHWH]. This is the meaning of "and they shall answer the earth." Then the Torah is blessed and the Great Name is unified in all its powers. Without this [awakening], there would be no place for the flow and blessing at all. Afterward, the blessing spreads to the lower ones, as it says, "and the earth shall answer [the corn...]," which is the secret of "And the land shall yield its fruit" <note>Leviticus 26:4</note>. And Israel is called "Jezreel" because they "sow God" <note>a play on the name Jezreel: *Yizra-El*</note> toward the heights and cause His kindness through their good deeds, which are the commandments. These are the intermediaries that awaken the High Form toward the lower, as mentioned above.

**And these are the words** of Rabbi Hiyya in the "Gate of the Chariot": The lower ones awaken the upper ones. It is explicitly stated: "Those who prepare the back [of the throne]" and "Everything He has made is for His sake." Through the medium of lower things, we can influence the upper ones. There is a great hint of this in nature in the matter of the **Magnet** stone <note>original: *Magnites*</note> that draws iron. For when you engrave it well and remove all its dross, and then break it in two and put one piece in one corner and the other piece in another corner—even if they are as far apart as you wish, even a thousand miles—if you place iron near one of these pieces, you will find that every movement that piece makes, the other piece makes at that very same moment. 

There is another great hint in the matter of wine in a barrel. For at the time that its "mother" <note>the vine</note> which is in the vineyard undergoes a change—that is, when it blossoms and its flower emerges—the wine inside the barrel also undergoes a change at that very same time, because of the change affecting its mother, even though that wine is far away and separated from the vine. This is like what is said in Tractate Bava Kama regarding wisdom... everything follows its generation. 

Similarly, our Sages said that "the lips [of a scholar] move in the grave" <note>Talmud, Sanhedrin 90b</note>. The meaning is that when one mentions a legal ruling in this world in the scholar's name, his lips also move in the grave at that hour, similar to what the wine does in the barrel. Also, fruits decay at the time when the trees are producing blossoms and sparks. From all these things, there is faithful testimony that man also makes an impression above with every step he takes below, whether for good or ill. This is because he was created from the supernal ones in the "Image of God." This Divine Image binds him to his God like an iron chain hanging in the air; when you move the lowest link in it, the highest one also moves. 

The commandments are the ten Sefirot <term>the ten divine emanations or attributes</term> and intentions. When a man performs them below, he—as it were—causes power to flow from the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term> into the Supernal Form through the "channels of thought" toward that specific attribute represented by that commandment. Then the upper ones are blessed because of the lower ones. This ends his words.

Conversely, God forbid, it is written: "You weakened the Rock that begot you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18</note>.
**Repeated in the Prophets:** "And what will You do for Your great Name?" <note>Joshua 7:9</note>.
**Tripled in the Writings:** "And David made a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>. The word "made" (*vaya'as*) implies "rectification" or "fixing," as explained in the Zohar. And regarding "David made a name" and "He made them" <note>referring to the commandments</note>, all will be explained later. This is why the pious are called "Men of Action" <note>Anshei Ma'aseh</note>, because through their good deeds they rectify and "make" the Glory, the secret of "Power," as in "Let the power of my Lord be great." 
Further in the Writings: "Our Lord, how excellent is Your Name in all the earth!" <note>Psalm 8:2</note>. Daniel said: "Cause Your face to shine upon Your sanctuary that is desolate, for the Lord's sake" <note>Daniel 9:17</note>—meaning, build the House so that the Queen <note>The Shekhinah</note> is not delayed in the house of the maidservant. For it is not the honor of the Queen to be outside her palace, and certainly not in another's domain. Since the Holy Temple is the throne for the Supernal Glory, which is the Shekhinah <term>the Divine Presence, often described as feminine</term> hinted at in this Name [Adonai], he said "for the Lord's sake." For when the Shekhinah dwells in the Temple and rests upon Israel, who are Her children, then the Great Name is unified in Its Glory, and the "mother of children is happy." Then the King Solomon <note>symbolizing the King of Peace/God</note> emanates light upon Her from the Source. For when the Lower Shekhinah dwells among the lower beings, the Upper Shekhinah also dwells among the upper beings. Since the dwelling of the Shekhinah among Israel is a "Divine Necessity," this is the reason for the sacrifices brought in the Sanctuary—to bring the Shekhinah down and keep Her constant among the lower beings. Through this, the supernal matters are unified from the beginning...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of "The Great Gate," specifically addressing the paradox of Divine foreknowledge versus human free will. It uses the biblical story of Ishmael and the theological teachings of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (the "Remak") to explain how human actions can actually "rearrange" the spiritual potential of the world.</meta>

# The Great Gate

My children, those who seek us, descendants of Ishmael, should have mercy on us, as it is said: "The caravans of the Dedanites" <note>Isaiah 21:13; the Midrash interprets "Dedanites" as "cousins" (*dodanim*)</note>. Do not read "Dedanites" but rather "beloved cousins." The text says they come out to meet them and bring them salted meat and puffed-up wineskins. The Israelites thought they were full of water, but when one puts it in his mouth and opens it, the air enters his body and he dies. These are the words of Rashi <note>The preeminent medieval commentator, 1040–1105</note>. One must ask: the Ministering Angels wanted to prevent the well from rising for Ishmael, for he surely would have died, as the verse testifies: "And she cast the child..." for she said, "Let me not see the death of the child" <note>Genesis 21:15-16</note>. If so, what was the angels' logic? What of the future, where the descendants of Ishmael would kill Israel with thirst? If Ishmael dies now, the future evil is canceled! However, the matter is as is known: Divine knowledge of the future is based on what is fitting, not on what is fixed. It is based on what is prepared for the current moment from the opening of the Source. At that moment, God’s knowledge communicated it as such. But it is possible for things to change through the power of human choice <term>bechirah; the fundamental principle of free will</term>. The Ministering Angels asked the Holy One, Blessed be He, to change what was "fitting" by necessity, but the Holy One did not wish to, saying instead: "Where he is now" <note>Genesis 21:17; the principle that a person is judged by their present state, not future potential for evil</note>. Choice is given; if Ishmael had wanted to overcome his nature and not sin, or if Israel in that generation had been righteous, the "fixed" reality would not have occurred as it was "fitting" to. Through this principle, all matters in the Torah are allegorical. For example, if the generation of Jonathan had not sinned, that specific hint would not have manifested in action. You might wonder how a hint can be utilized this way. Therefore, just as the Divine Will is a mixture of all opposites, so too is the Torah: all its words and hints change into many different matters and endless permutations, and all of them are true. Everything is included in the Torah, and "let him who chooses, choose." I will bring you proof from the root of all things: had the First Man <note>Adam</note> not sinned, this Torah would have been prepared in a different manner than it is now, as the *Pardes* <note>The book *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> wrote in the "Gate of the Soul," which I transcribed above.

**Likewise**, if Jeroboam ben Nebat <note>The first king of the northern Kingdom of Israel, known for leading the people into idolatry</note> had desisted from the altar and repented, then the spiritual preparation would have been such that his name and mark would have been etched into this holy structure. This preparation was according to what was "fitting," but it was hidden and reversed within four days. Afterward, it was extended through the power of his choices. Thus, we are informed that Divine knowledge does not change, for His knowledge is not external to Him; rather, His knowledge is the essence of His Will. Whether before human action or after, His knowledge is fulfilled because it is the knowledge of His own essence. And yet, choice is in the hand of man to make an impression above and to open the Source of Will according to his desire. For the Will includes everything—kindness, mercy, and even the "missing" <term>chata'ah; usually translated as "sin," but here implying a lack or void</term>. Man has the power to arouse the Upper Realm according to his choice. Because all things, above and below, were placed in his authority, the "key to the source" is in his hand. The advice and the service belong to him: "Choose life" <note>Deuteronomy 30:19</note>. The true Good is to do good for others, for such was His generosity—to bring existence into being so that it might be good and receive good, but only so that its merit might be earned, as I wrote above regarding the matter of "missing."

**Behold**, what I have written is close to the path of the Rabbi of the *Pardes* in Chapter 9 of the "Gate of Essence and Vessels." However, there is a great difference understood by one who contemplates deeply. If he sees it in my words, blessed be God, for I have aimed for his intent and to understand it well through a lengthy clarification. There is no doubt that this was the intent of the great Rabbi, the Remak <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, 1522–1570, a central figure in Safed Kabbalah</note>, of blessed memory, in the portion of *Vayeilech*, which I transcribed above within the "Vision of Knowledge."

## The Great Gate

Know, my sons, that in this power I have described—that the keys are in the hands of man—there is a hidden secret handed down to the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> who have entered the mystery of God. It is received from person to person back to Moses at Sinai. Truly, into the hands of man were given the keys to the external realms and the keys to the internal realms. He does not go out to the holy service merely to open things for himself; the primary goal of the service is for the sake of the High One, to unify the Great Name until the Infinite <term>Ein Sof; the "Endless," the most primordial, unknowable aspect of God</term>. This is achieved through the Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments, whose roots are the mystery of the Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term>. This was emanated for the sake of man, who is in the "image and likeness" of the High One. Through the fulfillment of Torah and commandments, one awakens the power above and, as it were, "strengthens" Him. I have already hinted above in several places that the general structure of the Emanation consists of Beauty <term>Tiferet; the male aspect of the Divine</term> and Sovereignty <term>Malchut; the female aspect or Shekhinah</term>. They are the roots of the worlds. They are the secret of "turning from evil and doing good." If a good deed is done below, then the "Head of Thought" reaches the "End of Action." Then, strength is added to the "Might" <note>Gevurah</note> above, as it were, and love and will and a great connection are formed between our two "Beloveds" mentioned above—the two Cherubim. They turn their "faces toward one another" <note>Exodus 25:20</note> like a man arousing his companion. For we, the House of Israel, emerged in our souls from the womb of our Mother, which is the Name *Adonai* <note>The name of God associated with Malchut/the physical world</note>, the source of Israel. As it is said in the congregations: "Bless the Lord from the Source of Israel" <note>Psalm 68:27</note>. Through the union of Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, which pours into his "Justice" <note>Tzedek/Malchut</note>, the secret of the world, from which souls bear fruit, for "the Living God is in our midst." Therefore, the families of Israel are small in number, as it is said: "The Lord has chosen you to be few among the nations" <note>Deuteronomy 7:7</note>. The nations of the world are 70, but Israel is 65, which is the numerical value of the Name *ADNY* <note>A-D-N-Y = 1+4+50+10 = 65</note>. When the "branches" within the attribute of *Adonai* (which are the roots of Israel) shine, they illuminate the "Face of the Great Name" <note>Y-H-W-H</note>. Then the Name is unified in its glory through the letters *V-H* <note>The last two letters of the Tetragrammaton, representing the connection between the heavens and earth</note>. This is the preparation that causes brotherhood and creates unity above. Then the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> dwells within Israel, as it is written: "And I will place My dwelling place among you" <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>. But if Israel sins, there is a separation between those who should be attached. The Divine Presence is, as it were, in exile, and "a handmaid shall inherit her mistress," as we will explain later. Then the Name is not "whole," as it were, for the letters *V-H* are missing. I have already explained above that the letters *V-H* are the preparation that causes brotherhood for the "external women" <note>a reference to the forces of the "Other Side" or *Sitra Achra*</note>. These are the words of Rabbi Galante <note>Rabbi Abraham Galante, a 16th-century Kabbalist in Safed</note>: Because of the fewness of the actions, the "affected" must resemble the "actor." Since His Essence is infinite, to create His creations, He had to emanate these ten Sephirot so that there would be some proximity and resemblance to us through their chain of descent, from Cause to Effect, down to the navel of the earth. Thus, the "affected" resembles the "actor" slightly. The beginning of the thought of Emanation is for the sake of the "end of the action"—that is, to emanate the final attribute <note>Malchut</note> which performs all actions. Therefore, through this attribute, all modes of governance rise and fall, whether for judgment or mercy or the opposite. As it is said in the Zohar, Portion *Terumah*: "Behold, now is a time to act, without repair and without perfection." Why? Because "they have made void Your Torah" <note>Psalm 119:126</note>. Because Israel below neglected the words of the Torah, that "Time" <note>the Shekhinah</note> either stands, rises, or falls according to the behavior of Israel. The meaning is that this "Time"—this final attribute—is not "made" (meaning perfected) on its own; it requires us to act and repair it. When it is damaged because "they made void Your Torah," then she is like a menstruant woman. Through the fulfillment of the Torah, she returns to her strength. This happens to her because she is the root of all the holy souls of Israel, and all their forms are engraved within her, as it says in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei Zohar</note>. When Israel below engages in Torah and commandments, the roots of their souls engraved in her sparkle and shine in the "radiance of the firmament." Then she rises, and the "arousal from below" reaches her, and she comes face-to-face with the Holy King and says: "With what have I come before You?" This is the secret of the Feminine Waters <note>Mayin Nukvin</note>. Through this, she rises in delight. Conversely, she descends through the strikes of the sins of Israel. When the wicked are in the world, she "abandons" those roots in which they are rooted, as mentioned in the *Tikunim*. They cease to be radiant and pure because of the accusations of the "prosecutors" <note>destructive spiritual forces</note> who surround the Palaces. Then He pours into her the power of the "shameful judgments," and she descends to pour judgments into the world. Then she is called "World of Debt" until she is purified by the source of her spirits and returns to "Understanding" <note>Binah</note> and to the "Field of Holy Apples" <note>a name for Malchut</note>, and is bound by the three colors of the will, and the world is established.

The matter is clear: when the Great Name is blessed, the worshiper draws down the blessing through his service. This was King Solomon, peace be upon him, who said: "He who blesses himself in the land..."

<column-break/>

...just as the nature of any craft or work. For any flaw that occurs in nature, a deficiency is prepared above. An action that comes from his hand is more of a "shell" <term>klipah; a spiritual husk or barrier</term> than an action that comes from elsewhere. To use a metaphor: a man mixes a cup of wine. If it is done at this time, it is easy for him to cause it or remember it, more than for a master to give his son great perfection. But if the messenger does not go out... [the text here becomes fragmented with metaphors about wine, masters, and servants]... without a doubt, if he sees that a person possesses great perfection, he will know and understand every holy thing. He will find within himself a strength to return to his heart more than what is necessary. That is to say, he is prepared for the honor of his Creator. The community will add honor quickly. But if he only does what is necessary, he is prepared for the King and the appointed task; when they fill it and train it, he will receive it quickly. But if he does not intend for the glory of the Creator, he only achieves it with great difficulty. This is "fitting" for you... in the path of the stars... for the one who causes the man to fall will be considered a possessor of excellence or a possessor of deficiency... as the philosopher wrote. However, I have seen that the matter is influenced by his traits and his additions. As I have demonstrated, the arguments for the actions of man being "fitting" are for a certain purpose... without adding to his excellence or deficiency, unless he has the "vessels" prepared for it...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of "The Great Gate," moving from the mechanics of free will to the profound Kabbalistic concept that human actions "awaken" or "empower" the Divine realms—a concept known as "Worship as a Divine Need."</meta>

# The Great Gate

In the land of the Blessed One, by the God of truth <note>original: *b'Elohei Amen*; literally "by the God of Amen." Amen and Truth (Emet) share the same numerical value (91) in some traditions, representing Divine reliability</note>, it is said that the discourse concerns the land because it causes the blessing to descend through the "God of truth." For one who worships with the proper intention <term>kavanah; focused heart and mind during prayer or a commandment</term> unifies the Divine Name through their movements. In doing so, they provide strength and power to the Divine, based on the secret of the verse, "In God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalm 60:14</note> and the secret of "Ascribe strength to God" <note>Psalm 68:35</note>.

The matter is this: Supreme Wisdom saw fit to repair the lower realms through the upper realms. As the Sages of Truth <note>a common term for Kabbalists</note> received in the teachings on the "Sections of Man," the human form is modeled after the sections of the Divine Chariot <term>Merkavah; the visionary "Throne-Chariot" representing the structure of the spiritual worlds</term>. From this, a person should understand that their physical structure is a reflection of the structure of the "Upper Man." This relationship implies that since man was "made in His image, after His likeness," when this "reflection" (man) moves through his actions below, the Upper Realm is likewise moved toward him, hearing and answering him.

It can be envisioned that through the awakening of the world below through service, the upper matters are awakened above. For the Torah and the Commandments <term>Mitzvot</term> are the intermediaries; this power was placed in their nature when they were emanated and engraved from the Source of Being and the Supreme Light. They serve as the "key" to open that very Source from which they flowed. Through their vitality, actions are perfected and ascended through the repair of the lower form, which is built in the likeness of the upper form. This is because all "buildings" (structures of being) relate to one another, as has been explained.

In the chapter "He Who Carries" <note>Talmud, Tractate Ketubot 104a</note>, at the time of the passing of Rabbi <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century editor of the Mishnah</note>, he raised his ten fingers toward heaven and said: "Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that I have toiled with my ten fingers in the Torah, and I have not derived personal benefit even with my small finger." Through this, at the time of his passing, he informed us that all his days he was a "True Unifier," raising all the "branches" (physical actions) and unifying them in their "Root" (the Divine). This was hinted at by the raising of his ten fingers. He confessed that in all his study and worship, he never asked for nor intended anything for himself; rather, his entire intention was for the "Divine Need" <term>Tzorech Gavoah; the radical idea that human action fulfills a "need" in the Divine economy</term> and nothing else. This is why he said, "I have toiled... and not derived benefit even with my small finger." And from this true acknowledgement for the Divine Need—even though he did not intend it for himself—wealth and honor flowed to him beyond all the sages of his generation.

As it says in a Midrash: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: "Go and tell Israel, 'My name is I AM THAT I AM'" <note>Exodus 3:14</note>. What is the meaning of "I AM THAT I AM"? The simple meaning is: "Just as you are present with Me, so I am present with you." Similarly, David said: "The Lord is your shadow at your right hand" <note>Psalm 121:5</note>. What does it mean that the Lord is your "shadow"? Just like a shadow—if you smile at it, it smiles back at you; if you weep toward it, it weeps in return; and if you show it an angry or welcoming face, it gives the same back to you. So, too, is the Holy One your shadow: just as you are present with Him, so He is present with you.

From this, we see that the upper worlds are awakened according to the awakening of the lower ones. This is why the upper realms are compared to the lower ones like a shadow to a form—because they are related and balanced with one another. Therefore, the shadow is stirred according to how the form is stirred. Thus, according to the actions awakened by those below, the upper ones will awaken either "good" or "evil." This is the meaning of "if you show an angry face..." and "just as you are present with Him..." All of this stems from the relationship and likeness between them. Therefore, the upper ones hear and answer the lower ones, the Upper Source is opened, and the flow of blessing and light descends.

This is the meaning of the future event mentioned by the Prophet: "And it shall come to pass in that day, I will answer, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth; and the earth shall answer the grain, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall answer Jezreel" <note>Hosea 2:23-24</note>. According to the text, it should have simply said, "I will answer the heavens." But it repeats "I will answer" to hint that the awakening rising from the land—the lower structure—awakens the Upper One and opens the Source, and the "Upper Heads" are blessed. This is the intent of the first "I will answer"—to say that the Source of Being responds to the awakening rising from below first. From there, the flow and light come to the "Upper Heavens," the secret of His Great Name.

As it says in the *Book of Bahir* <note>An early, foundational Kabbalistic text</note>: "How do we know that 'the heavens' refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He? As it is written: 'And You shall hear [from] the heavens'" <note>1 Kings 8:30</note>. This is the meaning of "I will answer the heavens." From there, the light and blessing spread until they reach the "Upper Earth," the Land of Life, the secret of the final letter *He* of the Divine Name. This is "and they shall answer the earth." First, the Great Name is unified and blessed in its various aspects; without this, there is no place for the flow and blessing at all. Afterward, the blessing spreads to the lower realms, as it says, "and the earth shall answer [the grain]..." This is the secret of "The earth shall yield her increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit" <note>Leviticus 26:4</note>. And through this, "Jezreel" <note>literally "God will sow"</note>—those who sow and pursue peace above through their good deeds (the commandments)—will be blessed. These deeds are the intermediary that awakens the Upper Realm toward the lower, as mentioned above.

<margin>
Check the end of the secret of "Sorting the Feminine Waters" <term>Mayin Nukvin; the upward spiritual energy created by human deeds</term> toward the Upper Light. In the Zohar, this "Sorting of the Feminine" is performed by the deeds of the righteous, as the verse says, "The memory of the righteous is a blessing" <note>Proverbs 10:7</note>. He is the "Life of the Worlds" and establishes the dwelling place for the Shekhinah <term>Divine Presence</term>. See the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note>, chapter 19, and the section on the "Reason for the Commandments" and its introduction.
</margin>

**These are the words** of the Pious Rabbi in the "Gate of the Chariot": The lower ones awaken the upper ones, as the verse says, "Ascribe strength to God" <note>Psalm 68:35</note>, and it is also written, "Everything has He made for His purpose" <note>Proverbs 16:4</note>. For through the medium of lower things, we influence the upper ones.

There is a great hint for this in the nature of the "Magnet Stone" <note>original: *magnit*; loadstone</note> that draws iron. For when you take a strong one, clean it, and remove all its dross, and then break it in two—if you place one piece in one corner and the other in another corner, even if they are as far apart as you wish, even a thousand miles—if you place iron next to one of these pieces, you will find that every movement that piece makes, the other piece makes at that very same moment.

There is also a great hint in the matter of wine in a barrel. For at the time that its "mother" from which it came—the vine—undergoes a change (when it blossoms and its flower emerges), the wine inside the barrel also undergoes a change at that same time, due to the change in its "mother," even though that wine is far away and separated from the vine. This is as the Sage said: "And like the best wine... that glides down smoothly for my beloved, moving the lips of those who sleep" <note>Song of Solomon 7:10</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "His lips move in the grave" <note>Talmud, Yebamot 97a</note>. The meaning is that when one mentions the teaching of a scholar in his name, his lips move in the grave at that hour, similar to what the wine does in the barrel. Also, fruits decay at the time when the trees put out blossoms and buds.

From all these things, there is faithful testimony that man also makes an impression above with every step he takes below, whether for good or for evil. This is because he was created from the upper realms "in the image of God." This Divine Image links him with his God like an iron chain hanging in the air: when you move the lowest link in it, the uppermost link moves as well. The commandments are the ten *Sefirot* <term>the ten Divine emanations or attributes</term> and intentions. When a man fulfills them below, he—so to speak—overflows power above from the *Ein Sof* <term>the Infinite, God's essence</term> into the Upper Form through the structures of thought, directed at that specific Attribute <term>Middah</term> associated with that commandment. Then the upper ones are blessed because of the lower ones. Thus ends his words.

This matter we have discussed—that worship is a "Divine Need"—is clearly stated in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, tripled in the Writings, and found in the Mishnah, the Talmud, the Midrashim, and—last and most beloved—in the Zohar.

**Written in the Torah:** "And now, I pray, let the power of my Lord be great" <note>Numbers 14:17</note>. And so it is written: "Who rides the heavens to your help" <note>Deuteronomy 33:26</note>. And conversely, Heaven forbid, it is written: "You neglected the Rock that begot you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18</note>.
**Repeated in the Prophets:** "And what will You do for Your great Name?" <note>Joshua 7:9</note>.
**Tripled in the Writings:** "And David made a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>. The term "made" (*vaya'as*) implies a "repair" or "correction," as explained in the Zohar (which I will quote later). The matter of "David made a name" is related to the verse "And you shall do them" <note>Leviticus 26:3; the Sages read "do them" as "making" the commandments themselves</note>. All this will be explained later. For this reason, the righteous are called "Men of Action," because through their good deeds, they repair and "make" the Divine Glory. This is the secret of the strength in "And now, let the power of my Lord be great."

Furthermore, in the Writings, King David said: "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" <note>Psalm 8:2</note>. Daniel said: "Cause Your face to shine upon Your sanctuary which is desolate, for the Lord's sake" <note>Daniel 9:17</note>. That is to say: rebuild the House so that the Queen does not sit in the house of a maidservant, for it is not the honor of the Queen to be outside her palace, and certainly not in the domain of another. Since the Holy Temple is the Throne for the Upper Glory—which is the *Shekhinah* (Divine Presence) hinted at by the name *Adonai*—he said "for the Lord's (*Adonai*) sake." For when the *Shekhinah* dwells in the Temple and rules over Israel, who are her children, then the Great Name is unified in its Glory, and "the mother of children is happy" <note>Psalm 113:9</note>. She then draws down light upon it from the Source. For when the Lower *Shekhinah* dwells among those below, the Upper *Shekhinah* also dwells among those above. And because the dwelling of the *Shekhinah* in Israel is a "Divine Need," this is the reason for the offerings that were in the Temple—the place of the *Shekhinah*—to draw it down and unite it with the lower realms. # The Great Gate

<margin>
In the section on the end of "Female Waters" <note>original: *Mayin Nukvin*; the kabbalistic concept of spiritual energy or "arousal" that rises from human action below to trigger a response from above</note> regarding the piety of the ladder, as mentioned in the Zohar. These "Female Waters" are the deeds of the righteous, intended to return the worlds and establish the "Salt Offering." See the *Pardes* <note>Referring to *Pardes Rimonim* by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> Chapter 19 and the section "From the Dust" in the Afternoon Prayer.
