"In the earth" and "Praise be to the God of Amen." It says that the reason one is blessed on earth is because they caused the blessing first through the "God of Amen." For one who serves with the proper intention unifies the Name from its beginning, and gives "Amen" its strength and power, following the secret of "Through God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalm 60:14</note> and the secret of "Ascribe power to God" <note>Psalm 68:35</note>. The matter is this: since the Supernal Wisdom saw fit to fix the lower form in the likeness of the Upper Form—as the Sages of Truth <note>a traditional term for Kabbalists</note> received regarding the "parts of man," which correspond to the "parts of the Chariot" <term>Merkavah; the Divine assembly or structure of the spiritual worlds</term>—man should understand that his construction is like a spring from the Upper Architecture. It follows, then, that this lower form has a relationship and resemblance to the Upper Form in whose image it was made. It must be believed that when this lower form moves through its actions,

the Upper Form moves toward it, hears it, and answers it. Thus, it can be imagined that through the arousal we initiate below through our worship, the upper matters are awakened above. The Torah and the Commandments <term>Mitzvot</term>, which are the intermediaries, have this power placed in their very nature. Since they were emanated and carved from the Source of Being and the Supernal Light, they act as the key to open that Source from which they flowed. They are perfected and ascend as a "rectification" through the lower form (man), who is built in the image of the Upper, because all structures relate to one another as explained. In the Talmud <note>Tractate Ketubot 104a</note>, in the chapter "He who Marries," it is told that at the time of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's passing, he raised his ten fingers toward heaven and said: "Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that I have labored with my ten fingers in the Torah, and I have not enjoyed [this world] even with my small finger." Through this, that holy man informed us at his death that all his days he was a "true unifier," raising all the branches and unifying them with their Root. He demonstrated this by raising his ten fingers. He showed that in all his Torah study and service, he never asked for or intended anything for himself; rather, his entire intention was for the "High Need" <term>Tzorech Gavoah; the concept that human service 'benefits' or completes the Divine purpose</term> and nothing else. This is why he said, "I labored... and did not enjoy even with my small finger." Because of this true unification for the High Need—despite not intending anything for himself—wealth and honor flowed to him beyond all the sages of his generation. As the Midrash says: The Holy One said to Moses, "Go tell Israel: My name is 'I AM THAT I AM'." What does this mean? Simply that "As you are with Me, so I am with you." Likewise, David said: "The Lord is your shadow at your right hand" <note>Psalm 121:5</note>. What does "The Lord is your shadow" mean? Just like a shadow: if you smile at it, it smiles back; if you weep at it, it weeps in return; if you show it a furious or friendly face, it gives the same back to you. So too, the Holy One is your shadow: just as you are with Him, so He is with you.

This confirms what I wrote: that the Upper Realms are awakened according to the arousal of the Lower Realms. For this reason, the Upper is compared to the Lower as a shadow is to a form, being related and intertwined with one another. Therefore, the shadow moves according to how the form moves. So, according to the actions initiated by those below, the Upper Realms awaken either goodness or, heaven forbid, judgment. This is the meaning of "If you show it a furious or friendly face," and "Just as you are with Him." All of this stems from the relationship and resemblance between them. Therefore, the Upper Realms hear and answer the Lower, which is the flow of the Supernal Source, bringing down the flow of blessing and light. This is the future matter mentioned by the Prophet, for then the relationship and resemblance will be preserved in perfection. It says: "And it shall come to pass in that day, I will answer, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth; and the earth shall answer the grain, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall answer Jezreel" <note>Hosea 2:23-24</note>. The verse repeats "I will answer, says the Lord, I will answer." It should have just said "I will answer the heavens." But it hints that the arousal rising from the lower form awakens the Upper and opens the Source, and the "Upper Primordials" are blessed. This is the "First Answering"—meaning the Source of Being answers the arousal rising from below first. From there, the flow and light come to the "Upper Heavens," the secret of His Great Name. As it says in *Sefer HaBahir*: "How do we know the Heavens are the Holy One? As it is written: 'And You shall hear in the Heavens'." This is "I will answer the heavens." From there, the light and blessing spread and come to the "Upper Earth," the "Land of Life," the secret of the final letter *He* [of the Tetragrammaton]. This is "And they shall answer the earth." First, the Great Name is blessed and unified in its letters—without this, there is no place for flow or blessing at all—and afterward, the blessing spreads to the lower ones, as it says, "And the earth shall answer..." This is the secret of "And the earth shall yield her increase." He calls those who awaken and cause this increase "Jezreel" <note>Hebrew: *Yizre'el*, literally "God will sow"</note>, because they "sow" and increase peace above through their good deeds, which are the commandments. They are the intermediary that awakens the Upper Form toward the Lower, as stated above.

**And these are the words** of the pious Rabbi in the "Gate of the Chariot": The lower beings awaken the upper beings. From your own soul, you can say this, and "From my flesh I shall see God" <note>Job 19:26</note>. It is also written, "He has made everything for His purpose." For through the intermediary of lower things, we perceive the upper things. There is a great hint of this in the nature of the magnet <term>makhni-shes; an archaic term for lodestone or magnet</term> that draws iron. If you polish it well and remove all its dross, and then break it in two, and place one piece in one corner and the other piece in another corner—even if they are as far apart as you wish, even a thousand miles—if you place iron near one of these pieces, you will find that every movement that piece makes, the other piece makes at that very same moment. There is another great hint in the matter of wine in a barrel. At the time that its "mother" from which it came—the vine—undergoes a change, such as when it blossoms and produces buds, the wine inside the barrel also undergoes a change at that same time, reacting to the change in its source, even though that wine is far away and separated from the vine. This is what is meant by "deep calls unto deep." Likewise, concerning the "movement of the lips" [in prayer], Rabbi Yohanan said: "Even his lips move in the grave" <note>Talmud, Sanhedrin 90b</note>. The matter is that when one mentions the power of a departed sage by name, his lips move in the grave at that hour, similar to what the wine does in the barrel. Also, the flowering of herbs occurs when the trees produce fruit and buds. All these things are faithful testimony that man also makes an impression above with every step he takes below, whether for good or evil. This is because of the "Form" created from the Upper Realms, the "Image of God" <term>Tzelem Elohim</term>. This Divine Image ties him to his God like an iron chain hanging in the air; when you move the lowest link in it, the highest link also moves. The commandments correspond to the Sefirot <note>the ten attributes or emanations of God</note>, and when a person fulfills them below with intention, he—so to speak—channels power from the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term> to the Upper Form through the "channels of thought" to that specific attribute which the commandment represents. Then the Upper Realms are blessed because of the Lower. These are his words.

## The Great Gate

The children of our generation and Ishmael <note>The ancestor of the Arab nations in biblical tradition</note>—may they have mercy on us—as it is said: "The caravans of the Dedanites" <note>Isaiah 21:13</note>. Do not read "Dedanites" but "those of our generation" <note>A play on words in Hebrew between *Dedanim* and *Dorenu*</note>. And it says
they go out to meet them and bring them salted meat and water-skins. The Israelites think they are full of
water, but when one puts it in his mouth and opens it, the wind <note>or "air"</note> enters his body and he dies. Thus far are the words of Rashi. And one must
ask: The Ministering Angels wanted to prevent the well from rising for Ishmael <note>referring to the story in Genesis 21 where Hagar and Ishmael are in the desert</note>, for surely he would have died, as
the verse testifies: "And she cast the child..." and "Let me not see the death of the child." If so, how could the Angels
think he should die? And what would become of the future events where Ishmael [his descendants] would kill Israel with thirst? If
he dies now, Ishmael is gone and the future is canceled! Rather, the matter is as is known regarding the future:
it is according to what is "fitting" and not "fixed," but rather according to what is prepared for the present moment from the opening of the Source. And then,
Divine Knowledge, in His knowledge of Himself, is such. But it is possible to change through the power of the overcoming of Free Will (*Bechirah*). The
Ministering Angels requested of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that He change what was "fitting" for that group, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not wish it, but rather said: "In the state he is currently in" <note>original: *Ba'asher hu sham*; a famous Midrashic principle that God judges a person based on their current righteousness, not their future sins</note>. Choice is given. If Ishmael had wanted to overcome his inclination and not sin, or if Israel
in that generation had been righteous, the future would not have been fixed as it was fitting. And in this manner, all matters
in the Torah are by way of metaphor and their changes are a hint to their essence and abundance. And it was fulfilled... and if they had not sinned,
this hint would not have manifested in action. And should you say, "What purpose did the hint serve?" observe that just as the Divine Will is blended
from all opposites, as explained, so too the Torah—all its words and hints change into many matters and permutations
of permutations. The cord of truth—everything is included in the Torah, and "he who chooses shall choose." And I will bring you proof from the root
of all matters: for if the First Man <note>Adam</note> had not sinned, then this Torah would have been prepared in a different
manner than it is now, as the author of the *Pardes* <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, in his work *Pardes Rimonim* (Orchard of Pomegranates)</note> wrote in the "Gate of the Soul," and as I transcribed above.

### And Likewise

If it were... and a fourth... the preparation that they would be worthy in order and like the matter of the buildings, the preparation was according to
the "fitting." And [the city of] Nineveh was overturned within forty days, but afterwards it was extended through the power of the strength of their choice. Behold,
the Divine Knowledge did not change and will not change, for there is never Knowledge outside of Him, only His Knowledge of the essence
of His Will, whether before the action of man or after the action of man. The Knowledge is established, for it is from the knowledge
of His essence and His Will, and it does not spread outside of Him. But choice is in the hand of man to make an impression above
and to open the source of the Will according to his desire and will. For according to everything, he understands wisdom and in His Torah. And this—that
man has the power to awaken the Higher Realm according to his choice and will—is because he was made in His image and likeness, a form
of both upper and lower beings. Therefore, the "key of the sources" is in his hand, and the offer of Knowledge to him is: "Choose life,"
the good and the true, to do good to others; for such was His generous nature—to be found good and doing good,
except so that it may be "goodly," as we explained above with God's help.

### Behold

Close to what I have written is the path of the Rabbi, the author of the *Pardes*, Chapter 9 of the "Gate of Essence and Vessels." However, there is a great difference understood by the one who contemplates
with the best of analysis... Blessed be the Name, for we have aimed for our religion and to understand it well through the lengthy clarification of the matter, which has no doubt that this is
the intention of the Great Rabbi, Nachmanides <note>original: *ha-Ramban*</note>, may his memory be a blessing, in the portion of *Vayelech*, which I transcribed above by way of a vision of knowledge.

# The Great Gate

And know, my children, and mark this "remembrance" that I mentioned, that its opening is a tradition in the hand of man. It contains a secret entrusted to the Sages of Truth,
those who enter the "Secret of the Lord," received from person to person back to Moses at Sinai. For literally in the hand of man are given
the keys to the external realms and the keys to the internal realms. And not to open for himself alone does he go out in the holy service which he performs; rather, the essence of the service must be for "The High" <note>God</note>, to unify the Great Name
unto the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). This is the unification of the Lord, the Torah, and the fulfillment of its commandments, whose roots are the secret of the Emanation (*Atzilut*) emanated for the sake of man, who is in the image and likeness of the Higher One. For through
the fulfillment of the Torah and the commandments, one awakens the Higher Power and, as it were, strengthens Him. For I have already hinted above in several places that the totality of the Emanation of the "Building" is the "Beauty" (*Tiferet*) and "Sovereignty" (*Malkhut*)...
the roots of the worlds. And they are the secret of "Turn from evil and do good." And then the good deeds of the lower beings arrive, for "the end of the deed was first in the thought."
Then strength is added to the "Strength" (*Gevurah*) above, as it were, and love and desire and a great connection between those two "Beloveds," and those two Cherubim "with their faces toward one another." It awakens
a man and his companion. For we, the House of Israel, emerged in our souls from the "Building of our Mother," which is the Name *Adonai*, the Source of Israel, as it is written: "In the congregations bless the Lord (*Adonai*) from the Source of Israel."
Through the circuit of the Beauty of the Lord... the Righteous One (*Tzaddik*), the Foundation of the World (*Yesod Olam*), from where the souls are fruits. For the letter *Aleph* is in our midst... seventy families of Israel... as it is written: "For you are
the fewest of all the peoples." And the nations are seventy, and Israel is sixty-five, corresponding to the numerical value of the Name *Adonai*. And it is written that the "branches" in the order of *Adonai*, which are the roots of Israel, then shine from the light
before the face of the Great Name. And then the Name is unified in its Glory with the letters *Vav* and *He*... and these are the words of the Rabbi, Recanati <note>Rabbi Menahem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note>: "To be partners..."
"I shall dwell in their midst." And if, Heaven forbid, Israel sins, then there is a separation between the connected ones, and the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is, as it were, in exile, and "a handmaid shall inherit her mistress," as we will explain later. Then the Name is not
complete, because the *Vav* and *He* are missing. For I have already explained above regarding the letters *Vav* and *He* that they are the plan where the external ministers have a hold. And these are the words of the Rabbi, Recanati: "To be a partner in
the action, the recipient must be similar to the actor." To fulfill this—His essence being infinite—to create His creatures who are finite, it was necessary to emanate from His light
these ten Sephirot, so that there would be a few "relatives" who resemble us in their chain-like descent and their lowering from cause to effect until the navel of the earth, so that the recipient would somewhat resemble
the Actor. And "the first of thought" in the Emanation is "the end of the deed," which is to emanate the Final Attribute <note>Malkhut/Sovereignty</note> that performs all the actions. Therefore, through this attribute, all the conducts
ascend and descend, whether for Kindness or for Mercy or the opposite. As it is found in the Zohar, Portion *Terumah*: "Also here, 'a time to act' <note>Psalm 119:126</note> was left without repair and without perfection.
Why? Because they 'made void Your Torah,' because Israel below were idle from the words of the Torah. For that 'Time' [the Shekhinah] stands or rises or falls because of Israel."
End of quote. This means that this "Time"—which is this Final Attribute—is not "made," meaning "repaired," but rather needs one to make it, repair it, and adorn it for Her, because they "made void
Your Torah." Then she becomes like a menstruant woman <note>a Kabbalistic metaphor for the Shekhinah being separated from her Divine partner</note>, and through the fulfillment of the Torah, she returns to her strength. And this happens to her—to be rising and falling—because she was the source for all the holy souls
of Israel, and all their forms are engraved in her. And as it is found in the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkunei HaZohar</note>: When Israel below engage in the Torah and the commandments, the roots of their souls
which are rooted in her sparkle and shine in the "Radiance of the Firmament." Then she rises and hovers over the lower beings and appears face-to-face with the Holy Dwelling...
in the secret of "Feminine Waters" <note>original: *Mayin Nukvin*; the Kabbalistic concept of human initiative/aspiration "rising" to trigger Divine response</note>. And by this, she rises and rests and descends, etc., if because of the sins of Israel...
guilty in the world, those gates in which she is rooted are opened. And even though there are many *Tikkunim* before us... and the "Master of Souls." And this is due to the accusation
of the accusers in the surrounding dwellings outside of the Palaces. And they draw into her the forces of the external dwellings. And then she descends to appear... to the world, and "remembers her labor in tranquility"
until she is purified from the source... and returns to her home and to the "Field of Holy Apples" <note>a common Zoharic name for the Shekhinah</note> and is bound by the three colors of the eyes. And this is "a time of repentance" and their love for the world. End of quote.
And the matter is clear: that when the Great Name, may He be blessed, is blessed, the worshiper draws the blessing through his service. And he is Solomon the Prophet, peace be upon him, in his saying, "Which I have loved..."

# The Great Gate

A person is naturally disposed toward a certain craft or quality. For every deficiency that arises in nature, there is a potential for a higher level, though it may be a lack that makes their actions initially lesser. It is slightly easier for a person to endure and remember their struggles in matters of the heart <note>original: *be-inyanei levavot*</note> more than one who possesses a shallow heart at any given time. However, if one does not merit the ease of mind that comes from time, one should not abandon learning at all. This is certainly more within the realm of law and reward. Thus, when they learn, they will clothe themselves in a nature that knows and understands, despite their natural tendencies.

Regarding this, our species in its world finds that temperament affects us more than is necessary. A "mighty man" <term>gibbor; often used in Jewish ethics to describe one who subdues their internal impulses</term> is one prepared for such strength. By behaving correctly, he will become a truly valiant man. Conversely, one who is naturally disposed toward excess beyond what is necessary is prepared for error and loss; yet, when they are taught and habituated, they will accept correction quickly. If one does not aim for such strength, they will only merit it with great difficulty, but it is certainly possible through habituation. I have explained to you that regarding the completion of the virtues, one should not be lacking in the qualities of a person of excellence or a person with deficiencies. Hold fast to what the Sage wrote, for these matters are like a beloved daughter. I make known that a matter is drawn toward its beginning. The philosopher <note>Likely referring to Aristotle, whose "Nicomachean Ethics" heavily influenced medieval Jewish thought on habit and virtue</note> says that the power of a person is to be found in the quality of their actions. This is not at all a simple matter of understanding; rather, every virtue or deficiency results from the preparation of the soul <note>original: *hachanah*; the internal readiness or "vessel" for a spiritual quality</note>. It will be easier in his eyes, and he will receive the reward he is owed, whether it be naturally within him or achieved through great effort.

<column-break/>

The people of our generation, the children of Ishmael <note>A traditional term for Arabs/Muslims</note>, had mercy on us, as it is said: "The caravans of Dedanites" <note>Isaiah 21:13</note>. Do not read "Dedanites" but rather "beloved ones" <note>original: *dodim*; a play on words from the Midrash</note> who go out to meet them and bring them salted meat and inflated water-skins. The Israelites thought they were full of water, but when they put them in their mouths and opened them, the air entered their bodies and they died. These are the words of Rashi <note>The preeminent medieval commentator (1040–1105 CE)</note>. 

One must ask: the ministering angels wanted to prevent the well from rising for Ishmael <note>Referring to the biblical story of Hagar and Ishmael in the desert</note>, for he surely would have died, as the verse testifies: "And she cast the child... for she said, let me not see the death of the child." If so, what was the thought of the Heavenly Angels? What would become of the future, where the descendants of Ishmael would kill the Israelites with thirst? If Ishmael died then, the future trouble would be avoided! 

However, the matter is as I have scattered throughout: the future is judged according to what is appropriate *now*, not according to what is certain to happen later. It is based on the opening of the Source at this moment, and God makes it known through His own knowledge. But it is possible for things to change through the power of human choice <term>bechirah; the fundamental principle of free will</term>. The ministering angels requested that the Holy One, Blessed be He, change what was "appropriate" because of how Ishmael would eventually choose to act, but the Holy One did not want this. He said, "As he is there" <note>Genesis 21:17; a key legal and theological principle that a person is judged by their current state, not their future sins</note>. Choice is given; if Ishmael wanted to overcome his nature and not sin, or if the Israelites of that generation were righteous, the tragedy would not have occurred. 

In this way, all matters in the Torah are like parables. For example, "and you shall remain long" <note>original: *v'noshantem*; Deuteronomy 4:25. The numerical value (Gematria) of this word was used to calculate the timing of the exile</note> served as a hint to the number of years. Had they not sinned, this hint would never have been realized in action. Similarly, you might wonder about the hints used throughout the scriptures. Just as the Desire <note>Divine Will</note> includes all opposites, so the Torah's words and hints change into many matters and permutations of permutations, and all of them are truth. All is included in the Torah, and "he who chooses will choose." I will bring you proof from the root of all matters: had Adam not sinned, then this Torah would have been prepared in a different manner than it is now, as I explained regarding the root in the "Gate of the Soul."

## And So
If Jeroboam son of Nebat <note>The first king of the northern Kingdom of Israel, traditionally viewed as a great sinner</note> had removed his hand from the altar and performed repentance, he and his generation would have had the preparation to be wise. Regarding the building of the Temple: it was built according to what was appropriate, but then it was overturned and hidden within forty days because of the strength of their choices. Behold, the Divine Knowledge did not change, nor will it ever change, for there is never knowledge "outside" of Him. Rather, His knowledge is the essence of His will. Whether before a human action or after, the Knowledge stands firm. He makes His essence known, and it does not spread outside of Him. 

Choice is in the hand of man to make an impression above and to open the source of Will according to his desire. For everything—absolutely everything—is His word and His mercy. He gave man the power to "awaken" the Upper Realm according to his choice. This is because man was made in His image and likeness, both upper and lower. Therefore, the key to the Sources is in his hand, and the counsel and the destiny are his: "Choose life!" For the Divine Will desires and is more awakened by the good, as it is the nature of the Truly Good to do good to others. His original generosity was to bring existence into being so that it might be good and receive good. Even the evil that He created was not essentially for the sake of evil, but so that good might come from it, as was clarified above with the help of the Holy One.

# The Great Gate
Know, my children, the couch of my heart: this that I have researched—that the unfolding of qualities is in the hand of man—contains a hidden secret entrusted to the Sages of Truth, who enter the secret of God. It is a tradition passed from person to person back to Moses at Sinai. For because the keys are "given, given" into the hands of man, he holds the keys to the external realms and the keys to the internal realms. He must not open them for himself alone to go out in the holy service; rather, the core of the service must be for the sake of the High, to unify the Great Name in its uniqueness up to the Infinite <term>Ein Sof; the Infinite, unknowable Godhead</term>. 

This is the unification of God, the Torah, and the fulfillment of its commandments. Their root is the secret of Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term>, emanated for the sake of man, who is in the upper image and likeness. Through the fulfillment of the Torah and commandments, one awakens the upper power and, as it were, strengthens it. I have already hinted above in several places that the general structure of the "Building" is the qualities of Beauty <term>Tiferet</term> and Sovereignty <term>Malkhut</term>. They are the root of roots of the worlds. They are the secret of "Turn from evil and do good." That is, if the lower beings do not maintain good deeds, then "the end of action" which was "first in thought" is affected. 

Then, power is added to the "Might" <term>Gevurah</term> above, as it were, or love and unification and a great connection between the "Two Beloveds" mentioned above—the two Cherubim—and their faces are "each toward his brother" as "one awakens his companion." For we, the House of Israel, emerged in our souls from the "womb of our mother," which is the name *Adonai* <note>The Divine Name associated with the Shekhinah or Malkhut</note>, the source of Israel, as it is written: "In the congregations, bless God, the Lord (*Adonai*) from the source of Israel." This occurs through the union of Beauty (*Tiferet*) and the pouring out of Righteousness <term>Tzedek; associated with Yesod, the foundational/generative attribute</term>, the foundation of the world, from which souls fly forth.

For "God is in our midst." The seventy-two families of Israel are a manifestation of Kindness and Mercy. As it is said, "The Lord did not set His love upon you... because you were the fewest of all peoples." The nations of the world are seventy, but Israel is sixty-five, the numerical value of the name *Adonai* <note>A+D+N+Y = 1+4+50+10 = 65</note>. When the "branches" within the quality of *Adonai*—which are the roots of Israel—shine, they shine toward the face of the Great Name. Then the Name is unified in its glory through the letters *Vav* and *Heh* <note>The last two letters of the Tetragrammaton, representing the connection between the upper and lower spiritual realms</note>.

This is the purpose of the limit, that there is a hold for the external forces. The Rabbi, the *Galanti* <note>Abraham Galanti, a 16th-century Kabbalist in Safed</note>, says: "that I may place My tabernacle among you." But if, Heaven forbid, Israel sins, there is a separation between those who should be joined. The Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> is, as it were, in exile, and "a handmaid shall inherit from her mistress," as we will explain later. Then the Name is not complete, Heaven forbid, for the *Vav* and *Heh* are missing. 

As I explained above regarding the letters *Vav* and *Heh*, which are the purpose of the limit, there is a hold for the external forces. The Rabbi, the *Galanti*, says: for the action to be successful, the recipient must resemble the actor. Therefore, the source of the vitality of His Essence is infinite. To create His creatures, he had to emanate from Himself these secret attributes <term>Sefirot</term> so that there would be a few "relatives" that resemble us in the chain of descent and the coming down from Cause to Effect, down to the "navel of the earth," so that the recipient might slightly resemble the Actor. 

The "First in Thought" of Emanation is the "End of Action"—that is, the emanation of the Last Attribute <term>Malkhut/Shekhinah</term>, which performs all actions. Therefore, through this attribute, all modes of governance ascend and descend, whether toward Kindness, Mercy, or the opposite. As seen in the *Zohar*, portion *Terumah*: "Behold here, 'a time to act' <note>Psalm 119:126</note> remains without repair and without completion. Why? Because they have made void Your Torah. Because Israel below was negligent in the words of the Torah, that 'Time' stands, or ascends, or descends because of Israel." 

This means that this "Time"—which is this Last Attribute—is not "made" (meaning repaired) but needs us to make it, repair it, and crown it. Because they "made void Your Torah," she becomes a "menstrual woman" <term>Niddah; a state of ritual impurity and separation</term>. Through the fulfillment of the Torah, she returns to her strength. This event happens to her—ascending and descending—because she is the root of all the holy souls of Israel, and all their forms are engraved in her. As seen in the *Tikkunim* <note>Tikkuni ha-Zohar</note>, when Israel below occupies themselves with Torah and commandments, the roots of their souls rooted in her sparkle and shine in the "Radiance of the Firmament." Then she ascends and the lower beings are unified, reaching her, and she appears "face to face" with the Holy King. She shows her face to Him and says: "Behold, with what have I come, *Adonai*, before You?" in the secret of "Feminine Waters" <term>Mayin Nukvin; the spiritual energy raised from below that triggers a divine union above</term>. 

By this, she ascends and is similar, or she descends etc. if because of the sins of Israel she is called "guilty in the world." We explained that the "sixty" in which she is rooted (as written in the *Tikkunim*) are "nations for the multitudes." The "Exile" is the dryness from the side of the souls. This is due to the accusation of the accusers in the "bitters" that surround the Palaces from the outside. They pour into her shameful, lowly powers. Then she descends to separate a spark for the world, and the world is called "sent away" until she is purified from the source of her spirits and returns to her home and to the "Field of Holy Apples" <term>Hakal Tapuchin Kadishin; a Kabbalistic name for the Shekhinah/Malkhut</term>. She then binds herself to the three colors of the thoughts. See within, and the world will be established. 

This is a clear matter: when the Great Name is blessed, the worshiper draws down the blessing through his service. This is Solomon the Prophet, peace be upon him, who said: "He who is blessed...

above, and as it is written, "and do good," which is the rectification of the Glory. And behold, this is for the sake of peace in the heavenly entourage <note>original: *pamalyah shel ma'ala*; refers to the celestial court of angels</note>, and he shall also "eat of the good and dwell in the land." This is the meaning of "dwell in the land"—the secret of the Land of the Living. It will be explained that as long as one does not perform this "good" mentioned here—which is the unification of the Righteous one with Righteousness <note>refers to the union of the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine, *Yesod* and *Malchut*</note>—it is impossible to dwell in the Land of the Living. But by awakening the "Good" to come and rest in its place upon him, it is as if he himself made and rectified it. And they established it: regarding this, "and you shall do them" is certainly used because they awaken [the realms] above to unite one with the other, so that the Holy Name is found to be fitting. "And you shall do them" certainly means that, as it were, he "made" the Name above. There was no king in the world who merited this through the paths of the Torah, performing the commandments and leading the Kingdom as is fitting, as it were "making" the Name above—there was no king in the world who merited this like David, as it is said: "And David made a name." And regarding this, it is written "and you shall do them." If you strive to do them, to rectify the Holy Name as is fitting, the Holy One, blessed be He, is not "found" until the Holy Name rises like a [fragrant] bundle <note>original: *ke-vursi*; likely a corruption of *kursai* (throne) or *kuvsi* (bundle)</note> through your movements, your speech, and your rectifications, as is fitting. End of quote.

From all this, it becomes clear that the righteous, through their service and good deeds, add strength to the Supernal Power, as stated in the Midrash on Lamentations cited above: "When Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, they add strength to the Power above," as it is said, "Through God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalm 60:14</note>. For through the "doing" that guides and dwells and draws strength from the Supernal to the Garden <note>The "Garden" is a metaphor for the *Shekhinah* or the Assembly of Israel</note>—which is the secret of the Assembly of Israel, called *Elohim*—they give power and strength. Then she prevails through the help of Israel, for she is the "Lower Power" (*Gevurah Tata'ah*). They draw to her light and "the strength from the head of Faith," and they cause her to shine with her Beloved—the secret of the Righteous One of the world, the light that illuminates her eyes. The righteous person below awakens the Righteous One above <note>the *Sefirah* of *Yesod*</note>, and both are rectified through the Supernal Glory, adding to and strengthening her power, this one from below and that one from above. The Righteous One above prevails when there are righteous ones below who strengthen the power, the secret of "Give strength to God." And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The *Bahir*, an early foundational Kabbalistic text</note>, it says: "There is a pillar from the earth to the heaven, and its name is 'Righteous' (*Tzaddik*), named after the righteous ones. When there are righteous ones in the world, it prevails; if not, it weakens. And it supports the entire world, as it is written: 'The Righteous One is the foundation of the world.' If it is weak, it cannot hold up the world. Therefore, even if there is only one righteous person in the world, he sustains the world." This is the same pillar mentioned in [Tractate] *Chagigah*, in the chapter "One does not expound": "Rabbi Eleazar ben Shammua says: The world stands upon a single pillar, and its name is 'Righteous,' as it is said, 'The Righteous One is the foundation of the world.'" It extends from the earth—the secret of the Land of the Living—to the heaven that stands in the middle. Concerning it, it is said: "For all that is in heaven and on earth," for it joins heaven and earth, and everything is awakened by those below.

# And in the Midrash *Shocher Tov* <note>Midrash on Psalms</note>: "I speak in righteousness, mighty to save"—through what righteousness? Through the righteousness you performed by accepting the Torah; for had you not done so, where would His kingdom be? And as the *Mechilta* says: "Who is like You among the mighty, O Lord?" <note>Exodus 15:11</note>—Rabbi Akiva says: Were it not for the scriptural verse, it would be impossible to say it: as it were, Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He, "You have redeemed Yourself." And so it is in the *Sifrei*.

## These are the words of the greatest of the later sages in the True Wisdom, the Ramaz <note>Rabbi Moshe Zakuto, 17th-century Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory. He wrote in his commentary: The power of the tongue contains a great secret, for according to the plain meaning, the dwelling of the *Shekhinah* among Israel is for the sake of the commoner <note>meaning, for the benefit of humans</note> and not for the sake of the High. But it is like the matter of the verse "Israel, in whom I will be glorified," and Joshua said: "And what will You do for Your Great Name?" And in the *Chapters of Rabbi [Eliezer]*: "He desired it for a habitation for Himself" <note>Psalm 132:13</note>, "Here I will dwell, for I have desired it." Because He desired it, he mentions it on earth. End of his words.

And these are the words of Rabbenu Bahya <note>13th-century commentator</note> on the portion *Va'era*, on the verse "For I am the Lord who brought them out of the land of Egypt to dwell among them": It says that the Exodus was on the condition "to dwell among them," for were it not so, He would not have brought them out. This indicates that the indwelling of the *Shekhinah* in Israel is a "need of the High" <note>original: *tzorech gavoah*; meaning the Divine "desires" or "needs" this relationship to manifest His glory</note>, and it is not only for the "need of the commoner." This is, in my opinion, what the prophet Hosea said: "And I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt, and you shall know no God but Me, and there is no Savior besides Me." It means: I did not bring you out of the land of Egypt only so that "I am the Lord your God," so that you would accept My divinity and not know any other god... And so I found in the Midrash of Psalms on the verse "When Israel went out of Egypt": Rabbi Yudan said, in the merit of the Tabernacle, Israel was redeemed from Egypt, as it says, "And God saw the children of Israel," and it is written, "And he anointed the vessels of the work." There is another place to learn this from: "who brought them out... on the condition that I dwell among them." End of the Midrash. This is why He "desired it for a habitation for Himself," and it is written, "Here I will dwell, for I have desired it." Many verses awaken us to this. And I have already mentioned this regarding the verse "And He spoke." End of his words. And on the verse "And He spoke," he wrote of the power of the languages, and so you will understand that the *Shekhinah* in Israel is not only for the need of the commoner, but a need of the High. For once the Unique Name is made known through [our] wisdom, behold, the Glory receives an addition of the Holy Spirit, and that is "May the glory of the Lord endure forever, let the Lord rejoice in His works." Therefore, Israel has the power to weaken or add strength to the Power above according to their deeds, for so it is written: "You neglected the Rock who begot you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:18; interpreted as "weakening" the Rock</note>, and it is written, "Through God we shall do valiantly." End of his words.

## Your eyes see the agreement of all [the sages] that the Divine service is a "need of the High," etc. In this, the Great Name is rectified, and the Righteous person "resembles the form to its Creator" <note>an idiom for imitating Divine attributes</note>, through the secret that the lower man is made in the image and likeness of the Supernal Man. When his internal and external limbs are sanctified, then his limbs sustain the limbs of the secret of the Supernal Chariot, adding strength.

But if, Heaven forbid, the "image of man" is changed—meaning he turns away from the side of holiness and cleaves to the side of impurity—then he blemishes all the worlds, and the blemish reaches even above, as explained in the Zohar and the *Tikunim* in several places. A small portion is brought in the portion *Acharei Mot*: Rabbi Judah said: At the time when the righteous increase in the world, a sweet scent rises, the Assembly of Israel is blessed by the Holy King, and the lights shine. But at the time when the wicked increase in the world, as it were, the Assembly of Israel does not emit a scent, she is diminished by the bitter "Other Side" <note>original: *sitra achra*; the realm of evil</note>, and then "He has cast down from heaven to earth," and darkness prevails. Rabbi Jose said: When the righteous increase in the world, it is written, "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me." But when the wicked increase in the world, it is written, "He has drawn back His right hand." Rabbi Hezekiah said: [It is like a King] who moves away from the Queen... Do not uncover the nakedness of your father or your mother... See there. Whenever Israel performs the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, He makes His dwelling in the Assembly of Israel. Why? Because Israel is the "firstborn son" to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: "Israel is My son, My firstborn." This "Mother" is the Assembly of Israel, as it is written: "And do not forsake the teaching of your mother." See there. See what is written: "A wise son makes a glad father"—when this son walks in the straight path and is wise, the Father is glad. This "Father" is the Supernal King. If this son is found in the path of stumbling, what is written? "But a foolish son is a grief to his mother." This is the secret of the matter: "For your transgressions your mother was put away." End of quote.

Furthermore, in the Zohar, of blessed memory: We have learned that, as it were, the wicked cause a blemish above. What is this blemish? As we have learned: "They have corrupted Him, not His children, it is their blemish" <note>Deuteronomy 32:5</note>. For all these rectifications are not found as they should be. One verse says: "And He put on righteousness as a coat of mail," and another verse says: "And He put on garments of vengeance for clothing." Rather, Rabbi Isaac said: "He put on righteousness" at the time when Israel is worthy, but when there is a blemish... what is the blemish? As we have learned: Like stones that are not satisfied to be blessed from that watering that descends... "They have corrupted Him, not His children, it is their blemish" above. And Woe! as long as the wicked increase in the world, as it were, the Holy Name is not blessed in the world. But as long as the wicked do not increase, the Holy Name is blessed in the world. This is what is written: "Let sinners be consumed from the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless the Lord, O my soul. Hallelujah." Rabbi Abba said: This verse is difficult, for it is written "They have corrupted Him, not His children, it is their blemish." Who caused this destruction? "A stubborn and twisted generation." Because they are wicked, it is so. Thus, after Moses said all these things and spoke the Holy Name as is fitting, he said: "He is righteous and upright"—speaking of His rectification; but "They have corrupted Him, not His children, it is their blemish"—why? Because "they are a stubborn and twisted generation." Rabbi Abba said: "To Him, not [His children]"—they have established it, and so it is. What is written in the Torah? "Do you thus repay the Lord?" <note>Deuteronomy 32:6</note> This is a repayment against [the Lord], for that which you caused and did against [Him]. End of quote.

It emphasizes that the Divine dwelling (Shekhinah) among Israel is a "Divine necessity" (Tzorech Gavoah), and that sin causes a cosmic blemish that disrupts the flow of blessing from above.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how human actions—specifically the "doing of good"—impact the celestial realms and provide "strength" to the Divine Name. It transitions from the physical predispositions of the individual to the cosmic responsibility of the Righteous person (Tzaddik).</meta>

# The Great Gate

The ultimate thought and end-goal is the unification of the Great Name. It has been found that the reason for the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah; the feminine aspect of God that dwells within the world</term> serving among those below is a "necessity on High" <note>original: "tzorech gavoah"; a radical Kabbalistic concept suggesting that God, in some sense, "needs" human partnership to achieve cosmic harmony</note>. Daniel, peace be upon him, knew this was so, and therefore he would pray for the Sanctuary—which is the place of the Divine Presence—so that it might return to its place. Through the Torah of Moses, it would also return to the heights, and then the intention of Creation would be fulfilled. For as our Sages of blessed memory said in *Bereshit Rabbah*: the primary dwelling place of the Divine Presence was originally among the lower beings.

## In the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Great is the Lord and highly praised" (Psalm 48:2). When is the Holy One, blessed be He, called "Great"? Only when He is within the Community of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael; the spiritual root of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</term>. This is what is written: "In the city of our God." For only "in the city of our God" is He "Great." Rabbi Yehuda asked: "What does 'our God' mean here?" He replied: "Indeed, this City is the pride and praise of Israel." What does this imply? It implies that without the Matronita <note>original: "matorinita"; a Zoharic term for the Shekhinah as the Divine Queen or Mother</note>, He is not [manifest as] King, nor is He Great, nor is He praised. From this we learn that if He is in the City that is "ours"—meaning He is in complete unity with it—then He is Great. The cause and trigger for this unity is the perfection of the soul through Torah and commandments. This is hinted at in the phrase "our God," meaning that we accept His Divinity and perform His commandments.

## In the Mishnah we learn: "And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven." This means to unify the "Name" (which is the attribute of Sovereignty <term>Malchut</term>) with "His Name" (which is the attribute of Beauty <term>Tiferet</term>), as is known. Furthermore, the Sages taught in the language of the Mishnah, in the chapter of Rabbi Meir at the end: "Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created only for His glory." This means that one should serve God for the sake of God's glory—to empower the Supernal strength and to unify the Great Name within His glory. He said that the plain meaning of "He created it for His glory" is like what is written in the Zohar: "In order that He may be known." That is, so there would be created beings who would know and recognize Him. Both explanations are true, and one depends on the other, as will be explained later.

## In the Talmud, in the first chapter of Berakhot, it is taught: Rabbi Ishmael ben Elisha said, "Once I entered the innermost sanctum to offer incense, and I saw Akhatriel Yah Hashem Tzevaot <note>original: "Akhatriel"; a name of God representing the "Crown" or a high angelic manifestation</note> sitting upon a high and lofty throne. He said to me: 'Ishmael, my son, bless Me.' I said to Him: 'May it be Your will that Your mercy suppresses Your anger, and may Your mercy prevail over Your [stricter] attributes, and may You behave toward Your children with the attribute of mercy, and enter before them beyond the letter of the law.' And He nodded His head to me." This teaches us that the blessing of a common person should not be light in your eyes. This passage is seemingly astonishing. Similarly, there is another passage there, the teaching of Rabbi Ishmael: "Do not be surprised." Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yose: "How do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, prays? Because it says: 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in the house of My prayer.' It does not say 'their prayer,' but 'My prayer' <note>Isaiah 56:7; the Hebrew grammar "Bet Tefilati" can be read as "The house of My prayer"</note>. From here we see that God prays." What does He pray? Rav Zutra bar Tuvia said in the name of Rav: "May it be My will that My mercy suppresses My anger... and I shall enter before them beyond the letter of the law." The explanation of these passages follows what I explained above regarding the Midrash: "In Salem also is His tabernacle." There it says that God prayed, etc. The matter is this: just as the union of *Tiferet* and *Malchut*—the secret of the name *Yah*, the roots of the worlds—is through the awakening of those below, so too the union of Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term> and Understanding <term>Binah</term> (which are the roots of the spiritual structure) is through the awakening of *Malchut*. This is the secret of "May it be the will from before Me"—which is the awakening of the Supernal Root. He then said "that My mercy suppresses My anger" according to the Midrash. For all is one unified unity—the root of the structure and the structure itself—except that one is in the secret of the "hidden" and the other in the secret of the "revealed." Such was the intention of the blessing of Rabbi Ishmael the High Priest: "May it be Your will *from before You*." He did not say "before You," but "from before You," referring to the Supernal Root. By the rolling of mercy over the attributes, or their mutual necessity for one another, as one awakens a companion, the flow of abundance descends below to lead the children "borne from the womb" with the attribute of mercy.

And in Tractate Shabbat, in the chapter of Rabbi Akiva: "When Moses ascended to the heights, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, tying crowns to the letters. God said to him, 'Moses, is there no "Peace" in your city?' Moses replied, 'Is there a servant who gives peace to his master?' God said, 'You should have helped Me.' Immediately, Moses said: 'And now, let the power of my Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying.'" According to the work *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>A major 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, this relates to the letters. What is the "tying" and "joining" and "unification" of the letters? It is the secret of the Crown of the Name, unified one with another. The "letters" <note>original: "otiyot"; also means "signs" or "arrivals"</note> come from the root of "coming" <note>Hebrew: "ata"</note>; thus, by tying the crowns, the light and abundance come constantly without ceasing. They called these powers "letters" because they come toward one another and unify with one another. These are the letters, and the Torah is the ladder by which one is bound to the Crown. It is a bond and a union of heat and flame, described as "letters" to faithfully inform us that the unification required on High depends on the engagement with Torah and its fulfillment. For this is the great cause of it. Conversely, neglecting the Torah causes the cessation of abundance and the separation of the unity. Therefore He said, "Is there no Peace in your city?"—meaning, when peace is removed from "the city of our God" due to the corruption of creatures and their transgression of the Torah. Therefore, I show you that I am tying [the crowns], so that this may be repaired through the tying of the crowns and their unification, provided they improve their deeds and return to the paths of the Torah. When you understand this, the repair for that corruption is [possible]. Then Moses wondered and said, "Is there a servant..." meaning, is it possible that a perfect servant could have such great power over the worlds? How could he draw this down? God responded, "You should have helped Me," meaning: Man, God has told you what is good and what He requires of you—to help in His action. If there is no support for the flame, how will the draw be pulled? The unity will not be awakened. Perhaps He, may He be blessed, revealed His precise secret to His faithful servant. Immediately, when Israel sinned, Moses needed that lesson and the correct advice. Fortunate is the one He advised and warned to repair the corruption... and when the secret is realized, it is sweetened by what is said: "And now, let the power of my Lord be great." This refers to the prayer for them, and in His response, it was said, "I have forgiven according to your word," and "But as surely as I live, the glory of the Lord shall fill the earth." Everything is rectified and explained to the wise of heart. It says "And now," and I have brought many proofs to say that You are the guide to finding the door of forgiveness, and the learning is the foundation of prayer and petition. Without Your desire to pardon and forgive, You would not have been found by those who did not ask for You. Thus ends the quote from *Avodat HaKodesh*.

## In the Midrash on the verse "And they went without strength before the pursuer" (Lamentations 1:6): Rabbi Azariah said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon: "When Israel performs the will of the Omnipresent, they add strength to the Supernal Power <term>Gevurah</term>, as it is said: 'Through God we shall do valiantly.' But when Israel does not perform the will of the Omnipresent, they—as it were—weaken the great power on High, as it is written: 'You neglected the Rock who begot you.'" Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said in the name of Rabbi Levi bar Tarfon: "When Israel performs the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, they add strength to the Supernal Power, as it is said: 'And now, let the power of my Lord be great.' But when they do not perform His will, they—as it were—weaken the great power on High, and they too 'go without strength before the pursuer.'"

## In the Zohar: Israel is the perfection of the Holy Name. When Israel below is perfected in their deeds, the Holy Name is—as it were—perfected [above]. But when Israel below is imperfect in their deeds and becomes liable, and is exiled from the land, the Holy Name is—as it were—not whole above. Furthermore, it says there: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'When Israel are righteous below, they strengthen the heavenly power. But when righteous people are not found, they—as it were—weaken the power above.'"

## In the Sifrei it is similar: "To You I lift my eyes, O You who dwell in the heavens" (Psalm 123:1). If not for Me [Israel], You would not—as it were—be dwelling in the heavens. And so it says: "He who builds His upper chambers in the heavens and has founded His vault upon the earth." In the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The Sefer HaBahir</note>, they said in this language: "How much kindness does one do for his Maker through the study of Torah! For anyone who studies Torah performs a kindness for his Maker, as it is written: 'Who rides the heavens for your help, and in His excellency on the skies' (Deuteronomy 33:26). This means: when a person studies Torah for its own sake, then 'You help Him,' and then 'I ride the heavens,' and then 'His excellency is on the skies.'" And in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai on the portion *Behar*, they said: "Come and see: 'Trust in the Lord and do good.' By the action below, the action above is awakened. For they established: 'And you shall do *them*'—it is as if *you* made them. Because that awakening of the husbands <note>the masculine divine forces</note> that you perform below awakens above. Therefore it is written 'do good.' And there is no 'Good' but the Righteous One (*Tzaddik*), as it is written: 'Tell the Righteous one that it is Good.' Because by your deeds, 'Good' is awakened... 'Dwell in the land and cherish faithfulness'—in every place 'the Land' refers to the Supernal Land <term>Malchut</term>. It has nothing in the world to be satisfied with until this 'Good' flows to it... 'And cherish faithfulness'—this is the 'Land' in every place, as in 'Your faithfulness in the nights.' 'And cherish faithfulness' means you shall provide food for your Companion." Behold the explanation: according to the deed below, so its likeness is done and awakened above. Through a good deed, the "Righteous One"—the Foundation of the world called "Good"—is awakened and unified with his Bride. By your good deeds, you cause this; it is as if you are "making" this thing happen, and the union occurs on High.

It cites various sources—Talmud, Zohar, and Midrash—to argue that the perfection of the Holy Name and the flow of Divine mercy depend on the spiritual state of Israel below.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the purpose of the Commandments (Mitzvot). Having established that human actions provide "strength" to the Divine, the author now refutes the idea that the commandments are merely for human discipline, arguing instead for their profound impact on the soul and the cosmic order of Emanation (Atzilut).</meta>

# The Great Gate

...to Israel except to refine them, as it is said: "The word of the Lord is refined" (Psalm 18:31). Behold, all of their words are directed toward the totality of the commandments, not just some of them as many believe. Furthermore, even their specific details were intended for the benefit of the soul, which is the ultimate success. This is what they said in *Leviticus Rabbah*, Chapter 8: Rabbi Berachiah said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: "The Holy One, blessed be He, will make a Great Feast <note>original: "Oriston"; from the Greek *ariston*, meaning a banquet or midday meal</note> for the righteous in the World to Come. Anyone who did not eat carrion <term>nevelot; meat from an animal that died naturally or was improperly slaughtered</term> in this world will merit to see it in the World to Come. This is what is written: 'And the fat of a beast that dies of itself, and the fat of that which is torn of beasts, may be used for any other service; but you shall in no wise eat of it' (Leviticus 7:24)—so that you may eat of it in the World to Come." Therefore, Moses warns Israel and says to them: "These are the living things which you may eat" (Leviticus 11:2). Behold, ritual slaughter at the windpipe and the gullet in a specific place—which is part of the commandment—purifies the living creature and prepares it for eating. From this follows a great benefit for the soul. However, slaughtering from the back of the neck, which makes the creature "carrion," defiles the soul and distances it from that ultimate success. We find, therefore, that cutting the gullet and the windpipe in a specific place—which is the major part of the commandment—was intended for that immense benefit beyond the mere commandment itself, contrary to the opinions of those others. This is in addition to what the Sages of Truth <term>Kabbalists</term> received regarding the reason for this commandment—matters that are the "secrets of the world" which were hidden from the eyes of the Master <note>The author likely refers to Maimonides (the Rambam), who argued that the specific details of ritual slaughter were purely for discipline and had no inherent spiritual reason</note>. And in the *Midrash Shocher Tov*, they said in these words: "As for God, His way is perfect" (Psalm 18:31). The way of God is perfect; how much more so is He? For what does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He, whether one slaughters at the windpipe and eats, or from the tail? Rabbi Berachiah in the name of Rabbi Jacob wrote: "The fat of carrion and the fat of torn beasts—if you did not eat them in this world, by your lives, a great Feast <note>original: "Oristuon"</note> is prepared for you in the World to Come. Eat and be satisfied." Their saying "the way of God is perfect" alluded to what was explained above regarding the secret of "refining the creatures," which is the perfection of the upper and lower worlds and their connection to one another. And to the Holy One, blessed be He, the Single Lord, it does not "matter" whether one slaughters etc., for it is all for the need of the one who chooses, within the secret of "refining" and the removal of boundaries and impurities and the merit of that refinement. It is found, then, that the commandments in their entirety and their parts are the version of that refinement, which is the perfection and connection of the upper realms to one another, while the lower realms are included and merit that perfection. Therefore, there is nothing in the commandments—not even a part—in which a purpose and benefit for the success and purification of the soul and the unification of the Great Name was not intended. This is known to those who know the "wisdom of the births" <note>likely referring to the secrets of creation or the lineage of souls</note>, that there is no word or story in the Torah that does not intend this benefit, and certainly the commandments in general and in their parts. The Master of Prophets <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, said: "Set your hearts unto all the words... for it is no empty thing for you" (Deuteronomy 32:46-47). Every type of perfection and success is attached to those words and flows from them, which is why he said: "For it is your life." By this matter, they shall prolong their days upon

->the land—to say that eternal life flows from them, as mentioned above in the book *Sefer Avodat HaKodesh* (Service of the Holy Work).<-

**Behold**, regarding the matter of the "connecting spark," his words are also correct and aimed well. For he explains the verses that imply human actions do not affect Him <note>God as the Infinite</note> as referring to the *Ein Sof* <term>The Infinite; God as He is in Himself, beyond all relation to the world</term>—this is the end of the secret. But in the realm of *Atzilut* <term>Emanation; the ten divine attributes or Sefirot through which God acts</term>, the deeds of human beings certainly have an effect. If so, what does it mean when it says, "If you have sinned, what do you do to Him?" (Job 35:6) and likewise "If you are righteous, what do you give Him?" (Job 35:7)? For even though one does not act upon or "give" to the *Ein Sof*, nevertheless one acts upon and "gives" to the *Atzilut*, which are the revelations of the *Ein Sof* through which all matters arrive. For the essence of the *Ein Sof*, by virtue of Its hiddenness, is concealed from all prayer and concealment, except through the *Atzilut*. Therefore, the *Ein Sof* is not hinted at in the Torah—not by any word, nor by any letter, nor even by the "crown" <note>the decorative tip</note> of a letter. Also, that which was said in the Midrash, "For what does it matter to the Holy One, blessed be He...", and the Master's explanation that this refers to the *Ein Sof*, is as far [from the truth] as light is from dark. For in the vast majority of cases, the term "The Holy One, blessed be He" in the speech [of the Sages] refers to the *Atzilut*. In most places,

->they hint at the Holy One, blessed be He, as the attribute of *Tiferet* (Beauty), and in some places as *Malchut* (Kingship).<-

<margin>
Therefore
And from the start
</margin>
My children, listen to me and your souls shall live! I shall enlighten you with understanding to comprehend the matter of the Service as a "necessity on High." I will bring the opinion of the later Kabbalists regarding this matter of "adding strength Above" or "weakening strength Above," and I will present their dispute. Afterward, I will say what the Lord has graciously granted me, of blessed memory, regarding the "Array of Divinity" in the act of engagement. For the thought in Creation was in *Tiferet* (Beauty) so that it would be worthy of the preservation of the species, as we touched upon above. But the thought is brought from potential into action through the "Crown" <note>the Sefirah of *Malchut*</note> which "became the head of the corner" (Psalm 118:22). Behold, she is the Prince of the upper world and is called the "Firstborn," meaning appointed with power, as in the matter of "I also will appoint him My firstborn" (Psalm 89:28). However, it is impossible to say she is called "Prince of the World" in the literal sense simply because she guides the lower world and watches over it. Rather, she "breathes" from above and influences below. In this matter, He "associated the attribute of Mercy with the attribute of Judgment and created the world." This is like the hint given in the parable of the sinner concerning the Architect. Regarding the verse "And He was grieved in His heart" (Genesis 6:6), they gave a parable of a king who built a palace through an architect; he saw it and it did not please him—against whom should he complain? Should he not complain against the architect? Another parable in the commentary on Noah: a king conducted trade through a broker <note>original: "sarsur"</note> and lost—against whom should he complain? Should he not complain against the broker? Yet another parable in the Midrash: a governor <note>original: "signa"</note> who scraped his palace with salt. These lofty parables refer to the removal of the "shining face" at a time of wrath, as in the matter of "And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth" (Genesis 9:14), hinting that the non-existence of the sun's light from the East has been felt. The words "Architect," "Broker," and "Nursemaid" refer to the Prince of the World, and likewise the word "Son of the King" refers to *Tiferet*. They hinted that if the work of the architect, or the trade of the broker, or the child of the nursemaid is good in the eyes of the king, the king comes to praise the building of the architect, or he stands by the merchandise of the broker, or with his children in his house, and he greets the architect, broker, and nursemaid, and all is in peace. But if their deeds do not please him because they follow the stubbornness of their hearts, then the king "grieves in his heart" and removes the mediator. Then the "serpent" is placed in his house, for "no man dwells in a house with a serpent," which is like a thorn in a basket. This addition and the placement of the serpent upon the thorn and the filth of the beasts will rise to greatness, for the princes appointed over them are sustained by it. When the Ascent is gathered on the side of the filth, then Israel is dominated by their sins and impurity, and they are sent away with "Man" from the land of their birth into the hand of the nations, to a land not their own, and they are enslaved and afflicted, for there lies their power. Because of the Mother's attachment to the children, she is in their distress as they are in distress, as it is said: "In all their affliction, He was afflicted" (Isaiah 63:9). This explains the matter of the "Dwelling" <note>the *Shekhinah*</note> that dwells in their servitude and the impurity that is defiled by their impurity. Furthermore, one should contemplate the matter of "they were exiled to Egypt, the Divine Presence was with them; they were exiled to Elam, the Divine Presence was with them"—which requires contemplation. Moreover, what was explained above: through the labor of the Righteous person (Tzaddik), who "likens the form to its Creator," the Divine Presence dwells among the lower beings and rests upon the pure sanctuary, for "kind has found its kind" and is awakened until "the female shall encompass the man" (Jeremiah 31:22). He becomes wise in Torah, wisdom, and the commandments he constantly toiled in, until he prophesies and knows the future. But when he turns away from the Torah and the commandments—which are the pattern of the heights—he defiles his form and his wisdom is darkened, becoming separated from the holiness and from the prophecy found in actions. He is not worthy to use the King's scepter. This is the secret of the matter: the entire matter of the removal of the Flow <note>the Divine influence/blessing</note> is not a matter of there being a "deficiency" in the Nursemaid <term>the Divine source of flow</term>, Heaven forbid, in any way! Rather, it is a deficiency in the children who receive the opposite of the flow of good. He is distressed by the day, and in the tranquility of the Mother, the children are sent away, as it is said: "Behold, I will destroy them with the earth" (Genesis 6:13), for when the earth is destroyed, they too are destroyed. For the sin of the daughter is a great blow, so that they might return from their way to return with her from the house of their servitude into the inner palace of the King. It is found that the deficiency is entirely for Israel, who receive the opposite of the good they deserve if they were good. This concludes the words of that Sage. [But I say:] This matter is not that there is a deficiency in the Nursemaid, etc.—the explanation is not that the primary intention is to cause a deficiency in her, for she did not sin, but rather it is to discipline the children. Yet by happenstance, a deficiency follows for her because of this, for it is impossible to discipline the children without the "Beast" being sent and she being driven out with them. I have pushed myself to explain the words of the Master in this manner, even though I know it is a "patch" that the language cannot truly support. For if this were not his intention, he contradicts his own words! For he said above regarding the parable of the merchant, the broker, and the architect: "if their deeds did not please the king, then he grieves in his heart and removes himself from the building, the broker, and the architect mentioned etc." This is the matter of the "Dwelling" that dwells in the "Tower" of Israel and the impurity that results from the filth, and the Divine Presence going with them into exile. Behold, his words contradict one another! Also, at the beginning of this gate, he said that when the woman rebels against her tasks, the husband sends a bill of divorce... he shall be embittered in his peace and leave his house and go to drive out his wife. And if the children are disciplined, he sends them away for their sins, and the woman is divorced from her husband, and the Father and the Merciful One go far away. Yet close to this, he said the opposite, as he wrote: "it is not a matter of there being a deficiency of power or a deficiency of holiness and glory in the 'Crown' <term>the Shekhinah</term>..." claiming it is caused by those below when they do not make their deeds worthy. For "far be it from God" as many light-minded people have thought in the weakness of their constitution regarding the words of our Sages of blessed memory and the words of the Kabbalists, etc. And now, my brothers, you have seen how his words contradict each other! If his intention is not what I have explained, then one who comes to "discipline" by hearing his words—and certainly by believing them—and follows after his opinion, is like the "beast of the wisdom of Kabbalah," which is entirely built upon this pivot. If you are wonder-struck by the matter of the Divine Presence—how it receives a "blemish" through the sins of Israel, and also Israel in the matter of the removal of the *Ein Sof* and the removal of the "Crown"—come and see in the *Book of Tikkunim* of blessed memory. Elijah said: "Master of the Worlds, You are the One who is known above all, and all the Sefirot—each one...
