<meta>This page continues the discussion on the spiritual mechanics of the Mitzvot (commandments). It specifically addresses the theological paradox: if God is perfect and self-sufficient, how can human actions possibly "affect" or "strengthen" the Divine? The author transitions from the Kabbalistic view of Divine-human reciprocity to addressing the philosophical objections raised by Job and Maimonides.</meta>

# The Great Gate

In the Zohar and in countless Midrashim, the Kabbalists have explained at length that when the Assembly of Israel <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael"; the spiritual personification of the Jewish people and a name for the Shekhinah</note> is whole in the Pure Land, conducting themselves properly according to the law and the Torah, the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah; the indwelling presence of God</term> dwells among them through the Holy Spirit—beautiful, permeated, and serving as a canopy of glory and a crown. As it is said, "This is known in all the earth" (Isaiah 12:5), and it is written, "The Lord reigns, let the earth rejoice" (Psalm 97:1), hinting at the "Land of the Living" <note>a Kabbalistic reference to the Sephirah of Malchut</note>. Conversely, God forbid, when they sin, She is like "a bird that wanders from her nest" (Proverbs 27:8), leaving behind Her strength and Her finest essence. This is the meaning of "A son causes shame and brings reproach upon his father" <note>paraphrase of Proverbs 19:26</note>, and it is written: "Why should You be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stays only for a night?" (Jeremiah 14:8). Our Sages of blessed memory elaborated on this matter of the Shekhinah in exile in the Midrash on Psalms: "I will rejoice in Your salvation" (Psalm 9:15). Rabbi Abbahu said: "This is one of five 'difficult' verses which indicate that the salvation of Israel is the salvation of the Holy One, blessed be He. It does not say 'our salvation' here, but 'Your salvation.' David said: Our salvation is Your salvation." Rabbi Berachiah the Priest said: "Consider what is written: 'He is righteous and saved' (Zechariah 9:9). It does not say 'He is a Savior' <note>original: "Moshiya"</note> but 'He is saved' <note>original: "Nosha"</note>. And when they are destined to return, the Shekhinah returns with them, as it is said: 'Then the Lord your God will return [with] your captivity' (Deuteronomy 30:3). It does not say 'He will bring back' <note>original: "Heishiv"</note> but 'He will return' <note>original: "V'shav"</note>." They elaborated on this extensively, for it is well-known throughout the breadth of Kabbalistic literature.

**However**, there is a massive difficulty regarding all the above from several verses that indicate that commandments and transgressions do not affect Him at all. For it says: "Is it any pleasure to the Almighty if you are righteous? Or is it gain to Him if you make your ways perfect?" (Job 22:3). Elihu said: "If you sin, what do you do against Him? ... If you are righteous, what do you give Him?" (Job 35:6-7), and there are many such verses. I found that the author of the *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai, 16th-century Kabbalist</note> was aroused by this, and I will copy his words here in full since it is a major inquiry, and afterward I will reveal my own opinion, with the help of God.

In Part 3 of *The Service* <note>original: "Avodah"</note>, he writes: "Our Sages have spoken words that, at first glance, seem to contradict what is received and established as truth beyond doubt—namely, that human service is a 'necessity for the High' <note>original: "Tzorech Gavoah"; the idea that human actions impact the Divine realm</note>. In the *Midrash Yelamdenu*, Chapter 8, they said: 'What does the Holy One, blessed be He, care whether one slaughters an animal and eats it, or stabs an animal and eats it? Do you benefit Him at all, or do you harm Him at all? Or what does He care if one eats pure things or impure things? As it says: "If you are wise, you are wise for yourself" (Proverbs 9:12). Behold, the commandments were given only to refine the creatures through them, as it says: "The word of the Lord is refined" (Psalm 18:31)... so that it may be a shield for you, as it says: "He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him."'"

**This** would seem to imply, upon first thought, that He does not care if one slaughters properly or kills an animal improperly <note>original: "m'navel"; making it carrion</note>, or if one eats pure or impure things, for none of these things harm or benefit Him, nor do they reach Him at all. This aligns with the plain meaning of the verses: "Is it any pleasure to the Almighty if you are righteous?"—which were the words of Eliphaz to Job. And Elihu said to him: "If you sin, what do you do against Him?... Your wickedness [affects] a man like yourself." And King Solomon said: "If you are wise, you are wise for yourself." From all this, it appears that man's good and evil deeds do not touch the "High" at all, but only the one who performs them.

**But** the opposite has already been clarified: that human service is indeed a "necessity for the High." Regarding forbidden foods, it is said in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may peace be upon him) in the *Zohar Chadash*:

> Anyone who eats of those forbidden foods attaches himself to the Other Side <term>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil/impurity</term>, and loathes his soul and his bones. A spirit of impurity rests upon him, showing that he has no portion in the High God, does not come from His side, and is not attached to Him. If he departs this world in his sin, all those who are attached to the side of impurity seize him and defile him, judging him like a serpent... It is written 'And you shall be defiled by them' (Leviticus 11:43) <note>original: "v’nitmeitem"; spelled without the letter Aleph in the Torah, which the Zohar interprets as 'you will be blocked'</note>, meaning there is no cure for his defilement and his impurity lasts forever. Woe to them and woe to their souls, for they will not be bound in the Bundle of Life... for they have defiled themselves... and of them it is written, 'For their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched' (Isaiah 66:24). They shall be a 'contempt' <note>original: "deraon"</note> to all flesh—what is 'contempt'? A stench. What caused it? That Side to which they attached themselves. Israel comes from the Right Side <note>original: "sitra d'yamina"; the side of Mercy/Chesed</note>, and if they attach themselves to the Left Side <note>the side of Judgment/Gevurah or impurity</note>, they cause a defect in the sapphire and a defect in themselves... and they cause a defect in this world and the world to come.

Thus, they explicitly explained that one who defiles himself by eating what the Torah forbade causes a defect in "this Side," which is the Right Side, for "Israel comes from the Right Side." This is the side of holiness and purity, the secret of Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term>. If so, then matters of purity and impurity *do* touch the "High" as well. This is found frequently in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, especially regarding the laws of skin afflictions <note>original: "nega'im"</note> and forbidden sexual relations. They say: "Rabbi Hiyya said in the name of Rabbi Isaac: A deficiency below is only found because it is found Above, and Above is only found when it is found below through the sins of the world... for everything is dependent, this on that, and that on this."

# And their saying
"What does the Holy One care..." and "the commandments were only given to refine..." does not contradict what I have written. Rather, it will be explained and understood by the "wise of heart" that human service is a "necessity for the High" as well, according to the secret intention. When they said, "What does the Holy One care," they were referring to the **Single Master, the Root of Roots** <note>the Ein Sof; God's Infinite Essence</note>, for whom it truly does not matter at all. All those verses from Job were also intended for this level of the Divine. From the perspective of the Single Master, man's righteousness or rebellion does not touch Him, only the actor. However, regarding the **Glory** <note>the Sephirot; God's manifest attributes</note>—to channel influence upon the "Upper Heads"—it is a complete necessity! This was the pure Will and holy Desire. To awaken this and complete the intention, all the commandments and services were given to us. Performing them and engaging in them constantly completes the intention, which is the **Unification of the Great Name** in His Glory. The proper intention in the commandments is what brings the world to "cleave" to the upper things, the secret of "to Him you shall cleave." It is the connection of the lower beings to the upper beings. This is what they meant by "refining the creatures"—it is the connection and cleaving to the Unique Name through the commandments, for they are the thread that connects the practitioners to the Unique Name. 

Transgressing the negative commandments defiles the "Glory," for one who defiles himself below, his impurity reaches even the Most Holy Sanctuary, as in the secret of "He has defiled the Sanctuary of the Lord" (Numbers 19:20). For the one who commits a sin awakens the external forces of impurity <note>original: "chitzonim"</note> which cast filth into the Sanctuary. We are commanded not to awaken that side—the "dross" that comes out of the silver—but to distance it so it does not enter the inner Holy Place, so the silver remains pure and free of dross, as in the secret: "Take away the dross from the silver... take away the wicked from before the king" (Proverbs 25:4-5). This is why the Torah warned against negative commandments. It is all "to refine the creatures"—meaning the refinement, connection, and unification of all things with one another, as well as the separation and removal of dross from the silver. This is why it says, "Every word of God is refined." From all this, it is clear that human deeds, whether good or bad, all touch the "High."

However, **the Teacher** <note>original: "HaRav HaMoreh"; Maimonides (Rambam)</note> in Part 3, Chapter 26 of his book <note>*The Guide for the Perplexed*</note> says: "I found a statement by the Sages which at first glance suggests that some commandments have no cause other than the decree itself... 'What does the Holy One care whether one slaughters from the throat or the nape?'... This statement is very strange... but I have interpreted it... every commandment has a useful purpose... for it is not a vain thing." Maimonides argues that the *general* commandments have reasons (like slaughtering for food), but the *specific details* (like where to cut) are only to "refine the creatures" by giving them a command to follow.

One might question Maimonides' view. While he interprets "slaughtering from the throat or the nape" as a detail, the Midrash also says "What does He care if one eats pure or impure things?" This suggests the Sages were speaking about the *entirety* of the commandments, not just their details. It seems they took these as examples for the whole system of Mitzvot. As it says in *Leviticus Rabbah*, Chapter 8: "Rav said: The commandments were given to Israel only to refine the creatures through them." This implies the entire "word of God" is refined. They also said in *Midrash Shocher Tov*: "Rav said: The Holy One, blessed be He, did not give the commandments to Israel [except to refine them]..."

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how human actions affect the Divine realm. It specifically addresses the concept of the "diminishing" of Divine light and whether this implies a deficiency in God Himself. The author uses the works of Rabbi Moses Cordovero (the Pardes) and Rabbi Sheftel Horowitz (Shefa Tal) to explain that any perceived "lack" is a result of human sin blocking the flow of Divine abundance, not a change in the Creator’s essence.</meta>

As in the matter of, "You came and defiled My land and made My inheritance an abomination" (Jeremiah 2:7), and it is written, "And they made the pleasant land a desolation" (Zechariah 7:14). The explanation of "pleasant" <note>Hebrew: *Hemdah*</note> is that it is "included," and it mentions God—as seen in the [writings of] the Radak and the Jerusalem Talmud.
The matter of "drawing" <note>original: *hamshacha*</note> etc., continues until one is cleansed from the forces of impurity; behold, these are the forces of holiness and purity, thus far. These are the words of our teacher Rabbi Meir di Lonzano <note>original: "Maharam di Lucrate"; likely referring to the 16th-century Kabbalist Meir ibn Gabbai or a commentator on the *Ma'arekhet Ha-Elokut*</note>: "And one is cleansed from the forces of impurity," etc. The explanation is that when
there is no righteous man on earth to arouse the Upper Combination, the forces of impurity—which are the messengers of Strict Justice—are aroused. They hasten to enter and cast their filth into their prosecution
from the power of the Primeval Serpent, which is Harsh Justice, to do their work. According to Strict Justice, the Moon <term>Malchut; the lowest Sephirah, representing the Shekhinah</term> then stands in her original intention to shine for them and supervise them, to act
through them according to their power. This is according to the Justice decreed by the Supreme King of kings to remove Her from the influence of Mercy and to elevate the holy Priests <note>metaphor for the channels of Mercy</note> who are His messengers of Mercy. This is the matter of "nursing"
and "emanation" mentioned everywhere in the *Pardes Rimonim*—that She nurses from them and their influence is within Her. The matter of "dominion" and "prostration" is also by way of a parable: it is as if the Leader <note>God</note> is distressed by this matter,
for She longs for Her first Husband. Because of these things, the "Earth" <note>Shekhinah</note> grumbles to take vengeance upon the children <note>humanity</note> so that they might turn back from their evil rebellion. I have elaborated on this so that you do not come to
error and claim, "Who can produce purity from impurity?" <note>Job 14:4</note> or suggest that there is a deficiency in the Divine Nurse, Heaven forbid. Rather, the deficiency is only in the Messianic children, as I explained above and at the end of the "Section on Reasoning," thus far his words.
This matter is explained well in the *Pardes* regarding the concept of nursing from the forces of impurity, and the matter of the Serpent coming upon Eve, and the matter of the "Concubine under pressure" <note>referring to the biblical "Concubine in Gibeah," used here as a Kabbalistic metaphor for the Shekhinah in exile</note>. All of this hints at the accusation
of the Prosecutor <term>Satan/The Accuser</term> which rises higher and higher before the Master of Truth, blessed be He. Then the "Good Influence" <note>Divine flow/Shefa</note> is withheld, etc. See there in the *Pardes*, Gate of Channels, Chapter 4, and Gate of Permutations, Chapter 6, at length.
I have copied the teacher’s words above. Truly, the questions asked by the pious Rabbi regarding the author of the *Ma'arekhet* <note>The book *Ma'arekhet Ha-Elokut*</note>, and the proofs he brought—any seeing person
can see they have no substance. For all the proofs he brought regarding the acceptance of deficiency or perfection by the "Prosecutor" <note>the Shekhinah when influenced by harsh justice</note> are not for Herself,
God forbid, but only regarding the need for Her influence on the created beings. This is indicated by the parable he brought: a nursing woman produces milk as long as the infant nurses, and the jug is emptied—this milk is not
a benefit for the nurse herself, but the benefit reaches another, namely the nursing infant. However, it provides her a sense of relief and a "lightness of spirit" when the infant has something to nurse.
So too, as it were, above: there is "satisfaction before Him, for I spoke and My will was done." The Good and True One desires goodness.

# **And for the Law**

I will first introduce the laws of the thirteen [levels of] Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest spiritual world</term>. Their measure is "Ten that have no end." This is a complete teaching from the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an ancient mystical text</note>: "Ten Sephirot of Nothingness <term>Belimah</term>, their measure is
ten that have no end." The *Pardes* explains: "Ten Sephirot of *Belimah*." This word is divided into two: *Beli-Mah* ("Without What-ness"). The explanation of "What-ness" <note>original: *Mahut*</note> is essence and character.
For the Ten Sephirot are "vessels of measure" because their essence is not attainable by us. Even if we say "this one is Justice" and "this one is Mercy" and the like, everything is understood by us through their actions. But from the perspective of
their essence, they are *Belimah* <note>nothingness/restraint</note>. This word is also related to "restrained" <note>Hebrew: *Balum*</note>, as in "He rides upon them to restrain." This means a person must "restrain" his mouth and not speak extensively of their exalted matters because of the short-reach
of the grasper and the depth of the concept. Or it might be from the language of "hiding" and "concealing," like "hidden genitals" <note>Hebrew: *eriva le-balum*</note>. Thus the Sephirot are called *Belimah*, meaning the Sephirot of Concealment,
for they are hidden. All three of these explanations lead to one place: the intention is to show their concealment and the shortness of our grasp, and that it is not proper to speak of them at length because of their hiddenness.
It says "their measure is ten" because the teacher implies they have a limit. Yet it says "they have no end." Although this is a contradiction—that we give them a limit and then
say they have no limit—it was already explained in the previous chapters. Relative to their aspect within the Emanator, the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term>, they have no limit. But relative to their aspect and actions which extend
to us, they have actions according to our reception, for we are beings of limit. This is the power of our Creator's might: that from the limitless, He creates a limit and contracts Himself <term>Tzimtzum; Divine contraction</term> to benefit the lower beings,
who possess limit and end. Regarding this, the eyes of the wise should not be alarmed, for it is not far-fetched. For "the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain Him" (1 Kings 8:27), yet blessed be He, and because of this—out of love for
Israel—He would contract His Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> between the two poles of the Ark, as our Sages explained. Thus far the words of the *Pardes*. Therefore, one cannot say there is "addition" or "deficiency" or "subtraction" in the world of Emanation
from the perspective of the Emanation itself, in the aspect of their existence within the Infinite, which is the Soul to them, and they are attached to Him. However, from the perspective of the "Influence" <note>the flow of Divine energy</note> to the lower beings, there is in this influence
a matter of "less" and "more," and it is all according to the arousal of the lower beings. To understand this secret, I will first present what the *Pardes* wrote in the first chapter of the "Gate of Essence and Character": the Unity of the Sephirot is
from many faces, etc. Now I will explain two faces: the "Face" and its "Opposite." I will mention it again at the end. These two faces I will bring at length, adding
a few words from the genius, our teacher Rabbi Sheftel <note>Rabbi Sheftel Horowitz, author of *Shefa Tal*</note> of blessed memory, and his book *Shefa Tal*. To enlighten the eyes of your intellect in understanding the secret: how can it
be said of *Malchut* <term>Sovereignty; the lowest Sephirah</term> that she is "empty of influence," God forbid? For She is the Master of all, in whose hand is all the good of Emanation, and She herself is the essence of Godliness and the essence of Emanation, as is known.
If so, how can "emptiness" occur in the light of Emanation? Furthermore, this would imply "cutting" and "separation," God forbid—that She is empty while the other Sephirot remain full. To settle this secret,
you must know that the Unity of the Sephirot, in general, occurs in three ways. Since our current purpose is to understand the matter of "emptiness" in *Malchut*, I will enlighten your intellect
with two types of Unity. Therefore, we will not trouble ourselves to explain the third type, but only two; for through these two, our objective will be clarified.
These are they: The first type of Unity is how they are united from the side of their Emanation. That is to say, in their vitality, which is from the Infinite <term>Ein Sof</term>, blessed be He, to create finite worlds and to maintain a limit.
From the "Nothingness of End" <note>limitless</note> He brings about a "limit" in order to manifest the power of His Godhood to others who are finite and limited, and to supervise them in all their needs, their repair, and their existence.
"The world follows its custom" and there shall be no destruction or nullification, Heaven forbid. This intention is not within the grasp of the power of the finite mind to understand how the Infinite produces the finite and the limited. For through the emanated [Sephirot], the world was spoken into being,
and worlds and levels and levels of Emanation descended until our level, through the secret of "Cause and Effect." The "Life of Worlds" <note>God</note> created them and established them as the "Throne of Glory." From the levels of Creation <term>Beriah</term>
they descended to ten levels in the secret of "Cause and Effect," which are the worlds of Formation <term>Yetzirah</term>. From the ten levels of Formation, they descended to the ten levels in the secret of Action <term>Asiyah</term>, until the levels reached a limit
and a concrete end, such that all the worlds are united and linked like a "Menorah of parts" <note>a lamp made of interlocking pieces</note>. Behold, from this perspective, the supervision of the Infinite, blessed be He, over them began at their emanation,
wherein He bestowed His flow of light upon them. Through that flow of light, they are united in a true, strong, and brave Unity. That flow shall never be lacking.
Through the drawing of that flow, they are nourished in an equal unity, full of satisfying abundance, full to their very banks with kindness and joy in their places. From the "Gate of Perfection," they influence
the other worlds—Creation, Formation, and Action—with their daily bread and sustenance. Upon that flow depends the existence of the connection of the worlds and the connection of the elements,
down to the navel of the earth. If one were to imagine, Heaven forbid, the withholding of that flow for even a single moment, all the physical worlds would be destroyed and perish
instantly, and the spiritual ones would return to their source as they were before emanation. This is the intention of the *Kiryat Shema* <term>The "Hear O Israel" prayer</term> according to the proper meditation: that one unites all the worlds from below to above, up to the First Cause,
blessed be He; that all are linked and united, one to another, effect to cause, according to the levels, up to the First Cause. For He, through the Great and
Holy Flow, links them, unites them, and sustains them from the First Point until the point of the earth's navel. Were it not for His wealth—Heaven forbid—the absence of His flow for one moment would cause them all to fall,
and the spiritual would return to its source. However, the aspect of the intention in the Unity of the *Kiryat Shema* is that the Infinite should flow into the emanated Sephirot an abundance that is even greater than the flow bestowed during emanation,
upon which the existence of the worlds and the elements depends (the "custom of the world"). For otherwise, His attainment in the Emanation itself would, Heaven forbid, sometimes be an increase in flow
and sometimes not such an increase. It is not that the increase itself is "lacking," but the proper intention in the *Shema* is to unite all the Sephirot, one to another, and all of them within the Emanator, and to crown Him King over all
existing things, great and small. For through His great and holy flow upon the emanated beings, He is the cause of their existence and our faith. But this is not to add or exceed the flow beyond the "custom" established
at the time of their emanation for the world's existence. For all the prophets, up to the most perfect Form <note>Adam</note>, were created as a light for all created beings in their full beauty and stature; they were created by [Divine] Will,
meaning with the most complete perfection. Therefore, nothing can be added to it and nothing subtracted from it.
And even though it is found in the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the Zohar</note> that through the Unity of the *Shema*, flow is added, the matter is this: because the First Adam sinned, and through our iniquities the land has become impoverished, the flow from Emanation to all the worlds has been diminished. It does not have the strength, valor,
and courage it had before the First Adam sinned. Because of this, we "add" flow through the Unity of the *Shema*—so that the World of Emanation will shine a great light into the worlds as it did
before the sin, and the worlds will be greatly strengthened. But this is not to say that a "new addition" of flow is created within the essence of Emanation from the Emanator, blessed be He. For the flow
within the essence of Emanation stands forever in its strength and might, as in the beginning, in its great light from the Emanator, blessed be He. Thus, in this Unity—which is their existence—
it never lacks and never exceeds. This is the first Unity of their emanation. The second Unity in Emanation is that they are full of satisfying abundance, the blessing of the Lord, to influence [the lower worlds]...

### The Great Gate

"He has a known name by which the angels are called, but You have no known name. You fill all names, and You are the perfection of them all; for when You withdraw from them, all the names remain like a body without a soul." Thus far his words <note>original: עכ"ל (ad kan leshono)</note>. Behold, according to this, there is in them [the Sephirot] perfection and deficiency, and everything is according to the deeds of man. I come now to clarify more: let us know what the concept of the "withdrawal" of the Infinite <term>Ein Sof; the unknowable, boundless aspect of God</term> from the Sephirot is, and also what the withdrawal of the Crown <term>Atarah; another name for Malchut, the lowest Sephirah</term> toward the Infinite is, and the nature of the "falling" of the attribute of Lordship.

Unless you have heard that the Crown is called "all breath," and she is one of the "vanities" <note>The Hebrew word *hevel* means both "breath/vapor" and "vanity."</note> about which the Wise King <note>Solomon, in the book of Ecclesiastes</term> said: "All is vanity" etc. For there, in that verse, the numerical value is "vanities," indicating the [spiritual] structure that is purified and yearned for through the "breath of the mouth" that comes from the mouths of the righteous—whether through Torah study or prayer. This is the secret of the verse, "There is a vapor <note>hevel</note> that is done upon the earth." And also, the Crown is the letter *He* [ה] and is the number thirty-two [ל"ב], and thus she is the "breath" [הב"ל]. And "All" [הכל] reversed is "Flame" [להב], for she is the flame bound to the coal. She is one of the flames of which it is said: "The voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire."

Upon these two matters—"Breath" and "Flame"—is founded the secret of the "rising vapor." For the breath that rises from the mouth is comprised of three things: from the moisture [water] that exits, from the heat [fire] that comes from the heart, and from the air that comes from the lungs. The letters that emerge are comprised of these three things through the five points of the mouth. For this reason, He created them with the "Mothers": *A-M-S* <note>Aleph, Mem, Shin—representing Air (Avir), Water (Mayim), and Fire (Esh) in the Sefer Yitzirah</note>. Therefore, the author of the *Book of Creation* <note>Sefer Yitzirah</note> said: "Twenty-two letters... fixed in the tongue like a spirit, dwelling in water, kindled in fire," etc.

These "breaths" rise up to the light of the Crown and are transformed from these qualities—water, air, and fire—which are the Crown. They strengthen it and add power to it, so that it expands and grows upward in the manner of vapors rising from the earth, which turn into clouds and rain in the light, and "pour out upon the earth." For "kind finds its kind" and is awakened. In any case, the awakening comes from below. But if, Heaven forbid, the power of the lights and the air that rises is weakened, the rain will not fall to the earth, as it is said: "A mist went up from the earth and watered the face of the ground"—no more and no less.

The matter is the same with the Crown. When she is "dry" due to the sins of Israel, she does not ascend, and her "oily vapors" do not descend from the Infinite in a way that would "pour out upon her." It is also necessary that if hidden vapors descend to her, they meet one another, in the manner of the sense of light and the light within the perceived object: sparks emerge from it and move toward the sense of the eye, and sparks also emerge from the eye to receive them, and they meet as one, as is known to the natural scientists. So too, from the Infinite, lights and emanations descend until they reach the Crown as hidden vapors, and these meet those. Then "joy and gladness shall be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of song."

I will give you a beautiful parable for this matter involving a magnet <note>original: even ha-sho'evet; literally "the drawing stone"</note>. Did not the sage Rabbi Azriel compare the Emanation <term>Atzilut; the world of Divine proximity</term> near the Infinite to a magnet that draws iron through its action? He further wrote elsewhere, saying: This matter is also from the perspective of the flame, for she is a flame with lights in her shades, which are also found in a rainbow. For when the three lights ascend—which are the clouds and air—toward her, because she is "the mirror that does not shine" <term>aspeklaria d'la nahra; a common term for Malchut, which has no light of its own</term>, the colors are found in her. But the light comes from above, and the colors within her rise to meet it.

The parable for this is a night lamp that has been extinguished, leaving a "smoky vapor" in it. If one places this lamp beneath a burning lamp, the smoky vapor in the [extinguished] lamp will draw the flame, and the fire is kindled because it is the nature of fire to ascend and to descend toward the smoky vapor in the lamp, even if they do not physically touch. When there is enough light to draw these "tablets," all is within the power of the matter in the Crown, which contains the likeness of "smoky vapor" for the qualities above her. For she is the "mirror that does not shine," and when the smoky vapor rises from her, it meets the flame from "The Mother" <term>Binah; the Sephirah of Understanding</term> and draws it down. All this occurs provided there is no hinderer—namely, the sins of Israel, which prevent the smoky vapor from ascending. "Guard this matter with all diligence, for from it flow the springs of life." Thus far the words of the Pious Rabbi.

The author of the *System* <note>Ma'arekhet Ha-Elokut; a classic 14th-century Kabbalistic text</note> further wrote in the section on "The Reason": "One must further contemplate and know that the thinkers consider our 'Crown' to be separate and to visit the 'All' and to supervise the lower world and lead it. This does not mean there is a deficiency of power or holiness or honor in her, nor a 'separation' caused when their deeds are not proper, Heaven forbid—not as many shallow-minded people think in their weak understanding of the words of our Sages and the Kabbalists. Rather, the 'thought' was for the ultimate perfection in the matter of Creation for the sake of its continued existence." Thus far his words.

The Pious One responds: "If it is not a matter of her having power and holiness, etc." If the Rabbi's intention is that the Crown does not receive a "defect" <note>pegam</note> through the sins of Israel—with all due respect, that is a philosophical view, but not the true opinion of the sages of Kabbalah. For what is the "descent of the nursemaid" or the "sending away of the Mother" of which it is said, "And for your transgressions was your mother sent away"? And what of the "cutting of the shoots" that Elisha ben Abuyah did when he committed sins, or the "restoring of the Mother" through the performance of commandments? Every single commandment depends on this axis! Rather, the purpose was to teach that our sins cause a "power of defect." Everyone understands that we "remove the Mother from the children," and in the *Zohar* it says: "'Do not take the Mother with the children'—do not remove the Mother from the children."

The "defect" is this: the illuminating light withdraws upward and does not "visit the earth," because the purpose of the "visitation" is to do good for the lower beings who raise the "formed matter" to its Creator. If there is no righteous man to draw the influence <term>Shefa; Divine abundance</term> from the Upper Constellation, it turns out that the Crown is also "defective" and lacking that abundance. This is the meaning of "And He was grieved in His heart," as Nahmanides explained.

I will give you a parable from human breasts: as long as the infant rests upon them, he sucks and draws the milk to the breasts from the source. But if the infant is missing, the milk is also missing. You will find the same thing with a well: as long as its water is drawn, the water increases; but if there is no one to draw it, the water does not increase, but rather diminishes. So it is in the world of Emanation.

I am astonished at the Rabbi <note>the author of the Ma'arekhet</note>, for it seems from his words that there is no distinction between the Emanator and the Emanated. This is the conclusion he reached, which forced him to say what he said. It would be acceptable if we were attributing this to the First Emanator, who is the "End of all Causes." But in the Emanation of the Torah, the "strap" is extended. I have already explained in the discourse on Emanation that initially, the Holy One, blessed be He, needed to create the world through the medium of Emanation, which receives perfection and deficiency in order to "do evil or do good." He himself said this at the beginning of this book: "You should know that when I mention 'beginning' and 'end' regarding the Sephirot, the intention is not, Heaven forbid, that God has a beginning and an end... but the intention is regarding the matter of Emanation, which has a beginning and an end for the purpose of the order and rectification of all created things." Perhaps we can defend him and "place a patch on his language" by saying he came to teach us not to err by thinking that the Crown was relegated to being the "head of the corner" <note>the lowest point</note> because of a lack of holiness, but rather for the reason he stated: it was necessary for the survival of the lower beings. Thus far the words of Rabbi Chait.

<margin>
The words of Rabbi P.Z. <note>likely Rabbi Perez Ha-Kohen</note>, which is also a commentary on the book *The System* [Ma'arekhet]: He wrote, "It is not a matter of there being a deficiency of power and holiness," etc. Even though it appears in the Written and Oral Torah that when the lower beings do not do the will of God, the "defect" rises above—Heaven forbid that this should cause any lack in the Divine Essences! Rather, when Israel does the will of God, the blessing is drawn from above to below, and then all those "faces" are ready to "seek their food" [from God]. The "accuser" <term>katigor</term> becomes an "advocate" <term>sanegor</term> for Israel, who are called "children of the Place," and then blessing is found in the world. "Strangers shall stand and feed your flocks." But if, Heaven forbid, they do not do His will, the influence, blessing, and providence are diminished from above, and providence withdraws from the lower beings and from the [celestial] powers that act in the lower world. Then those "young lions" roar for prey because there is no provider or helper. These are the "hinderers" of blessing and influence until they repent. For He, blessed and exalted be He, does not withhold good, but man himself causes the "hinderers" to exist. These were created only to execute true and upright judgment when the influence is withdrawn from them because of the lower beings. Then the advocates become accusers. It is clear that there is no [inherent] lack above because of the lower beings.

And if you ask: How can we reconcile the verses in the Torah that indicate a lack reaches above, such as "I am with him in distress," or "In all their affliction, He was afflicted," or "For your transgressions was your mother sent away"? The intention is that even though the Ruler remains in His house and His treasuries, He is not at ease as long as another power is given dominion, as if He were unable to provide what is missing except through other mediums. It is as if the Ruler is "distressed" by this matter. "For this the earth mourns... for a slave when he reigns, and a maidservant when she displaces her mistress." This is clear; one should not deviate right or right or left. Thus far the words of Rabbi P.Z.
</margin>

The explanation of the *System's* view follows Nahmanides' commentary on the book *The Portals*. A similar matter was written by the Kabbalist Rabbi Matitiah Delacrut in his commentary on Rekanati. I will copy the language of Rekanati from the beginning of the portion of *Noach*: "And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence" (Genesis 6:11). He said that the Upper Earth <note>Malchut</note> was corrupted through the sin of man. The term "corruption" <note>hashchatah</note> is related to "a companion to a man who destroys" (Proverbs 18:9). So too, "for your people have corrupted themselves" (Exodus 32:7). The meaning is that he "separated the Essences." Likewise, "corrupt children," "do not destroy its trees," "he corrupted the ground." The reason for "behold, I will destroy them with the earth" is as the Sages said in *Genesis Rabbah*: "A king who had a nursemaid; as long as he misbehaved, his nursemaid was punished." She is called "Nursemaid" <note>meneket</note> because from there everyone "sucks" <note>yonkin</note>... "you shall eat the good of the land." # The Great Gate

In its essence, etc. And these are his words: There is also a third union, which is specific to four Sephirot <term>Sephirot; the ten creative powers or attributes through which God interacts with the universe</term>: Wisdom [Chokhmah], Understanding [Binah], Beauty [Tiferet], and Sovereignty [Malchut]. This is the matter of "coupling" <term>Zivug; a Kabbalistic term for the union of divine attributes, often compared to human marriage</term> which is found only in these spheres. This matter is like the union of a man and his wife—something no human can truly grasp unless we compare the second union to the sustenance a man gives his wife in a slow abundance, sometimes through a third party. But the third union is like an actual coupling, joining with her to bring everything forth for its purpose. This is a sublime matter, so much so that "the mouth cannot speak what the ear can hear" regarding these things. We shall expand the explanation of this in a specific chapter of this Gate. Thus far his words <note>original: עכ"ל (ad kan leshono)</note>.

**And it is possible** to say that the doubts, the sayings, and the teachers—whether a man be righteous or wicked—do not affect the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the highest level of divine influence</note>. This refers to the "Constant Sustenance," which is the First Union of the spheres I transcribed above—the flow established at the beginning of Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term> for the sake of their existence, which is the "Acceptance of the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven." This never decreases or diminishes in its constancy. However, the deeds of human beings cause, through their actions, an *additional* flow within them, and from them it descends below. Thus, "he who is blessed on earth shall be blessed by the God of Truth" <note>original: אלהי אמן (Elohei Amen); Isaiah 65:16</note>, for according to the additional flow, the Name is blessed and unified. This is not a constant thing, but depends on human deeds. Those who gather [sinfully] withhold this good and diminish this perfection, which is dependent on man—for he was placed there "to work it and to keep it" <note>Genesis 2:15</note> and to establish this for the Unification of the Name.

**Further**, another explanation of the matter appears to me based on what was explained at length in the introduction: that man has no permission to contemplate anything except "Our World," our structure, which is the "Lower Building"—the Seven Days of Creation <note>The seven lower Sephirot from Chesed (Kindness) to Malchut (Sovereignty)</note>. From there, actions are drawn down, and—God forbid—deficiency [can occur], as "a world of deficiency shall be built." But from "Man's World" and above—meaning the "Three Firsts" <term>Gimel Rishonot; the three highest Sephirot: Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding</term>—they are considered as one. Regarding them it is said: "Seek not things that are too hard for thee" <note>original: אין לך עסק בנסתרות (ein lecha esek ba-nistarot); from the Talmud, Hagigah 13a</note>. They are not "Man's World" because actions are not drawn from there; they are the Hidden World, the worlds of Thought. Wisdom and Understanding are His very essence, which is beyond human attainment. From them, the flow is drawn according to the ways of men. In His World—the Three Firsts, which are hidden—whether a man be righteous or wicked, what can he affect? However, in "Man's World"—the Building—deficiency is possible. Therefore, it is right to speak of the "Power of Deficiency" and the "Power of Perfection" according to the arousal of man and his deeds. For from these [lower spheres] actions are drawn, and according to the actions, there is an arousal within them. Then they receive a great flow, generation upon generation, "strength and gladness" <note>1 Chronicles 16:27</note> in our introduction. For the entire structure of Beauty and Sovereignty is the source of Israel and the treasury of their souls. Sovereignty raises "Feminine Waters" <term>Mayin Nukvin; spiritual initiative or prayer rising from below</term> which is the arousal of worthy deeds illuminated in the roots of their souls. Then, Beauty shines toward her face with "Masculine Waters" <term>Mayin Dechurin; divine response and flow from above</term> which are poured upon it from its Holy Source. Then the Unification of the Name is perfect, and from there peace and blessing are drawn into all worlds. In the reverse—God forbid—there is no union above, so to speak, to pour out good, and there is no flow below. This is the state of separation, "impurity" <note>original: נידה (niddah)</note>, and "a handmaid that is heir to her mistress" <note>Proverbs 30:23</note>, when the narrow one and the enemy are in the Jerusalem Above. I have already written above in the name of the Sages of Truth that the student should not think that the "Husks" <term>Kelipot; forces of evil or concealment</term> actually enter into the realm of Emanation [Atzilut], as many of the pseudo-Kabbalists of our generation mistakenly think. This is foolishness. These matters must be understood and directed properly: the matter is that when the cry of the "Accusers"—called "Others" because they are outside the Academy and do not enter into the presence of the Lord—rises, they cry out regarding the debts and sins of Israel. They say, "These are idolaters and those are idolaters; these are forbidden-relation-revealers, etc." Then the anger and jealousy of the Lord are smoke, and instead of saying "they are My people," He says to them "not My people" <note>Hosea 1:9</note>, God forbid. In the place where it was fitting for a great flow of mercy to be poured out, the Attribute of Judgment is aroused, and the "dross of the gold" flows to the "External Ones" <term>Chitzonim; external spiritual forces</term>. The judgment is finalized. This is what is meant by their "entering into the holiness"—not that they literally enter, but that their claim and their teaching of the debts of the "enemies of Israel" <note>A common euphemism for Israel itself when discussing misfortune</note> enter there on high to arouse judgment and take vengeance. This is called "entering the holiness." It is not just the flow of judgment, but that in the place where judgment is aroused, the "Face of Mercy" withdraws, and Fear and Judgment prevail. That "Desire" is blemished until vengeance is taken, or until Mercy is revealed to illuminate the place of darkness, for "with much water, the fire is extinguished." The world is then judged, and the Creator makes that place—which is darkness through the hiding of the Face of Mercy—act through Judgment. From the "Building" and below, it prevents the beauty of the secret of This World <note>original: עה"ז (Olam Ha-Zeh)</note>, as explained above in the introduction. But from Understanding [Binah] and above, "the wine is straight," and it is the secret of the World to Come <note>original: עה"ב (Olam Ha-Ba)</note>. There, there is no need for "Might" [Gevurah] resulting from human actions.

**However**, one might seemingly ask: if man causes or prevents the union below—the coupling of Beauty and Sovereignty—then it follows that from Understanding and above there would also be no union. For if Wisdom and Understanding (which are "Father and Mother") [Abba and Imma] have no union, then Beauty and Sovereignty are not secure. As I wrote above, the union of Wisdom and Understanding exists after the creation of the beings. Granted, at first, when the Will arose to bring things into existence, the "Building" was emanated through Wisdom and Understanding. But afterward, what is the nature of their union? This matter is the explanation of Chapter 19 from the Gate of Essence and Conduct, and these are his words: For the existence of Emanation is through "Father and Mother." Behold, just as in the union of man and wife there are two aspects—the first to give birth anew, and the second to "grow the plants" (that is, so the child emerges from the union, as I said above in the Gate of the Roots, Chapter 3)—so too Wisdom and Understanding: their union is not to create a new living being, but to maintain the existence of the beings in their union so that they remain in their full form. And the matter is that...

<column-break/>

Chapter 4 of the "Division of the Hidden Portals," and these are his words: The window of the "Higher Foundation" [Yesod Elyon] is without deficiency. Therefore, that which was created from it was without distinction; it had no power of "The Separator" to join with deficiency. Its nature was like its Creator—infinite. But this was not the intention. Rather, He added "The Finite," and it was thus created. Because it was finite, it could not endure the Soul-Light <note>unclear reading</note>. It was impossible for the world to exist except through an intermediary that possessed both qualities: it must be both [infinite] and deficient, distinguishing between the Crown and the New. This is "The Limit" which contains both perfection and deficiency. And this was by the power of the Creator, blessed be His Name. He was found in the world, and for the sake of hearing alone was "The Separate" created. In the intelligence of the day there was... and deficiency... so that every creature in it, through a specific intelligence, would include both perfection and deficiency. Perfection by being at the Source of Flow; and the "Distanced Perfection" from the higher ones. Thus far. And it was written in the name of the Kabbalistic Rabbi Treivish <note>original: טירליכס"ס / טירל"ך</note> regarding the word "Foundation" [Yesod]... and these are his words: Which he received from the mouth of the pious Rabbi Isaac the Blind <term>Rabbi Isaac the Blind; a 12th-century father of Kabbalah</term>, son of the Ramban <note>This is a historical error or unique tradition in the text; Isaac the Blind was the son of Abraham ben David (the Ravad), not Ramban</note>, of blessed memory. He added an introduction... what is the power of the Creator that distinguishes the Ten Sephirot? For everyone agrees that in the "Infinite" [Ein Sof] they exist only in the Thought of the One God... and this is His perfection without deficiency... but Wisdom was the first to be "opened" as deficient. And the deficiency which is calculated and which is missing is far from Him. And since there is no... we must say that it was created so that there would be creatures without limit... the Ten Sephirot were created from the "Power of Deficiency"... they are called "Man"... and because they have the power of deficiency, they have the power to act within "The Finite" and deficiency, etc. See there.

->Conduct<-

The secret of the "Assembly of Israel" <term>Knesset Israel; the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people, often identified with the Sephirah of Malchut</term> is to take power... the Sephirot drawn according to the intention in the Gates. If we were worthy, we would achieve... in the high angels... the body of Enoch <term>Enoch; the biblical figure who, in mystical tradition, was transformed into the angel Metatron</term>... the Ramban established in his spirit... on the earth... a house of body and soul... and it shall be for the sake of anger... between Wisdom and the worlds... and the creatures came from the logical deductions... thus far his words. Further, the T.S. <note>likely a reference to a specific commentary or author</note> wrote: ...on the verse "I was not..." <note>text becomes highly fragmentary and idiomatic</note>... Her Majesty the Shekhinah... and I called her "Wisdom" here... that she was a wife to me... and they shall be... I took the Holy One, blessed be He... this is the hiddenness of the face of Moses... and this is the purpose... the piety blemishes itself in the intention... all the holy names... specifically in her... the blemish in the beginning and in every excess... as it is found in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkuney Zohar</note>. Thus far his words.

# The Great Gate

For all the worlds, according to what they were appointed over at the time of their emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest spiritual realm where divine light is first structured</term>, each and every sphere [Sefirah] has a storehouse under its hand. For example: **Crown** [Keter] is the storehouse of absolute, simple Mercy without any mixture; **Wisdom** [Chokhmah] is the storehouse of Wisdom; **Understanding** [Binah] is the storehouse of Repentance; **Kindness** [Chesed] is the storehouse of Loving-kindness; **Might** [Gevurah] is the storehouse of Wealth; **Beauty** [Tiferet] is the storehouse of the Torah. And so they all function according to the needs of the created beings and the requirements of the hour and time. 

For there are times when there is a need for mercy, or pardon, forgiveness, and atonement; then it is necessary to draw the flow [Shefa] from the "Upper Whiteness"—which is the **Crown** that whitens the sins of Israel—through **Understanding**, for she is the essence of Repentance leading to forgiveness. Through her, and especially through the "Father" (which is **Wisdom**), that flow is channeled to **Sovereignty** [Malchut]. Then **Understanding** and **Sovereignty** are awakened through the six middle spheres between them—namely **Greatness** [Chesed], **Might**, **Beauty**, **Victory**, **Splendor**, and **Foundation**. 

This is the secret of why the High Priest would count [on Yom Kippur]: "One; one and one; one and two; one and three; one and four," and so on until "one and seven" <note>This refers to the ritual in the Holy of Holies where the High Priest sprinkled blood and counted to track the connection between the highest Unity and the seven lower emotional spheres</note>. He would count "One" three times to return to the first three spheres, which are considered as one. He would count up to seven, which represents **Sovereignty** [Malchut]. In all of them, he counted "One" with them to demonstrate the descent of the influence through the levels, showing that their flow is equal. This is the core of the Yom Kippur service: drawing forgiveness and atonement down to **Sovereignty**.

There are also times when people need wisdom to become wise in the Torah; then the flow of **Wisdom** is channeled through **Kindness**. This is the meaning of the saying, "He who desires to become wise should turn south," <note>original: הרוצה שיחכים ידרים (ha-rotzeh she-yachkim yadrim)</note> because **Kindness** is associated with the South. From there, it flows to **Beauty**, which is the root of the Torah, and from there to **Sovereignty**, which is called "Lower Wisdom." 

There are times when one needs wealth; then he draws the flow of **Understanding** to **Might**. This is the meaning of "He who desires to become wealthy should turn north," <note>original: הרוצה להעשיר יצפין (ha-rotzeh le-hashir yatzpin)</note> meaning he should intend for **Understanding** to open for him the storehouse of Wealth that she holds in **Might**, and from there to **Sovereignty**. 

And sometimes they need might and strength to take vengeance on their enemies; then the flow is channeled from **Understanding** to **Foundation**, which is the root and nourishment of all life, and through **Might**, and from there to **Splendor**, and from there to the "Destroyer" who "avenges the vengeance of the covenant" with the help of **Victory** the conqueror. Then they will prevail over their enemies and defeat them. 

There are thousands upon thousands of such aspects, all of which are "renewals" based on the actions of the created beings, which are renewed by their deeds as needed. In truth, these flows do not come to any hidden place or connection through their rebellion, Heaven forbid, in the manner of "Cause and Effect" from the first movement to the last edge, for the sake of the world's persistence and existence in its place so that the world does not become a ruin. For even without these specific flows, the world would remain standing. Rather, these flows are according to the deeds performed and renewed by the created beings—the "actions of those below." As it is explained in the Zohar: "By an awakening from below, an action is awakened above" <note>original: באתערותא דלתתא אתערר עובדא דלעילא (be-itaruta de-letata itarar uvda de-leila)</note>.

It follows that this flow is a "good" and an "addition" in the realm of Emanation beyond the flow that sustains the world's natural order. Thus, there are two types of flow: 
1. The first flow, which is for the existence and persistence of the world.
2. The second flow, which depends on the deeds of those below. 

May the eyes of your intellect be illuminated by the light of the Living God in the secret of the "adhesion" found, as it were, in **Sovereignty**. We say that the foundation of the first Unity is the expression of all these spheres, and there shall be no void, gap, or separation between them, Heaven forbid. Rather, the Providence always dwells in them from the first sphere, **Crown**, to the last sphere, **Sovereignty**. They are all equal for good. Their names and their vitality in their light fill one another, and this is the source of all blessing—nothing shall be missing or diminished. For in the Divine boundary, there is neither deficiency nor excess, as explained in the book *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>Referring to Maimonides' philosophical work</note>. 

But regarding the "Second Unity," which is for the purpose of governance according to the actions and renewals of the created beings—this flow is not for the essential existence of the world or its connection as Cause and Effect. It does not touch the essence of the Divine Light itself, which is perfect, for no perfection exists above It. This flow dwells in its place, and He does not receive any perfection from another. Rather, it is for the sake of the created beings. This is the flow that is sometimes "missing" according to the actions of the creatures. In this context, "emptiness" may be attributed to **Sovereignty**. For example, if there is wealth "in the gates of Israel" but Israel is not worthy of it, **Understanding** will not flow wealth through **Might** to **Sovereignty**. Thus, **Sovereignty** is "empty," as it were, of wealth. Not that she is empty in herself, Heaven forbid—for she lacks no good—but she is empty in that she did not receive that specific wealth needed for Israel. 

Similarly, when it is time for Israel to take vengeance on their enemies but they are not worthy, she does not receive the Might and the strength of victory to bestow upon Israel. The same applies to all aspects of the flow she is meant to receive for Israel's needs. But let it not be thought that she has any literal void or deficiency, for she herself is full of all good, and the emanation required for the Divine boundary is in her hand. Thus far his words. 

**He further said:** ▢ When there is no flow for the governance of the lower worlds—which comes from the "awakening of those below"—all the spheres are, as it were, "dry" of that additional flow. For the flow needed for the lower worlds is only revealed through the awakening of those below when they are worthy of it. This is the secret of "The Shekhinah <term>Shekhinah; the Divine Presence, often associated with the sphere of Malchut</term> among the lower beings is a 'Need on High,'" as it were. When the Shekhinah bestows, it is the need of the "Inner Beings" who receive the flow through her. The Shekhinah serves as the place for them to bestow, and their own flow increases through the act of bestowing. 

Just as light increases when it follows a righteous person who serves as a "chariot" for it so that it may flow through them, she too increases her flow through her bestowing. It is like a nursing mother: the more she nurses, the more her milk increases. So too the Shekhinah—the more she bestows, the more additional flow she receives. And so it is for the sphere above her: whenever it bestows the "Hidden Flow" into revelation, it also increases its flow from the "Hiddenness" that is above it. 

For everything is called "Shekhinah" up until **Understanding**, and some say even up to **Wisdom**. For even **Wisdom** is called "Shekhinah," as **Sovereignty** is the "Lower Mother" and the Shekhinah of below, and she is appointed specifically over the righteous who are a "chariot" for her to bestow through them. **Wisdom** is the "Shekhinah" over **Understanding**, and **Understanding** dwells over **Understanding** and **Sovereignty** to bestow into them. 

Heaven forbid that you should think that "The Shekhinah among the lower beings is a Need on High" means the spheres themselves require this for their own essence. We have already said that the flow required for the Unity of the spheres' essence never lacks or diminishes, for they are in a state of perfection beyond which there is no higher perfection. Rather, the increased flow is for the sake of governing the worlds. It is like a mother's milk, which is not for her own sake but for the sake of the child. The reason she "pursues" the righteous person is because the abundance of flow she has is not for her own sake. It is the nature of the "Perfect One," because of His perfection, to complete others and bestow of His perfection to others. Therefore, she pursues the righteous to complete others and bestow through them to others. 

This is the "Need of the Spheres" we mentioned. Because they have no perfection above them, and the nature of the perfect is to bestow and complete others, the Shekhinah must be among the lower beings so that the spheres can fulfill their nature to bestow. Therefore, bestowing is a "need" for them to fulfill their nature of perfection. Thus far his words. 

It is therefore clear from his words that "Need on High" <term>Tzorech Gavoah; the concept that human action somehow "affects" or is "needed" by God</term> only means that there is "satisfaction" [Nachat Ruach] before Him, as it were, when His will is performed by His creatures to bestow good. This is somewhat inclined toward the saying of our Sages: "Fortunate is the man who grows up in the Torah... and gives satisfaction to his Creator" <note>original: ועושה נחת רוח ליוצרו (ve-oseh nachat ruach le-yotzro)</note>. This implies that human deeds are not a "need" for His essence or for any perfection of His, but only that it is a "satisfaction" to the Creator that His will is done.

**And then**, according to the verses and the holy [texts] which show whether a man be righteous or wicked, the matter does not touch Him, blessed be He. Only, as it were, He has "satisfaction" when His will is done, and the opposite, Heaven forbid, in the reverse case. 

However, in the book *Avodat HaKodesh* [The Sacred Service], in its introduction, he explains this phrase "gives satisfaction to his Creator" in a different way. These are his words: "The intention is more than just 'pleasure' [nachat]. It is the secret of 'Movement' [Horatzat] and 'Will' and the 'Holy Spirit' upon the upper heads, and from there 'satisfaction' and 'will' flow to the Creator. All of this comes through the fulfillment of the Torah and Commandments for their own sake." Thus far his words. 

The system of the author of *Avodat HaKodesh* throughout his book is well-known; he explains that divine service is a *literal* "Need on High" within the essence of Emanation, and it "adds strength," repairs, and unifies the Name. And the opposite occurs in the reverse case, Heaven forbid... Truly, in the plain meaning of the scriptures and the hinted-at sayings, the matter of "need" is treated as a literal need for the essence... as Maimonides said, "He was to help him and serve him," etc. "Who blessed me?" 

And so most verses and sayings indicate, especially regarding the "Third Unity" of the three unities in the spheres which he wrote about, explaining that there is a "granting of power" etc. and "strength was lacking," as I mentioned is famously written in Chapter 3 of the "Gate of Essence and Governance," which I intended above to transcribe. And this is a matter that concerns the Creator.

<summary>This page explores the Kabbalistic concept of "Need on High," debating whether human deeds actually "add" something to God or merely provide "satisfaction." It uses the metaphor of a nursing mother to explain how the divine flow increases through the act of bestowing upon the lower worlds.</summary>

# The Gate of Reward

...in it itself, etc. And these are his words: "There is yet a third Unification which is specific to four spheres [Sefirot]: **Wisdom** [Chokhmah], **Understanding** [Binah], **Beauty** [Tiferet], and **Sovereignty** [Malchut]. This involves the matter of 'Coupling' <term>Zivvug; a metaphor for the union of divine energies to produce spiritual results</term> which is found only in these spheres. This matter is like the union of a man and his wife—something no person can truly grasp unless we compare the 'Second Unification' to the sustenance a man gives his wife in abundance, sometimes through a third party, while the 'Third Unification' is like the actual coupling itself, where they unite to bring forth every action. This is a sublime matter, such that the mouth cannot fully describe it to the ear. We shall expand the explanation of this in this Gate in a specific chapter." Thus far his words.

**It is possible** to say that the verses and sayings regarding whether a man is righteous or wicked do not affect the "First Unification" (the constant unification mentioned above). That flow is established at the beginning of Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest spiritual realm</term> for the sake of the worlds' continued existence; it is the "Acceptance of the Yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven" which never fails or diminishes, for it is eternal and constant. However, the deeds of human beings cause—by virtue of their actions—an *additional* flow of influence within the spheres. From them, this flow descends below, so that "he who blesses himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of truth" <note>Isaiah 65:16</note>, for through this additional flow, the Name is blessed and unified. This is not a constant thing; it depends entirely on the deeds of mankind. Sinners prevent this good and diminish this perfection. Indeed, the purpose of man’s creation was "to work it and to keep it" <note>Genesis 2:15; interpreted here as serving the divine realms</note> and to establish this Unification of the Name.

**It further** seems to me that the explanation of this matter follows what was explained at length in the introduction: man is only permitted to contemplate the "Worlds of the Building" <term>the lower seven Sefirot, which correspond to the seven days of Creation</term>, for from there, all divine actions are drawn. God forbid that anything should be lacking there, for "a world of lack shall be built" <note>A wordplay on Psalm 89:3, "A world of kindness [Chesed] shall be built"</note>. But from "Man's World" and upward—namely, the three highest spheres which are considered as one—it is said: "You have no business with hidden things." These are not "Man's World" because actions are not drawn from there; they are the "Hidden World." Regarding them, it is said that "Thought [cannot grasp Him]," etc. **Understanding** and upward are His very essence, which is not revealed in a way that actions are drawn from them according to human ways. In the World of the Blessed One—namely, in the Three Highers which are hidden—if a man is righteous or wicked, what can he affect? However, in "Man's World"—namely, the Building—there is "lack." Therefore, it is appropriate to speak of a "power of lack" and a "power of perfection" in them, according to the awakening of man and his deeds. Actions are drawn from them, and according to those actions, there is an awakening in their secret place. They receive a great flow: "Glory and majesty are before Him; strength and joy are in His place" <note>1 Chronicles 16:27</note>. For they are all hidden: **Beauty** and **Sovereignty**, and **Sovereignty** is the source of Israel and the root of their souls. When **Sovereignty** raises "Feminine Waters" <term>Mayin Nukvin; spiritual initiative from below, i.e., human prayer or good deeds</term>—which is the awakening of significant deeds that shine upon the roots of their souls—then **Beauty** shines toward her face with "Masculine Waters" <term>Mayin Dechurin; divine response and flow from above</term> poured upon him from his holy source. Then the Unification of the Name is complete, and from there, peace and blessing are drawn into all worlds. But if, God forbid, there is no Unification above at all, then joy and good are absent and there is no flow below. This is described as a state of "impurity" or "the handmaid inheriting from her mistress" <note>Proverbs 30:23</note>—a state of harsh judgment where the enemy is in the "Jerusalem Above." I have already written in the name of the Sages of Truth that the student should not think there is any actual division within the Emanation. These matters must be understood and established properly. The matter is this: when the "cry of the oppressors" (called "Others" <term>Sitra Achra; the 'Other Side' or forces of evil</term>) enters—those who are outside the academy but enter to suckle from the sweetness of the inner chambers due to the guilt and sins of Israel—they say, "These worship idols and those worship idols," or "These are immoral," etc. This is "the anger of the Lord and His jealousy smoking" <note>Deuteronomy 29:19</note>. In the place where it should be said to them, "You are My people," it is said, "You are not My people," God forbid. The anger of the Lord burns in the place that should receive a great flow of mercy through the attribute of **Sovereignty**. The power of Judgment is awakened, and the "Golden Sin" <note>Refers to the Golden Calf</note> causes the flow to go to the "External Ones" <term>destructive spiritual forces</term>. Judgment is then finalized. This is what is meant by their "entering into the Holy"—not that they literally enter, but that their claims and the prosecution of Israel’s guilt enter there to rouse wrath and vengeance. This is called their "entry into the Holy." It is not just the flow of Judgment, but that in the place where Judgment is awakened, the Face of Mercy is withdrawn. Dread and Judgment prevail, and that spark is flawed until vengeance is taken, or until Mercy is revealed to illuminate the place of darkness, for "with much water, the fire is extinguished." When the world is judged and this place is flawed, it becomes darkness through the hiding of the Face of Mercy; this is the action of Judgment. From the "Building" and downward, the beauty and secret of this world are withheld. I explained this earlier in the introduction. But from **Understanding** and upward, there is the "Guarded Wine" <term>Yayin Meshumar; the spiritual reward stored since creation</term>, which is the secret of the World to Come. There, there is no need for the "Might" <term>Gevurah</term> resulting from human actions.

**However**, one might ask: if man causes the union of the Lower Unification—namely the coupling of **Beauty** and **Sovereignty**—it follows that he also causes an effect from **Understanding** and upward. For there is no coupling of the "Building" [the lower spheres] and **Understanding** (who are "Father and Mother" <term>Abba and Imma; Chokhmah and Binah</term>) except through a higher unification. As I wrote above, the coupling of **Wisdom** and **Understanding** occurs when there is a "bending of the corners." This is fine at first when there is a will for existence to come into being, but afterward, what is the nature of their coupling? This matter was explained in the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moses Cordovero</note> in the section on Essence and Conduct: just as in the union of a man and wife there are two aspects—the first to give birth anew, and the second to sustain the existing life (so the child may emerge from its boundaries, as mentioned in the previous gate, chapter 3)—so too, the union of **Understanding** and **Wisdom** is not to create a new living being, but to sustain existing beings upon their foundations so they may remain in their full form. The matter is that...

<column-break/>

Chapter 4 of the section "Openings of Pathros," and these are his words: "A single window above them, without lack... end of the abundance from it without ending. If there were power in it for its action and to receive lack, etc... for my house is crushed with cutting, and my bride is finite. This law, that the intention of the Sage adds a finite end and is not cut off—so it is. Despite being finite, it could not endure the generation of its reception... and the connection of every tongue from the nullifiers. It was impossible for the world to be created from that which is not... without there being two opposites in it: power and lack. They produce the finite and the light. The end of the receptions had power in it, and this is loss. This is the known sect... that was found in its cause and first in a thing cut off... in the individual power... it was Judgment. And this secret was hidden: because of its being uniquely included, it would include perfection and lack. Perfection in being the receiver of the flow; lack... from his world above him." Thus far his words.

<margin>End of Chapter</margin>
He also wrote there: "And the Third Unification, which is the unification of Coupling: in this unification, its reception of power is lacking. And from the connection of every tongue from the nullifiers, it was impossible for the world to be created from that which is not, unless there were two opposites in it: power and lack. They produce the finite and the light. The end of the receptions had power in it, and this is loss. This is the known sect that was found in its cause and first in a thing cut off in the individual power. It was Judgment. And this secret was hidden: because of its being uniquely included, it would include perfection and lack. Perfection in being the receiver of the flow; lack from his world above him." Thus far his words.

And so wrote the Kabbalist Rabbi Azriel <note>Azriel of Gerona, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note>, may his memory be a blessing, in the section on the Foundation [Yesod], page 80, column 3: "The Sage, the Kabbalist Rabbi Azriel, of blessed memory—who received from the mouth of the pious Rabbi Isaac the Blind, son of the Ramban <note>Nachmanides</note>, of blessed memory, who was the third generation [of the tradition]—added an explanation to the question: How does any mind grasp what is the root of the spheres? For all say they have no end [Ein Sof]. He was asked to explain how a thing can exist without lack. This is the secret: The Infinite [Ein Sof] has no limit. It has no power within a limit to give from its perfection. If it were not for the 'Power of Lack' <term>Koach ha-Chisaron; the divine ability to withdraw or limit light so creation can exist</term> which is found at the beginning of existence, the world could not be sustained. Therefore, within His perfection, we must say there is a potential for that which is created without limit. When His wisdom emerged from Him first, the ten spheres [Sefirot] were established as a power of lack and a power of perfection. They are the ones that receive the flow from His total perfection. They have the 'Power of Perfection' [when they receive], and when the flow is withheld from them, they have the 'Power of Lack.' Therefore, there is a potential for action in His perfection and lack, etc." Thus far his words.

<margin>Chapter Opening</margin>
**The Secret** of "The Congregation of Israel [Knesset Yisrael] shall be your mate" for the eight spheres, etc. They are like their powers. Since the intention in these gates is to explain that if they had not sinned... we would have merited a soul for the spirit, and our sustenance would be as a crown in the upper worlds. They would exist as the limbs in a human body. Their excellence would be greater than his, for he is a learner from what is below. Thus, after the heavens, one must divide the peace upon the earth. The essence of the Indwelling [Shekhinah] is in the lower beings, who are body and soul, learning from below. The Life of Lives stands to die in anger, and in his eye is the pressure of the two... the involvement between... to the women in heaven. And in the general powers are the redeemed ones, the righteous before the Shekhinah. Thus far his words. He further wrote in Section 109: "And in the Tikunim <note>The Tikunei Zohar</note> on the verse 'For I, the Lord, have not changed' <note>Malachi 3:6</note>: Certainly, the Shekhinah says: 'I have changed, and I have corrected you.' Also, 'I, I am He' <note>Isaiah 43:11</note>—I have not changed, and I have not been changed by a guard. And He does not change or hide. But 'as a father chastises his son,' the Holy One, blessed be He, hid from them... to hide the face of Moses. This is the ultimate flaw that results from sin: when the Intention was to dwell with honor in our midst, to be the life of all holy souls. But the 'Anger' <term>Af</term> flaws the Third, and 'He shall call and look from the hole' by giving flaws to the lower realm." Thus far his words.
