<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Unifications" [Yihudim], specifically contrasting the constant flow of divine energy that sustains existence with the "additional" flow triggered by human deeds. It addresses the philosophical problem of whether God "needs" human service.</meta>

# The Great Gate

...for all the worlds, according to what we have assigned to them at the time of the Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term> of each and every sphere [Sefira]. For each sphere, there is a "storehouse" under its authority. For example, He chose a storehouse for merciful and simple structures without any mixture. **Wisdom** [Chokhmah] is the Storehouse of Wisdom. **Understanding** [Binah] is the Storehouse of Repentance. **Kindness** [Chesed] is the Storehouse of Kindness. **Might** [Gevurah] is the Storehouse of Wealth. **Beauty** [Tiferet] is the Storehouse of Torah. And so they all function according to the needs of the created beings and the requirements of the hour and time.

For there are times when one requires strength for pardon, forgiveness, and atonement. Then, one must draw the flow of influence from the "Upper Whiteness"—which is the Crown [Keter] that whitens the sins of Israel—through **Understanding**, for she is the essence of Repentance that leads to forgiveness. Upon her, the "Father" (which is **Wisdom**) shines and transmits that flow to **Sovereignty** [Malchut]. Then **Understanding** and **Sovereignty** unite by means of the six middle spheres between them—**Greatness**, **Might**, **Beauty**, **Victory**, **Splendor**, and **Foundation**. 

This is the secret of why the High Priest would count: "One, and one and one, one and two, one and three, one and four..." <note>A reference to the Mishnah Yoma 5:3, describing the High Priest sprinkling blood in the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur</note> and so he would count until "one and seven." He would count the "one" three times to indicate the three highest spheres, which are considered as one. Then he would count up to seven, which represents **Sovereignty**. In all of these, he would count the "one" with them to indicate the descent of the influence through the levels, showing that their influence is equal. This is the core of the service on the Day of Atonement: drawing forgiveness and atonement down to **Sovereignty**.

At other times, people may need wisdom to become wise in the Torah; then the flow of **Wisdom** is transmitted through **Kindness**. This is the meaning of the saying, "He who desires to become wise should turn south" <note>Talmud, Bava Batra 25b</note>, for **Kindness** is the South. From there, it flows to **Beauty**, which is the Torah, and from there to **Sovereignty**, which is called the "Lower Wisdom." $\square$ At other times, one may need wealth; then he draws the flow of **Understanding** to **Might**. This is the meaning of "He who desires to become wealthy should turn north," meaning he should direct his inner focus to be given the Storehouse of Wealth which is held in **Might**, and from there to **Sovereignty**. $\square$ And sometimes they may need might and strength to take vengeance on their enemies; then the flow is transmitted from **Understanding** to **Foundation**—in the secret that she is the root and source of Judgment—then to **Might**, and from **Might** to **Splendor**, and from there to the "Sword that avenges the vengeance of the Covenant," aided by **Victory** the Conqueror. Then they will prevail over their enemies and defeat them.

These states of being exist in millions of variations, all of which are renewed according to the actions of the created beings. These actions are renewed through their deeds according to their needs. Now, in truth, these flows of influence do not come for the sake of the world’s general existence, its connection, or its attachment to its roots. The world's basic sustenance and existence, from the First Cause to the final point, is constant so that the world remains standing and is not destroyed. Even without these specific flows, the world would stand. Rather, these flows are according to the actions performed and renewed by the created beings below. As the *Zohar* says: "Through an awakening from below, there is an awakening of the work above" <note>original Aramaic: "be-it'aruta de-letata it'ar ovda de-le'ila"</note>. $\square$ Thus, we find that this flow is a "great goodness" and an addition within the Emanation, beyond the flow that sustains the world and allows it to function normally. $\square$

Now, since you have seen the secret of these two "Unifications" within the Emanation—the first being for the world's existence and permanence, and the second being according to the deeds of those below—the eyes of your intellect shall be enlightened by the light of the Living God $\square$ regarding the secret of the "emptiness" that is found, as it were, in **Sovereignty**. $\square$ We say that the first Unification is the union of all the spheres; no emptiness, gap, or separation ever falls between them, Heaven forbid. Rather, Providence always rests upon them from the first sphere, **Crown**, to the last sphere, **Sovereignty**. All are equal in goodness, light, glory, and joy, for we exist in their light when they are full of one another. In their essence, they lack nothing, and they do not tire. For in the "River of God" there is neither lack nor excess, as explained in the *Guide for the Perplexed*. 

But regarding the second Unification—which is for the sake of governance according to the deeds performed and renewed by the created beings and the actions of those below—this flow is not for the essential existence of the world. It does not touch the essence of the Divine light in terms of His own perfect self, may He be blessed, for there is no perfection higher than His. The power of this flow stands in its place and its union, for He is "strength and joy in His place" <note>1 Chronicles 16:27</note>. He is perfect and does not need to receive perfection from any other. But for the sake of the created beings, the power of the flow is sometimes lacking according to their actions. In this context, "emptiness" is attributed to **Sovereignty**. For example, when Israel needs wealth but is not worthy of it, **Understanding** does not transmit wealth through **Might** to **Sovereignty**. Thus, **Sovereignty** is "empty," so to speak, of wealth. It is not that she is empty in herself, Heaven forbid, for she lacks no good; she is only "empty" in the sense that she did not receive that specific wealth needed for Israel. $\square$

Similarly, when Israel needs to take vengeance on their enemies and they are not worthy, she does not receive the **Might** and the power of victory to transmit to Israel. This applies to all things. The flow she was meant to receive was for the needs of Israel; but it is not, Heaven forbid, that there is an actual "emptiness" or lack in her, for in her core essence she is full of all good, and all the goodness of the Emanation required for her Divine status is in her hand. Thus far his words. $\square$

He also said there: "When there is no flow for the governance of the lower worlds—which comes from the awakening of the lower beings—then, as it were, they are all 'dry' of the additional flow. For the flow required for the lower worlds is only revealed through the awakening of the lower beings when they are worthy of it. This is the secret of the concept: 'Service is a Divine Need' <term>Tzorech Gavoah; literally 'A need for the High One'</term>. When the Presence [Shkhinah] transmits influence, it is a need for the inner realms, for they too receive a flow of goodness. When they have a place to transmit influence, their own flow increases. This is the secret of why the Presence 'pursues' the righteous person to be a 'chariot' for her, so that she may transmit through him; for she herself increases her flow through the act of giving. 

She is like a nursing woman; as long as the infant nurses, the milk increases. So too with the Presence: as long as she transmits, she reveals an additional flow. And so it is with the sphere above her: whenever it transmits to the world to reveal that flow, its own flow also increases from the Hidden Realm above it. $\square$ For everything is called 'Presence' up to **Understanding**, and even up to **Wisdom**, for they are the 'Hidden Wisdom' within **Understanding**. For **Sovereignty** is the 'Lower Mother' Presence, and she dwells over the worlds below her and hovers over the righteous who are a chariot for her to transmit through them. **Wisdom** dwells upon **Understanding**, and **Understanding** dwells upon the six extremities and **Sovereignty**. 

But do not let it enter your mind, Heaven forbid, that 'Service is a Divine Need' implies that the spheres themselves increase their flow for the sake of their own essence. We have already said that the flow required for the union of the essence of the spheres never lacks or diminishes; they are in a state of perfection beyond which there is no higher perfection. $\square$ Rather, the increased flow is for the sake of governing the worlds. The flow increases within the spheres so they can transmit in great abundance to the worlds—just like the milk that increases in the nursing woman is not for her own sake, but for the sake of the child. Similarly, the flow that increases in the spheres is for the sake of the worlds below them. The reason she 'pursues' the righteous person—even though the increase of flow is not for her own need—is because the 'cow wants to suckle even more than the calf wants to nurse' <note>Talmud, Pesachim 112a</note>. This is the secret of the nature of the Perfect One: because of His perfection, His nature is to bring perfection to others and to bestow His perfection upon others. Therefore, she pursues the righteous to complete others and to transmit to others through them. $\square$

This is the meaning of the 'Service of Piety' we mentioned. The spheres are in a perfection beyond which there is no higher perfection, and the nature of the Perfect is to bestow and bring perfection to another. Therefore, the Presence must be among the lower beings so that through her, the spheres—whose nature is to bestow because of their perfection—can transmit. Thus, the transmission is a 'need' for them to fulfill the nature of their perfection." Thus far his words. It is clear from his words that "Divine Need" means nothing more than "satisfaction" [Nachat Ruach] before Him, as it were, because His will to bestow goodness was carried out. $\square$

This leans somewhat toward the saying of the Sages: "Fortunate is the man who grew up in the Torah, whose labor is in the Torah, and who gives satisfaction to his Creator" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 17a</note>, because His will was done. This implies that the deeds of man are not a "need" for His essence or for any perfection of His, only that it is a "satisfaction to his Creator" to do His will.

**And then**, according to the verses and the holy writings which show that whether a man is righteous or wicked, it does not affect Him, may He be blessed—it only brings Him, as it were, "satisfaction" when His will is done, and the opposite for the opposite, Heaven forbid. However, in the book *Service of the Holy* [Avodat HaKodesh], in the introduction, he explains this phrase "gives satisfaction to his Creator" in a deeper way. These are his words: "The intention is more than what the observer assumes. 'Satisfaction' [Nachat] refers to the secret of the descent [Hanchatat] of the Will and the life-force of the Holy Creatures upon the upper 'heads,' and from there, there is 'satisfaction' and will for the Creator. All this comes through the fulfillment of the Torah and the Commandments for their own sake." Thus far his words.

The author of *Service of the Holy* consistently explains in many places throughout his book that Service is a "Divine Need" in a literal sense—affecting the very essence of the Emanation, adding strength, and repairing and unifying the Name. And the opposite for the opposite, Heaven forbid. This leans toward the opinion of the Rabbi, the Author <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note>. The truth is that in the simple sense of the verses and the sayings that hint at this matter of "Divine Need," they refer to a need within He Himself, may He be blessed. For example, it says "the joy was for the workers" and that He should "rejoice and delight in the children of blessing." Most verses and sayings indicate this, especially regarding the matter of the third Unification of the three Unifications in the spheres, where he wrote briefly that the spheres have a "power of fullness" and a "power of lack," as written in the *Garden of Pomegranates* [Pardes Rimonim], Gate 3, "The Gate of the Essence and Governance," which I have intended to copy here. And this is a matter that touches Him...

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of "Unifications" [Yichudim], transitioning from the mechanics of divine flow to a resolution of a theological problem: if there are Ten Sefirot, does the inclusion of the Shekhinah [Divine Presence] make eleven? # The Great Gate 35

And a difficulty was posed to me regarding what you were taught in the "Secret of the Shepherds" <note>original: *Raza de-Rozin*; likely referring to the *Ra'aya Meheimna* or "Faithful Shepherd" section of the Zohar</note> which are hidden matters concerning the "Four Higher Secrets" <note>likely referring to the four letters of the Tetragrammaton</note>, the **Shekhinah** [Divine Presence], and the Holy **Matronita** [The Queen/Lady]. For if this is so, it would imply eleven divine emanations. Yet the "Master of the Book of Formation" <note>The author of *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note> stated: "Ten and not nine, ten and not eleven."

Therefore, you must know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the entire Heavenly Academy sent me to you to teach you the secret and the truth of the matter. You should know that the Four Higher Secrets were illuminated by the light of your study of the **Infinite** [*Ein Sof*], which struck and produced eight lights, encompassing three lights, and so on, until the "Eighteen Higher Secrets" were completed. Afterward, each one of them struck and produced eight lights in the manner of a "vessel" [nartika] like this "fist" <note>original: *komtza*; a measurement or a closed hand, often used as a metaphor for a vessel that contains light</note> which is a single unity with Him.

These ten lights that shine from the "Higher Secrets" are all included together, and that is the Great **Shekhinah**, who bestows the influence of the Ten Higher Sefirot to sustain the world. Her perfection is with the Ten Higher Sefirot, for she emerged through their "striking" <note>the mystical process of *Bitsh* or "striking," where divine lights interact to produce new emanations</note>. Because it was possible for one to think to count her separately and say there are eleven "Spheres" [*Sefirot*], the author of the *Book of Formation* taught you that this is not so. She is not like the higher Sefirot themselves, which are assigned power from the Infinite. Rather, the **Shekhinah** is a vessel for all of them; she emerged from all of them. Each of the Ten Higher Sefirot shone a single light, and she was the completion of all of them. Therefore, she is with them in "Unity" [Achdut] and not in "Emanation" [Atzilut] <note>meaning she is the vessel/manifestation of the unity of the ten, rather than an eleventh distinct source</note>.

All merits and sins depend upon her, to unite the Ten Higher Sefirot within her. They shine in her, and she is the one through whom the "Blessing of the King of the Universe" flows. Therein depend all positive and negative commandments—all to unite her with the Ten Sefirot. Just as she emerged from all of them, so must one unite her with all the Sefirot, and to align her ten "internal" Sefirot to correspond to the ten "Higher" Sefirot. When they are aligned as one, there is perfection and being in all the worlds. This is the meaning of "God said: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" (Genesis 1:26). This "God" [*Elohim*]—which is the sphere of **Understanding** [Binah]—said to the other Sefirot: "Let us make man," meaning each of us shall "strike" and produce one light, so that in the integration of all these ten lights, there shall be "Man" [Adam]. This is the **Matronita**, for the female is also called "Man." As it says: "To make man dwell in a house"—and who is the inhabitant of the house? It is the woman.

Therefore, this "Man" is "in our image," meaning she shall be the vessel [nartika] for each of us. "After our likeness" means she resembles us, being comprised of ten lights just as we are. The reason **Understanding** [Binah] said this is because the higher ones are included within her, and she decrees and fulfills through their word. You should not ask why she said this at that specific time and not before, for you have already asked "what is before and what is after," and like a flame to a coal, "do not seek what is hidden from you." 

From here we understand the secret of the "two-faced" being <note>original: *du-partzufin*; the Talmudic idea that the first man was created with two faces, male and female, back-to-back</note>. The light produced by each Sefirah was contained within it and was not yet "outside" until **Understanding** said "Let us make man." At that moment, they were united, and those lights were integrated, and this "Man" was made. And what the sages meant by "the back of the living creatures" refers to this light appearing as each individual Sefirah. But when **Understanding** said "Let us make man," those lights integrated and this "Man" was made, who is the "Female" counterpart aligned with all the "Male" limbs. When they are joined in a single union, and the ten Sefirot of the **Matronita** are aligned one-to-one with the ten Higher Sefirot, this is the joy, peace, and unity of all the worlds.

This is the secret of the "Unification" [*Yichud*] that we seek to effect. And this is the secret of taking the woman from the side of the man, as it says: "And the Lord God built the side" (Genesis 2:22). Just as the **Matronita** emerged from the "striking" of the Ten Higher Sefirot—which is the "Male" world—you can see how it is exactly like the Divine. The Infinite [Ein Sof] brought forth the Ten Higher Sefirot, and the Ten Higher Sefirot brought forth the **Shekhinah**, and all is one unity. So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, concerning the creation of man: "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7), which is a hint to the Infinite. That "breath of life" became the body of man, which is in the likeness of the Ten Higher Sefirot. And from the "side" [rib] of man, the female was created—a hint to the **Matronita** who was created from the lights of the Sefirot. As we said, each Sefirah shone a light into her that acts as a vessel for it. She is united with that vessel, and that vessel is perfectly united with her. All these ten lights were integrated and became one, and that is the **Shekhinah**, who is in the likeness of the female who receives. She was made from the "speech" of all the male limbs hidden within her. Likewise, the **Shekhinah** leads and distributes sustenance to all, for she receives from all the higher Sefirot and is made from them, distributing nourishment to the worlds. This is the secret and the truth of the matter that the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Academy sent to inform you. Until here are his words.

It is thus clear from his words that "flaws" and "obligations" only occur within the **Shekhinah** and the **Matronita**. Regarding her, Rabbi Nachman hinted <note>possibly referring to a specific Kabbalist or a misreading of a name in the manuscript</note> that "she is with them in unity and not in emanation." In the book *Yoshev Nevokhu* <note>The Settler of the Perplexed</note>, he explains his words. However, according to the explanation of the "Messenger" [Maggid], it is well explained that the **Shekhinah/Matronita** is with the ten higher Sefirot in a single unity, "like a fist whose garment is of itself." She is not with them in "Emanation" [Atzilut] because the ten higher Sefirot are like the Infinite, like "a flame bound to a coal." Concerning the **Shekhinah/Matronita** and the ten higher Sefirot, it is said: "If you are righteous, what do you give Him? If your sins are many, what do you do to Him?" (Job 35:6-7). 

According to what is understood from the words of the Maggid, his intention is that everything said regarding the "Unification of the Name" and the "Coupling of Beauty and Sovereignty" [*Zivug Tiferet u-Malchut*]—and many such matters—all of it refers to the illumination of the "vessels" of the pious ones mentioned. This is similar to what the book *Pardes Rimonim* <note>Orchard of Pomegranates, by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> wrote in the Gate of Essence and Conduct, Chapter 16. Also, concerning Ezekiel when he said "And I fell upon my face," he reached only until the latter stage. But never did he, nor any prophet in the world, perceive the "Emanation" [*Atzilut*] itself. Ezekiel perceived through his imagination the "Seal of Wickedness" <note>likely a reference to the shells/clippot or the lower worlds</note> and perceived this in the world of **Formation** [*Yetzirah*]. So it is written in the Gate of the Four Worlds [ABYA]. In the Gate of Palaces [Heikhalot], Chapter 2, it says: "Now it is proper to know that there is no place for prophets to draw from the Sefirot themselves, for no foot may ascend there in any way." 

Even for Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, the distinction between him and other prophets was that Moses prophesied from within the "Palace of Will," which is the sixth palace, while the rest of the prophets prophesied from the "Palace of Radiance" [*Nogah*], which is the third palace. Daniel and those who spoke through the Holy Spirit [Ruach HaKodesh] in visions and dreams look into this second palace where we are. The conclusion is this: when Moses prophesied from the Palace of Will through the union of **Beauty** [*Tiferet*] and **Sovereignty** [*Malchut*] revealed in that palace, his prophecy was from a "clear mirror" [*aspeklariya hametzachtzachat*], for he required no intermediary between himself and the palace to view the matters of prophecy. Therefore, it was "in a vision and not in riddles" (Numbers 12:8). But the rest of the prophets viewed the reflection of these Sefirot in the third palace.

### Thus
<margin>Thus</margin> I say, the intent of the Maggid is that everything said regarding the Unification of the Name refers to this "vessel" and "garment" which is the aforementioned **Shekhinah** and **Matronita**, who shines from her glory into the Throne. She is the "spark" from the Ten Higher Sefirot. The secret of the "Exile of the Shekhinah" is when this spark extends down into **Metatron** <note>the highest angel, ruler of the lower worlds</note>. What the sages said, "The Name is Peace and the Throne is Peace," means "The Name is Peace" refers to this spark called **Shekhinah/Matronita**, and "The Throne" is the World of **Creation** [*Beriyah*], for the "Name" is the soul of the "Throne." I will not elaborate further on this inquiry, for I have already been lengthy enough.

### Whatever happens
<margin>Whatever happens</margin> from everything mentioned until now, let it be as it may; in any case, it is known in truth that man, through the choice of his deeds, touches the highest of heights. In divine service, there is a "Higher Need" <note>the concept that human actions "affect" God, so to speak</note>. This is the goal of the servant: to do everything for the sake of His Name, to give "satisfaction to his Creator," not for his own need or to receive a reward, but for the sake of His Name in love. Ultimately, honor will come. For when the flow of influence increases above through the power of the servant's awakening, it then descends below, and there is peace in all.

### And then
<margin>And then</margin> man, through the Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments, is bound to the Holy One, Blessed be He. This fully explains the statement of the Zohar: "Three are bound together: The Holy One, Blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel," as was mentioned in the introduction.

## In the name of the Lord, this is the book "The Generations of Adam"
Blessed be the Lord who has helped me thus far. Many matters and great subjects have unfolded, through which the deeds of man are clarified—both in his form and in the likeness of his soul and body. Just as his Torah and his creation are clarified, the matter of the "garments of light" and the "garments of skin" <note>referring to the state of Adam before and after the fall</note> are explained, and his extremes—the "open eye," the great light from the "hidden light," and the matter of the true light. This will be revealed and ascended in the secret of "On that day the Lord shall be one" (Zechariah 14:9). All of this comes from the awakening of man, who has the power through his choice to awaken the Higher One. "Everything is foreseen, yet permission is given" (Ethics of the Fathers 3:15). Then the purpose of man in creation, the World to Come, and eternity will be realized. For the matter of the serpent—who pulled man through his sin toward evil—will end and turn to good. Then it will be a "world that is entirely good." All these things are clarified in this introduction, which is called by the name **Toldot Adam** [The Generations of Man], because it mentions every event and purpose of man.

To seal this introduction of the "Great House," I have seen fit to bring one creative act in which all the aforementioned matters are hinted at upon deep reflection. It is found in the Talmud, Tractate Shabbat, the chapter "He who builds" [Ha-Boneh]. This is the text: "And you shall write them"—that they should be written in a specific way:

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Four Higher Secrets" and the nature of the Ten Sefirot, specifically addressing the paradox of how the divine unity interacts with the lower, fragmented worlds. # The Great Gate

In order for **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note> and **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note> to be crowned, it is impossible for them to be enriched by those praiseworthy attributes and the lights of the Sefirot except through the unification of **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note> and **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>. This was also explained by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, may his memory be a blessing, in the *Zohar*...
<margin>We find that the matter of their union is not for their own sake, but for the needs of the "Building" <note>the lower structure of the divine attributes</note>. The root of this Building is **Understanding**, and from this root, it spreads to the five lower attributes. However, regarding the essence of **Understanding** and above, one does not occupy oneself with those hidden things. Not only is there no direct action upon humans there, but even in the *Pardes* <note>Rabbi Moses Cordovero's *Pardes Rimonim*</note>, in the section on the "Gate of Constellations," it says that the touch of the intellect to grasp anything from there is wonderous and concealed. Thus, everything is explained well. The "Ten Constellations" and the "Five Constellations" relate to the "Virtues" and **Kingship**.</margin>
**Furthermore**, see, I must inform you that even below in the "World of Emanation" <note>Atzilut</note>, regarding the structure of the "Shearing" <note>Gidul/Giluach; likely referring to the development of divine configurations</note>, it does not relate to the "Virtues."
Regarding the **Exile of the Shekhinah**: it is not the actual **Shekhinah** <note>the Divine Presence</note> itself, but a spark from her. As the *Pardes* says in the section on the "Gate of the Alphabet": This angel is called by two names. Sometimes he is called **Metatron** and sometimes **Mitatron** with the letter *Yod*. The intention is that when the angel is "clothed" in the Shekhinah, and the Shekhinah is hidden within him and shows her actions through him, he is then called **Mitatron** with a *Yod*. This is a hint to the **Shekhinah** being comprised of ten <note>the numerical value of the letter Yod is 10</note>, as she is hidden and concealed within him. It is not the actual Shekhinah, but a spark and the light that emanates from the Shekhinah. It is a spark of light comprised of ten sparks. Figuratively, this matter is called the "Exile of the Shekhinah." This was explained in the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei HaZohar</note>. To comfort us, it is written: "I am the Lord, that is my name, and my glory I will not give to another." <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>. It is already known from the preface of the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>Ra'aya Meheimna</note> that the entire secret of the "Exile" is only the Shekhinah of the "World of Creation" <note>Beriah</note>, meaning a single spark that shines from her into Creation. For regarding the Shekhinah of the "World of Emanation," it is written: "I am the Lord... and my glory I will not give to another."

## For the Completion of this Matter
I shall transcribe the words of the **Maggid** <note>a heavenly messenger or mentor</note> who appeared to the Great Rabbi, the Pious and Holy, and we were privileged to see his manuscripts. I will transcribe here what pertains to this matter; this is the text:

"Have you not heard, God of the World, the Lord? You must know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the entire Heavenly Academy and the 'Fine Ones' <note>subtle spiritual beings</note> send you peace. I was sent to you to inform you of high matters and the secret of secrets, so that you may know the great goodness of the Holy One, Blessed be He, His mercy and His kindness, and to understand His holy service.

I know that you find it very difficult regarding the holy Sefirot and the matter of **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>—how she is unified with the Sefirot. For in some places it appears otherwise. <note>original Aramaic: *דקשיא לך טובא* - it is very difficult for you</note>. And regarding the Priest <note>Chesed</note>... in many places it seems as if it were a sponge-like vessel. May the Merciful Master forgive him <note>likely referring to the author of the *Minchat Yehuda*</note> for saying that, for he did not intend to sin before God, but it is an utter mistake.

Furthermore, it is difficult because in some places we say she is the 'Daughter of Abraham' <note>associated with Chesed/Mercy</note>, and in others the 'Daughter of Understanding' <note>Binah</note>, and in others the 'Daughter of Power' <note>Gevurah/Judgment</note>. Furthermore, it seems as if there is change within the Sefirot, God forbid, as it says: 'He rose from the Throne of Judgment and sat on the Throne of Mercy.' One might think they are not the Divine Essence itself, God forbid! Furthermore, it says in many places that because of sin, the defect reaches the Shekhinah and the Sefirot, while in others it says nothing of the sins of man reaches the Holy One and His Shekhinah.

Now, as you see the 'Living Creatures' <note>Chayot; high angels</note> in the holy arrangement, we shall inform you of the truth. The secret is that the entire desire of the **Ancient of Ancients** <note>Atik Yomin; the highest aspect of divinity</note>, the Infinite [*Ein Sof*], was to create the worlds. He struck a light from Himself... and it comprised three. As the Rabbis said, a 'Point' comprises three: length, width, and depth. This light is one but comprises three: **Wisdom**, **Understanding**, and... <note>original: *ד'* - likely referring to the fourth attribute or the Tetragrammaton</note>.

When this 'Point' struck, a light emerged from it... which comprised **Kindness** <note>Chesed</note> and **Victory** <note>Netzach</note>, and with **Wisdom** itself, they are three. Then another light emerged... comprising **Power** <note>Gevurah</note> and **Glory** <note>Hod</note>, and with **Understanding** itself, they are three. Afterward, a single light emerged comprising **Beauty** <note>Tiferet</note>, **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>, and **Kingship** <note>Malchut</note>.

Because **Crown** <note>Keter</note>, **Wisdom**, and **Understanding** were one light, and **Kingship** emerged from **Crown**, while **Abraham** <note>Chesed</note> emerged from **Wisdom**, it is as if they both emerged from one place. This is why it says of Abraham: 'And yet indeed she is my sister; she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother.' <note>Genesis 20:12</note>. This means: I and she are drawn from the Higher Father <note>Keter/Chokhmah</note>. And why is she called the 'Daughter of Understanding'? Because **Understanding** is included in the **Crown**, when **Kingship** emerged from the **Crown**, it was as if she emerged from **Understanding**. And because **Power** is the fourth attribute and **Kingship** is the fourth attribute, she is said to suckle from it.

Each of these higher Sefirot is comprised of all ten. Since they were all included in the **Infinite**, when He brought out the first light, all ten were included in that light. Just as in a human, all the powers are included in him. Thus, these Sefirot rise to a hundred, and from a hundred to a million, for there is no number or limit. All of these are a single light, and they are the Divine Essence itself, for they are like 'a flame bound to a coal.' They are like the soul in the body; the parts are all one, a perfect unity without any side of separation in the world, God forbid. **Kingship** and the other Sefirot are all one in perfect unity with the **Infinite**.

From that point onward begins the 'World of Separation.' This means that the worlds all depend on the word of the Holy One, but they are not His essence. Between the 'World of Perfect Unity' and the 'World of Absolute Separation' exists a world that has a 'Side of Unity' <note>resembling the divine</note> and a 'Side of Separation' <note>acting as a garment/vessel</note>. This is called a 'Vessel' for the ten higher Sefirot... it is called **Metatron**, in whom all the Sefirot are included. This is where Elisha 'the Other' <note>the famous apostate Acher</note> erred, thinking there were 'Two Authorities,' God forbid, because he saw that Metatron governs the world of separated beings.

There, the secret of 'Other Gods' exists <note>the forces of evil/husks</note>... it is the mystery of the 'Slanting Serpent' <note>Nachash Bariach</note> that chooses to separate him from the World of Unity. Sins reach there, to separate the World of Unity from him. But in the Higher Attributes, there is no defect, God forbid, as it says: 'If you are righteous, what do you give Him? If your transgressions are many, what do you do to Him?' <note>Job 35:6-7</note>.

From there, it is divided into the 'Four Camps of the Shekhinah.' Between that world and the Four Camps is the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**. This is the secret of the 'Dragon' <note>Teli</note> whose head is good and whose tail is evil. There was the sin of Adam, who mixed good with evil. But the Higher Secrets are the Divine Essence itself, a perfect unity, and there is no change there at all; it is only that according to what a man does, so it is measured out to him."

Afterward, the **Maggid** came a second time and said to him: "The Lord be with you in all that you do. I have come to see your face... regarding what I taught you about the world between Unity and Separation. That world is the **Shekhinah**. She is unified with the Higher Sefirot. She is comprised of seven to correspond to the seven higher ones... and these seven are seven levels. The three higher ones are also included in her in a hidden and concealed way. It is all a single unity. God forbid that one should suggest any separation there! Whoever thinks so is 'Cutting the Shoots' <note>Katzitz be-Netiot - committing heresy by separating divine attributes</note>.

Whoever separates her from the Ten Higher Sefirot, his punishment is great. I only said there is a 'Side of Separation' because she bestows influence upon **Metatron**, who is the 'World of Separation,' and from him all the worlds are nourished. But she herself is in perfect unity. This is the secret of the Unification we perform: to unify the **Shekhinah** with the **Holy One, Blessed be He**."

Afterward, the **Maggid** came a third time and spoke of this difficult vision...

# The Great Gate

Regarding the difficulty you had concerning what I taught you in the secret of the "Thought of the Thoughts of the Hidden Ancient Ones," <note>original: *r’iyu d’atiqin*</note> who are like the **Higher Four**, the **Divine Presence** <note>Shekhinah</note> and the **Holy Matron** <note>Matronita; the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>: if this were so, the text should have said "eleven." But the "Master of Formation" <note>the author of *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient foundational Kabbalistic text</note> said: "Ten, and not nine; ten, and not eleven." 

I have come to make you understand that the **Holy One, blessed be He**, and the entire **Heavenly Academy** <note>original: *metivta ila’ah*</note> have begun to trouble themselves to teach you the secret and the truth of the matter. You must know that the **Higher Four** were illuminated from the **Infinite** <note>Ein Sof</note> in a particular way. I taught you that the Infinite struck a spark and brought forth one light that included all its lights, and thus the **Ten Higher Sefirot** <note>the ten divine attributes or emanations</note> were completed. Afterward, each one prepared the Ten Higher Sefirot, struck out, and brought forth a single light like a "casing" <note>original: *nartaka*</note> or like the "clinching of a fist." This light is a single unity with Him. All these ten lights that shine from the Higher Four were included together, and this is the **Great Shekhinah**, who overflows from the Ten Higher Sefirot to nourish all the worlds. She is the perfection with the Ten Higher Sefirot, for she emerged through their "striking" <note>the interaction of divine lights</note>.

Because it might occur to one's mind to count her separately and say there are eleven Sefirot, the author of the *Book of Formation* taught you that there are only ten. She is similar to the higher Sefirot. For if you count **Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding** <note>Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah</note>, they emerge from the Infinite. **Kindness and Understanding** emerge from **Wisdom**, and **Strength and Glory** from **Understanding**, and **Beauty, Foundation, and Kingship** from the **Crown**. But the **Shekhinah** is the vessel for all of them; she emerged from all of them. Each one of the Higher Four shines a single light, and she is included in all of them. Therefore, "she is with them in their 'back' <note>their external or lower aspect</note> and not in their 'Emanation' <note>Atzilut; the highest divine realm</note>." 

All merits and liabilities depend on her, to unify the lower world with the higher days so that there will be mercy within her. This is the secret of the phrase "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever" <note>original: *Baruch Shem Kavod Malkhuto L’olam Va’ed*</note>. Therein hang all the **positive and negative commandments**, all for the sake of unifying her with the entire Ten Sefirot. Just as she emerged from all of them, so must one unify her with all of them, and direct her ten internal Sefirot to correspond to the Ten Higher Sefirot. When they are aligned as one, there is perfection and Torah in all the worlds.

This is the meaning of "And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" (Genesis 1:26). This "God" <note>Elohim</note>—which is **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>—said to the Ten Higher Sefirot: "Let us make man." That is to say: let each one of us strike and bring forth a single light so that through the inclusion of all ten lights, there shall be "Man." This refers to the **Matron**, for the female is also called "Man" <note>Adam</note>. As it is written, "The beauty of a man is to dwell in a house" (Isaiah 44:13)—and who is it that dwells in the house? It is the wife. And let this "Man" be "in our image"—meaning she shall be the casing for each one of us—and "after our likeness"—meaning she shall be similar to us, comprised of ten Sefirot just like us. 

The reason **Understanding** said this is because it includes the two higher ones within it, and it decrees and fulfills according to their word. You should not wonder why it was said at that moment and not before, for "you may ask concerning the days that are past" (Deuteronomy 4:32), but "that which is too wondrous for you, do not seek" <note>A quote from Ben Sira, often cited in the Talmud regarding the limits of mystical inquiry</note>.

From here you can hear the secret of the debate: "Was [Eve] a face or was she a tail?" <note>Refers to a Talmudic debate in Berakhot 61a about whether the first human was created with two faces and split, or if woman was created from a tail-like appendage</note>. One who says "they were two faces" means that the light brought forth from each Sefirah was already included in the male and did not return to be prepared afterward until **Understanding** said "Let us make man." At that moment, those lights shone and were included as a single light, and this "Man" was made. One who says "she was a tail" means that this light was initially attached to each and every Sefirah. When **Understanding** said "Let us make man," those lights were gathered and this "Man" was made, who is the "Likeness of the Female," aligned against all the "limbs of the Male." When they are joined in a single union, and the ten Sefirot of the Matron are unified with the Ten Higher Sefirot, one aligned against the other, that is the secret of **Total Perfection** and the beauty of all worlds. This is the secret of the union we seek to achieve constantly. 

This is also the secret of "He took a woman from his side" as it is written: "And the Lord God built the side" (Genesis 2:22). For the Matron emerged from the "striking" of all the higher sources, which is the "World of the Male." 

Come and see: this female <note>the Shekhinah</note> follows the pattern of the male. Just as the Infinite brought forth the Ten Higher Sefirot, and the Ten Higher Sefirot brought forth the Shekhinah—and all is a single unity—so too did the Holy One, blessed be He, act in the creation of Man. As it is written: "And He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7), which refers to the **Infinite**. From that breath of life, the body of Man was unified, which is the secret of the likeness of the Ten Sefirot. And from the body of Man, the female was created—a hint to the Matron who was created from the light of the Sefirot. 

As we said, every Sefirah shone into her a single light which serves as her casing. She is unified from that casing, and through that union, there is a unified perfection. All those ten lights were included and became one, and that is the **Shekhinah**. She is the "Likeness of the Female" who receives and becomes pregnant from the Male; all his "limbs" <note>divine attributes</note> shine within her. Just as in the way of the world, she receives and then distributes nourishment to all, so the Matron receives from all the higher Sefirot, is "impregnated" by them, and divides nourishment to all the worlds. This is the secret and the truth of the matter that the Holy One and His Academy sent to inform you. Until here are his words.

It is clear from his words that the matter of "Wisdom and the Ten" <note>the structures of the Sefirot</note> refers only to the **Shekhinah-Matron**. **Nahmanides** <note>Ramban</note> alluded to this when he said "she is with them in their back and not in the Emanation." Many were confused by his words. However, according to the explanation of the **Maggid**, it is clearly explained: the Shekhinah-Matron is with the Ten Higher Sefirot as a "back" <note>a reflection or outer layer</note>, like the "clinching of a fist" <note>a condensed form</note> of the garment that comes from it. She is not with them in the Emanation, for the Ten Higher Sefirot are from the Infinite and are "as a flame is bound to a coal." 

If the Shekhinah-Matron is ten Sefirot within ten worlds, like a "clinching of a fist," what can you give to its magnitude? <note>How can a human grasp its greatness?</note> Let it be as understood from the words of the Maggid. His intention is that everything said regarding the "Unification of the Name" and the "Coupling of Beauty and Kingship" <note>the union of Tiferet and Malchut</note> and many similar matters, all of it is in the aspect of their illumination as a "casing" for their essences, as mentioned. 

This is like what was written in the *Pardes* <note>Rabbi Moses Cordovero's *Pardes Rimonim*</note> in the "Gate of Essence and Conduct," Chapter 15: Ezekiel said, "I fell upon my face" (Ezekiel 1:28) because he reached as far as the **Crown** <note>Keter</note>. But never did he, nor any prophet in the world, perceive the **Emanation** <note>Atzilut</note> itself. Ezekiel perceived through forms in the "Seal of Action" <note>Asiyah</note> and he perceived this in "Formation" <note>Yetzirah</note>. So it is written in the "Gate of the Four Worlds" <note>ABY"A: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah</note>. 

In the "Gate of the Palaces" <note>Heikhalot</note>, Chapter 2: "Now it is proper to know that the source of the prophets' sustenance is not in the Sefirot themselves, for the Sefirot are not a revealed thing in any way in the world, even to **Moses our Teacher** <note>original: *Mar’eh*</note>. However, the difference between Moses and other prophets is that Moses would prophesy from within the **Palace of Will**, which is the sixth palace, while the rest of the prophets prophesied from the **Palace of Radiance** <note>Nogah</note>, which is the third palace. Daniel and his companions, who spoke through the Holy Spirit in visions and dreams, looked into this second palace where we are." This means that when Moses prophesied from the Palace of Will, it was through the union of **Beauty and Kingship** revealed in that palace. His prophecy was from a "clear mirror" because he did not need an intermediary between him and the palace to view matters of prophecy. Therefore, he was "mouth to mouth" and not in riddles. But the rest of the prophets perceived the union of these Sefirot in the third palace, and those who spoke by the Holy Spirit perceived them in the second palace. And so on.

<insert>
**Thus** do I say: the Maggid's intention is that everything said about the unification of the Name refers to the light facing the Union, which is the **Shekhinah** and the **Matron** mentioned above. She shines from her glory into the **Throne** <note>the Throne of Glory</note>. She is the spark from the Ten Higher Sefirot. The secret of the "Exile of the Shekhinah" occurs when this spark spreads all the way into **Metatron** <note>the highest angel and heavenly scribe</note>. When the Sages said "the Name is whole and the Throne is whole," the "Name is whole" refers to the secret of this spark called the Shekhinah-Matron, and the "Throne" is the **World of Creation** <note>Beriah</note>, for the Name is the soul of the Throne. There is no need to expand further on this inquiry. Be careful with it and explain according to what I have said thus far.
</insert>

**Regardless** of all that has been mentioned, however it may be, it is known in truth that man, through the choice of his actions, touches the highest of heights in the celestial heights. There is a "High Need" <note>original: *tzorech gavo’ah*</note> in divine service. This is the ultimate purpose of the servant: to do everything for His Name's sake, to give "satisfaction to his Creator," not for his own sake to receive a reward, but for the sake of His Name in love. Ultimately, honor will come, for when the flow of abundance is increased above through the power of the servant's awakening, it then descends below, and there is peace in all.

**And then** man, through the medium of the Torah and the fulfillment of its commandments, is bound to the **Holy One, blessed be He**. This perfectly explains the statement in the *Zohar*: "Three are bound together: the Holy One, the Torah, and Israel." And so the introduction begins:

---

**In the name of the Lord, this is the book of the generations of man.** <note>Genesis 5:1</note> **My inquiries until now have evolved into many things and great matters. Through these words, it is made clear what the work of man is, both in his image and in the likeness of his soul and body. Just as his Torah is, so is his formation.** The matter of the "Light" and "Skin" <note>a pun on the Hebrew words *Or* (light) and *Or* (skin), which sound the same but are spelled with an Aleph and an Ayin</note> is explained: what was made into garments of *skin* in the past will in the future be a "watchful eye," a great light from the **Hidden Light**. This is the matter of the True Light, His light which is hidden for the future. May He be exalted and His name sanctified in the secret of "On that day the Lord shall be one" (Zechariah 14:9). All of this is through the awakening of man, in whose hand is the power—by virtue of his choice—to awaken the Higher One. All is foreseen, and new things are brought into being.

**These are the ultimate purposes of man in creation, and the matter of the Holy One and eternity.** For the entire matter of the "impurity of the serpent"—which man drew upon himself through his sin—is to be transformed into good. Then, it will be a "world that is entirely good." All these inquiries are explained in this precious introduction, which is called by the name **Generations of Man**, because all the entanglements, events, and purposes of man are mentioned in it. For the beginning of this introduction, "The Great House," I have seen fit to bring one creation in which all the aforementioned matters are hinted at after good reflection. It is in Tractate Shabbat, the chapter "One who builds" <note>Shabbat 103a</note>: This is the version: "And you shall write them"—a simple writing, so that he does not write **Alephs** as **Ayins**, **Ayins** as **Alephs**, **Gimels** as **Tzadis**, **Tzadis** as **Gimels**, **Bets** as **Kafs**, **Kafs** as **Bets**, **Dalets** as **Reshs**, **Reshs** as **Dalets**, **Hehs** as **Chets**, **Chets** as **Hehs**, **Vavs** as **Yods**, **Yods** as **Vavs**, **Zayins** as **Nuns**, **Nuns** as **Zayins**, **Tets** as **Pes**, **Pes** as **Tets**, **Bent** letters as **Straight** letters, **Straight** letters as **Bent**...

It also outlines the hierarchy of prophecy and emphasizes that human actions have a direct impact on the divine realm, concluding with the mystical significance of the Hebrew alphabet.</summary>

-># The Gate of Illumination<-
<meta>catchword: which is difficult</meta>

<margin>
Regarding **Understanding** <note>Hebrew: *Binah*, the third Sefirah</note>:
Above this level, there is no involvement in those hidden matters. Not only is there no impact from the deeds of human beings, but even the reach of the intellect to grasp anything from there is wondrous and concealed. Thus, everything is clearly explained.
</margin>

In order for **Beauty** <note>*Tiferet*</note> and **Kingdom** <note>*Malkhut*</note> to be crowned so they may be unified, it is impossible for them to be crowned with those "thickened" crowns—the **Kindnesses** <note>*Chasadim*</note> and the armaments of the Sefirot—except through the union of **Wisdom** <note>*Chochmah*</note> and **Understanding** <note>*Binah*</note>. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (may peace be upon him) explained this in the *Zohar*, and so on. We find, therefore, that the purpose of their union was not for their own sake, but for the needs of the "Building" <note>the structure of the lower six Sefirot</note>, as it is known that the root of the Building is within **Understanding**.

<margin>
*SG"ST* <note>Likely a scholarly abbreviation or reference code</note>
See the *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note>, Gate 50, concerning the inner gate. For there are [numerical values] for the letter *Heh* (5) from the waters of the Lord, and *Malkhut* is the letter *Yod* (10)... [the text here notes mystical letter permutations relating to divine names].
</margin>

**Furthermore**, I must inform you that even below in the world of **Emanation** <note>*Atzilut*, the highest of the four worlds</note>, regarding the "Building" and the manifestations of the **Divine Presence** <note>*Shekhinah*</note>, it is not the actual *Shekhinah* herself that is revealed, but rather a spark of her. These are the words of the *Pardes*, Gate 4, from the Gate of the Four Worlds: "This angel is called by two names; sometimes he is called **Metatron** and sometimes he is called **Mistron** <note>A name hinting at *Misterion* or mystery/hiddenness</note> with the letter *Yod*. The explanation is that when the angel is clothed in the *Shekhinah*, and the *Shekhinah* is hidden within him and shows her actions through him, he is then called Mistron with a *Yod*. This is an allusion to the *Shekhinah*, who is comprised of the ten [represented by the letter *Yod* which equals ten], and she is hidden and concealed within him. It is not the actual *Shekhinah*, but a spark and the light that emanates from her. It is a spark and a light comprised of seven sparks, and, as it were, this matter is called the 'Exile of the *Shekhinah*.' This is explained in the *Tikunim* <note>*Tikunei Zohar*</note>, see there." And regarding the verse "He has cast down from heaven to earth the beauty of Israel," you already know the introduction from the *Faithful Shepherd* <note>*Ra’aya Meheimna*, a section of the Zohar</note> that the entire secret of the exile—when we speak of "exile"—refers only to the *Shekhinah* of the World of **Creation** <note>*Beriah*</note>. That is to say, a single spark that sparkles from her into the World of Creation. For regarding the *Shekhinah* of the World of Emanation, it is written: "I am the Lord, that is My name, and My glory I will not give to another." End of quote.

**To complete this matter**, I shall transcribe some of the words of the **Maggid** <note>A celestial mentor or "preacher" from the world of spirits</note> who appeared to the great Rabbi, the author of the *Beit Yosef* <note>Joseph Karo, 1488–1575</note>. We have been privileged to see these notebooks, and I will transcribe what pertains to this matter. This is the wording: 

"Is it not known if the God of the world, the Lord, has not heard? You should know that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the entire Heavenly Academy send you peace. They have sent me to you to inform you of high matters and the secrets of secrets. Why should I not send you what I have said to you—that the Lord is Merciful, and His mercies and kindnesses are great, and His right hand is outstretched to receive those who return to the holy service? I know that it was very difficult for you regarding the matter of the **Holy Sefirot**; specifically regarding **Kingdom** <note>*Malkhut*</note>, how she is unified with the Sefirot and pierces through the place of the 'Eighth Site' <note>A cryptic reference to the transition between divine unity and the lower worlds</note>... [the Maggid addresses scholarly disputes regarding the *Minchat Yehuda*]. May the Merciful Master forgive him for placing us in that mindset... he shall not be punished for that word he spoke, for he did not intend to diminish the Holy One. But it is a complete error. 

Furthermore, it was difficult for you regarding what is written in the tradition of Hezekiah: we say she is the 'daughter of Abraham,' yet in some places we say she is the 'daughter of Understanding' <note>*Binah*</note>, and in others the 'daughter of Strength' <note>*Gevurah*</note>. Furthermore, it was difficult that there seems to be change within these Sefirot, as when it says 'He rose from the Throne of Judgment and sat on the Throne of Mercy,' until one might mistakenly say they are not the Divine Essence itself, Heaven forbid! Furthermore, it was difficult that in many places the Sages said that sin reaches the *Shekhinah* and the Sefirot, yet in other places they say nothing of man's sins reaches the Holy One and His *Shekhinah*. 

When you looked into the Holy *Tikunim*, we prepared for you the truth of the matter and the secret of secrets: You must know that every ascent above reaches the place of the 'Ancient of Ancients,' the **Infinite** <note>*Ein Sof*</note>. To bring the worlds into existence, He struck a single blow, and a single light shone forth which included three. In this light is the secret of a single point, which includes three: length, breadth, and depth. This is a single white light, and included within it are three: **Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge** <note>*Chochmah, Binah, Da'at*</note>. Afterward, each of these three struck out a light from itself. The Wisdom struck one light which included two: **Kindness and Victory** <note>*Chesed and Netzach*</note>, and with Wisdom itself, they were three. Likewise, Understanding struck one light including two: **Strength and Splendor** <note>*Gevurah and Hod*</note>, and with itself, they were three. Afterward, a light was struck from it including three: **Beauty, Foundation, and Kingdom** <note>*Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut*</note>. 

And because [Kingdom] is close to the mouth of the Infinite and is very hidden, she brings forth three inclusions in the manner of the Infinite. Now, because **Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding** <note>*Keter, Chochmah, Binah*</note> were one light, and Kingdom emerged from Crown, and Abraham from Wisdom... that is why it is said of Abraham: 'And yet indeed she is my sister; she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother.' This means: I and she are drawn from the **Higher Crown**, and He is the Father. And why is she called the 'daughter of Understanding'? Because since Understanding is included in the Crown, and the Crown brings forth Kingdom, it appears as if she emerged from Understanding. And as for the 'daughter of Strength,' since the attribute of Mercy <note>*Midat ha-Rachamim*</note> emerges from it, they say she emerged from it. 

Each of these higher Sefirot includes all ten. Since they were all included in the Infinite, when the first light was brought forth, all ten were included in that light in the likeness of the Infinite. Thus, as stated in the *Zohar*, 'The whole is the whole.' When that light struck and brought forth other lights, they were all included within it. Thus, each of these Ten Sefirot is comprised of all ten. It is found that these Sefirot are parts of Him... since there is no number or count, and all these ten Sefirot are one entity, and they are the Divine Essence. For they are within the Infinite like a 'flame bound to a coal,' and like the likeness of a soul in the body of a man with its limbs, where all is one. It is a complete unity without any side of separation in the world, Heaven forbid! 

**Kingdom** <note>*Malkhut*</note>, who is the **Matron**, and the other Sefirot are all one in complete unity with the Infinite. All that was, all that is, and all that will be is one. As Menachem Recanati wrote in the name of the *Zohar*: 'The whole is the whole.' This is the **World of Complete Unity**. From there onward begins the **World of Separation**, meaning that the worlds all hang upon the command of the Holy One, even though His essence is like the God of the Sefirot. 

Between the World of Complete Unity and the World of Complete Separation, there is a world that has a side of unity—it is comprised of all Ten Sefirot—and a side of separation—it serves as a **casing** <note>*nartak*</note> for the higher Ten Sefirot, like a snail whose garment is part of its own body. This is called **Beauty** <note>*Shapir*</note>. Concerning this, it is said: 'And he stood with him there,' and 'The Lord descended in a **Cloud**' <note>*Anan*</note>, which is the secret of the Name of 72 <note>*Ayin-Bet*</note>, and the secret of the straight *Nun* and the bent *Nun*, which are Wisdom, Beauty, and Kingdom. 'And the Lord passed by'—this refers to His face; not the face of Moses, but the face of the Lord. 

This world that exists between the World of Unity and the World of Separation is **Metatron**, in whom all the Sefirot are included. This was the claim of Elisha ben Abuyah <note>A famous apostate known as 'Acher'</note>, who said there are, Heaven forbid, 'two powers,' because he saw that Metatron governs the World of Separation. Therein lies the secret of 'other gods' and the grip of the guardian angels of the nations. For in the higher realms, no guardian angel is permitted to ascend. There is the place of the waste and the filth of the Serpent... the sins of man reach there to separate the World of Complete Unity from him. But in the higher realms, there is no blemish, Heaven forbid! As it is written: 'If you are righteous, what do you give Him? And if your transgressions are many, what do you do to Him?' 

From that mentioned world, it separates and becomes 'four heads,' which are the four camps of the *Shekhinah*. Between that world and the four camps of the *Shekhinah* is the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**... it is called 'suspended,' for its head is good and its tail is evil. Therein was the sin of Adam, who mixed good with evil. But the higher Sefirot are the Essence of God and are complete unity... there is no change there at all, except that as a person acts, so is it shown to him." End of quote.

Afterward, the Maggid came a second time and said to him: "The Lord be with you in all that you do. Behold, I have come out to seek you and to see your face, and I find you occupied with this secret. I am surprised that they are making your study of the holy Sefirot so difficult for you! I see you have not stood well on this matter. You must know that the higher Sefirot emerged from the Infinite in the way I taught you. And what I told you—that between the World of Unity and the World of Separation there is a world with a side of unity and a side of separation—**that is the Shekhinah**. 

She is unified with the higher realms, and she includes seven [lower Sefirot] corresponding to the seven higher ones... and the three higher ones are also included in her in a hidden and concealed way... and the whole is one complete unity like the higher Sefirot. Heaven forbid one should think there is any separation there! Whoever thinks so, Heaven forbid, 'cuts the plantings' <note>commits heresy</note>. The 'cutting' is specifically regarding the *Shekhinah*, which is this world I am speaking of. Whoever separates her from the higher realms, his punishment is great. Therefore, know and be warned that this world, which is the *Shekhinah*, is unified with the higher Sefirot in a perfect unity without separation. 

What I told you about there being 'separation' in her was not to say that she has separation within her, Heaven forbid! Rather, it was to say that because she overflows into Metatron... who is the World of Separation, and from there all the worlds are sustained... because she overflows into the World of Separation, we say she has a 'side of separation.' But she has no separation in her essence at all; she is in perfect unity with the higher realms. This is the secret of the unity: that the *Shekhinah* is unified with the Holy One, for I told you she is like the higher Ten Sefirot, like a snail whose garment is part of its own body. The garment and the body are all one without any separation at all." End of quote.

Afterward, the Maggid came a third time and said to him: "Behold, I see that it is difficult..."

It clarifies that while the Shekhinah acts as a bridge to the lower World of Separation, she remains in absolute, inseparable unity with the Divine Essence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Torah’s transformation. It moves from the heavy, analytical "darkness" of the Babylonian Talmud toward a vision of the future redemption where the Written and Oral Torahs—currently perceived as two separate "crowns" or "garments"—will merge into a single, unified Light. The author draws heavily on the famous passage in the Talmud (Shabbat 104a) where school-children interpret the Hebrew alphabet to reveal ethical and mystical truths.</meta>

-># The House of the Stream<-

They exerted themselves so much over it that the Torah eventually needed to be written down. Then it became explained through the "deliberations and calculations of the dead of the world" <note>This is a mystical interpretation of a phrase from the Talmud (Sanhedrin 24a) describing the Babylonian Talmud as "darkness," referring to the grueling intellectual labor required to uncover its truths in the long years of exile.</note>. This refers to the Babylonian Talmud—meaning, the darkness and the mortality that sin brought into the world caused this state of affairs. Had the original strength remained and the Light continued to grow stronger for all time, then the Torah would be pure Light, and it would gladden the heart; it would not be a matter of "darkness" or a person "killing himself over it" <note>A reference to the Talmudic saying that Torah is only preserved by one who "kills himself over it"—meaning one who sacrifices physical comfort for study.</note>.

This is the secret of the "Two Luminaries." It has already been written in the book *Kol Bochim* <note>A commentary on Lamentations</note> that the Hebrew word for "Luminaries" (*Me'orot*) contains the letters for both "Light" (*Ohr*) and "Death" (*Mavet*). Thus, through "deliberations and calculations like the dead of the world," death was fashioned from the luminaries; the letters of "Light" (*Ohr*) were transformed into "Darkness" and not Light. It was originally intended that the Torah be a single Light—one Torah—but now there are two Torahs <note>The Written Torah (Pentateuch) and the Oral Torah (Talmud/Tradition).</note>. In the future, the "Garments of Skin" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Ohr* with the letter *Ayin*. Genesis 3:21 describes God clothing Adam and Eve in skins after the fall.</note> will return to being "Garments of Light" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Ohr* with the letter *Aleph*. Kabbalists teach that before the fall, Adam's "garment" was made of divine light.</note>. Then, the Written Torah will be clear to us through the light of the intellect, and we will no longer require the explanation of the Oral Torah as a separate entity.

# And by the Power
of this concept, a difficulty regarding a passage in the first chapter of the laws of Hanukkah <note>Actually found in Tractate Shabbat 104a, which contains laws of Hanukkah</note> will be resolved. The text reads as follows: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Joshua ben Levi: "Children have come today to the study hall and said things the likes of which were not said even in the days of Joshua son of Nun:
*   *Aleph-Bet*: **A**cquire **U**nderstanding (*Aleph Binah*).
*   *Gimmel-Dalet*: **B**e kind to the **P**oor (*Gemol Dalim*).
...until the letters *Heh-Vav*: This is the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
*   *Zayin-Chet, Tet-Yod, Kaf-Lamed*: If you do this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, **S**ustains you, is **G**racious to you, does **G**ood to you, gives you an **I**nheritance, and binds a **C**rown for you in the World to Come.
*   *Open Mem and Closed Mem*: An **O**pen word and a **C**onsealed word.
*   *Bent Nun and Straight Nun*: A **F**aithful one who is bent, and a **F**aithful one who is straight.
*   *Samekh-Ayin*: **S**upport the **P**oor.
Another interpretation: **M**ake signs (*Simanim*) in the Torah and **A**cquire it.
*   *Bent Peh and Straight Peh*: An **O**pen mouth and a **C**losed mouth.
*   *Bent Tzadi and Straight Tzadik*: A **R**ighteous one who is bent and a **R**ighteous one who is straight.

The text continues: "The Torah added a 'bent' letter to a 'bent' letter; from here we learn that the Torah was given with a bowed head." Note that they explained all the "straight" <note>Final forms of Hebrew letters: ך, ן, ף, ץ</note> and "double" letters, mentioning the final letters *M-N-T-Z-P*, but omitted the final *Kaf* (ך). This is quite astonishing! However, according to what I have written, it becomes clear.

As a foundation, I will preface with the words of our Sages regarding Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Simai taught: At the hour when Israel prioritized "We will do" (*Na'aseh*) over "We will listen" (*Nishma*), sixty myriads of ministering angels came to each and every person in Israel and tied two crowns to them—one corresponding to "We will do" and one corresponding to "We will listen." But once they sinned, the crowns were taken away. Rabbi Yohanan said: Moses was worthy of them all and took them for himself. Rabbi Resh Lakish said: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will return them to us, as it is said, "And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with singing; and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads" <note>Isaiah 35:10</note>—this "joy" refers to the crowns that were once on their heads.

Understand this well: "We will do" and "We will listen" represent the Written Torah and the Oral Torah, and they are the two crowns. In the passage from the chapter on Hanukkah mentioned above, it says: "And He binds for you a crown (*Keter*) for the World to Come." The final *Kaf* (ך), which is the first letter of "Crown" (*Keter*), hints at this crown. Since there is no other explanation for the final *Kaf* beyond what was explained for the initial *Kaf*, it was not necessary to mention it separately. Instead, it was hinted at in the title: one *Kaf* alone points to the matter we explained—that in the future, the two Torahs (the two crowns) will become a single crown. This single crown will encompass both crowns because the "Garments of Skin" will return to being "Garments of Light." This is the secret of "Everlasting joy upon their heads"—the joy that existed at the beginning of the world's creation (the Light that was hidden) will return to their heads.

By way of a hint, the word "Joy" (*Simcha*) hides within it the Oral Torah. For the Oral Torah consists of the vibrant debates and arguments of Torah scholars, which are "for the sake of Heaven." The word *Simcha* (שמחה) serves as an acronym for "Torah Scholars Increase Peace" <note>Hebrew: *Talmidei Chachamim Marbim Shalom*</note>.

One should not ask: "When they prioritized 'doing' over 'listening,' why were they given two crowns and not just one? Why didn't the 'venom of the serpent' cease then, allowing them to wear 'Garments of Light' (with an *Aleph*) immediately?" This question was already asked in the book *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of the Soul." His answer was as follows: Even though the Sages said that the spiritual impurity (*zohama*) ceased at Mount Sinai, why weren't they brought into the lower Garden of Eden? Why did they still need to inhabit this physical world? The secret lies in the "Garments." After Adam was expelled from Eden, he lost his spiritual garment and remained "naked," as it is written, "for they were naked." The light was removed from them, and their spirits remained without a covering until the Holy One, Blessed be He, clothed them in "Garments of Skin" (*Ohr* with an *Ayin*) from the light of this world. To reside in the Garden of Eden, one needs a garment woven from the performance of the Commandments (*Mitzvot*). Even though the impurity ceased at Sinai, they had not yet fulfilled the Commandments; thus, they would have been "naked" in Eden. One cannot enter that realm in these physical garments. A person must first strip off the coarse garment through death or refinement and put on other garments suited to that world.

# However,
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bind a single crown, signifying a single, unified Torah. Afterward, they will rise higher and higher until this unified Torah is revealed in its most internal secret—that it is entirely composed of His Holy Names. At that point, physical actions will be nullified, and everything will be refined. This is similar to the way Torah is studied in the Garden of Eden, which was prepared for Adam if he had not sinned.

<margin>Let us return to the mystery of the two letters *Aleph* and *Ayin*.</margin>

# With the Two
As we see now, it is impossible to be without two Torahs: the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. This is the secret of why the Torah begins with the letter *Bet* (numerical value 2, for the two Torahs).
However, regarding the Ten Commandments, the *Zohar* states they correspond to the "Ten Sayings" of creation. They begin with the letter *Aleph* (in the word *Anochi* - "I am"). It would have been appropriate for the crowns to be represented by the final *Kaf* (ך) and not the bent *Kaf* (כ). At present, the importance is on the bent *Kaf* (symbolizing this world), but in the future, the importance will be on the final *Kaf* (the Crown). This is the meaning of "He binds for you a Crown (*Keter*) for the World to Come."

**The Alephs and the Ayins:** I have previously elaborated on the secret of the "Garments of Light" (with an *Aleph*) and how they later became "Garments of Skin" (with an *Ayin*). In the future, the "Garments of Light" will return with even greater intensity. Therefore, the first *Aleph* will not be mixed with the *Ayin*. Light will emerge from the darkness, and it will be an "open eye" (*Ayin*)—as in the verse, "No eye has seen, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. This "Eye" will be higher than the first "Garment of Light" (*Aleph*).

**The letter Chet:** In the Talmud, Tractate *Menachot* (Chapter *HaKometz*), Rav Ashi said: "I have seen meticulous scribes who add a 'roof' to the letter *Chet* (ח) and suspend the 'leg' of the letter *Heh* (ה)." The *Chet* signifies that God "lives (*Chai*) in the heights of the universe." Why was this world created with the letter *Heh*? Because it is like an "exedra" (a porch open on the side); anyone who wishes to go out (to sin) may do so. Why is the leg of the *Heh* suspended? So that if one returns in repentance (*Teshuvah*), they may be brought back in through the small opening at the top.

In Tractate *Berakhot*, Rabbi Yohanan says: "All the prophets prophesied only for the sake of the penitents (*Ba'alei Teshuvah*), but as for the perfectly righteous (*Tzaddikim Gamurim*), 'No eye has seen, O God, besides You.'" However, Rabbi Abbahu disagrees, saying: "In the place where penitents stand, even the perfectly righteous cannot stand." Know that these two masters do not actually disagree; they are speaking of different levels. We can distinguish between "Repentance out of Fear" and "Repentance out of Love." The perfectly righteous person is superior to one who repents out of fear, but the penitent is superior to the perfectly righteous if they repent out of love.

There is also a great mystical hint here: Had man remained in the "Garments of Light" as he was created, having not drawn the Evil Inclination upon himself, he would have been a "Perfectly Righteous" person. But once he was clothed in "Garments of Skin," he has no remedy except through Repentance. All his descendants follow him into the coarseness of matter. This state is "close to loss and close to gain." It is close to loss if he does not refine himself, but close to gain if he does. By breaking and humbling the "husks" (the *Kelipot*) and purifying them, the light that emerges from the darkness is of a superior quality. Thus, there are two sides: it would have been good if man remained a "Perfectly Righteous" being in "Garments of Light," but there is a "greater advantage" in becoming a penitent, for those who merit to ascend do so with extra strength and a higher degree. This relates to the debate between the Schools of Shammai and Hillel: "Is it better for man not to have been created than to have been created?"

# And Behold,
The letter *Chet* (ח) represents "Life (*Chai*) in the heights of the universe," which is the level of the Perfectly Righteous—the secret of the "Garments of Light" and the indwelling of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) in the lower worlds. From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired for the Presence to be below. In that state, the world is refined and pure, and God is "Living" (*Chai*) in the heights, from which vitality flows to man so he may live forever. But the letter *Heh* (ה) hints at the penitents, for whom the world is like an "exedra."
