# The Great Gate

Bent letters and straight letters, straight letters and bent letters; on the right they are supported, on the right they are supported; open sections and open sections; closed sections—an open section one should not make closed, and a closed section one should not make open. 
If one wrote an open section and it is valid, or if one wrote a song as if it were prose, or wrote without ink, or wrote the Divine Names in gold, behold these must be withdrawn from use <note>original: *ugnuzin*; referring to the practice of 'Genizah,' where sacred texts that are unusable or incorrectly written are stored away rather than destroyed.</note>. <margin>**In the Midrashim**</margin>
In this teaching <note>original: *Baraita*; an ancient oral tradition not included in the Mishnah</note> which includes the form of the entire Torah, there are many hints, wondrous things, and great secrets. Therefore, I have come to reveal them according to my ability. My heart tells me that they modeled all these things on the introduction, and the threefold word which connects the existence of the Blessed Name, the Torah, and Man with all the teachings. The Blessed Name revealed the reality of His Divinity through the world which He renewed *ex nihilo* <note>original: *yesh me-ayin*; something from nothing</note> in order that His Divinity would be known to Man, who is the purpose of creation, so that he might receive the Torah and fulfill its commandments.

## And behold the matter
of explaining the mysteries and secrets of this teaching—even though I will not explain the words exactly as they are joined in the teaching, I will explain according to the order of the subjects: the creation, the progression, and the arrangement of things according to the order of the letters of the alphabet, placing the earlier first and the later last.

And as it is written: "And you shall write them." Behold, through the medium of the Torah, we, the nation of Israel, are bound to the Holy One, Blessed be He. The six hundred thousand letters in the Torah correspond to the sixty times ten-thousand <note>600,000</note> souls of Israel; then together the Name shall be complete with them and His work. He, may He be blessed, is perfect and acts perfectly with the perfect—namely, the "Perfect Torah" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. And we, the House of Israel, are those of whom it is said: "You shall be wholehearted <note>The Hebrew word *Tamim* can mean perfect, simple, or wholehearted.</note> with the Lord your God."

Regarding the matter of the existence of the Blessed Name, they hinted at the letters *Dalet*, *Yod*, *Shin* and *Yod*, *He*, *Vav*, *He* and *Yod*, *He*, *He*. These indicate His blessed existence. For behold, the *Dalet* of the word "One" <note>original: *Echad* from the Shema prayer</note> is written large. So too, the *Dalet* of "One God" is written large. If one were to flip the *Dalet* (ד) to a *Resh* (ר), he would be a denier and a heretic <note>In Hebrew, the letters Dalet (ד) and Resh (ר) look very similar. Changing *Echad* (One) to *Acher* (Other) would change "One God" to "Another God."</note>. Regarding this it is said: "The overturners," those who flip the *Dalet* to a *Resh* and the *Resh* to a *Dalet*. But Judah still—meaning, with God—they are the faithful ones to God, not bowing to "Another" god (*El Acher*), but only to the Lord our God, the Lord is One.

**Vav-Yod-Vav**—this hints at a great secret that I revealed in this introduction regarding the Name of the Lord. There is a distinction in the levels of ascent between the letter *Vav* and the letter *Yod*. That is to say, while the "Living One" is still written in the aspect of *Vav* (the numerical value 6), it is in the aspect of *Yod* (value 10). But in the time of perfection, when the Holy Temple stood and the Name was "whole," and in the future when His great light—which is currently hidden—will be revealed in the aspect of *Yod*, it follows the secret of the Name in the aspect of *Y-H-H*. Therefore, in the past, one was not to write *Yod-Vav*, and in the future to come, it will not be written *Vav-Yod*. The very form of the writing of the Torah letters hints at the past, present, and future; therefore it shall not change, for this is from His Torah.

**Zayin-Nun-Nun, Nun-Nun-Zayin**—this hints at the renewal of the world which proves His blessed existence. Behold, it was already mentioned in this introduction regarding the great secret that six thousand generations <note>or years</note> are full and one is destroyed <note>The Talmudic idea that the world exists for 6,000 years and is desolate in the 7th millennium.</note>, corresponding to the days of work and the Sabbath day. It will be explained how the Name will be whole and His arm will be revealed until the fifty-thousand generations in which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to return the spirit to the heights. As explained above in the introduction, the entire seventh millennium, which is the Sabbath, is an addition of holiness. But one cannot compare the holiness of the seventh to the fifty-thousandth millennium. Keep this sign in your hand: Moses our teacher attained forty-nine gates of understanding, but the fiftieth gate was hidden from him <note>A famous midrash about the "50 Gates of Understanding."</note>. Currently, in the state of *Zayin* (7), do not contemplate the *Nun* (50). As the Rabbi said: "From one end of the heaven to the other..." a man has permission to inquire only about his own world, not what is before or what is after. When one trusts in the aspect of *Nun*, then he is no longer in the aspect of *Zayin*, for he has ascended to a great height.

**Tet-Pe, Pe-Tet**—this matter requires an investigation into the words of our Sages, who taught that there is a specific measure for the letter *Tet* regarding Light. Also, the *Rokeach* <note>Rabbi Eleazar of Worms, a 12th-century mystic.</note> wrote that there is a measure for the letter *Pe* regarding Light. I will explain the words of our Sages brought in the Talmud (Tractate Bava Kamma): Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: "One who sees the letter *Tet* in a dream, it is a good sign for him." Why? Because the first time it appears in the Torah is in the word "Good" (*Tov*). One might argue it refers to "I will sweep it with the broom (*Mat'ate*) of destruction"? We answer: The letter *Tet* follows the first mention of the letter in the creation story. From the beginning of Genesis until "And God saw the Light that it was good," the letter *Tet* is not written. 

Regarding the letter *Pe*, the *Rokeach* mentions it in the secret of the Tefillin and Yom Kippur. There are eighty (*Pe*) letters from "In the beginning" until "on the face of the waters," and afterward it is written "And God said, 'Let there be light.'" Therefore, the Light was created after eighty letters. Why was it created with the letter *Pe* (numerical value 80)? Because the luminaries were not hung to be seen until the beginning of the fourth day. If you count the hours of the first, second, and third days, they equal seventy-two hours. Add the dawn of the fourth day, and you reach eighty hours. This is why "The opening of Your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple." He went on at length there.

**Know** that the "Hidden Light" <note>original: *Ohr HaGanuz*; the primal light of creation hidden away for the righteous in the future.</note> of which it is said, "How great is Your goodness (*Tov*) which You have hidden for those who fear You; You have wrought (*Pa'alta*) for those who take refuge in You," exists in two levels. One level is the World of Souls, which is the World to Come—a world that is pleasant and never-ending. This is where the righteous are in their state of remembrance until the time of the Resurrection; they enjoy the Hidden Light. In the eternal World to Come, which is a world that is "entirely Sabbath," they will draw from and enjoy it in body and soul together. This will be a world that is "entirely good." Then the "Great Good" that is hidden will increase even more. This is hinted at by the letter *Tet* (*Tov* - Good); it begins with *Tet* and grows from *Tet* onwards. 

This is similar to what the *Rokeach* wrote: Yom Kippur corresponds to the letter *Ayin* (70) because the tenth day is the tithe. So too the World to Come is "the tenth," for the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years, then six thousand years of this world, then one thousand of desolation—and then in the tenth, the World to Come begins. When he says "begins," he means the beginning of the great intensification. For the seventh millennium of desolation—the millennium of the *Tet*—surely contains great spiritual pleasure for the righteous. Such light after the darkness of the night is a hint to the World of Souls which operates until now after death, when a man leaves this world (called "night") for the upper world. As it says in the Talmud (Bava Metzia): "You make darkness and it is night, in which all the beasts of the forest creep." "You make darkness"—this is this world, which is similar to night. "Creep"—this refers to the righteous. Of this it is said, "You have wrought (*Pa'alta*) for those who take refuge in You." "Wrought" is in the past tense. But the light for the world that will come after the Resurrection is still "hidden" and "concealed," and it is of a much higher level than the World of Souls. Therefore, distinguish between the name "Wrought" (*Pa'alta* - beginning with *Pe*) in relation to the "Hidden" which is more spiritual. Thus, one finds the aspect of *Tet* (*Tov* - Good) in "How great is Your goodness" and the aspect of *Pe* in "You have wrought." Therefore, one should not mix *Tet* with *Pe*, nor *Pe* with *Tet*.

**Bet-Kaf, Kaf-Bet**—this hints at the Torah and the light hidden within it. In Midrash Rabbah, Rabbi Simon says: "The word 'Light' is written five times in the account of creation, corresponding to the five books of the Torah." In the Talmud (Snathedrin), on the verse "He has set me in dark places like those long dead," Rabbi Jeremiah said: "This refers to the Babylonian Talmud." This is a transformation, for the Talmud is light and illuminates our eyes; the Torah is our life and the length of our days, yet he calls them "the dead of the world"? 

Also, the Midrash of Rabbi Simai explains the Light mentioned at the start of Genesis as the Five Books of the Torah. It is written there, "And God divided," meaning He hid it. How is "hiding" applicable here? It makes sense if it refers to light visible to human eyes. But the Torah is one, as it is written "One Torah," yet it is two Torahs—namely, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. In truth, it is all one Torah, for everything in the Oral Torah is hinted at in the Written Torah. There is nothing that is not hinted at in the Torah. It is only that the intellect became darkened and the light of the mind was diminished because of the sin of Adam. Then the "garments of light" <note>original: *Kotnot Ohr* (with an Aleph)</note> were hidden and he was clothed in "garments of skin" <note>original: *Kotnot Or* (with an Ayin)</note>. Because of this, "they have eyes but do not see." The Holy One, Blessed be He, foresaw this and hid the light. 

Behold, due to the diminishing of human intellect, the Written Torah cannot be understood except through great labor. As our Sages said: "How is the Torah preserved? Only in one who kills himself over it." Therefore, the Written Torah needs explanation and commentary—which is the Talmud. In previous generations, when they had clear intellect, they understood deep things without a commentary. Afterward, they could not understand without a commentary, and then a commentary upon a commentary—all according to the darkness of the mind. Therefore, had Adam not sinned, his intellect would have been clear and pure, and he would have understood the Written Torah instantly. Through that understanding, he would have known everything and would not have needed the Oral Torah as a separate labor. But because he sinned and removed the light, bringing darkness to the world, man was required to toil and have the Oral Torah as an explanation, and to "kill himself" over it.

Having previously discussed the scribal laws and the "Great Gate" of the Torah, the author now transitions into a kabbalistic analysis of the four directions (winds), the nature of repentance, and how the physical forms of the letters—specifically the Bet, Samekh, and Mem—represent the architecture of the soul and the universe.</meta>

# The Great Gate

The reason for this is that through the generosity and the voluntary offerings of the princes at that time, "And David blessed," etc. <note>referring to 1 Chronicles 29:10-20, where David and the leaders of Israel donate generously to the Temple</note>. Therefore, it is fitting for the power of the Divine presence to collect charity. This is not like what is done in other lands where the treasurer walks around during the Cantor's repetition of the prayer, for then the people's thoughts are not focused on hearing the prayer to say "Amen." Therefore, this custom <note>collecting charity during specific moments of the service</note> is good and beautiful.

->Let us return to the matter: behold, the East wind is named "Light," and it goes out to the world and is called "Face" <note>Hebrew: *Panim*; also meaning "forward" or "front"</note>, and thus it is said: "May the Lord shine His face toward you."<-

**The right hand** of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is outstretched to receive those who return <note>original: *shavim*; those who repent</note>. The South wind is "the Right," as it is written: "North and the Right [South], You created them" <note>Psalm 89:13</note>. Therefore, the tribe of Reuben was stationed there <note>in the desert encampment</note>. In the Midrash, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Reuben: "You were the first to open the way for repentance; by your life, your grandson's son will stand and be the first to open the way for repentance." And who was this? Hosea the son of Beeri, as it is written: "Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God" <note>Hosea 14:2</note>. 

One might ask: how can it be said that Reuben was the first to open the way for repentance? Did not the Sages of blessed memory recount in the "Light of Repentance" that Adam the First Man stood for 130 years in a fast and entered the waters of the Gihon, etc.? And likewise, Cain repented. Furthermore, "The Beginning of Wisdom" <note>likely referring to the book *Reshit Chokhmah* or the concept generally</note> established that they repented for violating a negative commandment. However, regarding the fulfillment of a positive commandment, Reuben was the first to repent—specifically regarding the fulfillment of honoring one's father and mother, which is a positive commandment. But this answer seems far-fetched to me, for the honor of parents is equated to the honor of the Divine <note>original: *HaMakom*; literally 'The Place,' a name for God</note>, as seen in the chapter "These Found Objects" <note>Talmud, Bava Metzia</note>.

It seems to me that the explanation is this: they [Adam and Cain] did not initiate repentance on their own before the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed them a hint of repentance. But Reuben initiated and was awakened from within himself, and no encouragement came to him from Above. With Adam, there was an "opening" provided by God, as it says in Genesis Rabbah: "And now, lest he put forth his hand." Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, opened for him a door of repentance, as the word "And now" <note>original: *Ve-ata*</note> always signifies repentance, as it is said: "And now, what does the Lord your God ask of you?" Likewise, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Cain: "If you do well, will you not be uplifted?" But Reuben initiated and was awakened entirely from himself. 

Furthermore, "opening" implies that something was closed and he opened it—revealing what was hidden. The sins of Adam and Cain were public knowledge, so it is no surprise they repented. But the sin of Reuben was hidden in total concealment. As the Sages said: "Anyone who says Reuben sinned is solely mistaken," for he was merely claiming the grievance of his mother <note>referring to Reuben moving his father Jacob’s bed after Rachel died to defend his mother Leah’s honor</note>. On the contrary, to an observer, he was performing a commandment. This is what the Sages hinted at: "One should search through his deeds"—meaning to search and examine if perhaps there is some hidden sin that is not revealed. This is what Reuben did; he reflected that even though he acted for the sake of Heaven and for his mother's honor, perhaps he nonetheless sinned against the honor of his father. This is the "opening"—he opened that which was locked by searching through his own deeds.

**His back**—regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, it is written: "And you shall see My back." This was to tell Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, the secret of the prayer of the "Great Gate." The West wind is... <note>text continues to explain the West</note> and this is why the Holy One, Blessed be He, wrapped Himself like a Cantor <note>original: *Shaliach Tzibbur*; the leader of prayer</note> and said: "Whenever My children perform this order, [I will forgive them]." Behold, West is called "Back," and the Sages of blessed memory said the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> is in the West. Therefore, we are obligated to direct our prayers and intentions toward the Holy of Holies, which is in the West. 

The tribe of Ephraim was stationed there, from whom came Joshua. The Sages said it is forbidden for a Torah scholar to fall upon his face <note>in the *Tachanun* prayer</note> unless he is certain he will be answered like Joshua. Thus, the Face [East], the Right [South], and the Back [West] hint at Repentance, Prayer, and Charity. This is the letter *Bet* at the beginning of "In the beginning" <note>original: *Be-reshit*</note>, which represents these three directions. 

The North wind remains open. The matter is that "From the North the evil shall be released," for in the North is the secret of Strength <note>original: *Gevurah*; the attribute of judgment</note> and the power of Law, from which the "husks" <note>original: *Klipot*; the spiritual shells of evil</note>—the messengers of Judgment—draw their sustenance. The Torah begins with the letter *Bet* to hint at these three directions [South, East, West], but it does not hint at the "lofty wall" of the Torah [the North]. The Torah preceded the world by two thousand years. The Midrash also says the Torah began with the letter *Kaf* <note>the first letter of the first word of the Ten Commandments, *Anokhi*</note> which signifies Blessing <note>original: *Berakhah*</note>. All their words are truth.

Now I will explain: if there were no "Evil"—if the wall of the soul and sins did not exist—there would be no need for Repentance, and even for Prayer there would not be much need, just as it will be in the future. In the secret of the "Wall of the Snake," the Land of Israel is destined to produce pastries and fine wool garments, and there will be peace and quiet in the land. Certainly, there will be no need for Charity, for there will be no poor person in the world, only the Torah and its delights. But now, due to sin, we are pushed toward the "Breath of the Snake." Therefore, the Torah starts with *Kaf* for Blessing, and *Bet* which represents these three directions:
<margin>And it was</margin> Repentance, Prayer, and Charity which repair the sin that resulted from the "Back" of the Snake.

Our Sages said: "The Holy One created the Evil Inclination, and He created the Torah as its spice [antidote]." That is to say, through the power of the Torah, we close off the Northern direction which is open to evil. We turn the bad into good, as the Sages said: "A Torah discussion requires a warm prayer like a day of danger," drawing [holiness] down. Therefore, the Torah was given from the mouth of the "Power" <note>original: *Gevurah*; another name for God</note> which is in the North. As Rashi explained on the verse "And God spoke": the name *Elohim* always refers to a True Judge. For although the root of Torah is Kindness <note>original: *Chesed*</note>—as it says "the Torah of kindness is on her tongue"—and it is taken from the Higher Wisdom which is Supernal Kindness, it was nonetheless given with a [mighty] voice and lightning through "Strength" which is on the Left [North]. This is "Length of days in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and honor." Regarding these riches, the Sages said: "He who wishes to become wealthy should turn North," referring to the wealth of Torah. Of this it is said: "Out of the North comes gold." 

In the word *Bereshit* <note>In the beginning</note> there is a hint to Aaron... <note>text becomes highly symbolic</note> One who wishes to become wise should turn South, for this is the part of the Torah's thought in the secret of "Spirituality," which the Sages called a "Great Matter"—the Work of the Chariot <note>original: *Ma'aseh Merkavah*; esoteric mysticism</note>. But from the Northern side is the secret of evil, or the "Good Wealth" I explained. Then the righteous turn the Attribute of Judgment into the Attribute of Mercy. Therefore, the North is open from the side of Law. 

There was stationed the tribe of Dan, who is named for Judgment <note>original: *Din*</note>, as Rachel said:
<margin>and etc.</margin> "God has judged me" <note>Genesis 30:6</note>. "Dan shall be a snake," for from there the power of the Snake draws sustenance. But "if this disgusting one [the Evil Inclination] meets you, drag him to the House of Study." At the giving of the Torah, the directions were completed and became a "Closed Samekh" <note>the circular letter *Samekh* (ס) or the final *Mem* (ם)</note>. This is the "Closed Mem" in the verse "To the increase of the government and to peace there is no end" <note>Isaiah 9:6, which uniquely uses a closed *Mem* in the middle of a word</note>.

<margin>And this is the secret of</margin> **And behold**, Man is an image standing on the earth with his head reaching the heavens. This means the body of Man was taken by the Holy One from the dust of the place of the Altar so that he would be sanctified, but his head—that is, the Soul—is from the highest heights. We, the nation of Israel, are called "Man" <note>original: *Adam*</note>. Behold the secret: Man has extremities, above and below, and four directions surrounding him which indicate the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Divine Presence is above his head. 

I found in *Wings of the Earth* <note>original: *Kanfei Ha'aretz*; a kabbalistic work</note> by R. Luria <note>original: *Ch’ali* - likely referring to the Ari, Isaac Luria</note>... the East, West, North, and South correspond to the four Divine Names that cannot be erased: *EL, Elohim, Y-H-V-H, Adonai*. These are the four Clouds of Glory that surrounded Israel from every side. Know that the name *Y-H* is not in this count, for it is the beginning, middle, and end. The name *Elohim* is the beginning... 

The East corresponds to the "River that goes out of Eden to water the garden." The word West <note>original: *Ma'arav*</note> has the numerical value <note>Gematria</note> of the 12 permutations of the Name of God (*Y-H-V-H*). The word North <note>original: *Tzafon*</note> has the numerical value of "Choice" <note>original: *Bechirah*; both equal 236</note>. This is the secret of Choice: because of the North, there is a need for the "profane sinner," and all is within righteous judgment. The mnemonic is "Salt is from the rebellion..." 

The mnemonic for the South is that it is a "good sign," for the word South <note>original: *Darom*</note> has the numerical value of 250, which is the same as "Lamp" <note>original: *Ner*; 50+200=250</note>. "A lamp of the Lord is the soul of man," for she is the "daughter of a priest," the daughter of Abraham the Pious. Here you have many secrets in the four directions.

**And now** I will explain the matter of the [letter] *Samekh* (ס) and the [final] *Mem* (ם). Behold, the *Samekh* is close to the closed *Mem*, except that one is a square and the other is a circle. There is a great hint here: this World of Action <note>original: *Olam Ha-Asiyah*; the physical world</note>, which includes the heavens and the earth and all their host, is circular, for we see the heavens are circular. Spiritual "Action" is within the heavens like the soul in the body, which is hinted at in the *Samekh*. 

Above it is the World of Formation <note>original: *Olam Ha-Yetzirah*</note>, where the camp of the Divine Presence resides: Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael. Corresponding to them were the four banners of Israel, as mentioned in Numbers Rabbah and the Zohar. These four camps of the Divine Presence are envisioned in our intellect as being square. They are aligned toward the world above them, the "Secret of the Living Creatures" <note>original: *Chayot HaKodesh*</note> which are square: Man, Ox, Eagle, and Lion, who carry the Throne. 

Now I will make known the secret: the Sages divided deeds between those done out of Love and those done out of Fear. Likewise, regarding repentance, there is a difference between repentance from fear and repentance from love, as stated in Tractate Yoma. One who acts from fear is attached to the physical—meaning from the fear for his own self—and then he is attached to the physical world whose root is hinted at in the shape of the *Samekh*. However, one who acts from love acts out of love for the Holy One and desires to cleave to Him; he enters the spiritual realm. To such a person is said: "I will give you a place to walk among these who stand." Great is repentance, for it reaches the Throne of Glory—that is, the square of the Living Creatures which is above the square of the heavenly camps. This is the secret of the "Closed Mem" (ם), and "of peace there is no end." 

When you place a circle inside a square, just as the World of Action is inside the Spiritual World, the square exceeds it at the four corners. These corners hint at the sinners [seeking atonement] through the sacrifices to the Lord, as we learned: "He comes to the Southeast corner, the Northeast, the Northwest, the Southwest." Regarding these corners, the hint is "He cut off in fierce anger every horn [corner] of Israel." For even if they brought sacrifices, a penitent acting only out of fear is not at the level of the "Mem" but only at the level of the "Samekh." As it is said: "He turned back His right hand..."

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic and ethical exploration of the Hebrew alphabet. Having previously introduced the symbolism of the letter He (ה) and the concept of repentance, the author now uses the physical shape of the letters to explain why those who return to faith require greater self-restraint than the lifelong righteous. He also integrates Maimonides' "Middle Path" philosophy, noting that humility is the one exception where an extreme approach is required.</meta>

# The Great Gate

"And behold, it is open at the bottom." These are the words of the Zohar <note>The primary work of Jewish mysticism</note> regarding the section on the creation of the world: "The world was created with the letter *He* (ה)." The Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world open toward the side of evil and sin, for there is no direction where sin cannot be found.
Evil emerges like an *exedra* <term>exedra: a Greek-style porch or hall open on one side</term>; it is not enclosed by walls but has a large breach open to the side of evil, toward the bottom. Anyone who wishes to leave their spiritual world has the power to do so;
they will not turn any way without finding a side of sin and iniquity through which to enter the "outer shells" <note>original: *chitzonim*; mystical forces of evil or impurity</note>. Yet, the letter is also open at the top <note>referring to the small gap at the upper left of the letter *He*</note> so that if one returns in repentance, they may be received. But it was asked: why is it not enough to simply return through the same large opening?
The reason is that for one who returns in repentance <note>original: *ba'al teshuva*</note>, it is not enough to be protected by the same "fence" that guards the righteous. For the righteous who have never sinned, a small fence is sufficient.
**However**, for the sinner who has sinned and then returned, a small fence will not suffice. Rather, they must build many difficult fences around themselves. Since that original small fence was already breached once, if they approach it again, their evil inclination will easily entice them. Instead, they must distance themselves very far indeed. For this reason, the penitent does not enter through the wide opening of the "porch" where the breach is, but rather ascends and enters through a narrow opening at the top. They must create many boundaries and self-imposed restrictions for themselves to seal the breaches. It is for this reason that "in the place where the penitent stands, even the perfectly righteous cannot stand," because the penitent did not enter through the gate of the righteous. To be with the righteous, they had to suffer and ascend through the upper gate, strengthening themselves against sin even more than the righteous. Thus, they ascended and stood at the level of the letter *He*, specifically the "Palace of the *He*" within the Garden of Eden—which is the roof of the *He*—while the righteous stand at the entrance of the *He*, at the opening of the porch. This is the meaning of "Return the *He* to its place" <note>a kabbalistic pun on the word *Teshuva* (repentance), read as *Tashuv-He* (the letter He shall return)</note>.

**And when they return**—when the light returns or when one reaches the level of the "perfectly righteous," the ultimate goal is that everything becomes good, for the dross has been removed and no sediment remains.
This is the secret of the verse: "No eye has seen, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. I have already taught this above regarding the hint that the letter *He* should not be exchanged for *Het* (ח), nor *Het* for *He*.
**The *Gimels* (ג) and *Tzadis* (צ)**: Our Sages also spoke about the cancellation of the "serpent’s filth." It is known that the root of all character traits is humility <note>original: *hachna'ah*</note>, and this is the essence of repentance.
->Regarding the virtue of humility: all character virtues depend on humility. Of our teacher Moses—than whom no greater prophet ever arose—<-
the Torah did not emphasize his praise except for the virtue of extreme humility that he possessed. The matter is thus: envy, lust, and the pursuit of honor remove a person from the world. Adam, the first human, was removed from the world and sentenced to death for all generations because of these traits, brought upon him by the serpent who was envious when he saw Eve,
or enticed her with lust (as it says, "it was a delight to the eyes"), and with the pursuit of honor (as it says, "and you shall be like gods"). Behold, this sin of Adam is a "root bearing gall and wormwood" <note>Deuteronomy 29:17</note> for all sins, bringing the serpent's filth and the evil inclination into the world forever. The remedy for this is the trait of humility. For one who is exceedingly humble, whose soul is like dust,
does not envy, does not lust, and flees from honor. It is said there in the discourse on humility: the "bent *Nun*" (נ) and the "straight *Nun*" (ן) represent the "faithful bent" and "faithful straightened"; the "bent *Tzadi*" (צ) and "straight *Tzadi*" (ץ) represent the "righteous bent" and the "righteous straightened." The Torah added a "bending" to his bending, meaning that the Torah was given as a primary fence.
The matter is explained according to what Maimonides <note>original: *Ha-Rambam*</note> wrote in the fourth of his *Eight Chapters* <note>the introduction to the Ethics of the Fathers</note>. He wrote: "Good deeds are the balanced deeds, the middle path between two extremes, both of which are evil—one being excess and the other deficiency. Virtuous character traits are psychological dispositions that are intermediate between two bad dispositions, one excessive and one deficient." For example: temperance is a middle trait between excessive lust and a total lack of feeling for pleasure. Temperance is a good deed, and the disposition of the soul from which it arises is a moral virtue. But excessive lust is one extreme, and the total lack of pleasure-sensing is the other extreme; both are entirely evil. These two soul-dispositions—lust (the excess) and insensitivity (the deficiency)—are both among the lowest of traits. Similarly, generosity is the middle path between stinginess and wastefulness; courage is the middle between cowardice and recklessness; dignity is the middle between arrogance and self-abasement. See there at length how he praises the choice of the middle path, except in the case of humility.
Between arrogance and lowliness of spirit, one should not remain in the middle, but should go to the extreme end and be "lowly of spirit," as the Mishnah says: "Be very, very lowly of spirit, for the hope of man is the worm." Maimonides also wrote this in his *Laws of Ethical Conduct*, chapter one. Our Sages elaborated on this, saying "very, very" to mean: do not follow the middle path, but go to the furthest extreme of lowliness. It is written regarding the "lights" <note>referring to Moses or the sun/moon</note> that he was "very humble," adding the word "very."
This is the meaning of "a righteous man bent"—adding a "bending" to his bending. However, in the first chapter of Tractate Sotah, it is said: "Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav: A Torah scholar must have an eighth of an eighth of pride" <note>1/64th part</note>. Rava also said: "One who has it is under a ban, but one who lacks it entirely is also under a ban." Rashi explains "pride" here
as being necessary so that people will respect him, giving him the power to rebuke sinners. For a Torah scholar should not lean entirely to the final extreme of lowliness, but should hold onto a tiny bit of dignity for the sake of the Torah's honor, so he may teach and rebuke. But for anyone else, they should not lean even a tiny bit toward any side that has a point of pride; they should go entirely to the extreme end of being lowly of spirit. With this, we can explain the matter of "the *Gimels* (ג) and *Tzadis* (צ)." Rashi explains there that they are similar in writing, except one is at the top and one is at the bottom. This means the "bent *Tzadi*" is at the top, hinting at what I wrote:
<margin>Nevertheless, let him have a tiny bit of pride, the smallest of small amounts, for the sake of Heaven; for a great man who is needed by the public—even though the Torah added a bending to his bending—must cast fear so that they will accept his rebuke.</margin>
Therefore, the "head" of the *Tzadi* remains at the top; even though it is bent, the "Righteous" (*Tzadik*) has his head upward. But the *Gimel* is "hollowed out," and its
head is downward. This hints that for an ordinary person, it is not enough to have a "bending upon a bending"; it should be as if they have no head at all, directed down toward the earth, to live literally like the "dust of the earth" and go entirely to the extreme end of lowliness. For this reason, the *Gimel* should not be mixed with the *Tzadi*, nor the *Tzadi* with the *Gimel*. The reason for this great virtue of humility is as I wrote: through it, one repairs the sin of Adam which includes all sins. In the future, when the serpent's filth and the "shells" are destroyed, it is written: "And I will lead you upright," for the Lord shall dwell within us, "The Lord reigns, He is clothed in majesty."

### From Mem-Nun to Mem-Chaf-Nun... The closed Mem (ם) has four sides. The Samekh (ס) is similar to it... the Pe (פ) is square and the Samekh is round. There are great hints in their forms.
It is written, "To the four directions of the heavens I have spread you out." The Sages said in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah: Just as the
world cannot exist without winds/directions, so too the world cannot exist without Israel. Therefore, Israel is hinted at by the "four legs" corresponding to the four directions. Know that there is a height in his spirit for the Seer.
Thus, Repentance is linked to Torah, Prayer, and Charity. Torah is the greatest of them, corresponding to them all. These are included in the teaching:
<margin>For the one who purifies his deeds: "Upon three things the world stands: upon the Torah, upon Service, and upon Acts of Kindness."</margin>
1. Torah. 2. Prayer (which is included in "Service," as the Sages said: "What is the service of the heart? It is prayer," which stands in place of the sacrifices). 3. Charity. And they are all joined by 4. Repentance. These four "walls" are the four directions, as I will explain.
God remains in the heavens, as it were, in the heights of the firmament, which is the "Upper Height." And Man is on the earth.
High and low—that is, the heavens above and the earth below.
<margin>There remain the four directions hinting at the aforementioned. Through them, man, who is on the earth below, may attach himself to the Upper Height. First, I will state that from below: East is called "Face" (Front), West is "Behind," South is "Right," and North is "Left."</margin>
Regarding the "Face" of the Holy One, Blessed be He, it is said: "In the light of the King's face is life," for He is Kindness and Charity, as it is written:
"A vision of kindness you have performed." And it is said: "Charity delivers from death," and "Kindness and Truth shall precede Your face," and "I, through Charity, shall behold Your face." Behold, the creation of the world
was from the aspect of Kindness, Grace, and Generosity, as it is written: "A world of kindness shall be built." And what was the beginning of creation? "And God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light."
This corresponds to the East wind, from where light comes to the world. It is written: "The sun of charity and healing in its wings." The East is called "Face" (Front) because "In the light of the King's face is life," and it is written: "Your charity shall go before you."
Therefore, the "leg" of the tribe of Judah was in the East, for the Kingdom of the House of David is established through charity, as the verse points out regarding David: "And David performed justice and charity."
Our Sages explained: even within a legal judgment, he performed charity. How? He would judge according to the law—ruling who was exempt and who was liable—and afterward, he would reimburse the liable party from his own pocket. Regarding this, he would pray: "I have performed justice and charity; do not leave me to my oppressors." For he feared that two people might conspire to trick him, so that one would be found liable and David would reimburse him, and then they would split the money between them. Therefore,
he prayed: "Master of the Universe, do not leave me to those who would defraud me." This is also explained in the Midrash on Samuel. And here in the book of Chronicles, you find that in the generation of the Temple, the princes
donated with a full heart and with joy. Then David blessed the Lord in the sight of all the congregation, as is explained in the Book of Chronicles. Therefore, the custom I have seen
in the communities of the Land of Israel seems correct to me: when the charity collector goes to collect in the synagogue, he goes after the "And David blessed" prayer, and they say... as is received in the name of the holy Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the great 16th-century kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory. And it is possible...

It also discusses Maimonides' theory of the "middle path," noting that humility is the only trait where one should seek the extreme end of the spectrum.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Hebrew letters and their spiritual architecture. The author moves from the shape of the letter He (ה) and the dynamics of repentance to the profound relationship between Divine knowledge and human free will, as expressed through the laws of writing a Torah scroll.</meta>

From our perspective, this is the secret of [Divine] Will and Knowledge, which I have elaborated on previously. Knowledge exists before the human act of choice; from the perspective of God’s essence, it is "open" according to how the source and root were revealed. However, from the perspective of what is established [in the physical world], it is "closed," as choice is in the hands of man. Thus, Divine knowledge is fixed according to the source that is open. Heaven forbid that any knowledge should spread outward from Him; rather, He knows through the knowledge of His own essence. This is the secret of the Name *Yod-Daled* <note>original: יוד"ד; a specific kabbalistic spelling or expansion of the Divine Name</note> hinted at in the "openings" and "closings." Everything comes from His power and none other, for His knowledge is His will, as I explained at length above. This is the secret of the phrase "Open and Closed." The definition of "Speech" [in the creation of the world] is "Will," as Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (1194–1270), a major medieval scholar</note> explained in his commentary on Genesis regarding every instance of "And God said," meaning "He desired and willed."

### An open section shall not be made closed, and vice versa
This will be explained according to what Rabbi Chaim Vital <note>The primary student of the Arizal and a central figure in Lurianic Kabbalah</note> wrote in his explanation of the "System of Names." He writes: "Just as a house needs a window for light, it also needs to close the breaches and weak spots so that thieves do not enter, for 'a breach calls to the thief.' So too, in the Torah scroll, there is a need for 'open' and 'closed' sections <term>Patuach and Satum: the two types of paragraph breaks in a Torah scroll</term>. If that which should be open is closed, or that which should be closed is opened, the scroll is invalid. For through the open sections, the 'window' of that side, the light comes to us. Regarding this, the Wise Man [Solomon] said: 'Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the lattices' (Song of Songs 2:9). It is necessary that the darkness of the 'External Forces' <note>original: *chitzonim*; mystical forces of impurity</note> does not enter through there. For there are places of retribution in the Torah where, if the Accuser <note>original: *Satan*</note> finds a path or a crack to enter, he will spit his filth and venom, and draw his bow against us to prosecute us. Therefore, we 'close off' the Accuser in the Torah scroll. In the Supernal Torah, which includes everything and is the Wisdom of Solomon, it is arranged so that the power of the blind and the impure cannot enter. Nevertheless, it is necessary to open a 'window' so we may receive the light appropriate for us in a way that the Accuser does not notice, so he does not prosecute us. He does not need more than 'peering through the lattices,' like one who gazes at his beloved in a hidden way. This is done so that Samael <note>The primary name of the Accuser/Satan in kabbalistic literature</note> and his company do not notice the matter. Regarding the 'final letters' <note>original: *Mantzepach* (מנצפ"ך); the five Hebrew letters that change form at the end of a word</note> that came into the world at the end of words: besides what I said above, there is another secret similar to what I mentioned. These letters represent the material of 'Great Judgment' <note>original: *Din Gadol*</note> and are like 'wine vessels.' Therefore, they always come at the end of a word, just as wine vessels and towers are placed to surround the house and the tower to protect it." Thus far are his words.

### Writing a Song or a Song-like Prose
Our Sages distinguished between a *shira* <note>feminine form of 'song'</note> and a *shir* <note>masculine form of 'song'</note>. A song of the future is called *shir* in the masculine, but the Song [at the Sea] and all songs that have already occurred in the past were in the feminine language, as it says, "this song" (*ha-shira ha-zot*). I might add that the entire Torah is spoken in the masculine language, hinting at the future.

**Or if not written with ink:** In the chapter "With what [may a beast go out]" <note>Talmud, Shabbat 55a</note>, the Holy One said to Gabriel: "Go and mark the foreheads of the righteous with a *Tav* of ink so the angels of destruction do not rule over them, and the foreheads of the wicked with a *Tav* of blood." The Attribute of Justice said before God: "Master of the Universe, how are these different from those?" He replied: "These are perfectly righteous and those are perfectly wicked." Justice said: "But they had the power to protest [the sins of their generation] and did not." God replied: "It is revealed and known to Me that even if they had protested, the wicked would not have listened." Justice argued: "If it is revealed to You, was it revealed to them?" This is why it is written [in Ezekiel]: "Slay utterly old and young... but come not near any man upon whom is the mark (*Tav*); and begin at My sanctuary." The Sages taught: "Do not read 'My sanctuary' (*mikdashi*) but 'My sanctified ones' (*mekudashai*)—these are the people who fulfilled the whole Torah from *Aleph* to *Tav*." The *Tav* indicates whether they shall live or die. The "Work of Heaven" <note>original: *Avodat HaKodesh*; a kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> says that the sin that occurred in the world affected both body and soul. The letters of the Torah are essentially spiritual lights, but they are "borrowed" to clothe the souls. This is hinted at in the Jerusalem Talmud: "The Torah given to Moses was written in black fire upon white fire." This refers to the revealed Torah which descends from the hidden, following the secret of "I am black but comely." Because souls have a root in the supernal heights, one must write with ink, which is black, upon white parchment.

### Writing the Divine Names in Gold
Because of the filth of the Serpent that Adam brought into the world, it was proper to repair this at the Giving of the Torah. They said, "We will do and we will listen." God said: "If you obey My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be My treasure... a kingdom of priests and a holy nation." This was to warn them not to follow the path of the first Adam, who abandoned his intellect and followed the path of the Serpent's "knowledge." Because He came to repair and renew the world through the Torah, He told them to listen to His voice—meaning His commandments—and not the voice of the Satan, who is the Serpent and the Evil Inclination. "Keep My covenant"—unlike Adam who violated the covenant. Rabbi Isaac said: "Adam was a 'puller of his foreskin'" <note>a Talmudic metaphor for trying to erase the sign of the covenant or acting like a non-Jew</note>. Rabbi Nachman said: "He was an atheist/heretic." Both are true, for he brought impurity into the world and damaged the Holy Covenant. Israel came to fix what Adam distorted. When Israel received the Torah, they "restored the crown to its former glory," and the decree of death and filth was abolished. As the Midrash says: "I said: Ye are angels... if Israel had waited for Moses and not committed that act [the Golden Calf], there would have been no exile and the Angel of Death would not have ruled over them." The word *Charut* (engraved) on the Tablets should be read as *Cherut* (freedom)—freedom from exile and freedom from death. This refers to all the goodness and happiness that flows from the Torah. "Kingdom of priests" refers to their status, and "Holy Nation" refers to their eternal existence. But they returned to their corruption when the Satan danced among them with the Golden Calf, and they said: "These are your gods, O Israel." Therefore, they wrote the Divine Names in gold <note>referring to a prohibited scribal practice linked here to the idolatry of the golden calf</note>.

**Therefore, these must be hidden away.** For the light remains hidden until the future time: "A new light shall shine upon Zion." May the verse "Arise, shine, for your light has come" be fulfilled in us. Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

### My children, may God protect you
You have seen the full extent of human elevation and how man is cleaved to the Blessed One through the secret of the "Image and Likeness," connected to Him through the Torah and the choice given to him. The purpose of man has been clarified: to achieve eternity. I have elaborated on this in this precious introduction, which I have titled **Toledot Adam** (The Generations of Man). May this set your hearts aflame to love the Lord with all your heart, soul, and might. May my words in this excellent introduction remain close to you as a "reminder between your eyes." Then, "the candle of the commandment and the light of the Torah, which is the way of life," shall not depart from your mouths. For this introduction is the opening and the gate to enter the "Structure of the Second House" <note>likely the second part of his book</note>, to study His Torah, fulfill the commandments, and clothe yourselves in fine character traits. These are the matters I will mention, with God's help, in the coming chapters. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, O Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer. You are my God; with Your help, I begin, and You shall complete it for me.

# The Great House
<meta>catchword: Mem (מ"ם)</meta>

<margin>
We have hinted at the two letters *Resh* (ר) and *Mem* (מ) <note>original: "ר'מ"; possibly referring to the word 'Ram' meaning exalted</note> as a reference to the *Shekhinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note>, which is called a *Sukkah* <note>a ritual booth</note>. It is both circular and square; the circle indicates *Chesed* <note>Loving-kindness</note> and the square indicates *Din* <note>Judgment</note>. This is why the word *Sukkah* <note>spelled Samekh-Khaf-He</note> has a numerical value <note>gematria</note> related to 26 and 26 <note>the value of the Divine Name YHVH is 26; the author may be using a specific mystical calculation here</note>. See above where I concluded the matter of the two *Mems*... regarding the 29 winds and the matter of the tax-collector... for the Sukkah depends on the point of the letter *Bet* (ב), which is also a great hint...
</margin>

<margin>
Reference: S.G.P.
However, at the end of the word, the world will be a "limit" to the miracle... for a moment, seven by seven in order... the world is currently square.
</margin>

We hinted [at the verse], "because of the enemy" <note>Lamentations 2:3</note>. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, "withdrew His right hand" which was open to receive those who return in repentance, because they did not repent out of love, but only "because of the enemy"—that is, out of fear. And then the destructive "horns" were cut down in a square over the circle. This is the secret of the verse, "And the daughter of Zion is left like a booth (*Sukkah*) in a vineyard." In my earlier remarks, I hinted at this through the word *Sukkah* (סכה), and through this hint, the laws of the Sukkah walls are explained.

The ideal performance of the commandment requires four walls, though it is valid even with three. The established law (*Halakhah*) is that even two walls and a "tiny bit" of a third are sufficient. The four walls hint at the four "fortresses" I mentioned: Repentance (*Teshuvah*), Prayer (*Tefillah*), Charity (*Tzedakah*), and Torah. Corresponding to this is the letter *Samekh* (ס) of the word *Sukkah*, which surrounds and encompasses every side. However, there are some in Israel who are not "sons of Torah" <note>unlearned</note> but have a heart to understand; they hold onto two walls, which are the three fortresses of Repentance, Prayer, and Charity. Corresponding to this are the letters *Khaf* (כ) and *He* (ה) of the word *Sukkah*, which surround three sides <note>The letter Khaf is shaped like three sides of a square</note>. 

Yet sometimes there are those who cannot even hold onto two [virtues], for they are not masters of Torah and they are also poor and cannot give charity; they then hold onto two walls, which are the two fortresses of Repentance and Prayer, which every person of Israel can fulfill. Furthermore, they add a "tiny bit" of the third, which means giving a very small amount, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "Even a poor person who receives charity must give a little charity himself." Corresponding to this is the letter *He* (ה) from the word *Sukkah*, which consists of two walls and a tiny bit <note>The letter He is made of two main lines and a small detached stroke</note. This is the law: "Two [walls] according to their standard, and the third even a tiny bit."

Behold, *Sukkah* and the "Fear of the Lord" share a connection... but "Through wisdom a house is built" <note>Proverbs 24:3</note>. The explanation according to the Kabbalists is that the large letter *Bet* (ב) of the word *Bereshit* <note>Genesis/In the Beginning</note> hints at Wisdom (*Chokhmah*)... and this is a "permanent house." As I hinted, the *Bet* of *Bereshit* hints at the Square, which later, upon the giving of the Torah, becomes a closed *Samekh* (ס). Then, at the time of the Redemption, the "Blessing of the Ten" will be fulfilled, for there is no redemption unless they perform complete repentance. Then prayer will be [answered], as it is written: "And I will make them joyful in My house of prayer"—the secret of cleaving and binding to the Divine. Then there shall be no more needy, and this is the secret of Kindness and Charity, for kindness applies to both the poor and the rich. Torah study will increase and be fulfilled, as "the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord." All of this is the secret of the letter *Bet* becoming a closed *Samekh*. Then it will be a "faithful house."

However, the *Sukkah* hints at the diminished and external state, about which it is said: "And the daughter of Zion is left like a *Sukkah*." Therefore, the *Bet* of *Bereshit* is large, while the *He* of *Be-hibare'am* <note>Genesis 2:4, "when they were created"</note> is small, as our Sages said: "He created them with the letter He." For the letter *Bet* has lines, and the letter *Chet* (ח) has three lines. The lines of the *Bet* hint at "there shall be no needy among you," while the lines of the *He* hint at "the needy shall never cease from the land." Everything depends on the abundance of one's actions. It is now clear why you must not substitute a *Samekh* (ס) for a [Final] *Mem* (ם). 

Behold, our Sages said that the letters *Samekh* (ס) and the Final *Mem* (ם) in the Tablets of the Ten Commandments stood there by a miracle <note>Since these letters are entirely closed, the center of the stone should have fallen out when carved through; their remaining in place was miraculous</note>. For *Samekh* and *Mem* both hint at that exalted matter... and the Final *Mem* is also holy. It is as they said: "A person should always occupy himself with Torah even if not for its own sake, for from 'not for its own sake' he will come to 'for its own sake'." But during the destruction of the Temple, because they did not act for its own sake, it is said: "She has become a tributary (*Lamas*)" <note>Lamentations 1:1</note>. The letters of *Lamas* (למס) contain the *Mem* and the *Samekh*. Do not wonder why the *Mem* in the word *Lamas* is "open" (מ) and not "closed" (ם); know that this is the secret of the walls of Jerusalem being breached. An "open" *Mem* appears in place of a "closed" one because "the breacher has gone up" and opened it. This is the meaning of "She has become a tributary (*Lamas*)": their deeds were "because of the enemy" (out of fear), which is the letter *Samekh*, and they never reached the level of the "closed" *Mem*. Instead, it became "open"—meaning breached and open to the outside. 

This is the secret of the *Masveh* <note>the veil</note> of Moses. When Israel sinned [with the Golden Calf], they could not look at the face of Moses. This began with the Calf and the destruction of the Tabernacle and the Tablets, and it continues in every generation, as it is said: "There is no visitation [of sin] that does not contain some punishment for the Calf." This continued until the destruction of the Temple. Then, due to our many sins, the judgments were [aroused]... and when the Tablets were broken, the miracle of the *Samekh* and the *Mem* was hidden, and the "closed" became "breached." This is the secret of the *Masveh* which separated [the people] from seeing the radiant face... this is the "Tax" (*Mas*)... this is the "veil" (*Masveh*)... and this is "How does the city sit solitary... she has become a tributary (*Lamas*)." I have already written at length regarding the hint that the Serpent (*Nachash*) had a letter *Vav* added to it... causing the Name to be incomplete. This will be repaired in the future.

---

<margin>
Reference: S.N.S.
This hint refers to the secret of the walls of the Sukkah... which is the secret of the circle... in order to be purified to cleave to the Supernal House, of which it is said, "In all My house he is faithful," and you shall enter into my place...
</margin>

**He said** afterward that one should not substitute a *Mem* for a *Samekh*, as they hint at the receiving of reward for the Torah and the refinement of deeds. This is according to what is written in the book *Avodat Ha-Kodesh* <note>a 16th-century kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, part 3, regarding eternal existence in the future. They said at the end of Tractate *Taanit*: "Rabbi Helbo said in the name of Ulla... in the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will arrange a dance (*Mahol*) for the righteous in the Garden of Eden, and He will sit among them, and each one will point to Him with his finger, as it says: 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He will save us...'" 

In the future, the Holy One will be the "head of the dance" for the righteous. The word for dance, *Mahol*, is related to the word for "pardon" and "circle." Each one will point with a finger... for the Lord will lead us eternally... in worlds that come one after another... the translation of Aquila <note>a famous convert and translator of the Bible into Greek</note> renders this as "a world where there is no death." 

The explanation of the "Sukkah," the "Dance" (*Mahol*), and the "Circle" is that a circle has no beginning or end. This is a parable for the delight that has no end or limit. Therefore, after the Resurrection of the Dead, it is called "a world that is entirely good, a world that is entirely long." Then the righteous will reach the ultimate perception, for the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is in the center and they are all around. This is the "Dance." To hint at this wondrous perception, they said: "Each one points with his finger." Thus, the circle indicates a thing that goes around and around without end. We find that the matter is "a circle within a square" and "a square within a circle." In this world, the "world of action," the square is superior to the circle and therefore encompasses it. But in the future "world of reward," the square will be within the circle, for the circle indicates eternity.

### Bent [letters] and Straight [letters]
This can be explained through the "Darderki" homily <note>lessons for young schoolchildren mentioned in the Talmud</note>: A "bent" *Nun* (נ) [represents] a faithful person who is bowed; a "straight" *Nun* (ן) [represents] a faithful person who is straightened. There is "open" and there is "closed"; a "bent" *Tzadi* (צ) and a "straight" *Tzadi* (ץ). Therefore, one should not substitute one for the other.

### Closed [sections] and Open [sections]

<margin>
Reference: S.G.S.
According to the explanation above regarding the "closed" Mem and Samekh... according to the secret... for the King, His acquisitions are hinted at in the "closed" place... to the Assembly of Israel... the open to the open, and the closed to the closed.
</margin>

This is also explained through the "Darderki" homily: an "open" statement and a "closed" statement. Rashi explains: "There are things which one is permitted to expound (open), and there are things you are commanded to keep hidden (closed), such as the Work of the Chariot <note>Ma'aseh Merkavah, or deep mysticism</note>." It is clear to me that they hinted at this with the two letters *Samekh-Samekh*... for how could we find other words for the thousands of *Mems*?

---

Regarding the "faithful bent" and "faithful straight," or the "righteous bent" and "righteous straight," this further indicates the perfection of the letters... as written in the *Pardes* <note>likely *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note>. Four letters indicate the unity of the Name *Y-H-V-H*, and their testimony is a "double seal," a "seal within a seal." The letter *Mem* (מ) contains an *Aleph* above, a *Yod* below, and a *Vav* in the middle, which equals 26 <note>the value of YHVH</note>... this is the shape of the *Khaf*... and above stands a *Vav* upon it, making 27. The *Mem* has a shape with three sides, and so does the "closed" *Samekh*, except that it was closed by the *Vav*. 

The "seal within a seal" refers to the letter *Aleph* (א), which hints at the power of the *Lamed* (ל)... and the *Lamed* hints at the power of the *Mem* (מ)... Now I will explain the matter: *Aleph-Lamed-Mem* hints at the reality of *Atzilut* <note>the world of Divine Emanation</note>. The *Mem* hints at that which is revealed from *Atzilut* to our side. How so? The *Aleph* hints at the *Yod* which includes all of *Atzilut* as it is revealed. The *Lamed* hints at the Name *Y-H-V-H* as it is hidden... for it is known that the *Lamed* is the "tower flying in the air"... Thus, the letters *Aleph-Lamed* hint at *Atzilut* in both its hidden and revealed states.

# Ten Sayings

He also spoke to multiply and enlarge the matter, for it is wondrous and a great wisdom. This refers to what he will say afterward: that this power will be granted to a prophet "under the sun," for the Supernal Will has come to grant its heavenly revelations, and the Great Name shall return to its glory. To me, this wisdom—which I have understood more deeply than I had grasped until now from wisdom and kingship—is great. This is because "breath" <note>Hebrew: *Hevel*, often translated as vanity, but here used mystically</note> has returned to the purpose of this rectification. Therefore, this goal was greater than all that came before it to assist the intention. When he says, "and it is great to me," it is a praise and Hallel <note>song of praise</note> to himself for [understanding] the secret and the "Correction of the Glory," which is the Secret of Unity and a great wisdom. For this reason, he described himself by the name "wise," as will be explained.

Such Hallel and praise are permitted to him because they involve the knowledge of the Lord, as it is written: "But let him who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows Me" <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>. This has already been discussed. Now he comes to reveal the secret, which is his saying: "There was a small city and few men in it; and a great king came against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:14</note>.

In the *Midrash Rut HaNe'elam* <note>The "Hidden Ruth," a mystical commentary found in the Zohar</note>, they spoke in this language: 
"A small city" refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*; the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>, which is called the Holy City <note>original: *Karta Kadisha*</note> in relation to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said: "My dove, my undefiled, is but one" <note>Song of Songs 6:9</note>. It is called "small" because of the sin of Adam, the first man, which caused the Presence to dwell within it and then depart. Noah came and brought it down to earth; the generation of the Flood came and it departed from the world. Shem his son came and brought it down; the generation of the Dispersion came and it departed from the world. Thus it says, "and few men in it." Abraham came and brought it down; the people of his generation came and it departed. And so it was with all of them; therefore, "few men were in it" to remain with it in the world. From a "few" it did not endure, nor from many. 

"And a great king came against it"—who is this "Great King"? This is the Holy One, Blessed be He, the King to whom peace belongs. Why did He "besiege it"? To be its guardian from all sides, as it is said: "For I, saith the Lord, will be unto her a wall of fire round about" <note>Zechariah 2:9</note>. "And built great bulwarks against it"—what are these "bulwarks"? They are the punishments of the Torah, the decrees, and the fines of the Torah, which act as a siege and as high fortresses to catch the guilty who sin and transgress the commandments of the Torah. 

"And there was found in it a poor wise man" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:15</note>—this is the King who gazes upon all the inhabitants of the world and found no man in the world who would stand with her <note>the Assembly of Israel</note> and occupy himself with her... except for a "poor man." And who is he? This is King David, who said: "For I am poor and needy" <note>Psalm 109:22</note>. And the "wise man" is King Solomon. It does not say "a man poor and wise" <note>implying one person</note> but "poor and wise" <note>connecting two figures</note>, for there was none in the whole world who busied themselves after her except for the son of David who is "poor" and Solomon who is "wise." One [David] prepared the lamp, and the other [Solomon] illuminated it with light. 

"And he by his wisdom delivered the city"—for he established "ears" for the Torah <note>original: *oznayim la-Torah*; a metaphor for making the Torah accessible or providing "handles" to grasp its meaning</note>. For we have learned that before Solomon, the Torah was like a basket without handles <note>original: *kaltat d'leit lah oznayim*</note>, and whoever approached it would be burned. Once Solomon came, he made handles for it, and the inhabitants of the world were saved. He gave the city "rests" <note>so to speak</note> and greatness through his wisdom and the rectifications he established. He labored in the Torah. The "poor man" is the King [David] because there was no man who labored after her like King David. 

This is the secret of the verse: "And David made himself a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>, for he rectified the Glory. "The Lord of Hosts" rectified the lamp which was heavier than the lamp of the past through his Torah and his deeds, as it is said in the first chapter of *Berakhot*: Rabbi Assi said, "Until midnight he was occupied with the Torah; from then on, with songs and praises." And his reward was that he was "fixing and making the Name" <note>establishing the Divine reputation or presence</note>. He became the "fourth leg" of the Chariot <note>original: *Merkavah*; the vision of the Divine Throne</note>, completing it. Concerning this, it was said to him: "And I will make thee a great name, like unto the name of the great men that are in the earth" <note>2 Samuel 7:9</note>. And they said in the chapter *Erev Pesachim*: Rav Joseph taught, this refers to the "Shield of David" <note>the *Magen David*</note>.

Thus, for a person to be rectified in his limbs and his form according to the "Rectification of the Supernal Man" <note>original: *Adam HaElyon*; the primordial spiritual structure of humanity</note>, he has the power to rectify and beautify it. When he completes and does this, the rectification is seen in that very same image that he fixed—it is "kind attracted to kind." When he is found, he is assisted; the Presence comes to him and dwells upon him, for there is no barrier or hindrance on his side, as he has completed what needed to be completed. This is achieved by guarding his actions according to the Torah, straightening his intention, purifying his thoughts, the holiness of his soul, and his cleaving above to the powers included in the Great Name. His wandering thought becomes a messenger of His Glory. 

He thus "likens the form to its Creator." This was the intention of the Sages in *Bereshit Rabbah* and *Kohelet Rabbah*: Rabbi Yudan bar Simon said, "Great is the power of the prophets, for they liken the form to its Creator." As it is written: "And I heard a man's voice between the banks of Ulai" <note>Daniel 8:16</note>. Rabbi Judah bar Simon said, "There is another verse that is clearer than this: 'And upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it'" <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>.

I say that it has already been clarified that when it says, "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him," the intention is not the physical body that comes from a "putrid drop" <note>a humble biological origin</note> according to the secret of the "Garment." That is merely the "flesh of man," not the "Man" himself. As it is written: "Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh" <note>Job 10:11</note>. If skin and flesh are the clothing of man, then the "True Man" is the internal spirit and the form within it. 

To indicate this, the letters of the word **ADAM** (אדם) hint at the entire emanation from beginning to end:
- The **Aleph** (א) hints at the beginning of existence in the secret of the "High Loftiness" <note>original: *Rum Ma'alah*</note>.
- The **Mem** (מ) refers to the "Closed Mem" <note>final Mem</note> of the Chariot.
- The **Dalet** (ד) refers to the secret of the letter *Dalet* in the word "One" <note>original: *Echad*; the declaration of Divine Unity</note>.

Thus, the letters of **ADAM** include everything above and below. This is the secret of the form of the lower man being like the form of the Supernal Man. It is known from the secrets of the Inner Wisdom that as the Supernal Powers are included and unified with one another, so too when rectification rises from below through the line of deeds and the awakening of the soul, the Supernal Inner Soul is included with them and dwells in them like a soul in a body. Everything is in one unique Unity. This is comparable to a body and soul which are one thing without separation. 

When a perfect person completes the requirements of the body and the internal spirit within it—each as is fitting—through the purity of deeds, righteousness, logic, Torah, and commandments, with the desired internal spiritual intention turned always toward the Hidden Unity, then the form is arranged in all this and guarded from every blemish and external distraction. In this way, it resembles its Creator, the secret of the Supernal Form. This is the "Whole of Man" above. For the reality of the secret of the Torah, with all the secrets of the Service and Unity, is engraved in its form. From there they came and were given, and the desired intention in them is their place and source, for everything comes from there and everything returns there. 

Thus, form is to the likeness of form. This is called **ADAM** and that is called **ADAM**, and each is included in the other. He who fills his hand and completes his form has likened his form to its Creator and found "kind joining its kind." He is assisted because there is no barrier or delay as he hopes toward the heights with the powers included in the Great Name. Since he occupies himself with His building—which is the Secret of Unity—God also unifies His Name upon him and rests His Presence in him and in his powers. 

This is the meaning of the statement: "Great is the power of the prophets who liken the form to their Creator." Rabbi Yudan brought proof from what Daniel said: "And I heard a man's voice between the banks of Ulai," and it is written, "Gabriel, make this man to understand the vision." This "Man" is the Man in the Chariot of Ezekiel the prophet. From Him, the voice extended to Gabriel, who spoke with Daniel. Daniel did not perceive the "Man" himself, only the voice, for he did not say "I saw" but "I heard." Although he perceived Gabriel, he did not perceive the Man in the Chariot. 

Since there is no "clear" proof from this verse that they "liken the form to its Creator"—as this "Man" might be a created being of the World of Formation <note>original: *Yetzirah*</note> and not part of the Unity, and Daniel is not counted among the [primary] prophets—Rabbi Judah brought a verse where the proof is clearer, from a prophet [Ezekiel]: "And upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it." 

The internal secret is that the "final He" (ה) [of the Name] is "Adam" when it is in unity with what is above it. The secret of the letter Vav (ו) is the "Supernal Man." The "Two Faces" <note>original: *Du-Partzufin*</note> together are called **ADAM**. This is why it says "above upon it"—meaning specifically with what is above it. This is the Creator, blessed be He, and the prophets liken the form to Him, for He is the Creator.

Furthermore, there is a wondrous matter in this statement: they want to establish for us a true teaching regarding the perception of the prophets, that it is clean and pure from all confusion or error. The secret is that although their perception involves this "Man" we hinted at, they do not err in believing that he is an independent power—God forbid that true and righteous prophets would think so, as Elisha ben Abuyah <note>the apostate "Acher"</note> erred. Rather, they perceive him and know that the True Authority is "above upon it," as in the matter of "one high official watched by a higher" <note>Ecclesiastes 5:8</note>. 

Because the matter is not fully explained by the verse Rabbi Yudan brought, Rabbi Judah said there is another verse more "clear" through which we can stand upon the secret: "And upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man." Although they change this appearance, they know the matter does not end there, but the True Authority is "above upon it." This is what they meant by "Great is the power of the prophets who liken the form to its Creator"—meaning they liken and attach that form which they perceive in their prophecy to its Creator. They know this [form] is an effect, and above it is its Cause. They do not err to believe it is an independent authority, heaven forbid, for their true wisdom, clean of all dross and filth, warned them and guarded them from this. For they are always enflamed in the courts of the King of the Universe and are accepted in His palace. Their comings and goings are known, and they recognize the "Forms of the Decrees" in every inner and outer palace. They accept that all are His ministers and servants, doing His will—small and great alike, all guard His watch. Nothing is confused for them, and they do not exchange the later for the earlier. Added to this, their righteousness and piety protect them, as it is written: "No mischief shall happen to the righteous" <note>Proverbs 12:21</note> and "He will keep the feet of His holy ones" <note>1 Samuel 2:9</note>. 

Thus ends the quote from the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>"Service of the Holy," a classic 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> that has been explained. Israel are called **ADAM**, and they are the servants of the Lord who were created like the "First Man" (*Adam Kadmaa*) to serve the Lord and to guard it, which is the fulfillment of the Torah, as the Sages explained in the Midrash...

# Ten Sayings
