->I begin the chapter of the Ten Sayings with the help of the Creator of the Luminaries.<-

## Through Ten

**Sayings** <note>original: *Ma'amarot*; often referring to the ten utterances through which the world was created</note> we shall clarify the service of man, who is the world. They are all included in one single saying, which is the "True One," the "One" whose unity is unique unlike any other, blessed and exalted be He. Now, I will hint at how these ten sayings are made and how they are all contained within a single saying; afterward, I will explain them according to the good hand of the Lord upon me. 

**First Saying:** The Lord is One. 
**Second Saying:** Israel is one nation. 
**Third Saying:** Inner fear and love. 
**Fourth Saying:** Servants of the Lord; the explanation of service as a "supernal need" to bring joy <note>The Kabbalistic idea that human actions provide "sustenance" or joy to the Divine realms</note>. 
**Fifth Saying:** Eternal service; explained as service within every measure <note>original: *middah*; refers to both character traits and the Divine attributes/Sefirot</note> that the Holy One measures out. 
**Sixth Saying:** The essence of service is in the heart. 
**Seventh Saying:** The gate of character traits. 
**Eighth Saying:** The cleaving of the heart in all the ways of its Beloved. 
**Ninth Saying:** Purity of thought within the heart. 
**Tenth Saying:** The Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> in the heart.

**The Explanation** of the Sayings: How they hang one upon the other like a chain and are linked together like the branches of a Menorah. In the first chapter of Tractate Berakhot, Rabbi Isaac said to Rav Hiyya bar Abin: "Those phylacteries <note>original: *Tefillin*</note> of the Master of the World, what is written in them?" He replied: "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?" Does the Holy One, blessed be He, really take pride in the praise of Israel? Yes, for it is written: "You have affirmed the Lord this day," and it is written: "And the Lord has affirmed you this day" <note>Deuteronomy 26:17-18</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: "You have made Me a single unit <note>original: *hativah*</note> in the world, and I shall make you a single unit in the world. You have made Me a single unit in the world as it is said: 'Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.' And I shall make you a single unit in the world as it is said: 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth.'"

The matter follows what I presented in the introduction to *The Generations of Man* regarding the subject of "Let us make man in our image" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. For the man below contains signs and hints of the likeness of the "Man Above" who sits upon the Throne. From the reality of His truth, there emerge matters and inner concepts that are extremely subtle and spiritual; these are the "sections of the Chariot" <note>original: *Perkei HaMerkavah*; the structure of the Divine realm</note> through which light and abundance spread to sustain this existing world, which is made in His likeness. They are called "hands," "feet," "eyes," and "ears"—not that the essence of a [Divine] hand is like a physical hand, or the form of a hand is like a human shape, Heaven forbid! For it is written: "To whom then will you liken God?" <note>Isaiah 40:18</note>. There is no comparison at all between Him and us in terms of essence or form. 

Rather, man was fashioned and made in this likeness so that if he merits to purify one of his limbs and perfect it through the commandment <note>mitzvah</note> dependent upon it, that limb will become like a "Chariot" and a "Throne of Glory" for that inner Supernal Heart. If it is an eye, it corresponds to the Eye; if a hand, the Hand; if a foot, the Foot; and so with the other limbs. One must understand our words and my speech, for regarding this it was said: "A limb supports a limb." For the complete man, who perfects himself for his Creator, being rectified in his deeds and his Torah and the purity of his limbs—he rectifies and establishes all his limbs and his form in the likeness of the "Great Man" <note>original: *Adam HaGadol*; the cosmic/divine structure</note>. Every limb in which he fulfills its specific commandment is then in the likeness of that Supernal limb. 

By this, a man preserves his "Image" and his likeness to the Supernal Likeness. When he completes all his limbs through the perfection of the commandments and their beauty, he becomes a Chariot and a Throne of Glory for the Supernal Form. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "The Patriarchs—they themselves are the Chariot." For Abraham [perfected himself] to be a chariot for the "Right," the secret of the attribute of Loving-kindness <note>original: *Hesed*</note>, because he performed its actions, purified and sanctified himself, and preserved his form. He made the "hand" of his form like the holy archetype. He "borrowed" <note>or "attached"</note> his blood/vitality when we say "my days, my hands" to the Lord, the Most High God. This is revealed to us in one of his limbs to draw an analogy to the rest of his parts, for the Lord added [a letter] to his name to complete his limbs <note>Reference to Abram becoming Abraham, where the letter 'He' numerically completes the perfection of his 248 limbs</note> so that all of them were pure and holy. Thus, he became a chariot for the attribute of Loving-kindness, for he fulfilled its commandment and walked in its ways. 

In this same way, Isaac [attained] the attribute of Fear <note>original: *Pahad*; the attribute of Gevurah/Strength</note> and became a chariot for it, and so did Jacob for the attribute of Truth <note>original: *Emet/Tiferet*</note>. And David, may peace be upon him, conducted his kingdom as was proper, as it is written of him: "And David made a name for himself." Thus, he was worthy to become the "fourth leg" of the Chariot <note>Completing the throne supported by the three Patriarchs</note>. Whoever perfects his form in the way I have written will ascend to the level of prophecy; he strips off his physical form, the spiritual form returns, and he dons the spiritual form which he has rectified and attained. That form is the "Form of Man" which he rectified and completed through the secret of: "And by the hand of the prophets I have used similitudes" <note>Hosea 12:11; original: *adameh*, related to *Adam* (man) and *domeh* (likeness)</note>. This is the secret of the "Man sitting upon the Throne," the secret of the final letter *He*. 

In *Bereshit Rabbah* (Chapter 26), Rabbi Yudan said: "Great is the power of the prophets, who liken the form to its Creator," as it is said: "And I heard the voice of a man (*Adam*) between the banks of the Ulai" <note>Daniel 8:16</note>. Rabbi Yudan bar Simon said: "There is another verse even more explicit: 'And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man (*Adam*) above upon it'" <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>. This is the secret of what is written: that the prophets rectify and complete their structure to match the structure of the "Great Man" and establish the secret of His form upon its base. This is the secret of those who liken their form to the form of the Chariot, and both of them <unclear>merited</unclear> the levels of prophecy that flow from that Form which they completed. <note>The text suggests that the prophet's own perfected "form" allows them to receive Divine transmission.</note> Because likening the form to its Creator is a great and proper thing—to empower the intellect over the material—who is he that is happy and <unclear>successful</unclear>? For this reason, he said "great is their power." 

In the verse Rabbi Yudan brought, the matter is not fully explained, as one might say it was the "voice of a man" and not a man himself. Furthermore, it does not say "and I saw." Moreover, that was a vision from the "separate supernal beings" <note>angels</note>, for Daniel did not reach the full level of prophecy. Therefore, Rabbi Yudan brought a verse from Ezekiel where the matter is clarified further. 

Furthermore, the author of the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>The Holy Service, by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> added in the first chapter of the section "The Crown of Torah": "It has already been explained in this book that the 'Little Man' <note>term: <term>Microcosm</term>: The human being as a miniature version of the universe</note> was rectified according to the rectification of the 'Great Man' in order to unify the Great Name in His Glory. The Divine Will desired his creation so that this person would be an 'appointed officer' to rectify the Glory through his rectified deeds. Thus, everything included in the Supernal Glory is included in him. The Supernal is above and the lower is below, one corresponding to the other, glorifying and rectifying the Glory. This is the secret of: 'Every one that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him' <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>." 

Since the lower man is inclusive of everything in the "Supernal Man"—for in him everything is called by the name "All" <note>original: *Kol*; often associated with the Sefirah of Yesod</note>—for the Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds, rectifies and establishes his world above and is called "All" because everything is within him. So too, the righteous one below, in rectifying and establishing this world, is within the secret of "The Righteous is the foundation of the world" <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>. He is called "All" by His name because he is <unclear>engaged</unclear> in the building of the Supernal world here below in the likeness of the Righteous One Above. It is fitting, therefore, that he be called by His name, and this is the secret of "Every one that is called by My name." This is also the secret of the verse: "And he called him 'El,' the God of Israel" <note>Genesis 33:20</note>. 

Afterward, he revealed the reason: "For My glory I have created him, I have formed him, yea, I have made him." The reason he is called by His name is that he includes within himself everything that is in the Supernal Glory. Behold, within him are [the worlds of] Creation (*Beriyah*), Formation (*Yetzirah*), and Action (*Asiyah*). This is in order to rectify the Lower Glory—the Glory of the Lord. The lower man has within him Creation, Formation, and Action so that he too may rectify that Glory from below. Behold, through him, the Great Name is unified in His Glory. For this reason, his limbs are arranged with wondrous precision to hint at the limbs of the Chariot. When he sanctifies and purifies his limbs below, that rectification ascends above and rectifies the corresponding Form. Through this, the Great Name is exalted by the deeds of the righteous, who, according to their level, rectify the Glory. They are literally in that same high rank below, and thus the Righteous One is literally called by His name. 

This is the secret of what is said in the chapter "One who reads the Megillah": Rabbi Aha said in the name of Rabbi Eleazar: "From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, called Jacob 'El'? As it says: 'And he called him El, the God of Israel.' Who called Jacob 'El'? The God of Israel." This is because our father Jacob, may peace be upon him, is the "Living Truth," the secret of the "Torah of Truth," the "Elder Israel" <note>original: *Yisrael Saba*; a high spiritual configuration</note>. He rectifies and beautifies the Glory above. So too Jacob below, in the secret of "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>, bore His name and He called him "El." The secret is as the Sages said: "The Patriarchs, they themselves are the Chariot," for they rectified the Glory below, and every limb became a throne and a holy dwelling for the Shekhinah. 

The people who reach this level are few, aside from the prophets and those possessed of the Holy Spirit. When King Solomon, may peace be upon him, contemplated this wondrous secret, he said: "This also I have seen as wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:13</note>. And regarding this he said:

To his eyes and for the life of his eyes—for the Holy One is as if [mirrored] in the likeness, and he is the Holy One, and he is the one who cleaves to the secret of the "Image" <note>original: *dyokan*; referring to the Divine form or blueprint of humanity</note>. However, if he behaves [poorly] with it, he is like an ape before a human. When he cleaves to their secret, to the angel who is the end of the nose and the heat <note>likely an anatomical-mystical reference to the breath of life or the "countenance"</note>, for this reason, choice was given to him. If you ask: if the purpose of this creation was for the Creator to do good for us for the sake of His glory, why the creation of man, who is a vessel that knows and recognizes His will? Both the celestial bodies and the elements, according to what they are, are living and intelligent beings. However, regarding the inanimate things like the stones, etc., and the elements, etc., what good reaches them? If you say that the individual was created for His own glory, as if He requires honor for Himself by creating in His poverty and His lowliness...

Even this is difficult. The answer to the matter is that the ultimate purpose of this creation is Man. Everything in detail exists for him. It is impossible to say [otherwise]—that they exist for their own sake. This entire creation was created by the Holy One, blessed be He, and everything is for the sake of Man. This is what the Rambam <note>Maimonides, the 12th-century philosopher</note> says in his introduction to the Order of Seeds <note>original: *Seder Zeraim*; the first part of the Mishnah</note>: They said that even the actions of the Holy One have only one purpose... If a person looks at this superficially, he will find it very far from the truth. As if, for example, for the sake of one stalk of wheat alone, the celestial sphere and the heavens and the wisdoms and the distinct sciences were created? If you look into this matter, you will find within it a wonderful kind of wisdom. Know that the ancients investigated with a deep inquiry, using the vision that time and the quality of thought granted them, until it was established for them that every existing thing must have a purpose for its existence; for things are not created in vain. When this general law was established for them in truth, to know the purpose of every created thing, they saw that every thing that is a "work" <note>meaning something fashioned or functional</note> has its purpose in the knowledge of its fashioning. Not all who investigate know the "work" unless its purpose is clarified within the human soul. Every creature and its work, its form, its engraving, and its natural wisdom—such as the species of plants and those that are gathered, and the species of minerals and the types of stones, and the species of animals—there are those whose purpose of existence is hidden and no one knows it at all, until it becomes known through experience in the future. In the investigation of the intellect, if it were not for the experience that says one knows the purpose of the thing, the internal forms would remain hidden within the bodies.

# The First Saying
->**It is the saying "The Lord is One," the root of all matters.**<-

The perfection and knowledge of the day, and "taking it to your heart that the Lord is God" [Deuteronomy 4:39]. This means knowledge in the heart through demonstrative proof, in addition to the tradition <note>original: *kabbalah*; here meaning the received tradition passed from generation to generation</note> from our fathers. As the author of *The Duties of the Heart* <note>Rabbi Bahya ibn Paquda</note> elaborated in the "Gate of Unity," this is hinted at in the verse: "Know the God of your father" [I Chronicles 28:9]. This means that in addition to the established faith in "the God of your father"—which is the tradition of one man from the mouth of another—you must also "Know the God of your father," meaning know through calculation and reason. This is the hint of the verse: "And you shall know this day and return it to your heart that the Lord is God." This means knowledge in the heart, which is demonstrative knowledge. This is the intention of the saying of the tradition brought by the author of *The Duties of the Heart*: when the investigation of the God of your father and our ancestors comes into your hand, it is proper that you should know Him with absolute knowledge in your heart and the understanding of the heart, for "the Lord is God... and you shall know this day and return it to your heart." Strength, knowledge, and intelligence will enlighten the eyes of both.

And from there, there are those with wings and those with tongues, those that crawl and those that walk on legs, and those with few legs. And what was mentioned: this is the law of birth. This is found in all things from the celestial spheres down to man. Their action is more revealed. Indeed, in knowing the purpose of their creation, the excellence of the wise in wisdom is seen. And the Sages said: "Who is the one who is more wise and great? The one who considers your handiwork." For his knowledge is like the thought of the king, and they are the work of his hands, and he made them to exalt His name, and through this, he will merit the eternal kingdom in the fear of heaven and the intention of the heart. There is a witness forever that the spirit of God is in him... to know the existence from the aspect of the celestial sphere. For the sake of the sun, they were created for the purpose of man, so that there would be some among them to serve him and to guide him, like the ox and the donkey. And there are some whose benefit is like the medicinal herbs that are combined, as they said to the spices and the heavens. They traveled a long way for us... those who lack knowledge have a rebuke; there is a benefit in them for man. Through the clarification of their nature, the mixtures, and the compositions, they are for our healing, and from them we cleave to Him. This is what was said: "What is this that is found among the animals and the plants?" For they have no speech and no movement, because the power of the soul is arranged for them. Therefore, everything that He made, every single species of the animals until the degree where they have a desire for the heavens, and the animals that are above them. For in every generation and generation, it grows according to the wisdom and the eyes of the existence. This was revealed to our ancestors, and there is benefit in them. He did not destroy the foundations of the world’s existence. Everything that was called "nature" is a way of sight which remains close. But if you say: Why were they created in such great numbers? You have no way of knowing their benefit unless you look at the wandering of those who were made by God, to prevent the wandering of those who would mistake them. Regarding the ape, I have written a great answer...

**And since** they found from the philosophers our God of the portions, these celestial beings... for they alone are said to be like the sun in the head of the soul. For the actors, as we have explained, are seen in their kindness; they do not have one single actor because they are said to be in the "seals" <note>patterns of reality</note>. When an existence is found from what is known alone, as we said, and whoever makes it... it is for the generation of the receipt of souls in a simple time. But man achieves many deeds in his existence. From this, we move toward all His actions. He acted like a master of existence to know the purpose of His creation from these actions. And they found that their purpose is one single action. And in His intention, they were created to be more than him, so that his existence would be in order that they might serve that one Action, which is the return [to God].

This is the end of the imagery of the secrets... that knowledge was given for eating, drinking, and for protection from the elements. It would have been better for him to be a king. For every man who puts his mind to it will not add to his strength through them... he is satisfied with the abundance of choice and the joy that is added to his internal strength. He moved him from a downfall in this to the excellence of glory... and man is a known foundation of this, as in the heavens. He was not included in the downfall of the species of animals, but in his logic—meaning in his reason—he plays with the abundance of choices to visualize the secrets of the Holy One, blessed be He. And all the greatness regarding this matter is the chain of the order of the sciences. The purpose of man’s existence is that he should have from them the knowledge of the heavens... all the wise who did not [attain this]...

<meta>This page continues the transition from the philosophical necessity of Man's creation to the practical and mystical application of that purpose. It introduces the "Ten Sayings" as a framework for spiritual development, moving from basic fear and love of God to the highest levels of sanctification in the physical world.</meta>

# Ten Sayings

The goal is for a person to have the fear of his Master upon him and to love Him. Therefore, the discourse on internal fear and love follows the "Sayings" concerning the Unity of God <note>original: *Hashem Echad*</note> and the uniqueness of the people of Israel. The power of this discourse ascends higher and higher toward the internal "innermost of the inner" service of fear and love, for the sake of God, following the secret of "Repairing the Name." This is the **Fourth Saying**: when all service is for His sake, may He be blessed, for the "Needs of the High" <note>A Kabbalistic concept suggesting that human actions "complete" or affect the Divine realm</note> and not for one's own needs, whether for a commoner or a prince. One must act with equanimity in whatever circumstance He measures out for him. This is the **Fifth Saying**.

Because a faithful servant who fulfills all his master's needs also handles his master's possessions—his garments, his cloak, and the like—one might think this applies to our service to the Blessed One. However, He is the ultimate Spiritual Being, hidden from every eye. Even the ministering angels ask, "Where is the place of His glory?" Therefore, it is impossible for us to have a "grasp" of Him through our service, except through the service that is entirely through this spirituality. Through it, our "cleaving" <note>term: *Dveikut*—the mystical state of attachment or meditative union with God</note> and service ascend. As the scripture says, "Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a good heart." The explanation is that even if you served God, if that service was not through the awakening of the heart and the enthusiasm of joy in serving Him—through the power of cleaving and labor—it is considered as having many flaws. One must approach every matter as if it were a new *Protogena* <note>original: *protogena*; likely a transliteration of a Greek term for "first-born" or "original/fresh start"</note>, with all one's strength—meaning with full intention. This applies not only to performing positive commandments but even to negative commandments. When one refrains from a prohibited act, it must be with an "awakening" and not like one who is drowsy or idle. As Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel taught: "A person should not say, 'I do not want to eat pig meat,' but rather, 'I want to, but what can I do? My Father in Heaven has decreed it upon me.'" This is the **Sixth Saying**.

The essence of service is in the heart. Then, it is not merely about the specific commandments, namely the 248 explicit "do" commandments, but also about all other character traits that have no fixed measure. Everything depends on the heart, and this is the **Seventh Gate**. Then, the sanctity of the heart extends to all paths. It is not only in matters of ritual purity, but even mundane matters are performed with the sanctity of the holy. This is as Maimonides <note>The 12th-century philosopher and legalist</note> wrote regarding the verse, "In all your ways, know Him." This is the **Eighth Saying**. Then follows the purity of thought, so that one sees no iniquity in his heart and it does not even arise in his thoughts; this is the **Ninth Saying**. Finally, the **Tenth Gate** is "Holy to God"—the Indwelling Presence <note>term: *Shekhinah*—the Divine presence that rests within the world or the individual</note> in the heart. As it is written, "I have set the Lord before me always." Thus the end is joined to the beginning: the Tenth Gate to the First Gate. Now I shall explain the Sayings one by one; they are all hinted at in this verse, the testament of King David, peace be upon him, to his son who was to sit upon his throne:

## "And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him with a whole heart
## and with a willing soul; for the Lord searches all hearts, and understands every plan of the thoughts.
## If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will cast you off forever."

This verse encompasses faith in the Blessed One, the Torah, and the commandments by which a person shall live and achieve eternal life. It includes the sublime character traits and the sanctification of both external and internal limbs, which the sages have discussed at length in their books, such as *The Duties of the Heart* <note>original: *Chovot HaLevavot*; an 11th-century work of Jewish ethics by Bahya ibn Paquda</note> and those who followed him in every generation—its seekers and its leaders. And "last but not least" <note>original: *acharon chaviv*</note>, the author of *The Beginning of Wisdom* <note>original: *Reshit Chokhmah*; a 16th-century Kabbalistic ethical manual</note> and all his holy colleagues. One who walks in their ways is one who follows God. "And you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today." All of this is hinted at in this verse. Reflect upon its ten sanctifications; its general principles are the "Ten Sayings." For the sake of these ten sayings, the world and all worlds were created.

---

<column-break/>

Page 63, section 80.
As it is written: I have written for the collective... to explain what has been handed down. Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created only for His glory, as it is said: "Everyone who is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, indeed I have made him." This can be interpreted in two ways. First, from the perspective of the Holy One, blessed be He: that the Return is one, as it is written "Our King," one Indwelling Presence, and everything is connected to one another. For the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world with blessing and in His great goodness to grant us merit. When our intellect reaches this level, our service becomes—as it were—a "High Need" and gives Him satisfaction when His will is done. Then His Name of Glory is repaired through the secret of the King, whose glory is always the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence. Through the secret of these gates, the Presence and the "Arch" ascend, and "the King of Glory shall enter." Who is this King of Glory? It refers to the matter of service as a "High Need." The master said in one saying: His essence and His Presence are one in the world.

Regarding the ten levels that comprise the truth of the world for the sake of the reward I have set... I have created and made. Even on the good Sabbaths, it is for our merit, so that we may know and recognize Him and become [His] creations. "The crown of Israel arose in thought." This is the meaning of "He created it only for His glory"—meaning so that we might merit to perceive His glory through the power of our merit in Him. This is the internal prophetic dimension...

On these two levels, the righteous are explained. Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world was created only for His glory, for the Perfect One was created to gather and preserve. The essence of service is a "High Need," to cause the King to dwell in glory always. The entire verse is explained by this: "Called by My name," etc. And in the end, all His creation is against these... the end is the ascent of all worlds to the Master, the Presence in His material world. Each "Saying" includes all worlds and the powers of creation. He saw that it would be so, for all created things, from the first point to the last point, are influenced by Him, the Blessed One—the spiritual, vital, internal Source. All of them are emanations from Him.

"Called by My name" refers to the World of Emanation <note>term: *Atziluth*—the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalistic cosmology, representing pure divine light</note>. The reason is that all creations are included in "I have created" (the World of Creation), "I have formed" (the World of Formation), and "I have made" (the World of Action). There is nothing in Creation, Formation, or Action that is not called by some name—the intention for it from the very beginning. As it is written, "And he gave names to all..." until the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "And what is My name?" He replied, "Lord <note>original: *Adonai*</note>, because You are the Lord of all." Our Sages of blessed memory said: "I am the Lord, that is My name"—the name that preceded me to the title of Lord. It is explained that there is nothing in the world that does not have a name by which it is called. "Everyone who is called" includes everything in the world. Creation, Formation, and Action are all "in My name"—meaning in my Emanation. For through emanation, they were created to be My name, because Emanation is the name of the Infinite <note>original: *Ein Sof*; the Boundless Godhead</note>.

Just as a name is the place of one's vitality—as when a word is spoken to one's soul—so too there is no place for any thing except from the aspect of His emanation and the revelation of His power. Therefore, "Everyone who is called by My name" refers to the general principles: "I have created it" refers to the World of Creation <note>term: *Beriah*</note>, "I have formed it" refers to the World of Formation <note>term: *Yetzirah*</note>, and "Indeed I have made it" refers to the World of Action <note>term: *Assiyah*</note>. These are the "garments."

"For My glory I have created it" means to reveal His emanation and glory. I created the world of *Beriah* (Creation) so that there would be a revelation. The word *Beriah* implies "clarifying" that it is for the sake of His glory. "I have formed it" refers to the World of *Yetzirah* (Formation), which is more hidden. And because the revelation of My emanation is not yet complete in the World of Formation, I said, "Indeed I have made it," referring to the World of *Assiyah* (Action). The word "indeed" <note>original: *Af*; in Hebrew, this also means "anger"</note> implies an addition. The World of Action is unique... because in it are many changes. The essence of His greatness and His Presence in the World of Action is among those who change.

There is a second reason for saying "Indeed" (*Af*) regarding the World of Action: *Af* also means anger, wrath, and fury. Because the forces of impurity, the Satan, and the "Other Side" <note>term: *Sitra Achra*—the realm of evil or "outer shells" in Kabbalah</note> clothe themselves in the World of Action, causing all anger and fury in the world, the word *Af* is used there. This is not the case in the two higher worlds, Creation and Formation, where Divine Unity and merit dwell.

This is the secret of the verse: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory." The three "holies" hint at the three holy worlds (Creation, Formation, Emanation). Even in the World of Action—"the earth"—it is "full of His glory" and His providence, for there is nothing outside of His holiness. He said, "Indeed I have made it," for all the work of His hands is exact and etched, unlike the scribes who say that He who created light did not create evil—heaven forbid! Rather, He created everything so that He might be magnified and exalted.

**Behold**, this saying "for His glory" has two interpretations. "For His glory" means through the labor of human service—through the study of Torah, speech, and thought. For this, it was necessary for the Divine to descend into the levels of Creation, Formation, and Action. Man is called "All" because he includes all the emanations. When God saw all that He had made, He saw it was "very good." Man is called "in My name" because the name "Man" <note>Hebrew: *Adam*</note> is hinted at in the Throne. *Adam* also has the numerical value of the Name of God <note>The name *YHVH* expanded with the letter *Aleph* equals 45, the same as *Adam*</note>. "For My glory" means he was conceived in Thought with the blessing of my Father... for Man, in his image and likeness, includes everything: the Soul, the Spirit, and the Breath <note>term: *Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah*—the three primary levels of the soul</note>. The *Neshamah* (Breath) comes from the World of Creation, the *Ruach* (Spirit) from Formation, and the *Nefesh* (Soul) from the World of Action.

# Ten Sayings: First Discourse

If He were to withhold His influence for even a single moment, existence would cease to be. This is the meaning of the verse: "Know today and restore to your heart that the Lord is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is no other" <note>Deuteronomy 4:39</note>. "There is no other" <note>original: *Ein Od*</note> does not merely mean there is no other god besides Him—for that is the plain meaning already revealed in the verse "Hear O Israel... the Lord is One." Rather, it means there is no other *existence* in the world aside from His existence, may He be blessed, for everything exists through His kindness. 

Regarding the statement that He "gave strength and power to [the celestial bodies] to be rulers within the world," the proof actually points to the opposite. It does not say He *appointed* them as rulers, but that He placed "power" <note>original: *koach*</note> within them. This means the power of natural behavior, just as wood is prepared to produce fire when rubbed. This is evidenced by the eye, the ear, and all the limbs, each performing its task through the power of the heavenly system. He gave them "strength and power" only as long as His abundance is flowed into them; they act according to their nature, whether for good or for ill. The matter of "overriding the system" <note>term: *Shiddud ha-Ma’aracha* — a miracle that breaks the natural laws of astrology or nature</note> requires a subtle intellect to understand. 

The following is the text of a tradition: Once, the people of Egypt came to a legal dispute with Israel before Alexander of Macedon <note>Alexander the Great</note>. They said to him, "The Torah says, 'And the Lord gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, and they lent to them' <note>Exodus 12:36</note>. Give us back the silver and gold you took from us!" 

Gabiha ben Pasisa said to the Sages, "Give me permission to go and argue with them before Alexander. If they defeat me, say: 'You have defeated an ignorant man among us.' But if I defeat them, say: 'The Torah of Moses has defeated you.'" They gave him permission. He went and argued with them, asking, "From where do you bring your proof?" They replied, "From the Torah." He said, "I too shall bring proof only from the Torah. It says: 'The residence of the Children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years' <note>Exodus 12:40</note>. Give us the wages for the labor of sixty times ten thousand <note>600,000</note> men whom you enslaved for four hundred and thirty years!" Alexander of Macedon said to the Egyptians, "Give them an answer!" They said, "Give us time." He gave them three days. They searched but found no answer. Immediately, they abandoned their fields and vineyards as they were planted and fled. That year was a Sabbatical year <note>term: *Shemitah* — the seventh year where land is left fallow</note>. This is the end of the account.

<margin>There is</margin> reason to awaken several doubts here. 
**Doubt 1:** Why did the Egyptians wait until the time of Alexander to sue Israel? They could have sued them from the moment they were exiled from their land by the wicked Nebuchadnezzar. One might answer that Israel was poor in exile, whereas they were full of goodness while living on their own land. 
**Doubt 2:** Was Gabiha ben Pasisa the wisest of the wise or not? If he was the wisest, it is obvious he should go; why did he need to say "Give me permission"? If the Sages were wiser than him, how was it just to send him? If he had lost, it would have been an immeasurable loss and a great danger for Israel. 
**Doubt 3:** Regarding the three days of time Alexander gave the Egyptians—this seems like a perversion of justice. When two litigants stand before a judge in monetary laws, "giving time" is not applicable, as they might use it to craft a lie. A judge should demand an immediate response. 
**Doubt 4:** How could Israel claim wages for 430 years when they were actually only enslaved for 210 years? While the verse says 430, Rashi explains this includes their time in other lands. 

The matter is this: The Sages of Israel understood that the Egyptians were arguing both "revealed" and "hidden" claims. It was difficult for the Sages to understand why the Egyptians cited the verse "And He gave favor..." rather than the verse where the Israelites actually took the vessels. The Egyptians were arguing before Alexander, who believed in the "eternity of the world" <note>The Aristotelian view that the world was never created and has always existed</note>. According to that view, Israel would be considered thieves. But if the Blessed Name created the world, then by His will He gave the gold to them. 

The Egyptians, after seeing the signs and wonders, recognized the existence of God and the creation of the world, yet they still harbored doubts. They argued that even if God created the world, He handed over power to the "Heavenly Host" (the stars), and that the world now follows its natural course, as if His hand were withdrawn. But the truth is as I stated: not for a single moment does the Holy One withhold His abundance. He only gave them "power"—meaning the power to act. 

The Egyptians believed that as long as the natural system is not overridden, the "gold" belonged to them. They were confused by the attribute of God's justice. Our true faith resolves this: the Egyptians weren't just paying for labor, but the gold was a transfer of divine abundance. 

<insert>and took from them money from their grace at that time</insert> The Egyptians wanted to prove this was not the case, arguing that the term "favor" <note>original: *chen*</note> implies the gold belonged to the Egyptians and was only "lent" through a feeling of grace. 

<margin>Gabiha</margin> ben Pasisa said: I will go and answer their inquiries. If I lose, tell them I am an unlearned man who does not understand "hidden" arguments. 

Returning to the matter: Gabiha ben Pasisa's reply was that the "favor" mentioned was actually a divine indicator of their debt. The true proof comes from the "430 years." Though they only served 210 years, in the celestial system, if one intends to commit a sin, it is as if he did it <note>This is a specific theological argument being applied to the Egyptian intent to enslave</note>. Since the Egyptians had the *potential* and the *readiness* to enslave Israel from the time of Abraham's covenant, they were liable for the full 430 years of wages. 

Even if the money we took was for the actual time in Egypt, we still demand the wages for the full 430 years! They could not pay this and had to flee. The fact that it was a Sabbatical year teaches us about the "Renewal of the World"—that He renews creation every day. From all this, we see that "the Lord is God, there is no other," and all power belongs solely to Him.

---

**Another** explanation of the verse "Know the God of your father" <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note> regarding His Unity and the knowledge of His Names and the Secret of Emanation <note>term: *Atzilut* — the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divinity</note>. The verse "I will set him on high because he knows My name" refers to the secret study of the Wisdom of Kabbalah. He said that the Sages are "open" <note>perhaps meaning receptive</note>, and one who has not seen the light of this Wisdom has never seen the light of day. One must understand the secret of His Unity and His Providence, and the meanings of the attributes mentioned in the Torah and Prophets, which the philosophers also investigated. Because many people have turned away from this Wisdom, and one who turns away from it turns away from eternal spiritual life, I will transcribe the words of the Sages of Truth <note>Kabbalists</note>.

The Rabbi, author of *Minchat Yehuda* <note>Judah Hayyat, a 15th-century philosopher and Kabbalist</note>, wrote in his introduction to *The System* <note>original: *Ha-Ma'aracha*</note>:

> A person should desire life in order to see the "Good," as it is said: "Who is the man who desires life... to see good?" The "Good" is the Torah, as it is said: "For I have given you a good teaching <note>original: *lekach tov*</note>, do not forsake my Torah." There are hidden tastes which those who taste them will merit to taste the "Hidden Good" reserved for the righteous in the future to come, of which it is said: "How great is Your goodness that You have hidden for those who fear You." Just as that Good is hidden for the righteous alone, the prophet said: "Behold, My servants shall eat, but you shall be hungry..."

<meta>This page continues the "Ten Sayings" framework, specifically transitioning into the first discourse which focuses on the philosophical and mystical foundations of Divine Unity (Achdut). It builds on the previous discussion regarding God's constant involvement in the world, shifting now to a formal defense of Monotheism against dualist or pluralist arguments.</meta>

# Ten Sayings: First Discourse

In one's intention and thought <note>original: "Machshavo"</note>, when we come to the word "One" <note>Hebrew: *Echad*, referring to the Shema prayer</note>, one should not prolong the letter *Aleph* so as not to appear as if—Heaven forbid—one is saying there is more than one. For the Lord is not like other "ones," such as a king who is "one" in his land but is not "one" from every perspective, since there are other men like him in his land, and in other lands, there are kings like him. Even if an angel from heaven were to descend to the earth, that angel would be "one" on earth, but not "one" from every perspective, for in the heavens there are other angels like him. But the Lord our God is not so; He is One from every side and perspective.

Rabbi Saadia Gaon <note>Saadia Gaon (882–942) was a prominent Jewish philosopher and legalist</note> wrote to answer the heretics who claim there are two or three deities: If one god cannot act without the help of his companion, then both are weak. If one can force the other, then both are constrained. If both are permitted to do as they wish, and one wants to revive a person while the other wants to kill him, that person would have to be dead-alive and alive-dead simultaneously in the blink of an eye. Furthermore, if one can hide a matter from his companion, then they are not all-seeing; and if they cannot hide things, then both are limited. He also wrote to answer those who challenge the verse "Let **us** make man in **our** image" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>, explaining that it is the way of the Holy Tongue for the great to refer to themselves in the plural even though they are individuals. Examples include "The man, the lords of the land, spoke" <note>Genesis 42:30; original: *Adonei ha-aretz*</note>, or "Let **us** go down and let **us** confuse" <note>Genesis 11:7</note>. He elaborated greatly on the matter of Unity, stating that all Israel is fixed in firm faith that the Creator of all is a unique One, as it is said: "The Lord is One," and "You have been shown to know," and "Know today and restore to your heart," and "I, even I, am He, and there is no god with Me" <note>Deuteronomy 4:35, 4:39; Isaiah 43:10</note>.

In the final discourse of the pious Rabbi Yosef Ya'abetz <note>Yosef ben Hayyim Ya'abetz (1460–1507), a Spanish exile and philosopher</note>, I found a further true explanation of "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." The essence of faith is the Name of Being <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note>, which itself explains "One." The word "One" indicates being "unique in excellence" such that his quality is not found in any other. For instance, "One of the people" refers to the most distinguished among them, like a king. Abraham was called "One" because there was no one like him in his time who called upon the Name of God. Thus, the word "One" points to our Creator's excellence, which is not found in any other. Unity is divided into three parts:

**The First:** Absolute Unity. He is the Creator alone, and no one is with Him, as the verse says: "You alone are the Lord; You made the heavens."

**The Second:** Our God is the True Overseer <note>term: *Mashgiach* — referring to Divine Providence</note>, and there is none besides Him. This part is not "absolute" like the first, because God created the world from absolute nothingness into existence. However, in this second part, He sometimes acts through intermediaries and sometimes not, as it is said: "To Him who alone does great wonders" <note>Psalm 136:4</note>. Since everything is by His will, no intermediary has the power to change His decrees. As the Sages said: "His work is truth and His faith is enduring."

**The Third:** This is not for the present time but is destined for the future, for which our eyes look out—that He alone will reign, as it is said: "For then I will turn to the nations a pure language" <note>Zephaniah 3:9</note>. Regarding this, the Sifrei <note>An ancient legal commentary on Numbers and Deuteronomy</note> says: "The Lord our God" in this world; "The Lord is One" in the World to Come. Then His kingdom will be recognized and publicized to all, just as it is known Above. This is the secret of the Name of Being: "He was, He is, and He will be." "He was" corresponds to the first Unity (He alone). "He is" corresponds to the second part (Providence). "He will be" corresponds to the third. The essence of faith in this is: "Lift up your eyes on high and see..." and "We have heard with our ears, our fathers told us..." We must believe with absolute faith that the Unity will then be complete. The Great Name <note>original: *Shem Ha-Havayah*</note> begins with the letter *Yod*, which is one of the "Eitan" letters that indicate the future tense. This is also the meaning of "I Will Be" <note>original: *Ehyeh*</note>, for in the future His Unity will be clarified to all His creatures, which is the purpose of creation.

These three are linked. Since it is written "In the beginning God created," and the proof of creation comes from the Creator, we understand He created out of a desire to do good to others. Therefore, He oversees all His creatures. This refutes the heretics who say His Providence only reaches the "sphere of the moon." This is a mistake; it is impossible for Him to have created them to be abandoned. On the contrary, if they are of "lesser value," they require *more* supervision. It is like a father who has sons; he supervises the one who is sick more closely. Furthermore, it is to His praise that a Master Craftsman's wisdom is publicized when he can work with unfit tools and unprepared material. Once Providence is established, the third faith is established: since He created the world for His glory and the benefit of creatures—to make His Godliness and the glory of His kingdom known—the act of creation would be in vain if the world did not reach this perfection of knowing Him. It is written: "The Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him" <note>Deuteronomy 32:12</note>. It is repeated in the Prophets: "It shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord of Hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land... and I will remove the spirit of impurity" <note>Zechariah 13:2</note>.

**And this is** "The Lord <note>before creation</note> our God <note>overseeing us now</note> is One <note>in the future</note>." He is always the Unique One, like whom there is no other. Later, in Tractate Tamid, the verse of the unification of the Name—"Hear O Israel"—will be explained well according to the Wisdom of Truth <note>term: *Chochmat Ha-Emet* — Kabbalah</note>.

**Furthermore,** I will discuss the structure of Divine Providence. The order of the world is based on the system of the heavenly hosts. The Creator, blessed be He, renewed everything from absolute nothingness; therefore, it is in His power to do as He wishes, to change and to straighten. In the beginning, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave the heavenly hosts the strength and ability to lead the world, and every star is appointed over its own kind. "The world follows its natural course." It is as if His "hand" is removed from them, unless at certain times He wishes to "override the system." As long as He does not override it, the world follows the power He instilled in them at the time of creation. However, the true faith in my eyes is that God "renews in His goodness every day, constantly, the work of creation," with specific intentions, flowing abundance...

<column-break/>

...the aforementioned <note>marginal: <margin>Annotation: This refers to the simple understanding that if He left the world to its own devices, it would fail. Just as a human king leaves his people to their own nature unless he gains something from them, God, who is perfect, acts out of pure kindness.</margin></note>. If he were to take a portion of it and begin to divide it among the craftsmen to build a foundation on the "navel of the earth" <note>a reference to Jerusalem or the center of existence</note> with lime and stones to raise a wall of filth upon it, and he knows that his life will not remain among the filth—what benefit is there for him to see a building made of mud that will soon be swept away? Likewise, all the pleasures of this world are fleeting and complete vanity. But they are the foundation of the world, and therefore the Sages called the unlearned man "the person of the earth" <note>term: *Am Ha-aretz* — literally "people of the land," meaning those ignorant of Torah</note>. That is to say, if not for the work of these people, the Sage could not exist. Therefore, they settle the world for the Sage.

If a man asks: "Behold, we see the fool and the boor, and the fool is great and does not toil, while others serve his lust and engage in his business," it is possible that the one engaging in the business is a Sage, while the one for whom it is done is a total fool. All the jewelry and beauty produced by the world's work is given to the fool, while the wise man recognizes the good and prepares the needs of life. The fool desires only to build a grand palace and to wear fine clothing, as the kings and their like do. It is possible that the palace prepared for the fool will eventually be inhabited by the righteous, as it is written: "The righteous shall wear it" <note>Job 27:17</note>. This is the meaning of the distinction between the righteous and the wicked.

The Sages explained this matter through Ben Zoma <note>Shimon ben Zoma, a 2nd-century scholar</note>, who stood upon the Temple Mount and saw the multitudes of Israel. He said: "Blessed is He who created all these to serve me." For he was a unique individual of great stature. He understood that someone without wisdom is deficient in all their deeds. This matter is necessitated by the path of wisdom. Therefore, when the dwellings are built, they exist so that scholars may learn. The greatness of the matter is to write words of wisdom and caution. Therefore I have written this, so that it may be known that even those of low status are part of the "ascended ones" <note>spiritual elite</note> in a small way.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, who stands by the wicked in their time, does so to help the righteous. As it is said: "Only the people have I kept before you for your own sake, so that the land shall not become desolate." This is the meaning of the Sages' statement: "The entire world was created only to accompany this one" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 6b</note>. This means to support and strengthen him. It is written that everything created was created for His glory. Everything found in the world, even the "worthless," is worthy for the Master of Wisdom and Action. You may learn from the Sages that God has nothing in His world except the "four cubits of Halacha" <note>term: *Halacha* — Jewish Law</note>.

->Addition<-

Furthermore, I have relied on this explanation for the word "Providence" <note>original: *Hashgacha*</note>. It is a great simplicity: just as a human king leaves his people to their nature when there is no benefit to him from the lowly, the Holy One, Blessed be He, oversees all—the high and the low, the fly and the gnat. There is no end to His wisdom. One might say: "What are these lowly things compared to Him?" But the artisan’s skill is recognized specifically when he works with poor materials.

It argues that God's constant supervision extends even to the lowliest creatures and that the entire social order, including the labor of the unlearned, exists to support the spiritual pursuit of the wise.</summary>

<header>Ten Sayings: First Discourse</header>

# Ten Sayings: First Discourse

<margin>
It seems to me, regarding the matter of their hiddenness, that the concealment of the early births <note>The "early births" likely refers to the primordial stages of creation or early mystical concepts.</note> is for a reason. For the engagement with these hidden matters was not intended to be public, but only for the unique individuals of the elite who fear the Lord in the depth of existence. This is so that—Heaven forbid—these matters do not fall into the hands of the common people, who might treat them with contempt or even fall into heresy. This has happened to those who spoke foolishly about the depths, or similarly regarding those who spoke of the "lower" forces <note>original: "pachuyot bakochot," referring to the *Klippot* or "husks" of impurity</note>, which are the secret of total darkness. Only when the "thorns" <note>The "thorns" represent spiritual obstacles or the *Klippot*.</note> and the foreign services are removed from the world, and the closer we get to the time of clarity, the more the light of holiness prevails over the husks. Therefore, one should not worry; only the holiness of the lights should be established, so that people do not fall into error. Through this, they will merit more lights, as the evil within the greatness will be rejected.
</margin>

**Permission** <note>original: "Reshut"</note>: This refers to whether one is obligated or merely permitted to contemplate. Our Sages of blessed memory stated in several places that one is obligated to contemplate, yet the matter is that while there is permission to contemplate this wisdom, there are nonetheless hidden matters where one has no "permission" to engage. As stated in the *Zohar* (Portion *Yitro*): "You shall surely send away the mother, but the children you may take for yourself" <note>This is a mystical interpretation of the commandment in Deuteronomy 22:6. The "mother" represents the higher, inaccessible Divine world, while the "children" represent the lower emanations accessible to human inquiry.</note>. This refers to the "Upper World" <note>original: "Alma Ila'ah"</note> where permission to look is not given; rather, one must "send it away" from their inquiry and contemplation. "But the children you may take for yourself"—this is as it is written: "Ask now of the days of old" and "from one end of the heavens to the other" <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note>. However, above the "end of the heavens," you must "send away" your desire to ask. The *Pardes* <note>The *Pardes Rimonim* ("Orchard of Pomegranates"), a foundational Kabbalistic text by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (1522–1570).</note> brought this discourse in the "Gate of Essence and Conduct," chapter fifteen, and explained the matter at length: in which levels of the Emanation <note>term: <term>Atzilut</term> (the highest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah)</note> a matter may be approached with questions and answers, and in which place there is a question but no answer, and in which place even a question is not permitted. What the nature of "question and answer" is, or "question without answer," is all well-explained there in that chapter; go look and let your heart rejoice. Regarding this, the verse says: "The hidden things belong to the Lord our God"—this is the aspect of "having no business with hidden things." "But the revealed things are for us"—this is the aspect of engaging in the secrets of the Torah that we have been permitted to contemplate. "To do all the words of this Torah"—this is the "revealed" part of the Torah and its 613 commandments, with their explanations and details, to perform them.

Similarly, there is the matter where the Sages of blessed memory said to Rabbi Elazar: "Come, and I will teach you the Account of the Chariot" <note>term: <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah</term> (the study of the divine "chariot" or the inner workings of the heavens mentioned in Ezekiel)</note>, and he replied, "I am not yet old enough." Certainly, in this wisdom, there are myriads upon myriads of levels. Regarding a deep matter in this wisdom, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The traditional author of the Zohar.</note> said: "Not every brain can tolerate this." For this, one needs a breadth of mind and great wisdom and understanding. But to study everything within one's ability to understand and grasp in this wisdom and its secrets is encouraged; only let a person sanctify himself with extra holiness in study and in practice. Then he shall "ascend the ladder that reaches the House of God" <note>A reference to Jacob's ladder.</note> to understand the glory of his Creator.

Specifically in this final generation, the light of Elijah the Prophet—which was previously hidden in the *Zohar*—has been revealed until the final generation. The wisdom of the *Zohar* was revealed so that in its merit, Israel might be redeemed. Just as Israel was redeemed from Egypt only after the Holy One, blessed be He, required them to be sanctified through the blood of the Passover offering and the blood of circumcision, so too the future Redemption will not occur until they merit this additional holiness. May it be the will of God, and happy is he who merits it! Of him, it is said: "I will set him on high, because he has known My name" <note>Psalms 91:14</note>.

The *Pardes*, in the first gate, chapter nine, debated within the wisdom: if one who denies the existence of the Sefirot <note>term: <term>Sefirot</term> (the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe)</note> is called a "heretic" <note>original: "Kofer"</note> or not. He said that if one does not know the matter of the Sefirot because he was not accustomed to them and the "Gates of Light" were not revealed to him, he certainly should not be called a heretic. **However**, it would be correct to say of him that he never merited to see the lights in his life, nor has he tasted the gift of the Torah and the honey of its pleasant words; he is like a group from the outside that does not see good. **However**, for one to whom the matter of the Sefirot and their existence has been revealed, yet he denies them because of his poor character—having been accustomed to "external wisdoms" <note>Often referring to Greek or secular philosophy.</note> and the offspring of his companions who mock—and he denies them, he is a heretic like one who denies the Oral Torah. Furthermore, such a person adds transgression to his sin, for from the denial of the Sefirot follows heresy regarding the clarity of the principles and foundations of the Torah. Since the "Simple One" <note>Referring to God's absolute, unchanging simplicity.</note> does not change, how could He be changed by fluctuating matters? And since He is One, how could He change across different types of actions? This would necessitate multiplicity, as is known. Therefore, one is compelled to believe in the Sefirot; otherwise, one might—Heaven forbid—deny God, as my masters have discussed regarding the removal of perception and the foolishness of those matters which should not even be put in writing. Thus, by necessity, through the belief in the Sefirot, one is not called a heretic.

In this way, one is compelled to say that whoever says he has "no business with Kabbalah" and does not want to direct his intent in his prayers except to the "Master of the Lights" <note>Referring to God's essence alone, ignoring the Sefirotic intermediaries of prayer.</note>—as many have thought—is certainly mistaken. For if a person comes to speak of the "Simple One" in terms of His essence in relation to His existence, and His essence in relation to the Sefirot, he ends up removing His actions from everything. For in terms of His own essence, He is Simple and not subject to changes—He does not change from Judgment to Mercy, nor does He provide abundance or change from one will to another through prayer—except in terms of His relationship to His Sefirot, which are His "conductors." Through them, the changes of Judgment and Mercy occur. Let the student not contemplate riding further into the depth of understanding the nature of these changes... for it will change his strength and bring no benefit. However, we shall explain the matter at length in the "Gate of Essence and Vessels," with God's help. The conclusion of the matter is that man is obligated to believe in the Sefirot so that he may be justified in the principles of faith and his intentions, to uphold the foundations of the Torah through them—meaning that through them, the Emanator <note>God, the *Ma'atzil*.</note> performs changes, yet He Himself does not change at all—Heaven forbid—as explained at length in that gate. From God we ask forgiveness; thus far the words of the *Pardes*.

**And you**, my children, may you be blessed! How good is your portion if you merit this wisdom in holiness, purity, and extra cleanliness! After you have "filled your bellies" with the study of the Talmud and the legal rulings <note>term: <term>Poskim</term> (decisors of Jewish law)</note> every single day, then afterward, set aside a fine portion of the day to cling to the study of this wisdom with additional holiness and great attachment to Him, blessed and exalted be He.

**And I shall return** to the verse: "Know the God of your father" <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note>. "Knowledge" is the knowledge of His Name, and one must first have it through tradition <note>original: "Kabbalah"</note>. This is why it says "Know the God of **your father**," as it is written: "Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you" <note>Deuteronomy 32:7</note>. **However**, one must also be wise and understand from his own mind more than what he hears from his teacher. This is the meaning of "Know the God of your father"—in addition to what you received from your father, you yourself should "know" the God of your father, as we learned in the *Book of Formation* <note>term: <term>Sefer Yetzirah</term> (an ancient mystical text)</note>: "Understand with wisdom and be wise with understanding." The *Pardes* explained this in the first gate, chapter eight, saying: "Understand with wisdom"—this means to look deeply into what you learned from your teacher regarding the "Wisdom of the Measures" <note>A term for the study of the Sefirot.</note>, of which only "chapter headings" are handed down. A person must understand one thing from another. This is the meaning of the Sages saying: "One does not discuss the Chariot unless he is wise and understands from his own mind." Thus, a person must compare one thing to another and derive one matter from another so that he is full of knowledge and not a "sterile intellect." And it says "be wise with understanding"—meaning, when you give birth to ideas and make comparisons in your mind and understand, you must contemplate it and filter it through the tradition of the Rabbis and their concise words, so that the matter is included in what was added to you, whether a great or small amount of grace. But "do not lean [on your own understanding]" <note>Proverbs 3:5</note>; thus far his words.

From this, I say there is a hint according to the secret in the Talmud (Tractate *Chullin*, chapter "These are Torn"): We learned there that "everything that has scales <note>original: *Kashkeshet*</note> has a fin <note>original: *Snapir*</note>, but there are those that have a fin and no scales..." and the Torah should have just written "scales" and not "fins." Rabbi Abbahu said... "to make the Torah great and glorious." Now, Torah scholars are compared to fish that "multiply and increase." In Tractate *Chagigah*, it says they are "like planted stakes"—just as a plant multiplies and increases, so do the words of Torah. Those who engage in the secrets of the Torah dive into "mighty and deep waters." They are holy and pure in their intentions. "Scales" refers to [the tradition]; "fins" are what allow one to "fly" through them. Now I will explain the secret: "Scales" hints at what he received from his teacher, which is the aspect of **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). "Fins," which spread out through them, are the aspect of **Understanding** (*Binah*), which is the intellect that gives birth to ideas and strength, making the Torah great.

**These are the words** of the Rabbi, Menachem Recanati <note>An important 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist.</note>, in the introduction to his book *Reasons for the Commandments*: "And you, understand what I say to you now. For in every place in the Torah where you can connect that action or that commandment to a higher matter, elevate it, and it will be good for you—even if you did not receive that specific reason from the mouth of a wise Kabbalist, or even if you did not see it in one of the books of the Sages. This is provided that you do not say the matter is not according to its literal meaning <note>term: <term>Peshat</term></note>. There is a hint to this "higher matter" in the verse: 'For one high official watches over another, and there are higher ones over them' <note>Ecclesiastes 5:7</note>. And provided you do not say that the reason you thought of yourself is the primary reason the Torah was given (i.e., for that specific commandment). Rather, you should say: 'If this commandment had not been given, it would have been worthy of being given for such-and-such a reason.' We are forced to say this because all sciences are hinted at in the Torah and there is nothing outside of it. The commandments are one thing, and they are suspended from the 'Upper Chariot,' each man to his task. Every single commandment is suspended from one part of the Chariot. If so, the Holy One, blessed be He, is not a side without a [connection], and the Torah is not outside of Him, and He is not anything outside of the Torah. Therefore, the Sages of Kabbalah said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the Torah." Thus far his words.

And what he wrote, "even if you did not receive that reason," means that he did not receive that specific *explanation*. However, the *truth* of the matter of this reason—its secret and its root—he *did* receive. That is, to explain a verse or a saying or to give a reason for a commandment based on the secrets he received from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher, all the way to Moses at Sinai, or based on the "branches" of the secrets in the aspect of "Understand with Wisdom" mentioned above. But one who explains a verse or a saying or the reason for a commandment based on "empty speculations"...

It encourages students to balance received tradition (scales) with their own intellectual expansion (fins) under the guidance of holiness.</summary>

# Ten Sayings: First Discourse

...and so on. Thus, the melodies of the Torah are enjoyed only by the "chosen elite." I have seen the "sons of the upper chamber" <note>original: "bnei aliya," a term for spiritually elevated individuals</note> and they are few; most of the world has distanced themselves from the paths of the <term>Wisdom of Kabbalah</term> <note>The received tradition of Jewish mysticism</note>. In this matter, people are divided into several groups.

The first group views it as something loathsome, for "a fool does not delight in understanding, but only in revealing his heart" <note>Proverbs 18:2</note>. This means they only care for "revealed" matters—the <term>Peshat</term> <note>The literal or plain meaning of the text</note>. They refuse to cross the shore even once to seek atonement, saying there is nothing in the Torah but the literal meaning.

A second group asks: "Who is he that would dare approach the King's gate?" <note>referring to the perceived danger of entering the mystical "Palace"</note>

A third group avoids it out of fear of making a mistake, for "an error in study counts as a deliberate sin." 

Woe to the first group and their fortune! It would have been better had they not been created. Come and see what is written in the *Tikunei HaZohar* <note>original: "Sefer HaTikunim," a core Kabbalistic text</note>: "In the beginning"—there it was dry. This refers to the "river" that becomes parched and dry <note>A metaphor for the flow of Divine wisdom being cut off</note>. At that time, when the land is dry, the children below cry out in unity saying "Hear O Israel," but there is no voice and no answer. As it is written, "They shall call, but I will not answer." This happens to anyone who removes <term>Kabbalah</term> and Wisdom from the Torah. Because of them, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah cannot unite in the world. They claim there is only the literal meaning in the Torah and the Talmud. Truly, the spring of that River and that Garden is then withdrawn. 

It is also written regarding such a person: "It would have been better for him not to have been created in the world, and let him not be remembered." <note>This is a severe warning against those who reduce the Torah to mere stories.</note> If one thinks the Torah is just a collection of mundane stories, such as those about Esau, Hagar, Laban, or Balaam’s donkey, and that God merely collected common words to make a book—if that were true, why would it be called the "Torah of Truth," "The Torah of the Lord is Perfect," or "More desirable than gold"? 

Rather, every word of the Torah comes to show us "higher matters." The external story is not there for its own sake, but to point toward the "General Principle." Whoever says the Torah is just a story—may his spirit blow away! For the Torah is a holy, supernal Torah of Truth. Even a human king would find it beneath his dignity to speak only of common things; how much more so the King of Kings! The Torah uses these "garments" to hide deep secrets. This explains the punishment awaiting those who reject the inner wisdom.

->**Whoever** belongs to the second group, the Wise One <note>King Solomon</note> said of him: "Wisdom is too high for a fool; in the gate he does not open his mouth." This means that because he views these wisdoms as "too high,"<-
->he becomes lazy in learning them. This is the reason that the "Exalted Wisdom"—which is the Wisdom of Kabbalah—is hidden from him; he does not open his mouth to study it.<-

->**Whoever** belongs to the third group, his intentions are desirable, but his actions are not. For one should not neglect the wisdom out of fear. May the good Lord grant atonement for him, for "love covers all transgressions."<-

An error in these matters is regarded by the Lord with love. It is written in the *Zohar*: "One who connects himself to laboring in the Torah but cannot find anyone to teach him—every word he speaks rises up, and the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices in that word and receives it." It is further said, "In her love, you will always stray" <note>Proverbs 5:19; here interpreted as: even if you "stray" or make mistakes while studying out of love for God, it is precious</note>.

This is explained further in the *Book of Ethics* by Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah: His students asked him about the verse "A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, concerning errors." They asked: should it not say "concerning a prayer"? He replied: Anyone who turns his heart from worldly affairs and gazes upon the <term>Work of the Chariot</term> <note>original: "Ma'aseh Merkavah," the study of the Divine throne and celestial hierarchies</note> is considered by God as if he prayed all day. What are "errors"? It is as the verse says, "In her love, you will always stray." 

Rabbi Dechumai said: "The way of life is the rebuke of discipline." This teaches that anyone regular in the study of the "Work of the Chariot" and the "Work of Creation" will inevitably stumble, as it says, "this stumbling block is under your hand." These are matters a person cannot understand unless they first stumble in them. The Torah calls this "the rebuke of discipline," but truly, he merits the "way of life." 

It is clear from this that one should enter this study to merit the life of the World to Come, even if they make mistakes. A person should not be lazy about it, even if they face "rebukes," for what is our hope in this world if not to acquire life in the World to Come? The benefits are well-known: besides knowing one's Creator and the secrets of the commandments (which are "sweeter than honey"), it instills a fear of sin and a state of solitude with the Creator. It also leads to performing commandments with perfection and great love. As the Sage said: "Many waters cannot quench love."

Furthermore, great benefit comes from this in the matter of Prayer. The *Zohar* states: "A man must arrange the praise of his Master from below to above, to raise the glory of his Master to the depths of the 'well.' Then he draws the flow from above to below, through every level to the lowest level, to bring blessings down. Then he must tie the 'Knot of Faith.' Such a man honors the Holy Name. Regarding him, it is written, 'Those who honor Me, I will honor; but those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed.'" Who is the one who "despises"? It is the one who does not know how to unify the Holy Name or tie the Knot of Faith to draw blessings to the proper place. Of such a person, it is said: "Better he was not born." 

I say: if one does not study, how will he know how to unify and tie these knots? As King David told his son: "And you, Solomon my son, **know** the God of your father and serve Him." Moreover, fools do not realize they will be held accountable for this. The Midrash on Proverbs says that on the Day of Judgment, a person is asked: "Did you gaze upon the Chariot? Did you gaze upon the Redemption?" 

Beyond the hidden good of the World to Come, one who strives in this wisdom tastes the flavor of the World to Come even in this life. He cleaves to God more than those who only master Scripture or Mishnah. The *Tikunei HaZohar* explains the commandment of "The Bird's Nest": The "chicks" are the scholars over whom the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note> rests. The "eggs" are the school children. These are the masters of Scripture and Mishnah; when they study, the Shekhinah hovers over them like a dove. But sometimes the Mother (the Shekhinah) departs from them. However, the "Sons" who come from the "inner womb"—these are the **Masters of Kabbalah**. Regarding them it is said: "You shall not take the Mother with the sons," for the Shekhinah never leaves them.

From this, you see that the Masters of Kabbalah have "ten portions" <note>a much greater share</note> over the masters of Scripture and Mishnah. Even if one cannot reach its ultimate depths, even a small amount attained in "Exalted Matters" is of greater benefit than a large amount of "Lowly Matters." 

How fortunate we are to have the *Book of the Zohar*! The earlier generations—who were much greater than us—did not have it. Great sages like Rav Hai Gaon, Rav Sheshet Gaon, Rabbi Eliezer of Worms, Nachmanides, the Rashba, and the Ra'avad—they all knew the "Hidden Grace" <note>term: "Chen," an acronym for *Chochmah Nistarah* (Hidden Wisdom/Kabbalah)</note>, but they did not taste its "honey" as it was not revealed in their time. Do not wonder at this; my Creator did not reveal it until the final generation in which we live. 

I found support for this in the *Tikunei HaZohar*: "Elijah said to Rabbi Shimon: Rabbi, Rabbi, how much 'sustenance' will be provided from this work of yours to the 'Upper Beings' until it is revealed to the 'Lower Beings' at the end of days! And because of it, 'every man shall return to his ancestral land.'" This means the Zohar was destined to be hidden, used by angels, until the final generation. In the merit of those who study it, the Messiah will come, for then "the earth shall be full of knowledge." This is the immediate cause of his arrival.

These words are from the book *Minchat Vira*. Also, the holy man of God, Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, in the book *Or Ne'erav*, brought these sayings and explained them with great taste and knowledge. He expanded on how the study of this wisdom is an absolute obligation. The great scholar Rabbi Isaac de Lattes also wrote a formal ruling (printed in the introduction to the "Small Zohar") on the duty to study Kabbalah. He answered those who cite the saying "Do not seek what is too wondrous for you; you have no business with hidden things." He argued that, on the contrary, this is proof that one *should* contemplate the secrets of the Torah. If the intention was to forbid it entirely, why would the verse say "meditate on what you have been permitted"? If that only meant the literal Torah and the details of the commandments, it would not use the word "permitted," which implies that there is a threshold of entry into the hidden realm...

It emphasizes that even an imperfect understanding of mystical secrets is spiritually superior to a mastery of only literal texts.</summary>
