<meta>This page continues the discussion on the spiritual connection between generations and the transmission of the "hidden wisdom." The previous page established that the "inner" Torah is reserved for those who seek it; this page explains how the soul of Moses is fundamentally linked to every Jewish soul throughout history.</meta>

<page-num>43</page-num>
<header>The Second Discourse</header>

The matter returns to this point, and this reasoning provides a slight hint for all those who come after him, for they were all included in that liberation <note>Referring to the Exodus or the spiritual liberation of the soul</note>, and it passes through and joins with all souls. We have a slight hint and evidence of this from the fact that Moses <note>original: "M"REH," an abbreviation for Moshe Rabbenu, Moses our Teacher</note> is associated with Seth, as interpreted in the *Tikunim* <note>The *Tikunei HaZohar*</note>. Regarding him, it is said, "he begot in his likeness and his image" <note>Genesis 5:3</note>, for he was comprised of the 600,000 <note>The traditional number of adult males at the Exodus, representing the totality of the community</note> who were within his father, for he is the son drawn from the father. Therefore, he brought 600,000 out of Egypt. Regarding him, it was said: "One woman gave birth to 600,000 in a single vineyard" <note>A Midrashic metaphor for Jochebed, Moses’ mother</note>. On this, they hinted that Moses is equal to all of Israel.

On this, they also said: "Six hundred thousand footmen are the people in whose midst I am" <note>Numbers 11:21</note>, for they were literally with him, emerged from him, and were included in him. Therefore, they all drew Torah from him. This is hinted at in the verse: "Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them?" <note>Numbers 11:12</note>, for they are included in him. Nevertheless, "I" <note>the ego</note> does not provide them with warmth, which corresponds to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine/immanent aspect of God</note> who becomes pregnant with them; nor does the "I" beget them, which corresponds to the <term>Tiferet</term> <note>Beauty/Glory, the masculine/transcendent aspect of God</note>, who is the father who begets. Regarding this, he said, "The Lord was angry with me for your sake" <note>original: "Vayit'aber," which also means "became pregnant" in Hebrew</note>, meaning the *Shekhinah* was made "pregnant" through me; that is, all her "embryos" <note>the souls of Israel</note> were within me, and I was your messenger for your sake.

Evidence for this is found in the *Tikunim*, which states that Moses our Teacher extends into every generation among the 600,000. This refers to the cycle of his <term>Gilgul</term> <note>The transmigration or reincarnation of souls</note>, regarding which it is said: "A generation goes and a generation comes" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:4</note>. The meaning is that the generation that goes is the same generation that comes. Therefore, in every generation, he extends into 600,000 souls, and his Torah illuminates within them, and all draw from him, as this matter is explained in the *Tikunim* on the verse "And she bore again..." 

This is also discussed in the book *Ra'aya Meheimna* <note>The "Faithful Shepherd," a specific section of the Zohar</note>, stating that Moses our Teacher is present in this world in a hidden body among Israel. God forbid we should think that Moses, the choice of all creatures, is literally reincarnated—certainly not in animals. Rather, the intention is the existence of the light of his Torah, which illuminates the masters of the Torah among the 600,000 who draw from him, even as they are built up among the common people. This is a truth in which there is no doubt. 

Behold, the sparks of Moses are in every generation, for all generations were present at Mount Sinai. Thus, in every generation, the verse is interpreted: "Not with our ancestors alone... but with us also," we who were there "face to face." In the generation of the wilderness, Moses was revealed, and that generation was revealed in their receiving of the Torah, and Moses' speech to them was revealed when he said: "The Lord did not make this covenant with our ancestors [alone]..." But all the generations to come after them were there in a hidden way, and the sparks of Moses were with them in a hidden way. This statement from him to us is also in a hidden way: "Not with our ancestors..." The hidden meaning is the spiritual awakening that touches us now as we emerge into action and reveal what was already ours "face to face" in the hidden realm. We were all at the cutting of the covenant and the receiving of the Torah through oath and swear, and later at the Plains of Moab at the cutting of the covenant: "You stand this day..." as it is written: "And not with you alone do I make this covenant and this oath... but with him that stands here with us this day... and with him that is not here with us this day." 

According to our Sages of blessed memory, citing the Zohar, all the prophets received their prophecy at Mount Sinai. Likewise, they said that whatever a veteran student is destined to innovate was already given at Sinai.

## Furthermore

There is a teaching of our Sages regarding this verse that says: "Know the God of your father" <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note>, from which the matter of all generations being there in essence will be well explained. It explains how the cutting of the covenant, the oath, and this curse are also literally with us. This matter requires contemplation. The author of the *Akedah* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama, author of *Akedat Yitzchak*</note> already investigated this in the portion of *Nitzavim*. I will bring his opinion and the strength he has to awaken interest in it, and afterward, I will explain the matter as the good hand of the Lord is upon me.

<margin>In the priestly gift <note>original: "Terumah"</note> he said to him, "I eat."</margin>
The author of the *Akedah*, of blessed memory, writes regarding the *Midrash Tanchuma*: When Israel sought to cast off the yoke of the Torah in the days of Ezekiel, what is written there? "In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, men from the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord and sat before him" <note>Ezekiel 20:1</note>. They asked him: "A priest who buys a slave, can the slave eat of the holy priestly gift?" He said to them, "He may eat." They said, "If the priest then sells him back to an Israelite, has he not left the priest's domain?" He said to them, "Yes." They said, "So too we have already left His domain and become like the nations of the world." Ezekiel said to them: "What comes into your mind shall never be, when you say, 'We will be like the nations, like the families of the lands, to serve wood and stone.' As I live, says the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with fury poured out, I will rule over you." For you stand under an oath... so that He may establish you today as His people, and He will be your God, as He spoke to you and as He swore to your fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—that I will not go back on the word I swore to your fathers. 

"And not with you alone did I cut this covenant and this oath," for the future generations were there at that hour, as it is written: "But with him that stands here with us today before the Lord our God, and with him that is not here with us today." Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Nachmani: Why is it written "stands" regarding those present, but "stands" is not said regarding those who are not here today? Because the souls were there, but the body was not yet created; therefore, "standing" is not mentioned in their regard. 

All these are the words of the Midrash to demonstrate that a person does not bequeath to his children after him the obligation of a vow or an oath of prohibition for all generations in a way that they cannot protest, as long as they did not take it upon themselves when they reached maturity, whether by consent or silence. For this is legally impossible, neither from the side of the body nor the side of the soul. Regarding the body, the future children did not exist at the time of the oath except in potential. It is clear that one cannot use this power to bind his children. Certainly, from the side of the soul, it is known that a father has no partnership in the soul <note>as the soul comes from God</note>. It is known that the soul is not bound by their oath and the prohibition he forbade upon himself. 

As is clearly explained in the words of Ezekiel the prophet: "What do you mean by using this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'? As I live, says the Lord God, you shall no longer have occasion to use this proverb in Israel. Behold, all souls are Mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is Mine; the soul that sins, it shall die" <note>Ezekiel 18:2-4</note>. This truly teaches that there is no parental bond between the soul of the father and the soul of the son, and they are equal before Him, blessed be He, without any partnership. Therefore, the soul that sins shall die for its own iniquity and not for the iniquity of its fathers. 

And even the hints of the Sages said such things, and Solomon the Wise spoke of this when he said: "There is one, and no second; he has neither son nor brother, yet there is no end to all his labor... for whom do I labor?" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:8</note>. For he speaks there of the intellectual part of man, as I have explained in its place. Since no punishment is paid to the soul of the son because of the father's actions, how can he be seized by his words or trapped by his speech? Certainly, how could this continue until the end of all generations, as seen from the verse: "But with him that stands here with us today... and with him that is not here"? And as found in the mouths of our Sages, every Israelite is bound by an oath from Mount Sinai regarding all the words of this Torah. 

However, it seems that what the Sages intended to resolve with the statement regarding "souls" is that all future people were present at that standing, and they established and accepted upon themselves to complete and uphold it until the end of all generations. But there is still much to investigate in this statement: how could souls be there without bodies? For the connection of soul and body is essential for a human being to be obligated by commandments, and it is the essence of his being. As it says in the Torah: "which if a man does, he shall live by them" <note>Leviticus 18:5</note>. It appears the obligation to perform commandments applies only while he is a "man"—meaning a combination of body and soul. When they separate, he is no longer a "man," and is not included in "he shall live by them," for "among the dead, one is free" <note>Psalm 88:6</note>. 

Furthermore, it is clear that the Torah and commandments are obligations of the body. There is a legal principle that one does not disadvantage a person in their absence; the person must be there to accept it upon themselves. The Sages said: "A minor who converts is immersed based on the knowledge of the court, but when he grows up, he can protest." How much more so when he wasn't there at all! 

Also, regarding what was said—that they were there as a collective population encompassing all generations and all "faces"—for they said that where there is a population of 600,000, one blesses "Blessed be the Wise One of secrets." From this, it would be impossible for any person in future generations not to have been there in his image and likeness, in body and soul. Thus, no man has the power to protest what they all accepted at Sinai with oath and swear. These, too, are difficult things for the intellect to accept. They are too weak to hang upon them this curse upon which the existence of the covenant and the oath depends. We are bound by it, and it requires absolute validation so that it shall never be nullified, as it is written: "If these ordinances depart from before Me, says the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before Me for all time" <note>Jeremiah 31:35</note>.

## However

I am awakening interest in the gravity of this oath. There is a great doubt here: concerning this oath, were those who took it able to violate it during their lives or not? If we say they did not have the power of choice to violate it, then the principle of Free Will—upon which all the rebukes and moral lessons of the Torah stand—would be nullified. For all those warnings were said only so that they would not fail to perform the commandments or break the covenant. Therefore, we must conclude that they have the ability to violate the oath by virtue of their potential, even though they are not permitted...

<margin>“When the <term>Shekhinah</term><note>The Divine Presence, often personified as feminine</note> dwells...” etc. in the introduction to *Chesed L'Avraham*<note>A Kabbalistic work by Abraham Azulai</note></margin>
And the logic that the philosophers devised, which is not "from the mouth of Moses from the mouth of the Almighty"—this man violates the prohibition of “Thou shalt not make for yourself a graven image,” as seen in the *Zohar* <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>. And these are its words regarding "Thou shalt not make for yourself a graven image":

Rabbi Isaac opened: "Do not let your mouth lead your flesh into sin" <note>Ecclesiastes 5:5</note>. How much must a person be careful with the words of the Torah, and how much must he be careful not to let his power stray or produce from the Torah that which he does not know or has not received. It is written, "Thou shalt not make for yourself a graven image or any likeness," for the Holy One, Blessed be He, is prepared to exact punishment from him in the World to Come. When his soul seeks to enter its place, they push it outside, and it is cut off from that place where the other souls are "bound in the bundle of life." Rabbi Judah said: As we have learned, "Why should God be angry at your voice?"—this refers to the soul of a person. Rabbi Hiyya said to him: It is written, "For I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God." Why? Because He is jealous for His Name in everything. If it is because of the "faces" <note>spiritual archetypes or images</note> placed for His Name, it is because he lies in His Name; if it is because of the Torah, we have learned that the Torah is entirely the Holy Name. Therefore, one must not err in His Name nor lie in it. And whoever lies in this world shall not be brought into the King's palace and shall be cut off from the World to Come. Rabbi Abba said: It is written, "Thou shalt not make for yourself a graven image," and "Thou shalt not make for yourself..." refers even to a "hewn stone." That is to say: do not make for yourself *another Torah* that you do not know and that your teacher did not tell you. Why? "For I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God"—I am the one prepared to take vengeance on you in the World to Come at the hour when the soul seeks to enter before Me; I am prepared to reject her and cast her into Gehenna <note>Purgatory or a place of spiritual purification</note>. Thus far [the *Zohar*].

And it is written in *Tola'at Ya'akov* <note>"The Worm of Jacob," a 16th-century Kabbalistic commentary on prayer</note> in the name of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov <note>A 15th-century Spanish rabbi</note>, may his memory be for a blessing: "Fix your eyes on the words of the Fathers of the World, the holy ones on high who see the King's face. See how they compared the path of error and [mere human] reasoning to idols and images. The reason is the same: because those who make images intend to create a vessel through judgment to receive from those [celestial] powers and to be directed toward them as a sign and a memorial. But there is no permission to make images except in the way that Bezalel and Solomon did, who knew how to combine the letters through which heaven and earth were created. They made them according to the Name, and they were sanctified. These forms were prepared and designated for the glory of the God of Israel, according to the measure permitted to each, like the vision that the Lord showed Moses for the pattern of the Holy Chariot—the hidden 'Chariot of Peace' in the ancient heavens. 

But when another person thinks to make a likeness of those forms which were not sanctified or prepared for His glory—just as a forged image is not prepared for the Soul to dwell upon it—the distance between them is like the distance between the Creator and the created. According to the hidden counsel, such a thing is prepared for the 'External Side' <note>The realm of spiritual impurity</note>, which is called the power of defilement. It is a lowly dwelling compared to the camp of the *Shekhinah*, for they open and draw near to the 'unclean prison' and strike at its gates. He who follows it errs and is bound in darkness, for he exchanges the King for a servant and replaces good with evil, lying against the Lord of All. So too in this analogy are the letters of the Torah: though they are its soul, they allude to the Divine Names and the powers emanated from the Lord of All. It is necessary to establish its 'body' and its 'separation' <note>its physical structure and specific laws</note> so that the hidden aspect may dwell within them, and mercy within them, as matter relates to form. But when one walks in another path, that [divine] Form is not prepared to sit or dwell upon that matter. Thus, his Torah and his wisdom are 'without God,' a disqualified and flawed wisdom, literally like those who make idols." Thus far the words of Rabbi Shem Tov. However, let us return to the Torah, Prophets, and Writings, and the words of our Sages according to the Wisdom of Truth <note>Kabbalah</note>. How fortunate we are, how good is our portion!

## The Second Discourse

*May he who has sinned not weep again, etc.* Blessed is our God who created us for His glory, separated us from those who stray, gave us the Torah of truth, and planted 

->eternal life within us. His unity has already been alluded to in the recitation of this verse, and so at every time and season, as is known.<-

It is as if one were a captive, plagued, stricken, and poor due to the darkness of everything <gloss>around him</gloss>. Then a great King came, redeemed him, exalted him, and made him so great that He gave him His only daughter. This is the "Line of Judgment" <note>A Kabbalistic term for a specific manifestation of divine law</note>. He gives all the days of his life, day and night; he shall not cease from serving Him with labor, carrying burdens, and the service of the community. How many more good levels has He increased for him? Not only did He ransom him and make him a free man, and heal him from every illness, and give him his wealth, and raise him to greatness, higher and higher, until he became the King’s son-in-law. 

So it was with our ancestors: with seventy souls our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we were captives, "a nation within a nation," submerged in the depths of Egypt like a plagued person in a sore. But the Great King, the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed His strong hand and outstretched arm, and performed wonders by overturning the natural order to show His divinity, His power, and His providence over us when He brought us out from slavery to freedom. He then gave us their wealth, brought us near before Mount Sinai, and gave us His daughter—the Holy Torah—which is the revelation of His blessed Divinity through the secret of His Names. This is what the ministering angels sought when they said, "Set Your majesty upon the heavens" <note>Psalm 8:2</note>, but "How majestic is Your name in all the earth!" He exalted us above every tongue and sanctified us with His commandments in order to give us life in a world that is entirely life, so that we might be greater and more righteous than the ministering angels, with our place deeper within the "inner chamber" of the King. 

And because He unified the "Other Side" <note>repressed the forces of evil</note>, and at the giving of the Torah the Lord spoke with us "face to face," and made a covenant with us—not with our fathers alone, but with us who are here today, all of us alive, and our children and our children's children until the end of all generations. All are equal for the good in this standing <note>at Sinai</note>, for our souls were there. And as the word went out from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, it gave to each individual specific strength and life, and He spoke with him alone. They all entered into the "Covenant of the Group." And who is he, and where is he, who would deny this glory and splendor? If he recognizes it, he will bring himself into the covenant with the King of Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, in love and with an oath. He will be filled with awe, fear, trembling, and quaking, and will be awakened with great cleaving, passion, desire, and eternal love. For He, blessed be He, is our Master, the owner of all our acquisitions since our days of servitude, and we are His servants. He is our Father from the perspective of the root of our soul, for it is a "portion of God from above," and we are His children—children of the Living God—if we cling to Him, as it is written, "After the Lord your God shall you walk" <note>Deuteronomy 13:5</note>. 

This matter of the making of the covenant is essentially from the perspective of our souls, in addition to our being "potentially" within our ancestors who stood there in body and soul. This is as it is written: "Know the God of your father" <note>I Chronicles 28:9</note>, meaning: do not let the covenant depend on your father alone, as if you were only in him potentially; rather, "Know the God of your father," for your eyes saw this great vision, and *you* entered into the covenant.

<margin>And this is "He made a covenant with us," as Moses said to Israel: "The Lord our God made a covenant with us in Horeb... Not with our ancestors did the Lord make this covenant, but with us, who are here today, all of us alive" <note>Deuteronomy 5:2-3</note>. And even though we have heard...</margin>
this verse applies to the generation of the wilderness who received the Torah—as it says afterward, "Face to face the Lord spoke with them"—and Rashi <note>The classic 11th-century commentator</note> wrote: Rabbi Berechiah said, so said Moses: "Do not say that I am misleading you about nothing, in the way a middleman does between a seller and a buyer; rather, the Buyer Himself is speaking with you," etc. Nevertheless, this verse is written in the Torah and it is eternal. Every generation reads this verse. And according to what Rashi wrote on the verse "as it is said this day, on the Mount of the Lord it shall be seen" <note>Genesis 22:14</note>—"this day" refers to the present and the future, like "until this day," which in every place refers to the coming generations who read the scripture. So too shall this verse be explained. 

First, I will introduce the words of the *Zohar*, portion *Lech Lecha*: 
Rabbi Simeon said: It is written, "This is the book of the generations of Adam" <note>Genesis 5:1</note>. Was it really a book? Rather, they established that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed Adam every generation, its seekers, and its leaders. How did He show them to him? We say he saw through the Holy Spirit that they were destined to come into the world. Is it like one who sees through wisdom what is destined to come? Not so; rather, he saw them all with his very eyes. He saw the very form they would take when they stood in this world. Why? Because from the day the world was clarified, all the souls destined to stand within human beings all stand before the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the exact form they are destined to take in the world. Just as all the righteous, after they leave this world, their souls ascend and the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepares another form for them to be clothed in, just as they were in this world. As mentioned, they all stand before Him, and He showed them to Adam with his eyes. And if you say that after he saw them they did not remain in their existence—come and see: all the words of the Holy One, Blessed be He, exist and stand before Him until they descend into the world. In this same way it is written: "Both with him who is standing here... and with him who is not here" <note>Deuteronomy 29:14</note>. They established that all human beings destined to be in the world were all present there. Here one must look closely, for it is written, "and with him who is not here," which implies all those who would issue from those standing there. For it is written "with us today" and not "standing with us today." Rather, certainly, all of them stood there, but they were not visible to the physical eye. It is written "with us today" even though they were not seen. And if you ask: Why were they not seen here as they were seen by Adam, who saw them eye to eye? Here the "veiling" was greater. But here, when the Torah was given to Israel, they saw another joy and higher levels, looking eye to eye. And this is why it was appropriate to look upon and see the glory of their Master, as it is written: "He saw and called out..." referring to the Holy One, Blessed be He, alone and not another. Therefore, all human beings destined to stand in the world all stand before the Holy One, Blessed be He, in that very form they are destined to take. This is the meaning of "Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in Your book all were written" <note>Psalm 139:16</note>. "Your eyes saw my unformed substance"—why? Because another higher form exists in this one. And as it is written, "Who is a Rock <gloss>Creator</gloss> besides our God?" Who is a good artist <gloss>who forms</gloss> like the Holy One, Blessed be He? Thus far [the *Zohar*].

And these are the words of the *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the second chapter of the "Gate of Vision": "When the Holy One, Blessed be He, emanated the soul of His handiwork, the emanation included 600,000 souls—for there is no generation with fewer than 600,000—as explained in the *Book of Tikunim*. Behold, the root of his soul is comprised of those 600,000. As long as people were increasing and multiplying, their souls were spreading within them. And his soul is never..."

# The Second Discourse

<note>This section discusses a famous philosophical problem: how can an oath taken by ancestors bind their descendants who were not yet born?</note>

...to establish even for one day. That which is not within the bounds of human nature to perform is considered an absolute impossibility. For instance, there is a "covenant cut" <note>An idiom for an unbreakable, eternal agreement</note> for all eternity that the people will never collectively choose to cease procreating or similar acts, even though it is possible for a single person from a city or a chosen individual to do so. For this reason, the covenant cut between us and Him, may He be exalted, is an eternal covenant whose violation cannot be imagined from any perspective. These are the words of the author of the *Akeidah* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama (15th century), author of *Akeidah Yitzchak*</note>. See there further, for he elaborates, and his intention is that it is not by the power of the oaths alone that the generations stood and maintained the Torah, but rather from the necessity of their union, which is a greater stringency than an oath. For they saw and recognized that if they were to imagine leaving His hand and His protection, they would all instantly be destroyed, killed, and lost, and that separating from Him is separating from life itself. Truly, his words are sweet.

And many "gracious sages" <note>A term for scholars of hidden wisdom/Kabbalah</note> explain that his words are sweet because they bring a person to spiritual awakening. However, in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory, it is clear that there was an actual **oath** sworn by the House of Israel, as seen in the tractate of *Nedarim* <note>Vows</note>, where it says that Moses told Israel: "I do not impose this oath upon you based on my own mind, but on the mind of the Almighty." Furthermore, I do not fully understand the words of the author of the *Akeidah*, for according to the plain meaning of his words, the punishment for the generations—should they refuse to maintain the bond of the ancestors—is merely that the Holy One, Blessed be He, removes His oath from them, meaning He removes His protection. If so, why does the Torah differentiate between punishments: lashes for one, death for another, <term>Karet</term><note>Spiritual excision or "cutting off" of the soul</note> for another, and the four types of court-ordered execution for another? This proves that the punishments are intentional and purposeful from Him, may He be exalted, as is the punishment of Hell, which has a set measure—spending this amount of time in Hell for this or that reason—and all according to the Torah. This proves that the original bond remains in its full strength, in its generalities and its details, until the end of all generations. And as for the difficulty the author of the *Akeidah* raised regarding the matter of the oath—whether the Almighty has a legal claim of an oath against them or not—this difficulty is of no consequence. For the matter of the oath was only the completion and strengthening of a mental <term>Kinyan</term><note>A formal legal acquisition or commitment</note> to show that they fulfilled and received the Torah with a whole heart and a willing soul. For without this, their statement "We will do and we will hear" would be like an <term>Asmakhta</term><note>A legal term for a promise made without full intent to be bound by it</note> which does not effect a legal acquisition. And all the promises of the Torah are in this manner: "If you walk in My statutes" or "If you despise My statutes," etc., and so too the entire Torah. However, with an oath, there is a total resolution in a whole heart that they received the Torah through their own good choice, and the concept of *Asmakhta* does not apply. And so ruled Rabbi Meir <note>Maharam of Rothenburg</note>: that a vow, an oath, and a "hand-clasp" <note>A formal handshake agreement</note> effect legal acquisition even in cases of *Asmakhta*.

**However**, what the author of the *Akeidah* wondered at—how it is possible for ancestors to bequeath an oath to their children—he does not doubt the words of our Sages who said that all generations were present there and swore for themselves. He only asks: since their bodies were not there, and the commandments are physical obligations, [how can they be bound]? Know, my children, that just as the souls of all generations were there, so too the center and the essence of the **bodies** were there. This is a subtle matter, and I will explain it in two ways.

The first way is according to what the author of the *Avodat Ha-Kodesh* <note>Meir ibn Gabbai (16th century)</note> wrote in Chapter 8 of the "Section on Unity." He spoke at length there regarding the matter of Man being in the "Image and Likeness" of the Supreme, hinting at the <term>Sefirot</term><note>The ten divine emanations or attributes of God</note>, and that his form also includes the entire "chain of descent" <note>The unfolding of spiritual worlds</note>. He wrote at the end, and these are his words: "I will return to the matter of Creation that I was discussing, and I say that the Sefirah of <term>Malchut</term><note>Kingdom; the lowest Sefirah representing the Divine Presence in the world</note> includes all forms... and the roots of the upper beings were preserved to give to each and every body the spiritual spirit that connects with the body—the soul, the form appropriate for it. And the secret of the matter is that the Unique Name includes all... which are the ten holy Names, and they are vessels for the separated intelligences that cannot be grasped by thought... and each and every name of these has 'appellations' (titles)... and everything hangs and stands upon the Unique Name... for the Divine Image is composed of three levels, one inside the other: <term>Nefesh</term>, <term>Ruach</term>, and <term>Neshamah</term><note>The three basic levels of the soul: the vital/animal, the emotional/spirit, and the intellectual/divine</note>... they also have a **spiritual body** <note>original: "גויה רוחנית"</note> to build the aforementioned spiritual structure, which connects the Form (soul) and the [physical] body." 

This spiritual body is what sustains the physical body, assisting the soul to be present with the body, for it would be impossible for two opposites [soul and matter] to connect except through an intermediary, which is the "Spiritual Body." Its connection to this coarse physical body is from the "Dust of the Temple" <note>original: "עפר ב"ה"</note> which is in Jerusalem... our Sages said in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Nachman: "Man was created from the place of his atonement, as it is said: 'An altar of earth you shall make for me.' The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: 'I will create him from the place of his atonement, and would that he might stand [endure].'" Thus far are the words of the *Avodat Ha-Kodesh*.

Behold, the secret of this **Body** is also the hidden root of the physical body. And there is no doubt that this matter of the "Spiritual Body" applies specifically to the souls of Israel, which are a "portion of God from above," the "lamp of God which is the soul of Man." It is the expansion of the First Adam. Just as 600,000 souls of Israel expanded from the soul of the First Adam, so too did the matter of this "Spiritual Body" expand. Therefore, Israel are called "Adam," for we are all truly the First Adam in soul and in body—which is not the case for the other nations. 

Through this, the Midrash of our Rabbis on the portion of *Mishpatim* will be clarified: "While the First Adam was lying as a <term>Golem</term><note>An unformed physical mass</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed him every righteous person who was destined to descend from him. Some hang from Adam's head, some from his hair, some from his forehead, some from his eyes, his nose, his mouth, his ear..." And know that when Job sought to argue with the Holy One, Blessed be He, saying, "O that I knew where I might find Him, I would set my cause in order before Him," the Holy One, Blessed be He, answered him: "You seek to argue with me? 'Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?'" <note>Job 38:4</note>. What is the meaning of "Where" (Hebrew: *Eiphah*)? Rabbi Resh Lakish said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Job, tell me, your *Eiphah* <note>A pun on 'Where' and a 'measure/place'</note>—in what place was it hanging? On the head, the forehead, or the ear? If you know where your place was, then you may argue with me." Thus far the Midrash. 

This Midrash hints at the matter of souls, as explained in the *Pardes* <note>The *Pardes Rimonim* by Moses Cordovero</note>. Nevertheless, one must examine why it says "lying as a *Golem*," for the term *Golem* refers to physical things. Although the *Pardes* settles this, writing: "It says the First Adam was lying as a *Golem* because after the Holy One, Blessed be He, established him in his full stature, the 'plantings' included in him expanded in the Garden of Eden until bodies were ready for them to inhabit. But they were all included in him before the completion of his creation as a *Golem*—like a rolled-up piece of dough." Nevertheless, I say the word *Golem* also hints at the physical power, the "husk" of the souls, which also expands in every generation within Israel. Therefore, Israel are essentially called "Adam." And the souls, along with these spiritual bodies, stood at Mount Sinai at the time of the receiving of the Torah through oath, curse, and covenant. Since the root and the refinement of this body was also present there in all generations, both in soul and in spiritual body.

**Furthermore**, there is a second facet which is close to the senses: Man was made with a "Body of Light," a clean body, and afterward was clothed in a "dark body," which is coarse matter, skin and flesh. He has three aspects: a soul in a clean body, which is then clothed in a dark body. For Rashi explained regarding the creation of Man from the earth: "from the altar of earth," or alternatively, "He gathered his dust from the entire world." These two explanations are both true: from the perspective of the clean body, He gathered dust from the Altar of Earth, and from the perspective of the dark body, from the entire world. And just as the earth grows both good and evil, growing many plants and matters that are good for food, and those that are medicinal, and similar things...

<margin>23</margin> -> The question regarding their oath <-

And behold, if that free choice were assumed <note>referring to the freedom of descendants to opt out of the covenant</note>, we would find that the status of his <note>God's</note> camp would be voided. This would nullify all the scriptures testifying that these severe oaths shall never be nullified for all eternity and shall not be forgotten for nothing; and this also obligates us for all time. ▢ And more difficult than this is what has been clarified by the mouths of all the prophets and through experience: that they have already all transgressed these oaths and "broken the covenant." ▢ If so, according to our assumption, the oath of God that relies upon them has also been nullified, and hope is already lost, Heaven forbid! ▢ And if you should say that the form of eternal existence is not the *observance* of the oath, but rather its mere *existence*—meaning that once He swore to them, He already gained the power through their oath to force and compel them toward their fulfillment, as it is said through Ezekiel: *“As I live, says the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with fury poured out, I will rule over you”* <note>original Hebrew: "חי אני נאם ה' אלקים אם לא ביד חזקה ובזרוע נטויה ובחמה שפוכה אמלוך עליכם"</note>, which He would not do to any others— ▢ behold, this is truly more difficult than the first question. For one must ask: does He, may He be exalted, have a legal claim of an oath <term>Din Shvuah; the legal obligation arising from a sworn promise</term> against them or not? If you say He has the claim of the law over them—meaning they are obligated to keep and perform all the words of the Torah on their own, and this oath is merely an "extra stringency," like one who makes his fellow swear to pay a debt— ▢ then this oath, for Him, may He be exalted, would be a "void oath." For that same compulsion He has in His hand to use against them by the power of the oath, He could use to compel them anyway. For what reason would the Master of the Earth make one of his servants swear to pay him a debt just so he could force him to pay? For even without the oath he can compel him; on the contrary, it is better to compel him without an oath than to compel him after he has already transgressed it! And if we say He has no legal claim of an oath against them, then truly the oath itself is the beginning and essence of the coercion. For He sought it from their hands, and through His prophet He enticed and seduced them into it. And what is the reason to compel them to do something that is already a necessity, and then entice them to swear upon its performance? If He permits Himself to coerce them because of the oath, He could permit it without it. We would say that by transgressing it, the power falls away. Furthermore, if so, He would only have the legal claim of the oath against them, not the essence of the Torah and the commandments. It is like if you say: "I owe you a debt, and I swore to you to pay it on such-and-such a day." When you transgress the oath, the creditor has two claims against you: the first is the monetary obligation itself, and the second is the obligation of the oath. ▢ However, if you swore to give him something you were not otherwise obligated to give, once you are lashed for the broken oath, you would be exempt from the money. So too, if they were punished merely for a "loose oath," they would already be exempt from the Torah and the commandments and have no further obligation toward them, as would appear from the scriptures we mentioned first. And what is this that Ezekiel said after the aforementioned statement: *"And I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples... and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant"*? He also said in another place: *"And I will cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my judgments and do them."* Behold, from all these sides it appears clearly: how could it be possible that the fathers had the power to make the children swear if there were no power in that oath to draw into the world an existence—and in its humility—to establish the eternal attachment that they desired should rest upon it?

# **Truly**
In my opinion, the matter of this oath is not as many have thought. The persistence and eternity of the Covenant of God and His love for this nation do not depend on the "severity of the oath." Rather, it is a natural, necessary attachment, greater and stronger beyond measure than any oath, such that its nullification is impossible in any way or matter in the world. It is a Law <note>original: "Chok"</note> that necessitates the nature of every existing thing not to separate from its life. Just as there is a "covenant cut" for every living being that it shall not destroy itself—which, though it might be imagined that one person in a city or a few over the course of time might violate that law and destroy themselves due to a corruption of the imagination—truly, its possibility cannot be imagined for all individuals of that species collectively. As it is said, "his evil remains with him" <note>idiom for natural self-preservation</note> for every man. And so, in this same manner, it is impossible to imagine the possibility of this nation being cut off from its God, His commandments, and His statutes in any way. For it is a law implanted in them, more severe and more of a law than the oaths of colleagues, which many have understood. We shall set forth a fitting and agreeable parable for this matter:

I raised a young man from the people, clever and strong. In his cleverness, he "took men by the heel" <note>a reference to the name Jacob/Yaakov, meaning "heeler"</note> and in his strength he struggled with princes. Because of this, many princes hated him and "archers bitterly attacked him," and he found no rest for the sole of his foot until he came to take shelter in the King's court, to hide under his wings. He girded his loins to strengthen himself in the King's service and the guarding of his palace, and he did his will and succeeded, until he found favor in the King's eyes. The King showed him kindness and said to him: "Stand at your watch and return to your service, and I will set my eye upon you to save you from all your enemies who rise against you. Furthermore, I will give you wealth and great possessions, and I will exalt your throne and give you honor above all the princes. And I will place my covenant upon all these paths between me and you, and between your offspring forever—provided only that your children keep their way to walk after me in all the service of the house and its guard, and that they swear to me regarding this matter." ▢ The young man heard this and it was good in his eyes; he prostrated himself before the King and accepted upon himself the service of the King and the charge of his house with all its conditions. He served him, as did his son, and his son’s son, and they succeeded in the service and grew very great. They built cities and settled in them, and they increased their servants and gathered wealth, honor, and property, until—at the fourth or fifth generation—when they heard of their wealth, they grew haughty and despised the service of the King and the guarding of his house. They refused his service and broke his covenant, and they regretted what their first fathers had done in accepting the yoke of the work of the oath and his covenant. They spoke out, saying: "Who gave power into our father’s hand to sell us into the hand of the King for eternity? Do we and our children not have the permission and ability to turn back from him and leave his service, and we would be free from him?" ▢ The King said to them: "As you say, so it is. Truly, if your soul despises being servants before me, I also am free from this point on from everything I promised you in my vows and all that left my lips." They went their way, and the King also withdrew from them. A proclamation went out through all his kingdom that these people were no longer under his protection, and he withheld his help and reward from them; he also removed all their glory. All the princes who had previously been their enemies heard this, and they rose against them, killed the men, made war on the cities, and took all their land from their hands. They plundered all their spoil until they perished from the land, and their enemies "shepherded" them and they trembled; those who remained among them were impoverished by the weight of poverty. ▢ Now, would you say to the King that he is "wicked" <note>original: "Beliyaal"</note>, claiming he punished them with all this punishment because they turned from his service, given that they had the power to turn away since their father had no power to commit them to that service forever? Surely not! For he did not punish them for turning away from him at all; rather, his kindness "departed its way" when they turned from sheltering with the King, where their father had established them. Because they separated from him, he also withdrew his kindness and goodness from them. ▢

Behold, for this reason, it is impossible for any person of intellect to imagine or agree in his mind to the nullification of this society and partnership, or to break its covenant in any way. For the obligation of such a covenant, if it exists, will never be broken, just as there is a "covenant cut" for every person of intellect that he should not destroy his property or kill himself. How much more so should this nature be strengthened and established with an eternal strength and permanence when the members of the covenant are many in number, like a great city or one whole nation. And so it is in our case: the matter of the closeness of this nation to God, may He be exalted, is beyond doubt. For behold, Jacob our father—the chosen of the patriarchs—from the beginning "took his brother by the heel" twice, and in his strength he struggled with greats, while he escaped from Esau, and already "struggled with man and with Laban," and he contended. And upon his return, he was "at risk of being a stench" to the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. He had no rest before them except by coming to take shelter under the wings of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah; the indwelling Presence of God</term>, as it is written: *"to the God who answered me in the day of my distress and was with me in all the way which I went."* ▢ And behold, according to his service, his deeds, and his labor before his God, He promised to guard him from all his enemies and save him in all his way, and He "cut a covenant" with him and with his children after him for generation to generation, as it is said: *"Behold, I am with you,"* etc., and the entire portion from beginning to end. ▢ Truly, this covenant with all its conditions was explained very well to his children's children, whether at the standing at Mount Sinai when He said: *"And now, if you will surely listen to my voice... then you shall be my treasure from among all the peoples... and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests,"* etc. It is even more clarified in the portions of the Covenants <note>referring to the sections of blessings and curses in Leviticus and Deuteronomy</note> and as it was clarified in saying: *"And the Lord has declared you today to be His people,"* etc. The end of the matter is that the whole Torah testifies that while Israel is at their watch and station, He too will be their help, guarding them, exalting them, and carrying them forever—all this with a "double condition" and a law from of old. ▢ Truly, if it were assumed that this nation and all its people together would rebel, transgress, and be foolish enough to turn away from after the Lord and to complain against the first fathers who brought them into this covenant, and they were to refuse Him, saying: "We want nothing of Him or His Torah," then in response to this, God would withdraw His company and His providence from them. They would be left to whatever follows from the ancient hatred and the uprising of enemies that occurs every day. Rather, it would happen suddenly, lest they wait, as it is written: *"And they forsook the Lord... and the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies"* <note>quoting the Book of Judges</note>. This is what He warns of throughout the book of Judges and what He says through Jeremiah: *"For behold, I am calling all the families of the kingdoms of the north, says the Lord; and they shall come and set every one his throne,"* etc. ▢ For once He issued a proclamation that they were not under His guard, those who rose did so on their own, and the power of their enemies stood. For behold, they are like a "vine tree among the trees of the forest" <note>a metaphor for Israel's vulnerability without God's protection</note>. ▢ And behold, when they are guarded or consumed, it will surely not be said that He "punished" them from Himself to bring upon them all this measure of destruction; rather, this was obligated upon them by His withdrawal from them, without doubt. And this is the essence of the covenant and the oath which shall never be nullified, for it cannot be imagined for a nation that it would choose to turn away from its God in any way, just as it cannot be imagined that all...

# Ten Utterances 45

עליו if he does not keep it, and behold, he is unable to protect himself and requires a guardian from the outside to protect him by the King's command. And the guardian is only capable of the protection entrusted to him by the hand of the King, etc. And behold, the one being guarded is greater than the guardian, just as the King is of higher standing than the craftsman. But the "guarding" of the Name <note>God</note> over Israel is the supreme guidance and the wondrous providence (*Hashgacha*) over them, which is a power set apart from every nation and tongue. No power or angel other than the Holy One, blessed be He, is capable of these two: the great cleaving <term>Dveikut; spiritual attachment</term> where He cleaves to them and they to Him, causing that Providence where there is no intermediary between them. And what is the Name called when supervising with such providence? "Guardian of Israel" <note>original: *Shomer Yisrael*</note>. From the perspective of this supreme guidance, He is called the "Shepherd of Israel." We do not find anywhere that an angel is essentially called the "Guardian" or "Shepherd" of Israel, as that would imply the essence of the guarding itself belongs to the angel. Rather, it says: *“For He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you”* <note>Psalm 91:11</note>, which indicates the ultimate distinction between one type of guarding and another—the difference between the Creator and the created. 

And as for the response regarding Michael being called the "Prince of Israel," our Sages of blessed memory already explained that he is only called so because he pleads for their needs and speaks as an advocate for them. In Exodus Rabbah, Chapter 18: "The Holy One established this Michael for Himself," as it says, *“At that time Michael, the great prince who stands over the children of your people, shall arise”* <note>Daniel 12:1</note>, meaning he pleads for the needs of Israel and speaks on their behalf, as it is said, *“Then the angel of the Lord answered and said: ‘O Lord of hosts, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem?’”* <note>Zechariah 1:12</note> and it says, *“And there is none that holds with me against these, except Michael your prince”* <note>Daniel 10:21</note>. 

Furthermore, these paths are only spoken of regarding Israel's superiority over the Ministering Angels <term>Malachei HaShareit; the angels who serve God</term> when Israel is righteous and performs the will of the Omnipresent. But when they do not perform the will of the Omnipresent, they are "servants to servants," for the nations that are given over to the rule of the Princes <note>the angelic patrons of the 70 nations</note> become their lords. At that time, it was from the kindnesses of the Name that Michael, the Prince of Kindness, was appointed to advocate for them. And in Exodus Rabbah, Chapter 1: "When Israel [sins], the Holy One says to Israel: 'If you had been worthy, I Myself would have been for you in the wilderness,' as it says, *‘And the Lord went before them’* <note>Exodus 13:21</note>. Now that you are not worthy, I am handing you over to a messenger." Thus, sin caused them to see a "reversed world"—the upper beings below and the lower beings above. 

As for the response regarding Joshua who prostrated to the angel and asked, *“What does my lord say?”* and also Daniel... our Sages said in Exodus Rabbah, Chapter 29, in this language: "The name of God was integrated with each and every one, like Michael and Gabriel." Behold, Joshua did not prostrate to the angel for its own sake, for he was greater than it, but he prostrated and called him "lord" because of the Name within him, since he was the messenger of the Name. It turns out the prostration was to the Name. Perhaps he said "What does my lord say," but in any other manner, he would not have prostrated to him at all; otherwise, he would have violated, Heaven forbid, the command *“You shall not prostrate to them.”* See there in *Etz Chaim* <note>Tree of Life, a kabbalistic work</note> where he elaborated and refuted his proofs. 

Furthermore, he <note>the author</note> wrote in the third chapter of the section on the Ultimate Purpose regarding the words of Ibn Ezra <note>Abraham ben Ezra</note>, who said: "And if because of his knowledge of the judgment of Gehenna and the Garden of Eden, we have not written to straighten the crookedness..." He wrote as follows: "Behold, this man, famous for his wisdom, his mind was not satisfied by merely hiding the heretical views—meaning he diminished the honor of Man who was made in the image and likeness—but he also cursed the perfect ones by the way his wicked tongue labored to judge the Torah, the righteous, and the upright who direct themselves [to God]. And moreover, there are people who occupy themselves with external matters in the manner of 'seeking a reward,' as our Sages said: 'Every one who occupies himself with the Torah of the burnt-offering, it is as if he offered a burnt-offering.'"

mentioned in the words of Ibn Ezra, of blessed memory. Rather, they <note>the righteous</note> "plow and think" first in the Kingdom; their existence is permanent in their station. This matter is rooted in the words of prophecy and is received by the holy Sages of Israel, by whose mouths we live. They said in Tractate Berakhot, Chapter 1: "Rabbi Eleazar said: The righteous are greater than the Ministering Angels, as it is said regarding the furnace: *'The king saw...'* and it is written: *'He answered and said, Lo, I see four men... and the form of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'*" <note>Daniel 3:25</note> And in Lamentations Rabbah, Rabbi Abba said: "In the future to come, the partition of the righteous will be further inward than that of the Ministering Angels, and the angels will ask them, 'What new laws has the Holy One renewed today?'" Once Nebuchadnezzar saw Gabriel, he immediately recognized him and said, "This is the one I saw in the war of Sennacherib, when he burned the army." When Nebuchadnezzar saw the proclamation, all his limbs trembled, and he said, "This is the angel I saw in the war of Sennacherib, who spread like a small spark of fire and burned his entire camp."

Gabriel said: 'The greatness of the Holy One is not manifested thus. I am the Prince of Fire; let me go down and cool it from the within and heat it from without, and I will perform a miracle within a miracle.' The Holy One said to him: 'Go down.'" And in another place: "The beloved friend Michael was with Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah." 

In any case, we have learned that the righteous are more numerous and more honored than the Ministering Angels, and they are not subject to the constant changes mentioned in the words of Ibn Ezra. Our Sages already explained: "He said to him, this is Michael and Gabriel, for the Princes above do not change, and they do not switch." And in *Midrash Shocher Tov* on Psalm 100: "That which six hundred thousand could not hear, Moses heard by himself when the Divine Speech called to him, as it says, *‘And He called to Moses’* <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>—not to the others—to teach you that the righteous are greater than the Ministering Angels, for the angels cannot hear His voice but rather stand and tremble, etc." And in the chapter "The Displaced Sinew": "*‘And he strove with an angel and prevailed’*—I do not know who became the prince over whom. When it says *‘For you have striven (sarita) [with God and man]’* it tells us that Jacob was the prince over the angel." And in Vayikra Rabbah, Chapter 24: "*‘And you shall be only (rak) above’*—I might think 'like Me'? The verse says *‘rak’*, which is a term of exclusion: My greatness is above your greatness." Behold, He only excluded His own greatness, but the greatness of man is above the greatness of the Ministering Angels. And in the book *Suri Dor*: "*‘And a man wrestled’*—some say it was the Prince of Esau, and some say it was Michael. Rabbi Marfon said: Michael was not permitted to move from his place until Jacob gave him permission. *‘He said, Let me go’*—Jacob said to him, 'Are you a thief or a kidnapper?' He said to him, 'Come and see the groups of Ministering Angels saying to Michael: Rise, for the time for song has arrived.' He said to them, 'I cannot because of this [man].'" 

And they said in Genesis Rabbah, Chapter 76: "Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Shimon disagree: Who is greater, the guardian or the guarded? From what is written, *‘For He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you,’* the guardian is greater than the guarded. Rabbi Yehuda says: Who is greater, the carrier or the carried? From what is written, *‘Upon their hands they shall carry you,’* the one being carried is greater than the carrier. Rabbi Shimon says: From what is written, *‘Let me go (send me),’* the sender is greater than the one being sent." Here they have explained that the status of Israel over the angels is due to the Torah and the commandments within them, and because of them, the carried and the guarded are of higher standing than the carrier and the guardian. And the matter is that Man is the "end of action" but "first in thought" and his soul...

Everything is the power above the participant, and the cause is above the effect. It turns out that the Holy One, blessed be He, is first and difficult for all of them, and the First Effect is a cause for all effects truly from Him, and they are elevated above his thought." 

And furthermore, most sages see this in angels because it was mentioned in the words of our Sages that the angels were created on the second day or the fifth day, according to how they disagreed on this. And it said that the angels were not in the creation of the Name—how is it possible to say that after they were created, He would justify the created? And he is humbled as she wrote to say that they preceded the First Cause, etc... checking in the name of Rabbi Gerushah. And furthermore, it is explained that a law was created for him, created as a seal in the likeness of the heavens... and the things are because he did not specify that it was in the glorious kingdom.

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of the human soul and its hierarchy relative to celestial beings. The previous page established the context of the covenant and the "Second Discourse," exploring how the physical body relates to the spiritual essence. This page specifically addresses the debate between the philosophers (like Maimonides) and the Kabbalists (like the author of Avodat HaKodesh) regarding whether humans or angels hold a higher rank in the cosmic order.</meta>

# The Second Discourse

**Increasing.** Just as it increases evil things like types of hot drugs, bitter things, thorns, and thistles, so too the human body can be and becomes as "clear as the very heavens for purity" <note>original: *ke-etzem ha-shamayim la-tohar*, a reference to Exodus 24:10</note> and like **Garments of Light** <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* spelled with an Aleph (א), referring to Adam’s state before the primordial sin</note>. Yet it is also a murky matter like **Garments of Skin** <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* spelled with an Ayin (ע), referring to the physical body after the fall</note>. Even now, while it is "Garments of Skin," whoever wishes to refine and sanctify themselves can cause their body to become clean and pure. The matter is as if you would say: the soul within the body is light, and the body’s light is within the body of skin—like "swallowing the holy" <term>Kibl’a et HaKodesh; a concept of spiritual absorption</term> within its sheath. But the Garments of Light were not nullified; they were merely absorbed into the sheath. This refined and subtle "light of the body" belongs specifically to Israel, drawn to them from the first Adam <note>The first human</note>; therefore "you are called Adam" <note>A famous Talmudic dictum from Yevamot 61a: "You are called 'Adam' (Man), but the idolaters are not called 'Adam'."</note>. At the time of the Giving of the Torah, when the "filth of the serpent" ceased, souls were clothed as if in Garments of Light—meaning they stood in a refined and subtle garment as clear as the heavens for purity, which is the power of the Garments of Light. Thus, they were complete in body and soul. Similarly, at the Plains of Moab, even though they were clothed in Garments of Skin, the refined and subtle body was nonetheless awakened within them because they were sanctified. It was a "perfect congregation," as it is written: *“But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today”* <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. This refined and subtle body extends through every generation to anyone who wishes to awaken it.

From this, what is written will be clarified: when death entered Adam, why did it enter all the generations that come from him? For the "leaven of the Orchard" <note>Referring to the sin in the Garden of Eden</note> would not suffice to explain this simply because Adam’s soul includes all souls; for death is not essential to the soul, but only happens to it by chance. One might say the matter is that since he became clothed in "garments of skin and flesh," and his offspring are like him, then death is natural because every composite thing is ultimately destined to be separated. That which was meant to be eternal life belongs specifically to the **Garments of Light** (spelled with an *Aleph*), as I elaborated in the introduction. This reasoning, however, only settles the matter regarding the nations of the world, and likewise for Israel when death stems from sin—then, according to nature, every composite must separate when its time comes. However, concerning those of whom the Sages said "they died only because of the counsel of the serpent" <note>Referring to four biblical figures who never sinned but died because death was decreed upon the human race</note>, meaning death entered Adam, this poses a local difficulty. Rather, the intention refers to "Adam" literally as explained: since death was decreed upon Adam himself, **it was also decreed** upon us, for we ourselves are "Adam," as Israel is literally called "Adam."

Through this, the verse *“Know the God of your father”* <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note> is clarified. For these are the "two faces" that were explained: on one side the souls are educated as a soul that is a "portion of God from above," and from the second side, it touches upon the "portion of your father," the "Beginning" <note>Hebrew: *Reishit*</note> in a high level. In their higher aspect, they are equal to the portion of God, and in their lower aspect, they are equal to the portion of the father, which is the physical part. Therefore, the oath took effect on all generations and generations of generations.

**Furthermore**, there is a hidden matter regarding what the Sages said: "To what is the matter comparable? To a king’s son..." etc. The phrase *“the God of your father”* teaches us about the great level of Israel through the medium of the Torah they received, for they are the purpose of creation. The purpose of creation was for the sake of the Torah and Israel; thereafter, all lower and upper created beings exist for the sake of Israel and their needs. The level of Israel is higher even than the levels of the supernal angels, for "the righteous are greater than the ministering angels" for a reason we will explain later. However, because there is a great dispute among the sages of Israel regarding this investigation, it is proper to elaborate, clarify, and white-wash the matter

->until it is fully clear:<-

## The View of the Philosophers
We have learned that the knowledge of Man comes from the light of the soul's springs. Maimonides <note>The Rambam</note>, of blessed memory, in Chapter 3 of the *Laws of the Foundations of the Torah*, agreed with their view, writing in these words: "The knowledge of the stars and the spheres is less than the knowledge of the angels, but greater than the knowledge of human beings." Thus, the Rabbi did not distinguish between those who received the Torah and others, for in this matter, [Rabbinic] wisdom and Greek [philosophy] united. He follows his own system, as he wrote in the *Guide for the Perplexed* (Part 2, Ch. 11 and Ch. 13), describing them <note>humans</note> as having less light than the light of the spheres, and certainly less than the angels. He wrote similarly in Chapter 2 of the *Laws of the Foundations of the Torah* that there is no difference in this regard between a human, a sphere, and an angel. In Chapter 4, he wrote regarding the "power of equilibrium" that a person should feel shame at his lowliness, worthlessness, and insignificance when he evaluates himself against one of the great holy bodies <note>the stars/planets</note>, and certainly against one of the pure forms that are separated from matter <note>the angels</note>. Behold, the Rabbi established a monument and many places to disparage and lower the "donkey-like" physical matter <note>A pun on *Chomer* (matter) and *Chamor* (donkey)</note> and the Supernal Image.

Abraham Ibn Ezra <note>The Ra'ba</note>, of blessed memory, also "sent forth his tongue" with pride and his anger flared against the one who "sent his hand" against the angels by saying that human beings are more honored than they. He wrote in his commentary on *Mishpatim* <note>Exodus 21-24</note> in these words: "Behold, I send forth my hand against the pride... may arrogance not go forth from his mouth" concerning the Gaon <note>Likely referring to Saadia Gaon</note> who said that humans are more honored than the ministering angels and that for the sake of humans they were created. His proofs were the words of the Sages, but they only spoke about the angels who are "renewed every moment," and their words are true. He <note>the Gaon</note> further brought proof from the verse *“Behold, I send an angel before you,”* arguing that the "one who is guarded" is more honored than the "guardian." To this, Ibn Ezra replied that his words are flawed, and one should "be careful of his presence" <note>a play on Exodus 23:21</note> because the purpose of the angel is to "guard you on the way." He argued against the idea that the "guarded" is more honored than the "guardian," noting that for the sake of our father Abraham, Moses, Aaron, and David our King, they were shepherds of sheep <note>guardians of animals</note>. Also, "the Lord our God neither slumbers nor sleeps, the Guardian of Israel." Are these four letters <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> "sheep"? If "the Lord does not guard the city," and "He will guard us like a shepherd his flock"—does that mean the flock is more honored than God? The scripture compares **the Name** <note>God</note> to a King, the angels to messengers, and humans to servants. It is also written, "the Prince of the kingdom of Greece" and "the Prince of the kingdom of Persia," and "Michael the Great Prince." Why would he be called "Prince over Israel" if Israel is more honored than him? And how would God command the "honored ones" <note>angels</note> to be careful of the one smaller in level than them? For the verse says, *“Be careful of his presence.”* As for what was said, *“for he will not pardon your transgression,”* it is because of his understanding and knowledge. There are no humans more honored than the Prophets, yet Joshua, of whom it was written "a prophet I will raise for them from among their brothers like you," when he saw the angel, he fell on his face and said, "What does my lord speak to his servant?" And so too Daniel says, "my lords," and "how can the servant of this my lord speak with my lord?"

And the "Tofkot" <note>unclear; likely a reference to a specific work or person, or a scribal error</note> said, "and my lord is wise like an angel of God," and she did not come to disparage David. Furthermore, it is written, "and the house of David shall be like God, like the angel of the Lord," which means "like the angels." **Furthermore**, "He charges His angels with error," even those who "dwell in houses of clay." He <note>Ibn Ezra</note> continues at length to prove from the words of prophecy the low level of man and his inferiority compared to the stars, and certainly compared to the angels. I have not seen fit to respond and elaborate on them, except for what is written at the end of *Bochan Dat Ve-Lashon* <note>Examination of Religion and Language</note>: I say that a child of a woman who thinks his hand has reached a high level in wisdom, let him see where he is—only within the category of the "living" <note>animals</note>, and our stomachs and our flight are like those of the beasts of the earth. If they treat his faith as vile, etc., and if because of his knowledge of the laws of damages <note>civil law</note>, for they were only given to straighten the crooked—if we were dwellers in a place where there is no ox, we would not need the "law of the goring ox." If we were dwellers in the tents of Kedar <note>nomads</note>, we would not need the laws of "uprooting and returning." If we were dwellers in the land of Hodu <note>India</note>, we would not need the laws of theft, murder, and false testimony. And if because of the knowledge of the Torahs and the commandments, there is no wise man who understands them—why fast on the Tenth <note>Yom Kippur</note> and the divisions of the sacrifices? The witness is what Moses said to the generation of the desert after saying, "I have made known the statutes of God and His laws" for forty years, yet "the Lord has not given you a heart to know." Behold, even he <note>Moses</note> said in the year of his death, he who is the Prophet of Prophets and the Sage of Sages: "O Lord, You have begun [to show Your servant Your greatness]," testifying that only now he began to know. For who can know the thoughts of the Name? For they are deep and exalted beyond all prophets. These are his <note>Ibn Ezra's</note> words.

However, in the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Service of the Holy by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, Chapter 4 of the "Section on Purpose," he rejected all of Ibn Ezra's proofs, and "a wind shall carry them all away." He wrote: As for what he replied to the Gaon by saying "Behold I send... I will go before you," I will answer this after I ask: why was the level of the Torah changed to be higher than the level of Israel? Regarding Israel, it is written "for My angel shall go before you," but regarding Cyrus it says "I will go before you." The answer to this is that the angel going before Israel is not a wonder, because Israel is more honored than him due to the level of the Torah they received and the soul within them, which is not the case for any other nation or tongue. Had it said regarding Cyrus "My angel shall go before you," there would have been room to err, thinking there is no difference between those who receive the Torah and the nations, and that even other nations are greater than the ministering angels. Therefore, it did not say "My angel" regarding him, but "I will go," so there would be no room for error. He further replied as he wrote regarding the claim that the "guarded" is more honored than the "guardian," which is the view of our Sages in *Genesis Rabbah* (Parasha 77). As for what he replied to the Gaon from the fact that the Patriarchs were shepherds of sheep, it is not a valid answer. It is surprising that he equated the whole matter, suggesting that because the "guarded" must be greater than the "guardian," there is no relationship or comparison between them in terms of form and intellect. No error should follow from this "guarding" to say the one guarded is greater; the guardian suffers no loss of honor through that guarding at all.

Most importantly, the guarding of the righteous by an angel is not like the guarding of sheep by a man. In this manner, they <note>angels</note> do not guard them to derive "fruit" from them like other tasks; rather, the task of shepherding came to the Patriarchs to distance them from settled areas and to be in the desert, etc. And his reply that God is called the "Guardian of Israel" is also not a valid answer, for these things are only said to the Prophets who are somewhat comparable; and certainly, if there is a level to this, it is not like the superiority the soul of the righteous has over the angel. Furthermore, the guarding of the Name over Israel is not like the guarding of an angel, for the guarding of an angel over Israel is only like the parable of a craftsman who guards the king's son from some damage destined to come

It contrasts Maimonides' and Ibn Ezra's view of human lowliness with the Kabbalistic defense (Avodat HaKodesh) that the Torah elevates Israel above the celestial hosts.</summary>
