<margin>
Behold, even the elements, which are raw materials like stones and heat upon which everything moves, and the "spirit upon the waters" <note>A reference to Genesis 1:2</note>—upon this rests the inanimate, the plant, and upon the plant, the abundance from the Divine Presence <term>Shechinah; the indwelling presence of God</term> draws near in stages. Together, the matter is placed, which is the vital force influenced within it. That light that shines in it is like a star, and when it separates, it returns to its elements alone. The light that shines in the aspect of the Divine Presence is as mentioned. And now, because the elements are gathered through eating, and because some are a collection of parts through the "shells" <term>Kelipot; the husks or shards of evil that conceal divine light</term>, they rise from level to level. From the living things that descend to the earth and nurse from that "arm," as it is known concerning herbs, etc., they draw closer to the divine. Concerning this, it is said that every herb has an appointed angel. Afterward, the beast eats the herb; if so, the light draws closer to it and a greater illumination grows within it than before, since they have ascended from level to level. And when the human eats, all four elements of the soul can reach their elements, for there is a place there where the power of the light of the King of Kings shines. Through this, the human is distant from the angel, and it is fitting, for there is no excellence in the gathering of his parts more than the second, in the power of the abundance. But the human is not so, for within him is this portion of light that illuminates his soul with a supreme light, drawing from that abundance over the angel for his own sake; for now, he receives the abundance from the very source of his soul.
</margin>

**Action** <note>Hebrew: *Assiyah*, the lowest of the four spiritual worlds</note> is like a silversmith of silver who separates each and every type for itself into four kinds. In the manner of Action, that which is in **Emanation** <note>Hebrew: *Atzilut*, the highest world</note> is the head of the Emanation in **Creation** <note>Hebrew: *Beriah*, the second world</note>, and Action in Creation is the head of Emanation in **Formation** <note>Hebrew: *Yetzirah*, the third world</note>, and Action in Formation is the head of Emanation in Action. From the chain of these levels, all the worlds evolved: from Emanation to Creation, from Creation to the Palaces, from the Palaces to the "Shells," and from the Shells to the reality of the Firmaments, which are the constellations. From them come the four elements and the fifth, which are the thick and complex ones.

It is found, according to this, that the four elements in the firmaments, with their vitality, are spread out. The four elements of the firmaments are the same as those in the World of Formation, and so on until the highest ones. However, the delay according to the chain is according to their distance from the place of wonder. There is nothing in the world that does not have abundance and light influenced upon it from above. It is impossible unless that abundance, in its distance, comes from the "backwards" side, which is the "face" to them <note>This refers to the Kabbalistic concept that lower worlds receive only a diminished, "hind-side" reflection of the divine light</note>. Thus, you will not find anything in this world that does not have some spirituality and vitality, according to the value of its body and matter, and according to the level of its distance from the Source.

**The Parable** is of a large lantern burning in the middle of a palace. The contents of the dwelling will not illuminate the corners of the palace in the far reaches except with a small amount of light. As long as the light draws closer to the lantern, the light is more beautiful, until one who reaches within four cubits of it will have their eyes dimmed by the greatness of its light.

They have this advantage over it: **Earth**, which is the last in level, does not move and its place does not shift. **Water** moves more, and the element of **Fire** is even more wakeful, rising by its nature higher and higher. Such is the order of the ascent of complex beings one over the other: over the animal, and over the speaking animal <note>The human being</note>. From this, we can understand the matter of the soul of the beast and the soul of a human. When that matter is gathered, composed of the four elements, and the beast is formed from it—the eating of the living creation—behold, because the elements were formed into a distinguished shape, they rose in level and drew closer to the vital light influenced within it. That light that shines in it is its soul. In truth, there is a "vital soul," but in the ultimate truth, there is nothing in that soul at all [of the higher levels], because like the source, upon separation, it returns to its elements to be distanced from the light. It has no "Soul," "Spirit," or "Breath" <term>Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah; the three primary levels of the human soul</term> that would ascend. It is only like the likeness of a star.

When it draws closer to the lantern, it shines within it, and that light is called its vitality. When it draws away, the light departs from it, and this is its death. In the manner of purity and holiness, the light that shines in them is purity and holiness. Therefore, the Torah forbade eating certain things that are known to be influenced by the "Shells." With this, we understand that all things in this world ascend. That seed, the thickness and fatness of the earth, and the powers of the elements from the trees, rise to become part of the "arm" of the sower. That which was previously under an appointed angel has now left its domain, and the angel appointed over the herb shines within it.

The herb is then eaten and becomes a part of the limb of the beast, formed in its image, drawing closer to its source. Because of its proximity to its source, it leaves the domain of the angel over the herb and enters under the angel appointed over the beast. And when the human eats it, it reaches an excellent level as it approaches the reality of the human, upon whom shines the light of the King of Kings, which is the supreme Divine Presence. Israel is not under any constellation, angel, or seraph; on the contrary, the angels receive abundance from the righteous. This is the reason that while Israel was in the world, the vitality of the abundance was through the Divine Presence itself. But when they sinned, He said: "Behold, I send an angel before you" <note>Exodus 23:20</note>, which showed the lowering of their level to be under the angels. All four elements of the soul, even in their [physical] elements, have rest within them. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "The first man was created from a high place, the place of the Altar," for there is the strength of the illumination of the King of Kings.

Behold, in this chapter it was explained that the angels are refined and pure, and their closeness to the upper elements is clear. In this regard, the human is distant and it would seem there is no excellence in the gathering of his parts compared to the gathering of the parts of an angel. But the angel has nothing in its interior but "simple light," in the way that light transmits light. The human is not so; he has within him a clean and pure soul, such that when he empowers the soul over the parts of his matter, the light of his soul—a supreme light—shines in him and draws abundance even over the angel. This is because his soul is [from the world of Emanation] and does not need to receive through any of the levels, but rather through itself, for the light receives abundance from the place of the source of his soul. Thus far from the Philosopher.

---

## Behold,
it has been explained to you from the words of the Philosopher that regarding the creation of the parts of the elements, the level of the angel is superior to the human. Perhaps the verses "Behold, in His angels [He puts no trust]" etc. <note>Job 4:18</note> revolve around this, indicating the lowliness of man compared to the angel. However, from the perspective of the soul, he is more than an angel; on the contrary, the angel longs for him.

---

## And Now,
the understanding is completed according to this. It was fitting for the human to have the preparation of his four elements be higher than the composition of the four elements of the angel, since the inner light within him is greater than the inner light of the angel. There is a second answer to the matter: the first is so that he may have **Free Will**. For then he is truly composed of both the good and the bad—the good from the side of the soul, and the matter is called "bad." When he triumphs from the side of the soul, then by justice his level is added to the level of the angel. This is the reason I wrote above, and like that which we learned: "According to the pain is the reward" <note>Pirkei Avot 5:23</note>. So too we say: the human is "commanded and performs," while the angel is not "commanded and performing" <note>A reference to the principle that one who is obligated to do a commandment and does it is greater than one who does it voluntarily</note>.

<margin>
Pinchas wrote:
From the language of the Philosopher, we will explain that which he wrote: in the days of the kings, they would receive from the aforementioned staff, and the constellation was born under the sign that speaks, and the understanding of what is written "and from the order of the stars in their paths" <note>Judges 5:20</note>, they fought against the angel. And so it is written in *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>A classic Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>.
</margin>

The angel does not act by choice, but only good, because he is entirely good. This is not the case for the human; the good he does is from his own choice. Even though the angel sometimes has some choice, as we find with the "angels of the heights" who sinned and were suspended <note>A reference to the fallen angels like Shemhazai and Azazel</note>, that is an uncommon matter. It is only because there is a deficiency included in being a "created thing" that clings to it. This is why, after the human clothed himself in "Garments of Skin" and returns to "Garments of Light," his level will be greater than it was at first. For then he was created with a hidden choice that was not so revealed; but now, choice between good and evil is revealed, and the sides are balanced, and it is in his hand to tilt the scales as he wishes. This is the reason that his four elements, even though they are superior, are nonetheless material—for his benefit, if he so desires. In the future, the part of evil that was revealed will be completely nullified at its root, and he will remain entirely good without dross, and merit being "all good."

<column-break/>

This is from the side of his choice. For from the side of matter, he would descend. The awe-inspiring thing in them is this choice; it is called choice in the matter I elaborated on in the introduction. It is greater than these, and this remains.

---

## The Answer
The second is that the Holy One, blessed be He, created the human to be a composite of both upper and lower beings—the entire chain from beginning to end. Therefore, it was necessary for him to be in this composition, for the One who composes, blessed be He, knows how to compose him so that there is within him the lower like the upper. On the contrary, this is the answer: that he is joined to a Divine Soul because he includes all of reality, as explained before us.

## The General Rule
The result of all that was mentioned is that when a human is stripped and naked of all perfection, he is considered as vanity, a worm, and a wonder; he and the beast are equal. Concerning this matter come the verses that exaggerate his worthlessness in comparison to the upper beings, as I hinted in the name of the "Philosopher" and their separation. However, when the power of the righteous grows—those who liken the "form to its Creator" <note>Genesis Rabbah 27:1</note> through their labor in wisdom, fear, and proper deeds—then they have the upper hand over all created beings, upper and lower. All this is through the Torah. This is hinted at by the mediator <note>Moses</note> in saying, "I stand between the Lord and you" <note>Deuteronomy 5:5</note>; behold, no creature intervenes or partitions between the Lord and Israel. Israel sits first in the kingdom, and Moses is above them.

With this, their words of blessed memory will be explained: when Moses ascended to the heights, the angels said, "What is this one born of a woman doing among us?" This is difficult, for is not their own prince, Metatron, the "Prince of the Face," also "born of a woman" according to the tradition of the Sages of Truth—namely, Enoch who became Metatron? This is a great difficulty. But the point is that when Moses was in the heavens, he ascended to the heights while still in flesh and blood; he did not remove the garment of matter. Just as he was born from a woman, so he remained, and yet he merited to ascend among them. This was not the case with Enoch; when he ascended, he removed the physical garment that came to him from being born of a woman. As it is brought in the *Book of the Palaces* <note>Sefer Hekhalot</note>: Rabbi Ishmael said: "I asked Metatron, 'Why are you called by the name of your Creator with seventy names? And you are greater than all the princes and all the angels, higher than all the ministers, more honored than all the hosts, and greater than all the mighty ones in greatness, kingship, and honor?' He answered and said to him: 'Because I am Enoch, the son of Jared, and when the generation of the Flood sinned and were corrupted in their deeds...'"

This is the secret of the covering, for those who did not know its secret, but for those to whom it was revealed, they know it. God forbid they should not know, and it would pass like a passing cloud, etc. Just as with the existence of the world, they were upon the fullness of that sign and name and light. I have placed a distinction between a drop and a star <note>A common Talmudic metaphor for the precision of divine providence</note> for the Holy One, blessed be He, for it is not mentioned in the assembly of daughters unless they give a woman, etc., in the way of the spheres. # Ten Discourses: Discourse Two

**In the image and likeness of God**, to repair the Supernal Glory, the King in His glory, through the action of the **deeds of the Torah** and the purity of one's thought and intention within them. To this end, all the virtues included in the Great Name were included in the human, so that he would have the power and sufficiency in his hand for this. For the spirit of the matter begins with this power being handed over to the human, who is created in the "image and likeness." His awakening below is the cause for providing that awakening above according to the proper intention, stirring the Supernal matters on high. He is the cause for giving that awakening so that the Great Name shall be in His glory, and this is the ultimate purpose of divine service and His will.

For this reason, the commandments and warnings of the entire Torah came about, and the necessity that this power be for the need of the "Emanation" <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, the realm of pure divinity</term>, which is the Godhead, to increase its light. This is for the "Needs of the High," as explained at length previously according to the great ones, that the actions of the righteous and their effects are even greater than those of the ministering angels. Because of this, they said that the Holy One, blessed be He, **longs for the prayers of the righteous**, but they did not say this regarding the service or songs of the angels.

In the *Chapters of the Palaces* <note>Pirkei Hekhalot</note>, chapter 9, they learned this and said to the angels: "Raise your eyes to the firmament toward your house of prayer at the hour when Israel says 'Holy' <term>Kedushah; the 'Holy, Holy, Holy' prayer</term> before Me. For I have no pleasure in all my world that I created except in that hour when your eyes are raised to My eyes and My eyes are in your eyes." Furthermore, the "Sanctification" reaches us from the Ministering Angels, as it is written: "And one called to another and said..." <note>Isaiah 6:3</note> but we do not find that this occurs when the angels sanctify, except through Israel. 

Additionally, according to Resh Lakish, in this language Rabbi Ishmael said: "Happy is Israel! How beloved they are before the Holy One, blessed be He, more than the ministering angels." For at the hour when the ministering angels seek to sing a song first on high, mountains of fire and hills of flame surround the Throne of Glory. But the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them: "Be silent, every single angel, every living creature (*Chayah*), every wheel (*Ofan*), and every burning one (*Seraph*) <note>These are different classes of angels</note> that I created in My world, until I hear and listen first to all the songs and praises of Israel." As it is written: "With the songs and melodies of Israel," which teaches that the voice of the songs and praises of Israel is sweeter to the Holy One, blessed be He, than that of the ministering angels. And it is written: "When the morning stars sang together"—these are Israel, who are compared to stars—and afterward, "and all the sons of God shouted for joy"—these are the angels. My glory is not in the earth, My glory is not in the heavens; those high ones of the world, my lovers in My name, His glory is above all the earth. 

These aforementioned statements and the superiority of the righteous over the ministering angels have already been transcribed in the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>Holy Service, by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>. The secret is that the "Discourse" is one that repairs the Name through the power of being made in the "image and likeness." The Rabbi wrote that "O Lord our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth" <note>Psalm 8:1</note> hints at this; meaning, the intention of the human in his creation is the unification of the Great Name in His glory. This is "You have made him a little less than the angels (Elohim)," where "Lord" and "Master" refer to two names <note>original: Yud-He and Aleph-Dalet</note>. 

And this is a wonder: that You placed this power and ability in a dweller of the earth, which is the human. Therefore, when a person contemplates the "construction of Your heavens," he sees how great his power is. This is what is meant by "How majestic is Your name"—meaning the human, who is made in the "construction of Your heavens," how great is his power! For his deeds and service will be the cause for "Your majesty to be placed upon the heavens." This refers to the abundance and light coming from the Supernal source upon the heavens, which is the Great Name, and through this, He is unified in His glory. This power was placed "in the earth"—meaning in the lower realms—which was not placed in the upper realms. 

Afterward, he says as if in wonder at this high level: "When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers... what is man that You are mindful of him?" I say in my heart, what is his lowliness compared to Yours? When a person examines himself, it becomes true to him that he is at the edge of deficiency compared to You. And even compared to the angels, he seems so from the visible side of man, when he is stripped of perfection. However, when he is at the peak of the aforementioned perfection and clings to Him, may He be blessed, behold, he is superior to the angel. This matter can be said regarding the soul—it is "a little less than God" <note>Psalm 8:5. The Hebrew 'Elohim' can mean God, judges, or angels; here the author plays on the soul's divine origin.</note>.

->**And behold**<-

<insert>**And behold**</insert> verses are stated which, from their plain meaning, seem to prove the opposite of what was mentioned: "Behold, He puts no trust in His servants, and His angels He charges with folly; how much more those who dwell in houses of clay" <note>Job 4:18-19</note>, and "Behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in His sight; how much more one who is abominable and corrupt, a man..." <note>Job 15:15-16</note>. 

In *Avodat HaKodesh*, chapter 8 of the "Parts of the Purpose," he elaborated on this and explained it clearly according to the commentators. They explained that angels are pure and clear, like the collection of the parts of the Kingdom and their closeness to the Supernal piety; in this respect, the human is distant from them. But in the **inner aspect**—that is, from the side of the soul—the human is above them. He elaborated in the chapter on the "Works of Creation" on this entire matter and its foundation. 

The matter is that the four Supernal elements are the secret of: the element of Water (*Gevurah*; Strength), the element of Fire (*Tiferet*; Beauty), the element of Spirit (*Malchut*; Sovereignty), and the element of Dust. They are unified in the ultimate unity. Through these four emanated elements, the elements in the order of Emanation, Creation, Formation, and Action <term>Abiya; an acronym for the four worlds of Kabbalah: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Assiyah</term> were produced and came into being, level after level, from cause to effect. All four levels in each and every one are separated within themselves: in Emanation there is "Abiya," and in the world of Emanation; in Creation there is "Abiya," and in the world of Creation; and so too in Formation and Action.

...and the secret of the covenant according to the beginning, it is found that the soul is distant from the body, and this is the third of the words of our Sages of blessed memory. This is the explanation of it all according to the *Chapters of the Palaces*. And these are the words of the Rama <note>Rabbi Menahem Azariah da Fano</note>, may his soul rest in Eden, on the standing of the three angels of the Lord, peace be upon Him, and he was prepared for the Lord, who was in the vision of the Glory. And this is "And behold, the covenant," and it was the secret of the multiplication, and they multiply in the way of cause and effect. To this I have understood that he was obligated so that they would not be in the level of the "smallness" of the soul, and those levels are ten: *Chayot, Ofanim, Arelim, Chashmalim, Seraphim, Malakhim, Elohim, Benei Elohim, Keruvim, Ishim* <note>The ten ranks of angels as categorized by Maimonides</note>.

And behold, Enoch was changed and refined more and more, and they sought him in many matters... the Ramban, may his soul rest in Eden, explained regarding the Repentance of the Apostles <note>original: "Teshuvat HaShlichim"</note>... and this is his language: "The explanation of 'And he saw three men' is that it was heard by the holy assembly... and behold, three angels in human form..." everything can be repaired and refined, and it is as if the kingship and the spirits were revealed. But for me, they are food for the multitude, and I have given to illuminate their knowledge... if only they would not sin, they would be songs and melodies and His glory for My creation. And I wait for the children of man to be clothed in light and in the refinement for the young ones, and I wait for the children of man. Had they not been in their state, all the merits of the fathers would be established, and he would be gracious to the children of man. Therefore, it is found that we have reached a great level in the hint. And everything is for the purpose of informing what was and will be in the level of the children of man. Until here are his words. 

And behold, according to this explanation, the angels were diminished in order to show the power of the Torah and its refinement. And the aforementioned is for the answer and the matter. And this is the matter of the three angels known as written, and the matters regarding their creation and their appointment. This is necessary for them to be in the world. And this is what the Zohar says: "He opened and said..." and this is the reason and this is the secret. And also, even he will warn from the Palaces of the worlds that inhabit the end of the world for life... but they did not know its secret... those who were revealed to know, did not know... but if it was not revealed to them, they did not know, God forbid. And it passed in the way of a vision... how many people and their existence were upon the fullness of that sign and name and light. I have placed a distinction between a drop and a star for the Holy One, blessed be He, for it is not mentioned in the assembly of daughters unless they give a woman, etc., in the way of the spheres. And the Ramban said these are things they did not know, but what was revealed to them, they knew... see the comparison of the Holy One, blessed be He, testifying about Himself on page 29 regarding the transition through the seven heavens, which is full of light for the vision... and those who are placed there know the depth of the soul, to be covered below like a person who is covered in his house, and they should not be completed as a person in the market, in order not to be revealed, as it is written: "And you shall not go out, every man from the door of his house," and from that he opened the gate.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of spiritual perfection, shifting from the metaphysical "garments" of the soul discussed on the previous page to the internal motivations of the human heart: Fear and Love. # Ten Treatises
-> Page 47 <-

...to another. This indicates that one who has the "fear of God" in his heart is essentially afraid of transgressing His commandments so that those punishments resulting from the forbidden acts do not befall him. Likewise, when a positive commandment comes his way, he performs it so that the reward inherent in and drawn from that commandment is not withheld from him. Thus, we find this person serving out of a love for reward and a fear of punishment. As they said in the Talmudic tractate *Sotah*, in the chapter "He Who Takes" <note>Sotah 22b</note>: "One who separates himself out of love, and one who separates himself out of fear." Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki (1040–1105), the foundational commentator on the Bible and Talmud</note> of blessed memory explained: "Separating out of a love for the reward of the commandment, rather than a love for the commandments of his Creator; and out of a fear of punishments." 

Now, service in this manner—while it is very good, as the person is careful and guards himself from doing evil so as not to defile himself and bring his impurity into the Holy Sanctuary—is not yet "perfect service" or "perfect fear." This is because such a person does not truly fear God; he only fears for himself. We have learned in the *Ethics of the Fathers*: "Let the fear of Heaven be upon you" <note>Pirkei Avot 1:3</note>, implying it should be fear of *Him*, not fear for *yourselves*. The one who fears and serves in the way we described fears only for himself—that he might be punished with those penalties the soul incurs for transgressing. 

There are others who are not held back by the dread of spiritual punishment, for such things seem light to them compared to the weight of their physical desires. However, they stay their hand and restrain themselves out of dread for the "reproof of the judges" appointed to punish those who violate the Torah and its laws. Still another type of person "fears," but his fear is regarding the "mishaps of time" and its troubles: he worries they might befall him, his children, his household, or his property and wealth. Out of dread that he might lack bread, or that his children might die in his lifetime, or that his body might suffer from "evil and persistent ailments," he keeps his hand from doing any evil. 

While these are certainly valid deterrents that prevent a person from sinning—and it is a good thing that he at least believes there is a Master who pays a reward to those who love Him—this is not the fear required of the "perfected ones." Nevertheless, any cause that prevents a person from falling from the heights of virtue or from being defiled by guilt is considered good, and one is permitted to engage in it. As the Sages said in the chapter "The Place Where They Customarily..." <note>Pesachim 50b</note>: "A person should always engage in Torah and commandments, even if it is not for its own sake (*shelo lishmah*), for out of doing it not for its own sake, he will eventually come to do it for its own sake (*lishmah*)." This "External Fear" is the gate and the beginning through which one enters into the inner holiness, which is the "Pure Internal Fear."

Similarly, there is a "Love" that stems from self-interest. Every love of kindness has an external part, where a person loves the Omnipresent because of his own success. When he sees himself succeeding in all his affairs, he loves God. If he sees that everything he does prospers, his love for his Creator is a "response" to that success. Sometimes he serves God specifically so that he will be "beloved in the eyes of God," so that God will bestow upon him great goodness—wealth, honor, children, and grandchildren. This is like "servants who serve the master on the condition of receiving a reward" <note>Pirkei Avot 1:3</note>. Regarding this and the matter of fear, it is said: "Let the fear of Heaven be upon you." This "Love" I have mentioned is an "External Service," even though it is a path and an entrance to the way of "Internal Love." This lower love reaches only "unto the heavens," whereas "Internal Love"—which is true Kindness—reaches "above the heavens." 

In the same chapter of the Talmud, Rava pointed out a contradiction: One verse says, "Your kindness is great *unto* the heavens" <note>Psalm 57:11</note>, while another says, "Your kindness is great *above* the heavens" <note>Psalm 108:5</note>. How can this be? One refers to those who act for God's sake (*lishmah*), and the other to those who act not for His sake (*shelo lishmah*). This is also the phrasing used in the *Sefer Mitzvot Gadol* <term>Smag; "The Great Book of Commandments" by the 13th-century Rabbi Moses of Coucy</term>, in the section on Positive Commandments, Commandment 3: 

**"And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might."** In three ways the Holy One, blessed be He, warned Israel regarding His service. Just as it is explained "Fear God" with the goal of "receiving a reward," so that "it may be well with you and your days may be lengthened," so too with Love, as it is said: "And you shall love the Lord your God." This is for their mutual perfection. For many people carry out the king's orders not out of love for the king, nor for reward, but out of fear of the king, lest he take vengeance. So too, there are people who say they will keep the king's statutes lest they die. This is certainly a "good trait," to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, as He commanded. But this is not the *essence* of the service, for the core of his motivation is for his own needs. One might also find many "Jewish gentiles" <note>Meaning people who are Jewish but act with the mindset of those who do not know God</note> who do not serve Him out of love or fear, but only to receive a reward. Likewise, people who serve God with the intent that He should treat them well in this world and the next—this is certainly a "good trait," for he believes God has the power to do good. But this is not the core of the service, for the core of his thought is for his own sake. Rather, the "Good and Supreme Level" in the service of the Creator is...

---

# Part Two: Internal Fear and Love

This internal level is what the Sage, Rabbi Joseph <note>R. Joseph ben Shem Tov (c. 1400–1480), a Spanish Jewish philosopher</note>, son of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov, considered to be true fear and service. But in truth, even this is still "on the outside." He wrote this in his book *Ein HaKore* (*The Reader's Eye*), and the author of the *Akedat Yitzchak* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama</note> copied it in his section on Service, in the chapter on the "Fourth Degree." This is the degree of one who performs the commandment for its "True Ultimate End," which is so that the "Divine Emanation" <term>Shefa; the spiritual flow from God to the world</term> might hover over him, so he may become a "Holy Man of God" resembling the ministering angels. Ultimately, he aims to "cling to the celestial." His proposal is to stand with the King, the Lord of Hosts, to delight in the "Radiance of the Divine Presence" (*Ziv HaShekhinah*), to merit the Life of the World to Come, and to behold the "Resurrection of the Dead." 

This person works and strives in this service with joy and a good heart because he desires to "cleave to his God" and lean upon his Support as much as possible according to his nature. He seeks that "Final End" and "Attachment to Perfection," such that every existing thing resembles, according to its nature, the "First World." If God should command something, even if it seems difficult, this servant will not be deterred. He will strive with all his might to do His will because it is a "Good Command," and it is proper to love it. 

This was the level of our father Abraham, who was called "The one who loves the Name" <note>Isaiah 41:8</note>. When he was commanded regarding the "Binding of his son, his only one," he did not go on his way out of fear that God would harm him if he abandoned the service. For it was said, "Take, please" (*Kach Na*), and the word "please" (*na*) implies a request or an entreaty <note>A common Rabbinic interpretation of the Binding of Isaac</note>, rather than a decree under threat of punishment. Nor did he cast away his only son out of a love for the "good of this world"—heaven forbid! Rather, he perceived that this command from Him, may He be blessed, was for a "Good End": the attainment of Abraham's perfection in a complete and blessed way. By this mode of service, he would most perfectly resemble his God. Out of his "longing and cleaving" to his Creator and his love, he "gave no sleep to his eyes or slumber to his eyelids" until he found a place for the Lord. He reached out his hand and sanctified his precious son to His Name, for he knew that in the end, he and his son would return to the ranks of the "Kings of Heaven." Abraham pictured in his heart that even if God had not moved him to do it, simply knowing that He, may He be blessed, commanded it, he would have done it out of love for his Creator. In my opinion, this is the "Ultimate Degree." We must realize it is not proper to strive in the performance of these commandments—which God commanded man so that he may live by them—merely for the sake of the "acquired perfection" they bring, even though He commanded them to us for that very purpose.

<column-break/>

**Kans** <note>Possible initials for a commentator or cross-reference</note>
Regarding the phrase "regularly in his mouth" <note>A common Talmudic expression for a habitual saying</note>: In the beginning of the tractate *Berakhot*, it is mentioned that one should always be "subtle" in the fear of God. This means one should act with "subtlety" regarding the reward, as if to say: "Do not seek the reward." The "subtle" person is one who acts as if he has "received the reward" already, and he performs the commandments not because he is afraid of punishment or because he hopes for a reward. Therefore, it says he should be "subtle in fear." This means he should act as if the reward is at the "end of the reward" <note>meaning, an afterthought</note>, and his service should be neither from fear of punishment nor from the hope of reward.

**Segal** <note>Likely "Sgan Leviah," a common title for a Levite scholar</note>
This refers to the concept that "from not for its own sake comes for its own sake." This will be explained and clarified further in Part 5. For the common people, who are not yet refined, they should learn for the sake of "Fear of the Honorable Name" out of dread of the "Great Punishments." They shall hear and fear, and they will be gathered in. Through "not for its own sake," they will come to "for its own sake." The inner secret of His Blessedness will be revealed to them. The reason the masses are deterred from sin is so they shall "fear before Him," as the Sages said on the verse "And God has made it so that men should fear before Him" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:14</note>. These are the "External Punishments." See Amos 3: "Shall a shofar be blown in a city, and the people not be afraid?" 

Furthermore, there is a great "perfection" in knowing the "fear of punishments," for through this, God is recognized as King. This "Internal Fear" resolves a great difficulty raised by the Zohar. It explains the "bitterness of the punishment" not as mere retribution, but as a "refined fear" that leads to the longevity of the soul and the life of the angelic King. Death is described as a "great exile" from the "Light of the Punishment" <note>likely referring to purgatorial refinement</note> which is more intense than all physical punishments. When a person is hidden in "Internal Fear," all his pains, sufferings, and tribulations are counted as nothing compared to the "bitterness of the punishment" of being separated from the Divine. As it says, "Bitter as death" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:26</note>—this refers to the "Judgment of the King." This is discussed in the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note> and in the *Beginning of Wisdom* <note>Reshit Chochmah by Eliyahu de Vidas</note> in the "Gate of Fear," Chapter 15.

<summary>This page analyzes the hierarchy of religious motivation, distinguishing between "External Fear/Love" (motivated by reward and punishment) and "Internal Fear/Love" (motivated by a selfless desire for divine attachment). It highlights the Binding of Isaac as the ultimate example of a "Perfected Servant" who acts solely out of love for the Creator's will.</summary>

# Ten Utterances
<columns>2</columns>

...to another level of Fear, which is "External Service." This is when a person has the fear of God in his heart, but he is primarily afraid of transgressing His commandments so that he will not be punished with those penalties that result from the sins he was warned against. Likewise, when a deed-based commandment <term>Mitzvah; a religious duty or good deed</term> comes his way, he fulfills it so that he is not denied the reward necessitated and measured by that commandment. We find that such a person serves out of love for reward and fear of punishment.

As they said in the Talmudic tractate *Sotah* <note>Sotah 22b discusses different types of "Pharisees" or pious people based on their motivations</note>, in the chapter "He Was Taking," regarding one who is a "Pharisee out of love" and a "Pharisee out of fear." Rashi <term>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent medieval commentator</term>, of blessed memory, explained: "A Pharisee out of love for the reward of the commandment, but not out of love for the commandments of his Creator; and out of fear of punishments." End of quote.

Behold, service in this manner—while it is very good, for the person is careful and guards himself from doing any evil so as not to defile himself and bring his impurity into the Holy Sanctuary—is still not "Complete Fear" or "Complete Service." This is because such a person does not truly fear anything except for himself. He does not "fear the Heaven that is upon you," <note>original: "ירא שמים עליכם"</note> which is the proper support; rather, he fears for his own person. He who fears and serves in the way we described only fears that he might be punished with those penalties that the soul incurs when it transgresses.

There are also those who do not tremble from the dread of the soul's punishments, for such things are light in their eyes due to their entanglement in their desires. However, such a person stays his hand and restrains himself out of dread for the discipline of the judges appointed to chastise and punish those who transgress the Torah and its commandments.

Furthermore, there is one who fears, but his fear is of "accidents of time" and its troubles—that they should not befall him, his children, or his household, nor his acquisitions and the wealth he has amassed. Out of dread that his bread might be lacking, that his children might be defiled in his lifetime, or that his body might be afflicted with suffering and evil, persistent illnesses, he keeps his hand from doing any evil. Although these motivations are what prevent the man from sinning, and from that perspective it is good—for he at least believes there is a Master who pays a reward to those who love Him—this fear is still far from the level required of the "Perfected Ones."

Indeed, any cause that prevents a man from entering into his "blood-guilt" <note>Metaphor for sin or spiritual ruin</note> and his wonder in faith is good, and permission is given to occupy oneself with it. As they said in the chapter "In a Place Where They Accustomed" <note>Pesachim 50b</note>: "A person should always occupy himself with the Torah and the commandments even if it is not for its own sake <term>Shelo Lishmah</term>, for through doing it not for its own sake, he eventually comes to do it for its own sake <term>Lishmah</term>." For indeed, this lower fear is a step; it is a grade and a beginning from which to enter into the Inner Sanctum.

This is the "Inner Fear"—the "Blackness" which is success—which comes from the side of Kindness (*Chesid*). The external part of it is when a man loves the Omnipresent <term>HaMakom; a name for God implying He is the "Place" of the world</term> because of his own success, perhaps so he may be cleared in all his matters. As the verse says, "He shall rise and fulfill his desire." Happy is he when he sees that all his integrity shall succeed because of the longing of his love for his Creator. Or, he serves God for himself, so that he will be beloved in the eyes of God and He will bestow great good upon him for generations—wealth, honor, children, and grandchildren. This is like "one who receives a prize." <note>A reference to Pirkei Avot 1:3, "Be not like servants who serve the master for the sake of receiving a reward"</note>

And regarding the matter of specific fear: "Let the fear of Heaven be upon you." Behold, the service I mentioned is "External Service," even though it leads to the "Inner Love" we wrote about. Even if it starts as "not for its own sake," this love still only reaches "up to the heavens." In contrast, "Inner Love," which is true Kindness, is "above the heavens." As it says in the place where Rava pointed out a contradiction between verses <note>Pesachim 50b</note>: "It is written, 'Your kindness is great *unto* the heavens,' and it is written, 'Your kindness is great *above* the heavens.' How can this be? One refers to those who act for its own sake (*Lishmah*), and the other to those who act not for its own sake."

This is also the language of the *SMG* <term>Sefer Mitzvot Gadol; "The Great Book of Commandments" by Rabbi Moses of Coucy</term>, Positive Commandment 3: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might." In these three ways, the Holy One, blessed be He, warned Israel regarding His service, with fear and love.

# Part
The second part concerns "Hidden Fear and Love." This is what the sage, Rabbi Joseph ben the Kabbalist Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov, considered to be true fear and service. But in truth, even this is still "from the outside." These are his words in his book *Ein HaKore* <note>The Eye of the Reader</note>... regarding the fourth level:

"He who performs the commandments for their true purpose—which is so that the Divine Overflow (*Shefa*) may hover over him, so he may be holy to God like the ministering angels, and reach the end of the matter where he merits Eternal Survival, to stand with the hosts of the Lord and enjoy the splendor of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*), and to live in the World to Come <term>Olam HaBa</term> when the dead are resurrected—this servant strives in this service with joy and a good heart. This is because his desire is to cleave to his God and take from His exaltedness as much as is possible according to his nature. For ultimate eternal life is the finding of the rest of perfection...

However, if this servant [serves because] He, may He be blessed, commanded it, he still does not withhold his effort. He strives with all his strength to do His will because doing His word is good and worthy of love. This was the level of our father Abraham, who was called 'the Lover of God.' When he was commanded regarding the binding of his only son, it was not out of fear of punishment, but he went his way to perform the binding. For it was said, 'Take, please' <note>Genesis 22:2</note>, where the language 'please' implies a request. He did not act out of fear of a Creator's decree regarding punishment, nor out of love for the good of this world. God forbid he should slaughter his only son for such reasons! Rather, he perceived that this word from Him, may He be blessed, was for a good purpose: the attainment of Abraham's perfection in a very complete way... to see his God in the most perfect way possible.

In his longing to resemble his Creator out of his love, 'he gave no sleep to his eyes nor slumber to his eyelids' until he found a place for the Lord, wherein he stretched out his holy hand to slaughter the son who was dear to him. By this, he ultimately reached the level of the Angels of Heaven. Abraham, in that service, knew that nothing would deter him, and that He, may He be blessed, had commanded him to act. He did it out of love for his Creator and his passion for Him. This is the true end of the levels..."

...this matter is close to itself... it may be divided into two parts. These are the wicked... and it is in the manner of "If a shofar is sounded in a city, will the people not tremble?" <note>Amos 3:6</note>.

However, there is another part of Fear: "Fear of Punishment." The foundation of this knowledge is a great perfection... it awakens a great difficulty which was hard for the Sages, especially in the *Zohar* <term>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</term>, which elaborated on the "Lamp" <note>likely referring to the *Ma'or*, a commentary or section</note>. # Ten Treatises

And they said to God, "Turn away from us." What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took me from among them to be a witness against them in the heights of heaven for all inhabitants of the world. Once the Holy One, blessed be He, took me to serve the Throne of Glory, the fire of the wheels of the Chariot, and all the needs of the Divine Presence, my flesh immediately turned into flame, my sinews and bones into rivers of burning coals, the light of my eyelids into the radiance of the firmament, the orbs of my eyes into torches of fire, the hair of my head into a blaze, all my limbs into wings of burning fire, and the bulk of my stature into a glowing fire. To my right and my left were flashes of fire, and surrounding me was a whirlwind and storm, with the sound of noise and thunder before and behind me. Thus far <note>This description of Enoch’s transformation into the angel Metatron is drawn from the Hekhalot literature, specifically 3 Enoch.</note>. However, according to our path, it is also possible for you to know what it was about Moses our teacher—may peace be upon him—that he ascended on high above them <note>the angels</note> and acted as a barrier and partition between Him and them. This is what they meant when they said: "Master of the Universe, let there be a person among us who shall be a partition between You and us":

->between You and us:<-

<margin>**And this is the verse:** "Know the God of your father." <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note></margin>
**Furthermore**, he hinted at this matter in a more internal way to his son Solomon, according to the secret of our Sages' statement: "Solomon reigned over the upper beings," as it is written: "And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord." He was on the level of the degree of Moses our teacher. Likewise, they said: "There has not arisen a prophet like Moses," implying that while no *prophet* arose like him, among *kings*, one did arise—namely, Solomon. Furthermore, the letters of *Mah* <note>original: מה - meaning "What," often symbolizing humility</note> belong to Moses, and this is the meaning of "Know the God of your father." This implies that David his father was the secret of the fourth leg of the Chariot <note>The "Divine Chariot" or *Merkavah* is envisioned as having four supports: the three Patriarchs and King David</note>. "The God of your father" refers to the essence of the Chariot, based on the secret that "the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot." And thus it is written in the section on the "Secrets of the Torah":

The Patriarchs, because they perfected this Chariot, and the Great Name was uniquely associated with them, became the Chariot for the Unique Name. For this reason, it was said of them: "The Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot," because each one of them took one divine attribute and unified all the others within it. However, that specific attribute was his primary guide, and he conducted himself by it all his days, becoming a chariot and a throne for the Glory. All attributes were included in that one attribute, and he clung to and was unified with it. Thus it says: "And God went up from Abraham," implying the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot, as the verse says "And God went up from Abraham" and "God went up from upon him" and "Behold, the Lord stood over him." Isaac was sanctified on Mount Moriah, and from the moment he ascended the altar and became a "perfect burnt offering," the Divine Presence never moved from upon him. For this reason, the language of "ascending" is not mentioned regarding him in the text. Since Jacob is the essence of the Patriarchs—for his "bed was perfect" <note>Meaning all his children remained righteous</note> and in him was perfection and unity, as he sustains everything—he forces the connection from end to end. His attribute is the attribute of Truth, through which everything is sustained. Jacob sustains everything, from above to below and from below to above. The verse "The Lord stood over him" is written concerning him specifically, rather than his fathers, because he is the essence of the Chariot and its perfection. In the chapter "He who recites," the Sages taught: "One does not call others 'Patriarchs' except for the three." Nevertheless, the Chariot is not less than four, for King David is in a unique union with the Patriarchs, and through this, the Chariot is complete. However, he is not called a "Father" because his attribute is of a feminine form <note>referring to the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship, which receives light rather than originating it</note>, and the light of the moon is not its own, but from the light of the sun. She is included in the letter *He*, but they are the secret of the Upper Chariot.

<column-break/>

This verse also hints at the memory of every pious person and every teacher, the "branches" included within the "roots." We find that the world has "right" and "left," and their branches are Abraham and Isaac. "His legs are pillars of marble" <note>Song of Songs 5:15</note> corresponds to right and left, and the trunk of the tree is Jacob, who decides between them. The Truth of his commands is like the thin wings of the *Sukkah* covering the Glory. This is the secret of the "Vavs of the pillars" <note>Exodus 27:10</note>, one large and one small, making ten "legs" of the Chariot. When the lineage was related, it spoke in the past tense. The word "longing" <note>original: כסיפת</note> is related to the word "end" <note>original: סוף</note>; at the end of the generation, the Chariot was completed and he merited kingship. Behold, he is the fourth leg with the Patriarchs in unity. Against them are the four faces fixed in the Chariot: the Face of a Man, the Face of a Lion, the Face of an Ox, and the Face of an Eagle.

The **Face of a Man** corresponds to Jacob, who is the reflection of the beauty of the first Man (Adam HaRishon). He includes all the faces, for through him the face was perfected. This corresponds to the supernal form, the Form of Man that includes all forms. For this reason, the Face of a Man was fixed in the Chariot as the face of the throne of four legs. The **Face of a Lion** is on the right, corresponding to Abraham. It would have been appropriate for it to be on the left to indicate "Might" (*Gevurah*), for the lion represents power. However, it was turned to the right to indicate the "Might" of Abraham's perfection. This is because every single day he overcame his inclination like a lion and went to slaughter his only son. Thus, the Face of a Lion was fixed on the right of the Chariot. The **Face of an Ox** is on the left, corresponding to Isaac. It would have been appropriate for it to be on the right, as the Sages interpreted regarding the "son of the herd" <note>Numbers 7:15</note> which corresponds to Abraham, of whom it is said: "And Abraham ran to the herd." However, it was turned to the left because Isaac offered his neck upon the altar like an ox. Thus, the Face of the Ox was fixed on the left of the Chariot. The **Face of an Eagle** corresponds to David, representing his attribute—sometimes fruitful and ascending like the way of an eagle in the sky, and sometimes molting and descending, all according to the awakening of his "chicks" <note>his subjects or his own spiritual state</note>. For this reason, the Face of the Eagle was fixed in the Chariot. Thus far his words.

---

**Furthermore**, they hinted at "Know the God of your father," level upon level, and the spirituality of the Patriarchs who are the totality of the "Building" <note>the Sefirot</note> from Kindness (*Chesed*) downwards. This is "the God of your father"—and "your father" is like "your fathers." It means the Patriarchs. The reason it says "your father" in the singular is because all are included in Abraham, as the Sages said: "One might think we conclude [the blessing] with all of them; therefore, the verse says 'And you shall be a blessing'—the conclusion is with you <note>Abraham</note> alone." This is clearly seen in the verse "Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them... to bring you out before Him," which begins in the plural and ends in the singular.

From all this, it is clear that Israel is a unique entity in the world. How fortunate we are, how good is our portion, that He chose us and gave us His Torah to inflame every heart and awaken it to holiness and purity, to serve God with all one's heart and to truly cling to Him. For there is no difference between Him and us, except that sin creates a barrier, as it is written: "But your iniquities have separated between me and you" <note>Isaiah 59:2</note>. And you, children of Israel, shall be those who cling to the Lord your God, to add holiness every single day, at every time and every hour, so that you may merit to behold the pleasantness of the Lord.

## Treatise 3
### Internal Fear and Love
## Treatise 4
### Service as a High Necessity for the sake of the Name of the Lord

These two treatises are linked, as I shall explain. Therefore, I will explain at once the purpose of man's creation: to serve the Lord our God. As it is written regarding creation: "To work it and to guard it." When man was corrupted, the Holy One, blessed be He, chose the Patriarchs and refined their seed in the "iron furnace" in Egypt. They were slaves there, and through this, the pious among them were refined to be pure for the service of God. Therefore, the Holy One, blessed be He, accustomed them to servitude so that afterward, when He took them out of Pharaoh's bondage, they would be servants of the Lord. As it says: "For the children of Israel are servants to Me," for He acquired them as servants when He redeemed them from the house of bondage. Therefore the verse says: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage," and it does not say "who created the world." This is because in Egypt, the renewal of the world was also publicized, and the purpose of that renewal—which is for the sake of Service—was revealed.

However, there is another deep matter here that will be explained at the end of this discourse. Service is found in the Torah in two ways: out of Fear and out of Love. Our Sages and the Kabbalists have written extensively on this. In the Zohar, it is noted there is "external service" and "internal service," meaning external fear and love versus internal fear and love. External fear and love are when a person fears for himself or loves himself. Internal fear and love are when one fears God and loves God. After my investigation into the wisdom of deriving "one thing from another" in this renewed discourse, I have found that service is divided into two which are four. Since our subject is "Aaron the Priest," this means that external fear and external love are each divided into two parts, called "outer" and "extreme outer." The "outer" is further out than the "extreme outer," and the "extreme outer" approaches the internal. Thus, there are "two which are four" in the external realm. Similarly, there are "two which are four" in the internal realm, for internal fear and internal love are each divided into two parts called "inner" and "innermost." Now I shall explain them one by one.

# Ten Treatises

> And they said to God, "Depart from us." What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He sent from among them a witness to testify against them in the heights of heaven for all inhabitants of the world. Since the Holy One, Blessed be He, intended for me to serve the Throne of Glory, the fire of the wheel of the Chariot, and all the needs of the Divine Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*, the indwelling presence of God</note>, my flesh was immediately turned into flame, my sinews and bones into coals of broom-wood, the light of my eyelashes into the radiance of the firmaments, my eyeballs into torches of fire, the hair of my head into a blaze and flame, all my limbs into burning wings of fire, and the bulk of my stature into a glowing fire. On my right were hewers of fiery flames, on my left were burners of fiery torches, and around me blew storm-winds and tempests, with the sound of noise and thunder before and behind me. Thus far. <note>This passage describes the transformation of the prophet Enoch into the angel Metatron, a common theme in mystical literature known as Hekhalot or "Palaces" literature.</note>

However, according to my path, it is also possible that the complaint of the ministering angels was because Moses ascended above them, acting as a partition and barrier between them. This is why they said, "Master of the Universe, what is one born of a woman doing among us?" <note>A famous Midrashic motif where angels challenge the right of a human to receive the Torah.</note>—meaning, why should he be an interruption between You and us?

**This is the meaning of the verse:** "Know the God of your father." <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note> Even though you are born of a woman from a human father, He is your God directly, without any partition or interruption, and only afterward is He the "God of the angels."
**Furthermore,** he hinted at this matter with deeper interiority to his son Solomon, regarding the secret of Solomon reigning in the celestial realms, as it is written: "And Solomon sat upon the throne of the Lord." He was at a level comparable to that of Moses. Thus they said, "No one arose like Moses among the prophets"—implying that among the prophets none arose like him, but among the kings, one did arise, namely Solomon. Likewise, the letters of the name "Solomon" <note>Hebrew: *Sh-l-m-h*</note> correspond to "for Moses" <note>Hebrew: *L-m-sh-h*</note>. And this is the meaning of "Know the God of your father," implying that David his father is the secret of the "fourth leg" of the Chariot. "The God of your father" refers to the essence of the Chariot itself, based on the secret that "the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot." <note>A classic Kabbalistic concept where Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob embody the divine attributes (Sefirot) of Kindness, Strength, and Beauty.</note> Our Sages of blessed memory explained this in the section on the secrets of the Torah: because the Patriarchs perfected this Chariot and unified it, the Great Name was unified through them, and thus they became a "chariot" for the Unified Name. They said the Patriarchs *are* the Chariot because each of them took one divine attribute <note>Hebrew: *middah*</note> and unified all the others within it. However, that specific attribute served as his "cornerstone," and he conducted himself by it all his days, thus becoming a chariot and a throne of glory for the Lord. Therefore, through that attribute, he was refined and unified with his divine image. Thus, "God went up from upon Abraham" <note>Genesis 17:22</note>—the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot, as it is said, "God went up from upon Abraham" and "And behold, the Lord stood upon him" <note>Genesis 28:13</note>. Isaac was sanctified at Mount Moriah, and from the moment he ascended the altar and became a "perfect burnt offering," the Divine Presence never moved from upon him; therefore, an "ascent" is not mentioned regarding him, but rather the word "upon him" is used in the text. Because Jacob is the essence of the Patriarchs—for his "bed was complete" <note>Meaning all his children remained righteous</note> and in him the unification was perfected, for he "sweetened" everything—his attribute is the "Attribute of Truth" through which everything is sustained. Jacob sustains everything above and below, and therefore the verse says "stands upon him," which is not written of his fathers. He is the essence and perfection of the Chariot. In the chapter "And it was when he read," our Sages taught: "We only call three 'Patriarchs,'" and yet the way of the Chariot is not less than four. This is because King David is in a unique unity with the Patriarchs, and through this, the Chariot is complete. However, he is not called a "father" because he represents the female aspect; the light of the moon does not come from itself but from the light of the sun, and she is included within it. Rather, they are the secret of the Supernal Chariot.

> The Chariot of the One who rides in the highest heavens of old. They are the seven existences included in the unity, for the branches are included in the roots. Thus the "Right" and "Left" of the world are found, and their branches are Abraham and Isaac, the pillars of the heavens. The body of the tree is "You give truth to Jacob," which decides between them. This is the secret of the "six pillars" <note>Hebrew: *vav ha-ammudim*</note>—one large *vav* and one small *vav*, totaling three legs of the Chariot. When David came, the Chariot was completed, and he earned the kingship. Behold, he is the fourth leg together with the Patriarchs in unity. Corresponding to them are the four "faces" fixed in the Chariot: the face of a Man, the face of a Lion, the face of an Ox, and the face of an Eagle. The **face of a Man** corresponds to Jacob, who reflects the beauty of the First Man <note>Adam</note>; he includes all the faces, for through him the supernal form was completed—the form of "Man" which includes all forms. Therefore, the face of a man was fixed in the Chariot. The **face of a Lion** is on the right, corresponding to Abraham. It would have been appropriate for it to be on the left to indicate "Strength" <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note>, as "Lion" <note>Hebrew: *Aryeh*</note> has the same numerical value as "Fear" <note>Hebrew: *Yirah*</note>. However, it was turned to the right because of the strength of Abraham, who overcame his inclination like a lion and went to slaughter his son. Thus the Left (Isaac) was included in the Right (Abraham). Therefore it says, "Now I know that you fear God." "Lion" <note>Aryeh</note> has the numerical value of 216, the number of letters in the 72-letter Name of God which begins with "Kindness <note>Chesed</note> to Abraham." Therefore, the face of a lion was fixed on the right of the Chariot. The **face of an Ox** is on the left, corresponding to Isaac. It would have been appropriate for it to be on the right, as our Sages interpreted in the portion *Naso*: "one young bull" corresponds to Abraham, whose lineage is defined by the verse "And Abraham ran to the cattle <note>Hebrew: *bakar*, same root as ox</note>." However, it was turned to the left because Isaac was willing to stretch out his neck upon the altar like an ox. Thus the Right was included in the Left, all to demonstrate Unity. For this secret, the face of the ox was fixed on the left of the Chariot. The **face of an Eagle** corresponds to David, to indicate his attribute—sometimes soaring and ascending in the "way of an eagle in the sky," and sometimes molting and descending, all according to the awakening of his fledglings. For this secret, the face of the eagle was fixed in the Chariot. Thus far.

**Furthermore,** there is a hint in the phrase "Know the God of your father" to level upon level. That is, "And you shall know" refers to a level higher than that of the Patriarchs, who are the general structure from "Kindness" <note>Chesed</note> downwards. This is "the God of your father"—and "your father" is like "your fathers." It means the Patriarchs. Why does it say "your father" in the singular? Because they are all included in Abraham. As the Sages said: I might think we should conclude the blessing with all of them, but the verse says, "and you shall be a blessing"—the blessing concludes with you <note>Abraham</note> alone. Similarly, we find a verse in *Va'etchanan*: "Because He loved your fathers, He chose their offspring after them, and He brought you out before Him." It begins in the plural and ends in the singular.

From all of this, the matter of Israel being "one unique nation in the world" is clarified. Fortunate are we, how good is our portion, that He chose us and gave us His Torah through the one who "illuminated all hearts," and designated us for holiness and purity, to serve the Blessed Name with all one's heart and to live in literal cleaving to Him if one so desires. For there is no difference between Him and us except for sin, which creates a barrier, as it is written: "But your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God." And you, my children, may you be those who cleave to the Lord your God, to add holiness every single day, at every moment and every hour. Then you will merit to behold the pleasantness of the Lord, "pleasantness in His right hand forever."

# Treatise 3: Inner Fear and Love. Treatise 4: Service Must Be for the Sake of the Most High.

-> I shall explain. <-

These two treatises are linked, as I shall explain. Therefore, I will explain them at once. The purpose of the creation of man is to serve the Lord our God, as it is written regarding the creation of Adam: "to work it and to guard it." When Adam and the generations after him became corrupted, the Holy One, Blessed be He, chose the Patriarchs and refined their offspring in the "iron furnace" in Egypt. They were slaves there, and through this, the dross was refined from them so they would be pure for the service of the Blessed Name. Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, accustomed them to servitude so that afterward, when He took them out from the servitude of Pharaoh, they would be eternal "servants of God," as it is written: "For the Children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants," for He acquired them as His servants when He redeemed them from the house of bondage. Therefore, the verse says, "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage," and it does not say, "who created the world." The reason is that in Egypt, the renewal of the world was also publicized, and the ultimate purpose of this renewal was revealed: it is for the sake of Divine Service. Thus He said, "who brought you out from the house of bondage." However, there is another matter in the depths of this subject, which will be explained at the end of this inquiry. Now, "Service" is commanded in the Torah in two ways: through Fear and through Love. Our Sages of blessed memory elaborated on this in the *Book of the Pious* <note>Sefer Charedim</note>. Also, in the "Light of the Foundations," there is "External Service" and "Internal Service"—that is, external fear and love, and internal fear and love. **External Fear and Love** is when a person sees himself and loves himself. **Internal Fear and Love** is when he fears the Blessed Name and loves the Blessed Name. After my contemplation in "understanding one thing from another" in this lovely inquiry, I have responded and found that Service is divided into two which are four. This is because Fear and Love each divide into two parts, called "External" and "Outer," where the "Outer" is even further out than the "External," and the "External" approaches the "Internal." Thus there are two that are four on the outside. Similarly, there are two that are four on the inside, for Internal Fear and Internal Love each divide into two parts, called "Internal" and "Innermost." Thus there are two that are four on the inside. Now I shall explain them one by one.
