<meta>The previous page introduced the concept of the "Lover of God" and began listing the ten essential attributes or "measures" <note>Hebrew: *Middot*</note> that define such a person. This page completes that list and provides a detailed commentary on how the patriarch Abraham embodied these traits, followed by a philosophical exploration of why the human soul is naturally drawn to the Divine, citing the classic ethical work *Sefer HaYashar*.</meta>

# Ten Essays

...of every pleasure. The sixth <note>The list continues from the previous page</note> is to loathe those who loathe the Creator and to love His lovers—may He be blessed—because his love for the good of the world is considered here only for the sake of the service of the Creator—may He be blessed. And the seventh is that every toil, lack, and affliction should be sweet to him in comparison to the love of God—may He be blessed. And the seventh <note>The text repeats "seventh," likely a scribal error for the eighth attribute</note> is that he puts the business of the God—may He be blessed—before any of his own affairs. The seventh <note>Likely the ninth</note> is to make known to other people his love for God—may He be blessed—and to glory in the Lord. The eighth is to listen to the voice of those who speak to him and inspire him in the service of the Lord—may He be blessed. The ninth is that if events occur to him, whether good or bad, he should abandon everything for the sake of the service of the God—may He be blessed. The tenth is that his service should not be for the sake of receiving a reward, for then his service would be "dependent on a specific thing" <note>A reference to the Mishnah, Pirkei Avot 5:16, meaning conditional love that fades when the cause disappears</note>. When these ten attributes are gathered in a person, he is called a "Lover of God" and he is a devout person <note>Hebrew: *Chassid*</note> in the ultimate sense. The Creator—may He be blessed—did not say of our father Abraham—peace be upon him—"the offspring of Abraham My lover" <note>Isaiah 41:8</note> until all these attributes were found in him.

And I shall explain to you from the scriptures:
**The first attribute:** Know that the love of Abraham—peace be upon him—was to teach all people the service of the Creator—may He be blessed—and to call out to Him always, as it says: "And there Abram called upon the name of the Lord" <note>Genesis 12:8</note>. And it says in another place: "And there he built an altar to the Lord and called upon the name of the Lord" <note>Genesis 13:4</note>. And it says: "And he planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and called there upon the name of the Lord" <note>Genesis 21:33</note>. This is to inform you that in every place he went, he would call upon the name of the Lord and occupy himself with His service, and he was not deterred by the fear of the terrors of the world. 
**The second attribute:** The devout person enjoys the love of His Divinity more than he enjoys all the pleasures of the world. For it is known that there is no pleasure or joy for a person like that found in children, as it is said: "Your father will be glad and she who bore you will rejoice" <note>Proverbs 23:25</note>. Yet Abraham—peace be upon him—took more pleasure in the service of God—may He be blessed—than in the love of his children, and he distanced himself from Ishmael his son out of his great love for God—may He be blessed. 
**The third attribute:** The devout person loathes all those who loathe the Creator—may He be blessed—and loves His lovers. For the Creator—may He be blessed—said to Abraham: "Go forth from your land and from your birthplace and from your father's house" <note>Genesis 12:1</note>, and he loathed his family and his father's house because they loathed Him and the God—may He be blessed—"and Abram went as the Lord had spoken to him" <note>Genesis 12:4</note>. 
**The fourth attribute:** To the devout person, his love for all the good of the world is considered as nothing compared to the love of God—may He be blessed—and the Torah of the Creator. The Creator—may He be blessed—said to Abraham—peace be upon him: "Take now your son, your only son, whom you love, Isaac" <note>Genesis 22:2</note>. He said "whom you love" to show people that even that which he loved with the ultimate love, he loathed and distanced for the sake of the love of the Creator—may He be blessed. 
**The fifth attribute:** The devout person considers all toil and burden as a pleasure and a delight in the service of God—may He be blessed. Abraham—peace be upon him—was afflicted on the roads and tested with many trials, yet he did not grow weary of them and accepted everything with a cheerful countenance. For the Creator—may He be blessed—tested him in his poverty on the roads, and afterward with the taking of Sarah from his sight, and afterward with the covenant of circumcision, and afterward with the trial of driving out Ishmael, and afterward the slaughtering of Isaac. Had his service been from fear and not from love, it would not have endured through all these trials; but because of his great love for God—may He be blessed—everything was sweet in his eyes, as it is said: "Many waters cannot quench love" <note>Song of Songs 8:7</note>. 
**The sixth attribute:** The devout person will not put any of his own affairs before the salvation of the commandments of the Creator—may He be blessed. We find that in everything the Creator—may He be blessed—commanded him, he did not put any action before it until he completed the commandment of God—may He be blessed. Regarding the circumcision, it says: "And God went up from him," and it is written: "On that very same day was Abraham circumcised" <note>Genesis 17:22-26</note>; he did not put any business first until he completed the commandment. And He said regarding Ishmael: "Whatever Sarah tells you, listen to her voice, for through Isaac shall your offspring be named" <note>Genesis 21:12</note>, and it is written immediately after: "And Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water, and put it on her shoulder..." <note>Genesis 21:14</note>. We learn from this that the matter was told to him in a dream at night, and therefore he rose early in the morning before doing any other deed to complete the command of God—may He be blessed. 
**The seventh attribute:** The devout person makes known to every person the love of the Creator—may He be blessed—and His ways. For so said the Lord—may He be blessed—concerning Abraham—peace be upon him: "For I have known him, so that he may command his children and his household after him..." <note>Genesis 18:19</note> that they may keep the way of the Lord—meaning, they know that they should be lovers of God through His love. He did not say "his children" alone, but "his children and his household"—meaning all who are joined to him and over whom he has authority. 
**The eighth attribute:** The devout person does not worry about the mockery of the mockers or the cheapening of those who blaspheme. They said that Abraham—peace be upon him—began to cling to the service of God—may He be blessed—from his youth, and the people of his generation blasphemed him, but he paid no mind to any man until they threw him into the fiery furnace and the Creator—may He be blessed—saved him, as it is written: "I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur Kasdim" <note>Ur Kasdim can be translated as 'the fire of the Chaldeans'</note>. 
**The ninth attribute:** When events of good or evil occur to the devout person, he does not cancel his service. So did Abraham—peace be upon him—for in everything that occurred to him, whether good or evil, his heart remained faithful, as it is said: "And You found his heart faithful before You" <note>Nehemiah 9:8</note>. 
**The tenth attribute:** The love of the devout person for God—may He be blessed—is not dependent on a specific thing or for the sake of receiving a reward. Because Abraham did not seek a reward for his service, therefore the God—may He be blessed—said to him: "Your reward is very great" <note>Genesis 15:1</note>. For it is one of the ways of the God—may He be blessed—with His devout ones: when they serve not for the sake of receiving a reward, He doubles their reward and gives them a double good, just as He said to King Solomon—peace be upon him: "Because you did not ask for riches..." and it is written afterward: "Also that which you did not ask for I have given you, both riches and honor" <note>1 Kings 3:11-13</note>. These attributes, this sophistication, and this wisdom—all who live by these ten attributes, their love is called "Perfect Love." Concerning these attributes it is said: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might" <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>. These are the words of our teacher, Rabbeinu Tam <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Meir, a leading 12th-century French Tosafist and scholar</note>.

# More
Our teacher, Rabbeinu Tam, wrote in *Sefer HaYashar* <note>The Book of Righteousness, a classic work of Jewish ethics</note> in the fifth gate, as follows: "Therefore, desire is formed by the joining of two parts: the first is from the attributes of the beloved, and the second is from the measure of the lover. According to the quality of the lover's attributes will be the strength of his love for the beloved's attributes which are within his beloved. Now I shall explain the attributes of the beloved and I say: the attributes of the beloved are the good Intellect <note>Hebrew: *Sekhel*</note> and the pure, clear, and upright Soul <note>Hebrew: *Nefesh*</note>. Just as some of these attributes will be drawn to love all in whom these attributes are found, because every species leans toward its own kind and distances itself from its opposite. Because of this, every man who possesses a good intellect and a pure soul will be drawn to the love of God, because the Creator is Devout <note>Hebrew: *Chassid*</note> and He is [the source of] upright attributes and general, true goodness. Therefore, when a person is drawn to His service, it is a sign that he possesses some of the attributes of the Creator—may He be blessed. He follows after Him just as the intellectual person is drawn to the company of the intellectual, every wise man to the company of the wise, every fool to the company of fools, the youth to the company of youths, the elder to the company of elders, every man to the company of his peer, and the celestial bodies to their own kind. 

Therefore, when you see a man distancing himself from the service of the God—may He be blessed—know that he possesses none of the attributes of the God—may He be blessed—at all, but rather their opposite. Therefore, he distances himself from them. If there be in him intellect, or holiness, or integrity, or uprightness, it is known that these attributes are the attributes of the Creator—may He be blessed. When a person has even a trace of them, his heart will draw him to God. This is just as the soul of a man is drawn upward—and he who is superior is drawn to that stature, even the stature of his soul, which is drawn to the place of the Intellect, which is its natural temperament. Conversely, the animal is drawn to the earth until it bows down and walks in a stooped posture because its soul is from the dust and it is drawn to its chains. 

Therefore, it is known that the good Intellect within a man is what stirs him to seek wisdom according to his attributes. The pure soul is to him like a 'molten mirror' <note>A biblical metaphor from Job 37:18, suggesting the soul acts as a polished surface that reflects divine truth</note> that reveals to him what is hidden of the secrets of God. For when the soul is pure and clear, the man sees through it the Creator—may He be blessed—His responsibility, His existence, and His other powers which are perceived by the intellect, just as a man sees in a molten mirror that which was hidden from him. If the soul is not pure and bright, he cannot ascend without it, for he will strike against the darkness. Nor can the viewer see what is behind him if there is not a clear and thin mirror through which the sight can pass. Therefore, when it is clear, the sight of the intellect passes through it and he sees what is behind it—and there is nothing 'behind' the soul except the Creator—may He be blessed. 

And for this reason, I said that when a person has these two attributes—namely, a good intellect and a pure soul—there will be awakened within the person a perfect love for the Creator, blessed be He. And when the love for God—may He be blessed—is perfect, fear <note>Hebrew: *Yirah*, which also means awe</note> will sprout from that love. For we see that whoever loves another person because of the good attributes within him, that love will be upon his neck and will humble him to seek the will of the beloved. He will find no rest except at the time of his toil in the business of the beloved, and the toil will be sweeter to his heart than rest. When the lover does something for the beloved that is good in his eyes, then the soul of the lover becomes precious in his own eyes, because he was able to find favor in the eyes of his beloved by doing something that was good in his eyes. And if it happens that he commits a sin or an error, or does something that is not good to his beloved, the lover will be filled with longing and shame, and he will sneak away as shamed people sneak away. This thing comes from the power of love that was in the lover. [Love] has three parts of good attributes... 'Love is as strong as death' <note>Song of Songs 8:6</note>. 

After the lover’s love leads him to double his efforts to do the beloved's will, we must explain why love has this power. We say that the lover’s love for his beloved is because of the good attributes in the beloved, and the lover's soul has some of those good attributes too. Therefore, this small amount of good attributes in the lover draws him [to the beloved] as every species is drawn to its kind. It is a sign of a person with a noble soul that he is drawn to every honorable thing, and this is Love. But the awakening in the lover toward his devout one and the desire for the beloved's will is due to seeing the beloved's superiority over him—just as the student recognizes the superiority of his teacher and the slave the superiority of his master. He desires his beloved while recognizing [the beloved's] superiority over him. It is not just the lover for the beloved, but like the slave for his master and the student for his teacher because of the superiority he has over him. Furthermore, he always hopes to learn from the teacher's attributes, his wisdom, and his ethics. These attributes will force the lover to be in fear <note>Awe/reverence</note> of his beloved. Thus it is clarified that from love comes fear. These are the words [of Rabbeinu Tam]."

## Ten Essays

...that we were commanded to do this or that. Regarding a negative commandment, one should think and say: "How great was my desire to eat pork," etc., and similarly with other things, "But what can I do? My Father in Heaven has decreed it upon me." This is the meaning of the verse *with all your heart*—with both of your inclinations <note>Hebrew: *Yetzer HaTov* (Good Inclination) and *Yetzer HaRa* (Evil Inclination)</note>. That is, in a positive commandment, or when the Evil Inclination is present, one conquers it. Thus, the commandment is fulfilled doubly: he performs the positive act through the counsel of the Good Inclination, and he conquers the Evil Inclination which pushes toward a negative commandment. Regarding the negative commandment, it is the reverse: the Good Inclination counsels him to abstain, and he conquers the Evil Inclination during the moment of temptation.

This I received from the mouth of a holy man of God, my father and teacher (may his memory be a blessing for the life of the world to come), explaining the passage in the Talmud, Tractate Chullin, in the chapter "All Flesh." It says there: Yaltha <note>The wife of the sage Rav Nachman and a scholar in her own right</note> said to Rav Nachman: "See, for everything that the Merciful One <note>God</note> forbade us, He permitted us something similar. He forbade us blood, but permitted us liver <note>which is full of blood but permitted after roasting</note>. He forbade the menstruant woman, but permitted the 'blood of purity' <note>blood seen during certain days after childbirth that is ritually clean</note>. He forbade the fat of domestic animals, but permitted the fat of wild animals. He forbade the pig, but permitted the brain of the *Shibuta* fish <note>a fish said to have the flavor of pork</note>. He forbade the female convert <note>at certain times</note>... <note>original: "Lishana de-Kuvra"</note> the forbidden wife of another man, but permitted the divorcee during her husband's life. He forbade the brother’s wife, but permitted the *Yevama* <note>the sister-in-law through levirate marriage</note>. He forbade the beautiful woman <note>in a forbidden context</note>, but permitted the 'Beautiful Captive' <note>taken in war under specific laws</note>. I wish to eat meat with milk." Rav Nachman said to the attendants: "Go and roast an udder for her" <note>the udder of a cow, which has a flavor similar to meat cooked in milk but is permitted under specific conditions</note>.

This raises a difficulty: Is it possible that a distinguished woman like Yaltha would seek a sinful thing from her husband, Rav Nachman? On the surface, these seem like idle words. Furthermore, why did the Sages see fit to record these words in the Talmud? One might say the Talmud collected them to teach the law regarding the roasting of an udder, as the commentators and legal decisors have discussed at length. But if that were the case, the Talmud should have been brief and only cited the beginning of the matter.

My father and teacher explained that these words contain a great secret. It relates to what I have said: that in every negative commandment, a person should consider in his heart the desire he has to do it, and yet he refrains for the sake of the glory of Heaven. As Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: "A person should not say 'I do not want to eat pork,' but rather 'I want to, but what can I do? My Father in Heaven has decreed it upon me.'" This is why Yaltha said that for everything the Merciful One forbade, He permitted a counterpart—so that we might taste and know the flavor of the forbidden thing, realizing its taste is "good" <note>pleasurable</note>, so that we might desire it and yet abandon the forbidden act for the sake of the Creator's glory. The taste of the udder is like the taste of meat and milk; thus we know the taste of meat and milk is good, we desire it, and yet we refrain for the sake of the Creator's glory.

Now we shall explain the levels of "Desire," "Passion," and "Delight." I will first present what is written in the *Reshit Chochmah* <note>The Beginning of Wisdom, a famous 16th-century Kabbalistic ethical work</note> in the "Gate of Love," Chapter 3. He writes that "Cleaving" (*Devikah*) refers to the soul of a person sticking to the soul of another, as in "Ruth cleaved to her" <note>Ruth 1:14</note>, meaning her will cleaved to hers. But this "cleaving" does not indicate total unity, for it is possible for the connection to be severed. The proof is from where the Sages learned "cleaving"—from a belt that clings to a man's loins, as in "as the loincloth clings to the waist of a man" <note>Jeremiah 13:11</note>. A belt is sometimes attached and sometimes detached. 

However, the word "Passion" (*Chashak*) indicates a stronger knot of love. We see this regarding the columns of the Tabernacle, which were "passion-joined" <note>Exodus 27:10; usually translated as "filleted"</note> because they were held together, attached and tied all around, like wooden hoops used to tighten a barrel. 

Even deeper is "Delight" (*Chefetz*), where the root suggests that a person’s will and all his focus are directed toward one face, never moving for even a moment. This is seen in the story of Shechem, who "delighted in Jacob’s daughter" <note>Genesis 34:19</note>; he did not delay the matter because he was, as it were, dying of love for her, having no other will in the world but this one. The word "Delight" is also associated with the source of life itself, as in the Queen of Sheba who asked for "all her delight" <note>1 Kings 10:13</note>, which the Zohar interprets as a union.

I will now add my own insight to these three levels: Cleaving, Passion, and Delight. They are three ascending steps.

**Path 1:** "Cleaving" is the human awakening to serve God using the Evil Inclination <gloss>by force</gloss> within the Good Inclination. This happens when one "conquers" the forbidden. Sometimes the inclination fights back, and the person performs the service with a sense of heaviness. Even though he wins, he does not do it with fiery joy. 

**Path 2:** This is deeper and more internal. It is not enough for the counsel of the Evil Inclination to be nullified; rather, one takes the energy from the Evil Inclination and uses it to create a stronger bond. When a person performs a commandment, he rises like a lion and prevails. This is the precision in the Mishnah: "Who is a hero? He who conquers his inclination." It does not say "he who pushes it away" or "nullifies it," but "conquers it," like someone riding and redirecting its power. This is "with all your heart"—with both inclinations.

The third level is "Delight" (*Chefetz*), which we might call "Eternal Love." This is a constant, unending will. Consider the human example: a man's desire for a woman might be sated after their union. But in the love of God, the "Delight" never ceases. Even after a commandment is fully performed, the person's passion and desire only grow. He is never "full" or satisfied with what he has done; instead, the cleaving creates an even greater hunger for more. This is "one commandment drags another in its wake." This was the level of Moses, who yearned to enter the Land of Israel to perform its specific commandments, even though he was not yet obligated in them. 

All of this is learned from the passage of "that wicked one" <note>Shechem son of Hamor</note>. One might ask: what benefit is there in learning from a wicked man? "Who can produce a clean thing from an unclean?" But according to what we said, it is fitting, for he "conquered" his own nature to pursue his desire. Rabbi Menachem Recanati <note>a 14th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote that the secret of Shechem's pursuit of Dinah is the secret of the Serpent who pursued Eve. Dinah represents a level of the Divine Presence <note>the *Shekhinah*</note>. Just as that wicked man's soul cleaved to Dinah through Cleaving, Passion, and Delight, so too should a person's soul cleave to the *Shekhinah*.

The *Sefer HaYashar* <note>The Book of Uprightness, an ethical treatise</note> notes that love is tested by ten things. The first is that he loves the Torah of his God. The second is that he finds pleasure in the delight of serving God...

<summary>This page discusses the psychological and spiritual transformation of the "Evil Inclination" into a vehicle for Divine service, using the levels of "Cleaving," "Passion," and "Delight" to describe the soul's progression toward a constant, insatiable love for God.</summary>

<margin>
"My son, let them serve Me" <note>Exodus 4:23</note> which is this, etc., and afterward, "servant."
</margin>

"My son, let them serve Me"—which is to say, it is not necessary to say "this" <note>this specific level</note>; first He called them "son" and afterward "servant."

# Therefore
You should know that while it is indeed true in the majority of the world that the rank of a "son" is greater than that of a "servant," among the "Children of the Ascent" <note>term for the spiritual elite; *Bnei Aliyah*</note>, the rank of "servant" is actually superior. To understand this matter, I must first present two introductory principles:

**First Principle:** The aspect of "King" is a higher rank than the aspect of "Father." For the Blessed One is called "King" by His very essence, even before the world was created—when He and His Name were alone. "The Lord is King" <note>Psalm 10:16</note>. He is King inherently, unlike a king of flesh and blood, for there is no king without a nation; however, He does not need a nation for His existence. He has the power to bring a nation into being whenever He wishes, and He lacks nothing. This is the meaning of the praise: "The Lord reigned" before the world was created, "The Lord reigns" in the present when the world is created, and "The Lord will reign" in the future when the world is renewed. He is not called "Father" except through His revelation—when creation emerges through the chain of cause and effect. Then the Cause is called "Father" and the effect is called "Son."

**Second Principle:** The aspect of "servant" reflects the "awe of a servant" before his master, while the aspect of "son" comes from love—the love of a son for a father. There is a greater closeness and attachment between a son and father than between a servant and master. According to this principle, "if we are like servants" <note>a reference to the liturgy of Rosh Hashanah</note>, it refers to a level of internal awe, and "if we are like sons," it refers to a level of internal love. This is true for the vast majority of people. 

However, the "Children of the Ascent" are few. They enter from internal love into a "higher awe" which is "inner-most." This is the aspect of "one who is pious with his Creator" <note>a *Chassid*</note>, who brings "pleasure to his Maker." His entire aim is attachment to the Blessed One for the sake of His Great Name, becoming a "Chariot" <note>a *Merkavah*, a vehicle for Divine presence</note> for Him. All his service is the service of the King. Regarding this, the hint was given: "A servant of the King is as the King himself." In this aspect, Moses was called "the servant of the Lord" <note>Deuteronomy 34:5</note> essentially—the rank of the Children of the Ascent. Moses includes them all.

Regarding these two kinds of service I mentioned, the verse hints: "If I am a Father, where is My honor? And if I am a Master, where is My awe?" <note>Malachi 1:6</note>. It is difficult to understand why "Masters" is written in the plural <note>Hebrew: *Adonim*</note>. Rather, as explained, there are two kinds of servants: one is below the level of a "son," and one is above the level of a "son."

Now, let us consider three levels in the service of the Place <note>God, referred to as *HaMakom*</note>, counting from the bottom up:
1.  **The lowest level:** One who serves in order to receive a reward—specifically the eternal reward of the World to Come. This is permitted, as the prohibition <note>of the Sages</note> against serving for reward only applies to rewards in *this* world. I call this level "one who serves himself," meaning he does it for his own sake so that he may merit the afterlife. Even so, it is a significant level.
2.  **The second level:** This is internal. One fulfills the entire Torah out of awe for his Master, fearing to violate His commands, whether positive or negative.
3.  **The third level:** In addition to what is commanded, he acts out of love and passion, loving the Lord with joy and a good heart. This level is called "Son."

However, the "Children of the Ascent"—and Moses rose above them all—reach the "inner-most awe." This is to be the "Chariot" for Him, to bring pleasure to his Creator. Even the reward he receives is the reward itself: to embrace Him, to awe Him, and to serve Him. This is what remains for him; his "servitude" is to be the Chariot that carries the Throne. He has no "rest" in the World to Come because "sovereignty is servitude." As stated, "the servant of the King is the King." Aside from the simple meaning, the servant of the King is the King himself <note>meaning he acts as the King's representative</note>, and there is his attachment; everything is for His sake. There is no servitude quite like that of one "born in the house" <note>*Yilid Bayit*</note> as opposed to one "acquired with money" <note>*Miknat Kesef*</note>. One born in the house is more attached to his master than a purchased servant. The aspect of a "servant" who is below the level of a "son" is called "purchased with money," while the aspect of a "servant" who is above the level of a "son" is called "born in the house."

Hints to these four levels appear in the Torah portion of *Emor*... The aspect of "serving oneself" for the World to Come, the aspect of the "servant" who works from internal awe, and the aspect of internal love that follows internal awe—which is the secret of "You are sons to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. This is the level of "born in the house." Concerning this, Solomon said: "My son, fear the Lord and the King" <note>Proverbs 24:21</note>. Understand this well.

Regarding the "final awe," it is written: "The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him" <note>Psalm 25:14</note>, for they stand within the secret of the Lord. Similarly, "How great is the goodness You have hidden for those who fear You" <note>Psalm 31:20</note>. Of the "initial awe" which precedes love, it is said: "Fear the Lord, His holy ones, for there is no lack for those who fear Him" <note>Psalm 34:10</note>. This is because "external awe"—fear of things pertaining to this world—contains "lack." When a person lacks something, he stops fearing God, as it says "when he is hungry... he will curse his King" <note>Isaiah 8:21</note>. However, in "internal awe" regarding holiness—the fulfillment of our holy Torah—there is no lack. Even in sickness, we accept it with love: "for I am sick with love" <note>Song of Songs 2:5</note>. The holy service is upon them... for "Your sanctuary is awesome."

Above this first internal awe is the one who "serves himself" for the sake of his service in the World to Come. Even though it is a kind of "sickness," it is a sickness of holy purity, since the reward he seeks is the World to Come. Purity leads to holiness—the level Solomon commanded: "Fear the Lord, His holy ones."

<margin>
The secret of the Book... the division of the verses to say the cessation of the world is like a servant... Moses is entirely light... for the time of the good...
</margin>

# And Now
The verses can be explained: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of servants" <note>Exodus 20:2</note>. I asked previously: why did He not say, "Who created the world"? I already know the beginning of the homilies that reveal this secret: the exodus from the "house of servants" to become "servants of the King" is a higher level than the creation of the world. The secret of the creation of the world follows the chain of ranks in the secret of Cause and Effect; then the Blessed One is called "Father" and we are "Sons." However, the aspect of "King" is higher, in the secret of "The Lord is King" which preceded the chain of creation, for the Blessed One is King by His very essence.

# However
There is yet another level above these levels, a hidden rank that no one among the Children of the Ascent has attained except for Moses our Teacher. This is a concealed path, a hidden secret, which we call "Great Love" <note>*Ahavah Rabbah*</note>. "Eternal Love" <note>*Ahavat Olam*</note> refers to the internal love that all who enter the world can merit. But "Great Love" was only attained by Moses. This is the secret of how Moses rose above the Children of the Ascent. This Great Love emerges from the "inner-most awe." In this state, one is called "Son," because love is the aspect of a son. Yet, even in the case of Moses, this rank is hidden; therefore, he is not called "Son" openly, but only by a hidden hint in the verse: "My servant Moses... in all My house he is trusted" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. The Hebrew initials for **B**eit (House) **N**e’eman (Trusted) spell **B-N** <note>Son</note>.

The matter is as I have written: "inner-most awe" is the secret of the "King's instrument," the union of Beauty (*Tiferet*) and Sovereignty (*Malkhut*). All the names are included in the Name of four letters <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> which includes the six extremities. There, distance is caused by our sins. However, there is a "hidden union," the secret of the first two letters of the Name (*Yah*), representing Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*), joined by Knowledge (*Da’at*)—the rank of Moses. In the Zohar, the sphere of Understanding (*Binah*) is called *Ben Yah* (Son of Yah), the secret of Knowledge which mediates between Wisdom and Understanding. There are the "Fifty Gates of Understanding" given to Moses. Therefore, he is not called "Son" openly here, but only in secret. 

The "inner-most awe" where the Children of the Ascent rise to the level of Moses includes the rank: "My servant Moses is trusted in all My house." But the "Upper House," of which it is said "By Wisdom a house is built," Moses was not yet "trusted in the entire house" because he lacked one gate—the Fiftieth Gate which transforms into Wisdom. Understand these things. In any case, awe was a "small matter" <note>a *milta zutrati*</note> for Moses. Understand this.

<margin>
There is a hint in the verse "And now Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear..." <note>Deuteronomy 10:12</note>. Awe is the service to the Master... Awe should be the face of the heart... seeking peace and mercy for love... from the entire prayer for love... Therefore they shall fear from awe... Regarding Moses, it is a small thing, for from Sovereignty to Understanding, Moses has an even more internal aspect...
</margin>

# And Then
The conclusion of the *Midrash Rabbah* that I cited earlier becomes clear, regarding "cleaving, desiring, and delighting." Rabbi Abba son of Elisha added two more: "in love and in connection." For Resh Lakish spoke of internal love (cleaving, desiring, delighting), but Rabbi Abba added "love upon love," which is the "inner-most awe" that emerges from love. This is why it is said of Abraham "he feared God" <note>Genesis 22:12</note> out of love. He also added "connection," a level only attained by Moses our Teacher, of whom it is said "Face to face I speak with him" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>, unlike the way He spoke to other prophets. The secret of this "speech" is the revelation of what is in the secret of Thought. The speaker, as it were, tells the one on high what was concealed and reveals it to him. This is the secret of the verse "Speak to the heart of Jerusalem" <note>Isaiah 40:2</note>. "Jerusalem Above" is the secret of Wisdom and Understanding, as explained at length in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*.

# Essay 3 and Essay 4

<margin>The Generations of Man</margin>
The rectification <note>Hebrew: *Tikun*, the mystical process of repairing or perfecting the world</note> depends upon us. This is the meaning of the phrase "to return to you," which implies that this return <note>Repentance or *Teshuvah*</note> shall be from your own hand to yourself. For, as it were, He relies upon it, as it is written, "there is and there is more" in the state of nullification. This refers to the "Small One" and the "Name," as explained at length above in the introduction to "My commandments," where our will becomes the commandment.

<column-break/>

According to the most inner secret way, this is hinted at in the verse "to keep" <note>Deuteronomy 10:13</note>. This "keeping" alludes to the attribute of Kingship <term>Malchut: the final of the ten Divine emanations, representing the manifest world</term> when it is joined with Beauty <term>Tiferet: the central Divine emanation, representing harmony and the sun</term>, as explained in the book *The Orchard* <note>original: *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the section on symbolic names. At that stage, the meaning of "commandment" <note>original: *mitzvah*</note> is derived from the word for "companionship" <note>original: *tzavta*</note>, meaning a bond of friendship. For Kingship is the companion of the Divine Name. They are like two beloveds, joined through the "Foundation of the Covenant of the Organ," which is called "Statute" <note>original: *Chok*</note>, as is well known. This is the meaning of "His commandments and His statutes." Furthermore, the attribute of Foundation <term>Yesod: the emanation that channels Divine energy into the world</term> is called "Good," as it is written: <insert>And he said</insert> "And the Good one shall redeem." This is the meaning of "to put to you" <note>original: *leshum lecha*</note>. The word "To You" <note>original: *Lecha*—Lamed-Khaf</note> is the reverse of "All" <note>original: *Kol*—Khaf-Lamed</note>. These point toward the attribute of Foundation in the verse "For *all* that is in heaven and earth" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>, which refers to the Foundation that unites Heaven <insert>and Earth</insert>. See *The Orchard* for the explanation of the verse "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power..." according to the path of "For All"; "All" is the seal that flips from "To You" to "All." See there.

This verse about "keeping the commandments of the Lord" concerns the matter of the "Fifty" <note>likely referring to the 50 Gates of Understanding</note> that I mentioned. It appears that this is the "Inner-most" level, from which one draws the strength to be "Fearful of Sin," creating a safeguard for a safeguard. This is why it says "To keep." Afterward, it says, "Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens..." <note>Deuteronomy 10:14</note>. Now he explains those fifty gates mentioned above—namely, inner Fear and Love, and the Inner-most Fear. By what path can a person merit them? He says: to reach Inner Fear, you must remember that "to the Lord your God belong the heavens and the highest heavens," just as I wrote above: because He is the Great Master and Ruler. From this, one is clothed in awe and also clothed in shame <note>meaning a humble bashfulness before the Divine</note>. 

This is also the path that leads to Inner Love: by contemplating how His loftiness and greatness exist even as He shows us His humility in the place of His great magnitude. This is the meaning of: "Behold, the Lord set His affection on your forefathers." This is similar to the Midrash: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'Is it possible [I am holy] because of your holiness? No, for I am holy—My holiness is above your holiness.'" And so, His being is above all desires; "My greatness is above your greatness." The point is that there is no separation between the greatness of Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He. We are above everything, even the angels; only His greatness is above our greatness. Thus it is explained here: in the place of His greatness, you find His humility. This realization brings one to Inner Love and Fear.

Since these are great matters in the service of God, may He be blessed, he repeated these words and doubled them. This is the meaning of: "Circumcise the foreskin of your heart... for the Lord your God is God of gods." In the *Yalkut* Midrash <note>a medieval collection of Jewish legends and teachings</note> it says regarding the verse "This is the thing which the Lord commanded": Moses said to Israel, "That Evil Inclination—remove it from your hearts, and you shall all be of one fear and one counsel to serve before the Omnipresent. Just as He is unique in His world, so shall your service be unique before Him." As it is written: "Circumcise the foreskin of your heart..." Why? "For the Lord your God is God of gods." If you do this, "The glory of the Lord will appear to you." 

Now, one might ask: what is the novelty in this verse? Or what is meant by "one fear and one counsel"? Or why does it say "Because the Lord your God..."? To the author of the Midrash, the difficulty was why the phrase "This is the thing which the Lord commanded" is mentioned here more than with other commandments. One cannot say it is just to show the commandment is beloved so that one does not pursue other gods, or that he only does it because God commanded—for this was already explained above when "Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel," explaining to them that it was by Divine word. 

Therefore, this verse is explained differently, according to the teaching: "'To love the Lord your God' means you should be certain in it... not for the sake of being called a Sage, nor for the sake of being called a Rabbi, nor to be an Elder sitting in the Academy. Rather, do things for their own sake <note>original: *lishman*</note>, and honor will eventually come." This is the meaning of "This is the thing the Lord commanded you to do"—meaning, do it because it is God's command, and do not do it for your own glory. Moses saw that when the Sanctuary was completed, and the clouds and angels did not immediately descend, and the Divine Presence did not rest upon Israel, they were in distress. They desired that the Divine Presence dwell in the work of their hands for all to see. Moses worried that perhaps they were seeking this honor for their own sakes, so that the common people would see that "the Name of the Lord is called upon them." Therefore, he warned them: "Do it for the sake of the Lord," meaning let the fear of Heaven be upon you, and then you will do it for its own sake, and honor will eventually come. Then he said: "And the glory of the Lord shall appear to you"—meaning, you do your part for His Name, and do not worry, for honor will eventually arrive. 

This is the interpretation of the *Yalkut* Midrash: "That Evil Inclination—remove it from your hearts." He is precise in his language. He said "That," meaning the specific deed you did in building the Tabernacle was a good deed, but there is a fear that some sin might be mixed into that good—as it is written: "There is no righteous man on earth who does good and does not sin." This means there should be no "sin" within the "good" he does—which happens when one mixes in an external intention, like doing it to receive a reward or for one's own glory and beauty. Regarding this, he says "That Evil Inclination" which is hidden in the heart and not visible to the eye. For the visible action is good, but sometimes the physical power hides an external intention in the heart. Remove *that* from your heart, so there is only "one fear and one counsel." "Fear" is meant literally, and "Counsel" is the awakening and enthusiasm which is the attribute of Love. He comes to exclude external fear and love—to remove them from your heart—so there is only one Fear and one Counsel, which is Inner Fear and Love, the Inner-most level. This is why it says: "Circumcise the foreskin of your heart." Why? "For the Lord your God..." Meaning, remember that He is the Great Master and Ruler, the Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome. Then you will be clothed in Inner Fear. Afterward, remember that "He executes the judgment of the orphan and the widow," and that in the place of His greatness, there is His humility. Wherever you find the greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He, there you find His humility, as written in the Torah, etc. Contemplating this brings one to Inner Love. When one reflects that a King so Great, Exalted, and Uplifted shows the love of His providence to us lowly beings, how much more so should we serve Him with love, joy, and a good heart from the abundance of everything. Thus, the Midrash and the aim of the verses are aligned. He repeats "And you shall circumcise..." to hint at the awakening of Inner Fear and Love, "For the Lord your God, etc."

Afterward, it says: "The Lord your God you shall fear, Him you shall serve, to Him you shall cleave, and by His name you shall swear" <note>Deuteronomy 10:20</note>. This fear is the "Fear that follows Love"—the Inner-most Fear. It is meant to "rectify the King in His glory" through the Name of the Lord <note>Y-H-V-H</note>. This is the "Secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him," involving the four Divine configurations. This fear comes after "cleaving," "desiring," and "delighting," reaching the level of "swearing by His name." Our Sages hinted at this by saying the word *Et* <note>a grammatical particle</note> comes to include Torah scholars—for they transition to and rectify the Divine Name. Then his name is known. 

Thus we have fifty ascents, one upon the other: Inner Fear, Inner Love, and Inner-most Fear. Regarding Inner-most Fear, Antoninus <note>A Roman figure in the Talmud</note> said: once one is warned to serve not for the sake of reward, this already hints at Inner Fear and Love. Naturally, what follows is "And let the fear of Heaven be upon you," which is the Inner-most Fear. 

All these levels were hinted at in the chapter "With what may we light?" <note>Talmud Shabbat 31a</note>. Rabbah bar Rav Huna said: "Any person who has Torah but lacks the fear of Heaven is like a treasurer who was given the inner keys but the outer keys were not given to him—how shall he enter?" Note that even Inner Fear is categorized here among the "outer keys"—not that it is external, God forbid, but because it is the key to entering the chamber. Furthermore, he shall enter with keys that are truly and essentially "inner keys"—namely, the Love that comes from Love, and the Fear that comes from Love. This is proven by what I explained regarding "Fear of Heaven" in this essay as the first Inner Fear. In the words of Antoninus, "Fear of Heaven" refers to the Inner-most Fear. For as seen in the chapter "The Place Where They Customarily Act" <note>Talmud Pesachim 50a</note>, one verse says "Your kindness reaches the heavens" and another says "above the heavens." This is not a contradiction: one refers to those who act for God's sake (*Lishmah*), and the other to those who do not. The matter of *Lishmah* is for the "Name of the Lord" <note>the Name *HaShem*</note>, meaning the union and coupling of the final *He* of the Name with the *Vav*. In any place where it says "For the sake of Heaven," it means to connect the "Name"—which is the attribute of Kingship (*Malchut*)—with "Heaven"—which is Harmony (*Tiferet*).

Thus we have explained the matter of Fear and Love: Fear and Love that lead to Fear, and Fear and Love that emerge from Love. The three are intertwined. This is indicated by the forms of their letters when written one above the other and divided lengthwise and widthwise like this:

<insert>
FE AR
LO VE
</insert>

-> Or you will find Fear and Love in a straight line <-
-> Love, namely from top to bottom, and Love <-
-> namely in the width <-

So too you will find Fear and Love in height, Fear completing Fear, and Love completing Love for all generations, for they are joined together. This is my intention in including the fulfillment of Prohibitions and Positive Commandments within "Fear," and likewise including Positive and Prohibitive Commandments within "Love." Although it is known in many places that Prohibitions stem from Fear and Positive Commandments from Love, nevertheless, since they are always joined and inclusive of one another, the whole is truth and clear to those who understand. 

To return to the matter of Inner Fear: a "Completely Righteous" person is an Inner Lover; a "Completely Righteous" person who cleaves with desire and delight possesses Inner-most Fear. This is the level of the "Pious One" <note>original: *Chasid*</note> who acts with loving-kindness toward his Creator and "rectifies the King in His glory." These are the "Children of Ascent" who raise up the holy sparks, but they are few. This was the superior level of Abraham our forefather: "For now I know that you are a God-fearer"—meaning a fear that stems from love. This is hinted at in the verse: "Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. For Moses, our teacher, rectified the "House" <note>the Divine Presence</note>; he built it into a permanent structure and did not move from it for a single moment. The intention was: "You did not fear like him." 

Now that these people have erred and considered themselves [on his level], there is a question on this verse which speaks of Moses' greatness: why is he called a "servant," as in "My servant Moses"? It should have said "My son," since it is commonly said in the world that the rank of a "son" is higher than that of a "servant"—as seen in the liturgy for Rosh Hashanah: "Whether as sons or as servants." And likewise in the prayer *Avinu Malkeinu*: "If as sons... if as servants." So too after his death, he is called a servant: "Moses My servant is dead." This difficulty—why he is not called a son—is indeed a strong one.

It reinterprets the biblical description of Moses as a "servant" not as a demotion, but as the highest possible rank of selfless devotion to the Divine.</summary>

# Essay 3 and Essay 4

And one should distance himself from sin, for then his soul is found to be flawed. A proof for this is what Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>original: RSB"Y, the 2nd-century sage credited with the Zohar</note>, of blessed memory, said to the companions: "And you, companions, behold! The Holy One, blessed be He, takes delight now in these words of Torah that you are innovating on this path. And you stand before their Master in your holy images <note>original: *dyuknikon kaddishin*, referring to the spiritual form or aura of a person</note>. For when I look at you and gaze upon your images, I see that you are inscribed with the secret of the First Man <note>Adam</note>. I know that your image is prepared above, and you are beloved, the righteous commanders <note>original: *ormana*, a high official</note> who are recognized by the eyes of all, showing a holy countenance before the whole world." This is as it is written: "All who see them shall recognize them, for they are the seed the Lord has blessed" <note>Isaiah 61:9</note>. And the secret of what Rabbi Isaac saw when he was reflecting on worldly matters—Rabbi Shimon said to him, "See how the cup completes your image, but there is one thing missing in you." Rabbi Yose arose, and they occupied themselves with words of Torah. Rabbi Shimon gazed at him and said, "Rabbi Yose, now you are complete before the Ancient of Days <note>a mystical name for God representing the most hidden aspect of the Divine</note> and your image is whole." Thus far his words.

And this is the aspect of the "Higher Fear": that a person should view himself as if he is always standing before the Cause of Causes <note>the ultimate Source of all existence</note>. For his spiritual image is engraved above in the secret of the soul. If, Heaven forbid, he should cause a flaw even in thought, his soul is found to be flawed and distanced from the light of the face of the Supreme King, as explained in the passage I cited. A person should think how much awe he would feel if he were standing before Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, who could recognize even a person's thoughts in his face. His companions stood in awe before him, for in standing before him, they were standing before the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the indwelling presence of God in the world</term> itself. In this same way, a person must fear the Creator, who stands before him and knows his thoughts.

And according to the degree that a person cleaves to the Creator and fears Him, so the Creator is found with him, as it is said: "If you seek Him, He will be found by you" <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note>. Thus far his words.

And all this is included in the "Fear of Sin," being so afraid of sin that it should not come to his hand. This is explained in the Midrash <note>original: *Tanchuma*</note> on the verse, "When a soul sins through an error" <note>Leviticus 4:2</note>. To what can this be compared? To two people who sinned against the King. One was a villager <note>original: *kartani*</note> and one was a son of the palace <note>original: *ben paltin*</note>. Although both committed the same sin, the King turned his face away from the villager, but to the palace official, the King gave a legal decree <note>original: *apophasis*, a Greek legal term for a sentence</note>. He said to the palace official, "My son, why did you change? We committed one sin, yet to the villager the King turned his face, while to you he gave a decree!" He replied, "I turned away from the villager because he does not know the protocols <note>original: *nimusei*, from the Greek *nomos* (law)</note> of the Kingdom. But the son of the palace stands with me every single day; he knows the protocols of the Kingdom and yet he sinned." So too, the body is the villager—"And the Lord God formed the man [from the dust]"—but the soul is the son of the palace from above, for He "breathed into his nostrils the breath of life." Since both sin, the verse emphasizes: "A soul <note>original: *nefesh*</note> that shall sin." What is the meaning of "through an error"? To teach you that anyone who sins accidentally is considered as if he transgressed the commandments of the Lord. And so it says, "And if you err and do not perform all these commandments..." <note>Numbers 15:22</note>. It also says: "Who can understand his errors?" and "Also from intentional sins keep back Your servant" <note>Psalm 19:13-14</note>, for an error in study is considered an intentional sin. Thus far his words. Just as there is a difference between the body and the soul, so there is a difference between one soul and another, according to the greatness of one's spiritual image and their closeness to the Source. And as it says in the Zohar <note>original: *Ra'aya Mehemna*</note> on the portion of *Naso*: "Whoever fulfills one commandment properly, it is as if he fulfills all 248 positive commandments, for there is no commandment that is not included in all 248." Thus far his words. From this, the punishment for the transgressor is known, for one who violates one commandment is as if he violates them all. This is the meaning of "if you err and do not do all the commandments." So wrote the author of *The Beginning of Wisdom* <note>original: *Reshit Chochma* by Eliyahu de Vidas</note>: <gloss>And guarding against sin is also a great virtue and a spiritual remedy, whereby a person should fence himself in with Torah and pursue it with speed</gloss> and alacrity, to seek out a commandment and perform it with beauty at every time and every moment.

## The Fifth Essay

Eternal Service: This means that in every measure that the Holy One, blessed be He, measures out to you, you must remain truly committed to Fear and Love. One should not fear for oneself or serve oneself, but only fear and love the Lord. Thus, he does not move from his service even in a time of distress. He accepts suffering with love and is found to be always serving God amidst his troubles. This is a great trait—to accept suffering with love. It is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, and tripled in the Writings <note>a common rabbinic phrase for a concept found in all three sections of the Hebrew Bible</note>, and we study it in the Talmud. It is explained in the words of the early and later sages regarding suffering that comes upon a person: it is not good for the perfect man to revel in suffering by rebelling against it, Heaven forbid. Rather, he should receive it with love and a pleasant countenance, bowing his shoulder to bear the yoke of hardships and events that come toward him. He should rejoice and be glad, knowing that He, may He be blessed, is a True Judge; all His ways are justice, a God of faithfulness without iniquity. "For whom the Lord loves He reproves" <note>Proverbs 3:12</note>, and "as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you" <note>Deuteronomy 8:5</note>. He should also think that no evil descends from above, and "whatever the Holy One, blessed be He, does, He does for the good," to cleanse his sins in order to benefit him in his end. For there is no suffering without sin. We study in the *Sifrei*: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says, "As long as a person lives in tranquility, his sins are not atoned for; but through suffering, he becomes reconciled before the Omnipresent, as it is said, 'For whom the Lord loves He reproves.'"

Furthermore, suffering causes a person to return in repentance. As Rava said: "If a person sees suffering coming upon him, he should examine his deeds." And in the chapter *Chelek* <note>of Tractate Sanhedrin</note>, Rabbi Akiva said: "Suffering is precious." It is written of Manasseh that he was twelve years old when he became king and reigned fifty-five years, and it says "he did evil in the eyes of the Lord." It also says, "These too are proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah copied..." Did Hezekiah the King teach Torah to the whole world but not to his own son? This is to tell you that all the toil he toiled in Torah did not bring his son to good, but only suffering did, as it says: "And the Lord spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they did not listen. So the Lord brought upon them the army commanders of the King of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh with hooks and bound him with bronze chains and led him to Babylon. And when he was in distress, he entreated the Lord his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers. And He was entreated of him and heard his plea and restored him to Jerusalem to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord is God." What did they do to him? etc. See there. Thus you see that suffering leads to repentance. And in the chapter *Chelek*: "'And behold, it was very good' <note>Genesis 1:31</note>—Rabbi Huna said, 'This refers to the attribute of suffering.'" Is it "very good"? I am astonished! Rather, it is because through it, creatures come to the life of the World to Come. And so Solomon said, "The way of life is the rebuke of discipline" <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>. And in the chapter *Kol Mevaser* <note>likely *Berakhot*</note>: Three good gifts did the Holy One, blessed be He, give to Israel, and all of them were given only through suffering: the Torah, the Land, and the World to Come. For our strengthening, through the suffering of the body, the soul is atoned for, for the soul is its opposite. Therefore, Abraham our father chose for his children that they should fall into exile for their sins so they would not fall into Gehenna <note>Purgatory/Hell</note>, as it is found in *Genesis Rabbah*. For it is better for Israel to suffer the body with pain, troubles, and exiles than to have their souls punished with eternal punishment.

And the main thing is that suffering leads to repentance. And this is what is searched and checked in the ten generations in the *Tikunim* <note>Zoharic literature</note> to praise it. For when a person is in days of tranquility, he does not recognize or examine the ways of truth because nature draws him away, always showing him pleasures and desires. But when he is in distress, he cannot open his heart in that way; therefore, he recognizes the truth clearly and seeks the Lord—not just to escape the trouble, but with the strength of his heart and his whole soul. For the intellect tends toward its natural inclination when there is no inhibitor. This is the secret of "Suffering of Love." For it is impossible for a righteous person, even if he does not sin and fulfills all the commandments, not to be slightly distracted by the desires of the world from cleaving to his Creator. Because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, sometimes brings suffering upon the righteous, even if they did not stumble in a transgression, only so that they may increase the strengthening of the "Wells of the Tree of Life" and not be seduced by the world at all. And in the chapter *The One who Hires Laborers* <note>Tractate Bava Metzia</note>, Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Shimon accepted suffering upon himself, and so did our Holy Rabbi <note>Judah the Prince</note> accept great and mighty sufferings. See there. We hear from all these that suffering is good for man. Therefore, just as we bless for the good with joy and a good heart, so we bless for the bad with joy, for God intended it for the good, even if this is hidden from human beings.

Hillel the Elder merited this level, as it is taught: There was an incident with Hillel the Elder who was walking on the road and heard a sound of screaming in the city. He said, "I am confident that this is not in my house." Concerning him, the verse says: "He shall not fear an evil report; his heart is firm, trusting in the Lord" <note>Psalm 112:7</note>. The book *Tefillah Le-Moshe* asks: How could Hillel elevate himself to say he was confident it was not in his house, given that "there is no righteous person on earth [who does not sin]" and there is no sin without the cleansing of suffering? Even if it were possible for a person to be without sin, is it right for him to praise himself? And it is already well known in the Talmud the measure of humility that Hillel possessed. But the matter is that Hillel rejoiced in suffering, receiving it with a pleasant countenance, and he had accustomed

<columns>2</columns>

his household members to this as well. Therefore, when he heard a sound of screaming in the city—people crying out over a trouble that had occurred in the city—he said:
"I am confident that this is not in my house." This refers to the *screaming*. He was not ruling out the possibility of trouble, Heaven forbid, for trouble could indeed be in his house. But as for the screaming and crying out over it, he was confident it was not in his house,
because they were accustomed to receiving troubles with a good heart. Regarding this, the verse says: "He shall not fear an evil report." This means: the verse does not say "an evil report he shall not hear," which would imply the absence of an evil report. Rather, it says "from an evil report he shall not *fear*," meaning even if he hears an evil report, he
will not fear it, for he knows it is for his benefit—that he heard the report to cleanse his sins. Thus, a person should not...

It builds upon the previous page’s discussion of the human image being modeled after the divine "First Man" (Adam Kadmon).</meta>

# Essay 3 and Essay 4

<margin>This concerns the secret of the "Sharpened Knife" <note>original: *skina putenta*, a Kabbalistic term for the power of discernment and judgment</note> positioned between Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the flash of intuition</term> and Understanding <term>Binah: the analytical processing of that intuition</term>. It relates to the secret of Kingship <note>Malchut, the lowest of the ten divine emanations</note> which is the "Lower Mother" compared to the "Higher Mother" <note>Binah</note>. Thus, the verse repeats "The Lord your God" twice; one refers to Kingship and Beauty <note>Tiferet</note>, and one refers to Wisdom and Understanding. Also, the word "Beloved [of] your God" <note>Yedid Elohecha</note> hints that the word *Yedid* (Beloved) is numerically equivalent to the name *Elohim* <note>Both sum to 86 in Gematria</note>. Through Wisdom and Understanding, they are unified by the hand of the name *Elohim*. Its interior is the "will" of the letters, for the letters of the name *Ehyeh* <note>I Am</note> sum to 45, the same as the name *Mah* <note>The numeric value of the name Y-H-V-H when expanded with the letter Aleph</note>. This is also the secret of the name *A-B-D-T*, which is a substitution for the letters preceding the letters of the alphabet. Before the letter *Lamed*, there is no letter <note>referring to a specific mystical cipher</note>, and before the *Mem* of the Shekhinah <term>the Divine Presence</term>, there is a lack. This is also the secret of the "Sharpened Knife" which disciplines children, as it is written: "He who spares the rod hates his son" <note>Proverbs 13:24</note>. This is the secret of the question: "What (*Mah*) does the Lord ask of you?" <note>Deuteronomy 10:12</note>.</margin>

The generations of Adam—and according to what I have written, it is explained in the verse: "The Lord your God you shall fear" <note>Deuteronomy 10:20</note>. This refers to the "Fear of the Inner-most Essence" that exists. By His name, whatever people do belongs to Him. I have already written regarding the "Rectification of the Name of the King in His Glory," which is the secret of Understanding, and the secret of the Shekhinah. As the Kabbalists have said: the secret of the "Seven" refers to the seven lower emanations used for building the world, but the secret of the "Vow" <note>Hebrew: *Neder*</note> is above them, in the secret of Understanding (*Binah*). *Neder* is spelled *Nun-Dar*: the fifty (*Nun*) gates of Understanding where Moses ascended. The wise will understand and contemplate the words I have written.

## The Third Essay: Inner Fear and Love

->I shall now return to the matter of the essays:<-

And now, the Third Essay concerns Inner Fear and Love. It says: "Know the God of your father and serve Him" <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note>. The use of the pronoun "Him" implies Him alone and no other. This excludes two "faces" or motivations of "partnership" <note>serving God alongside other motivations</note>. The first "face" is divided into two types: (1) One who performs the service of the Blessed Name so that people will praise him, or for some other reason, and does not truly fear Heaven in secret. (2) One who serves the Blessed Name even in secret, but desires and rejoices when it becomes known to people; this too is "evil and bitter." The second "face" is one who fears Heaven in secret and hides his deeds from the eyes of men, serving with all his heart and soul, yet he does it for the sake of reward in this world or fear of punishment in this world. This is called "External Love and Fear," because he serves for the love of himself. Even if he does it for the reward of the eternal world—which is permitted—it is still not service in its "Inner Essence." True service is for Him alone, may He be blessed—that is, for His glory, the ultimate purpose of the Great and Holy King, the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He. He is the Root and Foundation of all worlds. Lift your eyes and see: Who created these? He created absolute "something" from "nothing." Contemplate the greatness of the Lord's works in the creation of the earth and all its hosts: the inanimate, the growing, the living, and the speaking; the multitude of wonders, wisdoms, and life forces. He created species and diverse types, and He created wind and flaming fire. All of this is considered as spirit and void against the world of the Celestial Spheres. Each sphere is higher than the next, and all are considered as nothing against an Angel. And one Angel before another is "high above the high," by thousands and tens of thousands without number in His legions. And all of them are as if they were not when compared to the Throne of Glory, and the Throne against His Glory. He is the Cause of all causes and the Reason for all reasons, and there is none besides Him. Surely, by contemplating these things, any man would fear Him. This is "Inner Fear."

Afterward, he should remember that His humility is as great as His greatness. In His generosity of heart, He brought us into existence from nothing. A person should be awakened by the goodness and kindness God has performed, which are engraved to show His love. One should be awakened to "Inner Love" by remembering the kindnesses that have passed over him. It is not like a "full bull" <note>an idiom for someone who is sated and forgets his master</note>. A parable: Imagine a man whose leg was broken or whose eyes were blinded, and a great physician came and, with his great wisdom, healed him—even for a fee! Would he not love him all his life with an intense, boundless love? Behold, the Blessed Name gave him his eyes and legs and the power of sight, and He sustains him and watches over him. He gave him a soul so that he could attain eternity. If a person subdues his lower nature, his rank becomes higher than the Ministering Angels. When a person considers such things a thousand times—especially one whom God has granted wealth, honor, and greatness beyond others—he must fear all the more. This is how Jacob feared, saying "I have been diminished by all the kindnesses" <note>Genesis 32:11</note>, fearing his merits had been used up. He should be aflame with Inner Love, since God preceded him and showed him love as a gift and kindness, even if he did not deserve it. This is "serving Him with a whole heart and a willing soul." A "whole heart" is the service of the heart in Inner Fear. A "willing soul" is the passion and desire in Inner Love. For "He alone seeks"—meaning the true service for Him alone, as I said: not for the love of any reward nor the fear of any punishment. And Heaven forbid he should do it so that people praise him. Regarding this, they said: "Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven," meaning there should not be even the slightest bit of any other motivation. Because "the Lord searches all hearts," they said "serve Him" without partnering any other matter.

<margin>This is the secret of "Serve Him" (*Avdehu*). The letters of "Serve the Lord" (*Avad Y-H-V-H*) contain the letters *Vav* and *He* from the Name, representing the "Rectification of the King in His Glory." This is the Fear that is "within the within," which is drawn from Inner Love. This is hinted at in the verse: "Only in your fathers did the Lord delight (*Chashak*) to love them" <note>Deuteronomy 10:15</note>. The word "Delight" (*Chashak*) implies the unification of Beauty and Kingship. It is a desire in love and awe. The secret of the word *CH-SH-K* (Desire) is found in the vowel points: *Holam*, *Sheva*, and *Kamatz*. The *Kamatz* is the secret of Kindness (*Chesed*), as in "The Priest shall scoop (*v'kamatz*)" <note>Leviticus 2:2</note>, which comes from the side of Kindness and the "Kindness to Abraham." The *Sheva* is from the side of Strength (*Gevurah*), as in "And Sheba fell and took them" <note>Job 1:15</note>; the *Sheva* is the fire of the soul and the attribute of Isaac, the "Fear of Isaac." The *Holam* is the upper point, the secret of Beauty (*Tiferet*), the attribute of Jacob, the line that ascends to the very top, the "inheritance without boundaries." This is "He delighted (*Chashak*) in your fathers." 

One should remember the intention of the order of the Assembly of Israel: "In assemblies, bless God, the Lord, from the source of Israel" <note>Psalm 68:27</note>. The King in His Glory does not sleep. The name *A-D-N-Y* <note>Lord</note> is also pointed with the vowels of *CH-SH-K*. These are the "Four Legs of the Chariot" that comprise the entire spiritual building. This unification causes the "True Pregnancy" <note>a mystical term for the development of spiritual lights</note>. A person should not serve for his own needs or to make a name for himself; that is not the service of God. He should not rest or sleep, day or night, but labor to sustain the "River and its Radiance" through the light and heavy commandments of the Torah, the Rabbinic decrees, and the safeguards. He should be as afraid of sin as one is of a plunderer or an enemy. Just as one keeps a watch, so should he "make a guard for the guard" <note>a Talmudic concept of adding extra boundaries to prevent sin</note>. He should tremble and fear lest he stumble even unintentionally (*Shogeg*), for even an unintentional sin requires great atonement. This is explained in Tractate Nedarim, in the chapter "He who says": If a husband annuls his wife's vow and she did not know, the Torah says "the Lord will forgive her"—meaning she still needs forgiveness and atonement because she intended to violate a vow. When Rabbi Akiva reached this verse, he would weep: "If one intended to eat pork but [unintentionally] ate lamb, he needs atonement; how much more so one who intended to eat pork and actually ate pork!" Furthermore, Issi ben Judah says: "He did not know, yet he is guilty and shall bear his iniquity"—over this, all who grieve should grieve. 

Because the soul is so radiant and spiritual, emanating from such a high place, even an unintentional flaw darkens the soul. It is like a person who spills a drop of oil or ink on white, clean clothes; even if done unintentionally, the stain darkens the garment. Regarding this, it is said: "Let your garments always be white, and let oil not be lacking from your head" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:8</note>. This is also hinted at in the verse: "I have sinned because I did not know"—meaning even what I did not know and was unintentional, I still call it "sin." For man is always responsible, and he must contemplate the paths he walks so as not to stumble even in the smallest of small matters. How much more so must an important person take extra care. The higher one is, the more strictly he is judged. The acronym for "The Gate of Fear" is "The Hand of the Poor" <note>Yad HaAni</note>. The higher a man rises in rank, the more he is scrutinized, as in: "Around Him it storms greatly" <note>Psalm 50:3</note>. This is like the servants of a king: a king has many servants. Some stand before him in the inner palace, some in the outer house, some in the courtyard, and some outside the city. All serve and fear the king, but the closer one is, the more he trembles, for he stands directly before the king and must not be found with any error. Therefore it says "Around Him it storms greatly"—anyone close to the King must be "stormy" <note>agitated with awe</note>. Any place where "greatly" (*me'od*) is said, it means without measure. When the righteous man considers that he stands before Him in the Inner Palace, the life of his soul depends on it. His providence over all creatures never ceases. He is "around the King" because the King brought him close to know the secrets of His palace. Because the "Higher Soul" given to the righteous is greater than that of the common people, he must fear lest the Supreme King find any error in him, causing the light of Providence to be hidden and his soul to be distanced.</margin>

## The Fourth Essay: Service as a "Higher Need"

The hint in this verse "Know the God of your father" also means that he should strive all his days, in every path he turns, to bring near the ways of the Lord. This is the secret of the Prayer of Israel and the unification through the final letter *He*, which is the Great Name, the secret of the "God of David."
