# Gate of the Letters

**We have learned** in Tractate Shabbat, in the chapter "With what may a woman go out," that Samuel said he did not allow his daughters to sleep together, and so on. For behold, let us say this supports Rav Huna, for Rav Huna said: "Women who rub against one another <note>original: "Mesolalot," referring to lesbian physical contact</note> are disqualified from the priesthood." He <note>Samuel</note> held this view so that they would not become accustomed to another body. If so, for this same reason, young men should not sleep together in the same rooms. We emphasize this because the "brazen-faced" <note>shameless people</note> of this generation, when they sleep together, come to commit a transgression. Even though we learned in Tractate Kiddushin that Rabbi Judah says a bachelor should not herd animals, nor should two bachelors sleep under one cloak, while the Sages permit it—and in the Gemara <note>the commentary on the Mishnah</note> it is taught that Israel is not suspected of male-to-male intercourse or bestiality, and the law follows the Sages—nevertheless, it is stated there in the Gemara that many of the Amoraim <note>Sages of the Talmudic era</note> were extremely strict even regarding animals, and certainly regarding males. The *Tur* <note>a major legal code</note> also wrote in the section *Even HaEzer*, Chapter 24, that it is proper to be strict even regarding animals and even regarding being alone <note>original: "Yichud"</note> with them, and certainly in one bed. This was the careful practice in all of Spain, even regarding being alone together. Since I have already written that his generation is in a state of evil, I hereby command you that your sons shall not sleep in one bed, nor next to any young man. This warning is sufficient.

**You, my sons,** may God protect you, were warned with great clarity to marry off your sons while they are young, before they come to have sinful thoughts <note>original: "Hirhurim"</note>. Afterward, they may study Torah in purity. As it says in Tractate Kiddushin, Chapter 1, Rav Hisda said: "The reason I am superior to my colleagues is that I married at sixteen; and had I married at fourteen, I would have said to the Accuser <note>Satan</note>: 'An arrow in your eyes!'"

**And you were warned** with great clarity that before the wedding canopy <note>original: "Chuppah"</note>, the groom should not sit next to the bride as is the custom in this evil generation. Not only do they seat the groom next to the bride, but he even hugs and kisses her. Woe to the eyes that see such things, and woe to the ears that hear them! I wonder at the sages of this generation who overlook this great sin and remember it the next morning, yet do not protest. This is not only because if the maiden has reached the stage of menstruation <note>original: "Niddah"</note> she is subject to a Torah prohibition, as it says "Do not draw near" <note>Leviticus 18:19</note>, which forbids even drawing close. Even Rabbi Pedat and Ulla in Tractate Shabbat, who do not hold that "drawing close" is a Torah-level prohibition, nonetheless, Ulla said: "They say to a Nazirite: 'Go around, go around, but do not come near the vineyard!'" <note>A metaphor meaning one should stay far away from the source of temptation.</note>

**Furthermore,** even if she is still a young girl, the groom’s impulse <note>original: "Yetzer"</note> will overcome him and lead to physical closeness that results in the wasting of seed <note>original: "Hotza’at Zera LeVatala," male ejaculation outside of a procreative context</note>. Even if seed does not leave him, it is impossible that it will not lead to arousal <note>original: "Kishuy"</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory decreed against this, as I have written: the fear of arousal is a disgrace added to the prohibition he commits. Therefore, you my sons, may God protect you, and all the pious members of my family: I warn with the full strength of my authority that this abomination shall not be seen or found. The groom shall not sleep near the bride and shall not touch her at all.

**I have also come** to warn against a similar custom where they hold the wedding on Friday <note>original: "Erev Shabbat"</note>. Even if the bride is virtuous, the groom sleeps near her for several nights before he performs the mandatory act of consummation <note>original: "Be’ilat Mitzvah"</note>. He then falls into sin, for they likely sleep naked together, and he desires and lusts for her, his impulse overpowering him, yet he does not consummate the marriage. Most often, this leads to the wasting of seed or to forbidden intimacy. Let the Name of Heaven be held dear by you: arrange the weddings of your children according to the decree of our Sages—a virgin is married on Wednesday, and the consummation occurs that night. Likewise, if the wedding is on the Sabbath, the groom shall not sleep at all near the bride until the night he intends to consummate the marriage. All of this I command with a powerful decree, and it is upon you to fulfill the commands of a father and the commands of a student to his teacher. Guard yourselves carefully, and then God will guard you.

**And these are the words** of the pious Rabbi Eliezer Azikri in the book *Sefer HaCharedim* regarding an exceedingly evil and difficult matter. After discussing his kindnesses, he brought up the issue of one who has intimacy with his wife "not in her way" <note>original: "Shelo Kedarkah," referring to anal intercourse</note>, as was written above, for this was the sin of Er and Onan. This is explained explicitly in the *Zohar* in the section on the Palaces <note>original: "Heikhalot"</note>, which is brought into the synagogue on the Sabbath, regarding one of the names of the Evil Inclination called "Impure." And these are the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai there: "He opened and said: One of us stands... and this is his name... and how many thousands and tens of thousands are appointed under him. And he stands over all those who corrupt their way and spill seed on the ground, or those who emit seed in an unnatural way, or all those who stray in their bitterness—these are the ones who do not see the face of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> at all. When the soul leaves the person, this 'Impure' one and all those with him defile the soul and seize it... and these are called 'Evil Seed' and 'Defiled Spirits'..." <note>A translation of the Aramaic Zohar passage warning that those who waste seed are haunted by destructive spiritual forces in this world and the next.</note>

**There are some people** who err in this matter because they do not know it is forbidden. Therefore, those whose "fear of sin does not precede their wisdom" <note>a reference to Ethics of the Fathers 3:9</note>—who are not among those who tremble at His word—learn from the Gemara what appears on the surface to suggest there is no sin in this. For we learn at the end of the third chapter of Tractate Nedarim that a woman came before our Holy Teacher <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince</note> and said to him: "I set the table for him, but he overturned it" <note>a metaphor for unnatural intercourse</note>. He replied that it was permitted. It is also told of a woman who came before Rav, and they said it was permitted. Some commentators explained that this "overturning" refers to intercourse "not in her way." These people permitted it for themselves, but they did not set their hearts to descend into the depths of the law or look at the words of the Rabbis of Israel who explain the Gemara. All of them raised a difficulty against this passage from the discussion in Tractate Yevamot, in the chapter "Four Brothers," where it is said regarding the rejection of Er and Onan that they acted "not in her way." Our teacher Moses bar Maimon <note>Maimonides or Rambam</note> pointed out that this only means they did not waste seed inside the woman’s body. What Rav and Rabbi permitted regarding acting "not in her way" was only without the emission of seed <note>i.e., external stimulation without ejaculation</note>, but rather by acting in a manner of arousal, and then placing the seed in the proper place for procreation. This is the answer: "so that you shall not be like a companion," <note>unclear reference, possibly referring to a temporary or unnatural act</note> meaning only once in a while, and not like the way of the world. Those who think highly of themselves have taken a permission for themselves against these Sages, practicing unnatural intercourse and emitting seed in a place of filth. Think of the passage in Yevamot which says they were liable for death for this act, according to everyone, whether according to the Rosh or the Rambam. Indeed, the portion of such men is in the second level of Purgatory <note>original: "Gehenna"</note> called "The Pit" <note>original: "Shachat"</note>, and concerning him, Wisdom calls out: "He shall be called impure!"

**The truth is** that there is no permission at all for ejaculation in a place of filth. For the teacher, the Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel</note>, remarked on the Rambam’s answer that if it were true that Rabbi and Rav permitted unnatural acts only without ejaculation, they should have warned those people very strictly, for they could easily fall into a sin punishable by death. Therefore, the Rosh explained that it was only permitted once in a person's entire life. But even the Rosh's answer has a difficulty: they still should have warned the man not to make it a habit. Furthermore, if it is considered "wasted seed"—which is called "shedding blood" and brings a flood to the world, and for which Er and Onan died—who could permit it even once? If the Torah permitted it, as Rav and Rabbi said, then it is permitted. But if it is not "wasted seed," then who could forbid it even many times? These are things that the mind cannot tolerate. Further, their explanation is difficult because of what was said in the Gemara earlier, where Rabbi Yochanan ben Dahavai disagreed, saying that "one who overturns his table will have lame children." This implies he was speaking of intercourse that could result in offspring, not just a one-time act. The main proof of the commentators who permit unnatural intercourse is from what is said in Tractate Sanhedrin: "Rabbi Eleazar said in the name of Rabbi Hanina: A Son of Noah <note>a Gentile</note> who has intercourse with his wife not in her way is liable for death, as it is said, 'and he shall cleave to his wife' <note>Genesis 2:24</note>." Rava then asks: "Is there anything for which a non-Jew is liable but an Israelite is not?" Therefore, Rava concludes that a Son of Noah is exempt for such an act. However, the Ra’avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David</note> holds that this is no proof at all. For even according to their view, one can ask: why does Rava assume an Israelite is not liable? Perhaps Rava is coming to teach a different point... <note>The text enters a complex legal debate about whether certain sexual acts that are forbidden to Israelites carry a death penalty for non-Jews, arguing that the permission for Israelites is extremely limited or non-existent when it involves the wasting of seed.</note>

<summary>This page warns against immodest sleeping arrangements for young men and excessive physical intimacy between engaged couples, while providing a stern legal and mystical warning against the "wasting of seed" and unnatural sexual acts.</summary>

And Judah the Pious explained that since she <note>likely referring to a woman in a specific case mentioned previously</note> engaged in relations during her period of impurity <note>original: "Niddah"</note>, she must fast at least forty-nine days, even if she only transgressed once. And the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, a 13th-century scholar</note> wrote that one who has relations with a menstruant must fast three hundred and forty-five days, in addition to the other physical mortifications he prescribed. He wrote: "If we were to judge every single transgression, we would not have enough strength..." and so on. Thus, we see before us that he also holds that by the letter of the law, she would be obligated to perform repentance for every single act of intercourse, as mentioned above. However, he did not wish to overburden her because she was young, and in those years she would not have the strength to endure many harsh physical mortifications. Thus far are the words of my father and teacher, of blessed memory.

### Gate of the Letters

**And behold,** it is known that for every repentance, there are four types of repentance arranged by the *Rokeach* <note>Rabbi Eleazar of Worms, a 12th-century mystic</note>: Repentance for a Recurring Temptation, Repentance of the Fence <note>setting boundaries</note>, Weighted Repentance <note>penance equal to the sin's pleasure</note>, and Scriptural Repentance <note>penance based on biblical punishments</note>. If a sin carries the penalty of death <note>divine or judicial</note>, one must perform ascetic practices <term>Sigufim<gloss>physical acts of penance like fasting or cold baths</gloss></term> that are equivalent to death. One who wastes seed <note>referring to masturbation</note> is liable for death. The *Rokeach* and the godly Arizal <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century father of modern Kabbalah</note> have already arranged the order of repentance for this sin. Both are the "words of the living God," for repentance helps to repair the damage one caused, for example, in the World of Action <note>Asiyah</note> or the World of Formation <note>Yetzirah</note>. If one wishes to repair more deeply, one requires even greater repentance. Perhaps even then it will suffice! However, to truly repair how much one has turned from good and become evil—for he has done what is evil in the eyes of the Lord—he certainly needs more and more penance.

The matter would be easy if the sin had been committed only once. But in our many sins, for one who has become accustomed to the sins of youth through unseemly acts, leading to the wasting of seed—whether through lustful thoughts or "adultery of the hands" <note>manual stimulation</note> and the like—and has done so many times, he must perform the severe repentance mentioned above as many times as he committed the transgression. In such a case, his years would end before his repentance was finished!

This is what is hinted at in the Zohar <note>the foundational work of Kabbalah</note>: that "there is no repentance for this sin." This is because the one who does this clothes his vital life-force in the "external" evil shells of desire, acting as if there were no barrier to him. For in other sins, there are barriers involving another person—such as one who seeks a forbidden relationship; if the partner does not want to, he will not sin, or sometimes he refrains out of fear of other people. This is not the case with wasting seed; in our many sins, the transgression is in his own hand to do in secret whenever he wishes. Therefore, even if he performs repentance, it is often insufficient for a "complete repentance" due to the sheer number of times he is obligated to repeat the process.

Let him explain all his confessions clearly; let him weep and cry out like Rabbi Eleazar ben Durdia, who placed his head between his knees <note>a posture of intense grief</note> until his soul departed, as is stated in Tractate Avodah Zarah. Even for one who has reached a state where he committed this sin a hundred times, or eighty times, or without number, I say to him: "Be strong!" and it will be well. For it is known that the Holy One, blessed be He, joins a good thought to an action. If a person had a good intention to perform such-and-such penance and died before finishing the deed, the Holy One joins the thought as if the deed had been fully performed.

Let him study the order of repentance for this sin as written in the *Rokeach* and as written in the penances of the Arizal, which are printed at the end of the *Kitzur Likkutei Amarim* and are available to everyone. He set the number of fasts there at 310. One should be expert in that small book and in the secret intentions of the Divine Names. Before beginning to accept the fasts, he should go to the ritual bath <term>Mikveh<gloss>a pool of natural water used for spiritual purification</gloss></term> for the purpose of accepting repentance. My father and teacher wrote in the book *Brit Avraham* that there is a basis for this immersion in the Jerusalem Talmud: a story of a woman who was taken captive among the gentiles, and when she was released, they immersed her because she had been fed forbidden foods. Afterward, he should return to his house, "write his soul" <note>examine his conscience</note>, and weep for his spirit and soul in "Questions and Responds," a source found in the commentary of the Recanati, section 6. He wrote: "Our Master Simcha wrote that one who has relations with a gentile woman needs immersion for repentance, like the Fathers of Rabbi Nathan. However, the immersion is not the primary obstacle; rather, the secret is that as soon as he meditates on repentance, he is considered a perfectly righteous man, but he still needs to afflict himself."

**Behold,** he should lie in secret on the ground with his shoes removed, dust on his head and sackcloth on his flesh. He should weep with bitterness of heart before the Blessed Name over how he acted lustfully and how he sinned. He should be broken-hearted, with total regret and a will to leave his sin before the Lord, saying: "My God, I am ashamed and disgraced to lift my face to You, my God. I have no mouth to answer and find no way to lift my head, for my iniquities have multiplied beyond counting and my sins are more than the sand."

**Indeed,** I am full of sin and You are full of mercy. There is no end to Your mercies and Your grace, as it is written: "The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth... forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin." You assist those who return in every matter. I return in complete repentance before You, and I regret the past, weeping and confessing. Comfort belongs to the Lord; righteousness is Yours, and to me belongs the shame of face, for I have acted many times and stained my soul, spirit, and breath with many stains. Therefore, I accept upon myself fasting and mortifications to purify every trace of blemish. And You, O Lord—I am here, help me, O God of my salvation, and assist me toward complete repentance! Then he shall accept the fast upon himself with a broken heart and great weeping.

When the sun sets and he becomes pure on the night of that fast, he should isolate himself from his errors and perform repentance according to the tradition of the New Moon fasts.

**A piece of good advice** is that he should perform these 310 fasts in six periods—that is, three "breaks" <note>original: "Hafsakot"</note> of two days and two nights of continuous fasting. For every such break counts as twenty-six days, and three such breaks equal eighty-one days <note>based on mystical calculations</note>. Afterward, he should fast another fifty separate days, and other days as well. But in my eyes, it seems better to do three breaks of forty days each, so that every fast day is a full day, "and it was evening and it was morning, one day." How his eating should be arranged for the meal before the fast will be explained later at length in the Laws of Repentance. So too, he should afflict himself in his sleeping and his weeping, and perform this in every second "break" and yearly prayer. He should take it upon himself to do this all the days of his life without hesitation or weakening, even if he were to live a thousand years. Then, even if he dies, the Holy One will accept him as if he had lived a long time and performed this order of repentance as many times as the number of times he sinned, since he was ready and prepared to do so forever.

Furthermore, he should certainly do this in every season <note>the four *Tekufot* of the year</note>, ensuring he does not push himself too far and come to illness, danger, or the neglect of Torah study. However, every single day of his life, he should be in a state of repentance with a broken heart. Even if he is not afflicting himself harshly with fasts, nevertheless, with a broken heart—for this regret is what ascends on high. He must be extremely careful and take extra guard regarding the "Sanctity of the Covenant" <note>sexual purity</note>, so that he does not come to lustful thoughts and never places his hand below his navel. Every day he should weep, worry, and groan, saying the statement enclosed in Tractate Berakhot, page 10: "Rabbi Yohanan said in the name of Rabbi Yossi: 'One internal pang of regret in a person's heart is better than many lashes...'" and Resh Lakish says "better than a hundred lashes." This matter will be discussed at length in the Order of Repentance later, God willing; there you will find it, along with the order of prayer and supplications. I have come now only to record the chapter headings.

**Furthermore,** one needs to be mindful of the seventeenth chapter of the "Gate of Holiness" <note>by Rabbi Chaim Vital</note>. There you will find the repairs <term>Tikkunim<gloss>mystical rectifications</gloss></term> to fix this sin, because of which a person is called "evil." One must "turn from evil and do good," grasping onto good traits and the necessary kindness mentioned there. One's hand should not move from them day by day. You will also find there several matters that serve as a guard so that one does not come to an accidental nocturnal emission. All of this must be fulfilled all the days of his life, for these traits are not a physical mortification that would lead to danger or illness; rather, they are upright and good traits. Whereas for mortifications and fasts, it is enough to do them according to the aforementioned order once in every season for the rest of his life. But as for the traits he must grasp, he should not abandon their path; he should be strong and courageous, never turning from them forever. Then it will be well for him always, and he is assured that he will return as a "Son of the World to Come," on the condition that he increases his diligence in Torah, commandments, acts of loving-kindness, charity, and prayers with intention. His heart should always be broken within him, and he should pray: "Create in me a pure heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me." This whole matter will come, God willing, later at length in the place I have designated for the Order of Repentance.

**I shall return** to the statement of the Zohar regarding the idea that "repentance does not help." The matter is well known: the emanation of *Binah* <note>Understanding</note>, called the World to Come, is the secret of Repentance. There is the "wine guarded from the touch of a gentile," as I explained at length in the introduction to *Toledot Adam*. The secret of the blemish's "grip" is on the side of the Six Extremities <note>the lower emotional emanations</note>, for the "shells" <note>forces of evil</note> have a grip in their root there. Therefore, one who sins must perform repentance to sanctify himself to bring the root—which is the Mind, the place of the "Arm"—back. Regarding this, we say, "Happy is the departure of the branches back to their root." But repentance itself has a root. I mean to say, the root of the "severing" is in *Binah*, but the root of their root is in *Chokhmah* <note>Wisdom</note>, for "You have made them all with Wisdom."

The sin of wasting seed causes a blemish above in *Chokhmah*, which is the Mind, the place of the "Arm." Regarding this, we say: "Happy is the departure of man in Wisdom," because the measure of his stature comes from this source. Therefore, one who sins there must reach that place with his repairs, for that is the Root of Repentance. It is not enough for him to enter only the Gates of Repentance which are in *Binah*; rather, as I explained above, he must reach the Root of Repentance—that is, to perform a complete repentance with more inwardness, adding repentance upon his repentance, to cleave to the attribute of *Chokhmah*, where the level of exaltedness resides.

**After** I wrote all this, I found similar words in the book *Reshit Chokhmah*, which he brought in the name of the godly Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, and it pleased me very much. Know that the "Gate of Immersion" is a great opening for the cleansing of sin. It is always beneficial to immerse, and to understand the secret of the Mikveh as will be explained later. At the very least, he should not decrease

# Gate of the Letters

**Menstruation** <note>original: "Niddah," the state of ritual impurity resulting from menstruation</note> **is a matter of study.** It is forbidden to inquire after the welfare of a woman in her menstrual state. Rabbi Nehemiah said: even the speech from her mouth is impure. Rabbi Johanan said: a man is forbidden to walk behind a woman in this state or to tread upon the dust she walked on, for it is as impure as the dust of a corpse. Thus, her dust is impure, and it is forbidden to benefit from the work of her hands. However, if she is his wife, all the tasks a wife performs for her husband, a woman in this state may perform for her husband, except for making the bed, pouring his cup of wine, and washing his face, hands, and feet. This was established because the sages saw that the world could not endure more than this in terms of the lack of domestic service; yet, one who is stringent in these matters guards the sanctity of his soul.

**Every** form of distance must be maintained from her, both during the days of her menstruation and during her "white days" <note>the seven clean days required before ritual immersion</note>, for she remains in her impurity until she immerses in the ritual bath <term>Mikveh<gloss>a pool of natural water used for ritual purification</gloss></term>. This is the opinion of the Tosafot <note>medieval French and German commentators</note> in the first chapter of tractate Shabbat and Ketubot, and so wrote the Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel</note>, Maimonides (Rambam), the Smag <note>Sefer Mitzvot Gadol</note>, and the Rashba <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Aderet</note>. It is also the opinion of Rabbi Abraham ben David (the Ra’avad) and all the Geonim <note>leaders of the Babylonian academies</note>, as well as the *Sefer Ha-Terumah*. In the first chapter of tractate Shabbat, regarding a certain student of the school of Elijah who died young as a sign, the Tosafot wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Tam that they used to be accustomed to immersing twice: once after seven days when the bleeding stopped (before the seven clean days), because the prohibition then was only Rabbinic. Therefore, that student was lenient. But nowadays, when we are not accustomed to immersing until after the seven clean days, there is no distinction between the days of menstruation and the days of her purification. Who is he that would dare raise his head against the giants of the world and the early masters of law? Even if the common custom among the masses is different, "one must not follow the majority to do evil." Although the *Magen Avraham* cited the common custom, it is a great prohibition to be lenient in this. Solomon Luria (the Maharshal) wrote in his glosses on the *Tur* in the name of the *He-Chasid* <note>Rabbi Judah the Pious</note>: "Men who eat with their wives during the white days so the household members won't notice are shameful, for they transgress the words of the Sages." The communities accepted this upon themselves, and so it shall be.

->Solomon Luria also wrote in the name of the *He-Chasid*: "I have seen a great foolishness when men cut meat into small pieces and eat from the same bowl—one takes a piece and the other takes a piece. This is a great error, for it is clearly considered eating together."<-

**The Tosafot** in tractate Ketubot (page 61) wrote that she counts for herself. If you ask why women do not recite a blessing over this counting as we do for the Counting of the Omer <note>the 49-day count between Passover and Shavuot</note>, even though the Torah says "she shall count for herself," the answer is that we only bless over things that the court can count consistently every year. With the Omer, one can always count in order. But for this woman, if she sees blood again, her count is ruined and she must start over; therefore, she does not count with a blessing.

<margin>The Tosafot’s reasoning suggests it is inappropriate to bless because of the fear of a "blessing in vain" <note>taking God's name for a purpose that is cancelled</note>. However, she is still obligated to count without a blessing, as the Torah says "she shall count for herself." We cannot say that because she cannot bless, the Torah’s obligation to count is cancelled. Blessings are a Rabbinic institution, while the commandment to count is from the Torah. If the count is ruined, she starts again to fulfill "she shall count for herself" in consecutive days. When the Tosafot say "she should not count," they mean "she should not count with a blessing," for that was their starting point. It is possible there is a scribal error and it should read "she should not bless." I have practiced this all my life and commanded my wife to count in the evening before sunset: "Today is Day 1 of my purification counting," "Today is Day 2 of my purification counting," and so on for all of them.</margin>

**In a place where my royalty is lacking, there is a missing explanation regarding the Omer... so that all of Israel may have the right intention and protect everyone. For the counting of brides, they counted for her from the beginning to count... it was called a lamp... and no blessing is relevant since all of Israel is at the end.**

**It is good** to be careful regarding the impurity of the bed and seat of a woman in her menstrual state even in this time, and not just with one’s own wife, but with any woman in this state. So it is written in the Responsa of Rabbi Menachem Recanati: "It is good to be careful with the impurity of the bed and seat of a menstruant so that the law of purity is not forgotten from Israel." Even though, by Torah law, she makes a bed or seat impure as long as she has not immersed—even after her seven days are over, as it says "she shall be in her impurity" until she immerses in water—nowadays, since this is merely a remnant of the law, once she has washed after her seven days even in drawn water <note>regular tap or bucket water, not a ritual bath</note>, we do not distance ourselves from her seat. Look further into this.

**There is a dispute** whether immersion in its proper time is a commandment <note>original: "Mitzvah"</note> or not. The *Beit Yosef* <note>Rabbi Joseph Karo</note> wrote: "It seems that if her husband is in town, it is a commandment to immerse in its time, for we find that Joshua was punished for preventing Israel from procreation for even one night." If she delays immersing specifically to distress her husband, it is a sin in her hand. The *Zohar* mentions regarding the "Elder" <note>original: "Saba"</note> that a woman who complains against her husband in this world... unless he does not care or pay attention to this judgment.

**Included** in this are those women who make it a condition for their husbands: "If you buy me this jewelry or this garment, I will fulfill my marital duty." This is a great sin, even if said in jest. It is not just about the commandment, but about her being generally disobedient until her will is done; such a person is a deeply sinful soul. This matter is mentioned three times in the Responsa of Solomon Luria.

**Based on the reason** above, when her husband is in town, her immersion is a commandment. I permitted a woman to immerse on Friday night when the fast of the Ninth of Av <term>Tisha B'Av<gloss>a day of mourning where marital relations are usually forbidden</gloss></term> fell on it, since most authorities rule leniently in this case. Although the *Magen Avraham* was stringent, a commandment is different. When I was the head of the academy in the holy community of Frankfurt, I found old customs stating that a woman should immerse on a Friday night that falls on the Ninth of Av. This gave us pleasure.

**Regarding the blessing** of immersion, there is a dispute whether the woman should bless before immersion or after she rises from the water. I have seen pious men and "men of action" <note>those meticulous in ritual</note> who conduct their wives thus: after she immerses her whole body once, she recites the blessing, and after she blesses, she immerses a second time. By doing this, she adds extra sanctity and fulfills both legal opinions.

**It happened** in the case of a woman who was on the sixth day since her period began, but she had not had relations with her husband the night before she saw blood. I permitted her to wear white clothes on Wednesday and begin counting her clean days on Thursday. My reasoning was that even though there is a stringency not to start counting until the sixth day, and we in Rome are stringent even if she didn't have relations before, in practice, I did not want to be stringent. For this stringency would lead to a leniency <note>an unintended negative consequence</note>; if she waited until the sixth day to start counting, her immersion night would fall on the Friday night after the holiday. It is better to set aside the aforementioned stringency to keep the immersion close to the preparation, and immersing on a holiday night is more important than observing that stringency. Especially since the *Beit Yosef* already noted that we are not concerned with the opinion of the *Terumat Ha-Deshen* here. A woman may start on the fifth day, and all the waiting is only if she had relations before she saw blood. If she did not, she only needs to wait four days from the time she had relations. Although we are stringent with stringency upon stringency, in this case, it is better not to be. In the *Shulchan Aruch*, it says that if she transgressed and immersed on the seventh day during the daytime, the immersion is valid. However, the Maharal <note>Rabbi Judah Loew of Prague</note> wrote to be stringent even after the fact, and such is our custom.

**Within** the category of "turning away from evil" regarding the sanctity of the procreative act, it is also necessary to make known another matter mentioned at the beginning of tractate Sotah and brought in the *Tur*. Some people are not careful with this, and of them it is said, "He does not know that it is a sin." It says there: Rabbi Hanina of Sura said, a man should not say to his wife nowadays, "Do not be in seclusion with so-and-so" (Rashi explains: even in private between him and her). For we might hold like Rabbi Jose bar Judah who said that a warning of jealousy can be given by the husband alone, and if she is then secluded, she is forbidden to him. Since we no longer have the "Sotah waters" <note>the biblical ritual of the bitter waters to test a wife's innocence</note> to test her, he would forbid her to himself forever. Because I have heard of some who have done this, I have come as a reminder and a warning.

***

Thus far I have recorded a bit regarding "turning away from evil" in the sanctity of the procreative act; now it is time to speak of "doing good" in this sanctity.

### The Matter of the Union
When the union is performed in holiness and purity, it is exceedingly holy. It awakens holiness above and sanctifies from below. If one sanctifies himself a little below, they sanctify him much from above. Thus one fulfills "You shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy." For every union is a reflection of the union of Adam and Eve, who were made in His image and likeness. We, the House of Israel, are called "Man" <note>original: "Adam"</note> because we are truly Man, as is known. At that hour, what should one’s intention be? As brought in the Midrash earlier in the introduction. When one later engages in procreation in holiness and purity, he increases the "Image" and holiness increases. Regarding this matter, the Seven Blessings <note>recited at a Jewish wedding</note> were established, as explained in the book *Tola'at Ya'akov*.

# Gate of the Letters

**Rather**, we must conclude that to resolve all this, even according to the commentators, we must say that Rava is questioning the phrasing of Rabbi Elazar. Since he used the term "Son of Noah" <term>Ben Noach<gloss>a universal term for non-Jews in Jewish law</gloss></term>, it implies an intent to exclude the Israelite. If, as interpreted, this refers to non-vaginal intercourse or the wasting of seed, the Israelite should also be liable. Surely he is speaking of acts without the intent of procreation. Therefore, Rava asks: how is it possible to hold a Son of Noah liable while an Israelite is not? Rather, the explanation must be that Rabbi Elazar meant a Son of Noah who has relations with another man’s wife is exempt if the act is non-vaginal, whereas an Israelite remains liable. **And now** that you have reached this point, one could say there is no proof from here to permit non-vaginal intercourse at all, based on the discussion in Tractate Yevamot, which states generally that such acts are the sin of Er and Onan <note>referring to the biblical figures in Genesis 38 who were punished for "wasting seed"</note>, making no distinctions. As for the permission mentioned in Tractate Nedarim to "turn the table" <note>a euphemism for changing sexual positions</note>, this refers to vaginal intercourse in the place fit for procreation, but where the position is reversed (the woman on top and the man below). This is the explanation of Rashi, similar to the "reversal of the bed" mentioned in Tractate Berachot in the chapter "The One Who Sees." Alternatively, according to the Ra'avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières</note> in the *Book of Sanctity* (quoted in the *Tur*, Even HaEzer section 25), "turning the table" means the man’s face is toward the woman's neck, yet he still performs vaginal intercourse in the place fit for procreation, similar to the mating of animals. This matter is not entirely simple, as Rabbi Elazar’s words are analyzed deeply to suggest he never meant to permit such things. The truth of the matter is that there is a penalty of death—for both the Son of Noah and the Israelite—for the act of Er and Onan, for which the Torah explicitly mentions death. Rather, the one who heard Rabbi Elazar's words was confused between "exempt" and "liable."

**And if you should ask** why Rava raised this specific difficulty—that the Israelite should also be liable—it is because he lacked the strength to challenge it otherwise. For where do we derive this? Necessarily from Er and Onan, who were considered "Sons of Noah" since the Torah had not yet been given. Therefore, to challenge effectively, he must argue that it is impossible to say the Israelite is exempt while the gentile is liable. For surely, they must be equal in liability. Rabbi Elazar did not need to teach us that such acts are not called "evil," but rather he intended to teach us an exemption. This is the reasoning of the Ra'avad and the *Tur*. Although in section 25 he cited Maimonides' view, at the end of the book he brought the Ra'avad’s view on "turning the table"—that it is not like Maimonides’ interpretation but rather like the manner of animals. Since he brought this as his final conclusion, it seems he holds this view. His reason is: what permission could there possibly be for non-vaginal acts? One should not be lenient, for Rashbatz <note>Rabbi Shimon ben Tzemach Duran</note> wrote that there is no cure for this transgression except through great and awesome repentance. Indeed, an incident occurred here in **Safed** in the year 5308 [1548 CE] involving the great leaders: our teacher Rabbi **[Joseph] Karo** <note>author of the Shulchan Aruch</note>, our teacher Rabbi Isaac Masoud, our teacher Rabbi Abraham Shalom, and my teacher the pious Rabbi Joseph Sagis, and many other rabbis. A woman came and said her husband had relations with her non-vaginally; they issued a decree, excommunicated him, burned his clothes, changed his name, and so on. Later it was discovered she was not an Israelite <note>originally: "not of the seed of Israel"</note>. May it be His will [that we be protected from sin], Amen. This concludes his words.

**Generally**, one must "turn away from evil" regarding the sanctity of the covenant <note>referring to sexual purity and circumcision</note>. It is enough for a man to be purifying himself while his wife is in her state of impurity <term>Niddah<gloss>the ritual status of a menstruating woman</gloss></term>. Our Sages of blessed memory mentioned that the righteous, etc., who distance themselves from transgression. Let the heads of wisdom fear the Lord and be careful in all that is written in the Talmud and the legal Codes, more so than the people of our generation. I have come to record several essential matters and new insights:

**It was written** in *Terumat HaDeshen* (section 246) and brought in the *Tur* (Yoreh Deah section 190): It appears that if a woman felt her "source" <note>the womb</note> open to emit blood, but she checked afterward and found nothing, she must be considered impure. For certainly a drop of blood as small as a mustard seed emerged, and her check is not valid because the feeling she experienced is a biblical indicator. This applies even if she attributed the feeling to something else, as proven in the chapter "The One Who Sees" regarding stains. If she felt it in her thigh, she is exempt from a sacrifice, which implies that a direct sensation is of biblical weight since it would otherwise require a sacrifice. And since this is a biblical concept, even if she is "clean" upon checking, she is "impure," as stated in the chapter "All the Hand." In the *Beit Yosef* (section 188), he agreed that if she felt the opening, even if it was "thick and close," it is valid. He did not follow the *Terumat HaDeshen* who was inclined to be even more stringent. But if she felt it and found nothing, she is clearly impure. This must be made known to women because it is a biblical law.

**Immediately**, every woman who does not have a fixed cycle must separate from her husband on the corresponding nights. This means 30 days from her last period, which is the "average interval." Also, the "day of the month"—if she saw blood on the 3rd or 4th of the month, she must separate on the 3rd or 4th of the following month. Also, the "interval cycle"—if 40 days passed between her last two sightings, she must separate after 40 days. Many details of these laws are explained at length in the *Tur* (section 187) regarding the days of separation. In our many sins, most of the world is not careful and does not pay attention; therefore, I command you and warn you to be experts in these laws, to study and to teach, to keep and to do and to fulfill.

**Regarding colors:** it was explained in section 188 that a white appearance is pure, as is a green appearance, even if it is like the color of grass or gold. Certainly, green like a leek or herbs is pure. However, the Gaon Maharshal <note>Rabbi Solomon Luria</note> wrote that a green color requires further study, for Maharim Mintz wrote in his responsa in the name of the great ones that green is also forbidden. Therefore, one should not be quick to be lenient if it is the color of wax, and especially if it is the color of gold, unless there are three other sides and arguments proving it is not blood.

**And if** she found this green color through a sensation, it seems to me one should be stringent. If she found it without a sensation as a stain on her garment, even then, since she acquired this color without sensation, it is subject to the eye's assessment.

<margin><image-desc>A drawing of a hand with a pointing index finger.</image-desc></margin>
**See** *Shiltei HaGibborim* <note>a commentary on the Rif</note> surrounding the Laws of Niddah (page 5b), who wrote: "They asked the experts who are skilled in checking stains, and they found that the appearance of the check was not of the forbidden stains; upon this one may certainly rely to permit it." And there on page 7a, he wrote some of their signs: if one rubs the stain and it disappears, this is a sign of purity. Also, when there is no white circle around it as there is in forbidden stains. Furthermore, I heard that if a round stain is found, even if its color is not "treif" <note>ritually unfit/impure</note>, if a red-like thread surrounds it, it is rendered impure.

It is permitted to see the [menstrual] blood of one's wife, as per the chapter "All the Hand."

**How many** "distancings" were mentioned in the Talmud and the Codes regarding one's wife while she is a Niddah? He shall not touch her even with his small finger, and he shall not pass anything from his hand to hers, etc. These are the words of the Maharshal in his explanation of the *Smag*: the Tosafot wrote that even bringing a dish before him on the table is forbidden. Because of this, Maharash said he would bring the bowl to the table [but not directly to him]. If she makes a recognizable sign, such as placing it on the table with her left hand, we can permit it as we do with the pouring of the cup.

**And regarding** the prohibition of her pouring him a cup of wine: the Rashba wrote this specifically for wine, which leads to intimacy. Just as she is forbidden to pour for him, he is forbidden to pour for her. Not only that, but he may not even send her a cup of wine if it is designated specifically for her, so as not to direct his mind toward her. But when his wife drinks with the members of his household from a "cup of blessing," it is implied from the words of the Rashba that it is permitted. See the *Beit Yosef*.

<margin>\* My thought: The acronym of Niddah [N-D-H]: In the book *Menorat HaMaor* (Lamp of Light), it is written: In ancient days, those in a state of separation were distanced from people, for their name has always been "Niddot" [separated ones], so that they would not be called to any man nor speak with him.</margin>
**It was written** in *Reshit Chochma* <note>"The Beginning of Wisdom" by Eliyahu de Vidas</note> in the "Gate of Sanctity": A man must minimize speech with a woman as much as possible, and specifically with his wife when she is a Niddah. He supported this with the verse "I was dumb with silence" (Psalms 39:3). Furthermore, her gaze breeds disgrace and leaves a bad impression, as explained by the philosophers. Women used to sit in a room or a tent where no man would enter. Therefore, Rachel was forbidden to Laban... it was appropriate for her to hide because of her father... but your wife, no man shall eat or come near you. It was a wonder to walk in the tent so as not to tread on the dust of her feet... they would not speak with them at all because even their speech is impure. Because desires increased and knowledge decreased, and the nations were so steeped in this impurity that they forgot this evil, our holy Torah came to sanctify Israel and separate them from the nations, to guard them from this great damage so they may dwell in sanctity. Therefore, the Torah commanded the guarding of the days of Niddah and the days of a *Zavah* <note>a woman with an irregular discharge</note>, which are even stricter than the days of Niddah, requiring seven clean days and immersion afterward, as explained in the laws. This was His kindness, to be the healer of Israel, arranging this in His wisdom according to the needs known to Him. # Gate of the Letters

The holy ones hint at the divine Name <note>Y-H-V-H, the Tetragrammaton</note> through the letters *Yod* and *Vav*. These are the words of the *Chayit* <note>likely referring to a Kabbalistic work like *Sefer HaKanah*</note> in the section on the arrangement of names: The variations of the marriage betrothal, the sanctification (*Kiddushin*), and the seven blessings we perform during our pairing are a hint to this. Since the scripture states, "You are children to the Lord your God," it is fitting that our "fruit" <note>offspring</note> should be produced through the holiness of a union that mirrors the supernal union above. In that divine union, three things are joined: Blessing, Holiness, and Union. **Holiness** stems from the side of *Chokhmah* <term>Wisdom<gloss>the first conscious spark of intellect in the Sefirotic tree</gloss></term>, as it is said, "Israel is holy to the Lord, the first of His harvest." **Blessing** stems from the side of *Binah* <term>Understanding<gloss>the divine womb or palace that develops the spark of Wisdom</gloss></term>, as it is said, "to rest a blessing within your house"—and *Binah* is called "House." **Union** stems from the side of *Tiferet* <term>Beauty<gloss>the central balance of the divine emotions, associated with the male principle/Israel</gloss></term>, as it is said, "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land." Therefore, it is fitting that our union be through sanctification, blessings, and unity. Then, His holy Name dwells within this pairing.

This is why the ring with which we sanctify the bride is round, modeled after the shape of the letter *Yod* in the Name. The *Yod* represents the "blocked thought" which contains the power of holiness. It is also called the Holy Spirit and is associated with *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), which is called "Holy." Indeed, the term "Holy" (*Kodesh*) implies "Separation," as it is said, "You shall be holy," meaning you shall be separate. *Chokhmah* is the first *Sefirah* <term>Divine Emanation<gloss>one of the ten attributes through which God interacts with the world</gloss></term> that was "separated" from the ring <note>the Infinite</note>, as it is the "first of His harvest." Thus, the language of "Sanctification" (*Kiddushin*) denotes highness. Since it is the beginning of holiness, it is fitting to sanctify this union with something that resembles it: the hand, for the ring represents its height. Since this union is for the purpose of harvest and holy fruit, the two *Hehs* in the Name of *Havayah* <note>Y-H-V-H</note> are the two witnesses before whom he sanctifies her. The *Vav* represents the finger of the bride who receives the sanctification; the groom places the ring on her finger, and the ring then becomes like a crown on her finger. This hints at the letter *Lamed*, for when the *Yod* is placed upon the *Vav*, it forms a *Lamed* like this: [ל]. Because of this, she is worthy to receive seven blessings, and is then called "A Woman of Valor, the crown of her husband." For the husband is the *Vav* of *Tiferet*, and the *Yod*—which is the tenth—becomes the "crown" or "Beauty" of her husband.

Come and see in the *Tikkunei Zohar*: When the "husks" <term>Klippot<gloss>forces of impurity or shells that hide divine light</gloss></term>—which are "images"—need to be broken, the *Sheva* vowel point is called "broken." But her union is in the *Shuruk* point, which is the "Foundation of the Life of Worlds." These are the eighteen blessings of the prayer <note>the Amidah</note> which are said in union. Therefore, Israel must pray the prayer in silence. The secret of this is: "Bring it to her in silence." Just as in the standing prayer for Israel, there is no "help" beside it, the eighteen blessings are said in silence to draw down blessings for her. It is said of the "Living Creatures" <note>angels</note> that when they stand, "they let down their wings," meaning their voice should not be heard, as a way of guarding her: "and her voice was not heard." In silence, Israel must unite with their spouse: in silence, in awe, in fear, and in hiddenness. As the early sages established regarding the phrase "as if coerced by a demon," the proof is the word *Shaddai* <note>a divine name</note>. At that time, one is removed from the "Gate of Hurmuza." It is said, "And you shall write them on the doorposts (*Mezuzot*) of your house"—*Mezuzot* can be read as *Zaz Mavet* <note>"death moves away"</note>. If a voice is heard, immediately "sin crouches at the door." The early sages established: "Anyone who raises his voice in prayer is among those of small faith." At the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, unites with His *Shekhinah* <term>Divine Presence<gloss>the feminine aspect of God that dwells among the people</gloss></term>, all the "Living Creatures" receive blessings from one another, all in holiness. Therefore, the Sages established sanctifications and blessings for the bride, to receive holiness and the union of the Holy One, blessed be He. Thus, the unions of Israel must not be with a voice or in a state of obligation. In this way, all their "doorposts" are blessing and holiness. There is no holiness with fewer than ten, which is the letter *Yod*, and because the ring is a *Yod*, 

<margin>
(6)
In this
way,
the day
</margin>

the bride is sanctified through it. It must be placed on her finger to form a *Lamed*. At that time, she must be blessed with seven blessings, which the bride inherits. At that moment of union, "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth." What are the "kisses"? They are the four lips—his two and her two—representing the four "wings" of the Living Creatures, of whom it is said, "every one had four wings." When his two "faces" and her two "wings" are included, it is said of them, "every one had four wings," and "each had four faces." These are the six faces [of the *Sefirot*] and the four wings. The name *Adonai* joined with *Y-H-V-H* <note>spelled Y-A-H-D-V-N-H-Y</note> creates the name *Chashmal* <term>Electrum<gloss>the "speaking-fire" angels seen in Ezekiel's vision</gloss></term>. The word *Chashmal* [at times] stays silent and [at times] speaks. Regarding their construction, it is said: "Greater is the one who answers 'Amen' than the one who blesses," because the groom and bride are joined as eight letters as one. The "wings of the commandment" <note>the Tzitzit fringes</note> teach this secret: they are eight threads for each corner, corresponding to the four faces and four wings of each "Living Creature." This is the numerical value of the "Youth Enoch" <note>Metatron</note>. He is the Prince of the World. From him, the masters of the Mishnah taught that anyone who "flies" <note>is proficient</note> should not have fewer than six. Therefore, one who lends should not add more than ten, which are the six called "wings" at the beginning, hinting at the six names *A-B-G-Y-T-Z*, etc. Concerning them, it is said: "Seraphim stood above him; each had six wings." The bride flies higher and higher, and these are the forty-two letters <note>a mystical divine name</note> which are like the *Tefillin* <term>Phylacteries<gloss>ritual leather boxes containing Torah scrolls</gloss></term> of the arm and the *Tefillin* of the head. Of them, it is said: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you." These are the ornaments of the bride: the *Tefillin* are a golden crown on the head of the bride. The *Tefillin* of the hand are the ring of the arm. Once the bride is adorned in her jewelry, one must call to her groom, as it says: "Hear, O Israel." They are under the wedding canopy, where the holy people must stand before them with the groom to bless them with holy life. They "let down their wings." The *Tzitzit* also represent this union, and the *Tefillin* represent the Holy One, blessed be He, descending upon His throne. We call to the Holy One, blessed be He, who seals twelve wings. One must stand before Him in the standing prayer and bless them with seven blessings and sanctifications, which is holiness, etc. Until here are his words. The matter of the number eighteen (*Chai*) is that it consists of two orders: the first *Chet-Aleph* <note>spelling "witness"</note> testifies to the *Dalet*, and the last *Heh-Aleph* testifies to the *Vav*. Your sign is "the hand of the witnesses." The whole *Yod* is the four fingers. For those who do not understand the intention: the ring is the *Yod*. The groom extends his hand to give, and the bride extends her hand to receive—these are the two *Hehs*, as every hand has five fingers. Afterward, she extends the index finger [to receive] the coin <note>or ring</note>, which is the *Vav*. In this, the Name is completed.

***

**The Tur** wrote in *Even HaEzer*, section 62, in the name of the *Halakhot Gedolot* <term>HaG<gloss>a prominent 8th-century legal code</gloss></term>: One who marries a virgin and has relations with her should recite the blessing, "Blessed are You... who placed a nut in the Garden of Eden," etc. See there. The **Rosh** wrote in the first chapter of Tractate *Ketubot* that it is logical to bless her after he has found her virginity. So too wrote the author of the **Shulchan Arukh** and the **Remah**: that one should not bless her without a cup of wine. This is also the opinion of Rabbenu Yerucham in the book *Adam and Eve*, path 28. I am amazed that people are not careful with this blessing; surely this [omission] is a custom of ignorance and unlearnedness. For who are we to question the Geonim <note>the leaders of the Babylonian academies</note>, especially the author of the *Halakhot Gedolot*, all of whose words are tradition? Even for one who wishes to be concerned because the blessing is not mentioned in the Talmud, who gave permission to cancel it entirely? One should say it without the mention of the Name and Kingship <note>referring to the standard formula "Lord our God, King of the Universe"</note>. Regarding the rabbinic orders and the blessing "Who creates many souls," the Jerusalem Talmud seals it with a blessing. Since it is not mentioned in our [Babylonian] Talmud, we do not seal it with the Name, but we do seal it with the "Rabbinic Thanks" formula: "Blessed be the God, the Living," etc. So too here, "Blessed be the Life of the Worlds." Therefore, all God-fearing men should see to it that their sons recite this blessing after finding the blood of virginity. He should wash his hands, take a cup in his hand, and recite the blessing over wine, and then recite this blessing without the Name and Kingship, and give the bride to drink as well.

These are the words of the **Tola'at Ya'akov** <note>a commentary on the prayer service by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> regarding the secret of the virginity blessing: I have seen fit to recite this blessing even if it was not mentioned in the Mishnah or Talmud because of its high standing. The Geonim established it regarding the supernal "Nut." "Blessed are You... who placed a nut in the Garden of Eden"—the intention refers to the lower creation which was created in the likeness of the upper creation. The "Garden" refers to Adam and Eve being planted there, as it says: "the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, to be glorified." This hints at the supernal Adam and Eve (Wisdom and Understanding), who were "in the horns of grasshoppers" in the depths of Being until the Holy One, blessed be He, planted them and they became great cedars. This is the secret of the "cedars of Lebanon which He planted." He compared the bride to a "Nut" (*Egoz*) because she is closed up, and the "Seal of Truth" seals her. From the supernal Bride, this name was derived, and of her, the King to whom peace belongs said: "I went down into the garden of nuts." This is the garden of which it is said: "A garden locked is my sister, my bride." The secret is that just as a nut has several shells (*Klippot*) and the "brain" <note>the meat of the nut</note> is inside, so too it is written: "This is Jerusalem; I have set her in the midst of the nations, with countries all around her." Especially the "shell of shells" is like the Supernal Chariot; they surround on this side and separate on that side, just as the luminaries are in perfect union but separate each to its own task. As it is written: "And from there it parted and became four heads." Because this nut is planted in the garden, it is called the "Garden of Nuts" after its name. The Supernal Chariot is compared to a nut because the power of the nut is blocked on all its sides; so too the Supernal Chariot is blocked and hidden from all. The "Rose of the Valleys" is a name for the bride who is perfect in all beauty. As she says of herself: "I am the lily of the Sharon, the rose of the valleys." The "lily" (*Chavatzelet*) is called *Chabak*, and it is green <note>associated with the planet Venus or the attribute of Esther</note>. She was "the Sharon" who sang before King Solomon. Another explanation: "I am the lily of the Sharon" means she stands to receive living waters from the Lebanon, as it is written: "And the Sharon shall be a fold of flocks." She has six petals, corresponding to the bride who is composed of six "extremities" <note>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>. In the supernal depth, she was called "Rose." Just as a rose is varied in its colors—white and red—and turns from one to the other, so she varies in her attributes, sometimes Judgment (*Din*) and sometimes Mercy (*Rachamim*). Know that the reason she is first called "Lily" and then "Rose" has a secret: before her union with the King, she is called "Lily" and is thus green; afterward, a "thread of kindness" is drawn over her when she dwells with the King, and she is called "Rose," in the secret of "His lips are roses." No [foreign] hand shall rule over her. She is entirely hidden and guarded from all impurity, a place for the Sanctuary to enter, for "A garden locked is my sister, my bride, a spring sealed." In the place where they are drawn to enter, she is the "hind of loves" and the "hind of the dawn," a "graceful doe" who guards herself in purity. The law shall not be broken to go to another field, but "your eyes shall be on the field" of apples with the union of youth. When the virgin is in this path, she is in the likeness of the daughter of Israel, like the chosen land.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of marriage. While the previous page focused on the symbolism of the wedding ring and the three pillars of union (Holiness, Blessing, and Unity), this page delves into the cosmic necessity of procreation and the deep symbolic meaning behind the Seven Wedding Blessings (*Sheva Brachot*).</meta>

# The Order of the Wedding Blessings

->The following are words based on the holy *Zohar* <note>The primary work of Jewish mysticism, or Kabbalah</note>:<-

I shall first write the reason for the commandment to "be fruitful and multiply" <note>Hebrew: *pru u'rvu*</note>. It is taught in the Talmud <note>Tractate Yebamot, chapter "He who brings [his brother's widow]"</note>: Rabbi Eliezer says, "Anyone who does not engage in procreation is as if he sheds blood, for it is said, 'Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed' <note>Genesis 9:6</note>, and immediately afterward it says, 'And you, be fruitful and multiply' <note>Genesis 9:7</note>." Rabbi Akiva says, "It is as if he diminishes the Divine Image, as it says, 'For in the image of God He made man' <note>Genesis 9:6</note>, followed by 'And you, be fruitful and multiply.'" Ben Azzai says, "It is as if he both sheds blood and diminishes the Image." 

We have already written concerning the structure of man and how the Holy One, blessed be He, established him as a "supernal model" <note>A physical reflection of the divine structure above</note> so that the Name may bestow a soul upon him to guide him on a straight path, to know and recognize his Creator and the purpose of his coming into this world. This purpose is to spread true existence to no end, above and below without interruption. In our many sins, as generations pass, one must strive to multiply these divine models in the world to show that His presence is never-ending. When a person walks on the straight path, the "Attribute" <note>The divine emanation of *Yesod*, or Foundation</note> is comprised of the Righteous One above and the righteous one below. New souls are renewed and brought down, as we interpret: "The river that never ceases approaches her," and existence spreads into the Infinite (*Ein Sof*). 

This is impossible without a wife, for "male and female He created them." Therefore, they said in the Talmud: Rabbi Eliezer said, "Any man who has no wife is not a 'man,' for it says, 'Male and female He created them... and He called their name Man (Adam).'" A man must mirror the supernal creation—the "two faces" <term>Du-partzufin<gloss>The mystical concept that the male and female divine principles were originally joined back-to-back</gloss></term> within the divine beauty <term>Tiferet<gloss>The central Sefirah, representing the male principle or the 'Holy One, blessed be He'</gloss></term>—in order to "dwell in the house." Only then is he called a complete "Man," and only then does the blessing dwell in a place of peace. Through the union below, the union above is awakened, and everything is blessed from the Source. This gives him "power to perform deeds of strength" <note>Deuteronomy 8:18</note> and to give birth anew to his "fruits." These are placed in the treasury of the Kingdom <term>Malchut<gloss>The final Sefirah, representing the female principle or the Divine Presence (Shekhinah)</gloss></term>, and from there, they emerge into the world. 

Thus, one who engages in procreation causes the holy existence to spread infinitely and merits a "limitless inheritance." But one who is negligent in this diminishes the Divine Image, preventing its expansion. Because of this, the "river that flows from Eden" <note>Genesis 2:10, representing the flow of divine light</note> ceases to water the "Garden" <note>The Shekhinah</note> to grow its fruits. The "Land of the Living" <note>The spiritual realm</note> is left parched, for the "Comforter who restores the soul" has distanced himself from her. Sins live on, and Judgment is awakened. Such a person is considered a murderer, a shedder of blood, and is treated "measure for measure"—for he will be cut off and his seed destroyed from the World to Come. He has left no root to save his soul or to see the "light of life." He will be uprooted and his Torah and deeds destroyed. As it is written, "He shall see his seed and prolong his days" <note>Isaiah 53:10</note> in a world that is eternally long. Then the "will of the Lord" <note>The Torah</note> in his hand shall prosper. 

From the positive, you can infer the negative. We learn in the Talmud: Rabbi Tanhum said, "Any man who has no wife dwells without blessing, without good, without joy, and without atonement." In the West <note>The Land of Israel</note> they say: "Without Torah and without a wall." Rava bar Rav Shila said, "Even without peace, as it is written: 'And you shall know that your tent is in peace' <note>Job 5:24</note>." 

Behold, Truth has informed us that the wife is the cause of all these benefits, for through Eve comes man's completion, modeled after the secret of the "Image and Likeness" above. The desire of the supernal beings is to pour blessing into the "House," and through her, King Solomon <note>Representing the divine Male principle</note> is blessed. This is why it says of her, "My sister, my bride" <note>Song of Songs 4:9</note>. Our sages said in the *Midrash Chazit*: "My bride [is] my provider." When the King is distanced from the Queen due to a lack of awakening from below, the King is not "complete," for he is only "half a man." There is no "Good" except through completion. There is no "Blessing" because blessing is withheld from a man who has no vessel for it to rest upon. Joy is withheld because there is no Torah—for the "known woman" <note>The Shekhinah</note> is called Torah, as it is said, "See wisdom with the woman." She is also the "Wall," for "a female shall encompass a man" <note>Jeremiah 31:22</note>; she sits like a guard to ensure no "stranger" <note>impure forces</note> approaches the holy place. For one who has no wife, the fence is breached, and anger enters to search the King's treasuries. There is no "Peace" because peace is removed from the earth and a time of war comes upon it. 

One who understands all this will recognize the matter of marriage in its true depth and will strive to marry a wife "for the sake of Heaven" <note>With holy intention</note>, not looking only at external choices. When a man sanctifies himself with his wife with this intention, he gives the supernal forces a place to act in holiness and purity. A soul will come to him from a holy place. If he is a wise student, he will bring a "branch from the root" like himself. 

We have already written above that a virgin is married on the fourth day <note>Wednesday</note>. The reason given is "lest he have a claim regarding her virginity and rise early to the court." But in the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>The Zohar</note>, they asked: Why the fourth day? On the fourth day the moon was diminished <note>According to the creation story</note>; it was not fitting for the completion of a virgin bride! They answered: The marriage of a virgin was established on the fourth day to show the endurance and excellence of the "Virgin of Israel" <note>The Shekhinah</note>. Even if she was diminished on that day, she finds "satisfaction" through the earthly marriage, and she merits to say: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; though I have fallen, I shall arise" <note>Micah 7:8</note>. 

For this reason, a virgin is married on the fourth day. One must prepare a wedding canopy (*Chuppah*) with precious vessels to honor the Bride mentioned in the Song of Songs, who is invited to the joy of the bride below who mirrors her. The canopy is a model of the Supernal Canopy in which the Bride dwells, filled with beauty of many precious colors. Both the supernal and earthly Bride stand in one likeness. Just as she is blessed with **Seven Blessings**—the secret of the "seven rivers" that pour "good oil" upon her—so too is the earthly bride blessed with seven blessings mirroring the seven supernal ones.

<margin>
First
Blessing:
Creator of the
fruit of
the vine.
</margin>

**The First Blessing:** "Who creates the fruit of the vine." This is the secret of the wine that "gladdens God and men" <note>Judges 9:13</note>. It is the awakening of joy that comes to him from the side of Strength <term>Gevurah<gloss>The Sefirah of judgment and power, often associated with red wine</gloss></term>. That wine produces fruit, and the Tree of Life produces fruit through this testimony. She receives everything and "enriches the harvest" as if planting fruits.

**The Second Blessing:** "Who created all for His glory." This is the secret of the Pillar upon which the world stands <note>Yesod</note>. It is called "All" <note>*Kol*</note> because it includes everything. This is the secret of the "Friends," for the secret of union is suspended upon it. It receives the "oil" coming from above to produce fruit in that "Vine." You already know that the "good oil" descends from the brain through the spinal cord to the organ of union, and from there in the path of "seven." This is the awakening of the Right side <term>Chesed<gloss>The Sefirah of Lovingkindness</gloss></term>. 

The fruit only comes from the Left side awakening the water, which awakens the Right. "Joy" <note>Hebrew: *Simcha*</note> has the numerical value of 102, which includes the Right and Left in one another. This is the secret of Man in his perfection. Therefore:

**The Third Blessing:** "The Creator of Man." This is the "man dwelling in tents," the one who balances the first, the middle bolt within the boards, reaching from end to end <note>Exodus 26:26, referring to *Tiferet*</note>. This is the "Great Man" mentioned in Ezekiel.

**The Fourth Blessing:** "Who formed man in His image." This is the secret of the Right Pillar. The Right prepared the foundation <note>or "the understanding"</note> that comes from the "Victory" <term>Netzach<gloss>The Sefirah of Endurance/Victory</gloss></term> of the Moon and sends it to the lower land. "The face of Joshua is like the face of the Moon" <note>A Talmudic metaphor for a secondary but great light</note>.

**The Fifth Blessing:** "May the barren one surely rejoice and be glad." This is the "Barren one of the house," who is anxious to gather her children from the four corners of the earth. This is the secret of the eighth pillar, "Boaz," who possesses "strength and power" <term>Gevurah<gloss>Severity/Strength</gloss></term>, and joins with the Right Pillar to prepare for the "children of victory" and to be established "between the knees"— the secret of those "taught by the Lord." The reason they are called "willows" <note>which do not produce fruit</note> is that alone they do not produce fruit, but the "gathering of the children" is their fruit. And there is no one who awakens the gathering of the children to the Mother except the Prophets.

**The Sixth Blessing:** "Gladden the beloved friends." This is the place of the "Curtains," of joy and brotherhood. This is the "Foundation of the world" <term>Yesod<gloss>The Sefirah of Connection and Foundation</gloss></term>. To whom belongs all the "desire of Israel"? To the Foundation (*Yesod*) and the Righteousness (*Malchut*). These are the two "beloved friends"—"this is my beloved and this is my friend"—who are never separated from each other. "Two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies" <note>Song of Songs 4:5</note>.

**The Seventh Blessing:** This is the one that sustains everything. From it, all the "lights" are blessed, and it includes the "Ten Utterances" <note>of Creation</note>. Therefore, there are ten types of joy in this blessing: gladness, joy, groom, bride, love, brotherhood, delight, pleasure, peace, and friendship. 

Until here are the seven supernal blessings that the Supernal Bride inherits. Therefore, their model is given to the earthly bride. One who has relations without these blessings is like one who "enjoys this world without a blessing," which is considered "stealing from his father and mother." This includes one who has relations with an unmarried woman; even if she immerses <note>in a ritual bath</note>, he is "stealing from the Name, blessed be He." We have learned: "A bride without a blessing is forbidden to her husband like a menstruant (*niddah*)." The reason is that just as during her days of impurity the man is not truly "in her house," because the "bed is too short" to receive both the wife and her husband and the "Shepherd" <note>The Divine Presence</note>—so too, if there is no blessing dwelling there, the man is not "complete." They only unite through the blessing. As long as the blessings are not drawn down from above, the bride is forbidden. The "Individual" is called "All" <note>*Kol*</note>, and the bride is the final letter *He* of the Divine Name. When the "Righteous One" (*Zaddik/Yesod*) joins with "Righteousness" (*Tzedek/Malchut*), she is called "Bride" (*Kallah*), and then she is permitted to her husband, for the waters of the supernal blessing have been drawn to her. So too below, a woman is forbidden to her husband without a blessing because she would be in a state of "supernal anger."

The groom and bride must sanctify themselves very, very much when they enter the canopy. First, it is known what our sages said: "The Holy One, blessed be He, forgives their sins." Therefore, they should perform repentance (*Teshuva*) on the day before the canopy. It is the custom of all Israel to fast and awaken themselves greatly in repentance, to search their deeds from the day they were born until this day, to confess (*Viduy*), and to ask for forgiveness, pardon, and atonement from the Name, blessed be He. They should be "those who confess and forsake" <note>Proverbs 28:13</note>, and their repentance should be complete with a broken heart. They should make a strong resolution from this day forward to serve the Lord in truth and simplicity, and to be holy and pure. They should not do as is done in some places, where the groom and bride sit together and play cards and such, and afterward enter the canopy. Rather, they should pray that the Holy One, blessed be He, will cause His Presence (*Shekhinah*) to dwell between them, as our sages said: "A man and a woman—if they merit, the Presence is between them."

When the groom comes to sanctify the bride <note>The *Kiddushin* ceremony</note>, he should say: "Behold, I come to fulfill the commandment of sanctification as the Torah commanded, for the sake of the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, through the Hidden and Concealed One." He should think of the verse: "For I am holy, dear to you," for we are permeated with His great Name and the secret of the Holy Ones.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the mystical and physical formation of a child, moving from the philosophical necessity of procreation to the biological and spiritual mechanics of gestation, as understood by the Sages.
