# The Gate of the Letters

The explanation of the phrase "before God was" <note>original: "קדם שיהיה אלוה"</note> is a prayer: May He protect me and let me live through days that contain unities and not dualities. These are the "unique ones of their generation" <note>Referencing the righteous or perhaps the unified state of the soul before birth</note>. They teach the child the entire Torah [in the womb], as it is said: "And he taught me and said to me, let your heart hold fast my words; keep my commandments and live" (Proverbs 4:4). And it says, "When the secret of God was upon my tent" (Job 29:4). Why does it say "And it says"? Lest you say it was only a prophet who said this, come and hear: When a child enters the air of the world, an angel comes and strikes them on the mouth, causing them to forget the entire Torah, as it is said: "Sin crouches at the door" (Genesis 4:7). 

The soul does not depart from there until it is made to take an oath, as it is said: "To Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear" (Isaiah 45:23). "Every knee shall bow"—this refers to the day of death, for it says: "Before Him shall bow all those who go down to the dust" (Psalms 22:30). "Every tongue shall swear"—this refers to the day of birth, as it is said: "He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not taken My name in vain and has not sworn deceitfully" (Psalms 24:4). 

What is the oath they administer to the soul? "Be righteous and be not wicked; and even if the whole world says to you, 'You are righteous,' consider yourself in your own eyes as if you were wicked." Know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is pure, and His ministers are pure, and the soul He placed within you is pure. If you keep it in purity, it is well; but if not, I shall take it from you. 

The school of Rabbi Ishmael taught a parable: This is like a priest who entrusted *terumah* <note>The "heave-offering" or holy tithe given to priests, which must be kept in a state of ritual purity</note> to a commoner and said to him: "If you keep it in purity, it is well; if not, I shall burn it before you."

Rabbi Elazar said: What is the scriptural source? From the "hearing of the ear" <note>original: "ממשמע אוזן"</note>. How do we know that the word *navvi* <note>referring to a certain growth or hair</note> is a term for "beginning"? As it is written: "Shear your hair [nezerekh] and cast it away" (Jeremiah 7:29). 

Rabbi Elazar also asked: To what is a fetus in its mother's womb comparable? To a nut placed in a bowl of water; if a person puts a finger on it, it sinks here and there. So it is with a fetus: 
In the **first three months**, the fetus dwells in the lower chamber. 
In the **middle months**, the fetus dwells in the middle chamber. 
In the **final months**, the fetus dwells in the upper chamber. 
When its time to emerge arrives, it turns over and exits, and these are the "birth pangs of a woman." We have learned in a Mishnah that the birth pangs for a female child are more numerous than for a male. 

Rabbi Elazar said: What is the verse? "I was made in secret, embroidered in the lowest parts of the earth" (Psalms 139:15). If it only said "embroidered," how would we differentiate the pains of a female from a male? Rabbi Elazar also said: What is the verse? "I was made in secret," and "He who turns the face," and this is certainly the turning of the face, God forbid.

During the **first three months**, physical relations are difficult for the woman and difficult for the fetus. 
During the **middle months**, they are difficult for the woman but good for the fetus. 
During the **final months**, they are good for the woman and good for the fetus, for because of this, the fetus emerges "whitened and quickened" <note>original: "מלובן ומזורז", meaning refined and physically ready</note>. 

It was taught: One who has relations on the eightieth day <note>This likely refers to the calculation of the 40-day formation periods</note> produces a male. How would he know? Rather, Abaye said: He continues to have relations and "The Lord guards the simple" (Psalms 116:6). 

Rabban Simeon ben Gamliel says: The **male** provides the "white" seed, from which are formed the bones, the sinews, the nails, the brain in the head, and the white of the eye. The **woman** provides the "red" seed, from which are formed the skin, the flesh, the hair, and the black of the eye. And the **Holy One, blessed be He**, places within it the spirit, the soul, the features of the face, the sight of the eye, the hearing of the ear, the speech of the mouth, the movement of the legs, understanding, and wisdom. When the time comes for the person to depart from the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, takes His portion and leaves the portion of the father and mother before them. Rabbi Pappa said: This is what people mean when they say, "Shake off the salt and throw the meat to the dog" <note>A metaphor: once the soul (the "salt" that preserves the body) is gone, the flesh is merely biological matter</note>.

Rami bar Pappa taught: What is written? "Who does great things past finding out, and wonders without number" (Job 9:10). Come and see that the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like the attribute of flesh and blood. A human puts a precious object in a bound pouch with the opening facing upward; it is uncertain if it will be preserved or not. But the Holy One, blessed be He, forms the embryo in the womb of a woman which is open and facing downward, yet it is preserved! 

Another matter: A person puts materials into a furnace; at the time the crucible goes down, it descends. But with the Holy One, blessed be He, as long as the embryo grows, it ascends. 

Rabbi Yose the Galilean taught: What is written? "I will praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made; marvelous are Your works" (Psalms 139:14). Come and see that the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like the attribute of flesh and blood. A person puts different seeds in a garden bed; each one grows according to its kind. But the Holy One, blessed be He, forms the embryo in the womb of a woman, and all the diverse elements grow into a single kind [a human]. 

Another matter: A dyer puts various pigments into a vat, and they all come out as one color. But the Holy One, blessed be He, forms the embryo in the womb of a woman, and every appearance within it comes out according to its specific nature <note>e.g., eyes as eyes, skin as skin</note>.

Rabbi Joseph taught: What is written? "I will praise You, O Lord; though You were angry with me, Your anger is turned away, and You comfort me" (Isaiah 12:1). To what does the verse refer? To two people who went out to conduct business. A thorn got stuck in the foot of one of them [preventing him from traveling]. He began to blaspheme and curse his luck. After some days, he heard that his friend's ship had sunk at sea. He then began to thank and praise God. Therefore, it says, "Your anger is turned away, and You comfort me." 

And this is what Rabbi Eliezer said: What is written? "Who alone does great wonders, and blessed be His glorious name forever" (Psalms 72:18-19). Even the one for whom a miracle is performed does not recognize his own miracle.

Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa taught: What is the meaning of "You winnow my path and my lying down" (Psalms 139:3)? This teaches that a person is not created from the entire drop of seed, but only from the clearest part of it. The school of Rabbi Ishmael taught: It is like a person winnowing on the threshing floor; he takes the food and leaves the waste.

[...] It is written: "Who has counted the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel?" (Numbers 23:10). This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and counts the "quadrants" <note>referring to acts of procreation</note> of Israel: "When will the drop come from which a righteous person shall be formed?" On account of this matter, the eye of the wicked Balaam was blinded. He said: "Should He who is pure and holy, and whose ministers are pure and holy, look upon such a thing?" Immediately, his eye was blinded, as it is written: "The speech of the man whose eye is shut" (Numbers 24:3). 

And this is what Rabbi Yohanan said: What is written? "And he lay with her that night" (Genesis 30:16). This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, assisted in that act, as it says, "Issachar is a strong-boned donkey" <note>A play on words in Hebrew between *hamor* (donkey) and *hamar* (the act/matter), suggesting divine providence in the conception of Issachar</note>. 

Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Ami: If the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male. If the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female, as it is said: "If a woman bears seed and gives birth to a male" (Leviticus 12:2). 

The Sages taught: At first, they would say: If the woman emits seed first, she bears a male; if the man emits seed first, she bears a female. But the Sages did not explain the matter until Rabbi Zadok came and explained it from the verse: "These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, with his daughter Dinah" (Genesis 46:15). The verse attributes the males to the females and the females to the males <note>To emphasize the biological timing mentioned above</note>.

And there will be people in the world who are "mighty men of valor, trained for war" (Song of Songs 3:8), having many sons and grandsons. A person's desire is to increase children; but because they delay themselves in the womb so that they may emerge as male children, the Scripture considers it as if they are increasing sons and grandsons. This is why Rav Kattina said: "I could make all my children male." Rava said: "He who wants all his children to be male should engage in a second act of relations [immediately]." 

Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Rabbi Ami: A woman only conceives close to her menstrual period, as it is said: "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity" (Psalms 51:7). But Rabbi Yohanan said: Close to her immersion [in the Mikvah], as it says, "And in sin did my mother conceive me." How do we know that "sin" [*het*] is a term for purity? As it is written: "And he shall purify [*ve-hitte*] the house" (Leviticus 14:52), which the Targum translates as "and he shall cleanse the house." If you wish, I can say from here: "Purify me [*tehatte’eni*] with hyssop, and I shall be clean" (Psalms 51:9). 

Thus ends the words of the Gemara. Even if one's wife is already pregnant or elderly, he should pray in his heart for a holy soul, and that this child be one into whom that soul is flowed. Know that people exist in all levels of virtue.

## ->And this is the prayer of the Divine Kabbalist, the Ramban <note>Nachmanides, 13th-century sage</note>, of blessed memory, for the Night of Union.<-

May it be Your will, Rock of all worlds, Righteous One of all generations, for the sake of Your great Name that emerges from the verse "The Lord has remembered us, He will bless" <note>Psalms 115:12</note>, that You shall fill me with holy seed, desired and worthy, good and beautiful, prepared and accepted, fit to exist and endure without sin or guilt. 

Bless me with Your Name and bless my house with Your glory, and let me know that my tent is at peace. Draw forth the flow of his seed and all the springs of the source of Israel. Purify my body and sanctify my soul, my thoughts, my intellect, my knowledge, and the rest of my senses. 

May I be strengthened and emboldened, and clothed in Your good, pure, and generous spirit through the intent of my supplication, so that I may fulfill Your will. May You perfect my seed; may it be built, exist, be formed, and be made in truth and uprightness. May it be drawn and poured and stand in the place of its success. Establish all its benefits to complete it, sustain it, and set it with taste, grace, kindness, strength, health, courage, and might. 

Have mercy upon it in its making, its attachment, its joining, and its clothing [in a body]. Place it upon its healthy foundation in its being, its health, its formation, its making—in its spirit, its breath, and its soul within me and in its limbs. Let there be in it, and in any of its parts, no harm, no deficiency, no affliction, no accident, no illness, no stumbling, no pain, no suffering, no plague, no sickness, no weakness. May it not lack any good all the days of its life. And bless me, my household, and my seed with everything that completes...

# The Gate of the Letters

The holiness of Abraham was to give life to our portion and our inheritance, for those born in his house serve his service and keep his religion and statutes. They do not break the law or transgress the covenant to leave their place of holiness and wander in another field. For "of old your fathers dwelt beyond the river" <note>Joshua 24:2</note>, and "I took your father Abraham from there and led him through all the land of Canaan" <note>Joshua 24:3</note>. I planted him in the holy place and brought him into the secret of faith. Because He loved your fathers, He chose his seed after him to be a "treasured people" <note>Hebrew: *am segula*—a unique, precious nation</note> from among all the nations. Now, open the eyes of your intellect, and you shall know and understand the matters of the *Keresot* and the *Tur* <note>Likely referring to the sections of the Code of Jewish Law</note>, to understand in them what is worthy of intention. Strive to be among those who eat the "pith" and discard the "shell" <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for seeking the spiritual essence rather than the external material husk</note>. With all your gains, acquire understanding. See that everything comes with intention and everything is by the Supreme Will. For the essence is within and the shell surrounds it from the outside. The "sudden ones" <note>Those without spiritual discipline</note> pursue the exterior and waste away in the vanity of their days; they do not merit to sit with the King in His work. This is like the parable of the nut that we already mentioned: the King's friends look into the beauty of the inner fruit, which is their portion, while the shell on the outside is the portion of the children of Edom <note>Symbolizing the material world and the forces of judgment</note> who dwell in Seir. This is what is meant by "And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel" <note>Genesis 36:31</note>, for the shell precedes the fruit. In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring forward the pith without the shell, as it is said: "Israel is holy to the Lord, the first of His harvest" <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>. Even though the fruit comes first, who would dare stretch out his hand to eat of it? "All who eat of it shall be held guilty; evil shall come upon them, says the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>. For in the end of days, the knowledge of the Lord shall increase, and His glory will be revealed to the eyes of all. This is the meaning of "the first of His harvest"—the last letters of the name of the Lord <note>The letters *Heh* and *Vav*</note> shall be at the head just as they were in the days of youth, as it says: "And the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a consuming fire" <note>Exodus 24:17</note>. So too in the future to come, as it is written: "The voice of your watchmen! They lift up their voice, together they sing for joy; for eye to eye they shall see the return of the Lord to Zion" <note>Isaiah 52:8</note>. And it is written: "The Lord has bared His holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God" <note>Isaiah 52:10</note>. These are his words.

## B.A. Said:
"Who formed man in His image, in the image of the likeness of his form, and prepared for him from himself an everlasting edifice" <note>A variation of the traditional wedding blessing</note>. Know, my children, that there is no holiness among all holinesses like the holiness of marital union, if it is done in sanctity and one sanctifies himself during the act as our Sages, of blessed memory, warned. For then he is in the likeness of the Supernal Image and awakens the Supernal Union—the secret of the fruitfulness of the Kingdom <note>Hebrew: *Malchut*—the final Sefirah, representing the feminine divine presence</note>. Man and woman who unite in perfect unity are like the Supernal Covenant, the covenant that awakens the secret of the "Righteous One, the Foundation of the World" <note>Hebrew: *Tzadik Yesod Olam*—the Sefirah of *Yesod*, associated with procreation and the covenant of circumcision</note>. This is the secret of "I will establish My covenant" <note>Genesis 17:7</note>, the secret of the standing of the covenant of circumcision when a man joins with his wife. It is the secret of the preparation of the fine incense, "grind it well, grind it and refine it" <note>referencing the Temple incense</note>. These are deep secrets, explained and revealed to those who know understanding. Also the secret of the embrace is in the secret of "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me" <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>. So too the secret of the supernal kiss; all is explained well in the book *Pardes Rimonim* in the "Gate of Attributes and Conduct," chapters 85, 86, and 89, and in chapter 20. The secret of the supernal union of Beauty <note>*Tiferet*</note> and Kingship <note>*Malchut*</note> is through the Foundation <note>*Yesod*</note>, the covenant of the organ. The two "friends" <note>metaphor for the arms</note> are Kindness <note>*Hesed*</note> and Might <note>*Gevurah*</note>, and the two "thighs" are Victory <note>*Netzach*</note> and Splendor <note>*Hod*</note>. Thus Beauty and Kingship are joined through the six extremities. They are the secret of Man and Woman, and our Sages said: "If a man and woman are worthy, the Divine Presence <note>*Shekhinah*</note> dwells between them" <note>Talmud Sotah 17a</note>. This is represented by the name *Yah* <note>The letters *Yod* and *Heh*—the *Yod* is found in *Ish* (Man) and the *Heh* in *Ishah* (Woman)</note>. As it is written: "The tribes of *Yah*, a testimony for Israel" <note>Psalms 122:4</note>. It is known that the roots of the supernal extremities are above in Understanding <note>*Binah*</note>, and their ultimate root is in Wisdom <note>*Chokhmah*</note>, which are the secret of *Yah*, until everything is hidden in the concealment of the secret of the "point of the *Yod*." Thus the name *Yah* is between them, and the full "stature" is completed. The root of the holy seed is above in the power of the letters *Yah*. The seed travels through the spinal cord, which is the "Inheritance of Isaac," the bond of the whole body, and from there through the organ to the "well." This is the secret of the "union of man and his companion" <note>original: *ke-ma'ar ish ve-loyot*—a difficult phrase from 1 Kings 7:36</note>. The secrets are revealed to those who have reached understanding and knowledge. A person must awaken holiness in his thought, for when a person is righteous and sanctifies himself during the act, the supernal holiness is awakened.

### Concerning
the matter of union, one must learn, observe, and perform all the words of the *Tur* <note>The seminal code of Jewish law</note> in the section *Orach Chaim*, chapter 240, and in the *Tur Even HaEzer*, chapter 25. One should not lose the blessing of all that is mentioned there. A person should be fluent by heart in all the laws of circumcision and the laws concerning the "sending of the emissary" <note>metaphor for ejaculation</note> mentioned there. I have already written above what is recorded in this book of Chida'u <note>Likely a reference to Rabbi Chaim Joseph David Azulai or a similar authority</note>; to him you shall listen. Regarding the mystical hints and the intention of secrets, one must know, learn, and guard the "small in quantity but great in quality" work composed by the godly man, the Ramaz <note>Rabbi Moses Zacuto</note>, of blessed memory, called the *Holy Epistle* <note>Igeret HaKodesh</note>. His words are copied in the book *Menorat HaMaor*, in *Sefer HaMusar*, and in the book *Reshit Chochmah*, chapter seventeen of the "Gate of Holiness." Look there, for *Reshit Chochmah* added more beauty to this chapter from many passages of the Zohar and other excellent matters. Therefore, I command you to engage with that chapter from beginning to end. One who reviews his chapter a hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews it a hundred and one times. You, my children (may God protect them and grant them life), are warned of this, and your friends and your friends' acquaintances forever, and all the students who obey me: study these two chapters in the aforementioned *Tur* and chapter seventeen of *Reshit Chochmah* in the "Gate of Holiness." Study them so many times that they become fluent in your mouths. Then you will fulfill all that is written there. Then "happy shall you be and it shall be well with you" <note>Psalms 128:2</note> in this world and the world to come. Your children will be worthy through the power of your merit and purity; that is, you will increase many holy souls and build this matter for yourselves from here.

### Know
my children (may God protect them and grant them life), from every single act of union when it is done in holiness, a good effect comes forth. Even if his wife does not conceive, he nevertheless awakens the supernal realms and draws down a soul. The Kabbalists have spoken at length on this, writing that there is a permission to join with one's wife even if he knows she is pregnant, or nursing, or old, or barren. For he is not "wasting his seed," but rather a holy soul is formed from this. This is the secret of "And Sarah was barren, she had no child" <note>Genesis 11:30</note>. The Zohar asks: "She had no child" seems redundant after saying she was barren. It explains that this comes to teach the secret of union: Abraham would engage in the marital act with Sarah even though she was barren. Regarding the phrase "she had no child," the emphasis is on *to her*—*she* did not have one, but others did. For from every union, a soul was influenced, and these souls came to be born later. This is the matter of the "converts," for there is a bond of counting. Here, a soul is born when the blood and seed of Israel come from the side of the union of father and mother. But among the nations it is difficult, unless the souls influenced by the power of the union of the righteous spread out and come to take refuge [in holiness]. This is the matter of "Abraham converted the men and Sarah converted the women" <note>Genesis 12:5</note>; meaning, from the power of Abraham's holy thought during union, male souls were influenced, and from the power of Sarah's holy thought, female souls were influenced. It says, "The souls they *made* in Haran"—actual making through the power of union. This is the very thing they explained: Abraham converted the men and Sarah converted the women, and Abraham and Sarah "made" their souls.

### From this
one can understand the words of the Ari, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria</note>, in what he wrote in the introduction to *Midrash Shmuel* in his name on the verse: "The smallest shall become a thousand, and the least a mighty nation; I the Lord will hasten it in its time" <note>Isaiah 60:22</note>. One might observe that these seem to be two contradictory terms: if it is "hastened," it is not "in its time," and if it is "in its time," it is not "hastened." Our Sages were compelled to say: "If they merit, I will hasten it; if they do not merit, it will be in its time" <note>Talmud Sanhedrin 98a</note>. Although their words are correct, it is possible to say that through the life of "the small one becoming a thousand," He (blessed be He) will make it so that one woman will give birth to a great multitude at one time, so that all the souls in the "Body" <note>Hebrew: *Guf*—the heavenly storehouse of souls</note> will be finished. Then the son of David (the Messiah) will come. The redemption comes at the time when all the souls in the *Guf* are completed. This is "I will hasten it," for the speed is from Him (blessed be He), as He gives to one small person a thousand children. These are his words. And how will this thing be, that he will have a thousand children? It must be as we explained: that from every single union, a soul is formed, and these souls will spread out. Behold, the secret of union in holiness is a mirror of the supernal realm, as we explained the secret of the "Edifice." The root of the Edifice is in the secret of *Yah*, which is the secret of "Man and woman who were worthy have the name *Yah* between them." Then the "full stature" is completed and a soul is influenced. In this aspect, the union is called "Knowledge" (*Da'at*), as it is said: "And Adam knew his wife" <note>Genesis 4:1</note>. Now the liturgy is explained: "Who formed man in His image, in the image of the likeness of his form, and prepared for him from himself an everlasting edifice." Therefore, "You shall be holy" to sanctify yourselves with all types of holiness, even before the union, to examine your deeds, to meditate on repentance, and to give charity. I have seen that some are careful to separate from their wives... it seems to me that before returning to union, one should immerse in a ritual bath <note>Mikvah</note>, and then return, and the name of the Lord will be established for its fulfillment, which is the secret of the "Full Stature" mentioned above.

### And before
the union, one should engage in Torah study. How good and how pleasant it would be to engage in the laws of the *Tur Orach Chaim* chapter 240 and *Reshit Chochmah* chapter 7 of the "Gate of Holiness." If his soul desires to study and repeat laws, let him study the end of the chapter *Ha-Mapelet* <note>Talmud Niddah 30b</note>: "Rabbi Simlai preached: To what is a fetus in its mother's womb comparable? To a folded notebook. Its hands rest on its two temples, its two elbows on its two knees, its two heels on its two buttocks, and its head rests between its knees. Its mouth is closed and its navel is open. It eats from what its mother eats and drinks from what its mother drinks, and it does not produce excrement lest it kill its mother. As soon as it emerges into the air of the world, that which was closed opens, and that which was open closes, for otherwise it could not survive even one hour. A lamp burns over its head, and it looks and sees from one end of the world to the other, as it is said: 'When His lamp shined over my head, by His light I walked through darkness' <note>Job 29:3</note>. Do not wonder at this, for a person can sleep here and see a dream in Spain! There are no days when a person is in greater goodness than those days, as it is said: 'O that I were...'"

# The Gate of the Letters

<margin>
Kindness and endurance are great according to the measure of the intellect, to weigh all matters that were before and also one against the other, to elevate them in the work of righteousness, to sustain his words with judgment, and he shall never falter. Up to here are his words. <note>Original Hebrew: *E.K.L.*, an abbreviation for "up to here are his words," signifying the end of a quoted passage.</note>
</margin>

For the letter *Aleph* <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, symbolizing unity and the beginning.</note> was created in the likeness of the Upper Chariot. Behold, the world of Emanation <note>Hebrew: *Atzilut*, the highest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah</note> was emanated from the First Being, the secret of the triad of Kindness, Strength, and Beauty <note>Hebrew: *Hagat*, an acronym for *Hesed, Gevurah, Tiferet*</note>, and it seeks the end of existence through the secret of Knowledge (*Da'at*). From there, it reaches the secret of the Choice, the Foundation (*Yesod*) of the world, which pours out the "good oil" into its lamp, so that the Tabernacle becomes one.

**And from now on**, contemplate the secret of the union <note>Hebrew: *Zivug*, referring to both physical marital union and the mystical union of divine attributes</note>: how great it is and how much a person must sanctify themselves at that hour. One must focus their intent on the Supernal Height, for according to the thought and intention a person holds at that time, so shall the embryo formed from there be. The soul that comes to it will be drawn from one of the sides to which the person leans: if he leans toward the side of Good, the soul will come to him from the Holy Source we mentioned. But if he leans toward the side of Evil and does not sanctify himself at that hour, he draws a soul from an impure place. Of the one formed there, it is said, "The wicked are estranged from the womb" <note>Psalm 58:4</note>, and it is written, "They have dealt treacherously against the Lord, for they have begotten strange children" <note>Hosea 5:7</note>. These are the "brazen-faced" of the generation. Know that concerning this, our Holy Torah says by way of a hint: "Do not bring an abomination into your house" <note>Deuteronomy 7:26</note>.

**Know** that through the "Good Influence" <note>Hebrew: *Hashpa'ah*, the flow of divine energy</note>, good souls are emanated. But when the Evil Inclination overcomes the Good, the influence does not descend into the Holy Well, but into a "narrow pit" <note>A metaphor for impurity or the "Other Side"</note>. The souls that descend with that influence go outside and become defiled. From there, they come and wander. For all the spiritual powers are stacked one upon the other, resembling a tree. Just as a tree produces fruit through water, so too the Holy One, blessed be He, produces the fruits of this Tree through "water." The waters are those that descend from the Ancient Sea, and the fruits are the souls of the righteous. This is what is written: "I am like a leafy cypress, from Me your fruit is found" <note>Hosea 14:9</note>. Thus, one who sanctifies himself during the time of intimacy draws a soul from this Tree in a straight path, and that power will not be mixed with anything else. But one who follows the Evil Inclination causes that power to be mixed with an impure place, causing impurity above and below. Know that through the people of Israel, this Tree flourishes. 

The time for union during the weekdays applies to common people, but for Torah scholars who walk in the ways of the Place <note>Hebrew: *Hamakom*, a name for God</note>, blessed be He, their time is on Friday night <note>The Sabbath</note>. The secret of this will be explained in our second volume, God willing. During the weekdays, they wake at midnight and engage in Torah to connect with the Assembly of Israel <note>Hebrew: *Knesset Yisrael*, the mystical community of souls and the Shekhinah</note>. This was already hinted at in the words of our Sages (peace be upon them) when they said: "Behold, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord at night" <note>Psalm 134:1</note>. They said the "servants of the Lord" are the righteous who rise at midnight to engage in Torah and join with the "Doe of the Dawn" <note>A poetic name for the *Shekhinah* or the morning star</note> in the House of the Lord to praise the King. 

We have already written above that the "Union of the North" is awakened at midnight, drawing down a thread of grace. Tens of thousands of ministering angels praise before the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is an obligation to rise at that hour and engage in Torah. The Holy One, blessed be He, silences the heavenly host and listens to his voice, as it is written: "You who dwell in the gardens, companions are listening to your voice" <note>Song of Songs 8:13</note>. All the heavenly host and their companions gain wisdom from the praise rising from below from those who engage in Torah, saying: "Behold, bless the Lord, you bless Him, you praise Him." Then the Bride <note>The *Shekhinah*</note> crowns herself with that righteous person before the King, boasting of him and saying: "See the son with whom I have come before You." And who are those to whom this praise belongs? He returns and says: "Those who stand in the house of the Lord at night." They are called the servants of the Lord; they are worthy to bless the King, and their blessing is a complete blessing, as it is written: "Lift up your hands in holiness and bless the Lord" <note>Psalm 134:2</note>. "Holiness" is the source from which the heart is blessed, and the "hands" represent the upper purifications. They say: "May the Lord bless you from Zion"—the place of blessing for the Holy One, blessed be He, from the upper holy source, and He shall bless you and the Bride from the place called Zion. Just as they are joined together to praise the King, so from the same place she is blessed, you shall be blessed. That is what is written: "May the Lord bless you from Zion," for from there, life and blessing are required, "life forevermore." Up to here are his words.

<margin>
*Kuf* for Holiness (*Kedushah*). Since I wrote above that the holiness of his limbs is the measure of study until now, how the study of Torah depends on all the limbs of the body—and the laws were explained for all his limbs, the "Measurement of the Height" <note>Hebrew: *Shiur Komah*, referring to the mystical structure of the divine/human form</note> of the body—in order for everything to be in perfection, I will mention here further excellent measures regarding the limbs and the structure of the body.
</margin>

**And now**, since the matters of the holiness of food (which depends on the mouth) and the matters depending on the eyes or the senses have been explained—the holiness of all the limbs and the "Measurement of the Height" of man—everything has been explained well in this section, which is the letter **"Kuf" for Holiness**. Since I wrote above that the holiness of his limbs is the measure of study until now, how the study of Torah depends on all the limbs of the body, and the laws were explained for all his limbs, the "Measurement of the Height" of the body, in order for everything to be in perfection, I will mention here further excellent measures regarding the limbs and the structure of the body.

**Behold, this is the rule:** All of these are "vessels of thought," and thought must be holy, pure, and clean at every time and every moment. It is not only during the time one engages in Torah or during prayer that one should have pure thought and proper intention—whether according to the revealed way or the hidden way, according to the reach of his intellect—**or** at the time of performing a commandment (*mitzvah*). Commandments require intention, and one should perform them with the awakening of the heart and with intent regarding their reasons and secrets. Rather, even in his mundane dealings and physical affairs, he should do everything "for the sake of Heaven." In his thought, he should be cleaved to the Blessed Name and not separate from his thought. This is hinted at in the word "secretly." I have already written above in the section on the "Ten Utterances" regarding the service of the heart, and likewise regarding the letter ***Lamed***.

**And it is written** in the *Book of Tikkunim* <note>The *Tikkunei Zohar*, a seminal Kabbalistic text</note> and cited in *The Beginning of Wisdom* <note>Hebrew: *Reshit Chochmah*, a classic 16th-century ethical-Kabbalistic work</note>: The "Chariot of the Brain" consists of four things: Sight, Hearing, Smell, and Speech. He elaborates there that these correspond to the four letters of the Divine Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note>. Everything a person sees and hears is recorded in his thought and his reflection upon it. Likewise, speech emerges from the power of the intellect, from the soul, for external speech comes from internal speech, which is the intellect that is hidden. Also, the sense of smell is something upon which the soul depends.

**And just as** it is forbidden for a person to waste his seed below, it is a great prohibition to waste his "sight"—which is the Chariot of the Brain—by directing it downward. Therefore, there was a certain humble sage who would not look ahead of him or to his sides, but only within his four cubits. It goes without saying that one must shut his eyes from seeing evil, but even looking at a "permitted" thing outside of his four cubits is comparable to wasting seed. So it is written in *The Beginning of Wisdom*. It is known that the "month" <note>likely a scribal error for "light"</note> of a person's eyes is affected by his behavior, as Maimonides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon, the great 12th-century philosopher</note> wrote regarding one who is excessive in intimacy, that his eyes grow dim. Therefore, the hint "I made a covenant with my eyes" <note>Job 31:1</note> suggests that one should hold fast to the attribute of the eyes just as one holds to the attribute of the "Covenant" <note>the sign of circumcision/sexual purity</note>.

**And so** we find regarding speech, which is also a "Chariot of the Brain," for it is the "Covenant of the Tongue." These are pairs: the Covenant of the Fountain <note>the sexual organ</note>, the Covenant of the Tongue, and the Covenant of the Eye. It is written in *The Beginning of Wisdom* in the "Gate of Holiness" that just as the lower covenant must not waste seed, so one must not waste speech. 

**Likewise** it shall be with hearing: one should not hear any speech that is in vain, for the law is established that "one who hears is like one who answers." Similarly, smell should be a "pleasing aroma" and not "burning anger" <note>Hebrew: *Charon Af*, literally "burning of the nose"</note> at all—not even a little bit. Concerning this it is said: "Cease from man, whose breath (*neshamah*) is in his nostrils" <note>Isaiah 2:22</note>. All this concerns "turning away from evil," but concerning "doing good," one should cleave in his thought and see with his eyes. King David said: "Then I shall not be ashamed when I look at all Your commandments" <note>Psalm 119:6</note>. It is known that "looking" (*hibbit*) implies more concentration than merely "seeing," as Rashi explains on the verse "and he looked at the serpent" <note>Numbers 21:9</note>. David said: It is not enough that I see Your commandments, but I shall *look* at them. The explanation of the verse is also: one who has transgressed a commandment and is called to read from the Torah, when he sees that commandment, he feels ashamed. For one who does not keep the commandment should be ashamed and embarrassed when looking at the commandment written in the Torah. But David said, "I shall not be ashamed," etc. Likewise with hearing: for "doing good," he should hear and add to his hearing, as it says, "If you will surely listen" <note>Exodus 15:26</note>. If a person hears a law or a homily and has heard it once, he should not stop listening and say "I have already heard it." The commentators explain the verse "He who turns away his ear from hearing the Torah, even his prayer is an abomination" <note>Proverbs 28:9</note> to mean: if he lacks the ear to hear Torah that he has already heard, even though his prayer that he prays today is what he already prayed yesterday, it will be abominable in his eyes. Likewise with the "good scent"—the scent of the spices and the scent of the waters of the law. It is said regarding the "incense of the silence" and the holiness of speech.

**And also** "burning anger" should only be to be "zealous for the Lord of Hosts," as Phinehas did in his zeal, or to sanctify the Name of Heaven in public.

**The Holiness** of the hands and feet: One should not lift his hand or foot to perform any movement, even a tiny movement for an idle purpose, even if it contains no trace of transgression. A person should remember when standing before a king how he stands in awe and does not move; how much more so, with an incomparable logical inference (*kal v'chomer*), should the fear of the Divine Presence be upon him, for "the whole earth is full of His glory." He should be in great awe not to make any movement except for the service of the Blessed Name, or he should act with a "strong hand" and an "outstretched arm," and his feet should run toward the good. Even in his necessary dealings in business or performing work, he should use them, and all his intention should be for the sake of Heaven.

**The Holiness of the [Sexual Organ]** <note>Hebrew: *Ma'of*, likely a euphemism or variant for the organ of the covenant</note> requires extra guarding and an immense and awesome warning, so that one does not, God forbid, come to any suspicion of prohibition. One should regret any foolishness or sin and be careful from now on not to place his hand "from the navel and below," and be careful in deed, speech, and thought from all ugliness...
<meta>catchword: and abomination</meta>

# The Gate of the Letters

->May He who completes our knowledge, our intellect, and our senses to perform all deeds according to Your will, bless us with blessings of heaven from above and blessings of the deep that lies beneath. And from Your blessings, may the house of Your servant be blessed forever, amen, eternity, selah.<-

### Thus
You shall fulfill the secret of the union <note>original: *htsh* and *tskh*, likely codes for marital intimacy</note> with an awakening of the heart and purity of the soul, to complete the "rectification of deeds" <term>Tikkun HaMa'asim: the kabbalistic concept of fixing the spiritual world through physical actions</term> on every night of immersion <note>the night a woman returns from the Mikvah</note>, and it is proper to give charity beforehand.

> In the name of the Lord, wrapped in a red cloak, starting and remaining, do not wander and do not go out to another, nor in your evening. Return, return, for the sea is stirred; its wheels call to you in the holy field. I am held in the holiness of the King; I am enwrapped. <note>This is an Aramaic kabbalistic formula used for spiritual protection and sanctification of the environment.</note>

## It is forbidden
To engage in marital relations by the light of a candle. The Rema <note>Rabbi Moses Isserles, a major legal authority</note> wrote that if one makes a partition with a sheet, even if the candlelight shines through the sheet, it is permitted. However, in the pamphlets of the students of the Ari, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the father of modern Kabbalah</note>, they wrote in his name that it is forbidden whenever light is shining, and he was very stringent about this. It is a great danger to children; even if it is not the time of conception, if one has relations while the light shines, it is a great danger to them, Heaven forbid. And thus says the *Sefer HaYashar* <note>The Book of the Upright, an ethical treatise</note>: If there is light in another room and there is a window or doorway from that room into this one and the light enters—if the light enters directly and clearly, it is forbidden. For even though the candle is in another room, the light is performing its function, so what difference does it make if it is in this room or another? But if the light does not enter directly to illuminate well, but rather the path of the light is diverted so it illuminates the side of the room from another angle and the light is minimal, it seems to me that it is permitted.

<margin>
The order of the conclusion: I heard that there are those who skip certain times established for the holy union... at a fixed time... the Chanukah candles... the Mezuzot at their doorways at night and not by day... three houses... a night of added blessing. All thoughts should be focused... Friday night, four hours into the night. Its time is reversed from the weekday, hinting at the mystery of the "reversed" light. You will find that "In the year He sits us in the house," and perhaps this is the matter of the partition between him and the south. They should be male children, for the light before him is like half the night, and the light of the south is like half the day. The alignment must be from the North, which is the secret of the night, to the South, which is the day. Because the North is cleared from the weekday, the male aspect is awakened in the world of Mercy. And all the lower forces and those who externalize are subdued... an act to bring a soul from the world of the Male, and thus they will have male children. All this is said for one who wishes to be meticulous with himself at the time of rectifying his wife, that it should be entirely proper and accepted. Then this act becomes a "Judgment of the Names" <note>Hebrew: *Din Shemot*</note> as in *Etz Chaim* <note>The Tree of Life, a primary Lurianic text</note>. Regarding another matter: even without the knowledge of the soul, it is not good, but if the husband wants and she desires it, it is accepted... otherwise he may come to damage or wasteful thoughts... but the keepers of his covenant will do their deed in secret with a pure heart... and whatever is possible to change, he should change, and merit will be reckoned to him because he intends for the good, to crown the Kingdom of the Lord, which is a great secret.
</margin>

And regarding the matter of partitions placed around the bed in place of an actual room—such as a canopy or curtains <note>original: *kortinas*</note>—if the light shines well upon their faces, it seems to me it is forbidden, for the Sages did not intend for their enactment to be bypassed. All the reasons they gave apply to these partitions. Even if we say that these partitions are halakhically valid because they can stand in a "wind of commandment," nevertheless, in my humble opinion, partitions alone are not enough; we require the removal of the light from where the eyes can look. However, if the curtains are thick and heavy and darken the light, even if they do not darken it completely, it seems to me it is permitted because there are two reasons to be lenient: first, the candle is in another place and they are in another; and second, the candlelight is not serving him because it is darkened. If there are no partitions around him, it is forbidden to have relations even if the face of the candle is turned to the other side and does not shine much, or if it stands inside a lamp-stand <note>original: *lignoyira*, likely a specialized lantern or niche</note>... and even if he says "I will cover myself with my cloak and have relations," it is forbidden. Covering with a cloak was only permitted during the day for a Torah scholar who knows the hour is necessary and will not come to do this habitually. But at night, in the manner of relations, to cover with a cloak is not a permitted leniency... lest he come to have relations by the light of the candle, for he is not in control of himself once his inclination overcomes him, and "there is no guardian against immorality." It is forbidden entirely, even by covering with a cloak; this is a logical reason.

## And regarding
The light of the moon: it seems to me it is also forbidden if the light comes to them directly... but if the light enters through a window into the house, there is no concern, because the light of the moon is not so bright for one who is not standing directly under it... but if he is under the open sky, even if the direct moonlight is not on him but he sits in the shade, it is nonetheless forbidden, for since he is situated under the open sky, the light is bright.

## And regarding
The light of the stars: it seems to me it is permitted, for it is not considered "precious light." Even the light of the planet Venus <term>Noga: in Kabbalah, the "shining" shell that contains both good and evil</term>, which shines brighter than other stars, even near the light of morning, we do not fear it. It is possible that if the light shines on them very well, one should abstain.

## It is forbidden
To engage in marital relations during a famine or any trouble, Heaven forbid; but on the Sabbath, it is permitted. Likewise on the night of immersion. It is brought in the *Turei Zahav* <note>A commentary on the Code of Jewish Law</note> from the Jerusalem Talmud... and I received a tradition from my teacher, the Gaon Rabbi Falk Katz, who explained the difficulty: "Behold, Levi had relations during the years of famine, for Jochebed was born between the walls!" <note>Referring to the birth of Moses' mother during the migration to Egypt</note>. Several answers were given, but all were rejected in the *Ran*... however, there is a new, spacious answer: it is possible that Levi's wife conceived on the night of her immersion, and he did not have relations with her again. The mystical reason for the prohibition of relations during a time of trouble is that, so to speak, the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is not in her place in the secret of the Supernal Union; therefore, the lower union is forbidden.

->When he intends<-
To unite, he and she should mention the "Holy Offspring who are in the land," and the Holy Patriarchs and the Tribes, so that this seed shall be drawn after them. They should say: Adam with Eve; Seth; Noah; Enoch; Methuselah; Abraham with Sarah; Isaac with Rebecca; Jacob with Rachel and Leah, Bilhah and Zilpah; Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Joseph and Benjamin; Ephraim and Manasseh. They should pray in their hearts that this seed be drawn after the tribe they desire. If she is from the tribe of Levi, it is good. How beautiful it is to recite the passage of the union of the two Levite patriarchs mentioned at the beginning of the portion *Va'era*: "And these are the names of the sons of Levi..." until "these are the heads of the Levite families." One must learn this passage by heart because at that time there is no candle <note>meaning he cannot read from a book in the dark</note>. Then they must ensure their hands are clean; there must always be a vessel of water standing before the bed, and they should wash their hands before the act for the sake of holiness, and likewise after the act, as explained in the *Beit Yosef* and the *Shulchan Arukh*.

## And regarding
The time of the union: it should be at midnight. One who cannot restrain himself and wants to have relations as soon as he lies down, then when he recites the *Shema*, he should recite all the verses, but the blessing "He who causes the bands of sleep to fall" <term>Hamapil: the final blessing before sleep</term> should not be said until after the act. Otherwise, there would be an interruption between the blessing and sleep. Then he should say the *Hamapil* blessing and repeat the first paragraph of the *Shema*, for it is forbidden to speak after the *Shema*. See the *Beit Yosef*. The secret is that the hour appropriate for the "kneading of man" <note>a metaphor for conception</note> is from midnight onwards. For at the hour of the "night watch," the Holy One, Blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, and it is a time of favor. In that hour, mercies are awakened in the world. He who sanctifies himself with his wife at that hour and focuses on the proper intentions will have holy children, for they come from a holy source, and they are called "Children of the Living God." Before midnight, the Attribute of Judgment is present. "Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing." And one who looks closely at what Benjamin said: "Anyone who places his bed between North and South will have male children," for he intended this toward the Holy Faith and the Supernal Connection. Our Sages awakened us to a great principle: everything a man does, he must do in accordance with the deeds of the Supernal ones, in the likeness of the Supernal ones. He must know that matter and focus his intent on it; otherwise, there is no perfection in his deeds and they are not pleasing. Therefore, a man must sanctify himself at the time of relations.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on spiritual purity, moving from the specific regulations of marital conduct to the mystical intentions behind ritual immersion in the Mikveh and the broader sanctity of the Land of Israel.</meta>

# The Gate of the Letters

One should focus their intention on the three Divine Names mentioned, both generally and specifically, so that they rise to the numerical value of *Yabok* <note>Numerical value 112, representing the union of the names Y-H-V-H and A-D-N-Y</note>, as in the verse "May He **answer us** on the day **we call**." This is the secret of the verse "And he crossed the **ford of Yabok**... and he took them and sent them across the stream, and he sent across that which was his." This implies that through this immersion, performed with proper preparation and focusing on the Name *Yabok*—which rules and governs over holiness—the "garments" of the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the kabbalistic term for the realm of impurity or evil</term> from the weekdays are stripped away through the abundance of God's mercies. The phrase "Preserver of **kindness** for **thousands**" <note>Exodus 34:7</note> alludes to this, as he passes away all impurities from the side of defilement that belonged to him. This is the primary purification. Once he has been restored through God's mercy and kindness, he is like a newborn child, becoming "a man in His image, in the image of God." This is the secret: the word for "impurity" <note>Hebrew: *Tuma'ah* (טומאה)</note> has the same numerical value as "immersion" <note>Hebrew: *Tevilah* (טבילה)</note> when including the word itself in the count. This signifies that "Man" <note>Hebrew: *Adam* (אדם)</note>—meaning that through the first immersion, he removed the filth of his sin that had defiled him—becomes like a newborn child. After he emerges from the immersion and dresses in his way, he is then pure and holy, separated from the side of defilement that rested upon him previously. When this one rises, the other falls; when the immersion comes, the spirit of defilement falls, is cut off, and hidden. Likewise, the word "immersion" with its five letters equals the numerical value of "impurity." It is enough. Afterward, one should recite this prayer with the "utterance of his lips," which are like "the bulls of our lips" <note>Hosea 14:3; a reference to prayer replacing animal sacrifice</note>, so that the entire spirit of defilement is cut off. Indeed, "spirit of defilement" <note>Hebrew: *Ruach Mesaba*</note> has the same numerical value as "utterance" <note>Hebrew: *Siach*</note>. This is the secret and the foundation of our prayer and the foundation of the sages' statutes.

One should say: "May it be Your will that this immersion, by which I have purified my body, along with the utterance of my lips and the meditation of my heart before You, be accepted and considered as if I had stood here at the 'slaughterhouse rings' in the Temple <note>The place in the Temple where sacrifices were prepared</note>, and as if I had grasped the hands of the Priests in the two 'signs' of the neck <note>The esophagus and trachea, the two areas cut during ritual slaughter</note> to appease the final *He* of the Essential Name <note>The Tetragrammaton Y-H-V-H</note>. And may it be as if I were slaughtered with the specific knife for the slaughter of the burnt offering, and may it be accepted like a vessel of service in the North and be pleasing before You to appease the letter *Vav* of the Essential Name. And may it be as if I were burned limb by limb and included in the altar fires as a pleasing aroma before You to appease the first *He*. And may it be as if I were made into the white ash that was the remnant of the sacrifice, and as if I underwent the judgment of 'stoning' according to the commandment of 'removing the ashes,' which is the completion of atonement, to appease the letter *Yod* of the Essential Name."

"And You, in Your abundant mercies, may it be Your will that in the merit of Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah <note>The three youths thrown into the furnace in the Book of Daniel</note>, who were cast into the fiery furnace and were saved, so may You save me if I have incurred the penalty of **Burning** before You; let it be as if I were burned before You. May it be Your will that in the merit of Isaac our forefather, who was bound before You like a lamb to the slaughter to be killed and was saved, so may You save me from **Slaying** if I have incurred that penalty before You, for You are a merciful and gracious God. And if I have incurred the penalty of **Strangulation** before You, may it be Your will that You save me in the merit of Jacob our forefather, peace be upon him, whom You saved from the hand of 'Ipho' <note>Perhaps a scribal error or obscure reference to Esau's guardian angel or a companion</note> the son of Esau who came on the way to strangle and kill him, but he was saved; so may You save me from strangulation. And if I have incurred the penalty of **Stoning** before You, may it be Your will that You save me just as You saved Moses our teacher, as the scripture says: 'a little more and they will stone me,' yet he was saved. And just as You saved Moses and Israel from the stones that Og, King of Bashan, sought to drop upon them but they were saved; so may You save me in Your abundant mercies and great kindness if I have incurred the penalty of stoning. Please, do not turn me away empty-handed from Your presence, for I rely on Your abundant mercies. For You do not desire the death of the wicked, but that he return from his way and live, as it is said: 'Let the wicked forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts, and let him return to the Lord, and He will have mercy on him, and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon.' May He who loves the Patriarchs love the children; may He who blessed the Patriarchs bless the children; He who redeemed, He who felt, He who honored, He who awakened, He who remembered, He who graced, He who purified, He who made upright, He who acted with kindness, He who coveted, He who rescued, He who carried, He who supported, He who helped, He who made fruitful, He who justified, He who sanctified, He who had mercy, He who guarded, He who inaugurated the Patriarchs, may He support the children from now and forever, Amen Selah."

->And before one immerses, he should say: "And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas."<-

The word "Seas" <note>Hebrew: *Yamim* (ימים)</note> equals 310. The word "Water" <note>Hebrew: *Mayim* (מים)</note> is also calculated... <note>The text here follows a complex kabbalistic gematria involving the expansion of letters</note>. When standing in the Mikveh, one should say: "Who is a God like You... He will again have compassion on us... You will give truth to Jacob..." <note>Micah 7:18-20</note>. And one who has sinned through anger should think during immersion that "Anger" <note>Hebrew: *Ka'as* (כעס)</note> with the word itself equals the value of "Mikveh." He should abandon anger then and be purified. The reason "Anger" is included with the word itself is because most who get angry do so through the "word"—meaning the words of anger that leave their mouth.

->The secret of the form of the Mikveh was explained in the words of the Divine, the Holy Rabbi Isaac Luria in the service of Yom Kippur, and these are his words: "It is known that the secret of the forty *se'ah* of water is a rectification for the Shekhinah <term>Divine Presence</term> in the secret of the Upper Chamber, like this:"<-

<image-desc>A mystical diagram representing the "Secret of the Form of the Mikveh" (Sod Temunat Ha-Mikveh). It consists of a grid pattern of small dots. In the center is a large 'X' character. To the right and left are vertical columns of four dots each. Below the 'X' is a small circle with four dots arranged within and below it. The entire structure is arranged symmetrically to represent the 40 se'ah (measurements) of the ritual bath.</image-desc>

The meaning of the word "What" <note>Hebrew: *Mah* (מה)</note> which we explained elsewhere, also indicates the secret of the chain of emanation. Five levels: the central point, which is *Yod*, then *He* which is the second measure, then three points on four sides which is the third measure... these are forty, which is the letter *Mem*. The central point completes nine to ten, and four times ten is forty. Thus, a closed *Mem*, a *Yod*, and the points equal "Water" <note>Hebrew: *Mayim*</note>, which are the forty *se'ah*. The meaning of the points refers to Wisdom (*Chochmah*)... the closed *Mem* to the second measure, Understanding (*Binah*)... and these are Kindness, Fear, and Mercy, each including the three, rising to ten through Wisdom... for through Wisdom the attributes are included in ten, but through the crown they rise to forty... this is the secret of the forty *se'ah* of water, the secret of the purification of the Divine Presence. This is also the secret of "He who brings down the dew"... <note>Ending the quote from the Ari</note>.

When a person searches his deeds, confesses, forsakes sin, returns in repentance, and immerses with the great intentions mentioned above, the verse "Before the Lord you shall be purified" is fulfilled in him. He should say the verse: "Create in me a pure heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me," for now he has become a new creation. "Pure" <note>Hebrew: *Tahor* (טהור)</note> has the same gematria as the initials of "He immersed for the sake of..."

->Completed is the sanctity of the body, in general and in detail: that is, the sanctity of the individual limbs and the sanctity of the entire stature through the secret of the Mikveh. Then he is called a "son of the holy," for he is a branch extending from the holiness of the Patriarchs.<-

And now it is time to speak of the **Sanctity of the Place**. This is mentioned in the verse: "Then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the Land." Here, the holiness of the place and the holiness of the Patriarchs are mentioned together.

The sanctity of the place applies to the Land, etc. To speak of the creation of Man who was holy, whom God placed in the Garden of Eden; and when he corrupted his way and was banished from Eden, he was restored in the Nation of Israel, who are called "Man" <note>A talmudic reference: "You are called Man"</note> through the Torah. He gave them the Holy Land, which possesses a sanctity like that of the Garden of Eden, as written in Ezekiel: "This desolate land has become like the Garden of Eden." Even now in its destruction, it remains in its holiness; it is a "land that the Lord seeks out." The land of the nations is impure, and for any Israelite who is there, it is impossible for their prayers to ascend unless they send them by way of the Holy Land to Jerusalem, and from there to the Holy of Holies, for "this is the gate of heaven." There are many levels of goodness to the Holy Place. Our Sages taught at the end of Tractate Ketubot: "All may compel [a family] to move to the Land of Israel, but none may compel them to leave. All may compel to move to Jerusalem..." The Baraita teaches: "If he says to go up and she says not to go up, she is compelled to go up... if she says to go up and he says not to go up, he is compelled to go up." In the *Tur Even HaEzer*, section 75, it is written that all these laws apply even in our time... and as for what the *Tosafot* <term>medieval commentators</term> wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Tam that now there is no commandment to dwell in the Land because of the many agricultural commandments we cannot keep—those are the words of an individual. It is also not a reasonable argument... rather, "the righteous shall walk in it and the transgressors shall stumble in it." If one lives in the Land and does not fulfill his obligations, he is a transgressor. but one who sanctifies himself and maintains his dwelling there according to his strength, then happy is he. As for what we cannot be careful of, this is a case of being under duress...

# The Gate of the Letters

->...and abomination, and he shall choose the good; then he is a son of the World to Come. We shall now clarify the general concept of holiness and the secret of the Mikveh <term>Mikveh: A ritual bath used for spiritual purification</term>. The Mikveh is a great purification for the Name of 72 Letters <note>original: "ע"ב" (Ayin-Bet), the expanded name of God (Y-H-V-H) that totals 72 in numerical value</note>, which transforms "judgment" into "letters of judgment" <note>This refers to the linguistic and numerical process of mitigating harsh spiritual decrees</note>.

The special quality of immersion is to return the soul to its place. One who is ritually impure lacks a full soul; specifically, one who "damages the covenant" <note>A common idiom for sexual transgressions</note> causes his soul to depart. Every person requires immersion every Friday <note>original: "Erev Shabbat"</note>, as explained in the Zohar (Portion *Vayakhel*), in order to strip off the "weekday spirit" and clothe oneself in the "spirit of Sabbath holiness." This is a distinguished spirit originating from the *Atika* <term>Atika: "The Ancient One," the highest, most merciful level of the Divine</term>; perhaps, through this, the Holy Spirit will rest upon him.

<margin>
I also found this in "Wings of a Dove."
</margin>
In the book *Knafey Yonah* <note>original: "Wings of a Dove" by Menachem Azariah da Fano</note>, the secret of the Friday immersion is discussed. Specifically after midday, one should focus their intention on the word **Water** <note>original: "Mayim"</note>. Its numerical value is 90, corresponding to nine of the letter *Yod* found in the various expansions of the Divine Name: four from the Name of 72, three from the Name of 63, and one from the Name of 45 <note>These are the different ways the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-V-H) is spelled out mystically</note>. The word *Mikveh* has the numerical value of 151, the same as the Name *Ehyeh* <note>original: "I Will Be"</note> when spelled out with the letter *He*. Know that the Name *Ehyeh* serves as a "throne" for the Name of four *Yods*. One should also intend that he is immersing in the four *Yods* of the Name of 72, which represents forty *se'ah* <term>Se'ah: A biblical unit of measurement; a Mikveh must contain at least 40 se'ah of water</term>. A person is obligated to purify himself for the "Foot" <note>original: "Regel," meaning both a "foot" and a "pilgrimage festival"</note>. This is hinted at by two Divine Names that total 233 <note>the numerical value of "Regel"</note>: the expansions of the Lord and *Ehyeh* with the letter *Yod*. This is the meaning of "and he was like a grasshopper," which is a good sign for everyone on the eve of the Sabbath. However, during the three pilgrimage festivals, one must focus on two other Names of 72. In Part 3, Section 45, I found the following language:

One who immerses on Friday from the time of the Afternoon Prayer <note>original: "Mincha"</note> onwards should, while inside the water, bow toward the West. If he does not know which way is West, he should mentally envision the four directions and designate one as West. During the first immersion, he should say: "Behold, I am immersing to strip the weekday garments from my soul." If he is worthy of mystical sight, he may see something like smoke rising, forming many small faces from his fingernails <note>This represents the removal of the "husks" or external spiritual forces that cling to the body during the week</note>. Afterward, he should submerge a second time and say: "Behold, I am immersing to receive the illumination of the Sabbath—'Remember' and 'Observe' joined as one." He should focus on the numerical values 102, 161, and for "Observe," the expansion of the Name *Elohim* <note>original: God</note>, which totals 350... <unclear>various numerical permutations</unclear>. This represents the "Five Branches of Glory" that surround a person within the water. He should then submerge a third time and say: "Behold, I am immersing to receive the 'Additional Soul' <note>original: "Neshamah Yeterah," the extra spiritual level granted to Jews on the Sabbath</note>." He should focus on the Names totaling 161, 143, and 151. When he exits, he should walk backward, just as one leaves a Palace. When he dries himself and dresses, he should be mindful of the verse: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper."

The standard practice for every Friday is three immersions. However, one who immerses for the sake of repentance <note>original: "Ba'al Teshuvah"</note> on that day is required to perform fourteen immersions. Their reasons are explained in the holy writings of the Ari <term>Isaac Luria: The 16th-century father of modern Kabbalah</term>, scattered in various places. These are the instructions copied from the rabbi <unclear>Chukoresh</unclear> regarding the Sabbath Rectification:

**If** you find someone capable of such immersion, he is greatly praised and lauded. For there is no righteous man on earth who does good and does not sin. By this act, he returns to being "beloved" below and "exalted" above, following the custom practiced in the Holy Land of Israel to this day—immersing every Friday, for there is the "Gate of Heaven." They take upon themselves the Holy Kingdom, as explained in the "Rectifications of Repentance." Afterward, he should recite the *Akedah* <note>The biblical passage of the Binding of Isaac</note> from beginning to end and accept upon himself the "Four Death Penalties of the Court." These are arranged according to the specific sin one may have committed against the letters of the Divine Name.

He should say with heartfelt intention: "May it be Your will, O Lord my God and God of my fathers, if I have damaged the first letter of Your great and awesome Name, or the letters dependent on it, and have incurred the penalty of **Stoning** before Your Throne of Glory—may the merit of our father Abraham stand before You... and purify me through this immersion: my body in this world, and my spirit and soul above in the **River of Fire** <term>Nehar Dinur: A celestial river of fire that purifies souls</term>."

"May it be Your will... if I have damaged the second letter of Your Name... and incurred the penalty of **Burning**... may the merit of the binding of Isaac stand before You. Purify me through this immersion... and may it be as if my internal organs were consumed by the wick of fire."

"May it be Your will... if I have damaged the third letter of Your Name... and incurred the penalty of **Beheading**... may the merit of Your servant Jacob stand before You. Purify me... and may it be as if my head was removed by the sword."

"May it be Your will... if I have damaged the fourth letter of Your Name... and incurred the penalty of **Strangulation**... may the merit of Your Name stand before You. Purify me... as if I were strangled... and rectified according to the law of the Great Court in Jerusalem."

"Lord, hear; Lord, forgive; Lord, attend and act; do not delay!" He should then focus on the initial letters of the words "Hear," "Forgive," "Attend," and "Act," which correspond to the four penalties. Then he shall say: "You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for it is time to favor her." He should recite the "Psalm of Mishaps" <note>Psalm 91</note> to ward off the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: The realm of evil or impurity</term>, as well as the song of Rabbi Nehunia ben Ha-Kana: "We beg You, with the strength of Your right hand's greatness, untie the bundled sins..." <note>The famous "Ana BeKoach" prayer</note>. While standing in the water, when it reaches his throat, he should recite three verses: "Who is a God like You..." "He will again have compassion on us..." and "You will give truth to Jacob..."

He should say: "Just as I purify my physical body below, so may the ministering angels of the Most High purify my soul, spirit, and breath above in the River of Fire. Just as I sanctify my body below, so may they sanctify my soul above, in the Name of the Lord who is God, and in the Name of the Master, the Rock of the Worlds. Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."

**If** he is a penitent coming to purify himself on Friday—even though this is appropriate for every day of the week, not everyone can manage it—at the very least on Friday, which is a "time of favor" for the Sabbath Queen, he must perform these immersions. If he is healthy and can endure it, he should perform fourteen immersions to gain mastery over the "fourteen bad times" <note>referencing the times in Ecclesiastes 3</note> and turn them to good, giving him the strength to stand in the Palace of the Eternal King. These fourteen immersions sweeten the judgments.

The first set of immersions is to remove and purify; three others are to unite the first three letters of the Names of the Lord, *Ehyeh*, and the Master, according to the known order. The next sets of three are for the second, third, and fourth letters. The final immersion is to unite the three Names into one, so they may be a complete crown upon his head, to draw upon him the "Spirit of Purity" from the Source of all sources. The rest of the rectifications for penitents are explained in the "Order of Intentions for Immersion" in the "Treatise on Repentance," Chapter 6, and in the book *Knafey Yonah*. Regarding the Sabbath specifically, even if he says the aforementioned confession, he only strictly needs three immersions: the first <insert>using the name S-G-S</insert> to remove sins and the light of the "Other Side" that rules during the weekdays; the second <insert>a second immersion</insert> is a preparation to receive the sparks of the soul's garment; and the third <insert>using the name S-G-N-K</insert> to draw down the "Additional Soul." <unclear>Mystical abbreviations regarding names and numerical values: 145, 133</unclear>.
