# Tractate Chullin
<note>original: "Masachet Chullin"; while this is the name of a Talmudic tractate primarily concerning dietary laws, the text here continues a series of ethical and legal instructions on various topics.</note>

In truth, neither on the principal nor on the profit, until he swears upon a **Torah scroll** while it is uncovered, between the prayers of *Ashrei* and *Lamnatzeach* <note>Two specific sections of the daily morning liturgy</note>, regarding everything that the "steward" <note>the investment manager</note> claims. If he does not swear as mentioned above, woe to us, for we are obligated to pay one hundred and twenty, and he shall have the aforementioned time. Afterward, it follows all the "beauty of the contract" <note>the standard legal protections of a deed</note>. One must be careful to give him payment for his labor; however, if he wrote a waiver regarding his labor costs to give him only a small amount, that is sufficient.

Behold, in this matter of the **Investment Partnership** <term>Iska; a legal contract used to allow investment for profit while avoiding the biblical prohibition against charging interest (Ribbit) by structuring the loan as a partnership</term>, there is no doubt that it is "near to profit" <note>meaning the investor shares in gains</note>. Regarding what I wrote in the *Hanukkah* section <note>referring to a previous ruling or notebook entry</note>—that he should only be believed through an oath on a Torah scroll—even though by strict law he is not obligated to swear unless it is a matter of negligence, it is clear to me that even if we were negligent, the lender certainly made a profit. If he does not claim it as a certainty, he is only obligated to accept a "severe ban" <note>original: "Cherem S'tam"; a communal excommunication used to compel honesty</note>. One may initially stipulate this, as we learn: "A person may stipulate with a gratuitous watchman to have the status of a borrower."

However, as for doing what the common masses do—stipulating that the borrowers are not believed except through witnesses—you must distance yourself greatly from this interpretation! For then it becomes "near to profit and far from loss" <note>a situation where the lender takes no risk but takes all gain, which is considered usurious interest</note>. I have already written a major legal ruling on this, bringing the words of the *Terumat HaDeshen* <note>Rabbi Israel Isserlein, a 15th-century authority</note> on this matter, explaining his words and writing what appeared correct in my eyes. And you, my children, do not deviate from this. Let the fear of Heaven be in your hearts to understand and explain the matter of the **Investment Partnership** well to the borrower; then you will be cleared before Heaven, and the blessing of God will be in your money twofold.

When the time for repayment arrives and the lender wishes to leave the money with the borrower for another year of partnership, he must perform a new **formal acquisition** <term>Kinyan; a symbolic act that makes a contract legally binding</term> and a new deed. This is because the borrower is obligated to return everything written in the deed to the lender, and then take it anew as an investment. Otherwise, the first deed’s liens are considered waived; it becomes a deed where the debt was already "paid" and then borrowed against again, which cannot be used for collection. If he does not actually return it to the lender, then there is no specific object upon which the borrower can swear in the future saying, "I did not profit" or "I lost." Thus, the matter becomes a deceitful trick and a lie. Therefore, he is obligated to return it, and afterward, they make a new investment contract. Or, even if he does not physically return it, the borrower should bring him merchandise worth the amount he owes and transfer it to the lender with a complete acquisition in exchange for the debt. Afterward, the lender gives this merchandise back to him as a new investment contract with a new acquisition and a new deed, giving him a fee for his labor—and then it is well.

Know, my children, that this is the straight path to clarify these matters of investment. It is mentioned in the *Tur, Choshen Mishpat*, section 108. However, there are several matters mentioned in the *Tur* regarding the laws of interest which, in my view, are considered absolute interest in these generations of ours. For example, if the lender initially gives the borrower shops, knowing the borrower will act in such a way that the lender will certainly be "near to profit." Those laws mentioned in the codes apply specifically to cases of theft, but at the time they begin a partnership, such a thing does not enter our minds. For example, the *Tosafot* wrote (and it is brought in the *Tur, Yoreh Deah*, section 177) that it is permitted to give an investment for half the profit and stipulate that he should only deal in a certain commodity; if he changes it, the recipient bears all responsibility. Likewise, any condition he desires—such as stipulating that he must keep the money buried in the ground—if he deviates and loses, the loss is the recipient’s, but if he profits, it is split. This is only permitted when the condition is made with a whole heart and in total honesty, where the lender truly intends for the condition to be met. But one who knows for a certainty that the borrower will not do so, yet stipulates it anyway—meaning he acts without integrity—regarding this the Torah wrote concerning interest: **"And you shall fear your God."** Similarly, when judges rule leniently on this, it is only when things are done with simple integrity as they appear; but if one uses cunning tricks, the prohibition of interest remains in place and he shall surely be punished. Therefore, great caution is needed, for the human heart is covetous. A person must sanctify himself and fulfill: **"And you shall love the Lord your God with all your might"** <note>Deuteronomy 6:5, often interpreted as "with all your money"</note>.

***

Even though "his time is found in faith" <note>meaning his business is honest</note> and this is a great commandment, nevertheless, one should not waste his time in this. This goes without saying for a Torah scholar, who must certainly see that his Torah study is fixed and his work is secondary. But even for householders, it is written that those who have the fear of God in their hearts should contemplate and understand their end, fulfilling the ideal of "good is Torah study combined with a worldly occupation."

Our sages gave a sign: "May He be gracious to me (*Choneni*)," or "May you be wise (*Tashkil*)," or "May you succeed (*Tatzliach*)," or "May you sleep (*Tishan*)." One should divide the day—which is 24 hours—into three parts:
1.  **Eight hours** shall be holy to the Lord for Torah and prayer. (Mnemonic: *Tashkil* - "You shall be wise," which refers to the study of Torah).
2.  **Eight hours** he shall engage in buying, selling, and commerce. (Mnemonic: *Tatzliach* - "You shall succeed").
3.  **Eight hours** he shall sleep. (Mnemonic: *Tishan* - "You shall sleep").

However, in those eight hours dedicated to Torah and prayer, he should rejoice and be exceedingly happy with them, for they are a time of attachment to the Creator. These eight hours are holy to the Lord. The sign for this is: "The exalted King alone... *Me'az* (from then)." This means that from *Az* <note>The Hebrew letters Aleph (1) and Zayin (7), equaling 8</note> alone, he gains profit and wisdom from the King's gifts.

When he prepares for business, he should say: **"For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Shekhinah"** <note>A kabbalistic formula for intention</note>, "I am going about this business, and I trust in God, may He be blessed, that He will send me sustenance. This business is merely the 'cause' through which God will send a blessing to all the work of my hands." When God leads him and grants him profit, he should remember God and give Him thanks and blessing, as it is written: **"And you shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you the power to gain wealth."** <note>Deuteronomy 8:18</note>

When God bestows an abundant blessing upon him, his heart should not become haughty. On the contrary, he should be humble and embarrassed, saying: "Who am I that You have brought me this far?" He should remember the divine light, for perhaps God is "deducting" from his merits in this world, or perhaps God is testing him to see how he will behave with the money. Therefore, a wise man has "his eyes in his head" <note>Ecclesiastes 2:14</note>; he understands his end and behaves with the money by giving much **Charity** (*Tzedakah*) and many **Acts of Kindness** (*Gemilut Chasadim*), according to the blessing with which God blessed him, striving to be exceedingly humble.

The Torah already warned about this in the portion of *Ekev*: **"For the Lord your God is bringing you into a good land... and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless... Beware lest you forget... lest you eat and be satisfied... and your heart becomes haughty and you forget... and you shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you the power to gain wealth."** <note>Deuteronomy 8:7-18</note> And at the end of the song of *Ha'azinu*, it says of the one who becomes bloated: **"And Jeshurun grew fat and kicked; you grew fat, you grew thick... and he abandoned the God who made him."** <note>Deuteronomy 32:15</note>

God performed great salvations for Israel by the sea, saving them and giving them their money. They remembered this at the Sea of Reeds—this is the meaning of "And the Lord saved..." But then "Jeshurun grew fat and kicked."

If he incurs a loss, he should still thank and praise God, for it is certainly for his own good. Since he engaged in business faithfully, this loss—which seems "bad" in human eyes—is considered "good" by God.

If God grants him profit, he should immediately set aside a **Tithe** (*Ma’aser*). **"You shall surely tithe all the increase of your seed."** <note>Deuteronomy 14:22</note> The sages taught that this includes those who go out to sea, those who cross deserts, and those who engage in commerce. Even though we do not currently have agricultural tithes, a person is obligated to tithe from everything that comes into his hand. A person should have a special purse for his tithe money, and from it, he should give to the poor, both near and far. It is also a commandment to lend from it to people in their time of need; even for a wealthy man who is currently squeezed for cash, it is permitted to lend him from the tithe money, for "Acts of Loving-kindness" are also great when done for the wealthy.

Happy is the man who sets aside a **Fifth** (*Chomesh* - 20%). As Jacob our father said: **"I will surely tithe it to You"** <note>Genesis 28:22; the Hebrew repeat of the word "tithe" suggests a double tithe, or 20%</note>. Regarding more than a fifth, the Sages of Usha ordained that a person should not squander [more than that, so as not to become poor himself]. At the beginning of Tractate *Peah*, we learn: "These are the things that have no set measure..." and it lists "Acts of Loving-kindness." The **Ramban** <note>Nachmanides</note> and **Rabbi Ovadia** <note>Bertinoro</note> explain that this refers to kindness done with one's body, such as visiting the sick and burying the dead. But for kindness done with money—such as redeeming captives, clothing the naked, and feeding the hungry—there is a limit: one should give a fifth of the profit in his purse each time a commandment comes his way. He is not obligated to do more than that, for we say: "He who squanders should not squander more than a fifth." Therefore, a person should set aside a fifth of the profit at all times so it is available whenever an act of kindness comes his way, thus fulfilling his duty. Until here are his words.

Even if God grants him a large tithe, it is proper to "remove" it and distribute it in the third and sixth years of the Sabbatical cycle, according to the law of agricultural tithes. Those people who hold back their tithes so that they remain in their hands until after their death are fools walking in darkness, for they do not fulfill the commandment themselves.

I found in the name of **Maharar M. Katz** <note>Rabbi Meir Katz, 16th century</note> that one may use tithe money to hire a teacher for the child of a wealthy relative. The logic leans toward permitting this; while Maharar M. wrote that one may not give tithes to a wealthy relative for their basic needs, one may give it for Torah study if the father is unwilling to pay. I am also accustomed to instructing people that for any commandment that comes their way—such as being a *Sandek* <note>honor at a circumcision</note>, helping a bride enter the canopy, or buying books to study from and lend to others—if they would not otherwise have the means to do it, they may take the funds from the tithe. Until here are his words.

***

### The laws of tithing will be further explained on the next page:

I found in a certain book the following: Since we find the concept of "tithing" applied to several things, even to children, as it says in the Midrash (Genesis Rabbah, *Vayetze*): Rabbi Joshua of Sakhnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi: A Gentile once asked Rabbi Meir, "Do you not say that Jacob was a man of truth, as it is written: 'You give truth to Jacob'?" He said to him, "Yes." He asked, "And did he not say: 'And of all that You give me, I will surely tithe it to You'?" He replied, "Yes." He asked, "How is it that he set aside the tribe of Levi—one out of ten—but did not set aside a tithe for the two tribes Ephraim and Manasseh? If they are counted as two, then there were twelve sons, and he should have tithed differently!" <note>The question probes how Jacob fulfilled his vow to tithe his children</note>. He replied to him, "Are there not four mothers?" He said, "Remove the four firstborns..."

# Tractate Chullin
<note>original: "Masachet Chullin"; although this is the title of a Talmudic tractate regarding dietary laws, the text here functions as a compendium of various laws and mystical teachings, here focusing on Tefillin.</note>

Their placement testifies to His unity, may He be blessed, and that to Him belongs the power, the strength, and the dominion over the upper and lower worlds, to do with them according to His will—just as He performed signs and wonders in heaven and on earth during the Exodus from Egypt, and there is none who can say to Him, "What are You doing?" **Furthermore**, one should remember that placing the Tefillin <term>Tefillin; black leather boxes containing Torah scrolls worn during prayer</term> on the arm facing the heart and on the head facing the brain is done to subjugate one's brain and heart to the Holy One, blessed be He. These are the primary organs of a person, upon which life, thoughts, and desires depend. This was written by Rabbeinu Yonah <note>Rabbi Yonah Gerondi, a 13th-century ethicist</note> in the chapter "One who Recites," and the *Beit Yosef* <note>Rabbi Joseph Karo's legal commentary</note> cited it in the *Tur Orach Chaim* (Section 28) in the name of the *Zohar* regarding the statement of Rabbi Yochanan: "He who wishes to accept upon himself the complete yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven... should place Tefillin and recite the *Shema*..." and these are his words: that through the Tefillin on the head, a person subjugates to His Name, may He be blessed, the soul which resides in the brain; and through the Tefillin on the arm, a person subjugates his body. For this reason, they are placed opposite the heart, as the heart is the source of desires and thoughts. By this, he will remember the Creator and minimize his pursuit of pleasures. And when he recites the *Shema* and prays in this manner—subjugating his soul to Him—this is what is meant by "complete [acceptance]," etc.

**Furthermore**, he should remember that they [the Tefillin] correspond to the "twelve masters of the eyes" <note>An anatomical/mystical reference to the senses</note> at the head, and the second is in the middle of the body, which is the heart. Therefore, the Torah warned us to "place [them] as a sign upon your hand" opposite the heart, and to incline them toward your eyes to rectify the vision. And likewise, at the time of placing the Tefillin of the head, look at the folds in the stitching of the Tefillin, where one side has a *Shin* <note>The Hebrew letter ש</note> with four heads and the other has a *Shin* with three heads. This alludes to the 613 commandments (*Taryag Mitzvot*). How so? Two *Shins* equal the number 600 <note>Each Shin has a numerical value of 300</note>, and the two [letters] together are one word called "six" (*Shesh*), and the "heads" <note>the prongs of the letters</note> bring the total to 613. The letter *Shin* also alludes to the *Shekhinah* <term>Shekhinah; the Divine Presence or the feminine aspect of God</term>. The four heads correspond to the four "Living Creatures" (*Chayot*) in the Divine Chariot, which are against the four "Proud Ones" <note>Majestic creatures like the lion and eagle</note>, and He is high above all the proud. The three heads correspond to the three Patriarchs, according to the saying: "The Patriarchs are the Chariot." So says the author of *Sefer HaMusar* <note>The Book of Ethics</note> in Chapter 4: "And the secret of Tefillin is deep, who can find it? But I will write a tiny bit of what the Sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> have written. Know that one must enshrine within them the holiness and the revelation of the flow of the secret of the Holy Chariot. After the Temple was destroyed, the holiness and the *Shekhinah* departed, but regarding Tefillin it is said: 'Make for Me a sanctuary and I will dwell within them,' for through them the Holy One, blessed be He, rests His presence in Israel, as they are the secret of the Chariot and the Patriarchs. Therefore, they have a *Shin* of three heads on the right side, corresponding to the Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and on the left side, a *Shin* of four legs/heads for the four 'Living Creatures' that carry the Chariot." This is the summary.

In another way, it is explained why there is a *Shin* in the folds of the head-Tefillin: the reason is to correspond to the merit of Jacob, for *Shin* is the end of the name Jacob <note>In certain mystical letter-permutations</note>, and Jacob is called Israel. It is as if it were written: "The glory of that Israel in whom I will be glorified," and glory belongs on the head. The knot of the Tefillin at the back of the neck corresponds to Isaac... <note>The text continues with complex letter-substitutions/Gematria linking the knot to Isaac and the letter permutations to Abraham</note> Thus, the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note> is present in the Tefillin through the merit of the Patriarchs.

And so says *Ma'arekhet Elokut* <note>The "System of Divinity," a classic Kabbalistic text</note>: The *Shin* of four heads is on the right of the reader, and the *Shin* of three heads is on the left. Together they are seven heads, corresponding to the "Building" <note>the seven lower emanations/Sefirot</note>... The straps hanging down from the knot on either side allude to the influence that comes from the "Head." I have seen those who wrote the measurement of the straps... this is the matter of the head-Tefillin. But as for the hand-Tefillin, its placement is opposite the "Crown" (*Atarah*) to hint that there, everything is unified and all is included in the whole. In that tradition, the four passages are in one single compartment, and therefore it is called a "Bride" (*Kallah*), for it is "included" (*Kelulah*) from the thirty-two paths of Wisdom. It is placed on the hand opposite the heart as a hint to the "Crown" which is called "Hand"... The Torah says, "And it shall be for a sign upon your hand (*yadchah*)," and "sign" (*ot*) refers to the Foundation (*Yesod*), and "hand" to the "Crown." They interpreted the word *yadchah* as "the weak hand" (*yad kehah*) to hint at the left side, for the "Crown" is also called "Left." In general, the placement of the hand-Tefillin is so that there may be peace on earth.

**Corresponding** to these two *Shins*, the author of *Sefer HaMusar* wrote in a gloss: it is proper not to remove them until after the prayer *Kaddish Titkabal* <note>The prayer concluding the main service</note>... so that he rests with the holy Tefillin during the *Kaddish*... corresponding to the *Shin* of three legs... and likewise answers with them the "four sanctifications" corresponding to the *Shin* of four legs on the left side... One should behave with great holiness in them, as the name of the Lord is literally called upon him. Some say on the side of Kabbalah not to remove them until after three or four "Sanctifications," namely after the "Mourner's Kaddish." This is exactly the opposite of what was said in the gloss of *Sefer HaMusar*, and his words would not be feasible according to the custom of the communities who do not say the Mourner's Kaddish after *Aleinu*.

## This is the Language of Tola'at Ya'akov
<note>Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai's Kabbalistic work on the prayer service</note>
Know that these four passages, with their letters, crowns, and borders, allude to the Supreme Wisdom. For this reason, we were commanded to place them in two "dwellings" in the head, which are the heart and the brain <note>Kabbalistically, the arm-Tefillin relates to the "heart" of the head</note>. When they are written properly and placed properly, there is no doubt that their reward is great because their holiness is severe. Therefore, our Sages said: "Regarding those who lift a hand... they are like those who place Tefillin on their faces." This is because Tefillin, as we have written, are the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, the connection of the [divine] forms, and the recognition of the Master of All. All are subjugated to Him, just as a servant is subjugated to his master... By this, He wishes to make His kingdom known... and the heart receives influence from Him to recognize through it the Master of All... And as for those who cast off the yoke, the Sages said they are among those who "deny the Root" <note>i.e., God</note>.

Behold, these letters written on parchment are like the living generations... they are a hint to the entangled levels (**this is the World of Creation**) which are a throne for the Supreme Wisdoms (**which are the World of Emanation/Atzilut**). The letters allude to them, and the way each passage is separated within hints at other levels (**this is the World of Formation/Yetzirah; afterward, the boxes and the gate allude to the World of Action/Asiyah**). For everything cascades one from the other, one being a throne for the other, and the upper is to the lower as a soul is to a body... The "gate" <note>where the straps pass through</note> hints at a reality known to the Sages of Israel... it is to the upper ones like the "shell" (*kelipah*) that surrounds the fruit. For this reason, the law was given to Moses at Sinai that the Tefillin should be wrapped with hair... a hint to Esau, "a hairy man" (*ish sa'ir*). A covering of leather covers everything—this is the physical world of governance felt by us. The twelve [stitches] of the boxes hint at the twelve constellations and the twelve diagonal borders... and the twelve tribes of Israel, above and below. The straps come from the "box" to the knot to show how the world of the elements is tied to the Upper World, and the cascade of influence and providence to it from Him, by the power of the Ruler over all, may He be exalted.

## And these are the words of the Zohar
Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] said, etc.: "Come, and I will tell you a secret that was not given to be revealed except to those high holy ones. Come and see: To this place, which is the spirit of impurity, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave dominion in the world in several aspects, and it can cause harm... and we have a secret: we must give it a place and move it away from our holiness, so that no prosecutor is found within our holiness. For from our very holiness, its dominion emerges. And we need, in the secret of the Tefillin, to hide one hair of a calf that sticks out. And this is what emerges—this hair of impurity—for when that hair is joined and made according to the measure, it does not defile. But we must give it [the impure side] a place so it does not prosecute us... and it should stick out from that hair to the outside and be seen. And when the prosecutor sees this person in supreme holiness, and that its own 'portion' is shared there, it will not prosecute him or be able to harm him above or below, for he has given it a place... But if a person does not do this... it can harm him below and go up and prosecute him above... saying: 'This man did such and such on such a day...' until judgment reaches that man and he is punished by its hand. But when it sees [the hair]... it stays away... This is the secret of the hair... so that no prosecutor is found among them, and they will not come to mention the sins of Israel... for many bands and many camps [of angels] are ready to take a word from it when it comes to prosecute..."

# Tractate Chullin
<note>original: "Masachet Chullin"; while this is the name of a Talmudic tractate, this manuscript acts as a personal compilation of laws and mystical commentary.</note>

To the path of his steps: our Sages, of blessed memory, further stated in the second chapter of Tractate Berachot that it is forbidden for a person to set out on a journey before he prays, as it is written: "Righteousness shall go before him..." <note>Psalm 85:14</note>. "Righteousness shall go before him" means one should pray first. Our Sages also said in the chapter "One who Recites" <note>the second chapter of Berachot</note> that whoever prays and then sets out on a journey, the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills his desires, as it is written: "Righteousness shall go before him." Therefore, every person should accustom himself to reciting verses of mercy before departing. It is also good to study Torah before setting out on a journey, which is hinted at in the words "Righteousness shall go before him," as it is written: "Justice, justice shall you pursue" <note>Deuteronomy 16:20; the word "Justice/Righteousness" is *Tzedek* in Hebrew</note>. We interpret this in Tractate Sanhedrin to mean: "Follow after a righteous court." Upon leaving the city gate, one should say: "O House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord," and "For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever" <note>Micah 4:5</note>, as written by the author of *Tzedah LaDerech* <note>Provision for the Way; a 14th-century work of Jewish law and ethics</note> on page 41, column 1.

The *Chizkuni* <note>a 13th-century Torah commentary by Rabbi Hezekiah ben Manoah</note> wrote on the Torah portion of *Shoftim* <note>Judges</note> regarding the verse "and our eyes did not see": from here we learn that one who accompanies his fellow must stand in his place until the traveler is hidden from his sight. Regarding the ritual of the <term>Eglah Arufah; the "beheaded heifer" ritual performed when a murder victim is found between cities</term>, our Sages greatly emphasized this commandment of accompaniment. Among their words, they said: "Rav Yura said in the name of Rav: Anyone who accompanies his fellow even four cubits within a city prevents him from being harmed." Rashi <note>the preeminent 11th-century commentator</note> explains this refers to the one departing on the journey. They further said that the reward for accompaniment has no fixed measure. Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir: "Anyone who does not accompany another, or allows himself not to be accompanied, is as if he spills blood." Rashi likewise brought this regarding the verse: "Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see..." Could it enter your mind that the elders of the court are murderers? Rather, it means: "We did not see him and then let him depart without food (*mezonot*) and without an escort (*levayah*)." It appears from Rashi's words that he treats "they did not shed" and "they did not see" as one concept, meaning no accompaniment was provided. Thus far the *Chizkuni*. We, however, might have seen him and withheld food and accompaniment from him; had we done so, we would be like shedders of blood. According to what the *Chizkuni* wrote, you should explain "Our hands did not shed" as meaning: "We did what was required of us regarding food, giving him as much as the palm of our hands, and we also fulfilled the commandment of our hands properly," and "our eyes did not see" means they watched him until he was hidden from view. Thus, the commandment of provisioning for the way and the commandment of accompaniment are linked together.

->The version of the prayers for the journey from the book *Nisnas* and *Beit Shmuel* will be brought at length, with God's help, in the section on Prayer.<-

## The Chapter "Lamp of Commandment" is Completed
<note>original: "Ner Mitzvah"; likely a reference to Proverbs 6:23, "For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light."</note>

<margin>The chapter "Torah is Light": the Zohar says "light" has the numerical value of 207 (*Raz* - secret). I also will explain in this chapter the secrets of the commandments mentioned in the chapter "Lamp of Commandment."</margin>

### The Secret of Tzitzit
<term>Tzitzit; ritual fringes worn on four-cornered garments</term>
The word Tzitzit has the numerical value of 603 <note>usually 600, but here based on a specific spelling or tradition</note>, and with eight strings and five knots, it equals 613 <note>the total number of Torah commandments</note>. These correspond to the four corners of the garment for the four directions, acting as a "reminder between his eyes" so that whichever way he turns, he remembers the commandments of the Lord. The five knots of the Tzitzit correspond to the five commandments and transgressions dependent on the ear and the corner. In the second string, there are the two commandments and transgressions dependent on the mouth. In the third string, the swallowing of the esophagus. In the fourth string, the commandments and transgressions dependent on the ear. In the fifth string, the attribute of anger. In the sixth string, the commandments and transgressions dependent on the feet. In the seventh string, the commandments and transgressions dependent on the sense of touch. In the eighth string, the commandments and transgressions dependent on nakedness <note>sexual morality</note>. Therefore, in the inner realm... <note>The text here enters a complex Kabbalistic sequence of letter permutations and divine names including Y-A-H-D-O-N-H-Y, a combination of the Names YHVH and Adonai</note>... The final letter *He* is the *Shechinah* <note>the Divine Presence</note> who completes the Name... a hint to the 613 paths of wisdom. Every single path is divided into two: good and evil, etc. Guard the positive and negative commandments. Each one is comprised of nine <term>Sefirot; divine emanations or attributes</term>... the seven letters of the Torah... there are 613 commandments and the 32 paths return from above and spread out to the Throne... for every "Living Creature" (*Chayah*) of the Throne has four faces and four wings, totaling eight...

...Whoever wraps himself in the cloak of the commandment here prepares a throne for the Holy One, blessed be He. These are the names Y-A-H-D-O-N-H-Y for every side of the wings... they rise to the value of 72... This is "The lion has roared, who will not fear?" <note>Amos 3:8</note>. The wings of the commandment are these: eight strings for every side... a person should not have fewer than seven and should not add more than thirteen... these correspond to the seven days of Creation... "six wings to one" <note>Isaiah 6:2</note>... referring to the 42 divine names in the four heads of the <term>Tefillin; phylacteries</term>... and it is said: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" <note>Deuteronomy 28:10</note>. These are the Tefillin... the Head Tefillin is the crown and glory of the Bride... and the Hand Tefillin... one must call this beauty "Hear O Israel"... these are the five "holy ones" of the Tabernacle... with a blessing... with a clean and whole heart... and the secret of the blue thread (*Tekhelet*) is the attribute of Judgment... see in the "Gate of Holiness"... This commandment is equal to all the commandments. One must intend that the soul is wrapped in the light of the commandment, both below and above, so that the soul which is above will also be wrapped in the light of the commandment... This is the general rule for every commandment a person performs: he must intend that his soul, which is a portion of God from above, is carved with light through that commandment. Therefore, intend this for Tefillin. I heard from my teacher, of blessed memory, that the intention of wrapping oneself in Tzitzit is as our Sages said, that "Tzitzit" equals 613 commandments. The *Shechinah* is in his garments... the secret of the Tzitzit. For the wrapping is for the soul, and one must intend that in his soul there are 248 spiritual organs and 365 spiritual sinews, and all of them shall shine through the commandment of Tzitzit. This is the general rule of Tzitzit. The Tefillin are the "Face of Adam" who sits upon the Throne; thus Tefillin and Tzitzit represent the Name YHWH which is upon the Throne.

### The Secret of Tefillin
Our Sages said that the Holy One, blessed be He, puts on Tefillin. This hints at the attribute of *Tiferet* (Beauty) which is adorned with four lights... the four sections of the scrolls. The "Hand Tefillin" refers to *Malchut* (Kingdom) which is adorned by the Hand of the Lord. Even though we put on Tefillin made of leather (*Or*), in the upper realm they are made of light (*Or*). This is the secret of "And God made for Adam and his wife [garments of light/leather] and clothed them." The four sections of the head Tefillin hint at the Name YHWH (the *Yud* is Wisdom, the *He* is Understanding, the *Vav* leans to the right for Kindness, and the *He* leans to the left for Strength). The four houses of the Tefillin hint at the Name *Eheyeh*. The four sections of the hand hint at the Name YHWH... (see the *Pardes Rimonim* <note>an influential 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Moshe Cordovero</note>). The hand Tefillin has only one house <note>the physical box</note>, but the *Tikunei Zohar* says that one writes two scripts inside it so it contains four "houses" which is the Name *Eheyeh*... The 21 mentions of God's name in the head and hand Tefillin together equal 42, corresponding to the 42-letter Name of God. The knot of the Tefillin hints at the connection of the Kingdom. The right strap reaches the navel... the left strap is for the correction of the "other side" (*Samael*). In the future, we will be clothed in Tefillin of light. My father and teacher said: at the time of tying the straps... one should think in his heart that the Omnipresent commanded us to place these four sections which contain the Unity of His Name and the Exodus from Egypt upon the arm facing the heart and upon the head facing the brain. These are the most important organs in a person, so that we may remember through them the miracles and wonders that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed during the Exodus from Egypt.

# Tractate Chullin
<note>original: "Masachet Chullin"; refers to the laws of "profane" or non-consecrated items, but here used as a title for a section on daily life and mystical holiness.</note>

The hollow <note>likely referring to the armpit or the fold of the arm</note> above looks like the shape of the letter *Shin* (ש). When the left arm is stretched out, we compare it to the shape of the letter *Dalet* (ד). And the covenant of circumcision is in the form of the letter *Yod* (י). Together, these form the name *Shaddai* <note>שדי - Almighty</note>. For those in the world who do not have the circumcision, they only have the letters *Shin* and *Dalet* <note>שד - "Shed," meaning a demon or destroyer</note>. The name *Shaddai* is the Foundation <note>term: "Yesod"; the ninth emanation or Sefirah, associated with the procreative organ</note>, for in the end, all things draw close to the "God of the World." This is the meaning of "He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High" <note>Psalm 91</note>, for "Destruction [Shod] from the Almighty [Shaddai] shall come" <note>Isaiah 13:6</note>—this refers to the Righteous One <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note. It is said that he overcomes the celestial constellations; when the zodiac sign is not productive, He says, "I am God Almighty [El Shaddai], be fruitful and multiply" <note>Genesis 35:11</note>. Thus far his words. We find that the sign of the holy covenant is the letter *Yod*, for the letters *Shin* and *Dalet* without the *Yod* are impure. Through the *Yod*, it becomes *Shaddai*, and the sign is: "The tenth shall be holy" <note>Leviticus 27:32; the letter Yod has the numerical value of 10</note>.

## The Secret
Conducting business in faith <note>original: "Masa u'Matan be'Emunah"; referring to financial integrity</note> means cleaving to His attributes, may He be blessed and exalted. For "the word of the Lord is upright, and all His works are done in faith" <note>Psalm 33:4</note>, and "The Rock, His work is perfect... a God of faith without iniquity" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. Behold, his business dealings contain the secret of "Exchanges" <note>referring to the spiritual movement between different divine attributes</note>, turning from the Attribute of Mercy to the Attribute of Judgment, and from Judgment to Mercy. "The work of His hands the firmament declares" <note>Psalm 19:2</note>—that is to say, it tells that His works are in faith. "Day unto day utters speech, and night unto night..." Behold, the day receives from the night and the night from the day, and they all pay their debts to one another. It is already known that without the Attribute of Judgment, the world could not stand, yet the day operates with the Attribute of Mercy. "Truth and peace" exist between them "without speech and without words"—not like the business dealings of men, in which quarrels and loud voices never cease.

<columns>2</columns>
## The Innerness
The secret of conducting business in faith above: Behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, carries and receives the awakening from below to above, and gives the blessing from above to below. All of this is through "Faith," which is the secret of the attribute of *Malchut* <note>term: "Kingship"; the tenth Sefirah, often called Faith or the Assembly of Israel</note>.

## And If
If a person below conducts business in faith, then he walks in the ways of his Creator. Just as the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is "Truth" <note>Emet</note>, so you find in the creation of the six days of Genesis—which are the working days of business—the seal of Truth <note>Emet - אמת</note> four times, as the commentators have mentioned: 1) In the beginning <note>Ber**e**shit</note> created <note>Bar**a**</note> God <note>Elohi**m**</note> the <note>**Et**; the final letters of these words spell Emet/Truth</note>... [the text lists several verses from Genesis where the final letters of words spell "Truth"]. When one goes to do business, he should say: "I go to fear [God] and to give/receive in faith, for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note>, through that Hidden and Concealed One." And he should pray this prayer:

> ->Lord God of truth, give me blessing and success in all<-
> ->the work of my hands. I trust in You that through this<-
> ->business, You will send me blessing, and the verse<-
> ->shall be fulfilled in me: "Cast your burden upon<-
> ->the Lord, and He shall sustain you."<-

<column-break/>
<margin>from the book *Sefat Emet*</margin>
Of blessed memory: It is written in the book "Prayer for the Straightforward Man": To conduct business, to weigh and measure faithfully—this is *Malchut*, the secret of the Holy Assembly, the seal of Israel. A person should give and take so that everything is done in holiness, and he should not let any profit come from a place of falsehood or from the "Small Ones" <note>referring to external, impure spiritual forces</note> who suckle from such things. His business should be a holy act. Whatever he has in his book <note>account book</note>, the end of the matter will be found in the world of the souls. For this reason, the first judgment of the soul is: "Did you conduct your business in faith?" For faith is the primary sustenance of Israel. One who is not honest with his fellow man will not find faith in the end. Regarding this, "Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac," for though everything was given to him, he swore to him in faith. Because the "heads" <note>leaders</note> do this, those holy children who stand before faith... [the text continues with a complex Kabbalistic explanation of the attributes of Jacob, Isaac, and the "Fear of Isaac" as they relate to integrity]. Therefore, always cleave to faith, for it is the daughter of the King. *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> hovers over the foundation of *Malchut*. Connect the Kingship with the Beauty, and pray to the Lord in His glory... do not return to the "Sitra Achra" <note>the Other Side/Evil</note>... thus far his words.

When he mentions the Name, he should visualize in his mind the name *Yod-He-Vav-He* vocalized with the vowels of the Blessed One. Every point is a *Yod*. The shape of the *Kamatz* vowel looks like a ten <note>a horizontal line and a dot</note>, and the whole thing equals 72 <note>the Name of 72 letters</note>, the value of the Name when spelled out: *Yod-He, Viv-He*. He should think: "He will sustain you" <note>Yechalkelecha</note> which equals 133, the value of the "filling of the filling" <note>a method of gematria where each letter of a spelled-out letter is also spelled out</note>. This is the hint in the verse: "Behold, the Lord [Y-H-V-H] is one." The exodus from Egypt and the "splitting of the sea" <note>Red Sea</note> show that a man's sustenance is as difficult as the splitting of the sea. Therefore, it is good to mention this to provide for his sustenance. He should also think that the vowels of "He will sustain you" equal 127, which is the Name of *Yabbok* <note>יבק - 112; the text may be using a different calculation or including the word</note>, which equals the three names: *Yod-He-Vav-He*, *Adonai*, and *Ehyeh*. This is hinted at in the verse: "May the Lord fulfill all your petitions." "Now I know... He will answer him on the day we call." The name *Yabbok* is inscribed there. "The Lord God is Truth," and conducting business in faith is a true drawing-near to his God.

<columns>1</columns>
## The Secret
Regarding that "Imperialist Lady," the Matron, the Assembly of Israel: they are gathered and unified in a single unity from the side of their souls. they are "Internal," like the palace of the King, blessed be He. It is the city of which it is said, "The Lord is there." But outside of it is the place of the "External Ones" <note>the *Chitzonim*; demonic or shell-like forces</note>, the realm of Esau, the "man of the field." Behold, when a member of Israel leaves the city for the outside, the "hands of the roads" are in a state of danger, and the ministering spirit of Esau is awakened. Therefore comes the commandment of *Levayah* <note>term: "Escorting a traveler"</note>. *Levayah* means "attachment" or a "garland of grace" <note>Proverbs 1:9</note>. The intention is that those remaining in the city escort the one leaving and awaken the "Attachment." It is as if they say: "We are still attached; just as we are residents of the city, so are you like us." Through this, they awaken the Attachment above—that even though the physical bodies are separated, they are attached at their root. Then, when the "Attachment of the Field" is awakened, the one going out is not harmed. The spirit of the field is transformed from the spirit of Esau to the spirit of Isaac—a "Field of Blessing." This is the "Field which the Lord has blessed," the secret of the "Field of Holy Apples" <note>Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin</note>, which our Sages hinted at. From this, the greatness of the commandment of escorting a guest is understood. Therefore, one who walks on the road should always meditate on the blessing of the field. One who turns his heart to idleness forfeits his own soul.

## Now
I will explain the secret of the six days of work. Even though they are "profane days" <note>Yemei chol</note>, they nonetheless come from a holy place. For one who sanctifies himself, they become "Profane items handled in the purity of holiness" <note>a legal concept in the Mishnah</note>. Your sign is that "Tractate Chullin" <note>Profane/Mundane Things</note> follows the order of "Holy Things" <note>Kodashim</note> in the Talmud. A person should always awaken and remember every single day what its root is. Regarding this, it is said: "Remember the days of old" <note>Deuteronomy 32:7</note>. The "Days of Old," the holy ones, are the six supernal attributes <note>the Sefirot</note> about which it is said: "For six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth" <note>Exodus 31:17</note>. It does not say "*In* six days," but "Six days"—meaning He created the days themselves. The Zohar and all the Kabbalists explain that these "six days" *are* the heavens and the earth and their fulfillment. Through their existence, all actions are found. Through the emanation of the six supernal days—which are comprised of Judgment and Mercy, light and darkness, namely: *Chesed* (Kindness), *Gevurah* (Might), *Tiferet* (Beauty), *Netzach* (Victory), *Hod* (Splendor), and *Yesod* (Foundation)—all the works of creation were performed. Six days were made below, and every daily action is performed according to its day, as will be explained at length. The seventh day, the Holy Sabbath, is the seventh attribute <note>Malchut</note>. All six Sefirot rest on the Sabbath. Thus, all days are holy, and the Sabbath is the "Holy of Holies."

In the Zohar, section Yitro: "It is certainly written, 'Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,' and 'You shall be holy for I the Lord am holy,' and 'You shall call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the Lord honorable.'" The condition is that on that day, all the souls of the righteous delight in the pleasures of the "Ancient Holy One" <note>Atika Kadisha; the highest aspect of divinity</note>, the "Concealed of all Concealed." This spirit of delight spreads through all the worlds, ascending and descending, and spreads to all the "holy children," to all the guardians of the Torah. They rest in a perfect rest. All anger, judgment, and hard labor are removed from them. This is what is written: "On the day the Lord gives you rest from your sorrow and your trouble..." thus far his words. This is also written in the "Gate of Holiness": the intention of "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it" is that its holiness depends on our own self-sanctification. Similarly, our Sages said in the Mechilta: "'The children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to *make* the Sabbath'—Rabbi Eleazar ben Parta said: Anyone who keeps the Sabbath is considered as if he *made* the Sabbath." His intention is based on what is explained in the Zohar regarding the verse "And you shall *make* them" <note>referring to the commandments</note>: "Who is it that 'makes' them? It is one who performs the commandments of the Torah... it is as if he made the One Above. The Holy One, blessed be He, says: 'It is as if he made Me.'" For by awakening the higher worlds to connect one to another so that the Holy Name is established properly, it is as if "you made them." By saying "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it," we might think it refers only to its inherent holiness and purity, but regarding the other days, we have no proof we must sanctify them. However, from the verse "You shall be holy" stated generally, the intention is the sanctification of *all* days. He brought the verse "And the holy of the Lord honorable" to teach a comparison... for just as that verse refers to the Sabbath day itself which was sanctified...

# Tractate Chullin

<note>original: "Masachet Chullin"</note>

...so that his sins are not remembered Above and he is not changed for the evil. Thus far his words. Every letter of these sections must be written with the same care, for they resemble a Temple in the secret of the "Chain of Emanation" <note>term: "Seder Hishtalshelut"; the process by which the infinite Divine light descends into the physical world</note>. They are levels close to the Holy where lights are hidden. Regarding the hair <note>A tuft of calf's hair that protrudes from the Tefillin boxes</note>, its reason is like the meaning of a "gate." It follows the verse "the wicked surround the righteous" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>; this gate is part of our holiness because its existence comes from the Holy place. Because of this, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai—may he rest in peace—wrote that the hair should be visible on the outside. When the "Accuser" <note>the prosecuting angel/Satan</note> sees that we include him in our holiness, he departs and does not testify against us. But when he sees we do not care for him, he ascends and accuses, saying: "This person, who uses that holiness, committed such and such sins on that day," and the person is punished through him. The author of the *Worm of Jacob* <note>original: "Tola’at Ya’akov," a 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> writes that the Holy Lamp <note>a title for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> did not reveal to us from which scroll the hair should emerge. I have heard it must come from the section "Sanctify unto Me every firstborn," but I have not heard the reason. I say with awe, fear, and trembling, for that is the place of its existence. (See the book *The Holy Service* <note>original: "Avodat HaKodesh"</note> at the end of page 19). Regarding the secret of the "Garden of God," this refers to the Primordial Serpent. One who is wise will understand that this is the secret of "Conception"—knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain it. Thus far his words. I have received a tradition that the hair should be placed in the section "And it shall come to pass if you listen," which corresponds to Understanding <note>term: "Binah"; the third Sefirah, associated with the source of Divine Judgment</note>, for from Understanding, judgments are awakened. Therefore, it seems right to me to place it near that section on the side facing "Sanctify," to satisfy the opinion of the *Worm of Jacob*.

## The Secret of the Mezuzah
The Recanati <note>Rabbi Menahem Recanati, a 13th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote the reason for this commandment according to its plain meaning: it is known that one serves their Creator in their going out and coming in. According to the "Path of Truth" <note>a common euphemism for Kabbalah</note>, the Mezuzah hints at the "Assembly of Israel" <note>term: "Knesset Yisrael"; the Sefirah of Malchut or the Divine Presence on earth</note> above. Its placement is at the entrances of the gates, as our Sages said: "At that entrance, a servant is placed." They are placed at the entrance of the palaces of the "Powers" to execute judgment in the heavenly family and the earthly family. When the sun shines upon the entrance, all destroyers and damaging spirits flee from before it. This is hinted at in the word **Mezuzah** <note>מזוזה</note>, whose letters can be rearranged to spell *Zaz Mavet* <note>"Death moves away"</note>. There are ten names in the Mezuzah corresponding to the ten Emanations. On the outside edge, the name *Shaddai* <note>Almighty</note> is written, which is the secret of "Shaddai in my chambers" and "He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty" <note>Psalm 91:1</note>. Its placement is at the entrances because the Assembly of Israel is the gate to enter the name of the Lord. Some explain that the gates hinted at in the word "And in your gates" refer to the Fifty Gates of Understanding. You already know from the matter of the Tefillin that the scrolls hint at the attribute of Kindness, and it is hinted in this verse that within these mentioned gates shall be the "Eternal Arms," which are Greatness and Might. Thus far his words. The verse says: "This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it" <note>Psalm 118:20</note>. It is known that the Divine name *Adonai* <note>Lord</note> is the gate to the higher holiness—"O Lord, open my lips." Likewise, the word **Mezuzah** has the same numerical value <note>Gematria</note> as *Adonai* (65). Furthermore, the Aramaic translation of "gate" is *Tar’a*, which matches the full spelling of the name *Adonai* <note>Aleph, Dalet, Nun, Yod</note>.

## The Secret of Circumcision
"And God created man in His image; in the image of God He created him." The head, which houses the brain, the palate, and the tongue, corresponds to the three highest attributes <note>Keter, Chochmah, Binah</note> which are considered as one. The body and the "Covenant of the Organ," which is the conclusion of the body, correspond to Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> and Foundation <note>Yesod</note>. It is called a Covenant... the secret of "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph." The arms correspond to the "Eternal Arms," Greatness and Might <note>Chesed and Gevurah</note>. The thighs are like the two pillars, Jachin and Boaz, corresponding to Victory and Splendor <note>Netzach and Hod</note>. The "Crown" <note>the glans of the organ</note> corresponds to the Sefirah of Crown/Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>, which is the end of the "Building" and receives from all the levels. Through the secret of the "Six" <note>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>, all influences are mixed, and from there they multiply. The Foundation <note>Yesod</note> is the pipe to the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>. Our Sages said the world—which is Malchut—stands on one pillar, and its name is "The Righteous One" <note>Tzadik/Yesod</note>. From there, the influence descends for good or for ill, according to the preparation of those who receive it. "From my flesh, I shall see God" <note>Job 19:26</note>. There are two openings in the organ: one to provide the seed drawn from the brain to give birth in holiness and purity, and the second for the removal of waste. So too it is in the "Covenant Above," as explained in the *Orchard of Pomegranates* <note>original: "Pardes Rimmonim" by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of Pipes," chapter four. "The wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:8</note>—this refers to the external forces that demand "Give! Give!" And "darkness covers the earth"—this is the foreskin <note>Orlah</note>. Therefore, one is commanded to cut it. One who circumcises but does not uncover the crown <note>term: "Milah" and "Peri'ah"</note> is as if he did not circumcise at all, for one must reveal the power of the "Crown." Then he is "complete," as it is written: "Walk before Me and be complete" <note>Genesis 17:1</note>. Also, in the "uncovering of the uncovering," the foreskin is brought near to holiness, like the left hand that pushes away and the right hand that draws near. This is the secret of the "shattering of the vessels" <note>the Kabbalistic concept of "Shevirat HaKeilim," where sparks of holiness fell into the husks of evil</note>... they shall bow and fall, and give honor to His name... until the Crown is revealed, the "Crown of Beauty of Israel," with the point of Zion in the secret of the Altar. The merit of this is the "awakening of the man and his wife" in the secret of the Sign and the Covenant of Foundation. One must prepare a chair for the "Angel of the Covenant," who is Elijah, and say with his mouth: "This is the chair of Elijah." May it be His will that he be revealed to us speedily in our days, Amen and Amen.

And those who see the King’s face in beauty said that a man should say, when he comes to offer his son as a sacrifice to the Lord: "Happy is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts" <note>Psalm 65:5</note>. They know they should be modest and that they will be brought into the "Holiness of Your Temple." 
<gloss>Circumcision hints at the "Court"</gloss> 
<margin>The *Worm of Jacob* wrote</margin> 
that this is the first level, and "Jerusalem" indicates this attribute. It mentions "Your court" first, then "Your house," then "Your temple." This is because it is said, "He who remains in Zion and he who is left in Jerusalem." Regarding "Your house," it is said, "With wisdom a house is built," which is the "House of the World." "Your temple" implies the "Palace," which is the perfection of the upper and lower worlds. One level is completed, totaling ten "canopies" that the Holy One will make for the righteous in the World to Come. Therefore, in this verse, there are seven words: *choose, bring near, dwell, Your courts, satisfied, goodness, Your house*. <note>Translator's note: the text lists words to reach a count of ten</note>... "The holiness of Your temple" makes ten words. One who does not say this excludes himself from them. Therefore, one should be careful regarding the cutting and the uncovering. Circumcision and uncovering <note>Milah and Peri’ah</note> correspond to the Covenant Above which awakens the world, and the "Crown," the "great crown of gold." There are 100 "husks" <note>term: "Kelipot"</note> in the foreskin, one upon the other, corresponding to the three husks that surround the Covenant... King David said of them: "In the name of the Lord I will cut them off" <note>Psalm 118:10</note>, mentioned three times. The circumcision cuts the husk, and the "uncovering" reveals the Crown and the secret of the "Flowing Myrrh." These are the "stormy wind," the "great cloud," and the "flashing fire" <note>Ezekiel 1:4; the three impure husks</note>. This matter involves clearing the thorns from around the Lord of Hosts. Then the "vineyard of delight" answers her, and she "removes her widow’s garments." The harsh forces are removed... Therefore it says "And I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant." By this, Israel is assured they will search the King’s hidden treasures in the innermost chambers. For this reason, we bless "to bring him into the covenant of Abraham our father," for as long as one is not circumcised, they do not enter the holy faith. One who offers his son for this sacrifice is as if he builds an altar and offers all the sacrifices upon it. This is what is written: "An altar of earth you shall make for me." For this reason, we practice throwing the foreskin into the dust. So it is found in the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer: for all forty years Israel was in the desert, they did not perform the "uncovering" because of the exhaustion of the journey. When they would circumcise, they would take the foreskin and hide it in the dust. From that time on, they would place the foreskin in the dust. Know that there are specific messengers appointed over the "Blood of the Covenant"; they take it and place it in a specific palace among the six palaces of the King. In a time of Divine anger, He looks upon that blood, and the Accuser departs from there, and the Holy One has mercy on Israel. Know that the foreskin is the portion of the "Known Prince" <note>likely Samael</note> in that sacrifice. When he sees this is his portion, he is humbled and has no power to accuse; he ascends and speaks in defense of Israel. Secrets upon secrets are hidden in the treasuries of Wisdom. Regarding the reason for placing the foreskin in the dust, the Holy Lamp <note>RSBY</note> asked Elijah of blessed memory, and he replied: "I heard in the Heavenly Academy that the foreskin is the Serpent, and since we remove him from his place, we must give him his food, as it is written: 'And dust shall be the serpent’s food'" <note>Isaiah 65:25</note>.

## The Secret of the Blessing of Circumcision
"Who sanctified the beloved from the womb": This refers to our father Isaac, who was called "beloved" before he even entered the world. The "pangs of birth" were beloved by the Holy One, so that Sarah would not conceive and Isaac would not be born until Abraham our father became "perfect" through the secret of the Sign of the Holy Covenant. How wonderful are the ways of the Holy One! For He caused Ishmael to be born before Abraham was circumcised; therefore, Ishmael's place is the foreskin below in the "depths of the sea." But Isaac was born in holiness, and he is one of the legs of the Holy Chariot—the chariot of "He who rides the ancient heavens." For this reason, he is called "beloved," and He "placed the law in his flesh." The foundation of "law" <note>term: "Chok"</note> is the place of separation which is Holy, and from there onwards is "profane." This is the secret of "cutting," and from there onwards is the secret of the foreskin. This is the "law" placed in the flesh of the beloved to be sealed in the realm of Truth. "And his offspring He sealed with the sign of the holy covenant"—the small letter *Yod*. This means the extension of the letter *Vav*, which is the small *Yod*. Therefore, as a reward for this, "This is the sign of the covenant." This is the secret of "With *this* <note>Zot</note> shall Aaron come into the Holy." And from whom was *this*? From the "Living God," who is the "Life of the Worlds." He is the Law, the Treasurer, and He is our portion, our redeemer, and our rock. We are messengers for our God to save the "beloved" and the "holy friend" who does not descend... to say that the circumcised person does not descend to Gehenna <note>Hell</note>. This is the secret of the "vineyard of delight"... a "well of distress, a foreign woman, a narrow pit, there is no water in it." But snakes and scorpions are in it. Yet everyone marked with the Seal of the King is saved from it, because he is the portion of the Righteous One who inherits the land—the "Land of Life," the secret of the "Pleasantness" Above. Therefore: "And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever." Thus far his words. In the glosses of the *System of Divinity* <note>original: "Ma'arekhet Elokut"</note>, it explains: Why do we bless in the circumcision blessing "and his offspring He sealed with the sign of the holy covenant"? This is the explanation: because the letter *Shin* (ש) is the head of a man, and the letter *Khaf* (כ)... and his legs are standing...

# Tractate Chullin

<note>original: "Masachet Chullin"</note>

### Folio 118
### Section 32, Part 2
<meta>catchword: And behold</meta>

The verse explains **"Holy am I"** <note>Leviticus 19:2</note>; its intention is that hands should not be distracted during the sanctification [Kiddush], for the Sabbath is the root of all holiness. Therefore, it brings a teaching that at this time [the Sabbath], the **souls of the righteous** delight in the Soul of the **Ancient Holy One** <note>original: "Atika Kadisha"; the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine in Kabbalah</note>, the most hidden of all hidden things. It says that "Remember" and "Observe" <note>The two versions of the Sabbath commandment in the Ten Commandments</note> are both joined, and after this, holiness spreads to all things. Therefore, on the Sabbath, it is holy of itself, not just through my own sanctification, as stated in the *Tikkunim* <note>original: "Tikkunei Zohar"</note> on page 10 and in the *Mechilta*.

The phrase **"Holy am I"** means "I am holy" because of the word spoken in the discourse I transcribed in the chapter of the *Pardes* <note>original: "Sefer HaPardes Rimmonim" by Moshe Cordovero</note>. Happy is the one who decrees these; they are one holiness. If not, it is not sanctified. Regarding the phrase **"I am holy,"** even among those who serve stars <note>term: "Oveid Kochavim"; a common term for idolaters or heathens</note>, if they do not sanctify it, they are found to be damaging the structure. From his words, it is clear that a person is obligated to sanctify the Sabbath because there are "sanctified hands."

So too in the *Zohar* [on page 30], it says that all those six days of the week find their sustenance from this [seventh] day. The word **"Holy, Holy"** mentioned there means that they are invited and found within this secret. And since we have already joined the side of holiness, the "Other Side" <note>term: "Sitra Achra"; the realm of evil or impurity</note>—which is the "husk" <note>term: "Kelipah"</note>—cannot take hold of the holy spark of the **Holy One of Israel**. All those who occupy themselves with sanctification and the beauty of the Sabbath find that all six days are rectified.

Come and see: words of holiness shine in this manner. All those six days of the Sabbath <note>referring to the workdays that surround the Sabbath</note> are called the "Other Side" when they are not elevated by the "Point." But when the Point [the Sabbath] stands and is filled, they all dwell within the "Living of Worlds" <note>original: "Chai Ha-Olamim"; a name for the Sefirah of Yesod or the Divine source of life</note>, the place of the **Shekhinah** <note>term: "Shekhinah"; the Divine Presence as it dwells in the world</note>. These days are called "secular" [workdays], but they stand to be blessed forever. Now that the Point and the beauty of the Sabbath exist for Israel, this holiness ascends without being shamed.

It is written that these are the six days of Creation, and after them the secular days, which stand and look toward the Holy One for eternity. First, there are **39 labors** [forbidden on Sabbath] which correspond to the **39 curses** that were cursed upon Adam, Eve, and the Serpent. If not for the sin, the Ark would not have needed to descend to this lowliness, which requires renewal and change. One must have a "good eye" for receiving and guarding the boundaries, the positive and negative commandments, on a spiritual level, as it will be in the future after the Restoration [Tikkun].

When Adam fell into the "husks" and was destroyed by the labors, he was given the power to "Guard" and "Remember." These are the two pillars that sustain the world from the six external days. The leadership of the world during the six days is through **Metatron** <note>The supreme angel who governs the natural world</note>, who is called the "Prince of the World." Even though I have "now come" <note>referring to a verse in Joshua 5:14</note>, meaning he had to receive the leadership, in the future, it will be different. During the six workdays, the leadership is through the **Seraphim** <note>A high rank of angels</note>.

In the *Zohar* [Parshat Bereishit, page 40], it says: "For a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" <note>Ecclesiastes 10:20</note>. The "voice" includes the six secular days, and the soul draws from it. This is a hint to the secret of the "Central Pillar" <note>The middle path of the Sefirot</note>. So they said that the "eyes" are fixed upon the Sabbath and the secular day. The Sabbath and the secular day are not as distant as we once thought. In the discourse on *Parshat Vayikra*, they said there is "secular" even in the world of **Atzilut** <note>term: "Atzilut"; the highest of the four worlds, the World of Emanation</note>, but it is only the "external" part of it.

On the Sabbath, it is said "He rested and was refreshed" <note>original: "Vayinaphash"; Exodus 31:17</note>, referring to the soul. In the *Tikkunim*, it says that the six days are the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil**, which is Adam as he was first created. Before he slept, he was given power and paths. This should be understood simply: he is the leader of the six secular days from the inside, while the external days are on the outside. This is the reward for the Sabbath.

After the restoration, it will be in the secret of the "six days of the Sabbath." All angels and all prayers will be joined to every soul. Anyone who works and completes their reward is like the one who receives the prize. The "secular" days are the six [lower Sefirot] of the Queen. During the six days of work, there is the service of prayer, which is "work." However, on the Sabbath, these three—Atzilut, prayer, and the Kingdom—are one. It is explained that prayer is "Righteousness" [Tzedek] and "Goodness" [Tov].

<column-break/>

This means that the "External Ones" <note>The outer spiritual forces or angels</note> are sanctified by the light of the holiness of **Atzilut**, which is entirely holy and has no flaw. If Israel had listened and drawn holiness into the six lower days, they would be sanctified. Then the Sabbath, which is the "Inner Tenth," is holy even though it is "closed" during the six workdays. Israel draws from the light of the six Sefirot in Atzilut to sanctify what is secular.

Even though we say it is the secret of the six days, it does not mean that the inner Atzilut is not equal in its light and splendor to the Sabbath. Rather, the Upper Light is hidden within. It is in the "Seat of Mercy" [Chesed], which is in the inner palace.

**These matters** require further explanation. To clarify, let us bring this verse: **"The Sabbath is holy"** <note>Exodus 31:14</note>. I have called it Sabbath. Also, an oath is called "Sabbath," as it says: "Until the morrow of the seventh Sabbath shall you count" <note>Leviticus 23:16</note>, which the Targum <note>The Aramaic translation</note> renders as "after the seventh week." The explanation is that every living thing derives its power from its source. Before it arrived here, it was all under the name of "Sabbath." Rabbi Isaac said: "Do not let it be a clear resting place, for it requires seven levels of protection." It was all called by the name "Sabbath."

The *Pardes* elaborated on this in the "Gate of Days," noting that the Sabbath day is the **Central Point** upon which the circle of the six days revolves. It is called the "Inner Middle Point" in every point. It has six "extremes" [directions], as we shall explain. The point stands beneath the sphere of the moon and from there onward. This is the power:

<image-desc>A circular diagram divided into eight sectors by radial lines. Each sector contains a Hebrew letter: clockwise from the top pole are א, ב, ג, ד, ה, ו, ז, ח (Aleph, Bet, Gimel, Dalet, He, Vav, Zayin, Chet). The radial lines meet at a central point. Two vertical lines intersect the top and bottom poles of the circle.</image-desc>

The letter Aleph (א) is the upper extreme, and so on. Every extreme has a space [void] and an angle, but the **Middle Point** has no "partner" or "pair." Therefore, it is unique. All the voids, which are the extremes, draw from it and are filled by it. All the flow comes from the Point. The extremes are "secular" [workdays], and the Point is the "Holy."

So too, the **Great Sabbath**, which is **Binah** <note>term: "Binah"; the Sefirah of Understanding, often called the "Divine Mother"</note>, is the "Sabbath Point." Through the power of all the extremes, they draw from it. It is their root, and it fills them all. From it, they are all emanated. Therefore, the verse says: **"Those who profane it [the Sabbath] shall surely be put to death"** <note>Exodus 31:14</note>.

The word for "profane" [mechalel] is related to the word for "void" or "hollow" [chalal]. One who treats the Point (which is unique and holy) as if it were just the extremes makes it a "void." The extremes receive their portions and their "secular" nature from it. If one "hollows" it out, they shall die.

When the Sabbath emerges, the Point goes out with the extremes. The Sabbath with its extremes is called the "Sabbath of the World" after its emanation. But when it was hidden within the power of Binah before its emanation, it was called the "Secular Sabbath" and the "Point of All Things." This means even its extremes were in the secret of the Point.

The Point is the "Innermost." Without the Middle Point, you cannot find the six extremes [North, South, East, West, Up, Down]. You cannot draw a measure or imagine six directions—Up, East, West, North, South—if you do not first imagine a Middle Point from which the lines emerge to the boundaries. If you do not have a point, you cannot imagine the circle that includes the six extremes. From the Point, the "thread of everything" emerges.

The extremes are called **"voids"** [hollows] because they are the spaces between things. But the Point itself is not part of the extremes; it is their source. The extremes are the "branches." The extremes are called "hollows" because they have a "pair" or an "opposite"—Up has Down, East has West, South has North. But the Point is unique; it has no pair and no void at all. It is always full of the flow of the "Great Good."

One who "profanes" the Sabbath makes it a "void" in the Crown. This person prevents the flow of life, food, and sustenance from reaching the extremes. By doing "work" [melacha] on the Sabbath, they change the Sabbath into a secular day. Because they have made the Sabbath a "void" [chalal], their own body becomes a "void" [chalal]—a corpse—when the soul departs. This is the meaning of **"Those who profane it shall surely be put to death."**

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic concept of the Sabbath as the "Middle Point" or spiritual source of the six days of the week. It uses a geometric metaphor to argue that "profaning" the Sabbath (Mechalel) literally means creating a "void" (Chalal) by severing the world from its Divine life-source.</summary>
