<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Sabbath, specifically focusing on the metaphysical mechanics of how the Divine "finished" creation and how the Sabbath acts as a source of energy for the following week. It transitions from the previous page's discussion on the holiness of the body and Tefillin into the structural arrangement of the Sephirot (Divine emanations).</meta>

# Tractate Chullin

### Page 149
->**Tractate Chullin**<-
<meta>catchword: In the six</meta>

From all the work... the Worker through the seventh day. This is the meaning of: "And God finished on the seventh day His work which He had done." When He completed it and brought forth the time of the chosen dominion of the Lord, they all rested in the "dwelling of the secret." "And He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done." After the Messenger had completed His mission and arranged His work, He gave "his reward on his day." This is the secret of: "And God blessed the seventh day." 

He opened the "line of light" and caused it to flow upon it until it became a **pool** <note>The Hebrew word for blessing, *Berakhah*, is etymologically related to *Breichah*, a pool or cistern—implying the Sabbath is a reservoir of spiritual energy.</note> to water from there all the created beings that He created to sustain them. "And He sanctified it"—this is the language of **betrothal** <note>term: "Kiddushin"; the legal act of marriage/sanctification. The Sabbath is mystically "married" to the People of Israel.</note>. The Assembly of Israel was given to the Sabbath as its mate. 

For on it He rested, and it has already been said, "He shall rest on the seventh day." However, the rest is mentioned twice to say that within everything created in the first six rotations <note>original: "galgalim"; cycles or spheres of creation</note>, all the **Divine Personas** <note>term: "Partzufim"; the kabbalistic configurations of the Sephirot into "faces" or personas</note> were included. In all of this, the seventh day sent out the six days, and they rested within it upon the completion of the entire "Face." From then on, "there is nothing new," only the increase and expansion of the "Face" through the rotation and combination of letters. This is "bone of bone" and "being from being." All this is expounded by the power of the seventh day to act from that point forward. Also from this matter, they all rested on the seventh day, and this is the secret of "for on it He rested." From what was the rest? The text explains: "from all His work which God created to do" from then on. There is no new power or innovation from the Messenger, who was the ruler by the authority of the Sender and His power; this is its secret.

**From now on**, the verse is well explained: "That which has been is what shall be, and that which has been done is what shall be done, and there is nothing new under the sun" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:9</note>. For the first six days and the five **Sephirot** <note>term: "Sephirot"; the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite interacts with the universe</note> that sustained every existence brought everything from potential to actual creation day by day through the Sephirah of **Kingship** <note>original: "Malchut"; the final, feminine Sephirah that manifests Divine will into reality</note>. There they rested from their work, as it is written, "and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed." Through the Sephirah of Kingship, the creation of the six days emerged into action, and there also remained in potential that which is prepared to be done throughout the duration of the world’s existence, from the moment of grace until the hour of action. 

That is to say, "In the beginning," which is the "Is" <note>The Hebrew "Hoveh" refers to the present or ongoing state of being</note>, refers to the forms of what is fit to be. This power and the forms of their desire emerged from His Mind, and from there they went out during the six days and became actualized, hinted at by the first six days. It is found that the work of Being is the "Point," and the six days are the "Extremities" <note>In Kabbalah, the six directions (North, South, East, West, Up, Down) correspond to the six emotional Sephirot</note>. Afterward, this light expanded and became actualized, and then returned to its source in the Sephirah of Kingship, which is the Sabbath. Afterward, it returns and goes out to be actualized in the fifty days, and returns to its source, and so on in a cycle for their life. 

Everything is well-selected and precisely detailed as an obligation to perform, for "that which was done is what shall be done." It turns out all the "work days" are branches of the Sabbath, which is Kingship. Therefore, the **Divine Presence** <note>term: "Shekhinah"; the indwelling presence of God in the world, associated with the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> is also called "Sabbath." Our masters wrote that during the Afternoon Prayer [Mincha] of the Sabbath, it is proper to perform repentance so that the "Living Beings" return to their source purified of all sin, for they return to the Sabbath. The branches are always cycling; they emerge from the Sabbath, return to the Sabbath, emerge and return—thus they cycle and are renewed. They are the "Act of Creation," for "that which was is what shall be." This is the meaning of "He who renews every day the Act of Creation"—they are the Act of Creation and they are renewed. 

It is clear to you that every single Sabbath has a unification with the week that passed and with the week that is coming. This is the matter of the Priests in their **watches** <note>term: "Mishmarot"; the rotating groups of Priests who served in the Temple</note> who would work on the Sabbath day as two watches: the outgoing watch and the incoming watch. 

It was further explained that what was created and every Sabbath is a "Point," and the six are "Extremities" after the **Great Sabbath** <note>term: "Shabbat HaGadol"; refers here to the Sephirah of Binah (Understanding), the higher source of the Sabbath</note> which is the Sephirah of **Understanding** [Binah]. There, the six upper Extremities were hidden, and their nature was Understanding itself. The second is the Sephirah of Kingship [Malchut], from which the six lower Extremities expand in the order of the "Chain of Emanation." The perfection is the Point. The Great Sabbath is called the "World to Come," and this Sabbath is called the "This World" by comparison. 

However, regarding what the verse says, "those who keep My Sabbaths" [plural], and the Sages said: "If only Israel would keep two Sabbaths..." <note>A famous Talmudic teaching from Shabbat 118b: "If Israel kept two Sabbaths correctly, they would be immediately redeemed."</note>—this does not refer to the Great Sabbath, but to the world of action. But it is possible, and the matter will also be explained from what is found in the Zohar and the books of the Kabbalists: sometimes they call **Foundation** [Yesod] "Sabbath," and sometimes they call Kingship [Malchut] "Sabbath." It will also be explained why they sometimes say "the six days of creation" and sometimes "the seven days of creation." Behold, "these and those are the words of the Living God." 

It has already been explained that every Sephirah "rests" upon the revelation of the Sephirah after it, for then it rests from its initial activity. So too the second in the third, and the third in the fourth, and so on for all of them. At the beginning of the "Building" from Understanding [Binah], the days of work end at Foundation [Yesod], and thus Foundation is "Sabbath." But when you start from **Kindness** [Chesed], then the seven days of work end at Kingship [Malchut], and thus Kingship is "Sabbath." 

And so it is written in *The Holy Service* <note>original: "Avodat HaKodesh"; a seminal work by Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai</note> at the end of the chapter on the "Secrets of the Torah": However, the resolution of the matter is this: because the Building reaches until Foundation, and it is considered prepared for action from the "Right Hand" downward, and the seventh to the Building from Understanding downward, in it the Building is completed. I have already written that it is "She" [Kingship] and "He" [Foundation] that shine as one, and both are a "Sabbath unto the Lord." She is the "glory of the night" and He is the "glory of the day," and everything together is called Sabbath, "Remember" and "Observe" in a single utterance. Therefore it is written "Between Me and the children of Israel, it is [He/She] a sign" <note>Exodus 31:17. The Hebrew text notes a difference between the written form (*hi* - she) and the spoken form (*hu* - he) to hint at this mystical union</note> to indicate unifications. 

And so wrote *The Tailor* <note>original: "HaChayat"; likely referring to the kabbalistic work *Ma'arekhet Ha-Elohut* or its commentary by Joseph Hayyat</note>: "When you begin the count from Understanding [Binah], then Foundation [Yesod] is the Sabbath... and then it is also the Eighth." But there is another way of counting, which is the first I mentioned, starting from Kindness [Chesed]. According to this, the "Crown" [Atarah/Malchut] is also Sabbath because it is the seventh. The verse says, "on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed." Therefore, there are "two Sabbaths" corresponding to "Remember" and "Observe." From this, the intention of the Sages is known when they said, "If Israel kept two Sabbaths according to their laws..." and the verse says to the eunuchs "who keep My Sabbaths." The language of "Observe" [Shamor] is used for the "Salt" <note>Possibly a scribal error for "Malchut" (Kingship) or a metaphor linking preservation to salt</note>. 

The difference between these two ways of counting comes according to the context. Regarding the power of "Thought," which gives power to everything, we count from Understanding. But regarding the beginning of "Action," we count from Kindness, for "the world is built on Kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>. This is hinted at in what is said here regarding the Sephirot of Understanding: "and from there is the beginning to count all that is hidden and deep," meaning the thing that is still in Thought, hidden and quiet. 

Do not be surprised by this, for we find similarly that there is a "First in Thought" and a "First in Action." In the Book of the Zohar regarding the selling of Joseph, it says that even though Reuben was the firstborn in action, nevertheless, because he was not the firstborn in thought at the time of conception (for Jacob was thinking of Rachel), therefore the birthright went to Joseph, the firstborn of Rachel, for he was the firstborn in thought at the time of conception. So too here: from Understanding and above is the World of Thought and Impression; from Greatness [Chesed] and below is the World of Action and Engraving. If so, it is fitting that according to this intention, we begin the count from it [Understanding], and then the seventh to it will be Foundation—the "True Seventh." It is also fitting that the Crown [Malchut] should be Sabbath since it is the seventh to Action. 

These are the "Two Sabbaths," and they are one Sabbath, for the day is "Day and Night," "Remember" and "Observe" in a single utterance. Understanding, which is the "Great Sabbath," is the World to Come and is prepared. Regarding the two Sabbaths below, which are Foundation and Kingship, it is said "those who shall keep My Sabbaths."

**And regarding this**, the saying was explained: "The Sabbath said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: To everyone You gave a mate..." This statement was said by Foundation [Yesod], which is also called Sabbath, in which the six attributes (which are the seven days of creation from Understanding onwards) rest. Behold, in this calculation where we count from Understanding onwards, the Act of Creation is completed in Foundation. Therefore, Foundation said: "I have no mate like these six," as explained above in the gloss in the name of **Recanati** <note>term: "Rekanti"; Rabbi Menachem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist</note>, that each one rests through the Sephirah that follows it in the Act of Creation. 

And if you say it is a virtue for Foundation to remain a solitary "Point" in this totality—that is not so, for the Point that includes the six Extremities above is Understanding, and below it is Kingship. One must not remove even the "Mate" regarding the Act of Creation, like the six that are from Understanding and onwards. To this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, replied: "The Assembly of Israel is your mate," which is the attribute of Kingship [Malchut]. For you and she are a single point within the circle, like the secret of the attribute of "Night and Day," and everything is then "Remember" and "Observe" in a single utterance. The Point is the totality and shines...

<column-break/>

...from His work and gave rest within it. Therefore the seventh day is called "Sabbath." Since he knew that all perfections reach the soul according to the acquisition of wisdoms and their perfections... and so all of them until the end of the seventh, which is the Sabbath for all of them. For when all the powers of action—which are entrusted to bring forth from potential to the actual—completed their task, the Soul rested in action, having brought out the "general light" into action. 

There is no action after these seven days that was not already hidden within them and joined to them from the first day until the time of its revelation to the world in action. Our Sages of blessed memory said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Angel Gabriel: "Go and sign..." <note>A reference to a Midrash where Gabriel is commanded to mark the righteous and the wicked</note>. He said before Him: "Master of the Universe, it is already known and prepared from the seven days of creation..." etc. 

The language used is that it was "prepared from the seven days of creation" to swallow its creator. The hour and everything was decreed from the seven days of creation, as Jeremiah said (peace be upon him): "If these laws depart from before Me..." <note>Jeremiah 31:35</note>, meaning that compared to the making of the heavens and the earth, no word shall fail from You. Within the power of the word is nothing but the purpose of the Foundation, and this is "it was already done and finished," meaning the perfection of the building to make the fruit. 

Everything was prepared for its time to be revealed in action. For there is no "new thing" that has been renewed; it is only the power of the Kingship [Malchut] received from the Source of Life and from the Fountain that blesses all the generals in power and time. At every moment, in its light, it was in action; otherwise, the world would not be sustained. He, in His goodness, renews every day, always, the Act of Creation. This was with the secret of the "Complete Reward" <note>Ruth 2:12</note>, the attribute of His goodness... until the end of the verse. Thus far from the Rabbi, the **RK"N** <note>Abbreviation for Rabbi Menachem Recanati</note>.

# Tractate Chullin

### Page 149
->**Tractate Chullin**<-

And behold, it is necessary to clarify according to what I wrote: that you considered a single point without a pair. In the Midrash <note>referring to Midrash Rabbah on Genesis</note> it is said that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave her a mate. For it is taught there: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: The Sabbath said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Master of the Universe! For everyone You gave a mate, but for me You did not give a mate." The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to her: "The Assembly of Israel shall be your mate." And since...

Also, an explanation is needed regarding the essence of how the six workdays "suck" <note>term: "yonkim"; a kabbalistic term for drawing spiritual sustenance or energy</note> from the Sabbath. For this, I must first present an explanation from the parts of the "Secrets of the Torah" regarding the Holy Service. This is its version: I have written that the "Lower Elohim" <note>original: "Elohim shel mata"; refers to the Shekhinah or the final Sephirah, Malchut, which manifests the physical world</note> is the secret of the final letter **Heh** [ה] of the Name. He created, acted, and made the lower heavens and earth and all their hosts. This is the "Beginning," for she is the "Afterbirth" <note>A metaphor for the physical world being the result of the higher spiritual emanations</note> of the upper realms. This is the secret of: "These are the chronicles of the heaven and the earth when they were created" [*be-hibare'am*]. In Genesis Rabbah, Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rabbi Levi: "When they were created" [*be-hibare'am*]—He created them with the letter **Heh** [ה]. This alludes to the final **Heh**, for just as this letter is written small in the word *be-hibare'am* <note>In the Torah scroll, the letter Heh in this word is written smaller than the other letters</note>, she is called "Small Rachel" <note>term: "Rachel haktana"; a kabbalistic persona representing a specific state of the Shekhinah</note>.

And the "Upper Elohim" brought forth and emanated the Upper World through the "Beginning"—the world of separation—while the lower heavens and earth and their hosts were created as we wrote. To hint at these two creations and worlds, the letter **Bet** [ב] appears in the word *Bereshit* (In the beginning) <note>The letter Bet has the numerical value of two</note>; it is "Two Beginnings," as we have already hinted.

To complete the work of the Holy Service, I saw fit to write the tradition of the Sages of Truth <note>term: "Chachmei HaEmet"; a traditional title for Kabbalists</note> regarding this lower, tangible creation. I say that when God created the heavens and the earth, they were formed and stood before Him simultaneously, they and their hosts, as it is said: "I call to them, they stand together." All the generations and hosts and the "day" were all within the six workdays. In that first standing of the **sphere** <note>original: "galgal"; refers to the celestial spheres or cycles of time</note>, they went from potential to actual. In one movement, a certain action; in the second movement, a certain action; and so on until the completion of the third in six movements.

Behold, in the reality of days, there is only "one day" that rolled from the first movement, born in twenty-four hours according to the division of the **twelve diagonals** <note>term: "yod-bet alchansoniot"; a concept from the Book of Creation referring to the twelve boundaries of the universe</note>. These are included in twelve others, for the "Giver" returns to being the "Receiver," and the "Receiver" becomes the "Giver"; the front becomes the back and the back the front; the sun becomes the right and the right becomes the left. In this manner, the movements were established in perfection within twenty-four hours: twelve and twelve for the night. This is a balanced calculation, even according to what **Nachmanides** <note>original: "Ramban"; the 13th-century scholar Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman</note> said in the portion of *Bereshit*: that their existence was for one moment, yet it had the form of a twelve-hour measure. However it may be, only one day was initially created and renewed, born from the first movement.

Behold, from then until now, in every single movement, a day is created and renewed, continuing from the movement. In the first six days, all the roots of things went from potential to actual. On the seventh day, no new action was renewed other than the movement itself. All movements that came after them are renewed one by one. Six days have never existed simultaneously in reality; rather, when this one is born, that one exists. But what was created on the third day remains present without the absence of what came before. This is not the case with the reality of days, for they do not exist as one; yesterday and today never exist together, only one day at a time. This is the meaning of: "And it was evening and it was morning, one day."

The generations and their renewal in the spheres touch their end to their beginning and their beginning to their end. For this day is born and composed of the essence of the movements of the **ten spheres**, and though they differ in their movements, they are unified in the reality of this day. Because the combination and rotation of the **letters** through which heaven and earth were created return and rotate, cycle after cycle, and are inverted in every rotation, we see only one day. Just as the combinations of letters reach thousands and tens of thousands, and so too the drawing of their forms, so are these spheres and time. Every rotation creates and births "that day" in light and creation.

However, in the first six rotations, all the roots of things were brought to fruition by clothing "forms" in spiritual and physical "bodies." In the **seventh rotation**, no new body was renewed to clothe those forms that remained "naked." For the seventh rotation and combination produced the "Side of Holiness" for the "Free World" <note>original: "Olam haChofshi"; a mystical state of liberation and holiness</note>, which is distinct from the profane. The renewal of its rotation is the extension of holy forms and holy services. These are afterward clothed in bodies that were extended from the power of the six workdays.

The fifth sphere was... and became a partner with him through peace. These are the ten aspects of the... the ten spheres for all six "beloveds," their end touching their beginning and their beginning... twelve diagonal boundaries, and their end twelve diagonal boundaries. That day existed with light and darkness for twenty-four hours. This is the **First Day**, chosen from the power of all **Ten Crowns** <note>term: "Keterim"; here referring to the ten Sephirot</note>. Through them, twenty-four letters were established, and those letters combine in the unity of all the Crowns into thousands and tens of thousands. From the power of these combinations, the ten spheres take their strength, and from them is drawn the "day" composed of twenty-four hours.

Similarly, from every combination of the twenty-two letters established in the twelve Crowns—and I have already written above that six of them shine—it is only that each day is perceived through them. For they are thoughts in relation to the Seven. The "Clothers," which are the "Wings," and the "Distressors" <note>original: "metzarim"; often referring to forces of limitation or the 'husks'</note> are held from the start of the Seven and below. Therefore, the **Holy Light** <note>original: "HaMaor HaKadosh"; referring to the Zohar</note> said in the portion of *Terumah* that the beginning of the repair was from the foundation of the "Right Level," which includes all the Crowns. He drew its form in the tenth, lowest Crown, and it became "Day One" in the physical world, included of ten levels. A specific action was renewed for the "Right Crown." This is one combination of the letters of the ten Crowns for the "Left Arm," which also includes all the Crowns. He drew its form in the tenth, lowest Crown and brought that form into action, and it became "Day Two" in the physical world. Thus, the elements unique to the "Left Arm" were found.

Afterward, there was a third combination of letters established in the twelve Crowns for the "Middle Line," which includes all the Crowns. He drew its form in the lower Crown, and it brought into action in the physical world "Day Three," including ten levels. Thus, the elements for the "Middle Line" were found. In this manner, the fourth, fifth, and sixth were joined. When the seventh was clarified, its blessing of forms and plans was placed before it through the created powers and the **Chambers** <note>term: "Heikhalot"; the celestial palaces or structures described in early Jewish mysticism</note>. Through other holy levels...

This is why the sages of all bodies take and clothe themselves in forms, whether holy and pure or... whether of prohibition or permission. Every combination will be composed of twelve diagonals of the female. Since she is "Day," the point that appeared to be day has another point opposite it, which is "Night," and they are joined one to the other.

Behold, when there is a combination and rotation of the letters of the **Seventh Crown**, no new physical form is renewed, only the "Movement" itself, which is the preservation of all existing things in the order of **Male and Female**. In the other six rotations, the seventh level renewed everything below it, because the second letter moves faster than the one above it for that level in a certain combination, and all levels are included in that level, and so for all of them. It draws from itself "points and flames" in the secret of creation, worthy of being clothed in inner forms from their source. But on its own, it has nothing at all to renew as a "new creation" fit for permanence. When it would renew its Chambers, Chariots, and hosts and act through them, they were fit for permanence because she was complete from every one of the levels of the **Tree of Life**.

But now, in the seventh rotation, when the time of her dominion has arrived, if she were to act through her external levels—which are "profane" [*chol*] and she is their head—if her fear were not upon her, God forbid, there would be "two authorities" <note>original: "shte reshuot"; the heresy of dualism</note>. Therefore, anyone who performs any labor [on the Sabbath], intending for the natural world to spread and act in the way of the profane, behold, he is "**cutting the shoots**" <note>term: "kotzetz b'netiot"; a classic Talmudic metaphor for heresy or damaging the Divine unity</note>. Therefore, he is liable for death, for the **Tree of Knowledge** [of Good and Evil] rules. He has neglected to incline it toward the good and has inclined it toward the evil; therefore, he is liable for death.

Behold, the Sabbath—because it desired the permanence of all beings—included her in the sixth level to appease her mind and make her face shine. Thus, the sixth was also the seventh. For it is the sixth of the "Building" <note>referring to the six emotive Sephirot that "build" the world</note> starting from the Right Arm (the first light), and it is the seventh in count from the... and downwards. Because of this, the world of forms spreads and the physical world is quiet. The holy... and the levels of the profane rested and were diminished, for they do not draw now from their level, which is the Building. Their "Backs" are the "Wings," which are the "Distressors."

And now, a "Heritage without boundaries" <note>term: "nachala b'lo metzarim"; a spiritual inheritance that transcends physical limitations</note> has appeared, for there the entire physical world—meaning the **Husks** <note>term: "Kelipot"; the shells of impurity or materiality</note>—is found. The two lower levels, corresponding to **Remember** [*Zakhor*] and **Observe** [*Shamor*] <note>The two versions of the Sabbath commandment in the Ten Commandments, mystically representing the male and female aspects of the day</note>, were revealed. From their power, the days are constantly renewed. They are called a "Day of Rest," for the holy levels rested in it, and the profane levels were removed because their "Heads" were hidden. The seventh level was revealed, entirely included in the holiness of the "Firstfruits of Holiness." When this level desired to renew the **Eighth Day**, it returned to being a messenger for the first level of the Building through a different combination of letters, and so on through the six levels. It does not return to be renewed in other aspects, for they were already included in the first six rotations. In the other rotations, the power of our desire, the plan, and the **Personas** [*Partzufim*] increase and spread. Every single combination of letters is unlike another. Behold, the forms and Personas spread, different from one another, even if they are equal in species. Regarding all this, they said: "And the heavens and the earth and all their hosts were finished" [*Vaykhulu*]—the six Crowns, which are the work of heaven and earth, were blended into one another and from one another, and they brought out everything from everything.

It builds on the idea of the Sabbath as a "mate" for the Jewish people by explaining how the six days of the week relate to the Sabbath's holiness through the levels of the soul (Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah).</meta>

# Tractate Chullin

### Page 104
->**Tractate Chullin**<-

<meta>catchword: exits</meta>

Another explanation: the intention is that the Sabbath day is in the middle of the week. From Wednesday onward is considered "toward the Sabbath." The Sabbath exists in the realm of <term>Atzilut</term> <note>The highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure emanation</note>. Afterward, Sunday is in <term>Beriyah</term> <note>The World of Creation</note>, where there is a radiance for the soul. On Monday, in <term>Yetzirah</term> <note>The World of Formation</note>, there is radiance for the spirit. Afterward, it proceeds, and there is radiance on Tuesday in <term>Asiyah</term> <note>The World of Action</note>. Then it goes and increases in a fourfold manner. Perhaps the intent is for one to prepare himself to receive the <term>Nefesh</term>, <term>Ruach</term>, and <term>Neshamah</term> <note>The three lower levels of the soul: the physical-vitality, the emotional-spirit, and the intellectual-breath</note> for the coming Sabbath eve: Wednesday to prepare to receive the *Nefesh*, Thursday for the *Ruach*, and Friday for the *Neshamah*. And so it rotates in a cycle—three days before the Sabbath and three days after the Sabbath. These are the six branches of the <term>Menorah</term> <note>The seven-branched candelabrum of the Temple</note> that shine toward the face of the body of the Menorah. These are the "branches" of the Sabbath. This is the matter written in the portion of *Beshalach*: "A day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the Lord," and in the portion of *Vayakhel* it is written: "Holy, a Sabbath of rest to the Lord." Regarding why "holy" and "rest" change order, the author of the *Baal HaTurim* <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, a 14th-century commentator</note> wrote that it hints at adding from the mundane to the holy at its beginning and its exit. But it is still difficult; we have learned "Sabbath of rest" and "Sabbath." According to the aforementioned matter, it is settled. I will first clarify a detail of the Holy Tongue: the suffix *-on* indicates diminishment <note>original: "aktnut"; refers to a smaller or derivative version</note>, while the word "Sabbath" indicates greater magnitude (just as the word *Ish* [man] indicates greatness and *Ishon* [pupil of the eye] indicates smallness). Therefore, the small forms in the eye are called *ishon*. Similarly, Nachmanides wrote concerning the <term>Sambatyon</term> river <note>A mythical river that rests on the Sabbath</note> that it is named after the Sabbath because it hints at the Sabbath, as the river proves. Behold, the days Thursday and Friday which support the Sabbath have a partial elevation of the Sabbath; regarding them, it says "Rest-Sabbath." And Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday which follow the Sabbath have a partial elevation; regarding them, it says "Sabbath-Rest." Therefore, every single day a person should sanctify himself and focus on what level this day stands—whether *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, or *Neshamah*—and ascend accordingly to elevate it. Behold, the levels mentioned in the words of our Sages and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (peace be upon him) are Speech, Thought, and Action. It is stated in the *Tikunim* <note>The Tikunei Zohar</note> that these correspond to *Neshamah*, *Ruach*, and *Nefesh*: Thought corresponds to *Neshamah*, *Ruach* <note>here meaning "wind" or "breath"</note> to Speech, and Action to *Nefesh*. And why are there four elements of the body in which they dwell? This is "Everyone who is called by My name, and for My glory I created him, I formed him, even I made him" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. "I created him"—this is the *Neshamah*, the holy thought which is the World of Thought. "I formed him"—this is the speaking spirit, meaning the speakers. "I made him"—this is the *Nefesh*, for there lies "Action" which dwells in the 248 commandments. This is the end of his words. The matter of Speech, Thought, and Action includes everything, as will be explained at length in its place. Therefore, one should examine every day which level he stands upon. These three are <term>Beriyah</term>, <term>Yetzirah</term>, and <term>Asiyah</term>, as explained in the Zohar and as will be explained later at length.

**The general principle** that emerges: it is proper that every single day one should draw from the holiness of the Sabbath, each person according to his strength. It is proper for every man that he should occasionally desist from his labor and set himself apart to engage in the Torah, turning his thoughts away from worldly affairs. For it is not proper for a man to engage all day in labor, as it says in the Zohar: "In this way, they do not have faith in the Holy One, Blessed be He, for they do not desire the paths of piety; they wish to toil themselves all day long... lest they fail to bring home a piece of bread. Who caused this for them? Because they are not people of faith." End of quote. Therefore, it is proper for a man to make his Torah study a fixed habit and his work temporary, as it says in the *Tractate Avot*: "Rabbi [Judah the Prince] says: Minimize business and engage in Torah." And if you neglect the Torah, you will have many causes for neglect. This does not apply to Torah study alone, but to every commandment and act of kindness. Similarly, Rabbenu Tam wrote in *Sefer HaYashar* regarding the matter of love: that one of the aspects of love is to set aside one's own affairs for the affairs of God. And so it says in the chapter on the "Gate of Holiness," and in the *Mekhilta* the Sages said: "Six days you shall do work," yet another verse says "Six days you shall labor and do all your work." How can these two verses be reconciled? Rather, during the time that Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, their work is done by others, as it is said: "And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers" <note>Isaiah 61:5</note>. But when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent, their work must be done by themselves, as it says: "And you shall do all your work." Not only that, but "You shall serve your enemies whom the Lord shall send against you." End of quote. A similar idea was brought there in the portion of *Vayakhel* on the verse "Six days work shall be done"—behold, a person is not called to be engaged in labor that cancels his study of Torah, rather all his days should be like the Sabbath, engaging in Torah, while "strangers stand to do their work." This applies when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent. Yet one must be precise: for we find several pious ones in the Gemara who were engaged in their labor while also engaging in Torah, such as Hillel and his colleagues. Why was their work not done by others? It is possible to answer that the statement was only speaking about the collective—when [all] Israel does the will of the Omnipresent. Nevertheless, the question remains: why is every upright person not worthy of this? There are two other aspects to this. We find among the early pious ones that they would spend one hour before prayer, one hour during prayer, and one hour after prayer. That is three hours [per service], and so for every prayer—Morning, Afternoon, and Evening <note>totaling nine hours of prayer daily</note>. They asked in the Gemara: "When is their Torah and their work accomplished?" And they answered: "Because they are pious, their Torah is blessed and their work is done on its own." Thus, regarding such an individual, it is also said "work shall be done"—meaning they start a bit of the work, and from that work, blessing and success follow. This is not the same as when all Israel collectively does God's will—for "the resting of the many is superior"—where all their work is done entirely by others. When they do not do His will, it says "And you shall do all your work," meaning he must do all the labor by himself. The second aspect, which is not for everyone but for the Early Pious Ones, is the matter of the Tanaim and Amoraim <note>Sages of the Mishnah and Talmud</note> who would engage in their work for part of the day. However, their work was actually being accomplished by their <term>ibbur</term> <note>a mystical "impregnation" or assistance from a departed soul</note> or their thought, while they remained attached to the Blessed One and His Torah. Let this thing not be difficult in your eyes, as it is written in the book *Maaseh Hedyot* found in a manuscript... and in the commentary *Ma'ayanei HaYeshuah*... the pious man came to a settlement and they did not recognize him, so they made him a synagogue attendant. It is written that when he would check the oil in the lamps, he would spill the oil outside, because from his great attachment <note>term: "deveikut"</note> he could not focus on putting the oil into the lamps. The sage of the community understood this and said: "This attendant is worthy to be the sage in my place, and I shall serve under him." Of such a person it is said: "In her love you shall always be straying" <note>Proverbs 5:19</note>, for from the great love of Torah and attachment to it, he strays from worldly matters. It turns out that their souls were always sanctified with the holiness of the Sabbath, which is the "World of Thought," as I explained above. It is not proper for one who does not engage in Torah—his body and soul are entirely enslaved to labor. End of quote. In my humble opinion, it seems that what was done in the second aspect was the virtue of the early pious ones, and there was no difference between the early pious ones and other sages except in degree. The early pious ones had their thoughts completely attached Above; their work was not considered work at all, but rather like someone "acting unintentionally" <note>term: "mitasek"</note>. For according to the words of Rabbi Hayyim Vital, the work of the pious was a miraculous act: they did a small amount of work, and afterward the rest of the work was done on its own. Now, it is not a virtue for the pious to benefit from miracles, as we learn in Tractate *Shabbat*, chapter *Bameh Behemah*: "Our Rabbis taught: It once happened that a man's wife died and left a son to suckle, and he did not have money for a wet-nurse. A miracle was performed for him and his breasts opened like the two breasts of a woman, and he nursed his son. Rav Yosef said: Come and see how great this man is, that such a miracle was performed for him! Abaye said to him: On the contrary, how lowly is this man, that the order of creation was changed for him!" And in Tractate *Taanit* page 20, regarding the story of Rabbi Eleazar... and with this is settled what Abraham our Father (peace be upon him) said to the King of Sodom: "From a thread to a shoe-strap... lest you say, 'I have made Abraham rich'" <note>Genesis 14:23</note>. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, promised to enrich me. Now, would the Holy One, Blessed be He, make windows in the heavens and send down wealth? Rather, He surely prepares some cause for it. If so, why did Abraham not think: "Perhaps this is the time He will do this for me?" It was an act of miracles that Abraham with his servant Eliezer [defeated] kings and saved the spoil. Abraham said: "How can they make me rely on miracles?" Therefore, it seems to me to explain that the early pious ones did all their work with zeal and precision, but their thoughts were not entirely on the work. All the time, their thought was attached Above, and in their work, they were merely "unintentional actors." The sign for this is: "To do work and to think thoughts" <note>referring to the construction of the Tabernacle</note>—to do work below and to think thoughts Above. This only happens by spontaneous movement. When they sweetened their engagement in the matter according to the world's standard of labor, and shared their knowledge of the World to Come... but with a different thought... if one strengthens himself in a different thought, either the work is not done well, or the work is finished but the thought is not completed. But with the early pious ones, their work was done as "unintentional actors"—that is, their Torah was blessed. This clarifies that even though it is slightly outside of nature, it is not a "change in the order of creation," but rather help given to the weary. Other sages also followed this path, but the early pious ones were more engaged in the entire work from beginning to end. In any case, a person should sanctify four hours every day in godly attachment from the holiness of the Sabbath. For according to the calculation, there will be four hours of Sabbath [in every day] according to what I found in the book *Galya Razaya*...

# Tractate Chullin

The six days of creation spread out from it <note>referring to the Sefirah of Binah or Understanding</note> and downward, just as **Binah** is a general point above for the six extremities of the worlds. For <term>Yesod</term> <note>Foundation</note> and <term>Malchut</term> <note>Kingship</note>, and this for the "one," is called "inside the circle." The thirty-nine <note>original: "ל'" - likely a scribal shorthand for the 39 labors or a numerical value relating to the lower realms</note> extremities below are called the **World to Come**, and their depth is **Israel**, who merited the Sabbath in this world, while *Binah* is the World to Come. The physical **Assembly of Israel** below serves as a palace for the "Assembly of Israel" above. All the prophets engaged in this service. This is why the Midrash concludes: "When Israel stood before Mount Sinai, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them..." regarding that which I said: "The Sabbath is the mate of the Assembly of Israel, and the Torah is your mate." 

Therefore, it is also correct to hint that the six days of creation correspond to the six thousand years of the world’s existence, while the Sabbath corresponds to the **World to Come**, which is "entirely Sabbath," as the <term>Ramban</term> <note>Nachmanides, a major 13th-century scholar</note> explained at length in his commentary on Genesis. See also the saying of our Sages: "He who toils on the eve of the Sabbath shall eat on the Sabbath," for this world is the **World of Action**—"today is for doing them"—and tomorrow, which is the World to Come, is for "receiving reward." You shall "call the Sabbath a delight," for the World to Come is a day that is entirely Sabbath. The reward for the labor of this world is like the Sabbath below, and there is a Sabbath above. 

Every Sabbath is a point that includes the six extremities. Even though the Sabbath below is "two Sabbaths," it is nevertheless one Sabbath: "Remember" and "Keep" were spoken in a single utterance. This explains the phrase: "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it." If they wonder what is beautiful here, **Rabbi Isaac** says: "You should count [toward it]..." Both intended the same thing: to bring a person to an awakening of the Torah and its commandments in the World of Action. When a person "remembers" that the week is also called "Sabbath" <note>in Hebrew, the word 'Shabbat' can refer to both the seventh day and the week itself</note>, since the six days of action are drawn from that point as explained, then he will fulfill every single day the command: "You shall be holy." This is what he meant by saying one should count "first day toward the Sabbath, second day toward the Sabbath," meaning the six extremities drawn from the point which is "Sabbath to the Lord."

"And Keep"—it is already known to the Kabbalists that "Remember" and "Keep" are the secrets of **Positive** and **Negative Commandments**. From the seal of the "point" <note>the Sabbath</note> come the "extremities," which are the branches of that point. The first teacher in the Mishnah deals with the aspect of "six"—six days hinting at the six thousand years—while the Sabbath is the World to Come. In the World of Action, one must prepare during the week for the Sabbath of the World to Come, as hinted by "He who toils on the eve of Sabbath." This is why the first teacher said that our Sabbaths and festivals should be directed toward the Sabbath. The general rule is that every day is sanctified by the holiness of the Sabbath, though the Sabbath itself is the completion. This is the hint in the verse: "The Sabbath burnt offering in addition to the continual burnt offering," meaning that just as on a daily basis a person must be an "offering to the Lord" (meaning holy), on the Sabbath there is an extra holiness—the secret of the **Extra Soul** <term>Neshamah Yeterah</term>. 

When the wise man reflects on this and sanctifies himself every day, setting aside an hour to withdraw from the business of this world and cling to the Blessed Creator, then the six workdays—which are "profane" <term>Chullin</term> days—are transformed into the "purity of the holy." This is why **Tractate Chullin** is placed in the order of **Holy Things** (Kodashim). They are not called "mundane days" but rather the "six days of the Sabbath," as Rabbi Isaac said in the *Mechilta*. In truth, these days are mundane and not holy, as explained in the words of the *Reshit Chochma* that I cited. This is the hint of the **Havdalah** <note>The ritual separating the holy from the profane</note>: "He who distinguishes between the holy and the profane... between Israel and the nations." This means that although there is a distinction between the holy and the profane, do not understand it as being "completely profane."

<margin>
Rabbi Shimshon: The "distinction between Israel and the nations" means that among the nations, the profane is simply profane and not holy; but among Israel, etc.

As the *Reshit Chochma* writes in the "Gate of Holiness": I heard from my master, peace be upon him, regarding one who is walking in the desert and does not know when the Sabbath is: he counts seven days from the day he realized he was lost and sanctifies the seventh by performing **Kiddush** and **Havdalah**. He is permitted to observe the Sabbath even though it is not actually the Sabbath day. This is because the "Middle Point," which is the Sabbath, goes with them. He should do only enough work each day for his basic sustenance because every day is a "doubtful Sabbath." 

In practice, we can say this world is like a "desert." Man is an exile from his place of rest—the rest of the soul. In this world, being drawn after darkness by the counsel of his evil inclination, the Sabbath and the "Day that is entirely Sabbath" (the World of Souls) are his primary focus and home. Therefore, from the day he takes it to heart and wishes to return in repentance, his clothes must always be clean, and he should consider every day as a potential Sabbath—lest on that day he be summoned to the "World that is entirely Sabbath." As it is said: "Repent one day before your death." Therefore, he should not do more work than necessary for his sustenance, like someone preparing for a journey. For perhaps he has no life left but that very day; how then is it proper to toil and worry over a world that is not his? As the pious one said: "and leave their wealth to others."

Furthermore, they said in **Tractate Eruvin (54a)**: Samuel said to Rav Yehuda: "Sharp-witted one! Snatch and eat, snatch and drink, for the world we are leaving is like a wedding feast" <note>meaning it is fleeting</note>. Rav said to Rav Hamnuna: "My son, if you have something, treat yourself well, for there is no pleasure in the grave, and death does not delay." If you say, "I will leave a portion for my children in the grave," who will tell you? Human beings are like the grass of the field: these blossom and those wither. The explanation of "Snatch and eat" is: if you have money to benefit yourself, do not wait until tomorrow, for perhaps you will die and have no further enjoyment. We learn that "the world is like a wedding feast"—today it is here, tomorrow it is gone. If you have money, death has no delay; it comes suddenly. As for the "portion of food"—who will tell you if it remains in their hands? Perhaps they will lose it. "These blossom and those wither"—meaning they grow and their sustenance grows with them, so you do not need to worry about them.

One must sanctify the "seventh"—meaning one day a week should be entirely sanctified to the Lord to counter the days lost to the "foreign god" <note>the ego or evil inclination</note> within him. We have already expanded on this in the "Gate of Awe." One day must be sanctified to the service of his Creator with "holiness of speech" and the cessation of labor that cancels a man's cleaving to his Creator. It is good for him to seclude himself in a special place and be pious and God-fearing. He should not only repent on the Sabbath day; the Sabbath was given to him if he had not sinned. But since he has sinned and blemished many days, he must sanctify at least one day a week to the Lord. If he can do more, let him sanctify more. So it says in the **Zohar** (Vol. II): Two merchants left the settlement two days every week to engage in Torah. It is written there regarding Rabbi Hiyya, who was traveling and found two men in a mountain cleft. He asked them: "What is your business in this place?" They said: "We are merchants, and two days a week we separate ourselves from the settlement to engage in Torah, because people do not leave us alone [to study] during the other days." He said: "Fortunate is your lot." It seems to me these two days are Monday and Thursday, for it was explained above that the six lower days are the roots of the six heavenly attributes.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Sabbath as the spiritual root of time. It transitions from the general concept of the Sabbath to a complex Kabbalistic breakdown of how the four-letter Name of God (YHVH) governs the divisions of months, weeks, days, and hours. It explains that human moral behavior directly alters the "alignment" of these divine letters, changing the flow of divine energy from Mercy to Judgment.</meta>

# Tractate Chullin

Through its four letters <note>The Tetragrammaton: Y-H-V-H</note>, the Name branches into twelve "wings" or permutations, just as there are four weeks in every month. Within these weeks, the power of the Great Actor <note>The Creator</note> is divided. It has been explained that these letters branch into twelve permutations to act upon each and every week as three distinct "Beings" <term>Havayot</term> <note>Plural of 'Havayah,' a term for the Name Y-H-V-H, representing divine presence</note>. When divided into the four weeks, these three Beings per week total twelve, acting upon the twenty-four weekdays of the month. 

This is because in every week there is one day—the Sabbath—which is the source for the six weekdays. The Sabbath is the "universal day" that collects the three Beings that emerge from a single letter of the four-letter Name. On the Sabbath, they all rest and find repose in the secret of their source, for it is from there that the six workdays are nourished. Across the four weeks of a month, there are twenty-four such days, with the Sabbath standing between them. From the perspective of the resting Sabbath, the three Beings act upon the six days; including their source where they rest, the four weeks of the month (twenty-four days plus four Sabbaths) constitute the twenty-eight days gathered and included in a month. The source, which is the four-letter Name **YHVH** as a whole, alludes to the **New Moon** <note>Rosh Chodesh</note>, which encompasses and gathers them all.

Similarly, when we divide these three Beings that act in a single week into the days of the week, two letters from the Name emerge: one letter for the day and one for the night. Since three Beings consist of twelve letters <note>3 names × 4 letters = 12</note>, and there are twelve hours in a day and twelve in a night, it follows that one letter serves during the day and one letter serves at night. On the Sabbath, they do not "serve" in this way, as they rest in their source. 

From this, we see that the Sabbath—which is the source and the assembly point for the six days of the week—represents the reality of the "branches" of the <term>Sefirot</term> <note>Divine emanations or attributes</note> that spread out and reveal themselves within **Malchut** <note>Kingship, the lowest Sefirah representing the physical world</note>. Their expansion and revelation in *Malchut* are what we call "days." In the totality of this expansion, all the shifts in time's activities and the power of the temporal orders are included, flowing from the One who organizes them—that is, the power of the Divine Beings. This gathering of twenty-four hours (twelve by day and twelve by night) represents the branches spreading into *Malchut* itself from the seven branches <note>the seven lower Sefirot</note>. 

The Sefirah of **Malchut** is the secret of "particular sleep" <note>a state of diminished divine flow</note>, which has no independent action in the world. No action occurs at any time except through the power of the Name. All changes in activity, time, hour, or day are performed through *Malchut*, for she is the guide of specific actions. However, *Malchut* has no action of her own; she only acts based on what she receives from the higher principles. Therefore, she is the secret of the "Hour" in the sequence, which is specific, and she is the "House" mentioned previously. 

The letters that act one-by-one during the day and night are found to be "male" in the secret of **Direct Light** <note>Or Yashar: Divine energy flowing downward as pure compassion</note>, the masters of Mercy. For example, the letters *Yod* and *Heh* are male, representing Direct Light. This means that when the permutation is in its proper order, it is the secret of Direct Light flowing with Mercy—the *Yod* influences the first *Heh* (its mate), just as Wisdom (*Chochmah*) influences Understanding (*Binah*). Similarly, the *Vav* influences the second *Heh* (its mate), meaning the attribute of Beauty (*Tiferet*) influences Kingship (*Malchut*). In this state, the letters of **YHVH** are "male" through the secret of Direct Light and Mercy, positioned above the two *Hehs* which are "female." 

But if the *Hehs* come above the *Yod* or the *Vav*—meaning the female is "above"—then it is in the secret of **Reflected Light** <note>Or Chozer: Divine energy bouncing back, often associated with judgment or restriction</note>. This is the secret of **Judgment** <term>Din</term>, where they do not flow freely, because the *Hehs* have turned their faces upward. Just as the permutations of the letters can be reversed, you will find that one month is more inclined toward Judgment than another, and another month is more inclined toward Mercy. It all depends on the reversal of the light above, which follows the reversal of human deeds below. 

Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory hinted: <note>original: "גרודים" - likely a corruption of "צדיקים"</note> "Great are the deeds of the righteous, who turn the attribute of Judgment into the attribute of Mercy." And conversely, "Cursed are the wicked, who turn the attribute of Mercy into the attribute of Judgment." Just as you find this reversal in the months, you find it in the days. Every day, three letters serve; one letter for every few hours. Sometimes you find both are "male" (Mercy) and sometimes both are "female" (Judgment). It all depends on the deeds of those below, which make one day more judgmental than its neighbor, or more merciful.

To understand the secret of this matter, know that the four-letter Name is the very essence of the Ten Sefirot. Because the Sefirot are a complete unity, you will find the Name **YHVH** in every single Sefirah. Just as the Name encompasses all ten Sefirot, every individual letter of the Name also encompasses all ten Sefirot. Once you understand this, you can understand how the light can reverse even within a single letter that serves during the day. It can manifest as Reflected Light (Judgment) or Direct Light (Mercy) depending on human deeds. Even a single letter serving for a few hours can perform the actions of all ten Sefirot. 

Therefore, we should not wonder whether it is the "luck" of the day or the "luck" of the hour that causes things <note>The Hebrew 'Mazal' usually means zodiac/constellation, but here refers to destiny or flow</note>. As it says in the tractate of the Sabbath <note>Tractate Shabbat, Chapter 'Mi Shehechshich'</note>: "Is it the luck of the year, the month, the sabbatical cycle, or the jubilee that causes it?" In truth, it is none of these; rather, everything depends on the deeds of those below. Their deeds cause the Name and its letters to turn, for better or for worse. As the Sages hinted: "The Name awakens above exactly as a person awakens below." Like a reflection in water, if a person walks in a straight path, the Holy One reveals His "Face" to him—the four letters of His Name in the proper order of Direct Light. But if a person turns from the straight path, the "Face" of the Holy One—the letters of the Name—likewise turns. 

Let us return to our subject. It is now clear that:
*   **Hours** are the channels and branches of light flowing from the **Days**.
*   **Days** are channels of light flowing from the **Weeks**.
*   **Weeks** are channels of light flowing from the **Months**.
*   **Months** are channels of light flowing from the **Years**.
*   **Years** flow from the **Sabbatical years** (*Shmitot*).
*   **Sabbatical years** flow from the **Great Jubilee** (*Yovel*), which is the Sefirah of **Binah**, the root of everything.

There is no doubt that the branches always return to their source. The hours return to the foundation of the day. Therefore, the **Zohar** states that a person should repent for his sins before they "return." If one flaws a specific hour or a specific letter of the Name through sin, and does not perform **Teshuvah** <note>Repentance/Return</note> while that letter is still "serving," that letter then returns to its source carrying that flaw. It then becomes much harder to fix, for on the second day, a different letter serves, and one cannot easily fix with one letter what was ruined in another. 

Furthermore, the soul returns to its source every night to give an account. The days and nights return to their source, which is the Sabbath. This is why the Sabbath is a time of rest and gathering. One must repent before the light reveals itself to the source. If one repents before the Sabbath arrives, their sins are forgiven. This is the secret of "preparing" for the Sabbath—so that the six days of the week enter the Sabbath cleaned of sin, so that one's shame is not revealed before the Great King. This is why, through the blessing of the Sabbath, sins are forgiven for one who has done the work of return. Likewise, the weeks return to the Month, which is why we pray at the **New Moon**: "You have given New Moons to Your people as a time of atonement for all..." This is the secret of why people fast on the eve of the New Moon, to enter the new cycle in purity.

# Tractate Chullin 121

With its four letters <note>original: "בד' אותיותיו" refers to the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Name of God</note> dividing into four parts, it branches out into "two branches" and "two permutations." Likewise, in every month, there are four weeks in which the **Four-Letter Name** <note>original: "יהו"ד" - a scribal variant of the Tetragrammaton Y-H-W-H, using a 'D' to avoid writing the holy Name</note> that acts in that month returns to be divided by its four letters into four parts. This branches into twelve permutations and branches to act in each and every week as three **Beings** <term>Hovayot</term> <note>Permutations of the four-letter Name</note>. And when these are divided into four weeks, with three **Beings** for each week, there will be twelve **Beings** acting for the twenty-four days in the month.

For in every week, there is one day of **Sabbath**, which is the source for the six days of the week. It is the day that includes and gathers the three **Beings** that emerged from one letter of the four letters of the Name. On the Sabbath, they all rest and find repose in the secret of their source, for from there the six weekdays are nourished. These are the days of the week for every three **Beings** that rest on the Sabbath day. From this perspective, the three **Beings** act for six days, and including their source where they rest, they total seven days. In this way, the four weeks of the month, which are twenty-four days, along with their source—the four Sabbath days—total twenty-eight days which are gathered and included in the month.

The source, which is the four letters of the Name, generally hints at **Rachel** <note>In Kabbalah, "Rachel" represents the lower aspect of the Sefirah of <term>Malchut</term> (Kingship/Presence)</note>, who includes and gathers everything. When we divide these three **Beings** that act in one week into the days of the week, two letters from the Name will be assigned: one letter for the day and one letter for the night. Since three **Beings** consist of twelve letters, and there are six [work] days in the week, it follows that one letter serves during the day and one letter serves during the night. On the Sabbath they do not serve, as they rest in their source.

From this, we see that the Sabbath—which is the source and the gathering point for the six days of the week—is a hint to the existence of the branches of the **Sefirot** <note>The ten attributes or emanations of God</note> that spread and reveal themselves within <term>Malchut</term> <note>Kingship, the final Sefirah</note>. Their spreading and revelation in *Malchut* are called "days." In the reality of their total spreading to *Malchut*, all the changes in the actions of time and the orders of time are included, flowing upon her from the power of the source.

The "day" is a gathering of twenty-four hours—twelve for the day and twelve for the night—hinting at the branches spreading into *Malchut* herself from the seven branches of the *Sefirot*. One letter from the Four-Letter Name acts at night and one letter from the Four-Letter Name acts during the day, as we have explained. The Sefirah of **Malchut** is the secret of the flow of "particularity," for there is no action in the world that is not affected from there—no action that does not have a "where" and a "when." Likewise, all actions, all changes in action, changes in time, changes in the hour, or changes in days—whatever lives—everything is done through *Malchut*. For she manages actions in detail, one after another. *Malchut* has no power to act on her own, only what she receives from the higher totalities. Therefore, she is the secret of the "hour" in the row, which is particular.

The letters that act—one letter by day and one letter by night, as we mentioned—are found to be "males" in the secret of **Direct Light** <term>Or Yashar</term> <note>Divine energy flowing downward as pure compassion</note>, which are the masters of mercy, such as the letters *Yod* and *Waw*. They are males, Direct Light, meaning when the permutation of the Name emerges in its proper order, it is the secret of the Direct Light that bestows mercy. For the *Yod* bestows into the first *Heh* (Wisdom into Understanding), and likewise, the *Waw* bestows into the second *Heh* (Beauty into Kingship). This order represents males in the secret of mercy, where the Name is above the two *Hehs* which are females. 

But if the *Hehs* come before the *Yod* and the *Waw* (such as H-W-H-Y or H-Y-W-H), then it is in the order of **Returning Light** <term>Or Chozer</term> <note>Divine energy bouncing back, associated with restriction and judgment</note>. This is the secret of **Judgment** <term>Din</term>, where they do not bestow light downward, because the *Hehs* have turned their faces upward. According to how the permutation of the letters is reversed, so too will you find one month having more judgment than another month, or one month more [merciful] than another, and one day more than another. All of this is according to the reversal of the light above, which follows the reversal of the deeds of the lower beings below. 

This is what the Sages of blessed memory hinted at: "Great are the deeds of the righteous, who turn the attribute of Judgment into the attribute of Mercy." And likewise the opposite: the wicked turn the attribute of Mercy into the attribute of Judgment. Just as you find this reversal in months, you also find it in the days. Two letters serve each day: one letter during the twelve hours of the day and one letter during the twelve hours of the night. Sometimes a "male" letter comes during the day and a "female" letter at night; sometimes both are males, and sometimes both are females. It all depends on the reversal of the light, which follows the deeds of the lower beings, which makes one day more "Judgmental" than its fellow, or one day more "Merciful" than its fellow.

The secret of the matter is this: know that the Four-Letter Name is the essential vitality of the **Ten Sefirot**. Because the *Sefirot* are completely unified—such that they are all one power—you will find that the Four-Letter Name is the essence of all *Sefirot*, hinting at all ten. Likewise, you will find the Four-Letter Name within each and every *Sefirah*, for one power is in them all. Just as you find ten *Sefirot* in the total Name, you find that every single letter of the Name includes all ten *Sefirot*. Therefore, in every single letter, the Four-Letter Name is revealed.

Once you know this, you can understand what we explained about the reversal of light even in a single letter of the Name that serves during the day. It can be revealed in the secret of Returning Light (Judgment), and likewise at night it can turn into Direct Light (Mercy) or Returning Light (Judgment). For within every letter of the four letters of the Name, there are [sub-realms of] four letters that are revealed and reversed in their lights according to the deeds of the lower beings. 

Thus it is understood that even a letter serving for twelve hours of the night or day can perform all the actions of the ten *Sefirot* and their opposites equally. For in one letter, you find all four letters of the Name, which hold the power of all the actions of the ten *Sefirot*.

As we explained, when a letter of the Name serves for twelve hours during the day, it sometimes reveals itself in Direct Light as a male (Mercy), and sometimes it reveals itself in Returning Light as a female (Judgment). This is all according to the deeds of the lower beings and their spiritual arousal. The same applies to the letter that serves for twelve hours at night. This reversal of light is what the Sages meant when they said the righteous turn Judgment to Mercy and the wicked the opposite. 

Now, do not find it difficult to reconcile whether the "luck of the day" or the "luck of the hour" is the cause <note>referring to a debate in the Talmud, Tractate Shabbat 156a</note>. In the chapter "He Who Was Overtaken by Darkness" in **Tractate Shabbat**, it asks whether the luck of the hour, the month, the sabbatical year, or the jubilee year is the cause. In truth, neither this nor that is the cause; everything follows the deeds of the lower beings. Their deeds cause the Name and its letters to turn to act for either good or bad. This is hinted at in the phrase: "Arousal from below triggers arousal from above." Just as a person is aroused to act below, so is the Great and Holy Name aroused to act above—like a reflection in water. If a child walks in the straight path, the Holy One reveals His face to him—which are the four letters of His Name—in a straight and direct light. But if he turns from the straight path, the face of the Holy One—the four letters—turns into the secret of judgment. For the Holy "Faces" are revealed to everything equally, whether for bad or good, for they are the source of all existence and its opposite.

Let us return to our subject. It has been clarified that the **hours** are channels and branches of light flowing from the **times**; **days** are channels of light flowing from the **weeks**; **weeks** are channels of light flowing from the **months**; **months** are channels of light flowing from the **years**; **years** are channels of light flowing from the **Sabbatical years** <term>Shemitot</term>; and **Sabbatical years** are channels of light flowing from the **Jubilee** <term>Yovel</term>. The Holy One, who is <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding</note>, includes everything in her power, and all emerge from her power.

According to this, there is no doubt that the branches always return to their source. The hours return to the days. Therefore, it says in the **Zohar** that a person should confess his sins before retiring to repair what he twisted. For if he is flawed in one day, which corresponds to one letter of the Name, and he does not perform **repentance** <term>Teshuvah</term> for that letter while it is still serving, then once its service ends, it enters its source and is unified there. It then becomes more "totalized," and he must perform an even greater repentance to reach that source. On the second day, a different letter will serve, and he will not be able to repair with the new letter what he ruined with the previous one. 

Because of this, although these flaws enter the source and become more included in its powers, one must perform a stronger repentance, as we explained in the first introduction. Likewise, every night [the soul] returns to its source and confesses its sins. Similarly, the days and nights return to their source, which is the **Sabbath**. Therefore, the Sabbath atones, because it is the source where the days rest and are unified. One must perform repentance before his sin is revealed before the Source. In this way, when the Sabbath arrives, his sins are already atoned for through his repentance. 

This is the secret of the "Eve of Sabbath" <note>Friday</note>: so that the six days of the week arrive at the Sabbath clean of sin and iniquity, so that his shame is not revealed before the Great Source. For this reason, at the onset of the Sabbath, his sins are atoned for, provided he has repented. His repentance reaches until the Sabbath. Likewise, the weeks return to the month, and we say a prayer of atonement, as we pray: "The New Moons You have given to Your people as a time of atonement for all..." This is the secret of why people fast on the Eve of the New Moon <term>Erev Rosh Chodesh</term> and complete it until the New Moon, so that they may enter [the new month in purity].
