<meta>This page continues the exploration of Sabbath observance, moving from the mystical associations of the number thirty-nine to the practical and spiritual requirements of "Sabbath Delight" (Oneg Shabbat) in thought, speech, and action. It bridges the gap between legal prohibitions and the mystical significance of the "extra soul" received on the Sabbath.</meta>

# Tractate Shabbat

<margin>
Anyone who delights in the Sabbath is granted the desires of their heart, as it is said: "Delight in the Lord and He will give you the desires of your heart" [Psalms 37:4]. I would not know what this "delight" is, but when it says: "And you shall call the Sabbath a delight" [Isaiah 58:13], one must say this refers to the delight of the Sabbath. Furthermore, one should occupy their speech with words of Torah, visit their teacher, and refrain from mundane talk on the Sabbath, speaking instead words of peace and the like. This increases the sanctity of the Sabbath. I have also received a tradition that when a person visits a friend on Sabbath morning, they should not say "Good morning" <note>original: "צפרא טבא" (Tzafra Taba), the standard weekday Aramaic greeting.</note> as they do during the week, but should say "Shabbat Shalom" or "A Good Shabbat" to fulfill the commandment "Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy."
</margin>

**In Thought:** This refers to the contemplation and perception that a person is obligated to generate in their intellect—namely, new insights into the Torah <note>original: "חידושי תורה" (Chiddushei Torah), innovations or original interpretations.</note> every single Sabbath. This is the language of the Zohar <note>The primary work of Jewish mysticism.</note> in the portion of *Shelach Lecha* (page 153): "Come and see: when the Sabbath enters, souls descend and rest upon the holy people, while the souls of the righteous ascend. When the Sabbath departs, the souls that rested upon Israel ascend, and the souls that descended [the righteous] ascend as well. Once all the souls that rested upon Israel ascend, they stand in form before the Holy King. The Holy One, blessed be He, asks them all: 'What innovation of Torah did you say—you, the soul of so-and-so?' They all present new words in the two academies <note>Refers to the celestial academies of heaven and the Garden of Eden.</note> below, while the Holy One is above. When a word is innovated in the Torah, and the soul that descended on the Sabbath occupied itself with those new matters and ascended, the entire heavenly host listens to that word... but if the Holy One asks them and they do not understand and are silent, then the holy creatures <note>original: "חיות הקודש" (Chayot HaKodesh), a high order of angels.</note>... [are saddened]." Until here are its words.

**In Action:** This refers to the "delight of the Sabbath," which includes the three meals and the marital obligations of Torah scholars. Regarding the aspect of "turning away from evil"—that is, the negative commandments concerning speech—Rabbi Yochanan said in the chapter *Elu Ksharim*: "'And speak a word' [Isaiah 58:13] implies that your speech on the Sabbath should not be like your speech on a weekday." This means one should not discuss buying, selling, or accounts. This is the language of the *Tosafot* <note>Medieval commentators on the Talmud.</note>: "Your speech should not be like your weekday speech," meaning business dealings. However, Rabbenu Tam <note>A prominent 12th-century French scholar.</note> disagrees, for business is already forbidden by the phrase "pursuing your own affairs." Rather, as stated in *Vayikra Rabbah*, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai had an elderly mother who used to talk a lot; he would say to her, "Mother, it is Sabbath!" implying that there should be a general silence, as one should not speak as much on Sabbath as on a weekday. In the Jerusalem Talmud, they said it was only with difficulty that they permitted even greeting someone with "Shalom" on the Sabbath.

In the chapter *Kol Kitvei*, Rabbi Eliezer said: "How do we know that speech is considered like an action? Because it says: 'By the word of the Lord the heavens were made' [Psalms 33:6]." Rashi <note>The preeminent 11th-century commentator.</note> did not explain this, but the statement means that just as one must rest from physical labor, one must rest from speaking of mundane needs, for this is the commandment of the Sabbath. Since for six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth and on this day He rested, and the Holy One did not "work" through physical action but only through speech—as it is said "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made"—it follows that since He "rested" from that speech, you too must rest from mundane speech as if it were an action. We learn in the Jerusalem Talmud: "It is written, 'A Sabbath to the Lord your God'—just as He rested from the Utterances <note>The ten sayings through which God created the world.</note>, so you must rest from utterances." Rabbi Chananya said through the Holy Spirit regarding the greeting of "Shalom" on Sabbath: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that when Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai saw his mother speaking excessively, he would tell her, "Mother, it is Sabbath," and she would be silent.

It is written in the Responsa of the *Sages of Ashkenaz* <note>original: "ת' הס"א" refers to the responsa of the Ashkenazi authorities.</note> that telling stories about kings, ministers, wars, and the like is permitted if the person finds delight in the stories, just as it is permitted for youths to delight in running and jumping. But if the narrator does not find delight, or does so to save a friend and there is a concern of a prohibition for those who do not find delight—until here are his words. It seems to me that even though he permitted it for one who finds delight, this is not the "Path of the Pious." He who refrains from mundane speech shall be called "holy." The *Or Zarua* <note>A 13th-century legal code by Rabbi Isaac of Vienna.</note> wrote based on the Zohar that one who speaks mundane conversation on the Sabbath is like one who desecrates the Sabbath. This is the language of the Zohar in the portion of *Vayakhel*: "The time that is exchanged for other words and mundane matters—that person is as if they desecrated the Sabbath and has no portion in the holy people of Israel. Two angels are appointed over this on the Sabbath day; they place their hands on his head and say: 'Woe to so-and-so who has no portion in the Holy One.' Therefore, one must strive in prayer, songs, and praises of their Master and occupy themselves with Torah." Until here are its words.

Even among the masses where it is necessary to speak, men of pious action refrain from speaking on the Sabbath—even about necessities—except in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew.</note> and not in a mundane language, for the day is holy to our ears. It is a sign between Him and us; therefore, one should only speak in the Holy Tongue. Happy is he who is meticulous with himself to speak in the Holy Tongue even on weekdays, for the virtue of the Holy Tongue is beyond measure. Regarding the virtues of speaking in the Holy Tongue, the Zohar says on the portion of *Noach*: "And the Lord said: 'Behold, they are one people and they all have one language...'" [Genesis 11:6]. Because they were as one, they succeeded in their works... and were later scattered. What is written? "The Lord scattered them from there." You might ask why their language was confused; it was because they all spoke the Holy Tongue, and that language granted them assistance in their deeds. Those words reached high places to provide support... until their language was confused at Babel so they could not cooperate. Once their language was changed, they no longer succeeded, for the heavenly powers only recognize the Holy Tongue. When the language was confused, their power was weakened and their strength broken. This is because a word spoken below in the Holy Tongue is known by all the heavenly hosts, and they grant it strength. Other languages they do not recognize or know. Therefore, they immediately "ceased building the city," for their strength was broken and they could no longer do anything against the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. Until here are its words.

---

<margin>
Rabbenu Yonah <note>A 13th-century Spanish rabbi and moralist.</note> wrote in his *Letter of Ethics*: "It is forbidden for a person's heart to be preoccupied with their business on the Sabbath. Although the Sages said 'speech is forbidden but thought is permitted,' if the thought causes true distress of the heart, it is prohibited by the Torah, as it says, 'And you shall do all your labor.' The *Mechilta* <note>An early legal commentary on Exodus.</note> explains this to mean that all your work should be in your eyes as if it is already completed, so that you do not dwell on it. Thus we say in the prayer: 'A rest of peace, tranquility, and security, a perfect rest in which You find favor.' And in the Grace After Meals, we ask that 'there be no distress, grief, or sighing on our day of rest.'" Until here are his words. There is a story of a pious man whose field developed a breach, and he considered fencing it, but then remembered it was the Sabbath and refrained. He never fenced it, even after the Sabbath, so as not to benefit from that thought. Even though thought is technically permitted, it is the trait of piety to be as if all one's work is done. The Holy One gave him a reward and a miracle occurred for him: a caper bush <note>original: "צלף" (Tzalaf).</note> grew there, from which he derived his livelihood and the livelihood of his household.
</margin>

**In Thought** <note>This heading is repeated as the text transitions back to the internal state.</note>

**In Action:** These are the forty labors minus one, which have many "sub-categories" <note>original: "תולדות" (Toldot), derivative labors.</note> and sub-derivatives enacted by the Rabbis. Great care is needed not to transgress any of them. One who keeps the Sabbath according to its laws is as if they fulfilled the entire Torah, for the Sabbath is weighed against the whole Torah, as it is said: "And Your holy Sabbath You made known to them, and commandments, statutes, and Torah You commanded them by the hand of Moses Your servant" [Nehemiah 9:14]. It is known that the Sabbath testifies to the Oneness of God and the creation of the world. The Serpent denied the creation, saying that God "ate from this tree and created the world" [referencing a midrash on the Serpent's deception], thereby spreading slander. The Serpent was "cunning" and caused humanity to be stripped of "garments of light" <note>original: "כתנת אור" (Kotnot Ohr).</note>; then "the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin" <note>original: "כתנות עור" (Kotnot Or). A play on words between Light (Ohr) and Skin (Or).</note>. It is found in the words of our Sages that when the Serpent came to Eve, he touched the Tree of Knowledge. The Holy One said, "Let not the foot of pride come against Me" [Psalms 36:12], and therefore the Serpent's legs were cut off. 

This is hinted at in the words of our Sages regarding the Sabbath: "Your Sabbath clothing should not be like your weekday clothing," for now "garments of skin" are weekday garments, not holy, except from the perspective of the world's creation. But one must change their clothes on the Sabbath to hint at the World to Come, which is "entirely Sabbath," where there are only garments of glory—garments of light. Furthermore, "Your speech on Sabbath should not be like your speech on a weekday," for the Serpent's speech was mundane and not holy. Also, "Your walking on Sabbath should not be like your walking on a weekday," for your "foot" should rest; the Serpent's legs were cut off and he was pursued. There is a hint here that actions were sealed with the six seals of the Name Y-H-V, as mentioned above in Tractate Chullin. These letters in their "filled" form <note>A kabbalistic method of calculating the numerical value of letters by spelling out their names.</note> equal 39 <note>original: "ל"ט".</note>. The Serpent, who damaged the creation of the world, sinned and caused Adam to sin, and thus the world was damaged and cursed with thirty-nine curses, as explained in the beginning of the portion of *Bereshit*. This is the language of the Recanati <note>13th-century Italian kabbalist.</note>: "Our Rabbis said in *Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer* that thirty-nine curses were placed upon Adam, Eve, the Serpent, and the Earth. Therefore, the sinner who bears the seal of the Serpent's impurity is struck with forty lashes minus one [39]." It is said in the Jerusalem Talmud that the lashes must be in sets of ten corresponding to the ten curses of the Serpent, for the sinner follows the Serpent who enticed man...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Sabbath’s spiritual dimensions, shifting from the personal "extra soul" to the cosmic significance of the Sabbath as a testimony to Creation. # Tractate Shabbat

The beginning and fulfillment of the commandments is to serve the Blessed Name. Behold, the core of the service of the Blessed Name is the sacrificial service <note>original: "עבודת הקרבנות" (Avodat HaKorbanot)</note>, as the *Tur* <note>The Arba'ah Turim, a foundational 14th-century code of Jewish law.</note> wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Yonah at the beginning of his work, as follows: "The world was created for the sake of three things: the Torah, the Service <note>The Temple sacrifices.</note>, and acts of kindness." Regarding the Torah, it is written: "The Lord possessed me at the beginning of His way" [Proverbs 8:22]; the Torah said, "I was created before all creatures, and for my sake, all creatures were created." Similarly, for the sake of the Service, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, chose Israel from all the nations and chose the Temple from all places so they would serve Him there, and for this, the world was created. Likewise for acts of kindness, etc.—until here are his words. Therefore, it is written: "A continual fire shall burn upon the altar" [Leviticus 6:6]. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Were it not for the daily offerings, heaven and earth would not endure." The Men of the Stand <note>original: "אנשי מעמד" (Anshei Ma'amad) — groups of laypeople who represented the nation during the daily sacrifices.</note> would read the Account of Creation, because the ultimate purpose of the Account of Creation was that He created it for His glory and for His service, may He be blessed, and through this, there is endurance for the Account of Creation. These are the daily offerings, which never cease. It has already been explained that the entire Account of Creation is included in fire, and they are the "continual fire that shall burn upon the altar"—meaning, the fire that indicates the constant endurance of existence because they perform the service of the Blessed Name with fire. This causes the endurance of existence which came through fire. And "continual fire" refers to the fire from Above: "And fire came out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar" [Leviticus 9:24]. And on the Sabbath day: "two lambs..." in addition to the "continual burnt offering" [Numbers 28:9-10]. The matter follows the principle: "By the mouth of two witnesses shall a matter be established" [Deuteronomy 19:15]. Behold, we testify to the novelty of the world <note>The concept that the world was created ex nihilo (out of nothing) rather than being eternal.</note> and that He, blessed be He, is the Will of all the worlds, through two testimonies: one a negative commandment and one a positive commandment. The negative commandment is: "You shall kindle no fire in all [your dwellings on the Sabbath day]" [Exodus 35:3], which is our ceasing from work on the Sabbath. The positive commandment is: "A continual fire [shall burn] on the altar; it shall not go out" [Leviticus 6:6], for we serve Him with fire—a "fire-offering, a sweet savor to the Lord." The sign is that He is the Creator and He is the Finality. On the Sabbath, additional fire-offerings of sweet savor were added beyond the daily burnt offering to show that, on the contrary, the Sabbath indicates the end of the world <note>The goal or culmination of creation.</note> by virtue of the fact that the Blessed Name rested from His work on it. Therefore, we are forbidden from work for this very reason. It is appropriate to increase the Temple service with fire-offerings of sweet savor because that which my negative commandment "you shall not kindle fire" indicates, God's positive commandment indicates as well. Regarding "and on the Sabbath day, two lambs," the observance of the negative commandment points to the positive commandment, and they are one matter. Thus it is explained why "everyone who profanes it shall surely be put to death" [Exodus 31:14] and "on the Sabbath day, two lambs" were said in a single utterance <note>A reference to the tradition that the "Remember" and "Observe" aspects of the Sabbath were spoken by God simultaneously.</note>, for their testimony is aligned. One spirit said "Prepare," and the other said "Prepare." This is the meaning of "You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings" and "A continual fire shall burn upon the altar." "And on the Sabbath day, two lambs..." as the burnt offering of...

Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva: "One who prays on the eve of the Sabbath and says 'And they were finished,' the two ministering angels who accompany a person place their hands on his head and say to him, 'Your iniquity is gone and your sin is atoned for' [Isaiah 6:7]." <meta>This page continues the discussion on the laws of the Sabbath, specifically regarding the prohibition of benefiting from work performed by a non-Jew on the Sabbath. It transitions from these legalistic details (Halakha) into a deeply philosophical and mystical exploration of the Sabbath as the foundation of Jewish belief and its connection to the very act of Creation.</meta>

# Tractate Shabbat

Mar Zutra <note>A 5th-century Babylonian sage.</note> therefore did not wish to enter that house. However, if it were a complete contractual arrangement <note>original: "קבלנות" (Kablanut) — a fixed-price contract where the worker chooses their own hours, rather than being hired specifically to work on the Sabbath.</note> from a house outside the Sabbath boundary, as I have written, it appears that even an important person is permitted to enter; these are his words. My teacher <note>original: "ריבונא" (Ribuna)</note> did not write anything here regarding the Sabbath, but in Section 543 concerning the Intermediate Days of the Festival <note>original: "חול המועד" (Chol HaMoed)</note>, he wrote that if it was built by non-Jews, it is proper to be stringent and not enter it, and this will be explained there with God’s help. Our Rabbis wrote regarding the Intermediate Days that the reason is to prevent a "lonely heart" <note>An idiom suggesting a feeling of guilt or being out of place.</note> where a house was built through a Sabbath violation, and that it is proper to be stringent according to the school of Shammai. So it is written in the *Shulchan Aruch* <note>The Code of Jewish Law.</note>: if non-Jews built a house for an Israelite on the Sabbath through a forbidden act, it is proper to be stringent and not enter it. This is also the law regarding other things that come through a transgression—one should not benefit from them, as Maimonides <note>A leading 12th-century scholar.</note> wrote in Chapter 5 of the *Laws of Theft*, as cited in the *Tur*, *Choshen Mishpat*, Section 369.

## Chapter: Torah is Light
<margin>The laws of the Sanctification of the Name were divided above in letter M... and the secret will be explained in the work *As Amram Praised* <note>original: "כעמרם סילולים" (K’amram Silulim) — likely a reference to a specific mystical commentary.</note> in the Gate of Foundation.</margin>

Know that the Sabbath indicates the root of faith and the root of the entire Torah, for the Sabbath testifies to the "Renewal of the World" <note>original: "חידוש" (Chiddush) — the belief that the world was created at a specific point in time, as opposed to being eternal.</note>. It is known that the truth of Existence is His absolute existence, may He be blessed, who exists beyond time. This is hinted at in His essential Name, the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter Name of God, Y-H-V-H.</note>, which means "He was, He is, and He will be." He brings all things into being and sustains their existence, for He alone exists and there is none besides Him. All that exists, whether physical or spiritual, originates from His existence, for He renewed everything from absolute nothingness <note>original: "יש מאין" (Yesh Me-Ayin) — creation ex nihilo.</note> and is the Master of all worlds. Therefore, the Men of the Great Assembly <note>The governing body of Jewish sages during the early Second Temple period.</note> established blessings before the *Shema* prayer in the morning and evening that speak of Creation: that He, may He be blessed, created and formed, "creating light and fashioning darkness" in the morning, and in the evening, "bringing on the evening twilight with wisdom," "opening the gates," and "distinguishing between day and night." This is to indicate His unity—that one God created them, single, unique, and individual. This is the meaning of the blessing; then His existence and unity are understood, and we recite: "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One," which is the root of faith.

The entire Torah also depends on the faith in the world's renewal, as Maimonides wrote in *The Guide for the Perplexed*. Nahmanides <note>A 13th-century commentator.</note> also wrote at the beginning of the portion of *Genesis*: "The belief in the renewal of the world is the root of faith, and whoever does not believe this but thinks the world is eternal is a heretic regarding the fundamental principle and has no Torah at all." Therefore, the Torah was given on the Sabbath, because the Sabbath points to the renewal of the world. First, the Torah was given, and it is written, "A Sabbath unto the Lord," for just as His Name indicates "He was, He is, and He will be," so the Sabbath hints at "was, is, and will be." For there are three Sabbaths: the Sabbath of Creation <note>The past.</note>, the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah <note>The present/existence.</note>, and the Sabbath of the Future <note>The World to Come.</note>—the "day that is entirely Sabbath," which is the level of the Upper World.

Regarding this matter, the prayers were established as written in the *Tur*, *Orach Chaim*, Section 292: The reason they established three different themes for the Sabbath prayers—"You Sanctified" <note>original: "אתה קדשת" (Atah Kidashta)</note>, "Moses Rejoiced" <note>original: "ישמח משה" (Yismach Moshe)</note>, and "You Are One" <note>original: "אתה אחד" (Atah Echad)</note>—whereas on Festivals they only established one ("You Have Chosen Us"), is because these three prayers correspond to the three Sabbaths. "You Sanctified" corresponds to the Sabbath of Creation, as its content proves. "Moses Rejoiced" corresponds to the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah, for the world was completed when the Torah was given on the Sabbath. "You Are One" corresponds to the Sabbath of the Future. Thus, the Sabbath of Creation indicates the aspect of "He Was," the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah indicates "He Is" for our ancestors and for us and our children forever, and the Sabbath of the Future indicates "He Will Be," the eternal world. Within the Sabbath are hidden the three principles that include all other principles: the existence of God, Torah from Heaven, and reward and punishment. The Sabbath of Creation indicates the Creator’s existence; the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah indicates Torah from Heaven; and the Sabbath of the Future indicates the true, eternal reward for those who merit it, and the great Day of Judgment for the wicked, God forbid.

# And Now
I will explain how the Sabbath indicates the renewal of the world. Know that the renewal occurred essentially during the six days of work, when He, Blessed be He, was bringing things into being and renewing them. He then ceased and rested on the seventh day. Had He not rested and ceased, but continued to renew and bring things into being perpetually without the creation stopping, then people would have thought the world was eternal, never having started and never to end. However, since He ceased from the Work of Creation, everything now follows the pattern established in those six days, cycling back around. "What was is what will be," and every week is like the week that was. Truly, the Blessed Name renews [creation] every day continually, but it is nothing other than the original Work of Creation; His providence never ceases from having the Work of Creation cycle back. I have elaborated on this previously in Tractate Chullin, explaining that the Sabbath is a "point," and there is a hint that the days are the "edges" that emerge from the point and return to it, exiting and entering until such time as it is the will of God.

It is thus well-explained how the Sabbath relates to the renewal of the world: "For in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed." We testify to this through our resting on the Sabbath. This is mirrored by the six days of work that enter and exit from Sabbath to Sabbath. As I elaborated above, the matter of the candle's light <note>The Shabbat candles.</note>, which we are commanded to light at the onset of the Sabbath, and the light of the candle at the conclusion of the Sabbath to connect to it by reciting "Who creates the lights of the fire," is rooted in this.

The dispute between the School of Shammai and the School of Hillel will also be explained: Shammai holds one should bless "Who *created* <note>original: "ברא" (Bara) — past tense.</note> the light of the fire," while Hillel holds "Who *creates* <note>original: "בורא" (Borei) — present/continuous.</note> the lights of the fire." The Talmud in *Berakhot* says that "created" clearly implies the past, but "creates" can also mean the past. I have already elaborated on this in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*, but I will add a further explanation here. It will also be explained why the verse says, "You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings on the Sabbath day" [Exodus 35:3]—why was fire singled out more than other labors? Our Rabbis differed on this, but a verse does not lose its literal meaning. I mean to say there is a path according to the plain meaning <note>original: "פשט" (Peshat)</note> in addition to the legal teaching of our Rabbis, whose words are truth. It will further be explained why it says "those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death," and why on the Sabbath day "two lambs" are offered "as another matter" <note>A reference to the additional Sabbath sacrifice.</note>.

The verse "A perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out" [Leviticus 6:6] will also be explained. Rashi <note>The classic 11th-century commentator.</note> explained what he explained. Know that the first statement of Creation—"And God said, 'Let there be light'"—included all the other statements revealed afterward, for it is their head and root. As Rashi says on the portion of *Genesis*, everything was created on the first day, and the "becoming" was already sown. What the commentators say about the six days of creation is that while the text speaks of lower things, it hints at upper things, for "this corresponds to that" <note>A principle that the physical world mirrors the spiritual world.</note>. The world of *Atzilut* <note>The highest mystical world of "Emanation."</note> is the hidden essence of the world, and this is "Let there be light," which was sent into the inheritance of man. As it is said, "For the Lord your God is a consuming fire" [Deuteronomy 4:24]; the glory of the Sender created the worlds of *Beriah*, *Yetzirah*, and *Asiyah* <note>The three lower mystical worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action.</note> through the numerical value of "Let there be light."

And it says, "And there was light"—a light that already existed in secret before the world was created, and it is hidden now but was revealed during the six days of creation. These matters were already explained at length in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*. Concerning this, it is said "For the Lord your God is a consuming fire," and He illuminates the whole world with His glory. From this perspective, He is revealed, yet no intellectual grasp can perceive Him, not even the angels, as it is written: "For man shall not see Me and live"—not even the angels who are "living beings." Just as fire provides light but a person cannot touch it, so it is explained in the unfolding of "Let there be light" into the light of the world of *Beriah*, which is the light of a "torch." By way of metaphor: *Atzilut* is the light of a vast bonfire without measure; from that bonfire, a torch is lit <note>The world of *Beriah*.</note>; and from the torch, a candle is lit, which is the world of *Yetzirah*. This candle shines into the "dark house," which is the world of *Asiyah*. All is through the power of the Supreme One, may He be blessed.

This explains the words of Rabbi Eliezer the Great: "From where were the heavens created? From the light of His garment. And the light? From the snow beneath the Throne of Glory." It is known that "His garment" is the world of *Beriah*, and the light sparking from the garment is *Yetzirah*, and from *Yetzirah* it unfolds and spreads into "heaven and earth and all their host." *Beriah* is the Throne of Glory. Thus, the "light of the garment" and the "snow under the Throne" both hint at *Yetzirah*. From these levels, the powers of heaven and earth spread—the secret of spiritual and physical *Asiyah*. Heaven has an additional superiority over the earth. Go and see this in physical light: among the four elements, fire is at the top, air is in the middle, and water is below on the earth. Thus, the light of the elements, which is the element of Fire, includes all elements and encompasses them. As I said above, the light of the element of Fire includes all the utterances and all worlds, spiritual and physical. Therefore, all the work of the six days of creation in the world of Action is included in "Fire."

For this reason, the Torah said: "You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings on the Sabbath day." This includes the general command: "You shall do no work in all your dwellings," for the creation of the light of fire includes the entire creation of work that God created in the world "in the beginning." Behold, the creation of the world was for the sake of man, "to work it and to keep it" [Genesis 2:15]. This is explained as "to work it" through the positive commandments and "to keep it" through the negative commandments, for the world stands upon the Torah...

# Tractate Shabbat

The "mice" <note>In Jewish folk-tradition and some mystical texts, mice are often associated with the loss of memory or the disruption of "calculation."</note> will not let the calculation rise in the distance to sixty; it does not change the meaning for every Sabbath to protect its boundary for the night. The conclusion of it all is that it is "a spark in the eye" regarding the concepts of "Remember" and "Observe" the Sabbath, as it is written: "Fear is at the center."
Therefore, they are included in two laws: the calculation with the exchange of sixty <note>sixty is a recurring number in Jewish law representing a "nullification" of impurity or a complete unit.</note>... and every person of the right <note>meaning those who follow the holy path</note> considers the days of the week toward the Sabbath, and these will rise for him as standing before the Lord.
One should not find it difficult that the calculation will be more than two thousand <note>The "Sabbath boundary" or distance one may walk on the holy day.</note>, namely the Sabbaths of the Sabbath. Know that the "Sabbath of the Sabbath" is entirely holy, and the "sixty" precedes the "thirty" <note>referring to various spiritual levels or measures</note>. Almost from this, every soul of Israel was a "thirty" Sabbath; therefore, one must guard the Sabbath even more, for it is itself the "Additional Soul" <note>term: <term>Neshamah Yeterah</term> — a kabbalistic concept that every Jew receives an extra spiritual soul during the Sabbath to better experience its sanctity.</note>.

### The Secret of Cutting Fingernails 
From the work *Tola’at Yaakov* <note>A 16th-century kabbalistic commentary on the prayer service.</note>: Know that the "garment" worn by **Adam the First Man** before the Sin of the Chariots <note>the Fall of Man</note> was called "the Backs" and "Knowledge." These were garments made of nail. When he was in the Garden of Eden, all the celestial "Chariots" surrounded him, and no evil thing could approach him. However, when he sinned, those lights were removed from him, and he was stripped of that holy garment. Nothing remained of it except what is at the tips of the fingers. "Filth" <note>impurity or spiritual residue</note> now surrounds them. Because one must not bring impurity into the Sanctuary, one must cut them on the Eve of Sabbath <note>Friday</note>, so that holiness does not descend upon the impure. One should not cut them on Thursday, because that is the "third day" before the Sabbath, and God made them to be feared before Him. We learn in the Talmud <note>Tractate Moed Katan</note>: Three things were said regarding fingernails: "He who buries them is righteous, he who burns them is pious, and he who throws them away is wicked." The reason is that they hint at "Judgment" <note>term: <term>Din</term> — the divine attribute of strict justice and limitation.</note>. He who removes them causes peace and mercy to prevail in the world. This is the quality of piety—that he restores peace to himself and others. Burying them is the act of a righteous person, for even if he did not remove the "Judgment" from the world entirely, he at least removed the stumbling block and quieted the Judgment. But he is not like the pious person [who burns them]. He who throws them away is wicked, for he causes Judgment to be drawn into the world. In the chapter "These May Shave," it is said: What is the reason? Lest a pregnant woman pass over them and miscarry. Perhaps this was the punishment [for Eve] because she caused Adam to be stripped of his precious garments. Because the remaining nail became a place for that "filth" to take hold, it became her punishment. And since Jonathan threw them in the synagogue... may God show us wonders from His Torah.

### The Secret of Reading the Names
It is written in *Kanfei Yonah* <note>A kabbalistic work by R. Menachem Azariah da Fano.</note>, Part 3, Chapter 7: Know that there are three "shells" <note>term: <term>Klipot</term> — spiritual layers of impurity that conceal the divine light.</note> around holiness, and the fourth is the "Shell of Radiance" <note>term: <term>Klipat Nogah</term> — an intermediate spiritual state that can be turned toward either good or evil.</note>. Sometimes it is holy, and sometimes it returns to the "shells," forming four shells total, as it is written: "and a radiance [Nogah] was around it." Converts are from this shell, for *Nogah* can also belong to holiness. Sometimes it flips to impurity. Onkelos the Convert <note>The famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic.</note>, who was from the aspect of *Nogah*, wanted to rectify it; he created the Aramaic Translation (*Targum*) to include it within holiness. Therefore, on Friday, when the holiness begins to enter, it is proper to review the Torah portion twice in Hebrew and once in translation <note>original: "שמו"ת" (Shemot)</note>, and not on Thursday. Also on the Sabbath day, for since they are prone to other "shells" on Friday, the *Nogah* shell seeks to enter holiness, and others want to enter holiness as well... as it says in the Psalm for the Sabbath Day: "When the wicked spring up like grass... it is that they may be destroyed forever." This means they want to sprout and rise to holiness on Friday... and this is "all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered," meaning they are divided: *Nogah* goes to holiness and the [other] shells to impurity. This is a profound depth: from where is it possible to provide kindness to the "shell" so it may be joined? Because *Nogah*... brings them from the "Waters of Kindness." This is the meaning of "Stolen waters are sweet"—the Waters of Kindness that are "stolen" by the *Nogah* shells are sweet to the shells that bind them together. When we say the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is in exile, it means it is within the *Nogah* shell, or through *Nogah* the shells have a "grip" on the Divine Presence. For Above, there is only peace and no evil thing. These three shells are the three "weekday" faces that precede the Sabbath: from Wednesday until Sabbath, and three after the Sabbath until Wednesday. So too is "a land of wheat and barley, grapes and figs"—the dark place where everything is eaten... yet it has some "garment," though not very important. In the Talmud, Rava pointed out a contradiction: it is written "on the high places of the city" and also "on a throne." This refers to *Nogah*, which at first hovers on the outside near holiness, but in the end, it draws truly close to holiness. On the Eve of Sabbath from the time of the Afternoon Prayer (*Mincha*) and onward—that is, at six and a half hours, or at the latest nine and a half—one must prepare the *Nogah* shell to rise into the holiness of the "Names" <note>the Torah portion</note>, as explained in *Tola'at Yaakov*. The reason for the Aramaic Translation is the same as the reason for the two pairs of *Tefillin* <note>phylacteries</note>, which is a Law given to Moses at Sinai. The Torah descended wrapped in it, like the goat-hair coverings over the Tabernacle. And because the Sabbath is "perfection," one completes his days and years through it... The reason for "Twice Scripture" corresponds to [the divine names] *Chay* and *Hav*, and "One Translation" corresponds to the [divine name] *Et*... 

The Ramak <note>R. Moshe Cordovero, a leading 16th-century Kabbalist in Safed.</note> wrote: In the Talmud, it says, "Whoever completes his portions with the community, his days and years are lengthened." They hinted at a secret here: "completing his portions" refers to the rectification of the Moon <note>Malchut/Sovereignty</note>, which is a "portion." One must see the days and generations... the written Torah is given between portion and portion... "With the community" <note>original: "ציבור" (Tzibur)</note> refers to the secret of the *Tzibur*—the collection of the ten emanations <note>term: <term>Sefirot</term> — the ten attributes through which God interacts with the world.</note>. One must complete the attribute of Sovereignty (*Malchut*) with the community so it is bound with Beauty (*Tiferet*). This is the secret of the "Unification" <note>term: <term>Yichud</term></note> performed through the reading... "His days are lengthened" refers to the six directions <note>the six emotional Sefirot</note>... "His years" refers to the attribute of Understanding (*Binah*).
The essence of the act is "Twice Scripture" and "Once Translation"—meaning Kindness (*Chesed*), Strength (*Gevurah*), and Beauty (*Tiferet*). The Translation is the scripture where life resides and does not change... some explain "Twice Scripture" as the letters *Yud* and *Vav* (Beauty and Foundation) and "One Translation" as Sovereignty... 

In practice, there are 30 rectifications. When one begins to study, before opening [the book], he should focus his intention on the vowels, notes, and letters... he should open his eyes to the Name of the Lord... one reads three times for the three Patriarchs... after finishing the portion without any interruption of speech, even for a necessity, he performs a "Unification" for the Crown (*Keter*). Each verse is read twice—once in Scripture and once in Translation... if it is Sabbath, he says "A Psalm, a song for the Sabbath day," and if Friday, he says "The Lord reigns," to bind the writings—Foundation and Sovereignty—with the Prophets. He should read one *Mishnah* <note>a unit of the Oral Torah</note> nearby... he must always conclude with the Hebrew Scripture, not the Aramaic or any other language, to return and strengthen the "Right side" <note>Mercy</note> over the "Left side" <note>Judgment</note>. This way is straight and appropriate for the act and the Unification.

Regarding immersion <note>in the Mikveh</note>: One must immerse three times. The first immersion is to remove the "filth" of sins, and afterward, the immersions correspond to the promise: "We will do and we will hear." *Kanfei Yonah* wrote the secret of the Friday immersion: whether before or after the afternoon prayer, it must be after midday. One should intend that the word for "Heaven" (*Shamayim*) equals 90, corresponding to the nine *Yuds* found in the four Divine Names...

# Tractate Shabbat

<margin>
"Last in deed, first in thought" <note>A famous phrase from the liturgical poem *Lecha Dodi*, meaning that although the Sabbath comes at the end of the week, it was the original purpose of Creation.</note>. So too, the end of "And [the heavens and earth] were finished" (*Vayechulu*) is a merit... at the times of *Vayechulu* and in the judgment for the dead... until the wine of the [Sabbath] entrance.

**A**t the conclusion of the Sabbath, we recite a blessing over the candle, because that is the beginning of the days of labor, [corresponding to] "And God said, Let there be light, and there was light" <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. Its secret lies in the Work of Creation <note>term: <term>Ma’aseh Bereshit</term> — the mystical study of the origins of the universe</note>. Thus far, regarding the benefit [of the light], as a foundation for the dead to remove His wrath from us. Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that at the time of the conclusion of a matter, one is permitted to benefit from it. This is hinted at in: "And God said, Let there be light... and He divided." "Let there be light" refers to the eve of the Sabbath, and "He divided" refers to the conclusion of the Sabbath, as we say "Blessed be He who created the lights of fire," hinting at the link in the creation of light. Therefore, the word "Created" (*Bara*) is used—not that He created it once in the past, but "He creates" (*Borei*) the lights of fire. "Creates" means He created it already and continues to create it even today. This is the secret of the cycle of the six days of creation, "Who renews in His goodness every day, continually, the Work of Creation." Their statement that they are not "new" means they are part of the Work of Creation—entering and exiting, entering and exiting, circling back. Regarding this, it says "every day, continually," meaning its continuity remains, as explained by the verse "A constant fire shall burn." Therefore, "lights" (*Meorei*) is plural.

Behold, the Sabbath points to the renewal of the world and the faith that "with the letters *Yod* and *Heh*, the Lord formed the worlds" <note>A midrashic interpretation of Isaiah 26:4, suggesting God used the Hebrew alphabet to build the physical and spiritual realms</note>. He is the One who brings all existence into being; He was, He is, and He will be. Correspondingly, the Sabbath hints at three distinct types of "Sabbaths": the Sabbath of Creation, the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah, and the Sabbath of the Future to Come, as mentioned previously.

This is hinted at in the three mentions of the "seventh" in the passage *Vayechulu*: "And on the seventh day God finished His work which He had made"—this is the **Sabbath of Creation**. "And He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had made"—this is the **Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah**; therefore, the word "all" was added, because with the acceptance of the Torah, the work of heaven and earth was completed. As our Sages said: "The Holy One made a condition with the works of creation: if Israel accepts the Torah, you shall endure; if not, I shall return you to void." "And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work which God created to do"—this is the completion of the **Sabbath of the Future**, for the six days correspond to the six thousand years of the world's duration. The "seventh day" corresponds to the World to Come, which is "entirely Sabbath" and entirely delight for receiving reward. Then there will be total rest from the "work which God created to do"—namely, the performance of the commandments. Man’s role is "to do" and "to guard" them now, in order to receive their reward later, which is the spiritual pleasure of the "World that is entirely Sabbath," as it is written: "And you shall call the Sabbath a delight."

Corresponding to these three, there are three levels of the soul: **Nefesh** (Vital Soul), **Ruach** (Spirit), and **Neshamah** (Higher Soul), which ascend one above the other. The world was created with Ten Utterances and remained suspended until the Ten Commandments. In the Utterances, the purpose was Man, "and Man became a living soul (*Nefesh*)"—this is the level of *Nefesh*. In the Giving of the Torah, which was "engraved" (*Charut*) on the tablets, our Sages said: "Do not read it as *Charut* (engraved), but as *Cherut* (freedom)," for the spirit of life (*Ruach*) was given to them to release the soul from its bonds. And "the breath (*Neshamah*) of the Almighty gives them understanding" comes from the side of *Binah* (Understanding), which is the World to Come. And behold, the *Chayah* (Living Essence) is the *Yod-Heh*, as is known, and the "Architect" that the Sages mentioned in the building of the world is these three: *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah*. Those who are of "the ascending class" draw these upon themselves by restricting the mundane yoke of the six days of the week, particularly the level of the World to Come, hinted at in the conduct of preparing oneself.

Also, regarding this matter, one pleads by saying *Vayechulu* three times <note>In the Friday night liturgy, this passage is often repeated in the silent prayer, after the prayer, and during Kiddush</note> in addition to what I wrote above. For the first time, one draws upon himself the sanctity of the *Nefesh*.

# Emek HaBerakhah 139

To bring a person [from the state of] Torah study <note>The Hebrew acronym ת"ת (TT) stands for *Talmud Torah*.</note> from house to house within a courtyard, and if there is an *Eruv* <note>term: <term>Eruv</term> — a ritual enclosure that allows Jews to carry items in public spaces on the Sabbath.</note> from a house to an upper chamber—this refers to the "Kingdom" (*Malchut*) ascending to the level of "Understanding" (*Binah*). These "upper chambers" are counted among the "houses" in its explanation. Moving "from courtyard to courtyard" refers to moving from a "hole" to a "sprout." The intention here is the "Kingdom" (*Malchut*) below, which serves as the gateway and entrance to all the *Sefirot* <note>term: <term>Sefirot</term> — the ten creative powers or attributes through which the Divine interacts with the world.</note>. That is to say, courtyards are open into it, and houses are closed off toward the courtyards, because the "Kingdom" (*Malchut*) is situated below "Victory" (*Netzach*) and "Splendor" (*Hod*). In this arrangement, *Malchut* is over *Netzach* and *Hod*; therefore, houses are open to courtyards, and courtyards are open to alleys.

The alleyway is situated below, and it is not permitted to carry within it except through its unification with "Foundation" (*Yesod*). This is achieved through a "side-post" (*lechi*)—specifically through the "Life of the Worlds" <note>original: *Chay HaOlamim*</note>, meaning that on the side of the alleyway, *Malchut* is toward the side of *Yesod*, and *Yesod* is toward the side of *Malchut*. Alternatively, one uses a "crossbeam" (*korah*), which represents the upper letter *Vav*, signifying the "Beauty" (*Tiferet*). For this reason, a side-post can be of any size, but a crossbeam has a specific required thickness. The side-post must be within three [handbreadths] of the wall, because the "Foundation" (*Yesod*) should not ascend from the upper *Vav* more than three handbreadths. This is like the saying: "There is nothing between the upper waters and the lower waters but three fingers" <note>A Talmudic metaphor for the thin veil between spiritual realms.</note>, which are *Netzach*, *Hod*, and *Yesod*. This ensures one does not ascend higher than these emanations. 

However, the crossbeam—representing the upper *Vav*—is invalid if it is higher than ten or twenty cubits, because "Beauty" (*Tiferet*) does not ascend above it more than ten handbreadths from above to below and ten from below to above. Therefore, it is permitted via a crossbeam. The "merging of alleys" (*Shitufei Mevo'ot*) and the "merging of boundaries" (*Eruv Techumin*) can be done with any food, as that unification is light. However, the "boundary" (*Techumin*) involves the feet—meaning *Netzach* and *Hod*—which is why an *Eruv* is needed for boundaries. Yet, for "houses within," the *Eruv* must specifically be made with bread, which is "bread that sustains the heart of man" <note>Psalm 104:15</note>, representing the complete unification.

### The Secret of
**Lighting the Sabbath Candle.** It is written in *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>term: <term>Tola'at Yaakov</term> — "The Worm of Jacob," a classic 16th-century Kabbalistic commentary on the prayer book by Meir ibn Gabbai.</note> as follows: "In the way of Truth <note>A common euphemism for Kabbalah.</note>, the secret of the 'Sukkah of Peace' is the souls, which are the lamps of the world. They arrive and rest upon those who are worthy of them. Therefore, the 'Kingdom of Sabbath' (*Malchut Shabbat*) distributes an 'additional soul' to them, and these are her lamps." For this secret reason, it is incumbent upon the woman—who hints at the "Kingdom" (*Malchut*)—to light the Sabbath candle. It is a great merit for her, as she will be granted holy children who shine with the Torah, who create peace in the world, and she causes her husband to have long life. She must light two wicks, corresponding to "Remember" and "Observe" <note>The two versions of the commandment to keep the Sabbath found in the Ten Commandments.</note>. 

So ends the quote from the tailor <note>Likely referring to a specific author or copyist known by this trade.</note> in the Seventh Gate. They said it is a commandment to light a lamp on the eve of Sabbath so there will be "peace in the home." This is because the Sabbath hints at the "Seventh Millennium," when the moon will have light like the light of the sun. Because of this, we are commanded to light a lamp on Sabbath night. Since the "Hidden Light" is within the house, and the drawing forth from it in this world is through the "Seal," the woman is commanded in its lighting. She should be precise in lighting seven lamps, as it is correct that "the seven lamps shall shed light toward the face of the Menorah" <note>Numbers 8:2</note>. Some light ten lamps, as they all shine, and "both these and those are the words of the Living God" <note>A Talmudic phrase meaning both customs are valid.</note>. These lamps do not all need to be on the table where one eats; even if they are arranged [elsewhere], they join together to hint at this secret.

### The Secret of the Version of
**The Kiddush.** "Blessed are You, Lord... who has sanctified us with His commandments and taken pleasure in us, and with love and favor given us His holy Sabbath as a heritage, a remembrance of the work of Creation... a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt... Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies the Sabbath." 

It is written in the book *Tikunei Shabbat*: The Ari, of blessed memory <note>term: <term>The Ari</term> — Rabbi Isaac Luria, the most influential mystic of the 16th century.</note>, wrote that it is a great mistake to say "in His heritage" (*be-nachalatanu*) without the letter *Vav*. This holy version has 70 words, like a crown. How could *Tola'at Yaakov* suggest the version should only have 35 words? Also, the passage "And [the heavens] were finished" (*Vayechulu*) has 70 words. How do we reconcile this? See there. What is written in *Leket Shikcha v'Peah* is that one should say "By your leave, my masters" (*Savri Maranan*) so that with these two words, the count reaches 72 words. *Vayechulu* also deserves to be joined to the count of 70 to reach 72, corresponding to the "Name of 72" <note>term: <term>Name of 72</term> — a powerful mystical name of God derived from Exodus 14:19-21.</note>. For "the world is built on kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>, and "Kindness" (*Chesed*) has the numerical value of 72. 

However, according to our custom, we begin with "The sixth day" (*Yom HaShishi*), and these two words must be added to the count of 72. One should intend that *Vayechulu* combined with the *Kiddush* makes 70 words for the aforementioned secret, and then think that by adding the two words "The sixth day," it becomes 72. Nevertheless, I agree that every time one recites a blessing on the Sabbath, he should say "By your leave, my masters" in honor of "New Faces" <note>A term for guests or new spiritual energy.</note>, but he should not include these two words in his mental count for the secret of the number. This is clear to the wise.

In the *Sefer HaMusar* (Chapter 4, in a gloss), another way is written regarding the joining to 72: "The foundation of the Friday night *Kiddush*—the early sages said a person must stand during *Kiddush* because it represents the 'Complete Bride.' Just as the seven blessings of a bride are recited while standing, and she is the 'Chosen Kingdom,' so too for the 'Upper Bride.' Since we must stand during the *Kedushah* prayer to honor her, how much more so here! Do not treat this matter lightly, for it is deep and great. The Bride is sanctified and united with the King, the Lord of Hosts." 

Our *Kiddush* has 35 words to complete the 72 Names with which the Bride is crowned. *Vayechulu* also has 35 words, completing the 70 or 72 words of the Names of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to crown the Bride. *Vayechulu* itself equals 72 in Gematria <note>term: <term>Gematria</term> — a system of Jewish numerology where letters represent numbers.</note>. If you ask why 70 and not more, know that the essence is the secret of the 70 Names, and the two extra are "faithful helpers." They are like the Sanhedrin <note>term: <term>Sanhedrin</term> — the supreme council and tribunal of 70 elders in ancient Israel.</note>, which has 70 members, but two "clerks" sit before them as witnesses, bringing the total to 72. So too here, the two blessings—"Creator of the fruit of the vine" and "Who sanctified us"—each start with "Blessed are You" (*Baruch Ata*). These two instances of "Blessed are You" hint at the two witnesses who sign with His Name, which is 70, to crown the Perfect Bride, bringing the total to the secret of the 72 Names. Therefore, do not be annoyed to stand for the sanctification of the Bride, for the honor of God and her honor. "Happy is the people for whom this is so" <note>Psalm 144:15. The word "so" (*kakhah*) also has the numerical value of 72.</note>.

### Regarding
**The Double Bread (*Lechem Mishneh*).** It is written in *Tola'at Yaakov*: We learn in the Talmud (Tractate Berakhot and Tractate Shabbat) that Rabbi Abba said: "A person is obligated to break bread over two loaves on the Sabbath, as it says: 'They gathered double bread' <note>Exodus 16:22, referring to the Manna.</note>." Rav Ashi said: "I saw Rav Kahana holding two but only breaking one." The "double bread" corresponds to "Remember" and "Observe." Rabbi Todros HaLevi explained this regarding the verse: "You cannot see My face, for no man shall see Me and live." 

In the Holy Zohar (Parashat Emor), it says: "We have established that 'two breads' refers to the two Divine Presences (*Shekhinot*)—the Upper and the Lower. This hints that two houses were built for their children, so that twice on the Sabbath there is sustenance, one for the upper life and one for the lower." The "Upper Presence" is the secret of "Understanding" (*Binah*), revealed through the letter *Vav*. The "Lower Bread" hints at the "Crown of the Lower Presence" which is always attached to the letter *Vav*. Since the "Crown" is awakened on Sabbath night, it is appropriate to break the lower loaf, which hints at her. This is why it says "for their children, two breads."

### The Secret of the Three
**Meals.** The *Tola'at Yaakov* states: Rabbi Isaac said: It is written, "And God blessed the seventh day," yet it is also written, "Six days you shall gather it [the Manna], but on the seventh day... there shall be none." If no food is found on it, where is its blessing? Rather, all blessings depend on the seventh day. Why did the Manna not fall on the seventh day? Because from the Sabbath, all the six upper days receive their sustenance. Each day feeds the world from what it received on the seventh day. Therefore, every Jew must arrange their table with bread and food on Sabbath night and Sabbath day, so that their table will be blessed all the days of the week. Blessing does not rest on an empty table. 

Through the "Upper Mercy" and the "Great Light," sustenance descends from the "Head of the Holy One" to the "Field of Holy Apples" <note>A Kabbalistic term for the *Sefirah* of *Malchut* or the Sabbath assembly.</note> three times on the Sabbath. These are the secret of the "Meals of the King." Therefore, our Sages commanded us to eat three meals on the Sabbath to mirror the upper pattern. The holy light of the *Zohar* explains the order:
1. The **Night Meal**: Concerning this it is written, "I will cause you to ride on the high places of the earth." This is the secret of the Bride who is blessed on this night; it is a time of joy.
2. The **Morning Meal**: Concerning this it is written, "Then you shall delight in the Lord." This is the secret of the "Ancient of Days" (*Atik Yomin*) revealed at that hour.
3. The **Third Meal**: Concerning this it is written, "And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father." This is the secret of the "Beauty of Israel" (*Tiferet Yisrael*). 

Since this meal is the completion of all, everything is perfected through it. We find that the "Holy Lamp" <note>term: <term>Holy Lamp</term> — *Butzina Kadisha*, a title for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar.</note> said at the time of his passing: "I testify about myself that all my days I never missed these three meals, and because of them, I never needed to fast on the Sabbath... One who merits them merits complete faith: one meal for the Queen, one for the King, and one for the Holy Ancient One." From his words, it appears the morning meal is for the King (the "Middle Line") and the afternoon meal is for the Ancient of Days. This order is more correct because at the time of the afternoon (*Mincha*)...

This is the meaning of "This is the glory..." and the secret of why he said "I have washed my feet, how shall I soil them?"—to avoid blessing the "shells" below. The reason for hot water... with the departure of Sabbath... the spark rises on Friday... meeting the wicked who enter Paradise. He should intend when washing his feet the name *Sandalphon* <note>term: <term>Sandalphon</term> — an archangel who, in Kabbalah, is said to stand at the "feet" of the Divine Throne and weave crowns for God from the prayers of Israel.</note>, who is at the feet of the *Shekhinah* on Friday eve as she adorns herself for the union of Sabbath night. Then is the washing of the feet of the *Shekhinah*... and after the man washes his feet on Friday in hot water, he should wear his best clothes, especially if they are white... as we explained the secret of the four white garments. Then he should go out to the field to welcome the Sabbath. I also found in the holy writings of the Ari that the surest time for the commandment of reading the weekly Torah portion is Friday after midday. I also found that one should intend in the Psalm "Ascribe to the Lord, O heavenly beings" (Psalm 29) three times... to strike the flames of fire, hinting at the souls that come on the Sabbath—the Extra Souls. Some come from the side of Cain and some from the side of Abel, all hinted at in this Psalm. Those from the side of Cain come in the Psalm "The Lord reigns, He is robed in majesty" (Psalm 93)... the initial letters of "The floods have lifted up, O Lord" <note>original: נשאו נהרות ה׳</note> total the numerical value of "Cain."

# The Secret of the Eruv
<note>term: <term>Eruv</term> — the legal/mystical "blending" of boundaries to allow movement on the Sabbath.</note>

To say that they are many from the side of the "Kingdom" (*Malchut*). A person should say... within his house, which is "Understanding" (*Binah*), for these are the three rectifications for *Malchut* called "House." They serve from the side of "Wisdom" (*Chokhmah*) within it... the secret of the *Shekhinah* is the "tithe" (*Ma'aser*)... and she is blended from the side of *Binah*, which gives to *Malchut* the *Eruv*—which is the "blending" (*Ervu*) of the Name of 72 and the letter *Yod*, meaning Mercy and Strength. He creates a pregnancy through the "Tiferet" (Beauty), the middle line. This is the *Eruv* from the side of *Tiferet*... This is the *Eruv* of boundaries, the *Eruv* of courtyards, and the partnership of alleyways. The matter is that the boundaries are all in *Malchut*, which is the house and foundation for all Emanation. Wherever she places a boundary... immediately *Tiferet* makes an *Eruv*. The secret of these boundaries is the Name *Yod-Heh* and then 2,000 cubits to the South, North, East, and West: *Yod* for South, *Heh* for North, *Vav* for East, *Heh* for West. And the 4,000 cubits... 2,000 cubits for each direction... 1,000 for South, 2,000 for North, 3,000 for East, 5,000 for West. Behold, the *Eruv* of boundaries is to bind the letters of the South to the North and the letters of the North to the South, and likewise East to West. This is the secret of the "Bond of 18" or the "Bond of the Name." Likewise with the Name *Adonai* (*A-D-N-Y*)... this is the sign of the *Eruv* of boundaries: to give the *Eruv* a bond... and so too with the Name *Adonai*. The matter of the *Eruv* of boundaries from the side of *Malchut* is because she is the one who sets the boundary for Holiness, and one must not go outside of it. The *Eruv* of courtyards refers to "Victory" (*Netzach*) and "Splendor" (*Hod*). There are houses within them which are aspects of *Malchut*. Every courtyard has two houses, meaning the aspect of the House of *Malchut* from the right and *Malchut* from the left. One should not have fewer than three in a courtyard—Strength, Beauty—and there are four with *Malchut*, five from the side of Mercy, Strength, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, six from the six extremities, seven from the seven *Sefirot*, eight with the side of *Binah*, nine with the side of *Chokhmah*, and ten from the ten *Sefirot*.

<meta>This page concludes the mystical and ethical discussion of the Sabbath (Tractate Shabbat) and begins the section on Passover (Tractate Pesachim). It continues the theme of spiritual preparation, moving from physical rituals to the internal sanctification of the soul through action, speech, and thought.</meta>

<page-num>140</page-num>
<header>Tractate Shabbat</header>

According to the commentary of Rabbi Obadiah <note>Rabbi Obadiah ben Abraham of Bertinoro (c. 1445–1515), a leading commentator on the Mishnah.</note>, the "dread of the Sabbath" is upon him, meaning that people are more afraid to commit a transgression or to lie on the Sabbath than on a weekday. From this we learn that even an unlearned person <note>original: *am ha'aretz*</note> is more fearful and anxious on the Sabbath day than on other days. How much more so should this apply to one in whom is hidden Divine presence, understanding, and wisdom from the holiness of the Sabbath and the gift of the "extra soul" <note>term: <term>Extra Soul (Neshamah Yeterah)</term> — A Jewish mystical belief that a person receives an additional level of spiritual consciousness during the Sabbath.</note>. When one prepares oneself for holiness, then the three levels of the soul—Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah—become interconnected. As it is written in the Zohar: "Blessed are the righteous who attach the animal soul to the spirit, the spirit to the higher soul, and the higher soul to the Holy One, blessed be He." I have already explained at length above that the Sabbath is the root of all days, and the weekdays are the "branches" of the Sabbath. 

The Sabbath and the weekdays together are like the form of the Menorah <note>The seven-branched candelabra used in the Temple.</note>: three branches on one side and three branches on the other, all of them facing the center lamp, which is the body of the Menorah. Similarly, there are three days before the Sabbath in which one sanctifies and prepares oneself—the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah—and three days after the Sabbath in which the impression of that holiness remains. Then, in the following three days before the next Sabbath, one prepares again. Thus the cycle repeats. Therefore, one should contemplate every day the holiness within it, which is a reflection of the Sabbath's holiness. On the Sabbath day itself, all holiness is gathered into one. It is not enough to possess the holiness of one's own self; rather, by receiving the Sabbath, a person should learn how to conduct themselves with holiness in the coming days, which are the branches of that holiness.

To reach these levels of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah <note>term: <term>Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah</term> — The three primary levels of the soul in Jewish mysticism, corresponding to action/instinct, emotion/speech, and intellect/thought.</note>, one must sanctify oneself in action, speech, and thought. This means all one's "tools of action"—one's 248 limbs—must be holy and separated from all sin or even the "dust of sin" <note>A legal term for activities that are not direct sins but closely resemble them.</note>. This is the secret of "turning from evil." Afterward, one must see to "doing good," performing commandments and good deeds with all one's limbs; through this, one awakens the spirituality of the *Nefesh*. Next, one must sanctify speech by guarding the tongue from evil and the lips from speaking deceit. Even regarding speech that is not a sin, but merely "mundane talk," I have found nothing better than silence, as the Sages said. Through this, one awakens the spirituality of the *Ruach*. Finally, one must sanctify their thought, which is the purity of the heart, so that there is no "disgusting or rejected" thought in one's mind. Rather, the thoughts should be holy and pure, clinging to the Living God, focusing on the depths of the Torah and the intentions of the commandments. There is no commandment that should not be bound by action, speech, and thought. That is, at the time of performing a commandment, one should speak and say: "Behold, I am performing this commandment which You commanded, and I do so with tranquility, humility, and joy, for the sake of the union of the Holy One and His Presence <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu u-Shechinteh*</note>, through the Hidden and Concealed One." 

When one speaks the laws of that commandment with their mouth, expressing the desire to perform it with all its beauty, they merit performing the commandment properly. This is also hinted at in the words of the Sages: "Study leads to action." This means the study of the commandment in one's mouth leads to an action that is beautiful and pleasing to the Creator. When one acts with the proper thoughts and the "secret" of the commandment according to their strength, they sweeten their speech, thought, and action, fulfilling the verse: "It is in your mouth and in your heart to do it." These matters have been explained elsewhere and will be explained further, God willing. To one who comes to be purified, the Holy One helps them reach these levels. As the Zohar says: to cling Nefesh to Ruach, and Ruach to the Holy One. Through this, the Sages hinted: "Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy." If a person sanctifies themselves a little from below, they are sanctified much from above. In this world, they are sanctified for the World to Come.

The same was said regarding impurity—Heaven forbid—but here we speak of the holiness of action and the body, the "small city" <note>A metaphor for the human body.</note> and the few people within it. The Holy One assists him and bestows the holiness of the *Ruach* upon him, in the secret of the spirituality of the *Nefesh*, the secret of the World of Action <note>term: <term>Asiyah</term> — The lowest of the four spiritual worlds, representing physical reality.</term></note>. "How manifold are Your works, O Lord." The sanctification from below is the holiness of speech, through which one resides with the ministering angels—for the tongue is what the angels use. They sanctify him from above and establish his intention to be refined from vanities. He merits the *Ruach*, the secret of the World of Formation <note>term: <term>Yetzirah</term> — The spiritual world above Asiyah, associated with emotions and angels.</term></note>. In this world, it can be said that he who sanctifies himself for the World to Come—that is, in his lifetime—through the spirituality of thought, then merits the spirituality of the *Neshamah*. This is the secret of the soul carved from the Throne of Glory, which is the secret of the World to Come. These things have already appeared at length in the book *Reshit Chokhmah* <note>A famous 16th-century Kabbalistic ethical work by Eliyahu de Vidas.</note> in the "Gate of Holiness," regarding the levels of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah and the speech, thought, and action that correspond to them. The "Living God" has elaborated on them; happy is the eye that has seen all these, and happy is the ear that hears and the heart that understands. One is sanctified with these three sanctities and enters the category of the Righteous, who cling Nefesh to Ruach and Ruach to Neshamah and Neshamah to the Holy One. This is the binding of the spiritual worlds of Action, Formation, and Creation. Through this, they enter the innermost chambers to live in the House of God and visit His Sanctuary.

# Tractate Shabbat is completed with the help of the Cause of all Causes.
## Tractate Pesachim: The Root, Foundation, and Pillar of Kindness <note>original: *Chesed*</note>.
# (As kindness is like a tower in the festival of Pesach... and so on.) It contains three chapters: "The Lamp of Commandment," "The Lamp of Torah," and "The Way of Life and Moral Rebuke."

<margin>Chapter: The Lamp of Commandment</margin> This chapter will discuss certain laws of the Passover holiday and the Counting of the Omer. It will also discuss laws of kindness and the overall matters of the Passover holiday. We begin with "This month shall be for you," which refers to the New Moon <note>original: *Rosh Chodesh*</note>, the first commandment given to Israel. Therefore, it is appropriate to mention some laws of the New Moon. The secret of Passover is that a person should examine their deeds and contemplate repentance <note>original: *Teshuvah*</note>. Additionally, the eve of the New Moon is like a "Minor Yom Kippur" <note>term: <term>Yom Kippur Katan</term> — A traditional day of fasting and repentance on the day before the New Moon.</term></note> on which it is proper to fast, receive symbolic lashes, and perform complete repentance, as explained earlier in Tractate Chullin. The reason for this is to repent before entering the new weeks ahead. This is also the time of the "flaw of the moon" relative to the light of the sun. Nevertheless, the Holy One established atonement on the New Moon, as stated in the Talmud regarding the moon's complaint, where the Holy One said: "Bring an atonement for Me for having diminished the moon." Though this statement is astonishing and contains wondrous secrets, we learn from it that the New Moon itself is a time of atonement. Therefore, every Jew should contemplate repentance and mend their deeds. It is clearly appropriate to do so before the Musaf <note>The additional prayer service for holy days.</note> prayer, as is understood by the wise.

## Afterward
"Go, eat your bread in joy." It is a commandment to increase the festive meal on the New Moon, as it is compared in the Torah to the Festivals: "On your days of joy, your festivals, and your New Moons." In the Prophets it says: "From month to month and from Sabbath to Sabbath," and "Why are you going to him today? It is neither New Moon nor Sabbath." It is written: "I will put an end to all her mirth, her festivals, her New Moons, her Sabbaths, and all her appointed feasts." It is written regarding Saul's sons: "Even today to the bread," and Jonathan replied, "We have a family sacrifice." It is written: "And it was on the day after the New Moon, the second day..." and in the Scrolls: "He called a festival against me." We derive from these that the New Moon is called a "Festival" <note>original: *Moed*</note>. It says in the first chapter of Megillah that if the Purim meal and the New Moon meal were not commandments, they would not be listed together. In the Peskita, it says that a person's sustenance is fixed for them from Rosh Hashanah to the next, except for what they spend on Festivals, Sabbaths, and New Moons. I found another reason: because we recite the Hallel <note>Psalms of praise.</note> on it, and the Zohar says: "This is the day the Lord has made, let us rejoice and be glad in it."

The language of the *Tur* <note>The *Arba'ah Turim*, a 14th-century legal code.</note> (Section 417) states: The New Moon is not forbidden for work. It also says in the first chapter of Moed Katan: The New Moon is distinct in that it has an additional offering <note>original: *Korban Musaf*</note> yet work is permitted. That which is said in Megillah regarding the "cancellation of work for the people," such as on the New Moon and the Intermediate Days of festivals, refers to a custom of refraining from work. Since there is no formal cancellation of work, if they spend the day in the synagogue, the Sages enacted to add one person and read four people from the Torah. This custom of refraining from work applies to women, as the Sages said that "their work is work" <note>meaning they have a valid custom to refrain from it</note>. Thus it is in the Jerusalem Talmud: "These women who have a custom not to do work on the New Moon—it is a valid custom." In the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer, it explains that because the women refused to give their jewelry for the construction of the Golden Calf, the Holy One gave them their reward: that they observe the New Moon more than the men. Another reason for this is that the Festivals were established corresponding to the Patriarchs: Passover corresponds to Abraham (as it says "knead and make cakes" on Passover), Shavuot corresponds to Isaac (the ram's horn of the Torah-giving was from Isaac's ram), and Sukkot corresponds to Jacob (as it says "and for his cattle he made huts/Sukkot"). The twelve New Moons of the year, which are also called Festivals, correspond to the twelve Tribes. And when they sinned...
