Our master Bahya wrote in the book *Table of Four* <note>original: "Shulchan Arba," a work on ethics and dining by Bahya ben Asher</note>, Gate 1, as follows: "Behold, we have heard with our ears and many have told me of the great men of Spain and the community leaders who practiced a very noble custom. It spread among them from ancient times that when they passed away to their eternal home, they would make their coffin from the very table upon which they fed the poor. This was done to awaken and fix in people's hearts the idea that a person does not labor for the wind, nor does their wealth go up with them. A person carries nothing of their labor under the sun except the good they do and the <term>tzedakah</term> <note>righteous charity</note> they show when they have mercy on the humble, as it is said: 'and your righteousness shall go before you' <note>Isaiah 58:8</note>." And it is similar <margin>in the portion Terumah</margin> to the words of my father and teacher, of blessed memory, and likewise in the "Ethical Will of the Inheritors" <note>original: "Tzava'at Yesh Nochalim"</note>: Host guests in your homes—meaning the wealthy—for wherever the commandment of <term>Hachnasat Orchim</term> <note>hospitality to guests</note> is mentioned, it refers specifically to hosting the wealthy and distinguished when they lodge with someone. One must receive them with a shining countenance, treat them with honor, and prepare delicacies for them (for anyone traveling on the road is considered "poor" at that moment, as the Sages of the Mishnah said). Our father Abraham, peace be upon him, saw that the angels were guests and wanted to slaughter three bulls for them to feed them tongues in mustard. But hosting the actual poor is included under the category of charity. So it is also in the *Yalkut* of the Maharal: Hospitality is part of <term>Gemilut Chasadim</term> <note>acts of loving-kindness</note>, which applies to both the poor and the rich. However, hospitality for the poor is primarily for the sake of charity and kindness, as it is written: "Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?" <note>Isaiah 58:7</note>. This includes two matters: one, to spread a cloth on the table for them so it is honorable; and further, that the master of the house must cut the piece of bread for them so the guest is not shamed. So it is also written in the Zohar.

<margin>Sow for yourselves according to righteousness, reap according to kindness <note>Hosea 10:12</note></margin>
**I**n Tractate Sukkah, in the chapter "The Palm Branch and the Willow," Rabbi Eleazar said: "Acts of loving-kindness are greater than charity, as it is said: 'Sow for yourselves according to righteousness (<term>tzedakah</term>), and reap according to kindness (<term>chesed</term>).' If a person sows, it is uncertain if he will eat or not, but if he reaps, he will certainly eat." And Rabbi Eleazar said: "Charity is only rewarded according to the kindness within it." Our Sages taught: In three ways is kindness greater than charity: charity is done with one's money, while kindness is done with both one's body and one's money; charity is for the poor, while kindness is for both the poor and the rich; charity is for the living, while kindness is for both the living and the dead. And we say in the Talmud: A person's "blood-money" is buried. Rabbi Hanina bar Papa said: "Any person who has grace upon them is certainly a God-fearing person." Maimonides wrote in the *Guide for the Perplexed*, Part 3, Chapter 53: It is known that "acts of loving-kindness" includes two meanings. One is to bestow good upon one who has no claim on you at all. The second is to do good for one who is worthy of it, but in a measure greater than they deserve. Most uses of the word "kindness" in the prophetic books refer to benefiting one who has no claim at all. Therefore, every good that comes from Him, may He be blessed, is called "kindness," as it says: "I will mention the kindnesses of the Lord." Because of this, the whole of existence—meaning God bringing it into being—is kindness. It says: <margin>The world shall be built on kindness</margin> <note>Psalm 89:3</note>, meaning the building of the world is an act of kindness. And of His attributes, it says "Abundant in kindness." "Righteousness" (<term>tzedakah</term>) is derived from the word "justice" (<term>tzedek</term>), which is fairness. Fairness means giving every claimant what they are owed. Kindness is giving to every existing thing what is appropriate for it. In this way, what a person gives of their money to the poor who is pressed for a livelihood is called "charity" because it is a duty. But what a person gives of their money beyond what is required, or to someone who is not poor but is simply unable to support themselves at the moment, or when a person assists another with their physical body (even a wealthy person, or by consoling or showing favor)—to anyone where there is no obligation to do so—it is called "kindness." This is because it is righteousness performed through the attribute of kindness without any obligation. Regarding such righteousness, which is "acts of loving-kindness," it says: "Sow for yourselves according to righteousness, and reap according to kindness." The author says: Kindness to those worthy of it and to those not worthy of it; for if they are worthy, you will be praised in your place, and if they are not, you will still have done what is right. "The kindness of God is all day long"—it is proper for a person that there should be no day in their life where they do not perform an act of kindness, either with their body or their money. We learn in Tractate Kallah: How do we dance? <note>A reference to a discussion on how to praise a bride</note>. Rabbi Abba taught: Anyone who possesses these three traits is certainly of the seed of our father Abraham: merciful, bashful, and performers of kindness. Bashfulness is also required, as it is written regarding the great vision: "Behold now, I know that you are a woman of beautiful appearance" <note>Genesis 12:11; a midrashic interpretation regarding Sarah's modesty</note>. Abraham did not even have "mercy" on his own son <note>referring to the Binding of Isaac</note> to show his love for the Holy One. And the masters of secrets gave a sign: "For His kindness has prevailed (<term>gavar</term>) over us"—*Gavar* is an acronym for *Gomlei chasadim* (performers of kindness), *Beishanim* (bashful ones), and *Rachmanim* (merciful ones).

# Tractate Pesachim
->Page 145<-

When Israel was in Egypt, they were under "another authority" <note>This refers to being under the dominion of the spiritual forces of impurity associated with Egypt</note> and they were gripped by impurity <note>original: *masabuta*, an Aramaic term for ritual or spiritual defilement</note>, just as a woman is when she encounters her days of impurity. After they were purified, they entered into the holy portion which is called "Covenant." Once they were purified within it, the impurity ceased, just as the blood of impurity ceases for a woman. After the impurity subsided from her, what is written? "She shall count for herself seven days" <note>Leviticus 15:28</note>. So too here: once they entered the holy portion, the impurity ceased from them, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "From now on, counting is for merit." "And you shall count for yourselves" <note>Leviticus 23:15</note>—this is precise, just as it is written "She shall count for herself," meaning for her own benefit, so too here "for yourselves" is for your own benefit. And why? In order to be purified by high, holy species <note>spiritual emanations</note>, so that later they might come to be united with the King. This became the fence of the Tabernacle that issued from Him. And because of this, the Sabbaths are certain, for he brings them in like a woman who cannot be intimate <note>original: *le-vayala*</note> until she uses the eye-paint <note>cosmetics for purification/preparation</note> and until the dew descended upon the camp at night. "Upon the camp" is written, and it is not written "the dew descended at night." And when did this dew descend? When Israel approached Mount Sinai, a type of that dew that gives life to the dead shone upon them. <note>The author is linking the dew that fell with the manna to the "Dew of Resurrection" that will revive the dead in the future.</note>

This dew deepened from the source of "Existence" <note>original: *yesh*</note> which was prolonged, and with a "teacup's measure" they were awakened from the matter of the spreading forth that occurred after the creation of the world. "Egypt and the Serpent are seen," and he sat naked. Likewise in Egypt: "And you were naked and bare" <note>Ezekiel 16:7</note>. This was the sin of Adam, the sin of the wheat <note>A common Rabbinic tradition identifies the Forbidden Fruit as wheat</note> that fell into the "Hushon of the noise," the source of the filth <note>term: *zohama* - the spiritual residue or "grime" left by the serpent in Eden</note> that was drawn upon him and all his descendants. Those sins required refining and whitening, and this is the reason for the Egyptian exile. Just as silver is refined in a furnace, so were they in the "iron furnace" of Egypt so that all the sparks of silver might be turned upward. Therefore, all the individuals of the broken spirit were brought into exile so that perhaps the servitude might be repaired. It is said, "All that David inherited us," and regarding them it is said, "You shall deliver the quota of bricks," until all the silver came out refined and clean from all dross—six hundred thousand <note>60 *ribbon*</note>, corresponding to the number of the "six ends" and the seventy nations.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to purify the holy ones and took them out from Abraham, and from the "left side" of Isaac came Esau, until Jacob, who was pure, was ready to receive the holy portion. He was the barrier for the whole community. This is why they were refined like silver in the "iron furnace" <note>original: *kur ha-barzel*</note> in Egypt. They were refined until the number of six hundred thousand was reached. It was appropriate for them to receive the "yoke of converts" because all the sparks of holiness had already been gathered from among the "husks" <note>term: *klipot* - "shells" or "husks" that conceal the divine light</note>. Regarding this, it is said: "The nations saw and were ashamed." When Israel stood and saw, He permitted them the seven commandments, for there were no longer sparks to be found among them. This is also why we do not accept converts in the days of the Messiah. Because of the "mixed multitude" <note>original: *erev rav* - the group of non-Israelites who left Egypt with the Hebrews</note> and the sin of the Golden Calf, the matter returned to its ruined state, and they required the rest of the exiles. The final redemption will be "like the days of your coming out of Egypt." If not for the help of Heaven that assisted Israel in Egypt, they would have almost been sunk in the forty-nine gates of impurity, as the power of the impure husk grew and ruled over them. Therefore, they left in haste <note>original: *be-chippazon*</note> so as not to enter into the building of impurity. This will not be the case in the future redemption, as it is written, "For you shall not go out in haste" <note>Isaiah 52:12</note>.

Before the commandment of "freedom on the tablets" <note>The Torah given at Sinai</note>, with the breaking of the forty-nine gates, the renewal of the world began. Adam was steeped in the "filth of the serpent." *Chametz* <note>leavened bread</note> indicates the "sourdough in the dough," which is the evil inclination. But *Matzah* is flour and water as they are, not taken from anything else. It is a metaphor for the creation of heaven and earth. Even though they are made of other things, the essence of the reward is "water." The world had no father or mother other than the Holy One, Blessed be He, in His glory. Likewise, the heavens and the earth and all their host, upper and lower, were all created "something from nothing." Just as existence was made from absolute nothingness, and afterward the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought forth "something from something," so it is with the Passover offering. In the evening you shall eat *matzah* as an obligation on the first night, and afterward, for all seven days, it is optional <note>meaning one is not *required* to eat matzah, but is forbidden from eating chametz</note> to indicate the seven days of Creation. This matter will be explained further at length.

Regarding the secret of the New Moon and Adam: Adam the first man was the vitality of the world. When he corrupted and sinned, the filth of the serpent entered him—this is the "old sourdough" and the evil inclination. He caused death upon himself. This is the secret of "all leaven shall not be eaten." Leaven <note>original: *chametz*</note> has the numerical value <note>gloss: Gematria</note> of the letters *chet* and *tzadi*. 

<column-break/>

...corresponding to the number of the arrangements of twenty-six <note>the numerical value of the Tetragrammaton, God's name</note>. All agree that in Nissan the creation was in potential, and in the "count of the days of the year" it was in potential before us. Rabbi Yehoshua says that Nissan is the primary end, while Rabbi Eliezer says Tishrei is the primary end. This is what I have heard and what I have seen from a Kabbalist. Therefore, the obligation is so famous. 

And what I wrote about the "end of everything" occurring in Nissan—this is because the actual creation was revealed then. There is the nature of Tishrei and the nature of Nissan. They must be joined together. As it is taught in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah: "From where do we know that we count years from Tishrei?" It is said, "From the beginning of the year until the end of the year." Nissan is called the "first of months." 

It is known that the Exodus was with signs and wonders. We must say that the obligation of the seven days of Passover corresponds to the seven days of creation. Regarding the future, it is said that the eighth day will be the Great Day of Judgment. Likewise, in the month of Tishrei, we say it is a "day of blowing the horn" for our festival day. 

Jacob is the "sun" while the moon represents the future. It is said that there will be "two great lights." This means holiness will be increased. It is explained in the Zohar: Rabbi Yose opened and said: "The gates of the inner courtyard shall be shut during the six days of work, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened." This means the light of the six days of creation is hidden, but on the Sabbath, the light is opened. The light of the New Moon is also opened, but it is still hidden from the "prosecutors" <note>accusing spiritual forces</note>. Once the prohibition is removed, one can join with the King. This gate is not opened except on the Sabbath and on the New Moon. On the weekdays, the "lower gates" are the ones through which the sustenance flows to the world. But for Israel, they are crowned with the "sign of the covenant" and they prepare themselves to receive the light...

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic exploration of the Jewish calendar, specifically the spiritual link between Passover and Shavuot through the Counting of the Omer. It bridges the previous page's discussion on purification with a cosmological explanation of the "Fifty Gates of Understanding" and the Sabbatical cycles of time.</meta>

# Tractate Pesachim

After the days of labor, it is known that the root of the Days of Creation above is the "Secret of the Building" <note>This refers to the lower seven *Sefirot* or divine emanations: *Chesed* (Kindness), *Gevurah* (Strength), *Tiferet* (Beauty), *Netzach* (Victory), *Hod* (Splendor), *Yesod* (Foundation), and *Malchut* (Kingship).</note>. These are all interconnected, and this is the secret of their completion: each one is included within the others. 

Together, they form forty-nine levels, and with their singular root that encompasses them all, they reach fifty—the Fifty Gates of Understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note>. Forty-nine gates of Understanding were given to Moses and attained by him, but the fiftieth gate remained beyond reach. The "Building" emerged from Understanding starting from the attribute of Kindness, for it is said, "The world shall be built with Kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3; original: *Olam chesed yibaneh*</note>. Thus we have seven times seven. Similarly, in the physical world of Action below, every single day is naturally composed of all seven days, but the specific action of a particular day is simply the most revealed. I have already elaborated on this previously in Tractate Chullin <note>The volume of the Talmud dealing with dietary laws</note> and elsewhere: even each of the six weekdays contains a spark of the Sabbath, and therefore one must treat them with some small measure of Sabbath sanctity. This is why an oath <note>original: *shevuah*</note> is related to the word for Sabbath <note>original: *shabbat*</note>, as explained at length earlier. Conversely, the Sabbath includes all the days of labor, because on the Sabbath, "Rest" was created. The nature of this Rest is that it is never stagnant; as our Sages of blessed memory said: "Torah scholars have no rest in the World to Come, but go from strength to strength" <note>Psalm 84:8</note>, from one attainment to the next. This is a process without limit or measure, and this constant growth is itself the cause of spiritual rest, delight, merit, and the expansion of the soul within Israel. <margin>Regarding one's work during the weekdays: the forty-nine levels of action mirror their root above. The six days of the "Building" interact with one another to reach forty-nine, while their ultimate root is the essence of Understanding, where everything exists in a hidden state. These forty-nine levels correspond to the worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action, while Understanding remains hidden. They are revealed in the likeness of the three higher attributes and the six days of the Building that intermingle.</margin> In them, every day's work is elevated on the Sabbath to a spiritual level, for the commandment of the Sabbath is like the fulfillment of all commandments. All this was explained earlier at length, showing how every day is included in all days, making every day essentially a "week." It is known that the "First Point"—the something-from-nothing called by the letters *Yod* and *Lamed* <note>Referring to the first letter of the Name of God and the concept of "to/for"</note>—contains the entirety of the Work of Creation. This Point and the Work of Creation are like a "general rule and its details" <note>A classic rabbinic hermeneutic: the whole contains nothing but what is in its parts</note>; they are all one.

The "end of one thing is the beginning of another," and so it is below with variations. According to the Ramban <note>Nachmanides, a 13th-century scholar and mystic</note>, the Days of Creation hint at the ages of the world, each day representing a thousand years. When you calculate seven days times seven, you get forty-nine thousand years, which is the "reproach of the world," followed by the fiftieth millennium. <margin>This is the secret of the Sabbatical years (*Shmita*) and the Jubilee (*Yovel*) mentioned by the Kabbalists. There are seven Sabbatical cycles, each seven thousand years, and one year of desolation, totaling forty-nine thousand years. The fiftieth millennium is the Jubilee, which "builds the Great Jubilee" where all existence returns to its source, following the secret of "returning to one's sister" <note>A mystical metaphor for returning to the divine source</note>. This is the "Great Freedom," for there everything is preserved without the dross or "touch" of external, impure forces. In the realm of Emanation <note>original: *Atzilut*</note>, these hidden things will be clarified even for the external forces. This alludes to the "World to Come," both revealed and hidden—see "No eye has seen, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. I have elaborated on this "Preserved Wine" elsewhere. Thus the matter of Passover is clarified: the first day of Passover testifies to the renewal of the world, made famous through the people of Israel. For their sake, the Holy One, Blessed be He, renewed the world so they would receive the Torah. The choice of the fifty levels is for God's garden, and we are His people. After this choice, we were commanded to begin immediately from that day to count seven times seven—seven weeks. There is a commandment to count weeks and a commandment to count days, to show that every day is its own "week" and corresponds to a thousand years. Afterward comes the Festival of Shavuot <note>Weeks</note>, the holiday that includes all the weeks. This is the secret of Understanding (*Binah*), the limit of what can be given in the Torah, for then "the Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, clinging to the Name of God. This is the great spirituality of the World to Come. The Torah has "forty-nine facets" corresponding to the seven complete cycles. The Sages and Rabbi Yose disagree: one says the Torah was given on the sixth of Sivan, and the other says on the seventh.</margin> <margin>Both views point to the same thing. The Torah was given on the fiftieth day; the "branches" come from the fiftieth day, not just the forty-nine. Even though Moses attained forty-nine, the Torah was given after the fiftieth day because the Fiftieth Gate will eventually be reached in the eternal future. But the fiftieth day itself is a "surrounding" day, called the "Sabbath-hood" that includes all weeks. Just as the general rule contains only what is in the details, the forty-nine levels are revealed, and the fiftieth is the hidden root, just like the seven days of Creation where each day is included in the others. The "First Point" contains them all. What exists in the days is the same as what exists in the "primordial matter" <note>original: *hiyuli*</note> and the hidden power. Thus it is explained that we count fifty days—we count seven weeks—and even though they are technically only forty-nine, they are in truth fifty, because the Fiftieth Gate *is* the forty-nine, and the forty-nine *are* the fifty.</margin> <margin>Passover testifies to the renewal of the world, and the Counting of the Omer indicates the time of the future renewal and its purpose.</margin> Thus we find the world was created in the month of Tishrei <note>Autumn</note>, and the "Building" of its renewal was revealed. Everything you find in Tishrei, you also find in Nisan <note>Spring</note>. <margin>The first of Tishrei is the New Year, and the tenth is Yom Kippur, corresponding to the Ten Sayings with which the world was created.</margin>

---

Similarly, the first of the month of Nisan is the "first of the months of the year." Afterward, on the tenth, they were commanded to take the Passover lamb. That day was a Sabbath, and it is called "The Great Sabbath" (*Shabbat HaGadol*). <margin>The number 20 corresponds to 8... as hinted above. The Great Sabbath is always linked to the world... everyone agrees the Torah was given on the Sabbath. The days hint at the millennia... the forty-nine facets... the six thousand years and the one of desolation. The Sabbath, in its inner dimension, points to the essence of the Sabbath, like the "primordial matter" below and above. This is the Great Sabbath that points to the "renewals" where the husks will be nullified. This is the "binding" and the removal of "garments of skin" <note>referring to the physical body or material world</note>, showing the power of the Elevated One alone. After the day of eating Matzah, the first day of Passover, we begin counting forty-nine days, and then the Torah was given on the fiftieth day, which was the Great Sabbath. All this points to the future. Just as God gave the months in which Israel left Egypt and sat them in "Clouds of Glory"—for Sukkot in Tishrei commemorates this—so too after Sukkot is the "Assembly" (*Atzeret*) for God. Similarly, after the days of the Counting and the Great Shavuot, we circle the Altar seven times. On each day of Sukkot, they only circled once, but the seven circles hint at the seven cycles of the world—the six thousand years mentioned by the Kabbalists. The power of the nations diminishes as the festival sacrifices are offered. All this is hinted at in the days of the Counting. Afterward, the "Assembly" of Nisan (Shavuot) and Tishrei (Shemini Atzeret) are equal. <margin>And if you ask: what is the practical difference for this doubling? Or why in Tishrei is the "Assembly" attached to the seven days of the festival, while in Nisan it is delayed until after the Counting? Know that Nisan is the month of Spring (*Aviv*) and Sukkot is the Harvest Festival (*Asif*). Nisan hints at the World of Action—the "today to do them." It is the month of Spring, the time of man's standing and productivity. </margin> Tishrei is the time of gathering, the end and purpose of man, where he labors and gathers—hinting at "tomorrow to receive their reward" <note>A common rabbinic phrase distinguishing this world of action from the next world of reward</note>. It is as if to say: Nisan hints at the reason the world was created, which is for labor and guarding, for study and action—"today to do them." Tishrei hints at the final renewal of the world, the state of "tomorrow to receive reward," when the Hidden Light will be revealed. It is all one matter, for "the reward of a commandment is the commandment itself"—meaning its spiritual essence, as explained at length in the introduction. <margin>The history of man and the need for this world... "today to do them"... and the lordship over all impurity and dross. God chose us as His people... he saved them from the poverty and sinking of Egypt. Even though because of impurity she requires a counting, Shavuot follows, and then she is elevated above.</margin> The Zohar, in the portion of *Emor*, says: Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the road. Rabbi Hiyya said, "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Sabbath..." what is this dealing with? He said to him, the colleagues have already established it, but come and see...

Yom Kippur is like the Sabbath... the six days correspond to the Sabbath... as explained above in the laws... Afterward, the garments that were created... the Queen's garment... the attribute of Kingship (*Malchut*)... the Temple... the number 13... as is known... the secret of the Sukkah... the number 10... Similarly Jacob... Sukkot... the 50 gates... justice and mercy... Yom Kippur... all included in the Sabbath... this is for the wise... the year is nothing but... 355 days... everything is clarified in the calculation... then the hostage is released... twelve months are the details of the branches... It was clarified that in Tishrei the world was created... wisdom... It is said that Yom Kippur contains the power of all the permutations... Tishrei is the permutation of Tishrei... Passover is like the Sabbath... I have written this and it is close to the truth.</margin>

# Tractate Pesachim

...a message for every answer we are destined to receive in the end, which is the help of the Master of the World, destined to be renewed for us. Therefore, we remove the leaven <note>original: *chametz*</note> from the sixth hour and onwards to allude to the seventh millennium, which is the Sabbath <note>A common Jewish mystical belief that history lasts 6,000 years, followed by a 1,000-year "Sabbath" or Messianic age</note>. At that time, the "evil inclination" <note>original: *yetzer hara*</note> will be nullified from the world. Furthermore, this great matter of needing to remove the leaven hints to us a deep secret. Know that it should not be seen, for leaven represents the "Prince of the Shore" <note>A mystical reference to the forces of impurity or the *Sitra Achra*</note>. This is alluded to in the name of Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon, so as not to "cut the saplings" <note>A kabbalistic idiom for heresy or damaging the divine unity</note>. This ends the quote.

And these are the words of the *Book of Moral Instruction* <note>original: *Sefer HaMusar*</note>: Know further that the secret of removing leaven on the night of the fourteenth of Nisan <note>The night before Passover begins</note> is that the early sages—who were masters of truth—would take ten pieces of bread and place them in the ten corners of the house. They would then return to the first corners and take the piece they had placed there, reciting the blessing "over the removal of leaven." They would then gather them in a bowl and keep them until the next morning at the time of burning, when they would burn them in the usual way. 

But what is the secret of the matter? Why ten pieces—no fewer and no more? It is to allude to the "ten impurities" <note>The *Kelipot*, or shells of spiritual impurity that oppose the ten holy *Sefirot*</note> in order to nullify them and remove them from the world, so that no accuser remains in the world against Israel. Rather, Israel creates mercy for themselves on Passover. This is what is written: "It is a night of guarding for the Lord" <note>Exodus 12:42; original: *Leil Shimurim*</note>, meaning it is guarded from the "damagers," the catastrophes, and the accusers of the world. On this night, the people sit guarded in "freedom" <note>original: *benei chorin*</note> like good wine that has sat on its dregs, and like a protective shield against any evil mishap, evil Satan, or any accusation. Therefore, the Blessed Name commanded us to "nullify the leaven" on Passover. This is a structure for every wise and understanding person. The Sages of blessed memory also said there are two severe qualities in the world: leaven <note>*chametz*</note> and leavened grain <note>*machmetzet*</note>, representing male and female aspects of impurity. This ends the quote.

Thus, they have cut through the trap of the "husks" <note>original: *kelipot*</note>—for "the wicked walk on every side"—and achieved the Matzah <note>Unleavened bread</note>, which represents freedom. Likewise, the four cups of wine correspond to the four expressions of redemption. They are all guarded from the "Guarded Place" <note>A reference to the higher divine realm of *Binah* or Understanding</note> where there is no touch of the stranger and no nourishment for the "husks." This is the secret of the fruits of the Garden called the "World to Come." There, the Sages hinted at the "Guarded One" in his affairs, as they said: "No eye has seen it, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>—this is the "Guarded Wine" <note>A mystical concept of wine kept in its grapes since the dawn of creation</note>. There, the structure is firm, for the "touch of the stranger" only begins from the "Arms" and outward <note>A reference to the lower *Sefirot* of *Chesed* and *Gevurah* where external forces can sometimes attach themselves</note>, as the descendants of Ishmael have a hold in the Kindness of Abraham, and Esau in the Strength of Isaac. This is explained at length in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*. 

The Matzah is called *Matzah* because from eternity... the cups and the clarifications, and the "Guarded Wine." The Matzah and the wine are the rectification for the sin of Adam, the First Man. Some say the forbidden fruit of the Tree of Knowledge was wheat, and some say it was a cluster of grapes. The truth is both: Matzah is the rectification for the wheat, and the wine is the rectification for the cluster of grapes.

# And Behold

As for the commandments practiced on this holy night of Passover—the Passover offering, Matzah, Bitter Herbs <note>original: *maror*</note>, the four cups, the two dippings, and the reclining—they possess great reasons, both revealed and hidden, and secrets within secrets. It is a great commandment to tell of the Exodus; the more one tells, the more he is praised. Every person is obligated to tell of these things, to understand, and to gain insight as far as his intellect can reach. Among my beloved sons and brothers, I will arrange two matters which stem from a single root...

<margin>
Another matter: I will record some of the precious sermons we gave in previous years regarding the "Great Sabbath" <note>The Sabbath immediately preceding Passover</note> and the commandments practiced on Passover. They contain true things based on the truths of the Torah and precious reasons that differ in the stories of Egypt, including many beautiful literal explanations of the Haggadah.
</margin>

...this revealed the matter.

The building of the prayer through the secret of Kindness, for "the world shall be built with Kindness." It is the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>, the "Building of the Smallness" <note>A term for the *Sefirah* of *Malchut* in a diminished state</note> until it stands in its place and becomes a complete structure of the "Heaven" and the "Earth," which are the attributes of Beauty <note>*Tiferet*</note> and Strength <note>*Gevurah*</note>. When these are in their place, the "Smallness" is nullified and the "Greatness" <note>Maturity/expansion of the divine lights</note> returns to it, and it becomes "Face to Face." This is the higher ritual action that corrects the Divine Presence. 

When the light reaches the "Lower One" <note>The earthly realm or the final *Sefirah*</note>, it is as if the ends of the six directions are now two personifications <note>original: *partzufim*</note>, separated one from the other. And so it is with the three lower levels... the Holy One, Blessed be He, took pity on the upper ones... as it is written in the Zohar... 

This is the secret of the "Building" mentioned above: "And the Lord God built the rib" <note>Genesis 2:22</note>. From this, the "Building" is established below. This is why one must work and not resemble the lower ones. All those who seek to be corrected should be corrected towards the "Truth." Before this, they did not distance themselves... but once the "leaven" is no longer there, the "Upper One" can be arranged in its building... 

Therefore, it is established forever and ever, made in truth. Furthermore, they are established as "Face to Face," meaning they are the Divine Presence in its fullness. The light then shines upon the world, and everything is corrected. It is the secret of the Sabbath, which stands in its own right until the light is drawn down upon the "other," for the world was not created for the sake of the "husks." 

The "Building" is thus corrected, and the lower ones are arranged according to the "Upper Secret," which is the Holy of Holies. If the ritual action was not performed properly, the Presence of God would not rest upon the earth... as it says, "And a mist went up from the earth." This refers to the "vapor" of the lower ones that rises to the "Male" aspect to cause a union... This is the secret of the "Night of Guarding," for the light is awakened from below to the "Righteous One" <note>the *Sefirah* of *Yesod*</note>. Therefore, on Passover, they were satiated with the light of the "Inner Face," and the lower was elevated to the attribute of Beauty... 

Every person in their place... and this is the "Seven Days" and the "Ritual Action." These are the "Two Tables." This is the secret of the "Foundation of the Earth," for there the union of the Kingdom <note>*Malchut*</note> is revealed... following the words of the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel. The Sages said: "The secrets of the name *Y-H-V-H* are four," and they correspond to the "Head of the Thought"... and this is the revelation of what is written in the whole Torah... 

This is the "Precious Song" and the "Kingdom." It is impossible to bring the Presence down into the "Crown of Kindness" without first removing the "Leaven." This is the secret of the "Head of the Year"... and the "Life" in the attributes... This is the "Beauty of the Kingdom" in the secret of "Kindness." Afterward, everything returns to its order and becomes "Face to Face." The "Leaven" and the "Husk" are pushed aside, and the "Judgment" is sweetened... to be the "Living Water" to see every thing. This is the "Secret of the Foundation" which was corrected from the beginning. Through the "Ritual Action" of the "Early Ones," the thoughts and intellects in the actions of the Sages were aligned... the intention being to strengthen the "Mind"... and there would be no more "Two"... but a sweetening... for the world was created for the sake of the "Righteous," who is the "Beauty" and the "Prince"... and the "Kingdom" in the secret of "Kindness." All of this is connected to the secret of Passover.

# Tractate Pesachim

The proper intent of prayer is through <term>Kindness (Chesed)</term>, as it is said, "A world of kindness shall be built" <note>Psalm 89:3; original: *Olam chesed yibaneh*</note>, meaning the cause of its existence. It is also explained that the knife of <unclear>sanctity</unclear> and the secret of the <term>Sacrifice</term> stand in their place. This involves the seven <note>Referring to the seven lower *Sefirot* or divine emanations</note> and the four, and the seven heavens... and the heavens for His existence are <term>Kindness (Chesed)</term>, <term>Strength (Gevurah)</term>, and <term>Beauty (Tiferet)</term>. If they are not in their place within <term>Beauty</term>, there is no peace. This relates to the tenth <note>The Sefirah of *Malchut* or Kingship</note>... as it is written regarding the "face of the day," <note>original: *pnei yom*</note> that the three are from the beginning, and he is able to reach the place of his existence in <term>Beauty</term> and <term>Kindness</term>. When it is lacking from him, it is written that they are "face to face," <note>original: *panim b'panim*</note> which is the secret of the emanation of the <term>Crown (Atarah)</term> and <term>Kingship (Malchut)</term>... under him in the world of the four. It was as if they were as one, even though they are now "two visages" <note>original: *partzufim*; a kabbalistic term for divine configurations</note> separated from one another. And so it was with the bread, and from this you can understand the secret of the four visages. Afterward, the Holy One, Blessed be He, was revealed, for the lower world testifies to the Upper World. If you know the words of the <term>Zohar</term> <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> as hinted at... regarding the "Crown" from the Sabbath... and regarding the Tabernacle... the blessings are not found until the "forty-nine" levels of blessings... because it is written "for He did not bring rain," <note>Genesis 2:5</note> for with these, the union <note>original: *zivug*</note> was not found in the proper repair until <term>Foundation (Yesod)</term>... and all was not repaired until the Tabernacle was established. For the sake of the Tabernacle, which is called "The Fifty," <note>Likely referring to the 50 cubit measurements or the 50 hooks of the Tabernacle</note> the poor man... and until the lower is repaired, the upper is not repaired. When the two are repaired below, they are repaired above. Because the "knowledge" was not here, it was not repaired above, and the blessings were not found... and this is the secret of the verse, "for the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth" <note>Genesis 2:5</note>. Therefore, there is no work to be done... and the Lord, who is the Beauty of a woman, the Beauty of the three... and before this, there was no perfection. Therefore, there was no knowledge here... although they were prepared in every detail... and not yet above, to awaken the Upper World... male and female... to receive... for the world is lacking. Regarding the "Guarded Wine," <note>original: *yayin meshumar*</note> these are the words of the Sages... for these are the worlds... the world of the <unclear>throne</unclear>... the world was not yet repaired... because "the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth," for he had not yet created... and when the world was repaired below... and they were prepared for the Tabernacle... if the beginning was not... then the actions were not in the proper state of repair. Therefore "the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth." Despite all this, he created two visages... and it was not as one... for all that "the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth," etc. In any case, it testifies to the "forming of the heart"... for it was a commandment... and here are included the visages... in the "Secret of the Ten"... <note>original: *Sod Ha-Assarah*</note> spreading from the source and providing the intentions of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*)... as it is in the <term>Zohar</term>. And we find in the "Gate of Forty-Nine"... and it was not written... and see that in these visages... for they are the worlds... the words of the Sages who explained... there is the secret of the soul... the first and the last... and the secret of the repair of the "forty-nine"... the strength of the "fifty"... and these are the names of the Sages... for they are the "Living Creatures" <note>original: *Chayot*; the angelic beings of Ezekiel's vision</note>... the beginning shall be <term>Kindness</term> and <unclear>sustenance</unclear>... above nature... in the secret of the removal <note>original: *bi'ur*</note>... which is the secret of... the Tabernacle and the Wisdom in the secret of... the repair of the world... and he did not... for I did not... and those who dwell... as it is written in the "Maaseh Merkavah" <note>The "Work of the Chariot," an early form of Jewish mysticism</note>... and they are in the hidden heavens... and it was the secret of the heavens... <term>Kindness</term>... for the wicked... the sun shall be diminished... for the Lord is written in the heavens... and she is the Divine Presence in her repair... and this is the one above... <term>Beauty (Tiferet)</term>... near to the king's palace... "the King of Life"... the six kings... all is holy... in the name of Kindness...

<column-break/>

a message for every act of repentance that we are destined to receive at the end, and it is a great testimony to the "World to Come" <note>original: *Olam Ha-Ba*</note> which is destined to be renewed for us. Conversely, one removes the leaven (*chametz*) from the sixth hour and onwards to hint at the seventh millennium <note>The era of the Messiah</note>, which is the Sabbath; at that time, the "Evil Inclination" <note>original: *Yetzer Ha-Ra*</note> will be nullified from the world. Furthermore, this great matter hints to us that one must remove the "well-known leaven" <note>A common metaphor for pride or the ego</note> so that it is not seen between the "Six" — which are the six hours of the day — and the "Seven," which is the "Daughter of Seven" <note>original: *Bat Sheva*; a mystical reference to the Sefirah of Malchut</note>, the mother of Solomon <note>original: *Shlomo*, which shares a root with "peace/perfection"</note>, so as not to "cut the saplings" <note>A Talmudic idiom for heresy or disrupting the divine order</note> of the beautiful ones; thus far his words. And these are the words of the *Book of Ethics* (*Sefer HaMusar*): Know further that the secret of removing the leaven on the night of the fourteenth of Nisan is because the early Sages were "Sages of Truth" <note>original: *Chachmei Emet*; often refers to Kabbalists</note>. They would take ten pieces of bread and place them in the ten corners of the house, and then they would return to the first corners and take the piece they had placed there and recite the blessing "over the removal of leaven." They would then gather them in a bowl and keep them until the next morning at the time of the burning, and burn them according to the custom of the world. But the secret of the matter — why ten pieces, no more and no less? — it is to hint to you against the "Ten Impurities" <note>The ten levels of the "Other Side" or *Sitra Achra*</note>, in order to nullify them and remove them from the world, so that no "Accuser" (*Kategor*) remains in the world against Israel. Rather, Israel requires mercy, and this is its atonement. This is as it is written: "It is a night of vigil for the Lord" <note>Exodus 12:42; original: *Leil shimurim hu l'Adonai*</note>, meaning it is guarded from the "Damaging Forces" <note>original: *mazikin*</note> and the tribulations of the world. They sit as guarded people, as free men, because of the goodness that is guarded for those who keep it, who are secure without evil occurrence or the tools of the Accuser... and all that involves accusation. Therefore, the Name, may He be blessed and His name exalted, commanded us to nullify the leaven on Passover. This is sufficient for every person of intellect and understanding. And the Sages, of blessed memory, said: There are two attributes in the world of transformations: leaven (*chametz*) and bitter (*mar*); leavening is feminine. Thus far his words. 

The leaven is the secret of the "shells" <note>original: *kelipah*; the spiritual husks that conceal holiness</note> — "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>. And the Matzah is freedom. Likewise, the four cups correspond to the "four expressions of redemption" <note>Exodus 6:6-7: "I will bring out," "I will deliver," "I will redeem," "I will take."</note>; they are all guarded from the "Guarded Place" where there is no touch of the stranger <note>original: *goy*</note>, nor any contact or "nurturing" for the *kelipot* (shells). This is the Sefirah of <term>Understanding (Binah)</term>, which is called "Time" <note>original: *Et*</note>. Therein is hinted the 36 [levels of] Kindness... and the "Guarded Wine" <note>original: *yayin meshumar*</note>. In <term>Understanding</term>, the measure of the "forty" begins; the touch of the stranger does not start there, only from the external forces. Regarding the Ishmaelites... in the kindness of Abraham, and the "ten" in the value of Isaac; this is explained at length in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*. The <unclear>matzah</unclear> is called "Guarded Matzah," and so too the four cups are influenced by this "Guarded Wine." The Matzah is the secret of the repair for the sin of Adam the First; some say his sin involved wheat, and others say it was a cluster of grapes. Both are true according to the mystical account. The Matzah is the repair for the wheat, and the Wine is the repair for the cluster of grapes.

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic interpretation of Tractate Pesachim. # Tractate Pesachim

Like Isaac, who represents the **Attribute of Justice** <note>original: *Middat HaDin*</note>. He saw the letter *Mem* flying in the air, which is a sign of wrath and heat. This letter *Mem* flies within the four letters of the Divine Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> and the letter *Aleph*. This relates to the secret of "The woman took... and gave" <note>A reference to Eve and the primordial sin</note>. When the *Mem* is joined, it forms the word **Death** <note>original: *Mavet*</note>, which was rolled into the four winds of the world. Behold, this *Mem* exists within the "arrow" <note>original: *chatz*</note> and thus becomes **leaven** <note>original: *chametz*—the Hebrew words for arrow and leaven share the letters Chet and Tzadi</note>. The concept of the "arrow" refers to the evil that shoots like an arrow, originating from Adam the First Man during the 130 years he was separated from his wife, during which he fathered spirits and demons. Afterward, at 130 years, "he fathered [Seth] in his own likeness and image," through whom the world was established. 

Similarly, in Egypt, the Redeemer—Moses our Teacher—was born. He is the secret of Seth, as is known from the mystery that "Moses" [Moshe] equals "Shiloh" <note>Both have a numerical value of 345</note>. Jochebed was 130 years old when she gave birth to him, just as the original "Mother of All Life" <note>Eve</note> was repaired after 130 years. He is the **Foundation of the World** through the Religion and the Torah.

The author of *Tola’at Yaakov* <note>original: "Jacob's Worm," a 16th-century kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> wrote: Adam’s sin was the cause for the opening of a muddy spring, a source of impurity <note>original: *zuhama*</note> that was drawn upon him and all his descendants. Those souls required refining and whitening. This is the meaning of the **Exile in Egypt**, which is called the **Iron Furnace** <note>original: *Kor HaBarzel*</note>. Israel was exiled there to be purged of that original foulness and to leave behind their filth and impurity, which had been mixed into their forms by the power of the "serpent who was cunning." Therefore, they were "naked" <note>original: *erumim*—a play on the serpent's "cunning," *arum*</note> of the splendor of the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note>, as it is said: "And you were naked and bare." After the refining and whitening, they merited to be clothed in the splendor of the Divine Presence, as it is said: "And Your cloud stands over them."

Now, when Israel was exiled to Egypt, they fell under that "Foreskin"—the hard and bitter **husk of the nut** <note>original: *Klipat HaEgoz*—referring to the shells of spiritual impurity</note>. This is the **leaven** <note>original: *chametz*</note> of which it is said: "The mysterious one, a nazirite of wickedness, from the hand of the unrighteous and the leavened/sour man." This indicates the intensity of Judgment. It would have been impossible to be redeemed from under that servitude and that "husk" if the Supreme Light had not appeared. The spirits of purity were revealed to bring them out in haste and to untie the knots with which Israel was bound in Egypt. It was because of these knots that they were enslaved there. Therefore, the **Exodus from Egypt** is mentioned fifty times in the Torah, warning that they went out through the power of "Who" <note>original: *Mi*—the numerical value is 50, referring to the 50 Gates of Understanding</note>. They required the blood of the Circumcision <note>original: *Milah*</note> to emerge from under the "Foreskin" they were enslaved to, and to remove the **leaven** from their domain. Thus, they went out "from the hand of the unrighteous and the leavened/sour" to eat **unleavened bread** <note>original: *matzah*</note> and to cling to the Supreme Faith. Had the "Guarded Matzah" not appeared—signifying that no leaven was mixed in—they would not have been redeemed. 

Our Sages of blessed memory said in the first chapter of Tractate Kiddushin: "The dough they took out of Egypt had the taste of Manna." Behold, they explained that the source of the Manna is the source of the Matzah; they share the same spiritual place. Thus, one who eats leaven on Passover "cuts the saplings" <note>A term for heresy or damaging the Divine unity</note> of the holy blossoms, causing the withdrawal of the Chosen Light—the secret of the Guarded Matzah—and instead rouses the leaven.

It is known that the numerical value of "gods of molten metal" <note>original: *elohei masekhah*</note> is the same as the intention of the "outside forces." It is written immediately after: "The Festival of Matzot you shall keep." This teaches that anyone who does not keep the Matzot and eats leaven is as if they worshipped idols. Therefore, the Sages made a more stringent separation for it than for other prohibitions in the Torah. There is another hint in the **burning of the leaven**: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will remove the **Evil Inclination** from the world, in the secret of "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh."

->As a symbolic example of this, we were commanded to burn the leaven.<-
->The Exodus from Egypt represents trust in His salvation.<-

<column-break/>

<margin>And to provide from the hidden treasure, and not to think evil of us, but to have mercy and to remove the leaven.</margin> 

The matter of the **Sanctification of the Moon** <note>original: *Kiddush Levanah*</note> indicates the future repair... as mentioned in the version of the blessing for the New Moon. To explain this blessing: It is as the Sages said in Tractate Chullin regarding the "two great lights." Originally they were equal, but the Moon said to the Holy One, "Master of the Universe, can two kings share one crown?" He replied, "Go and diminish yourself." She said, "Because I spoke a proper thing before You, must I diminish myself?" He said, "Go and rule by day and by night." She said, "What benefit is there? A candle at noon is useless." He said, "Go, and Israel will count their days and years by you." She was still not appeased. Finally, the Holy One said, "Bring an atonement for Me for having diminished the moon." 

Through this story, the masters of Kabbalah have explained many secrets in their books. On the path of moral instruction, this represents the way of the wise. The "diminishing" refers to the end of the great emanations... the four **Divine Personas** <note>original: *Partzufim*</note>.

<note>The text here becomes highly technical, discussing the letters of the Divine Name and the Sefirot—Chokhmah (Wisdom), Binah (Understanding), Tiferet (Beauty/Truth), and Malkhut (Kingship). It explains how the letter Dalet [ד] expands into the letter Heh [ה] and how the "Foundation" [Yesod] connects the upper and lower worlds.</note>

The secret of the **Four Personas** was not revealed until the Holy One brought about the "faces" ... this is the mystery of the "shutting" which is the letter *Heh*. Who can tell of His wonders? Every prayer of a person is answered through this secret. We do not expound upon the "Work of the Chariot" <note>original: *Ma'aseh Merkavah*—the most guarded secrets of Jewish mysticism</note> except to those who are worthy.

The **Sefirah of Beauty** <note>original: *Tiferet*</note> is the "knowledge" <note>original: *Da'at*</note> which emerges from the brains of Wisdom and Understanding. It is the revelation of the Light of the Name. This is why Moses, who represents Tiferet, reached the level of Understanding... The secret of the "Ten Plagues" <note>original: *Eser Makkot*</note> also relates to the ten fingers and the ten Sefirot. The Matzah, which is the "Bread of Faith," allows us to connect to these high spiritual levels by removing the "leaven" of the material world.

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic commentary on Tractate Pesachim, further exploring the mystical significance of the moon's diminishment and transitioning into a profound philosophical inquiry regarding why the Torah's authority is historically linked to the Exodus from Egypt.</meta>

### Tractate Pesachim

...discerning and wise students who can understand one thing from another and become like an ever-increasing spring. And behold, I designate a name for this part of the homilies: **The Forehead of Action** <note>original: "Metzach Assiyah" — a kabbalistic reference to the lowest of the four spiritual worlds, Assiyah, and its crowning aspect</note>, for "vessels of the words of Torah are poor in one place but rich in another" <note>A Talmudic idiom suggesting that a concept obscure in one passage is explained more fully in another</note>. I support this with the "Bread of Poverty" <note>original: "Lechem Oni" — the matzah</note>, for the **Forehead of Action** belongs to the son of Judah the Great. I am aware that sometimes certain matters will appear in duplicate from what was mentioned in the homilies, and sometimes a topic will be repeated within this very composition. This is because I studied the homilies in my youth, but I wrote this composition in my old age. Thus, the words came forth sometimes in their initial form and sometimes with later safeguards, and for that reason, I did not remove them from their places. Regarding the second matter—the explanation of the Torah and its revealed aspects—I call it a "Guarded Commandment" <note>original: "Mitzvah Shmurah"</note>, for its end is rooted in its beginning. The Passover of Egypt also points toward the Passover of the future, and may our Father in Heaven establish the matter and wait for the time of wonders.

And behold, I will propose a great inquiry. Even though it is also mentioned in the homilies, nevertheless, because it is an essential obligation and encompasses the entire Torah, I have come to investigate it at length. It is this: Does the Scripture indicate that the commandments of the Torah are dependent on the Exodus from Egypt? This is a matter that challenges the intellect, for the Torah is eternal—would its existence then depend on the Exodus, as if, Heaven forbid, the Torah would not be sustained if the Exodus had not occurred? This issue has already been raised in the work *The Service of the Holy* <note>original: "Avodat HaKodesh," a foundational 16th-century kabbalistic text by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, where he treats it extensively. Because of the great necessity of the matter, I will copy that entire chapter from the book, and afterward, I will write my own opinion, of blessed memory.

**Chapter 38 from the section "Secrets of the Torah":**
The secret of the Torah depends on the Exodus from Egypt. This was the principle and the root for the acceptance of the Kingdom of Heaven, allowing the Divine matter to dwell upon us. This is repeated many times regarding many commandments, where we are commanded to observe them "in memory of the Exodus from Egypt." The Blessed One even made the acceptance of His Divinity over us dependent on it, saying: "I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God." The explanation and the secret of this is that He built the entire structure upon it. The beginning of establishing His Divinity over us was through it, as it is written: "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt..." and through it, His distinctiveness was accepted.

When we examine the statement "You shall have no other gods before Me," why was it said? Because it followed "I am the Lord your God." This is like a king who entered a province. His servants said to him: "Issue decrees upon us." He said to them: "No. When you have accepted my kingdom, only then will I issue decrees. For if you do not accept my kingdom, how will you fulfill my decrees?" So says the Omnipresent to Israel: "I am the Lord your God—you shall have no other gods." I am the one whose kingdom you accepted in Egypt. They said to Him: "Yes." He said to them: "Since you accepted My kingdom, accept My decrees." Thus, the acceptance of the decrees is dependent on the acceptance of the kingdom, and everything depends on the Exodus from Egypt.

This is because there, through what their eyes saw, the truth of the "Knowledge of the World" and the order of the upper and lower systems was verified for them. For He is the Almighty <note>original: "Shaddai"</note>, sufficient in His existence and Divinity, and He is able to exert His Divine providence over us without limit. He chose the land of Egypt to publicize His Divinity and His power there. As the Prophet said: "I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt."

And the teaching of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>the traditional author of the Zohar</note>, of blessed memory, explains: From the land of Egypt, they had a King, but He did not divide them. And is it not written: "And Jacob said to his household... remove the foreign gods"? And from Jonathan's translation: "And let us rise and go up to Bethel," and so on. Yet you say "from the land of Egypt"? Rather, the conclusion of the matter is that Israel in general did not recognize the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, until that difficult struggle. They cried out to their companions, and their lineage was not known, nor would they have ever learned, had they not seen every day how they were treated with cruelty and evil to enslave their women. They did not turn away from the "Other Side" <note>original: "Sitra Achra" — the realm of spiritual evil</note> to fear or be saved, and it was not certain. Until the very essence of the Holy One, Blessed be He, appeared, they were following the laws of their fathers. But when there were many signs and many wonders, the Holy One took them for His service. Because they all saw with their own eyes all those signs and wonders, He said: "I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt." There, He was revealed, and He called out to those born in darkness: "There is no other god who speaks with us, but I am the one you saw in the land of Egypt; I am the one who accepted you in your hatred in the land of Egypt." And because of this, "You shall know no God but Me." It was not through another's wisdom, but through revealing it all. This concludes the quote.

This is the first foundation of life and its base. However, our father Jacob, of blessed memory—the choice of the patriarchs—opened this path. The Master Craftsman corrected this more than his ancestors, for he burned away idolatry and removed the spirit of impurity through his burial. This is a great principle for the rectification of faith. Afterward, the Divine matter and the acceptance of the Kingdom of Heaven, its permanence and its fear, took hold. But it was not yet complete, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, had not yet revealed Himself to publicize His kingdom to all the inhabitants of the world through great miracles, signs, and wonders that change the natural order of the world. This happened in Egypt. Jacob was the first who began to publicize this, but only among individuals, for the time for the completion of the "nude" <note>perhaps referring to the "naked" soul or the unformed nation</note> had not arrived. But he made signs for what the Holy One would complete in the future. His kingdom was completed and known at first against alien faiths and strange opinions through the creations He performed in Egypt. He removed falsehood and the spirit of impurity, and afterward, the Divine matter took hold, and He became the true God to all the inhabitants of the world, His kingdom ruling over all. This was the primary establishment of faith and truth for Israel in Egypt, where all of this was publicized in its perfection. Therefore, the beginning of the acceptance of the Kingdom and Divinity over them was there, even if it had not preceded it. Therefore, he was obligated to say: "I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt," and he negated "you shall know no god but Me." For who is like God in heaven and earth who can perform according to His deeds and His wonders, and who possesses the strong hand and the immense power to make it known...

<column-break/>

...in the middle... My hand above, etc. Now, in their prayer, at any rate, there is a doubt regarding the "whiteness" <note>original: "Loven" — perhaps a reference to the mystical light of the Sefirah of Chesed</note>. And so Hezekiah, when he prayed for his life, it is written: "I have heard your prayer." And it is not for the sake of the standing that he adds to the individual, for the secret of the "Danger" adds a portion. Joseph adds money, as it is written: "The Lord will add [Yosif] to you." And finally, it is written: "Let him not add."

And so says the *Pardes* <note>original: *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in Chapter 6: Regarding the "diminishing" of children, life, and sustenance—this matter does not depend on merit but on "Mazal" <note>term: *Mazal* — literally "constellation," but kabbalistically refers to the spiritual flow from the highest Sefirot</note>. Its explanation is: even though all realities are through the Torah, and they conduct themselves through the merit of their deeds, as we explained in the values of the foundations, nevertheless, "Children, Life, and Sustenance" depend on *Mazal*. This is the secret of the influence from the hidden place of Wisdom and Understanding. Through them, these three—children, life, and sustenance—flow. For through the union and movement of Wisdom and Understanding, these influences are bestowed. Thus, it is explained that the blessings written in the book are not as Maimonides said in Tractate Shevuot, where he explained that they would mention the Blessed One regarding a specific name. We have explained the matter of "diminishment" as being in the lower realms, while in the higher realms, it is a great virtue in the worlds of Formation and Action. For "one is opposite the other," and from this, the worlds derive their influence.

The matter of the "diminishing of the moon" mentioned here was already discussed. And the matter of the "two great lights" is the secret of the Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> of the Throne, which is the secret of the "Flow" <note>original: "Hamshacha"</note>. The "storm of anger" is for the sake of the rectification of the high virtue in the secret of the "Names." And regarding these three matters—the homilies for the work of the day were written as mentioned above—for the rectification of the names, such as "To Him who makes the great lights," "The sun to rule by day," and "The moon and stars to rule by night." "To Him who makes the heavens with understanding" refers to the planting of the stars of the heavens with understanding and the constellation of the stars... The heavens for the earth, which is the beginning of the kingdom to distance the land upon the waters... For the foundation of the Kingdom's existence is from the word "He spread the earth upon the waters," for the Holy One took the water and made it into Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note>. And the secret of this Loving-kindness is the "Knowledge" <note>Da'at</note> that is known, and it is "above the heavens."

And there he beats the secret of the "Greenery," which is the plant that grows. This is the secret of the "Sickness." "To Him who makes great lights" is the aspect of the union of the "two great lights." "The sun to rule by day" and "The moon..." is the aspect of the "diminishing." And forever, Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> comes from the side of the "diminishing." Loving-kindness is extended throughout the day, and the revelations will overpower with a great light from the aspect of Loving-kindness. For when the moon <note>Malchut</note> is hidden, the "shells" <note>original: "Kelipot" — forces of impurity</note> gather, and afterward, a great light appears.

This clarifies the blessing of the **Sanctification of the Moon** according to the secret of the foundation we mentioned... which is the secret of the Firmament and the Heavens that I mentioned. "He spread the earth upon the waters." And know that everything is included in the secret of the "two great lights." For it is already known that this is "Tiferet" and "Yesod" <note>Sefirot of Beauty and Foundation</note>, which are the life and the water... the Oral Torah... to do the will of their Creator. This is the secret of the "Moon" and its "diminishing," so that it should not be thought that there are two kings using one crown, Heaven forbid. Rather, the matter was to do the will of their Creator, to act according to the law and what is proper, as I have explained.

And according to what I clarified above, one can then say: "A crown of beauty" <note>original: "Ateret Tiferet"</note>. In the future, they will be renewed like her, for the sake of the correct order of the upper virtue. In the secret of the "Crown of Beauty," there is the "Crown of the Husband," in the secret of her union, in the secret of the "Moon." And now, even though sometimes she is called "Moon" and sometimes "Fullness," "David King of Israel lives and endures." His secret is explained, as is the secret of the "blood of the covenant." It is known that **Nisan** is the first of the months of the year, as explained. Therefore, the redemption is in it. And it is because the sun is in all twelve permutations, which are the days they offered sacrifices... so the blessing is after the permutation of Nisan, the end of everything for everyone.

### Tractate Pesachim

Jacob Joshua <note>Referring to Rabbi Jacob Joshua Falk (1680–1756), author of the famous commentary *Pnei Yehoshua*</note> said to you: According to the parable, "as the day and its completion"—the strike of the day and the strike of the night are the "end of prayer" and the "Kingdom." This is the meaning of: "Yours is the day, and Yours also is the night; You have established the luminary and the sun" <note>Psalm 74:16</note>. At the end of the day and night strikes, everything is gathered into the King’s treasuries, which is my prayer. It is complete in the hand of those who bow before You. "Yours is the Kingdom" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note> and the dominion. In the heat of the moment, one should speak many words. The "Angel who encompasses his Master" <note>A poetic reference to a high spiritual level or a specific angelic force</note> is because my desire is for my end to be at a level close to His level. He asked: Why do the Children of Israel mention "day and night"? If the intention was not for it to be "daytime and good," then we have not reckoned with the Name of the Lord.

Those who pray are sometimes dismissed, like what I wrote above regarding the secret of the sapphire stone. Why is it a "commandment"? So that they shall be, and those who are struck by it shall find fulfillment on every surface. The essence of the foundation is the cycle of the year, and the year encompasses a specific person. They shall say of him: "A righteous man for your people." This is the secret of the "arousal from below" <note>original: *it'aruta d'letata* — the kabbalistic concept that human action triggers divine response</note> where the Great Ones shine, as it were, when she <note>The Shekhinah or Malchut</note> sings. This is the secret of the "Feminine Waters" <note>term: *Mayim Nukvin* — spiritual energy or prayers rising from the physical world to initiate a divine union</note> in the likenesses, to receive the influence and to say: "See how many souls have come to honor You." This awakens a "Union from Above" <note>term: *Zivug* — the balancing and unification of different divine attributes</note> through the ascent of the Master. Life is for everyone who receives "Knowledge" <note>term: *Da'at* — the Sephirah representing the bridge between the intellect and the emotions</note>. "Knowledge" is a connection, as in "And Adam knew his wife" <note>Genesis 4:1</note>, and this is not a visible connection that can be measured.

## The Second Matter: The Order of the Haggadah
### and its explanation, including several precious matters joined in love
<margin>From the place of hidden things, he shall set the order before him clearly. He needs words to clarify the order of the praises and the prayer, according to the order of the two great groups who were unified in fire and kindness, which are like his own body. A man is obligated to honor his wife <note>Metaphorically, the Shekhinah</note> more than himself, for she is the "crown of her husband" <note>Proverbs 12:4</note>. When she ascends, the Master himself ascends and is strengthened, and mercies descend for whoever is in the world above, as if in the Holy of Holies.</margin>
And within the order of the Haggadah, I shall write the reasons for the commandments practiced on the night of "Give thanks" <note>The Seder night</note>. I know they are not even like a drop from the sea compared to the true depth of the matter; nevertheless, "whether one does much or one does little, it is all the same, provided that he directs his heart toward Heaven" <note>A famous Talmudic dictum from Berakhot 17a</note>. And you, children of Israel, when the time comes to tell of the Exodus from Egypt and to fulfill the commandments of the Torah—my name is a treasurer for them. That is to say, we have occupied ourselves with what we are writing, and you are the wise ones.

Her first place is "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>, and she has the law of precedence in the second place, for she is "the crown of her husband." This is hidden in the world, for in the world that is prepared, these are her reasons. She shall be like the glow surrounding the pleasantness of the Master. For "The Stirrer" is the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Divine Name, representing the Sephirah of Wisdom</note>, and in its hiddenness, it stands upon the letter *Zayin* <note>The seventh letter, representing the Sephirah of Kingdom/Malchut</note>. (And this is the secret of the "Sanctification" <note>Kiddushin</note>—placing the seventy upon Wisdom, which is *Vav*, and it becomes *Zayin*.) If it were not for this, his goodness would be zero. 

I have already written about the matters below concerning the "Color" <note>A mystical appearance of a Sephirah</note>, which is the "Glory of the Beauty." As is seen in the writing, in the secret of the letter *Yod*, she has the right of precedence. These are the reasons for "In the beginning" in the world. But when one prays for an ascent below, at the time of the "Will" <note>term: *Et Ratzon* — a propitious time for prayer</note>, it is not right to increase her judgment, but rather to be in favor and even to rise higher. This is "Knowledge" being received. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is "Beauty" <note>term: *Tiferet* — the central Sephirah, often called the "King"</note>, becomes like dust for the feet of the Master, and He is the "City of the Lord." One should pray through the word "Upon" <note>Hebrew: *Ali*</note>. As it says, "when a crown is tied," there are two "Upon"s—literally one "Upon" the other—so that she may rise and be exalted and reach her place, which is the prayer in the sanctuary of the Holy of Holies. See the "Sapphire" <note>The *Sefer HaBahir* or a similar kabbalistic text</note> where it is explained that Jacob is the secret of the "Day of Atonement" in the standing of the lady...

<note>The text continues with complex kabbalistic associations between letters, the patriarchs, and the spiritual "repair" (*Tikun*) of the world through the Seder rituals. It mentions the "Kingdom of Isaac" and the concept of "God is One and His Name is One."</note>

...and this is the secret of the "Seven" and "Seven." What one asks to know is that the Holy Name is "One," and when you approach the "One," this is the repair of the prayers. All who come into the world shall know and inherit that You are God alone. When you approach the "Seven," it is the service of God... as it says, "Let everything that has breath praise the Lord" <note>Psalm 150:6</note>. This is the meaning of the "Seven Vowels" which are spread outward... I heard that when she was brought near the Sanctuary, her lack was filled... 

The conclusion of the matter is that everything is directed toward one goal. One should not think that God's desire is only for the mind to be settled. Rather, everything he said to you in prayer are "words of life," for everything is truth and uprightness. Everything follows the "arousal of those below" <note>human initiative</note>. This is for the maskil <note>the enlightened student</note> and the one who understands.

### And there are three aspects of the Name for the "Kingdom"
#### marked by three vowel points: *Holam*, *Shuruk*, and *Melach* <note>Likely *Melopum* or *Chirik*</note>, as explained in the *Tikunim* <note>The *Tikunei HaZohar*</note>.

The sages brought down in the "Gate of Vowels" that the *Holam* is the "Supreme Point" above the letter, representing the beginning. The *Shuruk* is in the middle, and the *Chirik* is below. *Holam* is the "Crown" <note>Keter</note>, *Shuruk* is "Beauty" <note>Tiferet</note>, and *Chirik* is "Kingdom" <note>Malchut</note>. This is the place of the beginning of the language. "Holam" comes from the language of "strength" and "health." "Shuruk" refers to the "whistling" of the vine. These aspects are explained... when there is "Wisdom," it is like the oil in the lamp. As I mentioned above, this hints at the "Daughter of my Father," for they were together above in the Holy Wisdom.
