<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic discussion of the soul's attachment to the Divine. It moves from the concept of "arousal from below" to the historical cycle of the Jewish people—from their elevation at Mount Sinai to their fall with the Golden Calf, and the subsequent need for the "refinement" of exile.</meta>

And we are "clinging" etc. Afterward, when they made the Golden Calf, they returned to their initial straying. It is written, "The stone the builders rejected" <note>Psalm 118:22</note>, referring to the First Man <note>Adam</note>. And in the wilderness "they shall be consumed, and there they shall die" <note>Numbers 14:35</note> until the final generation, as it is said of them: "But you who held fast to the Lord your God are all alive today" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. This alludes to the generation of the desert who were buried there and cannot leave until the coming of our righteous Messiah, speedily in our days, Amen. That Light was within their intellect, and they were prepared for the giving of the Torah, and they merited the Land of Israel—a land that "the Lord seeks out" <note>Deuteronomy 11:12</note> and so on. But they returned to corruption through sins, specifically through idolatry, and they required the refinement of exile once again. They were smelted in the "iron furnace" <note>original: *kur ha-barzel* — a biblical metaphor for the harsh slavery in Egypt, used here to describe the spiritual purification of exile</note> even more than the iron furnace of Egypt. "From the mouth of the Most High, woes do not emerge" <note>Lamentations 3:38</note>; rather, everything is for the good, so that we may be smelted and refined to merit the True Redemption. "As in the days of your coming out of Egypt, I will show him wonders" <note>Micah 7:15</note>. 

However, the Exodus from Egypt will be secondary, and the "Gathering of the Exiles" will be the primary focus. In the redemption from Egypt, the "New Song" was sung in the feminine form <note>original: *shirah* — the Hebrew word for "song" used at the Red Sea is feminine, which commentators suggest implies a redemption followed by further "birth pangs" or exile</note>, which is the secret of "The Lord is in His holy palace, let all the earth be silent before Him" <note>Habakkuk 2:20</note>. But in the future, it will be in the masculine form <note>original: *shir* — masculine "song," implying a final, permanent state of peace</note>: "Now I will arise, says the Lord" <note>Isaiah 33:10</note>. Then, the night will shine like the day, in the secret of "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" <note>Isaiah 30:26</note>. The word of the Lord will be explained at length in the homilies. And then, a "New Torah" shall go forth from Him—meaning it will be a "New Torah" in the feminine form, which is the secret of the "Openings of the Torah." And it says, "On that day it shall be said: Lo, this is our God; we have waited for Him" <note>Isaiah 25:9</note>. 

For the advantage of light comes from the darkness, through the power of the secret of the exiles and the refinement toward the essence of "clinging" (*deveikut*). The beginning of this clinging was when Israel went out of Egypt from the iron furnace. Therefore it is said: "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt," for the iron furnace is a refinement. For the iron furnace and the "dedication of the fragrant furnace" <note>A mystical metaphor for the sacrificial service</note> are the secret of the exiles and the secret of clinging. When Israel left Egypt from the iron furnace in the Name of the Lord, the command was "they shall go from strength [to strength]" <note>Psalm 84:8</note>. And in the future, "the earth shall be full of the knowledge [of the Lord]" <note>Isaiah 11:9</note>. The general rule is: the entire Torah is the Name of the Lord, and its three commandments are the secret of "This is My Name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>, referring to the hidden and the revealed in speech and action, clinging to the Name of the Lord. This is impossible without the refinement of the "matter" <note>original: *chomer* — referring to the physical body or the gross material world</note> that separates us. This is the refinement that took place in the iron furnace in Egypt. Therefore, the Torah links itself to the Exodus from Egypt. If there had been no refinement in Egypt, there would necessarily have been another refinement, for without it, perfection is impossible. Had Man not sinned, he would not have needed refinement, for the "filth of the Serpent" <note>A kabbalistic term for the spiritual impurity introduced by the fall of Adam</note> would not have existed. When the Scripture links it to the Exodus, it is as if to say that without the clinging to the Lord—and not that it began, God forbid, only in Egypt—but because Adam sinned, he needed refinement. And now that he sinned, he required refinement, therefore there was Egypt. If there had been no Egypt in the world, the clinging would have happened through another means; but since there was an Egypt, the refinement came through Egypt, which is the "Second Chariot" <note>original: *mirkavat ha-mishneh* — referring to the lower spiritual structures of Egypt</note> relative to the holiness of the Land of Israel, the land which the Lord seeks. This is sufficient for the wise.

->Now I will record the two columns: One named *Matzah Ashirah* and the second named *Matzah Shemurah*<- <note>Matzah Ashirah (Rich Matzah) and Matzah Shemurah (Guarded Matzah) are types of unleavened bread, but here they serve as symbolic titles for the two columns of text below</note>

# Matzah Ashirah

**And He spoke** etc., "This is the law of the Burnt Offering" (*Olah*) etc. <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. The emergence of changes in the separation of the sacrifices are many, and I have not come now to awaken even a small part of the generalities. Behold, there are four instances of "This is the law" (*Zot Torat*) regarding the "most holy" sacrifices: The law of the Burnt Offering, the law of the Meal Offering (*Mincha*), the law of the Sin Offering (*Chatat*), and the law of the Guilt Offering (*Asham*). There is a fifth regarding the "lesser holy" sacrifices: "And this is the law of the Peace Offering" (*Shelamim*). The change in the order from the portion of *Vayikra* is difficult: there, the order is the Burnt Offering, the Meal Offering, with the Peace Offering in the middle, followed by the Sin Offering and Guilt Offering. But in this portion <note>Parashat Tzav</note>, the Peace Offering is ordered last. 

Another difficulty in this portion: after "This is the law of the Burnt Offering" and "This is the law of the Meal Offering," the text interrupts with the "Offering of Aaron," and only afterward lists the laws of the Sin Offering, Guilt Offering, and Peace Offering. Regarding Aaron's matters, the proper time would have been to place Aaron’s offering next to the other matters concerning Aaron. 

A further difficulty: these four—Burnt, Meal, Sin, and Guilt—are "most holy." Yet the text only mentions "most holy" explicitly regarding the Sin Offering and the Guilt Offering. Regarding "This is the law of the Burnt Offering," as written in the portion of *Vayikra*, "it is most holy." Come and see: Rabbi Shimon says, from where do we know that a person should not say: "To the Lord, a Burnt Offering," "To the Lord, a Sin Offering," "To the Lord, a Meal Offering," or "To the Lord, a Peace Offering"? The Torah says: "An offering to the Lord" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>, to divide <note>the words</note>. This is to say: if for someone who is about to sanctify an object, the Torah said he should not mention the Name of Heaven until the word "Offering" has been said, how much more so should we not mention the Name of Heaven in vain! 

In the first chapter of Tractate *Nazir*, the Talmud brings Rabbi Shimon’s words in a different version: "From where do we know that a person should not say 'To the Lord, a Burnt Offering'... but rather 'A sacrifice to the Lord'..." etc. And in the portion of *Bereshit*, a third version says: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says... "An Olah to the Lord, a Mincha to the Lord, a Shelamim to the Lord." This is a "light and heavy" <note>original: *kal va-chomer* — an a fortiori logical argument</note> inference: If for one who intends to sanctify an object, the Torah says the Name of Heaven should not be invoked <note>prematurely</note>, then regarding those who blaspheme, curse, or serve idols—how much more so should they be wiped from the world! 

In the first chapter of *Nazir*, it explains: perhaps he will say "To the Lord" and then not say "Offering," thus having uttered the Name of Heaven in vain. The explanation in the *Yafé To’ar* <note>A 16th-century commentary on Midrash Rabbah by Rabbi Samuel Jaffe Ashkenazi</note> remains: that after mentioning the Name of the Lord, he might change his mind and not sanctify the animal, resulting in a vain use of the Name. He also wrote there: regarding the Sin Offering and Guilt Offering, which one is obligated to bring, why shouldn't he say "To the Lord" at the beginning? One could say we fear he might change his mind about *this* specific animal and choose a different one. In my humble opinion, it seems the concern is that he might say "To the Lord," and before he can say "Burnt Offering," he might die—for no man can trust in his speech for even a moment. If so, the difficulties we raised are answered. We will now present, with God's help, a good and upright order for all these changes. Their source is investigated through four inquiries... regarding the portion of the sacrifices and the *Haggadah* and the matter of Passover.

## First

We find great virtue in telling the story of the sacrifices, just as we find virtue in telling the story of the Exodus. Regarding sacrifices, our Sages said: "Whoever occupies himself with the laws of the sacrifices, it is as if he actually offered them." "This is the law of the Burnt Offering, the Meal Offering, the Sin Offering, the Guilt Offering, the Consecration, and the Peace Offering" <note>Leviticus 7:37</note>. Perhaps these "laws" (Torot) allude to this. One who occupies himself with the Torah in their place is given the same power. We find the same regarding the laws of Passover: We learn in the Mishnah that we mention the Exodus, and in the Haggadah, "Whoever expands upon the story is praiseworthy." Rabban Gamliel says: "Anyone who has not said these three things... Passover, Matzah, and Bitter Herbs..." He did not say "anyone who has not *done* these three things," but rather "said"—referring to the speech.

<column-break/>

# Matzah Shemurah

The order of Passover and the matter of the Haggadah: *Kadesh* (Sanctify), *Urchatz* (Wash), etc.

## And this is the Law of Jacob

The reason for the Four Cups: We have already written above that when Israel was exiled to Egypt, they fell under the power of the "Foreskin" <note>original: *Arlah* — a kabbalistic term for the forces of unholiness</note>. It has four harsh "husks" (*Klipot*). Anyone who falls under them no longer has a side of "freedom" according to the natural way of the world. Because of this, Jacob our Father was afraid to go down to Egypt, until the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Do not fear going down to Egypt... I will go down with you... and I will surely bring you up again" <note>Genesis 46:3-4</note>. He promised him that in every place Israel is exiled, the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is with them. When He comes to redeem Himself, He also redeems Israel. This is what David said: "Whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, a nation and its God" <note>2 Samuel 7:23</note>. 

When the time of redemption arrived, the Holy One, Blessed be He, had to break those "husks" to bring Israel out to freedom. This is the meaning of: "He smote every firstborn" and "Upon their gods, the Lord executed judgments." Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded the circumcision of the Children of Israel to remove them from under the "Foreskin." As soon as they were separated from the Foreskin, they immediately went out to freedom, as it is written: "By the blood of your covenant, I have sent forth your prisoners from the pit wherein is no water" <note>Zechariah 9:11</note>. 

Corresponding to the breaking of the four husks, four expressions of redemption were said in the Torah portion, in order to take Israel out from under their subjugation. Corresponding to these, we were commanded to drink Four Cups, and to do so while reclining in the manner of free men. Understand this: the "Lord who is guarded in His grapes" <note>A mystical reference to the wine of the future</note> was the power of Israel's redemption from Egypt, from under the Foreskin which possesses the four husks mentioned in the Chariot of Ezekiel the Prophet. Conversely, we have the Four Cups of wine on the nights of Passover. With the fourth cup, we complete the *Hallel* (Psalms of Praise), for then we...

# Tractate Pesachim

...Savior, there is none besides You. Since the arrangement of the celestial and terrestrial systems was set, their service there should have continued without interruption forever. Yet, the opposite occurred, for He brought them out from there into eternal freedom. It is therefore fitting, in contrast to this, that the memory of His wonders and awesome deeds "shall not perish from among the Jews, nor shall their memorial pass from their seed" <note>original: *lo ya’avor mi-tokh ha-yehudim ve-lo yasuf mi-zera’am* — a quote from Esther 9:28 applied here to the Exodus</note> for all eternity. This is the reason for the commandment: "That you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, for it shall be remembered throughout all generations. 

To fulfill all this, we became obligated to accept His kingship and His decrees, so that their "taste" remains in our mouths and their impression is recognizable in our every limb—the very essence of life and existence. The commandments of the Passover offering, the unleavened bread (*matzah*), and the bitter herbs (*maror*) provide us no rest day or night, for they are the "taste." As it says, "It shall be a sign for you upon your hand and a memorial between your eyes, so that the Torah of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt" <note>Exodus 13:9</note>. Behold, the Torah and its commandments were placed in our mouths and our bodies to remind us that with a mighty hand the Lord—and no other—brought us out of Egypt.

Thus, the commandment to recount all the laws and remember them is like "the good hand of our God upon us" <note>a phrase denoting Divine favor</note>, prompting us to seek insight and find "good taste and knowledge" <term>Ta'am va-Da'at: the deeper rationale and experiential wisdom behind the commandments</term> regarding the commandments in general and in detail, specifically regarding the confession of the Exodus from Egypt, each matter in its proper place. 

What we have written here is a great and true principle, and from it, a sufficient explanation is drawn. Upon this, hearts and thoughts wander to seek the word of the Lord, for people are astonished by this, saying: "Is it not established and accepted, and one must not turn right or left, for 'this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel' <note>Deuteronomy 4:44</note> and no other? Its commandments which He commanded us, and no others, are each a matter intended for its own sake." This is a "Requirement of the High One" <note>original: *tzorekh gavoha* — a kabbalistic concept suggesting that human performance of mitzvot affects the Divine realm</note> and not merely a human need for the "rectification of the Glory," as I have explained in the book *Toledot Yaakov* and *Koach Chesed*, with the help of Heaven. 

If so, how can they claim the Torah is only because of the Exodus from Egypt? If they had not gone into exile, would there be no Torah? If we were to say there is no place or need <unclear>for</unclear> this Torah and its commandments [without Egypt], Heaven forbid such a disparagement! Far be it from us to believe such a common thing of my fathers' glory. For the Torah preceded the world to reveal and make known that it is not dependent on time, nor on place, nor on any other thing; it is intended for its own sake. Because of this, our Sages said that the Torah is effectively the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Therefore, a duty of effort lies upon the believers to seek the truth from those who possess knowledge and those who received it, for "from them Torah shall go forth and with them wisdom shall be found." They are the ones who ascended to the heights of the "mighty ones" and showed the strength of its security and peace.

I say that the foundation of foundations and the pillar of wisdom is to know and understand that "the Lord is God, there is no other besides Him." To stand upon this principle, one must know that before the "Exile of the Glory"—the secret of the Lord God—all things were hidden and concealed in a state of undifferentiated equality. All opposites, letters, and utterances, along with souls, camps of light and darkness, good and evil, and all paradoxes were mixed together, like silver mixed with dross. Everything was in one place, from which all desires stem. "Darkness is as light" <note>Psalm 139:12</note>, for even though they were opposite things, they were mixed by the Simple Will. Through the longing of that Will, it becomes apparent that Good is the primary essence of the Will, and Evil exists only for the perfection of the Good—to strengthen it and sustain it. Thus, everything was hewn from one source. 

Because the "Glory" was not recognizable while things were in this state, the hidden, Simple Will desired to reveal His majesty for His glory. A "structure" was emanated containing all these things, and this is the secret of the **Upper Egypt** <term>Mitzrayim Ha-Elyonah: in Kabbalah, this refers to the Sephirah of Binah (Understanding), which "constricts" the infinite light but also serves as the source of liberation</term>. It is the "Understanding" that contains the opposites, mixed one into the other. From there, each was established in its proper place: the Good Light in its place, and the darkness, evil, and common in their place. The holy and pure souls were separated from the impure souls. Thought expanded and became clarified, and it was known that the Good is the essence. The opposites and letters were separated and became known in themselves. The Truth, which had been hidden and mixed with falsehood, was revealed and became an inheritance. His "hand," full of truth, was shown—exalted, great, and a "mighty hand." Through this, redemption and freedom were given to all things, for it was known in truth that "the Lord is God, there is no other besides Him." 

This was the **Upper Exodus from Egypt**—separated and necessitating the knowledge, recognition, and publicizing of this truth. This is the conduct of the souls. Furthermore, in the "thought of the intellect," they received the Torah. This is the secret: that all generalities and existences came into the 248 <note>the text mentions "P-G" letters, possibly a scribal variant or specific cipher for the structure of the Torah</note> letters of the Torah. Without the Upper Exodus and the expansion of Thought, there would be no engagement with the Torah, nor would it bring together the upper and lower realms. Divinity would not be known, and His Glory would not be recognized. 

Corresponding to this, God made the creation in the "Exile of Egypt," with roots and branches mirroring the Upper Pattern. There, "a nation within a nation" was mixed—pure and impure, good and evil, light and darkness, Israel and Egypt—until the Holy One, Blessed be He, was revealed to them to make His Name known and publicize His Divinity through great plagues, signs, and wonders. He also brought out redemption and freedom for Israel, separating them from the nations, refining them, purifying them, and sifting them from the dross mixed within them. He strengthened them and separated them to be His, as it is written: "Or has God ventured to go and take for Himself a nation from the midst of a nation" <note>Deuteronomy 4:34</note>—literally "a nation from the midst of a nation." And it is written: "I have separated you from the nations to be Mine" <note>Leviticus 20:26</note>. Thus, the light was separated from the darkness, and the good from the evil, and each was established in its proper place. 

Everything followed the Upper Pattern: redemption and the "Exodus to Freedom" below correspond to the redemption and "Exodus to Freedom" from the Upper Egypt. The redemption of souls above corresponds to the redemption of bodies below—intellect and the object of intellect. This is the "Fiftieth Year" <note>The Jubilee or the 50 Gates of Understanding</note> that brings both these and those to freedom. This is what is meant by "And the children of Israel went up *chamushim* (armed) from the land of Egypt" <note>Exodus 13:18</note>; the word *chamushim* is written such that it hints at "fifty" (*chamishim*), referring to the **Fifty Gates of Understanding**. Each one was a fiftieth year in five steps toward freedom. For this reason, the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned fifty times in the Torah. 

Fifty days after they left Egypt, they received the Torah, which is comprised of the Fifty Gates of Understanding. Behold, the souls received the Torah above, and the bodies correspondingly below; one mirroring the other. One has no life without its companion. [Had not] the Holy One, Blessed be He, [taken] our ancestors out of Egypt, we and our children and our children's children would still be enslaved to Pharaoh in Egypt, and they would not have received the Torah. They would be like the atonement and the law of the Exodus from Egypt above and below. 

It is found, therefore, that the Exodus from Egypt, the secret of existence, and the commandments are all a memorial to the Upper and Lower Exodus. The primary "treasure" and the Will was elevated to include the Lower Exodus and the receiving of the Torah. This was the expansion of the Upper Thought in revelation for the sake of the Upper Glory, and this is the secret of everything exiting the Upper Egypt. This, then, is the cause for the giving of the Torah and the commandments. It is fitting that everything be a memorial to this Exodus and this expansion. The primary intent of what I have written—this matter that "prepares the hand of a man," his righteousness and his truth—is that the Torah and commandments should be a memorial to the Exodus from Egypt, yet they are simultaneously intended for their own sake. They do not depend on anything, but rather all things above and below depend on them. Therefore, they are the wondrous "treasure" to bring down and rest the upper realms below and to elevate the lower realms above. They are the great cause of "cleaving" <term>Devekut: spiritual attachment or communion with God</term>, the form, and the strengthening of one into the other. Thus, they are found to be a memorial of all the wondrous redemptions and freedoms. This is what I wished to mention, and with this, we shall complete the intent of this chapter. These are the words of a wise man's mouth, full of grace. However, like a scale for wisdom and redemption, I have weighed my opinion in my spirit with words of truth; "these and those are the words of the Living God" <note>a Talmudic phrase meaning both perspectives hold divine truth</note>.

**It is known** that in the redemption from Egypt, there was revealed through Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, through all the signs and wonders, the "Essential Name," which is the four-letter Name of the Lord, may He be blessed. As it is said: "And God spoke to Moses and said to him, 'I am the Lord (Y-H-V-H)... but by My name the Lord (Y-H-V-H) I was not known to them'" <note>Exodus 6:2-3</note>. The commentators have already elaborated on this, and I too have elaborated on this in several discourses. 

The summary of the matter is this: before the world was created, "He and His Name" were alone in a state of concealment, which is the ultimate concealment. When He brought the world into being from nothingness, renewed it, and created it, He revealed His Name, may His Name be blessed, in such a way that "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. This means the Torah is perfect from beginning to end—it is all the Name of the Lord (Y-H-V-H). Indeed, it is entirely His names, branching out from the Name Y-H-V-H. 

If Man (*Adam*) had not sinned, he would have remained cleaved to the Lord, fulfilling: "But you who held fast to the Lord your God..." <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. For he was created in the "Image and Likeness" and was placed [in the Garden] "to work it and to keep it." Our Sages of blessed memory explained in the Midrash: "to work it" refers to the positive commandments, and "to keep it" refers to the negative commandments. These are included in the Name Y-H-V-H in the secret of: "This is My name... and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. "My Name" (*Shemi*) together with the letters *Yod-He* equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>; "My Memorial" (*Zikhri*) [together with the letters *Vav-He*] equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. These matters were discussed at length in the introduction to *Toledot Adam*. 

In the ten generations from Adam to Noah and the ten generations from Noah to Abraham, there was no separation between them and their Creator except for sins, which cause separation. The Holy One, Blessed be He, waited 26 generations, corresponding to the numerical value of the Name Y-H-V-H <note>Y=10, H=5, V=6, H=5; Total = 26</note>. Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, was the twenty-sixth generation. He was the redeemer—the redeemer from Egypt and the one who removes the yoke. The power of the Egyptian exile refined all the dross and rust of the First Man and all the descendants of Adam until his time. His prophecy was through a "Clear Mirror" <term>Aspaklaria Ha-Me'irah: a prophetic vision of direct clarity associated only with Moses</term>, the secret of which is *Y-H-V-H*. 

As it is written: "And God saw the children of Israel, and God knew" <note>Exodus 2:25</note>. This relates to what is written: "What is man (*Adam*) that You should know him?" <note>Psalm 144:3</note>. For the numerical value of *Adam* (אדם) is 45, which is the same as the Name Y-H-V-H when spelled out with the letter *Aleph* <note>original: *YOD-He-An-He* — actually YOD(20) HE(6) VAV(13) HE(6) = 45; this spelling is known as *Ma"h*</note>. This hints at the connection and "cleaving" to the Name Y-H-V-H, as it is written: "I will set him on high, because he has known My name" <note>Psalm 91:14</note>. "Knowledge" (*Yedi'ah*) is a term for connection, as in "And Adam knew his wife." When you cleave to Him, it is said of you: "But you [who held fast]..." etc. However, regarding the [Exodus], it is written: "And God knew," and He was elevated to the Name Y-H-V-H. For He did not redeem us through an angel, nor through a seraph, nor through a messenger, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, in His own Glory and Essence—that is, the Great Name, the Honored Name, the secret of Y-H-V-H—"went before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire" <note>Exodus 13:21</note>. 

Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, 13th-century scholar</note> wrote that they began to hurry completely during the days of the Counting of the Omer—seven weeks. Then, upon reaching the Festival of Shavuot, the Torah was given, which was the Name Y-H-V-H. It was an offering to His Great Name completely. It is written of the Giving of the Torah: "I said, 'You are angels, and all of you are sons of the Most High'" <note>Psalm 82:6</note>. For we were on the level of "Godly beings," and He is greater than all other powers because His Great Name is upon us.

# Tractate Pesachim: Enriched Matzah and Guarded Matzah

<margin>
Our God is the God of gods and Lord of lords; this is the secret of the "fifty thanksgivings" mentioned previously. Regarding the root of the "Yod-He" <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, often representing the higher spiritual realms</note> and the "fifty-two," Jethro said: "Now I know that the Lord <note>original: *Yod* — a shorthand for the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note> is greater than all gods." Previously, I only recognized the Name *Elohim* <note>The Name of God associated with nature and judgment</note> which extends to the "seventy" and Joseph. But now he recognizes the Name *Yod*. Similarly, Eve and Pharaoh eventually knew the "Righteous Yod." Regarding the Sukkot festival... the "Yod-He" surrounds it... however, one must delve deeply into this matter of "recognizing Him previously," and through this, we shall arrive at the clarification of these inquiries.

**And so**, I shall come to explain the last two inquiries—namely, the "Passage" <note>original: *avar*, referring to the root of "Hebrew" and the act of passing through</note> and the matter of the "Yod." We have heard these two: "We will do and we will hear" and "Grace," which are four: Speech and "You shall come." These are the first two inquiries, and these last twenty concern the "Passage of Yod." To this, our Sages and the masters of these eight hinted regarding the Name of the Lord: "Blessed be the Name of the Lord from now and forever," and "From the rising of the sun to its setting, the Name of the Lord is praised." He mentions the Name "Yod" <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> twice regarding praise and blessing, but the first time He did not say the Name "Lord" as He did in the three other times after... and regarding the matter of the "Passage" mentioned here, our Sages said: "The Lord passed over," and not "Pharaoh passed over." In this too, there was a deep hint. We shall first explain, as the good hand of the Lord is upon us, the matter of the Name "Yod" and the restoration of Israel through it when they left Egypt. 

The explanation of the "Passage" is the revelation of the Name "Yod" <note>The numerical value (Gematria) of the "Passage" (*avar*) relates to mystical calculations involving the Divine Names</note>. "And God said to Moses, and He said to him: I am the Lord," as it is written: "And the earth was full..." In the explanation of "What is His name? What shall I say?"—this is very deep. These are the words of the *Keter Torah* <note>A classic commentary</note> on this Torah portion. I will explain it according to my intellect. He began to raise the first question: What is this testimony of Moses our Teacher? Would they really ask "What is His name?" Or how could he err? It was written: "And we cried out to the Lord, the God of our fathers"—and this was before the revelation! And to Moses, He mentions the Name *Ehyeh* <note>I Will Be</note>; what does this hint at? Rashi explained it... and the Sages questioned this... especially the Maharsha... Rabbi Yaakov bar Avina answered in the name of the Zohar: The Holy One said to Moses: "Tell them, in this servitude I will be (*Ehyeh*) with them, and in future servitudes I will be with them." Moses said before Him: "Master of the Universe! Should I tell them this? Sufficient is the trouble in its own time!" God replied: "No, thus shall you say to the Children of Israel: *Ehyeh* [I Will Be] has sent me to you." I am informing *you* [Moses] of the Name *Ehyeh* which hints at future exiles... because their power is hidden... Moses did not delay... but rather "I Will Be What I Will Be" (*Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh*)... but my question is... according to the Sages, this is merely a general instruction, so "What is His name?" remains a question. He says further: "And God said moreover..." what is this? It almost contradicts what was said before... and now He mentions it to the elders of Israel... and the third mention includes the Patriarchs together, whereas before He specified "the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac..." What does this serve? He also mentioned the Name *Elohim* before explaining the matter.

We shall explain: These names hint at the *Sefirot* <note>The ten divine emanations/attributes in Kabbalah</note>. For "He spoke and it was light," and "He stood." It is already known that "Yod-He" is the Essential Name (*Shem HaEtzem*) representing His very essence, His primordial being. As the Sages said: "Before the world was created, He and His Name alone existed." "He" refers to His essence, and "His Name is One." Afterward, His names indicate the "Building of the World" and the renewed actions. Behold, the Name *Elohim* is the Building of the World, as it says: "In the beginning *Elohim* created." For through this Name, the world was satisfied and inaugurated... as the author of the *Arukh* wrote... every building needs a foundation, and that is the Name "He." The Name Y-H-V-H is from the language of "Being" (*Hovayah*), indicating a new coming-into-being. It is like an intermediary... between the King and the building. Initially, He was alone and the building did not yet exist. Afterward, it arose in His Thought to build the building. This Thought and Will is the intermediary between Him and the building, for Thought is cleaved to the thinker... so to speak, before the world was created, there was "He and His Name," meaning His Essence and His Thought. When the "Ascent of Thought" came before Him, the Will to bring things into being, that is the Name *Ehyeh* [I Will Be], derived from the unity of the Lord. Then the names for the building of the world and its actions were revealed. The matter of "I Will Be What I Will Be" is that My Will is enacted immediately...
</margin>

The Kindnesses (*Chasadim*) and the Powers (*Gevurot*) that are drawn down, etc., are the "Children of God" <note>original: *Bnei Elohim*</note>.
Behold, there are three ways the Name *Elohim* is "filled" <note>The practice of "Miluy" involves spelling out the names of the letters themselves (e.g., Aleph is spelled Aleph-Lamed-Peh). Different spellings yield different numerical totals and mystical meanings</note>:
1. Filled with the letter **Yod**: This has the power of Aleph-Lamed-Peh, He-Yod, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Mem-Mem.
2. Filled with the letter **He**: This has the power of Aleph-Lamed-Peh, He-He, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Mem-Mem.
3. Filled with the letter **Aleph**: This has the power of Aleph-Lamed-Peh, He-Aleph, Yod-Vav-Dalet, Mem-Mem.

Behold, the letter Aleph has two forms. Sometimes the Aleph equals 20 because it consists of a Yod above, a Yod below, and a Vav in the middle. Sometimes we calculate the Aleph according to the shape of the letters: a Yod, a Vav, and a lower Yod that is slightly distanced from the line and appears like a Vav.

Now, the Name *Elohim* filled with **Yod** hints at **Wisdom** (*Chokhmah*). Because Wisdom is called "Holy," the first cup of wine at the Seder, which corresponds to it, is used for the **Sanctification** (*Kiddush*).
The Name *Elohim* filled with **He** hints at **Understanding** (*Binah*). Therefore, it holds the power of telling the **Haggadah** (the Exodus story), for Binah is the "Higher Voice" from which voice and speech emerge. Also, the Exodus from Egypt is rooted in Binah.
The third filling, with **Aleph**, corresponds to **Kindness** (*Chesed*) and the fifth to **Strength** (*Gevurah*)... they are equal in the Aleph filling... therefore, one does not drink between the third and fourth cups. These and those are the "words of the Living God."

<column-break/>

---

**However**, these matters require explanation. In passing, we shall explain the matter of Egypt, which is a place of "narrowness" (*Metzarim*). Know that:
**Understanding** (*Binah*) is called the **World to Come** (*Olam HaBa*). From the level of Binah and above, the "External Forces" <note>The *Kelipot* or spiritual husks that represent evil/distraction</note> have no grasp or nourishment. Their nourishment only begins from **Kindness** (*Chesed*) downwards, which is called the "Building." It is from there that they draw sustenance. The External Forces are in the secret of "Ishmael the son of Abraham" and "Esau the son of Isaac." From there, there is "contact of the hands" in the external life—meaning, in the flow of influence. 

But the "bed of Jacob" was perfect. It was placed between North and South; he entered into the innermost part. "Jacob is the lot of His inheritance," and all of Israel has a portion in the World to Come. Regarding that realm, it is said: "No eye has seen a God besides You." Our Sages explained that this refers to the **"Wine preserved in its grapes since the six days of Creation"**—meaning, a level higher than the Seven Days of Creation. It is "preserved" from any external touch, for the External Forces have no nourishment there. 

Therefore, the Redemption from Egypt occurred through the revelation of *Binah*. They went out to freedom because there was no power there to hold them back. Because of this greatness, we have **Four Cups** corresponding to the **Four Expressions of Redemption**. These cups are of wine, and it is known that wine generally represents **Strength** (*Gevurah*), especially when it is red. When it is white, it leans toward **Kindness** (*Chesed*). However, it is called "Good Wine" when it is mixed with water—from the side of the "Waters of Kindness." From the side of *Binah*, it is called "Preserved Wine." 

To prepare you for this, I will first state that the Name Y-H-V-H, when vocalized with the vowels of the Name *Elohim*, hints at this, as explained in the Zohar. It is explained in the Zohar and the *Pardes* <note>A seminal kabbalistic work by Moshe Cordovero</note> that the Name *Elohim*, which hints at the Attribute of Justice, is not essentially in *Binah*. For the "Three Higher Crowns" are as one, and there is no "Justice" there. Rather, it is only from the side of *Binah* that Justice is awakened in its place.

Behold, since there is a revelation of His Godliness, even if it is hidden from our narrow straits, the matter of "it arose in His Thought to be revealed" creates a slight distinction. Just as in the lower worlds, when there is a "cause," the *Hyle* <note>term: Hyle/Hyuli — a Greek philosophical term for primordial, formless matter, used here to describe the earliest stage of divine emanation</note> begins and then the Creation, so too regarding the revelation of this Name—it is like the *Hyle* of His names. 

Note that *Ehyeh* [I Will Be] is in the future tense, but it is also known to be in the past tense, as in Job 10: "I was..." <note>original: *ahyeh*</note>. The Ralbag explained this as "He has now placed me..." The Aramaic translation of *Ehyeh* also supports this. Thus, *Ehyeh* in the sense of the **Past** refers to the highest level, cleaved to the "Yod." Then *Ehyeh* equals 21, the numerical value of the Name "Yod-He" without the doubling of the final He. From the aspect of that which is "destined to be revealed," *Ehyeh* is in the **Future** tense. 

This is the meaning of the verse: "For He spoke and it was." "He" refers to the state before the world was created, when "He and His Name alone" existed. "He spoke and it was" refers to the level of *Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh*. "He commanded and it stood" <note>Psalm 33:9</note>. Understand that "speaking in the heart" is **Thought**. "Will" is also called speech, as in "What will you say... and I will do it for you," meaning "What do you desire and want?" 

Thus, there are two aspects of "Speaking": 
1. "He spoke" — the aspect of being cleaved to Him. 
2. "And it was" — the aspect of the revelation of the "Higher Hyle." 

Afterward, His names were revealed for the building and the actions. This is "He commanded and it stood." Everything is drawn from "He," for He is the Cause of all Causes and the Reason of all Reasons. "In the beginning *Elohim* created"—this is the building of the world. *Ehyeh* is the foundation, like the Torah, through which the Holy One created the world. The letters are the foundation and the Torah is the building. Therefore, the Torah is called "Beginning" (*Reshit*). As it says: "I was then His delight" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. The Torah says: "I was the tool of His artistry." For the Name *Ehyeh* with an added *Vav* <note>original: *v'ehyeh*</note>... the letters of the alphabet... Aleph, Bet, Gimel, Dalet equal 6 (Vav). *Ehyeh* equals 21... this is the secret of the "artistry." 

When the world was built and active, He was called by the names *Elohim* and *Adonai* [Lord], for He is the "God of gods and Lord of lords." They were revealed from the highest level... which hints at the **Past** and is the root of the Name *Elohim*. The aspect of *Adonai*—the revelation in the **Future**—is the root of the Name Y-H-V-H. Sometimes, in a state of "diminishment," it is called *Elohim*... These names, *Elohim* and *Adonai*, operate according to the "Laws of Nature" and not through revealed miracles that change the natural order. Therefore, the Name "Yod" [Tetragrammaton] was revealed to the Patriarchs in action, changing the natural order. For all their miracles were within the realm of nature, but now the time has arrived to be revealed through all the signs and wonders...

<header>Guarded Matzah</header>

<margin>Servants of the Lord and not servants of Pharaoh; until here are his words.</margin>

### And this is the language of the Zohar:

Rabbi Jose said: Why are these four cups of wine poured? Rabbi Abba said: The colleagues have already established that they correspond to the four expressions of redemption. However, it is explained well in the tradition of Rav Yeba the Elder <note>original: *Rav Yeba Sava*, a recurring mystical figure in the Zohar</note>, who said that since the "holy union" is found on this night, and this union consists of four "knots" which are four levels that do not separate from one another, when this union is present, we awaken their joy because we have merited them. For whoever perceives this, perceives the whole. And why is this night distinguished from all other nights? Because we must make changes in everything on this night to correspond to these four pourings, both above and below. Furthermore, he said that we call them the four redemptions because the lowest level is called "Redeemer" <note>This refers to the *Sefirah* of *Malchut* or Kingship</note>, but it is only called "Redeemer" because of the higher level that stands above it and illuminates it. This higher level only radiates light through these two levels above it. These are the four redemptions; until here are his words.

And behold, at first Rav Yeba the Elder explained that since the "holy union" is found—meaning that once the "husk" <note>original: *kelipah*, representing spiritual impurity or evil</note>, the darkness, and the oppressor have passed and gone, then the union is found. This union exists in "four knots," which are the spiritual emanations of Wisdom, Understanding, Beauty, and Kingship <note>original: *Chochmah, Binah, Tiferet, Malchut*</note>. These are the secret of the entire world of Emanation <note>original: *Atzilut*</note>, corresponding to the four letters of the Name Y-H-V-H <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Name of God</note>. Afterward, Rav Yeba the Elder said that the four cups hint at the four redemptions, which are the levels of Kingship, Foundation, Victory, and Splendor <note>original: *Malchut, Yesod, Netzach, Hod*</note>. For Kingship is called "Redeemer," and it is called so because of Foundation, which is the secret of redemption, as our Sages of the Academy said: "Redemption reaches unto Beauty." This state does not exist now in exile. It is also written, "Tell the righteous that it is good," referring to the level of Foundation, and it is written, "If the Good One will redeem you." This refers to the flow from Victory and Splendor that is above it. All of this is drawn from the secret of Understanding, the secret of the Jubilee year, which is the essence of freedom. In this matter, the union of Beauty and Kingship—that is, the "Body" and its "Arms"—is achieved through the "arousing bolt," which is the level of Foundation. Victory and Splendor are the "vessels of the male," as explained in other places.

According to this, the four cups correspond to these four redemptions: Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Kingship. But according to what Rav Yeba the Elder said first, the four cups are the four letters of the Name Y-H-V-H. This is also found in the *Book of Ethics*, as follows: The **first cup** of Kiddush <note>The sanctification of the day</note> corresponds to the letter *Yod*, which represents holiness, as it is said, "Lift your hands in holiness." The **second cup**, over which we recite the Haggadah and tell of the miracles, corresponds to the letter *He*, from which miracles and the plagues are drawn. The **third cup** of the Grace After Meals corresponds to the letter *Vav*, which is found in the "heavens," as it is said, "Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you," for from there comes the power of sustenance. It is also said, "And You shall hear in heaven and forgive." The **fourth cup**, over which we say "Pour out Your wrath upon the nations," corresponds to the final *He* of the Name, which is the Attribute of Justice. If one says they will not drink it, they are liable for lashes by rabbinic law. One must drink, and this is enough for an intelligent person to understand; until here are his words.

From what I found in the words of the disciples of the Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century mystic</note>, it implies that the four cups correspond to Wisdom, Understanding, Kindness, and Strength, for Wisdom and Understanding are the roots, and Kindness and Strength include

->the Kindnesses<-

and not any other name, but the Name of the Lord alone. This answers the question of why Moses said, "I have come to speak in Your Name," for Pharaoh replied, "Who is the Lord that I should obey His voice?" The explanation is that all other Names represent the judgments in the world and the natural conduct of creatures. But "He was, He is, and He will be"—He is the Lord over everything, and it is in His power to uproot and change the orders of nature. "Give thanks to the Lord for He is good," for He created the heavenly systems, and they are masters as he said: the power and leaders of the systems are called *Elohim* <note>God, but also a term for judges or powers</note>, and they are

->our God<-

<column-break/>

<header>Tractate Pesachim</header>
<header>Enriched Matzah</header>

The *Tur* <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, a major halakhic authority</note> discussed the excellence of the "telling" and the "speaking" regarding the sacrifices and the laws of Passover. Why is it not the same for other commandments—to tell of the portions of tithes, Sabbatical years, Jubilees, or valuations of property? See the *Chomah* <note>likely *Chomat Anakh* or a similar commentary</note> on these many points. This is why we find scribes in place of magicians. Even the "telling" of the four special Torah portions <note>read in the weeks before Passover</note> depends on these: the two portions of Shekalim are for the need of sacrifices, as is the portion of the Red Heifer. The portion of *HaChodesh* is for the publicity of the commandment, and the portion of *Zachor* is the commandment itself to remember until the time for action arrives.

**Furthermore**, a second inquiry into the sacrifices and the laws of Passover: we find that they change for the better. Regarding sacrifices, it is written in the Midrash in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Yudan: This is like a king traveling in the desert, and his friend came and honored him with a basket of figs and one jug of wine. The king said, "Is this a great honor?" The friend replied, "My lord king, I have honored you according to the current moment, but when you enter your palace, you will see how much I truly honor you." So said the Holy One, Blessed be He, to Israel: "This is the law of the burnt offering." Israel said before Him: "Master of the Universe, these sacrifices are for the current moment, but 'when You do good in Your favor unto Zion, build the walls of Jerusalem,' then 'You will desire sacrifices of righteousness, burnt offerings, and whole offerings.'" Similarly, regarding the redemption from Egypt, it is written: "As in the days of your coming out of Egypt, I will show him wonders." It will change for the better, as it is written: "Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when they shall no longer say, 'As the Lord lives who brought up the children of Israel from the land of Egypt,' but, 'As the Lord lives who brought up and led the house of Israel...'" One must consider what these changes for the better are.

**Furthermore**, a third inquiry: "Servitude" <note>original: *avodah*, which means both "labor/slavery" and "divine service/worship"</note> is attributed to both. The act of sacrifices is called *avodah* (service) more than any other commandment, though they are all actions. Only sacrifices are called by the name "service." Similarly, regarding the matter of Egypt, "they served God <note>possibly a typo for *served with rigor*</note> in this generation." After the freedom, we are obligated to begin with the "disgrace"—"We were slaves." The Ten Commandments begin with "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage," and did not say "who created the world." The beginning of the laws of *Mishpatim* <note>the Torah portion following the Ten Commandments</note> starts with the commandment of the Hebrew slave, to keep the mark of servitude existing, for "they are My servants" whom I acquired previously, and many such examples.

**And regarding** four points, I shall answer. The fourth inquiry: We find in these two <note>sacrifices and Passover</note> all the attachments to the Essential Name, the Name of the Lord <note>Y-H-V-H</note>. Regarding sacrifices, our Sages said in the *Sifrei*: Rabbi Jose says, everywhere it says "sacrifice," the Name of the Lord (Y-H-V-H) is used, so as not to give an opening to the heretics to scoff. Rabbi Hezekiah asked: Why is it called *korban* (sacrifice)? It should be called *keruv* (bringing near) or *kerivuta* (closeness). What is *korban*? They told him: This is known to the colleagues. *Korban* means that those "holy crowns" <note>The Sefirot</note> are brought near all as one and tied to one another until they all become one in a perfect unity to establish the Holy Name properly. This is why it is written, "A sacrifice to the Lord"—a sacrifice of those holy crowns to the Lord, to establish the Holy Name and unify it properly, so that mercy may be found in all worlds and the Holy Name may be crowned with its bonds to become sweetened. The secret of this is to awaken Mercy and not to awaken Judgment. Therefore, it is "to the Lord" and not "to *Elohim*" (God). We need to awaken the Lord, Mercy, and not *Elohim*, Judgment. He said: Blessed is the portion of the one who asked this, for this is the clarity of the matter. But is it not written, "The sacrifices of God (*Elohim*) are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise"? It says "Sacrifices of *Elohim*" and not "Sacrifices of the Lord"! Indeed, it is so: "A *sacrifice* of *Elohim*" is not written, but "The *sacrifices* of *Elohim*." Therefore, the slaughtering is in the north <note>The north is associated with the attribute of Strength/Judgment</note>, to break the power and strength of harsh judgment. It is written "a broken spirit" to weaken that strong spirit of Strength, so that judgment may be sweetened and mercy may prevail over judgment; until here are his words. 

This matter requires explanation, but in any case, we see "a sacrifice to the Lord." Our Sages also said at the end of Tractate Menachot: Why is neither *El* nor *Elohim* mentioned in the entire section of sacrifices, but only the Unique Name? So as not to give an opening to the heretics. Thus it is said, "He who sacrifices to any god (*Elohim*) shall be destroyed, save unto the Lord alone." Similarly, regarding Egypt, the Zohar says in the portion of *Miketz*: "God (*Elohim*) shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace." Rabbi Abba said: Come and see that wicked Pharaoh, who said, "I do not know the Lord." Pharaoh was wiser than all the sorcerers, but he only knew the name *Elohim*, as it is written, "Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the spirit of God (*Elohim*)?" Since Moses only came to him with the higher Name, the Lord (Y-H-V-H), and not with the name *Elohim*, this was the hardest thing for him. He knew that the name *Elohim* rules on earth, but the Name of the Lord he did not know. Therefore, this Name was difficult for him, and it is written, "And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart," for this word strengthened and hardened his heart, as Moses did not reveal the secret of the Name to him. See more in the *Tzeror HaMor*. And as it is written on the verse, "And from the time I came to speak..." This is what the verse says later: "Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods." He explained the matter: Of all the names with which the world was created, He and His Name were alone. The Name Y-H-V-H "was, is, and will be," and everything is good because His kindness is everlasting. "Give thanks to the God of gods... Give thanks to the Lord of lords..." The matter is that He gave Strength and Might to be rulers in the world. He is high above the high, for there are "powers" that were the leaders of the nations, which the Lord allotted to every nation and tongue.

# Matzah of Ten
<note>Hebrew: *Matzah Asarah*. This is likely a Kabbalistic play on *Matzah Ashirah* (Rich Matzah), connecting the Matzah to the ten *Sefirot* (Divine emanations).</note>

Which is from the aspect of the name *Havayah* <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note>, there is to the name *Elohim* <note>The name of God associated with Justice</note> an aspect of "hidden things" from the side of the "filling" of the letter *He* with *Yod*, *Vav*, and *He*. And in the most hidden "children," which is the aspect of the letter *He* from the name *Havayah*, there is to the name *Elohim* a hidden aspect from the side of the name *Elohim* in a filling of *He* like this: *He-He*. In this way, the name *Elohim* from the side of Wisdom (*Chochmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*) and its combination of the letters *Yod-He* is "full of the blessing of the Lord" <note>Deuteronomy 33:23</note>. For from the filling of *Yod-He* the numerical value is twenty-six <note>The same as the Tetragrammaton</note>. However, the name *Elohim*, which indicates the Attribute of Justice, its place is in Might (*Gevurah*), and it has a filling of *He* with *Aleph* like this: *He-Aleph*. And to the *Aleph* there are two aspects: the aspect of *Yod* which equals twenty-six, like the value of *Yod-Vav-Dalet*. Therefore, from the side of Kindness (*Chesed*), which is also included in Might—except that Kindness prevails—and in Might it is in the aspect of the shape of the *Aleph* [composed of a] *Yod*. There is a hint to this matter: "the good is behind his right hand," for "Kindness and Might surround the wicked, they shall walk like a lizard" <note>A variation of Psalms 12:9, used here to describe the surrounding of external forces</note>. These are the "unjust" and the "vinegar" <note>referring to leaven/Chametz</note>. Nevertheless, they are not equal in their strength, for this is called "leaven" (*Chametz*) and that is called:
->Sourdough and Sourdough:<-

-><term>S-N-S-P</term><note>Likely an acronym or a mystical name related to protective forces</note><-
<gloss>Impulsive forces like a seal and a covering. And because it was explained that the 49 [levels] of <term>Metatron</term> are holy, like the removal of the [letter] *Shin* for the *Chet*... and the secret of "Guarded Matzah" in the secret of Understanding (*Binah*), which is the letter *He*, and its inclusion was the secret of *Yod* in number. But afterward, when they spread out, understand that there is a refinement for the fillings... inside the *He*... because of the holiness of the Torah scrolls.</gloss>

And sourdough (*Se’or*) and the commandment are more difficult, and it flees. "Sourdough" is written in the Torah deficiently <note>Missing a letter</note>. There, the letters of *Elohim* are revealed in all matters. The letters of *Elohim* in their fillings—*Aleph-Lamed*, *Lamed-Mem-Dalet*, *He-Yod*, *Yod-Vav-Dalet*, *Mem-Mem*—equal 300. The "backwards" spelling of the letters of *Elohim* (*Aleph*, *Aleph-Lamed*, *Aleph-Lamed-He*, etc.) equals 200. The letter *Vav* of the 10 [is] from the letters of the "rest" of the "Small Face" <note>original: *Zeir Anpin*, the emotional Sefirot</note>. And the *He* is an acronym for *Elohim*. Thus we have the simple, the filled, and the squared [names]. They did not hint at the name there with vowel points, only with full letters. But from the side of Understanding (*Binah*), which is the "Eternal Redemption" and the secret of the Jubilee—even though in Understanding the awakening of Justice reached Israel in their exile like in Egypt—nevertheless, it is written "Y-H-V-H *Elohim*" as a language of "knowledge" and "connection." For this Justice was only for the good, so that they would be refined and become pure like the fine flour of wine. Even the expansion from Wisdom and Understanding into "Covered Kindness" is all for the "One" to take hold of the Temple, which is the Redemption. From there, Israel went out to freedom. "From the narrow place I called out to the Lord (*Yah*)" <note>Psalms 118:5</note>; and this is the name *Elohim* from the side of the *Yod* and the side of the *He* in Wisdom and Understanding. And the leaven and the sourdough were ceased at night and at all times. And when they were in "Ten," the "Guarded Wine" was placed in the "Cup of Salvations" for the children of God. Then the name *Elohim* and *Yah* is filled entirely with mercy, and the "drunkenness" increased according to the secret of "extra guarding." This is the secret of "Guarded Matzah" (*Matzah Shmura*), for *Elohim* in its filling equals... on the condition that you write the letter *Tzadik* [in Matzah] as a *Kuf*... the sign is "Say of the righteous (*Tzadik*) that it is good" <note>Isaiah 3:10</note>. Like this: *Aleph-Lamed*, *Lamed-Mem-Dalet*, *He-Yod*, *Yod-Vav-Dalet*, *Mem-Mem* equals 300. And so too *Matzah* in its filling with the word itself: *Mem-Mem*, *Tzadik-Dalet-Yod-Kuf*, *He-Yod*. And even without the *Kuf*, when you fill the *He* with a *Yod*, the filling of *Matzah* will be the number of the "Squared Elohim" (200). So too the filling of *Matzah* (*Mem-Mem*, *Tzadik-Dalet-Yod*, *Yod-Vav-Dalet*) equals 200 with the word. And so the "Square of Matzah" is for the filling of *Elohim* with a *Yod* with five letters... equals 300 with the five letters of *Elohim*. And so the "Square of Matzah" rises: *Mem*, *Mem-Tzadik*, *Mem-Tzadik-He*. The secret of "Guarded Matzah" indicates the "extra guarding" in the essence of "belovedness" with Wisdom. It is known that the filling of the name *Yod* in Wisdom and Understanding equals 72 and 63 <note>Numerical values of different spellings of the Tetragrammaton</note>... and so too the word *Matzah* rises. And behold, the "narrowness" (*Metzar*) of the Kingdom is called "Affliction" (*Oni*) for them <note>referring to *Lechem Oni*, the Bread of Affliction</note>, but from the side of Understanding, it is "Rich Matzah" and "Guarded Matzah" and it approaches the Name of the Lord. The thirty cups of wine are drawn from the "Guarded Wine," and through this, all the leaven is removed.

<column-break/>

"And to keep my commandments all the days, so that it may be well with them," etc. And it is answered in the *Midrash Shmuel*: he was precise with the word "nest" (*ken*) from the language of "old" (*yashan*) <note>play on words between *ken* (nest) and *yashan* (old)</note>, which does not stand. Sourdough [is discarded] so as not to [serve] "on the condition of receiving a reward" (*peras*). He did not say anything but "on the condition of receiving reward in this world," because there is no reward for commandments in this world. But he did not speak of the reward of the World to Come, the spiritual recompense, etc. See there at length.

Now let us consider four matters in the service of the Place <note>God</note>, and let us count from the bottom to the top according to the order of the levels.
**The lowest level:** One who serves "on the condition of receiving a reward," meaning the eternal reward for the World to Come. This is only forbidden if it is on the condition of receiving reward in *this* world. This aspect is called "Bread" in the name of one who "serves himself"—meaning for his own sake for the World to Come.
**The second level:** The plain meaning of one who fulfills the whole Torah out of "Awe of the Master," in order to fulfill His commandments so as not to transgress the command of his Master. This is called "Inner Awe."
**The third level:** In addition to fulfilling the whole Torah, he becomes a lover and becomes inflamed, and serves the Lord with joy and goodness of heart, and loves Him with all his heart. This aspect is called a "Son to the Lord," and it is the upper level for the majority of humanity.
**However, the "Children of Ascent" <note>The spiritual elite</note>:** From there, one rises above them all. He fears [transgressing] before Him or causing a "blemish," and desires to be a "Chariot" (*Merkavah*) for Him to do "pleasure for his Creator" (*Nachat Ruach*). Even the reward they receive is themselves becoming closer to Him, to fear Him and serve Him. The "rest" given to him from his labor is to be the "bearer of the Throne" and the "Chariot." He has no "rest" from service, for the service is the rest. In this aspect, "The servant of a King is a King."

When we contemplate these four parts, we find they correspond to the cleaving of the Name (*Y-H-V-H*)... the beginning is the "Servant of the King" through the combination of the aspect of "Servant"... the aspect of "Moses, the Servant of the Lord"... And he is the "Servant of a King, a King." And the "King of the Holy King," for the Creator of the world, in His power, can always be that which approaches this aspect of the first *Ehyeh* ("I Will Be")... which is called [the level of] "Ascent." And "Ascent" is the aspect of the second *Ehyeh*, the aspect of Understanding (*Binah*)... "Inner Awe," the fulfillment of the Torah... which is the aspect of cleaving to the name *Elohim*, which is the aspect of one who "serves himself," i.e., for the sake of reward. And the lowest is the aspect of cleaving to the name *Adonai* <note>Lord</note>, which includes the hosts of Israel. 

Regarding these levels, the verse says: "I am your servant, the son of your handmaid" (*Ani avdecha ben amatecha*). "I" (*Ani*) is the aspect of serving for oneself. "Your servant" (*Avdecha*) is the aspect of Inner Awe. "Son" (*Ben*) is the aspect of "You are children to the Lord your God." And afterward... "Son of your handmaid"... King David feared the Holy One... And regarding the last level it is written: "For I feared..." and so it is written: "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You." 

The level of "External Fear" vs "Inner Love" is a high level... "You are children to the Lord your God." And the level of "Pious ones" and "Inner Awe," of which it is said: "Fear the Lord, His holy ones, for there is no lack for those who fear Him." For "External Fear" is for the sake of this world, because of all his "lack" he fears... as it is said, "And it shall be when he is hungry... he will curse his God." But in "Inner Awe" from the side of holiness, which is the fulfillment of our Holy Torah, then there is "no lack." For Kindness is Love. Even in my exile, we receive [suffering] with love. The holy service upon them is like a "Daughter who draws [the father]," for "God is seen from your sanctuaries." Below this is the lowest level, "one who serves himself" for his eternity in the World to Come. Even though it is "profane" (*Chullin*), nevertheless it is "profane matters handled in holy purity." As they explain, the place of the reward of the World to Come is also from the side of purity. And this purity leads to holiness, which is the level of which we said: "Fear the Lord, His holy ones." 

Through this, the Midrash is understood... "Lest I take... God of my father and I will exalt Him." I am a daughter, a daughter of kings; beloved, daughter of beloved ones; holy, daughter of holy ones; pure, daughter of pure ones. This is like a man who set out to betroth a woman and found her to be the daughter of so-and-so, shameful in her family... but I am not ashamed to say I am a daughter of kings, beloved daughter of beloved ones. Thus the four levels mentioned above are explained: the Servant of the King, the matter of Inner Love, the matter of "Fear the Lord His holy ones," and the matter of "Profane matters handled in holy purity." 

There are aspects in it: "I" in her family, the aspect of "Your Servant" in her closeness, the aspect of "Son of your handmaid." For in our exile, there is one path, for they are close to the mountains, the secret of "I Will Be What I Will Be" (*Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh*)... "Behold the Lord, children." Therefore, it does not end but with the praise of these qualities which are upper levels. Why "Beloved daughter of kings, daughter of beloved ones"? Because "Beloved" is the highest level of most people, and "Kingship" of the "Lord of Kings" is the highest level of those who ascend. Regarding this it is said: "The God of my father and I will exalt Him." 

And behold, the root of the holiness of the service of a "Servant of the Lord" is truly for His Name, to be thus for Him, as it is said: "Everyone who is called by My Name, for My glory I created him." And it is written "to fear the glorious Name"... It is said, "Blessed is He who shared His glory with those who fear Him." For the glorious Name is glory to those who fear Him... "the reward of a commandment is the commandment itself" <note>Ethics of the Fathers 4:2</note>. This means that the more one serves the Name, one becomes a "hand" for the World to Come, which is to say a "Chariot." This is our eternal reward, that his form is under the Throne of Glory, and he "bears the Throne" through the hearing of the Ministering Angels. This is the purpose that was desired in the Garden of Eden, in a spiritual place, "to work it and to guard it"—the commandments and the letters. For the eternity of the service is ours, for the Name and that which is similar to it. The "rest" given to us is the "service"... for there the work and the commandments are dependent on the Land. And the more one is connected, the more power the service has in the Holy Temple. This is the matter of the prostration of all Israel... the King bows... and the prayers according to the plain meaning. Whoever has more greatness needs to give more praise and thanks to the Name. However, according to our "Inner" way, the matter is that whoever is closer, or is the most close, is the most prepared for the service.
