# Tractate Pesachim
## Rich Matzah
<note>Hebrew: *Matzah Ashirah*. In Jewish law, this is matzah made with fruit juice or eggs; here, it is treated as a Kabbalistic concept related to the ten *Sefirot* (emanations).</note>

### Guarded Matzah
<note>Hebrew: *Matzah Shemurah*. This is matzah guarded from the moment of harvest to ensure no fermentation occurs.</note>

As mentioned in the Zohar in several places, from the "side of the children" judgments are awakened, but the judgment is not like the essence of the Name itself. It is close to the concept mentioned by the Sages of blessed memory <note>Hebrew: *Zal* (Zikhronam Livrakha)</note> that gifts were given through suffering, and one of them is the World to Come <note>Hebrew: *Olam HaBa*</note>. Now, the World to Come is a world of spiritual pleasure, yet it must be reached through "suffering of great love," an eternal love. This is as a man chastens his son, so the Lord your God chastens you <note>Original: "כאשר ייסר איש את בנו כה' אלקיך מייסרך" (Deuteronomy 8:5)</note>. And this "Wine" is great mercy, meant to be refined to the ultimate refinement to receive the influence of great holiness. This is the "Guarded Wine" <note>Hebrew: *Yayin HaMeshumar*. A Talmudic concept of wine preserved in its grapes since the six days of Creation for the righteous in the future.</note>, for the ultimate purpose is to be removed from all dregs and to be clean, clear, and pure. See the *Kefar* in the Gate, for in this secret it is exceedingly sweet, as mentioned above regarding Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chochmah*</note>, which is the root of roots in the way we have written.
---
<image-desc>Decorative flourish line</image-desc>

---

The soul of Moses was hidden above the high ones. If so, since the soul of Moses is so high and exalted, it is impossible for exile to rule over him. His entire tribe was saved through his merit, and for our teacher Moses, peace be upon him <note>Hebrew: *Marea"h* (Moshe Rabbenu Alav HaShalom)</note>, the verse is fulfilled: "I am with him in distress" <note>Psalms 91:15</note>. And here, he resolves his difficulty regarding the vocalization of the Name *Y-H-V-H* <note>Transcribed as *Y-V-D-D* to avoid writing the Name</note> within *Elohim* and *Adonai* as weak letters <note>Hebrew: *Refeh*</note>, for through them exiles are possible. Nonetheless, "I am with him in distress" because the root of their soul is established in the Supernal *Eheyeh* <note>The Divine Name "I Will Be" (Exodus 3:14)</note>. Now, we have already written "God has spoken once, twice have we heard" <note>Psalms 62:12</note>. I mean to say: from the hidden, the revealed is understood. The hidden <note>the root of his soul in the double *Eheyeh*</note> refers to "Israel in thought" and "Moses in thought."

"Tell the Children of Israel: *Eheyeh* [I Will Be]" <note>Exodus 3:14</note> only once, for they did not rise in thought except in the name *Adonai* <note>Transcribed as *A-D-D-Y*</note> as the lower aspect. It has already been explained that from this power, exile and the "Other Side" <note>Hebrew: *Sitra Achra*, the realm of impurity</note> are prepared, and the revealed is prepared so that no other exile will be revealed to them, so they will not be overly terrified. Thus, the mention was a connection of the event... once in a poor house and outside his difficulty, and in this way it was also removed so they would not err. And after he said, "Thus shall you say to the Children of Israel: *Eheyeh* has sent me to you," he said further... the Lord God of your fathers. That is to say, when they sit and begin to understand from the power of the latter *Eheyeh*, which is their aspect, they will be able to increase their perception of the value of the Tetragrammaton in its middle, which is the first *Adonai*. These are called "People of Ascent" <note>Hebrew: *Bnei Aliyah*, highly spiritual individuals</note> who cling to understanding. Moses ascended, but he placed them in stages—"precept by precept, line by line" <note>Isaiah 28:10</note>—therefore he went through the levels: "God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob." The general rule is: Moses is attached to *Eheyeh* which is *Eheyeh*, meaning he includes the secret of the soul of Israel and attaches to the first *Adonai*, and Israel is attached to *Adonai*. Through these names, they are attached to Him, may He be blessed, as in "And you who cling to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>.

And when I came "eye to eye" <note>Numbers 14:14; meaning a direct experience</note>, my father (may the good hand of the Lord be upon me) awakened in me the matter of serving the Name <note>Hebrew: *HaShem*</note> according to the aforementioned aspect. The verse will be explained as beginning the Hallel tonight: "Praise, O servants of the Lord" <note>Psalms 113:1</note>. The four types of praise and glory mentioned will be explained. Israel are called "servants of the Lord" and His beloveds. Israel are also called "sons to the Place" <note>Hebrew: *Banim LaMakom*; God is often called "The Place"</note>. It is common on people's tongues that the status of "son" is superior to the status of "servant," as is explained in the liturgy of *Hayom Harat Olam* <note>Liturgy from Rosh Hashanah: "If as sons, if as servants..."</note>. This is true in most cases. However, regarding the "People of Ascent" (who are few), the status of "servant" is superior to the status of "son," as we shall explain. By this, it will be answered why at the moment of mentioning the height of his level, Moses was called "servant" and not "son," as it says: "Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant, against Moses?" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. It does not say "against My son, Moses." Similarly, it is written: "Send out My son, that he may serve Me" <note>Exodus 4:23</note>. And so too after his death, when he attached to the supernal level, they called him "Moses, the servant of the Lord."

To explain this, I will provide two introductions. First, these two matters—whether as sons or as servants—are why we say "Our Father, our King" (*Avinu Malkeinu*). The aspect of "King" is more exalted in Him than the aspect of "Father." For He is called "King" by His very essence, even before the world was created, when "He was, and His Name was alone." The Lord is King in essence, not like a human king who is no king without a people. He, may He be blessed, does not need a people, for His existence and power are sufficient. This is the praise: "The Lord was King" before the world was created; "The Lord is King" in action when He created the world; "The Lord will reign" in the future when the world is renewed. (We have elaborated on this in my book *Sha'ar HaShamayim* <note>The Gate of Heaven</note> in the commentary on the prayers). He is only called "Father" in relation to His progeny, when creation and the chain of worlds began; then the Cause is called "Father" and the Effect is called "Son."

Second Introduction: Our service to Him is in love and fear, as written in the Torah. It is also written: "Serve the Lord with joy" <note>Psalms 100:2</note> and "Serve the Lord with fear" <note>Psalms 2:11</note>. Love is the aspect of a son's love for a father, and fear is the dread of a servant before his master. Antigonus already preceded this: "Be not like servants..." <note>Ethics of the Fathers 1:3</note> but let everything be for the sake of His Name, not out of fear of punishment nor out of love of reward. For such fear and love are called "external fear" and "external love." Only for His Name's sake, as the commentators have elaborated, saying that "internal fear" leads to "internal love." Internal fear means one is afraid to transgress the command of his Master—fulfilling the whole Torah. From this internal fear, one comes to internal love—doing everything with a flaming heart, with longing and desire, serving the Lord with joy and a good heart. This is the great level. 

However, the "People of Ascent" enter from internal love into a fear that is "inmost of the inmost." This is the aspect of the "Pious one who acts with his Creator" <note>Hebrew: *Chassid hamit-chassed im kono*</note>, who brings satisfaction to his Maker. His entire aim is attachment to Him for the sake of His great Name, becoming a "chariot" <note>Hebrew: *Merkavah*; a vehicle for Divine presence</note> for Him. I have already elaborated on the sermon of love and fear, see there. All his service is the "Service of the King." On this, the hint comes: "The servant of a King is a King" <note>A Talmudic maxim: *Eved melekh, melekh*</note>. The simple meaning of the hint is that the servant of the King is the King himself; there is his attachment, everything is for His sake. There are two types of service: "one born in the house" and "one bought with money" <note>Genesis 17:12</note>. One born in the house is more attached to his master than one bought with money. The aspect of a servant who is lower than a son is called "bought with money," but the aspect of the "Servant of the King" is like the one "born in the house." Thus it is written of Moses: "He is trusted in all My house" <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. "Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant?"—for the servant of a king is a king. The matter is also that he is attached to the root of the roots of his soul, in the aspect that attaches to the Primordial Being, the very essence of the Name *Havayah*, that "He and His Name are one." He is called "King." As explained above, Moses ascended in thought to the first point that approaches the Hidden One. In this aspect, Moses is called "the servant of the Lord" in essence. This aspect of "servant" is higher than "son" even for the few "People of Ascent." Regarding the two types of service, the verse alludes: "If I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is My fear?" <note>Malachi 1:6</note>. It is difficult that "Master" (*Adonim*) is in the plural; rather, it refers to two types of service and two types of fear.

Antigonus said, "Be not like servants..." After these introductions, the matter of the Name *Y-H-V-H* explained above and the matter of the "servant" will be clarified. One who serves for reward is the opposite. It is difficult, for the Torah is full of calls to people to serve the commandments for the sake of reward, saying "that it may be well with you and you may prolong your days" <note>Deuteronomy 5:16</note> and "that your days may be long and it may go well with you" <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note>. It says, "Keep His statutes and His commandments... that it may go well with you and your children after you" <note>Deuteronomy 4:40</note>, and in many places. Not only that, but the Holy One, blessed be He, in His own glory said: "O that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me..." <note>Deuteronomy 5:26</note>.

<column-break/>

The master of the house understands this... as was explained. "And they shall ask me, what is His name?" <note>Exodus 3:13</note> meaning: how is it possible for the influence of the Tetragrammaton to be recognized in the point of *Elohim* and *Adonai*? That is, to be united in essence, for in any case, it is impossible from the perspective of His essence except through His clothing Himself in them. (Is the Tetragrammaton not the aspect of "He was, He is, and He and His Name are one," or are the Names renewed after the life... and the distinction of the answer "I Will Be what I Will Be" <note>Hebrew: *Eheyeh Asher Eheyeh*</note>).

Now we shall explain the statement. Before the explanation, we provide an introduction: the Sages said that "Israel rose in thought," and similarly, "In the beginning (*Bereshit*)—for the sake of Israel." And they said "Moses rose in thought," as seen in Genesis Rabbah: "*Bereshit*—for the sake of Moses." Moses is equivalent to all of Israel. All of them are fixed in "Thought," meaning the root of their soul. I have already written of two aspects in the secret of Thought. We also say that the aspect of *Eheyeh* <note>I Will Be</note> indicates the past, the supernal aspect, the root of roots of the soul of Moses. Moses ascended... for from there is the emanation of the Name... and the root of the roots of Israel is from the "Latter *Eheyeh*," from which is the emanation of the name *Adonai*, "Lord of Lords," the Supernal Host. Therefore they are compared to stars, as it is written: "And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament; and those who turn many to righteousness like the stars for ever and ever" <note>Daniel 12:3</note>. They are called the "Host of the Above," as it is written: "The hosts of the Lord went out" <note>Exodus 12:41</note>. This is the secret of the "Impregnation" <note>Hebrew: *Ibbur*; a Kabbalistic concept of soul-joining</note> mentioned by the Sages... the secret of the impregnation of souls. Also *Adonai* is the source of Israel, as it is written: "In assemblies bless God, the Lord, from the source of Israel" <note>Psalms 68:27</note>.

Behold, the souls of Israel are high, but the soul of Moses is hidden above the high ones. If so, since the soul of Moses is so high and exalted, it is impossible for exile to rule over him. His entire tribe was saved through his merit, and those close to him. Israel, who are lower than his level, can experience exile. But since they draw from... "God has spoken once, twice have we heard," when the Name said "I Will Be what I Will Be," explaining it to Moses... and why did they err in thinking they would be in this exile and another? Because for them, exiles are possible. Nonetheless, "I am with him in distress" because they draw from the source whose root... which He revealed to Moses, the double *Eheyeh*. But to Israel, he said: "Thus [shall you say]..."

Thus, the mention was a connection of the event... once in a poor house and outside his difficulty, and in this way it was also removed so they would not err. And after he said, "Thus shall you say to the Children of Israel: *Eheyeh* has sent me to you," he said further... the Lord God of your fathers. That is to say, when they sit and begin to understand from the power of the latter *Eheyeh*, which is their aspect, they will be able to increase their perception of the value of the Tetragrammaton in its middle, which is the first *Adonai*. These are called "People of Ascent" who cling to understanding. Moses ascended, but he placed them in stages—"precept by precept, line by line"—therefore he went through the levels: "God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob." The general rule is: Moses is attached to *Eheyeh* which is *Eheyeh*, meaning he includes the secret of the soul of Israel and attaches to the first *Adonai*, and Israel is attached to *Adonai*. Through these names, they are attached to Him, may He be blessed, as in "And you who cling to the Lord your God."

And when I came "eye to eye," my father (may the good hand of the Lord be upon me) awakened in me the matter of serving the Name according to the aforementioned aspect. The verse will be explained as beginning the Hallel tonight: "Praise, O servants of the Lord." The four types of praise and glory mentioned will be explained. It does not say "against My son, Moses." Similarly, it is written: "Send out My son, that he may serve Me." It is difficult: if he is "My son," why say "serve Me"? It argues that Moses' title as "Servant of the Lord" represents a higher level of mystical union than being a "Son," as it denotes total nullification to the Divine King.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic and philosophical exploration of the Exodus symbols, specifically focusing on the spiritual ranks of the soul and the mystical meanings behind the Divine Names revealed to Moses. It develops the theme of "Guarded Matzah" and "Rich Matzah" as symbols of spiritual purification and the transition from the "husk" of exile to the "fruit" of the Land of Israel.</meta>

# Tractate Pesachim
## Rich Matzah
## Guarded Matzah

### קנד <note>Page 154</note> | לט ב <note>Folio 39b</note>

And this is not so, as it is written: "This is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan according to its borders." <note>Numbers 34:2</note> And at the beginning of the verse, it is written: "When you come into the land of Canaan." Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra <note>A 12th-century scholar and philosopher</note> explained this as meaning "and it shall come," and the meaning is that the land is indeed the Land of Canaan. From this, he wished to prove that they are an actual <term>Klipah</term><note>Literal: "husk" or "shell." In Kabbalah, this refers to the forces of impurity that surround and conceal holiness.</note>... and the one who says, as we have learned in the Mishnah: "If one is cast into a pit and says, 'Whoever hears my voice, let him write a divorce for my wife,' then they should write and give it." The <term>Gemara</term><note>The portion of the Talmud that comments on the Mishnah.</note> asks: "Should we not fear that it is a demon?" <note>Talmud, Gittin 66a</note> Rav Judah said: "Only if they see a human form." The Gemara asks: "But demons can also appear in human form!" They replied: "They see his shadow." The Gemara asks: "But they also have shadows!" Rabbi Hanina said: "Jonathan my son taught me—they have a shadow, but they do not have a <term>shadow of a shadow</term>." <note>Original: *bavu'a de-bavu'a*. This was a folkloric/mystical test to distinguish a human from a supernatural entity.</note> Thus we see that a "husk" can have its own "husk" <note>An outer layer of impurity</note>.

If Canaan himself was the "husk," and the land is his "shadow"—for it was the land of Canaan—then how could it say "according to its borders"? For the secret of borders is known to be the "shadow" of the inner essence within those borders. Rather, certainly Canaan is not the husk itself; the land was essentially a mission, taken by the Holy One from Canaan and given to Israel. Regarding the opposite view, I will show you from what remains that the Canaanite is indeed the husk, as it is written: "Cursed be Canaan, a slave of slaves shall he be to his brothers." <note>Genesis 9:25</note> As Rashi explained, "slaves" refers to Israel, and the "slave of peace" is the husk, which is cursed...

The ultimate purpose of the matter is that the essence of Canaan changed after the conquest of Israel. There are five levels of the commandment "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might." <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note> "With all your heart" means the body becomes a servant to the soul; "with all your soul" means the soul is acquired by God; "with all your might" means one's possessions are acquired for holy use. The Holy One purified Israel through these three: their bodies, their possessions, and their souls, as it is written: "When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God." <note>Exodus 3:12</note> And the wealthy "despoiled Egypt" <note>Exodus 12:36</note>. Regarding this servitude, He said: "Send My son that he may serve Me." <note>Exodus 4:23</note> This is why the First Commandment mentions "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage" <note>Exodus 20:2</note> and does not mention "Who created the world." The concept of "servitude" to God is of a higher spiritual rank than the creation of the physical world.

Furthermore, there is a secret in the word <term>Anochi</term> <note>Hebrew for "I," the first word of the Ten Commandments.</note>. It relates to the numerical value <note>Gematria</note> of the word <term>Kisse</term> <note>Hebrew for "Throne." Both *Anochi* and *Kisse* equal 81 in Hebrew numerology.</note>. This was the goal of the Exodus: "Send my son that he may serve me," and "You shall serve God on this mountain." Moses knew this purpose, which was the promise to Jacob: "I (*Anochi*) will go down with you... and I (*Anochi*) will also surely bring you up again."

<column-break/>

Afterward, we read the <term>Haggadah</term> <note>The text recited at the Passover Seder.</note> with joy. One should say: "For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God.</note>, through the Hidden and Concealed One, behold I am about to tell the story of the Exodus from Egypt." One should say this for every commandment—the four cups, the Matzah, and the Bitter Herbs (*Maror*). Throughout the year, one should perform commandments with joy. Now I will write the explanation of the Haggadah:

->### **This is the Bread of Affliction**<-
<note>Hebrew: *Ha Lachma Anya*. The opening paragraph of the Haggadah.</note>

<insert>
->Shmuel said:<-
->"Bread of Affliction"<-
</insert>

It is "bread over which many things are answered" <note>Talmud, Pesachim 115b. A play on words: *Anya* (affliction) and *Onin* (answering/speaking).</note>. Another explanation: Just as it is the way of a poor man to eat a broken piece, so too here. Another explanation: Just as it is the way of a poor man that he heats the oven and his wife bakes... It is written in the portion of *Re'eh*: "You shall eat no leavened bread with it; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, for in haste you came out of the land of Egypt, so that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life." <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>

One might ask: Was the "haste" not only on the first night? Furthermore, is "Rich Matzah" <note>Matzah made with juice or oil instead of just water.</note> forbidden all seven days? What is the virtue of "haste" that the Torah commanded us to remember it? Does it not say regarding the final redemption, "For you shall not go out in haste"? <note>Isaiah 52:12</note> This question also applies to the passage later: "This Matzah that we eat... because the dough of our fathers did not have time to leaven." But the commandment to eat Matzah was given on the first of Nisan, before they actually left!

The matter is this: The Holy One brings light out of darkness, and even the "evil messenger" <note>The impulse for evil or the oppressor</note> is forced to say "Amen." The very manner in which the Egyptians enslaved Israel was the very manner in which they were brought to freedom. How so? The Egyptians did not allow Israel to wait for their bread to leaven, but hurried them to their work in "haste." Thus, they could not eat leavened bread. So too at the time of the redemption, the "haste" was that of the Egyptians to send them away, not allowing the dough to leaven. This is a wonder of the redemption: through the very thing they intended for evil, they were corrected against their will. It was truly "from darkness to light." This was already in God's plan when He said, "In the evening you shall eat Matzah." By remembering that we once ate this in our poverty during exile, the evil is transformed into good.

Thus we understand Rashi’s words: "Bread of Affliction—bread that reminds one of the poverty and suffering they endured in Egypt." The obligation of "haste" applies specifically to the first night, and specifically to "Bread of Affliction," for the miracle occurred through the very conditions of their servitude. Therefore, one does not fulfill the obligation even with "Rich Matzah," because it must be a likeness of what happened in the exile which was then turned into redemption.

<summary>This page explores the mystical transition from the "husk" of Egyptian exile to the holiness of the Land of Israel, using the Passover Seder's "Bread of Affliction" to illustrate how God transforms the tools of oppression (haste and poverty) into symbols of liberation.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exploration of the Exodus, moving from the definition of "Guarded Matzah" to the concept of "Rich Matzah." It focuses on the transition from the impurity of Egyptian servitude (the "husk") to the holiness of serving God (the "fruit"). It also includes a famous historical-legal debate between the Jews and the "Africans" (descendants of Canaan) before Alexander the Great regarding the ownership of the Land of Israel.</meta>

# Tractate Pesachim

## Rich Matzah

Regarding the transgressions, etc. The Torah was given to us for greatness and sovereignty, as it is written: "By me kings reign" <note>Proverbs 8:15</note>. Yet, service to it is called for us *Tushiya* <note>A term for Torah; literally "wisdom" or "resourcefulness."</note>, for it "weakens the strength of man" <note>A Talmudic play on words: *tushiya* is read as *mateshet* (weakens). See Sanhedrin 26b.</note>. Through this, the statement of our Sages of blessed memory is explained: "Three things were given through suffering: Torah..." <note>Berakhot 5a</note>. 

First, let us look at "Hallelujah! Praise, O servants of the Lord" <note>Psalm 113:1, the beginning of the Hallel prayer</note>. This is a higher level than simply "Praise the Name of the Lord." It mentions the "Name" because the word "Name" (*Shem*) indicates the revelation of what was previously hidden, as is known from the words of the Kabbalists <note>The "Name" acts as a vessel for divine light that is otherwise too intense to perceive</note>. It hints at the province of the Name *Adonai* <note>The Divine Name associated with Lordship and the physical world</note>. The second part, "Blessed be the Name of the Lord," indicates even more revelation—specifically the level of *Elohim* <note>The Divine Name associated with judgment and the natural structure of the world</note>, the building of the world. This is why it says, "from this time forth and forever." 

"From the rising of the sun to its setting, the Name of the Lord is praised" refers to the aspect of one who serves God for his own sake, in order to receive the reward of the World to Come, which is the level of *Adonai*. It says "from the rising of the sun" because "what profit does a man have in all his labor which he labors under the sun?" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:3</note>. This is the meaning of "Praise, O servants of the Lord"—meaning, you are servants of the Lord and not servants of Pharaoh. 

There is a deep matter here. It is known that the <term>Klipah</term> <note>Literal: "husk" or "shell." In Kabbalistic thought, the "husk" of impurity must precede and protect the "fruit" of holiness until it is ripe.</note> comes first, similar to how Esau was born before Jacob, and the Evil Inclination comes before the Good Inclination. Wherever there is great holiness, there is also the "envy" of the husk, like the way "spirits cling to Torah scholars" <note>Mentioned in Berakhot 6a</note>, and the Evil Inclination is more powerful in Torah scholars than in anyone else <note>Sukkah 52a</note>. 

When the husk departs and is subdued, then the holiness remains refined and pure, without dregs. On the contrary, even the "evil angel" is forced to answer "Amen." Since the great level is to be "servants of the Lord," as explained, we could not have reached this level except through the precedence of the husk. The "husk of the servant" within holiness is the "servant to Pharaoh." Afterward, one must long for and meditate on the spirit of "release" (*periya*) <note>A wordplay on Pharaoh (Par'oh) and the act of uncovering or releasing (Periya)</note>. "And the Lord gave the people favor..." and he said "Rise up, go out..." 

This explains why we have learned in the Mishnah: "One begins with disgrace and ends with praise" <note>Pesachim 116a; the requirement for telling the Passover story</note>. In the Gemara, it asks: "What is the disgrace?" Rav said: "Originally our ancestors were idol worshippers." Shmuel said: "We were slaves." Now, one might ask: "At the time of our freedom, why is it necessary to mention the past trouble?" 

Rather, it is the freedom itself, the advantage, the closeness, and the acquisition of the "outer counsel." These two levels we mentioned—the matter of the Name Y-H-V-H and the matter of the "servant husk" that precedes the removal of the spiritual filth—emerge from the concept of faith. "Originally our ancestors were idol worshippers," and now the Omnipresent has brought us close, without any mixture of filth, removed from "external thoughts" and the preceding husk. The filth is removed from the "holiness of servitude" to become "servants of the Lord." This is its great advantage over the blessing. So too in the future: "To You every knee shall bend." This is the matter of the "Covenant between the Pieces" <note>Genesis 15; the covenant where God foretold the Egyptian exile to Abraham</note>.

<margin>If so</margin>

...which He struck with our father Abraham, a covenant that was the language of freedom. He informed him of the Egyptian exile—it is that which gives [the freedom]. The whole matter of Abraham our father... when [the servant] was killed, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "This one shall not inherit you, but rather he who comes from your own loins" <note>Genesis 15:4</note>. This refers to Israel, the "servants of the Lord." In order that their service be refined without dregs, they were "servants to Pharaoh," and once they entered [that state], then came the salvation of the "servants of the Lord" and not "servants of Pharaoh." Regarding this it is said: "Lighten our eyes... and let them see my salvation." The evil is [actually] for the good. Therefore, the "bitterness" (*mor*) is the opposite. For this servitude is actually sovereignty. Our level, higher than all highs, is "servants of the Lord." 

It is explained in the book *Ma'asei Hashem* <note>A 16th-century commentary on the Torah by Eliezer Ashkenazi</note> regarding the verse "a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers" <note>Genesis 9:25</note>. He asks: what is "a servant of servants"? Rather, the matter is that he shall be a servant to Israel, who are themselves called "servants" [of God]. This is the blessing: that he should be like the "evil angel who answers Amen" and be a servant to Israel. Canaan is the "husk of holiness," for true holiness is "submission" (*kena'ah*), and "servitude" is like "Canaan" (from the root "to submit"). Therefore, even after they conquered the Land of Israel, its name remained "The Land of Canaan," for there is the place of submission. When the husk departs, the submission remains, pure and without dregs. Understand this well. At first it was the "land of Canaan" [the land of the merchant/husk], and afterward it became "Holy Canaan" [submission to God]. 

Through this, we can understand what is taught in the chapter *Helek* <note>Sanhedrin 91a</note>: Our Sages taught: On the twenty-fourth of Nissan, the tax-collectors were removed from Judah and Jerusalem. When the people of Africa <note>Descendants of Canaan who fled to North Africa</note> came to litigate with Israel before Alexander of Macedon, they said: "The Land of Canaan is ours, as it is written: 'The land of Canaan according to its borders' <note>Numbers 34:2</note>, and Canaan was the father of these people." 

Gabiha ben Pasisa said to the Sages: "Give me permission and I will go and litigate with them before Alexander of Macedon. If they defeat me, say: 'You have defeated a commoner among us.' If I defeat them, say: 'The Torah of Moses has defeated you.'" They gave him permission. He went and litigated with them. He said to them: "From where do you bring proof?" They said: "From the Torah." He said: "I too will bring you proof only from the Torah, as it is said: 'And he said: Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers' <note>Genesis 9:25</note>. When a servant acquires property, to whom does the servant belong and to whom does the property belong? <note>A legal principle: what a slave acquires, his master acquires</note>. Not only that, but there are many years that you have not served us!" 

King Alexander said to them: "Give him an answer!" They said: "Give us three days' time." He gave them time. They searched but did not find an answer. Immediately they fled, leaving their fields sown and their vineyards planted. And that year was a Sabbatical year <note>A year when the land must lie fallow</note>. 

One might ask: Was Gabiha ben Pasisa the wisest of the wise or not? If he was the wisest, it is obvious he should go; why did he need to ask permission? And if there were Sages wiser than him, how could they send him? Perhaps, Heaven forbid, he would bring disgrace and a great loss to Israel? How could they say "you defeated a commoner among us"—would that be a remedy for such a great blow? We cannot say that they were wicked... for how could it enter one's mind that a great king like Alexander would act without the power of the question? Furthermore, why did they bring the verse "The Land of Canaan according to its borders" and not the verses in the section regarding Ham... as the inheritance belongs to Canaan. The Sages understood that since they brought this verse, there was both a revealed and a hidden aspect to their claim, based on philosophical inquiry. I will explain: they sent Gabiha, and if he did not win the case, the Sages would say: "We did not know they would claim something based on the hidden dimension of inquiry, for we thought to answer only the revealed claim." For even though they were wicked, they had this preparation... they did not have the "length" in the five points... and Israel had the "will for the covenant" from this verse.

<column-break/>

...the leaven (*chametz*) and the sourdough—which are the husks. Behold, all the hints I have written regarding the secret of the Four Cups are all true, even though they are from different perspectives. Everything goes to one place and returns to the Supernal Radiance. According to what I have written, they hint at two "unions" <note>*Yichudim*; the alignment of divine attributes</note>: *Binah* (Understanding) with *Tiferet* (Beauty), and *Tiferet* with *Malchut* (Kingship). I found a wonderful hint in the holy writings of the students of the <term>Arizal</term> <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century father of modern Kabbalah</note>. The four names of Unity—namely Y-H-V-H and A-H-Y-H—sum to 530 <note>This uses a specific Kabbalistic calculation known as "filling" or *Milui*</note>. So too, the "Square of Adonai" equals 126, like this: *Aleph*, *Aleph-Dalet*, *Aleph-Dalet-Nun*, *Aleph-Dalet-Nun-Yud*. Together with the 12 letters of *Adonut* <note>The spelling out of the name</note>, it all equals 530. Then, all "Chametz" is nullified, for the husk of **Chametz** <note>In Gematria, Chametz (חמץ) is 138, but the text associates its spiritual root with the number 530 (Taq-L)</note> equals 530. Then the "face of the field" is turned outward, and nothing [of the husk] shall be seen or found. Then it is revealed and desired: "In the evening you shall eat matzot."

### The Dipping

<insert>
First, the *Karpas* <note>The vegetable appetizer</note> in vinegar or salt water. See the responsa of the *Hatam Sofer*.

And they shall answer him: "We were slaves," for "He took us out," etc. For the letters of **Karpas** (כפרס) can be rearranged as *Samekh* (60) and *Perekh* (Back-breaking labor) <note>Exodus 1:13</note>. This hints at the 600,000 (*Samekh Ribbo*) who were in servitude. Also, **Karpas** (כרפס) equals the letter *Shin* (300) in its "filling" <note>The word *Shin* (שין) is 300+10+50 = 360; the author is using a complex Gematria</note>. I have already written that the Name *Elohim* in its filling equals 300, and *Karpas* is *Shin* in its filling. The "filling of the filling" of *Shin* equals 60, representing the spread of Judgment into the six extremities. All the "strength of the army" comes from this. 

The dipping is in vinegar <note>Original: *chutin*, likely a typo for *chometz* (vinegar) or referring to the "threads" of the vegetable</note>. For although they were enslaved, there was a "thread" of freedom. Vinegar represents the repair within the servitude, which is the "Grace" (*Hen*) of freedom, as is the custom of women. 

The matter of "looking to choke" refers to "Israel is His beloved"—meaning the beginning of their redemption, when they were in the "infancy" of their redemption, like the moment of birth when breathing is difficult. But when they grew great in the redemption, and the redemption became famous, afterward comes the telling of the *Haggadah*. 

After eating the vegetables, the middle Matzah is taken and broken in half. This hints at the "Bride" <note>The Shekhinah/Congregation of Israel</note> amidst the Assembly of Israel, which is a "broken matzah" between two whole ones. These represent the "arms of the world," and the "bed set between North and South." It hints at *Tiferet* between Judgment and Mercy.

This hints that through the "redemption of judgment," the Bride is sanctified to her Beloved, and then Israel was redeemed. I found in the holy writings of the Arizal: The Matzot are *Chokhmah* (Wisdom) and *Binah* (Understanding), where the "external forces" have no grasp. The letter *Heh* (ה) has two forms: *Dalet* with a *Yud*, or *Vav* with a *Gimel*. These are the *Heh* of the Name *Elohim*. Corresponding to the form of *Vav-Dalet*, we break the second (middle) Matzah into two. The one part must be larger than the second. The larger part corresponds to the *Vav* (6) and the smaller to the *Dalet* (4), for the number 6 is greater than 4. Corresponding to the form of *Heh-Vav*, we take the piece for the blessing of *HaMotzi* from the upper Matzah, which is a complete *Yud*. Also, the size of the *Motzi* is the size of a "Kezayit" <note>An olive's bulk</note>, which is [symbolically] 10 (the letter *Yud*). The *Kezayit* for the fulfillment of the commandment of eating Matzah comes from the broken piece, which is the secret of the *Dalet* (4) mentioned above. For that part which is *Vav* (6) is the **Afiqoman** <note>The hidden half-matzah eaten at the end of the meal</note>. And corresponding to the form of the letter *Nun-Vav-Yud-Nun*, we do as Hillel did [the sandwich] with the third Matzah, which hints at the *Nun*. He would wrap the Matzah, Maror, and Paschal lamb—three things together—corresponding to the *Nun-Vav-Yud-Nun*. Thus, I have found that the entire redemption is found within the "Mentalities" (*Mohin*) of *Chokhmah* and *Binah*, which equals 40 and 50, the Gematria of **Matzah** (מצה). <note>Matzah: Mem=40, Tzadi=90, Heh=5. This adds to 135. The author likely uses a different system or internal "filling" to reach 90 or 40/50.</note>. Corresponding to the forms of the *Heh* mentioned, we take these Matzot. This is the end of his words.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic analysis of the Passover themes, specifically focusing on the transition from the Exodus from Egypt (a "feminine" or incomplete redemption) to the Final Redemption (a "masculine" or complete redemption). It also links the Four Sons of the Haggadah to the Four Types of Bailees/Guards in Jewish law.</meta>

# Tractate Pesachim

## Guarded Matzah

Regarding the divine name and its permutations. The "Light" that was clarified is the "Light of the Beginning" <note>original: *Or ha-Ganuz* — the hidden light of creation</note>. This is the secret of the verse "Out of the depths I called to the Lord" <note>Psalm 118:5</note>. To the pious, in times of trouble, the Name of God is not whole; it is missing letters. When the letter *He* is missing from the Name, it is considered "bitter," and the goal of the Exodus was to make the Name whole again, as it is written: "The Lord is One and His Name is One" <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. Before the world was created, He and His Name were alone.

The secret of the sacrifice—"When a man brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>—is the secret of "clinging" <note>original: *devekut*</note> to the Divine. This was revealed in Egypt through the "Hand" <note>original: *Yad* — a reference to the "Mighty Hand" of God</note> and will be revealed even more gloriously in the future. The future revelation will be of a higher order, involving the "filled" Name of God <note>A Kabbalistic method of spelling out divine names to reveal inner dimensions</note>. The Exodus from Egypt was only a "New Song" in the feminine form <note>In Hebrew, the word *Shirah* (song) is feminine</note>, which represents the attribute of *Malchut* <note>Kingship or the Shekhinah</note>. In the future, it will be a "New Song" in the masculine form <note>The word *Shir* is masculine</note>. This is the meaning of the verse "The virgin of Israel has fallen, she shall rise no more" <note>Amos 5:2</note>—she will not rise again as a "feminine" recipient, but will be transformed into the "masculine" giver. The darkness itself will become light. This is the secret of the Chanukah Menorah <note>original: *Hagah Chanukiah*</note>, which represents the Assembly of Israel. In the future, everything will be filled with the secret of "May His Great Name be Blessed" <note>original: *Yehei Shmey Rabba* — the core of the Kaddish prayer</note>. This secret is hidden even from the ministering angels who ask, "Where is the place of His glory?" but it is revealed to Israel. This is why the *Kaddish* is recited in Aramaic—so the angels do not understand it and become jealous of Israel's intimacy with God.

Here, the secret of Divine Service is explained. Moses was a "servant of the Lord" <note>Deuteronomy 34:5</note>, while those in Egypt were "servants of Pharaoh," the "husk" <note>original: *Kelipah* — the shell of impurity</note> that mimics the holy service. Concerning Moses, it is written: "You have made him a little less than the angels" <note>Psalm 8:6</note>. Our Sages taught that there are 50 Gates of Understanding, and all were given to Moses except one. The Exodus corresponds to these gates. There are 49 "Pure Faces" of Torah and, opposing them, 49 "Impure Faces" of the Husk. Israel was sunken in the 49 gates of impurity in Egypt. If they had reached the 50th gate, God forbid, it would have been impossible to ever ascend. Since even Moses had not attained the 50th Gate of Holiness, he could not have pulled them out of a 50th Gate of Impurity. This explains the Haggadah's statement: "If the Holy One had not taken our ancestors out... we would still be enslaved." Therefore, in every generation, one must see himself as if he personally left Egypt. Every day we mention the Exodus because the daily holiness we attain and our closeness to God depend on that moment of leaving, which did not tarry for even a single second. From the "Impure Faces" of Egypt, we processed and refined the "Pure Faces" to cling to our Creator.

When the Temple stood, the sacrifice was made through cattle and sheep. But when the Temple is destroyed, a person offers *himself* through the story and the memory of the sacrifice. This is the meaning of "The Lord called to Moses" from the Tent of Meeting—the Zohar explains this refers to a time of weeping and mourning over the destruction. By surrendering our souls daily, we are "considered as sheep for the slaughter" <note>Psalm 44:23</note>. This is the root of our identity as "Servants of the Lord." The purpose of creation was "to work it and to guard it" <note>Genesis 2:15</note>. This "guarding" is found in the first commandment given to Israel: the law of the Passover and the "Guarded Matzah." Our Sages taught: "Do not read it as *Matzot* (unleavened bread), but as *Mitzvot* (commandments)." We find three types of "guarding" (Matzah, Mitzvot, and the Eye), and the night itself is called the "Night of Guarding."

There are four types of "Guards" <note>original: *Shomrim* — bailees in Jewish civil law</note> in the Torah, which correspond to the Four Sons. Between man and his fellow, there are:
1.  **The Unpaid Guard** <note>original: *Shomer Hinam*</note>: He guards for the sake of the task itself, without reward.
2.  **The Paid Guard** <note>original: *Shomer Sachar*</note>: He works for a reward.
3.  **The Renter** <note>original: *Socheir*</note>: Similar to a paid guard.
4.  **The Borrower** <note>original: *Sho'el*</note>: All the benefit is his.

As these four exist between men, they exist between man and God. The **Wise Son** is like the **Unpaid Guard**; his level is the highest. He does not serve for the sake of receiving a prize, but only for the sake of God's Name. He is exempt from everything because he is a "giver." The **Wicked Son** is like the **Borrower**; he wants all the benefit for himself and does not believe in reward or punishment; he is liable even for "accidents" (divine decrees). The **Simple Son** and the **One Who Does Not Know How to Ask** are like the **Paid Guard** or the **Renter**—those who say, "I am doing this charity so that my son may live."

Abraham is the archetype of the **Wise Son**. Our Sages said his kidneys acted as two springs of wisdom. He kept "My charge" <note>original: *mishmarti*</note>—meaning he guarded for God's sake, not his own. The Wise Son asks: "What is the good that God seeks from you?" It is to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly. He desires no reward, for the "reward of a commandment is the commandment itself." Just as the law states we do not eat anything after the Passover sacrifice <note>original: *Afikoman*</note> so its taste remains, so too with the Wise Son—all he does is for the sake of the Heavens.

<column-break/>

Regarding the use of languages and specifically the Aramaic translation <note>original: *Targum*</note>. Consider a king: he speaks freely with his household servants in the common tongue, but with his ministers, he speaks only a little, according to royal protocol. This is so the ministers do not begin to think they are his equals or that he has an excessive fondness for them. However, with simple servants, there is no such concern. Therefore, the ministering angels are familiar with all languages and there is no concern there. But with Aramaic, there is a concern of making the holy "heavy" or too common.

When Israel left Egypt, they went to freedom below and were exalted above. But the freedom from the "Husks" was not yet complete. Below, they still feared the Egyptians who pursued them. Above, the freedom was not finalized until the Giving of the Torah on Shavuot. On Passover, though God "exalted us above every tongue," it was not fully realized until the Revelation. In Egypt, they were "a nation within a nation," mixed with the languages of the gentiles. Only at the Giving of the Torah did the true exaltation occur. Our Sages taught in the tractate Menachot that the purpose of sacrifices is to bring peace to the world. We mentioned the three types of "guarding" corresponding to the secret of the Name. Everything is revealed in the secret of "May His Great Name be Blessed." This was revealed to Israel but hidden from the angels. Thus, the *Kaddish* is said in Aramaic. Moses ascended to God and was a "Servant of the Lord," while Pharaoh was the "Husk" of that service. Moses attained 49 Gates of Understanding. The Exodus happened in an instant because if they had stayed a moment longer, they would have sunk into the 50th Gate of Impurity. This is why we must remember the Exodus every day, for all the holiness we attain today is rooted in that liberation. When the Temple was destroyed, a man brings himself as an offering through the memory of the sacrifice. This is why we say "Remember, O Lord" <note>A prayer for the restoration of the Temple</note>. We have explained the four investigations and the root of everything: that we are Servants of the Lord. The purpose of creation was "to work and to guard." Abraham, the Unpaid Guard, is the Wise Son who keeps the "Charge" for the sake of the Beloved.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic and legal analysis of Passover, focusing on the divine names revealed to Moses and the spiritual definitions of "Rich Matzah" versus "Bread of Affliction." It transitions from the nature of Moses's prophecy to the specific laws of the Seder night.</meta>

# Rich Matzah

The phrase "And I will bring you out" refers to the "clinging" <note>original: *devekut* — a state of spiritual attachment</note> of a servant to the King, as I explained previously. This is the essence of the Midrash <note>Exodus Rabbah, chapters 3 and 15</note> where Moses our Teacher asks, "Who am I?" <note>original: *Mi Anochi*</note>. He wondered if he was the same "I" <note>original: *Anochi*</note> mentioned in the promise to Abraham, or the "I" God spoke of to Jacob, saying, "I will go down with you to Egypt and I will also surely bring you up." 

At the beginning of his prophecy, Moses had not yet reached this high level of vision. Rabbi Joshua the Priest, son of Nehemiah, said that when the Holy One was first revealed to Moses, the prophecy was overwhelming. God thought: "If I reveal myself with a Great Voice, I will terrify him; if I use a low voice, he will undervalue the prophecy." What did He do? He revealed Himself using the voice of Moses’s father <note>Amram</note>. Moses answered, "Here I am; what does my father want?" God replied, "I am not your father, but the God of your father. I came to you with a gentle persuasion so you would not be afraid." 

Later, the Midrash notes that when God said, "The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has sent me," Moses noticed God no longer mentioned his own father. Moses asked, "Master of the Universe, are there sinners in the grave?" <note>Meaning: "Why have You stopped calling Yourself the God of my father?"</note> God replied, "At first, I used persuasion, but from here on, I speak the truth: I am the Chariot <note>The divine vehicle of manifestation</note> with you." 

The essence is that the start of his prophecy was like a "dim mirror" <note>original: *aspaklaria she-eina me'ira* — an indirect vision</note>. Later, he progressed until "Moses ascended to God." By turning his gaze, the name *Elohim* <note>God as Judge/Nature</note> was transformed into *Anochi* <note>The Divine "I"</note>. God spoke in the singular: "I am <note>original: *Anochi*</note> the Lord your God," meaning: even though you are called *Elohim* <note>a title sometimes given to leaders or angels</note>, I am the Lord who is your God. 

This is hinted at in the verse, "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud so the people may hear." Moses entered the "thick darkness" <note>original: *arafel*</note> to reach the Divine. The term "Behold, I" <note>original: *Hineh Anochi*</note> implies closeness, yet it had to be clothed in the "thick cloud" so the common people could grasp it. Similarly, "Behold, I send an angel before you"—one might ask why it doesn't say "Here I am sending" <note>original: *Hineni*</note>. The meaning is that the Blessed One was there in His very essence, but the world saw Him through the "garment" of the angel. 

Israel, however, was not yet ready to see His glory without that angelic clothing. This relates to the secret of the letter *Aleph* in the word "I" (*Anochi*) and the *Aleph* in the word "And He called" <note>original: *Vayikra* — the first word of Leviticus</note>. In the Torah, that *Aleph* is written small because of Moses’s great humility. The text continues, "When a man brings an offering," because the secret of the sacrifice is the secret of service <note>original: *avodah*</note>. The servant of God creates a "pleasing aroma," which I explained earlier as the level of the "ascending souls." In the act of the sacrifice, a person offers up their own spirituality, becoming a "Chariot" for the Divine. By binding his spirituality to God, he is "the man who brings himself" as an offering.

He is the "Image of God," and he elevates his soul and life-force through "clinging" to the heights. This is the meaning of "To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul." The act of sacrifice is called "service" <note>original: *avodah*</note> because it represents the status of a servant. 

Now we shall explain the nature of the future Redemption and compare it to our departure from Egypt. Egypt was not just a physical exile; it was a spiritual displacement. In the future, the "Light" will increase. According to the Zohar, the letters of the Divine Name *Y-H-V-H* represent masculine and feminine energies. The first two letters (*Y-H*) are "masculine" <note>representing the source of flow</note>, while the final letters (*V-H*) are "feminine" <note>representing the reception of that flow</note>. In the future, the mercy will overwhelm the world, and the final letters will be as powerful as the first. This is why our song at the Red Sea was "feminine" <note>original: *shirah*</note>, but the future song will be "masculine" <note>original: *shir*</note>. On that day, "the Lord shall be One and His Name One."

The name of the first woman, Eve <note>original: *Chavah*</note>, should have been *Chayah* <note>"Living"</note>. But because of the sin involving the snake <note>original: *nachash*</note>, the light was hidden. The name *Chavah* relates to the "hidden" aspects of the Divine Name that will only be fully restored in the future.

# Guarded Matzah

Matzah should be praised as the "Bread of Affliction" <note>original: *Lechem Oni*</note> so that it does not ferment or rise. What we eat on the first night of Passover must be "Bread of Affliction" in every sense. On the other days, "Rich Matzah" <note>Matzah made with juice, eggs, or oil instead of just water</note> is permitted, provided it does not rise. 

The reason for this is that when the Israelites were enslaved, the Egyptians did not care if they ate "Rich Matzah." Their only concern was that the slaves didn't die and that the fermentation process didn't cause a "stoppage of work" <note>rising dough takes time and attention</note>. However, because of their status, the poor generally did not eat rich bread. Therefore, on the first night—the actual time of Redemption—we must eat true "affliction bread." Regarding other wheat products, rich matzah is allowed as long as it isn't leavened, and it is still called "Bread of Affliction" by association.

Furthermore, on the first night, it is essentially called "Bread of Affliction" because it is the "bread over which we answer <note>original: *onin* — a pun on *oni* (affliction) and *onah* (to answer/respond)</note> many matters" <note>referring to the telling of the Haggadah</note>. Why isn't it called "Bread of the Poor Person" <note>original: *Lechem Aniyah*</note>? The term *Oni* refers to the specific nature of the bread on this night. Another explanation: what is the way of a poor man? He lights the fire himself. We want to be joined in unity on all seven days, and thus all matzah is called "Bread of Affliction" because it is baked quickly and simply, like a poor man’s bread, without allowing it to rise.

---

## Passage

The sacrifice is increased with the language of the festival and the Passover, to give a reason based on what is explained. We must consider why the Haggadah begins in Aramaic <note>original: *Ha Lachma Anya* — "This is the bread of affliction"</note> but ends with the phrase "In the Land of Israel" in Hebrew? And then it says, "Next year we shall be free men," entirely in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note>. 

We also need to understand why we say "All who are hungry, come and eat." If we are inviting guests, should we not do so before we sit at the table, before we even start the sanctification <note>original: *Kiddush*</note> of the wine?

To explain this: even though Israel entered into holiness on the holiday of Passover, they were not *fully* sanctified until after they counted the days of the Omer <note>the 49 days between Passover and Shavuot</note>. That counting is a process of "whitening" or purification, leading to the spiritual "marriage" of receiving the Torah. The Zohar notes that we do not complete the full Hallel prayer on every day of Passover (unlike on Sukkot) because we have not yet reached the "complete bond" of faith that comes with the Torah. 

On Sukkot, we have already received the Torah and are surrounded by the "Seven Clouds of Glory," so the bond is complete. Regarding the Aramaic translation: Onkelos the Convert reached a level where his soul was drawn from the "translucent shell" <note>original: *Kelipat Nogah* — a spiritual realm containing both good and evil</note> that is closest to holiness. This is why the Aramaic translation <note>Targum</note> is so close to the Holy Tongue. It is said that the Ministering Angels do not attend to the Aramaic language, using only the Holy Tongue; however, Aramaic serves as a bridge for those who are still in the process of being redeemed.

### Tractate Pesachim: Rich Matzah and Guarded Matzah

Questions arise as to why the Exodus from Egypt is considered a "miracle of miracles" beyond all time, given that we are commanded by the Torah to remember the Exodus every single day. We answer that in the days of Haman <note>The villain of the Purim story</note>, the Israelites had already received the Torah, so "overturning the natural order" <note>original: *shidud hama'arekhet* — refers to God breaking the laws of nature/astrology</note> was not as revolutionary as it was during the Exodus from Egypt, when they had not yet received the Torah. Regarding this, the Scripture informs us that it is not merely a possibility, but that the Exodus could even be greater than any other overturning of the natural order. This is the meaning of "And I will redeem you" <note>Exodus 6:6</note>; the song of redemption was performed with an "outstretched arm," and the judgments against their gods were immense. "And I will take you to Me as a people, and I will be your God," for through the power of publicizing these miracles through Israel and the commandment to tell the story of the Exodus, they bring about the descent of the Lord's power, as will be explained later in the clarification of the blessing of the story.

To this, the answer is given: "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt" <note>A central line from the Passover Haggadah</note>—we were bound by a "bow and sword" <note>astrological or spiritual fate</note> from the side of the natural order, and no slave could ever escape. Yet, "the Lord took us out from there." This is "And I took you out," using the power that guides one on the straight path. It was through His strength—for the sake of the "blood on the threshold" <note>The blood of the Paschal lamb on the doorposts</note>—that the natural order was overturned. 

The *Zohar* <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> explains this at length, as does the author of *Tzeror HaMor* <note>Abraham Saba, 15th-century commentator</note> in the portion of *Bo*. They explain that Israel was almost lost within the "Husks" <note>term: *Klipah* — spiritual shells or impurities that conceal divine light</note>. They had entered the "Forty-Nine Gates of Impurity," which is the secret of leaven <note>term: *Chametz* — symbolizes the ego and fermentation of sin</note>. Had they stayed a moment longer, God forbid, they would have been lost. This is why He "pulled you out from the skins" of the Egyptian labor. Their dough did not have time to rise <note>leaven</note>, and they were redeemed through the secret of the "Three Gates of Understanding" <note>original: *Binah*</note>. 

The difference between Matzah <note>unleavened bread</note> and Chametz <note>leavened bread</note> is only a single point <note>note: This refers to the Hebrew letters He (ה) for Matzah and Chet (ח) for Chametz, which differ only by a tiny gap in the letter's leg</note>. This is why the Haggadah says, "Had the Holy One not taken us out..." This provides the answer to the question asked on this night: "Why is it all Matzah?" Even if "we were all wise" <note>another line from the Haggadah</note>, it means that even if such a miracle happened *after* the giving of the Torah, it would not have been as great. This also answers why we eat bitter herbs <note>original: *Maror*</note> on this night. It commemorates "And they made their lives bitter," and it suggests that without the Exodus, the world would have remained sunken in the Husks. If the Exodus had not occurred, the current exile and the future redemption would not be possible. Consider this well.

In truth, the miracle in Egypt was very great. "As they afflicted them, so they multiplied." Therefore, the eating of bitter herbs relates to sin <note>note: potentially referring to the "sin" of the Egyptians or the refinement of Israel</note>. All the commandments are "For we were slaves to the Lord." The Sages taught: do not read it as "because they found," but as a hint that through the Passover Seder—leaven, Matzah, and the whole order—redemption is encoded.

The "Burning Hearth" <note>original: *Mokedah*</note>, as mentioned in the teachings of the greats I cited above: Rabbi Yohanan said four things were shown to him—Gehenna <note>term: *Gehenna* — a place of spiritual purification/purgatory</note>, the Torah, the Sacrifices, and the Kingdoms <note>the four exiles</note>. The Holy One showed Abraham our father the Torah and Gehenna. The "Law of the Burnt Offering" refers to the Torah and the sacrifices rising above the four exiles. The "Burning Hearth" is Gehenna. The letter *Vav* in "Torah" appears in the Law of the Burnt Offering, the Meal Offering, and the Sin Offering. In the afternoon prayer <note>Mincha</note>, which Isaac established (as he was a "burnt offering"), it corresponds to the divine name. In the future, the last name shall be as the first <note>note: a Kabbalistic reference to the unification of the name Y-H-V-H</note>. This is the matter of the "Beloved descending to his garden." Our ancestors, by performing these words, established the ethics of the Exodus. It says "The voice of my beloved," but in the future, "His beloved" or "The son of his beloved" <note>referring to the Messiah, son of David</note> will redeem us.

Egypt occurred for the sake of Israel, so that they would not be enslaved. Therefore, when God changed His manner toward him <note>Pharaoh</note>, He gave him his "signs" where there were no Israelites. This means a revealed leadership that exempts Israel from the natural order. The beginning of the salvation comes from "The end is wedded to the beginning." "The King of Egypt died"—this refers to the Ministering Angel <note>term: *Sar* — the spiritual patron or guardian angel of a nation</note> of Egypt who was appointed over the depths of Gehenna. His death/fall happened because there were no Israelites there to be subject to his rule. 

Why were they saved? It says, "The Children of Israel groaned because of the labor." This means they had "groans of labor" in the revealed exile. Then it is written: "God heard their moaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob." 

It is difficult to understand why the word "with" <note>Hebrew: *et*</note> is repeated between each name. In the Book of Kings, it says, "For the sake of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob" without the repetitions. The reason is that here, it was necessary to clarify the different exiles to exempt them from their rule. This happens in three distinct places. 
1. Abraham: Clarifying the exiles. 
2. Isaac: Even though he did not "see the star," he saw the destiny; the proof is that the 400 years began from Isaac's birth. 
3. Jacob: Much later, he entered the chain of exile. 

This is the secret of why Joseph sent his father "old wine" <note>from a Midrash</note>, which puts the minds of the elderly at ease. The *Zohar* explains elsewhere that "Wine" indicates the strength of Judgment <note>original: *Din*</note>, while "Oil" indicates Mercy. Joseph hinted to his father not to be grieved by the descent into the Egyptian exile, for "old wine is with us"—the leadership of the elders, Abraham and Isaac. 

Abraham was the "chain" who chose the service of the Holy One. God made a covenant with him regarding the "Land" and the "Servant" (Eliezer). Abraham is the secret of the "Blessing." It is written of Abraham, "And he kept My charge," which is the secret of Matzah. Abraham was careful with the commandments, so much so that even Lot learned from him. The "Sayings" are the foundations of the commandments dependent on the Exodus: the Passover lamb, Matzah, and Bitter Herbs. 

- **Abraham** corresponds to "Guarded Matzah" <note>Matzah watched from the time of harvest</note>. 
- **Isaac** corresponds to the "Two kids of goats"—one for the Passover sacrifice and one for the Festival sacrifice, eaten to fulfillment. 
- **Jacob** is the one of whom it was said, "I had no repose, no quiet, no rest, but trouble came" <note>Job 3:26</note>. Everything ended for his good, and his "bed was complete" <note>meaning all his children were righteous</note>. Therefore, the bitter herb is called "sin" <note>note: or related to the struggle of Jacob/Esau</note>.

The "Four Cups" of wine also correspond:
1. **The First Cup:** "Who has chosen us from all nations." Just as Abraham was chosen from the nations and "converted the men," so too the women were converted by Rebecca.
2. **The Second Cup (The Haggadah):** It begins with "shame" <note>our idol-worshiping ancestors</note> and ends with "praise." So too, it began with the shame of Esau and ended with the praise of Jacob.
3. **The Third Cup (Grace After Meals):** Linked to **Rachel**, because Joseph provided for all the house of Israel, and she was the "mainstay of the home." As it says in the Talmud: "Blessing is only found in a man's house because of his wife."
4. **The Fourth Cup (Song/Hallel):** Linked to **Leah**. Rabbi Judah says "The Song of Praise," while Rabbi Yohanan says "The Soul of Every Living Being." From Leah came the "pleasantness and song" of Moses our Teacher.

Finally, the **Afikoman** <note>The final piece of matzah eaten at the Seder</note> is the "Guarded Matzah," the secret of the "Saying." Unlike the dough of the gentiles, which a person fills his belly with, one must eat a "kazaits" <note>term: *kazait* — an olive-sized portion</note> of Matzah at the end. Pharaoh's servants represent the "Husks," while we are "Servants of the Lord." Even though the author of *Zevach Pesach* <note>Isaac Abarbanel</note> says on "This is the bread of affliction" that the Egyptians fed them "affliction" <note>poor bread</note> to fill their bellies cheaply, we eat the Matzah at the end for the sake of the commandment. The bitter herb is transformed, fulfilling "They shall eat it with matzah and bitter herbs." 

# Let us Return
Let us return to the section and the sayings by way of hint. "The Law of the Burnt Offering" <note>Leviticus 6:2</note> refers to Abraham choosing Gehenna <note>to save his children from exile</note>. In the portion of *Lech Lecha* in the Midrash, it says God showed Abraham the exiles, the giving of the Torah, and the Temple sacrifices. The "Burnt Offering" <note>original: *Olah*</note> symbolizes the kingdoms rising over the world. However, the sacrifices are the Judgment. Our interpretations of the "Law of the Guilt Offering" and the "Burnt Offering" show they are entirely for the Lord. The "Meal Offering" is Matzah. Just as there is no Burnt Offering without a Meal Offering, the divine name will be complete in the future. This was revealed when Israel left Egypt with a "New Song." It is written: "The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes leaping over the mountains." The "mountains" and "hills" refer to the Patriarchs and Matriarchs, who are hinted at in all the commandments.

### Tractate Pesachim

### Guarded Matzah
<term>Guarded Matzah<note>original: *Matzah Shmurah* — Matzah that has been watched from the moment of harvest to ensure no fermentation occurs, symbolizing extra care in performing a commandment.</note></term>
They were exalted above every tongue, meaning they entered into the <term>Secret of the Holy Tongue<note>original: *Sod Leshon HaKodesh* — In Kabbalah, Hebrew is considered the primordial language of creation; "entering its secret" means achieving a high level of spiritual clarity.</note></term>. This is what is written in the <term>Mekhilta<note>An ancient Midrashic commentary on Exodus.</note></term>: "'Thus shall you say to them' means in the Holy Tongue." At that moment, "freedom was on the tablets" <note>A famous wordplay on Exodus 32:16; the word *charut* (engraved) is read as *cherut* (freedom).</note>. It was absolute freedom; anyone who engages in the Torah is called a "freeman." Even though they had now entered into holiness, they were, metaphorically speaking, "servants of the Lord" and no longer "servants of Pharaoh." They were like a <term>Canaanite slave<note>In Jewish law, a Canaanite slave who undergoes a partial conversion enters the covenant but is not yet a fully free Israelite.</note></term> who has entered the covenant but is not yet emancipated. However, when they received the Torah, they entered into the "Secret of Freedom." The core of the Torah is in the Land of Israel, for there the Holy Tongue exists in its essence, in the Holy Land.

Afterwards, when they sinned and were exiled, they were driven away from the Holy Tongue. Nevertheless, they were not rejected entirely; they only descended to Babylon into the <term>Secret of the Translation<note>original: *Sod HaTargum* — Refers to Aramaic, the "translation" language of the Babylonian exile, which is seen as a lower spiritual shell protecting the holy Hebrew core.</note></term>. During the Egyptian exile, they had not even reached the level of the "Secret of the Translation." Thus, when they sinned and were exiled later, they descended from the levels of the Translation. This is the meaning of: "Even though we have been exiled, the yoke of the Torah remains upon them." That which was attained through the Torah was not entirely lost. This is why in Babylon, the <term>Talmud<note>The Babylonian Talmud is written primarily in Aramaic.</note></term> flourished in the language of the Translation (Aramaic). 

Maimonides wrote regarding the version of the <term>Haggadah<note>The text recited at the Passover Seder.</note></term> that during the time of the Holy Temple, they did not say the paragraph "This is the bread [of affliction]" <note>original: *Ha Lachma Anya* — An Aramaic invitation to the Seder.</note>. It was only when they were exiled and the matter of "gathering the driven" returned that they began to say it. It means: "not at the time of the Lord," but rather for those who are "numbered" for the Passover sacrifice. But now it is changed; whoever wants may come. As for the statement "Anyone who is in need, let him come and perform the Passover," this means that even the <term>Afikoman<note>The piece of Matzah eaten at the end of the meal to represent the Passover sacrifice.</note></term>, which takes the place of the Passover lamb, does not strictly require being "numbered" for it beforehand, prior to the baking. 

Afterward, when it became a "remembrance of the Land of Israel," it was said in the Holy Tongue: "Next year [in Jerusalem]." For the Land of Israel is the place of the Holy Tongue, even though it was said "In the Land of Israel" in the language of the Translation <note>Aramaic</note>. This was accepted because of the years they spent in Babylon. Even when they returned to the Land of Israel, it was not entirely the "Holy Tongue" because they did not return to their original state of repair, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "The word 'And I shall be honored' <note>Haggai 1:8</note> is missing the letter *He*," implying five things were missing in the Second Temple. Afterward, this section was added regarding "Next year, may we be free men," referring to the Temple that is destined to be, where we will be completely emancipated and not merely "entering the covenant." The entire discourse was spoken in the Holy Tongue, for its atmosphere is one with the Holy Tongue.

### Paragraph
The wise son asked: Why do we not mention the "Ten Plagues" and similar things in the answer of "We were slaves"? For that answer lists other matters and not a direct response to his question. Furthermore, "If the Lord had not taken out [our ancestors]..."—what freedom do the people of the exile have now, simply because they were redeemed once? Are we and our children not still [enslaved]? Why would it have been impossible to take us out if He hadn't taken out our ancestors? 

Here he answers: the "Wise One" is the Master of the Deeds of the Lord. It seems to me that in the chapter [of the Haggadah] "We were slaves," he tells the reasons for the Four Questions of "What is different." It is not a case of a separate questioner and responder; rather, the Sage who compiled the Haggadah arranged the questions themselves, and he is the one who asks and the one who answers. And these refer to the Four Expressions of Redemption: "And I will bring out," "And I will save," "And I will redeem," and "And I will take."

For the lot was cast and overturned and completed. If they had been sold as slaves and handmaids, it would have been [permanent] for them, God forbid. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, descended to overturn it. This was not the case here, where only Israel was saved while Egypt remained. And there is...
