# Tractate Pesachim — Guarded Matzah
<meta>catchword: By the Hand</meta>

And [sin] caused death; thus the Torah was made physical so that it could be performed, and so that the physical commandments could be observed. Nevertheless, "He who opens the gold..." and so you will find in the Torah hints and allusions, just as the masters of secret meanings gave a sign for the parts of the Torah: **Pardes** <note>original: "PRD"S" — an acronym for the four levels of Torah interpretation</note>. The initials stand for **Plain** meaning, **Allusion**, **Inquiry**, and **Secret**. **Secret** <note>Hebrew: *Sod*</note> is the "Hidden Light" that is now concealed from us because of the removal of the "Garments of Light" <note>A mystical concept where Adam and Eve originally wore light, which became skin after the Fall</note>. This is the essence of the **Holy Language**. The **Allusion** <note>Hebrew: *Remez*</note> refers to the performance of the physical commandments. Since the letter *Mem* is the same as the "shaking" <note>unclear wordplay in original Hebrew</note>, and the secret of the "70 facets" of the Torah which were written... and there is nothing that is not hinted at in the Torah with great clarity, except that our intellect has been darkened from what it was meant to be. If it were not for this, "the earth would be full of the knowledge of the Lord." 

Instead, there is only the "Oral Torah," and the Written Torah cannot be understood except after great toil. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "The words of Torah only endure in one who kills himself over it," <note>Talmud, Berakhot 63b</note> as it is said: *This is the Torah regarding a man who dies in a tent* <note>Numbers 19:14</note>. For this reason, the Written Torah requires explanation and commentary—namely, the **Talmud**. We see this clearly generation after generation: the ancients, who possessed a lucid intellect, understood deep matters without commentary. Later, they could not understand without a commentary; and later still, they needed a commentary upon the commentary. Everything is according to the darkness of the intellect. 

Therefore, had Adam not sinned and had his intellect remained clear, he would have understood the Written Torah, and through that understanding, he would have known everything. He would not have needed an Oral Torah. It was only because he sinned and removed the Light, bringing death to the world, that toil and weariness were required. The Oral Torah had to be written down, and thus it is said: *He has placed me in dark places, like those long dead* <note>Lamentations 3:6</note>—this refers to the **Babylonian Talmud** <note>The author uses a classic play on words: "Bavel" (Babylon) sounding like "Bilbel" (Confusion) or "Balah" (Darkness)</note>, meaning that the darkness and death brought to the world caused its existence. If the "Hidden Light" were still present, as it will be in the future, then "the Torah is light" and it would gladden the heart without darkness and without needing to "kill oneself over it."

Regarding the "two lights," it is written in the book *Voice of the Doves* <note>original: "Kol Bomim" - likely *Kol HaTor* or similar mystical text</note> that the word "Lights" <note>Hebrew: *Me'orot*</note> contains the letters for **Light** <note>Or</note> and **Death** <note>Mot</note>. This is the meaning of "He placed me in dark places like those long dead." The seven names derived from "Lights" and the letters of "Light" from "Lights" are darkness and not light. It is also fitting that "the Torah is light"—one Torah. Yet He made two Torahs (Written and Oral). This relates to the law that "words written down may not be recited by heart, and words given orally may not be written down." 

The matter is explained in the chapter "The Builder" <note>Talmud, Shabbat 104a</note> regarding those excellent words taught by the school children about the alphabet. They said: "Make signs [for the Torah]." Rashi explains this as creating an order for the traditions so that they are not forgotten. The Oral Torah is "longer than the earth and broader than the sea," and who could remember all the vast depths hinted at within it? If the Written Torah were built upon its full clarity, one would remember everything through "signs." But we may not recite the Written Torah by heart when it contains "missing" or "extra" letters, and the Oral Torah should not be written because the essence is to remember it all. Because of our sins, we have been darkened since the destruction of the Temple, and the darkness increased until they were forced to write down the Babylonian Talmud. This is the secret of the "Hidden Light" in the fifth level...

...and from this, with great difficulty, each person according to their level—especially one who "kills himself over it." A great hint is mentioned regarding **Moses our Teacher**. *The Lord saw that he turned aside to see* <note>Exodus 3:4</note>. Moses saw with clarity; he is the secret of the "radiant mirror" because "the skin of his face shone." Moses' face was like the sun, which is "Torah is Light." When God gave him the Written Torah, there was no darkness before him; he had a clear intellect full of knowledge and understood the Oral Torah on his own. 

This is the secret of "Turning Aside." "Turned aside" <note>Hebrew: *Sar*</note> is an acronym for **Plain**, **Allusion**, and **Secret**. This is the meaning of the Midrash: "He gave to Moses... like a bride (*k'kallato*)." God gave him "general principles" (*klalim*), and he understood the Oral Torah on his own, as I have elaborated elsewhere regarding the "Cushite woman he married." And in Midrash Rabbah at the end of the portion *Ki Tissa*: "Write for yourself..." The angels were saying before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Are You giving Israel the ability to write whatever they want?" He replied: "I have given you the Torah; I am the one who wrote it." Even Moses' "beautiful labor" was trusted, as it says: *Not so my servant Moses; he is trusted in all My house.* Thus, it is called the **Torah of Moses** because Moses understood it from his own intellect and achieved the entire Oral Torah; therefore, it is named after him. And this is the meaning of *This is the Torah: a man who dies in a tent...*

Healing. Rashi and all the commentators sensed this and wrote what they wrote. It is according to what the **Zohar** says on the verse *Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed* <note>Jeremiah 17:14</note>. Since it says "Heal me, O Lord," why must it add "and I shall be healed"? Because all the healings in the world are from the Holy One, Blessed be He, but some are delivered through a **messenger** <note>gloss: namely, the Angel Raphael</note>, and some are not handed over to a messenger. Those handed over to a messenger are healings, but the illness may return. But those whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, heals Himself never return to their illness. Therefore, His healing is a healing that has no sickness in it at all. On this basis, the verse says: *I will build you again, and you shall be built* <note>Jeremiah 31:4</note>. Solomon built the First Temple and it was destroyed; Ezra built the Second Temple and it was destroyed. *Unless the Lord builds the house, its builders toil in vain.* But the building of God will be established forever. Thus it says, "I will build you [Myself] and you shall be [permanently] built." This also explains the verse: *All the sickness that I placed upon Egypt, I will not place upon you, for I am the Lord your Healer.* That is to say: if healing came through a messenger, the sickness might return. But since **I am the Lord your Healer**, I will not place it upon you again after the healing, for it is I, the Lord, and not a messenger.

## With a Strong Hand

It is difficult to understand: why are **Pestilence** and **Blood** considered more significant than the other plagues? Furthermore, what connection is there here to the destruction of Jerusalem... "blood and fire and pillars of smoke" in the future? It seems this comes to show an additional blow within these plagues that was not previously known. For **Pestilence** was in their cattle, yet here it implies that even the people who were mixed among them were struck by the pestilence. And "With an Outstretched Arm"—this refers to the **Sword**. Specifically, it comes to teach about the Midrash which says the plagues of Egypt were directed at their firstborns—that the blow to the "great ones" of Egypt was greater than the blow to the firstborns. For when the firstborns heard Moses' warning about midnight, they went to their fathers to demand they send Israel away, and the fathers refused; then the firstborns themselves were killed by the sword.

## And with Great Terror

This refers to the **Revelation of the Divine Presence**. The meaning is that the Power, Glory, and Terror were in the hands of the "Attribute of Justice," which was also prosecuting Israel, saying: "These [Egyptians] are idolaters and these [Israelites] are idolaters; these grow long hair <note>a sign of pagan practice</note> and these..." And it says: *Which the Lord did... before your eyes.* This means "not literally," as if one should not look behind them, for it is enough that you are saved and you are not worthy of seeing the others punished. But here, it was "before your eyes." And "With Signs"—this refers to the **Staff**, meaning the signs performed with the staff itself.

<column-break/>

They say... for the honor of the King, as is the custom for the "Gold Opener"... and so you find in the Torah "Hint" and "Allusion," as the masters of secret meanings gave a sign for the parts of the soul: 
**"May their souls be bound in the bond of life"**
with the souls of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, by the counsel of God. But He, may He be blessed, feels the distress Himself, as it is said, "And the Lord heard." Afterward, He added an awakening of mercy through the merit of the Patriarchs: "And He remembered His covenant with Abraham..." Afterward, "And He saw"—God added further providence from the "lower side," for He did not create the world for chaos. The expression "He knew" refers to the labor—this means **The Children**, to minimize their numbers. This was against the firstborns. "Oppression"—this refers to the **Pressure** to force them out of their faith, so they would speak like the Egyptians. Also, the pressure of neglecting their studies. As our Sages said: "Legal traditions require prayer."

"Not by an angel..." One may ask: is it not written, "And He did not allow the **Destroyer** to enter your houses"? This implies there *was* a destroying angel. The commentators wrote what they wrote, and I have written elsewhere that this is not a difficulty at all. The matter follows what our Sages said on the verse "The Lord will punish the host of heaven on high": **A nation does not fall until its Prince (patron angel) falls first.** When a Prince falls above, and one Prince is replaced by another, this causes the change in the nations below. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, subdued the Prince of Egypt above, tens of thousands of ministering angels below were subdued. But the Prince of Egypt could not be overcome by anyone else because he was the "Firstborn Prince," the first prince of Babylon. He would not have fallen unless the Holy One, Blessed be He, struck him down Himself. When God struck him down, his ministers below were subdued. 

Thus we can understand: "Had the Holy One, Blessed be He, not taken our ancestors out, then we..." This means that God Himself had to take them out to topple the Prince of Egypt, for otherwise, it would have been impossible for him to fall. Though I have explained this in another way, both are the "words of the Living God." It shows from the Secret (*Sod*) that Israel needed that time... even the Egyptian woman... they were in the furnace...

# Tractate Pesachim 164 — Guarded Matzah

"A goodness hidden in My treasure house I have for you; go and inform them." <note>A midrashic reference to the Shabbat as a hidden gift from God's treasury.</note> If the purpose was to sanctify us with the holiness of Shabbat, to remove the filth of the "serpent’s venom" <note>Hebrew: *zohamat hanachash* — the spiritual impurity introduced to humanity after the sin of Adam and Eve</note> which comes from the side of the mundane—then why did He bring us to Mount Sinai? For our Sages of blessed memory said: "When Israel stood at Mount Sinai, their filth ceased." And if the purpose was to increase our spiritual perception, why did He give us the Torah "face to face" <note>Deuteronomy 5:4</note> and not through the mediation of Moses alone? And if it was for the sake of "your eyes shall see your teacher" <note>Isaiah 30:20</note>—as Rav said: "The reason I am sharper than my colleagues is that I saw Rabbi Meir from behind; had I seen him from the front, I would be even wiser"—if so, why do we need the "air of the Land of Israel" which "makes one wise"? <note>Talmud, Bava Batra 158b</note> Rather, this indicates an even greater attachment, for the Land of Israel below corresponds to the Land of Israel above. Therefore, it is called *Da'at*, for from there the drop of union is drawn. Furthermore, this entire generation is the generation of Moses, as is known, and Moses is from the aspect of *Da'at*. This entire generation [in Egypt] was meant only to refine their souls, and therefore they entered into that servitude...

It is known that the Name Y-H-V-H is above nature, and so the perfect Torah is above nature. With this, we explain why the entire Torah is "sealed" with the Exodus from Egypt. Not because of Egypt itself, but because of this Torah that was known and revealed in Egypt—namely the Name Y-H-V-H which is eternal. If Man had not been corrupted, the Name would have been known to him and he would have received the Torah without the need for refining and reincarnations in the Iron Furnace. It is as if one said: "The Torah is suspended upon the Name Y-H-V-H." But according to my path, it is well-settled: "I am Y-H-V-H," and upon this Name the Torah is suspended, and we were refined to cleave to Y-H-V-H through the Exodus. # Tractate Pesachim

## Guarded Matzah

**This is** the reason Rabbi Yehuda used to give mnemonic signs <note>original: "Simanim" — Rabbi Yehuda grouped the ten plagues into three acronyms: Detzach, Adash, Beachab.</note> using plural language, hinting at the high mysteries of the Ten Sefirot <note>The ten creative attributes or "emanations" in Kabbalah through which God interacts with the universe.</note> and subsequently the ten celestial spheres. Rabbi Yossi the Galilean says... Rabbi Eliezer says... Rabbi Akiva says... <note>These are the standard opinions in the Haggadah regarding how many plagues struck the Egyptians at the Red Sea compared to the ten in Egypt.</note> One must ask: granted, Rabbi Yossi speaks well when he says every "finger" is comprised of ten, making the "hand" fifty; but what is the reasoning of the others?

In the book *Kol Bochim* <note>A 17th-century commentary, likely by Rabbi Yoel Sirkis, on the Book of Lamentations and the Haggadah.</note>, it is written that there is a hint in the verse: "Send, I pray Thee, by the hand of him whom Thou wilt send" <note>Exodus 4:13. Moses' plea to God to send someone else.</note>. He asked that God send "Na" (51) by the "Hand" (14) so they might be saved. Those letters also form the Name *Adonai* <note>The divine name associated with Lordship and the physical world.</note>. The punishment of Egypt is hinted at in the verse: "And also that nation whom they shall serve, I will judge" <note>Genesis 15:14. The Hebrew word for "judge" is *Dan* (דן).</note>. This "Dan" refers to the power of the ten plagues. The first plague, Blood, corresponds to the letter *Yod* (10), and the final plague, the Death of the Firstborn, corresponds to the letter *Nun* <note>The letter Nun has a numerical value of 50, often representing the "Fifty Gates of Understanding" or, here, the ultimate weight of the final plague.</note>.

Rabbi Eliezer expounds that "Send now by the hand" refers to the beginning of the "Hand," meaning ten plagues, each of which was fourfold. This is why it says "I will judge (Dan) Egypt," and the word *Dan* consists of the letters *Dalet* (4) and *Nun* (50)—suggesting four times fifty. Rabbi Akiva, however, expounds that there were five aspects to each plague, which is why he reckons the plagues at the sea as 250. This is all alluded to in the "judgment" (Dan) mentioned to Abraham.

**How many** levels of [goodness]... We must explain this, as many find it difficult: why does the Haggadah say "How much more so is the goodness doubled and redoubled"? Why not just "doubled"? If we say "redoubled," it implies the second level is also multiplied. If so, the numerical values and the logic would go up to fifteen. They ask: if God had only done one and not the other, why would it be "enough" (*Dayenu*)? For example, if He had not given us their wealth, but God had already promised Abraham "they shall come out with great substance." Or if He had not split the sea, they would have drowned—how could that be "enough"? Or if He had not given the Torah, God forbid!

The general principle is this: in the first goodness, the second goodness was already included potentially. Nevertheless, God returned and gave the second goodness as a distinct act of grace. Thus, each stage is a complete gift on its own.

<column-break/>

## Enriched Matzah

**The attainment** of secrets: you will find a hint that the words "bread" (*lechem*) and "wise" (*chacham*) are related in their essence. This explains the verse: "And when your son asks you tomorrow, saying: What is this?" <note>Exodus 13:14</note>. Rashi explains this refers to the "Stupid Son" <note>Commonly referred to as the Simple Son (*Tam*).</note>. Elsewhere it says: "What are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances..." <note>Deuteronomy 6:20</note>. This is the question of the "Wise Son." Both use similar language. Just as it says "when your son asks you" in the first instance, it says the same in the portion of *Va'etchanan*. It is visible to all that by rearranging the letters, "their bread" (*lachmam*) becomes "to the wise one" (*lachacham*).

Now I will explain the literal meaning of the passage: "What does the wise son say?" One might ask: the verse in *Va'etchanan* refers to the whole Torah, not just Passover! So why does the Haggadah apply it here? The answer is that the "Wise Son" is sharp-witted; he takes the general language of the Torah and applies its dialectics specifically to the laws of Passover. He asks about "statutes" (*chukim*) and "ordinances" (*mishpatim*). "Testimonies" (*edot*) are mitzvot that serve as reminders of historical events, like Maror (bitter herbs) reminding us of the bitterness of slavery. But a "statute" (*chuk*) implies a law without a revealed reason. If you say the "Statute of the Passover" means it is hidden from the world and only for Israel, this contradicts it being called an "ordinance" (*mishpat*), which implies a logical, civil law. The Wise Son is asking: is Passover a supra-rational decree or a logical law?

The answer we give him is: "One does not conclude the Passover meal with an *Afikoman*." <note>A law stating that the taste of the matzah must remain in one's mouth, and no dessert is eaten after it.</note> In the Talmud (Tractate Pesachim), there is an opinion that this means one should not move from group to group. This is the answer to his inquiry. Even though the verse in *Va'etchanan* refers to the whole Torah, the Torah itself anchors everything in the Exodus from Egypt. We tell him: "We were slaves to Pharaoh... and the Lord brought us out."

This addresses a great investigation: why is the foundation of the entire Torah based on the Exodus? Why are so many commandments tied to it? Was the Torah, which is eternal and preceded the world, dependent on us being slaves in Egypt? The answer is that everything depends on the Name *Havayah* (Y-H-V-H), the Essential Name—He who was, is, and will be. God, the Torah, and Israel are one. The Torah is entirely composed of His Names, which emanate from the Name *Havayah*. The Torah has 600,000 letters, corresponding to the 600,000 souls of Israel <note>A central kabbalistic concept: "Israel" (ישראל) is an acronym for *Yesh Shishim Ribo Otiot LaTorah* — There are sixty myriad letters in the Torah.</note>, all of whom are attached to the holiness of the Name. This was not fully revealed even to the Patriarchs, but only to Moses, through the "Strong Hand" and signs which are above nature. For the Name *Havayah* is greater than the name *Elohim* (God), as *Elohim* represents the hidden power within nature (having the same numerical value as *Hateva*, "Nature").

**After** speaking of the Name of Lordship (*Adonut*) and the uplifting of hands, we recall what is said in Tractate Eruvin: Rabbi Jeremiah said that since the Temple was destroyed, it is enough (*Dayo*) for the world to use only two letters of the Name, as it says: "Let every soul praise *Yah*" <note>Psalm 150. *Yah* (Y-H) consists of the first two letters of the four-letter Name.</note>. Therefore, the Haggadah mentions fifteen levels of praise, corresponding to the Name *Yah* (numerical value 15). These are called "Levels" (*Ma'alot*) after the fifteen "Songs of Ascents" that King David sang. Even in exile, we must give praise for the beginning of the redemption.

---

Here is the explanation of "When He brought us out of Egypt": It says the Egyptians asked, "What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?" Despite this, God executed judgments upon them and their gods. When judgments are executed on the "gods" (celestial powers) of a nation, their earthly power is weakened. Then He slew their firstborn, who represent the strength of their "chariot." Then Israel, God's "firstborn," took the inheritance. He gave us their wealth—great substance. Then He split the sea. Note that the splitting of the sea was not strictly necessary for escape—they could have fled elsewhere—but it was done to give them the "Spoils of the Sea," which were even greater than the spoils of Egypt. He led us through on dry land, where they found precious stones and pearls. Finally, He drowned our oppressors, and their horses and chariots washed up, providing even more spoils. All of this wealth was to provide for their needs in the desert so they wouldn't need to seek supplies from elsewhere.

And if it was to show us extra affection through His specific providence, why was it necessary? It was to give us a taste of the World to Come. As it says in Tractate Chagigah, the place where the heavens "grind manna for the righteous" is a preparation for the future. This is also why He gave us the Shabbat, which is called a "good gift."

### Manuscript
The cause of darkness brings about a greater light than what existed before. This verse is like the verse regarding the "superiority of grapes"—when grapes are mixed and the heavens are not recognized except by the wise. When they are crushed and become "guarded," afterward the wine remains "guarded," meaning removed from its dregs.

> <gloss>The matter of the "Guarded" ones is the secret of all the selection that was given to Man to choose good or evil, and in the future, the chosen good will be pure, just as everything was selected for the purely good world, and its guarding is most significant.</gloss>

And this is more than it was before the sin. This is the matter of the World to Come: "Wine preserved in its grapes" <note>A Talmudic metaphor for the spiritual rewards hidden since the creation of the world</note>. As our Sages said: "No eye has seen, O God, beside You" (Isaiah 64:3)—this is the preserved wine. The matter is that the light will be strengthened and hidden. It became "Garments of Skin" <note>original: 'Or, spelled with an Ayin</note> which turned from "Garments of Light" <note>original: Or, spelled with an Aleph</note>. This is the secret of the large letter *Ayin* in "Hear O Israel" (*Shema*) and the large *Aleph* in "Man" (*Adam*). *Adam* is the tithe of *Emet* (Truth). The world was created with Truth: "In the beginning God created" <note>The final letters of the first three words of the Bible—Bereshit Bara Elohim—spell Emet (Truth)</note>. The Serpent, who caused the sin, crumbled the *Aleph*, the first letter, and there remained "Dead" (*Met*). Likewise, the *Aleph* from *Adam* was removed, and there remained "Blood" (*Dam*). Then the *Aleph* of the "Garment of Light" was removed and became "Skin" (*'Or*). Therefore, the *Aleph* of "And He called" (*Vayikra*) is written small <note>In Leviticus 1:1, the Aleph is traditionally written smaller than other letters</note>, leaving the word "Incident" (*Vayikar*), a term for accidental impurity (*Keri*). This refers to Lilith, who bore from Adam during those 130 years and brought filth into the world. It says "When a man (*Adam*) brings an offering" because he is not currently close; he must bring an offering. I have elaborated elsewhere on the portions of the Priestly Code (*Torat Kohanim*) that revolve around this matter. All filth is drawn from this: "When a man has a mark on the skin of his flesh," because of the "Garments of Skin" and flesh created by the sin of the first Man. Only his stature remained. This continued until Jacob came, whose beauty was a reflection of the beauty of Adam. From him emerged seventy holy souls to rectify this. His time is for the World to Come in the secret of "Man, Generation, and Builders." Solomon was a son of that generation; the light of the moon was in its fullness. See the Midrash Rabbah on the verse "This month shall be for you." In the future, with the coming of the Messiah, it is written: "Arise, shine, for your light has come." The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, like the light of the seven days of creation—the hidden light that Adam used. That which was "No eye has seen" will turn into "The eye sees God." All this comes from the power of nullifying the dregs (the husks). "Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet" <note>Samson’s riddle, used here to mean that holiness is extracted from the impure</note>; intentional sins turn into merits. At that time, it will be said of Jacob and Israel: "How great are their tents," for Israel will be within the inner partition, closer than the Ministering Angels. We have already prefaced that Jacob is the beauty of Adam. Solomon's staff, with seventy souls... the marrow of a man after seventy years becomes a serpent... but it is written: "For there is no enchantment (*Nachash*—also means serpent) in Jacob." It is written: "Behold, the inheritance of the Lord is sons, the reward is the fruit of the womb." The "Womb" (*Beten*) is the side of the Serpent that "walks on its belly" (*Gachon*) due to the fruit of the Tree of Knowledge which caused evil, but—

And not any clothing, as it is during the time of wrath, when His holiness is clothed through the chain of emanations within the husks. He "did not look at iniquity nor see toil." In the nullification of the Passover, with haste, from the power of Israel to the House of Israel, He passed over the house of the Egyptian through the partitions to the house of Israel. So He did regarding the merits and debts of a person: to skip from merit to merit and pass from one wakefulness to another, so that the merits become a thick cord that ties the soul of man above—a "thread of kindness"—until it is bound above, and behold, he is an offering to the Lord. I received these main points from the notebooks of the Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foundational 16th-century Kabbalist</note>, and I have added further insights.

# Tractate Pesachim: Rich Matzah and Guarded Matzah

He is, as it were, to Him in the aspect of Soul, Body, and Clothing. Man was made in the "image and likeness" <note>Genesis 1:26</note> through his soul, body, and clothing. You will find that the secret of the three types of ritual impurity emerges from these three: impurity from a corpse <note>original: טומאת מת</note> comes from the soul's attachment to the body; impurity of the leper, the man with a discharge, and the woman with a discharge <note>original: טומאת מצורע זב וזבה</note> comes from the waste products of the body; and the impurity of clothing and garments <note>original: טומאת הלבוש</note> comes from the outermost layer. We find that clothing impurity applies only to wool, linen, and leather. It is known that Cain and Abel represent the secret of wool and linen <note>Cain brought flax/linen; Abel brought sheep/wool. Their "forbidden mixture" is a recurring theme in Kabbalah</note>. Regarding the leather garment, it is written that "from the root of the snake shall come forth a basilisk" <note>Isaiah 14:29</note>, which will be the rectification for the leather garments that became physical after the Fall.

The highest level of the Body is the secret of the Soul, which is the "Lower Aspect" of the Blessed One. Our souls are the secret of His "garment." Pride, however, pushes away the "feet" of the Divine Presence <note>The *Shekhinah*</note>, of whom it is said, "The Lord reigns, He is clothed in majesty" <note>Psalm 93:1</note>. The foundation of His garment is currently the "Hidden Light," but in the future, it will be revealed. This Hidden Light was created on the first day, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, hid it for the future—a "new light" for the world that is "entirely Sabbath." 

It is difficult to understand how "creation" applies to "rest" <note>referring to the creation of the Sabbath</note>, but the AriZal <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, 1534–1572, the father of contemporary Kabbalah</note> explained that the righteous have no rest in the World to Come, for they "go from strength to strength" <note>Psalm 84:8</note>. This is the Great Light surrounding the Crown (*Keter*) from which the soul derives pleasure.

In the first millennium, the Hidden Light shone, but it was hidden until the Seventh Day, which is the Sabbath of the seventh millennium. Rabbi Akiva said that when Israel sang the Song at the Sea, the Holy One, Blessed be He, wore a "Cloak of Splendor" <note>original: חלוק של תפארה</note> upon which every instance of the word "Then" (*Az*) in the Torah was engraved. When they sinned, He removed it. In the future, He will return it. The secret of "Then" (*Az*) is the beginning of the Hidden Light. 

The skin <note>original: עור, spelled with an Ayin</note> will eventually return to being light <note>original: אור, spelled with an Aleph</note>. Though wool and linen are forbidden as a mixture (*Kilayim*), they are permitted for the Priests, and it is written, "You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests." This is why the Torah uses the term "The Law of the Leper" <note>Leviticus 14:2</note>—to suggest that through the Torah, the "waste" is removed from the Soul, Body, and Clothing. In the future, the "skin" will return to "light," and creation will be renewed as it was in the first thought of "Let there be light." 

The Holy One, Blessed be He, is the True Light. The purpose of creation was for Israel to cause His Presence to dwell among them. He is One, and Israel is one nation. Now, in exile, the light is concealed and the Torah is written on physical skin (*Ohr*); in the future, it will return to Light (*Ohr*). The "Oral Torah" will shine clearly within the "Written Torah." Our current state, where we sit in darkness studying the Babylonian Talmud, involves the struggle between good and evil, pure and impure, permitted and forbidden—all part of the "Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil." In the future, the inner essence of the Torah will be revealed as light, and a man's clothing will be like a furnace of light. This will happen when our righteous Messiah comes.

->Hallelu<- <note>Praise</note>

<column-break/>

When the Matzah is whole or broken, at the moment he recites the blessing, he should eat an olive-sized portion (*kezayit*) from each to fulfill the obligation of both. 

**The Afikoman**, which is eaten at the very end, certainly points to the World to Come. It represents the "Guarded Matzah" <note>original: מצה שמורה</note> and corresponds to the secret of the "Preserved Wine." It is eaten when one is already satisfied <note>original: על השובע</note>, for one who is satisfied with the commandment, as it is written, "I shall behold Your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with Your likeness" <note>Psalm 17:15</note>.

Now, with the help of God, we shall further explain the matter of the **Maror** (Bitter Herbs):
**Maror** corresponds to death, which represents the "harsh judgments." One must chew them with the 32 teeth, which correspond to the 32 Paths of Wisdom <note>The 32 paths through which the world was created, according to the *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>. This chewing sweetens the bitterness within them. Therefore, if one swallows the Maror without chewing, he has not fulfilled the obligation, for he has not "sweetened" it. This is what I found in the pamphlets of the AriZal. It is known that Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) is the source of life; thus, death is transformed into life. This is the secret of why "the righteous in their death are called living."

The Maror is also called *Chasa* <note>Lettuce</note>. Why is it called *Chasa*? Because the Merciful One had mercy (*Chas*) on us and redeemed us. This is like a parable of a king who had a beautiful wife and wise children. When they went astray, he hated them and their mother. But then he had mercy on them again, saying, "I have pity on these children; why do you act in a way that makes your father hate you?" until they repented and did their father's will.

Now we explain the Hallel prayer. The purpose of the Egyptian exile was the revelation of the Four-Letter Name of God <note>The Tetragrammaton: Y-H-V-H</note>. This Name has four "fillings" <note>Gematria methods: Av, Sag, Mah, and Ban</note> corresponding to the four worlds: Emanation (*Atzilut*), Creation (*Beriah*), Formation (*Yetzirah*), and Action (*Assiah*). The first four psalms of Hallel correspond to these four worlds. 

->Hallelu<-

Then they hinted at the purification of "two birds" <note>referring to the leper's purification ritual</note>. Elijah the Prophet is the herald, and the "two birds" represent the two Messiahs <note>Messiah son of Joseph and Messiah son of David</note>. Even the "slaughtered bird" represents the Messiah son of Joseph, who will be killed but then return to life. Regarding them it is said, "As birds hovering, so will the Lord of Hosts protect Jerusalem" <note>Isaiah 31:5</note>. He will build the Sanctuary with cedar wood, as it says, "carvings of cherubim, lions, and palm trees." The "scarlet wool and hyssop" will pass away the spirit of impurity, fulfilling the promise: "And I will purify you." Amen.

### Guarded Matzah

One must "guard and do," and afterward achieve the level of "Soul to the Soul." These represent the secrets of the Torah revealed in this world to the "Lofty ones" and their students, who are called "Soul of the Soul" <note>original: *Nishmata de-Nishmata*, a Zoharic term for the highest level of spiritual insight</note>. This is the secret of secrets, the "Hidden Light" that will be revealed in the future. To remind them of this "Soul to the Soul," we have two cups of wine before the meal. The meal itself, which is the "Soul" comprised of its generations, stands in the middle, connecting the physical world to the spiritual realm.

The first two cups represent "Blessed is He who gave Torah to His people Israel." These cups signify that Israel was made with holy purity to differentiate between Israel and the nations, and between the sacred and the profane. In the first cup, we say "Who has chosen us..." <note>The *Kiddush* prayer</note>. 

<margin>The storyteller's craft: one who hears the tales of the righteous might think they are mere mundane stories, but they are "mundane matters handled in holiness."</margin>

Over the second cup, we tell the story of the Exodus from Egypt and conclude with the blessing "Who redeemed us," noting how He brought us from darkness to great light. This light is even more powerful because it emerged from the darkness; the "husk" <note>term: *Kelipah*, the shell of spiritual impurity</note> was transformed into a blessing. This is like the blood of a nursing mother turning into milk in the Zohar. 

After the meal, we have the Cup of Blessing for the Grace After Meals, which corresponds to the "wine of the world to come." The fourth cup is for the "Great Hallel" <note>Psalm 136</note> and the prayer "Soul of Every Living Thing," reaching the secret of "Soul to the Soul." 

In the middle, the Passover offering, the Matzah, and the Bitter Herbs <note>original: *Pesach, Matzah, u-Maror*</note> allude to loving the Lord your God, fearing Him, and cleaving to Him. The commandment of the Bitter Herbs <note>original: *Maror*</note> relates to "Fear," while the "Bread of Affliction" <note>Matzah</note> is the aspect of Love that includes Fear. Fear leads to Love, and Love leads to Fear, as I have explained at length in my work *Chased Le-Avraham*. The secret is that the Passover offering represents the punishment of all "other gods," while the Bitter Herbs remind us that He is the God of gods, and we must cleave to Him alone.

<column-break/>

### Rich Matzah

Regarding Cain and Abel: Moses, through Jethro, rectified what was broken between them. We know from our Sages that when the serpent came upon Eve, it cast a "venom" or impurity into her. Cain was born from this, and as the Midrash says, "The Lord set a sign for Cain" <note>Genesis 4:15</note>—some say he was struck with leprosy. 

When Moses' hand became leprous at the burning bush, it was to show the rectification of this primordial impurity. It is said that "the face of Moses was like the face of the sun." This relates to the "sign" of Cain being transformed. Moses' wife, Tzipporah, has a name that means "bird" <note>original: *Tzippor*</note>, because a bird is used to purify a house infected with leprosy. Moses, the "faithful servant in all God’s house," acts as the purifier.

The staff turning into a snake and the hand becoming leprous signify the descent into physical "skin" <note>original: *Or* with the letter Ayin</note> and the return to divine "light" <note>original: *Or* with the letter Aleph</note>. Moses served in the Tabernacle in a white tunic; this white tunic represents the "Polished Mirror" <note>term: *Aspaklaria ha-Meira*, clear prophetic vision</note>. This is why the verse says, "At all times let your garments be white" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:8</note>. Aaron, the High Priest, could only enter the Holy of Holies at specific times, but Moses could enter "at all times," for his "garments" (his physical state) were always "white" (pure light).

This is why Jerusalem and the Land of Israel do not receive the same type of impurity as other lands. In Jerusalem stands the Foundation Stone <note>original: *Even Shetiyah*</note> from which the world was woven. At this center, there is no "waste product" or "husk," only the direct light. 

This clarifies the connection between the three: The Holy One, the Torah, and Israel. The Torah is made of His names, and the 600,000 souls of Israel who left Egypt correspond to the 600,000 letters of the Torah. Just as a soul is clothed in a body, and a body is clothed in a garment, God is the "Soul" of all worlds, the Torah is the "Body" (with its 248 limbs/commandments), and Israel is the "Garment" that surrounds and reveals the light.

<column-break/>

<note>This column contains a repetition of the themes of Cain, Moses, and the white tunic, likely a draft or a pedagogical repetition emphasizing the transformation of the "sun" and the "leprosy" into holiness.</note>

There is no "mud or mire" for the one who takes the three Matzahs. According to the *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>A 16th-century Kabbalistic commentary on the Seder</note>, one takes a whole Matzah and a broken piece, placing the broken piece between two whole ones. We bless "He who brings forth bread" over the whole Matzah, which represents the "World to Come" and the attribute of *Binah* (Understanding), which is perfect and whole. We then bless "Regarding the eating of Matzah" over the broken piece, which represents the "Bread of Affliction" and the attribute of *Malchut* (Kingship/The Congregation of Israel). We eat them together to unite the "Lower World" with the "Upper World." 

Hillel the Elder used to wrap the Passover lamb, the Matzah, and the Bitter Herbs together. This sandwiching <note>original: *Korech*</note> reminds us of the Temple and signifies that even in the midst of "bitterness" (exile), the "Matzah" (redemption) is present. By eating them as one, we bind the brokenness of this world to the perfection of the Divine.

<column-break/>

### Matzah

The *Tola'at Yaakov* says: Take the whole matzah and the half that was put aside between the two wholes. The broken piece represents the "Bread of Affliction" (Israel in exile). We dip the Bitter Herbs into the *Charoset* <note>A sweet paste made of fruits and nuts</note>, which represents the mortar and clay of Egypt, but also the "sunken depths" of the sea of exile from which Israel emerged.

# Rich Matzah: Tractate Pesachim – Guarded Matzah

to send him away, for perhaps, Heaven forbid, through this, legal liabilities might arise and there would be an immeasurable loss to Israel, etc. As they might say, "Behold, we have conquered you in this," and it would be a "remedy for such a great wound," Heaven forbid. <note>The author is discussing a legalistic or "prosecutorial" argument in the heavenly court regarding the Exodus.</note> Even though Israel was accused of claiming what did not belong to them—since they said "Give us the wages for 400 years of labor," yet they were only in Egypt for 210 years—as for what is written, "The settlement of the children of Israel [was 400 years]," this includes their time in other lands, as Rashi explains.

I say: regarding the matter of the Egyptian exile, it is impossible to say it was merely a punishment. For the Lord made a covenant with Abraham and was with him in great love; how could it enter one's mind that in a time of favor, He would act toward him with anger? Therefore, we must say that even though the "revealed" aspect of the event was "evil and bitter," nevertheless, the inner essence of the matter was for the purpose of the **Absolute Good**, which we shall explain. As for the reasons our Sages of blessed memory gave in the chapter "Four Things" as to why Abraham was punished and his children enslaved—even if that sin had not occurred, the Holy One, blessed be He, would have brought about the "Absolute Good" through a different means that would not have involved such great suffering. But because of what happened, it became attached to this exile.

I say: the matter of the Egyptian exile was actually "good news," as in the Midrash Rabbah on the verse "Go forth from your land" (Genesis 12:1). Rabbi Phinehas said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Abraham, "Go forth and pave the way before you." Therefore, before we explain this statement, we will first introduce the concept of the benefit of the Egyptian exile.

It is written concerning the Land of Egypt: the text does not link the matter of Egypt to the Garden of Eden for nothing; it is to inform us that the matter of the Creation of the world and the matter of Israel are essentially one. And now we shall explain: before the world was created, there was only "He and His Name alone." He is the **Necessary Existent**, which is the true faith in the existence of God—the great principle that includes all other principles. Since the Blessed God is the Absolute Good, He desired to bestow good. Had He not created the world, He would have remained, as it were, alone, and would be "lacking" the ability to give a good reward. This leads to the second principle: **Reward and Punishment**. Everything stems from His goodness, and "no evil descends from Above." The world is merely a crucible for goodness, in the sense of "in order to afflict you, to do you good in your end" (Deuteronomy 8:16). Punishment is merely a cause and an awakening for future good.

Since His intention, from the side of His goodness, is for this reward and punishment, this is impossible except through the giving of the Torah, as it is written, "See, I set before you today..." (Deuteronomy 30:15). He gave the Torah—the Ten Commandments corresponding to the Ten Utterances of Creation—and it all rises on one branch. Here you have three principles: His Existence, the Righteousness of His Law, and the Torah given through the Torah, for it is entirely comprised of His Names. The revelation of Torah brings reward and punishment, for "the reward of a commandment is a commandment, and the recompense of a transgression is a transgression." A transgression creates a destroying angel, and I have elaborated on this elsewhere. Thus, there are "five pillars": Torah and Justice. The Torah is the "Man" who receives good and evil. Thus we find the three principles: the existence of God and everything else. So too you find His desire in "In the beginning God created the Heavens and the Earth."

In the book *Introduction to the Regions*: "The light of the Sage is to work it and to guard it." <note>A mystical interpretation of the Garden of Eden instructions.</note> Our Sages said "to work it" refers to positive commandments, and "to guard it" refers to negative commandments. They were warned of punishment: "On the day you eat of it..." Yet Adam sought it for all his seed and his seed’s seed, and it regressed. Because of the "bite of the serpent," the world was created through ten generations from Adam to Noah, and ten generations from Noah to Abraham. All these generations—the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion—turned from the path. But Abraham turned his face toward the Source and began to publicize the Divine work, for Abraham our forefather recognized his Creator and publicized the existence of God.

In the Midrash: "The Lord said to Abram: Go forth..." Rabbi Isaac said: This is like one who travels from place to place and sees a **palace in flames** <note>original: *birah doleket*. This is a famous parable: Abraham sees the world and wonders if it has no leader, until God looks out and says, "I am the master of the palace."</note>. The commentators explain that Abraham went from investigation to investigation until the Blessed God revealed Himself to him and said, "I am the Master of the world." Abraham knew and grasped the truth of God’s existence and believed in Him. It was revealed to him that the world was created anew and that God is the "Master of the Palace," meaning the Master of the world since He created it. Everything created must have a Creator who brought it forth. This matter was entrusted to him when God said "Go forth" for the reason we will explain later.

Behold, through Abraham our forefather, the encompassing principle of the secret of God's existence was publicized: "And he called there in the name of the Lord, God of the world." Isaac took hold of the attribute of **Justice** (*Din*) to publicize that "there is a Law and there is a Judge," unlike those deniers who believe God exists but think He abandoned the earth to humans to do as they wish. Jacob, "a dweller in tents," the student of Shem and Eber, is the essence of Judaism. Thus the Three Patriarchs publicized the **Three Principles**. Just as the principle of God's existence includes all others, so too Abraham, who publicized God's existence, included all of them, even the Torah. For our Sages said in Tractate Avodah Zarah: "The two thousand years of Torah begin from 'the souls they made in Haran.'"

Men of high standing see their "worlds" in their lifetimes; that is, the attainment they reach adds to their spirit. However, there is a great difference between what they attain here and there. After death, it is "Soul to the Soul."

As is known, the levels of Soul (*Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama*) correspond to the worlds of Action, Formation, and Creation (*Asiyah, Yetzirah, Beriah*), which in turn correspond to the Divine attributes of Sovereignty, Beauty, and Understanding. Corresponding to these, Israel below had four banners (*Degalim*) against the camps of the Divine Presence, the secret of **Argaman** <note>An acronym for the angels Uriel, Raphael, Gabriel, Michael, and Nuriel.</note>, as explained in the Zohar and the books of the Kabbalists.

This resolves the repetitive language: "What ails you, O Sea... you mountains, that you skip..." The text could have been brief, but the length shows a question: "If it is proper to serve the Lord with joy, why did the Sea and Jordan show fear? And if it is proper to serve with awe, why did the mountains and hills show joy?" Rather, the Midrash says the Sea did not want to split until the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared. The reason for the Sea's hesitation was that it was not yet the time for redemption, for the 400 years were not yet complete...

->**The Assembly of Israel**<-

**Hallelujah**
"Praise, O servants of the Lord." This psalm speaks of the day of the transcendence of the Blessed One. "The Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>original: "יי' אלהינו יי' אחד"</note> is the secret of the most unique **Emanation** <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure godliness</term>. It is the absolute truth within the Emanator. The name *Y-H-V-H* spelled out with the letter *Yod* <note>The "filling" or *milui* of the Tetragrammaton totaling 72</note> hints at this, as I have written. The reason is that Emanation consists of three "lines" that are unified in their root, which are three *Yods*—namely, Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge <note>Chochmah, Binah, and Da’at</note>. These three *Yods* are included in a single letter *Yod*, which contains three points: the body, the leg, and the crown-tip. This represents the **Hidden Crown** <term>Keter: the highest Sephirah</term> which is enclothed within the *Ein Sof* (The Infinite), the Cause of all causes and the Reason of all reasons, in the aspect of the "Three Refulgent Lights" explained in the *Gate of Lights* <note>A reference to the *Sha'ar HaTzachtzachot* in Kabbalistic literature</note>. 

The numerical value here <note>76</note> accounts for the four additional *Yods* found in this psalm: *Hamagbihi* (Who raises), *Hamashpili* (Who lowers), *Mekimi* (Who lifts), and *Lehoshivi* (To seat). These extra letters <note>referring to the archaic poetic suffixes in the Hebrew text</note> hint at the four *Yods* within the Name. Regarding the phrase "He transforms the barren woman of the home" <note>Psalm 113:9, *moshevi*</note>, there is yet another additional *Yod* which has also been explained.

Behold, our true faith is to be "servants to Him" and not to any other. This explains the psalm: "Praise, O servants of the Lord"—do not be mistaken to interpret this as praising or serving *His* servants <note>i.e., angels or celestial bodies</note>. This follows what Maimonides wrote in the *Book of Knowledge* and *The Guide for the Perplexed*: that early humans erred by calling upon the name of the Lord as a justification to worship angels and the heavenly host. They reasoned that since the servants are great, the Master is further removed. To this, the Psalmist says: "Do not err; the intent is that *you* are the servants of the Lord, so praise the name of the Lord." And if you ask: "Why was it necessary to speak at such length, saying 'servants of the Lord'? Why not just write 'Praise the Lord'?" To this, he answered what we have said: "Praise, you who are the servants of the Lord."

# Guarded Matzah
## Third Discourse

<margin>Talmud</margin>
**"This** is the law of the burnt offering... and this is the law of the meal offering..." <note>Leviticus 6</note>. The commandment is to eat the Matzah in a holy place. We eat it because "the dough of our fathers did not have time to leaven before the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed Himself to them." One might ask: Why was "haste" given as the reason for eating Matzah? It serves as a memory of the hurried freedom they had in Egypt, when they brought out cakes of Matzah because it had not leavened, for they were driven out of Egypt and could not delay. This implies that "haste" regarding redemption is a good thing. 

However, the opposite seems true in the words of the Prophet regarding the Final Redemption: "For you shall not go out in haste, nor go by flight" <note>Isaiah 52:12</note>. Now, without this specific paragraph, the verse itself in the portion of *Re'eh* says: "You shall eat no leavened bread with it; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, for in haste you departed from the land of Egypt." Rashi already sensed this difficulty and resolved it, saying: "The haste was not yours, but Egypt’s," as it says, "And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people." Undoubtedly, Rashi wrote this to answer the contradiction: haste is not a virtue when it comes from the one being redeemed; but here, the haste came from the Egyptians. They were the ones who sent the children of freedom away quickly, and that is a virtue. 

The *Yalkut* <note>Midrashic anthology</note> also brings this: "For in haste you departed—was it Israel's haste? No, it says 'no dog shall whelp its tongue against the children of Israel.' Thus, the haste belonged to Egypt, not Israel." But this paragraph in the Haggadah implies the haste *was* Israel's, for it says: "the dough of our fathers did not have time to leaven until the King of kings revealed Himself." This means the dough didn't leaven because the Holy One, Blessed be He, in His glory and essence, revealed Himself to them between Sukkot and... they traveled that path in haste because the Lord went before them by day. Thus, the haste was indeed Israel's. The Egyptian haste was at Rameses, but the haste from Egypt to Sukkot was Israel's. So our question returns to its place. Indeed, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha holds that the haste belonged to Israel, as cited in the *Yalkut* on Isaiah: "For you shall not go out in haste—because it was said of the Egyptian redemption, 'And you shall eat it in haste.' This was the haste of Israel."

**Regarding** the haste of Egypt, it is written: "And Egypt was urgent upon the people to send them out." And regarding Israel's haste, it is written: "They did according to the word of Moses and they borrowed from the Egyptians silver and gold vessels and garments." In the chapter *Chelek* <note>Talmud Sanhedrin</note>, it is told that once the Egyptians came to litigate with the Jews before Alexander the Great. They said: "Behold, the Torah says, 'The Lord gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians and they lent to them.' Return the silver and gold you took from us!" 

Gaviah ben Pesisa said to the Sages: "Give me permission to go and litigate with them before Alexander. If they defeat me, say: 'You have only defeated a commoner among us.' If I defeat them, say: 'The Torah of Moses has defeated you!'" They gave him permission. He asked the Egyptians: "From where do you bring your proof?" They said: "From the Torah." He replied: "I too shall bring proof only from the Torah, which says: 'The settlement of the children of Israel in Egypt was 430 years.'" He said to them: "Give us the wages for the labor of 600,000 men for 430 years!" Alexander the Great said to the Egyptians: "Give them their wages!" They asked for three days to think, but after checking the accounts, they immediately abandoned their fields while they were sown and their vineyards while they were planted, and they fled. And that year was a Sabbatical year. 

One might ask: Why did the Egyptians wait until the time of Alexander to sue the Jews? Why didn't they sue when the Jews were exiled under Nebuchadnezzar the Wicked? One could answer that the Jews were then poor and plundered, unlike when they sat on their land full of bounty. Furthermore, was Gaviah ben Pesisa the wisest of the Sages or not? If he was the wisest, why did he need to ask permission?

...the nights of their sale and their dwelling... at the time of sunset they linger in the west for seven days, and from then on, nights... as is written in the portion of *Nitzavim*.

**And if** you should ask: "In truth, why should we not just perform the commandments without this service? For the Lord is high above all nations!" Even the nations admit there is none like Him, as it says: "Among all the wise men of the nations... there is none like You." The Zohar explains that the wise of the nations admit "None is like You," yet they think there is a place vacant of the Divine Presence. This is the answer provided by the *Beit Yosef* and the Gemara: He is not like a king of flesh and blood. He does not dwell in a different category. Not like the thought of the nations who think our God is immovable, but that the "First Cause" is merely a ruler detached from them. But that is not so; the Divine Presence enters with mercy, lowering itself to see "in heaven and on earth." He is "the Lord our God Who seats Himself on high, Who humbles Himself to see," even though there is none like Him. He is perceived even by the lowest beings. Unlike those who imagine that providence over the lowly is beneath His dignity, David says in the psalm: He is perceived from the highest point to the lowest. This is the meaning of the four *Yods* mentioned earlier. And the matter of "He transforms the barren woman" <note>Psalm 113:9</note> is well known, referring to the worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action <note>Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah</note>.

"Praise the Lord, all you nations..." <note>Psalm 117</note>. This is an acknowledgment by the nations of the high level of Israel's attachment to God. Afterward comes the psalm "Give thanks to the Lord for He is good, for His mercy endures forever" <note>Psalm 118</note>, which includes all the eight preceding points, much like the Fifth Book of the Torah (Deuteronomy) includes the first four books.

## Guarded Matzah

->Matzah<-
And the truth of Jacob stems from the essence of Abraham and Jacob, for **Abraham did not know us and Israel <note>the Patriarch Jacob</note> did not recognize us**, as seen in the Talmud <note>Tractate Shabbat, chapter "Rabbi Akiva"</note>. They teach for the sake of His great Name, explaining the verse: "Why should the nations say, 'Where now is their God?'" <note>Psalm 115:2</note>

The word "now" <note>Hebrew: *na*</note> is always a language of entreaty. It is simple to understand that our questions toward the Blessed One are intended so that the nations do not "seize" the opportunity to say, as it were, that the words have become aged or weakened—God forbid! Even this is our request for our own sake: that they should not say, "Where is their God?" implying He has cast them away from His presence. This is what the nations say—those who believe in a "Trinity"—claiming that now they are no longer called "Israel" and that there is a "division," Heaven forbid! Quite the contrary: "But our God is in the heavens" <note>Psalm 115:3</note>. He is Eternal, as the Sages mentioned in their Midrash: when the world was first seen, the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: the Divine Presence manifested in the physical world</term> was seen below. It moved from firmament to firmament until it rested below in the Temple. But when they sinned, through ten journeys the Shekhinah ascended and returned to the heavens. Nevertheless, He does not withhold His providence from us. Even when endangered, one is certain that "He watches over all; whatever He desired, He has done." Note that it is written "He has done" <note>past tense</note> and not "He does" <note>present</note>. This hints at the statement "Let us make man" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>. Even though He consulted with the upper beings—which is why the plural language "let us" was used—nonetheless, He alone is the actor, as it is written: "And God created <note>singular</note> man." We were made in His image and likeness, and through the letter *He* <note>the breath of life</note> we have a connection to the Blessed One. If you were to say we are "abandoned," Heaven forbid, it would be written "the work of human hands"—which refers to the "External Shells" <note>forces of evil/impurity</note>—rather than "Man" <note>Adam</note>, which is a title of dignity. This is also hinted at in "Let us make man": that man was created for the sake of the Torah. The great superiority was found in the matter of **"We will do" preceding "We will hear"** <note>the Israelites' unconditional acceptance of the Torah at Sinai</note>. The Torah was given as a beauty, as it is written: "From the heavens He let you hear His voice," and "Like the beauty of a man." The idols of the nations, however, "have eyes but see not." Regarding the giving of the Torah, it is written: "All the people saw [the sounds]."

### Ears
"They have ears..." etc., but regarding the giving of the Torah, it is written that they "heard" and "saw that which is heard." Even "they have noses but smell not," yet at the giving of the Torah, Israel smelled the "Great and Salted Fragrance," as recorded in the chapter of "Rabbi Akiva."

### Their Hands
"Their hands, but they feel not." It does not simply say "hands," but "their hands," as explained above. The same difficulty applies to "their feet." The distinction is that not all of Israel is focused only on physical needs; rather, the "hands" of the collective of Israel were busy grasping the Tablets, as it is written: "The lips were..." etc. The Holy One held two handbreadths, and Moses held two handbreadths. Regarding "feet," it is said: "Who has ascended to the heavens?" referring to Moses alone. Similarly, "Come up to Me on the mountain." After it has been hinted that the nations are not truly "Man" <note>Adam</note> in their inner essence, but only Israel who received the Torah are called "Man," it says regarding the idols that "those who make them shall be like them." Regarding the holy ones, it is written: "Through God we shall do valiantly." Our Sages said: God considers it as if the person "made Me." And it says: "Or let him take hold of My strength, that he may make peace with Me."

"Those who make them shall be like them," for "they are vanity, a work of delusion." But we cling to His Blessed Name, and "Israel is in God," as mentioned. Regarding the "Final House" <note>the Third Temple</note>, it is written: "And he shall carry their names." The doubling of the language refers to the **Explicit Name of God** <term>Shem HaMephorash: the Tetragrammaton</term>. Regarding those who fear the Lord, it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you." I say that "those who fear the Lord" refers to those who walk in two paths. When Moses our teacher said "to us," it is written: "Gather to me..." etc. This refers to the "Holder of Blessing," which is the power of life. It begins with "Israel," for they are the ones who cling to Him, and from them the fear spreads like the fish of the sea. It also starts with Israel because through "Beauty" <note>the Sephirah of Tiferet</note> we exist. In this Psalm lies the secret of **Israel the Elder** <term>Yisrael Saba: a Kabbalistic configuration of the intellect</term>. "The Lord has been mindful of us; He will bless"—according to the plain meaning, He adds a blessing upon them. In the sections of "The Lord has been mindful of us," He blesses the males; "The House of Israel" refers to the children, as Rashi explains on the verse "Thus shall you say to the House of Jacob"—referring to the women. And regarding "those who fear the Lord," this hints at "the small with the great," for that tribe is destined to be counted.

## Rich Matzah

The aspect of matter <note>physicality</note> is used so that people become accustomed to the attribute of humility, which is the highest virtue. Regarding this matter, we find in the "Covenant Between the Pieces" <note>the prophecy given to Abraham in Genesis 15</note> during the news of the Egyptian exile: Israel is compared to a bird, and "the bird he did not divide." This means Israel is compared to a pure dove. Regarding the Egyptians, they said: "See, Jacob is descending in chains," but it is rather like the parable of the cow... [The author explains here that the descent to Egypt, though appearing as a misfortune, was for the ultimate benefit of the "Generation of the Wilderness."] Just as the end of a beast is to be slaughtered, the end of a man is to die—which is for his own good, like the reason for the descent to Egypt. It is written: "Every pure bird you may eat," and similarly regarding beasts. The bird that flies upward represents the refinement of the soul, while the dark beast represents the refinement of the body. Now the matter will be clarified: one master says one thing, and another master says another, and the third master explains both. The first speaks of the soul, which was sunk in the "Shells" <note>impure forces</note> to the depths; therefore, he uses the language of "sinking." This is the opposite of the soul's ascent, as the Holy One said regarding Rabbi Akiva: "So it arose in thought." The Holy One brings the soul down for two reasons: either for punishment for a sin, or for good—to be refined. This is the secret of "He brings down to the grave and raises up." Regarding this, he says "winged creatures" etc. And he says: "And the Lord saved <note>Vayosha</note> [Israel] on that day." This implies that if it were even one day longer, we would have remained enslaved. The 50 times the Exodus is mentioned in the Torah correspond to the 50 Gates of Understanding; Israel had sunk until the 49th gate of impurity. Through the three redemptions, the message was spread. We have already mentioned that the Torah is the ultimate reality, above and below; the essence of God's existence is revealed through the Torah, which is entirely His Names. From the Torah, we learn the reward of a commandment and the consequence of a sin.

The Torah was preserved in the days of the priests who descended from Egypt... The Zohar speaks of three wonders and three gates publicized in Egypt. This is the meaning of "Pesach, Matzah, and Maror." From the side of Matzah, there is another world. The innovation here is that the entire world is called "dough," a mixture of water and earth. Therefore, Man is called the "Challah <note>dough-offering</note> of the world." Now, **Chametz** <term>leavened bread</term> is taken from the "leaven" <note>S'or</note> to the crust. But Matzah is not "taken" from anything; it signifies a new creation. This proves that there is a creator who forms bodies. Even though the "Philosophers" <note>secular/Aristotelian thinkers</note> claim that matter is eternal, we are commanded to eat Matzah and forbidden from Chametz for seven days—corresponding to the seven days of Creation. The beginning of creation was a single point, which the Ramban calls "Hyle" <note>primeval matter</note>. Therefore, "at the beginning you shall eat Matzah." The difference between Chametz (חמץ) and Matzah (מצה) is the difference between the letters *Het* (ח) and *He* (ה). <note>The letter Het is closed at the top, representing no escape from sin/ego, while the He has a small opening for repentance.</note>

<margin>Pesach</margin>
This hints that God will be the "Master of Judgment" to argue against the heretics. Even those who believe in God's existence and that He created the world from nothing sometimes claim He has abandoned the world to humans. Against this comes the **Pesach** sacrifice, showing that the Blessed One performed judgment in Egypt even upon their gods and skipped over Israel. This is a hint to this Torah, which is a "Second Torah." According to the Zohar, the "Hand of God" is over the letters of the Torah, and they are one. The spiritual essence is in the hand of the Holy One. We join Pesach, Matzah, and Maror together because all three principles are included in one essence. Abraham our father publicized this principle, and therefore at the "Covenant Between the Pieces" he was told of the Egyptian exile and redemption. This is the meaning of: "Go forth (Lekh Lekha)—go and pave the way for your children." From there, Abraham went down to Egypt as a sign for his children, as the Ramban explains at length. A question arises regarding the portion of *Lekh Lekha* and *Vayeshev*: why did God tell Abraham to take Lot with him? Is it not written: "Because you have joined with the wicked, the Lord has broken your works"? Also, as long as Lot was with him, the Shekhinah departed from Abraham. Rashi notes on the verse "And the Lord said to Abram after Lot had parted from him..." Look deeply into the matter of Lot: "He baked matzot and they ate." Rashi says it was Pesach. One must wonder: was Lot so righteous as to observe this?

We have already said that the entry of Israel into Egypt was like the entry of the soul into the coarse body, for our sorrow there was in the removal of their filth within the strength of the *Klipot* <term>Klipot: "husks" or "shells," the Kabbalistic term for forces of evil or impurity</term> of Egypt. They were refined in body and soul. The refinement of the soul occurred because they were submerged and entangled in the *Klipa* of the Prince of Egypt, as elaborated in the imagery of the "donkey" on the verse "and they baked the dough" which I transcribed above. The sum of his words is that Israel was submerged in the *Klipot* until the very last moment. If they had stayed there one more moment, Heaven forbid, they would have been completely submerged in the fifty <note>gates of impurity</note>. This was the haste of the redemption. And then the passage is clarified... "the Matzah that we eat, for what reason?" etc. See in "Guarded Matzah" for the explanation of the Haggadah there; you will find everything at length. Because they were submerged in the full depth of the *Klipot* to leave the filth there, the result is that "every soul shall praise Him," for it is clean of all dross. Also, the animalistic body was refined through the weakening of its strength.

Even though I have written... the secret of the *Klipot*... for there the name of 53 <note>Name SaG</note> is in union. Nevertheless, it appears that this is in *Binah* <term>Binah: the Sefirah of Understanding</term>... the Sefirot of the soul... there is the filling of 25 <note>Name KoH</note>... which is the numerical value 86 <note>Elohim</note>... 63 <note>Name SaG</note>... three "Yods" and one "Aleph"... equals 161 <note>Name Ehyeh</note>... and thus the name of the Lord... and we find in the secrets... Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the Sefirah of Wisdom</term> is called "Honor"... hinting at the 32 paths of Wisdom. It has been explained that the name 63 in Understanding is the rectifier...

<column-break/>

It was revealed that the Holy One, Blessed be He, calculated the end <note>of the exile</note>, as it is written: "The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping over the mountains, skipping over the hills" <note>Song of Songs 2:8</note>. The reason this was revealed to them as "mountains and hills" was a good omen, for they were changed for the better. They ascended from the "matter of the fetus" which is the element of Earth to a finer element, the element of Water. For rocks were split for Israel in the desert and water came out of them. But the Sea and the Jordan were the opposite, for they split and turned into dry land. We find that "from before the Master" was the response of the sea, "from before the God of Jacob," who turned the flint into a fountain of waters. From what I have written, it is answered why it mentions here the turning of the flint into a pool of water—it should only have mentioned the turning of the sea into dry land. But according to what I wrote, it is fine: just as earth turned to water, so He brought out from the "dust of his matter" (which is earth) his life, as pure as water, from the side of his soul which is *Binah*.

**Not** to us, O Lord, not to us <note>Psalm 115:1</note>. The secret of the name *MaH* <note>Name of God equaling 45</note> is in *Tiferet* <term>Tiferet: the Sefirah of Beauty, Harmony, and the Heart</term>, which rectifies in the World of Creation. *Tiferet* is the "body" of the Emanation, as is known... the "bodies" of the Torah... from the side of the bodies of laws and judgments, to know what Israel should do. Behold, it is written of *Tiferet*: "the beauty of a man" <note>Adam</note>. And Wisdom is called "The First Man" <note>Adam HaRishon</note>, as is known, for *Tiferet* is to *Malchut* (Kingship) as Wisdom is to Understanding. In *Tiferet* there is the revelation of Wisdom. The matter of the name of 45... the Kabbalists explained... the power of *MaH* and *MaH*... which is the name of 48... which equals "Adam" <note>Man</note>... and these letters... the filling of the filling equals the value of 28... letters... and corresponding to... remember... in this secret, Israel is called "Adam" and not the nations... and Israel, when they do His will, they increase the power of the Place <note>God</note> above, and when they do not do the will of the Place, they, as it were, weaken the power of Above. Woe to the scribe <note>meaning: woe to the one who causes this</note>... and this is also hinted at in the filling of the name 63 (*SaG*) which is from the side of Understanding... "Wisdom," for the letters are Yod-He-Vav-He... the combination... for His name is called upon us... the secret of *Bereshit* (In the Beginning)... Jonathan translates "with wisdom," and our Sages interpreted "for the sake of Israel." Afterward, the name 45 (*MaH*) equals "Adam," and Israel are called Adam. Let us return to the matter of the name 45 which we are dealing with: in it is hinted the secret that "The Lord He is God" <note>YHVH Hu HaElohim</note>. For when you write the name *MaH* in its full spelling, it equals 86, the numerical value of *Elohim*. Thus it is hinted that His name... the letters 26 and 86. I have already elaborated on this elsewhere; it is the secret of the inclusion of Judgment within Mercy. The righteous turn Judgment into Mercy, while the wicked do the opposite. Rabbi Galanti explained in the Scroll of Fasts: "Remember, O Lord, what (*MaH*) has happened to us" <note>Lamentations 5:1</note>—the Name of God (*YHVH*) in its filling of 45 (*MaH*) was turned into the attribute of Judgment, hinted at in the word "to us" (*Lanu*), which equals 86, the value of *Elohim*. This is what is hinted here: "Not to us (*Lanu*), not to us, O Lord, not..."—let it be turned back to "to us" <note>meaning, let the Judgment be reversed</note>. "But to Your Name," which is *YHVH*, "give glory"—the influence of Wisdom; "and for Your truth"—*Tiferet*, which is Truth. These are toward the side of Kindness. All that I have written exalts the Psalm "Give thanks..." We are called "Adam" in the secret of "Let us make man (*Adam*) in our image," which is the secret of "and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man." I have already elaborated on this in the introductions to *Toldot Adam*. But the nations are the "likeness of a man of Belial," the work of human hands. He describes the five senses which have no substance in them: "Eyes they have but they see not"—the sense of sight; "Ears they have but they hear not"—the sense of hearing; "They smell not"—the sense of smell; "They feel not"—the sense of touch. And in place of the sense of taste, he said, "A mouth they have but they speak not," for the sense of taste is also in the mouth, and he mentioned one of them. We have established these things... and added "and for Your truth," for even though it is written "Truth to Jacob and Kindness to Abraham," we desire Your kindness and Your truth, to the exclusion of the "kindness of the nations"...
