# Tractate Pesachim: Guarded Matzah

## Guarded Matzah

He was a ruler in the world and would entice the creatures to follow him until he drew people away from the service of the Master of the Universe. Rabbi Simeon said: "In these garments, the companions <note>original: חבריי' - likely referring to the students of the Zohar</note> were faint..." This is mentioned in the *Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer* <term>Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer: An 8th-century midrashic work on Genesis</term>. It is found that Abraham and Nimrod were two opposites, with Haran as the middle ground. For Abraham believed that there is a Renewer, a unique God of the world, who is subtle and refined. But Nimrod doubted Divine Providence and the free will of man, for he thought that surely if God is the Creator of the world, there is no reason for Him to respond to others. He argued that after the creation, we could say He left humanity to act according to their own will, and there is no one to say to Him, "What are you doing?"

Even though Haran adhered somewhat to holiness, his attachment was not so great. This is why he was endangered by the separation and the turning away. This is hinted at in the verse: "A river went out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. The combination of the Divine letters *Yod* and *He* (YH) is the secret of Judgment <note>original: הד"ן - likely referring to the attribute of Din/Judgment</note>, understand this well. Now, Haran believed in the secret of Matzah, for Matzah alludes to the creation of the world out of nothing <term>Yesh Me-ayin: Creation ex nihilo</term>. This is because Matzah is made without the beginning of leaven <note>sourdough starter</note>; it is made without any prior material being taken from another batch to act as its predecessor. This hints that the existence of the world was made without a prior beginning.

This is not the case with *Chametz* <term>Chametz: Leavened bread</term>, which cannot transform in its usual way except through leaven—a starter from another dough, and that dough from another, and so on. Therefore, we were commanded not to eat leaven for seven days, corresponding to the seven days of Creation. The prohibition of leaven applies even to the smallest amount <term>Mashehu: An infinitesimal particle</term>, because true faith requires believing that there was no primordial matter, not even a "speck" of it.

This is also why there is no obligation to eat Matzah except on the first night, and thereafter it is optional during the seven days. This is because that "creation out of absolute nothing" occurred only at the first moment of creation, which is the revelation. Afterward, things emerged from potentiality into actuality. Therefore, the only difference between *Chametz* and *Matzah* is a tiny speck <note>The Hebrew letters for Chametz (חמץ) and Matzah (מצה) are identical except for the tiny gap in the letter He (ה) vs the closed top of the Chet (ח)</note>. This is the body of the analysis of the letter *He*.

This is the distinction between Haran and Haran. It is written: "And Terah died in Haran" <note>Genesis 11:32</note>. According to Rashi, Terah complained to Nimrod about Abraham our father, and "Haran died in the presence of Terah his father." Behold, Haran was attached to the secret of Matzah, but he was not attached to the secret of the Passover offering <term>Pesach: The Paschal lamb</term>, which indicates the existence of God and His providence to do bad or good and to humble all hands, just as He humbled the Prince of Egypt, who is great over all princes and the "Firstborn of the Chariot." For he is the Chariot of action for God's providence over the lower worlds, to give to them according to His will.

Since Haran was attached to the secret of Matzah, and Matzah alludes to the renewal of the Exodus from Egypt—He who brought us out of the "affliction of Egypt" and leads us to faith—for they were driven out of Egypt. Our Sages of blessed memory said that by the merit of righteous women, Israel was redeemed from Egypt. This is the secret of why the righteous women emerged from Haran. Similarly, Ruth the Moabitess is the secret from whom the Messiah shall emerge, for the future redeemer is revitalized through the redemption from Egypt, as it is written: "As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him marvelous things" <note>Micah 7:15</note>.

Benjamin was favored and gave grace to Hannah... and the Passover is the "Festival of the Ear" <term>Chag Ha-Aviv: The Spring Festival</term>, established by drawing down the eternity of the Exodus mentioned in the Torah. This is why it is written afterward: "And the Lord said to Abraham: Go forth..." <note>Genesis 12:1</note>, commanding him to go to the land of Egypt. And he took with him Lot, the son of Haran, for even Lot had a connection to this. This Lot, the son of Haran, baked Matzot <note>Genesis 19:3</note>.

Regarding the matter of leaven, our Sages hinted: "The search for leaven is by the light of a candle" <term>Bedikat Chametz: The ritual search for leaven on the night before Passover</term>. The light alludes to the light of the furnace into which Haran was cast... And since Haran had a miracle within the furnace for being a "commander" of the commandment, even though he did not believe in Providence, this is hinted at in the verse: "When the wicked perish there is a song of joy" <note>Proverbs 11:10</note>. And regarding the perishing of Egypt, it is written "Woe" and "Heaven."

Abraham, Nimrod, and Haran—all this revolves around the fact that Abraham our father represented the core existence of God. Nimrod was his opposite, a denier in Babylon. Haran was the middle ground; he believed in creation out of nothing but not in Providence. Terah, who complained to Nimrod, was a denier of Nimrod but not exactly like Nimrod, for he believed in creation but not in creation "out of nothing"—rather, he believed there was primordial matter. This is the point between the *Chet* and the *He*. This is the distinction between Haran and Haran—a single point, like the difference between *Chametz* and *Matzah*.

*Chametz* is the "husk" <term>Kelipah: A spiritual shell or force of evil</term>, the secret of "finding a harlot woman." This is hinted at in: "I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth" <note>Genesis 27:46</note>, for they come from the side of the Serpent and the Ox who saw her naked and desired her. For "sin" <note>Hebrew: Chet</note> leaves one with the "harlot woman," and there is no joy in leaven, the opposite of Matzah, where the *He* was flipped into a *Chet*. This is "I am weary because of the daughters of Heth." They said: "And Terah died in Haran"—the letter *Gimel* is reversed. Until Abraham, the world was in judgment... the core existence of the Blessed Name includes two actions of *Binah* <term>Binah: The Sefirah of Understanding</term> revealed in the secrets of the Torah, which takes hold of the existence of the Blessed Name, for the Torah is entirely His names. Afterward, it takes hold of the principle of reward and punishment: the reward for a commandment is the commandment itself, and the reward for a transgression is the transgression.

The matter of the 50 Gates of Understanding is revealed in the secrets of the Torah. Therefore, the letter *Nun* of "Fierce Anger" <note>Hebrew: Charon-Af</note> was transformed into the *Nun* that "fell" (not mentioned in the *Ashrei* prayer) into the *Nun* of the Gates of Understanding that became known through Egypt—the 50 levels. It is impossible to include them all. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Go forth, go out and conquer the way..." and he went to Egypt. Our Sages said: "And I will make you a great nation"—this is what we say, "God of Abraham," through whom the existence of the Blessed Name became publicized. He made Him great, as it is written: "Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods." "And I will make you"—this is what we say, "God of Isaac," for he is the "Arm" of Justice where there is Law and there is a Judge. And regarding this, he told his soul.

**The Matter:** From the side of *Binah* (Understanding), for the ear listens from above to below. In the days of "Action" <term>Asiyah: The lowest spiritual world of action</term>, it is said "her feet go down to death." This refers to its embodiment in Metatron <term>Metatron: A high-ranking angel in mystical literature</term> and in the "Heels," which are the secret of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. However, "Hevel" <note>Abel/Vanity</note> is for the good, for "it was good," the light of death, for it causes the attachment... And by the name Y-H-H I shall call... The union of the five names of God with each other... for the numerical value of 324 is found in *Malchut* (Kingship), meaning in the secret of her uniqueness. *Malchut* is the secret of the "Son and Daughter," and *Tiferet* (Harmony) is "The son is the leg of his father," *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), and *Malchut* is "The daughter is like her mother," *Binah*. "In His name I shall call, be gracious to me." The "Righteous" is the theme of this Psalm, to show that all events are from *Binah*, which is *Malchut* with the name *Ehyeh* (I Shall Be), the Leader according to Law.

<column-break/>

It is written: "Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity" <note>Isaiah 5:18</note>. This refers to speech. "And sin as with a cart rope"—who is "Sin"? This is the Feminine aspect <term>Nukvah: The feminine divine attribute</term> which is called "Sin-Offering" <note>Chatat</note>, which strengthens itself to become a fly to kill the "sons of vanity." See there: "For she has cast down many wounded" <note>Proverbs 7:26</note>. Who cast them down? That same Sin that kills human beings. What caused this? Come and see: one who has not reached the level of instruction but instructs... may the Merciful One save us.

On this, it said: "Blessed are you of the Lord, Maker of [Heaven and Earth]" <note>Psalm 115:15</note>. See what you cause through your engagement with the Torah, which He carved out! From your Torah, "New Heavens and a New Earth" are made, as it says: "For as the new heavens and the new earth which I make..." <note>Isaiah 66:22</note>. Behold, from the "Torah of the Lord," which are the spiritual laws, New Heavens are made. And from the "Torah of Man"—meaning the other matters of Torah, the strengthening and the literal explanations of the Torah and its ethics—a "New Earth" is made, which is the "Land of the Living." And this is "The heavens are the Lord's heavens" <note>Psalm 115:16</note>, meaning they are His choice, the secret of His names. "But the earth He has given to the children of men"—the Torah of man.

The secret of the New Heavens and Earth is that they are made from *Tiferet* (Harmony) and *Malchut* (Kingship), from which were given the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. So it is written: "From the heavens He made you hear His voice, and upon the earth He showed you..." <note>Deuteronomy 4:36</note>. "Voice" is *Tiferet*. The fire... is the analytical debates of the Talmud. These are the letters *He* from the five. These Heavens and Earth themselves, which are *Tiferet* and *Malchut*, were brought into being from the letter *He* of the Name <note>For with the letters Yod and He (YH), God formed the worlds</note>. *Tiferet* comes from *Chokhmah* (Wisdom), which is the first *He* of the five. *Malchut* is the final *He* from the first *He* of the Name, which is *Binah*. Thus, "The Torah of the Lord is perfect."

However, the "Heavens and Earth" that are brought into being from vanity and lies are in the aspect of "the cunning ones," and they have no connection to the letters *Yod-He*. These heavens and earth are called "dead," and they "descend to Silence" <note>Dumah: the angel of the graveyard</note>, as it is written: "Many wounded has she cast down, and numerous are all her slain." They do not "Praise the Lord." "But we will bless the Lord"—this "We" is the secret of *Tiferet* and *Malchut*. The "And" (of *V'Anachnu*) is the secret of *Da'at* (Knowledge) that ascends to the Divine Name, connecting to the first ten [Sefirot]. With intention in one's renewal of the Torah, one says: "We are attached to these lights to be New Heavens and Earth, living and wise." Then "We will bless the Lord..." from the conclusion of "Hallelujah."

**I love [the Lord]** <note>Psalm 116:1</note> "for the Lord hears my voice, my supplications." This is the secret of the Name *Ban* <note>Numerical value 52</note>, which is in *Malchut* as it is tied to the world of Action (*Asiyah*). *Malchut* is connected and receives from the ten primary days, which are the "Six Extremities" <term>Vav Ktzavot: The six emotional sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</term>. This is the Name *YHVH*, the secret of the Sabbath, which then flows downward into the world of Action. Then there are "six hours" of the weekdays, and the "living day" is holy—an example for them. To elevate the flow from the lower to the upper, the Upper One must "incline His ear to hear."

The matter of "hearing" is the gathering of the unification, as in "And Saul heard..." <note>1 Samuel 15:4</note>. Furthermore, you must know that "Voice" (*Kol*) is only in *Tiferet*, as explained in the *Pardes* <term>Sefer Ha-Pardes: "The Garden," a seminal Kabbalistic work by Moshe Cordovero</term> under the entry for "Voice." "Grace" (*Chaninah*) is in *Malchut* from the side of *Binah*. So wrote the *Pardes* regarding "Grace": "The explanation is *Malchut*. Aside from this, every language of prayer is *Malchut*, and it is called *Techinah* (Supplication) from the side of *Binah*, from the language of 'Gracious' (*Channun*) and one who asks, even if he is not worthy." For it is written: "The poor man speaks supplications," and "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious," even if he is not worthy—this is from the side of *Binah*, from which comes the "Free Gift" <term>Matnat Chinam: Unearned Divine favor</term>.

Behold, the Name of *Havayah* (the Tetragrammaton) is hinted at here... *Chokhmah* is *Malchut*, as is known. "Voice" is *Tiferet*. "The cords of death encompassed me," for regarding the days... this is the secret... and I shall call upon the Name of the Lord... on this he prayed... my soul... God Y-H, God 52 (N-B)... and Y-H-V-H hints... and in the Name of Y-H-V-H all the messengers... for service...

# Tractate Pesachim

### The Tenth Matzah
The Matzah of the commandment—even before the seed of Abraham was commanded—is significant. For it was Abraham who removed himself from the "East" <note>original: מקדמונו של עולם - a play on words meaning both "the East" and "the Ancient of the World/God"</note> and said, "I have no desire for my father Terah nor his gods," as Rashi explains on the verse, "And Lot journeyed from the East." Furthermore, great contemplation is needed to observe the deeds of God, who brought forth all the righteous women, our holy mothers, from Haran, the father of Lot. For Sarah was the daughter of Haran, as our Sages of blessed memory said <note>Sarah is traditionally identified with Iscah, daughter of Haran</note>. Haran was also the father of Milkah, who gave birth to Bethuel, who fathered Rebecca; he also fathered Laban, whose daughters were Rachel and Leah. Likewise, Ruth the Moabitess, the mother of the Davidic dynasty, and the Messiah himself, descended from Lot, the son of Haran. Truly, who can stand within the secret counsel of God? Nevertheless, I will present my opinion on all the above as far as my intellect can reach. 

First, I will preface what our Sages said: "Rabbi Levi said: 'And I will make you a great nation'—this refers to saying 'God of Abraham'; 'And I will bless you'—this refers to 'God of Isaac'; 'And I will make your name great'—this refers to 'God of Jacob.' One might think we should conclude the blessing with all of them, but the verse says 'And you shall be a blessing'—with you (Abraham) we conclude, and not with all of them" <term>The "Seal" of the first blessing of the Amidah prayer ends only with "Shield of Abraham"</term>. I have already written that the three Patriarchs publicized three fundamentals. Our father Abraham publicized the existence of God and that He guides the world. This explains the Midrash I mentioned: "Go forth (Lech Lecha)... Rabbi Isaac said: This is like a man traveling from place to place who saw a **lit palace**. He said, 'Can it be that this palace has no leader?' The owner of the palace looked out at him and said, 'I am the owner of the palace.' So too, because our father Abraham said, 'Can it be that the world has no leader?' the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked out at him and said, 'I am the Master of the world.'" 

The "newness of the world" <term>Creation ex nihilo: the belief that the world was created at a specific point in time</term>, which came about through Divine will, was for the sake of Abraham. As the Sages said: "'These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created (*be-hibare'am*)'—read it as 'for Abraham' (*be-abraham*)." Through the "newness of the world," the existence of God becomes known, as the "Master Teacher" <note>Maimonides (Rambam)</note> wrote in *The Guide for the Perplexed*, Part 2, Chapter 13: "Know that everyone who believes in the Torah of Moses our teacher believes that the world was created... that God brought it into existence after absolute non-existence." He further wrote in Part 1, Chapter 71: "If the world is 'new' (created), it certainly has a Renewer (Creator). This is a primary logical premise, for that which is 'new' does not create itself." 

Thus, the Rabbi explains that through the faith in Creation, we arrive at the existence of God through primary logic. Now, regarding Nimrod, he cast Abraham into the fiery furnace. What was the issue he held in doubt? He said, "If Abraham wins, I am of his; if I win..." as Rashi explains. Nimrod rebelled against the existence of God; he certainly did not believe in the Creation of the world by a Creator who has the power to change nature. Rather, he believed the world was "primordial" (eternal) and followed the path of Adam at the time of the Serpent's temptation. He believed the Serpent's words: "From this tree He ate and created the world," assuming there was a primordial matter from which the world was made—namely, the Tree of Knowledge. In this matter, Nimrod "clothed" himself in the garments of the first Adam, which he received and coveted. As the Zohar says: "He was a mighty hunter before the Lord... Come and see: he was a 'mighty' opposite of his garments... he knew how to trap creatures... he said he was the ruler of the world and people should worship him. Why was he called Nimrod? Because he rebelled (*merad*) against the Supernal King..." 

-> **HE RULED** <-

### Guarded Matzah
...was hidden from him.
Furthermore, they compared the completion of the body of Eve <note>This likely refers to a mystical configuration of the soul or the structure of the commandments</note>, which consists of the 613 commandments <term>Taryag Mitzvot: The 613 total commandments in the Torah</term>. At the beginning of the Psalm, it says "To Your name give glory," and now it says "The Lord has been mindful of us; He will bless." This follows the path mentioned in the Zohar: "The letters *Yod* and *He* (YH) with 'My Name' equals 365; *Yod* and *He* with 'My Remembrance' equals 248" <note>A famous gematria/numerical calculation linking God's name to the 365 negative and 248 positive commandments</note>. This is "To Your name" and "Our remembrance." 

Israel represents the secret of "Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah" <term>The three primary levels of the soul: Soul, Spirit, and Breath</term>. Praiseworthy are the righteous who cling—Nefesh to Ruach, Ruach to Neshamah, and Neshamah to the Holy One, Blessed be He. "The small with the great" refers to the secret of the "Large Face" and "Small Face" <term>Partzufim: Mystical configurations of the Divine attributes</term>. We find this below among Israel as well; some children are at the level of the "great ones," as found in Tractate Hagigah: "He saw a child of six years who was [learned]..." and we find a child who was expounding on the "Work of the Chariot" <term>Ma'aseh Merkavah: The highest form of Jewish mysticism</term>. Also, the famous "Child" (*Yenuka*) mentioned in the Zohar. If you ask, "How did he learn?" it is not a difficulty. In Tractate Taanit, it says that a certain Rabbi answered, "I have looked into it, it is not a difficulty." "The Lord shall increase you a thousandfold"—the Holy One, Blessed be He, adds to him from there. Even if they are not yet fully realized, God considers them as if they exist. 

This is the meaning of "And Joseph was..." and perhaps it follows the secret of the "Hard Sphere." He says in double language: "The Lord shall increase you and your children; your children and you." This hints that for one who is already "great," the Holy One adds to him as if he were even greater in years, like Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah who said, "I am like a seventy-year-old" <note>He was only 18 but miraculously grew a white beard to look older when appointed head of the Sanhedrin</note>. "And your children"—even those who have not reached greatness and are still children, like the "Child" who expounded on the Chariot.

"Blessed are you to the Lord, Maker of Heaven and Earth." To explain this, we must preface a teaching from the Zohar on the Torah portion of Bereshit (Genesis): Rabbi Simeon opened and said: "'And I have placed My words in your mouth'—how much must a person labor in the Torah day and night! For the Holy One, Blessed be He, listens to the voice of those who engage in Torah. With every new word of Torah produced by one who labors in it, He creates a **New Heaven**." 

We have learned: At that moment when a word of Torah is renewed from the mouth of a person, that word ascends and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He. The Holy One takes that word, kisses it, and crowns it with seventy engraved and carved crowns. A word of wisdom that is renewed ascends and sits upon the head of the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds" <term>The Sefirah of Yesod</term>. From there, it flies and soars through 20,000 worlds and ascends to the **Ancient of Days** <term>Atik Yomin: The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</term>. All the words of the Ancient of Days are words of wisdom, hidden supernal secrets. When this hidden word of wisdom—renewed here below—ascends, it joins those words of the Ancient of Days. It ascends and joins Him, entering 18 hidden worlds which "no eye has seen, O God, beside You."

They go out from there, soaring as complete and perfect words, and they stand before the Ancient of Days. At that moment, the Ancient of Days "smells" that word, and it is more pleasing to Him than anything. He takes that word and crowns it with 370,000 crowns. The word flies, ascending and descending, and is formed into a **New Heaven**. From every single word of wisdom, permanent heavens are created, standing in full existence before the Ancient of Days. He calls them "New Heavens"—renewed from the hidden secrets of Supernal Wisdom. All other words of Torah that are renewed stand before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and ascend to become "Lands of the Living" (New Earths). 

This is why it is written: "For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I **make**, shall remain before Me." It does not say "I have made," but "I make" (in the present tense)—He makes them constantly from those innovations and secrets of the Torah. Regarding this, it is written: "And I have placed My words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of My hand." They told him: At the time the Torah was given to Moses, many tens of thousands of supernal angels came to burn him with the flame of their mouths, until the Holy One, Blessed be He, covered him. Now, when this [new] word ascends and is crowned, standing before the Holy One, He covers that word and covers that person so he is not known to them and they do not envy him, until that word is made into a New Heaven and a New Earth. 

This is the meaning of "I have covered you." Why is it hidden and covered? For a high purpose: "To plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, 'You are My people' (*Ammi Atah*)." Do not read it as "My people" (*Ammi*), but as "With Me" (*Immi Atah*)—to be My partner. Just as I made heaven and earth with My speech, so too do you. Happy are those who labor in the Torah! 

But what if a person speaks a word of Torah that he does not truly know? Come and see: if a person renews words that are not correct, that word ascends and a "lying tongue" goes out to meet it from the "hole of the Great Abyss." It travels five hundred parasangs <term>An ancient unit of distance</term> to receive that word, takes it, and returns with it to a false firmament called "Tohu" (Chaos). That word is twisted through 6,000 parasangs in a single moment. As soon as that false firmament goes out, the "Woman of Harlotry" <note>A personification of impurity/evil</note> immediately takes hold of it and participates in it. From there, she goes out and kills many thousands and tens of thousands, for this false firmament has the permission and power to fly through the whole world in a single instant. His soul, and this is the essence of reward and punishment. I have already written that even punishment stems from His goodness, may He be blessed. In this light, we can explain the story in Alexandria: The Sages of Israel understood that the Egyptians who complained before Alexander the Great <note>original: "אלכסנדרוס"</note> argued, "We were revealed and we were sold," and they wanted to bring a claim against Israel. Why do they bring the verse "The Lord gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians" and so on, but did not stop at the previous verse "And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses, and they requested from the Egyptians vessels of silver and vessels of gold and clothing"? According to the order of generations, Israel would seemingly be robbers, God forbid! For if God created the world, then by His will He gave it, and by His will He took it <note>This echoes Rashi’s first comment on Genesis</note>. But only after they saw signs and wonders did they recognize the existence of God, the renewal of the world, His providence, and His power. With this, it is well known among the masses that I will explain... Even if Alexander were to say to the Egyptians: "According to your reasoning, do you not admit to the Renewal of the World?" he would still have to agree with their words, for his own opinion was even further removed. 

Now I will explain the reasoning of those who brought them out: It is true that the Blessed Name renewed the world, watches over it, and can change its course. Nevertheless, at the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave power and ability to the "Host of Heaven" <note>astrological forces</note> to lead the world, and every star is appointed over world affairs as its custom goes. This is their foundation and secret—unless at some time He wishes to change and alter them. As long as He does not change them, they lead by the power He placed in them at the time of creation. However, the truth of faith is that the Blessed Name "renews in His goodness every day, constantly, the work of Creation" <note>A phrase from the morning liturgy</note> with deliberate intent. If God were to withhold His flow for one moment, everything would cease to be and existence would be nullified. This is the meaning of the verse: "And you shall know this day and take it to your heart, that the Lord is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is none else." My interpretation of "there is none else" is not just that there is no other god, which is the plain meaning and explained in the verse "Hear O Israel," but rather it means there is no other *existence* in the world besides His existence, may He be blessed. For if He hides Himself, everything perishes. And when it says "He gave them strength and power to be rulers in the midst of the world," it does not mean they are independent actors, but only that they have the power of "readiness" to receive—just as the eye is ready to see when the flow of sight is given to it, and so the ear to hear, and so all limbs, each for its service, through the power of the heavenly arrangement. Power and strength were given to them as long as the flow is given to them; they act according to their nature, whether for good or for evil. "Changing the arrangement" means that even while the flow is given to them and they exist, they are made to act contrary to their nature. 

Behold, the Egyptians, according to their reasoning, thought that as long as the heavenly arrangement is not changed, His hand is, as it were, removed; thus, the one who receives the flow from the arrangement "owns" it. Even if the Creator, may He be blessed, chooses to change it, that change for that day is a "sale" <note>meaning God legally transferred the power to the stars</note>. Therefore, they cried out and said, "the judgment of the Holy One, blessed be He—is it not law and logic?" "According to his wickedness"—meaning you obligate a person for one act of wickedness, but you do not obligate him for two acts of wickedness <note>A legal principle in the Talmud: *Kam lei b'diraba minei* - one receives only the greater of two punishments</note>, as seen in Tractates Ketubot and Makkot. If so, why were the Egyptians punished with both death and loss of money at the Sea? And why were those who remained punished with both lashes and loss of money? For even they were struck, as Rashi writes in the portion of *Beshalach*. Of course, according to our true faith, this is not a question at all, for He always flows to him, and it is irrelevant to say He absolutely abandoned them and took money from them; He merely withheld money from them. But the Egyptians wanted to prove that this was not the case. If so, why is it written "He gave the people favor"? Among the nations, who are stuck in the heavenly arrangement, our Sages said: "If one intended to perform a transgression but did not do it, it is credited to him as if he had done it" <note>The text here seems to invert the usual rule for Jews, applying it to nations who follow the 'potentiality' of the stars</note>, for in the Supernal Daughter there is only potential. He added... saying that since it is potential and he intended to do it, it is as if he did it. Behold the reward for 600,000 workers—meaning years. And even if the money we took was for the reward of our labors while we were in Egypt, nevertheless, we seek the reward for the full 400 years, and they were not...

<column-break/>

And everything is for his good, to be credited to him in his end in the World to Come. That is, the "principal remains" etc. But the latter ones rob, saying with the first letter *He*, which is the *He* of Understanding <note>Binah</note>, the secret of the Name... the light of the fifty, the *He* of Favor <note>Chanina</note> from the side of Understanding. From there he receives... and this is "Gracious" <note>Channun</note>, may He be blessed, and He flows to the Tzadik <note>The Righteous One</note> who is the "Foundation of the World" <note>Yesod Olam</note>. It is performed through the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> which is called "Our God." This is "Salvation," and "Our God" is their attribute. That is to say, what you think is Judgment is actually Mercy. "The Lord preserves the simple" <note>Psalm 116:6</note>. And this is the sign for you, for "your sword is internal." "The Lord preserves," and what it says about "the simple" is according to what our Sages said... everything is a miracle mentioned in miracles. And what He flows sometimes as Judgment... "I was brought low, and He saved me." On the contrary, it is essentially for my salvation, so that "my soul may return to its rest." And "the Lord has dealt bountifully with you." "You have delivered my soul from death"—essentially free. "My eyes from tears"—for He will fulfill the renewal of sight... "my feet from stumbling"—they will return and you will have "walkways among those who stand" <note>Zechariah 3:7</note>. Not only this, but even more: "barking in the... to be before Me from the partition of those who stand." And this is "I will walk before the Lord"—meaning, inside the partition—"in the lands of the living." This refers to the World to Come, as we learned: "All Israel have a portion in the World to Come, as it is said: 'And your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.'" These are the eternal lives of which it is said "and lived by them in the World to Come." "I believed" that I would merit the lands of the living when I spoke "I was greatly afflicted"—meaning when I suffered poverty in this world. Just as I answered "Peace" concerning the... they are what bring one to the World to Come. However, what I said against the "observant pious one"—"I said in my haste, 'All men are deceitful'"—this is the secret of "for I believed now that it is not so."

# What
"What shall I return to the Lord..." <note>Psalm 116:12</note>—against the... the general rule of the world. And now David speaks for himself, for he is worthy of the "forty lashes" <note>Malkot - 39 lashes given as punishment</note> that we are dealing with... Therefore he specified matters concerning himself... and mentioned by hint "the cup" twice. "I will lift up the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord." For twice he will give thanks for it. And it is the custom of those who engage in... in this Psalm. And the matter of twice "the cup of the Lord I call" is once for before he sinned and once after he sinned. It hints that all the events that happened to him were all transformed for the good. "I will lift up the cup of salvations" and "I will call upon the name of the Lord"—mentioning two salvations that came to the generation, and afterward turned to him for honor and glory. The first: because the order of the Moabites came, and they were debating at the beginning if he was fit to "enter the congregation" <note>marry into the Jewish people</note>, until the law was decided: "A Moabite man [is forbidden], but not a Moabite woman." The second: that which occurred in the "Exchange" <note>the story of David's birth</note> as seen in the Midrash: Jesse had refrained from lying with his wife, but he had a handmaid in the house, and she said to the mistress... "my mistress, you are hollowed out, and Jesse is with me... come and you shall not... lie in my bed, and he will lie with you tonight." And so it was. "The God of Jesse... from... and this is 'I am your servant, the son of your handmaid'" <note>Psalm 116:16</note>. And they were both transformed into greatness, for they came from Ruth the Moabite...

# Fourth Homily, Tenth Commandment
## Homily for the Great Sabbath <note>The Sabbath immediately preceding Passover, known for lengthy sermons on the laws and themes of the holiday.</note>

**In the Midrash** <note>original: "במדרש"</note>, Rabbi Abba bar Yudan said: Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, disqualified in an animal, He qualified in a human. He disqualified in an animal: one that is blind, or broken, or has a split eyelid, or a wart; yet He qualified in a human: "a broken and contrite heart" <note>original: "לב נשבר ונדכה" — Psalm 51:19</note>.

(Blessed be the Name, for as it relates to the exalted, regarding one who is lowly... a broken and contrite heart is not considered a blemish but is rather more humble and submissive. One is the opposite of the other. The reason for this is that everything He disqualified in an animal—there is a distinction to be made between a sacrifice, which is like bringing a gift to a king, where the gift must be a perfect vessel, and a prayer. When you pray a word of prayer, the prayer of a poor person is more [acceptable] because he is more humble and more broken at the thresholds. This is how it should be answered according to the plain meaning.)

---

**"It is the burnt offering** <note>original: "היא העולה"</note> on its flame" <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. And behold, "a smoking furnace" <note>Genesis 15:17</note>. In the Midrash *Exodus Rabbah*, section *Pekudei*, chapter 21: The Holy One, Blessed be He, showed our forefather Abraham the Torah, Gehenna <note>term: Gehenna — the place of spiritual purification or punishment after death</note>, the Sacrifices, and the Kingdoms <note>The four historical empires that would exile Israel: Babylonia, Persia, Greece, and Rome</note>, as it is said... until "He brought us out to freedom." We must ask: It makes sense why Gehenna and the distress [of exile] were shown first, as "The Torah of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul," and even the way of the sphere of fire—for the fire of Torah, which is a "fiery law," extinguishes this [spiritual] fire. And the reverse is true. But regarding the "Kingdoms" <note>the exiles</note>, in what way do they correspond to the cancellation of the Sacrifices? Furthermore, it is difficult: why would one request one of these [exile or Gehenna]? Both are bad. This question is simple to answer: clearly Gehenna is worse than the Kingdoms, as King David (peace be upon him) said, "Let us fall into the hand of the Lord, for His mercies are great" <note>2 Samuel 24:14</note>. This only applies during life, because of freedom and repentance; but after death, in Gehenna, there is no repentance.

<margin>Repentance is not possible in Gehenna.</margin>
**"Upon its flame"** and so on, "fire on the Altar," etc. "I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans." In *Midrash Rabbah* at the beginning of section *Toldot*: "Isaac stood as a focus [of merit] for his descendants; the Patriarchs stood..." until "Jacob redeemed Abraham." This is difficult: it begins with two—the Patriarchs standing for the children and the children for the Patriarchs—but it only concludes with the case of Jacob redeeming [Abraham], which is children for the Patriarchs. Furthermore, what does it mean to say he "redeemed"? The relationship between fathers and children implies that it is not like a created angel... but a father does not save a son, as it says in Tractate Sanhedrin, chapter *Chelek*: "Hezekiah does not save [Manasseh]." Patriarchs do not save children—not Abraham for Ishmael, nor Isaac for Esau. Furthermore, it should have been Abraham, the "Head of Believers," whose merit justifies Jacob, for he is the primary root! And in his merit, it says "Jacob," etc. Furthermore, there is a redundancy in language regarding the future... later, why does it say Abraham is saved in the merit of Jacob? This is explained by saying that Abraham was worthy, and only afterward is it hung on the merit of Jacob. It is a commandment to tell of the Exodus from Egypt, "even if we are all wise." We must investigate several points: Who can truly tell [the whole story]? Only three "partners" are mentioned: the Holy One, Blessed be He, who decreed the exile and then became the Redeemer (as He said, "I Shall Be"); the second partner, Pharaoh and the oppressors; and the third partner, the oppressed Israelites. Regarding the investigation of the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Whatever He does, He does for the good"—so why did He decree this enslavement? I have already written the words of the commentators above in my first homily. We should also investigate why the decree was carried out through Abraham His beloved, and concluded through Jacob. Our Sages of blessed memory said in *Genesis Rabbah*: Rabbi Judah said, "Jacob was worthy of descending [to Egypt] in iron chains and collars, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed many maneuvers so he would descend there [honorably]," as it is said, "Joseph was sold as a slave" and "He called a famine upon the land." Why all this? "So that Israel should come to Egypt." Rabbi Pinhas said: This is like a cow they want to lead to the slaughterhouse <note>original: "מקולין" — butchery/slaughterhouse</note>, but she will not be led. What do they do? They pull her calf before her, and she runs after it. So did the Holy One, Blessed be He, lead Joseph to Egypt so that Jacob would follow him, as it is said: "I drew them with human cords, with bonds of love" <note>Hosea 11:4</note>. One must ask: what was his sin that he deserved [chains]? And what is written there—"with bonds of love"—is this love? The entire matter of Abraham was a hint to Israel in Egypt, as Nachmanides <note>original: "הרמב'ן"</note> wrote: Abraham descended to Egypt, Sarah was taken to Pharaoh, the Lord plagued him, and afterward he left with great wealth. So it happened to Israel. Rabbi Pinhas already said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Abraham, "Go and pave the way for your children." It began with Abraham and concluded with Jacob. Also, regarding the Redemption, we must investigate why it was not a "true redemption" <note>i.e., final</note> since it was followed by exile, but was rather like a female <note>referring to the Hebrew grammar of "Shira" (song) being feminine</note>, as the Sages said that the song [at the sea] is founded in feminine language. And as the Midrash explains regarding the "Song of Songs," that there were three stages of the revelation of the Kingship. The poet already lamented this matter: "I pursued the year of my redemption, and it was lacking." This is an investigation into the decree of God and the Redemption. Regarding Pharaoh the oppressor, we must ask why everything is dependent on the heart: "I will harden Pharaoh's heart," "he made his heart heavy." There are many teachings on this. Regarding the oppressed Israelites, we must ask: Are they not the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? The Study Hall never ceased from our ancestors, as the Sages said; so how did these holy people succumb to [Egyptian] faith <note>or "lose their faith"</note> even though they saw great signs until the splitting of the sea? It was only then that they "believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant." Even shortly after, when Moses told them to return to Egypt, they did so... though they showed they left with their hearts [still there]... it is a known rule: when Israel was good, they called him "Our Teacher Moses"; when they complained, they called him "The son of Amram" <note>Moses' father</note>. We could explain this simply: the laws were given by day, as the Sages said, and "the days passed"—how does "the son of Amram" change this for us? The good among them said, "You say 'son of Amram,' but we have nothing but the words of the son of Amram." This also hinted that Israel was not yet pure... Therefore, it was necessary to separate the investigations of the three partners. I will also explain the reason for the seven days of Passover, the prohibition of leaven <note>chametz</note>, and the eating of Matzah, which is only [obligatory] at the beginning, in the evening. And the seven cups, and the Paschal lamb, Matzah, and Maror <note>bitter herbs</note>. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Joshua disagree: Rabbi Eliezer holds the world was created in Tishrei <note>Autumn</note>, and Rabbi Joshua holds the world was created in Nisan <note>Spring/Passover season</note>. It has already been said of every dispute between Jewish Sages: "These and these are the words of the Living God." It is difficult: how can there be such a dispute according to the plain meaning? In Nisan, there are prohibitions and permissions, innocent and guilty, impure and pure... although the law follows one side, sometimes a cause arises where we join the other opinion... But regarding a physical action that was done—what was done, was done! The truth is there is a great and awesome secret in Creation, that both are true in the secret of "the birth of the month." However, to settle it according to the plain meaning: the purpose of Creation was for man, who is the form of the worlds. Even according to Rabbi Eliezer, we say "This day is the beginning of Your works," referring to the creation of Adam, for though the world was created on the 25th of Tishrei, Adam—who is of both the upper and lower worlds—was born on the 10th of Tammuz <note>This date varies in different traditions</note>. The intellectual, eternal soul descended into the body, as it will be in the eternal future, body and soul together, according to the opinion of Nachmanides and his school. I have elaborated on this in *Ateret HaKodesh* in other homilies and here, though I only record the main points here. "Man does not abide in glory" <note>Psalm 49:13</note> because of the woman who enticed him via the Serpent and Samael <note>term: Samael — the name of the accusing angel/Satan</note> the rider. Then the strength of the world was weakened into the "female" state, whereas it should have been a "male" world. The woman is a branch of her husband, for "she was taken from man," and the physical matter was pure and thin. And because they were enticed toward evening—"and it was evening and it was morning, the sixth day"—the Sages said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, made a condition. The works of Creation were hanging in the balance until the sixth day of Sivan <note>the day the Torah was given</note>. The earth feared and then was still. Until then, the world was shaky because the purpose of Creation was for Man, yet Man was compared to the animals. Until Abraham came, the "Head of the Believers," and he began... the secret of Abraha**m** <note>original: "אברה'ם"</note>, the acronym for **A**dam, **O**x, **E**agle, **C**herub <note>referring to the Four Faces of the Divine Chariot in Ezekiel</note>, as I explained in my homilies for the Great Sabbath. He was the "great man among giants." This is what the Sages meant by "In their being created" (*be-hibare'am*)—for the sake of Abraham (*be-Abraham*). The world was created, and [the holiness] continued through Abraham, Isaac... until Jacob, whose beauty was like the beauty of Adam, and whose form is engraved under the Throne of Glory. And on the hint of the Throne: "as the appearance of the likeness of a man." His bed was "perfect" <note>all his children were righteous</note>, and from him came the 600,000 holy souls <note>term: 600,000 — the traditional number of adult males at the Exodus, representing the totality of the Jewish people</note> which were the collective soul of Man. At the giving of the Torah, they separated from women because she had brought the ruin; but Moses our Teacher, the perfect intermediary, was separated from his wife entirely. He was the one who represented the 600,000 souls... and this is what is meant by "one woman in Egypt gave birth to 600,000" <note>referring to Jochebed giving birth to Moses, who was equal to the whole nation</note>. The opposite is found in Tractate Bekhorot...

It discusses the "three partners" in the Egyptian exile—God, Pharaoh, and Israel—and delves into the midrashic idea that Jacob's merit redeemed Abraham.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Passover liturgy and the spiritual symbolism of the Matzah, transitioning from the general laws of the holiday to the deeper Kabbalistic meanings of the Hallel prayer and the distinction between Matzah Shmurah (guarded matzah) and Matzah Ashirah (enriched matzah).</meta>

# Tractate Pesachim

## Guarded Matzah <note>term: Matzah Shmurah — Matzah made from grain that has been "guarded" from moisture from the moment of harvest to ensure no leavening occurs.</note>

<margin>
(Masekhet Pesachim) ... [This margin note consists of a long string of traditional Hebrew abbreviations, likely referring to specific page numbers, gematria (numerical values), or Kabbalistic ciphers that denote spiritual "measures" or cross-references to other texts.] ... his kingdom ... Jerusalem ... the world ... foundation ... the world of the Throne ...
</margin>

In truth, the matter is such that even the nations of the world admit and testify to the greatness of Israel and their attachment to the inner holiness through the secret of the Name <note>original: "יו"ד ה"י" — a two-letter form of the Divine Name</note>, the "Gates of Light." The seventy celestial princes <note>In Jewish tradition, each of the seventy nations has a celestial representative or "Prince."</note> are attached to Abraham and Isaac, for there the names *El* and *Elohim* are found, but not to Jacob, who represents the secret of the attribute of the Four-Letter Name <note>The Tetragrammaton (Y-H-V-H)</note>, may He be known. For from the "left side" of the First Man <note>Adam HaRishon</note>, the lowliness turns toward the realm of Action <note>term: Asiyah — the lowest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah, representing our physical reality.</note> for all the Princes and even for the filthy and external forces. Within the "drop" <note>the seed of life</note> there was leavening and the filth that the Serpent cast into the forces. Even though these matters are very deep, when the body of the First Man was made, it was meant to remove that filth, but it did not finish removing the filth from the beauty of Adam until it was cast out little by little through the righteous ones of the generations, like a smith refining metal in a furnace. 

How so? The time came when it was slightly engraved, as it is said: "He came in His likeness and His image," and he was called by the name of the daughter of Enoch—who was very old and strong—and "Enoch walked with God" <note>Genesis 5:24</note>. It came with even more strength as it is said, "Noah walked with God" <note>Genesis 6:9</note>. Then it came through Shem, who was even older, as it says, "And he dwelt in the tents of Shem." Then came Abraham, and he was even more refined, even though a bit of filth still emerged from him <note>a reference to Ishmael</note>. Then came Isaac, even more so, though a bit of filth still emerged from him <note>a reference to Esau</note>. Thus, it was found that the lineage emerged more refined, entirely good and without blemish. 

Thus, Jacob represented the "strength" of the First Man. Therefore, Jacob was afraid to dwell in the depths <note>Sheol</note> to depart from the world, lest there be any dross in him as there was in the lineage of Abraham and Isaac. He cried out, and they all said, "Hear O Israel..." <note>The Shema: "Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One."</note> meaning that the bit of filth from Abraham and Isaac was given to Ishmael and Esau and the Princes over them—this one on the right and that one on the left, this one in the likeness of white and that one in the likeness of black. But Jacob is the structure in the center, in the Name of the Lord. For His kindness has prevailed over us, and the truth of the Lord shall be forever. And the attribute of Truth is well known—"You give truth to Jacob and kindness <gloss>to Abraham</gloss>"—to the Lord for He is good, for His kindness is everlasting. 

This Psalm <note>Psalm 118, part of the Hallel prayer</note> is like a "repetition of the Torah," repeating what was mentioned in the first four books <gloss>and behold, the 28 [Hebrew letters] of kindness</gloss>. Regarding the unfolding of the Four Worlds <note>Atziluth, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah</note>: "Give thanks to the Lord for He is good" refers to the World of Emanation <note>Atziluth</note>. Afterward, He returned strength to the assembly of Israel and mentioned the Exodus from Egypt. Perhaps this is for the sake of Israel's priority. It is known that the secret of "all" includes the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshama <note>term: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama — the three lower levels of the soul, corresponding to action, emotion, and intellect.</note>, as explained at length in the "Gates of Light" regarding the secret of the 100 Blessings. It is known that these levels of the soul exist within the worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action, and everything is included in the Four-Letter Name. Therefore, the congregation repeats and says every time: "Give thanks to the Lord for He is good, for His kindness is everlasting." 

"Out of the depths I called to the Lord" <note>Psalm 118:5</note>—this is a prayer for the Name to be complete, for now, in the time of the "depths" (distress), I called upon the name *Ya* <note>Y-H</note>, and as it were, the letters *V-H* are missing. "The Lord answered me with expansiveness"—that the name *Ya* should expand to its full spelling <note>term: Miluy — a Kabbalistic method of spelling out letters (e.g., Yud as Y-V-D) to reveal hidden numerical values.</note>. *Ya* spelled out equals 26, which is the structure of the Four-Letter Name. "The Lord is for me, I shall not fear..." and this is the matter of salvation, that we should not fear their "Princes." Afterward, the Psalmist adds: "Not only this, but even that—I shall see vengeance upon my enemies." He says, "I shall see," and not "the Lord shall take vengeance," for this is an addition—that his eyes should live to see it, as in the secret of the verse, "Happy is he who... good to take refuge in the Lord." 

Adam was a "shekel" <note>a weight/currency</note> that included the "Unique One" and the seventy Princes who surround us. Those Princes who stand to the right are for us and our children, and the practice for the left is that they do not give even to their own nation except through the image of hardship. But we are built in spirit, and it is good to merit it from the powers in man. "All nations surrounded me" <note>Psalm 118:10</note>—with the Name above (the Tetragrammaton) in the center and the Princes surrounding it. So too below, the nations surrounded me, as it is written, "I have placed Jerusalem in the midst of the nations." Just as above, "I saw the Lord sitting on His throne and all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left," so too this phrase "surrounded me" is mentioned three times with the Name of the Lord.

And it says: Say and repeat in this Psalm three times. Know that seventy Princes were given to them... and they are four "husks" <note>term: Qlipot — "shells" or "husks" that conceal divine light and represent forces of impurity.</note> that separate Israel from the Lord, as it is written: "Your iniquities have separated [you from your God]." Three of them are "hard husks" to which Ezekiel hinted: "a stormy wind, a great cloud, and a fire flaring up" <note>Ezekiel 1:4</note>. Under these three, the earth quakes. The fourth husk is not so hard and approaches closer to holiness; Ezekiel hinted at it with: "and a brightness was around it." Thus, there are four that surround, and three are hard husks. Regarding them, it says three times "they surrounded me," to signify the cutting off of these husks. 

I have already elaborated on this in many places, for the deficiencies I had I have raised through the book "Gates of Light" in a broad summary. "You pushed me hard that I might fall, but the Lord helped me" <note>Psalm 118:13</note>—this hints at the merit of David which falls in exile, and the Lord Himself will raise it up, as it says: "Now I will arise, says the Lord." This happens at the time of the redemption, and I have explained this at length in its place. "The Lord is my strength and song..." I have already elaborated in many places that the deficiencies in exile and the light within us are all a "garment" and a benefit to remember our matter. We shall have light before the exiles, and light from the power of the "Sukkah of darkness" in which we sat in the dark. 

This is the secret of the "name" that was not complete, and because of this we walked in darkness. This shall be for us a salvation, and there shall be a "voice of rejoicing and salvation." It awakens the "right side," which is Kindness, and mentions "the right hand" three times, for such is the line of Kindness—threefold: Wisdom, Kindness, and Victory <note>Chokhmah, Chesed, Netzach</note>. In the future, the generations will return to the intention that was at the Creation, when man was meant to live forever. 

I elaborated on this inquiry in the book *Me'or* in the introduction to *Toledot Adam*. This is the meaning of "I shall not die, but live." "Open for me the gates of righteousness"—this is the attribute of Sovereignty <note>Malchut</note>, for the sovereignty shall be the Lord's. Indeed, "the builders rejected the stone"—meaning the Sovereignty that descended into exile, as it were, in the secret of the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> in exile. The "builders" above rejected it because the supernal flow was diminished from being in the secret of union. But in the future, they will say and live: "It has become the chief cornerstone," for its light will increase like the light of the moon becoming like the light of the sun. "This was from the Lord"—this is the Sovereignty called "This" (*Zat*), for "from man was *this* taken," the secret of connection and union. "This is the day the Lord has made..." Behold, now this day is light, and the day has brightness for the night. 

In the future, the "night shall shine like the day," like a woman with her husband. He spoke of two: "This day" and "This" <note>Zeh and Zot</note> shall be joined, and it is called a "new day" and "this day." This is the secret of the "New Song" in the masculine language. With a prayer that the poor, surrounded, and spoken-for one should come quickly: *Aga Aga* <note>a mystical acronym or name</note>. *Aga* equals the numerical value of "Friend" (*Yedid*) times the Name of the Lord. This is the four-fold expansion... he mentioned the Name of the Lord four times: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord," "We bless you from the house of the Lord," "The Lord is God and He gave us light," and the conclusion of the Psalm is like its opening—giving thanks to the Four-Letter Name for the four, and ending with what he opened: "Give thanks to the Lord for He is good, for His kindness is everlasting." Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders. Amen.

<column-break/>

<margin>
...he shall not spend the night, but it is very good for him. This merit is precious in the eyes of the Lord, as I have elaborated elsewhere. The goal of everything is the secret with which it concludes: "In the courtyards of the House of the Lord, in the midst of Jerusalem, Hallelujah"—which is the Land of the Living and the Supernal Jerusalem. Behold, the Psalms are explained based on the foundations of the four letters, and the name David in its full spelling, which hints at the four worlds and the levels of the Torah: the soul of the soul, the soul, the body, and the garment. It is all deep, deep, who can find it? For even the "garment," which are the mundane stories as they appear, are deeper than the sea and awaken wonderful secrets. This is salvation. They also hint at wonderful secrets as the Zohar elaborated; they are like the image of the Holy One's conduct of the World of Action, which is a world of transformation from judgment to mercy and from expansion to judgment. No human understands the nature of this conduct, and the words of the prophets complained about "the righteous who suffers and the wicked who prospers." However, we know that all His ways are justice, a God of faithfulness without iniquity, righteous and upright is He. "Praise the Lord, all nations; laud Him, all [peoples]..."
</margin>

## Enriched Matzah <note>term: Matzah Ashirah — Matzah made with liquids other than water (like wine, oil, or honey). While allowed in some circumstances, it is generally not used for the obligation of the Seder night.</note>

This is the name of the Holy One, for the Name of Being <note>the Tetragrammaton</note> rises... ten times, five times, six times, five times... this is "Blessed be the Place" <note>a name for God</note>. This corresponds to that, for the "husk" (*qlipah*) is like a monkey (*kof*) before a man, and its image is upon the Throne. The "Man" (*Adam*) also hints at the Name of Being in its full spelling: *Yud-He-Aleph-Vav-He-Aleph*, which equals the numerical value of *Adam* (45). This is the secret of the wings and the hundred maidservants, and then the husks are annulled in general and in particular. 

For all this, they "work with wool" <note>a metaphor for spiritual refinement</note>. It is known that wool and linen are *Shaatnez* <note>forbidden mixtures</note>. Wool comes from the sacrifice of Abel, who brought wool from the side of holiness, while Cain, from the side of impurity, brought linen. Therefore, in our discussion, this is all "forbidden mixtures" in order to bring the husk into holiness, and in the future, it will return to purity. 

And Samael <note>the personification of evil/the accusing angel</note> shall remain a "widow," as I wrote elsewhere, and everything will turn white—"it is pure." It is written: "Though your sins be [as scarlet], they shall be [white] as wool." This is the hint in what was said about "working with wool," for otherwise, it would be as if a "maidservant inherited from her mistress," which is the secret of the wayward woman, heaven forbid. 

But we, the Assembly of Israel, are His mate, as it is written: "And I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness." Therefore, we are compelled to see that our "blackness" <note>sins/exile</note> will be turned into our merits. Thus is fulfilled: "This is the law of the burnt offering"—"Who is this (*Mi Zot*) rising from the wilderness?"—referring to the redemption from Egypt. "And this is the law of the meal offering"—referring to the future redemption at the time of evening, when there shall be light. Then Elijah the Prophet shall be revealed and answered in his rest. We pray: "Have mercy on our sages and scribes." And the Matzah shall be eaten in a holy place. Israel is holy to the Lord. And fulfill "the light on the fourteenth [of Nisan]," for "at evening time there shall be light." The Kingdom of the House of David rises to the value of *Yedid* (friend/beloved)—return to his kingdom, and the Lord shall be an everlasting light. Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

# Tractate Pesachim
## Enriched Matzah <note>term: Matzah Ashirah — Matzah made with liquids other than water, such as fruit juice or eggs, which is subject to specific laws regarding its use at the Seder.</note>

**"And it is she who has stood for our fathers and for us..."** <note>A central passage of the Passover Haggadah emphasizing God's eternal promise of protection.</note> The plain meaning of the words suggests that this refers back to the preceding phrase: "Blessed is He who keeps His promise to Israel." This promise specifically concerned the Egyptian exile. However, the text then asks: how can we say that in "every single generation" they rise against us, etc.? Furthermore, the passage later says, "Go and learn what Laban the Aramean sought to do," and he existed before the Egyptian exile. Additionally, one might ask: what is the "goodness" in the fact that in every generation they rise against us and the Holy One, Blessed be He, saves us? Would it not be better if they never rose against us at all, so that we would not need a miracle of salvation?

Rather, the matter refers back to "Blessed is He who keeps His promise." This "keeping" or "guarding" refers to the fact that there was never a "true redemption" that was not followed by another exile. To this, the text answers, **"And it is she who stood,"** meaning the "Virgin of Israel" <note>A poetic and Kabbalistic term for the Congregation of Israel or the Divine Presence (Shekhinah).</note> has arisen, but not through a human "He." This is the secret of the verse "I shall arise" <note>original: "אקם"</note>. God said that the redemption was only a temporary cause because Israel was lacking in Torah and Commandments and could not achieve more. This is why in every generation they rise against us. "Go and learn": Pharaoh only sought to destroy the males, for his intent was only "lest they multiply" and he wanted to weaken them. But the "Female" aspect <note>referring to the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> was the essence of the redemption—she stood, she rose, and she remained standing. 

Consider this: this may be the intent of the *Rokeach* <note>Rabbi Eleazar of Worms (c. 1176–1238), a major legalist and mystic.</note> who wrote that one should hold the cup in one's hand while reciting this paragraph, based on the verse "I will lift the cup of salvations and call upon the name of the Lord." Even when "I find trouble and sorrow," I still "call upon the name of the Lord." For redemptions are like the "Female" aspect—the "Cup of Salvations"—followed by trouble. She <note>the Shekhinah</note> walks among the "Living Creatures" <note>term: Chayot — high-ranking angels in Ezekiel's vision.</note> which are four, and she is the fifth "Living Being" over them. This is the secret of the "Great Hand." Every finger is "the finger of God," for this Divine attribute is called *Elohim* in every place. The word "Cup" <note>original: "כוס" (Kos)</note> has the numerical value <note>term: Gematria — the Jewish system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters.</note> of 86, the same as the name *Elohim*. We have only four cups, but their symbolic number is five, corresponding to the final letter *He* of the Divine Name, which is the fourth letter. This is what "saves us from their hand," as is now explained.

Regarding all the inquiries of whether the world was created in the month of Tishrei or Nissan: the days of Passover correspond to the seven days of Creation. The counting <note>referring to the Counting of the Omer</note> is six times six, following the secret of the Sabbatical and Jubilee years, the seven days of the world. Just as the days of Creation hint at seven thousand years of history (as written by Ramban, Rabbeinu Bahya, and the Recanati), the "swift actions" of the Holy One, Blessed be He, correspond to the six days of Creation—six thousand years. 

Now we shall explain the **Four Cups**. Since the Exodus from Egypt was for an ultimate purpose, and the "circles" are circles of love, their removal from Egypt was for the sake of "You shall serve God on this mountain"—meaning the receiving of the Torah. The goal was to bring them to the Land, and the Land is the "Seven." The Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them three gifts through suffering: the Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. For the purpose of the Torah and the Land is the light attached to the vessel for the glory of God. Therefore, there are Four Cups corresponding to four levels that enter into the category of the "World to Come":

1.  **Perfection of the Soul:** This refers to the fourth level of God's will in life, where one attains what Jacob attained after his death, as mentioned in the Zohar.
2.  **The Lower Garden of Eden:** Attained after death, where the soul attaches to the lower spiritual realms.
3.  **The Messianic Era:** When souls will reach the level of "Priests of Light" and will enter the innermost chambers of the "Jerusalem Above."
4.  **The Resurrection of the Dead:** The Great Day of Judgment and eternal victory.

This is the calculation hinted at by the "four wings" of the celestial beings. This is why the composers of the liturgy established the prayer "There is none like You, O Lord our God, in this world," referring to these levels. Some merit the first level but not the second, while some merit the second as well. Every higher level is prioritized.

This also explains a puzzling statement in the *Midrash Rabbah* (Parashat Naso, chapter 14). Rabbi Isaac said in the name of Shmuel: "They sought to burn Solomon..." as is also mentioned in Tractate Sanhedrin (Chapter *Chelek*). It says that a fire came out from the Holy of Holies from Heaven. This raises many questions: why would they want to burn him? The Rabbis held him to be wicked, yet was he not the "Beloved of God" to whom God gave wisdom? Furthermore, why did his hand merit the opening of the Temple gates? <note>Solomon’s father, David, had to be mentioned for the gates to open.</note> He prostrated himself before God to plead for the soul of Solomon his son.

<margin>The Heavenly Court and the Earthly Court</margin> 

One must also ask: why did the fire from the Holy of Holies from Heaven help more than the first times? Why did the fire not come out during the first two attempts? To understand this: at first, they thought that Solomon had not even reached the level of the "World to Come" that exists within this world, for his kingdom on earth was not like the Kingdom of Heaven, unlike his father David. Our Sages said: "Anyone who denies the Davidic monarchy is as if he denies the God of Israel." When the image of David appeared and they prostrated themselves, it was a sign that he was like his father, and his status was restored. However, they still did not believe he reached the second level (the afterlife). When the "fire came out from heaven," it was a sign that Solomon also merited the pleasure of the World to Come. The "fire from the Holy of Holies" is the same as "fire from heaven." They still doubted the third level—the Messianic Era and the Jerusalem Above. But the Sages said: "I will not enter the Jerusalem Above until I enter the Jerusalem Below." Thus, he merited this as well. Finally, regarding the fourth level—the eternal Resurrection—even Samuel the Prophet was afraid of the judgment, as the Sages explain on the verse "I saw gods ascending." But a fire came from the Holy of Holies for this too. God pays a person for the commandment itself, which is eternal, while punishment is not eternal. As King Solomon said: "I kept my ways... I receive an eternal reward from the Commandment."

<margin>I saw this written in the *Sefer HaChayim* by our teacher Rabbi Chaim, the brother of the Maharal.</margin> 

The Four Cups of redemption correspond to these four stages:
*   **First Cup:** Selection of the World to Come in this world—"Who has chosen us... and sanctified us," meaning attachment to Torah and Commandments.
*   **Second Cup:** The *Aggadah* (telling of the story). It begins with shame and ends with praise. There is a dispute whether the soul, when it leaves the body, begins with "We were slaves" and ends with "Redemption." The soul is judged first for its sins and then brought close to the Shekhinah.
*   **Third Cup:** The Blessing after Meals, envisioning the Messianic Era when the Land of Israel will produce delicacies. We mention David, who is the Messiah.
*   **Fourth Cup:** The "Great Hallel." This is the eternal World to Come, which is the true, eternal Great Hallel. "The soul of every living thing" shall bless Your Name. "For His mercy endures forever"—the eternal mercy.

(Here one should sermonize on the Four Cups and the laws of Passover). Since the essence of the Commandment relates to the creation of the world in Nissan, and the world stands on three pillars: Torah, Service, and Acts of Kindness. These were revealed through three leaders: 
1.  **Moses:** The pillar of Torah. 
2.  **Aaron:** The pillar of Service (the Temple service). 
3.  **Miriam:** The pillar of Kindness (providing the well of water). 
The Torah was only given to those who ate the Manna (provided via Moses). The Clouds of Glory were via Aaron. The Well of Living Water was via Miriam. 
*   **The Paschal Lamb** represents Service (Sacrifice).
*   **Matzah** represents Torah...
