# Tractate Pesachim
## Enriched Matzah <note>term: Matzah Ashirah — Matzah made with liquids like fruit juice, used here as a springboard for discussing spiritual "richness" and refinement.</note>

Rabbi Joshua ben Levi noted, and the Tosafot <note>Medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> wrote, that there are 600,000 "husks" <note>term: Kelipot — in Kabbalah, these are the shells or forces of impurity that conceal divine light.</note>. The matter is that Israel is responsible for one another. Regarding the sinner, our Sages of blessed memory gave a reason: Adam was created last so that if he became haughty, they could say to him, "even a gnat preceded you" in creation. We find that a guarantor represents 600,000, and a guarantor represents 600,000 husks. Moses, and those like him, possessed the merit of the masses; 600,000 holy souls were dependent upon him. Just as the ultimate purpose of Adam's creation was to wear "garments of light" <note>original: "כתנות אור" — spelled with the Hebrew letter Aleph</note>, as I have elaborated in other sermons, so too with our teacher Moses (peace be upon him), "the skin of his face radiated" <note>Exodus 34:29</note>. It is not written that this radiance was a "repulsion," but rather "radiance" is already written. The matter is that at the time of the giving of the Torah, it was fitting for the purpose of creation to be realized, and for all of humanity to be clothed in "garments of light." However, the "ornaments" and crowns given to them at Horeb <note>Mount Sinai</note> were removed when they corrupted their ways with the Golden Calf. Then the Children of Israel were stripped of their ornaments—namely, the radiance of light. In the place where the ornaments and the tablets were returned, making them like "beings on high," it was removed from man—that is, from the "First Adam." Yet, for our teacher Moses, the radiance of light remained, for why should it be taken from him? This is proven in the Zohar. Do not wonder why many righteous and pious people who were present at that time and did not sin with the Calf also had their radiance taken. To my humble opinion, this is not a difficulty, because once the "air" of the world became impure and "husk-like," an impure happenstance occurred due to the collision, and "one sinner destroys much good" <note>Ecclesiastes 9:18</note>. But Moses, who was not in the "air" of this world but rather under the "shadow of the wings of the Divine Presence" <note>term: Shekhinah — the feminine, indwelling presence of God.</note>, was saved from this. As for what the Sages said in Midrash Rabbah on the portion *Ki Tisa*, "Moses merited the horns of his glory," the intention is not that he merited something brand new, but rather how he merited *not* to be coarsened by the air of the world. Study this statement well, and you can explain it in this manner. Regarding the explanation of the verse, "I said, you are gods, and all of you are sons of the Most High" <note>Psalm 82:6</note>, the purpose of man's creation is to be a "man of God," supreme, entirely governed by the mind which is his soul. His whole body should be intellectual, reaching from heaven to earth, entirely holy—and so it will be in the future "uprightness." Due to sin, man was diminished, as it is written, "You placed Your hand [Hebrew: *Kaf*] upon me" <note>Psalm 139:5</note>, from the language of the letter *Kaf* <note>The letter Kaf has the numerical value of 20, but the author is linking it to the ten fingers or ten spheres.</note>. At the giving of the Torah, the Ten Commandments were set against the ten lights that dwell in the created world, and when they are doubled, they become *Kaf* (20). Just as the Zohar elaborates on the matter of the "canopies," ten by ten, the "Kaf" in the holy weight. The *Pardes* <note>likely *Pardes Rimonim* by Moses Cordovero</note> copied this in the section "Reason for Emanation," chapter 2. The secret of the letter *Yod* (10) is ten courts... and when it is filled out, it has the power of the complete weight. This is the secret of the thought: the *Yod* was taken from Sarah until it was given to Abraham and Joshua. Why the complaint? Because the letter *He* was not put in its place in her name, but rather the "filling" of the *Yod*—namely the letters *Vav* and *Dalet*—whose value also equals 6, making the weight complete. Even though these are external matters, "before the line of the law," nevertheless, the letter *Dalet* in Abraham represents the attribute of *Elokim*, for he was a "Great Man." And *Adam* is the name of the value 45 <note>The numerical value (Gematria) of the name of God spelled out as *Yod-He-Vav-He* with Alephs.</note>. At the giving of the Torah, the world was re-created like the creation of heaven and earth, which were created on the first day but were "shaky" until the second day when God "spread out the firmament." So too, the world was shaky until the giving of the Torah, which is compared to a revelation of a single connection, as we shall explain. Since this is a world of "grasping," due to the sin, they had to hurry out of Egypt for "thirty pure days," as explained in the Zohar regarding the "impure place" that burns the foundations. If they had stood firm in their faith, they would have all been "beings on high" and death would have been swallowed up forever. "You placed Your hand [Kaf] upon me" meant that only a palm-full of spirituality remained in the heart. Therefore, see the composition of the sciences: instead of living forever, life is dependent on the heart. "He also set the world in their heart" <note>Ecclesiastes 3:11</note>, and even in this, free choice is dependent—whether to follow the straight path or the "crookedness," for "the inclination of man's heart is evil." The "neighboring adulterer" is the "man without a heart," which is the Serpent. As Rashi explained: the Serpent saw them occupied with physical intimacy... the Serpent is the Evil Inclination that entices man to diminish even the heart, so that no spirituality remains. This is the hint in the verse: "Man looks to the eyes, but the Lord looks to the heart" <note>1 Samuel 16:7</note>. This means that since the First Adam sinned by following his eyes—as it says, "And she saw it was a delight to the eyes"—he became physical, and the Holy One can no longer look upon him with desire, except for the heart. "The Merciful One desires the heart." This verse was said regarding the Kingdom of the House of David, which is the Messiah. Therefore, one should be "broken-hearted" to subdue the yoke. The First Adam "stretched his foreskin" <note>A Talmudic idiom for trying to hide one's covenantal identity or reverting to a primitive state</note>. "A wise man's heart is at his right hand" <note>Ecclesiastes 10:2</note>, for the place of the Lord's dwelling is always in the heart of man, which is in the center, said to be "opposite the right hand" of the Holy One, and all dross remains on the left, which is *Samael* <note>The name of the accuser or demonic figure in Kabbalah.</note>. This is the secret of the verse: "Do not stray after your heart and after your eyes" <note>Numbers 15:39</note>. It is also written, "He did not give him a wise heart to go and eyes to see." "And Jacob stole the heart of Laban the Aramean." "A wandering Aramean"—this could refer to the matter of Jacob's steps being in the order of the holiday of Matzot. There, there was an "embrace" and a "refinement," and he saved the spirit from the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion... see the *Pardes* in the "Gate of Gates."

---

The general point is that the sin of Adam caused a loss of "precious shelter," and they added to the "good" in order to weaken the physical matter and dissolve the filth of the "husk." This is the matter of suffering, as I have elaborated in other sermons.

<margin>
From the verses "I have tasted" and "they stood in their stubbornness," they did not remember and did not know what was secret, for they were corrupted.
</margin>

As I wrote in my work *Nachalat Yaakov* on the "Valley of Blessing" regarding the verse "And now, lest he put forth his hand"—"And now" refers only to repentance. All this belongs here. Therefore, they were brought to Egypt to the "exile of labor," sorcery, and husks, to be afflicted there in the "Iron Furnace." This is why Jacob "stole the heart" of Laban the Aramean, and "the Aramean went down to Egypt." For it was fitting for Jacob to go down to Egypt and be shaken and afflicted, not by his own choice, but for his own good, to refine the "First Adam." This is the meaning of "with the cords of man" <note>Hosea 11:4</note>. It is like a cow that suffers, and the suffering seems bad for her, but it is only for her good, for through this she reaches perfection. This whole matter is explained elsewhere. He also explained this regarding the Passover sacrifice; see there for the reason for the Egyptian exile. Therefore, the matter of Pharaoh was entirely about "hardness of heart" and the claim of being "cruel." "And I will harden his heart"—a point which all the early and later commentators struggled with. But for me, it is explained that the Holy One desired this. See the whole discourse and Rashi later in the portion of *Va'era*; the whole sermon belongs here, and then we shall return to the matter.

---

**When Israel went out** of Egypt, the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded the Tefillin of the hand, placed against the heart, and the Tefillin of the head, placed "between the eyes." I have already written in the name of the Zohar that the secret of the "Garments of Light" for Adam and his wife are the Tefillin of the hand and the Tefillin of the head. In the future to come, they will be actual light. When they corrupted themselves with the Calf, they began to repair this in the Tabernacle; therefore, it says "And every wise-hearted man" <note>Exodus 35:10</note>. Regarding Aaron, it says "he shall see you and his heart shall be glad," and he merited the Breastplate (*Choshen*), which is the reversal of the Serpent (*Nachash* <note>A common Gematria: Choshen and Nachash both equal 358</note>) who brought corruption to the world through a woman. Even after the "Iron Furnace," there was no power for the redemption to be "Male" <note>term: Zachar — representing a permanent, active spiritual state</note>. Since they were not yet crowned with Torah and commandments, the redemption did not endure, and it reverted to the "Female" world <note>term: Nekevah — representing a receptive, temporary, or vulnerable state</note>. The redemption was only held back until the "Female" power—that is, the side of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) that was with them in exile, as it says "and for your transgressions was your mother sent away" <note>Isaiah 50:1</note>. See the *Pardes* in the "Gate of Gates" that the redemption was only from the side of *Malchut* <note>term: Malchut — "Kingship," the lowest and most "feminine" of the ten Sefirot</note>. This is what the Sages meant by saying that all the "Songs" (*Shirot*) of the Bible are in the feminine form. It was fitting for it to be masculine at the giving of the Torah, but there too it says "You speak to us" <note>Exodus 20:16 - using a feminine form of 'you'</note>, which weakened the power, as it were, like a female. Then the "weakness" began until it moved from potential to action with the making of the Calf, when they dropped the letter *Lamed* from the "clari-calls" of Israel at the giving of the Torah. They thought an evil thought, as found in the words of our Sages: the Holy One said to Moses, "You see one vision," etc. If the world had returned completely to corruption, we would have decreed the "subjugation of the kingdoms." For if not for that, the Sages said: "Freedom from the Angel of Death, freedom from the kingdoms." Even the redemptions that occurred at various times were "Female" in nature, for the redemption only added power to the "Female" of Above, the Divine Presence in exile. This is the reason why all redemptions were through a female: the Sages said, "In the merit of the righteous women, Israel was redeemed from Egypt." So too, Media and Persia through Esther, and Greece through Judith. Until the Future Redemption arrives—the "True Redemption"—then a "New Song" (*Shir Chadash*) will be said in the masculine form. The world will return to its original intention, which was the intent of the Holy One at the redemption from Egypt at its start, had it been done properly. This is the meaning of "As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders" <note>Micah 7:15</note>. The word "I will show him" (*Ar'enu*) is difficult; it should have said "I will show you" (*Ar'ekha*). But it is as the Zohar explains on the verse "And because He loved your fathers... and brought you out in His presence" <note>Deuteronomy 4:37</note>. What does "in His presence" mean? Rashi explained... but it refers to the Patriarchs. The Holy One promised, "And also that nation [I will judge]." So too, "I will show him" refers to the Patriarchs—for the purpose of creation was "when they were created" (*be-hibare'am*), which can be read "through Abraham" (*be-Abraham*). This was meant to be fulfilled when Israel left Egypt, but they did not succeed compared to the Final Redemption. Then the Holy One will show us, and then the world will be "Male." The matter of "Male" and "Female" is like what the Zohar explains on "The virgin of Israel shall no more rise" <note>Amos 5:2</note>—meaning the Shekhinah—"for if you will not rise, then *I* shall rise," says the Lord. This is the Name *YHVH*, and He Himself will raise her. "The glory of the Lord shall be revealed." "The Lord will go forth and fight... the Lord is a man of war." The redemption will be from the side of "Man." Regarding this, we pray "May He raise for us the fallen sukkah of David"—namely, the Kingship of the House of David—and she shall not have to raise herself, as happened in the first redemption. This explains the passage:

->**And it is she...**<-

# Tractate Passover
## Fifth Homily: Enriched Matzah

->Another homily for the Great Sabbath, which I have hinted at briefly.<-

**"This** is the law of the burnt offering" <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. In the Midrash of Rabbi Phinehas of Zephnin, in the name of Rabbi Levi, he said: From the beginning of the book until this point, it is written: "And the sons of Aaron shall offer," "And the sons of Aaron shall place," "And the sons of Aaron shall arrange." Moses said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Is it because pride and plotting are beloved? To the wood, You have accorded honor for the sake of their priesthood <note>original: "כהנהן" — likely referring to the special status of the priestly families</note>, for all wood is fit for the altar pile except for the olive and the vine. Yet to Aaron himself, do You not accord honor for the sake of his children?" The Holy One, Blessed be He, replied: "By your life! Through your prayer, I shall bring him near. Not only that, but I shall make him the primary figure and his sons secondary, as it is said: 'Command Aaron and his sons...'" This concludes the words of Rabbi Phinehas regarding this statement.

One might ask: Why does he count only these four instances? Are there not more, such as "And they shall bring [the blood] to the sons of Aaron the priests" or the law of taking a handful of flour? Similarly, it is written in the section on Peace Offerings. It is true that according to the plain meaning <note>term: Peshat — the literal or direct meaning of a scriptural text</note> this is not a difficulty, for the Midrash only focuses on the specific variations regarding the burnt offering <note>term: Olah — a sacrifice that is entirely consumed by fire on the altar</note>. This also resolves why it is not a problem that Aaron and his sons were already mentioned earlier in the section on the meal offering, as it says "And what is left of the meal offering shall be for Aaron and his sons." However, it is difficult to understand why the distinction depends specifically on the burnt offering. Furthermore, a person is jealous of everyone except their own son or disciple; since the "sons of Aaron" are both, why were they placed before him? Additionally, regarding the "honor" given to the wood: it is considered an honor that they are disqualified from the altar pile? On the contrary, "every worker acts for his purpose" and "everything was created for His glory" <note>Proverbs 16:4</note>. It would be more fitting to explain that the honor consists of *not* cutting down these trees, so that the vine and olive remain available for the libations and the oil for the meal offerings. However, Rashi <note>A preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator</note> did not explain it this way, but rather because of the "settlement of the Land of Israel" <note>i.e., preserving productive fruit trees</note>.

"This is the law of the burnt offering..." and "Who is this that comes up from the wilderness, like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense?" <note>Song of Songs 3:6</note>. In the Midrash (Yalkut Song of Songs), it is explained: There are twenty-four "faces" <note>interpretations or aspects</note> to the meal offering... This refers to Abraham. Just as myrrh is the head of all spices, so too are the Priesthood, Levites, and Kingship all descended from Jacob. Thus ends the Midrash. It follows a sequence of four "faces": 1) Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; 2) Moses and Aaron; 3) The seventy elders; 4) Priest, Levite, and Israelite.

One must consider this statement: Was Abraham truly the "head" of the righteous? Were there not those before him, such as Adam, Seth, Noah, Enoch, Methuselah, Shem, and Eber? This is the meaning of "The God of our fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." "Our fathers" refers to Adam, Seth, etc. But Abraham is the "head" because he is the most significant. Furthermore, "frankincense" refers to Isaac; at the time Abraham offered him <note>The Binding of Isaac</note>, he was not intended for the altar as a meal offering <note>term: Mincha — a grain offering, distinct from the animal "Olah"</note>. Perhaps it can be answered that we do not find the term "intent" (intention/meditation) used for a sacrifice as much as with the meal offering, and Isaac established the afternoon prayer <note>also called Mincha</note>. It is possible he established it at the moment his soul almost left him upon the altar. Indeed, I found a reason why the afternoon prayer is called "Mincha" more than other prayers, though all prayers are an offering to God. It is because Isaac considered that there is no burnt offering without a meal offering, and he thought he would not ascend as a perfect burnt offering; therefore, he established a prayer in place of the meal offering. Thus, we call this prayer "Mincha."

We bring another statement of the "four faces," found in the Yalkut on the portion of *Beshalach* <note>Exodus 13:17–17:16</note> from the Midrash Abkir: "The waters were a wall for them" <note>Exodus 14:22</note>. When Israel went down into the sea, Gabriel descended with them and surrounded them with four walls. The water was transformed into walls for Israel because they were destined to receive the Torah from the right hand of the Holy One. [The Midrash mentions] the knot of the Tefillin <note>phylacteries</note> and the fringes of the Tzitzit behind them. This is also a teaching of the "four faces"—Tefillin, the sea, and Tzitzit. Why did he not count the Mezuzah on the left? Also, the Tzitzit are on the four corners.

We further bring a statement of the "four faces" from the Yalkut on *Devarim* <note>Deuteronomy</note>: Elijah and Israel were hidden/protected so that they would be fenced in against sexual immorality, did not change their names, did not change their language, and did not engage in evil speech <note>term: Lashon Hara — gossip or slander</note>. One might ask: What is the connection between these four and the Redemption? Also, regarding the claim that there was no evil speech among them—does this not contradict what is written on the verse "Indeed, the matter is known" <note>Exodus 2:14</note>, which Rashi explains as Moses realizing why Israel was suffering (because of informers)?

Before we explain the sixteen "faces" <note>4x4</note>, let us open a great and powerful gate regarding the Exodus from Egypt and the intellectual law of the altar. Regarding the telling of the Exodus in the *Haggadah*: it is a commandment to tell of the Exodus, and "all who increase [the telling] are praiseworthy." The double language and the change in phrasing are difficult. Our rabbis also asked this. It seems to me it can be explained in a beautiful and deep way. According to the version "And all who increase in telling," there is no difficulty: the commandment is to tell it with the mouth, and whoever does so more is praiseworthy. But for the standard version that lacks the word "telling" <note>original: "ספור"</note>, it is difficult. According to our way, a great and powerful investigation will be explained.

This constitutes the entirety of Chapter 35 from the book *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>A 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note> in the section on the "Secrets of the Torah." It concerns why they asked for a "wall" in the Exodus from Egypt, to which I have added some of my own insights. He asks: Why were the children of Abraham enslaved in Egypt? He mentions the statement from the first sermon above and gives three reasons: because Abraham asked "How shall I know?" <note>Genesis 15:8</note>. If he hadn't said this, would there be no Torah? For the Torah is dependent on the Egyptian experience. If they hadn't sinned, would they not have been in Egypt? Some explain that the Torah existed beforehand, but because of Abraham's sin, the Holy One "narrowed" it <note>i.e., made it necessary to go through exile</note> and informed him of the news of the exile. But all this does not satisfy our thirst for understanding.

Before explaining the answer, which is written at length in his book with several additions, I will first present a graceful introduction. In the beginning, light and darkness were mixed together. Then, "God divided the light from the darkness" <note>Genesis 1:4</note> and established a boundary for each. He hid the light for the righteous. This concept encompasses all the divine powers that were mixed. There was darkness for the Egyptians and light for the Children of Israel. This was a protective barrier. There are seven classes of dwellings... a river goes out of Eden and from there it divides into four heads. This represents the "unfolding" of the four worlds: *Atzilut* (Emanation), *Beriah* (Creation), *Yetzirah* (Formation), and *Assiyah* (Action) <note>term: ABY"A — the four spiritual realms in Kabbalah</note> from the side of holiness. Each of the four heads has four "faces." They are hinted at in the verse "In the day that the Lord God made heaven and earth..."

The "Earth" corresponds to the world of the Angels (*Yetzirah*). "Heaven" refers to the celestial spheres and everything within the four directions. These correspond to the **Four Sons**: the **Wise** son, the **Wicked** son, the **Simple** son, and the **One who does not know how to ask**. The Holy One's world... the "Wicked" son is the opposite, representing the lower world. The "Simple" son corresponds to the World of the Throne (*Beriah*), where the forms are engraved. The "One who does not know how to ask" corresponds to the World of Action (*Assiyah*), the world of the celestial spheres. As it says in the Midrash: the day borrows from the night and the night from the day... but in truth, they "do not know," meaning even if they are living, intelligent beings, they do not possess their own independent will <note>original: "מרכחו" — likely meaning "their own strength/volition"</note>.

Let us return to our subject: the world of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God</note> is conducted through four general attributes: the line of **Kindness** (Chesed), the line of **Judgment** (Din), the line of **Mercy** (Rachamim), and **Sovereignty** (Malchut).
1. **Kindness** is represented by the [letter] *Yod*, a single point, encompassing the spheres. For "the world is built on kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>.
2. The first *Heh* is **Might** (Gevurah), which opens from below... what is "might"? One who subdues his inclination.
3. The *Vav* is **Beauty** (Tif'eret), which is the Tree of Knowledge, including both good and evil, judgment and mercy. From there comes the Torah, which has "six orders" <note>The Six Orders of the Mishnah</note>, meaning it distinguishes between good and evil: forbidden and permitted, impure and pure, liable and exempt.
4. The final *Heh* is **Sovereignty**, the gate open to the lower beings to oversee the general and the particular, from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice. According to His greatness is His humility.

In total, these four attributes are: 1) Kindness, 2) Judgment, 3) Torah, 4) Humility.
There are also four "faces" to the **World of the Throne** (*Beriah*), which is His chariot: the Human, the Ox, the Eagle, and the Lion.
There are four "faces" to the **World of Formation** (*Yetzirah*): the angels Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael.
There are four "faces" to the **World of Action** (*Assiyah*), which stems from the spheres: the four directions of the heavens, and corresponding to them, the four elements as explained in the Zohar and the *Pardes* <note>term: Pardes Rimonim — a classic Kabbalistic text by Moshe Cordovero</note>.

These three systems of "four faces" receive their life-force from the upper system, the four letters of the Name of God, which carves out life for every living thing. This is the secret of the "four [cups of wine]." Regarding this, the Sages established the version of the **First Cup**: "Who has chosen us and sanctified us." This corresponds to the selection of Jacob as His portion and our sanctification with His holiness. Over the **Second Cup**, the *Haggadah* is recited, returning to the lights and signs and the praise of the World of the Throne, which is associated with Jacob. As it says in Tractate Chullin: [The angels] "ascend and descend," they saw his image engraved on the Throne and came to harm him, but the Holy One stood over him to protect him. Similarly, this was concluded at the time of Moses, as it says in the chapter "Rabbi Akiva," that the Holy One told him: "Hold onto My Throne of Glory."

This is the external context. The blessings of enjoyment established by Moses, the blessing of "Who feeds all," refers to the Manna, which is "bread of the mighty" <note>Psalm 78:25</note>, corresponding to the world of the angels. This is followed by "the Angel who redeems." The **Fourth Cup** is for Hallel (Praise), corresponding to "And I will take you to Me for a people, and I will be to you a God." It was previously established in the chapter "All Sacred Writings" <note>Tractate Shabbat</note> that whoever recites Hallel every day is "blaspheming and insulting." See Rashi, who explains this is because it seems forced/routine. But to me it seems that it is known that it is a great transgression to choose physical desires... It is said: "The Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome." If Moses had not said them... then we have permission to glorify...

# Tractate Passover
## Enriched Matzah

Rather, it is only flour and water. "If there is no flour, there is no Torah" <note>quoting Ethics of the Fathers 3:17</note>, and water refers to the Torah, as it is written: "Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the water" <note>Isaiah 55:1</note>. "Enriched Matzah" <note>original: "מצה עשירה" — Matzah made with juice or oil instead of water, symbolizing wealth</note> suggests that whoever fulfills the Torah in poverty will ultimately fulfill it in wealth. The Bitter Herb <note>term: Maror — the bitter herbs eaten at the Seder to recall the bitterness of slavery</note> corresponds to the three groups of sins and transgressions. It represents the freedom found through suffering, for suffering purifies. Through it, the circuit of the wicked is bypassed; "good" suffering serves to refine and purify the soul. However, sometimes there is "bad" suffering, such as that mentioned in the Baraita <note>term: Baraita — a tradition from the period of the Mishnah not included in the main text</note> regarding the heretics, informers, and skeptics, who have no portion in the World to Come. Purgatory <note>original: "גיהנם"</note> is its flame. Opposite this is the "root" of the bitter herb, which is eaten neither moist nor dry. Moistness hints at the good, while dryness indicates suffering. This dryness in the bitter herb hints at the essence of evil, for this root is from the "root of the snake" from which a viper emerges, a root bearing gall and wormwood. This persists until the future, when the snake will be abolished and the Angel of Death shall be slaughtered. Then, the Root of Jesse, which stands as a banner for the nations, will <unclear>hover slightly</unclear>. See the commentary of the *Tziyuni* at the beginning of the portion of *Toldot* regarding the many snakes. Close to this bitterness was the destruction of the second Holy Temple; as our Sages of blessed memory said: "The destruction of the Holy Temple was so grievous that even the angels of peace wept bitterly." In general, all herbs are compared to the Children of Israel: "I made you a myriad, like the plant of the field" <note>Ezekiel 16:7</note>. And it is said of Israel: "You only have I known... therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities" <note>Amos 3:2</note>. Therefore, the stalk is valid whether moist or dry, because dryness is "good" <note>meaning the suffering serves a positive purpose</note>, but the leaves—which are quite close to the "root of the snake," as it is said, "And they sewed fig leaves together," through which they were corrupted—from this is derived the "sound of a driven leaf." Therefore, if the leaf is dry, it is invalid, but if moist, it is valid, for then it follows the secret of "its leaf shall not wither" <note>Psalms 1:3</note>.

This is the general path. On a specific level, there are four matters regarding the bitter herb: 1) the requirement of the size of an olive <note>term: kezayit — the minimum volume required for a commandment</note>; 2) the bitter herb with Charoset <note>term: Charoset — a sweet paste symbolizing mortar</note>; 3) the bitter herb with Matzah; 4) being precise with its name, for "its name is fitting for it." These hint at four reasons why it is appropriate to receive suffering with love.

**Reason 1:** The Ran <note>term: The Ran — Rabbenu Nissim, a 14th-century Spanish scholar</note> wrote in his homilies that suffering brings a person back to the Torah. I have transcribed this later in the homilies outside the explanation of the words. Regarding this matter, I explained: "Great is study that leads to action," as explained later in the homilies for the wedding of the portion of *Ekev*. Suffering also leads to the searching of one's deeds, as explained in the homilies on Deuteronomy. <insert>This is the first reason.</insert>

**Reason 2:** A person often errs and thinks an event is bad in its moment. For example, Joseph was sold and brought down to Egypt; this was the very cause of Joseph becoming a king. The Midrash of our Sages says: "It has become my salvation." I have elaborated in the homilies for Sukkot that this is the meaning of "Do what is good in Your eyes," and not "what is good in my eyes," for I am prone to error. This is the meaning of "Answer me in the truth of Your salvation," not a salvation that is false—meaning what a person thinks is good but is actually bad. The matter is that the Blessed Name "inclines toward kindness," even if at first glance it appears bad. Regarding this, the verse is interpreted: "As for me, may my prayer... be in an acceptable time"—meaning that even the revealed aspect should be "acceptable," as our Sages said: "Who are the righteous? Those who eat from two worlds." This is "My prayer to You, O Lord"—that the name of Mercy (Hashem) should be merciful, and it should be an acceptable time. "O God, in the abundance of Your kindness"—even if it is the Attribute of Justice <note>term: Elohim — the Divine name associated with strict justice</note>, it is truly salvation. No evil descends from above, and even if it seems bad, it is to save one from a worse punishment which the person was destined for. (And as it says in Tractate Berakhot: "One should always be accustomed to saying, 'Whatever the Merciful One does, He does for the best,'" so they may be saved from Purgatory). At any rate, our Sages said four people "must give thanks," but they did not say they are "obligated." The nature of the thanks is for the fact that a greater punishment did not occur. They "must" because once they have endured the time designated for this, if they do not give thanks, it may return to that state. "And all that lives shall thank You forever."

Regarding the bitter herb, they said it is a "remembrance" according to the name. Lord, Master of the Universe, let us know what the sin was! The Holy One, Blessed be He, replied: "Heaven forbid that you should ask this; look toward suffering," as it is said: "The reproofs of instruction are the way of life" <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>. In the 100th chapter of Berakhot, regarding a tooth and an eye <note>referring to Exodus 21:26-27</note>, they are among the four things by which a person is set free. Suffering, which scours a person's entire body, does the same.

**Reason 4:** Since the Holy One, Blessed be He, pays a good reward to a person who fulfills a commandment even if it is burdensome, a person should likewise receive even punishment from the Blessed Name, even when it is "bad." This is what the Mishnah in Berakhot says: "'With all your might'—with every measure <note>original: "מדה" — a pun on 'might' (me'odecha) and 'measure' (middah)</note> that He measures out for you, thank Him." And so it says in the Midrash Song of Songs Rabbah on the verse "His palate is sweet": "So says the Lord to the House of Israel: Seek Me and live." Rabbi Aha and Rabbi Tanchum bar Hiyya in the name of Rabbi Yohanan said... He is faithful to pay a good reward. And it seems that according to the secret, this hints at the 100th chapter of Shabbat: "I have a hidden gift in My treasury, and 'Shabbat' is its name... its reward is not revealed." See what I wrote above in the homilies for *Vayakhel*. One can explain that "Shabbat" implies resting and pleasure. Therefore, from a legal standpoint, it would not be appropriate to receive a reward, as explained in the aforementioned Midrash. Thus God said: "Go and inform them that I give them a reward for this." This "reward is not revealed" means He will give a reward, but the intention is not that He revealed *what* the reward is. Think on this.

Furthermore, these four reasons are hinted at in the passage in chapter "The Seer" (Berakhot page 60): "Just as one blesses for the good... so one blesses for the bad." Rabbi Aha said in the name of Rabbi Levi: "From this verse... My help comes from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth." It is difficult to understand the intention here—why this verse specifically? It is the way of the Talmud to ask "What is [this verse] saying?" Rather, here there are four Sages. One said this, and one said that, and they do not disagree; rather, each one speaks from one specific reason. The first said: "I will sing of kindness and justice"—meaning it is proper to maintain the thanks for the commandments even in wealth (kindness) and even in poverty (justice/obligation), as I wrote in the name of the Ran. The second said: "In the Lord I will praise His word, in God I will praise His word"—this is the second reason I explained to you, where the Name of Mercy (Lord) and Justice (God) are both for the good. The third said: "I will lift the cup of salvations"—referring to the future, to be saved from Purgatory through the punishment of instruction when I am in distress. And "Lord, I called"—even if it is bad, they shall be praised... I asked of Him, blessed be He, and I will not depend on the nature of the time... As it says in the first chapter of Taanit, Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: "Anyone who rejoices in suffering in this world brings salvation to the world," as it is said: "The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away"—corresponding to the fourth reason: just as He gave, so He takes.

The order: the size of an olive (Kezayit) corresponds to the first reason, to bring one to Torah and good deeds, as it says in Tractate Menachot: Rabbi Yohanan said, "Why is Israel compared to an olive? To tell you that just as an olive only produces its oil through crushing, so too Israel only returns to the good through suffering." Therefore, [suffering] corresponds to the second reason: there is no "minor" evil, for that is sin. "Bitter herb with Matzah" which is freedom, is the third reason; even if you say it is "bad," the bad is for the good, to go out to freedom. This is the secret of the tooth and eye <note>the slave who goes free due to injury</note>. 
<margin>72</margin>
Charoset is also a remembrance of the clay <note>mortar</note>. Despite this, it is the first thing eaten... for sometimes one receives reward... "With every measure," etc. The entire homily hints at this.

After the sin of Adam, sacrifices were needed—that is, to bring the soul of the animal near in place of the soul [of man]. Adam the first man, when he sacrificed, it was a bull with a single horn on its forehead. The secret of unity points to the "Coats of Light" (written with the letter *Aleph*). There are seventy nations under the *Aleph*, corresponding to the secret of the Festival sacrifices. When they sinned, the letter *Ayin* <note>original: "ע"</note> prevailed over the *Aleph* <note>original: "א"</note>—that is, the "Coats of Skin" <note>original: "עור" vs "אור" — a famous mystical pun: Light vs. Skin</note> replaced the Kings... in place of the sacrifices. And instead of one horn, it is written in Daniel: "And it had a vision," and the horn was broken and four visions arose in its place toward the four winds of heaven.

The statement that Jacob "redeemed Abraham" <note>a Midrashic concept that Abraham was saved from Nimrod's furnace for the sake of his future grandson Jacob</note>... Abraham, in whom [the world] was established, is the cause. Yet we find righteous, pious, and holy ones of the Most High who died for the Sanctification of the Name and were not saved, like Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues. Similarly, Daniel said: "Be it known to you, O king, that we will not [serve your gods]," but he was worthy of being the pillar of the world. However, there is a novelty: for from the "chaff" came Ishmael, and from Isaac came Esau, but in Jacob, "his bed was complete" <note>term: "mittato shelemah" — meaning all his children were righteous</note>, so that Jacob would emerge from him purified, his beauty being a reflection of Adam’s beauty. Abraham is the "Great Adam," and Jacob is the reflection of the beauty of Adam. Thus, "the crown of the aged is their children's children," and the elders are all one matter.

Regarding what was explained at first: everything he disqualified was for the same reason he disqualified it. See *Kli Hemdah*, for "to you, Abba bar Yudan, it is difficult." "It is the burnt offering (*Olah*) on its firewood"—this is settled according to the Midrash: "Anyone who is prideful is judged by fire." See the long Midrash in *Bechukotai*. This verse belongs here, and the Midrash explains: "It is the *Olah* (that which rises up)"—referring to the kingdom. "On its firewood"—which is the fire of Purgatory. Then He brought us out to relief. It seems to me the reason they are judged by fire is that fire is the highest element, and pride reaches there. I have already explained that from the sin of man, the main thing is a "broken heart." Rabbi Alexandri speaks of the reality of the matter now due to the sin of Adam. He answers: "What is this 'It is the *Olah*'?" Rather, the intention of man is the "Olah" (the ascent), and he must be a "broken vessel," since the vessel—the physical matter—was made for a great purpose. Hinted at here is the reception of the Divine from Rabbi Isaac Luria (the AriZal) of blessed memory: "Broken vessels," but one of them was not broken. This is "The Holy One, Blessed be He, uses broken vessels." "This is the law of the burnt offering (*Olah*)"—this is the law of Man to ascend (*La'alot*), and he needs the breaking...

And this "He" (*Hu*) which is in the Torah, we read it as "She" (*Hi*). See what I wrote regarding the secret of "And it is this (*V'hi*) that has stood for our ancestors." And now there are sin-offerings (*Chatat*) because of sins. In the future, there will be no sin-offerings, for sins will be finished; there will only be voluntary burnt offerings (*Olah*). "Sin-offering" is feminine, while "Burnt offering" is masculine. "The song of the head... one is missing from the Name and the Throne." May the Lord... and enter into the palaces of Zion and Jerusalem, for the soul and the body, all in perfection. May it be His will. Finished.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic and homiletic exploration of "Enriched Matzah," moving from the symbolic nature of the ingredients to a complex discussion of spiritual archetypes—Abraham, the celestial Chariot, and the transformation of destiny—concluding with a commentary on Psalm 23.</meta>

# Tractate Passover
## Enriched Matzah

From the "Left Side" <note>the side of Gevurah or Judgment in Kabbalah</note> comes the "Goring Ox" <note>original: "שור מועד" — a legal term for a habitually dangerous animal</note>. Therefore, the text mentions frankincense, for they speak of the "Midrash of the Damagers" <note>the sect of harmful spiritual entities</note> who are the Goring Ox. Regarding Abraham, he said he was the "head of the righteous."

May their memory be a blessing; for their "groaning" <note>original: "נהים"</note> refers to their branches, and he is the head over them. It is known that he converted most of the proselytes after they had eaten and drunk, saying to them: "Bless the One whose food you have eaten." Then, "Abraham ran to the herd" <note>Genesis 18:7</note>; there were three thousand included in the "Ox." Moses and Aaron are the secret of the "Lion," while Joseph and the sacrifices <note>original: "וזב"א"</note> represent the secret of the 72-letter Name and the number 216, which equals the numerical value of "Lion" <note>original: "ארי"ה" (Aryeh)</note>. Through this, the splitting of the Red Sea occurred. I have written elsewhere the plain meaning of Rabbi Luria <note>The Ari, 16th-century mystic</note> regarding the "six hundred chosen chariots." The secret of the "Eagle" corresponds to the seventy elders of the Sanhedrin; see the section on the "Wings of the Eagle."
The blessing of the Messiah <note>original: "יז"לה דמשיחא"</note> involves the Priest, the Levite, and the Israelite descending from Jacob, in the secret of "Man." The beauty of Jacob reflects the beauty of Adam <note>original: "שופריה דיעקב מעין שופרא דאדם"</note>, and "He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life," which is the secret of the soul's levels: *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah*. These correspond to the Priest, Levite, and Israelite. The Midrash of the Rabbi says Aaron represents the World of Formation <note>original: "עולם היציר"ה"</note>. According to the plain meaning, the difficulties are resolved: everything is repaired. It was equal to him... for this reason, he made him a pottage of five types of wheat, like a burnt offering. Since he sinned with the Golden Calf, they "offered burnt offerings"; therefore, it was specifically a burnt offering.
<margin>According to this path, the matter of the Calf will be explained.</margin>
His three intentions: "I have surely seen" <note>Exodus 3:7</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: "You see one vision—how they come to Sinai to receive the Torah—but I see two visions... how they will act after My 'obscurations' <note>referring to the Golden Calf</note>." The "Face of the Ox" is on the left. Behold, the power of the spiritual attachments was weakened until the World of Creation because of the blemish, and the attachment remained only in the World of Formation. Thus, the demonic impulse grew strong. "Today the Lord appeared to you" <note>Leviticus 9:4</note>—this refers to Aaron and Michael, who is also the High Priest Above, offering the souls of the righteous. When there is no attachment in their world above in the World of Creation, they are called the "sons of Aaron." Understand this. Behold, the blood is the soul which Michael offers, and "the sons of Aaron shall present [the blood]"—this is Michael, who is the "Groom," and there is water around the Altar Above. "And they shall offer"—this is the service nearby, referring to Uriel, who leans toward Sachiel, the path of Fire. This is Gabriel, who is "Fire." The "arranging of the wood" is like Uriel. The action of the "latter Israelites" is the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, for afterward, in the cascading of the husks <note>term: Kelipot — shells of evil or impurity</note>, Samael is the evil one. For the supernal beings desire to bestow influence upon the lower beings. Regarding the "trees," it says "He shared His honor" <note>with the trees</note>. That is to say, the Torah did not publicize which tree Adam ate from, so as not to disgrace it. And if you say it is a hidden secret and it is not known where the Tree of Life is—this is not so; it is known. Nevertheless, the verse did not publicize it out of respect. He brings proof that it is known, for they take from it above because it was blemished by Adam’s sin.
As proven in the tracts of Blessings and Sanhedrin: Rabbi Judah said they were grapes, as it is said: "Their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter." Those clusters were the ones the spies brought into the world; thus it is known, yet the verse did not publicize it. Adam’s sin was similar to the sin of the Calf, for "Adam transgressed the covenant." Understand this. Midrash: "The mouse" <note>original: "אכב"ר"</note>... the collection of Torah, Tephillin, Circumcision, and Tzitzit. The World of Action vibrates within the spheres of the constellations.
There are three aspects to "Fate" <note>term: Mazal — literally "constellation," referring to destiny or luck</note> for Israel. Sometimes there is no "Fate" for Israel except from the side of sin, which is considered significant, or from the side of merit. Sometimes there is "Fate" for Israel who merit "two tables" <note>wealth in this world and reward in the next</note>, as our Sages said: "Is it hateful to the righteous to eat from two worlds?" This relates to the "Fate" that hovers over the... Sometimes the Holy One, blessed be He, turns an evil fate into a good one. This is the third aspect: not just nullifying the evil, but transforming it into good. For this reason, the great sages were anxious... and the Holy One transformed it into mercy through those who know, like Joshua. "They are men of form" <note>original: "אנשי צורה"</note>, meaning those who know the shapes of the stars and constellations and the lines of the face, and are familiar with the celestial systems.
They said what the system showed so that the Sage might transform his prayer for good. So too with Rabban Gamliel and his daughter. Regarding this aspect, it was said of old that "Circumcision... who turned into the blood of circumcision." And "inwardly" is the fate, for so it happened to Abraham, as proven in the chapter "One who was overtaken by darkness": Abraham said, "Master of the Universe, I have looked at my astrology and I am not fit to father a child." The Holy One said to him, "Go out [of your astrology]!" As it is written: "He took him outside." We conclude that he was raised above the "Mazar" <note>the zodiacal belt</note>, as it is written: "Who raised up one from the East <note>original: "מזרח" (Mizrach) — punning on "Mazar"</note>, whom righteousness calls to his feet?"
At the time he was commanded regarding Circumcision, the fate of "Abram cannot father" was transformed. It is written there: "And I will set My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly" <note>Genesis 17:2</note>. This indicates that at the time of "Fate" <note>Mazal</note>, his power... one who wishes to merit [wealth] should raise his hands in Tephillin. When he asked to become wealthy... and this is according to what is found in Tractate Chullin, where Rava expounded: "If [I take] from a thread to a shoe-strap"—this refers to Tzitzit and Tephillin. There it is said: "Lest you say, 'I have made Abram rich.'" Since that includes Tzitzit—as written there regarding the "thread"—the "inward Tzitzit" which are placed on the left side near the Tephillin, according to our custom, are included with the Tephillin. Thus, the difficulty I raised is resolved: Tzitzit are behind them, to the West, hinting at the rotation of the spheres and their setting in the West, to fulfill what is written: "and the host of heaven bows down to You," for the Divine Presence is in the West. One who returns to the Tzitzit merits and receives the face of the Divine Presence <note>original: "שכינה" (Shekhinah)</note>, as it is said: "And you shall see it"—the blue thread <note>term: Tekhelet — the biblical blue dye</note> is like the sea, the sea like the sky, and the sky like the Throne of Glory. May the Name be complete and the Throne be complete, Amen, may it be His will. Finished.

->Intent of the 83rd [Chapter]: Explanation of Psalm 23 "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want" regarding the word 'sufficiency'<-

**In** general, his request was like his prayer elsewhere: "Give me neither poverty nor riches," for poverty, Heaven forbid, might cause one to transgress the will of his Creator. Similarly, "riches are kept for the owner to his hurt." Just as Jacob prayed for "bread to eat"—not for luxuries. "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." It is known that being sunk in the desire for money is both a craving and a lack, for "one who has a hundred wants two hundred." Since he craves, he is in a state of "wanting." Therefore, it is said that "anxiety is broad," for out of the abundance of his praises he craves such a sum. It is said: "those who seek the Lord shall not lack any good thing"—meaning what is "good" in their eyes, for they are happy with their portion. In contrast, "Many are the sorrows of the wicked"—the wicked person has many sorrows because he craves to increase his strength. But he who trusts in the Lord, even if he lacks a specific thing, the "Good" will surround him as if he were full of all good. This is his prayer: "I shall not want."

**And** afterward he said: "I know that whether the Holy One, blessed be He, pities me with wealth or pities me with poverty, I will nevertheless cleave to Him." Nonetheless, my request is for the middle path, which the Holy One finds pleasant. "He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside still waters." This includes all good things, as written in the blessing of Issachar: "crouching... and he saw that rest was good." I know that "He restores my soul"—that the soul shall return to God, for it cleaves to Him. The reason is: "I will spend my wealth for the sake of His Name," meaning for Torah study, the building of the Temple, and for the poor. "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death"—which is the way to describe poverty, for a poor man is considered as if dead—"I will fear no evil." The reason is: "for I think that You are my staff," according to the Sages' saying: "It is enough for the servant to be like his master." For the Divine Presence, as it were, is in a state of lowliness during times of trouble. See the *Tola'at Yaakov* regarding the secrets of Shavuot and Sukkot concerning the matter of charity. Nevertheless, my request is for the "middle way," namely: "Thy rod <note>poverty/discipline</note> and Thy staff <note>support</note>, they comfort me."
And although our Sages said: "Is it hateful to the righteous to merit two tables?" I desire only the High Table hidden away for the righteous in the time to come. This is "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil." This will be explained with the Sages' statement in Tractate Shabbat: "'Let your garments be always white'—this is a parable of a king who invited his servants... those who adorned themselves for the feast sat and ate and drank, while those who did not adorn themselves stood and watched." Rabbi Meir said in the name of Rabban Gamliel: "Even they appear like attendants; rather, both groups sit, but these eat while those are hungry, these drink while those are thirsty." Some say: "'Let your garments be always white' refers to Tzitzit, and 'let not oil be lacking from your head' refers to Tephillin." This is a separate matter, and it adds to the first idea. It follows the statement: "The righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence." I will first mention what is written by the author of *Tziyuni* on the portion *Ki Tisa*: the "jewelry" that Israel merited when they said "We will do" before "We will listen" was spiritual light and Tephillin. Behold, the Tzitzit are on your "garments"—the "Sabbath and Festival garments" which are discussed elsewhere as the "secret of the soul's garment." Thus, the Tzitzit are the secret of the clothing, and the "crown on the head" and the "feast" mean enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence. This is "a table before my enemies," as it says there: "both groups sit." "Anointed with oil" is the secret of the Tephillin, as in "oil on your head." "My cup runs over..."

# Tractate Passover
## Enriched Matzah

...and to exalt Him, but only from the perspective of His actions, not from the perspective of His true essence. Therefore, the Hallel <note>The "Hallel" is a prayer of praise consisting of Psalms 113–118</note> is only recited upon the Exodus from Egypt, on all festivals that serve as a "remembrance of the Exodus," or during the days of Hanukkah, which was also a time of a great miracle. In these instances, we offer praise because of His deeds. However, on other days that are not days of miracles, His essence is perceived only as His essence—and "who can express the mighty acts of the Lord?" <note>Psalm 106:2</note>. To attempt to describe His essence is nothing but blasphemy and reviling. I have already elaborated on this elsewhere. This is the secret meaning of the verse: "And I will take you to Me for a people, and then I will be to you a God" <note>Exodus 6:7</note>; for other than through this relationship, you have no grasp of the Divine except through the miracles I perform for you.

(Here the secret of the Four Cups is explained to expound upon the laws of the Four Cups.) They instituted two cups before the meal and two cups after the meal. The meal itself is an allusion to the "Feast of the Leviathan" <note>A legendary banquet for the righteous in the World to Come</note>, which the righteous will merit. The level of the righteous is within the partition of the ministering angels, bound beneath the Throne of Glory. Thus, there are two cups before them and two cups after them. The level and perfection of the righteous is according to those three components in the verse: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might" <note>Deuteronomy 6:5</note>, which represent the perfection of the Soul, the Body, and Wealth. Correspondingly, there are the Passover sacrifice, Matzah, and Maror <note>bitter herbs</note> that come during this meal.

Through these three things, Israel was enslaved in their entirety: in the Soul—"a nation from within a nation," for these were idolaters and those were idolaters, hence the command "Withdraw and take for yourselves" <note>meaning "withdraw from idolatry"</note>; in the Body—through mortar and bricks; and if in their bodies, how much more so in their wealth, for "whatever a slave acquires, his master acquires." They were then redeemed through these three: "And I will take you to Me for a people and I will be to you a God" in spirituality; "You shall serve God on this mountain" in the body; and "the children of Israel went out with a high hand" regarding wealth, as they "plundered Egypt."

The Passover sacrifice corresponds to the perfection of the Soul, for it alludes to the nullification of idolatry. For the Lord is "greater than all gods"—if He is greater than the Guardian Angel of Egypt, who is the Great Minister, how much more so is He greater than the others. Even though that angel drew close to the Holy, the matter was not immediately nullified when the Lord struck the firstborn. The "Glory" remained until the splitting of the Sea, but it did not die, for it is like the matter of Israel's idolatry; it is not nullified even for His people. There was some holiness there, as the Egyptians were circumcised <note>A reference to a tradition that some Egyptians underwent circumcision</note>, therefore it was not totally nullified until the splitting of the Red Sea. This was the matter of Israel’s contention with Moses in the portion of *Beshalach*. At the splitting of the sea, it was totally nullified, and then Jethro said: "Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods." Then was fulfilled: "And it happened in those many days that the king of Egypt died" <note>Exodus 2:23</note>—meaning his spiritual power died completely. Although this verse is written while they were still in Egypt, it is only mentioned there because of the covenant of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; but "their cry went up" only because the King of Egypt, who was near to the Beginning, died completely only in "those many days," meaning at the time of the splitting of the sea. Then the perfection of the Soul was established.

Matzah represents the perfection of the Body. Adam the First distorted and ruined the world. He became like this skin that covers everything; matzah is "skin" <note>original: "עור" (or)</note> and not "flour" <note>original: "קמיח" (kamiah)</note>, the secret of the "garments of skin" <note>Genesis 3:21</note>. They were meant to be "garments of light" <note>a wordplay on "Or" with an Aleph vs "Or" with an Ayin</note>, "to work it and to guard it." Matzah is "guarded" (*shmura*). Adam "pulled his foreskin" <note>a Talmudic metaphor for distancing himself from God</note>, and it is written, "No uncircumcised man shall eat of it." I found in a book that for this reason, we do not give matzah to a child to eat, for it stands in place of the Passover sacrifice.

(Here one should expound all the laws of Chametz and Matzah, the laws of purging vessels, all the statutes, and the arrangement of the tables. One might say that their sustenance and livelihood come from the House of the Holy One, Blessed be He.) Here I will elaborate on the secret of Money: one should not be a hypocrite regarding money, but should rejoice in his portion even if his means are limited. He should rejoice in them, for the bitter herb (*Maror*) is called *Chasa* <note>lettuce</note>, implying that the wealthy should have "pity" (*chas*) on the bitter poor whose lives are embittered. Especially in this time when wealth was diminishing from above. Therefore, they were stringent to say "All who are hungry, let them come and eat."

This is the "Search for Chametz" <note>leaven</note> which the later authorities alluded to: all matters of leaven are mentioned in connection with the mouse. "A slave is sold..." and "it is enough that the mouse lies on the denarius." There is a "white mouse" and a "black mouse"—a white maneh <note>a unit of currency</note> and a black maneh. The matter of "entering and exiting" and "carrying out and bringing in"—all the inquiries can be explained through this. Also, be careful of leaven, for all the "honor of His name" which our Sages said is the "searching of the dogs." When Israel went out of Egypt, "no dog whetted its tongue"—meaning they did not sharpen their tongues.

Rabbi Eliezer ben Zadok was asked: Why does a cat recognize its master, but a dog does not recognize its master? He replied: One who eats from what a mouse has eaten forgets his learning; how much more so the cat who eats the mouse itself! His students asked him: Why does a mouse have more "rule" over everything than any other simple creature? He said: Because it is inherently evil. What is "evil"? Some say even the idols of the gentiles. He alluded that the one who performs charity creates a garment, as it is written: "He put on righteousness as a coat of mail." Rav Pappa said: Even the "guards of the cupboards" are miracles (for this matter of charity has the merit to protect one even in the grave). The cat—Rabbi Yochanan said: "If the Torah had not been given, we would have learned modesty from the cat." The explanation is that a cat does not relieve itself in front of anyone. One might ask: Why was man created last? So that if he becomes arrogant, they can say to him: "The gnat preceded you."

The cat has an "entry" but no "exit"—this is a hint to a miser who brings in but does not give out. The cat "brings out" its waste in secret, which is modesty and a good trait. But nevertheless, when it eats the mouse—which represents jealousy and stringency—it "does not recognize its owner" <note>meaning it forgets its spiritual source</note>. And the dog, which "recognizes its owner," is a miser and a glutton, yet it is remembered for charity and for all evil <note>the text here explores the complex symbolic nature of the dog in Jewish folklore</note>. Regarding such a dog, it is said "no dog shall whet its tongue." Regarding this dog, they alluded to the story in the Midrash Rabbah:

Even one who was a scholar but had not learned the entire Torah... Rami bar Hama did not include Rav Menashia bar Gada... who had learned Scripture, Mishnah, Talmud, and Aggadah, but had not learned the additional Sifra and Sifrei... Therefore, he is called a "dog." It is possible to say that this was the night of Passover, and he gathered him into his house to fulfill "All who are hungry, let them come and eat."

These matters are what he thought. The Four Sons of the Haggadah: The "Wise Son" is answered with Scripture. The "Mishnah" is the answer for the wise one where we say "one does not conclude after the Passover with a dessert"—that is a Mishnah. "Aggadah" is the answer for the "Wicked Son," for "because of this"—that is Aggadah and Midrash. "Talmud" is for the "One who does not know how to ask"... The man replied that he desired the Torah, and regarding Egypt it is written: "When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God

There are two explanations for this: either that he did not respond to the insult, or that he did not speak slander (*Lashon Hara*) about his fellow. Behold, the secret of the Four Cups and the Passover meal, with Matzah and Maror in the middle, is explained. They correspond to: *Chesed* (Kindness)—"The Lord is good to all"; their identity was not changed, and the change is only on the side of the recipients. They did not change their names, being fenced in from immorality, corresponding to the fear of God that flows from the side of *Gevurah* (Might/Judgment), the root of which concerns "nakedness" (immorality). This is why we read the portion of Forbidden Relations on Yom Kippur. From there, they should fear and "not approach the daughters of man." <meta>This page continues the discussion of Divine names and the spiritual significance of the Passover rituals, shifting from the specific laws of the Four Cups to a deep philosophical and Kabbalistic exploration of how God governs the world through both nature and miraculous providence.</meta>

# Tractate Passover
## On Divine Governance and the Two Names of God

<meta>catchword: to awaken</meta>

It is the custom of the Jewish people, based on our Torah, to believe that God "gives to a man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds" <note>Jeremiah 17:10</note>. See the book *Akedat Yitzchak* <note>A classic 15th-century philosophical commentary by Rabbi Isaac Arama</note> on the portion of *Pekudei* regarding these two modes of Divine conduct, for he elaborates on this at length. These two modes of conduct are represented by two Divine names: **YHWH** and **Elohim**. **Elohim** corresponds to the laws of Nature, while **YHWH** corresponds to Providence—the miraculous changing of nature. 

As the *Zohar* writes in many places, and as the author of the *Akedat Yitzchak* writes at the end of the third chapter, the name **Elohim** hints at the natural order and its fixed, customary arrangement. This is what the Sages meant when they said: "The world follows its natural custom" <note>Talmud, Avodah Zarah 54b</note>. Therefore, nature is attributed to the name **Elohim**. Furthermore, the word **Elohim** everywhere signifies "Judge," for He is the leader and arranger of all existing things according to the line of strict justice and natural law. This natural order remains constant and unchanging, a necessary chain of effects from their specific causes, which is why this name is used throughout the Account of Creation <note>Genesis chapter 1, where the name *Elohim* is used exclusively</note>.

However, at the conclusion of the account, it is said: "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created..." <note>Genesis 2:4</note>. This means: these are the natural developments of heaven and earth according to the simple nature placed within them at their creation. But when the need arises to change something within them—according to the requirements of Divine Providence and the "repair" of the world—this is done through the name **YHWH Elohim**. For this Great Name (**YHWH**) sits above and rules over the natural power created by the name **Elohim**. When the need arises, it is said: "The Lord is greater than all gods (*elohim*)" <note>Exodus 18:11</note>. On the day this "repair" is performed, the greatness of this Name (**YHWH**) is revealed over the name **Elohim**. 

Corresponding to these two modes of conduct, the New Year of *Tishrei* <note>Rosh Hashanah</note> was established as the beginning of natural existence, while the New Year of *Nisan* <note>The month of Passover</note> is the first for the "miraculous" conduct of Providence. These are the words of the author of the *Akedat Yitzchak*. Many commentators have already written that the name **Elohim** indicates Nature <note>In Hebrew Gematria (numerology), the word *Elohim* (86) equals the word *HaTeva* (Nature)</note>, while the name **YHWH** indicates He who "was, is, and will be," and that everything exists through His will and desire to change or arrange it.

Even though these two modes—Nature and Providence—seem to oppose one another (for when one rises, the other falls, as Providence overrides Nature), they are nonetheless one in their inner unity. Nature draws close to Providence through the secret of "Internal Unity." This is similar to what Rabbi Berab d'Orazio <note>Likely a reference to a specific Italian Rabbinic authority</note> wrote in his first discourse: 

"All that we discuss regarding the Account of Creation (*Ma'aseh Bereshit*) and all that the Sages understood of it is only through Divine influence... Regarding the Account of Creation, Maimonides <note>Rabbi Moses ben Maimon, 12th-century philosopher</note> said it refers to the Science of Nature. This contains great secrets. However, there is nothing in the study of the elements or the compounds derived from them that would necessitate such extreme secrecy or hiding from the public. If that were the case, we would have to know the limit of what can be said and what should not be publicized to the masses. There is no doubt that anything concerning the explanation of nature should not be hidden, but rather publicized; for medicine, agriculture, and shepherding are all derived from natural science, and those who settle the land and produce fruit are constantly 'studying' the laws of creation! Therefore, we cannot say that the Account of Creation refers *only* to natural science as humans understand it."

The Account of Creation is founded on the lower world, not the upper (which would be the Account of the Chariot/Metaphysics). If the Account of Creation is not merely the knowledge of nature and its affairs, then what is it? This creates a confusion that needs resolution. There is no doubt that the Account of Creation *is* the Science of Nature, but not from the perspective of human research and investigation. Rather, it is from the perspective of knowledge that is hidden from research and only known through Divine flow. It is the "sea" that connects to the world of Intellect. 

Through human investigation, we can know the "what" of a creature—its functions and commands—but we cannot truly know its inner "form" through research alone, unless experience brings it to light. Even when we know the *action* through experience, we do not know the *cause* of the action at all. For example, we may know through logic that a magnet <term>magnente</term> causes the death of fish <note>A folk-scientific belief of the era</note>, or we know that a human laughs, or that a lodestone attracts iron. We know these things because experience showed them to us, but the *cause* is unknown because these things stem from the "Form" <note>The "Formal Cause" or spiritual essence</note>. This gate is closed to all human philosophical inquiry.

The powers that arise from the *matter* of a thing are different from those that arise from the *essence* (Form) of the thing. The latter are hidden. This is why Abraham <note>The text likely means a philosopher or a specific historical figure cited by the author</note> laughed at Galen <note>The famous Roman physician/philosopher</note>, because Galen said he did not know the cause of why a human laughs. Galen admitted it was impossible for him to know the cause, because laughter is something that emerges from the very essence and form of the human being.

According to this, the **Account of Creation** is the *true* science of nature that philosophers seek—the knowledge of the true essence of things. This links the conduct of the "Forms," which are the Separate Intellects <note>Angels or metaphysical forces</note>. These cannot be known unless Divine influence brings them. Thus, the Account of Creation is actually a subset of the **Account of the Chariot** <note>Ma'aseh Merkavah - Metaphysics/Mysticism</note>. Since the Account of Creation is the knowledge of things that are suspended from and drawn from those Divine Names (the Separate Intellects), it is right to call it the Account of the Chariot.

You should know that there are two parts to the study of these Separate Intellects:
1. The connection and bond of that which is *below* them to them.
2. Their own dependence and emergence from that which is *above* them.

There is a massive difference between these two. The first is what we call the **Account of Creation**: knowing the true form of things, which is the "lower knot" that holds onto the Angels and the "Living Creatures" (*Hayyot*) of the Chariot. The second is the knowledge of the chain of emanation of the Angels themselves. These are the words of the Rabbi which I wished to transcribe. 

The general principle is this: Nature, in its inner secret, is close to the secret of the Divine. They are attached to one another in the secret of the "Holy Chain of Emanation," which has no separation or detachment. The two names **YHWH** and **Elohim** are a complete unity. However, the Name **YHWH** is more essential and internal than the name **Elohim**, just as the "Chariot" is to the "Creation," or the Soul is to the Body. The name **YHWH** is subtle and hidden, while the name **Elohim** is more revealed. 

Similarly, you find that the conduct of Nature is more revealed than the conduct of Providence. Nature follows its custom, but Providence—which is the higher power guiding nature—influences Israel according to their deeds and their spiritual awakening. This higher guidance is often hidden—"no eye has seen it, O God, beside You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>—except during the miracles of Egypt and the like, where this guidance was revealed "eye to eye." But usually, this guidance is hidden while natural guidance is revealed.

This is why Man was created in the "Image of God": to make His Divinity known. He was created with a revealed body and a hidden soul, corresponding to the two names **YHWH** and **Elohim**. Accordingly, he was given the Torah, which has revealed actions and hidden meanings. When a man cleaves to his good deeds and draws his physical matter closer to his spiritual soul, even though his body is "coarse," it becomes a "subtle garment." 

This is the secret of the bond between body and soul. Service of the Creator involves both, as the Sages said: "With all your heart—with both your inclinations, the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination" <note>Mishnah Berakhot 9:5</note>. The physical matter is drawn from the "Evil Inclination" <note>The physical drives</note> and the soul from the "Good Inclination." When they are united, the physicality is "clothed" within the spirituality. In this way, the body becomes a refined, pure substance, ready to receive intellectual concepts, just as Adam was before he sinned. At that time, he was clothed in **"Garments of Light"** (written with the letter *Aleph* - **אור**). The *Aleph* hints at the Unity of God. This is the secret of the cleaving of **YHWH** to **Elohim**—the revealed clinging to the hidden.

But after Adam followed his physicality and separated his matter from his soul, he was clothed in **"Garments of Skin"** (written with the letter *Ayin* - **עור**). The number of the letter *Ayin* is 70, representing the "70 Nations" whose conduct is left to nature, judgment, and the 70 celestial princes. This is the meaning of Nature from the perspective of coarse matter.

The ultimate goal is for the name **YHWH** to be his **Elohim**—not the "other gods" of the nations, but the inner **Elohim** which is the "Chariot" for the Tetragrammaton, in the secret of spiritual unity. Adam "cut the shoots" <note>A metaphor for heresy or causing separation in the Divine realms</note> and brought upon himself the "Garments of Skin" (*Ayin*). This is why it says of the Generation of the Dispersion <note>The Tower of Babel</note>: "And the Lord came down to see... which the sons of Adam built" <note>Genesis 11:5</note>. The Sages say this means the "sons of the first Adam." For in that generation, they actually separated themselves into the 70 Princes. At that time, the name **YHWH** (Providence) was not known to them, for they were ruled by the 70 Princes (Nature), and no spiritual awakening came from below **to awaken**...

<summary>This page discusses the Kabbalistic relationship between the Divine names YHWH (Providence) and Elohim (Nature), explaining that while they seem distinct, they are a single unity. It explores the philosophical limits of human reason in understanding nature and the transition of humanity from "Garments of Light" to "Garments of Skin" after the primordial sin.</summary>
