# Tractate Passover

In the future, when one leaves the banquet to drink, David will recite the blessing over the cup of wine, as it is stated in the chapter "Erev Pesachim" <note>Talmud, Pesachim 119b; refers to the messianic banquet</note>. Even though "surely goodness and mercy shall follow me" <note>Psalm 23:6</note> appear to be diminished or limited in this world, I will "return to the house of the Lord for length of days" in eternity. Furthermore, we can reconcile two verses that differ in their phrasing: one says "Gracious and Merciful is the Lord, slow to anger and great in kindness" <note>Psalm 145:8</note>, while another says "Merciful and Gracious is the Lord, slow to anger and abundant in kindness" <note>Psalm 103:8</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory explained: "Merciful" refers to a sinner who repents immediately; "Gracious" refers to a sinner who does not repent immediately. Thus, the flow of bounty coming from "Mercy" is more powerful than that which comes through "Grace," as the latter is logically more limited. Regarding the phrase "Abundant in Kindness," Rashi explains it refers to one whose merits and sins are perfectly balanced, where God "inclines" the scale toward kindness. For such a person, since he is not perfectly righteous, God bestows a great bounty in this world—this is the "Merciful" aspect—and in the World to Come, He bestows upon him from the aspect of "Grace." But for those who are "Great in Kindness"—meaning their merits clearly outweigh their sins—He bestows upon them in this world from the aspect of "Gracious," and the "Abundant Mercy" is reserved for the World to Come. Amen, may God do so!

***

## Sixth Sermon: Enriched Matzah
<note>Hebrew: *Matzah Ashira*; matzah made with fruit juice or eggs rather than just water.</note>

**"This** is the law of the burnt offering..." <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. In the Midrash, there is a parable of a king who had two stewards <note>original: *megayesim*; often meaning military officers, but here functioning as cooks</note>. The first made a dish for him that was pleasing, and the second made a dish that was also pleasing. We would not know which one was more pleasing, except for the fact that the king commanded the second one, saying, "Make this specific dish." From this, we know the second was more pleasing. Similarly, Noah brought an offering and it was pleasing, as it says: "And the Lord smelled the sweet savor" <note>Genesis 8:21</note>. Israel also brought an offering, as it says: "You shall be careful to offer to Me in its appointed time" <note>Numbers 28:2</note>. We would not know which was more pleasing, except that He commanded Moses: "This is the law of the burnt offering; it is the burnt offering." From this, we know it is more pleasing, as it says: "Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in ancient years" <note>Malachi 3:4</note>. "Days of old" refers to the days of Moses; "ancient years" refers to the days of Solomon. Alternatively: "Days of old" refers to the days of Noah; "ancient years" refers to the days of Abel, when there was no idolatry in the world.

In the Midrash Rabbah, Rabbi Eleazar says: Five letters of the Hebrew alphabet are doubled <note>The letters *Kaf, Mem, Nun, Pe, Tzadi*, which have a different form at the end of a word</note>, and all of them represent the language of redemption:
**Kaf-Kaf:** With which Abraham was redeemed from the "Ur of the Chaldeans," as it says: "Go forth [**L**e**k**h **L**e**k**ha] from your land."
**Mem-Mem:** With which Isaac was redeemed from the Philistines, as it says: "Go away from us [**M**ea**m**enu], for you are much [**M**ime**m**nu] mightier than we."
**Nun-Nun:** With which Jacob was redeemed, as it says: "Rescue me now [Hatzilei**n**i **N**a]."
**Pe-Pe:** With which Israel was redeemed from Egypt, as it says: "I have surely remembered [**P**akod **P**akadti] you."
**Tzadi-Tzadi:** With which God will redeem Israel in the future, as it says: "Behold a man whose name is Sprout [Tze**m**ach], and from his place he shall sprout forth [Yit**z**ma**ch**]" <note>Zechariah 6:12</note>.

<term>Erev Pesachim</term> <note>The eve of Passover; also the name of the 10th chapter of Tractate Pesachim</note>: Near the time of the afternoon offering, a person should not eat until it gets dark. Even a poor person in Israel must not eat until he reclines <note>the posture of free men</note>, and they must not provide him with fewer than four cups of wine, even if he is supported by the communal charity kitchen. In the Gemara, they asked: How could the Rabbis institute something that leads to danger? For it was taught: A man should not eat "pairs" [even numbers], nor drink "pairs," nor wipe twice, nor do his needs in "pairs" <note>Ancient folk belief that even numbers invited demons or bad luck</note>. Rabbi Nahman answered: The verse says, "It is a night of vigils [guarding]" <note>Exodus 12:42</note>—a night that is guarded from damaging spirits. Others say: The "Cup of Blessing" <note>the third cup</note> combines with the others for good but does not combine for evil. Ravina said: The Rabbis instituted four cups as a "way of freedom"; each one is a separate commandment in its own right.

In the Midrash Hazit <note>another name for Midrash Shir HaShirim Rabbah</note>, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai asked Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Yose: "Is it possible you have heard from your father the meaning of 'the crown with which his mother crowned him'?" <note>Song of Songs 3:11</note>. He said, "Yes." He asked, "How did he explain it?" He replied: "It is a parable of a king who had an only daughter whom he loved exceedingly, until he called her 'my daughter.' His love grew until he called her 'my sister.' His love grew further until he called her 'my mother.' So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, loved Israel and called them 'my daughter,' as it says: 'Hear, O daughter, and consider' <note>Psalm 45:11</note>. His love grew until He called them 'my sister,' as it says: 'Open to me, my sister, my love' <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>. His love grew until He called them 'my mother' [*immi*], as it says: 'Attend to Me, My people, and My nation [u-le'ummi], give ear to Me [immi—read as 'my mother']' <note>Isaiah 51:4</note>." Rashi <note>likely referring to a teacher, or a mistake for the Midrashic figure</note> stood and kissed him on his head, saying, "If I had come only to hear this thing, it would have been enough."

Let us return to the first points of the verses and sayings we brought to awaken our hearts:
In the portion "This is the law of the burnt offering," there are several points to consider:
1. What the Sages established in Tractate Yoma: from the phrase "all night," we already know it lasts until morning. Why then does the verse add "until morning"?
2. Why is it stated three times in the portion that "the fire on the altar shall not be extinguished"?
3. According to Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nahman, 13th-century scholar</note>, who explains that the priest needs all the priestly garments—four for an ordinary priest and eight for the High Priest—why does the verse mention the "tunic" more than the other garments?
4. Regarding Rashi's explanation that "he shall strip off his garments" is not a mandatory decree but a matter of "proper conduct" <note>derekh eretz</note>: Is the Torah coming merely to teach us etiquette? This seems impossible regarding commandments.

Regarding the Midrash of the two stewards, we must ask:
1. The parable does not seem to match the reality. The parable says the second steward cooked for the king, and *then* the king decided which was better. But in the reality, the offering of Israel (the second steward) was only brought because of God's command ("You shall be careful to offer to Me").
2. It is difficult when it says "Days of old refers to the days of Noah," for this seems to contradict the earlier point that Noah's sacrifice was not as pleasing as Israel's. We will offer another explanation in Chapter 4 to resolve the parable and its meaning.

Regarding the Mishnah's discussion of the Four Cups:
We must ask why our Sages interpreted these cups differently elsewhere? In Tractate Shabbat, they discuss various numbers of cups. Why did they establish this specific symbolic number for the cups and not for the types of food or other matters? While Rabbi Levi says they correspond to the four cups of Pharaoh's dream, and others say they correspond to the four cups of punishment God will give the nations, Rabbi Yochanan says they correspond to the "Four Redemptions": "I will bring out," "I will save," "I will redeem," and "I will take." We must investigate: why the danger of "pairs" in drinking? And furthermore: how does a person's "insistence" on not drinking pairs affect the spiritual "ministers" <note>spiritual forces/demons</note>?

Regarding the Midrash of "Daughter, Sister, Mother":
We must consider what these titles symbolize. Indeed, the Kabbalists have explained this Midrash thoroughly. See Nachmanides on the portion of *Chayei Sarah* regarding the verse "And the Lord blessed Abraham with everything [*ba-kol*]." However, I have come only to explain this Midrash according to its plain meaning.

The Sabbath before Passover is called "The Great Sabbath" <note>Shabbat HaGadol</note>. The *Tur* <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, 14th-century legalist</note> explains it is named after the great miracle that occurred then. I have already written questions on this in another sermon for the portion of *Tzav*, but a great difficulty remains. We must investigate the nature of this name "Great."

Furthermore, we must examine the Exile in Egypt, which was weakened <note>or processed</note> through the three Patriarchs. The decree was given to Abraham ("Know surely that your seed shall be a stranger"). The beginning of the decree was with Isaac (from the moment he was born). It was completed by Jacob, of whom the Sages said: "Jacob was worthy of descending to Egypt in iron chains," but God brought him there through the merit of his son. It is clear that the center of this chain of exile was Joseph. He was the one who heralded the redemption with the sign "God will surely remember you" [*Pakod Yifkod*]. Even Jacob's journey to Laban was for the sake of Joseph, as it says: "And it was when Rachel had borne Joseph..." <note>Genesis 30:25</note>. As the *Zohar* explains, Jacob's primary intention was for Joseph. Therefore, the birthright was taken from Reuben and given to Joseph. This is the meaning of "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph." Rashi explains that Joseph's life events led to the family's settlement in Egypt. This also explains why Moses took "the bones of Joseph" with him.

When you investigate this matter and the naming of the "Great Sabbath," all the sayings I brought will be resolved, including the purpose of the Egyptian exile. I have written my opinion on this at length in another sermon, but first, we must provide an introduction:
It is known that there are two types of governance through which God leads His world:
1. **Natural Governance:** The fixed celestial and natural order.
2. **Providential Governance:** <note>Text ends mid-sentence</note>

It introduces the distinction between God's "Natural Governance" and "Providential Governance" as a key to understanding the Exile and the "Great Sabbath."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse from the previous page, moving from the rewards of the righteous to the theological "rectification" (tikkun) of the Primordial Man's sin. It explains how biblical figures like David, Jacob, and Joseph worked to repair the spiritual damage caused by Adam and the Golden Calf, culminating in the redemption from Egypt.</meta>

# Sefat Emet (Language of Truth)

Regarding the sin of the Father, the Primordial Man <note>Adam HaRishon</note> who offered a bull [as a sacrifice], and the sons who took a "goat for a sin offering and a calf and a lamb" <note>Leviticus 9:3</note>. Therefore, the verses regarding the bull sacrifice were continuous (see there). Either the world returned to its corrupted state—as it is said: "I said, 'You are godlike beings... but like Adam, you shall die'" <note>Psalm 82:6-7; the author suggests that the immortality intended at the Giving of the Torah was lost due to the Sin of the Golden Calf</note>—and the world required a rectification exactly like the one needed at its creation. Just as the Sin of the Primordial Man occurred at the beginning of the world, so too it happened now at the Giving of the Torah, which was a "new creation of the world," through the Sin of the Golden Calf. This continued until the generation of King [David] arose and began to rectify the Sin of the Golden Calf. As our Sages of blessed memory said: Rav Hana bar Bizna said in the name of Rabbi Shimon the Pious: "A harp was hanging above David’s bed. As soon as midnight arrived, the north wind would blow upon it and it would play of its own accord. David would then rise and occupy himself with the Torah" <note>Talmud, Berakhot 3b</note>. This teaching alludes to King David’s rectification of the Sin of the Golden Calf, as I have explained at length in my discussion of these sweet matters. The name "ADM" <note>Adam</note> is a known acronym for the cycle of **A**dam, **D**avid, and **M**essiah. It was necessary for Adam to be reborn in that generation to rectify the iniquity of the Calf, which occurred at the start of the Giving of the Torah—which was a new creation of the world—resembling Adam’s sin at the very beginning of the world’s creation. This is the meaning of "Man [Adam] is born to toil" <note>Job 5:7</note>, as I wrote, for in the generation of King [David], may peace be upon him, there was wholeness in the "Three Covenants" that I mentioned: "Beholders of good" and "Goodly of appearance" <note>referring to David's physical and spiritual beauty</note>. That generation was "goodly of sight" and worthy of the "goodly building" <note>the Temple</note>, as it is written. This means he pleased the Holy One, Blessed be He, with songs and praises.

And the living truth was always in our mouths, the **Covenant of the Procreative Organ** <note>Hebrew: *Brit HaMa'or*; a reference to circumcision and sexual purity</note>, as is known regarding the matter of Abishag <note>the Shunammite woman who served David in his old age</note>. David guarded himself from her since she was not among his wives. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "He did not come near her" <note>1 Kings 1:4</note>, even though she served him constantly and lay in his bosom, and the cold was still in his bones. This is why he said, "Call Bathsheba to me," for he needed to utilize the matter of Bathsheba <note>to establish the kingship</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Anyone who says David sinned is but mistaken" <note>Talmud, Shabbat 56a</note>. This is the secret of what King Saul said: "Whose son is this youth?" <note>1 Samuel 17:55; Hebrew: *Elem*, meaning youth or hidden</note>. He saw signs in him that he was fit for the "Hiddenness of the Eye" and to be king over Israel, for *Elem* is a language of "strength" and a language of "hiddenness." This is a wondrous matter. Let us return to our subject: the Patriarchs were rectifying the **Three Covenants**, and Jacob was crowned with all of them, as it is written: "He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob" <note>Numbers 23:21</note>, as Rashi explains. He was perfect in the rectification of the three sins of the Primordial Man, as it is written: "Jacob was a whole man" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. "And Jacob arrived whole" <note>Genesis 33:18</note>—whole in his body, whole in his wealth, and whole in his Torah. "Body" refers to the **Covenant of the Procreative Organ**, as the Zohar mentions in many places that the body and the covenant are considered one. "Wealth" corresponds to the **Covenant of the Tongue**, for "Voice" <note>Kol</note> has the same numerical value as "Wealth" <note>Mamon</note>, and our Sages said that giving money to charity silences the Accuser more than anything else. "Torah" corresponds to the **Covenant of the Eye**, as it says: "Then I shall not be ashamed when I look upon all Your commandments" <note>Psalm 119:6</note>. This means he reached such diligence in Torah that he found in it something to focus his thoughts upon, to gaze at this spiritual form and lift his eyes [from worldly things]. But the righteous one who is attached to the Torah—we do not restrain him, rather he turns away [from vanity]. This is what the *Hadrat Kodesh* <note>a mystical commentary</note> alluded to. The "beauty" <note>Shofra</note> of Jacob was like the beauty of the Primordial Man before the sin. It is known that everything that happened to Jacob happened to Joseph, for he was the "extension of the father." This is the secret of "And Joseph was handsome of form and handsome of appearance" <note>Genesis 39:6</note>, in the secret of Jacob’s beauty, for we find that Joseph was perfect in these **Three Covenants**: 

1. **Covenant of the Eye**: Joseph merited the blessing "over the eye," as it is written: "Joseph is a fruitful bough... by a well [eye]" <note>Genesis 49:22; *Alei Ayin*</note>. He merited this because he stretched himself over his mother <note>Rachel</note> to hide her from the eyes of Esau.
2. **Covenant of the Procreative Organ**: As is known from the secret of the story of Potiphar’s wife, where he maintained his purity, and the "Righteous One" is beautifully connected in the language of the Kabbalists. 
3. **Covenant of the Tongue**: As found in the Talmud (Tractate Sotah, chapter "Elu Ne'emarin"): Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: At the moment Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Without you, no man shall lift his hand or his foot," his astrologers said to him: "Will you set a slave, whose master bought him for twenty pieces of silver, to rule over us?" Pharaoh replied: "I see royal traits in him." They said: "If so, he should know the seventy languages." Gabriel came that night and taught Joseph the seventy languages, but he could not learn them. Gabriel then added one letter from the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to his name, and he learned them, as it says: "He appointed it in Joseph [Yehosef] for a testimony... I heard a language I knew not" <note>Psalm 81:6; the letter 'He' was added</note>. In the morning, whatever language Pharaoh spoke, Joseph answered him. Finally, Joseph spoke in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note>, and Pharaoh did not know what he was saying. Pharaoh said, "Teach it to me," but he could not learn it. Pharaoh made him swear [not to reveal this]. 

Thus, Joseph was perfect in these covenants, which are the rectification for the sin of the Primordial Man. Therefore, he called out the "hosts of God" <note>the brothers</note> for lacking these three, according to his perception: the sin of "a limb from a living animal," "forbidden relations," and that they called the sons of the handmaids "slaves." Calling them names is a sin of the **Covenant of the Tongue**. Forbidden relations is a sin of the **Covenant of the Procreative Organ**. "A limb from a living animal" is similar to a sin of the **Covenant of the Eye**. For behold, an animal that is taken [while alive] is forbidden to the descendants of Noah, which is logical. But it would be proper for it to be permitted; however, the Torah shows us that the "limb" represents the whole body, and the body follows it. So too is the "Eye"—for everything follows the eye, as our Sages said: "The eye sees, the heart covets, and the physical organs complete the action" <note>Rashi on Numbers 15:39</note>. There is also a great secret here: the "limb from the living" <note>Ever Min HaChay</note> refers to Abraham, who represents the **Covenant of the Eye**. This is in the secret of the "Limb of the Chariot" <note>Ever HaMerkavah</note>, for wherever the holy sparks spread, they are called "a limb from the Living One" <note>meaning God</note>. Abraham is the secret of the Chariot. Indeed, the letters of "Abraham" <note>אברהם</note> can be rearranged as "Aver Mah" <note>Limb of What</note>, and the secret of "Mah" is the Name of God <note>the Tetragrammaton with a numerical value of 45</note> which fills all the joints and limbs of the Chariot. Abraham is so much the "Limb of the true Living One" that the holiness spread through him. Therefore, "a limb from the living" alludes to the **Covenant of the Eye**, which was perfect in Abraham; Abraham was the rectification of the Covenant of the Eye. Consequently, when Joseph saw the lack of these three covenants in his brothers, according to his perception, he complained to his father. He was perfect in these three to rectify the corruption of the Primordial Man. Thus, it is written at Joseph’s birth: "God has taken away [*asaf*] my reproach" <note>Genesis 30:23</note>. The philosophers wrote that "reproach" is the feeling of shame. Our Sages said that the Primordial Man "stretched his foreskin" <note>tried to hide his circumcision/covenant</note>. Joseph’s "tunic of many colors" <note>Ketonet Passim</note> was a "tunic of light" <note>Ketonet Or</note> for Joseph, in contrast to the "garments of skin" <note>Ketonet Or</note> of the Primordial Man. The Primordial Man "cut the shoots" <note>committed heresy/separation</note>; our Sages said he was a heretic. But Joseph was the "Gatherer" <note>Asaf</note>, a sign of unity. After the secret of Jacob and the tribes, "One" <note>Echad - Aleph, Chet, Dalet</note> is formed: **A**leph is Jacob; **Ch**et (8) is the four sons of the Matriarchs and the four sons of the handmaids; Joseph connects the letters of "One" together. He was a "Gatherer" into a single connection like his father, for whatever happened to Jacob happened to Joseph. He was the youth with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah—the **D**alet (4) of the "One"—merging the **Ch**et (8) with the **D**alet (4). 

On this secret of "One," I explained the verse: "And he went with Jacob to Padan Aram" <note>Genesis 28:5</note because of Joseph. I already wrote that the Primordial Man was a heretic and cut into the Unity. It is known that in the Torah, the letter *Dalet* of "One" <note>Echad</note> is written large, and the *Resh* of "Do not bow to an**other** god" <note>Acher</note> is written large. A person must see that he does not, Heaven forbid, swap a *Dalet* for a *Resh* or a *Resh* for a *Dalet*, for that would destroy the entire world. This is the meaning of the verse: "The perversions [D-R] are there," for swapping these letters causes ruin. I also wrote that the Primordial Man caused "garments of skin" <note>Or with an Ayin</note> for the "Eye" <note>Ayin</note>, which refers to the seventy [numerical value of Ayin] guardian angels of the nations. Because of this, the holy sparks of the souls were scattered and separated among the nations. Jacob had to go to Padan Aram to unify his soul with the holy souls there—the souls of the Matriarchs. This is the secret of "Aram"—through the sin of Adam, the *Dalet* turned into a *Resh* [making *Adam* into *Aram*]. Had he not sinned, there would have been no need to go to Aram, for holiness would have filled the whole earth. When Jacob descended there, his entire intent was for Joseph—meaning, to have one special person here who would rectify the sins of the Primordial Man. That was Joseph, who was the secret of "One." All of this was a rectification for the sin of the Primordial Man. 

Furthermore, let us look at the Patriarchs' desire to descend to Egypt: Abraham descended to Egypt with Sarah his wife. Isaac sought to descend to Egypt, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Dwell in this land... do not go down to Egypt" <note>Genesis 26:2</note> because he was a "perfect burnt offering." Jacob also descended and was there until the day of his death. The reason is that this "dwelling" <note>Gerut</note> was a rectification for the "expulsion" that the Primordial Man suffered when he was driven from the Garden of Eden. For it is written of Egypt: "Like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt" <note>Genesis 13:10</note>. This is the secret of the exile of the Israeli nation to Egypt: to refine, purify, and whiten the "filth of the soul" that was darkened since the days of the Primordial Man. So it is written in *Tola'at Yaakov* regarding the Festival of Matzot: "This is the reason for the Egyptian exile, which is the 'iron furnace'—the exile of Israel there was to be rectified from that dross and to leave their dirt and filth there, which was mixed into their form by the power of the 'naked soul' <note>the Serpent</note>." They became "naked" of the life of the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note>, as it is said: "And you were naked and bare" <note>Ezekiel 16:7</note>. After the refining and whitening, they merited to be clothed in the beauty of the Divine Presence, as it is said: "And Your cloud stands over them" <note>Numbers 14:14</note>. This reversal had to happen specifically in Egypt for the reasons I wrote. It was achieved through the three Patriarchs and Joseph the Righteous. The decree was told to Abraham: "Know surely..." <note>Genesis 15:13</note>, and it began when Isaac was born. Jacob and his sons descended, and the cause of their movement was Joseph, because the three Patriarchs and Joseph were rectifying the sins of the Primordial Man. When Israel left Egypt, it is said: "And Moses took the bones [*atzmot*] of Joseph with him" <note>Exodus 13:19</note>, which refers to the "essence" [*atzmiut*] of Joseph and his being. For he testified about the Israeli nation that "He beheld no toil in Israel" <note>Numbers 23:21</note>, for they were perfect in the **Three Covenants** mentioned. Thus our Sages said: "By virtue of four things our ancestors were redeemed from Egypt: Because they did not change their names, they did not change their language, they were guarded from forbidden relations, and there was no slander among them" <note>Midrash Lekach Tov</note>. These four matters are included in the **Three Covenants**: "Guarded from forbidden relations" is the **Covenant of the Procreative Organ**. "No slander" and "did not change their language" is the **Covenant of the Tongue**. "Did not change their names" is the **Covenant of the Eye**.

<summary>This page discusses how the Patriarchs and Joseph rectified the original sin of Adam through the "Three Covenants" of the Eye, Tongue, and Organ. It explains that the Egyptian exile served as a "refining furnace" to remove the spiritual impurity caused by Adam, eventually allowing Israel to be redeemed through their moral purity.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and kabbalistic analysis of the Passover Seder, specifically focusing on the symbols of Pesach, Matzah, and Maror as they relate to the three aspects of time and divine providence.</meta>

### Tractate Pesachim

For truth is a "precious vessel," and the author of this statement characterizes his denial as "bitter sense." Because of this, he referred to it with the word "he" <note>Hebrew: *hu*</note>, a pronoun that encompasses the idea that man is created in the image of God. According to our explanation, this refers to the aspect of "Life," meaning the specific Divine Providence that Pharaoh denied. And behold, Rashi explained our portion regarding "His truth" <note>original: *amito*</note> in the same way it is written regarding "the number of the fourth part <note>or "procreation"</note> of Israel." As Rashi explained this matter, the eye of the wicked Balaam was blinded by how the Holy One, blessed be He, supervises even this matter—namely, the reproductive acts of Israel. Regarding this, it says "He said," hinting at measurement and boundaries. Regarding Providence, he used the word "Truth." This means to say that His Providence has a limit. Every place explains how far the boundary of Providence reaches, as it is said: "Who measured the heavens with a span" <note>Isaiah 40:12</note>. This is like the claim of all heretics: "The heavens are the Lord's heavens, but the earth He has given to the children of men" <note>Psalm 115:16</note>.

The term "Old Man" <note>original: *Zaken*, referring to the Ancient of Days</note> hints at the aspect of "Will Be" <note>Hebrew: *Yihyeh*, the future</note>. For after all the wars that will occur in the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will reveal His divinity and remove the heart of stone. Then everyone will know that "The Lord is one and His name is one," and His glory will be revealed, full of mercy. This is as Rashi explained on the verse "I am the Lord your God" <note>Exodus 20:2</note>—see there. Also, at that time, the Holy One, blessed be He, will reveal that He is the "Ancient of Days," the beginning of all beginnings. Even the "gods of the nations" were created by Him, blessed be He; by His will He created them, and by His will He annuls them. But Pharaoh—may his name be blotted out—denied this, saying that He is not without end or purpose. This is why "He established Truth" <note>original: *V'tiken Emet*</note> has the numerical value <term>Gematria</term> of 441 <note>The word *Emet* (Truth) equals 441</note>, to explain this wondrous statement.

Regarding the study of these aspects, they said in the <term>Haggadah</term>: "Rabban Gamliel used to say: Whoever does not mention these three things on Passover has not fulfilled his obligation: the Passover offering, Matzah, and Maror." These correspond to the three aspects of time: **Was, Is, and Will Be.**

**The Passover Offering (Pesach)** represents the aspect of **"Was"** <note>Hebrew: *Hayah*, the past</note>, for He preceded everything, and no powers can stand against Him. This is hinted at by the Passover lamb, which was an Egyptian deity—the firstborn and the mighty among all powers, as mentioned above. As the *Me'or Enayim* wrote regarding the lamb that they tied to the legs of their beds: they held it for four days in the possession of Israel, and after the fourth day, they took it out for slaughter and then put it in the fire to be roasted, to fulfill what is written: "the carvings of their gods you shall burn in fire" <note>Deuteronomy 7:5</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, commanded that they should not eat it raw, so the Egyptians would not say that out of fear of the gods they worship, the Israelites were eating it in a hurry, raw and uncooked. If they had boiled it in a pot, it would not be visible, but by roasting it, it remained exposed. They then threw the remains so the Egyptians would see "its head with its legs," etc., so it would be recognized as a lamb. It was forbidden to break its bones so that the skeleton would remain whole, cast in the street for all to see. In this way, all the gods of the nations were nullified, and it became known that there is a "Cause of all Causes" who is primordial. This is the aspect of **"Was."**

**Matzah** represents the aspect of **"Is"** <note>Hebrew: *Hoveh*, the present</note>, hinting at His Providence. Since His Providence is the "Is" that we perceive—meaning through the lens of His actions—for other than this, His essence cannot be grasped even by the separate intellects. This is the secret of the blessings: "revealed and hidden." As the author of the *Akedah* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama</note> wrote regarding "In the beginning God created": the reason the Torah did not write "God created in the beginning" (as the sages translated it for King Ptolemy) is that God is known through the existence of the things He acts upon, not through His essence. (I have already elaborated on this at length in my sermon for the Giving of the Torah; see there).

It is known that Matzah <note>the Sages also called a simple, unfortified city "Matzah"</note> is simple, having no complex composition, consisting only of flour and water. Similarly, God's Providence is simple and contains no change or addition; even if He does good to the wicked or allows bad for the good, it all follows a chain of causality that is fundamentally simple. Change only exists from the perspective of the recipients, as the Kabbalists and philosophers have explained at length. But from His side, He is a perfect unity. This is the secret of the flour and water: they are simple elements, hinting at simplicity and unity. The flour undergoes many labors before its completion—as we learned: "forty labors minus one" <note>the 39 prohibited labors of Shabbat</note>, such as sowing, plowing, reaping, binding, threshing, winnowing, selecting, grinding, etc. This indicates the guidance of the recipients. Thus, Matzah indicates Providence, which has both a revealed and a hidden aspect. This is the secret of the Matzah bread: we uncover the Matzah during the telling of the Haggadah, which hints at His actions, blessed be He, being revealed to us. This is what the *Beit Yosef* (Chapter 473) wrote in the name of the German Responsa, bringing proof from the phrase "Bread of Affliction" <note>original: *Lechem Oni*</note>—bread over which many words are "answered" <note>a wordplay on *oni* (affliction) and *onim* (answering/speaking)</note>. The Matzah that we testify about is revealed. However, regarding His essence, which hints at the "hidden" aspect, it is proper to cover the Matzah, as the *Agur* wrote.

<margin>Therefore, a person must be careful—"commandment" (tzav) implies "alacrity"—in this place I will expound all the laws of Chametz and Matzah as I recorded in my last notebook of sermons. It is very long and contains new insights. I also added a reason for the two pieces of the *Afikomen*, which I wrote there in the name of the Maharal: they represent these two aspects, the revealed and the hidden. We eat from the "guarded" Matzah, hinting at "No eye has seen, O God, besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>, the life that has been "guarded" in the grapes since the seven days of Creation. This is a great secret explained to the Kabbalists; understand this.</margin>

Let us return to our subject: **Maror** (bitter herbs) hints at the aspect of **"Will Be"** <note>Hebrew: *Yihyeh*, the future</note>. The *Tola'at Yaakov* wrote that the bitter herb is called *Chasa* (lettuce). The best type of Maror is *Chasa*. He wrote there that it hints at the name of the Lord (YHWH). The letter *Vav* of *Chasa* <note>perhaps referring to its shape or numerical value</note> represents mercy, while the word *Chasa* itself hints at the name *EHYEH* (I Will Be), which is judgment, as is known. This is the secret of "The Lord is one and His name is one," which will be revealed in the future. I can also offer a wondrous intention regarding Maror called *Chasa* being revealed in the future.

First, I will preface what the Kabbalists said: that the <term>Kelipah</term> (the shell of evil), which is the "bitterness," has a root in the holiness above. It is extremely subtle. Only through the process of "unfolding" <note>descending through spiritual worlds</note> did it become loathsome and murky until it was separated. This is the secret of "Esau's head" being placed in the lap of Isaac in the Cave of Machpelah, as Jonathan ben Uzziel wrote in the Targum. This is also the secret of why the Angel of Death will be slaughtered in the future: the "redness" <note>Edom/Esau</note> within him will be annulled, but the holiness will remain. Even Samael, though he is an impure angel from the side of the "shells," has a root in holiness and is formed for good. The secret of his name is "Sam" (poison) and "El" (God). From the midpoint and above, the "poison"—the bitterness—will be annulled, and only "El"—the holiness—will remain.

This is the secret of "In the future, the pig will become pure" <note>a famous midrashic concept</note>, for the heavy shell will return to holiness. This is explained at length in the "Gate of the Palaces." See also the book *Kol Bochim* by Rabbi Abraham Galante on this wondrous secret. (See there at length and copy it here). See also the *Shorash Yishai* on the verse "The wicked shall return to Sheol," which Rashi explains even refers to barren trees. This relates to the secret of the "wood gatherer" mentioned here.

This is also the secret of the word "concubines" <note>original: *pilagshim*</note> written regarding the sons of Keturah, which is written without the letters *Yod* and *Vav*. Our Sages explained that Abraham gave them "names of impurity." The secret of the matter is that impurity—the "shells"—has an attachment above in holiness. As I explained regarding Samael, from the midpoint up he is called "El." This is why "concubines" (*pilagshim*) is missing the *Yod*: it becomes "Peleg-Shem" (half a name), meaning half of it is a holy Name. All of this will happen in the "End of Days," when the shell will return to holiness and "the idols will be utterly cut off" to perfect the world under the sovereignty of the Almighty. This is the secret of Maror being called *Chasa*—it hints at the future, the aspect of **"Will Be."** (You can see how great the hints of the commandment of Maror are! Here I will preach the entire sermon on Maror that I recorded in my last notebook for the Great Sabbath).

Since Pesach, Matzah, and Maror represent **Was, Is, and Will Be**, which is the secret of the Name YHWH, the author of the Haggadah used the expression "Why?" <note>Hebrew: *mah*</note>—asking "For what reason?" <note>original: *al shum mah*</note> of each one. The word *Mah* (45) is the numerical value of the Name YHWH when fully spelled out <note>the *Milui* of Alephs</note>. This is the explanation found in *Kol Bochim* on the verse "Remember, O Lord, what (*mah*) has befallen us": the attribute of Mercy (which equals 45/*Mah*) was turned into the attribute of Judgment (Elohim, which equals 86). We ask God: "Not for us, O Lord, not for us, but for Your name give glory"—meaning for Your Great Name. Understand this.

The sum of all this is that the sin of the First Man (Adam) was repaired in Egypt. This is the secret of why they could only be redeemed through the merit of the blood of the Passover lamb and the blood of circumcision. For when Adam sinned, he was enticed by the Serpent. As the Kabbalists wrote, the Serpent spoke falsehood, saying "Lest you touch it," and he added to the word "Truth" (*Emet*). When you separate the letter *Aleph* <note>representing the One/God</note> from *Emet* (Truth), what remains is *Met* (Death). He caused death to the world. That *Aleph* is the light of the "Chief" (*Aluph*) that I wrote about in my introduction. When that *Aleph* was separated from the word "Adam," what remained was *Dam* (Blood). This is why Pharaoh said, "See, evil is before you"—referring to the "Blood" (*Dam*) he saw for Israel. This is "Whoso sheddeth man's (*Adam*) blood (*Dam*)." This blood that remained from the word *Adam* is like the word *Met* (Death) that remained from *Emet* (Truth).

The secret of "When a man (*Adam*) brings an offering": the book of Chronicles begins with the creation of the world and is written in the "Book of Generations" to hint that "what was is what will be." The *Aleph* in the word *Adam* there is a large *Aleph* <note>in the Masoretic text</note>, for so was Adam at the beginning of his creation—the *Aleph* of light. This will be so in the future. But when he corrupted his ways, the *Aleph* was removed. It was fitting to be restored at the Giving of the Torah, but it was corrupted again by the Golden Calf. It was partially repaired when the **Tabernacle** was completed...

<meta>This page continues the philosophical exploration of the Divine Names and their relationship to history and the Exodus. ### Tractate Pesachim: The Tenth Commandment

->The Truth<-

As explained previously, He indicates and recounts the nature of Providence. In the Psalm established upon the theme of Providence, it says: "The Lord builds Jerusalem... He heals the brokenhearted... He counts the number of the stars, He calls them all by name" <note>Psalm 147:2-4</note>. After the "end of the race" <note>the predetermined period of exile</note> arrived, and man’s thoughts were overturned by his troubles, the time of redemption came. At that moment, the Divine guidance shifted to the mode of **Providential Conduct**, involving changes in nature and the overriding of the celestial systems. This was so that the Israelite nation could be chosen as a people for God, as it is written: "And you shall be My treasured possession" <note>Exodus 19:5. original: *am segula*</note>. They were to be led by this specific guidance—"at the bid of the Lord they would travel, and at the bid of the Lord they would encamp"—rather than by natural laws, which are the portion assigned to all other nations.

This is the essence of the Name **YHVH** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note>, which became known and revealed in Egypt, but not before then. As it is written: "And by My name YHVH I was not known to them" <note>Exodus 6:3</note>. Within that Name, three aspects were revealed: **He was, He is, and He will be** <note>original: *Haya, Hoveh, Yihyeh*</note>, which correspond to the three "covenants" mentioned above.

1. **The aspect of "He Was":** This indicates the **Renewal of the World** <note>The concept that the world was created from nothing at a specific point in time, rather than existing eternally</note>. It was revealed during the Exodus from Egypt, as all the commentators explain: the proof of the world's creation and its continued existence is dependent on the Exodus. Therefore, when we conclude the Torah with the verse, "And for all the mighty hand... which Moses performed in the sight of all Israel" <note>Deuteronomy 34:12</note>, we immediately begin again with "In the beginning God created," because the two are linked. The Exodus is the sign and wonder that proves Creation. This is also why our Sages taught that "Remember" <note>the Sabbath</note> and "Observe" were spoken in a single utterance: for through "Remember" you recall the Creation of the world, and through "Observe" <note>which mentions the Exodus in the Deuteronomy version of the Decalogue</note> you recall the Exodus. They were said in one utterance because they testify to each other: Creation proves God's Power, and His Power proves Creation. I have elaborated on this in another pamphlet.

2. **The aspect of "He Is":** This refers to active **Providence**, which was revealed in Egypt through the distinction: "And I will set a redemption between My people and your people" <note>Exodus 8:19</note>, and many similar instances.

3. **The aspect of "He Will Be":** This refers to the Divine Will that the Lord shall be King, and that all other "gods" shall be utterly cut off. This too was revealed in Egypt. Once the god of Egypt <note>the Nile or the sheep</note> was nullified by God’s power, it follows logically that we should believe all others will be nullified. For the "Ministering Angel" of Egypt is the "Firstborn" over all the celestial ministers above, who draws strength from them, as it is written: "And they rode in the second chariot."

I have already elaborated on this in my sermon for the Great Sabbath on the portion of *Tzav*. This is why it is said that Moses came to Pharaoh in the name of **YHVH**, mentioning this Name constantly. Pharaoh denied it because he only knew the name **Elohim**, which is appointed over the natural order. He had received and heard this name since the days of Joseph, who said to him, "God <note>Elohim</note> will give Pharaoh an answer of peace," and "What God <note>Elohim</note> is doing, He has shown to Pharaoh."

However, when Moses repeated the Name **YHVH**—representing the aspects of **Was, Is, and Will Be**—to Pharaoh, Pharaoh replied: "Who is the Lord <note>YHVH</note> that I should obey His voice to send Israel? I do not know the Lord <note>YHVH</note>, and I will not let Israel go." They responded: "The God of the Hebrews has met with us; let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest He fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword." They were hinting to him the three aspects of Was, Is, and Will Be within the statement "Thus says YHVH, the God of Israel."

They hinted that there is a **First Cause**, higher than the high, above nature. They hinted at this by calling upon the Name YHVH, which is higher than the name Elohim. This is the aspect of **"He Is,"** as the Sages said: "Before the world was created, there was only He and His Name." They hinted at the power of existence—**"He Was"**—and they hinted at **Providence**, specifically the individual Providence He exercises over the Israelite nation above all other nations. This is the meaning of "God of Israel." They also hinted at the aspect of **"He Will Be"**—that by sending the Israelite nation, the others will eventually be nullified in the future.

The wicked Pharaoh, who asked "Who is the Lord?", was questioning the source of these three aspects.
- Regarding **"He Will Be"**, which indicates the creation of the world, it is written: "Lift up your eyes on high and see: **Who** <note>Hebrew: *Mi*</note> created these?"
- Regarding **"He Is"**, it is written: "**Who** <note>*Mi*</note> can express the mighty acts of the Lord?", which speaks of His Providence.
- Regarding **"He Was"** <note>and the future recognition of God</note>, all nations will eventually confess His divinity and say: "**Who** <note>*Mi*</note> is like the Lord our God?"

This verse can be interpreted in the three ways mentioned above. First, I will introduce what the religious philosophers said regarding the **Renewal of the World** at the time it was created, and why it was not created earlier. They concluded that the world was not created out of necessity—as if God had any need for His world—but rather He created it out of the generosity of His heart and His "Good Will," in order to do good for others.

Since the world was created through **Will**, no human intellect can fully grasp it, for the Will follows His Wisdom and Power, and everything is part of His essence. Just as His essence is unattainable, His Will is unattainable. Thus, when Pharaoh denied the creation of the world, his denial manifested in the very difficulty that he found hard to resolve. He argued: "If the world is a necessity, meaning He is always joined to His world and—heaven forbid—His existence depends on the world being a partner to Him, then 'I do not know the Lord' <note>YHVH</note>." Or, "I cannot know what existed with God before the world was created, for on what did His existence—heaven forbid—depend before the world was renewed?"

"And if the world was created by Will, and He is not essentially joined to His world, and He is removed and abstract, then why the delay? If it is by Will, then 'I will not let Israel go' either." This means: if God created by Will, you must say He did it for the benefit of the created beings. If He did it for their benefit, then I too agree and desire this for my own benefit—and my benefit is *not* to send Israel away from serving me!

He also hinted at his denial regarding **Providence** and philosophical inquiry. He said: "If it is true that He is the Master of Providence, how can He watch over one people and not another? It would be one thing if you told me in His name that His will is for me, my people, the House of Israel, and everyone else to go into the wilderness—then I would believe He watches over all inhabitants of the world. But now, since 'I do not know the Lord'—meaning, I know nothing of this YHVH because I only know that my will is the will of all and for the good of all—but you say this is only for Israel, then 'I will not let Israel go,' for surely you speak a lie."

He likewise hinted at his denial regarding the aspect of **"He Will Be"** from a philosophical standpoint. He said: "You say that in the future, God will darken all the nations so they may know the Lord. If so, what is His reason for not doing it now? Why does He not now 'remove the heart of stone' from the whole world and give them a 'heart of flesh' to fear the Lord? Why is His divinity revealed specifically to Israel? Therefore, I do not believe them, and I will not let them go."

Moses and Aaron answered him: "The God of the Hebrews has met with us; let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest He fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword." With this verse, they gave him three correct and true answers to his objections, resolving all of Pharaoh's questions regarding this conduct.

First, I will mention that Onkelos <note>the famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note> translates "met with us" <note>Hebrew: *nikra*</note> as "was revealed" <note>Aramaic: *itgali*</note>. He said: "The God of the Hebrews was revealed"—meaning the revelation of His divinity through prophecy in the world. What was previously hidden and unknown to others, this "calling" was "upon us"—meaning **for our sake**. For the creation of the world was for the sake of Israel. They are the **Fruit**, and the other nations are the **Husks** <note>original: *klipot*</note> for them. It turns out that in truth, there is no "nation" other than Israel, and the other nations are merely shells for them. This is why there were kings for the other nations before a king reigned in Israel, just as the husk precedes the fruit.

He said: "And I remembered the goodness"—why is Israel the chosen people for whom the world was created? They answered: "Because they will receive the **Torah**." This is the ultimate purpose of creation. Since creation was for the benefit of the created beings, the primary benefit is that they receive the Torah. Even though this matter is difficult for them and they may receive many punishments for it—which might seem "bad" by human standards—nevertheless, it is essentially "good" in order to do good for them in the end. For this was the "Time of Will" and generosity from Him; since it arose in His mind to do good for His creations, it arose in His mind to do good with the **True Good**—to give them the Torah and punish them if they transgress, involving the creation of the **Evil Inclination**, which is actually for the benefit of the creations <note>as it allows for free will and reward</note>. This is found in the Zohar, in the third chapter of the Gate of the Exchange Palaces.

Regarding the acceptance of the Torah, he said: "Let us go a journey of three days in the wilderness." As the Talmudic tradition <note>Tanya/Bava Kamma</note> states: "They went three days in the wilderness and found no water." The "seekers of hints" <note>original: *dorshei reshumot*</note> said: "Water" means nothing other than "Torah," as it is said, "Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the water." Because they went three days without Torah, they immediately became exhausted. Their prophets arose and enacted that they should read <note>the Torah</note> on Sabbath, stop on Sunday, read on Monday, stop Tuesday and Wednesday, and read on Thursday... so that they should not spend three days without Torah.

From this, we understand that the primary good for created beings is to do what God desires, and to be punished if they violate His command. We also learn that Israel is the "Fruit" and the nations are the "Husks." Thus they mentioned all the histories: for in truth, the world was created by Will to do good for the creations. And if any creation should say, "This 'good' should be according to *my* will, not Yours," it is not within his power to say so. For the essence of the good is that he is punished if he transgresses. And the reason His Providence is more specific for Israel than all other nations is that they are the essential core, and the nations are the husk attached to the fruit—and generally, the fruit contains the husk. Thus, the nations are sustained by the "residue" of Israel.

Furthermore, regarding why His divinity will be revealed in the future and not now: it had to be this way, so that the husk precedes the fruit. These are the "gods of the nations," just as in the natural growth of fruit, the shell precedes the fruit. Thus, with their refined speech, they removed all of Pharaoh's complaints.

Regarding Pharaoh’s denials, the Sages hinted in Tractate Moed Katan (page 18a): "Rabbi Abitول said in the name of Rav: The Pharaoh who was in the days of Moses was one cubit tall; his beard was one cubit long; and his 'manhood' was a cubit and a half, to fulfill what is written: 'He sets up over it the lowliest of men.'"

On the surface, this statement is astonishing and demands interpretation. In my humble opinion, they were hinting at his three denials mentioned above. When they said "He was a cubit," they hinted at the aspect of **"He Was."** The intention is that the Holy One, blessed be He, is infinite and has no measure or limit, for He existed before everything—an endless continuation. Pharaoh denied this. It is known that man was created in the image of God; therefore, the Sages used a metaphor for the Divine, saying "He is a cubit." For a "cubit" <note>original: *amma*</note> hints at measurement and limit.

It explains the concept of Israel as the "fruit" of creation and the Torah as the ultimate purpose of existence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Divine Names and their role in human history, moving from the revelation of the Name YHVH to the cosmic struggle between holiness and the "extrinsic forces" represented by Samael. It links the Fall of Adam to the laws of the Passover Seder.</meta>

### Tractate Pesachim

And know that these are all the fruits from which Samael <note>In Jewish mysticism, the primary archangel of shadow and temptation</note> did not prevent his eating, so that he would not come to the aforementioned error. For this reason, He created man alone, so that he would not err as actually occurred when Samael came and clothed himself in the serpent. This was to test them—whether to believe in the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*</note> or in those other "earlier" forces. As it says: "from the tree he ate and created his world," etc. This is what happened to him when he "cut the shoots" <note>A Talmudic idiom for heresy or causing a rift in the Divine unity</note> and became a heretic and denied the Root. All of this followed from the eating of the fruit. After he was punished, it is known that he was held guilty, but he accepted repentance for it.

This is the secret of the "harlots" <note>original: *zonot*; here referring to the "extrinsic" or "impure" spiritual forces</note>, which is the count of the years drawn from Samael, who was clothed in the serpent. From this power, the eating of the fruit was drawn. This is the secret of the **Four Cups** of the Passover Eve. And this is the secret of the "forty-eight harlots"—one hundred minus two. <note>This refers to complex Kabbalistic calculations regarding the degradation of spiritual energy</note>

As for the one who is jealous of his kind on his left, and says, "we and you," that makes three. And if we hear one who says, "it is I," that makes four. If he says, "and I," that makes five... and so on until the embryo passes, until one hundred and one, and the silk bursts. <note>This passage appears to be a mystical or allegorical interpretation of a folk-tale or midrash concerning the multiplication of these extrinsic forces</note>. Thus, this flesh always counts the "harlots," for the princes are influenced by the side of Samael. The order is like that of his Creator; yet he [Samael] enticed the first man to believe in these extrinsic forces. But regarding Adam, his repentance was accepted, and he confessed at the end, as the Blessed One said. He understood that even though there are some created beings that exist in a different change, there is no difficulty from this, since He acts in truth upon the world by His Will, as mentioned above; and there is no "reason" for the Will. <note>The author argues that God's ultimate Will transcends human logic or "reasons"</note> (See further at length on this matter and the many sayings belonging to it).

This is why they said that regarding the matter of the cups, there was no fear of "harlots" <note>extrinsic forces</note>. This is the secret of the **Four Cups** established by our Sages of blessed memory to correspond to the four expressions of redemption, and not for four other matters. For the "harlots" [impurity] of the cups are the rectification for the sin of the first man, who squeezed a cluster of grapes <note>A Midrashic identification of the forbidden fruit as the grape</note> and caused the error of the "harlots," which is "duality." But these [Passover] cups are the opposite: they are the secret of the **four letters of the Name YHWD** <note>A mystical variant of the Tetragrammaton (YHVH) where a 'Dalet'—signifying King David or Sovereignty—is emphasized</note>, which is the rectification for the blemish of the first man, as I wrote above. (See the book *Matteh Moshe*, which explains how the four cups hint at the four letters of the Name).

It is known to the Kabbalists that there are two types of wine:
1. One wine is that which is "preserved in its grapes from the six days of Creation" <note>A Talmudic metaphor for the hidden spiritual rewards of the World to Come</note>. This is the secret of the influence from the emanation of **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*</note>, which is above the well-known six days of building. (This emanation is the secret of the World to Come and the secret of the "Great Sabbath." Regarding the World to Come, our Sages said: "Wine that [no eye] has seen," which is the preserved wine, etc. Understand this).
This is the secret of what Rav Nachman said there in "Passover Eve": it is a **Night of Guarding** <note>original: *Leil Shimurim*</note> from the "damaging spirits," for the damaging spirits cause the "harlots" and duality. Observe this closely.

There, the "preserved wine" is a place where there is no "touch of a stranger" <note>original: *maga nokhri*; usually referring to wine handled by non-believers, here used as a metaphor for spiritual impurity</note>. For the "touch of a stranger" begins from the level of Kindness <note>*Hesed*</note> and downward, where the "husks" <note>impure shells</note> have a hold.

This is the secret of the two Amoraim <note>Sages of the Talmud</note> I cited: the four cups correspond to the **four expressions of redemption**, which is from the side of blessing. As the Kabbalists wrote, the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned in the Torah fifty times, corresponding to the fifty gates of Understanding. Conversely, on the "Left" side is the secret of "libation wine" <note>wine used for idolatry</note> and the "touch of a gentile." Thus, the four cups are transformed into the **four kingdoms** <note>the four historical empires that exiled Israel</note>—the "touch of a gentile" who touches us to rule over us. This matter was hinted at in the words of the Sages I cited: Rabbi Yohanan said they correspond to the four redemptions, and Rabbi Levi said they correspond to the four kingdoms. "This master said one thing and that master said another," and they do not actually disagree. (Here I will expound on the matter of the four cups that I noted in my last sermon).

Let us return to our subject: according to what I wrote regarding the rectification of the Patriarchs, the first man sinned in the aspect of "He was, He is, and He will be"—the secret of the Name **YHWD**. This will clarify the difficulty regarding the letters *MaNTzePa"Kh* <note>The five Hebrew letters that have a different form at the end of a word: Mem, Nun, Tzadi, Pe, Kaf</note> that I cited. I asked: did not our Sages already interpret these letters in the chapter "The Builder"? The truth is that this is a different interpretation. This Midrash comes to resolve the linguistic order of *MaNTzePa"Kh*, for it is more common to say them in their alphabetical order <note>K-M-N-P-Tz</note>.

We resolve this by saying that these letters hint at the three Patriarchs, as I wrote in the sermon. They also hint at the "I have surely remembered you" <note>original: *Pakod Pakadeti*; the code-word for the redemption from Egypt</note>, which is the secret of the word *MaMaR* [word/saying]. It also hints at the **Future Redemption**, which is the rectification of the Messiah, son of David. It is known that all of this is the rectification of the Name **YHWD**. Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph rectified the sin of the first man to draw down the Name YHWD, as mentioned above. So too in the future, the Name will be complete. The aspect of the Name "He is, He is, He was, He will be" represents the "King who reigns, and will reign." In the gematria <note>alphanumeric code</note> of these letters: *Pe-Nun* equals "King" <note>Melekh</note>, *Tzadi* equals "reigned," and *Pe-Nun* again with a prefix implies "he will reign." If they were written in alphabetical order, this would not be hinted at. Observe this carefully.

Regarding this, the second statement about "Testing" <note>sacrifices</note> will be explained. This hints at two types of conduct: **Natural Conduct** and the **Conduct that transcends it**. The latter comes through the "arousal from below," for according to the strength of one's attachment, the higher Providences and conducts are aroused from above. It is known that through the **Sacrifice** <note>original: *Korban*</note> there was a great attachment. This is why it is called *Korban*—because it "brings close" <note>*mikariv*</note> the lower realms to the higher realms, returning the flow from above to below.

The sacrifice of the Nations is similar to a "sacrifice for himself," for everything follows the intention. The essence of the sacrifice is that a person brings *himself* close. As the commentators explain on the verse: "When a man among you brings a sacrifice to the Lord..." <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. Even the nations brought sacrifices, but the sacrifice of Israel was "sweeter." This resolves my question: was it not said of the sacrifice, "you shall be careful to offer to Me" as a command? However, according to my intention, it is well-resolved. The truth is that He commanded, "Be careful to offer to Me in its appointed time," but Israel did this of their own accord, to awaken within themselves and cause their attachment. Regarding this intention, He said: "This is the law of the burnt offering: it is the burnt offering..." <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. The word "It" <note>*He*</note> refers to the Intention. There are two aspects to the sacrifice: the **Revealed** and the **Hidden**. The "bringing close" of the Intention is the Revealed, and the "bringing close" of the Soul is the Hidden. This corresponds to Natural Conduct and Providential Conduct.

This resolves the third difficulty I raised: why does the verse say "As in the days of old, as in the days of Noah"? <note>Actually referring to Malachi 3:4 and Isaiah 54:9</note>. The sacrifice of the first righteous ones was from the "Hidden" aspect—"It is the burnt offering." This was sweeter in Israel than in the time of Noah. But in the "Revealed" aspect, it was sweet in Noah's time just as in Israel's. For even though Noah was not complete in the "Hidden" aspect like Israel, in the "Revealed" aspect—offering a sacrifice to the Name of Heaven to bring the lower realms closer to the higher—Noah was complete in his sacrifice just like Israel.

Now I have come to explain the Torah portion in the way I have paved. It begins by saying: "This is the law of the burnt offering." This is the general rule. This is the secret of the **"Holy linen tunic he shall wear"** <note>Leviticus 16:4</note>. Since the sacrifice is the secret of the Revealed and the Hidden—which are the two letters *Yud* and the *Aleph-Het-Samekh* that I wrote in my introduction—it is the secret of the Unity that rectifies. This rectifies the sin of the first man, who caused himself to be clothed in **"garments of skin"** <note>original: *or* with the letter *Ayin*</note> and was stripped of his holy garments, the **"garments of light"** <note>original: *or* with the letter *Aleph*</note>.

It is also hinted: "He shall take off his garments and put on other garments" <note>Leviticus 6:4</note>. This is the secret of **Reincarnation** <note>*Gilgul*</note>, where one is clothed in a different garment. The "garments" are the clothing of the soul, which is the body. He must strip off his thick, coarse physical nature and clothe himself in another garment, the "garments of light."

Regarding this, it says: "A holy linen tunic he shall wear." The three mentions of "Fire on the altar" hint at the three aspects I mentioned—the **Three Covenants**. Through these, we arouse the realms above. Even though the fire descends from above, there is a commandment to bring it from a "commoner," meaning that man must awaken from below, and afterward, the flow comes from above. As the *Zohar* explains on the verse "And a mist rose from the earth." "A constant fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out" <note>Leviticus 6:6</note>.

This refers to the **Future Redemption** and the **Third Temple**, which will be eternal and never abolished. Regarding the Future Redemption, it is said "A New Song" <note>*Shir Hadash*—masculine form</note>, unlike the redemption from Egypt, of which it is said "A New Song" <note>*Shira Hadasha*—feminine form</note>. May it be the will of our Father in Heaven that we merit speedily in our days the Third Temple, and then the revelation of the Name **YHWD** will be known to all the world, and "The Lord shall be one and His Name One." Amen, may it be His will.

### Thus ends the Order of the Guarded Matzah and the matter of "Enriched Matzah" with the help of Him who created all with a Word. Let us return to the text.

**Regarding** the **Counting of the Omer**: I have written above extensively on the secret of why we must count days and why we must count weeks. This hints at the Work of Creation and the secret of the Sabbatical years <note>*Shemitot*</note> and the Jubilee <note>*Yovel*</note>—six times six. The root of the Jubilee is the sixth emanation of the "Building," and each one is comprised of seven from the expansion of Understanding <note>*Binah*</note>, which is the "Fiftieth Gate." From this expansion, Israel was redeemed from Egypt. This is the secret of why the Exodus is mentioned **fifty times** in the Torah. This revelation was only for a specific need—so that the initial Kindness of Passover would prevail, allowing Israel to be redeemed. However, after the first day, this light ascended back up. Therefore, we do not recite the "Full Hallel" <note>psalms of praise</note> except on the first day, as explained in the *Zohar*. This is the meaning of "Passover" [passing over/skipping]. Nevertheless, they needed the "days of whitening" <note>purity</note> to draw from the higher emanations until the fiftieth day, and then the "Woman" [Israel] is purified for her "Husband" [God].

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Fall of Adam and its rectification through the commandments, specifically linking the blood of the Passover sacrifice and circumcision to the restoration of Divine Unity. # Tractate Pesachim

...Messiah. And because of the truth and the faith that was in Israel, they were redeemed from Egypt, as it is explained: "In the merit of the faith they believed in Me," etc. And the blood of Adam <note>The Hebrew word for "blood" (Dam) is contained within the name "Adam."</note> was also given through the **blood of the Passover offering** and the **blood of circumcision**. The blood of the Passover is a restoration for the sin Adam committed by withholding [his devotion]. As it is said, the mouth of the first man was meant to declare Unity and the Creator, blessed be He, and the nullification of "other gods." Furthermore, the first man sinned by "drawing his foreskin" <note>A Talmudic expression for attempting to hide one's circumcision, signifying a rejection of the covenant</note>, and the restoration for this was the blood of circumcision. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who is not circumcised, his foreskin is drawn out."

After this refinement and purification, the "Two Thousands" joined together—the "Thousands" <note>The letter Aleph signifies the number 1,000 and also refers to "Alupho shel Olam," the Master of the World</note> of Truth and the "Thousands" of Adam—and from them was made the **House** <note>The letter Bet, the first letter of the Torah, means "House"</note> in which the Torah was given. For the Torah begins with the letter *Bet*, and at that moment, the "filth of the serpent" ceased entirely. Our Sages alluded to this in saying: "Two thousand years of Torah," meaning two "Alephs." 

Let us return to our subject: at that time, the Name **Y-H-V-H** <note>The four-letter Tetragrammaton, the essential Name of God</note> was revealed. Then, the refinement of the material world was blessed, and the "revealed" was attached to the soul. This is the secret of the "seventy years" and the "Great Name" that governs the Sabbath. This Great Name has a connection to the Sabbath day, through the secret of the **Private Domain** <note>original: *Reshut HaYachid*; a legal category in Sabbath law referring to an enclosed area</note> that rules on the Sabbath. Our Sages said that a "Private Domain" must be ten [handbreadths] high and four wide. This alludes to the True Unity of the Name Y-H-V-H. As the Sages of the Zohar said (and as brought in the *Pardes* <note>A foundational Kabbalistic work by Moshe Cordovero</note>): the width of "four" refers to the four letters of the Name, and the height of "ten" refers to the letters in their "filled" form <note>A Kabbalistic method of spelling out the names of the letters: Yod-Vav-Dalet, He-Aleph, Vav-Aleph-Vav, He-Aleph</note>, which equals ten letters.

This is why we say "In memory of the Exodus from Egypt" in the sanctification of the Sabbath and all the Festivals. The Exodus was the revelation of the Name Y-H-V-H, and the Festivals all allude to this Name:
*   The Passover lamb was designated on the **tenth** of the month: this is the letter *Yod* (10).
*   Five days later is the first day of Passover: this is the first *He* (5).
*   The holy convocation on the 21st of Nisan (the 7th day of Passover): this represents the *Vav*.
*   The final *He* I will explain later.

Similarly with the other months: five days after [the 10th] is Sukkot on the 15th (Y-H). Ten days later is **Hoshana Rabbah**, the final sealing on the 21st (Y-H-V). **Shmini Atzeret** is a festival unto itself, representing the final *He*, as the Kabbalists say. Shavuot, which is linked to Passover, also represents that final *He* of the Name. It was given on Shavuot because the Ten Commandments written on the Tablets correspond to the "five visions" mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud. This was to awaken the people to the observance of the Festivals, since they hint at great secrets regarding the "Intermediate Days" of the festivals. 

Through the things I have written, the sayings and verses I brought will be clarified and whitened <note>meaning: purified and understood</note>. I will explain them from the bottom up. I began by saying that Israel ascended and clung to Him, blessed be He. Then the Name is called "that which ascends" (*Oleh*) for Israel, and they are called "those caused by Him" (*Alulim*). They are bound and connected to Him. I noted how spiritual matters are much more beloved than natural ones. It is said that they prostrate to all of them, and He called them "My Sister," for they are in a state of equality, as it were. To be called "Ascending," one must have an "Effect" <note>original: *Alul*</note>. In this sense, it is as if the Effect were the cause for the Cause. (And according to what the Kabbalists wrote regarding "Standing," this requires Strength; consider this.) In this sense, He called them "One," for the Cause and the Effect are attached and joined to one another.

Thus we find that the entire chain of being—from the first point to the last—is like one knot and one unity. His Providence spreads through all existing things and gives them life. I have already brought the words of the *Pnei Malkiel*, who explained this at length. All his words are "sweeter than honey" and "kissable to the lips." The core of his words is that the "clumping" together [of different things] is the opposite of the faith in the "Clinging to the Unity." I will write a bit of his words:

In Tractate Sanhedrin, it is asked: Why was the first man created "Alone"? So that the **heretics** <note>original: *Minim*; often referring to dualists or early Gnostics</note> would not say there are "Two Authorities" <note>Two gods or powers in heaven</note>. From my words, the sin of the **Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil** will be explained. The philosophers say that a "Simple Agent" (which is God) cannot perform two completely different actions. Since He is simple and One, He can only do one action, and that action performs another, and so on. They believe that if there are two opposite things, there must be two different "Starting Agents."

Maimonides (of blessed memory) argued that the highest celestial sphere is like a single person with limbs; just as a person is one, but his heart is the cause of all his limbs, so too is the universe. This is clear proof of the Unity of God. I asked: why would God care about these "pairs" <note>The Talmud discusses avoiding doing things in pairs (like drinking 2 cups) due to demonic concern</note>? The intention is that one might become confused and think there are two "Starting Powers." The Sages said Adam was created alone so heretics wouldn't say there are Two Authorities. In truth, there is no substance to their claim, for since He is Simple and acts by Will and Power, He can perform a thousand different actions. The question of how "Complexity" came from "Simple Unity" has been discussed by many. The answer is that since He acts by **Will** (choice) and not by necessity, everything is possible.

To prevent the heretics from erring, the Holy One maintained a specific order in His world. You will not find one person who exactly resembles another in three things: voice, appearance, and mind. Not even a donkey exactly resembles another, nor any other creature. Even though a man has double limbs (two eyes, two hands, two legs), they do not resemble each other; one is right and one is left.

Despite this, we see that while no creature resembles another, many things in nature *do* resemble each other, such as birds' eggs, fruits, or trees. All apples look alike; all wheat looks alike. One must understand why. It is so that man should not think, God forbid, that they do not have one Single Beginning. Every blade of grass below has a spiritual force above that commands it to grow. God commanded "a law unto Moses from Sinai" not to eat certain types of similar things <note>referring to laws of forbidden mixtures or specific sacrificial laws</note> so as not to fall into this error. 

This is the secret of why the first man was prevented from eating the fruit of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. He told him: "From every tree of the garden you may eat," but warned him regarding the Tree of Knowledge. "Good and Evil" refers to all the fruits in the world. They are called so because eating is "good" when it strengthens the soul, and "evil" when it leads to corruption—as happened to Adam. Before he sinned, the command was not to eat [of that specific variety]. They are called "Fruit of Good and Evil" because when man sees all figs look alike or all apples look alike, he might mistakenly say they have [multiple] separate beginnings. This error only occurs when they are eaten and found to be identical in taste; without eating, one might assume they differ internally. 

If you ask: why did God create them this way? The answer is that He did so to refine and purify the creatures. Just as He created [impure] animals and forbade their eating, He brought "Evil" into existence to warn us against it and test us to see if we would keep His commandments. This is the secret of why they were permitted to eat the fruits of the Garden—because they did *not* resemble one another; they were the "Tree of Good."
