<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic interpretation of the human experience and the commandments as tools for cosmic restoration. Having previously discussed the "blood of circumcision" and the "blood of the Passover" as remedies for the Fall of Adam, the text now transitions into the specific acts of "Loving-kindness" (Gemilut Hasadim) and how they mirror the inner workings of the Divine Sefirot.</meta>

<page-num>179</page-num>
<header>Tractate Pesachim</header>

**First**, just as at the birth of a human being one must provide every preparation for their sustenance, so too should one consider the time of the "birth" of <term>Tiferet</term> <note>Tiferet represents the Divine attribute of Beauty, Harmony, or the "Son" in Kabbalistic persona</note> from <term>Binah</term> <note>Binah represents the Divine Mother or Understanding</note>. When she is "in hard labor" <note>referencing Genesis 35:17</note> due to the side of Judgment, God forbid that the Tiferet should emerge toward the side of the <term>Gevurot</term> <note>Severities/Judgments</note>. Because its birth is difficult, one must prepare every possible path so that the birth of Tiferet occurs on the Right Side <note>the side of Mercy/Chesed</note>, so that the "offspring" shall be without any blemish at all. As it is said: "He shall bring our judgment to light as holy," meaning that the Tiferet (Judgment) should emerge toward the Light, which is the Right, and thus be holy and separated from the "foreign" external forces. This includes the primary intention of one’s actions: to always bind it to Kindness and to bring it forth from Binah on the side of Kindness. Then the offspring emerges swift and "whitened" <note>purified</note>. Almost every warning in the Torah is included in this, so as not to arouse the Severities—meaning, so that there is no "holy judgment" <note>original: "קדשי"</note> in its birth, God forbid.

**Second**, to circumcise the child: this means performing the rectifications of the commandments such that any side of the <term>Klipoht</term> <note>Hulls/Husks of evil</note> or "foreskin" that attaches itself to <term>Yesod</term> <note>The Sefirah of Foundation, associated with the covenant of circumcision</note> is cut away. One should pursue all those damaged areas of the "foreskin" and return them in repentance. In this way, when the "foreskin of their hearts" is full <note>meaning, removed through repentance</note>, it causes the "Upper Righteous One" <note>Yesod</note> to be without a foreskin, standing in strength to rectify all things that cause a foreskin there. For this reason, when Phinehas circumcised the foreskins of the Children of Israel, he merited the "Priesthood of Phinehas," for he was granted total Kindness with his Creator. By circumcising the Yesod from that foreskin, he merited Kindness (<term>Chesed</term>), and from this, one learns the way of all other attributes of Kindness.

**Third**, to visit the sick and heal them. It is known that the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> is "sick with love" for the Union <note>the joining of the Divine attributes</note>, as it is written: "For I am sick with love" <note>Song of Songs 2:5</note>. Her healing is in the hands of man, to bring her "good signs," as it is written: "Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples." The *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note> explain that the secret of "raisin cakes" refers to all the "chariots" that bind the Sovereignty (<term>Malchut</term>) to the fire of Kindness and the fire of God’s Severity in two arms, and there she is sustained by them. Whoever does this "sustains the sick in her sickness." It also says "refresh me with apples," which means to bind her between <term>Netzach</term> and <term>Hod</term> <note>Victory and Splendor</note>, for there is her bed, as they are white and red like these apples—both being joined through choice and kindness. One must visit her and remember her, and the "sick one" shall receive food and drink from the Upper Flow from which she herself originates. Her soul is "shortened" by the toil of Israel in a way that resembles physical illness. Thus, one must care for the "Upper Sick," for she is sick as we have said. She is sick for a moment behind the "World to Come" <note>Binah</note> in the Union behind the "World of Judgment," as it is written: "Like a bird wandering from her nest" <note>Proverbs 27:8</note>, which refers to the Shekhinah, "for a man wanders from his place." He [the Divine husband] is also "pained by our transgressions," and the healing of both of them is in our hands. It is proper to visit them and prepare their needs through Torah and commandments.

**Fourth**, to give charity to the poor and comfort them: these are <term>Yesod</term> and <term>Malchut</term>. The "charity" appropriate for them is explained in the *Tikkunim* through the acronym of the Hebrew word for "Gleanings" (L-K-T): the 90 (*Tzadi*) "Amens," the 4 (*Dalet*) "Sanctifications," the 100 (*Resh*) "Blessings," and the 5 (*He*) "Books of the Torah" every day <note>This is a complex mystical play on the Hebrew letters forming the word for Charity, Tzedakah</note>. Each person should do this according to their strength, drawing charity from Tiferet to these "poor ones," and preparing for them "Gleanings, the Corner of the field, and the Forgotten Sheaf" (*Leket, Pe'ah, Shichcha*). In the secret of "Forgotten Sheaf," the "Upper Tenth" (Binah) is exempt, and "the Corner" (*Pe’ah*) comes from the aspect of Malchut herself. It is written: "For the poor and the stranger you shall leave them," for even the Tiferet "dwells" below in the Malchut and needs to be given these rectifications. Likewise, the "Tithe of the Poor" is meant to raise the Malchut (the "Tithe") to the Yesod, who is called "Poor," and to give her drink from Tiferet. Many rectifications are included in this.

**Fifth**, hospitality to guests: these are Tiferet and Yesod. One must give them a "house of rest" to rest in, which is the Malchut. Since they are "travelers" in the secret of the Exile, searching for what they have lost, one must bring them in there. As explained in the *Zohar*, this commandment is fulfilled by those who travel on the road—those who detach themselves from their homes to engage in Torah. Their "paths" are the "guests" busy with the needs of the Malchut. Similarly, every act of "Union" for the Tiferet within the Malchut from below is called a "guest" turning to his destination, causing the "cow to be joined" and making his lodging in the Malchut. So it is explained in the *Tikkunim*. As for the "food for the guests," one must prepare eating, drinking, and escorting. That is, one must bring Tiferet and Yesod into the Malchut and give them "food" there, in the sense of: "I have come into my garden... I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>, which is the flow appropriate for the Lower Understanding that spreads from the side of Severity and is sweetened. And "drink," in the sense of: "I have drunk my wine with my milk," which is the inner flow from the "hidden wine" and the secret of "sweetened milk" to bind Tiferet and Malchut. Even the "poor and destitute" and the "Severity" in Netzach or Hod—for so it is explained in the *Ra'aya Meheimna* <note>The "Faithful Shepherd," a section of the Zohar</note>. And the "escort" (*Levayah*) is to bring oneself and one's soul there with them in the Upper Union, to escort them there further, and to bring the other Sefirot there with them to create a "good escort" (*Levayah Tovah*). Many things are included in this rectification. The general rule: when one walks on the way, they should intend through their hints and thoughts to act like Him—to emerge as He did after being in the house of rest, mentioning it with the mouth to restore it with life and our wise strength during the deed, "in your mouth and in your heart to do it."

**Sixth**, dealing with the living and the dead. This matter is the union of the "Orphan" above, which is very difficult, for it is the secret of the Sefirot that are "faint" and withdrawn into their source. One must "cleanse" them from the "rust of sin" and clothe them in white merits through the light of good deeds, to grant them an inheritance in the secret of "the other," to bind them above and carry them "on the shoulder"—the secret of the Sefirot being joined one to another until they reach above the "shoulder," which is the beginning of the connection of the arm to the body. Above this is the secret of the "Hiddenness" which cannot be perceived. One should have intention in the secret of "burial," to conclude the verse: "And He buried him in the valley" <note>Deuteronomy 34:6</note>, which is translated as the "source of the depths" that flow from <term>Keter</term> <note>The Crown, the highest Sefirah</note> in its aspects that face downward to show mercy in joining. From there the "grave" rises to the "Upper Eye"—the Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) within the Crown. This requires great settledness of the mind.

**Seventh**, bringing the Bride to the wedding canopy (*Chuppah*). This is the general principle: all prayers and "unions" are the secret of bringing the Bride to the Chuppah. Their essence is in the secret of Prayer, coming from several "countries" <note>stages</note> one after another: Sacrifices, Songs of Praise, the seated Prayer, the praise of the *Shema* and its blessings, and then the standing Prayer (*Amidah*) and the other rectifications that follow. All of these are "Acts of Kindness" to the Groom and the Bride, to look after their needs and provide their sustenance.

**Eighth**, bringing peace between a man and his fellow—these are Tiferet and Yesod. Sometimes they move far from each other, and one must make peace between them and establish them so they are equal and bound together in love and affection. This is achieved through the fitness of good deeds. For when the Yesod leans toward the Left and Tiferet toward the Right, or the Severities toward each other, [one must act] until the Yesod is on the Right like him. When, God forbid, there is some blemish of sin in the world, then there is hatred and dragging between them, and no "Union" or bond between the Sefirot at all. This must also be done between any two Sefirot, such as Right and Left, between Wisdom and Understanding, or between Kindness and Severity, or between Victory and Splendor. One must bring peace between them, and this is "bringing peace between a man and his fellow." Similarly, "between a husband and his wife" refers to the Yesod making peace between Tiferet and Malchut. All such things are "ways of peace," and they become "Acts of Loving-kindness" on high. Thus far his words.

### The Chapter "Torah Or" is completed.

<margin>Ethical Rebuke</margin>
## Chapter 4: Ethical Rebuke
The Ethical Rebuke for the New Moon (*Rosh Chodesh*): Since it is a time of atonement, a person should see to it that they perform complete repentance with a whole heart. That is, on the New Moon, one should act as if it were Yom Kippur, as many of the "High Pious Ones" are accustomed to do. One should rectify everything that was broken, whether in money, body, or soul. It should be done with great weeping and complete regret, abandoning one’s evil way. When the month enters, one should be like a "new creation," clothing oneself in holiness from then on, and his blessing shall be like the Crown (*Keter*). Regarding the "nullification of leaven" (*Bittul Chametz*) and its removal, one should remember that the leaven is the Evil Inclination—it is the Satan, the "leaven in the dough." Even a tiny amount of leaven must be pursued during one's life to remove and nullify it through the principle of "turn from evil and do good." One should purify oneself before the Holy Festival, for "The Lord has chosen us," etc., as I have elaborated above.
The "Greatness" (*Gedulah*): "The world is built on Kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>. Therefore, one must be very, very careful with Acts of Loving-kindness. One should see to it that no day of their life passes without an Act of Kindness, whether with the body, with money, or with the soul—meaning, teaching Torah to one's fellow or assisting them. Thus, "Kindness surrounds him all the day." Therefore, every single day one should seek out some Act of Kindness, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, will deal with him through the attribute of Kindness.

I also found in the pamphlet of the students of the <term>Ari</term> <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century father of modern Kabbalah</note> regarding the Counting of the Omer <note>the 49-day period between Passover and Shavuot</note>. Understand that the "garment of the King" <note>the way the Divine reveals itself</note> refers to how we prepare and rectify the forces of the "stars" <note>destiny/nature</note> during the Omer. This is precisely why on the night of the Passover Seder, the <term>Mochin</term> <note>Divine consciousness or "Brains"</note> enter all at once, in a "small" state, as they are found in the world. However, they are destined to be built up into the structure of the <term>Zeir Anpin</term> <note>the "Lesser Countenance," representing the emotional Divine attributes</note> through the counting of the days. This secret is found in the "fifty gates" of <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding</note>, for there are fifty days. When one says, "Today is such-and-such day," it aligns the day with the fifty gates. Then the Name of God will be complete. This is the matter of the eighteen mentions of God’s name...
</margin>

<margin>
I found in the pamphlet of the <term>Ari</term>, of blessed memory, that during these days, the attribute of Abraham <note>Kindness/Chesed</note> encounters the attribute of Judgment <note>Gevurah</note>. This was the encounter of Rabbi Akiva and his time, and his death, etc. Even though the name *Elohim* <note>the Name of God associated with Judgment</note> has five letters, it is known that the five letters that follow them in the alphabet have a specific power. The "backwards" spelling of the name *Ehyeh* <note>I Will Be</note> fills up to the value of one thousand. <note>The author is using complex gematria, or Hebrew numerology, to show how the Name of God representing the future expands to encompass all mercy</note>. 

Because during these days the "end" of the name *Elohim* <note>Judgment</note> rules, we calculate a permutation of the middle three letters to "sweeten" His judgment. The exchange is as follows: the letter *Dalet* becomes *Tet* and *Yod* <note>forming the word "Good"</note>, for "Your love is better than wine." The letters *Aleph* and *Mem*—which are the beginning and end of this Name—have no substitute, because they represent the "Mother" <note>Binah</note> who stands above Judgment. We pull these letters backward to weaken and sweeten the severity. Behold, the letter *Aleph* is the "Doe of the Dawn," the letter that precedes everything. 

This Name blossoms from the spiritual root of Understanding (*Binah*), where Judgment originates. We draw this "sweetening" from the "Supernal Mother" who spreads over the first twenty days with the letter *Heh*, and the last twenty days with another *Heh*, and in between with the letter *Tet*. When joined, they equal the number 53, which is the numerical value of *Gimel* and *Lamed* <note>33</note> in the Omer—the day the dying of the students stopped. 

Furthermore, I will add a "touch of my own" regarding the 33rd day of the Omer (*Lag BaOmer*). Let me offer a preface: The seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is **Truth** (*Emet*). Its height is based on the name *Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh* <note>I Will Be Who I Will Be</note>, for *Ehyeh* (21) times *Ehyeh* (21) equals the numerical value of **Truth** (441). **Man** (*Adam*) is a "tithe" of Truth, for "Blood" (*Dam* = 44) is the tithe of "Death" (*Met* = 440) <note>a mystical wordplay on the letters of Adam (Aleph-Dalet-Mem) and Truth (Aleph-Mem-Tav)</note>. This is the hint in the verse: "One man in a thousand I have not found," meaning one tithe in a thousand was not found. 

The Torah is the **Torah of Truth**, called the "Torah of the Lord" and the "Torah of Man." The Torah is divided into three parts: two parts are revealed—the Written Torah and the Oral Torah which teach upright character traits. The third part is the "Hidden Torah"—the depth of secrets, logic, and the thirteen rules of interpretation. The third part is above all, where the Torah is entirely His Names, a hidden light shining for the "children of the upper chamber" and the prophets. 

All three parts together are the **Torah of Truth**. The "small number" <note>the sum of the digits</note> of Truth (*Emet* = 441) is 9 (4+4+1). This number, when doubled and doubled again, always returns to 9. For example: 2 times 9 is 18 (1+8=9); 3 times 9 is 27 (2+7=9). Regarding this, Ibn Ezra gave the sign: "The lip of truth shall be established forever" <note>Proverbs 12:19</note>. 

The two parts called "the Torah of Man" <note>revealed law</note> are 20 times "Truth," and their small number is 18. This is the 18th day of the month of Iyar <note>Lag BaOmer</note>. The third part, which is above them, is 3 times "Truth," with the small number 9. 

There must also be a "complete number," meaning peace (*Shalom*) and brotherhood among those who study Torah. As it is said: "Scholars increase peace in the world." Even when there is a dispute in Torah, "Love is at its end." Each side of the debate points toward the Truth; this is "Truth and peace they loved." One must be especially careful with the Oral Torah and the disputes of the Sages, for "both these and those are the words of the Living God." 

However, the students of Rabbi Akiva—who was the root of the Oral Torah—did not have peace between them. Therefore, the attribute of Judgment (*Elohim*) struck them during the days of the Omer. The name *Elohim* (86) twice equals the value of "The World to Come" (*HaOlam HaBa*). The counting of the Omer hints at both "Harsh Judgment" and "Weak Judgment." This "Weak" aspect is hinted at in the name Akiva. 

It is known that the letters *Yod* and *Heh* of God's name represent more mercy than the letters *Vav* and *Heh*. We must blend the mercy into the harshness. I previously wrote that every letter of the name *Elohim* "builds 24 houses" <note>permutations</note>. By damaging the *Aleph* of *Elohim*, they damaged the source of these 24. This is the secret of the **24,000 students** who died. They stopped dying on the 33rd of the Omer (*Lag BaOmer*) because the attribute of Judgment moves backward. The numerical value of the "sweetened" name *Akdatam* is 33. Also, the 48th day is special, as the full spelling of the Name of God equals 48. On *Lag BaOmer*, the attribute of Judgment (*Elohim*) becomes a "Witness" (*Ed*)—for "Witness" (*Ed*) and "Judgment" (*Din*) share the same numerical value. This was the "Mound of Witness" (*Galed*) between Jacob and Laban, where the pursuit of Judgment was turned into Mercy.
</margin>

And the act of a complete union in Kabbalah: I have already hinted above at the secret of the letters of *Ehyeh* <note>I Will Be</note> which equals "Blood" (*Dam*). There are ten letters in its expansion, and ten times *Ehyeh* equals the value of "Justice" (*Tzedek*). The simple letters are forty, and together they equal fifty. Each day of the Counting of the Omer, one must "favor" <note>rectify</note> one letter. They spread through the Name of 45 (*Mah*), which also equals fifty in its expansion. 

Originally, the Name of 45 was missing one letter <note>The letter *Aleph*, which represents the attribute of Understanding/Binah entering the heart</note>. When it was missing, it equaled "Blood" (*Dam*). This is the secret of "blood touching blood" <note>Hosea 4:2</note>. When the Divine forces are far from each other, they are "bloods"—one above and one below—leading to bloodshed and being poured outward. 

The redemption from Egypt was the bringing down of Kindnesses (*Hasadim*) into the body of the "Lesser Countenance" (*Zeir Anpin*), who is called **Man** (*Adam*). When the Kindnesses were hidden above, they did not shine below, and only the "backside" of the Divine shone—the "Ten Bloods" mentioned before. This is why the Egyptians would wash in and spill blood. But when this power spreads, **Man** (*Adam*) is formed. This is the secret of what Rabbi Nathan the Babylonian said to the woman: "Do not circumcise your son until his blood is absorbed." Then the ten Names are completed. This is the secret of the verse: "I said to you: In your blood, live!" For through the entry of those "bloods" into the body, he shall live, whereas before they were hidden above. 

All of this I understood from the pamphlet of the student of the <term>Ari</term>, of blessed memory. These matters are deeper than the sea. I do not wish to expand upon them further according to his way, for it is very, very deep. His path is not for the many, but for the individual—meaning for the chosen few. This suffices. Nevertheless, the takeaway is that every single day of the Omer, a person must see to rectifying the "pipe" of one letter, for the days of the Counting are days of Judgment, where even Israel is judged.

## And to see the greatness of the merit of this night, how it is beloved before the Holy One, blessed be He, not to be silent for a single moment from cleaving to
### the Torah. There is also permission to pause between matters for words of awakening, ethics, and explanation of deeds, and to establish 
### regulations for the fear of the Lord. I will bring you an event that occurred close to our times, copied from the letter of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shlomo ha-Levi
### Alkabetz <note>author of the hymn "Lecha Dodi"</note> who was joined in the house of our teacher, the author of the *Beit Yosef* <note>Rabbi Joseph Karo</note>, and the Holy Spirit appeared upon him. And this is the text of the letter:

**Know** for yourselves that we agreed—the Pious One <note>referring to Rabbi Joseph Karo</note>, may his light shine, and I, his servant and your servant from among the companions—to stand for our lives on the night of Shavuot and to banish sleep from our eyes. And, praise be to God, so it succeeded for us, for we did not stop for a moment, except for what you shall hear and your soul shall live. And this is the order that I prepared and arranged on that night: First, we read the Torah from the portion of *Bereshit* until "And they were finished" <note>Genesis 1:1–2:3</note> in a pleasant, loud voice. Afterwards, in "the third month" until the end of the section. Further, from the portion of *Mishpatim*, "And to Moses He said" until the end of the section. Further, from the portion of *Va'etchanan*, "And Moses called all of Israel" until the end of the portion of "Shema Yisrael." Further, from the portion of *V'Zot HaBerachah*, "And Moses went up" until "before the eyes of all Israel." Further, the Haftarah "And it was in the thirtieth year" and the Haftarah "A prayer for Habakkuk the prophet." Afterwards the psalm "The heavens declare" and the psalm "Let God arise." Afterwards we prayed in the house without darkness. Afterwards the entire Scroll of Song of Songs and the entire Scroll of Ruth, and afterwards the final verses of Chronicles. And all this was done with awe, with fear, with melody, and with taste—it would not be believed if it were told. Afterwards we studied Mishnah in the order of the "Order of Times" <note>Moed</note>. And afterwards we studied according to the "Way of Truth" <note>Kabbalah</note>. And at the time we began to study the Mishnah, and we had studied two tractates, our Creator merited us and we heard the Voice speaking in the mouth of the Pious One <note>Rabbi Joseph Karo</note>, may his light shine—a great voice with distinct letters, and all the neighbors were hearing but not understanding. And the pleasantness was great, and the voice grew stronger and stronger. And we fell upon our faces, and there was no man who could lift his eyes or his head to see because of the greatness of the dread. And that Speech was speaking with us! 

It began and said: "Hear, my friends, who adorn me from among the choice ones! Pursue, my friends, lovers of peace. Peace be unto you! Happy are you and happy is she who bore you! Happy are you in this world and happy are you in the World to Come, for you have taken it upon yourselves to crown me on this night! For it has been many years since the crown of my head has fallen, and there is no comforter for me. I am cast in the dust, embracing the dunghills. And now, you have restored the crown to its former glory! Be strong, my friends! Be courageous, my beloved ones! Rejoice and lift up your hearts, and know that you are among the 'sons of the upper chamber' <note>a term for high-level mystics</note>. You have merited to be part of the King's palace! The voice of your Torah and the breath of your mouths has ascended before the Holy One, blessed be He, and pierced several atmospheres and several firmaments until it ascended. And the angels were silent, and the Seraphim were hushed, and the Living Creatures stood still, and all the heavenly host and the Holy One, blessed be He, are listening to your voice! And I, the Mishnah <note>The personified Oral Torah</note>, have come to speak to you. Had you been ten <note>a quorum/minyan</note>, you would have ascended even higher and higher. But nonetheless, you have been elevated. Happy are you and happy are those who bore you, my friends, who banished sleep from your eyes, and through you I have been elevated this night! And through the companions who are in the great city, a city and mother in Israel. You are not like those who lie on beds of ivory—sleep, which is one-sixtieth of death—and sprawl upon their couches. But you have cleaved to the Creator, and He rejoices in you! Therefore, my children, be strong and courageous, and ascend in my love, in my Torah, and in my fear. And if you could imagine one-thousandth of a millionth and the great myriads of myriads of the pain in which I dwell, joy would not enter your hearts, nor laughter your mouths, remembering that because of you <note>the sins of Israel</note> I am cast in the dust! Therefore, be strong and courageous and rejoice, my beloved children, who adorn me, and do not stop the study, for a 'thread of grace' is drawn over you and your Torah is sweet before the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, stand, my beloved children, on your feet and raise me up, and say in a loud voice: 'Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever!'" 

(And we stood on our feet, and our joints were knocking together <note>from fear</note>, and we said it aloud as we were commanded). 

And the voice returned and said: "Happy are you, my children! Return to your study and do not stop for a moment! And go up to the Land of Israel! For not all times are equal, and there is no restraint for the Lord to save by many or by few. And let your eyes not pity your 'vessels' <note>possessions</note>, for you shall eat the good of the Upper Land! And if you are willing and you listen, you shall eat the good of that Land! Therefore, hurry and go up, for I am the one who sustains you, and I will provide for you. And you shall have peace, and your homes shall have peace, and all that is yours shall have peace. The Lord gives strength to His people, the Lord blesses His people with peace." All these words he spoke to us and our ears heard, and many more like them concerning matters of wisdom, and many great promises. And we all broke out in weeping from the greatness of the joy, and also from hearing the distress of the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>the Divine Presence in exile</note> due to our sins, and her voice like a sick woman pleading with us. And then we were strengthened until the light of the morning, and the study did not cease from our mouths in joy and trembling. 

And it was in the morning, we went and immersed ourselves as we had done two days prior. And there we found three companions who were not present there that night, and we spoke to them and told them all the good that the Lord had done for us. And their hearts died within them, and they slapped their faces and broke out in weeping. And we also were strengthened and did our obligation as best we could. But we did not merit it again, and we stopped as mentioned above. And they said: "Who would give that on this second night we might join together and be ten?" And we agreed to do as we did the first night. For a single hour of our time we did not see even a moment like the point of a needle [of rest], and even during the day we did not let ourselves sleep because there was a sermon. And we returned, may our light shine, with our companions, and we sat there and worked at all this... while we fasted. And we did on the second night according to the order of the first. And from the great joy that we were ten, they did not wait until the time of the reading of the *Shema*, nor until midnight as on the first night. There, at the hour of half the night, just as we were reading the words of the Deuteronomy, when we reached the portion of "Hear" (*Shema*), the sound of the Voice's knocking came. And it began: "Hear, my beloved friends who adorn me, who speak! Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust..." <note>Isaiah 26:19</note> etc. We lightened two stanzas etc. and words of consolation of wisdom he said there. Afterwards he said: "Happy are you, my friends! Happy are you who raise me up! How much you have been elevated, for you are ten for every matter of holiness! Happy are you in this world, happy are you, and happy is she who bore you! Do not fear the reproach of men or their revilings, for you are the ones who elevate the Assembly of Israel. And know that you are among the 'sons of the upper chamber'..." etc., as above. And afterwards...

# Tractate Shavuot
## The Pillar of the Torah

<margin>
Chapter 54: The Commandment
</margin>

Regarding the festival of Shavuot <note>The "Festival of Weeks," celebrating the giving of the Torah</note>: This is what the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded us—to observe a festival after the seven weeks of the Counting <note>The *Sefirah*, the 49-day period between Passover and Shavuot</note>. I received a tradition from my teacher, the Torah giant Rabbi Shmuel (may his memory be a blessing) of Lublin, who received it from a chain of scholars leading back to the great Rabbi Yaakov Pollack (may his memory be a blessing): one should not recite the *Kiddush* <note>The sanctification prayer over wine</note> nor eat on the first night of Shavuot until the stars come out. The reason for this is that regarding the Counting of the Omer, it is written: "Seven weeks, they shall be complete" <note>Leviticus 23:15</note>. Therefore, if one sanctifies the holiday while it is still day, he diminishes that small portion of the forty-nine days of the Counting. Since Shavuot occurs *after* the Counting, if the Counting is still in effect, it is not yet Shavuot. By reciting *Kiddush*, he accepts the holiday upon himself and thus subtracts from the days of the Counting, resulting in them not being "complete." Do not challenge this by pointing out that we sometimes pray the evening service while it is still day; that is of no consequence, just as one might pray the Saturday night service while it is still the Sabbath (as mentioned in the tractate of *Berakhot*), even though it is still fully the Sabbath. Do not raise a difficulty from the practice of sanctifying the Sabbath early on Friday nights; that is only for the sake of guests and does not appear to diminish the "seven complete weeks," which is not the case here if every individual were to sanctify the day early for themselves. We also find something similar regarding the lighting of Hanukkah candles: on the Friday of Hanukkah, we pray early while it is still day, yet the congregation is obligated to wait to light their candles at home until the proper time for lighting arrives.

<margin>
Obligated in the Land of Israel
</margin>

## One is Obligated
to purify oneself for the pilgrimage festival and to go immerse in a ritual bath. This is especially true for this festival, during which all of Israel—men and women alike—immersed themselves by the command of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said: "Go to the people and sanctify them..." <note>Exodus 19:10</note>. The Sages explained that it is forbidden to hear the "voice of the world" <note>likely referring to idle secular chatter or distractions</note> after studying all night, and such is the custom in the Land of Israel. Nevertheless, it seems proper to me to also immerse on the eve of the festival so that one is pure upon the arrival of the holy day. This is also in memory of our ancestors who immersed on the eve of the festival before sunset, as implied in the chapter of "Rabbi Akiva" (page 86), proving they were "those who immersed during the day" <note>term: *Tevul Yom* — a person who has immersed in a ritual bath but must wait until sunset to be fully pure</note>. Rabbi Yannai also held this view, as did Rav Hanina bar Avin; both said the Torah was given to those who had immersed during the day. Maremar sat and stated this tradition, and Rabbi Hanina said to the eunuch: "Is this a settled law you are stating, or a potential reasoning?" He replied: "It is a potential reasoning," and Rashi explains: "I mean it was *fitting* for the Torah to be given to those who had immersed during the day." We have learned that the Torah was only strict about those who immersed on the day the Torah was given, and so it was heard; but regarding the sanctification of their hands and feet, it seems they were told to separate <note>abstain from marital relations</note> before the immersion. The time was not given to immerse until then because they had been given the command while it was still day and did not delay. If women had a discharge, they would return and immerse after dark, but they did not need to do so. On that night of the festival of Shavuot, sleep should wander from anyone who wishes to cling to holiness, and he should engage in Torah study all night long.

As it is told in the *Zohar* <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>: Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Hiyya were walking on the road. Rabbi Hiyya said: It is written, "And you shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering..." <note>Leviticus 23:15</note>. What does this refer to? He replied: The colleagues have already established this, but come and see: when Israel was in Egypt, they were under another authority and were bound by impurity, like a woman who is menstruating. We have learned that after she becomes pure, she enters the holy portion called the "Covenant." Once they clung to it, impurity ceased from them. Just as a woman, when the blood of impurity ceases, counts seven days, so too here, once they entered the holy portion, impurity ceased from them, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "From here on, the counting is for purity; come and count for yourselves." The word "for yourselves" <note>Hebrew: *lakhem*</note> is precise, just as it says of the woman "she shall count *for herself*" <note>Leviticus 15:28</note>—meaning for her own sake; so too here, for all of you, for your own sakes. And why? In order to be purified in the "living waters," and afterward to be joined with the King and receive the Torah. It is written, "she shall count seven days," and here too "seven weeks." Why seven weeks? In order to merit purification from that "River that flows and goes forth," which is called "Living Waters," and that river gives forth seven weeks.

Therefore, one counts seven weeks. If they wish to merit this, just as a woman prepares from night to night to delight in her husband, so it is written: "And when the dew fell upon the camp at night..." <note>Numbers 11:9</note>. It says "on the camp" and not "and when the dew fell at night." When did this dew descend? When Israel was ready at Mount Sinai, for then that dew descended in its perfection upon man, and their spiritual filth was removed, and they were joined with the King and received the Torah. As for the "Assembly of Israel" <note>original: *Knesset Yisrael*</note>, we have established that this is a time of joy, for "all the rivers go to the sea" to nourish and bring rest, and all are bound <note>variant: "sanctified"</note> and joined with the Holy King.

Come and see: any person who does not count this count of seven complete weeks to merit this purity is not called "pure" and is not included in the category of the pure; he is not worthy to have a portion in the Torah. But one who reaches this day in purity, and the counting has not passed him by—when he reaches this night, he must labor in the Torah and join with the Master of All. For on this night, the "Mother of the Torah" <note>a mystical reference to the Divine Presence or the source of Wisdom</note> rests upon him and makes him wise. In this night, the Supernal Torah is adorned, for they sparkle like the brilliance of the firmament from a deep river. Afterward, on that day, the Written Torah shall come and join with them, and they will be found in glorious beauty above. Then a proclamation is made regarding him: "As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have placed in your mouth..." <note>Isaiah 59:21</note>. The early pious ones would not sleep on this night but would labor in the Torah, saying: "Let us come and inherit the holy inheritance for us and our children." On that night, all are witnesses for them, and they prepare to be joined with the King. Both of these times are marked for those who merit this.

Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] used to say: At the hour when the colleagues gather on this night around the Bride <note>the Torah/Shekhinah</note> to prepare her ornaments, all those who wrap themselves in the "Queen's cloak" and prepare her for the King as is proper—meritorious is their portion! The King gives the Queen to those who prepared her ornaments, for he and the Queen establish her law, and there is no one in the world who knows how to prepare the "Bride's ornaments" except for the colleagues. Meritorious is their portion in this world and the world to come. We have seen that the King rejoices on this night, that we should rejoice in the joy of the Bride, crowning her with the crown intended for the King. Sometimes the King is prepared on this night to be found with her as a Bridegroom joining with the Queen, a holy and deep light of all lights. This is what is written: "Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Zion, upon King Solomon..." <note>Song of Songs 3:11</note>. Afterward, when the King is prepared and crowned, he comes to Israel, to the Queen and those found with her. Like a king who has a banquet and is joyous, he comes to the light. Not like that Supernal King who does not allow the night to pass—that Supernal night brings forth a supreme crown with seventy precious stones surrounding it, and she is crowned by it. She brings forth royal garments and dresses him, and they prepare with great breadth. Afterward, he enters the Bride's chamber, sees her maidens preparing her crowns, garments, and ornaments. She says: "Indeed, I have prepared my immersion, the light, the structure; I have brought forth spirits and perfumes." These are the ones who attend to the Bride; let my Bride come! Her attendants are great, and her maidens shall be purified in that place prepared by the colleagues. Like a bride, my people are like my building. Afterward, they prepare her ornaments, dress her in her garments, and crown her with her crowns. Tomorrow, when my children come to join with the Queen, they will prepare the palace for everyone, and a dwelling will be found among you together. Such is the Holy King and the Queen and the colleagues; and the Supernal Mother who prepares the Bride. Praised is the Supernal King and the Queen and the colleagues whose dwelling is together and shall never be separated. This is what is written: "O Lord, who shall sojourn in Your tent... he who walks uprightly and works righteousness" <note>Psalm 15:1–2</note>. Who is this? These are those who prepare the Queen with her ornaments, her jewelry, and her garments. And anyone who "works righteousness" is called Rabbi Hiyya. If I had only merited in this world to hear these words, it would be enough! And meritorious is the portion of those who labor in the Torah and know the paths of the Holy King, and whose desire is in the Torah. Regarding them, it is written: "Because he has set his love upon Me, therefore I will deliver him; I will set him on high, because he has known My name..." <note>Psalm 91:14</note>.

The order of study for this night has already been publicized and celebrated by the ancients, whose souls and intellects shine with brilliance. It has spread throughout the Land of Israel and all the kingdoms—none are exempt, all as one, from the great to the small, have established and accepted it upon themselves and their descendants. Since we have also added our own "embroidery" to the matter of the order of study for this night from the Forty-Two names, I will put it all together. The study for the merit of Israel, which shall be a structure of ten <note>a *minyan*, the quorum for prayer</note> where the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> dwells, must include parts of the Torah, Prophets, and Writings; the Six Orders of the Mishna; the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>Book of Creation</note>; and the *Zohar*. Now, for all the Torah portions I have written, one should read the [first three] verses of each and every portion, and similarly from every book of the Prophets and Writings—namely the first three verses and the last three verses. It is already known that the Written Torah corresponds to the letter *Vav* of the Divine Name, the secret of the "Pillar" and the "Connection," which is the attribute of *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> comprised of *Hesed* <note>Kindness</note> and *Gevurah* <note>Strength</note>, corresponding to the five first verses. The story, which is the plain meaning of *Tiferet*, is comprised of *Netzach* <note>Eternity</note> and *Hod* <note>Splendor</note>, corresponding to the last three verses in every year and every order. For the first five verses, one starts with *Bereishit* <note>Genesis</note> and reads the entire account of creation until "...which God created to do" <note>Genesis 2:3</note>. Afterward, the last three verses. Then: *Noach*, *Lech Lecha*, *Vayeira*, *Chayei Sarah*, *Toledot*, *Vayeitzei*, *Vayishlach*, *Vayeishev*, *Miketz*, *Vayigash*, *Vayechi*. The total for each is six verses, corresponding to the six first verses, and then the first three verses, and so on. "And the Lord said to Moses: Sanctify to me every firstborn..." <note>Exodus 13:2</note>

This "Living Being" <note>Hebrew: *Chayah zu*</note> refers to the World after the Resurrection. In that time, the denizens of that world will take pleasure in both body and soul together from the "Third Meal" designated for them, just as the First Man <note>Adam</note> took pleasure in both body and soul before he sinned. For then, the world shall return to its initial perfection. To symbolize this, the sacrifice on the Festival of Weeks <note>Shavuot</note> consists of both leavened bread and unleavened bread (*matzah*). The leaven corresponds to the body, and the unleavened bread corresponds to the soul. Just as the leaven and the *matzah* are offered together upon the altar, so too shall the soul and the body take pleasure together in the Eden of that World, which is the Radiance of the Divine Presence, as we find regarding Moses and his brother <note>Aaron</note>. Thus far are the words of the author.

# It was the time of the giving of our Torah; therefore, we are moved to consider several matters from the beginning.

**It is written:** "This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night" <note>Joshua 1:8</note>. This is also stated in the *Tur* <note>A foundational 14th-century code of Jewish law</note>, Section 246, and is transcribed from the words of Maimonides: "Every man of Israel is obligated in Torah study, whether poor or rich, whether healthy in body or suffering, whether young or very old—even a poor man who begs at doors, and even one who has a wife and children. He is obligated to set a fixed time for Torah study by day and by night, as it is stated: 'And you shall meditate on it day and night.'"

<margin>In the Midrash</margin> **Rabbi Pinchas** said in the name of Rabbi Chelkia: "One who sets fixed times for the Torah nullifies the Torah, as it is said: 'It is a time to act for the Lord; they have nullified Your Torah'" <note>Psalm 119:126</note>. At first glance, this is astonishing! Is not "setting fixed times for Torah" the very first virtue a person is asked about at their final judgment? However, there is no contradiction. A person who is free from worldly business and is not burdened with earning a living is obligated to study day and night without wasting a single moment, except for the time required for prayer, eating, and a little sleep. If such a person wishes to merely "set a time" <note>limiting their study to a specific hour</note>, he nullifies the Torah; rather, his desire should be for the Torah of the Lord, and he should meditate on it day and night. The question regarding "setting fixed times" was intended for one who is burdened with his livelihood or craft; such a person must at least set fixed times for the Torah. Note that it says "set times" in the plural, and not "set a time," for it is not enough to set a single session; rather, he should have many sessions throughout the day—that is, during all the times he is free from his business affairs.

<margin>And in the first chapter of Kiddushin</margin> **It is stated: Rav Safra said** in the name of Rabbi Joshua ben Hanania: "What is meant by the verse 'And you shall teach them diligently (*ve-shinnantam*) to your children'? Do not read it as *ve-shinnantam* but as *ve-shillashtam* ('you shall divide into three'). A person should always divide his years into three: one-third for Scripture, one-third for Mishnah <note>The first major written collection of Jewish oral traditions</note>, and one-third for Talmud." The Gemara asks: "Does a person know how long he will live?" The answer is: "No, it is necessary to divide one's days" <note>i.e., divide the study within each day or week</note>. The Tosafot <note>Medieval commentators</note> explain: "One needs to divide the days." The commentary of Rashi explains this to mean the days of the week—two days for Scripture, two for Mishnah, and two for Talmud. But this is not clear, for one could still ask, "Who knows how long he will live?" Therefore, it seems to me that on each and every day itself, one should divide his study into three. This is why the Order of Rav Amram Gaon <note>the first complete prayer book, 9th century</note> established the custom we follow every day before the "Verses of Praise" to recite a passage of Scripture, Mishnah, and Talmud. Rabbeinu Tam <note>a leading 12th-century French scholar</note> explained that we rely on the saying in the Talmud: "Babylon is 'mixed' (*belulah*) with Scripture, Mishnah, and Talmud," meaning that the Babylonian Talmud already contains all three components mixed together. Nevertheless, a person must be careful to ensure that the legal tradition (*halakhah*) of the Talmud is present in his study every single day of his life. Even though one fulfills the obligation through the Babylonian Talmud, a person should still see to it that he studies the Torah, the Prophets, the Writings, the Mishnah, and the Talmud. The study of the Written Torah (Torah, Prophets, and Writings) should be in order, one after the other, followed by the Oral Torah (the six orders of the Mishnah) in sequence, repeating them many times until they are fluent in his mouth by heart.

<margin>In the Midrash</margin> **"You are living human beings"** <note>Hebrew: *Atem bnei adam chayim*</note>. Those living in this world who are preparing to study: regarding Scripture, they should not stop until they have completed the Torah, Prophets, and Writings thoroughly. They should not skip from one weekly portion to another, but rather follow the sequence. The youths should study the verses until they know the word, its grammatical function, the connection, the context, and the structure of the verse. It is also good to study a large portion of the science of grammar while one is a youth, for then it is "written on the tablet of the heart" and serves as a permanent memory. Afterward, one should study all the Mishnahs of the Six Orders until they are fluent by heart, and only then the Talmud in its full breadth and depth, followed by the Legal Codes. Then "the earth will be filled with knowledge." The most essential point that includes everything: the concept of "In-Between Times" <note>term: *Bein HaZemanim* - the traditional vacation periods in yeshivas</note> should be uprooted and abolished from the world. It should not be mentioned or remembered. All times of the year should follow a single custom for Torah study, as it is written, "you shall meditate day and night." These divisions should be null and void; would that they had never existed in the world! Even if someone argues that this method <note>of dialectical study</note> is close to the literal meaning or clarifies many true matters, nevertheless, when even a single thing that is not true is mixed into it, it becomes forbidden in any amount. Who can measure the criminal iniquity of overturning the words of the Living God? I have heard the talk of some of the scholars of this generation who say that if these dialectics <note>term: *Chilukim* - sophisticated, often hair-splitting, logical arguments</note> were not used, what would distinguish the refined student? Or that many would rise to take a seat in the academy based on these things? It is proper to "tear one's garments" over this—to diminish the honor of Heaven in order to increase the honor of men! Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, for then knowledge would increase.

<margin>And behold</margin> **there is a sect of madmen** who say regarding the "vacation" period that it is not proper to rebuke them. They even turn it around and say: "Does one tell a person to sin so that he may merit a great and awesome holiness such as this?" Furthermore, when a student becomes "refined" <note>term: *mechudad* - sharpened/brilliant</note>, what is the nature of his brilliance? Is it not simply that he wastes his days on this matter and speaks falsely about the Torah of Truth? Furthermore, how did Rabbeinu Tam, the Ri, and all the authors of the Tosafot become "refined"? Only through the study of the Torah of Truth, expertise in the tractates, diligence, and constant review. "Time" and "In-Between Times" should be equal. These words are the words of the Living God. One who studies every day, regardless of the season, will find the Gemara, the Tosafot, and all the intricacies of Rashi. For in every single word of Rashi, there are wondrously distinct paths. All the students of the Yeshiva should make a "holy covenant" to look into Rashi's commentary on the Torah; what might seem simple at first glance is revealed as profound when one looks into the Super-commentaries <note>like the Mizrachi</note> and all who explain his words—you will find wonders. Rashi's commentary on the Gemara is likewise all given from "One Shepherd." Afterward, one should examine the Gemara and Tosafot with their questions and answers, resolving them according to the true paths mentioned above. This practice should be constant, through regular terms and vacations; the name "In-Between Times" should not be mentioned or remembered; let it be uprooted from the world. Then our Torah will be the "Torah of the Lord, which is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>. Woe for those who are lost! I have spent most of my days on great and wondrous dialectics <note>*Chilukim*</note>, and I have erred and sinned. Therefore, I have come to warn future generations. Through this, one's intentional sins may be turned into merits. Let them speak and see the Lord, and let them publicize all the above among all Israel to bring merit to the masses. As for the implication in the words of our Sages that one should be "sharpened" through the study of Talmud, one must indeed be "analytical" <note>*mipalpel*</note>, as it is found in the tractate of *Chagigah*: "'Every stay and every staff'—these are the masters of Talmud; 'the man of war'—this is one who knows how to give and take in the 'war of the Torah' <note>scholarly debate</note>." Thus, analytical study <note>*pilpul*</note> is an addition to the Talmud itself. Similarly, in the Chapter *Ba-Kol Mezakin*, it says: "One who dies leaving many possessions: 'rich in public display'—this is the master of Aggadah <note>homiletic lore</note>; 'rich in Sela-coins'—this is the master of analytical debate (*pilpul*); 'rich in oil/hidden things'—this is the master of traditional rulings." Everyone needs the "owner of the wheat" <note>the master of the core texts</note>. What is Gemara? It is the text of the Talmud with Rashi's commentary, the logical flow of the discussions, and the resolution of difficulties; this is the essence of Talmud. Naturally, analytical debate (*pilpul*) is a different matter—it is the sharpening <note>*hiddur*</note> that scholars provide for one another, as found in the first chapter of *Taanit*: "What is meant by 'Iron sharpens iron'? Just as one piece of iron sharpens another, so do two students sharpen one another." It also says there: "Why are the words of Torah compared to a tree? To tell you that just as a small piece of wood ignites a large one, so do lesser scholars sharpen the greater ones." Rabbi Hanina said: "I have learned much from my teachers, more from my colleagues than from my teachers, and from my students most of all." Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Sages already debated this: one said "Sinai" <note>the erudite scholar</note> is preferable, and one said "the uprooter of mountains" <note>the analytical scholar</note> is preferable. Rashi explains that the "uprooter of mountains" is the one who is sharp and analytical. Ben Azzai also used to boast of his sharpness and analysis, as it is stated in the last chapter of *Bekhorot*: "It was taught: Ben Azzai says, 'All the scholars of Israel are like a garlic peel to me, except for this bald one' <note>referring to Rabbi Akiva</note>." I found it written: Why did the Sages of Israel use the metaphor of a garlic peel rather than the peel of another fruit, such as a nut? The answer is because the peel of garlic is more pungent <note>or "sharper"</note> than all other fruit peels. It is inconceivable that Ben Azzai intended to belittle the honor of all the scholars of Israel. Rather, it seems the reason is the sharpness of the garlic. He was sharper than all of them, and they were like the peel; although the peel does not have the same pungency as the fruit itself, it is what holds the fruit together and preserves it. Thus, they were expert and wise in the Torah and "held up" the legal rulings <note>the *RIF* and the *Halakhah*</note>. When he said "they are like a peel *to me*," he was placing them above him, saying that in truth they were above him in wisdom, but he was simply "sharper" than them—he being the garlic, and they being the peel that preserves and sustains the garlic.

<summary>This page outlines a rigorous curriculum for Torah study, prioritizing systematic mastery of Scripture and Mishnah before Talmudic analysis. The author passionately argues for the abolition of vacation periods in yeshivas and critiques "dishonest" dialectics, favoring the traditional commentaries of Rashi and Tosafot.</summary>

...from the attachment, for the Glory hovers over your heads and a thread of grace is drawn over you. And were permission given to the eye, they would see the fire surrounding this house. Therefore, be strong and courageous, and do not break the upper connection. Recite "Hear, O Israel" <note>The Shema prayer</note> in a loud voice, and then "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever" <note>The second line of the Shema, usually whispered, but recited aloud on certain holy occasions</note> as on Yom Kippur.

And many other words were spoken for about half an hour, and then we returned to the secret of study. Afterward, around midnight, the Speech returned a second time and spoke for an hour or more. It returned to praise the matter of that study and said: "Did you hear a voice speaking within you? 'Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will say to you' <note>Deuteronomy 32:7</note>—if for several hundred years they have heard or seen anything like this. You have merited this! Therefore, from now on, let your eyes be open to your ways. Let each man help his fellow, and to his brother say, 'Be strong!' Let the weak say, 'I am a hero!' Consider yourselves great, for you are of the children of the King's Palace. Having merited the vestibule <note>Hebrew: *prozdor*—representing this world or an entry-level of holiness</note>, strive to enter the banquet hall <note>Hebrew: *traklin*—representing the World to Come or the inner sanctum of divinity</note>. Do not leave the vestibule, for he who leaves the gate of the vestibule, his blood is on his own head.

"Wake up, my sons, and see that I am mindful of you. Wake up, my beloved, strengthen yourselves and be men of valor. Now, do not scoff; be strong and rejoice, and return to the grace drawn over you from the heights daily. Go further and 'taste and see' <note>Psalm 34:9</note>, for you are drunk with the desires of the world. Wake up, you drunkards, for behold, a day is coming when man shall cast away his idols of silver and his scales of worldly pleasure, and the idols of gold and the desire for money. Ascend to the Land of Israel, for it is in your power! It is only that you are sunken in the mud of worldly desire. Would that I could remove from you the backward turning; his blood is on his own head! See what you have merited, which others for many generations did not merit."

And the voice spoke at great length on this matter. "And now, you among them, listen to me. Incline your ears, give your hearts, lest your hearing of these things be in vain, and one does not take the fat and butter <note>A metaphor for the spiritual essence</note>, and lest the heart be closed, and the Buyer <note>God</note> say: 'The eye is blind and does not see.' Do not despise this, and let him give his heart to return to the Lord with all his heart, all his soul, and all his might. For all of this [world] is but wind and silence. And all that you have seen here and in the pamphlets is not even one part in a hundred and one. Even in that pamphlet, you will see between word and word a special treasure many times over. This is proof that there was a hidden matter which I did not permit myself to write down."

Our brothers, my people, listen and your souls shall live! For the hand of the Lord was upon the perfect ones who saw all this; He placed a new spirit within them. Also, in the session of Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Yeshivat Chesed*—likely a specific study group</note>, the Speech returned to my beloved ones and wondered, praising what we had done during these two nights. It said repeatedly: "May your reward be complete... to the companions who are distinguished from their group. Since they have entered the vestibule, let them strive to enter the banquet hall, for he who goes outside, his blood is on his own head, and we are innocent."

Then the Pious One <note>likely referring to Rabbi Joseph Caro, who hosted these sessions</note> stood up before the morning meal and patted the pillows in the room, and the Speech and the flame and the Torah went forth in them as he commanded. Afterward, he said: "I am your servant and the one who does your will; ascend and let us say, 'We shall do and we shall hear'!" <note>The famous response of the Israelites at Sinai</note>. They enacted many regulations. One of them was that every Wednesday should be entirely dedicated to the memory of the Temple's Destruction, and that we should not eat meat or drink wine during its night or day for all four years, unless it be at a meal for a commandment, or for a guest, or one traveling on the road, or similar cases.

And you, my brothers, be strong, be strong and courageous! Ascend in the service [of God] and be strong in the service; be righteous among yourselves. See that just as the Mentioner <note>the Maggid</note> warned on the first night of Shavuot, so too you—all of you or some of you—have been stirred to serve the Lord. You have been chosen, and you shall recognize and succeed; you were not mentioned for naught. Therefore, stand for your lives and serve with all your heart. Would that the mouth speaking to you were here—you would see and wonder and open your eyes at what is written in this pamphlet regarding the final vision. For the Pious One mentioned it, and I heard it with my own ears, and the companions... "Angels came," etc. Let everyone take it to heart upon the void <note>original: *beli-mah*—a reference to Job 26:7, meaning "on nothingness"</note>. Let not the desires of the world or a lack of trust mislead your eyes, lest you regret it when it is no longer in your power. For it has already been said, "The time of singing has arrived" <note>Song of Songs 2:12</note>; you will have no other time. Let him not delay, let him not be too proud to extend this further in my eyes...

See how many causes God brought about for me to come there, and to the people of the city... so that the intention of the Blessed One was to show me this great matter. And you, also you, do not blame or consider... the one who takes it to heart, the perfect one shall say, "I am a hero!" and "Lord of the earth," and "each man shall help his fellow, and to his brother say, 'Be strong!'" Do not let your hands go slack. Know also that the companions accepted upon themselves that on the eve of the Ninth of Av, they would not eat any cooked dish, not even lentils. This is a living hint—almost a total fast—just dry bread and a measure of water, and many such things were with them to restore and return to the honor of His holiness, upon the foundation of the fear of Him, may He be blessed. We conducted ourselves this night thusly. May God Almighty plead in your hearts to have pity on yourselves, and may He merit us to be united with you in the Holy Land to serve Him with one accord, Amen. These are the words of my tongue, your beloved, Solomon Halevi Alkabetz, may he be remembered for the life of the World to Come. The language of the writing:

## Happy is the eye that saw all these; therefore, let everyone sanctify and purify himself with additional holiness and purity. It is good to stipulate that they shall not speak on that night in any secular tongue, but everything should be in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note>.

### The Haftarah
->of the holiday of Shavuot is the "Work of the Chariot" from Ezekiel <note>Ezekiel chapter 1</note>. I received from my father and teacher, of blessed memory, that it should be recited while standing. And as for the verse mentioned<-
->in *Hagigah*, chapter "One may not expound" <note>Talmud Hagigah 14b</note>, which says: It happened that Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai was riding on a donkey and was traveling on the road, and Rabbi Eleazar ben Arach<-

was following him. He said to him: "Rabbi, teach me one chapter of the Work of the Chariot." He replied: "I have not taught you... nor the Chariot to an individual unless he was a sage who understands of his own knowledge." He said to him: "Rabbi, permit me to say before you one thing that you taught me." He said to him: "Speak." Immediately, Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai descended from the donkey, wrapped himself [in his cloak], and sat upon a stone under an olive tree. He asked him: "Rabbi, why did you descend from the donkey?" He replied: "Is it possible that you are expounding on the Work of the Chariot, and the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> is with us, and the ministering angels are accompanying us, and I should ride on a donkey?" (Until here). The common people are not careful on the holiday of Shavuot when the attendant distributes smelling herbs to every single person at the time of the *Kedushah* <note>a central part of the prayer service</note>... they immediately smell them like messengers. This is not correct, for in any case, they commit a transgression if they recite the blessing over the scent, as it turns out they are interrupting with this blessing in a place where it is forbidden to speak. For it is forbidden to speak from the beginning of "Blessed is He who spoke" <note>Baruch Sheamar</note> until after the end of the prayer. And if they smell them without a blessing, it is difficult because of the teaching that it is forbidden to enjoy anything in this world without a blessing. Therefore, let everyone be careful not to smell them immediately upon taking them, but only after the conclusion of the prayer shall he find relief and salvation.

The world is accustomed to eating dairy foods on the holiday of Shavuot. Afterward, they eat meat to fulfill the commandment "And you shall rejoice in your festival" <note>Deuteronomy 16:14</note>, for there is no joy without meat. However, one must be careful to sanctify oneself, especially on a holy day such as this, which is the time of the giving of our Torah. One must clean and rinse the mouth well, interrupt with the Grace After Meals, wait one hour, and afterward spread another tablecloth. Then he may set the table and meat. There is a hint to this in the verse: "The first of the first-fruits of your land you shall bring to the house of the Lord your God; you shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk" <note>Exodus 23:19</note>—meaning, be careful not to mix them. And he who sanctifies himself in this, "holy" shall be said of him. The Great Genius, our teacher Rabbi Solomon Luria <note>Maharshal, 16th century</note>, of blessed memory, permitted milk that was cooked on the first festival day of Shavuot to be eaten on that same day. If it was milked on the Sabbath preceding it (the 5th of Sivan), it should not be eaten until the second day. See his responsa; so too did our teacher Rabbi Jacob Moelin <note>Maharil</note> instruct.

**A man is obligated** to rejoice on this festival more than others, for it is the day on which we merited the Crown of Torah. In *Pesachim*, chapter "These matters," they all agree regarding Shavuot that we also require "for you" <note>meaning, physical enjoyment like eating/drinking, not just spiritual study</note>. Mar, the son of Ravina, would sit in a fast the whole year except for Shavuot... because of the "day of the assembly" <note>Shavuot</note>. Joseph, on the day of Shavuot, would prepare a three-year-old calf for himself. He said: "If not for this day, how many 'Josephs' would there be in the marketplace?" <note>Meaning, without the Torah, he would be an ordinary person</note>. Nevertheless, one should "rejoice with trembling" in total repentance. The joy should be spiritual joy, giving thanks and praise to the Blessed Name for giving him the Torah. This should greatly stir his heart to sanctify and purify himself from his sins and iniquities through the radiance of the Crown of Torah, to fulfill "and you shall meditate on it day and night," for this holy day is a Day of Judgment.

And so it is written in *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>a mystical work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, page 58: "In the Midrash, the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to deepen and bring down the deeds of men on this day. It is the Day of First Fruits, for the Torah is the first, and it is the renewal of the world. Just as they established the saying 'This day is the beginning of Your works' according to the words of Rabbi Eliezer who said the world was created in Tishrei, such is the will on the day of the Giving of the Torah. For it indicates the renewal of the world, to supervise and demand an account of the deeds of the world and to judge it for the 'fruits of the tree,' as stated in the first chapter of *Rosh Hashanah*: 'The world is judged... on Shavuot for the fruits of the tree.' We have already explained that those 'fruits' are the souls that fly from the Tree of the Holy One, blessed be He. The world is judged on this day regarding the Torah given on it—that they neglected it. This is what they meant by 'fruits of the tree'—that they did not complete them with Torah and commandments as is fitting." Furthermore, regarding the speech of this holy day...
