<meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous page regarding the merits and conditions of Torah study. The previous page ended with a warning about the consequences of not studying for the sake of the Heaven. This page transitions into the legalities of "selling" Torah merit and the proper etiquette, timing, and restrictions regarding who may be taught the Torah.</meta>

### One might think
That a person can purchase from his fellow the reward for his study and his good deeds, or sell them to him before the act is even done. This was written by **Rabbi Yerucham** <note>Rabbi Yerucham ben Meshullam, a 14th-century halakhic authority</note> at the end of section 52, and it was brought by the **Beit Yosef** <note>Rabbi Yosef Karo's commentary on the Tur</note> at the end of the Laws of Talmud Torah <note>Yoreh De'ah, section 246</note>. One who occupies himself with the Torah, before he has the chance to stipulate that his fellow will engage in commerce and take a portion of his learning—similar to the historical arrangement between the tribes of **Issachar and Zebulun** <note>A traditional partnership where one brother (Zebulun) works to support the other (Issachar) who studies, sharing the spiritual reward</note>—can do so. However, after one has already studied, if someone gives him money for it, it is worth nothing. As the verse says: "If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned" (Song of Songs 8:7). This is seen in the story of **Hillel and Shevna** <note>Shevna was Hillel's wealthy brother who offered to split his wealth for Hillel's Torah merit only after Hillel became famous; Hillel refused</note> in the chapter "One Who Takes." It stands to reason that the one who studied loses his reward [if he sells it after the fact]; so wrote the commentators.

### We shall return
To the **Honor of the Torah**. We learned at the end of Tractate Sotah: "From the time Rabban Gamaliel died, the honor of the Torah was diminished." This is because until the time of Rabban Gamaliel, everyone used to learn while standing. Afterward, "weakness descended upon the world" and they began to learn while sitting. Nevertheless, it appears that it is forbidden to learn while leaning or reclining on one's side; rather, one should sit in awe and fear. This does not apply when one is reviewing his Torah study in bed at night when he wishes to sleep. Regarding one who forces himself to study Torah while standing as much as his strength allows, it is said: "One who honors the Torah, his body is honored."

### Included
In the **Honor of the Torah** is the requirement to honor the books themselves and the pages of books that have become worn out. This is mentioned in the glosses of the **Asheri** <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel, the Rosh</note> in the chapter "Rabbi Akiva," which states: "It implies that anything that comes from a holy source, even if it is ruined and no longer fit for its purpose, requires **Genizah** <note>Sacred storage for worn-out holy texts, preventing them from being treated as trash</note>." I am greatly distressed by the sin committed in these lands regarding the pages of small Gemaras <note>Volumes of the Talmud</note> [that are neglected]. One who fears Heaven should be careful, and warn others, to store them away properly.

### We have learned
In the chapter **Helek** <note>The 11th chapter of Sanhedrin</note>: Our Rabbis taught that one who reads a verse from the **Song of Songs** and treats it like a common song, or one who reads a verse at a banquet hall out of its proper time, brings evil to the world. This is because the Torah "girdles itself in sackcloth" and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He, saying: "Master of the Universe! Your children have made me like a lyre that foreigners play!" He says to her: "My daughter, when they are eating and drinking, what else should they occupy themselves with?" She says before Him: "Master of the Universe! If they are masters of Scripture, let them occupy themselves with the Torah, Prophets, and Writings. If they are masters of the Mishnah, let them occupy themselves with Laws and Homilies. And if they are masters of the Talmud, let them occupy themselves with the Laws of Passover on Passover, the Laws of Shavuot on Shavuot, and the Laws of Sukkot on Sukkot!" **Rabbi Ben Eleazar** said in the name of **Rabbi Simeon ben Hanina**: "Anyone who reads a verse in its proper time brings good to the world."

Until here is the construction of **Judah** <note>Likely referring to the author of the 'Me'at Mayim' or a similar compendium</note>. And they wrote in my name [the practice for] the month of Nisan in the chapter "Arvei Pesachim," and the **Rif** there. The intention of our master, the **Tur**, and the **Beit Yosef** is that the study for the holiday of **Shavuot** should be the accounts of the Giving of the Torah mentioned in the chapter "Rabbi Akiva" <note>In Tractate Shabbat</note>. Similarly, in the month of Av, one should study the Laws of the Ninth of Av and Fasts. Between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, one should study the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Tractate Yoma. On Sukkot, Tractate Sukkah. On Hanukkah, the Laws of Hanukkah. On Purim, Tractate Megillah. On the Festivals, Tractate Yom Tov [Beitzah] is appropriate. On all holidays, the study should be from the Talmud, the Rif, and the Tur, according to your ability to bear it. For this Torah study is most beloved and leads to practical action. On the holiday of the Giving of the Torah, this is exceedingly beloved before the Holy One, Blessed be He, for it is beautiful and in its proper time.

### The Honor
Of the Torah was given to Israel. A great prohibition is violated in some lands by some people who **study Torah with Gentiles**. **Rashi** <note>Actually referencing the Maharshal in Yam Shel Shlomo</note> in Tractate Bava Kamma writes: "Our Rabbis taught: The Wicked Kingdom <note>Rome</note> once sent two officials to the Sages of Israel saying: 'Teach us your Torah.' They read it, repeated it, and reviewed it a third time. At the time of their departure, they said to the Sages: 'We have scrutinized your entire Torah and it is truth, except for this one thing you say: If an ox of an Israelite gores the ox of a Gentile, the owner is exempt, but if the ox of a Gentile gores the ox of an Israelite, whether it is a first-time offender or a habitual gorer, he must pay full damages.'" 

The officials challenged: "Whichever way you look at it! If 'his neighbor' <note>The biblical term used in the law of damages</note> is meant literally, then even the Gentile's ox that gores the Israelite's should be exempt. And if 'his neighbor' is not literal, then even the Israelite's ox that gores the Gentile's should be liable!" The Sages did not reveal the underlying reason to them—which is that the property of a Gentile is legally ownerless—due to the danger. What we conclude is that we do not inform the government of this. The word "Sarditot" refers to messengers and officials appointed to carry out laws. They said to the Sages of Israel: "We will do you a favor and not report this discrepancy to the government." Therefore, even though the Sages impressed them, they did not reach the "Ladders of Tyre" <note>A geographical landmark, meaning they didn't get far</note> before they forgot everything.

I saw this in the long commentaries of the **Tosafot** <note>Medieval French/German commentaries</note> and it appears so from Rashi's commentary to those who look closely. The Tosafot asked: "But do we not say that teaching Torah to a Gentile violates a positive commandment?" Rashi explains that the officials of the government forced them to do so against their will, and the Sages were not obligated to sacrifice their lives. Alternatively, the officials made themselves appear as potential converts in the eyes of the Sages. 

It is implied from here that it is not permitted to teach Torah to a Gentile even for the sake of "peace with the government," and certainly not for payment or pleasure, unless it is by a decree of the king. Woe to those found in the lands of Spain, Italy, and the lands of the Ishmaelites <note>Muslim lands</note> who teach the Torah of the Lord with the nations for their own pleasure and payment. They are those who "accompany with a pleasant heart," but afterward they turn to heresy. This is not like the way the Holy One, Blessed be He, handed the Torah to Moses to give to Joshua, and Joshua to the Elders, etc. He did not permit writing down the Oral Torah so that they would not turn it toward heresy, as stated in the **Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer**. Those people who sin against their own souls and bodies by teaching with the nations put themselves at risk to nullify the counsel of the Lord. In my humble opinion, their sin is too great to bear. They shall not see the consolation of Zion.

I also heard from a great scholar that it is forbidden to change a law of the Torah [when speaking to them] through intentional interpretation; one is obligated to give his life for the **Sanctification of God's Name** <note>original: "Kiddush Hashem"</note> rather than lie about the Torah. Our teacher **Nachmanides** <note>Rabbi Moses ben Nachman (Ramban), a 13th-century sage</note> was subjected to a wicked decree <note>The Disputation of Barcelona, 1263</note>. Was it not difficult for him to say before the nations that we are exempt from damages while they are liable? Should he not have been concerned for the ruins of our generations and our times, especially under the wicked kingdom whose only thought is to fall upon our enemies? Some say it is better to change the law and say either both are liable or both are exempt, but the Talmud teaches that we are obligated to speak the truth for the Sanctification of the Name. If one, God forbid, changes this law, he is like one who denies the Torah of Moses. Presumably, the ministers asked specifically about every single law. Therefore, they answered the truth for the Sanctification of the Name, because they could not judge themselves. 

As for what is brought in the third chapter of Tractate Megillah regarding the event of **King Ptolemy** <note>The translation of the Septuagint</note> who gathered 72 elders and they changed the Torah—that was from Heaven, for they all agreed and it was a matter of the Divine Spirit. Furthermore, they did not change any matter from its true meaning; they only swapped words so that the Greeks would not flip the interpretation. The change they made reflected the true intent of the verse in its plain sense. But to say that one who is exempt is liable, or vice versa, is like denying the Torah of Moses. What is the difference between one word and the entire Torah? As it says in the third chapter of Yoma: "Rav said: Anyone who forgets one thing from his study causes exile for his children, as it says: 'Because you have forgotten the Torah of your God, I also will forget your children' (Hosea 4:6)." Thus, even one word of Torah is called the "Torah of the Lord."

Therefore, it is forbidden to teach a Gentile even one letter of the Torah; it is a great sin. A Gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable for death [by the hand of Heaven], and the teacher also violates "Do not place a stumbling block before the blind." One should only teach them the **Seven Noahide Laws** <note>Universal moral laws for all humanity</note> which they are required to learn, as mentioned in Tractate Hagigah and Tosafot. But anything beyond that is very severe, without distinction. This is especially true regarding the Torah portion of *Acharei Mot*. 

The work **Tola'at Yaakov** <note>A 16th-century Kabbalistic commentary on the liturgy by Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai</note>, regarding the secret of Circumcision, writes: "Anyone who is not sealed with this holy seal [circumcision] has no portion in the God of Israel and cannot recognize Him through His Torah, lest he be called 'unclean' and not 'holy.' For this reason, we do not teach them even the Alphabet (Aleph-Bet). Anyone who teaches him Torah speaks falsely regarding the Great Name, for the entire Torah is the Names of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Since they do not enter the Covenant of the Tongue (which is the Holy Torah) except through the Covenant of the Flesh [circumcision], this is a 'light to heavy' <note>a fortiori</note> argument: If the Passover offering, which is just a hint of holiness, says 'no uncircumcised person shall eat of it,' how much more so the Torah, which is the Holy of Holies and the Names of God! Therefore, it is forbidden to teach Torah to a Gentile, as it is said: 'He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and His ordinances to Israel' (Psalms 147:19), and it is written: 'Yet I had planted you a noble vine, wholly a seed of truth' (Jeremiah 2:21). One who teaches Torah to a Gentile testifies about himself as if he were not 'truth.' God forbid. If the Gentile merits the Covenant of the Flesh, that is the gate that brings him into the Covenant of the Tongue, which is the Torah, and then he is called a 'Righteous Proselyte'."

### So that
"The Torah of the Lord shall be in your mouth" (Exodus 13:9). I saw one of the meticulous scholars who had the 613 commandments recorded in a small notebook, and he used to review them every day until they were all fluent in his mouth by heart. He knew that a specific commandment was number 40, 1, 60, or 200, and so on. Anyone who dedicates his heart to the love of Torah should do the same.

### A great obligation
Lies upon one who travels on the road to occupy himself with Torah. As we learned: "One who walks on the road... and interrupts his study and says: 'How beautiful is this tree' [is liable for his life]." We also learn in Sotah (page 49) and in Ta'anit (Chapter 1): If two scholars walk on the road and there are no words of Torah between them, they are worthy of being burned, as it is said: "And it came to pass..."

<header>Tractate Shevuot</header>

The student poses a difficulty or a question and then resolves it. However, according to the version of **Rashi** and **Tosafot** <note>The primary medieval commentators on the Talmud</note>, the question remains standing; rather, the explanation is that a commandment that is incumbent upon a person and has a specific time—such as putting on **Tefillin** <note>leather boxes containing Torah verses worn during prayer</note>, which is an obligation for the entire day—must be performed early. The principle that "Torah study is greater" only applies when there is no specific commandment incumbent upon the person, or a commandment that can be performed by someone else. However, if a commandment is incumbent specifically upon him, he should not abandon it. This is similar to the case of **Rabbi Yochanan** who left the restroom and had not yet begun teaching the public. However, once he has begun teaching, he does not stop, even for a commandment incumbent upon him whose time might pass. This is like the case found in the chapter "One who Recites" <note>Talmud Berakhot, Chapter 2</note> regarding the recitation of "Hear O Israel" and "And you shall love the Lord your God," which was the **Shema** <note>The central declaration of Jewish faith</note> of **Rabbi Yehuda the Prince**; he would not stop to recite the entire Shema. Even though we learned in the first chapter of **Shabbat**: "We stop for the Recitation of Shema but we do not stop for the Prayer <note>The Amidah/Silent Prayer</note>," **Rabbi Yochanan** said this only applies to someone like **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai** and his colleagues whose "Torah is their profession" <note>meaning they study exclusively and do not work</note>. But for people like us, we stop for Prayer just as we do for Shema. 

The **Rosh** <note>Rabbi Asher ben Yechiel, a 13th-century legal authority</note> asked: why did Rabbi Yehuda the Prince not stop to recite the entire Shema, since we stop for Shema even for one whose Torah is his profession? The **Rambam** <note>Maimonides</note> answered that this applies to a person learning alone, but one who is teaching Torah to the public should not stop. If so, regarding our study, for those like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his colleagues whose Torah is their constant occupation, one should not stop even for a commandment incumbent upon him, even if the time for the commandment will pass. This is not considered disrespectful. The **Beit Yosef** <note>Rabbi Yosef Karo</note> wrote in the **Tur** <note>The Code of Jewish Law</note>, Orach Chaim section 70: according to the opinion of the Tur, the rule that one who teaches the public does not stop applies only if stopping to recite the Shema would cause the group to disperse so that they could not resume their studies later. 

It seems to me that the same applies to a commandment that is not strictly incumbent upon him—meaning it is not a positive commandment, but a mitzvah happened to come his way that cannot be performed by another—if he does not perform it now, it will be lost. Even if he is teaching the public, he should stop in the middle of his study. Perhaps he wrote that "teaching the public" refers to teaching people who do not know the laws and the "deeds they must perform." I have already written above that according to Rashi, it is a commandment to investigate the depth of the study, and we have found no one who disagrees with him, for it is a logical reason.

# Let us Return

<margin>
From the act of **Rabbi Yudel** <note>Likely a local or contemporary reference to a scholar named Yehuda</note>, he proved the general rule that one stops for Shema for the common people, as we learned: "We stop for Shema." According to the logic of the **Kessef Mishneh** <note>Commentary on Maimonides</note>, teaching Torah to the many is greater than performing acts of kindness. This is a great principle regarding stopping study. He holds that learning is greater than commandments and greater than [unclear]. But those who stop for Shema even if their Torah is their profession, this refers to those who are learning and their study was interrupted... <note>The marginal note is dense and discusses the nuances of whether public teaching takes precedence over individual prayer obligations</note>.
</margin>

# General Rule
The ultimate goal is the perfection of the person, but **Rabbeinu Bahya** <note>13th-century philosopher and commentator</note> says it is the perfection of the action—provided there is a proper intention, for "commandments require intention" <note>kavanah</note> for the act to be completed in its true perfection. The act must include both speech and thought; that is, the speech of the lips where we say, "Behold, we are doing what our Creator commanded us for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note>," and the thought is the intention and the hidden secret of the commandment. 

This is also explained in the book **Avodat HaKodesh** <note>original: "E.H." likely referencing *Etz Chayim* or ibn Gabbai's work</note>, chapter 27: True perfection is found in the action. The perfection we mentioned cannot be achieved except through the performance of the commandments and their actual fulfillment. Since the nature of man is to elevate the physical matter of his limbs and joints, and he possesses the "tools of action," the primary intention within them should be the actual service—to draw down the purpose for which he was created, which is the "Unification," and this is impossible except through action. Therefore, the practical commandments constitute the largest part of the Torah, as constant physical refinement is beneficial. 

Prohibitive commandments (the "thou shalt nots") are fulfilled only in the mind, as they help a person remain on the right path and not turn our minds away. This is the concept of "Fear of God." Just as the fulfillment of positive commandments in action is the cause of the world's building and existence, so too is the fulfillment of a negative commandment—for example, if a sinful matter comes to a person's hand and he is saved from it, he has performed a commandment by subduing his inclination. This is seen in the first chapter of **Kiddushin**. The reason is that when a man subdues his inclination and bows it under the Great Name, he becomes unified with His Glory and elevates the world. This is the fruit of action and the fulfillment of the commandments. In this way, a "negative" act becomes a "positive" one. The result is the elevation of the Attribute of Justice into Mercy, which is the complete Unification. This is the fruit of all Divine service. This is the secret of the "Gate" and the "Tree" and the commandments to be awakened to bring in a "good vessel," which is the root of the Love we were commanded: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart." We learned in the Mishnah in the chapter "One who Sees" <note>Talmud Berakhot, Chapter 9</note>: "With both your inclinations—with the Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination." For it is our duty to rectify all things, to straighten them and sweeten them as they were in the Supernal Thought before they were separated from there. For while they were there, they were good and upright. Therefore, we are obligated to love God even with the Evil Inclination—that it should be unified with the Good Inclination and they shall become one, so that one does not oppose the other. This is the secret of Love, which is the root of Unification. According to all this, perfection is in the performance of the commandments.

# The Purpose
The purpose of learning is "to learn and to teach, to keep and to do." My children, if a legal ruling comes before you and you are meant to be a **Moreh Hora'ah** <note>a teacher of legal rulings/a judge</note>, you must be cautious and fear the ruling so that you do not stumble, Heaven forbid, before the public. Before they issued a ruling, the law was clear when they examined it in their hearts. In all the writings of the authorities, you will see first in the book how the law is clear. If there is any doubt, do not be ashamed to speak of it with other scholars. For we have no one greater than **Rav Huna**, who when he had to rule on a case of a *Tereifah* <note>an animal with a life-threatening defect, making it non-kosher</note>, he would gather many scholars so that "the chip of the log would reach everyone" <note>a Talmudic idiom meaning that by sharing the decision-making, the responsibility/blame is shared</note>. Let the fear of God be in your hearts. Nevertheless, do not say "let us be strict" just because of the majority; this is not called a legal decider. To be strict on others against the law is wrong, though for himself, one may be as strict as he pleases. 

In Tractate **Berakhot**, first chapter, it says of King David that "his hands were soiled with the fetal sac and the blood... in order to purify a woman for her husband." It does not say "in order to purify or to make impure," rather he worked hard to see if it was clearly pure according to the law, so that, Heaven forbid, he should not declare her impure and be unnecessarily strict on others, causing them to neglect "fruitfulness and multiplication" <note>having children</note>. A legal decider must be careful not to cause others to stumble. We are taught "the power of leniency" <note>original: *koach de-heiteira*</note> and the power of the law in all rulings. Even for himself, while it is a trait of piety to be strict, this only applies when there is a basis for the stringency. But if there is no place to be strict, and he only wants to be strict because of a lack of knowledge—whereas if he had studied and investigated the law clearly he would see there is no room for stringency—and despite this he is strict, this is a **Chassid Shoteh** <note>a "pious fool"</note>. 

Regarding this, I heard an explanation of the statement in Berakhot: "Rabbi Hiyya said in the name of Ulla: Greater is one who enjoys the toil of his hands more than a God-fearing person." Regarding the God-fearing person it is written: "Ashrei (praiseworthy) is the man who fears the Lord," but regarding the one who enjoys the toil of his hands it is written: "When you eat the toil of your hands, you are praiseworthy (ashrecha) and it is good for you"—praiseworthy in this world and good for you in the World to Come. The question is famous: surely one who enjoys the work of his hands is also a God-fearing person, for otherwise, how could he be better than one who fears God if he is a sinner? Rather, you must say he is also God-fearing. If so, what is his greatness? Rather, a "God-fearing person" here refers to one who is simply strict and declares things forbidden. But greater than him is the one who toils in the Torah and studies until it is clear to him that the food is permitted. This is "one who enjoys the toil of his hands"—he merits being "praiseworthy" in this world by enjoying the food, and "it is good for him" in the World to Come because he occupied himself with the Torah and clarified the law.

# After
The ruling is clear, one should not let it "sour" <note>delay it</note>. He should answer the questioner immediately. Just as one must not delay a ruling in monetary laws, so too in all matters, especially regarding the laws of a woman to her husband, so that he does not let her case "lodge" overnight <note>delaying the possibility of a husband and wife being together</note>. In Tractate **Shabbat**, chapter "With what may an animal go out," Rabbi Shimon bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan: "Anyone who says the sons of **Eli** <note>The High Priest in the book of Samuel</note> sinned is but mistaken... rather, how do I fulfill the verse 'that they lay with the women'? Because they delayed their bird-offerings so that the women had to stay away from their husbands, the Bible considers it as if they had laid with them."

Verses and similar matters according to the traditions, along with what came before and what follows this; there are mounds upon mounds of laws. So it appears to me based on the plain meaning of the scripture: "He teaches his way," as I have written.
</margin>

And what is written afterward? **The heavens and the earth.** This refers to the Divine Wisdom, which is the Primordial Torah that preceded the world by two thousand years. As it was said elsewhere: "Then I was by Him as a nursling [Amon], and I was His delight day by day" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. The Torah says: "For two thousand years I was a delight in His bosom," for it is said "day," and a day of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is a thousand years, as it says: "For a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday" <note>Psalm 90:4</note>. The intention of "two thousand years" refers to the secret of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) and Understanding (*Binah*) <note>The second and third emanations/Sephirot in Kabbalah</note> which existed before the World of Construction. From these emanated the attribute of Beauty (*Tiferet*), the secret of the Written Torah. It is written that the son comes from the father; this is the place of the prophecy of the master of all prophets <note>Moses</note>. From there, he received the Torah, which consists of 613 commandments (*Mitzvot*) that were emanated from the Sephirah of Wisdom, received from the highest heights according to the secret of the 620 types of lights <note>620 is the numerical value of *Keter* (Crown), representing the 613 commandments plus the seven Noahide laws, or the total number of letters in the Ten Commandments</note>.

In the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah <note>The *Bahir*, an early Kabbalistic text</note>, they asked: "What is the reason for the raising of the hands to bless us?" It is because there are ten fingers on the hands, hinting at the Ten Sephirot <note>The ten divine attributes through which God interacts with the world</note> with which the heavens and the earth were sealed. Those ten correspond to the Ten Commandments. Within those ten, all 613 commandments are included. Count the letters of the Ten Commandments and you will find they are 613 letters <note>original: "תרי"ג אותיות"</note> up until the phrase "that is your neighbor's" <note>The end of the 10th commandment</note>. The total including the final words is 620 letters, corresponding to the 620 types of primordial lights from which they were emanated.

Because the Torah is the Name of the Lord, according to the secret of the "Beauty of Israel" (*Tiferet Yisrael*), the Unique Name, it is called the "Tree of Life" which finds pleasure in the higher life—the life of the King, the Mother of Children. Regarding this, we learned: "Great is the Torah, for it gives life to those who perform it in this world." It is known to the scholars of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> that the Written Torah is comprised of the Right and the Left <note>Mercy and Judgment</note>, for the Name of the Lord, the secret of the Beauty of Israel, is in the center, including both right and left. It is the flow that includes both positive and negative commandments. The Torah is comprised of all seven Sephirot <note>the lower seven attributes from Chesed to Malkhut</note>. Therefore, they said in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah: "This teaches that the Torah was given with seven voices." Thus, the Torah has eight "faces" <note>dimensions or perspectives</note>. One who is diligent in blessings merits the Torah which was given in five voices; the intention refers to the place of its source, the river that goes out of Eden. It includes the fifty gates of Understanding (*Binah*). Those who know it expound it with 49 faces of "pure" and 49 faces of "impure," for the fiftieth gate cannot be grasped even by the master of prophets. Therefore, it was given in Five Books of Moses to indicate the place of emanation.

Therefore, the Torah was given on the festival of *Shavuot* <note>The Festival of Weeks/Pentecost</note>, because during the days of the *Omer* counting, which are days of purification, Israel was purified through the 49 faces of purity. Also, the word *Shavuot* <note>Weeks/Oaths</note> indicates the seven "Sabbatical cycles" of the world's days, as explained above regarding the secret of the Counting. The fiftieth day is the secret of the Great Jubilee, when the hidden light of the Torah will be revealed. It is known what they said: "All of creation was suspended until the giving of the Torah; if they accept it, good, but if not, everything returns to chaos." Therefore, when the time representing the world's stability was completed, the acceptance of the Torah was required. Then "The Torah of the Lord is perfect"—a full Name for a full world—for the entire Torah is the Name of the Blessed One. It is proper for the observer to appreciate this regarding the Choice of the Holy Torah. To move from topic to topic, I shall make a separate discourse, and I call its name:
**Behold the Torah of the Altar.**
Since I have prepared six steps for the Throne of Glory of the Torah, I shall establish them upon those six verses: "The Torah of the Lord is perfect," etc., "The testimony of the Lord is sure," etc., "The precepts of the Lord are right," etc., "The commandment of the Lord is clear," etc., "The fear of the Lord is pure," etc., "The judgments of the Lord are true," etc. <note>Psalm 19:8-10</note>. In every verse, the Name of the Lord is specifically chosen to show that the entire Torah is His Names, and in every verse there are five words to indicate the "Upper Five" <note>likely referring to the five books or higher Sephirot</note> as mentioned.

### The Supreme Level: Blessed be the Place <note>God</note> who gave the Torah to His people Israel.
### 2. The Level of the Torah; 3. The Level of its Learners; 4. The Level of its Fulfillers; 5. The Level of the Narrative; 6. Other Levels. And the Torah is the secret of "These and those are the words of the Living God."

**The Supreme Level: The giving of the Torah, Blessed be He.** "The Torah of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul." The deep Kabbalists said that the Torah is the imprint of Divinity, and the world is the imprint of the Torah. I am here to truly explain this noble matter. The Torah is the imprint of Divinity, the secret of the revelation of the Essential Name, which is the Name Y-H-W-H <note>original: "יה"ו"</note>. He was, is, and will be; He who brought everything into being. He is the essence of true Being, and from Him, all that exists was brought into being through the revelation of His Essential Name in the secret of Emanation—in the secret of the hidden and the revealed. That is, the letters Y-H-H <note>original: "יה"ה"</note>, which are the "hidden things," the secret of His thought, wisdom, and understanding, where there is only a mental form for the intellect. The secret of this thought is the Primordial Torah, for the concept of "Torah" is like the word for "teacher" (*Moreh*). From this path, the secret of expansion becomes revealed. Afterward, the "Construction" was revealed in space through the secret of Y-H, which is the revelation from which the chain of spiritual and physical worlds is drawn.

Behold, Beauty (*Tiferet*) is the Written Torah, called Y-H-W-H in the vocalization of *Chashak* <note>a specific Kabbalistic vowel arrangement</note>. "The Lord is in His holy temple" and "The Lord from His dwelling place," etc., refers to the secret of Sovereignty (*Malkhut*), the Oral Torah, which is the explanation of the Written Torah. These channels and sparks are clothed in the spirituality of the heavenly commandments of the Torah, which is our freedom. This was clothed in the practical performance of the commandments of the Torah which Moses commanded us. Thus, the world is the imprint of the Torah, and "The Torah of the Lord is perfect."

It is written in *Sha'arei Orah* <note>"Gates of Light" by Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla</note>, page 2: "Know that all His holy and pure Names mentioned in the Torah are all dependent on the Four-Letter Name, which is Y-H-W-H. And if you ask: Is not the Name *Adonai* <note>Lord/Master</note> the main one and the source? Know that the Four-Letter Name is like the body of the tree, and the Name *Adonai* is the foot/base <note>original: "עיקר"</note> of this tree, from which roots take hold and branches spread to every side. All other holy names are like the branches. As a wise person understands, the tree and each of its branches go outward to the 'hallway.' Besides the known holy Names that may not be erased, there are many other 'attributes' <note>original: "כינויין"</note> dependent on each name. For example, the attributes of Y-H-W-H are 'Awesome,' 'Forgiver of Iniquity,' 'Passer over Transgression.' The attributes of *El* are 'Great,' 'Merciful,' and 'Gracious.' The attributes of *Elohim* are 'Mighty,' 'Judge,' 'Arbiter.' Each of these attributes has other matters dependent on it, and these are all the other words of the Torah. Thus, the entire Torah is drawn after the attributes, and the attributes after the Names, and the holy Names are all dependent on the Name Y-H-W-H. All are joined together, so the entire Torah is woven upon the Name Y-H-W-H. Therefore, it is called 'The Torah of the Lord is perfect.'"

Just as His Name has no end or limit, so too the Torah has no end. We learned in the *Book of Formation* (*Sefer Yetzirah*): "Two stones build two houses, three build six, four build twenty-four, five build one hundred and twenty, six build seven hundred and twenty, seven build five thousand and forty houses. From here on, go and calculate what the mouth cannot speak, the eye cannot see, and the ear cannot hear." Behold, the Torah has 600,000 letters. At first, three letters like *Bar* <note>Son/Pure</note>, then three like *Bara* <note>Created</note>, then four like *Berash* <note>At the head of</note>, and so on until the end. Can the intellect grasp how this can be measured? Afterward, in the secret of rectification, permutation, speech, inclusion, and calculation—as in the book *Ma'ayan Chakhmah* <note>Spring of Wisdom</note> cited in the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moses Cordovero</note>, "Gate of Essence and Conduct," chapter four—see there. Then you will know and understand that even for a single letter, there is no end or limit to its permutations, or to rotating it through the 22 letters, and making every substitution according to the numerical value (*Gematria*) of the words, and combining and exchanging them. Through speech, inclusion, and calculation, a person can grasp that there is no end to the matter.

The whole reason is that the Torah is the imprint of God, who has no end or limit, and the world is the imprint of the Torah. As our Sages said: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world." See the beginning of *Genesis Rabbah* on the verse: "**I was near Him as a nursling [Amon]**." Do not read it as *Amon* [nursling] but as *Omman* [artisan/architect]. Know and understand that just as the construction of the upper world in the secret of Emanation—which are the letters Y-H from the Name, the secret of the Written and Oral Torah—corresponds to the secret of the letters of the Primordial Torah, which is the secret of Y-H. This is explained in the Zohar and the books of the Kabbalists: the letters are in Understanding (*Binah*), the vowel points are in Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), and the cantillation marks are in the Crown (*Keter*). Thus they provide wisdom. This extends and chains down the construction of the world, namely from the letters of the Torah in its place, the secret of the Name *Mah* <note>The Name YHWH with a numerical value of 45</note>.

For this reason, you find in the Torah large and small letters. For example, the letter *Heh* in the word "when they were created" <note>Genesis 2:4 - *be-hibbare'am*</note> is small, and the letter *Heh* in "Do you thus requite the Lord?" <note>Deuteronomy 32:6 - *Ha-la-Y-H-W-H*</note> is large. It is the same with all other letters; I have not come here to list them all. This certainly points to the high status of the world; just as a builder of a tower sometimes needs large stones and sometimes small ones to build the structures, so it is with this matter: the life of the worlds, the expansion of the sparks of the Torah. This is the secret of "I was an artisan (*Amon*) near Him."

I have already written: the Essential Name is the Name of Being (*Havayah*), which indicates the primordial and eternal existence that brings all existence into being. Behold, the Name *Ehyeh* <note>I Shall Be</note> is also in the language of being, and it also equals the numerical value of 21 <note>A-H-Y-H: 1+5+10+5 = 21</note>. The letters of the Name of Being also equal 21, but its essence is from the perspective of the letters Y-H-D <note>a variant spelling</note> emerging into existence. For the Name *Ehyeh* exists when the flow of being comes from His very life-force. *Ehyeh* is the foundation of the construction, and the Name *Elohim* is the construction itself. This is the secret of "In the beginning, God (*Elohim*) created"—like the letters which are the foundation of being, and the Torah, and the construction. This is the secret of "I was near Him as a nursling," and the end of the word "And I was" <note>original: "ואהיה"</note> is the letter *Vav*. For up to the *Vav* is the secret of the letters of the Name Y-H-W-H, like this: 1, 2, 3, 4 equals 10; then 5; then 6; the numerical value rises to 7, 6, as the number of...

<meta>The previous page concluded a mystical exploration of the Torah as a primordial light and the blueprint for creation. This page shifts toward the practical and ethical dimensions of Torah study, detailing behaviors that affect memory, the structure of public sermons, and the Kabbalistic significance of the holiday of Shavuot.</meta>

->**Tractate Shevuot**<-

As they went on, walking and talking, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared <note>2 Kings 2:11</note>. The reason [they were protected] was because there was speech; if there were no speech, they would have been worthy of being burned. Therefore, a person should never cease from reflecting on words of Torah, so as to fulfill that which is written: "When you walk, it shall lead you" <note>Proverbs 6:22</note>. One should study by heart what he is able, or engage with certain Psalms or sayings to explain them, and many such things. Only, one must not let his thoughts cease from reflecting on the Torah; these constitute the refinement of good deeds and similar matters.

**A person** must be careful of things that cause one to forget his learning, as stated in Tractate Horayot, in the chapter "The Anointed Priest" <note>Horayot 13b</note>. Our Rabbis taught: Five things cause one to forget his learning: eating from what a mouse has eaten, or from what a cat has eaten, eating the heart of an animal—and the Maharal <note>Rabbi Judah Loew of Prague, 16th-century scholar</note> of blessed memory would refrain even from the heart of a bird, as mentioned in the *Tashbetz* <note>A work of Responsa by Rabbi Shimon ben Tzemach Duran</note> in sign 561—regularly eating olives, drinking the leftovers of wash water, or washing one’s feet one on top of the other. And some say: even one who places his garments under his headrest. Five things restore one's learning: eating wheat bread and certainly wheat itself, eating a soft-boiled egg without salt, regularly using olive oil, regularly using wine and spices, and drinking water from the leftovers of dough. And some say: even one who dips his finger in salt water and eats. And some say: even one who places his garments under his headrest <note>The text notes this action is cited for both forgetting and remembering; traditional commentators suggest different contexts for each</note>. For Rabbi Yochanan said: Just as an olive causes one to forget seventy years of learning, so does olive oil restore seventy years of learning. Being regular with wine and spices supports the heart, as it is said: "Wine and fragrances make one wise." Regarding dipping one's finger in salt, they mentioned Resh Lakish, and in one instance it is like a dispute among the Tannaim <note>Sages of the Mishnaic period</note>: Rabbi Judah says one finger and not two, while Rabbi Yose says two and not three. Ten things are hard for learning: passing under a camel and certainly under the camel itself, passing between two camels, passing between two women, a woman passing between two men, passing under a bridge under which water has not flowed for forty days, eating bread that is not fully baked, and eating "dirty meat" from a *listron*—the explanation of this is the spoon used to stir the pot, called "filth of the *listra*" because it moves the scum to both sides. Also: regularly eating two *smordim* <note>Likely a type of small fish or herb</note>, drinking from a water channel that passes through a graveyard, and looking at the face of a corpse. Some say: also reading the script upon a grave. Scholars are careful with these matters; may [He] magnify the Torah and make it glorious.

**In the Yalkut** <note>Yalkut Shimoni, a medieval midrashic compilation</note> at the beginning of the portion *Vayakhel*: "And Moses assembled..." The masters of *Aggadah* <note>Non-legalistic homiletic teachings</note> say: From the beginning of the Torah until its end, there is no portion that begins with "And he assembled" except this one. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Make for yourself large assemblies and deliver sermons before them in public regarding the laws of Shabbat, so that future generations may learn from you to gather assemblies every single Shabbat, and to enter the houses of study to teach and instruct Israel in words of Torah—what is forbidden and what is permitted—so that My great Name may be praised among My children." From here they said: Moses instituted for Israel that they should preach on the subject of the day—the laws of Passover on Passover, the laws of Shavuot on Shavuot, and the laws of Sukkot on Sukkot. Moses said to Israel: "If you act according to this order, the Holy One, Blessed be He, considers it as if you have crowned Me in My world," as it says: "You are My witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God" <note>Isaiah 43:12</note>. And so David says: "I have preached righteousness in a great assembly" <note>Psalm 40:10</note>. What "good news" [righteousness] did Israel need in David’s day? For were not all the days of David like a reflection of the Messiah? Rather, he would open and preach before them words of Torah that the ear had never heard before. However, the preacher of the sermon <note>The text reads "Resha," likely a scribe's error for "Darshan" (preacher) or "Drash" (sermon)</note> must ensure he preaches for the sake of Heaven, to be meritorious and to bring merit to the masses. Every sermon should be divided into three parts: The first part: good words of plain meaning (*Pshat*), like the choice fruit of the commentators, saying them in their name and adding according to his own good intellect. The second part: he should state the laws (*Dinim*) to teach the masses, especially those who are not scholars, and specifically the necessary laws such as the daily order, laws of Tzitzit and Tefillin, the blessing over bread, the laws of Shabbat, and household conduct such as the laws of marriage and intimacy, and many such things. The third part: words of ethics (*Musar*) to rebuke the hearts, from *Reishit Chokhmah* <note>"The Beginning of Wisdom," a 16th-century ethical-Kabbalistic work</note> and many similar works. In all the ethics he preaches, he should ensure he fulfills "correct yourself first and then correct others." Finally, he should provide the best of it. Rabbi Meir was a master of parables; he would preach parables such as the Fox Fables mentioned in Tractate Sanhedrin. When he delivered a sermon, a third was legal tradition (*Shematta*), a third was homily (*Agadata*), and a third was parables. Certainly, these parables were to teach the ways of ethics. Thus, the three aforementioned parts are explained: *Shematta* are the laws, *Agadata* are the sweet plain meanings, and *Mashli* are the ethics. "And a threefold cord is not quickly broken" <note>Ecclesiastes 4:12</note>.

## The Chapter "The Lamp of the Commandment" is Completed

<margin>
And in this way one understands the 613 [commandments]... that they explained forty-nine facets for ritual purity, and in another place they said seventy facets to the Torah, and in another place they said that upon every "thorn" [stroke of a letter] there are mounds upon mounds of laws. Even though there is a reason, it can be settled: what they said about "seventy facets to the Torah" refers to the "face" of the Torah that extends downward from the Sephirah of Malchut <note>Kingship/Kingdom, the final emanation</note>... and the forty-nine gates of the heart are few in the eyes of God... forty-nine facets, meaning forty-nine reasons and structures. And that which is said "upon every thorn," etc., they are the collective, adding much from a single verse or a single word...

**The Chapter** "The Torah is Light": The secret of the holiday of Shavuot, the holiday that includes the seven weeks which are forty-nine days. The holiday itself is the fiftieth day, hinting at the Fiftieth Gate of the Gates of Understanding (*Binah*). This includes the forty-nine gates from which come the forty-nine facets [of interpretation], as explained above regarding the secret of the counting [of the Omer]. This is the first letter *He* [of the Divine Name] which returns... and reveals the secret of the letter *Yod*... and five times *Yod* equals fifty. In this place, it is said "forty-nine facets of purity" corresponding to the forty-nine gates of Understanding. And this is the secret of the "Staff (*Matteh*) of Moses," for he returned the forty-nine (*Mem-Tet*) gates into Understanding (*Binah*), which is the first *He*. When *Mem-Tet* (49) is joined with *He* (5), the Staff is elevated. Of him it is said: "You have made him a little less than God" <note>Psalm 8:6</note>, meaning that one letter is the "little" that is missing from the name *Elohim* [God], which is the *Aleph*... and one gate remained, for this gate touches and equals the secret of the Hidden Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), which is the Primordial Torah... but there remains an "eye" (*Ayin*) in the word "little" (*Me'at*)... forty-nine facets... "Seventy facets to the Torah" are revealed in the secret of the revelation of the Torah in the World of *Atzilut* <note>Emanation, the highest of the four worlds</note>. For the Primordial Torah, which is the secret of Wisdom revealed slightly in Understanding, is the secret of the letters *Yod-Chet* (thought), while corresponding to them in *Atzilut* is the secret of *Vav-Chet*... the secret of *Tiferet* and *Malchut* which include the whole construction. *Tiferet* is the secret of the Written Torah... and *Malchut* is the secret of the Oral Torah which reveals and explains the Written Torah. It is said: "From the heavens He let you hear His voice, and upon the earth He showed you His great fire" <note>Deuteronomy 4:36</note>. "The heavens" is *Tiferet*, the secret of the Voice, for it is the voice that emerges from the Shofar, and the voice of the Shofar is very strong. "The earth" is the Supernal Earth... and there the fire is the Oral Torah, the secret of sharp dialectic (*Pilpul*). These include the flow of the Sephirot of the "Construction," and every Sephirah is comprised of all ten Sephirot, totaling seventy facets. These seventy facets are like branches to the fifty facets... the hidden things belong to the Lord our God, and the revealed things to us and our children. The "hidden things" are the letters *Yod-He* and the "revealed things" are the letters *Vav-He*. This matter will be explained further at length. Even though there are seventy facets in the collective sense, nevertheless, this collective is also included [in further levels], until the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), as explained in the *Pardes*. Regarding this, they said: "Upon every thorn, mounds upon mounds," without measure or limit, for there are "faces within faces." To this, the hint was: "Face to face the Lord spoke with you" <note>Deuteronomy 5:4</note>... and in this matter I found in the book *Etz Chaim* <note>"The Tree of Life," the primary text of Lurianic Kabbalah</note>... that the entire Torah is from the "Twenty-Eight" of *Bereshit* <note>The 28 letters of the first verse of Genesis</note>...

<meta>The previous page discussed practical ways to preserve one's memory of Torah study and avoid forgetfulness. This page moves into a deeper philosophical and mystical discussion regarding the balance between spiritual devotion and physical enjoyment on Jewish festivals, specifically focusing on a famous narrative involving Rabbi Eliezer and his students during a holiday sermon.</meta>

->**Tractate Shevuot**<-

One must be careful to fulfill the requirement of "all for you" <note>This refers to the Talmudic debate in Pesachim 68b: should a festival be spent "all for God" (in prayer and study) or "all for you" (in eating and drinking)?</note>. It should not be said that Rabbi Eliezer was angry because the students intended to spend the whole day on themselves, for if that were their intention, they should have left even earlier while it was still dark. This is not the case. The meaning of "all for God" does not literally mean every single second, just as "all for you" does not mean eating from morning until evening, as one must still pray the Morning and Evening services. Rather, it is a matter of proportion, as explained in the *Tosafot* <note>Medieval commentaries on the Talmud</note>. There it is written: "Either one eats and drinks, or one sits and studies." Even though Rabbi Eliezer told his students earlier to "eat fatty foods and drink sweet drinks" <note>Nehemiah 8:10</note> because of the joy of the festival, it was because on other days they would also eat after the sermon.

Furthermore, we must ask: if the students believed they were the ones being rebuked for leaving late, why didn't the Rabbi stop his sermon earlier? And why would the students be lazy if they were in such awe of him? Additionally, according to their understanding that he was angry at those who left late, why did he react oppositely to the sixth group, calling them "owners of a curse"? Rashi <note>The primary 11th-century commentator</note> explains that the study hall was very far away, and leaving so late was disgraceful in the Rabbi's eyes. Rashi notes that the students' faces changed because they thought he was angry at the sixth group for staying too long, and they worried, "How much more so is he angry at us who stayed even longer!" But this is difficult: why call them "owners of a curse"? This implies they were acting lawlessly or gluttonously.

However, we find in the Talmud that their primary conduct was compared to "one who brings a jug of wine from place to place." The wording "It is not to you that I speak" implies "I am not angry at you." He did not say anything that should have made them worry; when he said "owners of a curse," he was referring to those who were emptying the study hall, but the students themselves were still showing honor to the place. It seems the matter is best explained as follows: regarding the first groups who left early, he was not angry at them because he thought they were choosing the path of "all for you," and it is acceptable to not spend the whole day in study. He calmly called them "owners of a fine meal" <note>original: *pamtein*</note> or "owners of a barrel," acknowledging their choice.

But when the last group began to leave, after a large part of the day had passed—perhaps even past the usual mealtime—Rabbi Eliezer thought this group was not choosing "all for you" but "all for God." He assumed that even though they were leaving the study hall, they intended to study at home. He became angry and called them "owners of a curse" because they were emptying the public study hall. The students, however, misunderstood; they thought he was angry because the choice between "all for God" and "all for you" depends on the desire of the teacher. They thought Rabbi Eliezer believed it impossible for a large group of students not to desire the physical pleasure of "all for you," for while a single individual like Rabbi Eliezer might despise the pleasure of eating in favor of the joy of Torah, surely a large crowd has physical cravings.

When Rabbi Eliezer saw their distress, he said, "I am not saying this to you." This phrase has a double meaning. He revealed he wasn't angry at them, but also hinted at why: "I am saying this *for* you," referring to the specific requirement of the Shavuot festival <note>The Feast of Weeks/Pentecost</note> that it must be "for you." Even though usually one can choose "all for God," on Shavuot, one must include physical rejoicing. I am not saying you *must* choose the "better" part of "all for God." While one who chooses "all for God" is praiseworthy, and "according to the pain is the reward," legally one may choose either path. 

On the holiday of Shavuot, Rabbi Eliezer agrees that we require the "for you" element. This is also true of the Sabbath, in honor of the Torah which was given on the Sabbath. He says we need "half for God and half for you." The main point is that even though it is a commandment to rejoice and drink, the "for you" should also be "for God"—the physical joy should be a spiritual joy. This is the secret of the festivals of Passover and Sukkot, which commemorate the physical and spiritual Exodus from Egypt. Physical redemption is literal, and spiritual redemption is perfection through Torah. Rabbi Joshua holds one must fulfill both. But Shavuot hints at the "Great Jubilee" of the World to Come. As I explained in the introduction to *Toldot Adam* <note>A work by the author's circle or a referenced text</note>, eternal perfection involves both body and soul. Though some say the World to Come is for the soul alone, the sages of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note> agree that after the Resurrection, the body will be refined and become pure light, like the soul. This is the secret of "also for you"—the body's joy becomes entirely "for God."

<column-break/>

-> **The Mystery of the Name** <-

The Name Y-H-V-H <note>The Tetragrammaton, God's four-letter name</note> represents all existence and reality in the worlds of Creation, Formation, and Action. The purpose of all that exists is Man, who was made in the "image and likeness," the secret of the "Upper Man" in the sphere of *Tiferet* <note>The Kabbalistic sefirah of Beauty/Harmony</note>. God created, formed, and made him for His glory, as it is written: "Everyone called by My name, I created for My glory, I formed him, even I made him" <note>Isaiah 43:7</note>. The lower man is a "small world" mirroring the Upper Man who sits upon the Throne. This is hinted at in the verse "to work it and to keep it" <note>Genesis 2:15</note>. These are the two aspects of action and study: "to work" is the performance of commandments, and "to keep" is the study of Torah. As Rashi explains on the verse "You shall keep and you shall do": "keeping" refers to the study of Mishnah, and "doing" is literal. This is all for His glory, for the service of deed and contemplation is a "high need," not just a human one. Through this, one rectifies the Name and brings unity to the letters Y-H and V-H. Be careful to "do them," for as the Zohar says: whoever performs the commandments of the Torah and walks in its paths, it is as if he "made" the One Above <note>An audacious Kabbalistic idea that human action "completes" or "actualizes" the divine presence in the lower worlds</note>. This is why it says "and you shall make *them*" (the commandments)—it is as if you are making the Holy Name. This is what is meant by "And David made a name" <note>2 Samuel 8:13</note>; because he walked in the paths of Torah, it was as if he "made" the Name above. This is a great and noble concept discussed elsewhere at length.

**D**o not mistake the plain meaning of the holiday to say that there is no "for you" purpose. For it is certainly so, a hint to the word of God. Since the Sages said "and half for you," the numerical value <note>Gematria</note> of the word "Lachem" (for you) hints that Israel will merit His light. May it be His will that the "S-M" and "T-M" <note>Possibly abbreviations for spiritual impurities or specific forces</note> be nullified through the half-word of "Lachem," directing us toward the other world.

**A**nd do not mistake the festival of Shavuot to think there is no "for you" purpose. For it is certainly so, a hint to the word of God. Since the Sages said "and half for you," the numerical value hints that Israel will merit His light. May it be His will that the "S-M" and "T-M" be nullified through the half-word of "Lachem," directing us toward the other world.

# Tractate Shevuot

The letters of the Torah are related to the verse: "Then I was beside Him as a confidant [*Amon*]" <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. The Sages taught: Do not read it as *Amon* (confidant), but as *Oman* (artisan/blueprint) <note>Midrash Bereshit Rabbah 1:1; this suggests God used the Torah as a blueprint to build the world</note>. Now, you might ask: Did not our Sages, of blessed memory, say regarding the verse "For in Yah, the Lord, is an everlasting rock" <note>Isaiah 26:4</note> that the World to Come was created with the letter *Yod* and this world with the letter *Heh*? If so, how can we say the world was created with the twenty-four <note>original: כ"ד; likely referring to the twenty-two letters plus the two forms of certain letters, or a specific grouping</note> letters of the Torah? The answer is that these letters are included within the mystical secret of the Name *Yah* [Yod-Heh] through the system of Gematria <note>Hebrew numerology</note>, whether in units, tens, or hundreds. This is the "Alphabet of *Adam Kadmon*" <note>The "Primordial Man," a high level of divine emanation in Kabbalah</note> arranged in columns:

<columns>2</columns>
"And I was beside Him as a confidant." I have already written in the additions regarding the letter *Vav* on the letters that indicate the Name of the Lord [Y-H-V-H]. Behold, when you combine the Name *Y-H-V-H* and the Name *E-H-Y-H* <note>The Name "I Am That I Am" from Exodus 3:14</note> like this: *A-D-Y-H-V-H*, twenty-six letters emerge. The letters *Y-H-V* ascend to this place. This Name is the inner essence of the "Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom" <note>The 32 paths mentioned in the *Sefer Yetzirah* (Book of Creation), consisting of the 10 Sephirot and 22 letters</note>. And the verse says: "The mentioners of the Name..."

***

In the Beginning [*Bereshit*]: The Jerusalem Targum <note>An ancient Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Torah</note> translates this as "With wisdom." This accords with the verse: "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth" <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>. The general principle is that the world and the Torah are one. This is why when a person innovates a Torah insight, they create "new worlds." As it is seen in the Zohar <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>, Portion *Bereshit*, page 4: "He opened and said: 'I have placed My words in your mouth' [Isaiah 51:16]. How much must a man labor in the Torah day and night! For the Holy One, blessed be He, listens to the voices of those who occupy themselves with Torah. With every new word of Torah produced by one who labors in it, He creates a new firmament."

We have learned that at the moment a word of Torah is innovated from a person's mouth, that word ascends and is crowned before the Holy One, blessed be He. He takes that word, kisses it, and crowns it with seventy engraved and carved crowns. A word of wisdom that is innovated ascends and sits upon the head of the "Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds" <note>A Kabbalistic term for the Sephirah of *Yesod*</note>, and it spreads through seventy thousand worlds. It then ascends to the "Ancient of Days" <note>*Atik Yomin* - the highest, most ancient level of Divinity</note>. All the words of the Ancient of Days are words of hidden wisdom. When this word of wisdom ascends, it joins the words of the Ancient of Days and descends to become a "new firmament." Those hidden things which "no eye has seen but Yours, O God" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note> emerge from there. All the hidden letters of the Ancient of Days ascend and are crowned before Him. At that moment, the Ancient of Days smells the fragrance of that word, and it is more pleasing to Him than anything. He takes that word and crowns it with one hundred and seventy thousand crowns. Thus, every single word of wisdom creates a lasting firmament. These are called "New Heavens"—heavens renewed by the innovations of supreme wisdom. And all other words of Torah that are innovated before the Holy One, blessed be He, ascend and become "lands of the living."

Thus, the worlds that the Holy One, blessed be He, created were through the medium of the Torah. This is the meaning of "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made... and all their host by the breath of His mouth" <note>Psalm 33:6</note>. It is possible that the letter *Resh* hints at the Torah, which is called "Heavens," and "Breath" refers to the Oral Torah. Their "Host" refers to the people of Moses, the earth, and all that is upon it—all of them are the host of the heavens.

**And by this**, we can explain a statement in the Midrash <note>Homiletic teachings</note> regarding the "twenty-four thousand columns" in the section on the "Flying Scroll" <note>Zechariah 5:1</note>. Manoah the Righteous said: "Is it forever?" One out of three thousand two hundred... in the Oral Torah. Another statement appears in the chapter "One may make partitions" [Tractate Eruvin 21a]: Rav Hamnuna said, what is the meaning of the verse, "And he [Solomon] spoke three thousand proverbs" [1 Kings 5:12]? This teaches that Solomon said three thousand proverbs for every single word of Torah, and for every single plain meaning of wisdom, there were three thousand proverbs. The "two hundred" mentioned there refers to the verse "A thousand for you, Solomon, and two hundred for the guardians of its fruit" <note>Song of Songs 8:12</note>.

It can be said that these three thousand correspond to the two thousand years that the Torah preceded the world, which are revealed to the sages of Israel, each according to their level of attainment, while the third thousand is hidden. Perhaps they correspond to the three parts of study: one-third Scripture, one-third Mishnah, and one-third Talmud. The third, hidden thousand was revealed only to Moses and later to Solomon, who was "wiser than all men." The Sages taught: "No prophet arose like Moses," but among kings, none arose like Solomon. Therefore, "the thousand is for you, Solomon"—specifically for you. In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will reveal an additional "fifth," which is the "two hundred for the guardians of its fruit."

The three thousand are the trunk and body of the tree. The "fruit" is the hidden essence of the Torah, the impression of Divinity and life. In every world, the Name *Y-H-V* brings all existences into being. This is the secret of the spiritual "Face of the Torah."

Everyone agrees that the Torah was given on Shabbat <note>The Sabbath</note>, as stated in the chapter of Rabbi Akiva <note>Tractate Shabbat 86b</note>. Shabbat indicates the renewal of the world, and the renewal of the world indicates the existence of God. Through the Torah, we cleave to the Name *Y-H-V-H*. This is why the Sabbath before Passover is called "The Great Sabbath" [*Shabbat HaGadol*], for "the end of the action was first in thought." The beginning of Israel's strength began on that Sabbath before Passover when they were commanded to take the lamb <note>The Paschal offering</note> and enter into the Name of the Lord.

On Shavuot, after the forty-nine days of the Counting of the Omer, it also hints at a "Sabbath that is entirely Sabbath," the secret of the Jubilee [*Yovel*] after the Sabbatical cycles. Then the reward will be eternal—the reward for Torah and deeds. This is the essence of the "Great Sabbath." Three Sabbaths are hinted at together: the Sabbath of Creation (the renewal of nature), the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah (the purpose of creation), and the Sabbath of the Jubilee (the great reward/freedom). Therefore, we are obligated to rejoice greatly on this holiday with spiritual joy. For as the Talmud says in Tractate Pesachim and Tractate Beitzah: "If not for this day [of the giving of the Torah], how many 'Josephs' would there be in the market?" <note>Meaning: without the Torah, I would be just an ordinary person</note>. What would our lives and our purpose be?

In Tractate Pesachim and Beitzah, it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says a person has nothing for a festival day except *either* eating and drinking *or* sitting and studying. Rabbi Joshua says: Divide it—half for eating and drinking, and half for the House of Study. Rabbi Yohanan said: Both derived their views from the same verses. One verse says "A solemn assembly [Atzeret] for the Lord your God" [Deuteronomy 16:8], and another says "It shall be a solemn assembly for you" [Numbers 29:35]. Rabbi Eliezer thinks it is *either* all for God *or* all for you. Rabbi Joshua thinks we should divide it.

However, Rabbi Eleazar said: "All agree regarding the festival of *Atzeret* [Shavuot] that we also require 'for you' [physical enjoyment]." Why? Because it is the day the Torah was given. The text tells a story of Rabbi Eliezer, who sat and lectured all day long on the laws of the holiday. The first group of students left, and he said: "These are owners of barrels" <note>Meaning they are rushing to their wine barrels</note>. A second group left, and he said: "These are owners of jugs." A third: "Owners of pitchers." A fourth: "Owners of flasks." A fifth: "Owners of cups." When a sixth group began to leave, he said: "These are owners of a curse!" He looked at his remaining disciples and saw their faces changing color (in fear). He said to them: "My sons, I am not speaking to you, but to those who left, who abandon eternal life and occupy themselves with temporary life." At the time of their departure, he said to them: "Go, eat fatty foods and drink sweet drinks... for the day is holy to our Lord; do not be sad, for the joy of the Lord is your strength" <note>Nehemiah 8:10</note>. It is difficult to understand: why was Rabbi Eliezer angry at the groups who hurried to leave? Did he not say himself that one has the choice to make it "all for you"? Perhaps they were...

# Tractate Shevuot

The status of a righteous person [*Tzaddik*] or a penitent [*Baal Teshuva*] <note>original: ב' ת'</note> who touches the Throne of Glory; and how this stands against the status of study [*Talmud*] and action [*Ma'aseh*] which touch the Name of the Blessed One. On this matter, the Tosafot <note>Medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> permit "death" <note>likely referring to the legal concept of self-sacrifice or spiritual transition</note>. Why were they counted in this specific order?

Look closely: I will now explain if the word "lifting" [*Se'et*] <note>Genesis 4:7: "If you do well, will you not be lifted up?"</note> refers to the spiritual flow [*Shefa*]. Why was this separated? It was because the "garment of skin" was originally a "garment of light" <note>A common mystical teaching that before the Fall, Adam wore garments of light (*Or* with an Aleph), which became skin (*Or* with an Ayin) after the sin</note>, and this is what the Sages meant regarding the side of the Serpent. It is explained in the Zohar that the light was clothed in "intentions" [*Kavanot*]. Furthermore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Cain: "If you do well, you shall be lifted up," or rather, you will have a great elevation and an advantage of light coming from the power of the darkness that was overcome, as explained at length in the introduction to the book *Toldot Adam*. 

And if "lifting" is not connected to what is above, the explanation is as follows: "Is it not that you have the choice?" If you want, you can improve the "vessels of light" <note>original: כחנות אור</note>, using the language "when he cleans [*Heitiv*] the lamps" <note>Exodus 30:7</note>. Then you will be like that "good" [*Ki Tov*] which filled the house with light, as in "He saw the light, that it was good." But if you do not "lift," then "when a man has a swelling [*Se'et*] on the skin of his flesh" <note>Leviticus 13:2, referring to leprosy</note>—then the understanding of choice is on your part: skin [*Or*] or light [*Or*]. But light is superior to skin. There is no definitive ruling here, and therefore the Torah wrote it this way so we would interpret both meanings, for both are true regarding the "spiritually ascended" who were masters over the garments of light before the sin. However, for the rest of humanity, it would have been better had Adam remained in garments of light, for the responsibility of the "ruin" is very great—whether one will prevail or not. Even if a distinction remains between one type of repair [*Tikkun*] and another, just as we find a distinction in repentance [*Teshuva*] between that done out of love and that done out of fear. All this was discussed at length above in the aforementioned introduction.

Second: the "almond-shaped" [*Meshukadim*] <note>Refers to the design of the Menorah in Exodus 25:33</note> corresponds to the world of the spheres and the constellations. The Aramaic translation of *Meshukadim* is "depicted" or "carved," and so Rashi explains. These depictions are the sparks of the spheres. The influence of the "four cups" alludes to the nations of the world, and your sign for this is: "The cups of those who practice divination" <note>original: הנביעי' בן מנחשים; a wordplay on cups and divination</note>. There are four, as stated in the Jerusalem Talmud, Chapter "Four Cups" <note>Tractate Pesachim</note>: The Rabbis say they correspond to the four cups of punishment that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will eventually give the nations of the world to drink, as it says: "For thus said the Lord, the God of Israel, to me: Take this cup of the wine of fury..." <note>Jeremiah 25:15</note>; and "A golden cup in the hand of the Lord"; and "For a cup is in the hand of the Lord, and the wine foams... for the wicked, fire and brimstone and a burning wind shall be the portion of their cup" <note>Psalms 11:6</note>. Behold, the Lord apportioned the host of the heavens to the nations. The Aramaic translation of "cups" [*Gevia'im*] is "vessels" [*Kalayin*]. As it is found in the language of the Talmud: "Look at the stars." 

But the "knob" and the "flower" represent Israel, as it is written: "Israel shall bud and blossom" <note>Isaiah 27:6</note>. The "knob" [*Kaftor*] is round, like the seating of the Sanhedrin <note>The high court</note>, which was like a circular half-threshing floor. In Midrash Rabbah, it says that when Rabbi Tarfon saw a certain light from the Breastplate, he exclaimed: "A knob and a flower!"

The Menorah, with its seven lamps, corresponds to the seven wandering stars <note>The planets</note>, as found in Midrash Tanchuma, portion *Beha'alotcha*: "These seven are the eyes of the Lord, which range through the whole earth" <note>Zechariah 4:10</note>. What are these seven? They are the seven lamps corresponding to the seven stars that serve the whole earth. When we apply the term "almond-shaped" to the four cups, the intention is specifically that the nations have a "lot" [*Pol*], but not Israel. But when we apply "almond-shaped" to the "knob and flower," it implies that Israel also has a "lot." Both are true, for at one time, the Israelite needs a "lot," but later, when he transmigrates a second time, the Holy One, Blessed be He, guides him according to his deeds, as a system according to what is fitting for him. This is the secret of the "second match" which is "according to one's deeds." This matter is explained at length in the book *Rav Peninim*.

## The Third Matter

Regarding the "World of the Garment," the righteous person [*Tzaddik*] is alluded to by the angels. Behold, Esau stands outside, for the angel came with his strength, and Jacob the Righteous fought with him: "He strove with an angel and prevailed" <note>Hosea 12:5</note>. Nevertheless, "He touched the hollow of his thigh." Some say the "hollow of his thigh" refers to anger. Behold, there are two sides to this: the "striving" mentioned above suggests the level of the angel is superior, but through the separation of the righteous—which becomes a crown for the head of the Holy One, Blessed be He—by this merit, the righteous person is superior. As our Sages said in Tractate Chulin: "The ministering angels do not sing praise above until Israel sings below." As it is written: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place." This refers to the inner chamber and the gathering. And this is why it says: "Let me go, for the dawn has broken" <note>Genesis 32:26</note>. At that point, we say the level of the righteous person is superior at all times... and therefore he relied on starting the day with war. Nevertheless, the next day he prayed because it was a public fast, as it is written: "The adversary who distressed and afflicted them," for "salvation belongs to the Lord." 

If we read "sprout" [*Tzemach*] in the context of the battle with Amalek, it is written: "And I will stand on the top of the hill" <note>Exodus 17:9</note>, and he prayed to "establish" through prayer, implying your God, thus the level of the angel is superior. But if we read "pure" [*Tzach*] in the context of the war with Amalek immediately, then I will pray, proving the opposite. Both are true: for the body of the angel is superior to the body of the righteous, but the inner essence of the righteous is superior to the inner essence of the angel, as explained in the *Pardes* in the section on "Action."

Regarding the "World of the Throne," the division is whether the light of the righteous is superior <margin>103, Chapter 60</margin>

->The root of the light according to Rashi and Tosafot is superior, for even "Cursed" is like "Ox" and "Atone"<-

<columns>2</columns>
It is known that the "Shell" [*Kelipah*] of service is like a serpent wound around his days. This is the secret of "Cursed" [*Arur*] versus "Ox" [*Shor*]. Do not stir up love from my mouth. The "Holy One" is superior because he is gripped by the Shell, even though he enters holiness... For "happy is he who saw and did not sin," or "one who does not return to being cursed." On the contrary, they called the "Ox" a term of excellence, as in "much increase comes by the strength of the ox" <note>Proverbs 14:4</note>. 
Behold, there is a difference between one type of repentance and another—namely, repentance from fear. Alternatively, regarding the dispute of Maimonides [*Rambam*] in his "Eight Chapters," where he distinguishes between rational commandments and heard [*revealed*] commandments. See there at length.
