This is why we find twice in the Talmud: "Moses, you have spoken well!" <note>A common Talmudic expression of approval</note>—this comes from the spark of Moses our Teacher that has spread. The aforementioned hint is "Wayward" <note>original: שובב</note>, for though you are wayward, you have a stature among the 600,000 in every generation. 

If this refers to the spiritual flow that indicates the superiority of the "heard" [*revealed*] commandments, the explanation of the verse follows what I heard regarding the portion of *Nitzavim*: "Lest there be among you a man or woman... who blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I shall have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart'" <note>Deuteronomy 29:18</note>. The matter is that such a person says: "Why do I need to fulfill the commandments in action? It is enough for me to contemplate and use my intellect to grasp the spirituality of the commandments and understand everything, for my heart has seen much wisdom." Regarding this "stubbornness of heart," it says the Lord will not be willing to forgive him. For "the secret things belong to the Lord our God" <note>Deuteronomy 29:28</note>—I do not fulfill my obligation through knowledge of the secrets, for there is no "secret" known to us, only to the Lord our God. Rather, the primary obligation placed upon us is "the revealed things," which means "to do all the words of this Torah" through the physical performance of positive commandments and the guarding of negative commandments. 

Similarly, this verse will be explained: "This people will rise up and go astray" <note>Deuteronomy 31:16</note>. This is a prayer. The matter is that we should contemplate "rising," which means to walk in the stubbornness of one's heart—that is, the investigation and engagement in the "secrets." To this, he returns to inform us that *Action* is superior. Yet both are true, for there is an aspect where Study is great, and an aspect where Action is superior. This was mentioned above in Chapter 54. There is a secret in this, and it will be explained shortly. 

Now their essence will be explained: Seventh, "Do not murder" corresponds to First, "I am the Lord your God." Man is made in the "Image of God," and it is written: "Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God He made man." This applies only in the heavens and to man on the earth, and above the earth, "and he watered the whole face of the ground." It is explained in the Zohar that through the arousal of man's actions below, a corresponding arousal occurs above, and from this, he draws down the spiritual flow from above to below; this is the meaning of "and he watered the whole face of the ground." 

It is possible that regarding the matter of Study and Action, I have already written precisely in Rashi's commentary and the Words of Torah: whether Study is greater or Action is greater, you will find that Action is great because it is the ultimate goal. So we have learned: "Anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom, his wisdom will endure." And so we learn from the verse: "The revealed things are for us and our children, to *do* all the words of this Torah." Thus, the essence of the Torah is the action. 

On this matter, they alluded to the excellence of Israel who prioritized "We will do" [*Na'aseh*] over "We will hear" [*Nishma*]. For "We will do" refers to action, and "We will hear" refers to the study—to hear and to learn. One might ask a great question: if Israel prioritized "doing" over "hearing" before they reached the ultimate attachment, when they ascended to the level of prophecy at the time of the giving of the Torah—why, when they reached the collective attachment, did they reverse it to "hearing" then "doing"? As it is written: "You go near and hear all that the Lord our God says... and we will hear and we will do" <note>Deuteronomy 5:24</note>. Now, the matter is turned toward today: to learn in order to receive a reward. The reward for a commandment is the commandment itself—that is, the enjoyment of the commandment. And the "hearing" and "doing" of the commandment is called "Action," while the "Spirituality" is called "Study." This is the matter of "We will do and we will hear" from his side. "And a mist went up from the earth"—in this world, which is the "World of Action," the arousal comes from below. Through the refinement of action into spirituality, the spiritual flow is drawn down. For through our actions, we repair His Great Name, as I wrote elsewhere regarding "And David made a name for himself." From the side of the Holy One, Blessed be He, the reward is prioritized; "We will hear" precedes "We will do," for He will open...

# Tractate Shevuot

## And the Nature
The service of the Unique Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-W-H</note> with the specific intention whose matters we have made known—to open the Source and to draw down the emanation of blessing from the "Head of Thought" <note>The highest realm of divine intellect</note> to its end. From there, the blessings spread to the lower beings who cause this through their service. The meaning is: the Name is blessed, and the one who performs the service is blessed as they draw the blessing down through their work. This is what the Prophet <note>Peace be upon him</note> hinted at by saying: "He who blesses himself in the earth shall bless himself by the God of Truth" <note>original: *Elohei Amen*; Isaiah 65:16</note>. He said that the cause of one being blessed on earth is that one was first blessed by the "God of Truth." For the one who serves with proper intention unifies the Name through its powers, and his own power gives strength and might to it, according to the secret of "Through God we shall do valiantly" <note>Psalm 60:14</note> and the secret of "Ascribe strength to God" <note>Psalm 68:35</note>. From that strength, power is given back to that servant, and all of this was explained above.

Thus, the purpose of creation is for Man to "work and to guard" <note>Genesis 2:15</note>, which refers to action and study for a "Higher Need." For kindness rises from the earth—meaning an awakening <note>original: *it'orerut*</note> rises from below to above. Then, "limb supports limb," so to speak, "eye for an eye and hand for hand" <note>interpreted here as a mystical correspondence between human actions and divine responses</note>. This is the meaning of a "Sacrifice to the Lord" <note>original: *Korban l'Y-H-W-H*</note>, as the letters of the Name Y-H-W-H are brought together in wondrous unity. This matter cannot be completed except through Man, who is the "beginning of thought and the end of action." Man was made in the image and likeness encompassing both the upper and lower worlds. Because free choice was given to Man, he might potentially corrupt the closeness. Therefore, the "remedy for the blow" was created: Repentance <note>original: *Teshuva*</note> was created before the world was created, as it is written: "Return... and the song of the Lord," for "He shows sinners the way" <note>Psalm 25:8</note. It is stated in the Midrash <note>Ancient rabbinic homilies</note> that the angels complained regarding prophecy, wisdom, and the Torah, and they did not receive an answer that was beneficial until the Holy One, Blessed be He, answered them Himself in His glory and provided Repentance. For "Good and upright is the Lord, therefore He shows sinners the way" <note>Psalm 25:8</note> so that they may be repaired. Then one returns from evil to good to awaken through good deeds from below to above. As it is said, "part of him is above," and through good deeds, he awakens the "Straight Light" from above to below. This is the meaning of "Good and upright is the Lord," etc. Since the Creator established the repair of the Name in His glory specifically through the "Complete Man" <note>a person of high spiritual integrity</note> who conducts himself with piety, the level of the "Complete Ones" is higher than the level of the angels. This topic was explained at length above, noting that their level is above the "host of heaven" and that "Israel has no constellation" <note>original: *Ein Mazal l'Yisrael*; meaning Israel is not bound by astrological fate</note>. Because Man was created for this purpose, "God made Man upright" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29</note> in "Garments of Light" <note>original: *Kotnot Or*, spelled with an *Aleph*</note>, as if he were worthy to be a living being forever. But through the corruption of sin, the verse was fulfilled: "You change his face and send him away" <note>Job 14:20</note>, and he was clothed in "Garments of Skin" <note>original: *Kotnot Or*, spelled with an *Ayin*</note>. He repaired them through death, and even during his lifetime, he needs much refinement until he is purified into a luminous being, turning evil to good. Then there will be an "advantage of light over darkness," and he will merit the "New Light" in the future—the Great Light—and he will be truly alive in an attachment <note>original: *devekut*</note> like the letters *Yod* and *Vav*. This is explained at length above.

## And When We Contemplate
In what I have written, there are five things corresponding to our Master <note>God</note>: 
1. Study and Action. 
2. The Righteous [*Tzaddikim*] and the Penitent [*Baalei Teshuva*]. 
3. The level of the Righteous versus the Angel. 
4. The matter of the constellations [*Mazalot*]. 
5. The "Garments of Light" and "Skin." 
And these five are the secret of the unfolding chain:

->1. Study and Action<-
Which the Blessed One brought into being—for which reason He is called Y-H-W-H, who was the true eternal vitality from which everything that exists comes into being. This touches upon the secret of the "Repair of His Name," the "Service for a Higher Need." 
2. The matter of Repentance touches the "World of the Throne," which is the "World of Creation" <note>Beriah</note>, as the Sages said: "Great is repentance, for it reaches the Throne of Glory." 
3. The level of the Righteous over the Angel concerns the "World of Angels," the "World of Formation" <note>Yetzirah</note>. 
4. The matter of the "host of heaven" <note>the stars/planets</note> which the Lord allotted to the nations, but from which He removed Israel to be under His direct providence. 
5. "The earth and all their host," and "Man was taken from the earth." There is a distinction if it is "holy ground" (the secret of Garments of Light) or if it is materiality and the "filth of the earth's sins."

## And in the Giving
Within the essence of the Name Y-H-W-H, all of this was revealed. 
1. "We will do and we will listen" <note>Exodus 24:7</note> is Action and Study, for "listening" is learning. 
2. The secret of Repentance, which reaches the Throne. We find this in the building <note>structure</note> that was above with the ministering angels, as seen in the story of Rabbi Akiva: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses, "Grasp the Throne and give them an answer." The secret is that the ministering angels prosecuted, saying, "What is man that You should remember him?" <note>Psalm 8:5</note>, for he is prone to ritual impurity and sin; how can the Torah be given to him? Through this Repentance: "Grasp the Throne and give them an answer," meaning tell the angels that there is hope for Man even if he sins, through the Repentance he will perform, for "Great is Repentance for it reaches the Throne." In this secret, the Messiah at the Throne overcomes the forces from below and above. 
3. The level of the Angel versus the Complete Man: "Holy chariots" came at the Stand at Mount Sinai, and there were 22,000 myriads of angels corresponding to the 22,000 banners of the Sanctuary and the Levites, as seen in the Midrash. The ministering angels served Israel with their crowns, and "the kings of hosts did flee, did flee" <note>Psalm 68:13</note>. As seen in the chapter of Rabbi Akiva, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired their elevation to nullify the "host of heaven" in the presence of Israel and to bring the Earth closer to Heaven. This hints at the "Garments of Light," and "the Earth shall be full of knowledge," and the verse "those who lead many to righteousness shall shine like the stars" will be fulfilled. For so it was with the First Man before he sinned: the skin of his heel outshone the sun's orb. So too did Israel return to a level higher than this at the receiving of the Torah—the Light of Secrets and the Crowns—except that after they sinned with the Golden Calf, "they were stripped of their ornaments" <note>Exodus 33:6</note> and returned to their previous state. About them it was said: "I said, you are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High; but like Man [*Adam*] you shall die" <note>Psalm 82:6-7</note>—meaning like the First Adam, from whom the Garments of Light were removed and replaced with skin. They became skin like the secret of "garments of plague" and so on. But Moses our Teacher remained with the "Radiance of Light" <note>original: *Karan Or*; Exodus 34:29</note> that he earned. 

Regarding these five aforementioned points, a hint appears in the Tablets, which were five opposite five. It is written, "Your two breasts are like two fawns" <note>Song of Songs 4:5</note>, and they said: "arranged in rows like lilies." Rashi <note>the premier medieval commentator</note> explains: "Your two breasts" refers to the Tablets, "twins of a gazelle," for both are of the same measure, five commandments on this one and five on that one. They correspond to each other: 
- "I am the Lord" <note>1st</note> corresponds to "Do not murder" <note>6th</note>, for the murderer diminishes the likeness of the Holy One, Blessed be He. 
- "You shall have no other gods" <note>2nd</note> corresponds to "Do not commit adultery" <note>7th</note>, for one who strays after idolatry is like a woman who commits adultery under her husband. 
- "Do not take the Name in vain" <note>3rd</note> corresponds to "Do not steal" <note>8th</note>, for one who steals will eventually swear falsely. 
- "Remember the Sabbath" <note>4th</note> corresponds to "Do not bear false witness" <note>9th</note>, for one who desecrates the Sabbath testifies falsely against the Creator, as if to say He did not rest during the six days of Creation. 
- "Honor your father and mother" <note>5th</note> corresponds to "Do not covet" <note>10th</note>, for one who covets [another's wife] will eventually father a son who dishonors him and honors one who is not his father. 
These are his words. One must understand what the practical difference is that they correspond five against five. In Tractate Yoma, in the chapter "They brought out to him," it is taught that Ben Yehuda says: "There are five verses in the Torah whose [grammatical] resolution is undecided..." <note>Original: *Se'et, Meshukkadim, Mahar, Arur, Vakam*; these are words that could belong to either the preceding or following phrase</note>. The Tosafot already questioned... why they were not counted... and they answered what they answered, leaving it as a difficulty... for they do not come out in the order they are written in the Torah. It should have said: *Se'et, Arur, Mahar, Meshukkadim, Vakam*.

## Five
Regarding these five aforementioned matters, we find disputes among the Sages: 
1. **Study and Action:** At the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin, when Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders were reclining, a dispute broke out among them whether Study is greater or Action is greater. 
2. **The Perfectly Righteous and the Penitent:** A dispute between Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Yochanan over which is superior. 
3. **The Perfectly Righteous and the Angels:** Maimonides and Ibn Ezra <note>12th-century philosophers</note> and their followers held that angels are superior, but according to what is found in the words of our Sages, the level of the Righteous is superior. This was explained at length above. 
4. **The Constellations of the Host of Heaven:** A dispute among the Sages of Israel whether "Israel has a constellation" or "Israel has no constellation," as mentioned in Tractate Shabbat, chapter "One who darkened." 
5. **Garments of Light and Skin:** There are inquiries into which is superior: would it have been better had the Garments of Light remained, or is it a "descending for the sake of ascending" that they became Garments of Skin so as to return to a "New Light," the "Hidden Light," the "Great Light"? This stems from the dispute between the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel: "Is it better for Man not to have been created than to have been created?" 

All these matters were mentioned at length above in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*. Truly, "both these and those are the words of the Living God" <note>A Talmudic phrase meaning both sides of a holy argument contain truth</note>. All their foundations are in different aspects. To this, a hint was given in these five verses that have no decided resolution—so that we may interpret them with what precedes them and what follows them. And as the Tosafot questioned... they are indeed interpreted both ways, and both are true in different aspects. These five follow the order of the "Chain of Descent" from below to above: 
- *Se'et* <note>Lifting/Elevation</note> corresponds to the physical/earthly part, whether it be Light or Skin. 
- *Meshukkadim* <note>Almond-shaped/Watchful</note> corresponds to whether there is a constellation or no constellation. 
- *Mahar* <note>Tomorrow</note> corresponds to the level of the Righteous or the Angel. 
- *Arur* <note>Cursed</note> corresponds to the level of...

# Tractate Shevuot

## The Nature of Divine Justice
Regarding the aspect of the soul and as explained: Might <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note> and Endurance <note>Hebrew: *Netzach*</note> are known. Might is the name *Elohim* <note>The name of God associated with Justice</note>, which is the depth of Justice in its truth and not a compromise to change the Attribute of Justice. Therefore, the name *Elohim* is numerically equivalent <note>term: *Gematria* (the calculation of the numerical value of Hebrew letters). Both *Elohim* (אלהים) and *HaTeva* (הטבע - "The Nature") equal 86</note> to "The Nature" <note>original: *HaTeva*</note>, as hinted in the Zohar. That is to say, according to the nature of the matter, from this there is existence and strength for the conduct of Nature, for there He set a law and a fixed decree that shall not be transgressed.

The attribute of Endurance <note>Hebrew: *Netzach*</note> is the attribute of the world's victory, as written in the *Pardes* <note>A seminal Kabbalistic work by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Entry of Appellations" under the entry for *Netzach*. So too wrote our teacher Menachem Recanati, that in this attribute, Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> and Merit victory over the Accusers. From this, one can easily understand the matter of "Nature" as it pertains to the constellations <note>original: *mazalot*</note>—that there is both "destiny" and "no destiny," and there is a deciding factor between them, for both are true in different respects, as I have explained.

### ->Endurance and Splendor<-

These are the "two thighs" of the [Divine] Body upon which the body stands. From this follows the matter of the "priestly garments of light" <note>original: *Ohr* with an *Aleph*</note> and "garments of skin" <note>original: *Or* with an *Ayin*</note>. We can easily understand that even though we made two divisions—the Righteous <note>Hebrew: *Tzaddik*</note> and the Penitent <note>Hebrew: *Ba'al Teshuvah*</note>—asking which is superior, and similarly regarding the garment of light or skin and its return to light: which is superior? These latter ones are drawn from the former. For if the Penitent is superior, then the aspect of the "garment of skin" <note>the physical/material</note> that transforms back into light is superior. The opposite is also true, and it all rises as one; these branch out from those. The "garments" of Kindness and Might are joined; the Righteous and the Penitent, and Endurance and Splendor <note>Hebrew: *Netzach* and *Hod*</note> are the branches of Kindness and Might, as is known. Therefore, they hinted to us in Endurance and Splendor the matter of the garments of light and skin, which are branches of the aspects of the Righteous and the Penitent. The factor that decides between them determines that both are true in different respects, as I have explained. All of this was hinted at in the secret of the Unity of Emanation, five against five, and the deciding factor rises and unifies and ties everything in a true unity, as written in the *Pardes*, first chapter of the first gate.

Similarly, when we contemplate how the "ways of the Lord" lead to one place—namely, the purpose for which Man was created, "to work it and to guard it" <note>Genesis 2:15</note>, which is the secret of Action and Study. For "guarding" refers to the Mishnah <note>The oral law</note>, as Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the premier medieval commentator</note> wrote on the verse "And you shall guard and you shall do"—guarding is the study of Mishnah. He preceded "working it" <note>action</note> in the sense of the declaration "We will do" before "We will hear" <note>The Israelites' response at Sinai</note>. Like a worker, man acts and repairs the Name, as I wrote above, for everything was created for His glory; this is the general principle that includes everything. From this branches out the matter of the excellence of Repentance <note>Hebrew: *Teshuvah*</note>, where man repairs himself and afterwards repairs the Higher Law even more. The higher repair specifically happens through Man, who is a blessing and an image encompassing the higher and lower worlds. Therefore, his excellence in his inner essence is greater than that of an angel... From this repentance is drawn the excellence of the "garments of skin" which return to being a great "light." The totality of all is the Service, the Action, which gives power to the Doer.

Therefore, He opened with "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage" <note>Exodus 20:2</note>, meaning so that we should be servants to Him, blessed be He. This is the complete service, the Action that precedes Hearing. Everything is for the "Higher Need," for "I am the Lord your God." This is the matter of all Ten Commandments being spoken in a single utterance. One might ask: what results from this and what is the practical difference? The Holy One, blessed be He, answered this: even though this is the action of God... let me give you a parable to contemplate: one person writes the Ten Commandments, one person reads them, and one person thinks them in his heart. Behold, the one who reads them does not take as long as the one who writes, for reading is done with speed. Similarly, the one who meditates on them does so in a tiny moment. The matter is that the more spiritual a thing is, the more it is unified and joined. Writing is physical, speaking is finer, and thought is more spiritual. Go and learn: the Holy One, blessed be He, replied that Speech [at Sinai] was spiritual, the ultimate spirituality in the Infinite <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*</note>; there, everything is unified as one matter.

This is explained through logic, but we can also find a reason for it: it is the very thing I spoke of, to show that all is included in the first utterance: "I am the Lord your God... from the house of bondage" to serve Him for His glory. The reward for the service is "I am the Lord your God" <note>the realization of God</note>. To hint at this, He opened the Ten Commandments with the letter *Aleph* <note>The first letter of *Anochi*</note> and ended with the letter *Kaf* <note>The final letter of the last word *le-re'ekha* (your neighbor)</note>.

I will further explain in another way the reason why all the commandments were said in one utterance: they are all an explanation of "I am the Lord your God." On the word *Anochi* <note>I</note>, one must ask: why in the whole Torah is it written "Ani" <note>I</note>, but here the language is *Anochi*? The answer that *Anochi* is an Egyptian word <note>A common Midrashic explanation</note> is not sufficient... But Israel, as our Sages of blessed memory said, were redeemed because they did not change their names... Rashi explains the verse where the Holy One, blessed be He, said "I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt" because they saw God at the Sea as a warrior, and now they see Him as an elder full of mercy. Lest you think, God forbid, that there are two powers, He said "I am the Lord your God who brought you out"—the same power that was at the Sea.

According to Rashi's way, the previous question is also answered: why say *Anochi* and not *Ani*? Because the spiritual letters, as written, "see the heard and hear the seen" <note>A Midrashic description of the Sinai experience</note>, and the letters were flying in the air. In the letters of *Ani* (אני), there is room for error when it is not vocalized, to read *Ani* as "not I" <note>changing the Aleph to an Ayin or misinterpreting the Yod/Vav</note>... Therefore He said *Anochi* (אנכי), where there is no room for error. He rooted in us the faith that even though one sees changes in the image—once as a master of war (acting in Judgment) and now as an elder full of mercy—it is all one unity. Regarding this He said "I am the Lord <note>The name of Mercy</note> your God <note>The name of Judgment</note>."

Behold, the name "Lord" is Mercy and "God" is Judgment. He said *Anochi*—for there is room to err, Heaven forbid, and think that Judgment is only Mercy when it is done at the Sea to save Israel. But the Judgment that occurs in the world which is "bad" and not merciful—there is room for the heretics to err and say: "He who does good does not do evil." But we believe with true faith, mentioning the attribute of Night during the Day and the attribute of Day during the Night <note>A reference to the liturgy acknowledging God as the creator of both light and darkness</note>. On this comes the warning afterward: "You shall have no other gods"—in no way in the world. For everything that happens in the world, whether good or bad, is from Him, and all is unified... and He said three times "Which" <note>Hebrew: *Asher*</note>: "Which is in the heavens above," "And which is on the earth beneath," and "And which is in the water." This is an example of the Higher Unity... so that we understand that their cause is hidden above, everything is One, Unique, and Unified.

<margin>
And why... as written "He hides His face and they are troubled"... and since we have written this... he was called to the evolution of the worlds... for there is no end to the kindness in the world of the Holy One, blessed be He...
</margin>

<column-break/>

Behold, I have written in any case the secret of *Shevuot* <note>Pentecost / The Feast of Weeks</note>, the secret of secrets... the spread of the teachings of the ancients... the seven secrets of holiness... the root that spreads... I wrote that the end of this is a hint that the Merciful One... as it is mentioned "Remember" <note>original: *Zakhor*</note>... the matter of its beginning being in its end and its end in its beginning. For the *Aleph* [1] is written and the Crown <note>Hebrew: *Keter*</note> is One. And "other gods" are not mentioned in this verse of "I am the Lord"... even though several reasons were said for this, I also wrote reasons and justifications... according to the "Garment" <note>a Kabbalistic term for the manifestation of light</note> to explain the evolution of the worlds, as I wrote above... against the worlds of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the World of the Intellect and the World of the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence</note> and the Angels... This is the name of the Lord... as Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai... "And the Torah of kindness is on her tongue"... who can say that the Truth is hidden from this? For they only said it regarding David, who [was like a] shepherd of five worlds and said a song... he said the song "Bless the Lord, O my soul" <note>Psalm 103</note>... "and all that is within me, bless His holy name." He returned to the world and looked at the stars... and said the song "Bless the Lord, all His works"... including the angels and their powers... and he looked at the wilderness and said the song "Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits." What are "all His benefits"? Rabbi Abbahu said: He made for her a dwelling place in a place of wisdom... why? So that she should not look at a place of nakedness... so that she should not suckle from the place of the "External Ones" <note>Hebrew: *Chitzonim* - demonic or impure forces</note> at the dwelling of the wicked. And he said the song "Let sinners be consumed from the earth"... "Bless the Lord, O my soul, Hallelujah." ... "Bless the Lord, O my soul, O Lord my God, You are very great; You are clothed in glory and majesty."

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic analysis of the Ten Commandments, shifting focus from the nature of the Sefirot (Divine Attributes) to the specific mystical correspondences between the two tablets of the Covenant. # Tractate Shevuot

The source of the spring opened the secret of spirituality and watered the earth—which is Man. He proceeds from "we will hear" <note>Hebrew: *nishma*</note> to reach "we will do" <note>Hebrew: *na’aseh*</note>. My intention is that when he heard the blessing and descended from the place of "hearing," the influence descending from above became somewhat coarsened by necessity. This is the meaning of its connection to "we will do." This is the explanation of the words, as Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> explained regarding the verse "God [made] the firmament." At the receiving of the Torah, when Israel was at a supreme spiritual level and saw their world in their lifetime—the level of the World to Come—they preceded "we will do" to "we will hear." <note>A reference to Exodus 24:7, where the Israelites famously accept God's laws before even hearing the details.</note> 

And now, why have you turned away? For the purpose of "doing" is to reach the World to Come, the level of "hearing." Now that we have reached this, there is no need for coercion if we add ourselves to hear, and so on. Regarding their time, they said "to hear," meaning their desire is that there be an additional secret of "hearing" <note>original: *shemaia*</note> for us at our death, more than what we have now. And we are protected from the wicked so that we may live. A similar explanation was given by Rabbi Moses Almosnino <note>original: *Ha-RAM Al-Mashunino*; a 16th-century philosopher and rabbi from Salonica</note> of blessed memory.

The general principle is that "doing" and "hearing" are within the secret of the letter *Vav* that ascends. From the perspective of Man, he was "made" in the [Divine] image and likeness; but from the perspective of the Holy One, blessed be He, he is "heard" and "done," in the secret of "and he watered," like the image of a seal that is reversed.

Accordingly:
**"Do not murder"** corresponds to **"I am the Lord your God."** He is His Name, may He be blessed, and "Do not murder" relates to the secret of the [Divine] image and likeness.
**"Do not commit adultery"** corresponds to **"You shall have no <insert>other</insert> gods."** The verse "You shall have no other gods" hints at the act of Repentance <note>Hebrew: *Teshuvah*</note>, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "There shall be no 'strange god' within you"—who is this 'strange god'? It is the Evil Inclination. For the sinner attaches himself to the "Other Side" <note>term: *Sitra Achra* (the Kabbalistic realm of evil and impurity)</note>, to the side of impurity. God forbade the Torah to him [the sinner] in the sense of "bowing down," and his only existence is "you shall surely perish." One must hasten after him [with repentance]; this is the Repentance of returning to the side of Holiness, which is "the Lord our God," to be our God. 

The verse **"Do not commit adultery"** hints that one should not come to this, to draw near the opening of a harlotrous, adulterous woman. This is the level of the "Perfect Righteous" <note>Hebrew: *Tzadik Gamur*</note> who never came to sin. The Zohar has already compared the Evil Inclination to a harlot who entices one to sin with her. In the Midrash: "'Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered' (Psalms 32:1). Rabbi Shimon ben Levi said: This is like one who threw a stone into hot water and it turned black. He began saying before people, 'Happy is the water'—meaning she who drank the Bitter Waters <note>A reference to the *Sotah* ritual in Numbers 5</note> and was found pure. Another man said to him, 'Happy is the mother who never needed to drink them at all!' Thus, David said, 'Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven,' but the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, 'Happy is the man to whom the Lord does not impute iniquity' (Psalms 32:2)." This is "Do not commit adultery"—that he should never come to a state of moral contradiction.

**"Do not steal"** corresponds to **"Do not take [the Name in vain]."** Regarding the matter of angels, it is explained in the *Pardes* <note>The *Pardes Rimonim* by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the tenth chapter of the "Gate of the Palaces" that Love and Fear are the foundations for the attribute of Mercy. Even though it is necessary, it is nevertheless distant from the illumination that comes to an angel from the side of his elemental composition. [The soul] is clothed in the upper spirit and soul, higher than the "Living One" <note>Hebrew: *Chaya* (a high level of the soul)</note> of God. And from above the "Five" <note>referring to levels of the soul or Sefirot</note>, there are two that distress the superiority of the angel over the man, and the superiority of the man over the angel.

And regarding **"Remember"** and **"Do not take [the Name in vain],"** and against it **"Do not steal"**: in the fear of "Do not take," there is a hint to the superiority of the Righteous in spirituality; his strength rises upward on the ladder of his soul higher than an angel. This is hinted at in this verse—the Light and Splendor and the rest of the ranks—for the angels are those who serve the prayers of the Righteous to bring them higher and higher, beyond measure or number, for every generation, and they make of it a crown
->upon the head of the Holy One, blessed be He.<-

In Tractate Chullin, chapter 3, it says: "Israel praises the Name after two words, and the ministering angels after three words." <note>Israel says "Hear, Israel, the Lord..." while angels say "Holy, holy, holy..."</note>. This concerns the level of spiritual intention. For the external things are in the Throne of Glory, and the Throne itself and the world of Emanation <note>Hebrew: *Atzilut*</note>—these are the "two words." However, the angels are in the world of Formation <note>Hebrew: *Yetzirah*</note>; thus they are after "three words." Therefore, they rejoice in the prayers of the Righteous. 

This is hinted at in the utterance **"Do not take [the Name in vain]."** As stated in Tractate Berakhot: "One who recites a blessing that is not needed violates 'Do not take.'" The reason is that when a person mentions the Name, it pierces all the firmaments and dwellings of all the [Divine] Chariots and shakes all the angels who carry this mention in vain. This is the meaning of "For the Lord will not clear him who takes [His name in vain]"—meaning, the one who causes the Name to be carried in vain by an angel. It is written here "takes" <note>Hebrew: *yisa*</note> and it is written there "you shall not carry <note>Hebrew: *tisa*</note> a false report." And even though they said in the *Keter* <note>The "Crown" or a specific section of a text</note>: "Why was 'You shall not take the name of the Lord your God' said? Because it says 'You shall not swear by My name falsely,' I might think it only applies to a false oath. How do I know it applies to an unnecessary oath? The Torah says, 'You shall not take...'" Before we accept to swear, He is "God" to you; once you have accepted to swear, He is "Judge" to you. Returning to our subject: the internal superiority of the Righteous over the angel is clear.

Against it is **"Do not steal,"** because from the side of the "melody," Adam the First "stole." <note>A mystical interpretation of the first sin</note>. This was corrected through the awakening, and he returned to clarify his foundations, and the Holy One, blessed be He, established them as the "fixers of the soul." This is "Do not steal" regarding souls.

**"Do not bear false witness"** corresponds to **"Remember the Sabbath day."** The Sabbath indicates the renewal of the world "something from nothing" <note>Latin/Hebrew: *Ex Nihilo / Yesh me-Ayin*</note>. Consequently, the power is in His hand, blessed be He, to change the celestial arrangement; thus, "there is no constellation <note>Hebrew: *mazal*</note> for Israel." I have already elaborated on this in Tractate Shabbat regarding the saying "There is no constellation" (Berakhot 1). Now, when we keep the Sabbath, we testify to this matter when we say "And they were finished" <note>Hebrew: *Vayechulu* (Genesis 2:1-3, recited on Friday night)</note>, which is a testimony from us. As I mentioned above regarding the Sabbath liturgy: "Do not bear witness [falsely] against your neighbor"—meaning, sometimes you should not bear this testimony that "there is no constellation for Israel" if one's actions are lacking. This is hinted at in the verse "and a witness in the sky is faithful," which refers to the eternal existence of the stars' instruction, as in "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today."

**"Do not covet"** corresponds to **"Honor your father and your mother."** There are "three partners in Man" <note>The father, the mother, and God</note>, and the Holy One, blessed be He, joined them to understand that they should be honored, even though they only provide the material parts of him, while the spiritual is in the "garments of skin" <note>A reference to the physical body given to Adam after the fall</note>. This shows that the "garments of skin" cause an effect Above; through these physical garments, one can merit a great and awesome Light. **"Do not covet"** instructs one to overturn and nullify "coveting," which causes the "putrid drop" <note>a reference to semen/physical conception</note> from which the "garments of skin" were formed. These five matters are within the secret of the Holy Emanation <note>Hebrew: *Atzilut*</note>, which is five against five in the reversal of its form. This is brought at the beginning of the book *Pardes*: "Ten Sefirot of nothingness <note>Hebrew: *Bli-mah*</note>, the number of ten fingers, five against five, and the covenant of the Unique One is placed in the center, in the word of the tongue and the circumcision of the flesh."

These five pairs correspond to each other. The places that require enforcement are five against five: 
1. Wisdom (*Chokhmah*) against Understanding (*Binah*).
2. Greatness (*Gedulah*) against Might (*Gevurah*).
3. Kindness (*Chesed*) against Glory (*Hod*).
4. Victory (*Netzach*) against Victory (*Netzach*).
5. Victory (*Netzach*) against Glory (*Hod*). 
See his book at length for the explanation.

I say that in the "five against five," Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> is the secret of thought, which is the secret of the Primordial Torah. Understanding (*Binah*) is the secret of action, for it is the root of the Six Days of Action. So says the *Pardes* regarding appellations: "Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, called Understanding 'Action' and Wisdom 'Thought.'" It is known that because Understanding is the root of the six days, it is also "Thought," but from the side of its concealment in unity with Wisdom, it is perceived as the Ten Crowns. Then this world is explained as the "World of Action," the six days of work, and similarly the six thousand years of the world. This world was created with the letter *He*, and the World to Come—the world of reward for action—was created with the letter *Yod*. Therefore, from the perspective of Wisdom, which is essentially the *Yod* of Thought, it is the Primordial Torah, and from there "hearing" precedes "doing." But from the perspective of Understanding, which is the root of the days of action and is called "Action," from there "doing" precedes "hearing."

---

## Kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note>

From them [Kindness and Might] comes the secret of the "Perfect Righteous" and the "Penitent" <note>Hebrew: *Ba'al Teshuvah*</note>. It is as Rashi explained: "In the beginning God created"—at first He intended to create the world with the Attribute of Justice <note>Hebrew: *Midat HaDin*</note>, but He saw the world could not stand, so He partnered with it the Attribute of Mercy. My father and teacher explained in the book *Emek HaBerakha* that the meaning is: from the perspective of Justice, Repentance would not help. Once a person deviates from the line of Justice and sins, then from the depth of Justice, he would not be worthy of atonement. But He saw the world would not stand, so He partnered Mercy with it. The matter of "partnership" is that if he does Repentance, he is atoned; if not, he dies for his sin. Thus, from the side of Might (*Gevurah*), which is Justice, the level is the "Perfect Righteous," the "Mighty One who conquers his inclination" and has not sinned. But from the side of Kindness (*Chesed*) is Repentance; it is the "Right Hand" of the Holy One, blessed be He, stretched out to receive those who return. For Kindness is the Right Hand, and all Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are for Repentance. The deciding factor between them "inclines toward Kindness," specifically for Repentance out of love, for Kindness is love.

### Kindness and Glory <note>Hebrew: *Chesed* and *Hod*</note>

Regarding the superiority of a righteous man or an angel, they said in the Midrash Rabbah: "When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to create Man, Kindness said, 'Let him be created, for he performs acts of kindness.' Truth said, 'Let him not be created...'" and God threw Truth to the ground. Thus, Man is from the side of Kindness. And it is written, "He shall inherit Glory" <note>Hebrew: *Hod*</note>—this refers to Man and the angel from the side of Glory. For the essence of the angels' activity is all song and thanksgiving <note>Hebrew: *hodaya*</note>, as the stars sing and the Seraphim rejoice. As stated in the books *Sha’arei Ora* and *Sha’arei Tzedek*, and cited in the *Pardes*, the term *Hod* refers to all types of thanksgiving. Our teacher Menachem Recanati wrote that *Hod* is from the language of "giving thanks to the Lord." The decision between them is that the law follows both: the angel is superior in terms of his elemental composition, but Man is superior...

# Tractate Shevuot

...the form of **Chaos and Void** <note>Hebrew: *Tohu va-Vohu*</note>, which were dispersed and required water to rise and cover the world, returning it to its former state. This continued until the Holy One, blessed be He, summoned a certain appointed angel, **Ye’uriel**, who is in charge of seventy keys of the Proclamation of the Holy Name. Because of this, the form was revived and engraved with letters as before, and thus the world was established and the waters returned to their place. Concerning this, it is written: **"You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain"** (Exodus 20:7).

The same applies when one mentions the Name for no purpose; for anything done "in vain" lacks true existence, whereas He, may He be blessed, is the Absolute Existence. Behold, the verse says: "After the Lord your God you shall walk... and Him you shall serve, and to Him you shall cleave, and in His name you shall swear" (Deuteronomy 13:5, 6:13, 10:20). This is the matter I wrote of: "The whole earth is full of His glory" (Isaiah 6:3), and all existence stems from His existence, may He be blessed.

The ultimate purpose of existence is Man, that he might fulfill the Torah and the commandments, for the Torah is His Name, may He be blessed. Thus, one who fulfills it cleaves to the Luminary of His Name, and He establishes his intention. Therefore, one should remember His Name. But one who distances himself "pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence" <note>A Talmudic idiom meaning to act as if God is not present in the world</note>, as it were. Then, according to the degree of his distancing, he lacks form and returns to **Chaos and Void**, for he removes his own existence from His Existence, may He be blessed. Then, he is removed from the Good, and Evil is revealed to him. This is the secret of the **Hiding of the Face** <note>Hebrew: *Hester Panim*; the theological concept of God's apparent absence</note>.

Then, the Evil is permitted to do harm according to the measure of the wrong committed. This is how it is for the foolish; it is not my intention to say that Evil is merely the Hiding of the Face and not an actual essence, as might be understood from the words of the philosophers who spoke on this. Rather, Evil exists with purposeful intent, even if the intent of Evil is not for the sake of evil itself, but for the sake of Good. For if harm did not reach the wrongdoer—which is the greatest evil—then there would be no Good. For evil "pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence" and returns existence to Chaos and Void. If He did not perform Good even specifically for the wicked, the result would be total Chaos.

It is clear that Good is intended for its own sake, for "The Lord is good to all" (Psalms 145:9), and Evil is intended for the sake of Good, so that everything will eventually perform Good. Thus, everything goes to one place: He, blessed be He, is the "Place of the World" <note>Hebrew: *Maqom*; a rabbinic name for God implying He contains the universe</note> and He sustains everything. God is recognized through His descriptive titles. But the purpose of existence and everything within it comes from His Existence. Even the "voids" <note>likely referring to spiritual vacuums</note> proclaim, as it is written: "Because of your humility, the All-Powerful..." Even though influence flows to the "vessels" of Evil, it is so that the "divider" <note>the barrier between man and God</note> may be removed. Then the name **Elohim** <note>The Divine Name associated with Judgment</note> acts with Justice, and Justice is harsh and doubting.

The Divine descends through the four orders within the general attribute of Mercy, for Justice exists for the sake of Mercy. It is only the sinner who causes the activation of non-mercy. One who "lifts" or "carries" <note>a play on the word *Tissa* (take/carry) from the commandment</note> the four orders elsewhere—this is "You shall not take [the name]." Then the Lord descends from that level, "for He will not clear the guilty" (Exodus 20:7). You will understand this through what the Sages said regarding the "inner chambers" <note>reference to the Talmud, Hagigah 5b</note> which I brought above, that he separates the connections. All this is relative to the resulting action. However, from the perspective of the Ultimate Purpose, everything is for the best. Sometimes Justice contains even more Mercy, and all Justice is the essence of Mercy, like the "suffering" that comes to consume the evil, so that one might accept discipline and improve his ways. This is why it says, "I will give thanks to the Lord, for You have answered me" (Psalms 118:21). There is a great hint in the verse: "Only you have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities" (Amos 3:2). In this aspect, "God is indignant every day" (Psalms 7:12). It is known that *El* <note>the specific name for God used in that verse</note> is the attribute of Mercy. Its explanation is like an "ambush" in another place; this is a "Jealous God."

There are also sufferings that stem from great Mercy—the secret of **"Sufferings of Love"** <note>Yissurin shel Ahavah; suffering that comes to the righteous to increase their reward without being a punishment for sin</note> which I explained elsewhere. Through this, the necessity is explained: how we are affected by the unity of the action of Evil and the union with the Good. The measure of this is to contemplate what we have said: that there is no other existence besides Him. He, may He be blessed, constantly bestows influence and sustains. There is nothing truly new, only what was brought into being during the six days of Creation, after which the process of "new creation" ceased. Despite this, He is the constant Vitality. Concerning this comes the utterance: **"Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it, for in six days..."** (Exodus 20:8-11). It says, "Therefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it"—meaning the Sabbath, which points to the Sabbath of Creation, did not emerge for its own sake alone, but it is the Vitality and sustenance for that which is renewed constantly every day in the "Work of Creation." The Heavens are branches that emerge from the Sabbath, and through miracles they return to the Sabbath, going back and forth as explained at length in Tractate Hullin and Tractate Shabbat. It is a constant cycle from Sabbath to Sabbath, returning to the primordial state, resting and returning. "And He sanctified it"—so that the "Counsel of Time" shall not interrupt.

### The Utterance
It was stated afterward in the Midrash: "And the Lord descended... all the kings of the earth... hear the words of my mouth" (Psalms 138:4). For when the utterance began with **"I am the Lord your God,"** the nations of the world said, "He is only seeking His own honor." But once they heard Him say, **"Honor your father and your mother,"** they conceded.

The matter is as our Sages of blessed memory said: **"There are three partners in [the creation of] man: The Holy One, blessed be He, the father, and the mother."** The portion of the Holy One is the essential part and includes them all. It is fitting that in the world, the Holy One shares these portions; even if there is no physical substance to it <note>the soul</note>, yet there is existence. Therefore, the Holy One commanded to honor the father and mother since they have a part in the existence of the child and are a cause for it. If so, we learn from this that the "effect" <note>the child</note> is obligated to honor the "cause" <note>the parents</note>. How much more so is this true regarding the Divine Presence!

Thus, it is clear that when He commanded "I am the Lord your God"—He who is the Cause of all causes—He did not say it for His own honor, but for the sake of the truth of the matter: that your existence depends on Him. The Holy One, blessed be He, taught us the truth of Justice to guide us in the straight path. The truth of the utterance "I am the Lord" was clarified by the utterance "Honor your father."

However, there is another hidden matter in the book of the **Zohar** (Proverbs 23:25): "'Let your father and your mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice.' Since it is written 'your father and your mother,' why add 'her who bore you'? One would suffice. Rather, 'your father' refers to the Holy One, blessed be He; 'your mother' refers to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael; the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</note>; 'and let her who bore you rejoice' refers to the one below." Thus, the Holy One, blessed be He, oversees through the order of the Supernal Union from which souls emerge, and their teaching is below. This "lower" union is for the birth of the body. It is also known that the Holy One and His Shekhinah are the secret of the **Written Torah** and the **Oral Torah**, who give birth to the "fruit of the commandments." As found in Tractate Hagigah (3b), in its literal sense, they are interpreted as "be fruitful and multiply," even though there are five types of "fruitful and multiplying," and they are the fruits of the commandments. They explained in Tractate Sotah regarding the "beheaded heifer" <note>Eglah Arufah; a ritual for an unsolved murder</note> that it is killed in a place that does not produce fruit, to atone for the killing of this person whom they did not allow to produce fruit. One might ask, what of an old man? The answer is: what fruits? The fruits of good deeds. For this purpose, the commandment of procreation was given.

The secret of the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton</note> includes all that was brought into existence. It is the Crown <note>Keter</note> or Wisdom <note>Chokhmah</note>.
The letter *Vav* <note>The third letter</note> represents the six general directions of beauty, the six intentions.
The first *Heh* <note>The second letter</note> represents the "Sovereignty" <note>Malchut</note> which is the Written Torah.
The second *Heh* <note>The fourth letter</note> represents the Oral Torah.
The letters *Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh* are the secret of "I will be" <note>Ehyeh</note>. Higher than this is the secret of the **Holy of Holies**, which is wondrous. Even **Moses our Teacher** <note>original: *Ma-Ra-SH* (Moshe Rabbenu)</note>, who attained the Gates of Understanding <note>Binah</note>, did not attain the fiftieth gate. This gate is unified with the *Yod* of Wisdom, etc.
Wisdom is hinted at by the "Acquirer of the Nest," which is the end of Wisdom—meaning the secret of the **Crown of the primordial Torah**. It is the secret of the "Transverse Bolt" mentioned above.
Thus, the chain of generation is the chain of the Torah, and "The Torah is perfect" (Psalms 19:8). The letters *Yod-Resh-Dalet* <note>spelling 'Yarad' - descended</note> will also be explained in the verse "The Torah of the Lord is perfect," for just as He, blessed be He, is the perfection of all perfections, lacking nothing and having no excess, so too His Law, which He gave for our benefit, possesses the powers of perfection. If one were to subtract from them, he would make them deficient; if he were to add to them, it would be as if they were not perfect. Therefore, it is forbidden to "add or diminish" (Deuteronomy 13:1).
It says "restoring the soul"—for the Torah was taken for them, as it says: "Come, eat of my bread" (Proverbs 9:5), for it is the food of the soul. It is called "wine," as in "He brought me to the banquet house [house of wine]" (Song of Songs 2:4). Physical food, which is bread, sustains the physical life, while the "living wine" of the throat is separated from the bread and wine of the physical. For everything taken for physical nourishment does not remain perfect, but the Torah, which is perfect, restores the soul—the soul that was taken, which was lacking, is restored to perfection. This is like one who "lights one candle from another."

**The second level** is the virtue of the Torah: "The testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple" (Psalms 19:8). I have already written that the Torah is life and existence. It is a "sure testimony" to this: the Secret <note>Yesod</note> which gives the Torah through five voices and seven voices, as mentioned. Everything belongs to Him and from Him. They were included in the "Tree of Life." It consists of five books <note>the Pentateuch</note> and it is seven <note>referring to a tradition that the book of Numbers is actually three books due to the inverted 'nuns' surrounding verses 10:35-36</note>. Even though there is a dispute about this in Tractate Shabbat in the chapter "All Sacred Writings," "these and these are the words of the Living God" in different aspects.
And so it is brought there... "And it was when the Ark traveled..." (Numbers 10:35). The Holy One, blessed be He, made signs above and below, to say that this is not the [original] place for this section. Why was it put here? To separate between the first "retrogression" and the second "retrogression." What are these retrogressions? The taste of their "complaining" and "punishment."
The "punishment" refers to "The people were like complainers" (Numbers 11:1). Rabbi [Judah the Prince] says it is a book in its own right. Thus there are seven books of the Torah. I have written above about the matter of the "Heifer." I wrote concerning the secret of the "vav" of the six directions, which is the Written Torah. The number seven includes all of them. Regarding the "five voices," they are the secret of the Torah as it was revealed in the Oral Law... as I explained in the "Gates of the Gates," Chapter 10 and 7. Now, it is revealed to every researcher that existence here reaches the Kingdom <note>Malchut</note>, which is the "end of the thought." The structure of the Name is included in the five [attributes of] Kindness and the six [of Beauty/Gevurah-Tiferet]. The Kingdom stands alone, for the Foundation <note>Yesod</note> and Kingdom <note>Malchut</note> are unified.
Regarding the "seven," they are found... below... the Foundation and Kingdom. Foundation is the spreading of the Beauty which was in its perfection. # Tractate Shevuot

He created seven heavens above, and He created seven lands below; seven seas, seven rivers, seven days, seven weeks, seven years, seven cycles, and seven thousand years that the world exists. The Holy One, blessed be He, is the seventh of all. There are seven heavens above, and in each one are servants, stars, and constellations that serve in every single firmament. All of them are arranged as chariots <note>Hebrew: *merkabot*, referring to organized angelic legions</note> one atop the other, accepting upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of their Master. In all these firmaments, there are different types of chariots and servants, some distinct from others: some have six wings, some have four wings; some have two faces, some have many faces, and some have only one. Some are a consuming fire, some are water, and some are wind. This is the meaning of the verse: "He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire" (Psalms 104:4). All these firmaments are layered one above the other like the skins of an onion <note>A classic medieval metaphor for the celestial spheres</note>, some below and some above. Every single firmament moves and trembles from the fear of their Master; by His word they travel, and by His word they stand. Above them all is the Holy One, blessed be He, who sustains them all with His strength and power.

In the same manner, there are seven lands below. All of them are inhabited, except that some are higher and some are lower. The Land of Israel is the highest of all, and Jerusalem is the highest point of all inhabited areas. Our companions have given a hint to this: Come and see in the ancient books and in the *Book of Adam* <note>A legendary mystical text attributed to the first man</note> how he describes all those lands which are found below, mirroring the firmaments above, layered one upon another. Between each land, there is a firmament that separates one from the other. Therefore, all these lands are distinguished by their names, and between them are Paradise and Hell. They contain creatures that differ from one another, just like the chariots above: some have two faces, some many, and some one. Their appearance is not like our appearance. If you should ask, etc.—see there at length. Thus, "that which is in the heavens above is on the earth beneath," and "that which is on the earth beneath is that which is in the heavens above." This means that whatever exists on dry land has a counterpart in the sea. This points to the Divine Unity. From this, you can respond that "One high official is watched by a higher, and there are yet higher ones over them" (Ecclesiastes 5:7). Everything is unified by His blessed Unity. "Do not bow down to the nations" <note>Referring to the prohibition of idolatry</note>. And this is what is meant by: "Know that the Lord your God is He"—He is the attribute of Mercy, and all stems from Unity. This is why the text later brings together good and evil: "a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers," etc., and "showing mercy to thousands," etc. In the plain meaning of the verse, why does it mention "doing mercy" in the context of those who worship idols? For us, it is comfortable to know that God is the "Friend" <term>Yedid (Beloved/Friend)</term>, but the philosopher still has no place to rest: how can evil emerge from the essence of Good? Since He, blessed be He, is the Absolute Good, how can evil be drawn from Him? However, look and you shall find that in the explanation of the prohibition of the Oath, this matter will be clarified.

The Holy One, "the whole earth is full of His glory," as it is written: "Know this day and take it to your heart, that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other" (Deuteronomy 4:39). "There is no other" does not merely mean there are no other gods <margin>rather the explanation is</margin> besides Him—which is already the plain meaning of "The Lord our God, the Lord is One"—but that no thing exists except for His existence. For He, blessed be He, brings everything into being and gives life to all. He is the very existence of all existing things. If there were any existence outside of His existence, Heaven forbid, there would be a separation. Everything is attached; one existence evolves from another existence, and all is the First Power. This thing is without end. Therefore, one who swears by His God, his intention is to mention His blessed Name, as if to say: "He brought this specific thing into being in such-and-such a way, and He gave the power to act thus." If he swears falsely, saying a thing was not as it truly was, he is effectively believing <margin>for the Holy One</margin> in another god—that He did not bring the thing into being this way, but rather someone else did. This would mean that power or godhood belonged to another authority, Heaven forbid. He thus uproots the Holy One from that thing. This is the language of "You shall not take" <note>Hebrew: *Lo tisa*</note>, which implies "uplifting" or "exalting." According to this, Maimonides explained the end of the matter, saying: "Know that one who swears in vain is 'cutting the plantings'" <term>Katzitz bi-Neti'ot (a term for heresy or disrupting the Divine order)</term>. This is why it says "You shall not take" rather than "You shall not swear"—it means you shall not uplift the object of your desire for vanity. This is the gravity of "He will not cleanse [the one who takes His name in vain]." And in the Zohar, my own work, it is written: "And she shall be cleansed and shall conceive seed" (Numbers 5:28); this is the opposite of "He will not cleanse." Similarly, the Zohar explains "You shall not take" as an expression of uplifting. I will copy his full language here, for from it, it will be clarified that a false oath causes the cancellation of existence. He writes: "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain"—when a man is rectified and does not fear to be rectified, or in the reverse, this is like a tree... the companions established this: when the Holy One blessed be He planted the world, He sank a single form into the abyss, engraved with this Name. He sank it into the depths... the waters wanted to rise and flood the world, but that form rises and receives that oath <note>Aramaic: *Oma’ah*</note>, and through the name of the Torah, it forces the abyss back, and the world is established. On that oath of truth, the world stands. But when men swear a false oath, that seal <note>Aramaic: *Tzrora*</note> rises up against that falsehood. Then that seal of spirit retreats, and the letters of that 

->seal<-

the search for death and the end of the world. This parable is for one poor man... and the ladder of the spheres, and their gathering into the worlds, etc. The companion... for his ancient sin, and he thinks and always stands upon his folly... as King Solomon said... for He is the place of the world... more so as they believe from the source... a place of rest and to eat... one should cling to whoever knows and to the heights... and so my beauty is for our spirit to diminish a little, like the foundation of pressure... when the waters gather little by little, and it is for the birth of existence to be, etc. Water, water. And the masters of the Talmud wrote on the verse "the spirit of God hovered"... the honor will be lacking... for he shall stand and give... the smallness... because after it is burnt, it hides... for the world... the spirit of the sons of the world for the ascent... and good to go down to the earth... and it exists... and return to the foundation of the spheres... it was made... it was turned to... for it too is much until the world... in the matter I mentioned... soul and spirit upon the... souls... in my God... the soul... the soul is like a dove, for it has in it strength and life to spread out in all... and the spheres... there... for life... height and... for mercy. And our Sages said: "In the soul that He placed in his heart..." and all of them shall be drawn to God... and so it said "and my soul found rest for you"... for in the secret of the spheres... they shall begin... they shall not cease from the circuit of the sphere. And this is the secret of the well-known word: "The Beloved" <note>Hebrew: *Yedid*</note>... my heart... for the thousands... who were removed there... to the world... and it was not given... like the soul of the Lord... "Bless the Lord, O my soul," and all my inner parts... the secret of the "Beloved" <note>A reference to the name *Yedid*</note>... for the Holy One, blessed be He, is full of glory... the word "flesh"... and this is the meaning of "There is none holy like the Lord"... "and there is no rock <note>Hebrew: *Tzur*</note> like our God," for there is no "Designer" <note>Hebrew: *Tzayar*</note> like our God... the spirit... as mentioned... "my inner parts"... all that is spread out... only a part... the secret of the matter... whoever approaches... then spirit and soul spread out to be within him. And on this it is said: "Forever... that which is close..." to exclude the "external ones" <note>A Kabbalistic term for demonic forces or "husks"</note>... the Greek sects... which are the cause... from the source as is known... and the place... is the source and the world of the spheres that were created... the heavens... as mentioned in the thought.

<meta>This page continues a mystical exploration of the Ten Commandments and the divine structure of reality. # Tractate Shevuot

...the Great [Luminary] and the Small Luminary <note>Refers to the Sun and the Moon, symbols for different aspects of the Divine</note>, which is to say, the unfolding of Sovereignty <note>Hebrew: *Malkhut*, the final of the ten *Sefirot* or divine emanations</note> to its place. From this, you will understand the matter of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. For the Beauty <note>Hebrew: *Tiferet*, the central *Sefirah*, associated with the Written Torah</note> precedes Sovereignty, as is known in the secret of "Flow and Recipient." For the flow of the Oral Torah comes from the Written Torah, and from it, the Oral Torah draws its sustenance to bring evidence from the Written Word. The Written Torah was spoken by the Master, and it flows into the Oral Torah. These attributes are called "Sun and Moon," for the light of the Moon comes from the light of the Sun. They are also called "Heaven and Earth," for the Heavens answer the Earth.

Behold, in the aspect of the "Seven Voices," they are two distinct Torahs: the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. But above, in the secret of the One, they are a single Torah. For Wisdom and Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah* and *Binah*</note> are like two companions who never separate. There, the "Son" is found in Wisdom and the "Wise" in Understanding, as we have learned in the *Book of Formation* <note>Hebrew: *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>. 

However, to understand how the Written and Oral Torah are one, you must know everything I wrote previously in *The Generations of Man* <note>Hebrew: *Toldot Adam*</note> regarding the inquiry: why is our language called "The Holy Tongue"? There you will find this matter explained. Many sayings are clarified there, such as the saying: "A small matter and the corners of a square are a great matter, the Work of the Chariot" <note>Hebrew: *Ma'aseh Merkavah*, referring to the highest form of mysticism</note>; and the saying: "In my thoughts, I thought of this, which is the Babylonian Talmud"; and the saying regarding the two staffs, one called "Destruction" and one called "Pleasantness." All of these belong here.

And these are the words of the *Toldot Adam* [on page 116]: Also, what I wrote at the end of *Toldot Adam* in the explanation of the saying "And the writing was the writing of God, engraved <term>Hebrew: *charut*, which the Sages also read as *cherut*, meaning 'freedom'</term> on the tablets," explaining why one should not write with certain decorative crowns... all of this belongs here. Then you will understand that now, in the aspect of the "Seven Voices," there are two Torahs—Written and Oral—and they are the Great Luminary and the Small Luminary. 

But in the future to come, "the light of the Moon shall be like the light of the Sun," and "two kings shall use a single crown." On this, we may explain the verse: "The testimony of the Lord is faithful" (Psalms 19:8). Then, "other faces" etc., for the servants shall sing over the Torah... as we find in the first opening of *Great Lamentations* <note>Hebrew: *Eikhah Rabbati*, a collection of Midrash on the Book of Lamentations</note>: When the Holy One, blessed be He, said to our father Abraham, "Your children have sinned," Abraham asked, "Master of the Universe, who testifies against them?" The Holy One, blessed be He, replied, "Let the Torah come and testify."

Behold, then, "testimony" implies at least two. The explanations of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah are the two witnesses. We find this also in the physical world, when Moses, our teacher (peace be upon him), called "Heaven and Earth" as witnesses against Israel. They are the source of the secret of the Written and Oral Torahs. We find this similarly at the start of the opening of *Great Lamentations*.

Regarding this, it says: "The testimony of the Lord is faithful." That is to say, in the future, when receiving testimony from the Written and Oral Torah in the aspect of the "Seven Voices," it is well that they are two witnesses. But in the higher aspect where they are one Torah—even though Sovereignty and Beauty (the roots of the two Torahs) are always distinct spheres <note>Hebrew: *Sefirot*</note> even when using one crown—nonetheless, in the aspect of the "Two Great Luminaries" that shall be, the matter of testimony requires two witnesses who are not entirely nullified into one.

As it is found in the Jerusalem Talmud, and brought in the *Tur, Hoshen Mishpat*, section 28: Rabbi Hiyya saw a witness... he would return and see the witness's son... he would explicitly intend that when he saw witnesses whose testimony was perfectly identical in language, he would suspect they were lying and had conspired together. He would then investigate and search them. But if they did not speak in the exact same language—this one saying it this way and that one saying it that way—provided their testimony was consistent and not contradictory, he would not investigate so much. 

So it is below with the words of Moses our teacher: the language of "Heaven" and the language of "Earth" are different because he speaks to the Earth. Thus, they are not perfectly identical in language... yet "the testimony of the Lord is faithful" even if they are not perfectly identical. This is hinted at in what follows: "making wise the simple." I have already written above about the "song of the Torah" and the matter of "missing and extra" letters in the hints of the Written Torah, which includes everything in the Oral Torah. 

In the future, "the earth shall be full of knowledge," and we shall sit in light and not in darkness. The seven days of construction shall be reunited with their root and become one in five voices. Then the Oral Torah will be revealed to the intellect within the Written Torah. But regarding the secrets and mysteries of the Torah, in the secret of the Essential Name... these are higher attributes in Understanding... in the secret of the attainment of the mind, the secret of Thought, Wisdom... in a place of wonder... that the very attributes of holiness shall "make wise the simple." Even one who is wise in the secret of the hints is still "simple" compared to the secret of the hidden wonders, until the verse is fulfilled: "They go from strength to strength" (Psalms 84:8)... "The testimony of the Lord is faithful."

We can also explain this verse—"The testimony of the Lord is faithful"—as referring to the Written Torah on its own and the Oral Torah on its own. Regarding the Written Torah: its very letters testify for us that we merited to see His glory, as it says in the Portion of Yitro: "And all the people saw the voices," for they saw that which is usually heard. And in the Portion of Va'etchanan: "The sound of words you heard, but a form you did not see; there was only a voice." So says The Tailor <note>Hebrew: *He-Hayyat*, likely referring to a commentator on the Kabbalistic work *Ma'arekhet Ha-Elohut*</note> in *The Order of Divinity* at the end of page 198.

<column-break/>

...Regarding the correction to the aforementioned book, Rabbi Joshua ben Levi <note>A famous 3rd-century scholar known for his piety and mystical encounters</note> merited everything... as the Sages taught... I did not hear it from him... so said Samuel bar Nahum to me in the name of Rabbi Isaac... they did not call him by the name of Rabbi Isaac... because in the end they would benefit... and if they benefit, what of it?... 

This requires explanation. How could he not know that "Good" <note>Hebrew: *Tov*</note> was written for the benefit of the schoolchildren? Why did he not reveal the verse to him? He said: since they did not know it then, how could he say... it is difficult, for since he didn't know "Good" was written there, how could it be said that "Good" was not said to them? Furthermore, it is difficult: why did he ask further? 

There are three answers... The Torah is a "positive commandment" that follows him... They remember her merit... "Better to me is the Torah of Your mouth" (Psalms 119:72)... and knowledge for kings is "Good"... as it says, "there are the rebukes," and "on the one who strikes"... 

He attributed it to "it is Good" in the Midrash... the depth of the rebuke... and he saw that "the light was Good" (Genesis 1:4)... and for him it is "Good"... as it says, "the rebukes are light"... Rabbi David [says]... and He hid it for the righteous in the future to come. For just as the light which He hid from everyone in this world... so too the Torah in its revealed state... so in the future to come, the light that is now hidden must be grasped in secret, as David (peace be upon him) asked: "Teach me good taste and knowledge" (Psalms 119:66). What is hidden now, and which some of the [Sabbath-keepers] merit, will be revealed and famous to the righteous. Then they will be elevated in spirituality... "And the Lord shall be your everlasting light." There, in the World to Come <note>Hebrew: *Olam HaBa*</note>, which is entirely "Good"... 

It is explained in the verses: "How great is Your Goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You" (Psalms 31:20). This refers to the Hidden Light, which in the future will be actualized and revealed to people... 

Explanation of the saying of Rav Adda bar Abba... why did he return to the plain meaning and not the interpretation of "Good"? So he will say regarding the First Commandments <note>The first set of the Ten Commandments given at Sinai</note>, and there they will not say "Good" in the Commandments... "so that it may go well with you" <note>This phrase appears in the second version of the Decalogue in Deuteronomy, but not the first in Exodus</note> refers to the World to Come, in which they were worthy... 

The reason "Good" was not said in the First Commandments is because of the "breaking" [of the tablets]. This is what you are asking me: why is "Good" said in them? I am the one who sees that there are two paths... The First Commandments [lack "Good"] because of the end... the end of the World to Come was there... it was not said in them "Good"... meaning the "Good" of this world, and that is why the man was in doubt... 

It comes to teach about this world... he asked him: since "Good" is to merit the Goodness of God... why is it mentioned in the second set? There is proof... for he should have said: since in the First Commandments... and to remove the doubt... he asks: why was it said in the first ones since they were destined [to be broken]?... and in the second ones... why did it not need to be added?... The "Good" of the World to Come is worthy of being mentioned. Conversely, since he mentioned it in the second ones, why did he not mention it in the first? Therefore, he asks in the name of "this world," he knew the meaning of "Good"... until the Sage said...
