->**Tractate Shevuot**<-
<note>Tractate Shevuot is a volume of the Talmud dealing primarily with oaths, but here it serves as a jumping-off point for homiletic and mystical discourse regarding the "oath" taken at Sinai.</note>

<margin>
Regarding the concept mentioned: "There is no 'before' or 'after' in the Torah" <note>original: "אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה"; a classic rule of rabbinic interpretation suggesting the Torah's sequence is not strictly chronological but follows a deeper logic</note>. This is because the Torah, in its essential form, is a sequence of letters that form Divine Names. This explains why the text might appear out of order—it is following the arrangement of these Holy Names rather than a historical timeline. As Nachmanides <note>A 13th-century scholar and mystic</note> explained, the entire Torah is comprised of the Names of God.
</margin>

Regarding the explanation of the matter: "I was lost in my poverty, and today they take the Torah," as the saying goes. I will add a "decorative gem" <note>A poetic way of saying he will offer further insight</note> to these words to clarify the final verses. First, I will offer a preface to address several difficulties concerning the dispute with the angels. When the angels said, "Place Your glory upon the heavens" <note>Psalm 8:2</note>, their intention was that the Torah should remain in the celestial realms. They argued that the physical Torah could not possibly be given to the ministering angels, for they lack physical bodies. If so, why did Moses answer them by asking, "What is written in the Torah? Does it say you should not kill? Do you have a jealous impulse?" <note>Referring to the debate in the Talmud, Tractate Shabbat 88b</note>. This raises a question: why not give the spiritual essence to the angels and the physical laws to humans?

We can resolve this by noting that the entire Torah is composed of Divine Names. It was originally written as a continuous string of letters. These combinations were all Names of God, as Nachmanides writes in his introduction to the Commentary on the Torah. Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, rearranged these letters into the words we recognize today—commandments and stories—so that it could become a "Torah for man." This explains why the angels were envious; they saw the Torah as it was in the heavens.

-> The letters were not originally read in the order they are written now, but according to how they were written in ancient times. <-

Let us contemplate the reality of the "fire" that results from the study of Torah. Our Sages of blessed memory spoke of <term>Jonathan ben Uzziel</term> <note>A premiere student of Hillel the Elder; it was said that when he studied, any bird that flew over him was consumed by fire</note>: when he sat and expounded, any bird flying over him was burned. Similarly, the Midrash describes Ben Azzai <note>A famous 2nd-century scholar known for his intense devotion to study</note> sitting and expounding, surrounded by flames. The Midrash says: "The words were as joyful as when they were given at Sinai." We must investigate why the Torah was given with seventy "faces" or languages. Moses, our teacher, clung to this excellence. Later, Onkelos <note>The famous convert who translated the Torah into Aramaic</note> returned and translated it. The Oral Torah was clarified through the Mishnah of Rabbi Meir and the works of Rabbi Akiva.

To understand this, I will offer three premises:
1. The souls of Israel are far superior to the ranks of angels. The souls of Israel are "hewn from the Throne of Glory" <note>A phrase indicating the soul's divine origin</note> and have their root in the highest realm of Emanation <note>original: "אצילות" (Atzilut); the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah</note>. As it says, "For the Lord's portion is His people" <note>Deuteronomy 32:9</note>. Angels, however, belong to the world of Formation <note>original: "יצירה" (Yetzirah)</note> and draw their sustenance from below the heavens.
2. The soul of Israel is the spirituality of the Torah itself. Just as the Torah was in the root of Adam, so too is it in his soul. The Talmud says: "The Torah was given in forty [days] and the soul was formed in forty [days]; whoever guards the Torah, his soul is guarded." This is why some say the Song of Songs was said by God, while others say it was Solomon. The spiritual essence of the Song of Songs is "Holy of Holies" and is attributed to Solomon because it is his soul. Similarly, when a sage like Rabbi Eliezer says "my son," or when a law is cited in the name of a specific Tanna <note>A teacher from the Mishnaic period</note>, that law is a spark of his specific soul. This is why one who teaches his friend’s son Torah is as if he birthed him; the teacher provides the soul.

It is said that "one woman gave birth to 600,000 in one birth"—this refers to Yocheved, who birthed Moses, who is equal to all of Israel. Moses' soul was the soul of the first man (Adam), which encompasses all souls. His soul spread through the 600,000 letters of the Torah. Thus, Moses is the "whole," and the people of Israel are his parts. This is why he said, "The six hundred thousand footmen *among whom I am*" <note>Numbers 11:21</note>; he is literally within them. This "Spark of Moses" extends to every generation. 

Why do we call him "Moses our Teacher" (*Moshe Rabbeinu*) and not "Our Teacher Moses" (*Rabbeinu Moshe*)? Before he received the Torah, he was simply "Moses." After the giving of the Torah, he became "Our Teacher." Even after his passing, he remains our teacher in every generation. This is why the Talmud sometimes says, "Moses, you have spoken well!" <note>original: "משה שפיר קאמר"; a common Talmudic idiom</note>—it means the spark of Moses is shining through that specific scholar's statement.

When God spoke, the souls of the people left them and were kissed by the Divine. The fire of Torah study is the light of the soul meeting the light of the Torah. The third premise is that God and the Torah are one. Through the Torah, the upper and lower worlds are unified. This unification can only happen through Man, who is composed of both soul (from above) and body (from the dust). 

The angels were jealous. They asked: "What is one born of woman doing among us?" They didn't understand that God wanted the Torah to dwell below. Moses was afraid the angels would "burn him with the breath of their mouths" because of his human flaws. But God told him to "Take hold of the Throne" <note>A symbolic act of connecting to the soul's divine root to find protection from the angels</note>. By holding the Throne—the source of souls—Moses proved that he belonged in the highest realms more than the angels themselves. The Torah serves to link the highest peak to the lowest center, a task only a human with a divine soul can achieve.

And the whole area is written with the Holy Letters and the laws of the Cantor and the Stone. This is what is meant by "at the time of eating," which is through "one who toils on the eve of the Sabbath shall eat [on the Sabbath]" <note>A Talmudic proverb meaning spiritual rewards must be earned through effort in this world</note>.

The word "to make wings" is not used except for one who is elevated. This is the "Kilay" who sets his eyes upon it to draw from it. And like the gate that was in the house and the knife, and the convert Ruth, who strives to rest in holiness. He said, "Let us ascend," as it is said, even though his time had not yet come. The Tree is very much limited by twelve diagonal borders <note>A reference to the *Sefer Yetzirah*, an ancient mystical text describing the structure of the universe</note> of its fruits, as it is said: "I am like a leafy cypress; from Me is your fruit found" <note>Hosea 14:9</note>. It turns out that they are the "face" of the deeds of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And from that Tree comes their fruit. However, existence and "He" ascend; therefore, "Is Ephraim my dear son?" <note>Jeremiah 31:20</note> for they are His deeds. They are "borne from the womb" <note>Isaiah 46:3</note> and not from the "wings," for it is from the belly, and he is the fruit of Israel. To show that they are real, it is written, "And his sons were sent after him, a living soul." Thus, Israel is "borne from the womb" in the secret of the Sephirah <term>Sephirah: one of the ten divine emanations in Kabbalah</term> of *Malchut* (Kingship), whose union is with *Tiferet* (Beauty/Harmony); its fruits are the souls that include all ten Sephirot. This is the secret of "Israel counts by the moon," etc. It is known that the secret of the "Upper Moon" is the attribute of *Malchut*. And they said in the chapter *Elu Terefot*: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said, "Hands shall be called to life in Your name." The paths of the deer are in the stars, and the living beings <gloss>Chayot: a high order of angels</gloss> are in the stars above, as are the sparks of the souls. Regarding them it is said: "And those who lead the many to righteousness are like the stars forever and ever" <note>Daniel 12:3</note>. Far from this is the level of the angels.

With this, we can explain a statement in the Talmud, Tractate Sanhedrin, in the chapter "One [may judge] monetary cases" <note>Sanhedrin 38b</note>. Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rav: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to create Man, He created a group of ministering angels. He said to them, "Is it your will that we make Man in our image?" They said to Him, "Master of the Universe, what are his deeds?" He told them, "His deeds are such and such." They said, "Master of the Universe, what is man that You should remember him, or the son of man that You should take notice of him?" <note>Psalm 8:5</note>. He extended His little finger among them and burned them. So too with the second group. The third group said before Him: "Master of the Universe, the first ones who spoke, what did they achieve? The whole world is Yours; whatever You wish to do in Your world, do it." When they reached the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion <note>The Tower of Babel</note>, whose deeds were corrupt, the angels said before Him, "Master of the Universe, did not the first ones speak well before You?" He replied, "Even to old age I am He, and even to grey hair I will carry you" <note>Isaiah 46:4</note>.

This is difficult: when He created the first group, why did He not ask the angels who were already created? Since the Holy One, Blessed be He, asked their advice, why was He angry with them when they answered according to their intellect? And the second group—when they saw what happened to the first, what were they thinking when they said the same thing? Furthermore, what is the meaning of the "little finger"?

I have already written that the soul of Israel, from the perspective of their source above, is beyond the grasp of angels, for the soul of Israel is "borne from the womb," which is the Sephirah of *Malchut*. You must also know that there are great levels among the angels, and their levels are not equal. There are those angels who are the secret of the "Upper Chariot," and there are the "creators of ministers" who are "judgments for the mornings," and those whose service is "from the days of old." This statement speaks of the aspect and side of the "ministers" who do not reach the place of Israel's comprehension from the perspective of their souls. When He wanted to announce the creation of Man—for the secret of His thought was that their level is very great—He showed them that they do not reach the level of the soul of Man. And this is why He "extended His little finger among them and burned them."

To understand this, I must first present two small introductions. One: we learn in *Sefer Yetzirah*: "Ten Sephirot out of nothing, the number of ten fingers, five against five, with a single covenant in the middle." The term "little finger" <note>the pinky</note> refers to *Malchut*, which is the tenth Sephirah. Our Sages called it "a small meal in your poverty" <note>original: "סעודה קטנה בעניותך"</note>. Regarding the counting of the Assembly, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: "Make for Me a small meal." The Kabbalists explain that this refers to the Sephirah of *Malchut*. Therefore, in the context of naming them as "fingers," it is called the "little finger."

The second introduction: as mentioned in the book *Brit Menuchah* <note>Covenant of Rest</note> regarding the "Graves of Craving": "there they buried the people who craved" <note>Numbers 11:34</note>. This hints at those who approach and crave a level that is vastly greater than their comprehension; they become non-existent, like a fly that approaches the light of a candle out of its craving and is burned. So too here: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed these angels His "little finger," they ceased to exist because it was not in the power of their comprehension to reach there, yet they craved it. The second group thought that it was in their power to ascend there, but they erred, thinking the first group was not equal to them in level; in truth, they were no better, and they too ceased to exist. However, the third group understood the matter: that one cannot reach this level except for Man, who is made "in the image and likeness" and includes both the upper and lower worlds. This is what is meant by "The whole world is Yours"—and Man is the [entire] world. Only later, when they saw the Generation of Enosh and the Dispersion who destroyed the world, did they say, "The first ones spoke well." The Holy One, Blessed be He, replied, "Even to old age and grey hair," meaning He suffers and overlooks the rebellious so that they might mend their deeds, as it is written: "You return man to contrition" <note>Psalm 90:3</note>—until the weeping of the soul, etc. And everything will be mended in the future, and the Name will be full as the world is full.

Incidentally, regarding these verses of "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name" and "What is man that You should remember him," I will explain this entire Psalm. They said: "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name." We find that the word "What" <gloss>Mah</gloss> has two meanings. Sometimes it is an expression of greatness, as in "How <gloss>Mah</gloss> great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You." And sometimes it is the opposite, an expression of belittlement: "What <gloss>Mah</gloss> is his strength?" In the first instance they said, "How majestic is Your name in all the earth," they meant the word "What" as an expression of diminishment—meaning, the comprehension of Your name to know it "in the earth" among physical bodies is diminished. Therefore, "Place Your glory upon the heavens," the portion of the soul; place it among bodies that are spiritual and not physical like us.

We can also interpret "How majestic is Your name in the earth" as meaning: how great is the goodness that exists in this, that Your name is majestic in the earth—that Your name is known and they believe in You. As explained in *Midrash Shmuel* on the verse "Your faithfulness is for all generations," for it is enough for them to be strengthened by the faith they have in You, and they will have existence. But the "knowledge and comprehension"—that "Place Your glory upon the heavens." "From the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength" <note>Psalm 8:3</note> refers to what was said above in the explanation of the statement: this is an answer to those who said that they [the angels] would be burned by the breath of their mouths. The "babes and sucklings" are the answer to this, for their breath is a breath that has no sin. And it says, "because of Your adversaries, to silence the enemy and the avenger," as our Sages said: "The schoolchildren <gloss>Tinokot shel beit rabban</gloss> nullify the decrees." And those who interpret signs gave a mnemonic: "And a soft tongue breaks the bone" <note>Proverbs 25:15</note>; the Hebrew initials of "Soft Tongue" <note>Lashon Raka</note> and "Breaks" <note>Tishbar</note> spell "Tinokot" <note>Children</note>.

<summary>This page explores the mystical superiority of the human soul over angels, explaining that souls originate from the Sephirah of Malchut (the "little finger"), a level of divinity that consumes angels who attempt to grasp it. It reinterprets Psalm 8 as a dialogue about whether the Torah and Divine Name should reside in the physical world or remain in the spiritual heavens.</summary>

<header>Tractate Shevuot: The Excellence of the Mediator, who is Moses our Teacher</header>

# The Excellence of the Mediator

<margin>The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever <note>Psalm 19:10</note>.</margin>

->**It is written: "Many daughters have done valiantly, but you excel them all. Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain; but a woman who**<-
->**fears the Lord, she shall be praised" <note>Proverbs 31:29-30</note>. "Many daughters" refers to the great ones of the nations... and "And this is the blessing" <note>Deuteronomy 33:1</note>.**<-

<margin>
Adam the First’s status was like the status of Enoch, for he did not come from a "foul drop" <note>a reference to biological birth</note> but was the direct handiwork of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Therefore, he was clothed in "garments of light" <note>original: "כתנות אור" - a play on "garments of skin" in Genesis 3:21</note>. Moses replied to him: "I have ascended beyond this level; that glory was taken from you, but when God gave me the radiance of my face, it remained with me even in death, and certainly during my life." Therefore, Moses ascended on high among the angels in his holy body, which was entirely light. As stated in the first chapter of Tractate Yoma: "And the cloud covered the mountain... and He called to Moses" <note>Exodus 24:16</note>. All of Israel was standing there, but the verse comes only to grant honor to Moses our Teacher. A Tanna <note>a sage from the Mishnah period</note> says: The verse comes only to "purge" the food and drink in his bowels—meaning to cast them off like a ministering angel. 

This is difficult, for surely Moses did not eat anything but the Manna, which is holy and from heaven, and the Manna was absorbed into the limbs. It seems the intention refers to the physical materiality of the body that resulted from Adam the First's eating and sinning with the "cluster of grapes" <note>a common Midrashic identification of the forbidden fruit</note>, because of which he was clothed in "garments of skin." The cloud came and purged and purified Moses' body until it was clear and thin like "garments of light." Since the primary rooting of materiality in man is in the intestines, the sage said "to purge the dark filth" that comes from eating and drinking. Through this, he became like the ministering angels. 

Now, since all this revolves around the excellence of his prophecy—that he was the greatest of prophets and none has arisen or will arise like him—one might ask: if Moses himself said he was the greatest, what of his humility? "And the man Moses was very humble" <note>Numbers 12:3</note>. Would Moses really say he was greater than all other prophets? This matter is one of the Thirteen Principles of Faith; how could he deny a core principle? Rather, when the verse says he was "humble," it means he honored every person exceedingly and lowered himself. This is according to what is written in *Duties of the Heart* <note>a 11th-century work of Jewish ethics by Bahya ibn Paquda</note> and as Maimonides wrote to his son: "The musar (ethical teaching) of humility will wipe away your ego. You are obligated to honor every person. If he is greater than you, honor him by right. If you are greater than him, consider that his sins are not as grave as yours, for you know more than him." 

This matter is explained at the end of the chapter [in Sotah]: "And she saw him that he was good" <note>Exodus 2:2</note>. Rabbi Meir says: "Good" was his name. Rabbi Yehuda says: "Tobiah" was his name. Rabbi Nehemiah says: He was "fit" (hagun) for prophecy. Others say he was born already circumcised. The Sages say: When he was born, the whole house was filled with light. It is written here "that he was good," and it is written elsewhere "And God saw... that it was good" <note>Genesis 1:4</note>.
</margin>

"Many daughters have done valiantly, but you excel them all." What is meant by "you excel them all"? This speaks of Moses, who was elevated above everyone. How so? 

Adam the First said to Moses: "I am greater than you, for I was created in the image of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it says, 'And God created man in His own image.'" Moses said to him: "I was elevated more than you. The glory given to you was taken from you, as it says, 'Man does not lodge in honor' <note>Psalm 49:13</note>. But the radiance of the face that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to me remains with me, as it says, 'his eye was not dim nor his natural force abated' <note>Deuteronomy 34:7</note>." 

Another explanation: Noah said to Moses: "I am greater than you, for I saved the generation of the flood." Moses said to him: "I was elevated more than you. You saved yourself but did not have the power to save your generation. I saved myself and I saved my generation when they were sentenced to destruction for the Golden Calf, as it says, 'And the Lord repented of the evil which He thought to do unto His people' <note>Exodus 32:14</note>." To what is this comparable? To two captains on the sea: one saved himself but not his ship; the other saved himself and his ship. Whom do they praise? The one who saved himself and his ship. Thus, Noah saved only himself, but Moses saved himself and his generation. Therefore: "you excel them all." 

Another explanation: Abraham said to Moses: "I am greater than you, for I used to feed wayfarers." Moses said to him: "I was elevated more than you. You fed people on the earth, but I fed people with heavenly food <note>the Manna</note>. Moreover, you fed them in a settled land, while I fed them in the wilderness." 

Isaac said to Moses: "I am greater than you, for I stretched out my neck upon the altar and I saw the face of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah)." Moses said to him: "I was elevated more than you. You saw the face of the Shekhinah and your eyes went dim, as it is written: 'And it came to pass when Isaac was old his eyes were dim from seeing' <note>Genesis 27:1</note>—what is 'from seeing'? From seeing the Shekhinah. But I spoke with the Shekhinah face to face and my eyes did not go dim, as it says: 'And Moses knew not that the skin of his face shone' <note>Exodus 34:29</note>." 

Jacob said to Moses: "I am greater than you, for I encountered the angel and overcame him." Moses said to him: "You encountered the angel in your territory <note>original: "פורפורין" - possibly referring to human boundaries or 'garments'</note>, but I went up to him in his territory, and they were afraid of me, as it says, 'Kings of hosts flee, they flee' <note>Psalm 68:13</note>." 

Solomon said: "Many daughters have done valiantly," etc. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "You have ascended and excel them all." Through this, Moses received the Torah for Israel. There is another verse that asks what is meant by "you excel them all." It refers to how he took precedence over Adam, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when they mentioned their blessings saying, "I am greater than you." When Moses replied to all of them, he used the language "I was elevated" <note>original: "אני נתעליתי"</note>, which was not an act of arrogance but an observation of fact. And if you ask about "Moses was humble," this is not a contradiction, for it was necessary to say this so you would not think Moses’ words were empty. Furthermore, the verse "Many daughters..." speaks of the people, as if they are the ones speaking and noting that Moses' level is above them all. 

Regarding the five matters: Maimonides (Rambam) explained the difference between the prophecy of Moses and other prophets through four distinctions: 
1. Any other prophet was spoken to only through an angel, but to Moses it was "mouth to mouth." 
2. Other prophets received prophecy only in a dream or a night vision, or during the day after a deep sleep, such that their senses were nullified. But of Moses it is said: "not so My servant Moses... mouth to mouth I speak with him." 
3. Other prophets, when the prophetic flow came to them, were terrified and trembled, their physical strength failing. Moses spoke "as a man speaks to his friend." 
4. Other prophets did not have prophecy rest upon them whenever they wished, but only at God's will. Moses was prepared at all times; whenever he wished for the Spirit of God to rest upon him, it did, as he said: "Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you" <note>Numbers 9:8</note>.

There is also a fifth distinction: he ascended to the heights in his body among the angels, which caused the angels to complain: "What is a mortal born of a woman doing among us?" This explains the phrase "you excel them all"—it would have been enough to say "you excel," but "on all of them" <note>Hebrew: "על כלנה"</note> implies he possessed the unique merits of each patriarch but surpassed them. His prophecy was in the "clear mirror" <note>term: *Aspaklaria HaMe'ira* - the direct, luminous prophetic vision unique to Moses</note>. Isaac saw the Shekhinah, but it cost him his physical sight; Moses saw it and was physically transfigured into light. Jacob wrestled an angel, but Moses commanded them.

# Tractate Shevuot

<margin>
* Rectification * of the * House * of Rabban * Lights * Evil * They nullify "When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars which You have established" <note>Psalm 8:4</note>. This is a living response to the accusation of the Ministering Angels <note>original: "מ"ה" - *Malakhei ha-Shareit*</note> during the creation of man. For the matter of Creation and the matter of the giving of the Torah are one and the same: Ten Sayings <note>by which the world was created</note> and Ten Commandments. This is hinted at in the creation of man where it says "God said, 'Let us make man'"—meaning, for the sake of [the Torah], let man be made. Indeed, the word "Let us make" <note>Hebrew: *na’aseh*</note> is written such that it can be read as "I will make" <note>Hebrew: *e'eseh*</note>. When the angels protested the creation of man, the Holy One, Blessed be He, extended His little finger... and I have explained this secret above, that his soul emerged from between the little finger which includes all ten fingers. Regarding this, it says here: "When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers," and mentions "the moon and the stars which You have established." The commentators ask why the sun is not mentioned. They answer as they answer, but according to the above, it is possible that the "little finger" refers to the moon. (According to the plain meaning, it seems to me that when it says "When I behold," it means he wanted to contemplate their greatness, which is impossible to do with the sun because its light is too powerful for the eyes to see directly).
</margin>

The "little finger" refers to the moon—the secret of the "Upper Moon"—and its length is reflected in the stars above, after which the righteous are named. Their merits are as numerous as the stars. "What is man that You are mindful of him, and the son of man that You visit him?" <note>Psalm 8:5</note>. This refers to their path: "Even to old age, I am He" <note>Isaiah 46:4</note>. The matter of the future will be entirely clear. Then, the "Enosh" <note>mankind/frailty</note> and the Generation of the Dispersion—those who built the tower—will be rectified, for the "husks" <note><term>Kelippot: spiritual layers of evil or concealment</term></note> will cease to exist. From this power come the revealed punishments, and then "the superiority of light will come from the darkness," as I have written in several places. Then they will reach the ultimate purpose, and the verse "You have made him a little lower than the angels" <note>Psalm 8:6</note> will be fulfilled in them, for the earth will be filled with knowledge. Each person will reach a level of understanding where they know the forty-nine gates of understanding, lacking only that "little bit"—the fiftieth gate. By way of a hint, this is the "little bit" taken from the <term>Samael <note>the accuser/Satan</note></term>. When this small portion is refined, it is as the verse says: "He afflicted you and famished you... to do you good in the end" <note>Deuteronomy 8:3,16</note>. The goal is to be just "a little lower than God," and so to speak, one becomes a true "Man of God." The text says, "And crowned him with glory and honor." "Glory" refers to the inner, upper aspect, while "Honor and Majesty" <note>original: *hod ve-hadar*</note> refers to the spirit. From this power, majesty will be added. As I wrote: the superiority of light comes from the refinement of darkness and adversity. It then says, "You made him ruler..."—this is not just the high spiritual level of the soul of Israel through receiving and fulfilling the Torah, but even in their physical bodies they rule over all existence. "Everything is placed under his feet: sheep and oxen, all of them..." He lists the animals, and certainly below them are plants and inanimate matter. From the perspective of his soul, man is higher than the angels; thus, he rules over all. When the angels returned to this matter, they admitted and said: "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" The word "How" <note>Hebrew: *Mah*</note> implies a great abundance. They admitted that the majesty of His name is great on earth through the Torah He gave them, which gives life to everything on earth. There is also a hint in the word "Majestic" <note>Hebrew: *Adir*</note> to the height of Israel; even in the earthly realm, they are like the angels above—the four camps of the Divine Presence <note><term>Shekhinah: the localized presence of God</term></note> with the Presence in the center, just like the four flags of Israel's tribes. The four flags represent the four directions: the flag of the camp of Judah, the flag of the camp of Reuben, the flag of the camp of Ephraim, and the flag of the camp of Dan. These correspond to "Majestic" <note>the Hebrew letters of *Adir* (אדיר) are used here as an acronym or cipher for the tribes and divine attributes: Truth (Emet), Redemption (Pidyon), Daniel, Judah, Ephraim, Reuben</note>.

# The General Principle
The excellence of Israel and the giving of the Torah through them is because they include everything, upper and lower. By the power of their souls and bodies—since the spirituality of the Torah is their very souls—all prophecies, yearnings, homilies, and wisdom were received at Sinai. Through our study, these emerge from the "womb" into the light. Through this, we can explain the extra verses starting with the letter *Lamed* found in the *Midrash Shmuel*: "I will never forget Your precepts, for with them You have given me life" <note>Psalm 119:93</note>; "I am Yours, save me, for I have sought Your precepts"; "The wicked have waited for me to destroy me, but I will consider Your testimonies"; "I have seen an end to all perfection, but Your commandment is exceedingly broad." It has already been explained regarding their role that these verses and midrashim indicate a great love and a "great voice." When a person comes into the world and innovates words of Torah, these are the very words he received at Sinai, which were never forgotten. This is "I will never forget Your precepts." The matter is that this spirituality is his soul, as said above: "With them You have given me life," for it is my soul and the life of my soul. This is "I am Yours, save me"—as we learned earlier, man asks for his soul. Wisdom is called "their heat" <note>original: "חמיהם"</note>. In truth, it is the "heat" (or light) of the Holy One, Blessed be He, but man brings it out from the darkness into the light. This belongs to the "Prince" <note>a high angel</note>, but I speak of it in my name because it must be my salvation; therefore I need Heavenly assistance, so I ask "Save me," for in truth "I have sought Your precepts"—the precepts "deposited" <note>a pun on *pikudecha* (precepts) and *mufkad* (deposited)</note> with You. Regarding the final verse which deals with the body and the material side, it says "The wicked have waited for me to destroy me"—these are the Evil Inclination and its legions who incite and lead astray. But there is a remedy for this: "But I will consider Your testimonies." Through the light of God, one is saved from this robbery. Finally, he concludes with the concept of the "great voice that did not cease": "I have seen an end to all perfection, but Your commandment is exceedingly broad."

# The Excellence of the One who Performs and Fulfills
## The commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes <note>Psalm 19:8</note>

->This verse speaks of the excellence of the Deed, while the verse before it speaks of the excellence of Study.<-
->Similarly, the Sages agreed: "Study is great because it leads to Action," as I have already written above.<-

<margin>
And it awakens the 248 <note>the numerical value of *Ramach*</note> limbs and spirituality in the secret that the Divine Presence is upon them... and this is explained in the *Zohar* and the Talmud: "The wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament" <note>Daniel 12:3</note>.
</margin>
The action is the core, for it is the ultimate purpose. Whatever they said about "Study being great," I have explained it all above in the first chapter... in a way that clarifies that the "remainder" (the goal) is the deed. For then a person's 248 limbs and 365 sinews are mentioned, as this constitutes the whole man. His soul is influenced by the secret of the 613 <note>original: "רי"ג" - the total number of commandments</note> roots of the soul's spirituality, based on the secret of "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>. "My Name" <note>Hebrew: *Shemi* (שמי)</note> with the letters *Yod-He* equals 365, and "My Memorial" <note>Hebrew: *Zikhri* (זכרי)</note> with *Vav-He* equals 248. This is explained at length in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*. Then his body is purified and becomes a "speculum" <note><term>Aspaqlarya: a visionary looking-glass or mirror</term></note>. It is said "The wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament," and the 22 [letters] shine in them when they keep them "at the end/heel" <note>original: *ekev rav* - a play on Psalm 19:11</note>. The sage Rabbi Shmuel Vidas explained: "Shine" is the language of "brightness," for the body is refined and glows. This is why it concludes with "In keeping them there is great reward" <note>Hebrew: *ekev rav*</note>. The care in performing commandments becomes so great that one merits the future world. This "Great Heel/Reward" refers to the state of Adam before he sinned, when the light of his skin and his heel outshone the sun. Regarding this, it says "The commandment of the Lord is pure"—referring to the choice, care, and purification of the person that causes the fulfillment of the commandment in deed. It says "Enlightening the eyes," hinting at what the Sages said: "Great is the power of the prophets, who liken the form to its Creator." The matter follows the verse "And all flesh shall see," and our Sages said: "In the way one comes to see, so one comes to be seen." Vision is like a speculum—a clear copper mirror—in which a man sees his own image. If the mirror is not dark on the other side, it is a "non-shining speculum" <note>original: "אספקלריא שאינה מאירה"</note>. If it were not so, the image of the viewer would not be captured there, but would pass through from one side to the other. All the prophets prophesied through a "non-shining speculum." Therefore, when they saw the glory of the Divine Presence—the aspect of "fear of seeing"—they saw their own image as they saw it there. When they completed the "measure of their stature" by fulfilling the 613 commandments in their 248 limbs and 365 sinews, the prophets rose and "saw" the Divine Presence in the "likeness of a man" <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>. This is the form of the very essence; it is the "Man" made in the image and likeness of God who is upon the Throne, as explained in the introduction to *Toldot Adam*. In truth, it is the Divine Presence appearing like a mirror where the form of man is seen, but in truth, it is the essence of the mirror itself. This is the meaning of "likening the form to its Creator." This is the secret of the Sages' saying: "There is no artist <note>Hebrew: *tzayyar* - also meaning "former" or "painter"</note> like our God; the Holy One, Blessed be He, forms a shape within a shape." But Moses our Teacher looked through a "shining speculum" <note>original: "אספקלריא המאירה"</note>. There was no interruption/barrier in his vision. Therefore, it is written "And he beholds the image <note>Hebrew: *temunah*</note> of the Lord" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>, and not "His image." This resolves the verse that says "Face to face the Lord spoke with you," implying there was no barrier, yet it also says "I stood between the Lord and you" <note>Deuteronomy 5:5</note>. There are several explanations for this, but it is resolved by what I wrote: for Moses, there was no barrier because he was using a shining speculum, where everything passes through from side to side. But other prophets saw through a non-shining speculum—the aspect of "fear of seeing"—where the way one comes to see is the way one is seen. This is the meaning of the verse "For they shall see eye to eye when the Lord returns to Zion" <note>Isaiah 52:8</note>, and this is "The commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes."

<summary>This page explores the mystical connection between the Ten Commandments and the Ten Sayings of Creation, asserting that man's spiritual and physical fulfillment of the 613 commandments allows him to transcend angelic status. It concludes by distinguishing Moses' direct "shining" prophetic vision from the self-reflective "non-shining" vision of other prophets.</summary>

# Tractate Shevu'ot

"God [saw] the light that it was good." Concerning this, I have already written above the distinction between *tov* [good] spelled with a *cholam* <note>The Hebrew vowel 'o' written as a dot above the letter.</note> and *tov* spelled with a *melafum* <note>Also known as Shuruk, the 'u' sound; the author is distinguishing between phonetic or mystical spelling variations.</note>. For *tov* with a *cholam* refers to the revealed good, while with a *melafum*, it refers to the character of the **hidden good**. And "Tobiah" <note>A name given to Moses in Midrashic tradition based on the verse "she saw that he was good."</note> with the addition of the letter *He* from the Name [of God], from which the entire Name was filled—this equals 14 and 5, which in <term>Gematria</term> <note>Jewish numerology where letters have numerical values.</note> equals 27, like the count of *Chai* <note>Meaning 'Life,' usually 18, but here likely referring to a specific mystical configuration of the number 27.</note>, which is the place of the prophecy of Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him: the <term>Luminous Mirror</term> <note>Original: *Aspaklaria Ham'ira*. A clear, direct prophetic vision, unlike other prophets who saw through a "dim mirror."</note>, the secret of the Hidden Light. 

Now I shall explain: Rabbi Meir says, "Good is his name." The intention is that in Moses, the purpose of creation was completed, and he, peace be upon him, was its ultimate goal. Therefore, he was in a state of peace and perfection from the day he was born. Rabbi Meir's opinion is that this is what the verse intended by saying, "And she saw him, that he was good" (Exodus 2:2). The meaning of "Good is his name" is that when speaking of his completed rectification, it is fitting that he be called by the name "Good." Since he is fundamentally good, that is his appropriate name, as it indicates a thing that is essentially perfect. To demonstrate this, the scripture did not follow the usual path of naming him [at birth], for usually a name does not fully reflect the essence of the thing named. Instead, it says, "and she saw him, that **he was good**"—meaning, the desired thing was completed and reached its final rectification, existing in its state of goodness, which *is* his name. Thus, Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, is the sum total of creation. 

Similarly, they said in the <term>Midrash</term> <note>A genre of rabbinic literature that interprets biblical texts.</note> on the word *Bereishit* [In the beginning]: "For the sake of Moses," as it says, "And he saw the beginning (*reishit*) for himself" (Deuteronomy 33:21). Behold, creation exists moment by moment by the Word; if the Holy One, blessed be He, were to withdraw His providence from it for even a single moment, everything would cease to be. So too was the prophecy of Moses our Teacher: because it represented the perfection of creation, the attainment of prophecy never ceased from him even for a single moment. 

Rabbi Judah says: "Good is his name" refers to <note>Original: *Lamesgus* (possibly a corrupted Greek or Latin term meaning "excellence" or "greatness").</note> the level of goodness mentioned by Rabbi Meir... and according to <term>Rashi</term> <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent medieval commentator.</note>, the secret of the Luminous Mirror, meaning without interruption, for the prophecy of Moses was attached to the Name <term>YHWH</term> <note>The four-letter Name of God, often associated with the attribute of Mercy and the highest level of revelation.</note> as is known, and he saw through the Luminous Mirror without any intermediary. Rabbi Nehemiah says: "He is fit for prophecy." This means his name is called "Good" because of the verse "And God saw the light, that it was **good**," and "God called the light Day." This is the meaning of "And she saw him, that he was good." 

Now, the words "him" (*oto*) and "he" (*hu*) in the verse seem redundant. However, the word *Hu* [He] refers to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often described in feminine terms in Kabbalah.</note>. As the <term>Zohar</term> <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note> explains on the verse "And it was evening and it was morning," she saw that he was fit for prophecy by day and not by night. Others say he was born already circumcised, which represents the perfection of the faculty of *Binah* [Understanding] without any loss of spirituality. We find a parallel to this in Abraham: before he was circumcised, it is written, "And Abraham fell on his face," but after he was circumcised, he did not [collapse in the presence of God]. Moses our Teacher, having been born circumcised, never lost any of his [spiritual] strength or sensation. And the Sages say: "The whole house was filled with light." This refers to the concentration of the four aforementioned levels of prophecy... the secret of "garments of light" <note>A pun on Genesis 3:21, where "garments of skin" (*or* with an *Ayin*) are transformed into "garments of light" (*or* with an *Aleph*).</note> which he will have in the future, like the "ray of light" (Exodus 34:29). Furthermore, "the house was filled with light" indicates that his entire "house"—meaning his soul and his body—was entirely light. The body is called a "house," as it is said, "the guard of his house."

---

->The secret of the excellence of Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him: and according to what we have written, he is a "window" for their souls, for the Torah was written by one who "stands between the Lord and us."<-

**"Grace is false and beauty is vain..."** (Proverbs 31:30). In the *Yalkut* Midrash: "Grace is false"—this refers to the grace of Noah; "Beauty is vain"—this is the beauty of Adam, whose heel eclipsed the orb of the sun, which You, O Lord, created first. And Moses, through whom this entire Name was filled, says: "Seek me out!" The matter is as follows: ...the Seven Noahide Commandments. It is found that "Grace" (*Chen*) ascended to a great level of power... and this is linked to <term>Metatron</term> <note>A high-ranking angel in mystical tradition, often associated with the celestial scribe or the heavenly priest.</note> who is greater than all the princes. The matter is as the Sages said at the end of the portion of *Bereishit*, that "Noah found grace (*chen*)," and likewise with Enoch... Metatron ascends to the Garden of Eden... "Grace is false," meaning this is not the ultimate level. "Beauty is vain"—the word "Vain" (*Hevel*) is the name of Abel, the son of Adam. All of it is the beauty of Adam, for Cain was born from the "nest of Samael" <note>The angelic name of the Accuser/Satan in Jewish thought.</note>, but Abel was the "mold" of Adam. He was reincarnated into Seth, and from Seth unto Moses, in the secret of the "70 souls." And the soul of Adam includes all souls. Therefore, "A woman who fears the Lord shall be praised"—this refers to Moses. 

I have already written above that the spirituality of the Torah is the sum of all souls. The Torah is perfect... 100 verses, and 180 of Talmud, and 100 of the Secrets of the Torah... the Torah begins with the letter *Kaf* and ends with *Lamed*... the letters of *HaKol* [Everything/All]. One will not find the extent of his prophecy... the six orders of the <term>Mishnah</term> <note>The first major written collection of the Jewish oral traditions.</note> are the letters of "The Name." This is the "hundred secrets of the Torah," for the attachment of his prophecy was to the Name **YHWH**, which includes all of <term>Atzilut</term> <note>The World of Emanation, the highest of the four spiritual worlds in Kabbalah.</note>. Just as in *Atzilut* we are permitted to use a metaphor for the Emanation in relation to the Luminary above... the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him in a "flame of fire," which is the secret of the flame that rises on its own. Also, the great matter of "The Lord, God of Israel"... Moses our Teacher's name equals 613 [in Gematria], and the Holy One said to Moses, "Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear..."

**Concerning** what was said that "Abel is the beauty of Adam whose heel eclipsed the orb of the sun"—it was already said that "The face of Moses was like the face of the sun." If his heel eclipsed the sun, how much more so his face! For there is a difference between the "orb of the sun" and the sun's actual power. "The face of Moses like the face of the sun" hints that he dwelled in a high place, the secret of <term>Tiferet</term> <note>The Sefirah of Beauty or Harmony, often associated with the Written Torah and Moses.</note>. Now, there is a great difficulty: Israel is compared to the moon and the nations to the sun. Is the sun's level not superior? And the proof is that Moses' face was like the sun! It says in the *Zohar* that the "face of the sun" refers to the sun in its circuit... as the wicked are described in Ecclesiastes. But the level of the sun "standing still" is a great level for Israel, as in "the sun stood still in Gibeon." This level is elevated... where God says to other prophets "In a dream I will speak to him," but "Not so my servant Moses... mouth to mouth I speak to him" (Numbers 12:7-8). Rashi explains "mouth to mouth" as "Stand here with Me." This is a great hint: since your prophecy is like the sun, and your face like the face of the sun—what aspect of the sun? The aspect of "Stand here with Me," which is the sun standing still, not its circuit.

**However**, it remains for me to explain why he called Moses by the name of a "Woman" in the verse "A woman who fears the Lord." It says in the Midrash: "When He finished (*ke-challoto*) speaking with him" (Exodus 31:18)—the word is read as "His bride" (*ke-challato*). This implies the Torah was given to him like a bride. These two Midrashic interpretations are one: "He gave him general principles" refers to the Gematria of Moses... and after he received the Oral Torah, and the Holy One informed him of the explanations of the commandments, he became like an "ever-strengthening spring" of analysis. Thus, he is the Master of the Talmud, and the Torah is called by his name, "Remember the Torah of Moses my servant." The Written Torah is called the "Torah of the Lord" regarding its words, letters, and crowns, which the Lord gave—he did not add or subtract, Heaven forbid. But the Oral Torah, which he increased through his analysis as "words of the Living God," is called by his name. It requires memory because it was not [originally] permitted to be written down. It is known that the Written Torah and Oral Torah are *Tiferet* and *Malchut* <note>The masculine and feminine divine emanations.</note>, called "Man" and "Woman." The attachment of Moses' prophecy was from *Tiferet*, and he is the Master of the Talmud; he is, so to speak, the "Man of God" and the "Husband of the Matron" <note>A bold kabbalistic term suggesting Moses was "married" to the Shekhinah (the Divine Presence/Oral Torah).</note>. Therefore, the Oral Torah is the Bride of Moses. Moses our Teacher separated from his physical wife and "took" this woman [the Torah]. According to what we said, that the Oral Torah is a woman from Seth... this explains the verse "Go say to them: Return to your tents, but you, stand here with Me." I will also explain the passage "For he had married a Cushite woman." Some commentators say that the call to Moses was because, through him, prophecy rested upon Aaron and Miriam. They were not [initially] prepared... just as with the seventy elders... through Moses, the light of prophecy appeared to them, and without Moses, they could not receive it. This explains Joshua's jealous anger at those prophesying in the camp... they established a place for themselves as if they were separate from him. This answers the question of why Joshua was zealous for Moses' prophecy—he feared they were implying prophecy could be received without Moses.

It explains Moses' unique relationship with the Oral Torah, describing it as his "bride" and the reason for his separation from his physical wife.</summary>

# Tractate Shevu'ot 199

Regarding what is written about "a good purchase" <note>Referencing the Talmudic saying in Berakhot 5a: "I have given you a good purchase (Torah), do not forsake it."</note> and the blessing of one's property... see Rashi's commentary. The general principle is that one should ensure their fellow is not harmed through them. Behold, in a worldly purchase, if the buyer is happy, the seller is often sad <note>Because he lost the item</note>. However, in the "purchase" of the Torah, everyone is equally satisfied. To know if a purchase is truly good, it is revealed through the "broker’s fee." The "broker" here refers to the mediator who makes an agreement with the buyer to receive a tenth of the profit, or more. When it is seen that the broker receives a large portion, it is revealed that the purchase is truly excellent. 

Behold, "the Torah is light" (Proverbs 6:23), for the profit of the Torah-purchase is the **Hidden Light**. Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, took a small portion of this profit in this world, for "the skin of his face radiated" (Exodus 34:29). By this, we can know how good the purchase of the Torah is. 

In contrast to a worldly purchase, which is not safe from robbers or can be lost, the Torah is different. One might say, "But there are fields and vineyards" <note>as collateral</note>; here too, there is "property security." Silver and gold a person can take with him, and there is a virtue in this that is not in that. Regarding the idea that the seller is usually sad, it is said that the Giver of the Torah is happy, for—as it were—He is "sold" along with the purchase <note>A famous Midrash suggests God says: "I have sold you my Torah, and I have been sold along with it."</note>. He sells with a "generous eye" and gives with a spirit of contentment, for "I have spoken and My will was done." "The Lord shall rejoice in His works" (Psalm 104:31). 

"Now, let the power of the Lord be great" (Numbers 14:17)—as it were, humans add power to the Divine, which is the opposite of "You weakened the Rock who birthed you" (Deuteronomy 32:18). Choice is given to human beings, though "everything is in the hands of Heaven except [the fear of Heaven]." This is why one "cannot do" anything without that ultimate virtue upon which the two previous matters depend. This is the meaning of "And they shall take for Me an offering" (Exodus 25:2)—as it were, "it is Me you are taking," for the Tabernacle is the dwelling of the Torah, and it is called the "Tabernacle of Testimony" because the Tablets were there. 

It is thus explained that "I have given you a good purchase." He said: "Do not forsake the purchase I gave you," meaning My Torah. This refers specifically to the purchase and is not a separate matter. Otherwise, there would be a contradiction between "purchase" <term>Lekach</term> <note>Something bought or taken</note> and "giving" <term>Netinyahu</term> <note>Something given freely</note>. But if the word "Torah" refers to the Higher Realm, then it is settled: for in truth it is a "giving," as it is written, "For the Lord gives wisdom" (Proverbs 2:6). However, there is a "giving of contentment" and "strength to the Supernal Might," and then it is considered a "purchase," for—as it were—He "purchased" the contentment. This is "And they shall take for Me," for He is sold with it.

## The Virtue of "These and Those are the Words of the Living God"

<margin>The giving of the Torah depends on man, regarding the formula "The Giver of the Torah." All of this belongs here; we shall return to the matter of the six verses mentioned above.</margin>

<margin>**"The judgments of the Lord are true; they are righteous altogether"** (Psalm 19:10)</margin>

It is clear from this verse that all [opinions] are true, and even when there is a dispute, "they are righteous altogether," for "these and those are the words of the living God." This matter requires explanation, and as I have explained with God's help at length, breadth, and depth in the introduction to *Toldot Adam* regarding the formula of "The Giver of the Torah." All of that is relevant here. 

Let us return to the six verses: "The law of the Lord is perfect," etc. Since the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a covenant with us through the Oral Torah—as our Sages taught regarding the verse "For by the mouth of these words I have made a covenant" (Exodus 34:27)—I will divide these six verses according to the **Six Orders of the Mishnah**. 

In every verse, He mentions His Name (YHVH). The Name YHVH technically has only three distinct letters (Y, H, V) because the 'H' is doubled. These correspond to the **Six Seals** mentioned in *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The Book of Formation, an early mystical text</note>, Chapter 1. As it is taught there: "He chose three letters... and sealed the six directions." 
1. He turned Upwards and sealed it with Y-H-V. 
2. He turned Downwards and sealed it with Y-V-H. 
3. He turned East and sealed it with H-Y-V. 
4. He turned West and sealed it with H-V-Y. 
5. He turned South and sealed it with V-Y-H. 
6. He turned North and sealed it with V-H-Y. 

Corresponding to this are the six orders. "The law of the Lord is perfect" follows the Name YHVH. See *Sha'arei Ora* and *Sefer Yetzirah* regarding the six seals of Y-V-W <note>a variant of the name</note>, which are Height, Depth, East, West, North, and South. Against these are **Six Holinesses**:

<margin>1. The Supreme Holiness: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts." 
2. The holiness of Israel: They are sanctified with two holinesses: forbidden foods ("And you shall be holy men to Me; you shall not eat torn flesh") and forbidden sexual relations ("You shall be holy," and Rabbi [Judah the Prince] says: "Wherever you find a fence against immorality, you find holiness"). 
3. Three holinesses: Sabbath, Festivals, and Yom Kippur ("a holy convocation"). 
4. The holiness of Israel and the seasons. 
5. The holiness of the Sanctuary: the holiness of the value and the body of offerings (Lesser Holies and Most Holy). 
6. Holiness in species: regarding the Holy Shekel.</margin>

<margin>And according to this, what we wrote above on page 143 will be understood; see there.</margin>

Regarding this, the explanation of the four orders is as follows: "The law of the Lord is perfect" refers to the purity and beauty by which our Creator, may He be blessed, sanctified us to be holy and pure. So it is written: "Do not make yourselves detestable" and "Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy." This entire statement refers to the "External" <note>The physical world or the external aspects of the commandments</note>, whose details and beautification must be handled with utmost care. This is the seal of **Height** and **South**. 

*   A blessing over food (Tithes, *Orlah* <note>fruit of young trees</note>, First Fruits)—all this is the **Holiness of Food**. This is the seal of **Below**, for "as the earth brings forth its growth." 
*   The Order of *Nashim* (Women) is the **Holiness of Intimacy**. This is the seal of **East**, for "from the East I will bring your seed." 
*   The Kabbalists wrote that the Order of *Moed* (Festivals) is the **Holiness of Time**, which is associated with the sunset, for that is when the day begins, and the sun sets in the **West**. 
*   *Nezikin* (Damages) is the **Holiness of Wealth**, and "one who wishes to become wise [or wealthy] should turn North." This is the Order of "Salvation." 

There is another hint in the Mishnah of *Sefer Yetzirah* regarding the six seals: they represent the parts of Study, Action, and Character Traits, around which this entire work revolves.

<margin>"A commandment is a lamp, and Torah is light, and the way of life is the rebuke of discipline" (Proverbs 6:23)</margin>

It is known that the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world. All of creation consists of three dimensions: **Length, Breadth, and Depth**. These three are found in the Torah. 
1. "Broader than the sea" (Job 11:9)—these are the Laws (*Dinim*). 
2. "Longer than the earth in measure"—these are the Character Traits (*Middot*). 
3. "Deeper than the abyss"—this is the Study (*Shema'ata*). 

These are three from the perspective of the Giver, and three from the perspective of the Receiver. The seals of **Height** and **Depth** represent **Depth**. Toward the Holy One, "Height" is as we say "It rose in His thought," and its manifestation is "Below." The depth of the Law is from **East** to **West**, which is **Length**, meaning the Character Traits. These are called "Front" and "Back." From the side of the East... they are called "Front" and "East." Conversely, in the attributes of the Holy One, they are called "Back," as it is written, "And you shall see My back" (Exodus 33:23). The three dimensions from **North** to **South** are **Breadth**, meaning the Commandments. They are "Right" and "Left." The Holy One, Blessed be He, wraps Himself in a *Tallit* and dons *Tefillin* and the like—these are spiritual matters, the right and the left.

The interpretation is that the Lord returned to the Torah of the Lord, His desire... "The law of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul"—what the soul receives from the tradition. "The testimony of the Lord is sure"—this is the Oral Torah... making wise the simple. "The precepts of the Lord are right"—even though it is written "visiting the guilt of the fathers," His ways are upright and rejoice the heart of the one who turns from evil. It descends from Above only to return. From our side, the second commandment was to learn, "enlightening the eyes"—this is the general knowledge of the commandments. "The fear of the Lord is pure"—when we focus our eyes to know matters, "enduring forever." "The judgments of the Lord are true"—the law is spoken in its truth.

<margin>**"More desirable"**</margin>
**"More desirable** than gold, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb." Our Sages, of blessed memory, explained this until the verse says: "O how I love Your law! It is my meditation all the day" (Psalm 119:97). This means that with all physical things, like honey, "once you have had your fill, you stop eating." But the Torah is so beloved to me that even though it is my meditation all day long, I never tire of it. Regarding this, he said it is "sweeter than honey." Furthermore, it can be explained that there is **External Desire** and **Internal Desire**. External desire is for things seen by the eye, like silver, gold, and precious stones. Internal desire is for eating and drinking. As the verse says: "The tree was good for food [internal] and a delight to the eyes [external]." So too, the Torah has a Revealed aspect and a Secret aspect. Of the **Revealed** (visible to the eyes), he says: "More desirable than gold." And of the **Internal/Secret**, he says: "Sweeter than honey and the honeycomb."

---
->The chapter "Torah is Light" is completed<-

### Chapter: The Way of Life is the Rebuke of Discipline

<margin>The explanation of "Face to face the Lord spoke," etc.</margin>
One should meditate on the standing at Mount Sinai as if we were all there and received the Torah. Blessed is He who separated us from those who err and gave us the Torah of truth, planting eternal life within us. One should consider that "Face to face the Lord spoke with us" (Deuteronomy 5:4). One should think of the oath we swore, for we are all "oath-bound and standing" from Mount Sinai. One should think of many such things until he is filled with trembling and quaking, a heart of awe. He should make a strong resolve that "now, on this very day, I have received the Torah." He should fix in his heart a deep love for God, to serve Him with joy and goodness of heart.

This festival is called the **Festival of Shavuot** <note>Weeks/Oaths</note>. The root is "Seven" (*Sheva*). The initials of its names are **S**havuot, **B**ikkurim, **A**tzeret. Look at what I wrote above: this festival is unique because at the Giving of the Torah (which happened on the Sabbath), the secret of **Three Sabbaths** was joined: the Sabbath of Creation, the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah, and the Sabbath of the World to Come (which is entirely Sabbath). It is truly the "Great Sabbath." The matter of the Sabbath of Creation points to the seven days of Creation, and the obligation of the counting of seven weeks... points to the secrets of creation. Therefore, it is called the Festival that includes the **Weeks** (*Shavuot*). Afterwards, it is called **First Fruits** (*Bikkurim*), corresponding to the Giving of the Torah, when they brought the Two Loaves of wheat... the Two Loaves correspond to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. Afterwards, it is called **Assembly** (*Atzeret*).

It concludes with a meditative guide on the spiritual significance of the holiday of Shavuot as a reenactment of the Sinai experience.</summary>

# Tractate Shevu'ot
## And in Tractate Shabbat

In the chapter titled "Rabbi Akiva" on page 86 <note>original: "Perek R. Akiva, Daf 86" in Tractate Shabbat</note>, the Sages said that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, separated from his wife of his own mind <note>meaning, by his own reasoning rather than a direct command</note>, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him, as it is written: "But as for you, stand here by Me" (Deuteronomy 5:28). The *Tosafot* <note>medieval French and German commentators on the Talmud</note> questioned there: How do we know that Moses separated of his own mind before he heard God speaking with him? Perhaps this was a complete command that God gave him to separate? Rabbenu Tam <note>a leading 12th-century scholar</note> wrote on this—see there. To me, it settles well, because after Moses exerted himself in the Torah and cleaved to the "Woman" mentioned above <note>a mystical reference to the Torah or the Divine Presence</note>, it was of his own will and through his own choice. For "all is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven" <note>a famous Talmudic maxim</note>, as choice is given to man. Then, the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed and commanded him to separate from his physical wife. And it is through the imagination of this matter that all those things he did are answered.

The Tanna <note>Sage of the Mishnah era</note> taught there: Three things Moses did of his own mind, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him. He added one day [to the preparation for receiving the Torah] of his own mind; he separated from his wife; and he shattered the Tablets.

**He added one day of his own mind:** What was his interpretation? "Today and tomorrow" (Exodus 19:10). Just as tomorrow includes its preceding night, so too "today" must include its night. But since the night of this day has already passed, we learn from this that there must be two full days excluding this one. How do we know God agreed with him? For the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shechinah"</note> did not descend until the morning of the Sabbath.

**He separated from his wife:** What was his interpretation? He performed an *a fortiori* <note>term: a fortiori (Kal Vachomer) - a logical inference that if a rule applies in a minor case, it must apply even more so in a major case</note> argument within himself. He said: If the people of Israel, with whom the Divine Presence spoke for only one hour and for a fixed time, the Torah still said to them, "Be ready for three days; do not go near a woman"—then I, with whom the Divine Presence speaks at every hour and without a fixed time, how much more so should I separate! How do we know God agreed with him? For it is written: "Go say to them: Return to your tents" (Deuteronomy 5:27), and it is written immediately after: "But as for you, stand here by Me."

**He shattered the Tablets:** What was his interpretation? He said: If the Passover offering, which is but one of the 613 commandments, the Torah says of it: "No stranger [apostate] shall eat of it" (Exodus 12:43)—then the entire Torah, while Israel are currently apostates <note>due to the sin of the Golden Calf</note>, how much more so! How do we know God agreed with him? As it is said: "[The tablets] which you shattered" (Exodus 34:1), and Resh Lakish said: "May your strength be firm <note>original: "Yasher Kochacha"</note> because you shattered them."

The *Tosafot* wrote that this is not a "perfect" interpretation <note>original: "derasha gemura"</note>, but rather it implies "today" literally, for if it were not so, it would not be "of his own mind." Furthermore, the *Tosafot* ask regarding "If Israel... etc.": You might ask, why is it called "acting of his own mind" if it is a law of the Torah? For an *a fortiori* argument is a valid way to derive Torah law. One can answer that it is not a "perfect" *a fortiori* argument, for there it was because of the Ten Commandments... see there. They also wrote regarding "If the Passover...": This is not a perfect *a fortiori* argument because if an apostate is forbidden during the hour of the sacrifice, he still should not have withheld the Torah from them, but rather brought them to repentance. Further, they wrote regarding "But as for you, stand here by Me": If you ask why it is called "acting of his own mind" since God told him? They answered what they answered.

But it seems to me that the explanation of these three things can be understood in two ways: From the side of the choice given to him, Moses caused himself to separate thus, and it was "good in the eyes of the Lord," and He agreed. To this, I will preface two short introductions:

1. It is written, "Serve the Lord with fear" (Psalm 2:11) and it is written, "Serve the Lord with joy" (Psalm 100:2). A person must fear and worry that perhaps he is falling short in the service of the Name, and the awe must be upon him so that he does not become lazy in any commandment—this is "Serve the Lord with fear." But at the time of the service and the performance of the commandment, he should do it with a whole heart, with agility and joy, as it is written: "Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a good heart" (Deuteronomy 28:47)—this is "Serve the Lord with joy."

2. The second introduction is also included in "serving God with joy," and it is what I explained elsewhere on the verse: "How fair and how pleasant you are, O love with delights" (Song of Songs 7:7). The explanation is that there is great pleasantness and beauty in how we are beloved to God by fulfilling His commandments, which are "delights." There are commandments of action that are a burden to fulfill, such as fasting on Yom Kippur or giving charity, and regarding these, "the reward is according to the pain." But to receive a reward for commandments that are *delights*—such as delighting in the Sabbath or fulfilling the commandment of procreation <note>original: "Pru Urvu"</note>—this is a "special endearment." Thus, we are not only servants of God from a place of fear, but we become servants of God even when fulfilling commandments that involve joy.

According to the first introduction, it is clear why Moses added a day of his own mind...

<margin>
It appears there is a secret: that Fear is a vessel for all rectification. Furthermore, there was a secret regarding the Divine Presence, and this is sufficient for the wise.
</margin>

...And we learned from the greatness of the reward of one who engages in procreation. Behold, Moses learned an *a fortiori* argument: "If Israel, with whom the Divine Presence did not speak... etc." And the *Tosafot* questioned this as above. But the matter is that "words of Torah do not contract ritual impurity" <note>Berakhot 22a</note>. Moses saw that holy Israelites are holy during the time of intimacy and intend in their union to awaken the **Higher Union** <note>a mystical concept where physical acts on earth mirror spiritual alignments in heaven</note> to draw down holy souls. And especially when God fixed a time of holiness for them, so that there would be no accidental emission—which is evil resulting from "lightheadedness"—but only holiness to awaken a great awakening of the Higher Union. Despite all this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not want them to be in a state of union when receiving the Written and Oral Torah, which is itself the Higher Union.

Moses said: If so, all the more so I, whose holiness is greater and more constant, am obligated to separate from the lower union and be attached to the upper union always. And so it was in truth... and therefore the *a fortiori* argument that Moses made was good and beautiful. For it is a perfect argument: "If Israel, who need to draw down holy souls through a lower union... and even so God did not want them to be in a union below... I, whose holiness is very great and do not need to add souls, for I am equal to all of Israel... how much more so should I separate from union." And the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him and said: "But as for you, stand here by Me."

These two are "of his own mind" from the aspect of action. The third is the aspect of study, which was Moses' choice to choose the holiness of the Torah and not to cleave to its holiness unless the "filth of sins" was removed. As it is said: "But to the wicked, God says: What right have you to recite My laws?" (Psalm 50:16). Just as by law one is forbidden to study Torah near excrement, so too it is forbidden to study near the "excrement of sins." Therefore, he shattered the Tablets until they repented. These three were from Moses' own mind—meaning, from his choice. Thus, I have explained a bit of the dominion of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the "broker" through whom the Torah was given.

---

->And the choice of the holy broker served as the purchase of the Torah:<-

# In the Midrash
Rabbah, Portion of Terumah: "'That they take for Me an offering' (Exodus 25:2). This is what is written: 'For I have given you a good purchase; do not forsake My Torah' (Proverbs 4:2). Do not forsake the purchase I have given you. There is a man who buys a purchase... until it is said, 'And let them make Me a sanctuary.'" We must contemplate how this connects to "a good purchase" and what benefit there is in the reversal of "do not forsake the purchase I have given you." Also, why does it elaborate on imaginary matters like debt and Torah?

The general matter is that the "purchase" of the Torah is higher in quality than the purchase of worldly matters in three ways, for there are three types of liability in a worldly purchase:
1. Who knows if it is a "good purchase," or if it was just called that?
2. Even if it is a good purchase, who knows if it is guarded? Perhaps robbers will come.
3. It can be measured...
