<header>Tractate Taanit</header>

The verse states, "The virgin of Israel shall rise again" <note>original: "תוסיף קום בתולת ישראל"</note>, but "fallen" is also said, as in "The crown of our head has fallen," referring to the Sanhedrin <note>The supreme religious and judicial body in ancient Israel</note>. It is written in the accounts here, "The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground..." and similarly in the verse regarding the fall, it mentions the "virgin." This stems from the strength of the spirit, and in place of the "Daughter of Zion," we find the "Daughter of Babylon, the devastated." However, King David hinted that "The Lord supports <note>Hebrew: *Somekh*</note> all those who fall," and the numerical value of "supports" (*Somekh*) is equal to the name of the angel of death <note>The author uses gematria to link the support of the fallen to the ultimate victory over death</note>. It is written, "They collapsed and fell, but we arose..." and after the construction of the spirit, they are bound to the prophecy of the "hidden and revealed," mentioning the merit of Abraham and the merit of Jacob. To them, the matter of the subjugation to the foreign kingdoms was revealed as a "good tidings" regarding eternity. There is also a secret regarding the length of the exile and what the Sadducees thought—to break the oath. See the commentary of Rabbi David Luria <note>An 18th-century scholar</note> on the verse "He who weakens the nations," regarding the acts of King Nebuchadnezzar with other kings, and how he even sought to do so to King Zedekiah. The Kabbalists say that here the male soul is reincarnated in a rabbit; therefore, Zedekiah wanted to restore it because the spark was in a cycle of returning in body and soul. This is the truth: just as bodies are scattered, so too souls are driven and wander from "push to push." See the Rosh Chodesh prayer in the Cordovero prayer book <note>The *Siddur* of Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, a leading 16th-century Kabbalist</note> regarding the phrase "and gather our dispersed," and the blessing "Sound the great shofar for our freedom." For just as the soul of the king of the nations is scattered from its true path—as in the case of Nebuchadnezzar—so too the souls of Israel who have sinned wander and are pushed from their true, proper path, each according to their bitterness. The portions of *Mattot* and *Masei* hint at this through their secrets. For the perfect enlightenment that was prepared for your hearts in the Land of Israel—meaning the body in the earthly Land of Israel and the souls in the heavenly Land of Israel, the "Desirable Land"—is where the Torah concludes, because afterward begins the "Repetition of the Torah" <note>The Book of Deuteronomy</note>. Thus come the hints: "If a man vows a vow" <note>Numbers 30:3</note> hints at the souls. A "vow" (*Neder*) comes from the level of *Binah* (Understanding), as it is written, "The breath of the Almighty gives them understanding." This is the secret of a "new soul." An "oath" (*Shevuah*) is that which is already sworn and established, referring to a "reincarnated soul." The matter of the oath and the vow is as our Sages said: "For to Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear," and I have elaborated elsewhere on this discourse. The verse "That which passes your lips you shall observe" and the verse "Better that you should not vow" and the verse "If a man vows a vow" mentions "he shall not break" and mentions "according to all that proceeds from his mouth he shall do"—this refers to both the positive and negative commandments. But afterward, regarding a woman, it only mentions the negative, because she is exempt from time-bound positive commandments. This is the purpose of the souls coming into this world, and the root of corruption causes exile for the bodies. Nevertheless, the souls are also driven and scattered. Then another oath takes effect, which the Holy One, Blessed be He, made us swear, and we accepted it as an oath: not to "force the end" <note>A traditional concept of not prematurely attempting to bring the Messiah through human action</note>. This divine matter is found in the *Book of the Palaces* <note>Sefer Heikhalot, an early Jewish mystical text</note>, where they say "Strong One of Israel, permit, permit..." And behold, the Assembly of Israel is compared to a woman, as it says, "For your Maker is your husband." The Holy One is, so to speak, the husband, who returns to forgive and establish, all on "the day he hears." The Zohar has already written on the verse "All the day she is faint," that destruction was decreed for a year, which is a "day" of the Holy One <note>Based on the idea that one divine day equals 1,000 years</note>. For even in exile we are called "children," as the Sages said: "Woe to the children who were exiled from their father's table." The Assembly of Israel is a wife, but the Holy One changes us through the "Breastplate"—that is, the ministering angel of the nations in this world. And what we learned about "one who leaves his wife in the care of a third party," and the "vow of a widow or a divorcee," Heaven forbid it should stand... but it is written, "She was like a widow," but not a literal widow. It is written, "Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement?" and "She shall return to her father's house." Afterward, the text begins to tell of the conquest of Midian and the division of the Land, the gift and the strength. Regarding the conquest of the Land and the division, I have already written that the lower Land of Israel is the place of the body's holiness, corresponding to the heavenly Land of Israel, the place of the soul's holiness. May it be His will that we merit this, Amen.

## Discourse on Mattot and Masei

**"A**nd not one man of us is missing." "We will pass over armed." "These are the journeys of the children of Israel." Regarding the matter of the journeys, it is difficult to understand: for what practical purpose were they mentioned? Regarding the discourse of Rabbi Meir, it is difficult from the case of the *Sotah* <note>The woman suspected of infidelity</note> which existed in their time. I read concerning them: "The clouds of glory accompanied them." Regarding "And these are their journeys according to their starting places," the repetition is difficult, as is the reversal of the language. Furthermore, it is difficult that several places are mentioned here—such as Zalmonah and Punon—which were not mentioned at the time they occurred. "And the Canaanite, king of Arad, heard," yet the scripture does not mention what followed from his hearing. Four journeys were made wandering in the desert.

<margin>These are the journeys</margin> In Tractate Rosh Hashanah: The Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) made ten journeys: from the cover of the Ark to the Keruv, from the Keruv to the threshold, from the threshold to the court, from the court to the altar, from the altar to the roof, from the roof to the wall, from the wall to the city, from the city to the mountain, and from the mountain to the desert. From the desert, it ascended and sat in its place, as it is said: "I will go and return to My first place." Corresponding to these, the Sanhedrin was exiled. There is a reason for their conduct in the nature of these journeys. In Lamentations Rabbah: "In fierce anger, He has cut off every horn of Israel." There are ten horns: the horn of Abraham, the horn of Isaac, the horn of Joseph, the horn of Moses, the horn of the Torah, the horn of the Priesthood, the horn of the Levites, the horn of Prophecy, the horn of the Holy Temple, and the horn of Israel. Some say also the horn of the Messiah. All of them were placed upon the head of Israel, but when they sinned, they were taken from them—this is "He has cut off in fierce anger every horn of Israel"—and given to the nations of the world. Regarding the eleventh horn <note>original: "קרן יא"</note>, it is written "which had eyes in its head," etc. When Israel performs repentance (*Teshuvah*), the Holy One returns them to their place, as it says: "All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up." We must know the world's need for these horns. When does He return them to their place? When the Holy One exalts the horn of His Messiah, as it is written: "He will give strength to His king and exalt the horn of His Messiah." It is difficult to say that the horns of the Patriarchs, the Torah, Priesthood, and Levites were given to the nations—are there priests and Levites among them? And Prophecy? Did not Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, ask, "That I and Your people be distinguished"? Rather, what was written is that they were removed when the pillars of the world were found. There are ten levels of holiness, which are three sets of three, and the tenth is holy to the Lord. They are: the three pillars of the world according to Shimon the Righteous—Torah, Service, and Acts of Loving-kindness; and remember the three of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel—Justice, Truth, and Peace; and the three common practices—Repentance, Prayer, and Charity. You can find them in one verse as a discourse: "And the tenth shall be holy to the Lord," the secret of Faith. It is seen at the end of Tractate Makkot: Habakkuk came and established them upon one principle, as it is said, "But the righteous shall live by his faith." "But because of our sins we were exiled from our land," etc., for Israel transgressed all of them. Regarding Torah, it is written: "And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken My Torah," and "Would that they had forsaken Me but kept My Torah, for the light within it would have returned them to the good." Regarding Service, it is written: "To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?" and "They offer incense to vanities." Regarding Acts of Loving-kindness, it is written in Hosea: "For there is no truth and no kindness." "The men of truth have perished." Justice: as it is written, "Your princes are rebellious," and "the cause of the widow does not reach them." Truth: as it is written, "And truth is missing." Peace: "Behold, for peace I had great bitterness," and because of the sin of "baseless hatred," the Second Temple was destroyed. Repentance: all the prophets warned "Rising early and sending." Prayer: "Even when you make many prayers, I will not hear," and "Do not pray for this people." Charity: "Hearken to me, you stout-hearted, who are far from charity." "Stout-hearted" refers to the wicked. And it is written, "Not in truth and not in charity." They denied His faith and committed idolatry. These ten horns correspond to these ten qualities: Abraham is "Kindness to Abraham," "I have lifted my hand to God Most High... who bestows good kindness." Isaac is the attribute of Justice and the "Fear of Isaac." Joseph is the Covenant of Peace. Moses is Truth, "trusted in all My house" and the "faithful shepherd." Torah is literal. Priesthood is Service. Levites is the commandment of Charity, for even a poor person who receives must give, and a Levite gives a tithe of the tithe. The Holy Temple is the place of Prayer. Israel—and some say Messiah—"On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one." (If we had listened to the voice of our teachers and followed in their footsteps... now the horns have been taken and given to them—God forbid—for through them we are driven toward these horns. This is what Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer in chapter *Chelek*: "If they do not repent, they are not redeemed, but the Holy One raises up a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel repents and returns to the good." Therefore, the removal of the ring was greater than the prophecy... and in the future, "I will restore your judges as at the first.") Behold, the Divine Presence and the leadership moved between places and were removed—namely, from Shiloh to Nob, to Gibeon, and to the Eternal House <note>The Temple in Jerusalem</note>. The sign is "for he was punished," as it is written "Remember the world." The First Temple and the Second Temple... and the removal of the horns each time. This is the reason the letter *Nun* was not mentioned by David in the *Ashrei* prayer <note>Psalm 145</note>. Afterward, it is hinted: "The Lord supports (*Somekh*) all those who fall," as seen in the first chapter of Berakhot. Behold, the name *ADNL*... regarding the inverted *Nuns* in the Torah: one *Nun* is a sign of life in the journey, and the other *Nun* is a sign of the departure of prophecy. It is said, what became of their souls from the "House of Prayer"? It is the restoration. "Your iniquity is finished..." A Psalm of Asaph: "O God, the nations have come into Your inheritance." The Gemara asks: it should have said "A Lamentation of Asaph." But in truth, the lamentation causes the psalm. "The Lord has supported me," for He has exhausted His wrath on wood and stones—this refers to the souls of Ruth and David. For "He exhausted His wrath" <note>Hebrew: *Kilah Chamato*</note> is the language of Ruth and the language of "Exaltation" (*Romemut*), causing the exaltation so that "the children of iniquity shall no longer afflict them," and "Great shall be the glory of this latter house." And our fast days will be turned to joy. Then the "Hidden One" will return. Why is the month of Av called a "Moed" (Festival)? Because it coincides with the day of Passover. Therefore, "And it came to pass when the Ark set forward..." and the reversal of the *Vav* and the *Nun*... according to the word of the Lord they journeyed and according to the word of the Lord they camped. They journeyed from the *Nun* and returned to the *Gimel*. Behold, these verses were said by Moses, for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him...

# Discourse for the Torah Portions of Mattot and Masei

This discourse concerns the First Temple and how the Rebuke <note>original: *Tochacha*; the sections of the Torah containing warnings of punishment</note> in the book of Deuteronomy refers to the Second Temple. Regarding this later Rebuke, our Sages of blessed memory said that Moses spoke it "from his own mouth" <note>Moses delivered the warnings in Deuteronomy in the first person, though still under Divine inspiration, unlike the warnings in Leviticus which are spoken directly by God</note>. I have written elsewhere regarding the verse "Moses spoke from his own mouth" and the discussion of Israel regarding the Torah. Israel is bound as one "cord," for after the initial destruction, the power of the Rebuke continues in this world. This explains the book of Deuteronomy, where Moses says, "You are standing today," for even your failures sustain you. Afterwards comes the portion "And this is the Blessing." The secret of the matter is that the "feet" are the blessings. It is said there are one hundred curses minus two <note>referring to the 98 curses in Deuteronomy</note>, and some ask why it is not a full hundred. However, even if specifically it seems to lack two, they are still considered a hundred when one includes the general phrase "and every sickness and every plague which is not written" <note>Deuteronomy 28:61</note>. This is what the *Rokeach* <note>Rabbi Eleazar of Worms, a 12th-13th century scholar</note> wrote. These hundred curses are subsumed within the secret of the "One Hundred Blessings" <note>A Jewish practice to recite 100 blessings daily</note>. The entire matter revolves around our central point: that the troubles caused by the foreign kingdoms are for our ultimate good and are the essence of our <term>Tikkun<gloss>rectification/restoration</gloss></term>. In this way, "by our being killed, we become merits," and the "evil angel" is forced to answer "Amen."

Now I will explain the concept of "a lion against a lion," which is a transformation similar to a fruit and its peel; the peel is what protects and rectifies it. Behold, the destruction of the Land was carried out by "N.B." <note>Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylon</note>, who is the "nakedness" of the land. Through the power of this nakedness, the Land "vomited" its inhabitants. I explained elsewhere the secret of the verse, "He is a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in secret places" <note>Lamentations 3:10</note>. This was fulfilled through Nebuchadnezzar, who descended from the "arm of David" called the "lion." This occurred when Solomon lay with the Queen of Sheba and she conceived; from that seed came Nebuchadnezzar. Jeremiah was a reincarnation of the soul of Solomon. Our Sages asked about a union that is not on the side of holiness: "Just as a lion has strength and tramples, so too the common person..." Therefore, he was like a lion.

The "Keri" <note>the way a word is read vs. written</note> is "Bear" (*Dov*), and it is written *Db*.
All is truth regarding the Bear.

Our teacher Moses (M"R) is a hint and a rectification.
He teaches the Torah.
The 6th of Sivan <note>The holiday of Shavuot</note>; also Levi is "attachment" (*Leviyah*).
Also "Greece" (*Javan*) contains the letters of "Levi" in reverse.
Man is Levi: the revealed part is called this.
Man balances all fifty levels, for man is a "living, speaking" being.

They are paired against the enemy lion, for one cannot face the enemy unless a "box of reptiles" <note>A metaphor for having a humble or flawed lineage that prevents arrogance</note> is hanging from his neck. All of this is within the secret of purifying the *Kelippah*. In the First Temple, the holiness was like a lion. See my explanation on the *Zohar* regarding the "generations of the kingdom" using the name "Eagle." When we subdue the *Kelippah* of the lion in its literal sense—that is, Nebuchadnezzar—then the "Lion of the Kingdom" is rectified through the letter *Yod* of David. This is the meaning of "a troop shall overcome him" <note>Genesis 49:19</note>. The destruction was a "trouble born of breadth," as we explained regarding the secret that Jacob's "bed was complete." According to the secret, this hints that Judah's map was complete and peaceful. Reflect on this.

# Homily for the Portions of Matot and Masei

This is the essence of the universal rectification that encompasses all fifty "horns," for "the horn of his face radiated" <note>Exodus 34:29</note>. This corresponds to the Fifty Gates of Understanding <term>Binah; the divine attribute of structural intelligence</term>, which possess power during the sixty days <note>represented by the Hebrew letter Samekh, which has a numerical value of 60</note> that comprise the fifty days of the Omer and the ten days of repentance. This is the secret of his presence on the Mountain. This is why our sages said that even so, the letter *Samekh* follows it, as in "The Lord supports [*Somekh*] all those who fall" <note>Psalm 145:14</note>. In the West <note>The Land of Israel</note> they used to say: "She has fallen and shall not rise again" <note>Amos 5:2</note>. However, as explained in the Zohar <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>, the verse continues, "Now I will arise, says the Lord." This is the meaning of "The Lord supports," etc. The letter *Nun* <note>numerical value 50</note> was folded over in the secret of "and it was when the ark traveled" <note>Numbers 10:35</note>, and it shall have support from the Lord. Then the salvation will be exceedingly great, for everyone will merit the Fifty Gates of Understanding, which previously only Moses merited. Even among the great leaders of Israel, only some achieved this; Moses passed it to Joshua, who is called "the son of Nun" because he had the preparation for the fifty gates, as well as sixty-five of them. The air of the Land of Israel makes one wise, but through sin, its "gates"—which are the Gates of Understanding—were satisfied <note>closed or filled with judgment</note>. In the future, these gates will return (and they are the Gates of Repentance, as is known to the Kabbalists).

This is the secret of the eleven verses that begin with the letter *Nun* and end with the letter *Nun*. The first verse is from our portion: "We [*Nachnu*] will cross over armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance shall remain with us on this side of the Jordan" <note>Numbers 32:32</note>. The other ten verses are: "When the plague of leprosy is on a person, he shall be brought to the priest" <note>Leviticus 13:9</note>. "A prophet from among you, from your brothers like me, the Lord your God will raise up for you; to him you shall listen" <note>Deuteronomy 18:15</note>. "There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy dwelling place of the Most High" <note>Psalm 46:5</note>. "In the sight of their fathers He did wonders in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan" <note>Psalm 78:12</note>. "You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron" <note>Psalm 77:21</note>. "I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon" <note>Proverbs 7:17</note>. "The lamp of the Lord is the soul of man, searching all the inner depths" <note>Proverbs 20:27</note>. "Your lips drip honey, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the scent of your garments is like the scent of Lebanon" <note>Song of Songs 4:11</note>. "His lamp shone over my head... and from the land of the Chaldeans go out..." <note>A composite or variant of Job 29:3 and prophetic verses</note>. "They were armed with bows, using both the right hand and the left to hurl stones and shoot arrows with the bow; they were of Saul’s kinsmen from Benjamin" <note>1 Chronicles 12:2</note>.

The verse "When the plague of leprosy..." etc., raises a great inquiry: why did the Lord make our strikes so wondrous as to be like a plague of leprosy? This refers to the Great Destruction <note>of the Temple</note>. As it is brought in the "Openings" of the Midrash on Lamentations: "And the leper in whom the plague is..."—this refers to the Holy Temple. "The plague" refers to idolatry. "His clothes shall be rent"—these are the priestly garments. "And his head shall be bare"—as it says, "And He uncovered the screen of Judah." "And he shall cover his upper lip"—since Israel was exiled among the nations, no one was able to bring words of Torah out of his mouth. "And he shall cry: Unclean, unclean!"—the destruction of the First Temple and the Second Temple. I saw in the book *Rokeach* <note>Eleazar of Worms, 12th-13th century</note> that it is written regarding the leper, "he shall dwell alone," and it is written regarding the exile, "How does the city sit alone" <note>Lamentations 1:1</note>. The entire matter of the leper was fulfilled in the destruction of the Temple. 

"The plague appears to be in the house"—this was when King Manasseh placed an idol in the Sanctuary. "Then the owner of the house shall come"—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He—"to the priest"—this refers to Jeremiah the priest. The priest shouted, "Clear the house!"—he prophesied the destruction and the plundering of the vessels and the bronze sea. "And the priest shall see the plague"—this is Ezekiel, who was in the exile and saw what the Holy One, Blessed be He, did: He took the Cherubim that stood in the Temple and showed him every form of idolatry they portrayed on the walls of the Temple, as it says: "He put forth the form of a hand and took me... and behold, the plague was in the walls of the house." "Seven days"—these are the seventy years in Babylon. "And the priest shall return on the seventh day"—this is Ezra the Priest. "And they shall take other stones"—this is the building of Ezra. "And they shall take other mortar"—this refers to the Second Temple. "And he shall break down the house, its stones and its timber"—this is the destruction of the Second Temple, regarding which they said, "Raze it, raze it to its very foundation." This is all from the manuscript of the *Rokeach*. 

Regarding this, one wonders about the "plague of leprosy": Why is there this great fierce anger? It is also said, "he shall be brought to the priest" above, as it were; so was His will, as our Rabbis said: "I and the wrath of the house," and even the angels of peace weep bitterly. Afterward, ten verses begin with *Nun* and end with *Nun*. Every verse hints at another movement away from the ten nations mentioned above who journeyed from here. But they shall journey to this and return to the *Nun*—and on the contrary, to an even higher level. For the fifty wings hint at the eternal Kingdom... "Before the sun, his name is *Yinnon*" <note>Psalm 72:17; Yinnon is a name for the Messiah</note>. 

"We [*Nachnu*] shall cross over armed"—this corresponds to the pillar of the Torah. Initially, they are called such in the Masorah <note>The tradition of biblical text transmission</note>. There are three instances of the word *Nachnu* <note>a shortened form of 'Anachnu' (we)</note>. One is with a *Kuvva* <note>vowel point</note> and two with *Petach*. "We are all the sons of one man"; "On the day we..."—the spies did not cross over. "We shall cross over armed..."; "We have transgressed and rebelled; You have not pardoned." This corresponds to the Giving of the Torah, and they aimed for fifty levels: 
1. Repentance and Prophecy, as it is written: "Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking..." 
2. The attribute of Sovereignty—either freedom from the nations or essential kingship, for "all Israel are the sons of kings." 
3. The giving of the Land essentially, in order to fulfill the commandments dependent on the Land. 
As Rabbi Isaac said at the beginning of Rashi’s commentary: "The Torah should not have begun [with Genesis] but rather with the three crowns: the Crown of Torah, the Crown of Priesthood (which is the sanctity of the Temple), and the Crown of Kingship." These were hinted at during the Giving of the Torah: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests," etc. 

And behold, we find these two concepts of unity: Regarding prophecy, our Rabbis said in the first chapter of Berakhot that Moses requested of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that the Divine Presence rest only upon Israel, and we were set apart, "I and Your people." In that uniqueness, "You are One and Your name is One." Regarding Sovereignty, there is one leader for a generation; the earthly kingdom is like the heavenly kingdom. Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord, and it was given only to his generation and his seed. The sanctity of the Land is also a unity: "A land which the Lord..." and all lands are nourished from its essence. Similarly, the Land of Israel and the Holy Temple correspond to the Heavenly Temple and are united with it. "And they shall be joined together... and the Tabernacle shall be one." "We are all the sons of one man"—this is the vitality corresponding to the Crown of Kingship. As in the Midrash Rabbah on the portion of *Vayeshev*: "For behold, the kings assembled"—this refers to Judah and Joseph (in the coming of the Holy Temple). The Holy Spirit was victorious through them, and their like refers to the future: the Kingdom of the House of David and the Kingdom of Ephraim. All of them, due to our many sins, were nullified, and the final heavy blow was the destruction of the Temple and the Divine Presence in Egypt. 

"We [*Nachnu*]..." etc. through the mother <note>referring to the attribute of Binah/Understanding</note>, and a weeping for generations was established due to the sin of the spies. Upon this comes the hint through the taking: "Are we not the sons of one man, clinging to the beginning of faith?" Every word is a true crown. "We are not among those who reveal secrets in their heart," like Joshua and Caleb. "Why then did you not succeed?" Therefore, it is written with a staff <note>or a specific scribal mark</note>, for the power of rectification is the strength that they lacked. I have already mentioned the desire for the Kingdom during the giving of the Torah, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: "Grasp My throne" <note>The word for Throne, *Kisseh*, relates to the Divine name</note>. Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord, and behold, as it were, the heavenly throne of Sovereignty lacks an *Aleph* <note>The word 'throne' is sometimes spelled without the final Aleph</note>, and when it is established forever and ever, then the Sovereignty is restored above (Messiah son of Joseph and Messiah son of David). Israel will no longer be divided into two kingdoms but will be one scroll and one tree. 

"We shall cross over armed"—this corresponds to the level of the Land of Israel and the Holy Temple. The sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben, when the Holy Spirit shone upon them, they saw they would be exiled first. "A hurried inheritance." They said, "Why is this? What is our sin? Behold, we shall cross over armed to do more than our obligation, to go at the head of the army." This is the plain meaning of "He executed the righteousness of the Lord," which I have written elsewhere. Also here, holiness is with us: "For with us is the possession of our inheritance"—this refers to Moses our teacher; "The Torah that Moses commanded us is an inheritance." But the word for "Return" [*Teshuvah*] lacks an *Aleph* in the Zohar on the portion of *Vayikra*... for the "tent of meeting" was delayed. This is the secret of the small *Aleph* <note>In the first word of Leviticus, the Aleph is written small</note>, for the Tabernacle, which is in the secret of the *Aleph*, will rectify and join but not be totally nullified, Heaven forbid. For the first sanctity was for its time and for the future. But the inheritance of the sons of Gad and Reuben—their sanctity was minimal. When the *Aleph* departed, it was completely missing. This was their sin, that they were not in a place of sanctity. I have already written the sign: "He gave recessed ledges to the house round about outside" <note>1 Kings 6:6</note>. The acronym is *MNRT*: Manasseh, Gad, Reuben. So it is written in the book *Ten Utterances*. This was the distortion they could not rectify—that they were "outside" and were thus sent "outside" <note>into exile</note>.

I say there is a hint in this portion... as is known from what the Zohar says regarding the thirty fasts of the destruction, based on the verse: "Therefore the children of Israel shall not eat the displaced sinew [*Gid HaNasheh*]." Here there are hints in the names: *NIR* <note>lamp</note> refers to the Soul, hinting at *Manasseh*. *Reuben* has already been hinted at: "The Lord has seen [*Ra'ah*] my affliction." I, the heavy one, see the affliction and understand. "We have transgressed and rebelled; You have not pardoned"—this corresponds to the levels of Repentance and emptiness. He says it is like a gift. This is the meaning of "We have transgressed," for it is our nature, but You are the Master of Pardons—why did You not pardon? Then the verse was fulfilled: "Your iniquities have separated [you]," so that there could be no emptiness. Here "Repentance" [*Teshuvah*] lacks an *Aleph*, which is the "garments of light" [*Ohr* with an Aleph]... At the giving of the Torah, the spiritual impurity ceased, but afterward it returned. There is no rectification for it except through breaking. Then "the earth shall be full of knowledge," for behold, "We" [*Nachnu*] who speak from the Crown of Kingship are "cut off" and not "open," for it is not open to any man except to his generation. # Tractate Taanit

<margin>Charcoal <note>Hebrew: *Pacham*</note>—their origins for their journeys, but let their journeys be for their origins, as it is written: 'from place to place'.</margin> **"These are the journeys..."** their journeys for their origins, as it is written: "from place to place." Behold, there are twelve journeys until the Wilderness of Sinai, where they received the Torah—a <term>perfect Torah<gloss>Hebrew: Torah Temimah</gloss></term>. These correspond to the twelve permutations of the name <term>YHVH<gloss>The four-letter Name of God</gloss></term> which is "One." And all their wives, the twelve tribes of Israel, were as "one man." All the journeys are permutations of Divine Names; see the illustration of the <term>Tur<gloss>The 'Rows,' likely referring to a specific kabbalistic diagram or the Code of Law</gloss></term> in this Torah portion. After the Wilderness of Sinai, there were twenty journeys. At **"the Graves of Craving"** <note>Kivrot HaTa'avah</note> they began to corrupt their ways, but it left no lasting mark until **Ritmah**, for from there the spies were sent, and a "weeping for generations" was established. From Ritmah until Mount Hor, you will find nine journeys, corresponding to the ten journeys the <term>Shekhinah<gloss>The Divine Presence</gloss></term> traveled <note>when leaving the Temple</note> and corresponding to the exiles of the Sanhedrin, and so on.

There Aaron died, in the fifth month <note>the month of Av</note>, on the first of the month. Therefore, **"When Av enters, we diminish joy."** When he died, they retreated eight journeys backward. Counting one journey for each day, it turns out they arrived back there on the <term>Ninth of Av<gloss>Tisha B'Av, the day of the Temple's destruction</gloss></term> and held a lamentation. Nevertheless, the first High Priest, who is Aaron, corresponds to the First Temple. For Aaron represents the First Temple, while Ezra represents the Second Temple. Ezra is also a <term>reincarnation<gloss>Hebrew: Gilgul</gloss></term> of Aaron, as his name's <term>small numerology<gloss>Mispar Katan</gloss></term> equals that of Aaron. Therefore, his death is mentioned twice: in the portion of *Chukat* and in this portion <note>Masei</note>. In *Chukat*, the "death by a kiss" is not mentioned, because the destruction of the First Temple was more severe. Even though the destruction of the Second Temple was worse in some respects, ever since we lost those great virtues of the First Temple, we have not yet merited their return; five things were missing. And who caused all this? **The Canaanite, King of Arad.** "Canaanite" in numerology equals "Covered"—this is the **Evil Inclination**, who is Satan. Allegorically, he is the King of Arad, as Rabbi Hanina said in the tractate of *Berakhot*: "It is not the wild ass <note>Arad/Arod</note> that kills, but sin that kills." He is the one who sent the wild ass and the informer, etc.

It is found in the Jerusalem Talmud, and cited in the aforementioned *Tur*, that there are women who have a custom not to drink <term>wine<gloss>Hebrew: Chamra</gloss></term>, and some read the word as <term>wool<gloss>Hebrew: Amra</gloss></term> <note>meaning they do not weave wool</note>. This matter relates to the "squeezing of the cluster of grapes" caused by the serpent's provocation, which led to the Temple's destruction; see the Zohar on *Naso* and the book of *Lamentations*. **"How <note>Eikhah</note> does she sit solitary, the city that was full of people."** The first letters of "How" <note>A-Y-K-H</note> spell "Evil" <note>R-A-H, perhaps an interpretive rearrangement</note>. It was the cause of the "First Av" <note>Adam</note> who included all souls returning to the dust. As the Talmud says in *Sanhedrin*, the Divine Presence cast a soul into him, and from the moment he was separated for nine hours, it corresponds to the Ninth of Av. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: **"Where are you?"** <note>Ayeka, spelled the same as Eikhah/How</note>. See the first introduction to Lamentations. 

Aaron is the rectification of the "First Adam." Thus it is correct that women have the custom from the start of Av not to drink wine. Therefore, I also interpret the version of "wool" <note>Amra</note>: the primary priestly garments were made of <term>Techelet<gloss>Biblical blue wool</gloss></term>. Aaron is the repair for Adam. Note that the serpent's gold caused the birth of Cain and Abel, representing the mixture of evil, linen, and Esau, for all is "wool of the sheep." In the priestly garments, this mixture is permitted <note>Shatnez</note>, for the blue wool overcomes the linen. **"And all the House of Israel wept for Aaron."** All these are the "House of the Women"; look carefully into these matters. Afterward, there were eight journeys until they were close to entering the Land of Israel; these are the eight exiles. The Midrash says: "They sinned doubly, were punished doubly, and will be comforted doubly." Thus the four exiles are eight. How? When the destruction was prepared, the Chariot above moved... [describing the Lion, Ox, Eagle, and Man]. Not only were we exiled from this glory, but because of our many sins, it was overturned. How? At the destruction of the First Temple—**"When Av enters"** <note>the acronym of "Man" (Adam), "Lion" (Aryeh), "Eagle" (Nesher)</note>—"Woe, the **Lion** has come up from his thicket." At the destruction of the Second Temple, it was the **Eagle**, as it says in *Lamentations Rabbah* that Trajan said, "I am an Eagle." Between them is the "Master of Radiance," the **Man**, as it is said, "When a man <note>Adam</note> rises against us"—referring to a man, not a king. The "red wine" they forbade is like writing on the horn of the **Ox**, "You have no portion..." 

Thus, the 42 journeys hint at the departure and entry of souls, and the number of journeys is 42, like the **Name of 42**. Rabbi Moshe Cordovero wrote that this surrounds the soul upon its departure... he wrote the beginning of the Torah with the Name of 42 because it is hinted at in the first portion of Genesis. Likewise, there are 42 journeys at the end of the Torah. Because these are the words spoken in "this year," it is written "at the command of the Lord." This is connected to the rectification of the soul. See the diagram of the *Tur* regarding the journeys, how the Holy One, Blessed be He, counts all the places where they provoked Him until they came to the Land. So too, He counts now in exile all the degradations and wanderings, and all will be reckoned when "the Lord returns the captivity of Zion." Therefore, the division is mentioned immediately after the journeys. Then He will fulfill "not one man was missing from us," for the "Man" of the House of Israel will be gathered one by one. This is the final correction in the Plains of Moab, hinting that "not one man was missing." As it says in the chapter *Chelek*, Ezra said that the people of Ammon and Moab, who wept over the ruins of Jerusalem, when they heard Nebuchadnezzar... they sent to him, "The Man is not in his house," and "Man" refers only to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is said, "The Lord is a Man of war." They sent to him: "He has already set a time for them." This is why Naomi said, "Call me Marah <note>Bitter</note>" when she came from the fields of Moab, for they are rebellious. But the sweetness was fulfilled there, for King Messiah comes from Ruth the Moabite, about whom the King of Moab said, "It is a statute from me." This is the "Secret of the Plains of Moab"—the bitter turns to evening <note>Erev</note> and sweetness. Then no man will be missing. 

Upon this, the Psalm hints: **"By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat..."** We sat when we reached Babylon, "remembering Zion." "Also we wept"—what is the meaning of "also"? Plainly, it means an abundance of weeping. The Midrash says on "Our necks are under pursuit," that Nebuchadnezzar commanded: "Do not allow their merciful God to accept them in repentance." Another Midrash: why did Israel choose to weep by the Euphrates river? Rabbi Yochanan said: "The Euphrates killed more of Israel than the wicked Nebuchadnezzar did." Then they had permission to weep: "Also we wept when we remembered Zion," while the enemies thought the weeping was for the pain of the Euphrates. **"Upon the willows <note>Aravim</note> in her midst we hung our harps."** Simply, they hung harps on the willow trees. But it also hints at "The harp has turned to mourning." The liturgical poet for Sukkot explains four types of people in Israel; the "willows of the brook" are the wicked who have neither taste nor smell. The hint is: Why do You associate the righteous with the wicked? "Because all Israel are **Guarantors** <note>Areivim, same spelling as Aravim/Willows</note> for one another." 

Another hint: The Midrash on Psalms says, "My son, if you have become a guarantor for your neighbor"—this refers to the time the Torah was given. The Holy One said to Israel, "Give Me guarantors that you will keep the Torah." They said, "Our ancestors are our guarantors." He said, "They are already indebted to Me." They said, "The children shall be our guarantors." Immediately they brought the infants; the pregnant women's bellies became transparent like glass, and the infants saw the Holy One. He said, "Will you be guarantors for your fathers?" They said, "Yes." Thus: "Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength." This hint came when they arrived in Babylon, that place of bitterness—"I too am pained for them, for they are lacking and do not fulfill the Torah." Another interpretation: Rabbi Hiyya said, "As it were, I too participate so that the children shall bless Me." When they arrived in Babylon, where the "craftsmen and smiths" <note>the Torah scholars</note> were, as it says in *Sanhedrin*, God did a charity for Israel by sending the exile of Jeconiah before the exile of Zedekiah, so Torah would be established. Then they remembered the precious children of Zion and wept with strength over the **Guaranty** <note>Areivut</note> that was seized for their sins. Instead of rejoicing and singing, the captors asked of them "words of song." On the "Willows/Guarantors"—the "Mixed Multitude" <note>Erev Rav</note>—we hung our harps. When the captors said "Sing for us," the Levites bit off their own fingers so they could not play the harps. This is "from the song"—only a part, not the whole. For the song of the Levites required both hands and mouth. We were too overwhelmed by weeping to sing. "How can we sing the Lord's song on foreign soil?" 

**"If I forget you, O Jerusalem..."** He spoke of "forgetting" regarding this long, current exile; he said, "I will not forget you." Regarding Babylon, he said "I will remember." Therefore, the Torah warns: "Remember... and do not forget." This refers to the pride of the close relationship. Afterward, he prayed: "But You, O Lord, remember the children of Edom immediately," so that the exile would not be prolonged. Therefore, "If I forget you..." it is a great obligation to mourn

# A Discourse for a Eulogy on the Merit of the Righteous and the Destruction <note>The Hebrew header ends with "of it," likely referring to the Temple or Jerusalem.</note>

Whether the whole world exists for the sake of the righteous person—which is the primary way people should take a moral lesson and be awakened—or if they are taken like the wicked. That is to say, even if one is righteous, they are "seized" by the same fate, so that in this regard he is
->treated like the wicked and seized, though he is righteous.<-

### Furthermore
He said "Far be it" a second time, for it is one of the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that sometimes a righteous person dies for no reason other than those mentioned above, but rather because they did not rebuke their generation. This is found in the Talmud, Tractate Shabbat, in the chapter "With what [animal] may it go out," regarding the matter of the mark placed on the forehead <note>original: "v’hitveita tav," referring to Ezekiel 9:4 where a mark was placed on the foreheads of the righteous who groaned over the city's sins.</note>, see there. On this point, the Prophet rebuked them: "Roam through the streets of Jerusalem... if you can find a person of faith." This is difficult to understand: were there not many prophets, supreme pietists, and people of faith? Indeed, the "Craftsmen and the Smiths" <note>term: "Cheresh v'Masger" — the intellectual and social elite of Jerusalem exiled to Babylon.</note> were among them! Rather, he rebuked them because they did not "roam through the streets" to see the deeds of every individual and rebuke them. And even though they were perfectly righteous "sons of the upper chamber" <note>term: "Bnei Aliyah" — a term for those of high spiritual standing who see the Divine Presence clearly.</note>, <margin>this</margin> they were nevertheless held liable for this failure. Regarding this, our father Abraham said: "If I find *within* the city," meaning righteous people who were roaming *within* the city to rebuke the inhabitants. Similarly, it is said in the Lamentations: "They sent <margin>within it</margin> to rebuke." Or "Far be it from You," and the Blessed Name showed that He agreed with his words by saying "If I find... then [I will spare it]." Thus it is understood from all we have written that the death of the righteous
->atones because it causes people to repent.<-

<margin>
And perhaps someone might say: "From where do we know that the death of the righteous is recorded near the section on the Day of Atonement <note>original: "Yom HaKippurim"</note> to teach us that their death only atones for those who repent? Perhaps the text itself comes to teach us that the day of a righteous person's death is a day that atones regardless, atoning for both those who repent and those who do not?" To this, he answered that we already know the death of the righteous atones from the verse "And they buried the bones of Saul..." and even more so from what follows. Therefore, the verse comes to teach a new matter. What is this new matter? That it only atones specifically for those who repent. And we say that the Day of Atonement also only atones for those who repent, as proven from the verse "However, on the tenth [of the month]..." And one should not ask: "Perhaps the reason it was written near the Day of Atonement was simply to tell us that the day of a righteous person's death atones? For what would you say to that? That we should learn it from the verse regarding the bones of Saul?" Is it appropriate to say the Torah would rely on what is written in the Prophets? One can answer: concerning atonement, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Is there anything written in the Prophets that is not hinted at in the Torah?" Surely there is already a hint of this in the Torah. And it is true that there is a hint, as our Sages said nearby: "Why is the death of Miriam placed next to the section of the Red Heifer? To teach that just as the ashes of the Red Heifer atone, so the death of the righteous atones." Now, one should not ask why the author of the Midrash did not bring this juxtaposition to prove the atonement of the righteous, but instead brought a verse from the Prophets about the bones of Saul. One could say that the juxtaposition is remote, and we would not have known its meaning if we hadn't seen the verse in the Prophets. Once we saw the verse in the Prophets, we knew they had found a hint in the Torah. And do not ask why they didn't learn it from the Torah originally from the fact it was written near the Day of Atonement—for that itself teaches that the day of death atones, and we might have said the hint regarding Miriam's death had no substance. Or regarding the Prophets' verse about Saul, we might have said their hint came from the fact that the death of the righteous is written near the Day of Atonement. Rather, it must be that the hint used by the Prophets was the juxtaposition of Miriam to the Red Heifer. Thus, the death of the righteous atones to such a degree only to teach us that it atones for those who repent, and by bringing them to repentance, it atones.
</margin>

### And then
The previous statement will be clarified: "Just as the Day of Atonement atones, so the death of the righteous atones." That is, just as the Day of Atonement only atones for those who repent—as it says "However, on the tenth of the month," it atones for those who repent and not for those who do not—so too the death of the righteous only atones for those who repent.

### I have heard
Interpretations that "just as the ashes of the Red Heifer atone," meaning they wipe away the spirit of impurity that comes from the power of Samael <note>term: "Samael" — in Jewish tradition, the primary archangel of death and the accuser.</note> who is the Angel of Death, so the death of the righteous atones. That is, it helps one turn back from Samael by wiping away the spirit of impurity from him and from the filth and materiality that comes
->from Samael, who rode upon the Serpent. It removes the thickness of the coarse "Serpent" <note>referring to the base animalistic nature</note> so that the matter and form will be stripped of their distress, becoming refined and pure physical matter on high.<-

### Just as
The Day of Atonement atones, etc. I have heard an interpretation: It is known that the very essence of the Day of Atonement is a "Day of Will" <note>original: "Yom Ratzon" — a day of Divine favor or grace</note>, for so the Holy One, Blessed be He, established it once a year; therefore, the essence of the day atones. Likewise, the day of a righteous person's death is a "Day of Will," for even though it is a day of trouble on earth, nevertheless, from the perspective of the Will Above, it is a day of
->celebration <note>original: "Hillula" — literally a wedding feast, used to describe the anniversary of a Sage's death when their soul unites with the Divine.</note>, as explained in the Zohar regarding the "Hillula." Since it is a Day of Will, it therefore atones as well.<-

<margin>And I will speak regarding the righteous</margin>

### In the chapter
"And these may shave" <note>Tractate Moed Katan, Chapter 3</note>, Rav Ashi said to Bar Kipok: "On that day [of the funeral], what will you say?" He replied: "I will say: 'If a flame falls among the cedars, what will the hyssops of the wall do? If the Leviathan is pulled up by a hook, what will the small fish of the marsh do? If a hook is dried up in a rushing stream, what will the pond-water do?'" Bar Abin said to him: "God forbid!" and his tongue was tied. "And what would you say?" "I would say: 'Weep for the mourners and not for the lost one, for he has gone to rest, and we are left to sigh.'" Rav Ashi was upset with them, and their feet were turned backward <note>a miraculous punishment for their perceived disrespect</note>, and he did not come to the eulogy... It is difficult: what is the meaning of these three poetic phrases that Bar Kipok used in his eulogy? We must contemplate the nature of the punishment
->of their feet turning backward.<-

### The Eulogy
of Bar Kipok was accustomed to being "for a reward," meaning that his teaching would give the living a moral lesson and awaken them to repentance, as I wrote earlier in this pamphlet. He mentioned three matters: "If among the cedars," "Leviathan," and "Rushing stream." For the stream has three times and images of the soul: past, present, and future. The "past" refers to the soul before it comes into the body. There is a disagreement among the philosophers: whether the soul is complete in its existence before its arrival, or if it is only potential and grows as the body grows. The author of the *Akeidah* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama, 15th-century philosopher.</note> discussed this at length. However, hear this from the masters of Truth <note>The Kabbalists</note>: all souls recognize the world of reincarnations in their full stature. They are like the "Cedars of Lebanon," not like small saplings that grow only later; rather, they are chosen "among the cedars which the Lord planted." This refers to the "Past" of the soul. The second is the "Present," which is when it is joined with the body; either the wicked person dresses it in filthy garments or the righteous person in garments of glory, all according to the multitude of one's deeds. The third is the "Future," meaning after death, when the body is then purified in the "River of Fire" <note>term: "Nehar Dinur" — in Jewish mysticism, a river of fire that purifies souls as they ascend to heaven.</note>. After purification, it goes from strength to strength in its ascent. Thus says the *Tikunim* <note>Tikunei HaZohar</note>: "And I was among the exiles by the river Chebar" <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note>—this is the River of Fire, and it comes forth from before Him, "a thousand thousands minister to Him and ten thousand times ten thousand stand before Him" [Daniel 7:10]. And souls immerse in this River of Fire to cleanse their filth from this world. I found written that the reason souls need to immerse in the River of Fire after being purified in Gehenna is that there are two types of purification for the soul. The first is through punishment, to purify what it damaged by heating itself with the "fire of the Evil Inclination" to transgress the commandments. The second is to purify the soul because it did not sanctify itself in that which was permitted to it, as they said: "Sanctify yourself in that which is permitted to you" regarding eating, speaking, and other matters explained in the subjects of holiness. These matters are not a complete blemish to the soul, for a blemish only comes from a negative commandment. However, it is the "filth of this world" and its desires, clothed in the "skin of the Serpent." When a person does not separate from it, that filth remains tied to his soul. The fire of Gehenna does not purify [this], for it only purifies the "soul-blemish," which is the fire of the Evil Inclination—a great blemish. But this, which is not a blemish, requires a fine and spiritual fire: the River of Fire that flows from beneath the Throne of Glory. In this way, the soul strips off all the materiality of this world. Thus says Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "And these four heads of rivers... what is their immersion? Trembling and shaking... from the sweat of their immersion is made that River of Fire... and souls when they ascend, they bathe in that River of Fire and ascend to their place." And they are not burned, but rather they bathe. Come and see... the garment... because it is an immersion, that garment is not burned except in fire. Fire consumes this filth, and the garment is purified. The soul also—sometimes it is necessary... fire is made and it bathes, and the fire consumes all the filth... and the soul is bathed and shines. And if you say: if so, does the soul have no punishment in this? Come and see: woe to the soul that must endure fire and strangeness even though it is refined. But when the filth is great upon it, woe to the soul that endures that
->punishment.<-

# The Light of the Torah: On the Matter of the Divine Service

Therefore, one must stand at the altar feeling shame for one’s deeds, so that the "strong spirit" <note>This refers to the "spirit of folly" or the animalistic urge</note> might be subdued, and all this is done so that the image of the Throne [of God] may be realized, allowing Mercy to prevail over Judgment. This ends his words.

### Furthermore

It is stated in the Zohar <note>The primary work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah)</note> that the secret of the sacrifice <term>Korban; literally "drawing near"</term> is the mystery of the four engraved faces upon the Throne. This is the Throne of the Holy King: the face of an Ox, the face of an Eagle, the face of a Lion, and the face of a Man, who includes them all. All these faces look toward one another and are included within one another. From them, many aspects and tens of thousands of upper and lower beings spread out, without measure, number, or calculation.

The face of the Ox extends to the domestic animals, which branch into four types, all included as one: bulls, sheep, goats, and <insert>turtledoves and</insert> young pigeons. These are the ones designated for the sacrifice. Because their root is in those holy portions that extend from the face of the Ox, they are brought near to their own foundation <term>Yesod; the spiritual source or base</term> and are nurtured by that foundation and their "garment" <note>The spiritual outer layer or physical manifestation</note>. If a person does not bring them to their foundation in this world, they cannot be brought near there. This provides "rest" for the Holy Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> through their spirits. She draws near to receive the spirit of that animal and is nurtured by it, for that spirit originated from Her. Thus, these animals are carved out from the side of their secret source and are prepared from that "garment" for the offering, for they were part of Her garment.

The face of the Eagle extends to the birds; the spirit comes from it and remains in two sides. The hint for this is the verse "and let birds fly" <note>Genesis 1:20</note>, referring to the two sides. Because of this, [the Divine] descends and spreads to the right and left of the birds. From all these types, only the dove and the turtledove are brought near, as they are truly faithful to their mates compared to all other birds. This image <margin>A note on the text: "Sometimes in Judgment, sometimes in Mercy, and therefore they have names and are remembered as birds."</margin> is sometimes in Judgment and sometimes in Mercy. Their beauty stems from the fact that they do not seek rest outside [their pairing]. The nourishment from the sacrifice protects the "beasts" there, and they draw near to the holy living creatures <term>Chayot; the angelic beings carrying the Divine Chariot</term> and are prepared from their foundation and root.

And if you should ask: how does one species extend into so many branches and hosts without measure? Regarding the "Master Ox," it is taught: "The Ox lives," and from it the whole world is sustained. Furthermore, it is explained that the sacrifices only come from those sides engraved upon the Throne. Now, on the "Left Side," there are four types engraved on the Throne. Why are no other sacrifices brought? It is because everything is contained within the mystery of the sacrifice. 

The Lion is engraved on the Throne. At the time of the sacrifice, it appears as a consuming fire upon the altar, eating and deriving pleasure there. "Man" is engraved on the Throne—the "Man" who includes all. His spirit and soul are brought near there, and the "Supernal Man" <note>Adam Kadmon; the primordial Divine structure</note> is nurtured by the "man" below. Every species is brought near to its own kind and is nurtured; even a single drop is nurtured by its actual spirit and its foundation. 

And if you should ask: "The Lion has no lower foundation [animal] among the sacrifices?" The Lion is included in all of them, for the fire on the altar <note>The "Lion of Fire" described by the Sages</note> consumed all of them. No others from the "Right Side" eat from them. All four images engraved on the Throne draw near to the sacrifice, and thus the sacrifice is "complete." Through it, they are nurtured by their foundation and root. Then [Divine] pleasure descends to the Elohim <note>The Divine name associated with Judgment</note> because of them; the upper beings rejoice. To what do they give the essence and root? To those upper levels of theirs. Each level gives its essence. 

The four images of the Throne appear first in Mercy, but in the end, in "Old Age." The pigeons draw near first for nourishment. The "Face of the Ox"—these are the bulls <note>The OCR contains a parenthetical variant reading about the Ox and bulls here which is slightly fragmented</note>. All those that extend into the "eyes of Judgment," as we said, draw near to their root and foundation. The "Face of the Eagle" is as we described. The "Lion" is the Throne as mentioned. "Man" refers to the person who brings his spirit and soul near to the "Supernal Man." The Priest of Purity—the Holy Name—draws near to the Supernal Priest <note>The Archangel Michael</note>. He enters the Holy of Holies and offers the sacrifice, which harmonizes the colors and forms to the inner closeness below.

The Levites sing with pleasantness, for the lower "Ox" is the Levite <note>In Kabbalah, the Levites are associated with the Left Side/Ox</note>, and he illuminates the faces. Israel stands over the sacrifice in prayer, for prayer is above all else. Israel, the Throne and the Holy Seal, illuminates them. Each species illuminates the face of its own kind, and the whole host circles around. Everything is elevated and finds favor in the upper levels. Even though the levels engraved in the Priests and the Assembly are four in the sacrifice, they are their foundation. Those hidden upper levels are all prepared for the "feast" and rejoice. Yet, none of them has permission to taste of the sacrifice until the Supernal King eats and is satisfied and gives them permission. After He has given them the "kisses" <note>Divine communion</note>, each one eats and enjoys as is fitting. 

This is what is written: "I have gathered my myrrh with my spice" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>—these are the upper levels. "Myrrh with my spice"—this is the image of the "Right Side." "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey"—this is the "eating" as is fitting. "I have drunk my wine with my milk"—this is the joy of the "Left Side," the good wine which the upper levels eat. The Holy King is satisfied by them first; this is His food and His pleasure. The food of the Supernal King comes first, and from then on, it is given to the images engraved on the Throne and to all who extend from them, to enjoy and eat. This is why it says: "Eat, O friends" <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note>—these are the four images we mentioned. "Drink, and be drunk with love"—these are all who extend from them. All of them eat and are nourished as is fitting, and their faces shine upon all the worlds in joy. Every single one, whether from the upper levels or the lower levels, draws near to their foundation and enjoys. This is the mystery and the secret of the sacrifice as it should be.

Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba and all the companions came and prostrated themselves before him. Rabbi Ammi said: "If the Torah had not been given at Mount Sinai, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, had only said: 'Behold Bar Yochai, the Torah and its witness live forever,' it would be enough." When he departs from the world, who will illuminate the lamps of the Torah? Everything will be darkened from that day until the King Messiah comes. Not in this generation, nor in a generation like this, will we hear what we heard from Rabbi Shimon, through whom the Divine Presence dwells. This ends his words.

### And these are the words
of the Recanati <note>Rabbi Menahem Recanati, a 13th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> on the portion of Vayikra: Know that there are some obligatory sacrifices that are eaten by the altar, the Priests, and the owners, such as the Peace Offerings <term>Shelamim</term>. Some are eaten by the Priests, such as the Sin Offerings <term>Chatat</term> and Guilt Offerings <term>Asham</term>, etc. He notes there that the burning of the choice parts <term>Emurim</term> is for the atonement of the transgression. However, the Burnt Offering <term>Olah</term> is entirely consumed; no physical being has permission to benefit from it. This is because the transgression was in the mind—a "wicked thought" from the soul to the flesh. Therefore, everything must return to "spirit" just as the essence of the sin was in the spirit. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Thoughts of sin are harder than the sin itself." This ends his words. By "wicked thought," he means that these offerings come essentially for the sin of the heart's thoughts alone. Since in a physical act of sacrifice, the mind is not as preoccupied with the "service" [of the heart], and because that thought is the essence of everything, it was necessary to offer the Burnt Offering entirely—from soul to flesh—so that everything returns to spirit.

### Behold,
I have recorded only a tiny fraction of the general intention of the sacrifice. As for the details—such as the four types: Burnt Offering, Meal Offering, Peace Offering, and Sin Offering; or the Guilt Offering of the Levite and the Certain Guilt Offering—I have not lengthened the discussion. If your soul longs to know more of them, "go and read" in the Zohar and the Recanati. Happy is the man who knows the secrets of the sacrifices in general and in detail, and directs his heart during the time of "eating the separated parts" <note>Referring to the consumption of the sacrifice by the priests or the fire</note>. He prepares his heart with complete repentance, confession, and regret, confessing and forsaking his sin. He should consider himself like a sheep for the slaughter, feeling as if he were an offering entirely consumed for God, for the sake of the holiness of His Name. 

He also justifies the Divine Judgment upon himself through the "four deaths" of the court: Stoning, Burning, Beheading, and Strangulation. He says: "You are righteous in all that comes upon me," and rejoices in suffering. He even withholds himself from seeking mercy, even when a sharp sword is placed upon his neck, yet he prays for mercy and supplication that God might wipe away his sins with great compassion, but not through suffering and evil illnesses. He accepts his "broken heart" in place of animal sacrifices, for the intention of the sacrifice is to break the person and make him live in humility, as it is written: "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise" <note>Psalm 51:19</note>. That is to say, God will not despise a broken spirit and accepts it in place of animal sacrifices. According to this path of the sacrifices, those who have not understood or gained wisdom—blessed is the one who gains wisdom. The author of the *Akedat Yitzchak* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama</note> also wrote on this matter in Gate 51. This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it.

### Now
I have come to mention a little of the secret of the Incense <term>Ketoret</term>. Know that nothing is more beloved of all the offerings than the Incense. It is more internal than the animal sacrifice that comes for atonement, for it brings all powers near to their truth. Its name, *Keturah*, proves this, for it "binds" <note>In Aramaic, *Keter* means to bind or tie</note> and links the inner essence of the matter with the very "aroma of pleasing rest." 

Therefore, it is performed on the Inner Altar. These are the words of the Recanati on the portion of Tetzaveh: "And you shall make an altar to burn incense..." This altar was the Incense Altar, as it says: "And Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it every morning... and when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it." This brings mercy upon the Divine Presence. 

For this reason, it was plated with gold, as it is said: "His dwelling is gold, her clothing." In the language of our Sages, which is Aramaic, the word implies "binding" and "joining" the Supernal Chariot. And because it is the "portion" that rises to the Attribute of Judgment, it is written: "They shall put incense in Your nostrils" <note>Deuteronomy 33:10</note>, and "Oil and incense rejoice the heart" <note>Proverbs 27:9</note>. They hinted at the well-known "Glory," which is why it says regarding "strange incense": "Upon the face of the vile people I will be honored" <note>An interpretive rendering of a verse regarding the misuse of the service</note>. This is the measure of the "vial," for "He will not forgive your transgressions." Be careful of His honor, and be careful not to offer "strange incense" upon it. The commandment and the intention is that it should ascend from "Name to the Great Name..."

יתעלה <meta>catchword: may He be exalted</meta>

It emphasizes that physical offerings atone for spiritual sins and that a broken heart is the ultimate replacement for animal sacrifice.</summary>
