# The Time of Repentance

### And since I have seen that because of the length of their matters they would make a great interruption
### in the middle of this tractate of Yoma, I resolved in my mind to arrange them at the completion of
### the tractate. With the help of the Blessed Name, the chapter "Ner Mitzvah" <note>Hebrew: "The Lamp of Commandment"</note> is completed.

---

<margin>
I found in the notebooks of the students of the Ari, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria (1534–1572), the father of modern Kabbalah</note>, the custom of my teacher, may his majesty live: he would slaughter a white rooster on the eve of Yom Kippur during the early morning watch after the *Selichot* <note>liturgical poems of repentance</note>. There should be roosters according to the number of people in the house: a male rooster for a male, and a female hen for a female. Even for a pregnant woman, he slaughters three for her: one for her, and two for the fetus—one male and one female—due to the doubt of whether it is male or female. This is the secret of the "subduing of the Severities" <note>term: *Gevurot* (the divine attribute of Judgment)</note>, for a rooster is called *Gever* <note>meaning both "man" and "rooster" in Hebrew</note>. It represents the secret of the Severities of the *Yesod* <note>the Sephirah of "Foundation"</note> called *Gever*, which is the Foundation of the Feminine. This occurs on the ninth day, corresponding to *Yesod*, and we slaughter it to sweeten the Severities of the Foundation within her and to humble them. However, on Yom Kippur itself, these are the Severities of *Malchut* <note>the Sephirah of "Kingship" or "Sovereignty"</note>, which are harsh judgments; corresponding to them is the Scapegoat. Thus, this rooster is like the Scapegoat, only it is more "sweetened" <note>mitigated</note>. Therefore, it is slaughtered during the early morning watch, for that is when Mercy prevails, as is known. These are his words.
</margin>

## Chapter: The Light of Torah on the Subject of Kapparot <note>The ritual of "Atonements" performed with the rooster</note>

<margin>
These are the words of the divine Ramaq <note>Rabbi Moshe Cordovero (1522–1570), a leading Kabbalist in Safed</note> in the book *Avodat Yom HaKippurim*: It is the way of every upright person to rejoice on the eve of Yom Kippur and to prepare a fine meal. Likewise, the *Sefer HaChinuch* <note>a 13th-century work on the 613 commandments</note> explained this regarding the first commandment. However, the reason for this is explained by the question: why is there no obligation [to rejoice] on Yom Kippur itself?
</margin>

### The Secret of Eating on the Eve of Yom Kippur

It is a positive commandment, and in every positive commandment, joy is required. If so, one might think that since the essence of repentance is humility and worry, then joy during repentance would be its opposite. They answered regarding our matter that on Yom Kippur itself, there is no joy because of the worry over sins and the affliction of all Israel; they are weak before their Father in Heaven, seeing that their lives hang in the balance of judgment, and thus there is no joy. Therefore, they moved the joy ahead of the commandment. It is thus proper to prepare the house on the night following [the 8th] and a table full of the Lord's blessing on the eve of this day [the 9th] to rejoice in it with the joy of the commandment.

In response to this, they said in the Gemara <note>The Talmud</note>: "Anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth, it is accounted to him as if he fasted on both the ninth and the tenth." This is because the affliction of the tenth is not pleasing to God if it is done in a state of worry alone; but if one rejoices beforehand, the fast of the tenth is accepted. Thus, the joy of the ninth is a reflection of the fast of repentance and the tenth, and therefore it is credited to him as if he fasted on both.

Behold, on Yom Kippur itself there is no eating, because one must afflict the body and weaken the "excess," which is the animalistic vitality, in order to strengthen the soul. The "food" of Yom Kippur is the food of the World to Come; therefore, one must afflict this animalistic soul to empower the spiritual soul from the abundance of the coming day. The reason for this is that the food of Yom Kippur is to take pleasure in the Radiance of the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*).

The law of the Torah desires by nature that the lower, soft, and physical things exist, for the Creator only brought existence into being for the sake of these lower realms. If they were to die, the world would cease in an instant; therefore, one must sustain and provide for them. For this reason, one must provide them with food and sustenance beforehand. Just as on the Eve of the Sabbath there is a "double portion" of food to sustain them, so too does the Holy One have mercy and provide a double portion on the eve of Yom Kippur for this physical sustenance, so that they do not suffer and die on the eve. The lower life-forces are drawn and nourished from the Supernal abundance. Because of the desire of the spiritual for the physical—since the Upper has no existence except through the awakening of the Lower—it is said: "Anyone who eats on the ninth, it is as if he fasted, etc." For this eating is a "requirement of the High" <note>a spiritual necessity</note> for the preservation of the lower beings, which are the cause for the preservation of the Upper beings.

It is known that the ninth [day] is the secret of Wisdom (*Chokhmah*)... as explained previously. Therefore, eating is canceled to establish the Supernal rest from the evening, similar to the concept that "the world exists for six thousand years and in the seventh it is destroyed," and the lower creatures are sustained by what they toiled for on the Eve. This is the preservation of their spirituality from the Supernal light, and it is all one matter. These are his words.

> And these are the words of the Zohar in the portion of *Acharei Mot*: "You shall afflict your souls" (Leviticus 16:29). This is said because Israel is found before the Holy King, and their will should be toward the Holy One, blessed be He, to be remembered by Him so that their sins may be atoned. Therefore, whoever eats and drinks on the ninth and delights his soul with food and drink, it is found on the tenth that the affliction of the soul is in two parts <note>both the physical hunger and the spiritual transition</note>, and it is found as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth. "Your souls" is used to include everything—body and soul—to humble them on this day to atone for their sins. Until here [is the quote].
> The explanation: "Your souls" hints at the three levels of soul, namely body and spirit. The affliction of the body is the fast, and the "affliction" of the soul [on the ninth] is the eating <note>Paradoxically, the Zohar suggests that the soul is 'afflicted' by being forced into the body through eating on the 9th, or that the preparation makes the 10th more significant</note>. By this, they are both afflicted. The reason for the joy on the Eve is that it is a name of "good heart" on a Festival; we believe with complete faith that it is a day of purity and mercy, forgiveness and atonement for all the people of Israel, and its merit is joy, eating, and drinking. Therefore, it is considered as if he fasted, for it is the joy of a commandment, the commandment of Yom Kippur in which he believes. Further reasons for the secret of this eating will be explained later in this work.

---

<margin>
The divine Rabbi Moshe Cordovero wrote in the book *Avodat Yom HaKippurim*: It is known that for all transgressions between a person and God, Yom Kippur atones. However, for transgressions between a person and his fellow, Yom Kippur does not atone until he appeases his fellow. Therefore, one must search into this and return to appease his fellow. The reason for this is that the souls appear before Him on this day in the secret of the "Base" <note>the *Shekhinah*</note>, which is the root of the souls. The souls that are humbled in repentance go from the supernal awakening... to spread from their lower branches. Through sins between a man and his fellow, a "stain" <note>Hebrew: *Tina*</note> is formed; he separates and divides the Supernal Root and prevents the light from resting upon it... for it is a "breach." How is it possible for the light of repentance to be poured upon him if he is causing separation, Heaven forbid? Therefore, the men of action in the generations of the Tannaim and Amoraim <note>Sages of the Mishnah and Talmud</note>, even if they were the ones insulted, would present themselves to their offenders so they might be reconciled to one another, as is proven in the Gemara. The matter is this: the secret of the souls is sixty myriad [600,000], and they are all spirits, and so are the souls in the secret of the *Shekhinah*, *Tiferet*, and *Malchut*. This is "a generation goes and a generation comes," and no generation is less than sixty myriad. To draw from the Supernal Light, the sixty myriad must be of "one heart" so they may be unified in the Supernal Holy Name—for the abundance does not rest except in complete unity. Therefore, the hearts must be unified below, and the souls, spirits, and breaths unified above; then certainly the Holy Name rests in the secret of unity. Therefore, one must mediate peace, hold fast to it, and unite with one heart to draw the aforementioned Name upon themselves. These are his words.
</margin>

## The Secret of Loving Peace and Forgiveness Before Yom Kippur

<margin>
The words of *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>A 16th-century Kabbalistic commentary on the prayer service by Rabbi Meir ibn Gabbai</note>: Yom Kippur is the day of the revelation of the Supernal Luminary... from which all other luminaries and their radiance originate. It is the secret of the World to Come, in which there is no eating or drinking; therefore, we were commanded to fast on it. We draw close to the Luminary revealed on that day, in whose revelation all kinds of gladness, joy, and atonement appear. Therefore, it is called the "Day of Kippur," for it wipes away all kinds of filth and sprinkles [purity] before it, as it is written: "For on this day He shall atone for you..." (Leviticus 16:30). The secret of the verse is that first He atones and wipes the Supernal Sanctuary... and afterwards "upon you," for your sake, He shall remove the idols and the spirit of impurity from the Sanctuary to purify you from all your sins. Therefore, the Torah explained the essential counsel of the Scapegoat, as it is written: "And he shall atone for the holy place from the uncleanness of the children of Israel and from their transgressions." It should have said "for all their sins," but the Awesome Torah hinted to us that Israel must give "satisfaction" to all the Accusers in order to entice the S"M <note>Samael/Satan</note> so that they do not prosecute us. Not only that, but on this day, he becomes an advocate, and the Holy One, blessed be He, hears his testimony and atones for us. That world is only hidden from those who are "children of the soul"; therefore, Israel must cleanse their souls on the day that is a likeness of the World of Souls. The cleansing of the soul is to return in complete repentance from ways between man and God and from ways between man and his fellow.
</margin>

# The Secret of Repentance
The word Repentance <note>Teshuvah</note> can be read as *Tashuv-He* <note>original: "תשוב ה'," meaning "The letter He shall return"</note>. This refers to the final letter "He" of the Divine Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note>, which represents the Shekhinah <note>the Divine Presence</note> who is in exile because of sins, as it says: "Because of your transgressions was your mother sent away" <note>Isaiah 50:1</note>—she is the final "He." When a person returns from his way, then the "He" returns to her place to be unified with the "Vav" <note>the third letter of the Name, representing the male aspect/Tiferet</note>, and this is hinted at in the word *Tashuv-He*. This is what is written: "If you return, O Israel, to Me you shall return" <note>Jeremiah 4:1</note>. Furthermore, they hinted at a higher level, for through our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, the first "He" of the Name—which is the "Upper Mother" <term>Imma Ila'ah; another term for Binah</term>—is "the mother taken from above the children." Repentance is great because it brings the Mother back to her children, making "the mother of children joyful" <note>Psalms 113:9</note>. In Understanding <term>Binah</term> is the root of Repentance, as is known, for Understanding is the secret of Repentance, as I have elaborated in several places. Just as the six upper days <note>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note> are the secret of the "Building," and the "Lower Mother" has her root in Understanding, and from Understanding they branch out and to Understanding they return; so too, a person must occupy himself with repentance every single day of the six days of work. Even on the Sabbath, he should meditate on repentance. Thus we learned: "Rabbi Eliezer says, repent one day before your death." His students asked him: "Does a person know which day he will die?" He replied: "All the more so, let him repent today lest he die tomorrow." Then, when he performs repentance every day, the branches return to their root, and all is in the secret of Repentance, which is Understanding <term>Binah</term>. She is the secret of the World to Come, as is known, concerning which it is said: "No eye has seen a God besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>. The author of *Tola’at Ya’akov* wrote: "We have already made known the benefit of Repentance; that awakening rises up to the Supreme Repentance, which is the secret of the 'Great Sea.' Repentance is great for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it is said: 'Return, O Israel, unto the Lord your God.' She is awakened and returns to her children, and this is the secret of 'Return and cause to return'—that they should return, and then they will return the Mother to her children, and this is their rectification." It is already known that the status of the Penitent <note>Ba'al Teshuvah</note> is higher than many, as Rabbi Abbahu said: "In the place where the Penitent stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand." For the place of the Penitent is very high; it is the Supreme Light, the World to Come called "Repentance." Therefore they are called "Masters of Repentance" <note>Ba'alei Teshuvah</note>. The place of the righteous is below it by several degrees... the pillar of the world... the Land of the Living below, and these know the Land of the Living above. "No eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for those who wait for Him." He says "acts" <note>in the third person/hidden</note> in reference to the Supreme Jubilee, the World of Freedom, and therefore it uses hidden language. Thus far his words.

**And in the Zohar** we learned: A prepared place is designated for those of complete repentance. We learned that nothing in the world stands before repentance, and for everything, the Holy One, Blessed be He, forgives and accepts.

# Way of Life: Moral Reproof

He guards the steps of His devout ones, overlooking their stumbles with kindness <note>original: "ושונה כל רגלי חסידיו משגהו בחסד"</note>, much like a person might be spared from sin on three separate occasions. Regarding this, the Sage Resh Lakish said: What is the meaning of the verse, "If it concerns the scorners, He mocks them, but He gives grace to the humble" (Proverbs 3:34)? If a person comes to defile themselves, the way is opened for them; if they come to purify themselves, they are assisted.

The Academy of Rabbi Ishmael taught a parable: This is like a man who sells both kerosene <note>original: "נפט" (naphtha/petroleum), known for its foul odor.</note> and balsam oil <note>original: "אפרסמון", a highly prized, fragrant perfume of antiquity.</note>. When someone comes to buy kerosene, the seller says, "Measure it out for yourself." But when someone comes to buy balsam, the seller says, "Wait for me, I will measure it with you, so that both you and I may become fragrant."

The Academy of Rabbi Ishmael also taught: Transgression dulls the heart of a person, as it says, "Do not defile yourselves with them, that you should be defiled [**ve-nitmetem**] by them" (Leviticus 11:43). Do not read it as "you shall be defiled" (*ve-nitmetem*), but rather as "you shall be dulled/blocked" (*ve-nitmetem*). <note>A linguistic play on words: the Hebrew root for defilement is linked here to a word meaning "clogged" or "insensitive."</note>

Our Rabbis taught: If a person defiles themselves a little, they are defiled a great deal. If they defile themselves below (in this world), they are defiled from above. If they defile themselves in this world, they are defiled in the World to Come.

Our Rabbis taught: "Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy" (Leviticus 11:44). If a person sanctifies themselves a little, they are sanctified a great deal. If they sanctify themselves below, they are sanctified from above. If they sanctify themselves in this world, they are sanctified in the World to Come.

Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "If it concerns the scorners"—if one comes to join with scorners, "He mocks"—meaning God will not prevent him, but He will not help him either. "If to the humble"—if he comes to join with the humble, God "gives him grace" and helps him. When a buyer comes to measure foul-smelling kerosene, the seller says "measure it yourself." "Dulls" means it blocks and seals the heart away from all wisdom. The word "and you shall be dulled" is written with a missing letter *Aleph*. "They defile him a great deal" means they leave him to become very defiled. This is what the verse means: "Do not defile yourselves," for if you do, the end result is that you will be dulled. "Sanctify yourselves a little, and you will be holy a great deal"—he who comes to be pure is assisted. These are his words.

In the Talmud (Tractate Yoma, page 80), regarding "Do not defile yourselves with them," Rav Papa said: From here we see that physical impurity is from the Torah. But the conclusion is that it is a Rabbinic decree, and the verse is merely a support <note>term: <term>Asmachta</term> (a scriptural support for a Rabbinic law rather than a direct biblical command).</note>. Rashi explains that the verse does not literally refer to ritual impurity—since the only food that makes a person ritually impure by eating it is the carcass of a pure bird—rather, it is a support. The core meaning of the verse, as derived in the chapter "All Are Valid," is that a person who dulls themselves a little is dulled a great deal. This teaching is not merely an incidental homily, but the essential, true meaning of the verse.

What excellent things do we learn from these sayings of Rav Hamnuna? That when a person begins to restrain himself from sin, the Holy One, Blessed be He, actually assists him from that point forward to "turn away from evil." And when he begins to sanctify himself, the Holy One actually adds holiness upon his existing holiness to "do good."

However, regarding impurity, the Holy One does not add impurity to him; He simply does not hinder him, and "they open the way" for him. Why is there active help for holiness? Because the verse says, "You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy" (Leviticus 19:2). When a person begins to be holy, he connects to the Source of Holiness, for He—Blessed be He—is the True Holiness: "Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts." When a person starts this process, he clings, as it were, to God's holiness, and the Source opens up. Therefore, the Blessed One actually assists him to become even more holy.

This is not the case with the "Side of Impurity" <note>original: "סטרא דמסאבא", the Kabbalistic term for the forces of evil.</note>. It is written, "Evil shall not dwell with You" (Psalms 5:5), and "The wicked walk [far from holiness]." How could it be said that He, Blessed be He, would actually assist in making someone impure? For there is no actual evil in the highest realms.

The teaching about the severity of transgression needs to be understood: when sources of holiness are opened from above, they grow stronger. This is not the case with atonement. The "shells" <note>term: <term>Kelipot</term> (spiritual husks or forces of impurity).</note> resulting from sins do not—Heaven forbid—gather impurity in the heights. Rather, the voice of accusation rises above and awakens Judgment, as I have elaborated in my awe-inspiring sermon on the verse "and it shall suffice by a hair's breadth." Regarding the kerosene, the merchant says "measure for yourself," but for the balsam perfume, he says "I will measure with you, so that both I and you become fragrant."

**See** how precisely the verse speaks regarding holiness: "Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy." But regarding impurity, it does not say "and you shall be impure," but rather "do not defile yourselves and [consequently] you will be defiled." This is because the addition of impurity to a person is not—Heaven forbid—from Him, who brings everything into being, but rather the path is simply opened. This is because impurity, which is the "venom of the snake," cannot dwell with Him, as it is written, "Evil shall not dwell with You."

Note that the word "and you shall be dulled" <note>original: "ונטמתם"</note> is written without the letter *Aleph*. This hints at the soul, which is compared to a pomegranate <note>A play on "rimon" (pomegranate) and "romam" (uplifted).</note>, which lost the letter *Aleph*. By separating the *Aleph* (representing the One God) from "Truth" (*Emet*), one is left with "Falsehood" (*Sheker*) against the Creator, who created the world with the attribute of Truth. As I have written elsewhere, the beginning of Creation hints at Truth (*Emet*): **B**ereshit **B**ara **E**lohim <note>The translator is likely referring to the final letters of the first three words of the Torah: "Bereshi**t** Bar**a** Elohi**m**," which rearrange to spell "Emet" (Truth).</note>. Similarly, at the completion of Creation: "God saw everything He had made... [it was very good]"—the final letters spell Truth. When the *Aleph* is separated and removed from Truth (*Emet*), what remains is "Dead" (*Met*), for sin brought death to the world. But for the addition of holiness, there is true vitality from the Blessed One, for He actually assists and adds holiness.

**A person** who is a serious Penitent <note>term: <term>Baal Teshuvah</term> (one who has returned to religious observance).</note> must "suppress his merits" and "carry his debts." By this I mean that even if he has many merits, he should suppress them and view them as small. He should think: "What am I worth? If a righteous person were to become proud, Heaven forbid, his glory would be nothing. If so, what are my merits? They are almost void, barely worth the life the Blessed Name has granted me by feeding and sustaining me."

Regarding his "debts" (sins), he should magnify them and carry them, saying: "How numerous are my sins." King David said, "My sin is before me always." If David, the servant of God who was at the height of spiritual levels, said this, what should lowly people like me do? Thus, a person's thoughts should always be humble.

God then repays "measure for measure." The Holy One will "suppress his merits" <note>This seems to be a rhetorical reversal, meaning God hides the sins or compresses them.</note> and "carry his sins" for his benefit. If a person is exactly balanced between merit and guilt, the School of Hillel says: "He who is abundant in kindness tips the scale toward kindness." The Gemara asks: How does He do this? Rabbi Eliezer says "He suppresses" [**kovesh**], as it says, "He will again have compassion on us, He will suppress our iniquities" (Micah 7:19). Rabbi Yose bar Hanina says "He carries" [**noseh**], as it says, "He carries iniquity and passes over transgression" (Micah 7:18).

Rashi explains: "He suppresses" means He pushes down the scale of merit so it outweighs the sins. "He carries" means He lifts the scale of sin [to make it lighter].

**However**, according to what we said—that a person must "carry" his obligations and "suppress" his merits—God does both. For Rabbi Eliezer, He suppresses the debts; for Rabbi Yose, He carries the sin. They do not actually disagree. I believe that according to our Rabbi's view, Rabbi Eliezer's "suppressing" refers to the sins themselves. This can be understood through a physical principle: when you have two things of equal weight, but one has more "volume" (bulk) than the other, it is harder to carry. Sometimes something doesn't weigh as much as another, but its volume makes it seem equal.

The Holy One, "Abundant in Kindness," wants the scale of merit to weigh more than the scale of debt. He wants the "volume" of the debts to be minimized. What does He do? He takes the sins and compresses them together—not that He pushes the scale, but He compresses the sins themselves, squeezing them together to reduce their bulk. The two scales are still technically equal, but then He "lifts" the scale of debt. The scale of merit then outweighs it. By compressing the sins first, they no longer have more bulk than the merits. Thus, He literally "suppresses sin" and "carries sin." This awakens the Divine Names "Suppressor" and "Carrier."

Even when a person suppresses his own merits and the Holy One suppresses his sins, there is a hint that for Penitents, their intentional sins are transformed into merits.

**If** a person accidentally commits a sin that requires a sacrifice, he should record it in his notebook <note>original: "פנקסו" (pinkas), a ledger or diary.</note> as a reminder, in the hope that he will merit the rebuilding of the Holy Temple and then bring the sacrifice. We find this in the commentary on the chapter "With what may we light," regarding Rabbi Ishmael ben Yose. He once read by the light of a lamp and accidentally tilted it [which is forbidden on the Sabbath]. He wrote in his notebook: "I, Ishmael, read and tilted the lamp; when the Temple is rebuilt, I shall bring a fat sin-offering."

---

# Turn from Evil and Do Good

Similarly, we learned: Repentance and good deeds are like a shield against calamity. "Repentance" and "Doing Good" refer to good deeds. The concept of Repentance was explained above; now it is proper to explain the awakening of "Good Deeds," namely the performance of commandments.

Know that the Torah and the Commandments are the Name **Y-H-V-H**. In the Midrash on Ruth, it is taught that the four holy letters are called "Adam" (Man), and regarding them, the Holy One said, "Let us make Man in our image." From the **Yod**, fear of the Master of Masters is awakened, so that a person fears for his wealth. From the **He**, repentance is awakened. From the **Vav**, Torah is awakened. From the [final] **He**, good deeds are awakened.

This Name is hidden. Just as the Holy One is hidden in His world, so this Name is hidden within Man. The **Yod** corresponds to Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), which is called the Fear of God. The first **He** is in Understanding (*Binah*), which is called Repentance. The **Vav** is in Beauty (*Tiferet*), which is the Written Torah. The final **He** is in Sovereignty (*Malkhut*), which is called the world of Action. These letters, hidden in the name "Adam," assist a person in achieving these spiritual attributes.

# Way of Life: Reproof of Instruction

"Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a good heart out of the abundance of all things," <note>Deuteronomy 28:47</note> which means out of the abundance of all types of pleasures in the world, and from much gold, fine gold, precious stones, and pearls.

**The fifth condition** is that one should perform the commandment in its entirety and not just a part of it, as it is written in the portion of *Ekev*: "The whole commandment... you shall observe to do." <note>Deuteronomy 8:1</note> Rashi wrote there in the name of the Midrash: "If you have started a commandment, finish it." As we find with Joshua bin Nun, the leader of Israel, who performed a great commandment but failed by merely removing the guards that Jeroboam <note>The text here attributes the roadblocks to Jeroboam, though historically Jeroboam came after Joshua; the author likely refers to the general concept of preventing the pilgrimage to Jerusalem.</note> had placed on the road to prevent Israel from ascending [to the Temple]. Joshua said, "Whoever wants to go up, let him go up," but he did not decree that they *must* go up. Therefore, he was exiled and the ten tribes were exiled with him. Furthermore, the Sages said that one who begins a commandment but does not finish it will be buried by his wife and children <note>A stark Rabbinic warning about the spiritual weight of leaving holy tasks incomplete.</note>, for a commandment is only credited to the one who completes it. Nevertheless, if it is not in his power to finish it at all, he should not refrain from doing what is in his power to do, as we find with Moses our Teacher. It is written in the portion of *Va'etchanan*: "Then Moses set aside three cities" <note>Deuteronomy 4:41; Moses designated the Cities of Refuge even though they wouldn't function until the land was fully conquered.</note> as Rashi of blessed memory wrote there. (But it is difficult, for regarding Joseph’s bones he did the same, as it says, "And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him." <note>Exodus 13:19</note> He intended to bring them to the Land to fulfill the command to bury them in the Land, but God did not want this because He had sworn [that Moses would not enter]. Why then was he punished that his name was omitted regarding the bones? For it says, "The bones of Joseph which the Children of Israel brought up," <note>Joshua 24:32</note> not mentioning his name. But we hold that if one begins a commandment and is prevented by force from finishing it, it is considered as if he did the whole thing. This was Moses! Why was it not called by his name at the burial? The answer is: because the beginning is more than half of everything, and since it mentions he took them to fulfill Joseph's wish, it was as if he did it all. But in their burial, God wanted to make known the gravity of the commandment, and to teach us that while Moses provided the start, the Israelites completed it to atone for their sin of leaving Egypt to chase after spoil while Moses was busy with the commandment. Yet, when Moses died, the one who brings out and brings in, the world felt the loss, and the burial was credited to the people as a complete commandment.) However, if one has the power to finish and does not, he is liable for his soul and the loss of his wife and children, as we find with Judah, who began the commandment of saving Joseph but did not finish it; he was demoted from his greatness and buried his wife and children.

<margin>The sixth condition</margin>
**The sixth condition** is that he should perform the commandment with proper preparation, including all its details and precise requirements.

<margin>The seventh condition</margin>
**The seventh condition** is the running and alacrity toward it, as it is written: "I will run the way of Your commandments." <note>Psalm 119:32</note>

<margin>The eighth condition</margin>
**The eighth condition** is that with any commandment that comes to your hand, do not let it "sour" <note>A play on the word *matzah* (unleavened bread) and *mitzvah* (commandment); both must be done quickly before they "leaven" or spoil.</note> through delay, nor perform it with haughtiness which outweighs its merit. Even on the Sabbath, the cantor... <unclear>should occupy themselves with the essence</unclear>.

<margin>The ninth condition</margin>
**The ninth condition** is that the commandment which comes to one's hand first should be performed first. One should not leave it to do another first, as the Sages said: "One does not pass over commandments."

<margin>The tenth condition</margin>
**The tenth condition** is not to do two commandments as one, lest he be unable to be careful with both, as the Sages said: "One does not perform commandments in bundles." <note>Rituals should be given individual attention rather than being "clumped" together to save time.</note>

<margin>The eleventh condition</margin>
**The eleventh condition** is that he should be careful with the honor of the "vessels" of the commandment, such as the blood of a slaughtered animal—one should cover it with his hand and not his foot, so that the commandment is not treated with contempt. This is a primary principle for all commandments. In the Midrash Tanchuma, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said, "See how they honor the commandments, for they are My messengers, and a person's messenger is like himself. If you honor them, it is as if you honor Me; if you despise them, it is as if you despise Me."

<margin>The twelfth condition</margin>
**The twelfth condition** is not to delay the commandment; as soon as it reaches his hand, he should hasten to do it and not delay even for a moment. As Shimon the Righteous said: "And you shall watch the commandments" <note>Exodus 12:17</note>—our Sages of blessed memory read this as "And you shall watch the *matzot*," but the root is the same. Note that Joshua, because he was lazy/slow, his years were shortened by ten years. He was supposed to live 120 years like Moses (as it says "as I was with Moses, so I will be with you"), but he only lived 110.

<margin>The thirteenth condition</margin>
**The thirteenth condition** is that his intention and longing should be: "When will the commandment come to my hand so I may fulfill it?" As it is written: "And you shall learn them and keep (*ushmartem*) to do them," using the language of waiting, as in "and his father kept (*shamar*) the matter." <note>Genesis 37:11; here 'keeping' means 'watching and waiting' for a dream to come true.</note>

<margin>The fourteenth condition</margin>
**The fourteenth condition** is the beautification of the commandment (*Hiddur Mitzvah*), as it is said: "This is my God and I will beautify Him." <note>Exodus 15:2</note> The Sages said: Beautify yourself before Him with commandments—a beautiful Sukkah, a beautiful Lulav, a beautiful Tallit, and so with all commandments. They also said one should spend up to a third more for the beauty of a commandment.

<margin>The fifteenth condition</margin>
**The fifteenth condition** is great profit for himself according to his means, by being early in his honor to perform it. We learn this from Abraham, of whom it is written: "And Abraham rose early in the morning." From here we learn that the energetic are early for commandments. Likewise, anything whose commandment is at night should be done at the beginning of the night. In Tractate Nazir, it says one should always be early for a commandment, for as a reward for the older daughter [of Lot] preceding the younger [in her action], she preceded her by four generations in reaching royalty.

<margin>The sixteenth condition</margin>
**The sixteenth condition** is that a person should strive to perform the commandment in the most ideal way, specifically the study of Torah. Our Sages explained that the "sword of Israel's enemies" <note>A euphemism for a sword against Israel</note> is stayed when they occupy themselves with Torah. Furthermore, there is more reward when a commandment is performed by many people, as said in Tractate Yoma regarding the Temple service: the one who slaughters, the one who receives the blood, passing it to his fellow, and his fellow to his fellow, so that many may be occupied with the commandment until the blood reaches the priest closest to the Altar.

->But the priest closest to the Altar must pour the blood against the foundation.<-

<margin>The seventeenth condition</margin>
**The seventeenth condition** is that he should not perform the commandment for free, but should purchase it with a good and full price. This is a general rule to remove the spirit of impurity, as seen in the Zohar...

<columns>2</columns>
Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: Whoever wishes to exert himself in a commandment and to cleave to the Holy One, Blessed be He, must exert himself. He should not give [to a poor person] food or drink to have the person work for him for free, but should pay him properly according to his strength. We have established this in several places: a man should give "according to the gift of his hand." <note>Deuteronomy 16:17</note> And if you say, it is written: "Come, buy and eat... without money and without price, wine and milk," <note>Isaiah 55:1</note> that refers to the gift and effort of Torah study. Anyone who wants to merit Torah can do so without any payment at all. However, regarding the exertion of a physical *deed* [a mitzvah], one must not try to get it for free or at a discount, for then he will not merit at all to draw upon himself the Holy Spirit. Only through a full wage [is it earned]... and the Holy Spirit is not merited except with a full wage. And when a man exerts himself and pays the price of the commandment with the desire of his heart and soul, then the Divine presence may dwell with him. These are the words of the Zohar. And in the book *Shushan Sodot* (Lily of Secrets), sign 130, he wrote: These words are appropriate and obligatory for all masters of Torah who wish to fulfill the commandments. These seven principles should be before their eyes, corresponding to the seven *Sefirot* <note>The seven lower Divine emanations in Kabbalah: Kindness, Strength, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Sovereignty.</note>. Even if they are not in order, they are:

And these are the words of the author of *Lechem Mishneh* who wrote in the chapter "The Stolen Sukkah" regarding the altar being near money... <unclear>and you shall not go up by steps upon my altar</unclear>. This is connected to the commandments of the Sukkah... for from money a person grows great... one who steals straw and hay... and how does he then bless? Such a person is not blessing but blaspheming... for this is a "commandment brought about through a transgression," as it says in the chapter "The Stolen Lulav." One must take "for yourselves" <note>Leviticus 23:40</note> specifically from what is yours. <unclear>Rabbi Jozabad</unclear>... for it says "For I the Lord love justice, I hate robbery with a burnt offering." <note>Isaiah 61:8</note> Rashi and the Midrash say... a king passing through a customs house tells his servants, "Pay the tax to the tax collectors," even though all the tax belongs to the king. He does this so that others will learn from him not to steal... for the Lord loves justice.

**The first principle** is that one should not perform the commandments with levity or contempt. As we learned in the chapter "The Covering of the Blood": "And he shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth." <note>Leviticus 17:13</note> With that which he poured, he should cover—meaning he should not cover it with his foot, so that the commandments are not despised by him. The reason is that the commandments are rooted in the Upper Strength, in a place of purity and holiness in the "Body of the Tree" [of the Sefirot]. Therefore, their fulfillment should be in cleanliness and honor.

**The second principle** is that the commandment should not be performed through an intermediary in a way that diminishes its quality. As we learned regarding the Lulav and Willow: one should take it directly. The hand takes it with honor, not in a contemptuous way. The reason, as explained, is that the hands with which one takes the Lulav represent the ten *Sefirot*. Therefore, there should be no "interposition" (*chatzitzah*) of impurity between them and the Lulav, which itself hints at the Divine.

**The third principle** is that one should not use the body of the commandment for his own personal needs. As Rav Judah said in the name of Rav: "It is forbidden to count money by the light of the Hanukkah candle." The reason is that the commandments represent the Holy Place; therefore, one should not use the "service of the King" for himself, but only for the sake of another commandment, such as lighting one holy candle from another.

**The fourth principle** is that the commander of the commandments <note>God</note> is mentioned in the book as being more honored than the honor of the commandments themselves. As we learned at the end of Tractate Keritot: Four cries did the Temple Courtyard cry out. The first: "Depart from here, sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, who defiled the Sanctuary." The second: "Lift up your heads, O gates, and let Ishmael ben Phiabi enter." The third: "Open the gates and let Issachar of Barkai depart," for he honored himself while despising the holy things of Heaven. What did he used to do? He would wrap his hands in silk and then perform the Temple service. You see from...

# Way of Life: Reproof of Ethics
### Page 244 (Sig. 73)

A servant should not be arrogant before the King, as it is written: *Do not glorify yourself before a king* <note>Proverbs 25:6</note>. It is also written: *And the Lord your God is your King*, and we are always before Him, for *the whole earth is full of His glory.*

It is written: *Will you not fear Me? Will you not tremble before Me?* <note>Jeremiah 5:22</note> and it is written: *He who covers Me before my face always.* A person must be proper in their clothing, for the Sages called their garments "those that honor me." Beauty, splendor, and glory belong only to the King of the universe, as it is written: *He is majestic in His apparel* <note>Isaiah 63:1</note> and it is written: *The Lord reigns, He is clothed in majesty.* Our Sages hinted at this in the commandment of <term>Tzitzit</term> <note>The ritual fringes worn on four-cornered garments</note> on one's clothes: *And it shall be to you for a fringe.* The numerical value and the Name contain twelve permutations, and this is one of the reasons for the commandment—it is the word <term>Melech</term> <note>King</note> in rearranged letters. By seeing them and rearranging them, one fears His signs. A servant should not wear pride, but rather intend through his clothing to honor the King, for *one cannot enter the King's gate clothed in sackcloth.* If a person distinguishes himself for God’s sake, he will find favor. It is written: *Bowing to the Lord in the beauty of holiness,* yet we also read this as "in the trembling of holiness," as mentioned in Tractate Berakhot. This is because you should not glorify yourself before the King for your own honor, but for His honor. We say every day: "Blessed is our God who created us for His glory," and not for our own glory. Thus, the maintenance of honor combined with a humble heart is found in the section regarding the ritual fringes. This is what is written: *From the ends of the earth we have heard songs...* <note>Isaiah 24:16</note>. The Midrash explains this refers to the "wing" (corner) of the fringes. According to this, "the earth" hints at Israel, who humble themselves like the earth. Regarding them, our Sages said: *A generation goes and a generation comes*—these are the nations of the world—*but the earth stands forever*—these are Israel, as it is written of them: *And you shall be a land of delight.* The wing of the fringes is a hint to Israel and a sign for them to humble themselves. The warning is hinted at in the second section where it is written: *And you shall eat and be satisfied,* followed by: *Take care lest your heart be seduced.* This means: lest you be drawn after the desires of the world. Rather, as soon as you are satisfied, your hand should be restrained. For if you are seduced and drawn away, it causes you to turn from the good path little by little until you serve "other gods," as it says: *They sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.* The Sages explained that "playing" includes idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed. Similarly, this corresponds with the power of <term>Samael</term> <note>The primary archangel of internal accusation and temptation</note>, for as soon as the Accuser sees a person indulging in excessive eating and drinking, he dances before them to make them stumble in all manner of transgressions. The "jealousy" associated with the <term>Mezuzah</term> <note>The parchment scroll placed on doorposts</note> is in the first section. At the end of the first section of the <term>Shema</term>, we have a tradition received from our father Jacob at the time he departed from the world; he commanded and exhorted us regarding the unity of God, as found in Tractate Berakhot and the writings of Maimonides. Regarding the verse *Gather yourselves and hear, O sons of Jacob,* one might ask: why say "gather" when he already said "assemble"? They were already before him! Rather, "assemble" refers to the body, but after they were before him, he commanded them to remove from their hearts all jealousy, hatred, and strife, as if they were one man with one soul. If they do not do this, it is impossible to truly accept the Unity. As Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: *He is in one, and who can turn Him?* <note>Job 23:13</note>. The verse is difficult: it should have said "He is One." What does "in one" mean? It means the Blessed One only dwells when Israel is "in unity"—one heart without jealousy, like the ministering angels of whom it is written: *They are all beloved... and they all accept the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven.* It is said in the *Ethics of Rabbi Natan* that they look at each other, and each one says, "You start, for you are greater than I." So too in the Midrash regarding the Cherubim: *Their faces were toward one another.* This teaches that one should give honor to others. Therefore, every person, at the time of reciting the *Shema*, should unite their heart with the entire congregation of Israel and speak of them: "Hear, O Israel—all of us together in love and bound with one heart without jealousy or hatred." And now we accept the perfect Unity of our God, saying: *The Lord our God, the Lord is One.* Thus far the words of the *Book of the Pious*.

**Every** story of a voice that merits quickening the living: if one is sated with reproach, he should be as happy with that humiliation as if he had eaten and been satisfied. This is a wondrous form of <term>Teshuva</term> <note>Repentance/Return</note>. This was a common saying in the mouth of my teacher, may his memory be a blessing. He would say that of all the types of repentance in the world, the most effective for scouring away sins, iniquities, and transgressions is the enduring of insult, shaming, and blasphemy. It is superior to all the fasts and self-afflictions in the world. If a man humbles his heart and is "sated with reproach"—which is the language of a "living person" <note>Hebrew: *Chai*</note> who cannot be bothered with a sinner—so too with lashes and the like. However, with this trait of enduring insult, you may eat and drink while your sins are atoned for and built up. His language was: "If they tell you to murder, and you suffer a loss of money or health, will you say no? And if they tell you to accept the 'attribute of children' <note>humility/vulnerability</note>, will you say 'God forbid'? Rather, You, O Lord, shall guard them." If the Accuser says you should be satisfied with a maidservant or a harlot, one immediately runs to it; to this, you should say "May the Merciful One save us." And if they fall upon his house and his pleasures, or on the cycles of suffering, to all of them he says "God forbid." If so, tell him: "The sins and transgressions I have committed, whereby I corrupted the high levels of the worlds of Action, Formation, Creation, and Emanation <note>The four Kabbalistic worlds: Asiyah, Yetzirah, Beriah, and Atzilut</note> through the conduct of my soul from the day I was upon the earth—how shall they be atoned?" This folly remains every day and follows you until destruction, for the Accuser has no other work. He said: "No one ever defeated me except a master of one craft." The Accuser goes about and entices. This is a wondrous thing: it will wake you from your sleep. And if you have merited it, I have brought you to taste the flavor of the coming of the "bound ones" of night and day, so that you do not forget your thoughts. From every transgression, a knot and a yoke are made, a binding of prosecutors, as our Sages said: "He descends and entices, ascends and prosecutes." The Holy and Just Judge has His ears attuned to the voice of the Accuser. The Lord will not comfort them until the servant of the King comes, who conquers and plows with a blade in his hand, and says, "Where is the mercy of the King?" Then He will look upon him... and forget his yoke. What can be said? How will you answer His reproof? Therefore, this is the counsel advised by the Lord of Hosts: Let your heart be ready to be "sated with reproach." As he mentions and weeps, let the smile of your God be with you always, and nothing else shall ever be placed there. Thus far his words.

**And always** there should be humility in a man’s heart. In the first chapter of Tractate Berakhot (page 7), Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yose: One internal "chastisement" <note>Hebrew: *Mardut*</note> in a man's heart is better than many sets of lashes, as it is written: *She shall run after her lovers... then she shall say, I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now.* Resh Lakish said it is better than a hundred lashes, as it is written: *A rebuke enters deeper into a man of understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.* Rashi explains that *Mardut* refers to submission and humility that a person places upon his own heart of his own accord. When she sees there is no helper, she sets it upon her heart to say, "I will return." A "rebuke to the understanding" means the person understands repentance through self-recognition. The linguistic root of the word *Tachat* <note>Under/Instead</note> here is unique; it is a noun that means "submission," unlike the usage in "do not fear and do not be dismayed," where the grammar is different. Here it implies that the person places the matter upon himself; he humbles himself rather than being humbled by force.

### In my Volume on Tractate Chullin

I wrote many ethical words regarding daily matters. At the end, I wrote the general conduct of the godly Rabbi Moshe Cordovero <note>The 'Ramak', 16th-century Kabbalist of Safed</note> according to the Kabbalah. And look, I found in the notebooks of the holy Isaac Luria <note>The 'Ari', 16th-century Kabbalist</note> a general secret, as follows: A beautiful order to purify the soul, to illuminate it, and to add strength and light to it so it may be bound above in the supernal holiness. At night, before you occupy yourself with Torah, you should intend all the meditations that we will explain with God's help. Afterward, at every hour and every moment, you should also intend them. According to how much you increase these meditations, so the light in your soul will increase. How good and how pleasant if they are before your face all day long, for this repairs the soul and illuminates it greatly with the light of the "Sabbath rest." The order of the first meditation is this: Meditate on the Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term> expanded with the letter *Yod* <note>Spelling out the letters so they total 72, known as the Name of 'Av'</note> and then the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> expanded with *Yod* alongside it. Then meditate on the Name expanded to the value of 63 <note>The Name of 'Sag'</note> and the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> expanded with *Yods* with it. Then the Name expanded to 45 <note>The Name of 'Mah'</note> and the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> expanded with the letter *Aleph* with it. Finally, the Name expanded to 52 <note>The Name of 'Ban'</note> and the Name <term>Ehyeh</term> expanded with the letter *Heh* with it. Behold, the four expansions of the Name are joined with the four expansions of *Ehyeh*—these represent the Supernal Father and Mother <note>Abba and Imma, Kabbalistic archetypes</note>, their connection and their drawing down. The essence of all this is to interweave them together, one with the other. How? Take the letters of the expanded 72-name and the 10 letters of the expanded *Ehyeh* and interweave one letter from this with one letter from that until you complete them. Do the same for the 63-name with its counterpart, the 45-name with its, and the 52-name with its. Then, always return to the Name *Y-H-V-H* and then the Name *Ehyeh*. If you are meditating on this interweaving during the day, you should then interweave the four letters of *Ehyeh* with the four letters of the Tetragrammaton, starting with the letter *Aleph*... this brings together Father and Mother. Afterward, meditate on joining the three *Yods* with the Name <term>Adonai</term> <note>Lord</note>. If you are doing this at night, you should do the opposite... The reason for this is that the union of the last five names corresponds to the "double kisses" as explained in the Zohar, portion Terumah. When the names are joined and then return to being whole names, it signifies that even after the union and interweaving, they return to their original state. During the day, one should include the attribute of Night within the Day, and therefore *Ehyeh* and *Adonai* are used. But at night, the attribute of Day must prevail to include the day within the night; therefore, one precedes the Tetragrammaton (the Day) to *Ehyeh* and *Adonai* (the Night). In the beginning, the Male attribute is first; during the day, the Female attribute is first.

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic and ethical instructions regarding the spiritual transition between the Sabbath and the weekdays, as well as the transition between the High Holy Days and the festival of Sukkot.</meta>

<header># Way of Life, Rebuke of Ethics</header>

<margin>I am also arranging the ten unified Sephirot <note>The ten divine attributes in Kabbalah</note> because the three worlds of Beriah [Creation], Yetzirah [Formation], and Asiyah [Action] unite so that your intention may be ordered all at once, though there is no need to establish them all simultaneously. I have already informed you that the three worlds—Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah—each have a specific spiritual essence. The spirituality of the world of Beriah is associated with the name *El Shaddai* [God Almighty], the world of Yetzirah with *El* and the letters *Y-H-V*, and the world of Asiyah with *El Adonai* [God the Lord]. You already know that a person receives an "additional soul" on every Sabbath from the levels of Atzilut [Emanation], Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah. At the conclusion of the Sabbath, the level of Atzilut departs. Then, on Sunday, three levels remain with him from the Sabbath. On Monday, the level of Beriah departs, leaving Yetzirah and Asiyah. On Tuesday, Yetzirah departs, leaving only Asiyah. Then on Wednesday, the Asiyah level from the previous Sabbath's "additional soul" also departs. You already know that the Sabbath is the seventh day and the center; therefore, on Wednesday, a person begins to acquire the "addition" for the coming Sabbath from the level of Asiyah. On Thursday, he acquires from the level of Yetzirah, and on Friday from Beriah. On the Sabbath itself, the level of Atzilut is added. Therefore, on Sunday, you should always focus your intention on *El Shaddai* <note>original: אל שד"י</note> to bring illumination from there to sustain the remnants of the previous Sabbath's addition. On Monday, focus on *El Y-H-V*, and on Tuesday on *Adonai*. Afterward, on Wednesday, focus on drawing illumination for the coming Sabbath from *El Adonai*, on Thursday from *El Y-H-V*, and on Friday from *El Shaddai*. Know, however, that during the first three days, you should intend for *El Shaddai* and *El Adonai*—which are the "feminine" aspects of Beriah and Asiyah—to be Leah, and *El Y-H-V-H* to be within Israel the Lesser Persona <note>original: "Zeir Anpin," the emotive divine attributes</note>. Then, during the final three days of the week, focus them toward Jacob and Rachel.</margin>

Furthermore, follow the aforementioned order, and if you wish to perform each of these orders that we will write—God willing—each one individually, that is also good.

<margin>* The prayer "We beseech You by the power of Your greatness" <note>the *Ana B'Koach* prayer</note> contains the 42-letter Name of God. This belongs to the world of Yetzirah [Formation]. Focus your intention on the eight names to elevate your soul from Asiyah [Action] to Yetzirah through this 42-letter Name. However, during the second sequence, focus on how the initials *K-R-A S-T-N* <note>meaning "Tear away the Adversary"</note> overcome all else so that the soul may ascend through the "hidden things." One should focus on how the initials *Ch-B-T T-G-A* overcome. It is also necessary to interweave and link this Name with the last one. The explanation is that since your intention is to receive the "addition" of the Sabbath, and you already know that the secret of the Sabbath day is the name *S-K-V-T-Z-T*, a person must link and interweave every weekday—if it is Monday, for example—with the name of the Sabbath, which is *S-K-V-T-Z-T*... and if it is Tuesday, he should interweave the addition of *Ch-K-B T-G-A* with the power of *Ch-T-G* so that the illumination of this day receives from the Name of the Sabbath.</margin>

There is also another order: on Sunday focus on the name *S-G* <note>numerical value 63</note>, on Monday on the name *M-H* <note>value 45</note>, and on Tuesday on the name *B-N* <note>value 52</note>. Afterward, focus from bottom to top: Foundation, Today, the name *M-H-M*, and the name *S-G*. There is also another order: on Sunday focus on the letter *He*, on Monday the letter *Vav*, and on Tuesday the letter *He*. Then afterward, from bottom to top: Foundation, Today, and the name *H-I-V*. Also another order: when it is Monday or Thursday, when we take up the "Reparations" <note>Tikkunim</note> in the world of Yetzirah, which is *El Y-H-V*, and so it is correct in my view to use the eight names of the *Ana B'Koach*...

There is also another proper order to elevate the soul from the Waters of Asiyah to the River of Yetzirah in this manner... and it was shown to me that this is the secret of the "flying wings" that carry a person upward. As is known, a bird only flies by its wings; the wings of a bird correspond to the arms of a human being. It is already known that the five "Kindnesses" <note>Chasadim</note> spread to the two extremities of a person. Some are revealed and some are concealed. There are twenty Kindnesses: five in the right arm (Kindness), five in the left arm (Power), and some in the torso (Beauty). Thus, these two lines [the arms] contain the secret of a person's "flight" through the wings—which are the arms—and not through the legs or other limbs. Know that because the Kindnesses in the arms are "closed up," they cannot shine or spread. As you know, anything situated in a narrow and cramped place feels great pressure; therefore, wings were given to them to move here and there and emerge. This movement is the "flight." These Kindnesses have their root above... These spreading Kindnesses are lights that move away from their source and desire to ascend to their root in the "Knowledge" <note>Da'at</note> to be nourished and strengthened. When they ascend from their cramped place, they carry the person upward. This is why the "wings" are in the arms specifically. Therefore, your intention should be that all ascents are by the power of the 42-letter Name. Intend that the name *A-B-G Y-T-Z* is in the right arm, the name *K-R-A S-T-N* is in the left arm, and the name *N-G-D Y-K-S* is in the upper third of the torso (the concealed part). Through these three names, those Kindnesses "fly" to ascend higher and higher to their root in Knowledge. On their way up, they carry the person to the world of Yetzirah... To strengthen this flight further, focus on returning the Kindnesses to the Lesser Persona for the sake of divine union. By this, strength is added to the Kindnesses, and you will ascend from Asiyah to Yetzirah. These are the words of a wise and gracious mouth.

# The Tractate of Yoma is completed • With the help of Him who hangs the earth upon nothingness
## Tractate Sukkah • The Pillar of Peace
->( And he spread the protection of peace over us )<-

---

<margin>From our teacher of blessed memory <note>Maharzal</note> in the laws of the conclusion of Yom Kippur, it is written as follows from our teacher Isaac Luria <note>Maharaq/Arizal</note>: Between Yom Kippur and Sukkot, we do not fall on our faces in prayer <note>supplicatory prayers/Tachanun are omitted</note> because those are six days. The Holy One, blessed be He, gave the Torah to Israel to forgive their sins during all those four days, and He does not begin to count their sins until the first day of Sukkot, as it says: "And you shall take for yourselves on the first day," meaning the first day for counting transgressions. Similar language is found in the books of customs.</margin>

**Chapter:** The Commandment is a Lamp. During the four days between the Day of Atonement and Sukkot, the Children of Israel are busy with the commandment of the Sukkah and the Four Species <note>the Lulav, Etrog, etc.</note>. These actions bring a person to remembrance, that they may remember the details of the Commandments and cleave to Him. Therefore, these days are like festival days since holy engagement brings about this awareness to rejoice with spiritual joy and to serve God with gladness and a good heart. As it is written in the Midrash Tanchuma... at the conclusion of the Day of Atonement, they engage in the commandments of Sukkah and Lulav and do not commit sins; therefore, we call the first festival day "the first for the reckoning of sins." Another reason given is that during these days, the building of Solomon's Temple was completed; therefore, they are days of joy, fit for rejoicing and cleaving to Him, may He be blessed.

**And regarding the Interpretation:** At first glance, their words seem to imply that whatever a person sins during these days, God will not count the transgression. Heaven forbid we should believe this! It is impossible that four days of the year should be "lawless," where every man does what is right in his own eyes. For even regarding one day a year, the Talmud states in Tractate Chagigah: "Whoever commits even one transgression a year, the Scripture regards him as if he transgressed the entire year." This is learned from the verse "according to the number of days you scouted the land, forty days, a day for a year." This applies even more so to these holy days, for three reasons: First, the Holy One has shown that He is merciful, gracious, and forgiving; would someone then rebel against the King while He is still at His table? Heaven forbid! On the contrary, Israel is obligated to pray with joy the morning after Yom Kippur so that the Accuser [Satan] does not prosecute them, for they are still standing in judgment, and the final "seal" occurs on Hoshana Rabbah and Shemini Atzeret. How could the time of repentance and the awakening of mercy be a lawless time for sin? Second, one reason for the Sukkah being established in the month of Tishrei—as our teacher Maharil wrote—is that one must wander from his house to the Sukkah, a hint of "exile" which atones for sins. To sin during these intervening days would be like saying "I will sin and then repent," for which opportunity to repent is not given. Third, these days are sanctified by commandments and sit between two sanctities: the holiness of Yom Kippur and the holiness of the Festival of Sukkot. They are like the intermediate days of a festival (*Chol HaMoed*). Naturally, a person is obligated to increase their level of holiness. As Rabbeinu Yonah wrote, the days between the New Moon and the fast are like the intermediate days, and it is proper to limit work and increase holy service. Therefore, heaven forbid these days should be lawless; on the contrary, the punishment for a transgression committed during holy days is more severe. The meaning of the Midrash, which says the first day of Sukkot is "the first for sins," refers to the majority of the people. The text means that Israel *does not* commit sins during those days because they are all busy with commandments; therefore, the first day of the festival becomes the first opportunity for a new transgression to be recorded. Note the wording: "they do not commit sins, therefore it is called the first day for reckoning." Since they are busy with commandments, they are not available for sin. Who is it that does not engage in a commandment? Only one who is not commanded. This is the conduct of atonement and purity from their sins.

...one [merit] is found to tip the scales, and he is found righteous; through this, the entire world is tipped toward merit because the majority are now righteous. These are the words of Rashi. <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki (1040–1105), the preeminent commentator on the Torah and Talmud.</note> The *SeMaK* <note>Sefer Mitzvot Katan, "The Small Book of Commandments," by Isaac of Corbeil (13th century).</note> wrote similarly in Sign 204, as follows: "A person should imagine as if he and all of Israel are half-meritorious and half-guilty. destroys much good' <note>Ecclesiastes 9:18</note>—this is a beautiful teaching, meaning a 'slip'—and he tips the scales to the side of guilt. But if he performs one commandment, happy is he! For he has tipped himself and all of Israel to the side of merit." 

Thus far are his words. It is also found in the *Book of Knowledge* <note>Sefer HaMada, the first book of Maimonides' Mishneh Torah.</note> in the Laws of Repentance, Chapter 3. We find that one who sins through jest and lightheadedness on a Festival is [judged] more severely than during the rest of the year. Since the world is judged through a single sin, it is possible he might tip the world to the side of guilt, and then all those poor people who die or suffer due to the afflictions of hunger and thirst—all of them are dependent on him. 

And it is not only that a person's sustenance depends on these [days], but also a person's life and soul depend on the judgment, as the author of *The Beginning of Wisdom* <note>Reishit Chokhmah, a 16th-century kabbalistic ethical work by Eliyahu de Vidas.</note> wrote in the Gate of Holiness, Chapter 12; see there. Because the Festivals are days of judgment, Rabbi Yitzchak said: "A person is obligated to purify himself during the Festival" so that he may enter the Day of Judgment in purity, just like Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. 

Since it is clear that these are days of judgment, it is not proper for a person to be lazy in them, neglecting to plead for his soul in prayer and supplications according to the law of the day, just as it is not proper to be lazy during the High Holy Days. We say in the Jerusalem Talmud: "This person who sleeps at the beginning of the year, his judgment sleeps [with him]," etc. This does not literally mean one who sleeps, but rather anyone who sits idle; even if he is awake, he is called "asleep" because he is idle and performs no good deed on the Day of Judgment. The same applies to the other days of the year, meaning the days of judgment mentioned above. 

There is no "good" for a man except to eat and drink and let his soul see "good"—and there is no "good" other than the <term>Torah</term> <note>Meaning Divine Law and study.</note>, for it holds the right of the firstborn and "double the wisdom" in the matter of study and self-training, more so than other days. This is because these are days of "holy convocation" and days of rest, free from all labor, which is a great and powerful reason to study with perfect intention, even more than during the working days. I have elaborated on this somewhat at the beginning of my small composition which I titled *The Hands of Abraham*. 

The author of *The Principles* <note>Sefer HaIkkarim by Joseph Albo (15th century).</note> wrote similarly regarding the Sabbath in Chapter 10 of *Vayakhel*, Gate 25, as follows: "The primary intent of the rest they innovated for us is to fix in our hearts the study of the Torah and a withdrawal, according to our hours, from all the distracting worldly affairs. For this reason, their hearts will turn to assemble and stand for their lives according to the teacher, and to call out all together: Scripture, Mishnah, and Talmud—each person according to his value. The wise will find satisfaction in it, for they seek Torah from their mouths," etc. Until [he quotes] the Jerusalem Talmud: "Sabbaths and Festivals were given to Israel only for the purpose of studying Torah in them," etc. He elaborated on this, and at the end of his words there: "And not for those who have become accustomed to sitting idle... those who stir up jealousy and hatred between a man and his brother... who stir up strife and contention, which disturbs the prayer, the Festivals, and the Torah. They are included in the prohibition 'You shall not kindle fire in all your dwellings on the Sabbath day' <note>Exodus 35:3; interpreted here as the fire of anger/strife.</note>." 

These words require our attention. It is possible that this is the meaning of [the statement]: "An additional soul <note>Original: *Neshama Yeteira*.</note> is given to a person by the Holy One, Blessed be He, on the Sabbath" (Tractate Beitzah, page 16). According to the literal meaning of this statement, it is difficult: why is it given to him on the Sabbath if it leaves him at the close of the Sabbath? As it is said there: "Woe, the soul is lost!" <note>The Hebrew *Vayinpash* is punned as *Vai-Nefesh* (Woe, soul).</note> Also, what benefit comes to a man from this additional soul while it is in him on the Sabbath? 

It seems to me that the intention of our Sages, of blessed memory, in this is as follows: since man is composed of body and soul—one body and one soul together—the soul engages in intellectual pursuit and the body in eating and drinking all the weekdays, and one does not cancel the activity of the other. But on the Sabbath, he has an "additional soul" as mentioned. Therefore, the body is alone between two spiritual entities, and the two souls easily overcome it and cancel the body's physical activities, so that he does not eat on the Sabbath as much as on a weekday. For the two souls that are now in the one body overwhelm it and cancel its custom and nature, for "one in the place of two is nothing." 

Thus, the spiritual powers easily hold the physical ones toward the spiritual, for the terrible physicality [is consumed], and it does not drink from pleasure... the pleasure is great in attaining the intellectual concepts associated with the soul, meaning the repeated study is more attainable for pleasure, as mentioned nearby. This is the ultimate intent of the Blessed Name in giving an additional soul to man on the Sabbath day—not merely to enjoy the pleasure of the body. For the explanation that an additional soul is rested upon a person on the Sabbath so that his eating and drinking may be greater than on weekdays—this is not so! It is not the nature of the soul to eat and drink, and it has no pleasure from this at all, except that its desire and great pleasure is in the Torah of the Lord. 

Therefore, He gave man an additional soul on the Sabbath so that the heart would be wide open on the Sabbath day, which is prepared for this because it is free from all thoughts and labor... and anyone who eats and drinks on the Sabbath day more than his soul desires, in a way that results in the neglect of Torah, the Scripture considers him as if he were liable for his life. For he has "lost one soul"—meaning the additional soul given to him to study and teach on the Sabbath more than other workdays and the Festivals. This is what they interpreted there: "*Vayinpash*—Woe, the soul is lost!" Meaning: Woe to those creatures who lose the soul! For by eating and drinking far more than is proper, they neglect the Torah, for which purpose this additional soul was given to us on the Sabbath. They are as if they destroyed this soul, since it sits idle with him, away from the "work of Heaven" for which it was given. This is simple to understand. 

And even though these things—meaning what I brought just now in the name of the author of *The Binding of Isaac* <note>Baal HaAkeidah, Isaac Arama (15th century).</note> and what I wrote myself regarding the additional soul—refer to the Sabbath, it is proper that we learn from them for our current subject. For there is no difference between a Festival and the Sabbath in this matter at all; they are one and the same. 

Similar to this, our Sages said (in the chapter *Chelek*): "Any scholar who sits and engages in Torah, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and reads opposite him." But one who ceases [Torah study] for a feast at an improper time brings evil to the world, because the Torah girds itself in sackcloth and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He, saying: "Master of the Universe! Your children have made me like a lyre that people play!" He says to her: "My daughter, when they eat and drink, what should they occupy themselves with?" She says before Him: "If they are masters of Scripture, let them occupy themselves with Torah, Prophets, and Writings; if they are masters of Mishnah, let them occupy themselves with Mishnah, Laws, and <term>Aggadah</term> <note>Non-legalistic homiletical teachings.</note>; and if they are masters of Talmud, let them occupy themselves with the laws of Passover on Passover, the laws of Pentecost on Pentecost, and the laws of the Feast on the Feast." 

Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar testified in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Hanina: "Anyone who reads a verse in its [proper] time brings good to the world, as it is said: 'A word in its season, how good it is!'" Rashi explained: "One who reads the Song of Songs and treats it like a [secular] song, with a melody other than its own... even though it is from the Song of Songs and its essence is a song, it is forbidden to treat it as a secular song. Rather, it refers to one who reads a verse in a banquet house at an improper time... making a joke out of words of Torah and calling out verses in a loud voice to laugh at them in the banquet house. But if he said it in its time, such as when it is a Festival and he takes a cup in his hand and says *Aleinu L'shabe'ach* <note>The "It is our duty to praise" prayer.</note> and verses relating to the occasion, he brings good to the world." 

In the *Midrash Tanchuma* (brought by the *Rokeach* in Sign 54) on the portion *Vayakhel*: "Moses said, 'The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: Assemble a great congregation to lecture to them in public on the laws of the Sabbath, so that future generations will learn from you to assemble congregations every single Sabbath to lecture to Israel on what is forbidden and what is permitted.'" 

The *Knesset HaGedolah* wrote on this: "From here, they relied in all the communities of the Diaspora to gather in synagogues to read Scripture and to lecture to the public on <term>Aggadah</term> after the morning meal." (The *Tur* wrote in Sign 290, and it is likewise in the *Shulchan Aruch*: "After the morning meal, they establish a study session to read from the Prophets and to lecture to the public on <term>Aggadah</term>; it is forbidden to set a [large] meal at that time.") 

It was taught in the school of Elijah: "It is a commandment to assemble in synagogues to lecture on the matter of the day for women and children." And regarding *Vayakhel Moshe* ("And Moses assembled"), the masters of <term>Aggadah</term> would say: "From the beginning of the Torah until its end, there is no portion that begins with the word 'Assemble' except for this portion alone. And why so? The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: 'Go down and make for Me great congregations on the matter of the Sabbath, so that all generations coming after you will learn to assemble congregations every Sabbath and to enter the synagogues and study halls to teach Torah to the public.'" 

Another explanation: "And Moses assembled"—The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: "If you assemble every single Sabbath in synagogues and study halls and read from the Torah and Prophets, I will consider it as if you made Me King in My world. For so the prophet Isaiah explains: 'And you are My witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God'—you testify concerning Me that I am God in the world." 

Ibn Shu'aib wrote in his sermon for the first day of Passover: "'You who dwell in the gardens, companions listen for your voice; let me hear it' <note>Song of Songs 8:13</note>... until the end. And this verse we began with is interpreted in the *Midrash Chazit* as referring to Israel when they gather in synagogues and study halls to pray and to hear words of Torah on Sabbaths and Festivals, which is more accepted and pleasing before the Holy One, Blessed be He, for they leave their desires and their pride and come to hear words of Torah. Concerning this, it said: 'How beautiful and how pleasant you are, O love, with delights'—meaning, this love is more beautiful than all other loves when it occurs on a day of delights, at the head of which is a great love for the Name. Even though it is good at any time, it is especially good on days of delight when people gather to pray on Festivals, fulfilling the 'voice in songs and praises,' and the Name and the ministering angels 'listen for your voice, let me hear it.'" 

I must be brief here. From all these [sources], we have learned that Sabbaths and Festivals were given to Israel only to rejoice in them with the joy of the Torah, each according to what he is—whether masters of Scripture, or masters of Mishnah and Gemara, etc. They should hear the sermon from the mouth of a sage who lectures to them on the subject of the day, such as the laws of Passover on Passover, etc., combined with mentioning the miracles that the Blessed Name performed for us in those days. Especially in the Diaspora, where there is no joy except in [Torah] as already
