# Matters of Prayer and Torah Reading

Rather, one should maintain silence, as it is said, "For with You..." <note>A truncated reference to Psalm 130:4, often cited in discussions of awe and silence.</note> and they did not answer, etc. The *Beit Yosef* <note>The primary legal commentary by Rabbi Joseph Karo, 1488–1575.</note> wrote that Rabbi Yonah stated in the first chapter of *Berakhot* that even though it is permitted to speak between the calling up of different individuals to the Torah, it is forbidden for others once the Torah scroll is opened. One must not converse even if there are eight pages between them and the reader. Even though some say it is only forbidden while the scroll is actually open, it implies that from the moment the first verse is opened, it is forbidden to speak at all until they conclude the entire portion. These are his words. It appears the reason is for fear that the conversation will extend into the time of the actual reading. However, it seems that it is not strictly forbidden from the moment it is opened, but rather from the moment the reader begins to read; such are the words of Maimonides, may his memory be a blessing.

If it is forbidden to speak even between readers while the scroll is closed, then what will those who chatter during the actual reading answer on the Great Day of Judgment? Woe to them and woe to their souls! The Warning <note>likely referring to the *Zohar* or another ethical work</note> elongated significantly on their punishment; therefore, those who remain should hear and be afraid. Their eyes and hearts should be directed toward the reading of the <term>Chazzan</term> <note>The Cantor or designated Torah reader.</note> to hear every single word he reads from the Torah scroll. I have already written previously in the tractate *Shabbat* that one should complete the portion of "twice Scripture and once Translation" <note>The practice of *Shnayim Mikra ve-Echad Targum*, reading the weekly portion twice in Hebrew and once in the Aramaic translation.</note> before the Sabbath, and during the public reading, one should listen to the Cantor. Such is the <term>Sephardic custom</term>, as they do not bring any printed Bibles to the synagogue; they all sit, remain silent, and listen to the Cantor. This is proper in my eyes.

There are those who permit studying quietly, and some say that if there are ten people listening to the Torah scroll, others are permitted to speak (of words of Torah). Some permit it for one whose "Torah is his craft" <note>A scholar whose sole occupation is study.</note>, and some permit it for one who, before the scroll is opened, turns his face away and shows that he does not wish to hear the Torah scroll but rather to study, and begins studying. To read the "twice Scripture and once Translation" during the public Torah reading is permitted. However, all this does not apply to the portions of *Zachor* and *Parah* <note>Special annual readings regarding the memory of Amalek and the Red Heifer, considered by many to be biblically mandated obligations.</note> which require a <term>Minyan</term> <note>A quorum of ten.</note> by Torah law, where one must focus and hear them from the mouth of the reader. The correct path for all portions is for one who is meticulous in his actions to focus his mind and hear them from the reader. All this is explained in the *Beit Yosef*.

The one who reads from the Torah opens with: "Bless the Lord who is blessed." The *Radbash* <note>Rabbi David ben Solomon ibn Abi Zimra, 1479–1573.</note> wrote that he must say "Bless" in a loud voice to include anyone who has not heard it. For it is a woe—I say, a woe!—if they are ten and they said it quietly, it is considered a private act and does not benefit those who did not hear him. Those listening who say "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed" should not say so unless they heard the blessing. Rather, when the Cantor finishes "forever and ever," they say "Amen," just as we say regarding the Grace After Meals: if one arrives and finds them saying "Let us bless He of whose [food] we have eaten," he says "Blessed is His Name, the glory of His kingdom, etc." If he arrived at the response, he says "Blessed is He of whose [food] we have eaten," and says "Amen." Therefore, it is good to say it in a loud voice. Even though the reader says "Bless," he is not excluding himself from the community since he includes the word "The Blessed." Rabbi Judah al-Bargeloni <note>An 11th-12th century scholar from Barcelona.</note> wrote in the name of Rav Saadia Gaon that even though he says "The Blessed" and has not excluded himself, he must return to the count and say "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed," just as in the Grace After Meals where even though he said "Let us bless," he must return to the place he stopped—namely, "Blessed is He of whose food we have eaten and through whose goodness we live."

The Sephardic custom is that the one who says "The Blessed" says "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed" in a loud voice and not quietly, and it is a beautiful custom. Afterward, he returns and blesses "Who has chosen us." The custom of the pious is to answer "Amen" before the reader begins to read in a loud voice so the congregation will understand and hear when he begins to read (from the *Maharam*). Everyone who goes up to read the Torah opens with a good matter and concludes with a good matter. <margin>Chapter Thirteen</margin> When he finishes reading, he rolls the Torah scroll and recites the blessing... in the *Mordechai*, the *Kol Bo*, and the *Abudraham*, regarding the final blessing, it is: "Who gave us the Torah of Truth and planted eternal life within us." For the "Torah of Truth" is the Written Torah, and "planted eternal life within us" is the Oral Torah, as it is written: "The words of the wise are like goads and like nails firmly fixed." This excludes those who say "and for eternal life He planted within us" <note>original: "ולחיי עולם נטעה בתוכינו"</note>. These two blessings contain forty words, corresponding to the forty days Moses stayed on the mountain. One finds that the final blessing opens with "Blessed" because it is adjacent to the first blessing of the Torah reading, so it is not considered an interruption, as we find with the blessings of the *Shema* and the "Blessed is He Who Spoke" (*Baruch She'amar*) and "Praised" (*Yishtabach*). This is the opinion of the *Tosafot* <note>Medieval French and German commentators on the Talmud.</note> in the chapter "Three who Ate" regarding the reason: because they were accustomed that only the first reader blessed the first blessing and the last reader blessed the final blessing, and there was a great interruption between the first and the last. Later, they instituted both blessings for every single reader because of those entering and leaving the synagogue.

**And it seems** to me that in the *Abudraham*, another reason was written: because these do not have a "fixed" status. His explanation is that the blessings at the beginning and end of the Torah reading, as well as the blessings for the <term>Haftarah</term> <note>The reading from the Prophets.</note>, are not fixed—meaning, sometimes they bless over this portion and sometimes over that portion. Similarly with the Prophetic readings, sometimes over this one and sometimes over that one. Since they are not fixed, they do not have the law of a blessing "adjacent to its fellow." This is not the case with the blessings of the *Shema*, or *Baruch She'amar* and *Yishtabach*, which are fixed. You will never find the blessings of *Baruch She'amar* and *Yishtabach* in any other place except in the "Verses of Praise" (*Pesukei D'Zimra*). Similarly, the blessings of the *Shema* are specifically for the *Shema* and nowhere else. Since they are fixed and established, they have the law of a blessing adjacent to its fellow.

## It is Forbidden
to sleep in the synagogue, even a temporary nap, as seen in the story of the house of Rabbi... <note>referring to a Talmudic anecdote in Megillah 28b</note>. All the more so those people who are likened to animals, who slumber and sleep at the hour when the sermon is being delivered or when the service is taking place... by avoiding hearing the Torah, even their prayers become an abomination. Children's chatter in the synagogue is a great prohibition. Here I will copy words of ethical instruction that I found in a book called *Derech Chayim* (The Way of Life), page 76 and 7: We learn at the beginning of tractate *Chagigah* that Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah expounded: "Assemble the people: the men, the women, and the little ones." The men come to learn, the women come to hear, but the "little ones"—why do they come? In order to give a reward to those who bring them. The *Tosafot* wrote there that on this basis they relied to bring small children to the synagogue. 

Menachem <note>The author's voice.</note> said: In this time, there are "little ones" who come to the synagogue to bring *punishment* to those who bring them! For the child comes to desecrate the holiness of the House of God and to play in it with lighthearted laughter. They stand up to play with one another; this one mocks that one, this one hits that one, this one provokes and this one cries, this one talks and this one screams, this one runs here and this one runs there—a runner toward a runner he shall run. Some even relieve themselves in the synagogue. And if they are told something, the father may even show him a book while the child throws it to the ground or even tears it into ten pieces before their eyes! In the end, from the sound of their folly, the concentration of the worshippers is interrupted, and it results in the Name of Heaven being desecrated. 

One who brings a "little one" in this manner to the synagogue should not hope for reward but rather fear retribution. To what is this comparable? To a man who has a foolish servant and went to speak to the King, and his servant was with him. The servant stood in his folly and struck the King and insulted him, while his master saw and remained silent. Will the King not be angry with the servant's master? He will say to him: "It was not your servant who struck me, but you!" And he will punish him according to his wickedness, while to the servant he will do nothing. The servant has no sin because God withheld wisdom from him and did not grant him understanding. Thus is this matter. 

Furthermore, sometimes even the fathers play with them to pass the time... and it is even worse because the boys grow up with this bad habit and strange character. As they grow, they will continue to rebel, and the matter of the synagogue and its holiness will become trivial in their eyes, and they will not give honor to the Torah. Once a person commits a sin and repeats it, it becomes permitted to him; even when he grows old, he will not depart from it. The conclusion of the matter: it is proper for a person not to bring a very small child to the synagogue, for he will lose by bringing him and gain nothing. Even a slightly older child—he should bring him but not let him move from his place, and should teach him and instruct him to answer "Amen," "Kaddish," and "Kedushah." He should not let him speak idle words and should teach him to sit there in awe and fear. In this, he will have a good reward from the Blessed Name. "We have prepared the Tree of Life" etc.—the Torah is called a Tree of Life. It is written that he should raise his son for the study of Torah, for this will be the reason that the boys grow up, and even until old age and gray hair God will not forsake them. But if he disciplines them from the start of their youth to follow after vanity, wealth, and merchandise, it is likely that because of this they will die in the brevity of years. Thus said our Sages of blessed memory in the *Sifrei*: When a child begins to speak, his father speaks with him in the Holy Tongue and teaches him Torah. If he does not speak with him in the Holy Tongue and does not teach him Torah, it is as if he buries him, as it is said: "And you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them..." so that "your days and the days of your children may be multiplied." If you teach them to your children, your days and your children's days will be multiplied; if not, your days and your children's days will be shortened. 

It is a commandment for every person to have a lamp before them. This is what the *Orhot Chayim* <note>original: "ר"ח", likely Orhot Chayim by Aaron ben Jacob ha-Kohen of Narbonne</note> wrote on page 88: that the prophet said, "Therefore, honor the Lord in the fires" <note>Isaiah 24:15</note>. And they said elsewhere... and even though this was said as a parable, not a single word was written in the Prophets in vain; rather, they all pertain to actual practice. In the Midrash, we find support for this in the *Yalkut* on the portion of *Behaalotecha*: Lamps of flesh and blood, made of clay or copper—all is according to a person's honor. And the honor of the Sabbath—its lamps are its honor. If you keep the lamps of the Sabbath, I will show you the lamps of Zion, as it is said: "At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps." I will not make you dependent on the light of the sun for illumination, but rather I will illuminate for you with My Glory, as it is said: "The sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give light to you; but the Lord will be your everlasting light." And the nations are destined to walk by your light, as it is said: "Nations shall walk by your light." And what light does the Holy One, Blessed be He, shine for Israel? Like the light of righteousness, as it is said: "But for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall rise." And all this—why? In the merit of the lamps that they light on the Sabbath. Know how great the obligation was...

It concludes with the spiritual significance of lighting lamps for the Sabbath and the sanctuary.</summary>

# **Torah Or**

One must give thanks, etc. This is the place of "Thanksgivings," and here lies the secret of *Gemilut Chasadim* <note>Acts of loving-kindness</note>. Therefore, we say the blessing "He who bestows good things upon the guilty," and the secret of bowing and the *Modim* <note>The prayer of "We give thanks"</note> prayer is established in its proper place. The sign for this is the verse: "For to You every knee shall bend." The secret of the "Rabbis' Modim" <note>A specific communal version of the thanksgiving prayer</note> is established in this place, as it is written: "The Lord of Hosts." These represent the attribute of "Disciples of the Sages who increase peace in the world." Its secret is known to those who possess "Hidden Wisdom" <note>Kabbalah</note>, for they are the ones who increase peace. As it says regarding the knowledge of peace: "The vine shall give its fruit, the earth shall give its produce, and the heavens shall give their dew." You already know that the "Dew of Hermon" which descends upon the mountains of Zion refers to the attributes of *Netzach* <note>Victory/Endurance</note> and *Hod* <note>Splendor/Gratitude</note>. Since these are the places of "Thanksgiving" and the secret of "every knee shall bend," the Sages of blessed memory said: "One must bow during the *Modim* prayer." Every blessing that comes into the world comes through these attributes. Therefore, one who does not bow during *Modim*, his spine becomes a snake after seventy years. The secret of the seventy years refers to the seventy "Ministering Princes" who stand in a circular row, while the "Snake" stands outside as an ambusher against *Netzach* and *Hod*. Anyone who is not careful with the Disciples of the Sages, or with *Netzach* and *Hod*, deserves to be bitten by the snake. This is why they said: "Anyone who transgresses the words of the Sages is liable for death" and deserves to be bitten by the snake. Therefore, when the Name called *Adonai* <note>The Lord</note> clothes itself in the garments of *Netzach* and *Hod*, all the wars of Israel are fought for us against our enemies, and He pays recompense to all the enemies of our souls. We must therefore give thanks to the One who clothed Himself in the garments of *Netzach* (Victory) and *Hod* (Splendor)—"You are clothed in glory and majesty." This is the meaning of "God of Thanksgivings, Master of Wonders." Observe that wherever you find the language of "Thanksgiving" <note>Hebrew: Hoda'ah</note>, it corresponds to this mystical place. This ends his words.

We shall arrange what is written here regarding the offering of the Princes <note>Nesi'im</note> and the reading for the first day of Hanukkah: "And the princes of Israel, heads of their ancestral houses, brought offerings." This refers to figures like Mattathias. The miracle was performed through Mattathias the High Priest. The Holy One, blessed be He, hinted to Aaron, who was the first High Priest, about this matter in the portion of "When you mount the lamps," as Nachmanides explained. Originally, Aaron's place was in the attribute of *Chesed* <note>Kindness</note>, but later he rose much higher. Similarly, it is taught in the Tractate *Derech Eretz* that seven fathers "cut a covenant": Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Phinehas, and David. These correspond to the seven *Sefirot* <note>Divine emanations</note> of the building. In their secret, there are seven items in the Breastplate corresponding to these seven. The Sephardim have a commentary on the verse "And all was delivered into his hand"—referring to Aaron the Priest from the aspect of *Hod*, who then rose to *Chesed*, as it is written: "Your *Thummim* and *Urim* belong to Your pious man (*Chasidecha*)." Just as Knowledge <note>Da'at</note> rises to the attribute of *Tiferet* <note>Beauty/Harmony</note> in the secret of "Knowledge from above." From the side of *Chesed*, there is the Name of 72 <note>The 72-letter name of God</note>, which is the numerical value of *Chesed* <note>Chesed = 72</note>. Likewise, Judah the Maccabee performed great deeds of power with the help of the Name. "Maccabee" <note>M-K-B-Y</note> numerically equals 72 when using a specific calculation. <gloss>M-K-B-Y: Who is like You among the gods, O Lord</gloss>. Also, the letters of Maccabee (*M-K-B-Y*) are the letters of "Laundry of the Law" <note>K-B-S D-T</note>, standing for: "The Glory of His Residence from His Place." (And it seems to me this hints at what the Sages said: "One who disputes the Kingdom of the House of David is like one who disputes the Divine Presence." Behold, the Hasmoneans were the ones who took the kingdom for themselves, even though the kingdom was already decreed for the tribe of Judah, as the Sages established on the verse "The scepter shall not depart from Judah." Regarding this, the Maccabee hinted at "The Glory of God from His place," for "Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen." The Hasmoneans did not flaw the glory of the Divine Presence by taking the kingdom; their honor was for the sake of Heaven, and their actions were only like an error proceeding from a ruler). Great miracles were performed through these holy priests, and they restored the crown of the Torah to its former glory and the fulfillment of its commandments. It is written: "For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light." Therefore, a miracle was revealed in the Holy Temple through the Menorah.

As written in *Avodat HaKodesh* <note>A classic 16th-century Kabbalistic work</note>, Chapter 24 of the Section on Unity: The Supreme Glory is unified from its two sides. On the right, the light is grasped by the opening, so that there is an abundance of flow in that light... and the blue color from the upper side is grasped and unified with the white color. From below, it is unified and grasped at the beginning, which prepares it to shine. Without this preparation, there would be no place for this repair. For Israel is like the wick to the Glory; the Glory is grasped and unified through them, and they prepare it to shine. From the side of that preparation, the Glory is unified and grasped above in the White Light. The way to achieve this is through the fulfillment of the Torah and commandments and service with all one's heart and soul. End of quote.

He further wrote in the aforementioned chapter: In the order of the "Visions of the Hosts," he said this: Know and see that there is no awakening to light this "Blue Light" <note>Symbolizing the lower Divine presence or Shekhinah</note> and to make it cling to the upper Light except through Israel, who cling to it from below. Even though the nature of this Blue-Black Light is to consume everything that clings to it from below, Israel clings to it and endures because their souls are from it and not from elsewhere. This is the meaning of "But you who cling to the Lord your God"—it does not say "our God," but rather "your God," meaning to that Blue-Black Light which consumes what is below it, yet you cling to it and remain alive, as it says, "are all alive today." End of quote. And the "H" (*He*) is the final letter of the Holy Name, the "Holy Oil," which is the Blue-Black Light that unites with the "Y-H-V" (*Yod-He-Vav*) which is the White Light. Understand this. Come and see: sometimes this Blue Light is called *Dalet* <note>The 4th letter, meaning "poor"</note> and sometimes *He* <note>The 5th letter</note>. When Israel does not cling to it to seal it and light it and unify it with the White Light, it is a *Dalet*, meaning poor and wretched. But when they awaken it to connect with the White Light, it is called *He*. As it says regarding the "young maiden" (*Na'arah*), it is written without the *He* because she had not yet connected with the male. Wherever the connection of male and female is not found, the *He* is not found; it departs from there and leaves only the *Dalet*. But as long as she connects with the illuminating White Light, she is called *He*, for through this, everything is unified. She clings to the White Light, and Israel clings to her from below and stands beneath her to light her, and thus everything becomes one. End of quote.

# **And Now**
I shall copy a teaching from the writings of the disciples of the Ari, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foremost 16th-century Kabbalist</note>. During the eight days of Hanukkah, it is forbidden to do work <note>Usually referring to the time the candles are burning</note>. This is because the light is received through the attribute of *Netzach* (Victory). In the time before the repair, the light was "turned into a destroyer," but now *Netzach* is repaired as "The Strength (*Netzach*) of Israel will not lie." Therefore, everything receives the light of the "White" <note>Pure Divine mercy</note> through *Netzach*. Through this, the Hasmonean priest John <note>Yochanan</note> returns during these eight days. She <note>The Shekhinah</note> can receive the light of *Hod* from *Hod* itself... Therefore, we say the "Al HaNissim" <note>For the Miracles</note> prayer during the blessing of *Modim*, which corresponds to *Hod*.

Know that there are three types of Unifications. One corresponds to *Ne-Ch-Y* <note>Netzach, Hod, Yesod—the "lower" emotional attributes</note>... in this unification, the Name is *Yod-He-Vav-He* and *Adonai*. Sometimes it corresponds to the "Chavah" <note>Eve/Manifestation</note> and there it is *Y-H-V-H* and *Elohim*. Sometimes it rises all the way to His *Keter* <note>Crown/The highest sefirot</note> and then it is *Y-H-V-H* and *Ehyeh*. The numerical value of these names in unification equals *Channu* <note>The first part of "Hanukkah," meaning "they rested"</note>. Hanukkah corresponds to *Ne-Ch-Y*, and we draw down to her the light of our Sanctuary, "The Lord is above us," to make her a "Lamp." The intention of the lighting is that a person should have his hand ready to light. It is placed above three handbreadths <note>Tefachim</note>, corresponding to *Ne-Ch-Y* which are three handbreadths, and below ten handbreadths because it does not rise to the "Head." We draw the light to her from the Head; therefore, if one places it within the ten handbreadths, he has fulfilled the obligation, for this is called her place, as she takes the light from all ten levels. But above ten handbreadths, Hanukkah has no place. On the Sabbath day, she rises to His *Keter* (Crown), and then her place is truly within all ten. Then she is called the "Sabbath Lamp" in perfection. Therefore, if one's hand cannot afford both oil for the Sabbath lamp and for the Hanukkah lamp, the Sabbath lamp takes precedence, for it is better to raise her to the very top, through all ten levels, rather than the Hanukkah lamp which is below. Even though the light comes to her from all ten, it is proper to light the Hanukkah lamp on Friday before the Sabbath lamp, because one should raise her little by little, from bottom to top, from level to level. But if one lit the Sabbath lamp first, she has already risen to the Head—how then could he light the Hanukkah lamp afterward and bring her back down to *Ne-Ch-Y*? Reflect on this.

# **Know**
That we light the lamp at sunset, for then it is the attribute of night, and she descends below to the "World of Creation" to "provide food for her household and a portion for her maidens." At that time, we draw down to her those lights that she had above. Since the essence of this drawing down is the light that comes to her from the "Head," which is the Name *Y-H-V-H Ehyeh*—which when filled with the letter *Yod* equals 210—this light can only be drawn to her for a short time. Therefore, the commandment of lighting is only for a short time: "until the feet leave the marketplace." The "marketplace" refers to the lower worlds. This lasts until that "trace" of light that followed her down to her place is exhausted. Therefore, the act of "lighting" constitutes the commandment, not the "placing" of the lamp. We do not raise her from her place at all, but rather draw light down to her place from above; this is the meaning of lighting.

Therefore, it is forbidden to make use of its light. Since the upper holy light descends all the way down to a place where the "External Forces" <note>Sitra Achra/Forces of negativity</note> are present, we are concerned that they might attach themselves to the upper light. Therefore, one must not derive benefit from the light. The intention of the blessings is to focus on the first Name *Y-H-V-H* in the blessing, aiming toward the unification of *Y-H-V-H* and *Ehyeh* filled with the letter *Yod*, which is the supreme unification we mentioned. For the word "To Light" (*LeHadlik*), one should intend the Names of 72, 63, 45, and 52 <note>Kabbalistic expansions of the Name YHVH</note>, for they equal the numerical value of *LeHadlik*. When we draw these three names from Him to her, she burns and shines and becomes a "Lamp" (*Ner*). Intend for the word "Lamp" (*Ner*) the names *Chanoch* and *Metatron* that we mentioned. In the initial letters of "To Light a Hanukkah Lamp" (*LeHadlik Ner Chanukkah*), which spell *NaChaL* <note>River/Stream</note>, one should intend the light that comes to the "Small Face" <note>Zeir Anpin/The emotive attributes</note> from the "Supreme Stream." For by the power of this light coming from above, he has the light to give to her to light her and make her shine. The intention is the Name of 48, the power of *Y-H-V-H*... and then the Name that equals *NaChaL*... for that is what was seen... the "shining of the face" for a time... and the *Aleph* within it becomes a simple, double, triple, and quadruple *Ehyeh* as follows: *A*, *A-H*, *A-H-Y*, *A-H-Y-H*, which equals 44, which is...

# The Matter of the Torah Scroll and the Matter of the House of God

And if it is impossible for the husband to fast, then a "break" <note>original: *hafsakah* — likely referring to a specific period of refraining from food or speech rather than a full daylight fast</note> is how good and how pleasant; in any case, let it be a complete fast according to all the regulations of public fasts.

->And this is the version of the prayer:<-

**You** are the Lord our God before You created the world; and You are our God since You created the world, and from world to world You are God. You created Your world so that Your divinity would be known through Your holy Torah, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "'In the beginning' <note>referring to the first word of Genesis</note>—for the sake of the Torah and for the sake of Israel." For they are Your people and Your inheritance whom You have chosen from all the nations, and You gave them Your holy Torah and brought them close to Your great Name. Regarding the sustenance of the world and the sustenance of the Torah, two commands came to us from the Lord our God. You wrote in Your Torah, "Be fruitful and multiply," and You wrote in Your Torah, "And you shall teach them to your children." The intention of both is one: for You did not create the world for emptiness, but created, formed, and made it to be inhabited for Your glory. This was so that we, our offspring, and the offspring of all Your people the House of Israel, may be knowers of Your Name and students of Your Torah. Therefore, I come before You, Lord, King of Kings, and I offer my supplication, my eyes hanging upon You until You show me grace and hear my prayer: to prepare for me sons and daughters, and that they too may be fruitful and multiply, they and their children and their children’s children until the end of all generations. This is for the purpose that they and I and all of us shall engage in Your holy Torah, to learn and to teach, to keep and to perform and to fulfill all the words of the study of Your Torah with love. Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah and make our hearts cling to Your commandments, to love and fear Your Name. Our Father, Merciful Father, give us all long and blessed lives. Who is like You, Father of Mercy, who remembers His creatures for life in mercy? Remember us for eternal life, as our father Abraham prayed, "O that Ishmael might live before You," which our Sages interpreted as "living in the fear of You." For this reason, I have come to request and plead before You that my seed and the seed of my seed forever be worthy offspring. Let there not be found in me, or in my seed, or in the seed of my seed forever any disqualification or blemish. Rather, let there be peace, truth, goodness, and uprightness in the eyes of God and in the eyes of man. May they be masters of Torah, masters of Scripture, masters of Mishnah, masters of Talmud, masters of the Secrets <note>Kabbalah</note>, masters of the Commandments, masters of acts of loving-kindness, and masters of noble character traits. May they serve You in love and in fear—an inner fear, not a superficial fear. Give to each and every body among them enough for their needs with dignity. Grant them health, honor, and strength. Give them stature, beauty, grace, and kindness. Let there be love, brotherhood, and peace among them. Provide them with suitable matches from the families of Torah scholars and righteous people. And let their spouses be like them in all that I have prayed for them, for one remembrance rises for both sides. You, O Lord, know all secrets, and the hidden things of my heart are revealed before You. For my intention in all this is for the sake of Your great and holy Name and for the sake of Your holy Torah. Therefore, answer me, O Lord, answer me for the sake of the holy ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; because of them, save the children so the branches resemble their roots. And for the sake of David Your servant, the "fourth leg of the Chariot" <note>A Kabbalistic concept where the Patriarchs and David form the foundation of divine presence</note>, who sang by Your holy spirit: "A Song of Ascents: Happy is everyone who fears the Lord..." until "Peace be upon Israel." Please, O Lord, Who hears prayer. May the verse be fulfilled: "As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have placed in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the Lord, from now and forever." May the words of my mouth be acceptable...

->To ensure that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not "deduct" my merits in this world <note>a fear that enjoying material wealth now uses up the reward meant for the afterlife</note>, and the oaths/weeks a day before the eve of the New Moon of Nisan. For in Nisan they were redeemed, and they are also written in my name.<-
->And this is the version of the prayer:<-

**You** are the God who feeds all, from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice. You are the one who prepares all their needs. In addition to the necessary needs, You are the one who gives in fullness, abundance, wealth, and honor. All this You do out of the generosity of Your good heart, for You are truly generous—not like a human who is sometimes called "generous" but whose generosity is not true, being only a repayment of a debt or for a favor previously received, like a merchant. But Your grace is encompassing and Your providence is from the generosity of Your good heart. You are good and do good to all, and to me, Your servant, You have done more good than all, giving me wealth and honor from the Creator of all. You have blessed me with everything. You have given me many books, silver and gold in abundance, garments of honor, a dignified dwelling, and possessions acquired through kindness and mercy which You have performed for me. You have been great toward me, and I am very small in comparison. Let this not be, Heaven forbid, like "wealth guarded for its owner to his hurt," to feed me the meager merits I have in my hand. If it be so, take back my blessing, but let me not see my ruin in the world to come, the eternal world. But if it is Your good will to give and not to take back, put into my heart and the hearts of all who accompany me not to use Your gifts for physical pleasures; rather, let Torah scholars, upright people, and worthy people be supported by it. Let us perform justice, kindness, and acts of loving-kindness for those near and far. And the word of the Lord shall stand. May the words of my mouth be acceptable...

<margin>It is proper to establish a fast regarding the matter of repentance, and the matter of the Torah and its commandments, and regarding the character traits—specifically the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He. One should make the "break" <note>hafsakah</note> during the month of Tammuz; if he cannot, he should fast on the 17th of Tammuz and pray. For from the 17th of Tammuz it is fitting that the "days of darkness" begin. From this, everything written begins to darken from the 15th of Av onwards... and in the meantime, they should not fast on Sabbaths or Festivals and the like. And I say to begin early from the 17th of Tammuz, when judgment is intensified, and he should fast for an equal number of days, and in any case, they should all be days of repentance.</margin>

And he said: "Blessed is our God who created us for His glory..." and let us not go into confusion, and return us in complete repentance before You to be protected by the Throne of Glory. Sanctify us, purify us, and place Your love and fear in our hearts—an inner love and fear—to fulfill the entire Torah for its own sake. Let us cling to You so that we may emulate Your holy attributes which are possible to cling to, and these are some of Your ways: As it is written in Your Torah, "And the Lord passed by..." <note>referring to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy</note> until "and He clears." I have offered my prayer to You at an acceptable time, that You should place kindness in my heart always—will and kindness, and remove anger from my heart. May it be Your will, Lord our God, who guards the trust...

They should turn their faces to the wall... and pray:</margin>

Answer us, O Lord, answer us on the day of our fast... until "and I will hear." Answer us, O Lord, answer us... Who answered [the righteous]... and at the time of the reading, Merciful One, have mercy on all the births of the daughters of Israel, and among them Your handmaid, my wife [Name] the daughter of [Name]. Show us grace before You, Merciful and Gracious One, for Your mercies are many. And as the Lord holds this "Key of Birthing" and has not handed it to a messenger, so remember Your mercies, O Lord... You who desire life, remember her for salvation and mercy. May the child be a viable and worthy seed from the side of holiness. And she said: "Remember me and I shall give birth." As King David said: "I was answered and I hoped." He said: "From the depths I called to the Lord, the Lord answered me with expansiveness. The Lord is with me, I shall not fear." "For the Leader, a Psalm of David: May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble..." until "He will answer us on the day we call." May He who heard the prayer of David hear our prayer in the merit of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs—in the merit of He who answered our mothers with their pregnancies: Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel, Leah, and Hannah, and all the righteous and pious women. May He answer us. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable...

# Completed: The Chapter "Lamp of Commandment"

### **Chapter: Torah is Light**

They established Hanukkah to praise and give thanks with the blessing of Thanksgiving, and to light candles for eight days. Hanukkah is eight days, corresponding to the eight *Sefirot* <note>Divine emanations</note>... thirty gates of light. In the books of the Zohar, the secret... is clothed in the attribute of *Gevurah* <note>Strength/Judgment</note> and power to humble the enemies and win wars and save those who love the Lord... because this is the place of victory in wars and the performance of miracles and wonders. Regarding this place, the "Arms" <note>the sefirot of Netzach and Hod</note> are mentioned, and all types of thanksgivings that David (peace be upon him) said in the Book of Psalms are associated with these two adjacent attributes. The thanksgivings for miracles and wonders are fixed in this place... "His wonders to the children of men." In the secret of the "Four who must give thanks": a sick person who was healed, a prisoner who left the dungeon, those who cross the seas, and those who walk through deserts. In this place, He "bestows good things upon the guilty," for in these two attributes, He inclines the sources through which angels are appointed to tear up a person’s sentence if death or other punishments were decreed upon him. This is the secret of what the Sages said: "It tears up a sentence of seventy years," for seventy princes <note>guardian angels of the nations</note> stand in the Heavenly Court... and that verdict which the witnesses sign there has a remedy in this place. Therefore, the four must...

# The Matter of the Order of Fasting

And if it is impossible for the husband to fast or to perform a "break" <note>Hebrew: *Hafsaqah*, referring to a specific mystical practice of fasting for consecutive days</note>, how good and how pleasant it would be for the fast at least to be carried out completely according to all the laws of a public fast:

->And this is the text of the prayer:<-

**You** are the Lord our God before You created the world; and You are our God since You created the world, and from world to world You are God. You created Your world in order to make Your Divinity known through Your holy Torah, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "In the beginning" <note>The first word of Genesis</note>—for the sake of the Torah and for the sake of Israel. For they are Your people and Your inheritance whom You have chosen from all the nations, and You gave them Your holy Torah and brought them close to Your great Name. For the existence of the world and the existence of the Torah, two commands came to us from our God: You wrote in Your Torah, "Be fruitful and multiply," and You wrote in Your Torah, "And you shall teach them to your children." The intention of both is the same, for You did not create the world for emptiness, but created, formed, and made it to be inhabited for Your glory; so that we, our offspring, and the offspring of all Your people the House of Israel, may be knowers of Your Name and students of Your Torah. Therefore, I come before You, O Lord, King of kings, and I lay my supplication before You, and my affairs are dependent on You until You show me grace and hear my prayer: to provide me with sons and daughters, and let them also be fruitful and multiply, they and their children and their children's children until the end of all generations, for the purpose that they and I and all of us shall engage in Your holy Torah—to learn and to teach, to observe and to perform and to fulfill all the words of the study of Your Torah with love. Enlighten our eyes in Your Torah and make our hearts cling to Your commandments, to love and fear Your Name. Our Father, Merciful Father, grant us Your mercy and long and blessed life. Who is like You, Merciful Father, who remembers His creatures for life in mercy? Remember me for eternal life, as our father Abraham prayed, "Would that [Ishmael] live before You," which the Sages explained as: "living in the fear of You." For this reason, I have come to request and beg before You that my offspring and the offspring of my offspring forever shall be worthy offspring. Let there not be found in me, or in my offspring, or in my offspring's offspring forever, any blemish or stain; but only peace, truth, goodness, and uprightness in the eyes of God and in the eyes of man. May they be masters of Torah, masters of Scripture, masters of Mishnah, masters of Talmud, masters of the Secret <note>Kabbalah</note>, masters of the Commandments, masters of acts of loving-kindness, and masters of noble character traits. May they serve You in love and fear—an internal fear, not an external fear. And provide for all their needs, for each and every body among them, enough for their lack with honor. Give them health, honor, and strength. Give them stature, beauty, grace, and kindness. Let there be love, brotherhood, peace, and friendship among them. Provide them with suitable matches from the families of Torah scholars and righteous people, and may their spouses be like them in everything I have prayed for, for one memory rises for both this and that. You, O Lord, know all secrets, and the hidden things of my heart are revealed before You; for my intention in all of this is for the sake of Your great and holy Name and for the sake of Your holy Torah. Therefore, answer me, O Lord, answer me for the sake of the holy Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and because of them, save the children for the sake of the fathers—the branches similar to their roots—and for the sake of David Your servant, the fourth leg of the Chariot <note>A mystical reference to King David as a support for the Divine Presence</note>, the singer through Your holy spirit: "A song of Ascents: Happy is everyone who fears the Lord..." until "Peace be upon Israel." Please, O Lord, Hearer of prayer, let the verse be fulfilled: "As for me, this is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have placed in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your offspring, nor from the mouth of your offspring's offspring, says the Lord, from now and forever." May the words of my mouth be acceptable, etc.
<note>This is the famous Tefillat HaShelah (Prayer of the Shelah) for children.</note>

->It is proper to say this every eve of the New Month, and specifically the eve of Rosh Chodesh Sivan; for in Nisan they were redeemed, and from blood to blessing I have opened my eyes.<-
->And this is the text of the prayer:<-

**You** are the God who sustains from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice <note>A traditional phrase meaning God cares for all creatures, from the largest to the most minuscule</note>; and You are He who prepares all their needs. In addition to the necessary needs, You are the one who gives in fullness, abundance, wealth, and honor, for this follows the ten [attributes] as You have spoken. For You are truly generous—not like a human is sometimes called generous, for his generosity is not true but only to repay a favor or because of a previous kindness, making him like a merchant. But from the first to the last, and especially from Your good heart: You are good and do good to all. I am Your servant, spread out before You, and You have given me wealth, kindness, and blessing in all the work of my hands. You blessed me "with everything, from everything, in everything." You gave me many books, much good, many clothes, honor, and a respected dwelling. I am unworthy of all the kindnesses You have done for me. May it be Your will that I should be very mindful of my soul, so that, God forbid, wealth should not be "guarded for its owner to his hurt" by consuming the few merits I have. If it is so, take my blessing, for I do not wish to see my misfortune in the eternal world to come. But if it is Your good will to do good to me, let my silver, my gold, and everything attached to me not be used for physical pleasures, but let Torah scholars, worthy men, and upright men be sustained by it. Let it be used to perform charity and kindness for relatives and strangers. May the word of the Lord stand. May the words of my mouth be acceptable, etc. It is proper to set times for the awakening of repentance, the awakening of Torah and its commandments, and the awakening of character traits—specifically the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Perform the "interruption" <note>consecutive fast</note> on the 7th of Tammuz, and if impossible, fast on the 17th of Tammuz and pray. For the 17th of Tammuz is the peak of sickness and the waters of repentance. For the Maharal of blessed memory wrote to begin fasting from the 15th of Av onwards, those who fast forty days and recite Psalms for forty days and perform the "Repair of Kindness" eighteen times, and so on. But I say to begin earlier, on the 7th of Tammuz, which is the "Fast of Raziel," and fast during those fearsome days, but let all of them be days of repentance. And say: "Blessed be our God who created us for His glory, etc." We shall not go to destruction. Return us in complete repentance before You, so that it reaches the Throne of Glory. Sanctify us and purify us, and place in our hearts Your love and Your fear—an internal love and fear—to fulfill the entire Torah for Your Name's sake. Cling to Him so that we may be doing Your will, and he shall be dismissed from riding upon them; and these are some of Your ways, as it is written in Your Torah: "And the Lord passed before him..." until "and He clears [the guilty]." As for me, my prayer is to You, O Lord, at an acceptable time, that You place the desire for the King's pleasantness in my heart. May it be Your will, O Lord our God, and guard us from investigation, etc. When a woman is confined in her pregnancy in the ninth month, it is proper to establish a fast. Toward evening, before she eats, they should give charity to worthy poor people, search their deeds and rectify them, and repair any damage to this one's life and that one's life, and pray: "Answer us, O Lord, answer us on our fast day," etc. until "and I will hear. Answer us, O Lord, answer us, our God, answer us, etc." "He who answered..." until "and in a time near." O Merciful One, build up all the young women of Israel, including Your handmaid Sarah Malchut <note>original: שרה מלכות</note>, my wife. May they grant kindness and answer with kindness before You, O Merciful and Gracious One, for Your mercies are abundant. Blessed be the Lord who desired her. Grant my vision a living child and not a dead one, for peace, and with a male child. Remember Your mercies, O Lord, and support, O Lord our God, who desires life, to visit her with salvation and mercy. Let her give birth with ease and not in pain, with a stable birth... and let her be prepared for Your visitation. And I am the "pleasant singer of Psalms," who said: "From the depths I called to God; God answered me in the expanse. The Lord is with me, I shall not fear." "For the conductor, a psalm of David: May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble," etc. until "He will answer us on the day we call." He who heard the prayer of David, He shall hear our prayer in the merit of the Patriarchs and the Matriarchs. He who answered our holy mothers Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel, and Leah, and Hannah, and all the righteous and pious women—He shall answer us. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable, etc.

# The Chapter "The Lamp of the Commandment" is completed

## Chapter "The Torah is Light"

**Chapter: The Torah is Light.** They established Hanukkah to praise and give thanks with the blessing of Thanksgiving, and to kindle lamps for eight days. Hanukkah is eight days... and so it is written in the *Sefer Sha'are Orah* <note>Gates of Light, a famous Kabbalistic work by Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla</note> in the section on the Attribute of Secret, which is called *Chesed* <note>Kindness</note> when it is clothed in the attribute of *Gevurah* <note>Might</note>. It merited to humble the enemies and win wars and save us. O Lord, Your kindness and splendor turned upon me for a family, and it did not pass... It is the place of victory in wars and the wealth of miracles and wonders. Regarding this place, the Zohar says—and it is a hint that David, peace be upon him, said in the book of Psalms regarding these two attributes [Netzach and Hod]—Succoth and thanksgivings for the miracles and wonders. In this place of holiness... "They shall give thanks to the Lord for His kindness and His wonders to the children of men." There are four who must give thanks: such as a sick person who was healed, a prisoner who was released from jail, those who cross the seas, and those who walk in the desert. In this place, He bestows good things upon the guilty. During these days of Hanukkah, there are portions in which angels are appointed to collect the judgment of a person, if death or other punishments were decreed upon him. This is the secret of what the Sages said: "It tears up a decree of seventy years," for there are seventy princes who stand in the Supernal Court and one who tips the scale. That verdict which they sign there still has a remedy in this place. Therefore, four require [thanksgiving]...

# Completed is Tractate Tamid with the help of the Creator and Sustainer of all.
## Tractate Megillah: The Pillar of Charity

->The verse: A pillar of charity for the weary, for in it you shall guard a crown from the pit, gifts for the needy.<-

<margin>Regarding the Four Portions <note>Special Torah portions read in the weeks leading up to Passover: Shekalim, Zakhor, Parah, and HaChodesh.</note>, the ears of all the people must be directed toward the Cantor <term>Shliach Tzibbur|The community representative who leads the prayer and reading.</term> while he reads the portion from the Torah scroll, so that they hear it from his mouth. Some of these readings are a biblical requirement, as written.</margin>
**Chapter 54: The Commandment of the Four Portions and Purim.** A bridegroom <note>original: "Chatan"</note> as mentioned in the second chapter of Megillah. Similarly, in the *Sefer Mitzvot Katan* <note>A 13th-century legal code by Rabbi Isaac of Corbeil.</note>, he counted the remembrance of the deeds of Amalek as a positive commandment; this is the portion of *Zakhor* <note>"Remember," read before Purim.</note>. Therefore, Mahari Sh. <note>likely Rabbi Isaac Stein</note> wrote that those who cannot come to a prayer quorum <term>Minyan|A group of ten Jewish adults required for communal prayer.</term> for the portion of *Zakhor* must be careful to say it themselves with the proper cantillation and melodies. In the *Tosafot* <note>Medieval commentaries on the Talmud.</note> for the chapter "The One Who Reads," they wrote that the portion of *Zakhor* and the portion of *Parah* <note>"The Red Heifer."</note> are biblical obligations. Further explanation is found in *Orach Chaim* section 147 and section 684. Mahari L. wrote in the *Book of Customs* that according to the consensus of opinion, regarding the portion of *Parah*, whatever the case may be, the obligation falls upon every person by Rabbinic decree at the very least to hear its reading from the Torah. It was said that this is even more significant than the readings of the rest of the year, which are also a communal obligation. Nevertheless, if there are ten people present—that is, the Cantor and nine others—it is well, and there would be permission for others to engage in Torah study [privately], as explained. But for these specific portions, the obligation lies upon every individual Israelite to hear them, some by biblical law and some by Rabbinic law.

Now I shall explain the matter for the rest of the year. We learn in the chapter "These are Spoken": "When it was opened, he returned and spoke to the book, even in matters of Torah." For it says, "And when he opened it, all the people stood," and "standing" refers to nothing other than silence, as it is said, "For they stood and answered no more." Regarding what is said in the chapter "Those who Bless," that one may review his portions even while the Torah is being read—Rashi <note>The preeminent 11th-century commentator Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki.</note> explained that he would study in a whisper. The prohibition against speaking refers specifically to speaking loudly, because it prevents others from hearing. However, in a whisper, it is permitted. This is the fourth view: that it is proper to forbid speaking only if there are not ten people listening to the Torah scroll. But if there are ten listening, it is fine. A third view is more pressured: [it was permitted to] Rav Sheshet, whose Torah study was his sole occupation, but for any other person, it is forbidden. In the Responsa of the Rosh <note>Rabbi Asher ben Jehiel.</note>, he wrote: they desire that there be ten people listening to the Torah reading, but if there are only ten present, it is forbidden for anyone to speak, even in a whisper, for there must be ten people actively listening to the scroll. All individuals are only permitted when there are [already] ten others listening. Rashi did not permit it even with ten, except in a whisper; out loud, it is forbidden. 

Consider what was said in the chapter "These are Spoken": once the Torah scroll is opened, it is forbidden to speak even in matters of Torah. In *Orach Chaim* section 100, it says if there are ten listening, it is permitted even out loud, and that the passage in "These are Spoken" refers to when there are not ten. Rashi, however, believes that "These are Spoken" refers to when there are not ten, as it states plainly "once the scroll is opened it is forbidden," meaning even out loud. According to the Rif <note>Rabbi Isaac Alfasi, 11th-century legalist.</note>, there is no permission at all except for one whose Torah is his sole occupation. But according to all opinions, there must at least be ten people listening, for if not, the enactment of the early sages to read the Torah in public is nullified, and all the blessings would be in vain. Even for those individuals mentioned above, there must be ten others listening, as the *Beit Yosef* <note>The 16th-century legal commentary by Rabbi Joseph Karo.</note> wrote there in section 146. 

Note that all these types of permissions written by the commentators to be lenient regarding hearing the Torah reading do not apply to the portion of *Zakhor*, which is biblically mandated to be heard in a quorum of ten, as explained in the words of the Rosh in the third chapter of *Berakhot* and in the *Smak*. The *Tosafot* also wrote that *Zakhor* and *Parah* are biblical. This means that in those cases, the entire congregation is required to listen. Even regarding the other [two] portions which are Rabbinic, they are still weightier than the readings of the rest of the year where there might be a side of leniency. For these special portions, there is no side of leniency, just as with *Zakhor*, for all four portions are linked together. Every Rabbinic enactment is modeled after a biblical one. Would that even during the rest of the year, a person would remain utterly silent during the Torah reading and not rely on the aforementioned leniencies. This is also implied in the *Shibolei HaLeket* <note>A 13th-century Italian halakhic work.</note>, which the *Beit Yosef* cited: "I found written in the name of our Master Simcha: why is it the custom now to read and look into books while they are reading the Torah? It could be said that only speaking is forbidden so as not to be distracted from listening, but reading in a whisper is fine. However, my father wondered at this, for it is also a commandment to hear the Torah reading, as it is written: 'And the ears of all the people were toward the book of the Torah.' If one reads from a [private] book, he cannot understand what is being read [publicly]. Therefore, it appears to be forbidden." Thus far are the words of the *Shibolei HaLeket*. And regarding Rav Sheshet, Rabbeinu Yonah wrote that since he was blind, he was not obligated in the Rabbinic reading from a written scroll, and thus could study by heart. But any other person who can see and is obligated in the reading is forbidden from speaking. Therefore, I say: "Happy is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it" <note>Isaiah 56:2</note>, that he should not rely on the leniencies even during the rest of the year, and his hearing should never cease from the Cantor's reading from this book.

<margin>A voluntary offering must come only from secular funds <note>original: "chullin"</note>, as stated in Tractate Chagigah regarding the burnt offering of appearance and the festival offering, which do not come from tithe money but from secular funds. Likewise, the entire matter of Purim involves merit through the half-shekel, and certainly *Mishloach Manot* <term>Mishloach Manot|The practice of sending gift baskets of food to friends.</term> and gifts to the poor. A person should spend his own money on these, not his tithe money <term>Ma'aser|The tenth of one's income set aside for charity.</term>. As I found written: "Specifically from his own," as Mahari Weil responded. With tithe money, one does not fulfill his obligation toward the poor. It seems to me that in those places where they set a fixed assessment for every soul to maintain the Purim charity fund, they do not fulfill the obligation of 'gifts to the poor' through this, for it is included in the community fees. If one did not pay that assessment, the Cantor's salary would have to be increased. Thus, that charity would be for his own benefit [to pay his debts] and not for the poor. Rather, one must give regardless, according to the generosity of his hand. However, if he has already set aside what is required by his means and wishes to add more, it seems permitted to add from his tithe money.</margin>
**Everything**

<margin>The reading of the Megillah is stringent and is a greater commandment than those of the Torah <note>A traditional rabbinic phrasing emphasizing the importance of Rabbinic decrees.</note>. It is a commandment that comes only once a year, yet the world is not careful to read from a proper Megillah scroll written on parchment with ink according to all its laws, or to hear it entirely from the mouth of the Cantor. This practice is evil in my eyes, for the noise of the people is so great in the synagogue that it is impossible to hear it all from the Cantor. Some are so distracted that they open a printed Pentateuch <term>Chumash|A printed book of the Five Books of Moses, as opposed to a hand-written scroll.</term> and read from it. Consequently, these people do not fulfill the commandment of reading the Megillah, which is a fleeting commandment with no substitute throughout the year. This undermines the very essence of the commandment. Therefore, a man should awaken and take this to heart, doing one of two things: either go and stand next to the Cantor as he reads, or have a proper Megillah scroll open before him to read from.</margin>
**Commandment**

<margin>When reciting the blessings over the Megillah reading and the *Shehecheyanu* <note>The "Who has kept us alive" blessing for seasonal occasions.</note>, one should intend to fulfill the obligation of these blessings also for the Purim meal he will eat and the commandment of sending portions. For the Purim meal and *Mishloach Manot* are also commandments from the Words of Tradition <note>Prophetic/Hagiographic books, specifically Esther.</note>, and it would have been appropriate to bless over them separately. *Shehecheyanu* is said for things that come from time to time, just as we bless on Hanukkah. Specifically, the blessings for the Megillah refer to the reading itself and the fulfillment of the positive commandment of the meal and the sending of portions. Just as the *Shehecheyanu* in the holiday Kiddush covers the Sukkah, so too must the one hearing the blessings intend for them to cover these as well.</margin>
**When blessing**

<margin>In lands outside Israel, there are ancient Persian cities that are large and fortified. There is a doubt regarding them: perhaps they were walled in the days of Joshua son of Nun. Therefore, it is proper for one who has the fear of God in his heart to be stringent and read the Megillah from a proper scroll on both the night and day of the 15th [of Adar] as well, though without a blessing. I have already hinted that a man should be fearful and anxious regarding the commandments, and certainly for a fleeting commandment that only occurs once a year; one should be doubly and triply diligent.</margin>
**There is**

**Purim:** It is permitted to do work, but in a place where the custom is not to work, one does not work. One who does work will never see a sign of blessing from it. In the Yemeni glosses on the "Questions," it is written...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the laws and mystical meanings behind the Hebrew calendar and the four special Torah readings leading up to Passover. It transitions into a deep Kabbalistic analysis of King Saul, Samuel the Prophet, and the struggle against Amalek.</meta>

<header>Candle of Commandment 263</header>

Before Passover, they perform the Passover sacrifice in a state of purity. The portion of *HaChodesh* <note>The "Portion of the Month," Exodus 12:1–20, the fourth of four special Shabbat readings</note> is read on the fourth Sabbath because of the New Moon of Nisan, which is the essence of the day, as the month of Nisan is the head of all months and the order of the festivals. Our Sages of blessed memory said that by law, the portion of *HaChodesh* should have preceded the portion of *Parah* <note>The "Portion of the Red Heifer," Numbers 19:1–22, dealing with ritual purification</note> because the Tabernacle was erected on the first of Nisan, while the Red Heifer was burned on the second. 

Why then does the portion of *Parah* come first? Because it represents the purification of Israel from the impurity of death, so that they will not be excluded from the Passover sacrifice and forced to wait for the "Second Passover" <note>A makeup date for those ritually impure during the primary holiday</note>.

---

## From the words of *Kanfei Yonah* <note>original: "Kanfei Yonah" (Wings of a Dove), a classic Kabbalistic work by Rabbi Menahem Azariah da Fano</note> (Section 23): The secret of Purim is *Netzach* and *Hod* <note>The Sefirot (Divine emanations) representing Victory/Endurance and Splendor/Glory</note>, the two halves of the "body," which are Purim and Hanukkah.

->Hanukkah is in *Hod* and Purim is in *Netzach*<-

Who can estimate the victory of Israel in the days of Purim? It is written concerning the kingdom of Saul, where Samuel the Prophet said: *“And also the Victory of Israel will not lie”* <note>1 Samuel 15:29. The word for "Victory" (Netzach) is also the name of the Sefirah</note>. It is also said: *“In the morning he shall devour the prey”*—this refers to Saul; *“and at night he shall divide the spoil”*—this refers to Mordecai and Esther <note>Referencing the blessing of Benjamin in Genesis 49:27, as both Saul and Mordecai were from the tribe of Benjamin</note>. There is a great matter in this verse: *“And also the Victory [Netzach] of Israel will not lie.”* It is known that *Netzach* and *Hod* are the thighs: *Netzach* is the right thigh and *Hod* is the left thigh.

Mordecai did not bow with his hands <note>to Haman</note> and he bound his strength in his "thigh." This relates to the "bill of sale" by which Haman was sold to him <note>Midrashic tradition states Haman once sold himself as a slave to Mordecai for bread</note>. For Esau likewise sold his birthright to Jacob for food, as it is written: *“Feed me, I pray thee, of that red, red pottage.”* The author of the *Tzioni* <note>Rabbi Menahem Tzioni, 14th-century Kabbalist</note> on the portion of *Toledot* writes: *“And the first came out red [admoni], all over like a hairy garment.”* It is understood that he was the dross of Isaac. This is the secret of *“Amalek was the first of the nations”* <note>Numbers 24:20</note>. Amalek is the root of the Primordial Serpent. The Kabbalists wrote that he had the image of a serpent on his thigh. Onkelos <note>The famous Aramaic translator of the Torah</note> translates *“He shall bruise your head”* in a way that alludes to the serpent's power in the thighs. Regarding Jacob, it is written: *“And he touched the hollow of his thigh”* <note>Genesis 32:25</note>. The serpent saw Jacob appearing like the face of Adam the first man and saw he could not overcome him. Regarding the "Serpent of Ammon" <note>Nahash the Ammonite</note> at the start of Saul’s reign—behold, the serpent dwells in the thigh because the "offspring of the angels" originate there. <note>original: "ע' חטא שאול משד ק"ל" - likely a reference to a specific Kabbalistic calculation or source regarding Saul's sin</note>. 

Look there in the gloss: It is said, *“And the first came out red [admoni],”* but this is not like the "redness" of David, of whom it is said he was *“ruddy [admoni] with beautiful eyes and goodly to look at.”* Therefore, David's descendant Perez *“breached the fence”* of the serpent. Because David was "red" from the aspect of "beautiful eyes," he stems from the attribute of Mercy (*Chesed*) of Abraham and "goodly to look at" from the attribute of Beauty (*Tiferet*). These two attributes were joined; in every generation, he fought with Justice (*Din*), but when he sustained Israel, he did so with "beautiful eyes and goodly to look at," according to the order of the Torah. 

To descend to the depths of this matter, one must know what was written and explained regarding "Jacob’s thigh" and the commentary of Galante <note>Rabbi Abraham Galante, a student of the Ramak in Safed</note> on the verse *“They hunt our steps”* etc. Galante writes: It is worthy to consider what deed Samuel did to revive this bitter state, and what connection he had with Saul in the species of "rectification" (*Tikkun*). When Saul corrupted what he was meant to do, Samuel said to him: *“And also the Victory [Netzach] of Israel will not lie nor repent...”* What is the meaning of the verse, and why does it say "And also"? Furthermore, what did David rectify, and how? Is it because he said *“At Your right hand are pleasures forever [Netzach]”*? And why was it Samuel specifically who had to rectify this more than other prophets?

The matter is that the very first of the first foundations of the Righteous One were his "first stones." This was a wonderful virtue that was not corrupted by Esau as his brothers were, for Benjamin <note>the ancestor of Saul</note> was not yet born when the others bowed to Esau. Esau corrupted the thought and the flow from above to below. After Esau followed the stars and corrupted himself into the "Other Side" <note>term: *Sitra Achra* — the Kabbalistic realm of evil or impurity</note>, the Prince of Esau <note>the angel Samael</note> struck the thigh of Jacob in the evening, in its place, and the "Other Side" gained power through this. As the Zohar asks: *“And Jacob passed before them and bowed to the ground seven times”*—how could the perfect Jacob bow to the wicked Esau who is of the "Other Side"? They answer there that it was the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) passing before them, and he bowed to the Divine Presence. However, this defense only applied to Jacob; the other tribes actually bowed. But the righteous Benjamin, who was not yet born, did not receive any law or influence from Esau's hand. 

Therefore, it was within the power of Saul, Benjamin's descendant, to subdue Amalek. Through him, the "thigh" was to return to its place on the Right and rectify the blemish that Samael caused to Jacob’s thigh (*Netzach*), which represents the power of accusation that draws Judgment (*Gevurah*) from the side of the evening. 

When Samuel anointed Saul with the Holy Spirit, he knew the rectification would be done through Saul via the anointing oil. Samuel said: *“Set aside the portion which I gave you.”* It is written: *“And the cook took up the shoulder, and that which was upon it, and set it before Saul.”* Samuel said to him: *“Behold that which hath been reserved! Set it before thee and eat; for unto the appointed time hath it been kept for thee.”* This was a hint that the "shoulder and its upper part" and "Jacob's thigh" are the root. Prophecy cannot be manifest without this, as it is written: *“The word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no frequent vision.”* This source of prophecy was closed and sealed by the power of Judgment. Samuel told him "Behold that which is left," meaning: here is the remnant that did not bow to Esau like the other tribes. Now, go with this strength of yours and rectify it. "For the appointed time it was kept," meaning through the cycles of times it was kept for you to rectify. 

As soon as Saul ate and took it upon himself to rectify, he immediately opened the source of prophecy. Samuel told him: *“You shall meet a band of prophets... and the Spirit of the Lord will come mightily upon you, and you shall prophesy with them, and shall be turned into another man.”* When those who knew him previously saw him prophesying, they were amazed and said, *“Is Saul also among the prophets?”* Even Saul, who had been a herder of cattle, became a prophet. This is the secret of the verse: *“Beforetime in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, thus he said: 'Come and let us go to the seer'; for he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer.”* This change happened specifically from that day forward, because previously the word of the Lord was "precious" (rare). 

The reason this was drawn down through Samuel is that he was a Levite, and his root was in Judgment (*Gevurah*). By drawing down the oil, which comes from Wisdom (*Chokmah*), the Judgments in this "thigh" were sweetened so it could be rectified and return to the "Right" side. Samuel hinted at this: *“The Lord sent me to anoint you to be king.”* Specifically with oil, for through this it is partially rectified. *“Now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord”*—meaning the inner meaning of the words—*“and smite Amalek.”* Since you are from Benjamin and Amalek is the son of Esau, Amalek can only fall by your hand. Samuel warned him: *“Though you be little in your own eyes, you are the head of the tribes of Israel.”* Because Benjamin the righteous did not bow to Esau, you, coming from his power, are the "head," and no one can rectify this but you. 

When Saul had pity on Agag <note>The King of Amalek</note>, it grieved Samuel greatly, and he cried to the Lord all night, fearing that this matter would return to oblivion. His cry helped somewhat, for he later said: *“And also the Victory [Netzach] of Israel will not lie nor repent.”* Meaning: even though you sinned and transgressed the word of God, the "Victory of Israel" will not lie in its faith; it remains rectified in the secret of the Right and will not turn back to the Left. 

Later, when Saul sent messengers to take David, they also prophesied, and Samuel was standing as head over them. They all prophesied from his power. However, it was not fully established until David came. This was hinted to Samuel when he first saw Saul: *“This one shall govern [ya’atzor] My people,”* meaning he shall "restrain" the blemish so it does not spread, but he will not rectify it completely. The blemish would remain covered until David arrived. 

When Saul realized he had sinned, he entreated Samuel: *“Honor me now before the elders of my people... that I may worship the Lord.”* He hoped that through his bowing, he might destroy the "feet" of the external forces, following the example of Benjamin the righteous who did not bow to Esau. Samuel complied: *“So Samuel turned back after Saul; and Saul worshipped the Lord.”* 

When Agag heard that Samuel intended to kill him, he said: *“Surely the bitterness of death is at hand.”* He thought that since Saul had delayed, the blemish would remain in its place. Had Saul killed him and all his people and possessions, he would have wiped out that blemish from that place. But because he had pity on Agag and the best of the sheep, he corrupted what he had begun to rectify. Therefore, Samuel mourned, thinking the "thigh" would never return to its strength, until God said: *“How long will you mourn for Saul? Fill your horn with oil.”* Draw down the holy anointing oil from the source of oil and go to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen a king among his sons who shall rectify...
