# Part Two of the Two Tablets of the Covenant

**This pamphlet** I am now composing with the help of the Blessed Name; I shall keep the utterance of my lips and fulfill two promises I made to compose works. First, in Tractate Shabbat, regarding the matter of the "lot of the commandments" <term>Shnayim Mikra ve-Echad Targum; the practice of reading the weekly Torah portion twice in Hebrew and once in the Aramaic translation</term> which our Sages (of blessed memory) commanded us to complete. Surely the intention is to learn and to teach, to keep, to perform, and to fulfill. Therefore, a person must know and reflect upon every single portion and every matter of the commandments written in that portion, whether they are positive commandments or negative prohibitions, until the completion of all 613 <term>Taryag; the total number of biblical commandments</term>. Even though there are many portions where a specific commandment is not found, or it is not an individual commandment among the 613, it is nonetheless a "great commandment" and a branch of a commandment counted among the 613. Afterward, I shall explain the reasons for the commandments and their secrets <note>mystical or Kabbalistic meanings</note> according to the reach of my intellect. Following that, I will explain the character traits and ethical lessons <term>Musar</term> emerging from the portion. These three paths are: **The Lamp of the Commandment**, **The Torah is Light**, and **The Way of Life is Ethical Rebuke**. <note>A reference to Proverbs 6:23: "For the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life."</note> Happy is the one with a "good eye" regarding this composition. "The Way of Life" and the count of the commandments in each portion—this is the **Lamp of the Commandment**. The reasons and the secrets—this is **The Torah is Light**. And this, my children, and the ethics and traits—this is **The Way of Life**. And you, my sons (may God protect and sustain you), with this I have come to reveal a small drop from the sea in every portion of the week. May you be like an ever-strengthening spring, adding more and more in wisdom, knowledge, and understanding.

**Now**, the proper place for this would have been earlier in Tractate Shabbat, regarding the obligation to complete the portions, to write a summary of each portion. However, so as not to cause an interruption there, I left it to be a separate pamphlet. This is the name by which the section composed on the Torah portions shall be called: **The Written Torah**.

**The second promise** I made was in Tractate Shevuot, where I intended to speak of the excellence and loftiness of the Sages (of blessed memory) in the Talmud and the *Aggadah* <term>homiletic or non-legal teachings</term>, and the rope that ascends, for "it is not an empty thing"—and if it is empty, it is from us. <note>A play on Deuteronomy 32:47; the Sages taught that if the Torah seems empty of meaning, it is because of the student's lack of effort.</note> Whoever wishes to taste the sweetness of the honey of their pleasant words must be expert in them, their names, their matters, and their signs. Therefore, the thought arose in my mind to compose a pamphlet to reveal some of the principles of the Talmud and its discussions. So as not to cause an interruption there, I likewise decided it should be composed as a separate pamphlet. This is the name by which this section shall be called: **The Oral Torah**.

Since these two Torahs are one Torah—for together they were complete—therefore the collective name for both of them is **The Two Tablets of the Covenant**. And these are the words of the *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>A 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>: "Know that the Written Torah is the secret of the 'Beauty of Israel' <note>Tiferet; the central divine emanation associated with the masculine principle</note>, the King you shall behold in His beauty. It is called the 'Torah of Truth,' as it says: 'The Torah of Truth was in his mouth.' The Oral Torah is the 'Bride' mentioned in the Song of Songs. It is called 'Torah from the Writing' <note>original: "תורה שבכתב"</note> and not 'of the Writing' <note>original: "שבעל הכתב"</note> as we say 'Torah of the Mouth' <note>original: "שבעל פה"</note>. The reason is that the Supernal Torah is hidden and concealed, and it is 'within the writing,' the secret of the Supernal Palace that is hidden within. They are in complete unity, and from there they emerge to be revealed below. This is what is written, 'which I have written to teach them.' To teach whom? The Torah and the commandments mentioned in the verse... the secret of the supernal wine <note>Binah; Understanding</note> drawn through its grapes... and from there the Torah goes forth. Therefore, it is called the Written Torah. It is called the Oral Torah because it stands upon the lower kingdom <note>Malchut; the feminine divine emanation</note> below... And because they are not part of the [original] Unity and are not the Palace of God, they are called 'by mouth' <note>al peh</note>. For this secret reason, they are called the Oral Torah. This is the secret of the two lovers, the two fawns, twins of a gazelle." And as the Sages said in the Midrash <note>Midrash Chazit and Pesiqta</note> on the verse "My dove, my perfect one" <note>Song of Songs 5:2</note>: Rabbi Yannai says, "'My twin'—I am not greater than she, nor is she greater than me." Since the Written Torah is hidden and concealed, the Oral Torah was needed to explain its secrets and bring out its hidden things, just as the supernal Exalted One, through whom all things are revealed and the supernal lights are known, brings her powers into action. To this the Knower of Secrets alluded by saying, "Her husband is known in the gates" <note>Proverbs 31:23</note>—meaning that through the "Gates of Righteousness," the Supernal Name is known in the world. As in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah: Rabbi Rahumai said, "This teaches that she is the light of Israel... it is written: 'For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light.' The 'lamp' is the commandment, and this 'commandment' is the Oral Torah. The 'light' is the Written Torah. But because the light is sustained within her, she is called light." Just as a person cannot see inside a modest, dark room at the back of a house even during a bright day unless they bring in a lamp, so too the Oral Torah—even though it is a lamp—needs the Written Torah to resolve its difficulties and explain its secrets. Until here <note>end of quote</note>. When Israel engages in these two Torahs for their own sake, they then mirror the model above: "they shall be joined one to another," in the kiss of the brother and his sister. All of this is the secret of what the Sages said in the chapter *Elu Kasharim* <note>Tractate Shabbat 114a</note>: "Who are the 'builders'? Rabbi Yohanan said: These are the disciples of the wise who engage in the building of the world all their days." This is the supernal mystery of bringing the Holy One, Blessed be He, close, which is the preservation of all the worlds. And in the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunia ben HaKanah: How much could the word of our comfort be... it was joining the Torah above to bring [the light] close... for every hour that a man studies Torah for its own sake, the Torah above connects to the Holy One, Blessed be He. This is what we said earlier: "A person should always study Torah even if not for its own sake, for from doing it not for its own sake, he will come to do it for its own sake." Until here. Behold, when Israel engages in Torah, the "Man" above is awakened before his "Beloved" and she says: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>. This follows the way of lovers to kiss one another on the mouth to show that they share one spirit because of their great love. This is mirrored in the two "Beloveds" mentioned in the Song of Songs... like the Bride saying: "Give me his kisses," as if coming in a hidden way before the kissing. And after the man is in his house, it says, "For your love is better than wine"—meaning, your love is sweet and good to me. When Israel engages in the Torah, which is compared to wine, it completes the bond between us. Thus, Israel increases the love between the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel when they engage in Torah for its own sake. End of words.

...that he should repair the aforementioned spiritual flaw through his songs and melodies. Now see, look closely at how Saul was punished "measure for measure." He did not wish to repair this spiritual attribute from which the Holy Spirit—the "Good Spirit of God"—is drawn. Therefore, "the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord terrified him" <note>1 Samuel 16:14</note>. That evil spirit would not depart from Saul except through David, who played music with the secret of "sweetening the judgment." He was the one who achieved the essential repair. This is the meaning of "Saul was refreshed and the evil spirit departed from him." Yet it also says, "On the next day, an evil spirit of God came mightily upon Saul, and he raved in the middle of the house" <note>1 Samuel 18:10</note>, because his prophecy was not a vision for good, but for ill. From then on, Saul was David's adversary, setting his eyes upon him to kill him. From this, we have a sound reason why God did not answer Saul—neither through dreams nor through prophets—because he had damaged the "place of prophecy," as mentioned.

Once David came with his songs and melodies, he repaired that attribute fundamentally. It seems this is why David changed the order of the service. He did not say, "Your singers shall sing and your Levites shall be of the sons of Levi," but rather: "Master of the Universe, let the order be thus: that the pious shall sing through their piety and their song." These are the two "faces of sweetness," and through them, everything that needs sweetening is sweetened. From that point on, the source of prophecy was opened, for all the prophets prophesied during the days of the kings who came after David.

In this, you will taste the "sweetness of the honeycomb" <note>meaning: deep wisdom</note> from the words of the Old Man <note>Rabbi Yeiva Saba</note> in the Zohar, portion Mishpatim (page 112): "Mordecai was a brother to that wicked Haman... in the secret of the thigh..." <margin>of blessed memory</margin> until the end of his words. The intention is that Mordecai, being of the tribe of Benjamin—who did not bow down to Esau—stood firm in his power and would not kneel or bow. This is the "place of the knees," the right leg in its proper place. Therefore, the entire "other side" <note>the Sitra Achra, or forces of evil</note>, which is the musician... <note>The text here uses dense Kabbalistic imagery to link the anatomy of the Sefirot (knees/thighs) to the conflict between Mordecai and Haman</note>. This is the secret of "his wrath kept forever" <note>Amos 1:11</note>, meaning he kept the transgression in the place of Netzach (Eternity), seizing it and darkening it. Thus far, the Lord has helped us to sweeten the verses with the sweetness of the honeycomb and their drippings. And Joseph added... <note>referring to a previous work</note>. I have written at length on this in the discourse on the portion *Ve-Atah Tetzaveh*; there too is found the secret of the Purim feast.

# The Divine Ari, of Blessed Memory
<margin>of blessed memory</margin> The Divine Ari <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foremost 16th-century Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory, delved very deeply into the secrets of Purim, the Megillah (Scroll of Esther), and the feast. However, since "not every mind can tolerate this," but only the wise in secret, I will not copy his words, except for a tiny bit from what his students recorded regarding the secret of the feast.

<gloss>The Ari said:</gloss> "Eating" (*Achilah*) has the numerical value of "Earth" (*Eretz*), which is mundane. This is "Eating-Yah" <note>Achilah + the name of God, Yah</note>, for through it, "Mentalities" are drawn down, all of which are in the secret of the name *Yah*, as we have explained elsewhere. Also, the word... they are in the secret of Hokhmah and Binah (Wisdom and Understanding) called *Yah*. Its partner is the "Voice" (*Kol*).

Regarding the reading of the Megillah: Its purpose is to bring the "Fathers" out from the "Foundation of Rachel" through the secret of *Megaleh* (revealing) what is hidden. This is enough for the wise. This is the secret of "Upon the Reading of the Megillah." Leah went out to meet him <note>Jacob</note> to bring forth and reveal the secret of the blessings, like other blessings for commandments.

**Blessed** (the building) **Art Thou** (Hokhmah), **Lord** (Binah), **Our God** (Tiferet), **King of the Universe** (Binah), **Who has sanctified us** (Binah) **with His commandments** (Netzach and Hod) **and commanded us** (Yesod) **concerning the reading of the Megillah** (Malchut/Kingship). *Megillah* signifies the female principle, the revealing of the light from the Foundation (Yesod). This is the secret of "And Mordecai went out... in royal apparel... and a great crown of gold" <note>Esther 8:15</note>, from the side of the Great Father (Abba), who is above all, the Primordial Man (*Adam Kadmon*). This is for the understanding reader. This is the secret of "From before the King"—revealing what was hidden within the Kingship. This is the secret of "Who performed miracles for our ancestors," at which point Agag was subdued and Haman (the revealed power of evil) was ended. This is "that which has never been before." Also, "Who has kept us alive" (*Shehecheyanu*) is in Yesod, "And sustained us" (*Ve-kiyemanu*) is the secret of the Assembly of Israel, and "Brought us to this season" (*La-zeman ha-zeh*) refers to Malchut (the "this"). These are the attributes of Netzach, Hod, and Yesod (N-H-Y) coming out to be revealed externally. This is enough until the time that God arouses the day of Purim.

Regarding the "Sending of Portions" (*Mishloach Manot*): Our Sages said, "Two portions to one man, and two gifts to two poor people." Let us see why they chose to say "portions" for the individual and "gifts" for the poor. You already know that the attribute of Yesod is called "Man." The essence of love is found here, and on this day, the Yesod of Abba (the Father) is revealed. It is male, but since it is clothed within the Yesod of the "Man" (Zeir Anpin), it says "portions." ... And regarding "gifts to the poor" (*Matanot La-Evyonim*), they are from the female side. The "two poor people" are Netzach and Hod, who are called "poor" because they have neither "taste nor smell" <note>spiritual influence</note> of their own, as the Mother (Binah) only extends until Hod.

Our Sages also said: "On the days of Purim, we give to anyone who stretches out his hand." The matter is this: usually, charity is given through Yesod. During the week, one must investigate the recipient to see if he is worthy. But now, when the light of the "Father's Yesod" is a great illumination, one should not be particular; rather, "anyone who stretches out his hand, we give to him."

And regarding the statement that "one must drink wine until he does not know [the difference between 'Cursed be Haman' and 'Blessed be Mordecai']": The intention is that there is always a spark of holiness within the "Husk" (*Kelippah*) that illuminates it from within. Therefore, one must say "Blessed be Haman" to draw light even to that spark. However, one must say it without conscious intent—while drunk and out of his mind. For if it were done with intent, God forbid, he would also be illuminating the Husk itself. It seems to me that it was through a miracle that a great light from Binah descended upon Rachel through the "great wine" of intense illumination, giving her the power to illuminate even that spark within the Husk. One should first have the intent of the names... <note>The text describes specific mystical letter combinations (Gematria) to contemplate while eating and drinking to draw down the mentalities of Wisdom and Understanding</note>. Know that in the female principle (Nukva), the "Mentality of Understanding" (Binah) prevails; therefore, the drinking on Purim must be greater than the eating.

**The Secret of Charity:** Know that when the "Righteous One" (Yesod, the foundation of the world) flows into the attribute of "Justice" (*Tzedek*, which is Malchut), that flow is called *Tzedakah* (Charity). Thus, the one who gives charity arouses the Attribute of Justice to unite with Charity, bringing peace between them and joining the Sefirot in unity. This is the meaning of "The work of charity shall be peace" <note>Isaiah 32:17</note>.

<margin>of blessed memory</margin> *Tola'at Ya'akov* (The Worm of Jacob), page 71: "Know that the virtue of the commandment is unity and connection..." until the end of the chapter. In the first chapter of Bava Batra, Rabbi Isaac said: "He who gives a small coin (*perutah*) to a poor man is blessed with six blessings, but he who consoles him with words is blessed with eleven blessings." This is the secret of the word *Perutah* (coin)... and he should think upon the Name of God so that they shall be individualized and there shall be peace.

### Chapter 4: Ethical Reproofs
->On Purim, one should fulfill the commandments with joy and a good heart—namely, the reading of the Megillah, the sending of portions, the gifts to the poor, and the drinking. A "good heart" at the feast will arouse a spiritual cleaving to the Blessed Name. Regarding this, it is said: "Anyone who is enticed by wine possesses the knowledge of his Creator."<-

One should consider that the day of Purim is the completion of the receiving of the Torah. As our Sages said in Tractate Shabbat (Chapter 9, page 88a): "'And they stood at the foot of the mountain'—this teaches that God overturned the mountain over them like a tub... Nevertheless, they re-accepted the Torah in the days of Ahasuerus, as it is written: 'The Jews ordained and took upon themselves'—they ordained what they had already taken upon themselves." The hint for this is "And the law (*Dat*) was given in Shushan the capital," for *Dat* refers to the Law of the Torah. Therefore, it is fitting to rejoice with the joy of the Torah.

Regarding charity: In Tractate Shabbat, chapter *Sho'el*, it was taught: Rabbi Simeon ben Eleazar says, "Do what you find and what is available to you... while you still find one to whom to do it, while you have the money, and while you are still on the way—while it is still in your power before you die." This seems difficult, for obviously one should do it before dying! Can one do it after death? Rather, the intention is that one should give charity while healthy, not like those who only give during illness when they reach the gates of death. The verse hints at this: "I will love them freely, for My anger is turned away from him" <note>Hosea 14:5</note>. That is: "When do I love a free-will gift? When the giver does it while My anger is turned away"—meaning, not in a time of personal distress, but when he is in his full strength. When one gives only during his time of misfortune, the gift is not as beloved.

The author of the book *Sefer Ha-Yashar* (The Book of the Upright) wrote in the third gate (page 7): "And this shall be the sign for you, that the service of God is the ultimate purpose..." until the end of his words.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the spiritual perfection of the soul, moving from the specific repairs performed by King David and King Saul to a broader theological question: how the Patriarchs and modern Jews can fulfill the 613 commandments when many are physically or legally impossible to perform.</meta>

# The Tablets of the Covenant

**And if** you should raise a difficulty, asking: "If this is so, did the Patriarchs and the first pious ones of the world not bring these general principles from potential into actual practice?" <note>The author is addressing the problem of how the Patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob) could be considered "complete" if the 613 commandments had not yet been formally given at Mount Sinai.</note> Know that they indeed brought them forth, and they brought them forth through the power of their understanding. By this, I mean they were attached with the ultimate attachment to the Creator, may He be blessed, and they were joyful and happy to do the will of their Maker in whatever He might command them. They were prepared for this with the ultimate preparation, with joy and a good heart. This "preparation" is considered like the actual deed itself. I mean to say that, in any case, regarding the commandment they did perform, all the 613 commandments <note>original: "תה"ג" - an abbreviation for Taryag, the 613 commandments of the Torah</note> were included within them. It was only that the power had not yet descended below into physical action for all those included principles. Since they are in a state of "potential," the "Throne" below is the lot of their preparation, which is equivalent to action. We find a hint to this law of "preparation" in the fact that preparing on a holy day for a mundane day is forbidden—such as from the Sabbath to a weekday, or from a Festival to a weekday. In the language of the Talmud, this is called "the way of preparation" <note>original: "הכנת דרכה"</note>. Truly, the secret of preparation is great for our purposes. The preparation of the early ones was so strong that the few commandments they did physically perform were sufficient for them, as all 613 were included within them. Through the power of their great preparation, they brought out the general principles and became a vehicle <term>Merkavah; a spiritual structure that hosts the Divine Presence</term> for all of Divinity. One should not ask: "Why did the Holy One, blessed be He, obligate them in only seven commandments? <note>Referring to the Seven Noahide Laws given to all humanity before the Revelation at Sinai.</note> Would not one commandment have sufficed?" This is no difficulty, for the Giver of the Commandment, blessed be He and blessed be His name, is the one who knows how much must be done in actual physical practice and how much through preparation; then the body becomes a complete whole and merits 

->to be a Divine Chariot:<-

**After** the time arrived when the Holy One, blessed be He, saw a generation worthy of the 613 commandments being given to them, they were given in such a way that each individual fulfills of the 613 whatever is possible for him to fulfill. Then, when he does so and intends to do what is possible, and he is joyful in the service of God and ready to fulfill everything that is possible for him—then that which is impossible for him to fulfill is considered as if he fulfilled it, since he was ready to do so and the prevention was not on his part, but due to external factors. In any case, the 613 were fulfilled by all of Israel collectively: the "Law of the Priests" <note>Torat Kohanim; the laws of sacrifices and Temple service</note> was fulfilled by the Priests; the commandment of Levirate marriage by one to whom the opportunity came; and so on for all of them. For one who could not possibly fulfill a specific deed but fulfilled all that was possible and was occupied with the Torah "for its own sake" <term>Lishmah; studying with pure intent rather than for status or reward</term>—the definition of "for its own sake" is that while he is occupied with Torah, he does so in order to learn, to teach, to observe, and to do. That is to say, he wants to fulfill whatever he finds in the Torah that the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, has decreed to be done. Therefore, even if he did not fulfill it because there was a barrier preventing him, because he was ready to fulfill it, it is credited to him as if he had, for he brought it from potential to actual through his preparation. To this, our Sages of blessed memory hinted: "If one intended to perform a commandment and was prevented... the Scripture credits him as if he had performed it." For the Torah is the script of the King of kings, which He wrote for His faithful servants, the nation of Israel. Consider a human king who writes to his servants: "I command you to prepare yourselves for war against the enemy; you must see to the preparation of the walls, the fixing of weapons, and the gathering of food," and many similar decrees. Now, those who are diligent in the work of preparation are tasked with building the walls; those diligent in fixing weapons are tasked with that labor; and the farmers gather the food. If there is one wise man who knows how to do one task and also another, he is obligated to do all he can. Each one fulfills the king’s command since he does all he can, and he would be ready to do even more if it were possible. Regarding this, the book *Ma'or* <note>Likely referring to the author's own work or a classic ethical text</note> says: "Anyone who occupies himself with Torah for its own sake merits many things." This does not just mean "many things" in a general sense, but rather that he is called a "friend" and "beloved" of God. Furthermore, when he studies for its own sake—which I have defined as studying to fulfill every command he finds that he is capable of performing—it is as if he fulfilled even that which is impossible for him. Since he prepared himself for all that is written and the prevention is not on his part, he "merits many things," meaning he merits the "many things" he did not physically do, so that it is as if he did them. I have expanded on this in *Ma'or* in the chapter "The Ten Utterances."

## The Matter of Preparation
The essence of preparation is that a person fulfills all that is possible for him to fulfill. Regarding that which he is prevented from performing, he should still do whatever is possible, such as studying that specific commandment. This is in accordance with what our Sages said: "Anyone who occupies himself with the laws of the burnt offering is considered as if he offered a burnt offering." Also, if the Holy One, blessed be He, gave him wisdom and understanding, he should contemplate and comprehend the secret of the commandment; for although he cannot fulfill the mitzvah in action, he fulfills it in the mind by understanding it. Furthermore, if this commandment happens to be available to his fellow man, he should assist his fellow, encourage him, and cause him to fulfill it. Through this, the virtue of preparation is completed, and it is credited to him as if he fulfilled it in action. The verses hint at this: "For this commandment which I command you today, it is not hidden from you, neither is it far off. It is not in heaven... neither is it beyond the sea... but the word is very near unto you, in your mouth, and in your heart, that you may do it" <note>Deuteronomy 30:11-14</note>. These verses reveal all I have written: that every person is obligated to fulfill all 613 commandments, but since it is impossible to fulfill them all—as there are barriers for the Priest, the Levite, and the Israelite—the verse addresses this. I have already written that there are four types of barriers. **First**, commandments that are "hidden" and concealed from him with no possibility of fulfillment, like the Priestly laws for a Levite or an Israelite; regarding this, it says, "it is not hidden from you"—do not say it is hidden and unreachable. **Second**, things that are possible but only through a "distant" cause, such as the commandment of Levirate marriage or returning a divorced wife who had remarried; regarding this, it says, "it is not far off." **Third**, things that are "near" but prevented by lack of means or wealth—for example, if one cannot afford to build a house that requires a Mezuzah and instead lives in a tent, or does not have a garment to which he can attach Tzitzit (fringes). This is not in his hands but in the hands of Heaven, for wealth and poverty are decreed by Him; regarding this, it says, "it is not in heaven." **Fourth**, commandments that apply only in the Land of Israel, which is "across the Jordan," and do not apply in the diaspora; regarding this, it says, "it is not beyond the sea." All these barriers are not true barriers because there is a remedy for the matter, and that is "the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it." These are the very things I mentioned above: whatever is possible to do, he must do, and this is included in the word "to do it." And what is impossible to do himself, the remedy is "in your mouth"—namely, studying the commandment, for one who studies it is as if he fulfilled it since he does all that is possible. "In your mouth" also includes teaching the commandment to others who *can* fulfill it and encouraging them. "In your heart" refers to the preparation of the commandments by knowing their secret meaning, each person according to his intellect. Then, it will be as if he physically fulfilled all 613 commandments. Furthermore, it must be known: it seems we can ask regarding the negative commandments (prohibitions), where one must be careful to "sit and do nothing"—how are they included in the word "to do it"? I have written about this at length in the chapter "The Ten Utterances," explaining that even a "thou shalt not" is included in "doing." It is not enough for a person to simply refrain from what the Holy One, blessed be He, warned against; rather, he must awaken himself—that is, he should desire the thing in his heart but refrain from it because the Creator commanded him. As it is taught: "Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: A person should not say, 'I cannot stand the taste of pork,' but rather, 'I would like it, but what can I do? My Father in Heaven has decreed it upon me.'" This awakening of thought is considered an action and is included in the word "to do it." I have expanded on this there.

### Page 267
#### The Tablets of the Covenant

In the chapter where it is stated "You shall not eat over the blood" <note>Leviticus 19:26</note>, this applies to all of them. And if the questioner asks: what is the difference between the **grape-skin** and the **grape-seed**, **raw** and **boiled**, **mill** and **upper millstone**, **leaven** and **honey**, **widow** and **divorcee**, or **harlot** and **profaned woman** <note>These are pairs of items or persons mentioned in single prohibitions in the Torah.</note>? For in these cases, one is liable for each individual item. Yet, for the **fat** of an ox, a sheep, and a goat, one is only liable once! This is what we call a <term>General Prohibition</term> <note>Hebrew: *Lav she-bi-klalut*. A single negative commandment that encompasses multiple distinct prohibitions. Whether one is punished for each item or just once is a major legal debate.</note>, as seen in the chapter "All Forbidden Fats" in tractate *Keritot*. There we learned: "Bread, parched corn, and fresh ears you shall not eat" <note>Leviticus 23:14</note>; one is liable for each one because of the extra wording. Likewise, for the "tithe of your **grain**, your **wine**, and your **oil**," one would only be flogged once if not for the extra wording, as seen there in *Keritot*. One could answer that grape-skin and grape-seed are two distinct names, as are leaven and honey, and so with all of them. If you wish to warn someone about them, you must mention each by its own name. However, the "fat" of an ox, sheep, and goat is all under the single name "fat." Similarly, bread, parched corn, and fresh ears are under the single name of "bread," and so too with the tithes. These are his words.

I have seen in the Jerusalem Talmud, in the tractate *Nazir* (Chapter: Three Species), that from the implication of the word "mill," I would know that the "upper millstone" is included. Why then does the verse say "mill and upper millstone" <note>Deuteronomy 24:6</note>? It is to make one liable for this one individually and for that one individually. Behold, you have learned from the words of Rashi and the words of **Rabbeinu Isaac ben Samuel** <note>Also known as the "Ri," a famous 12th-century Tosafist.</note>, who is a pillar of legal instruction, that leaven and honey are two distinct things, as are the "harlot’s hire" and the "price of a dog," and "raw" and "boiled," and "grape-skin" and "grape-seed." But the "mill and upper millstone" are considered a single category, and "Ammonite and Moabite" are two. These are the words of the **Smag** <note>Rabbi Moses of Coucy, author of the *Sefer Mitzvot Gadol*.</note>.

**However**, the great master **Maimonides** <note>Rabbi Moses ben Maimon (Rambam), 1135–1204.</note>—the spirit of the Lord spoke through him—has already removed these complaints. His words appear at length in the "Fourteen Roots" which he placed as an introduction to his counting of the commandments. In the **Ninth Root**, he elaborated on this matter, clarified the issues, and sifted the topic like fine flour. It is a wonder to me how the *Smag* did not see or did not know the words of Maimonides and the **Rashbatz** <note>Rabbi Shimon ben Tzemach Duran, who wrote a commentary on Maimonides' roots.</note> there in the Ninth Root. What should be remembered regarding this root is what I shall now relate:

When I say it is proper to count the matters commanded or forbidden, it is on the condition that there is a specific "No" for each and every matter, or a proof that the scholars rely upon to show that the Torah distinguished one part from another, requiring a separate warning for each. However, when there is one general term that includes many matters, then only that "No" itself is counted, not the individual items included within it. This is a "General Prohibition" for which one is not flogged <note>A standard rule in Talmudic law: one is only flogged for a specific, clear prohibition, not a general one that requires interpretation.</note>. For example: "You shall not eat over the blood." The Sages explained this in various ways:
1. Where is the "No" for one who eats from an animal before its soul has fully departed? It is here: "You shall not eat over the blood."
2. Where is the "No" for one who eats sacrificial meat before the blood has been sprinkled on the altar? It is here: "You shall not eat over the blood."
3. **Rabbi Dosa** says: How do we know we do not provide a meal of comfort for those executed by the court? From "You shall not eat over the blood."
4. **Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Hanina** says: This is a warning to a court that executes a person, that they should not eat on that day.

Behold, these are five different matters, all forbidden, and they are all included under one "No." Furthermore, they said: How do we know one should not taste anything until he has prayed for his own life? From "You shall not eat over the blood"—do not eat until you have prayed for your blood (your life). It was explicitly stated in the Gemara of tractate *Sanhedrin* that for all of these, one is not flogged, because it is a "General Prohibition." And for any General Prohibition, one is not flogged. Therefore, it is not proper to count every specific forbidden thing included in this "No" as a separate commandment; rather, the "No" itself is counted as one commandment.

Another example of this kind of "No" is "You shall not put a stumbling block before the blind" <note>Leviticus 19:14</note>, for it also includes many different matters. This is one type of General Prohibition.

The **second type** is when a single "No" comes to forbid many things that are linked together (conjunctive), such as saying "You shall not do this and that." This type is divided into two parts:
1. There are those about which the Talmud says one is liable for a flogging for each and every item listed.
2. There are those about which they said one is only liable for one, because it is a General Prohibition.

For those where one is liable for each item, we count each item as a separate commandment. But where they clarified that one is liable only once for all of them, we count it as one commandment. This follows our principle that a person should never receive two floggings for a single "No." When the Talmud clarifies that for each of the linked matters one is flogged individually, it is as if they were each given their own "No," and we count each specifically. I will mention many examples of these two parts so the matter is perfectly clear.

Regarding the commandment of the Passover sacrifice: "Do not eat of it **raw** or **boiled** in water" <note>Exodus 12:9</note>. We count this "No" as one commandment. We do not count "raw" as one and "boiled" as another, because the Torah did not give a separate "No" to each; it did not say "Do not eat it raw" and "Do not eat it boiled." It used one "No" to include two matters. In the second chapter of *Pesachim*, **Abaye** said: "If one eats it raw, he is flogged twice; if raw and boiled, he is flogged three times." He believes one is flogged for a General Prohibition. But **Rava** said: "One is not flogged for a General Prohibition." Some say he gets at least one flogging, and others say he gets none at all because the "No" is not specific like the "No" of "You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads" <note>Deuteronomy 25:4, the classic example of a specific prohibition.</note>. It has already been clarified in the Gemara of *Sanhedrin* that we do not flog for a General Prohibition, and therefore Abaye's view is rejected. The truth is that one is only liable for one flogging, whether he ate it raw and boiled, or just raw, or just boiled. Therefore, "Do not eat it raw or boiled" is counted as a single commandment.

Similarly, Abaye said: "If a Nazirite eats a **grape-skin**, he is flogged twice; a **grape-seed**, twice; both, three times." But Rava said: "One is not flogged for a General Prohibition," referring to the verse "from anything that is made of the grapevine" <note>Numbers 6:4</note>. Likewise, regarding one who offers **leaven or honey** on the altar, Abaye said he is flogged for the leaven, for the honey, for a mixture of leaven, and for a mixture of honey. This is all based on Abaye's principle. But Rava said: "One is not flogged for a General Prohibition."

Since it has been clarified that "Do not eat of it raw or boiled" is one commandment, so too all the prohibitions regarding a Nazirite are one commandment, as they are all details of one general rule. Likewise, "all leaven and all honey" is one commandment. We also count "An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter" <note>Deuteronomy 23:4</note> as one commandment, and "You shall not afflict any widow or orphan" <note>Exodus 22:21</note> as one, and "You shall not pervert the justice due to the stranger or the fatherless" <note>Deuteronomy 24:17</note> as one, and "her food, her clothing, and her marriage rights he shall not diminish" <note>Exodus 21:10</note> as one. This is because each of these is like "raw or boiled" or "leaven and honey." Similarly, "You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the price of a dog" <note>Deuteronomy 23:19</note> is one "No." And "Do not drink wine or strong drink... that you may differentiate... and that you may teach" <note>Leviticus 10:9-11</note>—this is a single "No" warning against entering the Sanctuary or teaching Torah while intoxicated. This is the first part of the second type of General Prohibition.

The **second part** of this type is similar in form, but we have a tradition that one is flogged for each and every linked item individually, even if he did them all at once. An example of this is: "You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your **grain**, your **wine**, or your **oil**" <note>Deuteronomy 12:17</note>. In tractate *Keritot*, they said: if one eats the tithe of grain, wine, and oil, he is liable for each one. They asked: "But isn't this a General Prohibition?" The answer was: "There is an extra verse." Since the Torah already said "You shall eat before the Lord... the tithe of your grain, etc.," why repeat "You may not eat within your gates..."? It must be to divide the items and make one liable for each. The Sages debated whether "parched corn" (*kali*) needed to be mentioned if "bread" was already mentioned; it was concluded that it was mentioned to divide the items, so that one is liable for each.

Following this same logic: "There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, one who uses **divination**, an **observer of clouds**, an **enchanter**, a **witch**, a **charmer**, a **medium**, a **wizard**, or a **necromancer**" <note>Deuteronomy 18:10-11</note>. Each of these listed things is a separate "No," and they are not like the first part of this type. The proof is that "observer of clouds" and "enchanter" appear in the middle of the list, yet they are clarified elsewhere as individual prohibitions: "You shall not enchant nor observe clouds" <note>Leviticus 19:26</note>. Just as these two are separate, they define the items before and after them as separate, just as they explained regarding "bread, parched corn, and fresh ears." Others have erred in this matter, either because they did not grasp all these details or because they forgot them, and they counted the verse regarding the priests...

<meta>This page continues the philosophical exploration of Divine thought, the creation of the world, and the hierarchy of souls, specifically focusing on the elite righteous known as the "Children of the Ascent."</meta>

May His Name be blessed; knowledge and information are before Him, and everything is revealed. It is not only the final outcome that is known to Him, but both that which emerges into reality and that which does not, from every possible angle of existence. Both are known to Him equally, even though the specific realization of existence that was most appropriate for its purpose was what actually came to be. This explains the phrase "the thought ascended" <note>This refers to the Kabbalistic concept that the idea of Creation first "arose" in the Divine Mind</note>—that He first thought and then acted. This also explains Rabbi Abbahu’s statement that "the Holy One, blessed be He, built worlds and destroyed them." <note>A famous Midrashic teaching suggesting that our world is the final result of many conceptual attempts.</note> His knowledge of all possible sides of existence is what is called "building and destroying"; the versions that remained only in Divine thought are the "destroyed" ones, while the others were known to Him as well. This is the simple meaning.

**However**, listen closely so your soul may live. Know that whatever arose in the Divine thought is considered to have a lasting existence. First, I will preface with what our Sages of blessed memory said: that the Holy One, blessed be He, is more exacting with the righteous than with others, judging them "to a hair's breadth." This is because whoever is closer to the King—the Holy One, blessed be He—must be more refined, holy, and pure. One who enters the King's courtyard is not the same as one who enters the King's inner palace; one who enters the palace is not like one who touches the King’s feet; and one who touches the feet is not like one who touches the King's very self. There are many levels, one above the other, and the higher one wishes to ascend, the more exacting and refined they must be, so that not even the slightest blemish or hint of sin remains. This is like what we learned in the tractate *Chagigah*: the garments of an ordinary person are considered "treading-unclean" for those who separate themselves for holiness (*Perushim*); the garments of the *Perushim* are considered unclean for those who eat *Terumah* <note>The sacred portion of produce given to Priests</note>, and so on. I have already elaborated on this teaching elsewhere.

Therefore, the "Children of the Ascent" (*Bnei Aliyah*)—those who merit the high levels of the soul's ascent into the innermost chambers, following the secret of the "Primordial Torah" and the secret of "Israel arose in thought"—these elite souls, whose root is in the Supernal Thought, are judged much more strictly than the rest of the world whose level is below them. For these souls, the reality remains that the world was created through the **Attribute of Justice** <note>original: *Midat HaDin*; the Divine quality of strict law and accountability</note>, because they themselves ascend to that high place. Thus, they are always scrutinized by the Attribute of Justice. This is what is meant by "In the beginning, God (*Elohim*) created..." <note>Genesis 1:1</note>; the Sages explained that "At first, it arose in thought to create the world with the Attribute of Justice." This does not mean that He changed His mind, Heaven forbid. Rather, "At first" refers to the word "Beginning" (*Berashit*), which points to the root of all things, for the root is the beginning of all that spreads out from it. The root is hidden and concealed, while the revelation is the expansion from that root. He said "At first" to mean that for those "Children of the Ascent" whose level is in the hidden root—which is the "Beginning" and the "Start," the secret of "ascending in thought"—their reality is one of strict Justice, as they are scrutinized to a hair's breadth.

Similarly, when the Holy One, blessed be He, answered Rabbi Akiva regarding his suffering under the Attribute of Justice, and Rabbi Akiva questioned it, God replied: "Be silent! Thus it arose in thought." This answer was not a dismissal, but a true response from God regarding the secret of the matter. God was saying, "Be silent, for this punishment is due to your great stature." Because his level was that of "arising in thought"—such is the height of his soul—he was therefore judged by the Attribute of Justice. Even for a light sin, he was judged as another man would be for the most serious of crimes. This is the meaning of the Rabbinic saying, "A distinguished person is different." This is fitting for the Children of the Ascent who go up to experience the "delight of the Lord" and the "hidden light," of which it is said, "The hidden things belong to the Lord our God."

**But** those who are distanced from this, who exist within the secret of "expansion" and the chain of cause and effect, and who reside in the realm of "revealed things"—of them it is hinted: "He saw that the world could not endure." The word "saw" (*Re'eh*) hints at the place of sight, which is revelation. These people are in the realm of the revealed "Work of Creation" that happens every day, as it says, "And God saw..." For these, He partnered the **Attribute of Mercy** with the Attribute of Justice. "He saw that the world could not endure"—the "world" refers to the secret of the structure below the level of Thought. There, existence cannot be sustained by strict Justice alone because of its distance from the Source of all sources. Therefore, God joined Mercy with Justice for them.

This is also the meaning of the Sages' statement: "Every judge who judges a true judgment according to its truth (*Emet l'Amitto*) is considered a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the Work of Creation." The *Tosafot* <note>Medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> already questioned the double language of "true judgment according to its truth." Based on our words, this is well-explained: there are two types of judgments, and both are "true," but one is "more true" than the other. The Sages commanded a judge to seek a compromise (*Peshara*) as much as possible. If he does so, he has performed a kindness and acted with righteousness and truth. Through this, the world is sustained, for it is often impossible to establish the strict religious law perfectly, and the world cannot endure without someone leaving satisfied and at peace. This is called "judgment and peace." Even though a compromise is not the absolute "truth" according to the microscopic religious law, the matter is "truthful" because "truth shall sprout from the earth" to sustain the world and remove strife.

However, if two litigants want the absolute, complete truth of the law, and neither denies the other's claim or lies, but both are righteous and neither wants to steal from the other—they simply want to know who is legally entitled to the property or inheritance according to the center-point of the truth—and the judge rules accordingly, then that is "true truth" (*Emet l'Amitto*). It is truth sprouting from the center to sustain the world through peace, because they both desire the truth. Each wants to merit only what he is truly entitled to. When the judge rules according to the exact law, that is "true truth." This judge becomes a partner in the Work of Creation. I have already written that "In the Beginning" refers to the "At first" stage where everything is hidden and rooted. There it says "In the beginning God created," and "Beginning" is the thought of the final action. It is written, "The beginning of wisdom..." <note>Psalm 111:10</note> because it is the secret of Thought, the place of the Children of the Ascent. Therefore, such a judge becomes a partner because he reaches that level of Thought in the Work of Creation—meaning, the deeds that belong to the secret of the "Beginning," which is the root of the soul. But in the realm of action, meaning the expanded structure, "the world shall be built on kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>, and from there comes the joining of Mercy with Justice. That is "true," but not "true truth." Regarding this, it is said, "The Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without iniquity, righteous and upright is He" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, as explained before. (And this explains the Midrash where Abraham was shown the building and destroying of worlds and said, "This one pleases me, and that one does not." One might ask: was God seeking approval? But according to my path, it makes sense: "This one pleases me" refers to the world for most people, which is based on Mercy... while "This one does not please me as much" refers to the strict world of Justice, but this is not the place to elaborate.)

**Let us return** to the matter. The general principle of "that which ascends and descends" refers to the souls of Israel. They are the Torah. The "Revealed Torah" is the secret of "the revealed things are for us and our children, to do all the words of the Torah." But the "Primordial Torah," which is hidden, is the root of the souls of the "Children of the Ascent" who rise in the secret of Divine Thought.

# The Tablets of the Covenant

<margin>
The numerical value <note>Gematria</note> of these words suggests that wisdom and intelligence were present from the day the sun was created... if you write it to remember the truth in your heart... the Serpent’s intention was to deceive, and through his words of "wisdom," which were actually lies, he convinced her. He wanted to hear words of greatness... even though the intention was destructive. Therefore, do not be surprised that he pushed her... as he said with his mouth, so it was in his heart... to lead her to sin. The intention of the Serpent was to bring her to this... how could she be so easily convinced? It can be said that she was tempted because he mixed the truth with the Holy One, blessed be He, regarding touching the tree as well as eating... and this is the secret of the "death" mentioned... it was clear to the Serpent that if she touched it and did not die, she would believe the rest... this is the explanation of the temptation... and the Earth itself was affected by this corruption.
</margin>

This is the way of the intellect, which does not desire to dwell in such a place; rather, it is the way of the <term>Evil Inclination (Yetzer HaRa)</term><note>The innate human drive toward selfish or physical desires.</note> which begins with "soft speech" until it eventually tells a person to commit <term>idolatry</term><note>The original text uses the abbreviation "A.Z." for Avodah Zarah, meaning foreign worship</note>, may God preserve us. First, I will preface by saying that the <term>Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil</term> was unique: the taste of the wood was exactly like the taste of its fruit. While the rest of the Earth changed <note>According to Midrashic tradition, Earth was commanded to make trees taste like their fruit, but only the trees in Eden complied</note>, the trees of the Garden were the "planting of the Lord," and He planted them according to His will so that the wood's taste would mirror the fruit's taste.

The Serpent deceived Eve with words, suggesting that what the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term><note>Original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu</note>, forbade was only *eating* from the wood itself, because humans do not merit tasting wood that is equal to its fruit. He argued that it is a supernatural thing for all trees in the world *not* to have wood that tastes like fruit. But as for the fruit itself—what reason would there be for a prohibition? Therefore, the Serpent specifically mentioned the "tree" in his words and not the "fruit," to show that his language was precise based on God's command, which also mentioned the "tree," as it is written: "And from the tree of knowledge you shall not eat." 

The Serpent argued: "But as for the fruit, what reason do we have to refrain? We should eat from the fruit of the tree, and not just from the tree itself." Even though God said "from the tree" and not specifically "from the fruit of the tree," the term "tree" generally includes the fruit that the "food-tree" produces. If this were not so, God’s words would be difficult to understand: why did He say twice "from it you shall not eat" and "for on the day you eat from it"? Rather, the second mention of eating, if it is not needed for the act of eating itself, should be applied to the act of *touching*. 

This means that the fruit and the most essential part of the wood, which is supernatural, are forbidden even to touch. This is what the Serpent claimed to clarify: "You shall not eat from it" refers to the fruit, and "You shall not touch it" refers to the tree wood. What did he do? He pushed Eve against the tree and said: "Just as there is no death in touching it, so too there is no death in eating it." The Serpent was very cunning; he understood that the literal meaning was not as he presented it... but he understood the simple truth: one command followed the other. One was for the warning and one was for the punishment, for "one is not punished unless one is first warned." Both warning and punishment are expressed in the phrase "You shall not eat from it."

Therefore, he pushed Eve, and this is the secret of the verse "And she saw that it was good"—meaning she saw there was no death in touching. The Serpent intended to corrupt her so that she would take from the fruit and give it to her husband, following the way of women who tell things to their husbands, so that her husband would die and he (the Serpent) could take her. Then "their eyes were opened"—to foolishness, as Rashi explains. He told her that since she saw there was no death in touching, there would be no death in eating, and God's reason for the prohibition was only because "God knows [that you will become like Him]." Then Eve was enticed, and "the woman saw that the tree was good for food and that it was a desire to the eyes"—meaning, after she saw that the literal warning did not result in immediate death, she thought that whatever the Serpent said must be true.

<margin>
The Name... and it should not be difficult to understand, for the Serpent was clever... he said to them... it was a matter of touching through the woman... and the Serpent did not reveal the literal truth that applied to the tree specifically... and thus he permitted the fruit... and for the second command he said it refers to eating... and it can be said that later she wrote... to strengthen her... a touch in the fruit... a truth... and one should not explain... and regarding what I wrote in the "Gate of Heaven"... the prohibition of the Serpent... and the prohibition is for them... regarding the garden... so too was the prohibition...
</margin>

...And she saw "that the tree was good for food," meaning it was her intention to damage the soul beyond the natural order, whether it was according to the Serpent’s later words about "being like God, knowing good and evil," or that "it was a desire to the eyes," etc. Therefore, she took from the fruit of the tree. The essence of the damage was the separation of the taste of the wood from the taste of the fruit, which occurred in all other trees of the world. If all the trees in the world had remained equal in this regard, there would have been no room for all the aforementioned deception, and they would not have come to sin. Therefore, when Adam and Eve were corrupted, the Earth was also corrupted. But initially, the Earth was not corrupted, for its intention was for good; it thought, like the light of the moon, that this would be hidden. But the purpose of creation was that the "outer vessel" should be like the "inner vessel"—that is, the body and the soul should be in the image of the Supernal Form.

From this, the secret of the "Image" (Tzelem) and "Likeness" (Demut) of the two formations is explained. Know that the spirituality of the Torah and the roots of the souls of Israel and their sustenance are one. This is what our Sages meant when they said: "The Torah was given in forty [days], and the soul was given in forty [days]." I have expanded on this teaching in my commentary on the Tractate Shevuot, in the chapter "Torah Or" (Torah is Light).

In the holy writings of the <term>Ari</term><note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foundational 16th-century Kabbalist.</note>, of blessed memory, I found a manuscript stating: The totality of all souls is 600,000, and the Torah is the root of the souls of Israel. Therefore, there are 600,000 explanations for every verse in the Torah, and from each explanation, the root of one soul was formed. In the future to come, every single person will read and know the Torah according to the explanation that reaches their specific root, through which they were created. This is also true in the Garden of Eden for a soul that includes several interpretations. 

The soul of <term>Moses our Teacher</term><note>Original: Moshe Rabbeinu</note>, of blessed memory, included all 600,000 souls; therefore, he knew all 600,000 explanations. This is why, after the soul leaves the body during sleep, if it merits ascending, it reads the specific explanation that belongs to its root. However, there are different levels; on one night it illuminates more, and so on for eight nights, and on another night it stops—this is all according to one’s deeds. Regarding this, the Sages said that a teacher would see in a person which verse illuminated them most, and would then explain it to them according to the interpretation belonging to their soul. By seeing this on the person's forehead, the teacher could explain it so that when they read it while awake, their soul would ascend infinitely, and other hidden things would be revealed to them. These 600,000 interpretations exist on the level of the "Plain Meaning" (Pshat), and corresponding to them are levels in <term>Kabbalah</term><note>The Jewish mystical tradition.</note>, for there is no soul that is not comprised of all of them.

Just as there are Five Books of the Torah, there are five parts of the soul: <term>Nefesh</term> (Vitality), <term>Ruach</term> (Spirit), <term>Neshamah</term> (Soul), <term>Chayah</term> (Living One), and <term>Yechidah</term> (Unique One). One might wonder why the <term>Zohar</term><note>The primary work of Kabbalah.</note> and most Kabbalistic books usually only mention the first three: Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah. I have explained this at length in my introduction to "Toledot Adam" (The Generations of Adam). The summary is that Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah correspond to the <term>Sefirot</term><note>The ten Divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe.</note> of Binah, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and Malchut—the secret of the "Structure" comprised of the Ten Personifications. Tiferet and Malchut are the secret of "This World." 

However, *Chayah* and *Yechidah* come from the "Higher Union" of <term>Chokhmah and Binah</term><note>Wisdom and Understanding, the highest intellectual attributes in Kabbalah.</note>, which is the secret of the "World to Come." Now, the "Children of Ascent" <note>Original: Bnei Aliyah—highly righteous individuals who achieve elevated spiritual states.</note>, who are few, see their world in their lifetime—meaning they also merit the secret of *Chayah* and *Yechidah*. This is the meaning of the verse "And man became a living soul (Nefesh Chayah)" and "Eve was the mother of all living (Chai)." I have explained this at length there.

**And all** souls are rooted in the Torah. There are two "Torahs": one is the Torah given to us from the secret of the Ten Personifications of Tiferet and Malchut, which are the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. About these, it is hinted: "From the heavens He made you hear His voice, and upon the earth He showed you His great fire." Heaven and Earth correspond to the Ten Personifications, as is known. 

However, there is a "Primordial Torah" hidden in the secret of the "Hidden Light." Regarding this, our Sages said: "The Torah preceded the world by two thousand years." The Kabbalists explain that every <term>Sefirah</term> is considered a "thousand" in the general count. Since "the world is built on kindness (Chesed)," the structure begins from Chesed. Therefore, Chokhmah and Binah are the "two thousand years" (the two Sefirot) that precede the "world" (which starts at Chesed). The roots of Tiferet and Malchut—which include the whole structure—are in Chokhmah and Binah. We are not to contemplate the [pre-creation] structure; rather, "the hidden things [Chokhmah and Binah, the Primordial Torah] belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things [the Torah given to us] belong to us and our children." 

Almost everyone’s soul comes from this Torah given to us, from Binah downwards, through the "Lower Union" of Tiferet and Malchut, and they merit Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah according to their level. But the "Children of Ascent," the elite of the world, also possess *Chayah* and *Yechidah* from the secret of the Primordial Torah. About them, it is said: "Israel arose in [Divine] Thought before the creation of the world." It is known that Chokhmah is "Thought." This also explains the saying of our Sages: "Initially, it arose in Thought to create the world with the Attribute of Justice; He saw the world could not endure, so He joined to it the Attribute of Mercy." This does not mean God "changed His mind," Heaven forbid, for He is not a man that He should repent. Rather, it means that He, **Blessed be He**...

# Written Torah - New Adar 271

Man is the secret of the **Upper Earth**, the place of the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Hebrew: *Knesset Yisrael*, a mystical representation of the collective soul of the Jewish people</note>, for the Divine Name **ADNY** <note>original: "אדנ"י" - Adonai, often associated with the Sefirah of Malchut/Sovereignty</note> is the source of Israel, as I have elaborated elsewhere. **Sovereignty** <note>Hebrew: *Malchut*</note>, which is the Upper Earth, is the end of the spiritual levels above and the beginning of the **Primordial Thought**. From there, through a process of spiritual evolution, this lower earth was drawn down, from which Man was taken; the Holy One, blessed be He, gathered his dust from the entire earth. Thus, the Heavens represent the Torah, and the Earth represents Man. I have already written about the superiority of the "elevated souls" over the Torah, and the superiority of the Torah over Man. Thus, the words of the schools of Shammai and Hillel are both justified, as are the words of the Sages. In one respect, the essence of the Torah is the soul of Israel—our spirit and our life. The **Primordial Torah** is the soul of the elevated ones, while the **Given Torah** is the soul of the majority of Israel. Thus, they are joined together as brothers and companions: the Torah and the souls. A similar explanation of this divine concept was given by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero <note>A leading 16th-century Kabbalist in Safed</note> in his book *The Gates*, in the section:

->The Diminishing of the Moon, Chapter Three; see there.<-

# And regarding
the connection of these three mentioned above—the Holy One, blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel—the passage at the beginning of *Midrash Rabbah* <note>An ancient collection of homiletic teachings on the Torah</note> will be explained. The master craftsman opened with the verse: "I was with Him as an **Amon**, and I was His delight day by day..." <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>. The word *Amon* can be interpreted as a **pedagogue** <note>a tutor or nurturer</note>, or as something **covered**, or as something **hidden**, and some say *Amon* means **great**. 

*Amon* as a **pedagogue**: as it says, "as a nursing father (*omen*) carries the infant" <note>Numbers 11:12</note>. 
*Amon* as **covered**: as it says, "those who were nurtured (*ha-emunim*) in scarlet..." <note>Lamentations 4:5</note>. 
*Amon* as **hidden**: as it says, "And he was the guardian (*omen*) of Hadassah" <note>Esther 2:7, referring to Mordechai hiding Esther's identity</note>. 
*Amon* as **great**: as you might say, one who considers a vessel "great" (*amon*), etc. We find that this term comes from Alexandria, where they call a person of light a "great one."

First, I will explain the plain meaning of the passage. The difference between "covered" and "hidden" is that "covered" refers to something that is not truly lost to us, but is simply draped with a garment; once the cover is removed, it is revealed. Thus the verse says, "those who were nurtured in scarlet," meaning those who were dressed and adorned in scarlet garments have now become naked and embrace ash heaps, needing to cover themselves in the refuse to stay warm. "Hidden," however, refers to something truly stowed away and concealed, like "he was the guardian of Hadassah," for Mordechai was stowing her away and concealing her as much as he could. *Amon* as a **pedagogue** suggests a beautiful form, teaching you that these concepts apply to the Torah, which was given power over the "son." 

The meaning of the **pedagogue** is that the Torah was with Him, may He be blessed, like a tutor with a king, disciplining the king's son so he may grow. Similarly, through the Torah, the Holy One brings forth the created beings, as will be explained shortly, and He appointed the Torah over them to be their leader and guide. This is also the explanation given by the author of *Kanfei Yonah* and similarly by Gersonides <note>Rabbi Levi ben Gershon, also known as Ralbag</note>. 

However, I find it difficult to say that *Amon* is merely the name of a pedagogue. Rather, it means a "nurturer" (*oman*). It is possible that the word *Amon* is a linguistic variation of "pedagogue," used in the sense of "faithfulness" (*emunah*). Ibn Ezra explains that at the time of her greatness, she was with Him, or she was "nurtured" and raised in His lap. Her upbringing was thus of the highest degree, as the Torah is emanated from Him. 

Now, there are seven aspects of "faithfulness" and three primary themes. Some add more, but how can there be a dispute between them? Both are the "words of the Living God." It will also be explained what the connection of these matters is to the explanation of "In the beginning" (*Bereishit*). Even though the book *Yafah To'ar* states that "many have sought to find a connection between these matters and the meaning of *Bereishit* but have followed vanity," because they did not know the way of the Midrash, which often brings a verse from elsewhere to explain a concept and then returns to the main topic. Rashi <note>The primary medieval commentator on the Bible and Talmud</note> wrote that this verse reveals deep and hidden things, and this verse is helpful here because of the subsequent teaching: "I was His professional tool," which relates directly to the beginning of the Torah, as we will see.

# From
the beginning, I say that if this statement is interpreted as a true matter, it has a proper connection to the verse "In the beginning God created." This is good and acceptable. 
<margin>One, because the seven names correspond to the "Beginning of Wisdom" <note>Hebrew: *Reshit Chokhmah*</note>, which is the Primordial Thought. Wisdom consists of the thirty-two paths of wisdom. Therefore, Onkelos <note>The famous translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note> translates "In the beginning" with a term meaning "at the start."</margin>
I will first introduce the intention of "In the beginning" (*Bereishit*). The Jerusalem and Yonatan Targums <note>Aramaic translations/paraphrases of the Bible</note> translate it as "With wisdom," while Onkelos translates it as "At the start." Yet everything leads to the same place. 
Why does it say *Bereishit* with a "B" <note>The Hebrew letter *Bet*, which also means "two" or "with"</note> and not just *Reshit* (Beginning), which refers to Wisdom? 
The Zohar explains: "*Bereishit* starts with a *Bet* because Wisdom is **second** to the hidden Supreme Crown <note>Keter</note>. The Crown is the absolute first, and because of its intensity, its power is not revealed. Thus, Wisdom is called *Reshit* (Beginning), but it is the second beginning." 

The book *Sha'ar* <note>likely referring to *Sha’ar HaHakdamot* or a section of the *Pardes*</note> in the chapter on whether the **Infinite** (*Ein Sof*) is the Crown, explains this as follows: It was difficult for him to understand the word *Bereishit*, because the letter *Bet* is large and hints at Wisdom, as is known. But the word *Reshit* also hints at Wisdom. Thus, Wisdom seems to be hinted at twice in this one word, which is not right. The explanation is that both the *Bet* and the word *Reshit* hint at Wisdom, but they show that the world is "double." *Reshit* implies a beginning, and it might seem that Wisdom is the very first point of emanation. But this is not so, for the **Crown** (*Keter*) is the true beginning of emanation. Therefore, the word starts with the letter *Bet* (numerical value 2) to say: even though this is called "the beginning," it is actually **second** in the count of the Sefirot. The Crown is the true first. 

This is why the Zohar says it is "second in the count." Wisdom is called the "beginning" because it is the place where people might err, thinking it is the absolute start. In truth, the Crown is first, but it is "hidden and concealed" and not fit to be called "beginning." The word "beginning" implies the **start of revelation**, and revelation begins in Wisdom, not in the Crown. Even though the Crown is not called "beginning," it is still the start of the emanation and is included in the count. This is why the word *Bereishit* is "doubled" (Bet + Reshit), to tell you that Wisdom is called the beginning, but even as a beginning, it is second. 

Based on this, I would say that while the word *Bereishit* hints at Wisdom, its "tail" <note>the small stroke on the bottom right of the Hebrew letter Bet</note> points toward the Crown. The sages of the school of Rabbi Akiva say: We ask the *Bet*, "Who created you?" and it points with its tail toward the *Aleph* <note>The first letter, representing the One/Crown</note>. The intention is that the *Bet* itself is Wisdom, showing that there is no "start" to the emanation except that it is a second emanation. It has a tail behind it to point toward the *Aleph*, showing anyone who asks if it was emanated by an emanator or the First Emanator, that it is the second emanation and that the *Aleph* (the Crown) preceded it. 

The book *Pardes* <note>*Pardes Rimonim* by Cordovero</note> in the section on the "Reason for Emanation," Chapter 3, writes: "The opinion of Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, or Ramban</note> in his commentary on *Bereishit* is similar. The word *Bereishit* hints at Wisdom, which is the 'Beginning of Beginnings,' as the Jerusalem Targum explains: 'With Wisdom.' And the word is 'crowned' with the Crown of the *Bet*." The meaning of his words is that the letter *Bet* hints at the Crown because it is the "house" (*Bayit*) for all the Sefirot. This is evident from his language when he says the word *Bereishit* hints at Wisdom—meaning the word itself, not the letter *Bet*. He notes that the word is *Reshit* (Beginning), but the word is "crowned" by the letter *Bet* which acts as the Crown.

# And this
matter is explained in many places: the revelation of the Ten Sefirot is from Wisdom downwards. Within Wisdom is the Name **Y-D-H** <note>A variation of the Tetragrammaton</note> which acts as a "chariot" for the Crown, as the Zohar says on the verse "There is none holy like the Lord." The Name **Y-D-H** is the chariot for the luminary that is the Crown. **Knowledge** (*Da'at*) completes the count because it is the aspect of the Crown that is revealed. The Name **Y-H-W-H** includes the entire emanation: the *Yod* is Wisdom, the *Heh* is Understanding, the *Vav* is the six directions <note>the middle six Sefirot</note>, and the final *Heh* is Sovereignty. All of them were "made with Wisdom," for Wisdom is the Primordial Thought. 

This is the secret of the letter *Yod* expanded <note>Gematria method called Milluy</note> in the secret of the **Name of 72** (*Ayin-Bet*): *Yod-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Yod, Vav-Yod-Vav, Heh-Yod*. From this, all existence spreads out, for "the world is built on Kindness" (*Chesed*), and the numerical value of *Chesed* (Kindness) is 72. Below *Chesed* is the secret of "offspring" and "building," but above, it is hidden within the **Supreme Kindness**, which is Wisdom, the head of the pillar of Kindness, the "Beginning of Wisdom." Now, the "Building" consists of three pillars: the pillar of Kindness (*Chesed*), the pillar of Judgment (*Din*), and the pillar of Mercy (*Rachamim*). The root of the Building above is Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge. Knowledge is the aspect of the Crown that is revealed. It is written: "The Lord **with Wisdom**..."
