# The Tablets of the Covenant

With **Wisdom** He founded the earth, and with **Understanding** He established the heavens, and it is written: “By His **Knowledge**, the depths were broken open.” These three represent the roots of the three pillars: **Wisdom** <note>original: "Hokhmah"</note> is the root of the Pillar of Kindness; **Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"</note> is the root of the Pillar of Judgment; and **Knowledge** <note>original: "Da'at"</note>, in its aspect of the **Crown** <note>original: "Keter"</note>, is the root of the Pillar of Mercy. These three principles, when manifested within the structure of the world, appear as the dimensions of the lower realms, but above in their root, they exist as the form of the letter *Yud* <note>the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often depicted as a single point</note>—specifically as points. I have elaborated on this teaching in its proper place. These three "Yuds" are the three points found in the full spelling of the Divine Name mentioned above, and they hint at the revelation of His Godhood through His descent to Israel, who are the "building of the world." There is also a fourth aspect in that Name: the *Yud* of the full spelling <note>spelling the letter Yud as Yud-Vav-Dalet</note>. For these three Yuds enter into a single *Yud*, which is the "root of their roots," where they are contained in profound concealment. Even the single letter *Yud* possesses three subtle aspects: the **tip** of the *Yud*, the **body** of the *Yud*, and the **foot** of the *Yud*. This hints at the unification of these three together in their source above, until they become a single *Yud* from the perspective of the **Crown**, within the mystery of the "Primordial Light," the "Pure Light," and the "Scintillating Light." This is explained elsewhere as the root and the root of their roots, a place of ultimate concealment. I will not lengthen the discussion here, as I have done so in its proper place. This concept surrounds the discourse found in the Midrash *Bereshit Rabbah*. The sage Rabbi Oshaya Rabbah speaks of the aspect of the three Yuds which constitute the "Beginning of Wisdom," in the mystery of **Thought**. For "Thought is the beginning, and Action is the end." It is established that "In that which is too wondrous for you, do not seek," referring to the absolute wonder of the **Crown**, which is the mystery of the "Spark," as is known. This is the mystery of the "Ascent of Will," where the letter *Vav* <note>representing a vertical line or connection</note> is the beginning of revelation, the mystery of Thought. Of this wonder, one does not speak, except regarding the first roots of revelation, which are the mystery of Thought—the three Yuds. I have already elaborated above that "Israel arose in Thought," meaning they are the mystery of the "Supernal Children," the root of the "Primordial Torah" and the root of the souls of the "Children of the Upper Chamber." This hints at the revelation of His Divinity: the mystery of the letter *Yud*, the root of **Emanation** <note>original: "Atzilut"</note>, the Ten **Emanations** <note>original: "Sefirot"</note>. The Name spelled out as *YUD* <note>Yud-Vav-Dalet</note> includes all of Emanation and is hidden within the single *Yud*, as I will explain shortly.

## The Pedagogical Architect
The text says "Amon" <note>from Proverbs 8:30: "I was with Him as an 'Amon'"</note> and not "Oman" <note>artisan</note>, because it hints at two matters: the **Primordial Torah** is "Faith" <note>original: "Emunah"</note> to Him—literally faithful with Him—forming a single impression. It is also a "Pedagogue" <note>original: "Pedagog," a tutor or nanny</note>, for it is the root of the souls of the Children of Israel, His children, who were cared for in His Thought. Whether "Faithful" or "Artisan," all these meanings are included within it. This hints at the mystery of the subtle *Yud* of Kindness, the *Yud* of Israel, the "Children of the Upper Chamber," regarding whom it is said they were created "In the Image and Likeness." In a wondrous way, the "Man below" <note>humanity</note> points toward the "Man above" <note>the Divine form</note>. This is achieved through the **Torah of Hidden Light**, which is the "Specular Mirror" <note>a clear looking glass</note> through which a person sees and takes delight like a "Child of the Upper Chamber."

## The Covered Architect, The Hidden Architect
Now he speaks specifically of the letter *Yud* of the Torah, saying it is "covered" and "hidden." This means the **Primordial Torah** is hidden and stored away, the mystery of the **Hidden Light**. This Torah given to us is "covered." I have already explained that "covered" means something that stands before us but requires revelation—as in the phrase, "If I toil and find, believe it; if I do not toil and find, do not believe." However, the **Hidden Primordial Torah** is entirely beyond reach. These three are the beginnings of the "Beginning of Thought," which the Midrash *Bereshit Rabbah* discusses regarding the word "In the beginning" <note>original: "Bereshit"</note>. Our Sages hinted: "In the beginning"—for the sake of the **Torah** and for the sake of **Israel**. Therefore, Rabbi Oshaya Rabbah linked his words to the verse "In the beginning." The verse he cites, "And I was His delight day by day," hints at the **Beginning of Thought**, the mystery of the Primordial Torah which existed two thousand years before the world, as mentioned above. The foundation and secret of the Holy One is "a thousand years," as will be explained.

## And Some Say "The Great Amon"
These scholars hint at the "Wonder" <note>the Crown</note> which is hinted at in the first letter of the Torah, the *Bet* of *Bereshit*. As Nachmanides <note>original: "Ramban"</note> hinted, the letter *Bet* points to that which comes after, while the letter *Aleph* points to "Wonder" <note>original: "Pele," an anagram of Aleph</note>, which is the **Crown**. I have more to explain regarding these deep matters until we reach the phrase "Blessed is He." This will also align with the discourse of the "Chapter of the Young Girl" I wrote above. One must provide a reason for the ruling that in the chapter "The Sons of the City," one does not mention the "New Moon" except to marry a woman. The reason given is "He did not create it for chaos, but formed it to be inhabited" <note>Isaiah 45:18</note>. It is difficult to understand why the verse "Be fruitful and multiply" is not cited instead. This difficulty appears at the beginning of Tractate *Hagigah*, where it says "the world was only created for procreation," yet it cites the verse "He did not create it for chaos." The Tosafists <note>medieval commentators</note> addressed this, noting that procreation is a "Great Commandment," but their words remained cryptic as to why this specific verse is stronger.

## And Now
Listen, and your soul shall live! I will reveal a tiny portion of the mystery of the **Act of Creation** <note>original: "Ma'aseh Bereshit"</note>. I will reveal part of the secret of the name *YUD* <note>Yud-Vav-Dalet</note> and the secret of the name *ADU* <note>Aleph-Dalet-Vav</note>, and the significance of the name *ADU* in its expansions. These are hinted at in the verse Rabbi Oshaya brought: "And I was with Him as an architect" <note>original: "Amon"</note>. All the acts of creation exist in their simple form in the lower realms, but they also exist spiritually and through hints in the upper realms, as Abraham Ibn Ezra <note>original: "Ra'ba"</note> and Nachmanides wrote regarding the Garden of Eden and its rivers. From the ten hidden spiritual "Utterances," an unfolding chain descended—without measure or estimate—until reaching the ten physical "Utterances" that built this physical world. The physical is like a condensed crown of the spiritual. The hint for the building of the physical world is in the secret of the name *YUD* <note>the numerical value of Yud is 10</note>, corresponding to the Ten Utterances. For the spiritual mystery above, I will first quote Nachmanides at the beginning of Genesis: "We must understand that the Holy One created all beings from absolute nothingness. There is no word in our Holy Tongue for bringing something out of nothing except 'Created' <note>original: 'Bara'</note>... He brought out from absolute, total nothingness a very thin foundation, having no substance, but it was a 'formative power' ready to receive shape and move from potential to actual. This is the **First Matter**, called by the Greeks **Hyle**. After this *Hyle*, He created nothing else, but rather formed and made things from it... In the *Book of Creation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note>, it says He 'formed substance from void'..." Nachmanides explains this at length. It appears to me that this "point of thought" was the power of God, so to speak, that shaped it. It is the **Foundation Stone** <note>original: "Even Shetiyah"</note> from which the world was watered. Therefore, at first, God created from absolute nothingness a point called "Chaos" <note>original: "Tohu"</note> in the Holy Tongue, "Foundation Stone" by the Sages, and "Hyle" in Greek. Then God "milked" that point to give it form—the four elements. Then it expanded, and what was "Chaos" <note>Tohu</note> became "Void" <note>Bohu</note>, meaning "it is in it" <note>a play on the word Bo-Hu</note>. Afterward, it expanded further in length and width to sustain life. There is no action or thing that does not come from the four elements. All of this is hinted at in the letter *Yud*, for with Ten Utterances the world was created. The letter *Yud* in its full spelling represents the **point** <note>the letter Yud itself</note>, the **expansion of four** <note>the letter Dalet, which equals 4, representing the four directions or elements</note>, and the **expansion of length and width** <note>the letter Vav</note>. Rabbi Azriel wrote in his book that every point contains three dimensions: length, width, and depth. Rabbi Judah Hayyat challenged him, arguing that dimensions belong to quantity, and a point has no quantity. The book *Pardes Rimonim* explains this at the beginning of the "Gate of the Reason for Emanation": "Every physical body has length, width, and depth. If we imagine only two dimensions—length and width—it is called a **surface**. If we imagine only one—length—it is a **line**. When we imagine the absence of all three, it is a **point**. This does not mean it exists physically; it is a 'conceptual point' used to define the absence of dimensions." With this, we understand Rabbi Judah's objection to Rabbi Azriel. A point is the "end of a line." There is no consensus among the wise; some say two or more points joined together create a line. Whether the point is conceptual or not, it is hinted at by the *Yud*. When it moves into action to become physical, it becomes a **line** (the letter *Vav*) and a **surface** (the letter *Dalet*). So it is above in the mystery of the hidden spiritual realm: the "Hidden Hyle" is the *Yud*, the mystery of the point which is **Wisdom** <note>original: "Hokhmah"</note>. This is the *Yud* of the Name *YUD*. They call it the "Hidden Supernal Point" and the "Beginning of Thought," which is the "End of Action." This is the "filling" of the *Yud*—the letters *Vav* and *Dalet*—which are the mystery of the six directions and the four aspects of the "Face," namely Beauty <note>Tiferet</note> and Sovereignty <note>Malkhut</note>. Beauty is the line and the expansion; Sovereignty is the surface of the building. This teaching is explained at length in its proper place. These two letters, *Vav* and *Dalet*, were expanded through **Understanding** <note>Binah</note>, which is the first letter *He* of the Divine Name. When a *Yud* enters a *Dalet*, it becomes a *He*. This *Yud* of Wisdom is the mystery of "Something from Nothing" <note>original: "Yesh me-Ayin"</note>. Above the "Wonder" is "Nothing" <note>Ayin</note>, and Wisdom is called "Something" <note>Yesh</note>. "Wisdom is found from Nothing"—meaning its existence comes from the **Crown**, which is called "Nothing" <note>Ayin</note>. This is hinted at by the **tip** of the *Yud*. The name "Nothing" is not applied to the Crown in a literal sense, but only in conjunction with Wisdom and Understanding. The reason is that "Nothing" can only be applied to that which the mind can partially grasp as a necessary existence, but then retreats from that grasp, realizing it is unattainable. But that which the mind cannot grasp at all...

It is known that the *Hiriq* indicates "crushing" <note>deka</note> and the lowering of the upper to the lower, as explained in the *Pardes* in the Gate of Vowels. Therefore, "Magnifier" <note>Magdil</note>, which has a *Patah* under the *Mem*, is not as good as the level of "Tower" <note>Migdal</note>, which has a *Hiriq* under the *Mem*. Then, when the "Who" <note>Mi</note> is great <note>Gadal</note>, his name is a great darkness, hinting at the exile...

And behold, the Holy One hinted to Noah to make an Ark like a tower, for "I have seen you as a righteous man," and he was a "righteous and whole man." In the future, one should take a lesson from this, that from now on there shall be the glory of the "Tower," and there shall be established in it a "Tower of Strength, the Name of the Lord; the righteous man runs into it and is exalted." <note>Proverbs 18:10</note> The matter is that he must make a lower building of thirty-six levels, one atop the other. The lowest levels, which are for waste, correspond to the World of Action <note>Asiyah</note>, which is soiled and surrounded by "shells." This is as the Zohar explains... the "birds" refer to the angel Michael (as it is written, "one of the Seraphim flew to me") and Gabriel (as it is written, "the man Gabriel... flying in weariness"). The third levels are for Man, the mystery of the Throne <note>Kisse</note>, where the form of Jacob is engraved. Above them all, at the head of the tower, is the Name of the Lord <note>Y-H-V-H</note>; "into it the righteous man runs and is exalted." 

Behold, beneath the Throne of Glory and below, from which the world of angels was spread out, the righteous man is destined to be between them. Regarding him, it is said: "I will give you free access among these who stand here." <note>Zechariah 3:7</note> For the angels are called "standers" because they stay in their place, but Man is called a "walker" <note>mehalekh</note> because he goes from perfection to perfection until he merits to cling between these holy groups. One who is especially righteous and merits the Name of the Lord—this is "into it the righteous man runs and is exalted to His Name," attaining a reward that cannot be grasped. Compared to him, even angels are merely "walkers." This is the secret of one who merits to ascend to the "Tower of Strength, the Name of the Lord"—he runs and is exalted above all, and his level is greater even than that of the angels, for his attachment is from the Throne of Glory and above. 

This was hinted to Noah in the building of the Ark, that it should be a tower with one story above another—meaning an awakening from below to above, until the height of the levels. Through this, "make a window <note>tsohar</note> for the Ark," and the Ark shall shine. This is the "Tower of Worlds, the salvations of His King." But the Holy One also hinted at the aspect of "Magnifier" <note>Magdil</note>—if there is no awakening from below to above, but only from above to below. This is hinted in the instruction: "place the door of the Ark in its side," for this Ark hints at the word "Magnifier" <note>Magdil</note>... and there is a *Patah* vowel under the *Mem* as we explained. 

Against these matters was the Generation of the Division <note>the Tower of Babel</note>, who built themselves a tower and sometimes a "magnifier." The matter of the "Tower of David, built for an armory <note>Talpiot</note>"—the hill <note>tel</note> toward which all mouths <note>piyot</note> turn—is the Sanctuary <note>Beit HaMikdash</note> which corresponds to the Sanctuary above, and "I shall dwell among them." # The Written Torah — Tower of Strength

It is known that from the day a person comes into being, what his end will be is already known. If his beginning was exalted, so too will be his end. Even though at the start of his creation, the Midrash Rabbah states that "Moses was a novice <note>Hebrew: *tiro*, meaning an inexperienced recruit</note> in prophecy," he ascended level by level until "there arose none like Moses." He was eventually called the "Man of God" <note>Hebrew: *Ish Ha-Elohim*</note>. Nevertheless, even at the beginning of his high status, he was called "a man," as in "an Egyptian man" <note>Exodus 2:19</note>, just as he was later called a "man" of high degree, namely "the Man of God." This indicates that even in his beginning, his Godliness was sparked within him. This is hinted at by the "Egyptian man" whom he slew <note>referring to Moses' first act of divine zeal</note>, which was the beginning of his greatness and his zeal for his God. He was cleaved to his God, specifically to the Explicit Name <note>The Tetragrammaton</note>. Thus, even in his lower state—as the "Egyptian man"—he was attached to the Divine.

Contrast this with Noah: even at the height of his excellence, when he is called "Righteous," he is also called "a man of the earth" <note>Hebrew: *Ish Ha-Adamah*, Genesis 9:20</note>. The intention here, according to the Midrash I cited earlier, is that Noah was actually included in the decree of "I regret that I made them" <note>Genesis 6:7</note>. The only reason he remained alive was for the sake of the "earth" <note>*Adamah*</note>, for the earth itself had not sinned and was to endure forever. Therefore, he is called "man of the earth," meaning he remained a "man" only for the sake of the earth (the world). Thus, at the very moment of his greatness where they call him "Righteous," the text calls him by the name "man of the earth."

Regarding the Midrash on the verse "Grace is false and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord shall be praised": "Grace is false" refers to Noah, and "beauty is vain" refers to the beauty of Adam <note>the first human</note>. "But a woman who fears the Lord shall be praised" refers to Moses. This statement clearly agrees with what I have written.

However, I say there are further hints in this passage. From the time of the "Garments of Light" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Ohr* (with the letter Aleph), referring to Adam's pre-fall state</note> until they were clothed in "Garments of Skin" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* (with the letter Ayin), the post-fall physical state</note>, the Light found no resting place until Enoch. God took him and he became an angel, namely Metatron. There were ten generations from Adam to Noah. Noah was a righteous man in his generation, and through his survival, he caused the world to endure. Therefore, the name Noah <note>Hebrew: *Noach*, meaning 'rest'</note> relates to the verse "This one will comfort us" <note>Genesis 5:29</note>. His name is half the name of "Enoch" <note>Hebrew: *Chanoch*</note> and also half the name of "Metatron" <note>In certain Kabbalistic calculations, the numerical value (Gematria) of 'Metat' (a shortened form of Metatron) equals 58, which is the same as Noah</note>. The value is 216 <note>Hebrew: *RIV*</note>, from the language of "burning fire." Enoch was transformed into a torch of fire and became Metatron. 

What remained of Enoch after he was "taken" was the life-force <note>Hebrew: *Chai* = 18</note>. This hints that "The Lord your God is a consuming fire." Thus, the excellence of Noah is called "Grace" <note>Hebrew: *Chen*</note>, which is like half of this. "Grace is false" implies this was not the ultimate, true excellence. Similarly, "Beauty is vain" refers to the beauty of Adam, for he followed "vanity" <note>Hebrew: *Hevel*</note>. This word *Hevel* <note>also the name Abel</note> hints at Abel, the son of Adam. "The Lord turned to Abel" <note>Genesis 4:4</note>. Abel was the true "beauty" of the first Adam because Cain represented the side of impurity, while Abel represented the beauty and the exaltation of the soul. As the Kabbalists say, the soul of Moses is a reincarnation of Abel <note>The Hebrew name *Moshe* (Moses) is an acronym for *Moshe, Shet, Hevel* (Moses, Seth, Abel)</note>. It is said that the heel of Adam outshone the sun, and the face of Moses was like the face of the sun itself—indeed, even greater than the sun’s sphere. The soul of Adam was the universal soul, passing through Seth until it was established in Moses. Moses ascended to be a "Man of God" and separated from his wife to become the "husband of the Matronita" <note>a Kabbalistic term for the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note>. This is the meaning of "A woman who fears the Lord shall be praised"—this refers to Moses. This also explains why Moses is hinted at in the context of the Flood... "Since he is also flesh" <note>Genesis 6:3</note>, the word "also" <note>Hebrew: *Be-shagam*</note> has the numerical value of "Moses" <note>345</note>.

<column-break/>

<note>This column contains a complex Kabbalistic interpretation of Ecclesiastes 10:20: "For a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice, and a winged creature shall tell the matter."</note>

The "Watchers" and the "Seers" <note>angelic beings</note> observe all secrets. All that is hidden is revealed to them. Regarding the sin of the generation of the Flood, even though they thought their deeds were hidden, "the bird of the heavens" carries the report. This refers to the spiritual forces and ministers who oversee the twelve constellations and the four directions. 

When a person speaks or acts, these "winged creatures"—the spiritual powers that fly through the world—take that "voice" and elevate it. Even if a person thinks they are in the innermost chamber, the "lord of wings" will tell the matter. This is why the judgment of the Flood was decreed. These "birds" are the messengers who testify before the Heavenly Court. The "birds of the heaven" are the holy forces, while the "winged creatures" can also refer to the forces of judgment. 

Nothing in the world is lost; every word "tells the matter," even those spoken in secret. Therefore, the "Egyptian" whom Moses slew was part of this divine accounting. The "birds" represent the oversight of the Higher Governance over the lower deeds. Even the "beauty of Adam" which was lost was recorded and returned through the lineage of the righteous. This oversight is constant, ensuring that "grace" and "beauty" are measured against "fear of the Lord."

# Let Us Return
<margin>See Section 55.</margin>
Let us return to the matter of Noah from the perspective of "top-down" <note>Divine grace descending to man</note>—at that level, he was a completely righteous man. But Abraham our father worked "bottom-up" <note>human effort ascending to God</note>. Moses our teacher went even higher, becoming the "Man of God." There is a great distinction between the Ark of Noah and the "ark" <note>basket</note> of Moses.

I will now explain the matter of the Ark according to the hints I have written, beginning with the verse: "The name of the Lord is a tower of strength; the righteous runs into it and is safe" <note>Proverbs 18:10</note>. I say that "Tower of Strength" <note>Hebrew: *Migdal Oz*</note> refers to the Ark, and the "Righteous" refers to "Noah, a righteous man." 

I will also explain the concept of the "Tower" <note>*Migdal*</note> and the "Tower of Salvation" <note>Psalm 18:51 and 2 Samuel 22:51</note>. In the book of Psalms, it is written *Magdil* <note>"He makes great the salvations of His king"</note>, but in the book of Samuel, it is written *Migdol* <note>"He is a tower of salvations for His king"</note>. It is customary to say this verse after the Grace After Meals. The later authorities wrote that on weekdays one should say *Magdil*, but on Shabbat and Festivals, one should say *Migdol*. They gave a mnemonic: "On Shabbat and Festivals, the text follows the scripture" <note>referring to a specific liturgical tradition</note>.

There is a third "Tower" mentioned regarding the generation of the "Tower of the Generation" <note>Babel</note>. Before providing the reason for this, I will quote a Midrash from the end of Genesis. This all circles back to what I wrote above. Rabbi Simon said: "The Holy One found three 'finds': Abraham, as it is written 'And You found his heart faithful before You'; David, as it is written 'I have found David My servant'; and Israel, as it is written 'Like grapes in the wilderness, I found Israel'." 

His colleagues questioned Rabbi Simon: "But it is written, 'And Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord'?" He answered: "He <note>Noah</note> found it, but the Holy One did not 'find' him." 

One might ask: why aren't these listed in chronological order (Abraham, then Israel, then David)? This relates to the "Generations" mentioned above. All "generations" in the Torah are written defectively <note>missing a letter Vav</note> except for "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth" and "These are the generations of Peretz." As I wrote, the status of the first Adam, had he not sinned, would have been a "bridge" between the higher and lower worlds, similar to Moses who "did not move from the Divine Presence." The goal is for the Shekhinah (Divine Presence) to dwell among the lower beings. But because Adam failed, he was clothed in skin and the Shekhinah departed. The ultimate perfection is to awaken from below to above. 

In the End of Days, the creation will be renewed. The original intent of creation—which has not yet been realized for even a single day, because "Adam in his glory did not abide"—will be fulfilled when the Messiah comes. Then the Lord will "rejoice in His works." Israel, whose excellence lies in their awakening from below ("We will do and we will listen"), are called "Adam." They will be like Adam before the sin, and the verse "I shall dwell among them" will be fulfilled. Then "Generations" will be written in its full form, as the intention of creation will be complete.

# The Tablets of the Covenant

I have found in the holy writings of the author <note>Referring to the Shelah, Rabbi Isaiah Horowitz</note> regarding the four types of existence: Mineral, Vegetable, Animal, and Communicative <note>Human</note>. At the time of the world's creation, the most select level was established, which is Man. Before the sin, Man was on such a high spiritual level that he was forbidden from eating meat, as everything was already elevated. However, after the sin, the levels fell, and it became necessary to eat meat so that the human could elevate the sparks of the animal level back to the level of "Communicative" <note>Human</note>. This is why Noah was permitted to eat meat. Even in the Temple, through the sacrifices, they would rectify all four types of existence together with the Human. This is the secret of the sacrifices: they must be brought from the "clean" animals and accompanied by grain offerings and wine, elevating everything back to its source.
</margin>

<margin>
Regarding the generation of the Flood, they had stayed at a base level, and their merits were not enough to save them. The author explains that spiritual levels descend from above to below. In the future, we will merit the levels that were briefly glimpsed at Mount Sinai, where the physical and spiritual were merged, as mentioned previously.
</margin>

That is to say, the body itself will become a garment of glory, just as the soul is clothed in light. Similarly, the physical clothing we wear will become "garments of honor." We saw a glimmer of this in the desert, where the Bible says, "Your clothes did not wear out" <note>Deuteronomy 8:4</note>. In the future, our Sages teach that the Land of Israel will naturally produce fine cakes <note>original: "גלוסקאות"</note>—representing the holiness of food—and finished silk garments—representing the holiness of clothing. These are the two things Jacob the Patriarch prayed for: "Bread to eat and a garment to wear." 

Noah began this process of "rectification." He fixed the realm of food by feeding all the creatures in the Ark, and he began fixing the realm of clothing when he took a garment to cover his father's nakedness. This process will be completed in the future. Because Noah fixed the realm of food, he was elevated above the level of Adam in that he was permitted to eat meat. We see this holiness even in the commandment of *Tzitzit* <note>ritual fringes</note>, where the law permits "forbidden mixtures" <note>shatnez</note>—combining wool and linen—which is otherwise forbidden. Originally, Cain (who brought flax/linen) and Abel (who brought sheep/wool) were divided, but through the commandments, these elements are unified. In the future, the "bread to eat" will be the "Bread of the Mighty" <note>Manna</note>, ground in the celestial heavens, and we will wear royal garments of light. The spiritual jewelry that the Israelites lost at Mount Horeb will be restored to them speedily in our days, Amen.

->**The Way of Life: Moral Instruction**<-
->The "Covenant of the Organ" <note>Circumcision/Purity</note> is the light that protects each generation.<-

The generation of the Flood failed because they did not sanctify themselves, acting like animals. One must be holy during intimate moments, with pure thoughts. If not, the Sages say of such a person, "Cursed is he who lies with an animal." In this portion, the Torah mentions the animals: "Of every clean beast you shall take seven pairs, a man and his mate; and of beasts that are not clean, two, a man and his mate." Why does the Torah use the human terms "man and his mate" <note>ish ve-ishto</note> for animals here? It hints that the generation of the Flood had blurred the lines, acting like animals, and the animals in turn acted like humans. On a mystical level, some souls from that generation were even reincarnated into animals. I have expanded on these matters in the "Gate of Letters" under the letter *Kof* for *Kedushah* <note>Holiness</note>.

### **The Zohar**
The Zohar warns many times in this portion regarding the time of intimacy and the preservation of the "seed of life." When there is destruction in the world, a person should "withdraw his feet" and hide in private. One should not leave the entrance of their house so the "Destroyer" <note>the Angel of Destruction</note> does not look at him. As long as the Destroyer does not see a person's face, he has no power over them. This is why Noah was saved in the Ark; he was hidden from the "waters of the Flood," which are also called the "waters of destruction." One who guards his soul will distance himself from all corruption and hide until the wrath has passed.

### **And He Said**
"The Lord said to Noah: Come into the Ark." From here we learn that one does not have the right to enter a home or a lodging without the permission of the owner. Noah did not want to enter the Ark until the Holy One, the "Owner of the Ark," commanded him to do so.

### **For You**
"For you I have seen to be righteous." From here we learn that one should not accept a guest into their home unless they are considered upright by the owner. We also learn that if a host gives a guest permission to stay, the guest has no right to bring in additional guests without the host's consent, for the verse says: "Come you *and* all your household." The Zohar writes all of this. Also, one must distance oneself from drunkenness, seeing what happened to Noah because of wine. I have elaborated on this elsewhere.

Regarding the additional perception that Abraham merited until he cleaved to the Upper Land, the verse says: "And the Lord appeared to Abraham and said, 'To your offspring I will give this land,' and he built there an altar to the Lord who appeared to him" <note>Genesis 12:7</note>. 

It is difficult: why does it say here "And the Lord appeared and said," while at the beginning of the portion it does not say "And He said"? Furthermore, why the extra language "who appeared to him"? This difficulty can be resolved to make known the praise of Abraham our Father: that his primary praise and the building of the altar were for the sake of spiritual increase—that is, for the revelation of His Presence <note>original: Shekhinah</note>, the glory of the Lord—and not because of the news that was told to him regarding his offspring and the giving of the land. However, according to our way, it reinforces the additional vision of perception. Thus it is written in the **Zohar** <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note>: "And the Lord appeared to Abraham—here was revealed to him that which he did not know [previously], that deep power that rules over the land. She proved it was a spiritual light, for if it were physical, how could she "see after seeing"? It is a known thing that one who looks at a great physical light, like the light of the sun, finds their eyes dimmed. But the opposite is true with spiritual light: the more one looks and perceives, the more one is able to perceive. This is how the author of the Zohar <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> looked... and this is what she meant by "You are a God of seeing," for certainly "I have seen after my seeing." So too it says here of Abraham: "who appeared to him" after the initial vision. 

The matter of the altar he built hints at the "Square Altar" which is in the celestial form. Regarding the aforementioned matter, that Abraham returned from his fullness and his father's house—which are "external wisdoms" as explained in the Zohar—and "He took him outside," outside of the land. # Tablets of the Covenant

And these are the <term>Kelipot</term> <note>Hebrew: "husks" or "shells"; in Kabbalah, these are the forces of impurity that conceal the light of holiness</note>, for "the pit was empty, there was no water in it." It is written, "God (<term>El</term>) is indignant every day," but also "God is indignant every day." <note>This refers to the interplay between the name El, usually associated with Kindness, and its use in contexts of judgment</note>. The name <term>El</term> represents the attribute of Kindness (<term>Chesed</term>), yet it also states that He possesses the attribute of indignation and wrath. This is because He is indignant toward the "husks" to nullify them, and this itself is an act of Kindness. Perhaps this is the meaning of the verse: "I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleanness," because the "filth" and "pollution" of the husks—which arise from sins—are washed away. And this water is called "a little water," for the husk does not "be fruitful and multiply," whereas holiness continually increases. As it says, "Many waters cannot quench love"—the eternal love—and the essence of the attribute of Kindness is found in the secret of those "many waters." However, at times, as in the verse "Let a little water be fetched," it is the property of Kindness to clothe itself within the husk to subdue it. Therefore, he said, "Let a little water be fetched" to wash away the pollution of the husks, and it is also washed away through the expression "let it be fetched" by means of a messenger.

For the essence of the attribute is the secret of "many waters," while "a little water" is the secret of clothing oneself in the husk to subdue it. And although the Sages of blessed memory gave another explanation for this—that because "it was fetched" by a messenger, the Holy One, Blessed be He, repaid Abraham's children through a messenger—nonetheless, the truth is surely that they hinted at this: it would have been better had human beings acted well and not come to the point of sin, requiring washing and cleansing. Then, there would have been an attachment to God "face to face" without any intermediary. This is the matter of the "messenger." Furthermore, on one level, the secret of the "upper waters" is missing, as it is written "and the waters were firm in their place." And he said, "and rest yourselves under the tree"; the <term>Targum</term> <note>The ancient Aramaic translation of the Bible</note> of Onkelos renders this as "under the terebinth." This means that if humans are good, the Tree is there to take refuge under its branches from the "heat of the day." And when he says, "I will fetch a morsel of bread," we find that he actually took and made a great deal of bread. The scripture testifies that he used "three seahs of fine flour," and specifies "three seahs of flour" rather than "he baked," because completed attributes are more expansive when measured individually than when measured all at once, due to the overflow. This indicates the extraordinary generosity and "good eye" of Abraham our Father.

Thus, there was much bread, yet it is not mentioned that the bread ever reached the table. Rashi, on the verse regarding the flour, wrote what he wrote, and it will be explained further on. It is possible to say that since only a tiny fraction of what was baked reached the table, the merit of baking so much was not counted. We can understand the "tongues" <note>Abraham served three tongues with mustard</note> that he prepared to feed them, but why did he make so much bread? One could say the verse explains this: "I will fetch a morsel of bread, and satisfy your hearts; after that you may pass on." That is, "I will give you provisions for the way, so you will have bread to eat and satisfy your hearts after you leave here." This is what the Sages said in the chapter *HaChovel*: "Eat early in the summer because of the heat," etc. At that time, there was a great heat, and Abraham understood to give them food for the journey.

And it says, "And he stood over them... and they ate." This is like the verse "And they beheld God, and they ate and drank," for Abraham worked over them to bring them "under the wings of the Divine Presence" (<term>Shekhinah</term>). He did this to act with kindness toward his Creator, as Rashi explains. This is the explanation of these expressions according to the path where Abraham thought they might be mere men or desert-dwellers. Then, he was given the news of Isaac's birth, who was of an exalted level. This relates to the Binding of Isaac (<term>Akedah</term>), which is also the aspect of a "pious man who acts with kindness toward his Creator," as will be explained later. This attribute was revealed at the time he was promised Isaac. His intention then was to teach human beings the good path, so they would enter under the wings of the Divine Presence. Because of this, he is the "source of fire" from which instruction went out to the world.

# The Second Path

This is the path wherein Abraham our Father thought that these were angels. In that case, he intended this meal for another purpose: the secret of the sacrifices. And this is the matter of:

-> The Holy One, Blessed be He, remembered Abraham, as seen in Midrash Rabbah on the portion regarding sacrifices: "When a bull, or a sheep, or a goat is born." "A bull"—this is Abraham, as it is written: <-

"And Abraham ran to the herd..." and "Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah and said: 'Hurry, three seahs of fine flour...'" This corresponded to the <term>Minchah</term> <note>The grain or meal offering</note>. Wine is not mentioned, though it would have been appropriate to mention it for the secret of the wine libation. In its place, he mentioned "milk and butter," for as is known, milk comes from the side of Kindness (<term>Chesed</term>), while wine comes from the side of Judgment (<term>Din</term>). Here, the entire awakening was from the side of Abraham's kindness. Now, the bread was not brought to the table; the Sages explained that Sarah had become a <term>niddah</term> <note>menstrually impure</note>, as her "way of women" had returned to her that day. Abraham our Father ate even non-sacred food in a state of ritual purity. One might ask: if Abraham was strict with himself, how could he be strict with others? Some say it is not proper etiquette to give a guest food that the host himself cannot eat. Rabbi Bahya answered that because Sarah became impure, there was a delay in seeing what would happen with her, so she would not feed Abraham impure dough. Because of this, the dough sat long enough to become leavened (<term>chametz</term>), and it was then forbidden because it was Passover—not because of the impurity of the dough. However, in Rashi, this is not implied. According to our approach, it fits well: since he thought they were angels, the meal was in the secret of a sacrifice. It is absolutely obvious that it was forbidden to offer the bread, for it is like holy things, and it was not prepared in a state of sacred purity but became defiled. This matter, that the meal was like a sacrifice, is hinted at in Midrash Rabbah (Section 71, Paragraph 77). It says regarding the eating that "each first portion disappears." He understood this "disappearing" from the words of Manoah <note>The father of Samson</note>: for when the heavenly fire descends upon it, the sacrifice is consumed on its own. This is hinted at with Manoah, when the angel ascended in the flame of the altar, as it says, "And the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame of the altar." It is known that Manoah did not build an altar but offered upon a rock; however, the angel ascended in the flame of the *heavenly* altar from which the fire descended. Therefore, the angel told him: "If you detain me, I will not eat of your bread," for it is an abomination to the Name to offer to an angel; rather, it must be offered only to the Unique Name, as it says, "None but to the Lord alone." And "If you offer a burnt offering, offer it to the Lord," and then it will be good for me, for the angel will ascend in the upper light and be elevated in the flame of the heavenly altar. So too, Abraham's intention was not to feed them, for he knew that angels do not eat. Rather, his intention was:

For the sake of the Unique Name, which was revealed in the verse "And the Lord appeared to him," to arouse an overflow of abundance and blessing as if he had offered a sacrifice with the proper intention upon the altar, where the "first portions disappear" in fire toward the heavens. This food would disappear, and through this, an additional overflow and blessing would come to them, and they would be elevated to the level of Emanation (<term>Atzilut</term>), and that Emanation would be elevated and unified with the First Cause. This is similar to what was said of Manoah: "And Manoah and his wife saw and fell on their faces," and they knew. This is enough for the wise.

<margin>Notes on the three men: Perhaps he knew the food would disappear first, as it is the 'chariot of the world' for the altar.</margin>

It is possible that from here Satan found a reason to prosecute, for it was during this meal that the birth of Isaac was announced. See Recanati (Parashat Vayeira) on this matter, explaining the "secret of providing for the belly" <note>giving a portion to the forces of judgment to quiet them</note>. Satan complained: "From all the feasts Abraham made, he did not offer before You a single bull or a single ram." God said: "Has he done anything except for his son? If I were to say to him: 'Sacrifice him before Me,' he would not refuse." Perhaps the prosecution was that even though at the time of Isaac's announcement Abraham offered to the Unique Name through this meal, as I wrote, nevertheless, the beginning was through the intermediary of an angel. He should have "offered before You"—the word "before You" is precise—meaning to prioritize the Unique Name first without any intermediary, and only afterward to bring down the influence to the spiritual powers. This is as the Zohar writes (Parashat Vayikra) regarding the sacrifice: "I have gathered my myrrh with my spice <note>original: 'Ariti mori im besami'</note>... these are the high levels... myrrh and spice, this is the right arm, the angel Michael... I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey... I have drunk my wine with my milk, this is the left arm in the right hand... these are all high levels that the Holy King enjoys first, for this is His food and His pleasure. The food of the Supreme King is first, and from here onward He gives permission to the four directions of the Throne and all those who spread out from them to enjoy and eat," etc. See there at length. This was the content of Satan's prosecution: that in all the feasts he made for Isaac, he did not offer a sacrifice. And even in the feast made at the time of Isaac's announcement, which was *like* a sacrifice, he did not offer it "before You." Even though he offered to the Unique Name, it should have been "before You" without the intermediary of an angel. The Holy One, Blessed be He, answered him: "He has already offered before Me," for the matter of circumcision is a sacrifice—both the circumcision he performed on Isaac his son and the circumcision Abraham performed on himself. Thus he fulfilled "When a man brings an offering," for he offered himself. There is a hint of this in the portion *Lech Lecha*: "And Abram offered" was fulfilled later as "And Abraham offered himself." It is already known that circumcision is a sacrifice. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Satan in the same way that Isaac replied to Ishmael (who had boasted to Isaac that he did not resist being circumcised): "You boast to me about one limb? If the Holy One, Blessed be He, were to say to me, 'Sacrifice yourself,' I would do it." After these words, "God tested Abraham"—meaning after the words of Ishmael and after the words of Satan, for all these interpretations are true, and these and those are the words of the Living God, as will be explained.

And so, here at the meal, it was a "burnt offering without a meal offering," for they did not bring bread. Similarly, with Isaac, who became a "burnt offering" due to the prosecution that was missing here (as explained above), we do not find that there was a meal offering (<term>minchah</term>) there, only "a lamb for a burnt offering." And I found that the afternoon prayer is called <term>Minchah</term> more than any other prayer. Are not all prayers a "gift" (<term>minchah</term>) sent to God? Rather, Isaac said: "What is this? We have a burnt offering here but no meal offering of fine flour!" He stood and established a prayer that would take the place of the meal offering. Therefore, this is called:

# Tablets of the Covenant: Mother of All Living

Understand this in relation to the term "youth" <note>Hebrew: *na'ar*</note>. Rebecca, the insightful prophetess who knew matters through a spiritual lens, fulfilled the requests for Laban. As I have already written, although Laban was wicked, he was a great scholar. Therefore, the text does not refer to Eliezer simply as "the servant," but as "the man" <note>Hebrew: *ha-ish*</note>. This was because they held in their hearts that he was a person of distinction, and the Torah speaks in the language of how they perceived him. Yet, when they called Rebecca a "young woman" <note>Hebrew: *na'arah*</note>, she is referred to as such and not as a "maiden" <note>Hebrew: *almah*</note>. Note that it is written: *And they rode upon the camels and followed the man; and the servant took Rebecca and went.* This is because the "servant" was actually the high celestial messenger, Metatron <note>A powerful angel in Jewish mysticism often associated with the transition between the divine and physical realms</note>, who was present here until the mission was completed. Only then did he return to his place. The mission was not finished until they were established on the road. Thus, it says *And Rebecca arose* and *they followed the man*, but as soon as they were on their way, Metatron departed. Then it says, *and the servant took Rebecca and went.* It is possible that the word "went" refers to "the man" mentioned earlier, returning to his heavenly source. This is the meaning of the Midrash <note>Ancient rabbinic homilies</note> in Genesis Rabbah: *Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house—whose facial aura resembled his own—who ruled over all he had—meaning he mastered his physical impulses just as Abraham did.* Later, the Midrash says: *The servant said to him... Canaan has the scales of deceit in his hand to oppress.* <note>The Midrash contrasts the servant's high spiritual potential with his origins from the cursed line of Canaan</note>. This excellence of his "facial aura" came to him from the power of the glory of the Celestial Servant...

->...who was hovering over him.<-

**The general principle** of the matter is that the Patriarchs are the perfection of the world and the secret of its foundation. The world's purpose is for the sake of the "First Adam." Abraham is considered the "Great Adam," and Sarah is the "Mother of All Living." Isaac and Rebecca's facial features and the beauty of Jacob are reflections of the beauty of the first Adam. These three aspects—Mother, Sister, and Daughter—are hinted at in the verse: *A daughter of 100 is like a daughter of 20 for beauty, and a daughter of 20 is like a daughter of 7 for sin.* <note>A classic commentary on Sarah's age, implying she was as pure and beautiful at 100 as she was as a child</note>. This relates to the "Higher Mother" <note>Hebrew: *Imma Ila'ah*, a kabbalistic level of divine understanding</note>, the secret of the Light of the Seven Days of Creation that was hidden away. Afterward, it was hidden and grew dark, but at the time of the giving of the Torah, the "filth of the serpent" ceased, and the light returned to be as it was. This is hinted at in the word for "the Tabernacle," which equals the numerical value of "Light" twice <note>The Hebrew word *Mishkan* (Tabernacle) and *Or* (Light) are linked through Gematria/numerology</note>, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. This is also the aspect of the number 27 mentioned in the Zohar regarding the divine names. If they had not sinned with the Golden Calf, they would have been blessed with the Torah and reached the level of "Mother." The hidden light would have been revealed. But initially, the spiritual light was like the "Light of the Seven Days," categorized as "Sister," as in the verse: *Say to Wisdom, ‘You are my sister.’* When they sinned with the Golden Calf, they damaged this level, and the spiritual "building" was diminished. A partial repair was made with the building of the Temple, which was 100 cubits high. This is the "daughter of 100" who is like a "daughter of 20" regarding sin, for the sacrifices provided atonement. They were then in the category of the "Daughter of Zion" or "Daughter of Jerusalem." Eventually, the presence was further diminished until only a "spark" <note>Hebrew: *Labbah*</note> remained, like a "daughter." After the destruction of the Temple, the power descended even further, and they only had access to the "Divine Voice" <note>Hebrew: *Bat Kol*, literally "Daughter of a Voice"</note>. Now, due to our sins, we have neither, until our righteous Messiah comes and the light shines upon Zion. If you contemplate the secret of these things, the "Light of the Seven Days" has the same numerical value as "The giving of the Torah from Heaven." The building of the Temple relates to "Kingship" <note>Hebrew: *Malchut*</note>. There are three levels to Kingship, symbolized by three vowel points. When it is below, it is the "Daughter." When it rises to the level of "Beauty" <note>Hebrew: *Tiferet*</note>, it is the "Sister." When it becomes a crown for her husband, it is the "Mother." Then it will be as written: *Go out and see, daughters of Zion, the crown with which his mother crowned him.* May we merit this soon in our days, Amen.

## The Way of Life: Moral Instruction

<margin>
In the Midrash
**Tosefta** <note>An "addition" or supplement to the Zohar</note>
</margin>
The hidden parts of the Zohar hint in this Torah portion to the matter of the body and soul, the return to dust, and the time of the soul's return, and many moral lessons emerge from this.
**Tosefta:** Blessed is he who makes himself small in this world; how great and high he shall be in that world! The sages of the Academy said: He who is small is great, and he who is great is small. For it is written, *And the life of Sarah was... one hundred years...* <note>The Hebrew text breaks the numbers up strangely</note>. For "one hundred," which is a large number, it writes "year" (singular), for even a wicked person who lives long will have his life buried. But for "seven," a small number, it adds "years" (plural). We can also find a moral hint that a person should strive to increase in virtue every single day. When one grows older, they must increase their virtue even more. This is the concept of "Scholars": as they age, they add wisdom; whereas "Ignoramuses": as they age, they add foolishness. This might be the reason Laban and Bethuel are mentioned; Bethuel, being old and foolish, required Laban to answer for him. Regarding scholars, Sarah's last seventy years are referred to in the plural ("years") because in those years her wisdom increased the most. According to the Tosefta of the Zohar, which hints at the humility of making oneself small—which is certainly the great virtue of the penitent <note>Hebrew: *Ba'al Teshuvah*</note>—I say there is also a great hint in the word "And they were" <note>Hebrew: *Vayihiyu*</note> regarding repentance. Repentance is linked to the Hebrew letter *He*, which is open at the bottom and the side for penitents to enter. In the word *Vayihiyu*, the *He* is in the middle, with a *Yud* and *Vav* above it and a *Yud* below it. This hints at humility and accepting suffering with love. *Happy is the man whom You, God, discipline*—one who accepts suffering and lowliness in this world enters the opening of the letter *He* and is repaired. This is because he has the *Yud* (the divine) below in this world through suffering. But if he is arrogant in this world, he receives the *Vav* and *Yud* only above (in the next world), and the "opening" remains closed to him. Therefore, happy is the man who is humble in this world.

**And Abraham was old, advanced in days.** From this comes a great moral: a person must ensure that every single day of his life is filled with good and not evil. Then, there is a reality of "life" for that day. *The fear of the Lord adds days*—meaning every day has vitality because of the good deeds done in them. But *the years of the wicked shall be shortened*—meaning even if they live many years, they are considered dead because they did nothing good in them. Abraham was "old, advanced in days" because every day was filled with life. I have written extensively on this in *The Luminary* regarding moral instruction: that a person must repent every day and fix his actions.

**Who ruled over all he had.** This can be interpreted as referring to Abraham. Eliezer was a servant and the elder of the house of one who "ruled over all he had." The hint is this: if God grants someone great wealth but he is stingy and does not increase in charity and generosity, then certainly there are "husks" and "accusers" <note>Spiritual forces of negativity/clippot</note> dwelling on his wealth, preventing him from truly ruling over what is his. But Abraham was a great philanthropist and a master of charity; therefore, he truly ruled over all he had.

**For** a person should see to it that through God’s power he matches his sons or daughters with the best of people, as the Sages warned. One should learn from Abraham, who chose the righteous prophetess Rebecca, who came from a distinguished family of that time. Happy is the man who does this.

**And she hurried and emptied her jug into the trough and ran again to the well to draw.** Look and contemplate the wisdom of the character of Rebecca in how she practiced "honor for fellow creatures." Initially, Eliezer drank, and water remained in the jug. Rebecca did not know what to do: if she gave the remaining water to the camels, it would look as if she were equating the animal to the human by having them drink from the same vessel. If she poured the water out, it would be a slight to the honor of the man, as if the water he touched was now waste. Therefore, she "ran" to give them water, and through the speed of her running, she made it look as if the jug tipped over on its own and the water spilled out. Then she refilled it with fresh water. In this way, Eliezer's dignity was preserved.

**Genesis Rabbah:** Rabbi Yovin said: The Torah teaches you that if a person has adult sons, he should marry them off first, and afterward he should take a wife for himself. From whom do you learn this? From Abraham. First, *Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother*, and only afterward, *Abraham took another wife.*

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the mission to find a wife for Isaac, focusing on the character of Laban, the wisdom of Rebecca, and the mystical identity of Abraham’s servant, Eliezer. It bridges the literal narrative with Kabbalistic teachings regarding the angel Metatron and the spiritual significance of the gifts given to Rebecca.</meta>

# Tablets of the Covenant

When the man <note>Eliezer</note> entered the house of "fortune" <note>Laban’s home</note>, and received affection and fodder, Laban did not do this out of righteousness. This is why Laban jumped ahead of his father and said, "The matter stems from the Lord," for he was afraid there might be some delay, and he was hurrying for the sake of the money that had been promised. He seized upon the matter and said the deal was already concluded with "good luck and a good sign," and that there was nothing more for them to say. 

When the match was finalized, and Laban said, "Behold, Rebecca is before you; take her and go, and let her be a wife to your master's son, as the Lord has spoken," Eliezer’s heart relied even more on Divine Providence. He brought out silver and gold vessels and gave them to Rebecca, and to Laban he gave "sweetmeats" <note>Hebrew: *migdanot*</note> but not the silver and gold he had expected. Laban thought to himself: "It seems this man is enjoying himself; he gives me sweets but withholds the silver and gold he promised me." Therefore, he sought pretexts to delay the matter and said, "Let the young woman stay with us for a year or ten months..." 

What did Eliezer do? He held fast to his successful lot, seeing that the matter had already been decided—that "it came from the Lord" and she should be a wife to Isaac as the Lord had spoken. Regarding this, he said, "The Lord has made my way successful"—meaning the matter was already fully and perfectly completed. 

Rebecca was a woman of great wisdom; she understood all the deception and feared that Eliezer might be changed by Laban's trickery, or that he might fear him and give him a bribe. Therefore, she said, "I will go," even if her family did not want her to. Through this, she saved the "bribe" <note>the wealth</note>, for any money in the hand of the servant belongs to her and her heirs. Such were the ways of Laban. But Rebecca judged between the lower realms and saw that it was fitting to join Abraham’s house to perfect the world. 

Regarding the aforementioned idea—that the Patriarchs are the perfection of the world and the expansion of creation—Isaac represents the secret of the "Eye of the Knowledge of Good and Evil." As it is written, "for Isaac shall be a laughter <note>Hebrew: *metzachek*</note> to us," and Rebecca contains both good and evil <note>being the sister of Laban yet the wife of Isaac</note>. 

This brings us to the matter of the separation and the sending of the servant. There are several subtle points to examine here: 
1. Why does the servant mention his own praise, saying he is the "elder of the house" and "rules over all that he has"? 
2. It is difficult to understand why the text mostly refers to him as "the servant" <note>Hebrew: *eved*</note>, but then writes "And the **man** wondered at her," and "Laban ran to the **man**." It says, "The **man** spoke thus to me," and "he came to the **man**," but afterward he is called "servant" again. 

Though he called himself a servant to speak the truth of his status, the Torah also calls him "servant," as in "And it was when Abraham’s **servant** heard their words..." and "The **servant** brought out..." Yet later it says, "Will you go with this **man**?" Even more striking is one verse that mentions both names: "And they followed the **man**, and the **servant** took Rebecca." 

Furthermore, regarding the statement "Come, you blessed of the Lord," why is the servant called "blessed"? He was a descendant of Canaan <note>who was cursed</note>, which is why Abraham did not want to bond with his seed, saying "You are cursed and my son is blessed." How did he leave the category of "cursed" and enter the category of "blessed"? From where did Laban get the power to declare this? 

Additionally, we must understand the "House" and the "Parable." Laban held the servant in great and wondrous esteem; from where did he derive this? Also, in Eliezer's retelling, he says "I asked her... and I put the ring on her nose," whereas in the actual event, it implies he gave the ring and bracelets *before* he asked who she was. 

Our Sages said: "Any divination <note>Hebrew: *nichush*</note> that is not like that of Eliezer or Jonathan is not considered divination." The Tosafot <note>Medieval commentators</note> asked: if divination is forbidden even for Noahides <note>non-Jews</note>, how could they do this? They answered that Eliezer relied on a miracle. He did not actually give the rings first and then ask "Whose daughter are you?" as it seems in the first section; rather, he asked first and then gave the rings, as he says in the second section. 

However, even if he gave the rings after asking, he still relied on his "sign." If he didn't rely on the sign, even if he knew whose daughter she was, how could he be sure she would agree to marry Isaac? He certainly relied on the sign. 

The secret is that the <term>Metatron</term> <note>The highest-ranking angel who serves as the celestial scribe and guardian</note> of the world is called "Youth" <note>Hebrew: *na'ar*</note>. As the verse says, "I was a youth and now I am old" (Psalm 37:25)—the Sages say the "Prince of the World" <note>Metatron</note> said this. He is the youth who serves above, as the Kabbalists write. They gave a sign for this: "Educate the youth <note>Hebrew: *na'ar*</note>," for he is the Guardian of the Gate. 

The matter is that **Enoch** is Metatron. The Tosafot questioned the statement that the Prince of the World spoke during the creation, while Enoch lived long after creation. But according to those who enter the "Secret of the Lord," this is no contradiction. The Prince of the World has existed since creation and is called Metatron because he is the "Guardian" <note>Hebrew: *shomer*</note>. The word for "ruler" <note>Hebrew: *moshel*</note> is a translation of "guardian." Enoch became Metatron and was absorbed into him. 

This is the lower aspect of Metatron called the "Shoe" <note>Hebrew: *min'al*</note>. Metatron and Sandalfon <note>another high angel</note> are the secret of the "Shoe and Sandal," as in "How beautiful are your steps in sandals." This is the secret of the Midrash saying that "Enoch was a cobbler." I have explained this elsewhere at length. 

Metatron is the Guardian of Israel and the messenger of the upper realms. Rabbi Bahya <note>13th-century commentator</note> wrote in the portion *Mishpatim*: He is called Metatron because in the Greek language <note>actually likely Latin *metator*</note> the name implies a "guide of the way" or a "messenger of the master." It can also mean "guarding," as the translation of "watch" <note>Hebrew: *mishmeret*</note> is *matrat*. He is the "Guardian of Israel." From his name, we understand he is master over all beneath him; the entire heavenly host is under his hand. He is the messenger for the One above him, who gave him dominion over all. He is called "Master of the Youths" and "Ruler over all his possessions." 

He is called "servant" <note>Hebrew: *eved*</note>, as explained in the *Zohar* and the *Pardes*. There is a distinction: "You are children to the Lord your God" refers to the world of *Atzilut* <note>Emanation</note>, while Metatron represents the aspect of "servitude." Thus, Metatron is the "servant and elder of the house who rules over all that is above" by the will of the Creator. Regarding him, it is said, "Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way." It says later, "for My Name is within him," which Rashi explains means his name <note>Metatron</note> has the same numerical value as the name of his Master <note>Shaddai = 314</note>. 

The matter here is that Abraham sent a "servant and elder who rules over all he has" below, and there was sent with him the "servant and elder who rules over all that is above." Regarding this, Abraham said, "He will send His angel before you." I am sending my angel below—meaning you, Eliezer, who are a "Hebrew servant." Even though he was a Canaanite, he was a servant to a Hebrew, for Abraham was called "the Hebrew." And God sent His angel, who is also called "servant and elder of the house" above. 

When the text uses the term "servant," it hints at the servant below <note>Eliezer</note>. When it uses the term "the man," it hints at the glory of the celestial servant <note>the angel/Metatron</note> through whom one clings to holiness. An angel is called "man," as in "the **man** Gabriel." 

Thus, it is written: "The **servant** ran toward her," but then, "And the **man** wondered at her." The running refers to the servant below, while "the man" stood and contemplated, receiving influence from above, "to know if the Lord had made his way successful." The word "to know" <note>Hebrew: *la-da'at*</note> refers to the secret of the "Eye of Knowledge." The success of the way hints at Jacob and Esau—one successful and one not. It is known that the root of the "Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil" is on the side of Metatron. As it says in the *Tikunim*: "The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil is below; the Good is Metatron, and the Evil is Samael." 

From the perspective of the angel, there was the knowledge that the way was successful and she was the intended match. He saw that the gifts of the ring and bracelets should be given. Thus it says, "The **man** took a golden ring of a half-shekel weight and two bracelets." From the perspective of "the man" <note>the angel</note>, they were ready to be given, as if they were already given (in the way of prophecy). But below, in action, the servant did not put them on her until after the question. Therefore, it does not say here "he put them on her hands," as it does in the servant's later retelling: "I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands." In actual physical reality, they were only placed after the question. 

Once the servant below asked "Whose daughter are you?" the Holy Spirit rested upon him through the celestial pillar hovering over him. He then placed the ring and bracelets, relying on the Holy Spirit and not on divination. Because of this spiritual connection, he bowed and prostrated himself, and he is called "the man," as in "And the **man** bowed his head." 

This explains why, in the physical act, the weights are mentioned: "a half-shekel <note>Hebrew: *beka*</note> weight" and "ten gold shekels weight." In the retelling, the weights are omitted. In the act itself, "the man" <note>the spiritual aspect</note> hints at spiritual matters. As Rashi says, the *Beka* hints at the half-shekel <note>given by Israel in the desert</note>, and the "ten gold" hints at the Ten Commandments. The retelling, however, is the story of the physical servant below. 

Rebecca, in her prophetic intellect, recognized the matter and perceived the celestial messenger through "the man," which hints at the Great Name of Gevurah <note>Strength/Judgment</note>.

### Tablets of the Covenant

The upper systems and the soul require a person to bless one hundred blessings <note>The Jewish practice of reciting 100 blessings daily (*Me'ah Berakhot*)</note> daily, and this corresponds to the level of **Israel**. From these one hundred blessings, ten are reached which are the "tithe" for the Spirit, which corresponds to the level of **Levite**. And from the ten of the Levite-Spirit, one is given to the Soul-of-the-Soul, which corresponds to the level of **Priest** (*Kohen*). If this is so, it is found that if a person’s soul does not recite one hundred blessings every day, one blessing will not reach the highest soul, since ten blessings did not reach the Spirit—which is the secret of the Levites who take a tithe from Israel and then give one-tenth of what they took to the Priest. This is the secret of the Torah portion regarding the tithes of the Levites, Priests, and Israelites. Therefore, the Torah says: *“Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you take from the Israelites the tithe which I have given you from them as your inheritance, you shall set aside from it a gift for the Lord, a tithe of the tithe.”* The secret of "a tithe of the tithe" is the secret of the letters *Koph* <note>numerical value 100</note>, *Yod* <note>value 10</note>, and *Aleph* <note>value 1</note>; for if there is no 100, there is no 10, and if there is no 10, there is no 1. Therefore, a person must be careful to bless one hundred blessings, and if, God forbid, even one is missing, he causes a spiritual blemish. These one hundred blessings are like the "one hundred silver sockets" <note>original: *Adne HaKesef*; used in the construction of the Tabernacle</note> through which the flow of the Master of the World <note>original: *ADNY*</note> spreads to every side into "one hundred pools" <note>a play on the word *Berakhot* (blessings) and *Berekhot* (pools)</note>. Thus far are the words of the sage.

<margin>
Regarding the start of the Torah with the letter *Bet* <note>the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>: It is asked why it does not start with *Aleph* <note>the first letter</note>. According to the secret meaning, the letter *Bet* represents "Blessing" (*Berakha*). Even though the *Aleph* has its own high qualities, it also signifies "Cursing" (*Arira*). Therefore, the world began with a *Bet* so as not to give an "opening of the mouth" to the Accusers of the world to claim the world cannot stand because it was created with a language of curse. Rather, the Holy One said, "I create it with a language of blessing, and if only it may stand!"
</margin>

**And now** I will explain more clearly the matter of the blessing and the matter of the Priest, Levite, and Israelite. It is known that the "three faces of the Chariot" <note>mystical vision of Ezekiel</note> correspond to Kindness (*Chesed*), Strength (*Gevurah*), and Beauty (*Tiferet*), which are the secret of the Patriarchs: "Kindness to Abraham," "Fear to Isaac," and "Truth to Jacob." For Jacob is the "complete man" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>—the letter *Mem* <note>at the end of the word *Tam* (complete)</note> is sealed with the "complete ones"—he is the "dweller of tents" between Abraham and Isaac, deciding between them and completing them. I have already lengthily explained earlier in the portion of *Chayei Sarah* that the Patriarchs are the perfection of the world, for the world was created with Kindness, as it is written, "The world shall be built with kindness." In His kindness and goodness, the Creator desired to bring forth creatures who would recognize His divinity. However, even though it was created with Kindness, the "First Thought" was to lead it with the Attribute of Judgment, to give to each man according to his ways and the fruits of his deeds according to the line of law, whether good or bad—this is the attribute of Isaac. But since the world cannot endure on judgment alone, He combined the Attribute of Mercy with the Attribute of Judgment—this is the attribute of Jacob, who is comprised of both.

Therefore, the Patriarchs are the secret of Creation. This creation was done through "Blessing," as found in the Midrash <note>*Bereshit Rabbah* 1:10</note>: Why was the world created with the letter *Bet*? To let you know there are two worlds (*Bet* = 2): this world and the World to Come. Another explanation: Why with *Bet*? Because it is the language of Blessing (*Berakha*). And why not with *Aleph*? Because it is the language of Cursing (*Arira*). The Holy One said, "I create it with a language of blessing, and if only it may stand!" Thus, the world was created with blessing, and the foundation of the world is the Patriarchs. As it is said: "The source of blessings was handed over to the Patriarchs." God said to Abraham, "And you shall be a blessing"—the blessings are handed over to your hand. After Abraham, Isaac inherited them, as it says, "And it was after the death of Abraham that God blessed Isaac his son." Over this blessing, Jacob and Esau struggled, and Jacob inherited it and was blessed, meriting the blessing of Isaac. 

The summary of the matter is that the Patriarchs are the perfection of the world, which was created with blessing, and they are the root of the Priest, Levite, and Israelite, which is the secret of the tithe and the offering. This secret of the tithe—which is the number ten—spreads into three "good gifts" given to Israel: the Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. The entire Torah is rooted in the Ten Commandments, which are the source for all 613 commandments. The commandment "I am the Lord your God" is the tenth from the bottom up, the head and the source, the holy root that includes everything. 

Regarding the Land of Israel, there are "Ten Sanctities," as taught in the Mishnah <note>Tractate Keilim, Chapter 1</note>: The Land of Israel is holier than all lands... walled cities are even holier... the Temple Mount... the Women’s Courtyard... the Israelite Courtyard... the Priests' Courtyard... until the tenth, which is the Holy of Holies. 

These three gifts correspond to the three Patriarchs:
1. **Torah** is from the Torah of Abraham our father, as it says: "Two thousand years of Torah began from 'the souls they made in Haran.'"
2. **The Land of Israel** is for Isaac, for he was told not to leave the Land for foreign soil.
3. This explains the matter of the **digging of the wells** mentioned in the text. One might ask: It was written just before this that "the Lord blessed him," so why did he face such strife with the wells?

Regarding the first and third wells, the Torah gives the reason for their names: "He called its name *Esek* <note>Contention</note> because they contended with him," and the third, "*Rechovot* <note>Wide Spaces</note>, for now the Lord has made room for us." But for the middle well, it does not state the reason so clearly. The matter is that after Isaac was sanctified with the holiness of the Land, these wells became hints to the history of the Holy Temple. As Nachmanides <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman / Ramban</note> explained: "The well of living water" refers to the House of God which the children of Isaac would build. 
*   The first well, **Esek** <note>Contention</note>, refers to the **First Temple**, during which nations contended with us and waged wars until they destroyed it. 
*   The second well, **Sitnah** <note>Enmity/Hate</note>, is a harsher name than the first; it refers to the **Second Temple**, for it is written that during the beginning of the reign of Ahasuerus, they "wrote an accusation" (*Sitnah*) against the inhabitants of Judah. Throughout its days, the enemies acted as an adversary (*Satan*) until they destroyed it and we went into a bitter exile. 
*   The third well is **Rechovot**, which refers to the **Future Temple** that will be built speedily in our days. It will be built without strife or quarrel, and God will expand our borders, as it says, "And if the Lord expands your border." In the Third House, it is written "it was broader and wound higher and higher." Then we shall be fruitful in the land, and all nations will serve Him with one accord. Thus, all questions are answered, for the wells are great prophetic signs of the Sanctuaries.

<margin>
Regarding the verse "And the man became great..." <note>Genesis 26:13</note>, our Sages said that people would say: "The dung of Isaac's mules is better than the silver and gold of Abimelech." This is because God prepares the healing before the blow.
</margin>

**Behold**, the destruction of the Second Temple followed from the spiritual lack in the First Temple. Our Sages said that five things were missing in the Second Temple <note>including the Ark and the Divine Fire</note>. Therefore, the "Contention" (*Esek*) remained until the Third House is built, when "the Lord will make room for us." The word "Now" (*Atah*) is added to hint that at any time, the matter is in our hands—just as the Messiah answered "Today!"—meaning, "Today, if you will listen to His voice."

Finally, I will explain the verse "until he became very great." Our Sages explained that people said the "dung of Isaac’s mules" was worth more than Abimelech's gold. How is this possible? It means that even the waste of a holy person is more valuable than the core of a worldly king. There was also a mockery in that generation that Sarah had been impregnated by Abimelech. Therefore, God made Isaac’s facial features exactly like Abraham’s, so everyone would have to admit "Abraham fathered Isaac." Isaac was sanctified in his father's holiness and blessed within the Land of Israel, and he was forbidden from leaving its holiness. This is what the Holy One showed to the world.
