<meta>This page continues a Kabbalistic and Midrashic analysis of the names of the Patriarchs—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and their mystical connection to the name "Israel" and the lineage of King David. It builds on previous discussions regarding the "husks" (shells of impurity) that emerged from the holy lineage.</meta>

<margin>
As we hinted, the name "Jacob" (Ya’akov) contains the word "heel" (Akev) in all its forms. Jacob had the power to encompass everything, for even in the poverty of the Accuser <note>The Hebrew abbreviation S"M refers to Samael, the primary accusatory angel in Kabbalah.</note> there is a spark of good—the "serpent on the shore." To all of them, he is called the "Intellectual Spread" <note>original: Peras Sasun</note>.
</margin>

# The Written Torah

The son of Abraham, and Abraham and Jacob, were both called by the name "Israel," as it is written: "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel." This is explained through shorthand and textual divisions, for the "heel" (Akev) follows everything to its side, yet "Jacob" had the power to become "Israel." Isaac was also called by the name "Israel" <note>The author is citing a tradition that all three Patriarchs share the title of Israel in a spiritual sense.</note> in the land of Canaan and in the land of Gerar <note>original: Gershon</note> for four hundred and thirty years; thus far the quote.
Regarding Jacob: Abraham was called Israel. Rabbi Nathan said this is a "deep matter," and it is cited in the *Zohar* within the *Tikkunim*.
They dwelt in Egypt, the land of Canaan, and the land of Gerar for four hundred and thirty years; thus far the quote.

Now, one must ask: why is it necessary to mention that Abraham was called Abraham and Jacob was called Israel? This is already explicitly clear in the Torah! Furthermore, since the Patriarchs are included within their own names, why wasn't Jacob called "Abraham," or Isaac called "Abraham," and why wasn't Abraham called "Isaac"? Additionally, why did the author bring the verse from the beginning of the Book of Exodus to prove Isaac was called Israel? He should have brought the verse from the portion of *Vayigash*, where it is written: "And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt, Jacob and his sons..." There, it is much clearer that Isaac is called "Israel" than in the verse at the beginning of Exodus which mentions "with Jacob." Finally, what did Rabbi Nathan mean by calling this a "deep matter"? What "depth" is there in stating something already known?

I have already written in the portion of *Chayei Sarah* regarding the concept of "All, from All, with All" <note>A reference to the blessings given to the three Patriarchs: Bakol, Mikol, Kol.</note>. From Abraham emerged the "husk" <term>Klipah: literally a "shell" or "peel," referring to the external forces of evil that conceal holiness</term> of Ishmael, and his grandson was Esau. From Isaac emerged the husk of Esau. The emergence of these husks from the Holy Patriarchs is like the peel that forms before the fruit; the fruit cannot exist without the prior formation of the peel, which is the bud and the flower. Jacob is the "fruit" itself. However, there is a secret in this matter: the husk has a hold on the side of holiness, ten against ten. Rebecca was in holiness, while the impurity was in its expansion.
In the future, the husk will return and be purified through the holy righteous ones who subdue it, following the secret of "Remember the Sabbath day." I have explained in several places that the goal is not to kill the "Evil Inclination" <term>Yezer Hara: the internal drive toward selfishness or sin</term>, but rather to conquer it, place it under oneself, and purify it. One takes the attributes of the Evil Inclination and uses them for the service of the Creator—for example, using "jealousy" as "the jealousy of scribes" (which increases wisdom) or "desire" to desire the "Hidden Treasure" (Torah), and many similar things.
This is what the sages meant when they said to the Patriarch, "You are a prince among us." They meant: "In our innermost parts—that is, in our roots—you are a prince, and through you, we will be purified in the future." All the nations admitted this, as our Rabbis of blessed memory said, "It was a deep thing," for they all agreed and made Abraham king over them. This is the aspect of the husks emerging from Abraham.

But Abraham himself is the essence of the "Brain of the Intellect," which is "Israel." His merit is higher than the other Patriarchs. The matter of the name "Israel" is more hidden... and the name "Abraham" refers to being the "father of a multitude" <note>Abraham's name is interpreted as "Av Hamon Goyim," Father of a Multitude of Nations.</note> of nations. This is the meaning of "You are a prince among us," for they are attached to their root.
Behold, Abram was called Abraham because Ishmael emerged from him while his name was still "Abram." This "H" <note>The Hebrew letter 'He' added to Abram's name.</note> is the entire secret of "Father of a multitude." While he was Abram, he was only added to the mundane.
Regarding Isaac, from whom emerged Esau who encompasses all the husks: notice that in this current exile, we are called by the name "Edom" (Rome/Esau), even though there are three other great kingdoms, including Ishmael and many others. They are all included under the name "Exile of Edom." Nachmanides <note>Ramban</note> elaborated on this in the portion of *Balak*. Thus it is explained: Abraham is called Abraham, and Isaac is called Abraham because from him came Esau who encompasses all the husks; therefore, Isaac is also a "father of a multitude."
But for Jacob, that name is not appropriate. And Abraham and Jacob were not called "Isaac" because there was no reason for them to be called by that name.
Jacob was called "Israel" to teach us that you should not think the name "Jacob" indicates the secret of "evil" coming through "deceit" <note>A play on the Hebrew words 'Ya'akov' (Jacob) and 'Akbah' (deception/heel).</note> and trickery to push the cursed Esau off his back and take the blessing. Rather, the name "Israel" indicates "doing good"—that is, his cleaving to the Supernal realms. Conversely, the name Jacob was never uprooted even when he was called Israel. For in Jacob's inner essence, there is also a hint to "the day to do them," as written: "Because (Ekev) Abraham listened..."
The letters of "Jacob" (Y-A-K-B) hint at "cleaving." In its simple sense, the Evil Inclination descends and misleads, then ascends and accuses, but one should pull it into the House of Study. This is the "grasping of Esau's heel." The letter *Yod* (at the start of Jacob) is as I mentioned above. It also hints at the letters of Esau, for he conquers his inclination under him. As mentioned, Esau "covets good money," but Jacob conquers it under him... Jacob conquers the "Ruddy One" <note>Admoni, a nickname for Esau</note> under him.
From Jacob emerges a "holy and pure Ruddy One," which is King David, who is called "Ruddy, with beautiful eyes and goodly to look at." Esau is ruddy from the side of evil, but David is "Ruddy with beautiful eyes" from the side of good. Therefore, from him came Perez <note>ancestor of David</note>, the "breaker of fences," whose neighbor is the serpent. The serpent is the power of Esau. Rabbi Menachem Azariah <note>The Rama"z</note> interprets "Israel" (Y-S-R-L) accordingly. When King Saul sinned, he was attacked by Nahash the Ammonite, but King David—the Messiah—is "one who bites and guards like a serpent." About him it is written: "For from the root of the snake shall come a viper." This is why Jacob gave his son Joseph's years to King David, as explained in the *Zohar* (Portion *Vayishlach*). The seventy years of David's life were those missing from the Patriarchs.

**The Zohar states:**
Rabbi Shimon said: It is taught that David had no life of his own at all. But Adam the First Man gave him seventy years of his own. Thus was the existence of King David—seventy years. The life of Adam was meant to be a thousand years, but it was minus seventy. Thus, within those first thousand years, we find Adam and King David. He opened and said: "He asked life of You, and You gave it to him, length of days forever and ever." "He asked life of You"—this is King David. For when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the Garden of Eden, He placed the soul of King David there. He looked at it and saw it had no life of its own at all. It stood before Him every day. When Adam was created, he said, "This soul is worthy of existence," and from Adam came the seventy years that David lived in the world. Furthermore, the Patriarchs left him life from their own years—each one blessed him. So too did Isaac and Joseph. Isaac left him nothing because David comes from the "side of Isaac." Abraham left him five years, for he was meant to live 180 years but lived 175. Jacob was meant to live as long as Abraham but lived only 147 years, missing 28 years. We find that Abraham and Jacob together left him 33 years. Joseph, who lived 110 years, was meant to live 147 years like Jacob, but he was short 37 years. These are the seventy years that they left for King David to exist. Through these years, David existed, and no more.
Now, why did Isaac not leave him anything like the others? Because Isaac is "darkness" <note>In Kabbalah, Isaac represents Gevurah/Judgment, often associated with restricted light or "darkness."</note>, and David comes from the side of darkness. One who is in darkness has nothing; he has no life. Therefore, David had no life of his own. But those who had "light" shone it upon King David, and their life was needed to illuminate and purify him. Life that comes from the side of darkness has no life at all. On this account, Isaac did not enter the calculation.
If you ask about Joseph—why did he give? Certainly, Joseph is in his light like all of them because he is called "the Righteous" (Tzadik), and he is the one who illuminates the Moon <note>The Moon represents the Shekhinah or the Davidic Kingdom</note> more than all of them. Therefore, he left for King David more than anyone else, as it is written: "And God placed them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth." Thus far the quote from the *Zohar*.

Thus, Jacob rectified the "Ruddy One," as did Joseph, who is the adversary of Esau. And what the Sages said—that Adam gave seventy years to David—is all true. For the ultimate goal is the rectification of "Adam," who encompasses the whole world and was made in the image of God. Adam was rectified through the Patriarchs, as I explained in the discourse on *Chayei Sarah*. That is, the seventy years of Adam were rectified and illuminated by the seventy years of Jacob and Joseph. For the beauty of Jacob was a reflection of the beauty of Adam, and the beauty of Joseph was from the beauty of his father. So too, David was "beautiful of eyes and goodly to look at." When the Messiah comes, Adam will be completely rectified through the secret of A-D-M: Adam, David, Messiah.
Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Whoever does not bow at *Modim* <note>The 'Thanksgiving' blessing in the Amidah prayer.</note>, his spine becomes a serpent after seventy years." Bowing represents choice. The word "Choice" <note>Hiru-kh</note> is related to "Serpent" <note>Nahash</note>. One who does not bow at *Modim* is the opposite of David, whose entire essence was praise and thanks to God (as seen in the wisdom of Psalms). If one does not follow David's rectification, which lasted seventy years, his spine becomes a serpent after seventy years.
It is known that Jacob represents the secret of the spinal cord <note>The central pillar/Tiferet</note>. One who does not bow turns into a serpent. The matter of the "Seventy" refers to the level and seed of Jacob, corresponding to the Seventy Supernal Princes. With seventy souls, Jacob descended to Egypt to undergo refinement and purification in the "iron furnace." These seventy princes are thirty-five on the right and thirty-five on the left, as the Kabbalists have written. Corresponding to them in Israel are the seventy elders of the Sanhedrin. Their impurity is transformed through the side of holiness; therefore, "you shall not turn aside..." even if they tell you right is left or left is right. The twenty-four authorized judges are called "Elohim" (God/Powers).
The concept of "Ordination" <note>Semikhah</note> is the reception of influence from one to another, reaching back to Elijah the Prophet, may his name be blessed. This is the secret of those "connected" to one another up to the House of Study <note>B-Y-T</note>, as it is written: "And you who cleave to the Lord."
These seventy princes are called "other gods" (Elohim Aherim) because they are the gods of the seventy nations. Jacob's power is "contending with God" (Elohim). From the seventy princes come the "garments of skin" (Or) from the Tree of Knowledge, but above them shines the inner light of holiness—the "garments of light" (Ohr). This was a wondrous choice for the seventy members of the Sanhedrin. The head of the Sanhedrin corresponds to the "contending with God" which equals eighty in numerical value. There are two names that are "connected"... it was for the sake of Adam. Seventy is the value of "Hand of the Lord" (Yad Y-H-W-H) in its full spelling. The name of 42 letters equals 80...
Jacob is called "Israel" because the name Jacob in its inner essence indicates the matter of "Israel." However, the name "Israel" is a much higher elevation than the levels of the other Patriarchs; they are hidden within it. This name was only revealed in Jacob because from him emerged a "complete nation," which were the People of Israel. You will find a wondrous thing in the words...

<meta>This page continues the kabbalistic analysis of Jacob’s dream of the ladder, connecting the structure of the ladder to the giving of the Torah at Sinai, the Hebrew alphabet, and the architectural elements of the Temple.</meta>

## Gate of Heaven: The Written Torah

"Formation" and "Creation"—world and formation—descend in their value. Behold, the Name of God <note>original: "יו"ד ה' ו' ה'" (Y-H-V-H)</note> stands over it. The World of Emanation <term>Atzilut: the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah, representing pure divine light</term> is hinted at in the Name: the letter *Yod* represents Wisdom (*Chokhmah*), *He* represents Understanding (*Binah*), *Vav* represents Beauty (*Tiferet*) including the six extremities, and the final *He* represents Kingdom (*Malkhut*). All the chain of existence followed this order, and the Torah followed as is known. Therefore, the vision of the ladder relates to the standing at Mount Sinai and the giving of the Torah, as stated in Genesis Rabbah: "The Rabbis interpret the ladder as Sinai." "And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder"—this is Sinai; "set on the ground"—and they stood at the foot of the mountain; "and its top reached to the heavens"—and Sinai trembled in fire until the heart of the heavens. The four letters of the word "Ladder" <note>original: סלמה (S-L-M-H)</note> equal 130 in numerical value <term>Gematria: the system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters</term>, which is the same as the value of "Sinai." "And behold, the angels of God"—these are Moses and Aaron. From where do we know that prophets are called angels? As it says, "Then Haggai, the angel of the Lord, spoke." "Ascending"—this is Moses who "ascended to God"; "and descending"—this is Moses who "descended from the mountain." "And behold, the Lord stood over him"—and the Lord "descended upon Mount Sinai to the top of the mountain."

One must consider the difference between this interpretation and the first one. They did not explain in the first way what the "angels of God ascending and descending" meant. It seems that according to the first way, which hinted at "standing at the foot of the mountain" and "its top reaching heaven," the concept of angels ascending and descending was also hinted at. The intention is that the angels of God are the righteous; they are the messengers of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who perform His word and fulfill the commandments of the Torah. They are stationed below on the earth, but their "head" reaches the heavens, for the awakening caused by their actions travels from below to above. This creates an awakening above, and then the divine flow <term>Shefa: divine abundance or influence flowing from the higher worlds to the lower ones</term> descends from above to below. This is why it begins with "ascending" and afterwards "descending."

When it says "and behold, the Lord stood over him," it hints that everything lives only through God. Even though things depend on choosing the good, nevertheless, "one who comes to purify himself is assisted." This explains a puzzling statement in Genesis Rabbah on this portion: "He encountered the place <note>Genesis 28:11</note>." Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Ammi: "Why do we use a nickname for the Holy One, Blessed be He, and call Him 'The Place' (*HaMakom*)? Because He is the place of the world, but the world is not His place." Rabbi Isaac said: "It is written, 'The eternal God is a dwelling place' <note>Deuteronomy 33:27</note>. We do not know if the Holy One is the dwelling place of the world or if the world is His dwelling place, until it says, 'Lord, You have been a dwelling place for us' <note>Psalms 90:1</note>. Thus, the Holy One is the dwelling place of His world, and His world is not His dwelling place." Rabbi Abba bar Yudan said: "This is like a hero riding a horse with his gear draped on either side; the horse is secondary to the rider, and the rider is not secondary to the horse, as it says, 'You ride upon Your horses' <note>Habakkuk 3:15</note>."

This is difficult: why did the Midrash say "we do not know," etc.? How could one even think to say that the world is His place, Heaven forbid? Therefore, why did it teach two verses on the same subject? The first: "Behold, there is a place with Me," and the second: "Lord, You have been a dwelling place." This all relates to the concept of "The Place." The intention lies in the secret of "garbing," which occurs with angels, as explained by Nahmanides and the earlier commentators at the beginning of the portion *Vayeira*. When angels are mentioned as "men," it refers to a form created for the angels, which is the secret of the "garment" visible to eyes of flesh. It follows that when an angel is "clothed" in a form, the physical world becomes his place.

But regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, who appears to prophets according to their capacity—appearing at the Sea as a "hero of war" and at the giving of the Torah as an "elder full of mercy"—this is a sign within His heavenly host. But for Him, Blessed be He and Blessed be His Name, it is inappropriate to say He "clothes" Himself in the way we say of angels. He is always the place of the world, and the world is not His place, because He who is "clothed" does not become restricted to a place even through garbing. The matter is that for the Divine Presence to dwell among the lower beings, it requires, as it were, preparation. Human service <note>referring to prayer and commandments</note> is a "higher form," as explained at length in its proper place. Through the power of the good deeds of those below, a rectification and unification is made above. Then, when the Name is blessed, the lower beings are blessed. In this respect, it is almost possible to say the world is His dwelling, because the actions of those below cause "peace in the upper house." Regarding this, it says, "Lord, You are the dwelling place." Truly, the lower beings cause the service of the "higher form," but it is done with Divine help, for as soon as they come to purify themselves, they are assisted. He brought the parable of a hero riding a horse: it is not that the hero *needs* the horse to run, Heaven forbid, yet the horse is secondary to the rider.

This is hinted at here by "ascending and descending": ascending from below to above, and afterwards the flow descends from above to below. Nevertheless, "the Lord stood over him" to help him. The matter of "ascending and descending" is the same concept as "set on the ground and its top reaches the heavens."

<margin>And this is the secret of "He encountered the place" <note>Genesis 28:11</note> which equals "Ladder" in gematria <note>The Hebrew phrase 'Vayifga BaMakom' equals 433, while 'Sullam' (ladder) equals 130. The note likely refers to a different calculation or a symbolic connection</note>. For just as Jacob saw the ladder from below, so He stands over us to help us.</margin>

**Behold**, in the first interpretation of the ladder—hinting at the Torah—you should explain it according to the performance of the commandments of the Torah. For action affects the higher realms, as they said: "Service is a higher need." The "other thing" <note>alternative interpretation</note> regarding the ladder hinting at the Torah refers to the *study* of the Torah. The chain of descents and the stages of Moses's ascents hint at the depth of comprehension. For the term "ascent" refers to the beginning of comprehension, as it is said in several places, "it ascended in his thought" or "it ascended in his mind." And the term "descent" is used for the depth of comprehension, as it says, "So-and-so descended to the depths of his mind." Therefore, they first "ascend" and then "descend," as is clear to those who understand.

Also mentioned here is the center of the world, which is the Holy Temple, as explained in Genesis Rabbah: "Behold, this ladder is the ramp; 'set on the ground' is the Altar, as it says 'An altar of earth you shall make for Me'; 'and its top reaches the heavens' refers to the sacrifices whose aroma rises to heaven; 'and behold, the angels of God' are the High Priests; 'ascending and descending' on the ramp; 'and behold, the Lord stood over him'—I saw the Lord standing over the Altar."

Finally, it hints at the building of the Temple, its destruction, and its future rebuilding, as will be explained later. It further hints that all these matters belong to Jacob and his children, the Jewish nation; they are the purpose of the world, and to them the Torah and the Temple were given. The power and action of the root of Jacob's seed—the Holy Patriarchs—will be explained. The Patriarchs and all of Jacob's seed turn toward the portion of the World to Come. In a general way, this is hinted at in the word "And he lay down" <note>Genesis 28:11, "Vayishkav"</note> in that place. The word "Vayishkav" contains the letters *Y-S* <note>numerical value 310</note>, hinting at the World to Come, as it is written, "to bequeath to those who love Me *Yesh* <note>Substance/310</note>," for in the future every righteous person will inherit 310 worlds, as our Sages said.

This belongs to the Jewish nation, which is hinted at in the number 22, representing the 22 letters of the Torah. In the *Book of Formation* <term>Sefer Yetzirah: an ancient mystical text on cosmogony and the Hebrew alphabet</term>, it elaborates extensively on the 22 letters of the Torah, dividing them into three groups:
1. Three "Mother" letters: *Aleph, Mem, Shin* (A-M-S). He explained they are the foundations of all letters and represent the three elements: Air, Water, and Fire.
2. Seven "Double" letters: those that receive a dagesh (hard sound) or rafe (soft sound), which are the letters *Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaph, Pe, Tav* <note>B-G-D K-P-T</note>.
3. Twelve "Simple" letters: *He, Vav, Zayin, Chet, Tet, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samekh, Ayin, Tzadi, Qof*.

You find these three categories in the world: the three elements; the seven wandering stars <note>planets known in antiquity</note>; and the twelve signs of the Zodiac. All of this cascaded down from higher and higher levels until you find these matters in the World of Emanation (*Atzilut*). Namely, the first three Sephirot are the "Foundation of Foundations," the root of the three columns: the Column of Kindness, the Column of Judgment, and the Column of Mercy. Then the seven Sephirot of the "Building": Kindness, Strength, Beauty, Victory, Splendor, Foundation, and Kingdom. Then the twelve permutations of the Name of God <note>Y-H-V-H</note> that spread out from Beauty (*Tiferet*).

The Jewish nation is likewise established on three foundations upon which all Israel leans: the Patriarchs—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—who correspond to Fire, Spirit, and Water. Corresponding to the seven "Double" letters are seven levels based on their specific matters, seven gates, each according to its level. These are, in order: Israelite, Levite, Priest, Commoner, High Priest, Head of the Court, Prince, and King. Truly, these levels are founded upon Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who were the foundations for all these seven levels into which all Israel is divided. And the twelve "Simple" letters are the twelve Tribes of Israel, who lead these seven gates we mentioned. Within these twelve, these seven levels revolve. The structure of Israel was perfected in three divisions following the order of the 22 letters of the Torah, which were hinted at in the vision of the ladder.

So too, the Tabernacle hinted at in the vision of the ladder is also divided into three parts according to the 22 letters. Corresponding to the three "Mothers" is the verse: "And this is the offering you shall take from them: gold, silver, and copper." Gold belongs to the world above, copper to the world below, and silver mediates between them. Corresponding to the seven is the seven branches of the Menorah, which shines like the seven planets. Corresponding to the twelve are the twelve stones of remembrance on the Breastplate (*Choshen*). All this is for Israel, who are in the secret of the letters *Vav* and *Vav*. This is why there are 310 worlds to "bequeath to those who love Me *Yesh*." The word "And he lay down" (*Vayishkav*) is read as *Vayeish-Kav* <note>And there is 22</note>.

Regarding this, the hint "A star shall step forth from Jacob" applies. In the Zohar, it says 20 and 20, or 26, hinting at My Name <note>Y-H-V-H = 26</note> and the hand (*Yad* = 14) which contains 12 permutations... they emerge from Beauty (*Tiferet*), the attribute of Jacob. Afterwards, with his "perfect bed," the 22 was completed—the Patriarchs and the sons. This indicates perfection, namely the twelve tribes hinted at here. For now he went to find a mate and establish the twelve tribes; therefore they are hinted at here. In Genesis Rabbah: "He took from the stones of the place"—he took twelve stones. He said: "If these twelve stones merge into one another, I know that I will establish twelve tribes." Once they merged, he knew he would establish twelve tribes. Behold, the letters of the Torah are synthesized in the term "stones," as taught in the *Book of Formation*: "Two stones build two houses, three build six, four build twenty-four," etc. Now I will explain the hints of the tribes and the building of 22... In Genesis Rabbah, Rabbi Shimon bar Yohai said: "The power above is no higher than the power below... and this is the gate of heaven" in numerical value...

# The Tablets of the Covenant

To distinguish, as we see in the chapter "How do we bless?" <note>referring to Tractate Berakhot in the Talmud</note>, but regarding the blessing over bread, there is a dispute. Even though the law was decided regarding the phrase "Who brings forth" (*HaMotzi*), nevertheless, how powerful it was to use the clarified language.

The Tosafot <note>medieval commentators on the Talmud</note> there wrote what they wrote. But know that in its intended construction, we say the language of "Who brings forth" (*HaMotzi*) which indicates both the past and the future. For we refer to the holy bread that existed in the past before Adam sinned, and that which will exist in the future. You will find this similarly in Genesis Rabbah, section 15: Rabbi Nehemiah and the Sages. Rabbi Nehemiah says: "Who brings forth bread from the earth" means He who has *already* brought forth bread from the earth. The Sages say: "Who brings forth bread from the earth" means He who is *destined* to bring it forth in the future, as it is said: "There shall be an abundance of grain in the land..." <note>Psalm 72:16</note>. "And the Lord shall be my God" <note>Genesis 28:21</note>:

Know that regarding the Name <term>Y-H-V-H|The four-letter Tetragrammaton, the personal name of God</term>, it usually has three vowel points. It is often pointed with the *Cholam* <note>an 'o' sound</note> of the letter *Yud* and the *Kamatz* <note>an 'ah' sound</note> from the name *Adonai* <note>meaning 'My Lord'</note>. Sometimes it is pointed with a *Chirik* <note>an 'ee' sound</note> under the *Vav*, which is the pointing of the name *Elohim* <note>meaning 'God' in the aspect of Judgment</note>. According to how it is pointed, so is its reading. Behold, when it is pointed with the vowels of *Elohim*, it corresponds to the level of <term>Binah|Understanding; a high spiritual emanation or Sefirah</term>, as is known. This is explained at length in the book *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimmonim by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the Gate of Essence and the Gate of the One Who Enjoys, chapters six and seven. There, the Name Y-H-V-H pointed with the vowels of *Adonai* is <term>Tiferet|Beauty/Harmony; a central spiritual emanation</term> in His holy palace.

The Name *Yud-He* within *Adonai* is the lower manifestation, the secret of Jacob within Rachel <note>referring to a Kabbalistic union of spiritual forces</note>. And above, in *Binah*, it is the secret of Jacob within Leah, which is why it is pointed with the vowels of *Elohim*. This is the secret of <term>Da'at|Knowledge/Connection</term> as I wrote above. However, Jacob himself belongs to the secret of *Tiferet*, possessing only some attainment in *Da'at*. Leah comes to him through *Chesed* <note>Loving-kindness</note>, and in the future, his level will be elevated, and he will exist in the secret of *Da'at*. This is what is meant by "And the Lord (*Y-H-V-H*) shall be my God (*Elohim*)," meaning the Name Y-H-V-H pointed with the vowels of *Elohim*, which is *Binah*.

Regarding these two "unions" <note>spiritual pairings</note>, they hinted at the secret of the "Well," as the scripture says: "Jacob lifted his feet... and behold, a well." It says a well happened to be there for him suddenly. One might ask: what is the greatness of a well, or what is the matter that every union of the Patriarchs occurs by a well? Know that a "well" (*Be'er*) is the Source of Life from the hidden Tree of Life. "Well" in Aramaic is translated as *B'er*, and the phrase "May His Great Name" (*Yhei Shmei Rabba*) is related. The <term>Ari|Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century mystic</term>, of blessed memory, wrote that the numerical value of "Well" (*Be'er*, 203) equals the combination of the names *Yud-Adonai* and *Yud-Elohim*. According to what I have written, these names are the secret of the two unions, and in the future, the Name will be completed and become *Rabba* (Great).

God enlightened my eyes in the holy writings of the Ari, of blessed memory, who wrote on the verse: "And they took Lot and his property (*Rachusho*), the son of Abram’s brother." One might wonder at this verse: was the property the son of his brother? It should have said: "And they took Lot, the son of Abram’s brother, and his property." Rather, the Torah wrote it this way: *Rachusho Ochiv* (His property, his brother), and they hinted to me... that it will be *Rabba*. The matter is that for all the dangers Abraham put himself in to pursue the four kings to rescue Lot, the *Zohar* writes that he did this because he saw through the Holy Spirit that the Davidic Monarchy and the Messiah were destined to come from Lot <note>through Lot's daughter, the ancestor of Ruth the Moabite</note>. Then the Name will be *Rabba* (Great). Thus, Abraham intended this for the sake of the name *Yehei... Rabba*.

Therefore, I say this is the secret of the "Well" (*Be'er*), and there Jacob met his pairings. Know that the story of the well is a hint to the vision of the Ladder. The vision of the Ladder was in "visions of God," and the matter of the well is the impression of that vision manifested in action. Just as they interpreted in Genesis Rabbah the matter of the ladder as referring to the Torah and the Temple, so too regarding the well. Rabbi Yochanan interpreted it regarding Sinai: "And behold, a well"—this is Sinai. And there were three <note>flocks</note>—the Priests, Levites, and Israelites. For from that "well," the Ten Commandments were given. And before that, he interpreted the whole passage regarding Zion, the Land of Israel, and the Sanhedrin <note>the high court</note>. For all the events of the Patriarchs indicate the future: the receiving of the Torah, the Land of Israel, its prosperity, and its destruction, and the future to come which is the ultimate purpose and eternity. "And the Lord shall be my God," and "Rachel his daughter came with the sheep." The "sheep" refers to the exile of Israel, for in their transition they are called "sheep," and in their redemption, they are called "Man," as it is written: "And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are Man" <note>Ezekiel 34:31</note>. That is to say: now you are like sheep, but when you are redeemed, then you are "Man." See the words of our Sages.

Behold, Rachel was buried on the road so that she could be an aid to her children when they went into exile, as the Midrash says: "A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping; Rachel weeping for her children..." until the Holy One, Blessed be He, answered her: "There is a reward for your work... and the children shall return to their own border." This is the meaning of "Jacob kissed Rachel and lifted up his voice and wept." Rashi <note>the premier medieval commentator</note> wrote that he wept because he saw through the Holy Spirit that she would not enter the burial cave with him. One might ask: would he weep just because she wouldn't be buried with him? Rather, the explanation is this: he saw she wouldn't be buried with him, and he saw through the Holy Spirit that the reason for this was so she could be an aid to her children when they went into exile. As Rashi says in the portion *Vayechi*, he therefore wept because of the destruction and the exile that he foresaw. Now Israel is called "sheep," and the Holy One is the Shepherd. The name Rachel herself signifies "sheep" <note>the Hebrew word *Rachel* means ewe</note>. Therefore, hints were given: "Follow the footsteps of the sheep," which indicates our state in exile. Thus far his words; see Rashi there on the Song of Songs.

In the time of the Temple, there will be the "shepherding" and the holy spreading of light. This is what Jacob hinted at when he said: "And I did not know," and now he knows "And the Lord shall be..." This will be in the time of the Temple, the time of prophecy and promise... Then Israel will be called "sheep," and the name Jacob indicates the "heel" (*Ekev*) and lowliness—this is "the footsteps (*Ikvei*) of the sheep." The letters of *Ikvei* (footsteps) are the same as *Yaakov* (Jacob). And the "fairest among women" is Rachel, who comes with the sheep, and she is the fairest among women as it is written: "Rachel was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance."

This is the matter of the many sheep that Jacob had. In Genesis Rabbah, Rabbi Levi said there were 600,000 dogs; the Sages said 1,200,000, and they do not disagree. The one who said 600,000 meant one for each flock, like Rachel. The one who said 1,200,000 meant two for each flock. Rabbi Levi and the Sages... and Jacob had 600,000 flocks. One opinion says there was one dog per flock, and the other says two dogs, one in front and one behind. Know that 600,000 flocks signify the 600,000 of Israel who are never missing from this count. flock, there was a dog guarding it. It is known that "dogs" signify the <term>Klipot|Husks or shells; spiritual forces of impurity</term>. As it says: "When the dogs howl, the Angel of Death has come to the city," but "against any of the children of Israel, a dog shall not whet its tongue." Therefore, Jacob subdued the "dog" to be a guardian for the sheep so that the *Klipot* would not overpower them in exile. The opinion that there were 1,200,000 dogs follows what is found in the Talmud, Tractate Shabbat, chapter "Rabbi Akiva": when they made the Golden Calf, 1,200,000 angels of destruction descended to remove their crowns. Jacob our forefather wanted to subdue them for the sheep, so they would be "dogs"... and be completed with him. Thus, the "sheep" indicate Israel. A sign for this: "Sheep" (*Tzon*) has the numerical value of the 12 tribes from these four: Leah, Rachel, Zilpah, and Bilhah. Leah and Jacob passed through the sheep and gave them to him or the women.

Then they were signaled about the future regarding the matter of "the sheep conceived," as our Sages said: "Violence was done by His kindness in this." It is difficult: how did the Holy One, Blessed be He, create something new now—that they conceived from the rods without a male? Is it not written "There is nothing new under the sun"? Rather, it appears to be like what is found in the chapter "With what may we light?" where Rabban Gamliel taught: "In the future, a woman will give birth every day." They asked: "How is this possible? Will every husband be with his wives every single day?" They explained the matter is like a hen, which has a cluster of eggs and conceives them all at once, and afterward, an egg comes out of the cluster every day. So too here: the husband is known to the woman; not a single drop is wasted, and from every single drop, there will be a child, and she will give birth to many, many children from one conception. Rabban Gamliel answered the scoffer: "Come, and I will show you an example in this world," and he showed him the hen.

So was the matter here with the sheep: all the drops of seed they received from the males remained in them and had dried up. What did the Holy One do? He sprayed upon them those waters <note>referring to the miracle of the peeled rods in the troughs</note> which moistened the dry places, and the seed within them became as if it were just now coming from the male; they conceived and gave birth. This was a sign for the future. And upon this comes the hint: "The daughters are my daughters, and the sons are my sons, and the sheep are my sheep, and all that you see is mine." I have already written that in exile we are called "sheep," and so it is written "We are counted as sheep for the slaughter." But when we are at our high level, we are called "Man," as it is written "You are Man."

However, there is a distinction within "Man" itself between male and female, as it says: "Male and female He created them... and called their name Man." Behold, in all the redemptions that have happened already, we were only compared to females, as it says "A new song" (*Shirah Chadashah*—feminine form). But for the future, it is written "A new song" (*Shir Chadash*) in the masculine form. These are two matters: in our times of tranquility, we were "Man" from the female aspect, and now in exile, we are "sheep." But in the future, we will be "male sons." Concerning this, he said to Jacob: all the levels of Israel—whether daughters, sons, or sheep—all that you see in your prophecy (for a prophet is called a "Seer"), "it is mine"—it all comes from Me. At first, Laban sought to uproot everything, but afterward, he became a lover and answered "Amen" against his will. For in the future, the "sheep" will be called "Man," and we will sing a "new song" in the masculine. And "Male" (*Zachar*) has the numerical value of "Blessing" (*Berakhah*), and this is the source of

->The Blessings. Speedily in our days, Amen.<-

# Written Torah: Page of Grace

I also hinted above at the matter of Samael <term>Samael</term><note>The name is interpreted here as 'Sam' (poison/medicine) and 'El' (God), implying a mix of bitter and divine</note>, which is both evil and good. Similarly, the Angel of Death: "Death" is evil, but "Angel" is good. Also, the evil is mixed with the good, and this is the secret of "Let me pass now with you," meaning the people who are with me, which is the secret of the additional converts. And because he spoke, and after Jacob said, "Until I come to my lord at Seir," hinting at the future when the Messiah shall come, as Rashi wrote. And in the holy Zohar: "I shall come *to* [El] my *lord* [Adonai] *Seir-ah*" <note>the final letters of these Hebrew words in the original text spell out "Ayeh" (Where?)</note>, as the author of the *Ba'al HaTurim* wrote. Therefore, Jacob considered the acceptance of converts: "Why is it that I should find favor in your eyes?" For we do not accept converts in the days of the Messiah, as they only convert for the sake of the "Groom" and the "Thread of Loving-kindness" that is drawn over Israel. "And Jacob journeyed to Sukkot" <note>Booths</note>; the translation/Targum implies that after the act of the scapegoat <note>original: Sa'ir</note> of the Day of Atonement, then comes the commandment of the Sukkah for Israel, which is the "Sukkah of Peace." This is the meaning of "And Jacob came whole" <note>Shalem</note>.

**And he called** him "The God [El] of the God of Israel." Our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: Hazal</note> said: "The God of Israel called Jacob 'El' <note>Strength/God</note>." The hint is that Samael is a divided name, half of which is "Sam" <note>blindness/poison</note> and half is "El." We unite the name at its root. But Jacob was called by the name "El," for Jacob exists in the secret of the inner holiness and is entirely dedicated to God [El]. Therefore, his seal is "El," and his name testifies for him—that is, the calling of the name "El." Until here was the matter of Jacob with Esau and Samael, where "Jacob’s hand was on top," and there was fulfilled in him: "For you have contended <note>original: Sarita</note> with God and with men." For he won two wars: a war below with Esau and a war above with Samael. And as I have written, "And they gave a beautiful name to Israel"—this is the name given to him by Samael, the guardian angel of Esau himself, who then conceded to him regarding the blessings. However, at Bethel, the Holy One, Blessed be He, called Jacob "Israel," and then the name "Israel" was changed for a greater excellence than when the Angel called him Israel. For the Angel called him Israel based on the past, subduing the name "Jacob" which referred to the past—how he took the blessings through trickery <note>original: be-akvah</note>. The Angel said that he should no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, because he had contended. But God renewed his names with a chosen, eternal excellence for the future, as I will explain shortly. But in the meantime, he was also called "Israel" by the angel since he had contended with God and Esau. Therefore, the words of Rashi are correct in explaining that Jacob called to the Holy One: "You, You are my God, for my name is Israel." Likewise, regarding the verse "For he committed an outrage in Israel," the Angel promised him that in the future the Holy One would change his name and bless him. Despite all this, Jacob did not let him go until the Angel was forced to bless him, for in the meantime, the war with the Angel and the name change had passed. Afterward, this became a tangible reality in himself and his generations with greater excellence. Before he received the name change and the blessing from the mouth of God Himself, there was still a trace of Samael’s touch on the socket of his thigh, for he defiles through touch. This manifested in those who emerged from Jacob’s thigh, such as the matter of Dinah with Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite—"Hamor" <note>Donkey/Materiality</note> being the daughter of the soul called "Hivya" <note>Serpent</note>. For the serpent is in the thigh, which is the spirit of harlotry, as mentioned regarding the "Sinew of the Hip" <term>Gid HaNesheh</term>. Likewise, later with the matter of Reuben when he lay with his father’s concubine—though he did not truly sin, as our Sages said, nevertheless the Scripture accounts it to him as if he had—as if these actions emerged from the serpent's touch. But afterward, the impurity of the serpent was removed entirely, and Jacob’s thigh remained clean of all dross and was made whole within. Then the Holy One, in His own glory, called his name "Israel" and blessed him.

At first glance, this is puzzling: he called the place "Alon Bachut" <note>Oak of Weeping</note> and interpreted it as mourning for his mother, as Rashi wrote. And after this, the Holy One came to Jacob and said, "Israel is your name," the great eternal excellence, as I shall explain. How could this prophecy and great attachment be revealed to him during a time of mourning? For prophecy does not rest except in a state of joy. But our Sages clarified the matter: it was specifically at the time of his mother’s mourning. First, I will explain the loftiness of the name "Israel" and also the name "Jacob." We have already spoken on the verse, "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel." We learned: Not that the name Jacob shall be uprooted, but that "Israel shall be your name"—Israel will be primary and Jacob secondary. Rabbi Zechariah said in the name of Rabbi Hama: "Jacob is your name, but Israel is your name"—Jacob is the root and Israel is an addition to it. Thus, "both are the words of the Living God." First, I will premise what I received regarding the statement of our Sages that "Jacob our father did not die," which is to be understood literally, even though the embalmers embalmed him. How so? He has two names: Jacob and Israel. The multiplicity of names indicates a multiplicity of soul-powers and spirits. When he mourned for Joseph his son for many years, the "Jacob-soul" departed and that part died, leaving only the "Israel" part. This happened after the mourning and pain intensified, namely when they took Benjamin, and Jacob their father said to them, "You have bereaved me; Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you would take Benjamin!" At that moment, the soul of "Jacob" flew away from him, and from that time he was not mentioned by the name "Jacob," only as "Israel," for "Jacob" was dead. This lasted until the news of Joseph—that he was alive—"and the spirit of Jacob revived." The spirit of Jacob returned to him and lived. Even though earlier, before "the spirit of Jacob revived," it is written "and they came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father and told him saying 'Joseph is still alive,'" since at that moment he returned to life, they called him Jacob. For surely, as soon as Joseph revealed himself to his brothers and the news was in their mouths, the vitality of Jacob began to gather. Thus, the "Jacob-part" lived a "Resurrection of the Dead," and it is not right that he should ever die again. That part remained eternally alive after the resurrection. The physical vitality was from the "Israel-soul," and this part died, as it says, "And the days of Israel drew near to die." But "Jacob" remained alive, hovering over the soul in his garment, as hinted by the <term>Recanati</term> at the end of the portion *Vayechi*, who expanded on this. Our Sages said, "Jacob our father did not die"—literally, he was clothed in a form like the body of the First Man <note>Adam</note> before his sin. This is the meaning of "a dweller of tents," for the benefit of the holy people. The meaning of this Midrash is that the souls of other righteous ones are forms whose existence is spiritual and they are not clothed in any garment unless at specific times—like those "excavators" in Tractate Shabbat, chapter *Sho'el*, or the story of "Our Holy Rabbi" <note>Rabbi Judah the Prince</note> in Tractate Ketubot, who would visit his home and perform the Friday night Kiddush. So too with Rabbi Jose the Galilean, who came to his house every Sabbath eve, and students passed by and heard his voice studying Torah. But Jacob our father was able to clothe himself and appear like the Prophet Elijah, of blessed memory. When Israel is in distress, Jacob stands in this garment and prays. This is what Rabbi Johanan said in the first chapter of Tractate Ta'anit: "I derive this from a verse: 'Fear not, my servant Jacob...' just as his seed is alive, so he is alive."

With this, the verse "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel" is explained. Know that when he was born, he was called Jacob because his hand was holding the "heel" <note>Ekev</note> of Esau, and Esau interpreted it as "crookedness" <note>Akbah</note>, saying "Is he not rightly named Jacob, for he has outwitted me <note>Vaye'akveni</note> twice?" One thing depends on the other, for Jacob’s hand held Esau and did not want to let him leave the womb first, since Jacob was truly the firstborn, born from the first drop, as Rashi wrote in the portion *Toledot*. Since Esau exited the womb first, measure for measure, Jacob clothed himself in "heel-ness" <note>crookedness</note> and cunning to take the birthright and the blessing. This was the state of Jacob initially. But after he died and returned to life—"and the spirit of Jacob revived"—he was called Jacob for another reason. For "Jacob" comes from "Ekev" <note>Heel/Consequence</note>, which refers to the eternal World to Come, which is the "End" and the "Ultimate Purpose," about which it is said, "In keeping them there is great reward <note>Ekev Rav</note>." This is a hint to what Rashi brought: "And he called his name [Ya'akov]"—that the Holy One called him Jacob. Another interpretation: his father called him Jacob because of the holding of the heel. All these words are true. The Holy One did not call him Jacob because of holding Esau’s heel, but because of the "Heel" which is the End—namely, the World to Come. The name of the Holy One rested upon him after "the spirit of Jacob revived," for then the Jacob-part remained eternal. Thus the verse is understood in two ways: "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel." First, the Jacob-part would die, and only the Israel-part would remain. This was the case until the news of Joseph. Therefore, the Holy One hinted to him now, during the mourning for his mother, because this came to him as a result of the punishment for the commandment of honoring father and mother. For Jacob was in pain for twenty-two years, corresponding to the twenty-two years he did not fulfill the honoring of his parents, as Rashi wrote in the portion *Vayeshev*. Jacob said to Laban, "These twenty years I have been in your house..." The removal of the "Jacob-spirit" was permitted at the time of his mother’s death, for her death was a result of the curse she took upon herself so that Esau would not kill him. As the <term>Nachmanides</term> <note>Ramban</note> wrote on the verse "And Deborah, Rebecca’s nurse, died," the reason for the "weeping" is not clear since he was mentioned at the death of Isaac ("and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him"). But it is possible to say that she did not have honor at her death because Jacob was not there, and Esau hated her and did not come, and Isaac’s eyes were dim and he did not leave his house. Therefore, the Scripture did not want to mention that her sons buried her. On this matter, I found in *Deuteronomy Rabbah*: Rebecca said, "Who will go out first? Abraham is dead, Isaac sits in his house with dim eyes, Jacob has gone to Padan Aram. If the wicked Esau goes out first, people will say, 'Cursed be the breasts that nursed him!'" Therefore, they took her coffin out at night. Rabbi Jose bar Hanina said: Because they took her out at night, the scriptures did not explicitly detail her death. Rather, it is alluded to by the "Oak of Weeping" [Alon Bachut]—two weepings. This is why "God appeared to Jacob... and blessed him"—He gave him the "Blessing of Mourners." Thus, he was comforted because...

# The Tablets of the Covenant: The Column of the Torah

The kindnesses You have done for me. Therefore, Jacob now comes with supplications to the Blessed Name <note>original: HaShem</note> that He should also perform a miracle for him now to save him from the hand of Esau. He mentioned the Divine Name Y-H-W <note>a three-letter variant of the Tetragrammaton</note> according to the secret of the verse: "Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will mention the name of the Lord our God," for salvation belongs to the Lord. Regarding this, he said, "I am not worthy," but rather "do it for the sake of Your Name." And against his Accuser <term>Samael</term><note>The guardian angel of Esau and a figure of accusation in the heavenly court</note>, he said, "I have become small <note>original: Katonti</note> from all the truth." For Jacob’s specific spiritual attribute is Truth, as it is written, "You give truth to Jacob." This attribute is the "Torah of Truth," for the Torah was given from the attribute of Jacob, as it is known to the Kabbalists that he represents the "Day" and is "one who dwells in tents" <note>referring to the tents of Torah study</note>. Jacob said that the essence and the root of the Torah is the attribute of Truth, and this is hinted at in the word "I have become small" (*Katonti*). This follows the teaching at the end of Tractate Sotah: "Rabbi Yosei was the smallest <note>meaning the most humble or the final remnant</note> of the pious." Rashi explains this there, and Maimonides explains that he was their "sum and their root," because the root of a thing is small at its beginning. Therefore, it hints at the central point that includes everything. For this reason, Jacob is called "the small one." This is the hint of "I have become small" in his prayer against Samael. Regarding this, Rabbi Levi said: "I am worthy..." for "with my staff I crossed this Jordan." Rashi explains that he had no gold or silver with him. This was to counter Esau; the Holy One, Blessed be He, put it into Esau's heart to think that the father's blessing had not been fulfilled in Jacob, as Rashi wrote previously on the verse "I have oxen and donkeys" — "donkey" <note>original: chamor</note> is singular, implying it was not part of the grand blessing of his father.

Rashi also wrote, citing the Midrash: "With my staff" — that the Jordan split for him by itself, showing Jacob's great spiritual power. The Holy One, Blessed be He, places these great intentions into the heart of Samael so that he will not prosecute. Know that it is a tradition in our hands that Jacob awakened great and awesome holy names here. The numerical value of "With my staff" <note>original: Be-makli = 132</note> is linked to the name M-B <note>The 42-letter name of God</note> and the name "Maccabee." At the crossing of the Yabbok river, the acronym of the verse "Who is like You among the mighty, O Lord" <note>original: Mi Kamokha Ba-elim Y-H-W-H</note> emerges. Afterward, the letters Q-L-H <note>135</note> emerge from the verse "For Your salvation I hope, O Lord" <note>original: Li-yeshuatcha Kiviti Y-H-W-H</note>. "Save me from the hand of my brother" — above, "and from the hand of Esau" — below. "For I fear him, lest he come and strike me, mother with children." This was explained above: he feared on account of a potential sin, and Samael would strike. He says here, "I fear he will prosecute because I took two sisters as wives." This might cause the "mother and children" to be struck. He mentioned only one "mother," hinting at Rachel, for he carried the sin of marrying her sister Leah; but in marrying Leah, there was no guilt. Likewise, in taking Bilhah and Zilpah, even though they were sisters, they were not sisters from the same mother. There is a principle that "Gentiles have no paternal lineage" <note>original: Ein Avot l'Goy</note>, as discussed in the portion of Vayetze on the verse "She is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother." If you ask how he could marry two sisters, know that for a convert, they are considered as if they were newly born, and they have no legal lineage to their previous father or mother. However, one could say that before the Giving of the Torah, everyone was categorized as "Children of Noah," including the Patriarchs. Therefore, from the mother's side, they did have a lineage. Thus, Jacob feared that "mother with children" would be struck — meaning Rachel and her children. Therefore he prayed, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, accepted his prayer. On the contrary, from Rachel’s children emerged the adversary of Esau, who is Joseph the Righteous. "And You said, I will surely do good with you" — good in your life, and "I will do good" above after your death. "And I will make your offspring as the sand of the sea which cannot be numbered for multitude" — "as the sand of the sea" refers to below, while "cannot be numbered" refers to the stars of the heaven above, as it is written, "Count the stars if you are able to count them." This refers to the stars and the five books of the Torah.

---

->After he finished the prayer, he began to attend to the matter of the gift. He sent a gift that hinted both below and above, for Jacob's children were destined, in the time of the Holy Temple, to send the Scapegoat to Azazel. This is the matter of the question: "To whom do you belong? Where are you going? And whose are these before you?" Regarding the gift to Esau, it is according to its plain meaning. Regarding Samael and his cohorts, it hints that he wanders and looks to investigate two things about Jacob's descendants. "To whom do you belong?" means "What is your nature?" — that is, where did you come from? "Where are you going?" means what is your destination? "And whose are these before you?" refers to the gifts of your deeds. For through the performance of commandments, camps of angels are created, and from transgressions, camps of destructive angels are created, Heaven protect us. On this, he stood to receive judgment. He said "reveal yourself" and "before me," explaining "Where is the wealth..." etc. Those who are before the Holy One, Blessed be He... and the poison <note>a play on the name Samael</note> that is not mentioned in these three is certainly a sinner. After all this, he searches and prosecutes. And it says "To your servant, to Jacob" — this is the physical answer regarding the gift to Esau. "And to your servant" is also the answer regarding the gift to Samael. For he takes our sins when we send him a gift, and this is the secret of the Scapegoat <note>original: Se’ir Ha-Mishtaleach</note>. These are the words of the *Tola'at Yaakov* <note>a 16th-century Kabbalistic work by Meir ibn Gabbai</note>: The secret of the Scapegoat is as we have already made known; because of God’s pity for His people, He advised us with several good commandments to be saved from the hand of our brother, the children of Esau and Ishmael. Regarding the goat of Ishmael... as it is hinted at. Behold, it is found that we send the goat to Azazel. First, one must know and understand that the event that happened to Jacob our father, peace be upon him, with his brother Esau, was entirely a sign for his children. He, in his kindness, prepared himself for prayer, which is a sign for us in the exile, for because of our sins we have no Scapegoat, but we offer "the appeasement of our lips" <note>prayer instead of sacrifice</note>. Afterward, he prepared himself with a gift. This was a sign for us when we were on our land. Behold, the High Priest would first confess the sins of Israel over the goat, and it is written: "And the goat shall bear upon it all their iniquities." It is written regarding Jacob: "And he lodged there," for he held in his hands the transgressions with which they were soiled all year, and the goat carries them as a gift to our brother Esau, as was explained. Then: "Two hundred she-goats," etc. From the dawn of time, what appears in our Holy Torah regarding the goat is a hint to the signs of our forefathers, peace be upon them. Why this act on Rosh Hashanah <note>the New Year</note> involved a goat and not a sheep is known to the Sages of Truth. It is because as things extend further down from the impure emanations, impurity is more drawn into them. Thus, anything far from its fellow is more impure than its fellow. Therefore, all things drawn from that "Ox" <note>a mystical archetype</note>, the goal of the "Hair" <note>original: Se'ar, a pun on Se'ir/Goat and Se'ir/Esau's land</note> is upon it. All his deeds are with the goat, whose wealth is more abundant than other animals, and it indicates the strength of Judgment, just as they indicate the strength of anger and wrath. But that Ox is king over them all, and its impurity is not like theirs. However, its place is closer to the Sanctuary than theirs. Therefore, his portion is the goat—which is neither fully "hairy" <note>Se'ir</note> nor fully "smooth" <note>chalak</note>. A smooth man <note>Jacob</note> is for that in which there is impurity, and that goat, for its impurity is not as severe as the other lower ones. Therefore, his portion is the goat and not something else. Furthermore, there is a hidden matter in this. It is a requirement among the masters of sorcery that all their deeds involve something that has never mated with a female... therefore, when asking the "Kid" <note>original: Kedod</note> who is king, they give him a goat that has not been given to a pig. This goat was given to the aforementioned Minister <note>Samael</note> to occupy him while he was still with his father. By this, they would remove him from the Sanctuary. This counsel was fulfilled to atone for Israel, and he would enjoy the King's table. Therefore, there are two goats, so that he would not feel bad in his soul. For when Israel sends him this gift, he rejoices in his soul that he is feasting with the King. This is the hint of "Moreover, Esther the Queen did not bring..." etc., and it is written, "And Haman went out on that day joyful and glad of heart," and immediately he turns to speak in favor of Israel. The Holy One, Blessed be He, hears his testimony and atones for them. The Holy One, Blessed be He, casts all the sins of Israel upon his head and distributes them to his people, as it is written: "And the goat shall bear upon it all their iniquities," and it is written: "And You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea." This is a parable for all that is drawn from him; he is the "depth" and the "final sea." They think they are receiving great gifts that the Holy One, Blessed be He, removed from Israel and gave to them. This is "a gift sent to my lord."<-

---

Afterward, Samael was revealed: "And a man wrestled with him," etc., until he called his name Israel.
And he said, "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel." Our Sages of blessed memory said, "Hush," <note>a wordplay on Rashi's name or a call for silence</note>
for their goodness is not complete, as he did not call him by the name Israel except regarding the past—that is, the struggle he engaged in—
so they would not say he attained things through "heel-tripping" <note>original: akvah, a pun on the name Yaakov/Jacob</note> and deceit, but rather through lordship. But there is another,
more internal explanation for the names Jacob and Israel, which hints at the future. This was done at Bethel by the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who blessed him
and drew a blessing upon him from the Source of Blessings, as I will explain later. "And he kissed him and they wept." Rashi brought
that there are dots over the word "and he kissed him," and opinions differ in the old Sifrei: some interpret these dots to say he did not kiss him
with all his heart, but Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said he did kiss him with all his heart. One master said one thing and the other said another, but they do not actually disagree.
For Esau below is like Samael, his power above. Behold, our Sages of blessed memory said that the Holy One, Blessed be He, turns the Accuser into a Defender. He said,
"You have one nation on the earth." I heard a plain explanation from my father and teacher, may his memory be for a blessing: one could ask how
Samael can act as an advocate and speak good? Are not angels not composed of physical matter? Poison <note>the "Sam" in Samael</note> is good when it rejoices
over good, and he who is over evil is evil. So how does Samael speak good? Rather, the matter is that the "good" is actually "bad," and the "defense" is actually an "accusation." It is as if he is saying: "Look, when Israel wants to behave
in holiness and purity and to be whole and perfect, theft is in their hand and it is a deception..."

# Tablets of the Covenant
### Page 300

If man had not sinned, he would have merited to offer himself as a sacrifice. That is to say, his very life would be a "living sacrifice" to God forever, and he would be attached to the Blessed Name just as the righteous are destined to be after their deaths. This involves three levels which are explained: the vitality of the "Living Creatures" <note>The *Chayot* or celestial beings from Ezekiel’s vision</note>—the Ox shall remain an Ox, and it will be refined into the "Lion of Judah," and then finally it will be fulfilled by being carried "on the wings of eagles." Thus, the incarnations of Israel correspond to the four "Living Creatures": Man, Ox, Lion, and Eagle. Regarding the level of unity, it will be fulfilled as it is written: "On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one." The end of that verse spells out "Generation to Generation" <note>The final letters of the Hebrew words *Adonai Echad U'Shemo Echad* spell out *Dor VaDor*</note>, representing the perfection of body and soul together; both will be eternal according to the original intent of creation. 

I have already elaborated on this in the introduction to my work **The Generations of Adam** (*Toldot Adam*) regarding the dispute between Maimonides <note>Rambam</note> and Nachmanides <note>Ramban</note> as to whether the final perfection is for the soul alone or for both the body and soul. The true opinion is that of Nachmanides—that it is for both. On these matters, we shall explain a passage from the Midrash (*Bereishit Rabbah*, Portion of *Miketz*) which reads: "Only as regarding the throne will I be greater than you." Resh Lakish said: Moses wrote two sections in the Torah, and we learn their true meaning from the section of the wicked Pharaoh. One verse says: "And you shall be only (*rak*) above"; one might think this means "like Me," so the text says "only"—My greatness is above your greatness. Similarly, it says: "Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy," one might think "like Me," so the text says: "For I, the Lord your God, am holy"—My holiness is above your holiness. And we learn this from the section of the wicked Pharaoh: "I am Pharaoh," one might think "like me," but the text says "I am Pharaoh"—my greatness is above your greatness.

This raises a question: which is superior, greatness or holiness? If greatness is superior, the limiting word should be written regarding holiness to show that God's holiness is higher, and it would not need to be written regarding greatness, as it would be understood through a "fortiori" argument <term>Kal V'Chomer: A logical inference from a minor premise to a major one</term>. If the reverse is true, the same difficulty applies. And if they are equal, why not just write it for one of them? Furthermore, why does it say "Moses our Creator wrote for us"? Moses wrote the entire Torah! Why mention his name specifically here? Additionally, the order is reversed: here "only" (*rak*) comes before "I," but later "I" comes before "only." 

Furthermore, why is the phrase "Can it be like me?" expressed as a wonder regarding greatness, but not regarding holiness? And finally, why must we learn such great and holy matters from the wicked Pharaoh? I have already written that we could not have reached these levels of holiness except through Pharaoh and the exile in Egypt, emerging from the "materiality of the serpent" which was refined by His right hand. There, we were purified so that we might live as complete beings in body and soul. This was achieved through the incarnation of Joseph; through the impurity of the "shrouded lip," one is refined until, in the future, even the body will be as holy as "garments of light" <note>A play on the Hebrew words *Or* (skin) and *Or* (light), which sound the same</note. All of this is through the Torah, which consists of study and action. Study is the intellectual attainment of the soul, and action is performed by the body. 

I have already written above that in the name of God (*ADNY*), there is the letter *Lamed* <note>meaning 'to learn'</term> hidden in each letter's full spelling. The *Aleph* is the foundation of Wisdom—the Throne—and Wisdom extends into greatness (*Gedulah*). Similarly, at the giving of the Torah, the Blessed Name told Moses our Teacher: "Grasp onto the Throne," as seen in the Talmud (*Shabbat*). This is the hint in "the Throne I shall be greater" (*Agdal*), which ends in the letter *Lamed*. Pharaoh, even though he did not know the power of the One Above, knew of the greatness prepared for Joseph's people, and said, "Only as regarding the throne will I be greater than you." This hints that the Throne is a "curtain" or "veil," yet My name is called upon you. 

Indeed, we were refined through Pharaoh because of the subjugation under him. This is why "we learn from the sections of that wicked man" who acted wickedly through the enslavement of Israel. Moses wrote this for us in the Torah to show that from the perfection of body and soul—study and action—we will merit the future perfection of body and soul, the secret of the "garments of light." This was seen in Moses, His chosen one, whose face and body shone with beams of light and were refined; Moses did not need to nullify his physical body during prophecy like other prophets, for he perfected both body and soul during his lifetime. Therefore, he recognized the "Throne." 

The hints mentioned in this passage are "Great" and "Holy." "Greatness" corresponds to the soul, which is separate, while "Holiness" corresponds to the body. The "Kingdom of Earth" mentioned regarding Pharaoh hints at the "Kingdom of Heaven." Just as man has two levels—soul and body, hidden and revealed—so too does the Holy One separate Himself in the world. From the perspective of His essence, He is hidden; from the perspective of His actions, He is revealed. To Him belongs "Greatness" regarding His essence, as He is the One who brings all into being, and to Him belongs "Holiness" regarding His glory. 

Our own "Greatness" and "Holiness" are the reverse, for the world of action is a ladder to ascend to the world of intellect; from the revealed, one arrives at the hidden. Therefore, regarding the earthly kingdom which hints at the heavenly kingdom, "Greatness" precedes "Holiness." "Greatness" is the level of the soul—"Can it be like Me?" This is phrased as a wonder, meaning: it shouldn't even enter your mind that you could be like Me! It is obvious that a limitation is needed, for how could one think greatness would be equal? The word "only" (*rak*) comes to teach that we are limited only by His greatness, but we are higher than all other forms of greatness, even that of angels, for the Righteous Person is the "conduit" from God to the worlds below. If the word "only" were not written, one might think Israel could even surpass the Divine, but "only" teaches that nothing is above Israel except the Holy One Himself in His glory. 

"You shall be holy" refers to the world of action. Choice is given to man, and here the phrase "Can it be like Me?" is *not* followed by a note of wonder. This is because one might actually think "exactly like Me"—meaning, just as I have the power to do what I do without anyone stopping Me, so too the performance of deeds given into your hands is by your own choice. For "everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven." In the Talmud (*Shabbat*), Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: The Holy One has nothing in His world except the fear of Heaven, as it says, "And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear..." And it is written, "Behold (*Hen*), the fear of the Lord is wisdom." In Greek, the word for "one" is *Hen*. 

He was precise in saying "in His world," referring to the world where choice exists. The verse says "The fear of the Lord is His treasure," for it is the way of kings to put rare things in their treasuries. The Lord of Hosts owns everything, so what could He possibly "collect" that is rare? Only that which is left to the choice of human beings and is not in the hands of Heaven. Therefore, it says "Like Me"—just as I act by My will alone, so you act by your will without assistance. To this, He says: "My holiness is above your holiness." Our Sages said: "He who comes to be purified is assisted." They also said: "One who sanctifies himself a little below is sanctified much from above." Thus, after a person begins to choose good, God assists him and adds holiness. This addition is much greater than what the person achieved through his own choice. This is the meaning of "My holiness is above your holiness"—the holiness I bestow upon you is higher than the holiness you achieve through your own choice.

# Let Us Return
To the matter of Joseph's kingship: it was only to prepare Israel to become a nation and to establish the Kingdom of Judah. The brothers did not understand this; they thought Joseph sought the monarchy for himself and his descendants. Therefore, they went to Dothan <term>Dothinah: A play on the Hebrew word *Dat*, meaning law</term> to seek "legal pretexts," that is, to judge him according to the law of the Torah. They all agreed he was deserving of death—even the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, who loved him, agreed based on the law.

<columns>3</columns>
Since he opposed the kings of the House of David, and anyone who opposes the House of David is as if he opposes the Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*).
<column-break/>
Therefore, when Joseph made himself known to his brothers and they saw his success, they wanted to kill him even more, seeing his thoughts moving from potential to action. But the Holy One sent an angel and scattered them. Or, "Joseph said to his brothers: Come close to me"—he wanted to reveal that it was not as they thought, but that God had sent him before them to prepare the way for Israel to become a nation. Three times he said "God sent me before you": 1) For sustenance during the famine. 2) To ensure a remnant on earth. This verse seems contradictory, as a "remnant" is small but "great deliverance" is large. This hints at two missions: to establish the Kings of Judah so Israel would be worthy of kingship. Then, when they left Egypt, "Judah became His sanctuary," leading to the House of David. 3) In the future, he will send Mashiach ben Yosef <note>The Messiah from the line of Joseph</note> to clear the way for Mashiach ben David. He will be killed for the sanctification of the Name. This is hinted at in Reuben's words: "Behold, his blood is required." Even though they did not understand it then, the Holy Spirit spoke through Reuben.
