# Lift up the Written Torah; The Flock of Joseph #

<margin>
A good provider <note>Hebrew: *Parnas Tov*</note>, because since the land and nature are his signs, the goodness of the Kingdom is also upon you, for in it Israel and Joseph are bound together. This is the secret of his dream being fulfilled... a sign and a voice that a good provider was established... they relied on the [wisdom] of Egypt. This is the secret of the "Valley" <note>Hebrew: *Emek*</note>, meaning the depth of the fulfillment... the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they will be upon him.
</margin>

One [argument] concerned him and their debate regarding the Kingdom of the House of David, specifically the spark of the Holy Spirit <note>Hebrew: *Ruach HaKodesh*</note> within them. The holiness of the Kingdom is the Holy Land, which contains the sanctified Jerusalem. Joseph was connected to them from the time they were exiles, and he hinted at the matter of the spies <note>Hebrew: *meraglim*</note>—that the leaders of the tribes would eventually speak ill of the Land. However, Joseph loved the Land, as did his descendants—namely the daughters of Zelophehad <note>Who petitioned Moses for a portion of the Land</note>—and from him came Joshua, who led the nation into its inheritance. Even though it might seem a spy came from him, that influence was nullified in his case. 

Joseph said to them, "You have come to see the nakedness of the land," because it is written concerning the spies: "Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt." Judah, who was the head of the wilderness camps, replied to him. Afterward, the most distinguished of the tribes was Levi, who was sanctified. The answer was: "Your servants were not spies," for Caleb son of Jephunneh from the tribe of Judah remained righteous, and from the tribe of Levi, there was no [wicked] spy. He said "they were not," but in the future, there *would* be spies—referring to when Joshua sent two righteous spies, who were from Levi and Judah: specifically Phinehas from the tribe of Levi and Caleb from the tribe of Judah. Therefore, they answered regarding that time of the spies to which you are hinting. You foresee through the Holy Spirit that at *that* time your servants were not spies, but they would be at the time of the conquest of the Land. 

Alternatively, he said, "Bring Benjamin to me," for the Temple <note>The *Beit HaMikdash*</note> was destined to rest in his territory. Since the ultimate purpose of these matters was the Kingdom over the Holy Land where the Temple stands, Joseph, through the Holy Spirit, foresaw the destruction of the Temple and wept upon Benjamin’s neck. Afterward, he was comforted by the "changes of clothes," which allude to the future when the Hidden Light <note>Hebrew: *Ohr HaGanuz*; the primordial light of Creation</note> will return, and the clothes will be exchanged for "garments of light," as mentioned above. 

Regarding the fact that the tribes did not understand Joseph's intentions, it is explained in a Midrash <note>Ancient rabbinic commentary</note>: "And Reuben heard" (Genesis 37:21). Rabbi Isaac bar Marion said: This verse comes to teach you that if a person performs a commandment <note>A *mitzvah*</note>, he should do it with a whole heart. For had Reuben known that the Holy One, Blessed be He, would record of him, "And Reuben heard and saved him from their hand," he would have carried Joseph to his father on his own shoulders! Had Aaron known that the Holy One would record of him, "Behold, he is coming out to meet you [and will be glad in his heart]," he would have gone out to meet Moses with drums and dances! Had Boaz known that the Holy One would record of him, "And he reached her parched corn, and she ate and was satisfied and left over," he would have fed her fattened calves! 

Now, there is a difficulty between the beginning and the end of this teaching. At first, it says one should perform a deed with a whole heart for the sake of the commandment itself, not for any other motive, such as self-aggrandizement. But the end suggests that if they had known, they would have done more to be honored! However, the explanation is this: To perform a deed with a "whole heart" means to descend into the depths of the intellect to understand the spiritual power and reach of that deed. When one understands the greatness of the matter, he performs it with more alacrity and the utmost beauty <note>Hebrew: *hiddur*</note>. 

These three—Reuben, Aaron, and Boaz—did not descend into the full depth of the commandment. On the contrary, they thought what they were doing was "beyond the letter of the law" <note>Hebrew: *lifnim mishurat hadin*</note>. Had they known the Torah would record it as a formal commandment, they would have acted with even greater zeal. Reuben thought that according to the depth of Joseph's "sin," he deserved death for rebelling against the Davidic Kingdom. He only intended to save him as a temporary measure, using whatever small merit could be found. But in truth, Joseph was not guilty of anything; he did not desire the throne nor rebel against David’s line. On the contrary, his essence was to support the Davidic Kingdom. It is like the High Priest <note>Hebrew: *Kohen Gadol*</note> who holds the Crown of Torah, the Crown of Priesthood, and the Crown of Kingship. Priesthood and Kingship exist for the sake of the Crown of Torah, and Joseph represents the Crown of Torah. Therefore, the transformation of Israel to sustain a nation worthy of kingship had to happen through Joseph. He is the "oil" that nullifies Esau. Judah represents the power of the adversarial forces <note>Samael and the Evil Inclination</note>, which the Crown of Torah drives away. As the Sages said: "If this repulsive one [the impulse to evil] meets you, drag him to the House of Study." 

This is why, when Israel was in the wilderness, they carried two chests: the Ark containing the Tablets of the Torah and the coffin of Joseph. They carried them together to say, "The one in this [coffin] fulfilled what is written in that [Ark]." They carried them on their shoulders <note>Hebrew: *batef*</note>. Regarding this, it was said: Had Reuben known this, he would have carried Joseph on his shoulders. 

Similarly, Aaron thought that Moses being the redeemer was an extra honor, a mere kindness from God to glorify those who fear Him. He did not realize it was essential, thinking "The Lord of Hosts is our Redeemer" directly. Even Moses himself initially thought this, saying, "Please send by the hand of the one You will send," meaning the ultimate Redeemer. He asked, "Who am I that I should go?" The Midrash notes that "I" <note>Hebrew: *Anochi*</note> hints at "I am the Lord your God," meaning God Himself should redeem them. But God's intent was to magnify Moses, as it says, "See, I have made you as a god to Pharaoh." Afterward, the Torah was given through him to "magnify the Torah and make it glorious." Aaron did not know this depth at the time, thinking it was just a gesture beyond the law. Had he known the Torah would record it, he would have understood that the Redeemer must specifically work through this mediation; then he would have met Moses with drums and dances, just as Miriam did at the Sea.

Regarding Ruth, Boaz made a mistake. When he "reached her parched corn," it was a hint at the Messiah who would descend from her. Boaz thought it was a lowly thing for the Messiah to come from such a union, or that a redeemer was unnecessary because "God will be King." This is similar to the Prophet Samuel’s anger when Israel asked for a king. He did not realize that "the kingdom on earth is like the kingdom in heaven" and that God desires His Presence <note>The *Shekhinah*</note> to dwell among those below. Had he known the Torah would record his act, he would have fed her fattened calves.

Therefore, the portions of Judah and Tamar are placed next to the selling of Joseph, for it was all from God for one purpose: Joseph's descent to Egypt would bring about the Kingdom of Judah. The Midrash hints that while the brothers were busy selling Joseph, the Holy One was busy bringing about the Messiah. Afterward, the text mentions Joseph's time in prison—this was the cause for him to rule in Egypt and ride in the "second chariot." Then it tells of the revelation through Pharaoh's dreams of the seven stalks of grain. I have already explained that Jacob and Joseph are essentially one. Jacob is the "beauty of Adam," and Joseph is his direct image. The purpose of Creation was for Man. Jacob "sought to dwell in tranquility," but the "Satan" <note>the ordeal of Joseph</note> jumped upon him. This is like the creation of the world, where chaos preceded stability. 

Creation will not be fully corrected until the coming of the Messiah, for the "husk" <note>Hebrew: *Kelipah*; spiritual impurity</note> preceded the fruit. This is the meaning of the Midrash on Genesis: Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish interpreted the verses as referring to the four kingdoms. "The earth was **formless** <note>Hebrew: *Tohu*</note>"—this is the Babylonian kingdom. "**Empty** <note>Hebrew: *Bohu*</note>"—this is the Median kingdom [Haman]. "**Darkness**"—this is the Greek kingdom, which darkened the eyes of Israel with decrees, telling them to "write on the horn of an ox that you have no part in the God of Israel." "**Upon the face of the deep**"—this is the Roman/Edomite kingdom, which is as bottomless as the deep. "And the **spirit of God hovered**"—this is the spirit of the Messiah. In whose merit does it come? In the merit of Repentance, which is compared to **water**, as it says, "Pour out your heart like water." 

The matter is that through Adam's sin, the "husk" was brought in and the light was hidden. Therefore, there is a need for refinement and purification through the exiles. Then your "labor" will be completed, the Messiah will come, and the verse "Let there be light" will be fulfilled—the Hidden Light. Like the redemption from Egypt, where Israel was purified from the "impurity of the Serpent," they emerged with signs and wonders that prove the world was created by God and that He changes the laws of nature at His will. God hinted here at the other exiles, saying "I will be with them in this exile and I will be with them in others." Likewise, at the "Covenant Between the Parts," when God informed Abraham of the Egyptian exile, He hinted at the four kingdoms with the phrase "a great dark dread fell upon him." Once they left Egypt and received the Torah, they were totally purified and were fit for eternal life, but they corrupted this at the Golden Calf and thus required the refinement of the four exiles. Since Jacob is the "beauty of Adam" and the purpose of Creation, the exiles were hinted to him. As Rabbi Josiah ben Levi said, the verse "May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man" refers to the Holy One, as it is said, "The Lord is a man of..."

# The Written Torah: The House of Israel, the House of Jacob, the House of Joseph

Come and see: Rabbi Yehuda said, Jacob said, "I will lie with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place." We have learned there: regarding one whose soul departs in a foreign land and whose body is then buried in the Holy Land, it is written: "And you came and defiled my land and made my inheritance an abomination" <note>Jeremiah 2:7</note>. Yet Jacob said, "bury me... in their burial place," even though his soul departed in a foreign domain? Rabbi Yehuda said: Jacob is different, for the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence</note> was holding onto him and attached to him. This is as it is written: "I will go down with you to Egypt" to dwell in the exile, "and I will surely bring you up again" <note>Genesis 46:4</note> to join your soul, so that your body will not be buried <unclear>alone</unclear> in the graves of your fathers. What is this saying? Even though his soul departed in a foreign domain, etc. Until here are the words of the Zohar.

However, one might still ask this question regarding the sons of Joseph, who died in an impure land and were later brought up to be buried in the Land of Israel. It is possible that Joseph's situation is permitted for the same reason. I see, according to what the Zohar wrote elsewhere, that the reason Joseph was brought to Egypt before his father and brothers and their household was so that there would be a dwelling place for the Divine Presence to dwell with them in exile. For wherever Israel was exiled, the Divine Presence was exiled with them. If so, we can say that the Divine Presence also accompanied the soul of Joseph.

Indeed, I have answered this, with God's help, in this way: behold, when all the seed of Israel are together in their <unclear>dwelling</unclear>, the "air of the Land of Israel" <note>original: *avir d'Eretz Yisrael* - a concept that the spiritual atmosphere of the Holy Land can exist where the community gathers</note> is present there. There it was permitted to offer the sacrifices that Israel made in the desert for forty years when they established the Tabernacle and offered sacrifices; it was not called "slaughtering outside" <note>original: *shchutei chutz* - a prohibition against sacrificing outside the Temple</note>, Heaven forbid. Even though it was not the physical Land of Israel, nevertheless, at that time when all of Israel was together, the air of the Land of Israel was there. We find that when Jacob and Joseph died, and all of Israel was gathered together, they died in the air of the Land of Israel. Only after Israel left Egypt did the air of the Land of Israel depart from there, and the land remained in its impurity. Therefore, Jacob did not want to be buried there. The superiority of the Land of Israel is such that even if all of Israel is not gathered in it, but only some of them, it is still the air of the Land of Israel.

And Jacob said to Joseph, "I will lie with my fathers," hinting at this matter to him, as if to say: "Do not think that I am dying in an impure land, Heaven forbid; I am simply lying with my fathers who are in the Land of Israel, for now, the air of the Land of Israel is here." This answer that I have written—I intended it because I learned it from the words of the Zohar in another place, but its exact location is not known. Afterward, I found in the book *Kol Sofer* on the portion of *Vayechi*, and these are his words: "Rabbi Shimon said... although Jacob's soul departed in Egypt, it did not depart into a foreign domain... for Joseph saw Jacob's bed at the time he was departing from the world, and his soul was immediately bound to its place..." These words clarify the matter: that Jacob our forefather died in a holy place, and the Divine Presence did not move from him. He is a holy branch whose death also brought a strong branch to the Holy Land, the husband of the Matronita <note>A Kabbalistic term for the Shekhinah</note>... and he dwells upon her. Until here are his words.

"And it was a very heavy camp" <note>Genesis 50:9</note>—those who saw this camp saw the camp of the Divine Presence, as it is written: "And the angels of God, clouds ascended above them," and the sight of the fear of the Lord was hidden... and this is the meaning of "very heavy honor" (*kavod me'od kaved*), which equals twenty-seven, the numerical value of the letter *Yod* from the name of the Land of Israel. The honor of a man like Jacob is from the beauty of Adam... Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

## Way of Life: Moral Rebukes

<margin>"And deal with me in kindness and truth" <note>Genesis 47:29</note>. See the Zohar, *Vayechi*, page 216b: "Come and see, kindness that is complete and truthful is that which a person does with the dead, for he does not look for a reward from the other. This is 'kindness of truth' (*chesed shel emet*)." See there and reflect.</margin>

**And deal** with me in kindness and truth. The essence of kindness is when one performs it without the intention of receiving a reward; this is called "kindness" and the person is called "generous" (*nadiv*). But one who performs it to receive a reward or benefit is called a "merchant" (*socher*) and not a generous person, and he does not possess the greatness of the attribute of kindness. Therefore, a person should <unclear>conduct</unclear> himself with "true kindness," not only with the dead but even with the living. Then he walks in the ways of God and clothes himself in His attributes, blessed be He. For He, may He be exalted, performs kindness for free. About this it is said: "Because Your kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise You" <note>Psalm 63:4</note>. This means: it is the way of people to perform "true kindness" with the dead and not the living, but Your true kindness is "from life"—that which You do for us in our lifetimes. For what reward can we pay You back? Only "my lips shall praise You," for through His desired kindness, He creates satisfaction and spirit for us to delight in, merely to thank Him. As our Sages said: "Four must give thanks," and this is "my lips shall praise You." So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, provides us with food and sustenance through His great kindness, and we have nothing to do but bless Him... and with our lips, we give thanks.

<margin>"And Israel strengthened himself," etc. See the book *Ohel Yaakov* at the end: "Therefore it does not say 'and he sat *in* the bed' but 'upon the bed,' for it was his support in death, and his support was the Lord, may He be exalted, and he trusted in Him." He concludes there at length; see there.</margin>

**And Israel strengthened himself** and sat upon the bed. He strengthened himself and his seat there because of the "bed," for his "bed was complete" <note>A Talmudic idiom meaning all his children remained faithful to his teachings</note>. Happy is he who merits this. Every pious person should pray to God... so that no flaw is found in his offspring... for a person has nothing in the world except when he leaves behind worthy children. Regarding the matter of when Jacob blessed Joseph's sons, it is written: "And he blessed Joseph." He gave them the blessing of Joseph... "And your offspring which you beget after them shall be yours" <note>Genesis 48:6</note>—meaning, if he begets more children and they are worthy like these, they shall "follow after their attributes." "They shall be yours"—to whom does this merit belong? To you. For happy is the father who leaves behind worthy children and a kosher seed.

<margin>"And he blessed Joseph," etc. It is wonderous why he mentioned the Patriarchs but did not mention His name, may He be exalted. The explanation for this is that Joseph is the "last level" of <term>Atzilut</term> <note>the world of Emanation</note>, and from him, all worlds are influenced... and here too it said, "the God before whom [my fathers] walked," He is the one who feeds and sustains, and He is the "Redeeming Angel," etc. See there.</margin>

**And he blessed** Joseph and said, "The God before whom my fathers walked." The phrasing "before Him" hints at an "arousal from below to above" <note>original: *it'aruta d'letata* - the concept that human action initiates divine response</note>, which is the most excellent level when a person initiates from below, and then he draws down the worlds from above. I have elaborated on this in the portion of *Noach*. This is the secret of "walking before Him." When there is no arousal from below to above, and it comes from His kindness alone, one merits only a small amount.

In the passage "And he blessed Joseph," Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish disagree. Rabbi Yochanan said: It is like a shepherd who stands and watches his sheep. Resh Lakish said: It is like a prince who walks with the elders before him. According to Rabbi Yochanan, we need His honor; according to Resh Lakish, He "needs" our honor. This statement requires explanation. One should also look closely: Rabbi Berachiah opened but did not explain whether he agreed with Rabbi Yochanan or Resh Lakish.

I have already elaborated on this in the portion of *Noach* and other places: the greatness of the matter of "arousal from below to above"—that is, from our actions. Then, as it were, "strength is added to the Power above," as our Sages said: "When they do His will, they add strength to the Power above." Then the service requires <unclear>strength</unclear>. This is what is meant by "He needs our honor" <note>Meaning God's presence in the world is made manifest through human deeds</note>. This speaks of when there is no arousal from below, only from above, in the manner of "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious"—giving free gifts even to one who does not initiate. This is "we need His honor," that He should act out of His abundant mercy and kindness, free kindness. Then He humbles Himself and "watches His sheep," for He gives "sustenance to the animals." The "looking" is from above to below, as Rashi says in the portion of *Lech Lecha* on the verse "Look now toward the heaven," for then the arousal is from above to below, and the looking is from afar. But when the arousal is from below to above, then the Holy One "walks" below, as it says: "And I will walk among you."

Thus, Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish are both right; one spoke of one case and the other spoke of another. One spoke of arousal from above to below, and the other spoke of arousal from below to above. From this, we can learn how great is the power of arousal from below to above, as our Sages said: "A person sanctifies himself a little below, and they sanctify him much from above." For when a person prepares himself, the Divine Presence rests upon him... and from this will be explained the Midrash in *Bereshit Rabbah*: Rabbi Azariah said: At the time Jacob blessed Joseph, half of Egypt went out... and the tribes said, "Is this whole nation standing because he is a king?" Jacob said to them, "Fear the Lord, His holy ones..." Jacob was afraid they might think he was showing favoritism <note>original: *chanufah*</note>, and favoritism is a great evil... but the beauty of Joseph was because his father's spirit was reflected in him...

It also explores the ethical concept of "True Kindness" (performing good deeds without expecting reward) and the mystical importance of human initiative in triggering Divine blessing.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Book of Exodus (Shemot), specifically focusing on the mystical implications of the names and the reincarnation of souls from the beginning of creation.</meta>

# Tablets of the Covenant

These are the names of the Torah portion, associated with the **Forty-Two Letter Name** <note>A mystical name of God in Kabbalah comprised of 42 letters, derived from the first 42 letters of Genesis</note> which represents the beginning of the revelations in Egypt. It is stated in the **Zohar**: Rabbi Shimon said, when the Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> descended into Egypt, a living celestial being descended with it, the likeness of the patriarch Israel <note>Jacob</note>, accompanied by forty-two holy servants. Each one was sanctified by the Holy Name, and they all descended with Jacob to Egypt, as it is written: *"And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob"* <note>Exodus 1:1</note>. This is the end of his words. The explanation of his statement is that he interpreted "Names" <note>Shemot</note> as if it were vocalized to mean "His Names," referring to the Names of the Blessed One. He stated that these names are forty-two in number, corresponding to the numerical value of the word **"And these"** <note>original: "Ve-eleh" (ו-א-ל-ה) equals 42</note>. Thus, forty-two names came with Jacob. The general principle that emerges is that the Exodus from Egypt points toward the "renewal of the world." The "Refining Pot" <note>a metaphor for the hardships of Egypt</note> served to purify the souls that had damaged creation. This refers to the 130 years during which Adam was separated from Eve and spirits and demons issued from him. At the end of these 130 years, Moses our Teacher, the Redeemer, was born. I have expanded on this in the book *Ma'or* and regarding the verse *"And behold, a dread, a great darkness, fell upon him"* <note>Genesis 15:12, referring to Abraham's vision of the future exiles</note>.

The **Ari, of blessed memory** <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century father of contemporary Kabbalah</note>, wrote: "**Dread**" refers to the generation of Enosh, in whose days the ocean flooded a third of the world. "**Darkness**" refers to the generation of the Flood, regarding which it is said the celestial luminaries did not function. "**Great**" refers to the Tower of Babel. "**Falling**" refers to the overturning of Sodom. We have borne the weight of their iniquities. Moses our Teacher, who is equal in stature to all of Israel, fulfilled the rectification for all of these: he was cast into the water <note>the Nile</note> in place of the ocean's flood. The account of his "ark" <note>tevah</note> was as if the sun and moon grew dark for him, just as in the Flood. It was as if, God forbid, he was "struck" like the men of Sodom. The mention of **clay and bricks** <note>Exodus 1:14</note> was to purify the "clay" <note>materiality</note> that the generation of Babel used for their tower. The "burning of the kilns" for firing bricks was rectified here. His "heaviness of mouth and tongue" served to rectify the confusion of languages at Babel. Furthermore, the enslavement of Israel and their labor in mortar and brick, and the casting of children into the Nile, served as a memorial for those drowned in the waters of the Flood.

Behold, the beginning of creation was **Adam** and his children, **Cain and Abel**. Now, the process returns to the rectification of Israel, who must be refined, and who are called "Man" <note>Adam</note>. **Abel** is Moses our Teacher, as the Kabbalists have written, and **Cain** is Jethro. When the "envy" <note>Hebrew: "Kinah," related to "Cain"</note> was removed, Jethro separated from the negative side of Cain. Through this, several matters are resolved based on a lack I found in the words of the Ari: that the *Nefesh* <note>the lower level of the soul</note> of Cain was reincarnated in the **Egyptian** whom Moses killed, while the *Ruach* <note>middle level</note> was in Korah, and the *Neshamah* <note>higher level</note> was in Jethro.

Behold, Cain killed Abel because of an "extra twin" <note>born with Abel</note>, and this twin was reincarnated as **Zipporah**. Therefore, Jethro brought Zipporah back and gave her to Moses. This explains how Moses could marry the daughter of a pagan priest—it was because she was essentially his own "rib" <note>his predestined soulmate from a past life</note>. Thus, when Jethro came to the wilderness, he said: "Go out to your wife whom I am giving to you," along with her two sons. Instead of "blood and enmity" <note>the original conflict between Cain and Abel</note>, Jethro says, **"I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you"** <note>Exodus 18:6</note>. Jethro said, **"Now I know..."** because in his previous life as Cain, he sinned by saying "There is no justice and no Judge, and no other world," as explained by the Sages and brought in the Targum Yonatan <note>an Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Torah</note>. Now he rectified this; instead of "no Judge," he said, *"Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods"* <note>Exodus 18:11</note>. The refinement of Cain allowed him to be established as a judge. Jethro also gave Moses sheep to tend, corresponding to the sheep Cain kept after killing Abel. Moses considered them "Jethro’s sheep" because he did not want to benefit from them improperly, as the Sages said, "the spirit of the wise is not pleased" by such things.

Through this, we can explain a statement in **Exodus Rabbah**: "An Egyptian man saved us" <note>Exodus 2:19</note>. Moses, after being bitten by a snake... the daughters of Jethro said to Moses, "May your strength be firm for saving us from the shepherds." Moses replied to them, "That Egyptian whom I killed is the one who saved you." Therefore, they said to their father, "An Egyptian man"—meaning, who caused this man to come to us? It was the "Egyptian man" whom he struck.

The matter is that the "Spirit of the Egyptian" was an essential breakage, not an accidental cause. It was the killing of Cain’s soul in the form of the Egyptian, and then Cain's soul was refined in Jethro to be joined with Moses, and envy was removed. Through this, I can explain Jethro’s words: *"And he said to his daughters, 'Where is he? Why did you leave the man? Call him, that he may eat bread'"* <note>Exodus 2:20</note>. Jethro's thoughts were alternating between two paths: is he an "Egyptian man" in the literal sense, or is it based on the secret mentioned above? Therefore, he said, "Call him that he may eat bread," which has two meanings: if he is literally an Egyptian, let him eat bread literally to repay a good deed. But if it is according to the secret, then "Call him" means to bring him close through the power of his spiritual essence, for Zipporah is his wife.

The text also mentions "my mother and my father," as if repeating his words. This hints at "Where is Abel your brother?" and the letter *Vav* (ו) in "And where" <note>Ve-ayo</note> hints at the name of God and the "sign" <note>Oat</note> given to Cain. In the Zohar, it says the letter *Vav* from the Holy Name was the "sign," which is why it is written he was "a fugitive and a wanderer" <note>Na va-Nad</note>. This explains the Midrash: "Why was she called **Zipporah**? Because she cleansed the house like a bird <note>Tzipor</note>." This means a bird cleanses a house afflicted by leprosy. A man’s wife is called his "house," and her "house" was under the dominion of Cain's "envy of impurity" stemming from the filth of the Serpent. Moses, however, is from the **Tree of Life**, a secret realm where there is no sin. Abel lived for 49 days, as the Ari wrote, which is seven times seven. The names **Jethro**, **Cain**, and **Egyptian** <note>Yitro, Kayin, Mitzri</note>... Abel lived 49 days in this world which was created with the letters *He* and *Vav*. Moses later became the "Staff of Moses." When Moses was sent on his mission, which represents the "renewal of the world," the staff turned into a snake and his hand became leprous <note>Exodus 4:3-6</note>.

In the Midrash **Genesis Rabbah**: *"The Lord set a sign for Cain"* <note>Genesis 4:15</note>. Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Nehemiah disagree. Rabbi Judah says: He made the orb of the sun shine for him. Rabbi Nehemiah said: Would the Holy One make the sun shine for that wicked man? Rather, it teaches that He caused leprosy to break out on him. These are not actually in conflict. "The orb of the sun" refers to the face of Moses which was like the sun. Rabbi Nehemiah is explaining that for Cain himself, there was only darkness, but later in his reincarnation, he received the "orb of the sun" through Abel/Moses. This is the hint: *"If the thief is found breaking in..."* <note>Exodus 22:1</note>, this refers to Cain who "stole the mind of the Above." *"If the sun has risen upon him"* <note>Exodus 22:2</note>, this refers to the orb of the sun shining for him as mentioned.

Regarding what I wrote about why Moses gave a reason for naming his son **Gershom** here, but did not mention the reason for **Eliezer** until the portion of *Jethro* <note>Exodus 18</note>: It says there, *"And the name of the one [ha-echad] was Eliezer,"* when it should have said "the second." Furthermore, it should have been the first son named Eliezer, because God’s help in saving him from Pharaoh’s sword happened before he arrived in Midian. According to the literal meaning, Moses did not want to publicize the miracle yet so that word wouldn't reach Pharaoh. However, according to the secret of reincarnation (Abel-Seth-Moses): when he was in the body of Abel, he did not live long. Then he was reincarnated in a "foreign land," meaning the body of Seth. But he was only a "stranger" (Ger) in that body. Now, in this reincarnation, Moses exists fully even in the body, his eye did not dim, and no man knows his burial place. He became a "resident" <note>Toshav</note> only at the giving of the Torah. The name **Eliezer** ("God is my help") refers to the "One" <note>Echad</note>, the unique level that was not revealed until the Revelation at Sinai. Moses was prepared for this great wisdom. "Wisdom is found from nothingness" <note>Job 28:12; Ayin (nothingness) is an anagram of Ya'in</note>. The letters of Moses (M-Sh-H) contain hidden depths. The word "From nothingness" <note>Me-Ayin</note> equals 101 in Gematria, which hints at the saying "one who reviews his lesson 100 times is not like one who reviews it 101 times." Moses' teacher was the angel **Zagzagel** (numerical value 52) which combined with other factors reaches 101.

Thus, "Wisdom is found from nothingness" refers to Moses. He was prepared for wisdom because he is the "Abel" (breath/thread) of the Torah in which there is no sin. He is Seth, from whom the world was established, for the world stands on the Torah. He attached himself to Jethro, who held the spark of Cain. Moses killed the Egyptian, who was the reincarnation of the negative part of Cain. A hint to this: "He struck the Egyptian" <note>Vayach et ha-Mitzri</note>; "The Egyptian" has the same numerical value as "Moses." Moses had six names. The Ari wrote that when he killed the Egyptian, he did so using the **Name of 42** to elevate his soul. Jethro had seven names and he atoned for his idolatry. But for Balaam, Moses did not want to leave him with the Holy Name, only with the "impure serpent." Thus Balaam did not say "Let me die the death of the righteous," but "Let my soul die," for his soul was death itself.

Regarding the matter of killing the Egyptian with the Explicit Name, I have explained the Midrash on Genesis, portion *Noach*: Rabbi Berechiah said, Moses is more beloved than Noah. Noah, after being called a "righteous man," was called a "man of the earth," but Moses, after being called...

It explains how Moses' life events and the names of his children serve as rectifications for ancient sins and the "confusion of languages" at the Tower of Babel.</summary>

# Tablets of the Covenant

Regarding this, he said: *By my openings I came to you.* <note>Reference to Song of Songs 7:14, often interpreted as the gates of the soul or reproductive openings.</note> It is through the power of the enticement by which Adam and Eve were enticed; it hints that the "drop" <note>Original: *tipah* (semen)</note> became foul, for if they had not sinned, the "knowing" of Adam would have been entirely holy. The matter of the **Covenant of the Member** <note>The organ of circumcision, representing the sanctification of procreation.</note> is holy to the Lord, like the laying of Phylacteries <note>Original: *Tefillin*</note> in its root above; for the world stands upon a single pillar, which is the **Righteous One, the Foundation of the World**, the secret of the Covenant. This is the secret of the Holy Covenant that procreates in His image.

However, after the sin, "they knew they were naked" and felt shame. The matter became "nakedness" <note>Original: *ervah*, implying both physical nakedness and sexual prohibition.</note> and required great protection. This was complicated by the clinging of the "External Forces" <note>Original: *Chitzoniyot*, the spiritual forces of impurity.</note>. Therefore, people did not merit the level of the **Glowing Lens** <note>Original: *Aspaklaria HaMe'irah*, a clear, direct prophetic vision attributed only to Moses.</note> that Moses reached. This is the secret of the "equality in prophecy," namely the seventy middle levels called "Personalities," which is the secret of the "Married Woman." <note>A Kabbalistic metaphor for a lower, bounded level of prophecy.</note>

It was said to him: *The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,* for they were all "rectifications" for the First Adam, as explained in several places. Afterward, Moses grew stronger and ascended from level to level to purify his physical matter, until he eventually separated from his wife. All this was to refine the matter of the "drop." Regarding this, it is said: *There has not arisen in Israel a prophet like Moses, and there shall not arise.* This represents an additional excellence even over the angels, who have no physical matter; he possessed physical matter yet refined it to the point that even his physical substance became intellect, and he acquired the "Light of his Face." This is what is meant by: "The Father was counted, and not only that, but he is greater," etc. Behold, his deeds were so great that he refined even the portion of the Father, and his mother was included with his father. Through this ascent, Moses was a prophet [greater than] other prophets.

In the aspect of the "Married Woman," he then grew and became "God-like." <note>Original: *Elohim*. In this context, it refers to a judge, master, or a divine spiritual rank rather than literal deity.</note> "There did not arise one like Moses," and his level of prophecy was evaluated. At first, it is written: *He is Aaron and Moses*, implying Aaron was equal or even greater than Moses because he was a prophet before Moses was. Therefore, the text praises Aaron and his son, who filled his place in the matter of marriage and matchmaking, for marriage below hints at marriage above; at that time, Aaron was truly greater than Moses. This is the meaning of "He is Aaron and Moses." But afterward, when Moses grew and "Moses ascended to God" to become God-like and finally separated from his wife—then it is "Moses and Aaron," with Moses preceding Aaron. May the greatness of Moses be praised for all the signs and wonders he performed.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, lowered and humbled the "Prince of Egypt" beneath his feet—Egypt being the firstborn and the chief of nations. Thus, Moses "gave to God." The matter of *See, I have made you* <note>Exodus 7:1, "I have made you a god to Pharaoh."</note> is like the matter of *See, I have given before you Sihon, King of the Amorites.* The Holy One, Blessed be He, cast down the Prince of the Amorites <note>The guardian angel/spiritual representative of that nation.</note> before Moses' feet. First over the "host of the height in the height," and then over the "kings of the earth on the earth." This is "See, I have made you," for behold, the Prince of Egypt is like a bird under your feet. He was a great and lofty Prince, as written at length in the Zohar on the verse *And a new king arose*—an "arising" occurred for him where he was strengthened, and the "Ministering Power of Egypt" stood up and was given strength and dominion over all other nations. For initially, that Prince above has dominion, and afterward, the nation below [gains] greatness.

Therefore, Moses ascended to the God-like level and subdued him. Israel ascended to become the "Hosts of the Lord" and to receive the Torah. In the beginning <note>Original: *Bereishit*</note>, they said: "For the sake of the Torah and for the sake of Israel." The Torah is called "the beginning of His way," and Israel is called "the beginning of His harvest." They also said: "For the sake of Moses," as it is said, *And he saw the beginning for himself.* I have already elaborated in many places that the Exodus from Egypt indicates the "Renewal of the World." Israel was refined there as in an "iron furnace" to remove the "filth of the serpent" from them and to become a "New World." Therefore, the matter was revealed: *In the beginning*—for the sake of Moses, for the sake of Israel, and all for the sake of the Torah given to Israel through Moses. Then the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired for His Presence <note>Original: *Shekhinah*</note> to be among the lower beings.
<margin>City and Name</margin>
The reason is a "Higher Need." <note>Original: *Tzorekh Gavoah*, the idea that human actions affect the divine realm.</note> The matter of the desire of the Name to rest His Presence among the lower beings is because Man includes both the lower and the upper realms. In his image and likeness, he includes the entire "Chain of Being," as explained in the book of Job in the introduction to *The Generations of Adam*, regarding the matter of the likeness, the image, and the inner essence of Man.

Even in his visible form, let us contemplate the unfolding of all worlds: The body corresponds to this lowly world; the Spirit and Soul <note>Original: *Nefesh* and *Neshamah*</note> correspond to the "World of the Spheres" <note>The celestial bodies/planets.</note> which possess movement; and the Vital Breath <note>Original: *Ruach*</note> corresponds to the "World of Angels," as it is said: *He makes His angels spirits.* The High Soul <note>Original: *Neshamah*</note> corresponds to the "World of Emanation" <note>Original: *Atzilut*, the highest of the four worlds in Kabbalah.</note> where the Lord dwells. Therefore, the Perfect Man is a dwelling for the Divine Presence and clings to the secret of the "Supernal Man" who is upon the Throne, in the secret of "Likeness and Image."

And behold, "God made one corresponding to the other," for there is a "Wicked Man" from the side of the "Husks" <note>Original: *Kelippot*, forces of evil.</note>, and he is like "a monkey before a human." Israel is called "Man" <note>Original: *Adam*</note> because they are in the secret of the "Inner Man." The "Wicked Man" [of the nations] has no portion in the God Above, heaven forbid, while Moses is "the cord of His inheritance." But the nations are placed under the "Constellations," and over them is the Lord. The Prince of Egypt is the first Prince and is taller than them all.

Regarding this, there is a hint in a statement by our Sages of blessed memory which is very wondrous. It is found in the Tractate Sotah: *Rav Avital said in the name of Rav: The Pharaoh who was in the days of Moses was one cubit tall, his beard was one cubit, and his "appendage" was a cubit and a span, to fulfill what is written: 'And He sets up over it the lowliest of men.'* Behold, this statement cries out for interpretation! Heaven forbid we should say it was not so according to the plain meaning, for no scripture or word of the Sages loses its plain meaning. However, I will tell you hints as to why the Creator created him in this form and measure.

I already said that Man includes the entire Chain of Being. But he who is like a "monkey before a human" has no power except in this world. Afterward, they are revolved there with extra substance, for the "Host of Heaven" was allotted by the Lord to the nations, and their roots are in the essence of their constellation. The lower part is the "Husk," the "Exterior," and the "Armor" from which comes their vital breath; from there came the sorceries that were in Egypt. Behold, for every "god-like power" there is a measure and a limit, but for Israel—
<margin>70 Holy Fastenings</margin>
—there are seventy holy fastenings in the "God-like" name <note>Original: *Elohim*</note>, a cleaving. This is what I mean by "In my going out," it has no end or limit. Therefore, the Hand of the Lord spoke of "a cubit, a cubit, a cubit," meaning the "Man of the Building." For all of them have a measure, and a finite measure to say that it is "six handbreadths." How so? His body was one cubit, because his body corresponds to This World, as I wrote. Behold, This World diminishes and goes until it is one cubit. This world is a journey of 500 years, which is 26 days, each day being ten parashangs <note>Ancient unit of distance.</note>, each parashang four miles, and each mile two thousand cubits. And a cubit is the handbreadths of a man. Just as a cubit has six handbreadths, so the world has six days of creation and shall stand for six thousand years.

He said "his beard was a cubit"—this corresponds to the "World of the Spheres," the western ones, for its measure also ends at a cubit. A journey of 500 cubits from the earth to the firmament, and between each firmament a journey of 500, and so between every firmament. A cubit is six handbreadths; so too the Constellations are twelve signs—six above the earth and six below. Behold, they hinted that the head of a man is the dwelling of power. In the True Man, the power is a "Chariot" for his soul. But in the nations, it is a Chariot for the "Husks." Afterward, the beard which is on the head represents the sparks that exit and are birthed. Pharaoh was very much attached to the Constellations, for the first [Prince] is very high in the constellations, and his service is "Labor," as is known. Therefore, all the power of the sparks spreading to him is from the side of the Constellations. Thus, the hairs of his beard exiting and spreading from the head hint at the spreading of the types of celestial influences, which have a limit. This is "his beard was a cubit."

"His appendage was a cubit and a span" <note>Original: *Amah ve-Zeret*</note>—this hints at the power of his Prince. This matter requires an introduction: Man was created to be in the "Likeness and Image," so to speak, of the "Supernal Man" upon the Throne. Behold, the body was commanded regarding "fruiting and multiplying," as it is written: *And God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply,"* to be a human making a human, so to speak, just as the Supernal Man upon the Throne created the Lower Man. Had he not sinned and clothed himself in the "filth of the serpent," there would be no "nakedness" (shame). On the contrary, the act of fruiting and multiplying would have been like laying Tefillin or other practical commandments. The flow of seed coming from the brain to make a human is in the likeness of Creation. Only afterward, when he clothed himself in the "filth of the serpent," did it become "nakedness."

The Israelites are holy, and they must sanctify themselves during intimacy, as explained elsewhere at length. He who sanctifies himself is "Holy Seed," and it will be said of him according to the measure of his holiness. Moses was so sanctified that even the portion he had from his father and mother was refined, as mentioned above, and he became a "Glowing Lens." But the Princes of the nations—their flow comes from the power of the serpent; they are from the side of "nakedness." The Prince of Egypt is the first, and his nation below, the Egyptians, were "steeped in lewdness," with "the flesh of donkeys and the emission of horses," for the darkness and the power of nakedness are there. Egypt is the "Nakedness of the Land."

He said "he was a cubit" because even though they are spiritual, they have a dwelling. For our Sages gave a measure even to the angels, as seen in Tractate Chullin, chapter *Gid Ha-Nasheh*: "We have learned that an angel is two thousand parashangs." Even if there is some secret in their measures, nonetheless, the concept of "measure" remains. And behold, it all ends at a cubit. A cubit has six handbreadths, corresponding to the "six wings"—*six wings for each one*—and these unfold one from another until the Princes of the nations. The Princes of the nations, the power of their influence is in the Constellations, which are the Host of Heaven, and it is written: *And the heavens He gauged with a span.* <note>Isaiah 40:12</note> This is why it says "his appendage was a cubit and a span," hinting at his Prince who influences the Host of Heaven.

But we say that the path of Israel reaches the "Supernal Head." Generally, a man is three cubits tall excluding the head, as the Tosafot wrote in Tractate Shabbat, chapter *Ha-Matznia*. Thus, the three cubits are the "Three Worlds," and afterward the Head, in which the brain is a "Chariot" for the soul, which corresponds to the world where the Lord dwells. So it is with the Children of Israel and their cleaving to the Lord—it is "in my going out" without measure. But the nations of the world, even though their form is like the form of Israel, they are "like a monkey before a human," as it is written: "and they err toward the Supernal Head." They are the "lowliest of men," which is why it says *And He sets up over it the lowliest of men.* But Israel are the "Men" who sit in the secret of "Adam," and Israel are called "Adam." Let us return to the matter: Moses, on his mission from the Creator, revealed to him [Pharaoh] that there is one "High over the High," and He is the name **Y-H-W-H**, the Leader, who provides the reward and directs the Constellations, for He is the essence of all and watches over all, and He **is able**—

# Written Torah: Exodus

->313<-

Tomorrow this sign shall come to pass, namely the letter *Vav* <note>The letter Vav (ו) often symbolizes connection or the physical world in mystical thought.</note>, which will be filled with fruit and also redemption. He said that this sign is like "this" <note>original Hebrew: *zot* (זאת)</note>, hinting at a matter where the "small gematria" <note>A system where double digits are reduced to single digits (e.g., 10 becomes 1).</note> of *zot* equals the same as "and the crushed" <note>original: *v'dach* (וד"ך)</note>.
It also equals seven, representing two combinations of the Name of God <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>, that "the Lord shall be one and His name One." It is written: "As in the days of your coming out of Egypt, I will show him wonders" <note>Micah 7:15</note>. However, the exodus from Egypt will be
secondary, and the final redemption will be the primary one. Then He will truly arise "so that I may set these signs of Mine" <note>Exodus 10:1</note>. Let us return to the matter of the "clothing" of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the indwelling presence of God</term> in the darkness; this is a great elevation for the darkness.
But afterward, it is overturned to rule over it for evil and to subdue it, as mentioned above. This concerns the Ministering Angel <term>Sar: a heavenly prince or guardian angel of a nation</term> and the moment of the strike, darkening him, lowering him, and subduing him, as it is said: "How long will you refuse..." <note>Exodus 10:3</note>.
What was said regarding the Ministering Angel of Egypt is understood: for when the Prince is at the height of his greatness, he is not mentioned in the letters. "From a high roof he falls into a deep pit," and the very "clothing" that caused him
greatness now causes him to be inherited by the heavens and the sky. He, Blessed be He, knows the time and the moment to strike, to darken him, to humble him, and to subdue him, as it says: "How long will you refuse
to humble yourself before Me?" The matter of subduing is to turn from evil to good, similar to the matter of Samael <note>The guardian angel of Esau, often associated with the accuser.</note>, the Prince of Esau, who admitted to the blessings. This is the secret of "finding favor in the eyes of the people" to fulfill
"and they despoiled Egypt." In the end, Pharaoh said, "and bless me also," for you are the essence of blessing, and from your blessings, I too shall be blessed. This is the secret of what Pharaoh said: "Not
so," for a curse issued from his mouth when he said, "Look, evil is before your faces" <note>Exodus 10:10</note>. But a "bad angel" answered against his will and said "not so"—meaning, it shall not be as I said. "Blood" <note>Hebrew: *dam* (דם), found in the word "evil" (*ra'ah*)</note> that I
see refers to the evil, but on the contrary, it points to the good, which is the blood of circumcision. This is the hint of "not so." And even though Pharaoh did not intend this, nevertheless, many
times a word leaves a person's mouth and he does not know how far the power of that word reaches, for it is from the Mouth of the Most High. I found something close to this in the book *Kanfei Yonah* <note>original: "Wings of a Dove," a kabbalistic work.</note>, section 68, as follows:
"Look, evil is before your faces"—the word "not" <note>Hebrew: *lo* (לא)</note> has the numerical value (71) of "Michael," who was judged there. There, in Pharaoh's mouth, was the annulment of his curse. When this evil angel Pharaoh was transformed into a messenger of Michael,
and said "not so," then the letters *Yod-Daled* <note>Representing the Hand of God</note> of Michael were added to that angel to transform the ten names of *Eh-yeh* <note>"I Will Be," a name of God</note> which equal 540, the numerical value of "this" <note>original: *az* (א"ז)</note>. The six words of "Look-evil-is-before-your-faces-not"
equal the numerical value of "mercy upon Israel," for they are also the numerical value of "the blessing of Abraham." End of quote.

**And from now on** the verses and the discourse shall be explained based on what I prefaced: two things draw vows
and freewill offerings among Israel...
Regarding what is written in the portion of *Balak* on the verse: "Behold, a people that dwells alone and is not reckoned among the nations." When the nations are in distress, there is
no nation that rejoices with them, as it says: "The Lord alone did lead him." But when the nations are in a good state, they [Israel] eat with everyone,
yet they do not enter into the accounting. This is "is not reckoned among the nations." End of quote. So is the matter of sacrifices from
gentiles and freewill offerings of gentiles that Israel offers. Behold, through sacrifices, they are drawn closer to
the Holy. And because there is an "eagle" <note>A metaphor for spiritual protection or elevation</note> above in the holiness, bringing down abundance from above, and the power of that abundance
also flows to Israel and they rejoice with them. However, the awakening caused by the sacrifices of Israel, who sacrifice
themselves in their inner essence and their actions above—this is what is "reserved for them in the future," a physical eternity
which has no value or measure and is unattainable, regarding which it is said: "No eye has seen, O God, besides You." End of quote from *Heishar*, *Zohar*, and *Hechai*.

Upon this, the verses shall be explained: "And Pharaoh called to Moses and said, 'Go, serve the Lord.'"
This is as explained above. Moses our teacher replied: "You must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings
that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God." That is to say, through vows and freewill offerings from yours that we sacrifice in Your Name to the Lord our God, then
you will strengthen us, for we also have a portion in this abundance, and thus we benefit from this abundance. "Our livestock also
shall go with us," meaning that which constitutes our sacrifices, this shall go with us to the World to Come. And he said "shall go with us" because with us it is
specifically "The Lord alone did lead him." Afterward, he said: "not a hoof shall be left." This hints at the firstborn of darkness, who is
the firstborn of the hour, the Prince of Esau. And behold, he has a permanent sign: the "hoof," in which there is a grip
on holiness, for it is known that Esau is called a "pig." As it is said: "the boar from the forest ravages it" <note>Psalm 80:14</note>. And the pig "stretches out its hooves"
as if to say: "See, I am a pig that possesses a cloven hoof" <note>Midrashic reference to the pig showing its hooves to appear kosher/pure.</note>. And your sign is "his hand holding the heel of Esau," for in the hoof of
Esau there is a sign of purity, "cloven-footed." And regarding this, he said "not a hoof shall be left of him," for "from it
we must take to serve the Lord our God." This is in the way mentioned above regarding the Prince of Egypt: "You must also give
into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God." So it is said here regarding the Prince of Esau: "not a hoof shall be left,"
meaning the cloven hoof shall not be left entirely rejected for being completely wicked; rather, "from it we shall take to serve
the Lord our God," for we benefit from this as well. But the abundance that comes from the essence of
our sacrifices is the greatness of knowledge. And this is why "our service—we do not know until we arrive there," for
we cannot grasp the greatness of the spirituality, for "no eye has seen, O God, besides You," and we shall not know until we arrive
there. And this is hinted at in the Midrash: "Do not be like a pit that is not present from ours at all," meaning do not let it
enter your mind that we shall eat from our sacrifice, for we have no portion in this world from the great spiritual reward,
only from what you have "from it shall we take," namely from what we sacrifice in Your Name. But that which
we sacrifice for ourselves—that is "no eye has seen," etc. And we shall not know or grasp this until we arrive
there. May it be His will that we merit eternal attachment, as it is said: "One thing I have asked of the Lord, that I will seek:
that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord and to visit His temple. Amen."

### Way of Life: Moral Reproof

**Way of Life: Moral Reproof.** "And you shall guard the *matzot*" <note>Exodus 12:17</note>, etc.
Rashi wrote: "Guard the *matzot*" so that they do not come to a state of leavening <note>original: *chimutz* (חמוץ)</note>. From here they said: "A detached piece of dough in cold water..." Rabbi Josiah
says: "Do not read it as *hamatzot* (the unleavened bread) but as *hamitzvot* (the commandments)." In the same way that one does not let the *matzah* become leavened, so one should not let a *mitzvah* <term>Mitzvah: a divine commandment or good deed</term> become "leavened." Rather, if a commandment comes to your hand, do not
delay it; perform it immediately. End of quote. There is an inquiry here: Behold, in this portion, it speaks of the matters of Passover and *matzot*, so how does it hint at commandments in general? See, Josiah explains
this verse of "And you shall guard the commandments" as not letting the commandment "sour" but doing them immediately. On the contrary, we find the word "guarding" <note>original: *shmirah* (שמירה)</note> elsewhere whose meaning is the opposite—namely, waiting, as in "and his father kept <note>original: *shamar*</note> the matter in mind" <note>Genesis 37:11</note>,
which means he waited for the matter. See, accept the reading, for in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, it is implied that there is some proof in the scripture not to read it that way. And what
is the proof? The commentators have already elaborated on the hint of leaven (*chametz*) and *matzah*—that they represent the two inclinations. Leaven is the fermenting dough, and the yeast is the "yeast in the dough."
For the body of a man is like dough, and the combination of place and water creates the human as a whole. And this Evil Inclination is the leaven in the dough. But the *matzah* is the Good Inclination, which causes
a person to be humble and not "rise up" high like leavened bread. And then he is humbled before his Creator and does not come to sin. This is the concept of "turning away from evil and doing good," and walking [in God's ways].

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Ten Commandments, specifically focusing on the mystical and kabbalistic meanings of the first few utterances. It transitions from the general experience of the Israelites at Sinai to a letter-by-letter analysis of the word "Anochi" (I am).</meta>

**Written Torah - Portions of Exodus**
Manuscript: P A 80 I Israel

**These words** the Lord spoke to your entire congregation and placed them in writing on two stone tablets; for just as He spoke them to your entire congregation, so He wrote them upon the tablets. Now, I will explain to you some of the <term>Sod</term><note>The mystical or "secret" level of Torah interpretation.</note> provided by our Sages, of blessed memory, in clarifying the Commandments. "Israel heard from the mouth of the Almighty" is meant according to the literal sense of the scripture. However, regarding the rest of the words of the Commandments that were said: they would hear the utterance and understand it from Him just as Moses understood it. Therefore, He speaks with them as a master speaks to his servant, as I have mentioned. From that point onward, regarding the rest of the Commandments, they would hear the sound of the speech but not understand it, and Moses would need to translate every single utterance for them until they truly understood it. This is the end of his quote.

However, according to what was written, it is literal: the first time, they heard all ten Commandments at once. The second time, when they were detailed, they only heard "I am" and "You shall have no other." It appears that this was the intention of Rashi, who wrote: "All these words—this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said all ten Commandments in a single utterance, something impossible for a human being to say." If so, why does the verse then specify "I am" and "You shall have no other"? Because He went back and detailed each commandment individually. 

At first glance, this is puzzling: why ask "why does it say 'I am' and 'You shall have no other'"? Do we not need to be informed what the ten Commandments spoken in one utterance actually were? Rather, Rashi is hinting at the teaching of our Sages that "I am" and "You shall have no other" were heard directly from the mouth of the Almighty. The difficulty is that we already said *all* the words were heard from the Almighty since they were said in one utterance! To this, he explains that it refers to when He went back and detailed them.

The concept of "One" is hinted at in the word **I am** <note>Hebrew: *Anochi*</note> according to a squared calculation: 1 times 1, 8 times 8, and 10 times 10. This sum equals the numerical value of "I am" <note>This is a mystical gematria calculation where the squares of 1, 8, and 10 ($1 + 64 + 100$) equal 165. The author likely links this to a specific spelling or expansion of the word "Anochi."</note>. Behold, "one" does not multiply, for 1 times 1 remains 1, hinting at the Absolute Unity, as I wrote previously.

Thus, the word **I am** is clarified, along with its four letters as I have explained. The collective word "Anochi," which includes four letters, hints at the hidden and the concealed: at the Absolute Source, hidden in the ultimate concealment, from which everything originates. He is the Cause of all causes and the Reason for all reasons, who is not called by any name except by a hint toward His concealment—that is, the Infinite (*Ein Sof*)—and is defined by Necessary Existence.

Its beginning is the <term>Tetragrammaton</term><note>The four-letter name of God, Y-H-V-H.</note>, which includes the "Brotherhood" of all things, upper and lower. This is the chain of the four worlds: Atziluth (Emanation), Beriah (Creation), Yetzirah (Formation), and Assiyah (Action). In Atziluth, this is the secret of the Hidden Chariot, four corresponding to the four letters of the Name: Kindness (*Chesed*), Strength (*Gevurah*), Beauty (*Tiferet*), and Kingship (*Malchut*). In the World of Beriah, there are four pillars. And there are the four Living Creatures (*Chayot*) that carry the Throne: the Human, the Ox, the Eagle, and the Lion. In the World of Yetzirah, there are the four camps of the Divine Presence: Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael. In the World of Assiyah, there are the four elements. The Patriarchs themselves are the Chariot: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob corresponding to Kindness, Strength, and Beauty, while David is the fourth leg of the Chariot, representing the Kingdom of the House of David.

# You shall have no other gods before Me
This speaks to the lower realms but hints at the upper realms, and everything goes to one place in the secret of the Name of the Lord. The Essential Name speaks below, prohibiting all worship except to the Lord alone. It forbids the worship of angels, stars, and constellations, which are not gods, as Nachmanides elaborated in his commentary.

Nachmanides wrote, based on the Midrash and the Zohar, that the beginning of the lapse into idolatry was actually for the sake of Heaven. People thought that through the moving constellations, the decree of the Master could be known—for the servant of a king is also a "king," and if we honor the servant, how much more so are we honoring the Master? This began in the generation of Enosh, when they started calling the worship of angels by the name of the Lord—meaning, for the sake of the Lord's inheritance. Afterward, this spread into worshiping the "hosts of heaven" until they fell into the error of not understanding, eventually worshiping physical idols.

Therefore, the Torah warned us not to worship other gods even if they possess "godliness"—meaning a great power, like the angels who are princes over the nations. The point is that one cannot say "the greatness of the servant reflects the greatness of the Master," for this only applies to a flesh-and-blood king whose peers derive power from him and whose kingdom depends on them, since they could replace him. But He, may He be blessed, is the Essential Foundation. All existence was brought into being from Him; they depend on Him, but He does not depend on them. He exists forever even if they were to be nullified. This is what is meant by "You shall have no other gods **before Me**" (*al panai*). Our Sages interpreted this to mean "as long as I exist." 

One might ask: why is this written here more than anywhere else in the Torah? The intention of the Sages regarding "before Me" is a hint that He is eternally existent; if so, no power is ever nullified in His presence, nor does the power of created beings nullify His existence. This was written here to explain why we should not serve other gods or follow the commands of those who worship stars and constellations. It says that regarding the Blessed One, this does not apply, for they depend on Him but He does not depend on them; He alone is eternally existent. Furthermore, "before Me" hints that "the Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance."

"Other gods" are the portion the Lord assigned to all the other nations. The matter is that we are very closely attached to the Lord, "Face to Face" (*Panim el Panim*), as it says: "The Lord spoke with you face to face." However, there is a "face to the face" that is seen, but also a "back," and a "back of the back" in the mystery of the spread of existence, until "God made one corresponding to the other." There, on the "Left Side" (*Sitra de-Smala*), the nations are attached to their gods. All the wise men of the nations and their kingdoms know that "there is none like You, O Lord," and our Sages said that they call Him "the God of gods." But they cling to the "back" of the emanations. Israel, however, is on the inside, attached to the inner holiness. This is the meaning of "before Me"—since you are attached to My "Face" (*Panimi*).

There is also a great secret in this and a hint to the higher realms, regarding the secret of the Tetragrammaton which includes all of Emanation (*Atziluth*): that it should not even enter one's thought that there is any god besides Him. That is to say, the power of the Emanator, the Infinite (*Ein Sof*), is the source of the godliness indicated by the Name. This is hinted at in "You shall have no..."—referring to the secret of Godhood. 

Another interpretation of "before Me" is like saying "Before the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He." He is the "Building" that includes them: Beauty (*Tiferet*), which is the Holy One, Blessed be He; the "Kings" of Wisdom and Understanding (*Chokhmah* and *Binah*); and the "King" of the Crown (*Keter*). "Before Me" hints at the "running and returning" <note>A reference to Ezekiel's vision of the Chariot, signifying the pulse of divine energy.</note> toward the Infinite that precedes them. The words of our Sages are all "sparks of holy grace," as they said: "that it should not enter one's thought that there is another god"—meaning even the Highest Thought, which is the Crown (*Keter*), is not a god apart from the Cause of all causes, the Emanator who brought forth the emanated beings, which are bound to Him like a chain in the Lord's inheritance, and all is one, single and unique.

## You shall not make
for yourself a carved image or any likeness. "Likeness" (*Temunah*) refers to the Kingdom (*Malchut*), the likeness of the Tetragrammaton, and of it, it is said: "he beholds the likeness of the Lord." As the Kabbalists wrote, specifically the Recanati: "I have already informed you that the actions of those below affect those above." Anyone who makes a carved image or a likeness is "cutting the plantings" <note>A metaphor for heresy or causing a rift in the divine unity.</note> and separating himself from the Divine Building. It says "Do not make *for yourself*," but in the Sanctuary, where the Name of the Lord resides, the two Cherubim were permitted. They hint at the "Two Faces" <note>The male and female aspects of the divine emanations.</note>, for then they are in the Unity of the Name. They wrote that "likeness" refers to the human face, which is the secret of "the beauty of a man."

## You shall not bow down
to them. Every act of bowing hints at bringing down divine flow from above to below; this is the meaning of bending the head downward. Even though the nations draw down influence, they are bowing to "vanity and emptiness" because they are at His "back" and the "back of the back." We, however, bow before the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He. Bowing is like the "Face to Face" service mentioned above, for we are in the presence of the Face.

## You shall not serve them
in the manner of their worship. It is forbidden even if the manner of worship is disgraceful, such as uncovering oneself before Peor or throwing a stone at Merkolis <note>Mercury/Hermes</note>. Since that is the way it is worshiped, it gives a foothold to the "Left Side" (*Sitra de-Smala*). One must distance oneself from vomit and filth, for "your camp shall be holy"—meaning the 248 limbs and 365 sinews of a person must be a camp for the Lord your God.

## You shall not take the name of the Lord your God
The Recanati wrote: "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, etc. Know that one who swears in vain 'cuts the plantings.' This is the reason for 'You shall not take' rather than 'You shall not swear'—meaning, do not remove the 'Bridegroom' from his power... for the Lord will not clear [the guilty]." For when the union is perfect, it is written "she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed." He who breaks this causes the "will not clear." These are his words. An oath (*Shevuah*) touches the Name of the Lord, specifically the aspect of Beauty (*Tiferet*), which is the sum of the "Building" of the seven upper days; therefore, "oath" (*Shevuah*) is from the word "seven" (*Sheva*). I have elaborated on this further in the book *Me'or* on the tractate of Shevuot, and in *Torah Or*, in the section called "Torah-Tiferet."

## Remember
the Sabbath day to sanctify it. The Sabbath indicates the Name of the Lord: He was, He is, and He will be. He gives life to everything, for He gives life to the world "something from nothing." "Remember" (*Zakhor*) and "Observe" (*Shamur*) were said in a single utterance. In "Remember," the creation of the world is written; in "Observe," the Exodus from Egypt is written, where the Name of the Lord was made known as the Renewer and the Almighty. Regarding the commandment to "Remember," one should remember it over wine, for the Sabbath points toward the "World that is entirely Sabbath," which we will merit in the World to Come through the power of keeping the Sabbath in this world. The Sabbath of the World to Come is the secret of Understanding (*Binah*), which is known as the World to Come, and there is the "wine preserved in its grapes," as I have explained at length elsewhere. This is the secret of remembering it over wine.

## You shall not
do any work. Behold, 39 "Categories of Labor" (*Avot Melakhot*) are forbidden. Rabbi Menachem of Babylon wrote that these 39 labors correspond to the 39 lashes that would have been given to Israel...

It also interprets the Sabbath and the prohibition of oaths through the lens of the Sefirot.</summary>
