# The mystical secret of the Sabbatical year, the Sabbath, and the stages of each is explained in its primary place.
## The first fruits of your land: the secret of the First Fruits will be explained in the Torah portion of *Bikkurim* <note>First Fruits</note>.

**The reason for the prohibition of meat and milk:** The Recanati <note>Menachem Recanati, a 13th-century Italian kabbalist</note> wrote that this is the secret of *Kilayim* <note>forbidden mixtures</note>, as it mixes higher spiritual powers. The intent is that meat, which is red, stems from the power of *Din* <note>Strict Judgment</note>, while milk stems from the side of *Rachamim* <note>Mercy</note>. □ The Recanati expanded on this further; see also the book of Rabbeinu Bahya <note>Bahya ben Asher, 13th-century Spanish commentator</note> regarding what he wrote on the matter of meat and milk.

After the discussions of civil laws and judgments were concluded, the verse says: *Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way* <note>Exodus 23:20</note>. □ In the *Midrash Rabbah*, it is taught: *The angel of the Lord camps around those who fear Him and delivers them* <note>Psalm 34:8</note>. If a person performs one *mitzvah* <note>commandment</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him one angel to guard him, as it says: "The angel of the Lord camps..." If he performs two commandments, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him two angels to guard him, as it says: *For He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways* <note>Psalm 91:11</note>. □ If he performs many commandments, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him half of His heavenly camp, as it says: *A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand* <note>Psalm 91:7</note>, and this constitutes half of His camp, as it says: *God’s chariots are myriads, thousands upon thousands* <note>Psalm 68:18</note>. Thus far the Midrash. □ This is difficult, for there is no number to the heavenly host, and they cannot be measured! However, regarding the verse "God’s chariots are myriads," these are not merely types, but also... □ Therefore, you will find the secret of the legal judgments in the giving of the number ten (*Yud*), and when the letter *Yud* is spelled out in full <note>The letter Yud (י) spelled as Yud-Vav-Dalet equals 20</note>, it is like the two utterances, which are the full *Yud* amounting to twenty. This relates to what the *Zohar* says on the verse *Ten gold shekels by the sanctuary weight* <note>Numbers 7:14</note>, for the complete shekel is twenty, and the half-shekel is ten. The matter is that there are Ten Utterances <note>with which the world was created</note> and corresponding to them are the Ten Commandments, which are intertwined with one another and repeated together as twenty, which is the letter *Kaf* <note>numerical value 20</note>. This is the "Holy Shekel," the complete weight. This is the reason for the commandment of the half-shekel, for the tenth is divided into ten. Now, the Master <note>likely referring to a specific Kabbalistic authority</note>, in the discourse he wrote dividing the commandments, is in the portion of *Mishpatim*; it is appropriate to speak of his subject. Let us return to the matter of the legal judgments, for they are in the secret of ten, namely the letter *Yud*, and the secret of "opposite" and "opposite" <note>Hebrew: *mul*</note>. Thus, the letter *Yud* spelled out equals 100. □ How so?...

The Talmudic sages said the reason for this number <note>of judges</note> is because it is written: *The congregation shall judge and the congregation shall save* <note>Numbers 35:24-25</note>. There must be a judging congregation and a saving congregation, and one must add more power to decide the case. They mentioned that for acquittal, a majority of one is sufficient, but for conviction, it must be a majority of two. If so, one must add two, and even this is not enough... but the essence is ten against ten: a judging congregation (the scale of guilt) and a saving congregation (the scale of merit), and both are unified in the secret of the letter *Yud*. Now we shall explain well the secret of *Yud*. It is found in this discourse of "Behold, I send..." that there is a chain of tens throughout all the worlds: in *Beriah* <note>Creation</note>, *Yetzirah* <note>Formation</note>, and *Asiyah* <note>Action</note>, as mentioned at length in the *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moses Cordovero</note> in the section on the Four Worlds (*ABY"A*) and the *Sefirot*. The Throne, which is the world of *Beriah*, has six steps and four supports <note>totaling ten</note>. □ In *Yetzirah*, the world of angels, there are ten classes. In *Asiyah*, the spheres are nine □ plus the Active Intellect, making ten. In the counting of the higher powers that move them according to the will of their Creator... □ *Atzilut* <note>Emanation</note> and *Beriah* <note>Creation</note> are in total unity, and it is impossible for *Atzilut* to be revealed except through *Beriah*. In this, the Throne is complete in its intellect. Therefore, the secret is hinted at in the full spelling—that is, *Atzilut* and the four of *Beriah*—and everything is unified.

However, the two other worlds <note>Yetzirah and Asiyah</note>, which are also ten, are like a shadow to the first *Yud*. □ Man was made in the "Image of God" (*Tzelem Elohim*); he has ten fingers and ten toes, totaling twenty. □ There is a hint in his being: there are three partners in man—the Holy One, Blessed be He, his father, and his mother. They counted ten things that the Holy One gives, which are spiritual—the soul and speech—while those given by the father and mother are physical and material, created to serve in the work of the Torah and commandments. □ Thus, at the Giving of the Torah, through the secret of the Ten Commandments which correspond to the Ten Utterances, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him: "Grasp My Throne." ... Regarding the Throne, the Holy One said: *God’s chariots are myriads, thousands upon thousands*. □ To understand this, one must first present what the Kabbalists wrote regarding the "Small Number" <note>*Mispar Katan*</note>, which is the side of Enoch-Metatron, who is "Small" <note>*Ze'ir*</note>, found in the secret of the first Ten—that is, *Atzilut* and *Beriah* in their perfection... until the totality reaches ten thousand (*Revavah*). For both of them, it is two myriads. It is found that from *Yetzirah* downwards... namely *Yetzirah* and *Asiyah*, they are "two thousands" in the secret of the Small Number. The Blessed Name, at the Giving of the Torah, revealed Himself in the secret of two myriads—*Atzilut* and *Beriah*—and you, along with the ministering angels, also increased the heavens (the spheres) to the earth... □ in the secret of two thousands. This is the meaning of: *God’s chariots are myriads (two myriads), thousands (two thousands) upon thousands*. And of man it is said: *If a man lives a thousand years twice over* <note>Ecclesiastes 6:6</note>. It is difficult; it should have said "two thousand years." □ But first you must know that the three levels of Speech, Thought, and Action correspond to the secret of *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* <note>the three parts of the soul</note>, which are *Asiyah*, *Yetzirah*, and *Beriah*, as explained in the *Zohar*, the books of the Kabbalists, and the book *Reshit Chochmah*. We will speak at length in the section on Action regarding the fact that action and speech correspond to the *Nefesh*; study (*Talmud*) rises higher and clings to *Yetzirah* and the *Ruach*; □ and thought rises even further to *Beriah* in the secret of the *Neshamah*, which returns to God, for it is hewn from beneath the Throne of Glory. □ However, the "People of Ascent" <note>elite spiritual individuals</note>, who are few, rise even to the "Thought of Thought," which is the *Nefesh*, *Ruach*, and *Neshamah* in the secret of *Atzilut*. □ The author of the discourse on "Behold, I send an angel" is speaking of the majority of the world... in the branches of *Asiyah*, *Yetzirah*, and *Beriah*. When a man does one commandment, it does not mean a single specific deed, but rather one "category"—meaning he merits a *Neshamah*, and one angel is given to him, which is the spiritual aspect of *Asiyah* known as Sandalphon. If he does two commandments—meaning two categories, such as study and action—two angels are given to him, including *Yetzirah*, which is Metatron. These two are the secret of the letter *Yud* spelled out... as mentioned above. It says "if he did two commandments" and not "if he does"... □ rather, study leads to action, and immediately when he studies, it is considered as if he has acted. □ Likewise, with many commandments that a person cannot physically fulfill, such as the laws of the Priesthood if he is not a Priest, the study leads to action; when he learns them, it is considered as if he did them... □ And it said: for one commandment, one angel is given. □ This is the matter of: *Even if there is over him one interceding angel out of a thousand* <note>Job 33:23</note>. If he does another commandment—another category like study—then he has two angels, which are two thousand, the "thousands" mentioned in the verse "God’s chariots..." □ If he does many commandments, this is the secret of Thought, for deep study and repetition include everything, and spirituality is without end; then he rises to *Beriah*, which is "half His camp." As mentioned, the essence of the letter *Yud* spelled out represents the Name and the Throne, His camp. Thus, *Beriah* is half the camp, which is one myriad (*Revavah*). He brings the verse: *A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand (Revavah) at your right hand*. It is written: *Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor* <note>Proverbs 3:16</note>. Riches and honor here refer to study and action—the richness of study and the honor of deeds. All this is included in the Left, relative to Thought, which is in the Right, as it is written: *A wise man's heart is at his right* <note>Ecclesiastes 10:2</note>, and *Pleasures are in Your right hand forever* <note>Psalm 16:11</note>. □ Of the Left it is said: *His left hand is under my head* <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>, for the head is the place of Thought, and the Left is beneath it. Now, from the side of the aforementioned riches and honor, which are called the Left, they are the secret of the Thousands that fall... even though the Holy One gives him an angel to guard him. □ And if he has two commandments, He gives him two thousand; and the "ten thousand" (*Revavah*) is at your Right, from the side of Thought, reaching the myriad which is half the camp. □ As for what is written: *The Lord is your shadow upon your right hand* <note>Psalm 121:5</note>, implying a shadow exists even in the half-camp, this is not a difficulty... from the power of your great merit above on the side of the Right, which is the myriad, or the Holy One Himself is your shadow. □ Just as the Midrash says on the vision: *The Lord is your shadow*. □ Just as a shadow—if you smile at it, it smiles back at you; if you weep toward it, it weeps toward you; if you show it a grim or angry face, it gives you the same—so is the Holy One, the Lord is your shadow: just as you behave with Him, He behaves toward you... from the higher awakening. □ This is from the side of the great height and loftiness that the Groom has, which is for the Lord, to awaken the Supernal. □ Further, it can be said: the "shadow" refers to the moons—namely, *Yetzirah* and *Asiyah* along with them in the secret of the "thousands." This shadow is like the "shadow of a shadow" mentioned by Rabbeinu Bahya of blessed memory. But the shadow of *Beriah* is: *He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High shall abide in the shadow of the Almighty* <note>Psalm 91:1</note>.

And regarding the aforementioned Right, there is a hint: *The right hand of the Lord is exalted; the right hand of the Lord does valiantly*...

The author of *The Man* <note>original: "HaAdam," likely referring to a specific Kabbalistic work or the "Primordial Man" discourse</note> wrote as follows: "And now that you know the structure of the human form, you can understand—if you have received the truth of the prophetic vision through oral tradition—what the prophets saw. Our Sages, of blessed memory, called this vision **The Measure of the Stature** <term>Shi'ur Qomah<note>A mystical concept describing the metaphorical dimensions of the Divine presence in the world.</note></term>. This is the 'Secret of the Creator' about which one sings: 'The Creator of the Beginning.' Concerning this, the Scripture says, *'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,'* and regarding this vision it is said, *'And by the hand of the prophets I have used parables.'*" Until here are his words.

The pious author of *Ha-Katzah* added: If you have received the truth of the prophetic vision from mouth to mouth, you know this tradition depends on five external factors. The first is the "Image of God," which consists of the Ten <note>The Ten Sefirot, or Divine emanations</note>. It is called thus because it is a **mirror** <term>Ispaklariya<note>A visionary lens or looking-glass.</note></term> that receives all the other mirrors above it. Within it are six chambers, one chamber for each attribute of the "Building" <note>The six emotional Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>. No human has ever ascended from there and higher, except that every prophet perceived from the chamber appropriate to his spiritual level. But Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, ascended above them all until he reached the **Chamber of Will**.

Of him it is said: *'And he beholds the image of the Lord.'* He beheld the image of the Lord because none of the chambers were hidden from him. Just as one sees his own image in a sapphire-like mirror, so too in this mirror called the "Image of the Lord," every individual would perceive through it according to their own level within that chamber. Each saw according to their attainment; some saw through one partition, some through two, and some through three. The general rule is that the partitions multiplied according to the limitations of the perceiver. One whose soul assisted him and whose inner senses were refined needed only a thin partition to see through the **Luminous Mirror** <term>Ispaklariya HaMe'ira<note>The highest level of prophecy, attributed solely to Moses.</note></term>, which is like the sun in its full strength. But one whose intellectual eyes were weak needed many partitions to look at that light, for he could not perceive more than that with his eyes, lest he be blinded by the Great Light without those many filters.

Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, did not need a partition, as it is said: *'And he beholds the image of the Lord.'* And if we speak of these types of prophecy, the prophet Isaiah alluded to them when he said: *'I have spoken to the prophets, and I have multiplied visions...'* The word *El* (to/towards) hints at the first type of prophecy, which rises above all prophetic levels and is called the Luminous Mirror. You will find this only with Moses, the master of all prophets, of whom it is said: *'The Lord spoke to Moses face to face... mouth to mouth I speak with him, in a vision and not in riddles.'* The second type of prophecy is that which speaks to the other prophets through riddles, parables, and hints. To the extent that a prophet's perception was weak, the riddles and imaginings in that prophecy increased. This was due to the need for more partitions. This is the **Non-Luminous Mirror** <term>Ispaklariya De-la Nahra<note>Prophecy received through metaphors and dreams rather than direct clarity.</note></term>. The term "Vision" (*Hazon*) indicates this, as in the phrase *'A harsh vision is told to me.'* Even with Abraham, before he was circumcised, it says the word of the Lord came to him *'in a vision'* (*ba-machazeh*).

The phrase *'And by the hand of the prophets I have used parables'* means that the number of partitions (many or few) and the variety of parables and riddles among the prophets were all according to the purity, strength, and character of each individual prophet. The term "hand" here refers to the completion of the Tabernacle, as in *'if his hand cannot reach.'* Furthermore, the "Second Finger" <note>a mystical rank</note> indicates that the Name included in the world of Emanation (*Atzilut*) is "Man," and he is the essence of the Divine Chariot. The **Lower Man** <note>Humanity</note> is a throne for the **Upper Man** <note>The Divine archetype</note>, for the physical organs in the human body hint at the spiritual forces above; they are Divine powers. It was not for nothing that it was said, *'Let us make man.'* Since this image is the image of the Upper Form, and the prophet is a physical man who, at the time of prophecy, is almost transformed into a spiritual being—his external senses weakening and his internal ones strengthening—he sees the "Likeness of Man" in that vision, like one seeing his image in a glass mirror. But not everyone attained the same thing; each perceived according to the spiritual organ from which that prophet's soul was emanated.

The author of *Tziyoni* <note>Rabbi Menahem Tziyoni</note>, in the portion of Noah regarding the Tower of the Generation of Division, elaborated on the matter of the **Divine Stature**. He wrote: "I have seen other Kabbalists explain the verse *'Great is our Lord and abundant in power'* <note>The word 'Power' (Koach) has a gematria of 28</note>... 6,000,000,000 parasangs of the upper parasangs. This measure hints at the fact that 'The All is All.' A parasang is four miles, a mile is two thousand cubits, a cubit is six handbreadths, and a handbreadth is four spans (*zeret*). An 'Upper Span' is a journey of 500 years, as it is said: *'Who measured the heavens with a span.'* From the *Book of the Stature* (*Sefer Qomah*), I understood that this measure hints at six things... to our understanding, they are without number." This is the secret of the "Standing Cedars" of the Tabernacle. When the Tabernacle was erected below, the Tabernacle was erected above. This is the secret of the "Measure of the Stature," 236,000 upper parasangs <note>A traditional mystical number for the Divine dimensions</note>. No mouth can speak it and no ear can hear it. It is like a small measure compared to a great measure. His height is 236,000 parasangs, which corresponds to the number of the unique Name of the Creator when spelled out: **Yod-He, Hi, Viv, Hi** <note>The name YHVH spelled with 'Yod' fillers equals 72, etc.</note>. The total sum is 236. I have received a true tradition that this measure refers only to the angel **Metatron**, who is the "Upper Man." But regarding that which is above him, the prophet says: *'To whom then will you liken God?'* Anyone who says otherwise has not seen the light.

From all their words, we learn that the "Stature" refers to the "Building," meaning the seven Sefirot in their positions and their enclothing within Metatron. The *Pardes* <note>Moses Cordovero's Pardes Rimonim</note> says regarding "Stature": "The Stature is the extension of authority from the neck—a contribution from Understanding (*Binah*)—and it is called Stature until the secret of the end of the thighs, including the extension of the Foundation (*Yesod*). It is called Stature in Beauty (*Tiferet*) and the Righteous One (*Tzaddik/Yesod*), with the connections above in Binah, descending below to the Sovereignty (*Malkhut*), from one end of the heavens to the other." Until here are his words. It is already known that from one end of the heavens to the other, man has the power to contemplate the "Upper Building," but from there on, the gate is closed. This was the intent in the Talmud (*Hagigah*, chapter 'One does not expound'): "One might think a person may inquire what was before the world was created... but the verse says, *'Since the day God created man on the earth.'* One might think one cannot ask about the six days of creation... but the verse says, *'Ask of the first days.'* One might ask what is above, what is below, what is before, and what is behind... but the verse says, *'From one end of the heavens to the other'*; you may ask from one end of the heavens, but you may not ask what is above, below, before, or behind." Behold, perception and prophecy exist only within these limits.

This is also the secret of the **Menorah** (Candelabrum). Recanati wrote: "The wisdom of the Menorah with its cups, knobs, and flowers was hidden from the light of the Holy Ancient One, such that Moses found the construction of the Menorah difficult." The Menorah has seven branches—three on this side, three on that side, and all their faces are toward the center. This is a hint to the seven extremities of the Holy Place. Therefore, it was difficult to hint at the unity of "The All" within it. Thus, the Menorah follows the secret of the seven attributes of the "Building." I have already written that the Building is in the **pattern of a man**. In the form of the Menorah, the human form is hinted at: there are three branches on each side; the bottom ones are larger than the middle, and the middle larger than the top. In the center is the body of the Menorah. In man, there are three protrusions from each side with the body in the center: the legs, the arms, and the ears. The protrusion of the legs is larger than the arms, and the arms larger than the ears. The height of the Menorah was 18 handbreadths, which is 3 cubits. This is the height of a human from the shoulder to the ground, as the Tosafot say in tractate *Shabbat*. The *Tanchuma* also says the Menorah hints at the seven planets.

Now I will explain the other vessels of the Tabernacle: the Ark, the Table, and the Incense Altar. On each was a crown. Our Sages said: "There are three crowns: the Crown of Torah, the Crown of Priesthood, and the Crown of Kingship. But the **Crown of a Good Name** <term>Keter Shem Tov<note>The highest virtue, representing the essence of a person's character and divine connection.</note></term> rises above them all." The **Ark**, which held the Tablets, hints at the Crown of Torah. The **Table** is the table of kings, hinting at the Crown of Kingship. The **Altar**, upon which the service was performed, hints at the Crown of Priesthood. Regarding the "Crown of a Good Name" being above them: on the surface, this is difficult—are the others not a "good name"? It seems that these three crowns shared by Israel below are influenced by these three crowns above. "Good" is the Name of the Blessed One, as in *'The Lord is good to all.'* The Crown of Torah is the secret of *Tiferet* (Beauty), which is the Written Torah placed in the Ark. The Ark hints at the *Shekhinah* (Divine Presence), which is the "receptacle" for *Tiferet*. The crown upon it hints at the "Crown of her Husband."

The four rings hint at the four "legs" of the Divine Chariot. The Tablets were six handbreadths long and six wide, and each was three handbreadths thick. In total, they equal 36. Kabbalists write that 36 letters correspond to the number 72 <note>The Name of 72 names</note>, which is the gift of Moses... the Written Torah is the secret of the letter *Yod*. The Table hints at the table of kings, but it receives influence from the hidden "Table of Kings," which is the secret of the Kingdom of Heaven (*Malkhut*). From there, the Davidic dynasty receives its influence; therefore, one who disputes the Davidic monarchy disputes the Shekhinah. Furthermore, it hints at something even more internal: *'This is the table that is before the Lord,'* which is the World to Come. Since all Israel are "sons of kings," they all have a portion in the World to Come. Therefore, the Table was placed in the North, representing the "hidden good" stored for the righteous. Recanati hints at this: the word "Tradition" (*Masoret*) indicates a hidden thing. The light is hidden within its four rings, just like the four rings of the Ark. The rings influence the "frame" <note>of the Table</note>. Remember that with "knowledge the rooms are filled." The "housing for the poles" hints at *Binah* (Understanding).

# Tablets of the Covenant

## Tetzaveh

### Candle of Commandment
**Commandment 99:** To prepare the perpetual lamps before the Lord <note>Hebrew: *HaShem*</note>, as it is said: "Aaron and his sons shall set it in order" <note>Exodus 27:21</note>. This means setting the lamp before the Lord, which is the commandment of "preparing the lamps" mentioned in the Talmud.
**Commandment 100:** The commandment of wearing the priestly garments, as it is said: "And you shall make holy garments..." <note>Exodus 28:2</note>.
**Commandment 101:** The commandment of the Breastplate <note>term: *Choshen*; the judicial breastplate worn by the High Priest</note> being placed over the Ephod <note>term: *Ephod*; a decorative apron-like garment</note>.
**Commandment 102:** Not to tear the Robe <note>term: *Me'il*</note>, as it is said: "it shall not be torn" <note>Exodus 28:32</note>.
**Commandment 103:** The priests were commanded to eat some of the meat of the sacrifices, such as the Sin Offering and the Guilt Offering, as it is said of them: "And they shall eat those things wherewith atonement was made" <note>Exodus 29:33</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory said: "The priests eat, and the owners of the sacrifice are atoned for."
**Commandment 104:** The priests were commanded to burn incense of sweet spices twice every day, as it is said: "And Aaron shall burn thereon incense of sweet spices every morning" <note>Exodus 30:7</note>.
**Commandment 105:** Not to offer "strange incense" <note>incense not made according to the specific divine recipe</note>, nor any burnt offering, upon the Golden Altar.

---

->And the "Light of the Torah" <note>a section title</note>: I have already established in the introduction that the light of the Torah shines from the attribute of <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Kindness</gloss>.<--

**And now** I will begin with the help of God. I have already explained at length in the portion of *Terumah* that the Tabernacle <note>term: *Mishkan*</note> corresponds to the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all their hosts, both above and below. The Tabernacle is a "rectification" <note>term: *Tikkun*; the mystical process of repairing the world</note>. Aaron serves as a rectification for Adam <note>the first man</note>, who had become distanced from God. But regarding Aaron, it is written: "And bring you near unto you Aaron" <note>Exodus 28:1</note>. This is the secret of the Infinite <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*</note> showing mercy to the "Primordial Man." The world was created with kindness, as it is written: "A world shall be built on kindness" <note>Psalm 89:3</note>. The supernal building—the secret of the ten internal days of Creation—begins with Kindness <note>*Chesed*</note>.

Similarly, regarding Aaron, it is written: "Let Your Thummim and Your Urim be with Your pious one <note>Hebrew: *Chassidecha*, from the same root as *Chesed*</note>" <note>Deuteronomy 33:8</note>. This is his attribute within the secret of "Priest, Levite, and Israelite," which correspond to <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Kindness</gloss>, <term>Gevurah</term> <gloss>Strength/Severity</gloss>, and <term>Tiferet</term> <gloss>Beauty/Harmony</gloss>.

When man sinned, his "garments of light" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* (spelled with the letter Aleph)</note> were removed from him and replaced with "garments of skin" <note>Hebrew: *Kotnot Or* (spelled with the letter Ayin)</note>. The priesthood of Aaron restores this. It is written for Aaron’s sons: "And you shall make for them tunics." They needed to be clothed in "holy garments," meaning their bodies were anointed with the holy anointing oil, and then they were clothed in holy garments to separate them as a holy generation from the Upper Realm. Life force came to the first man through the filth of the Serpent, and this requires rectification. Aaron, the "Man of Kindness" who represents the building of the world, must be set apart so that his body becomes a holy vessel. Then, he is clothed in the holy garments of the Tabernacle—special garments for "glory and beauty"—which are woven like those original "garments of light." The filth of the Serpent is transformed into the "Gold" <note>Hebrew: *Chash*</note> upon his heart.

This is explicitly concluded with the twelve stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel, and the names of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for they are the "Chariot." These twelve stones correspond to the twelve tribes of God. Through the holiness of eating the sacrificial meat, a person achieves a state of holiness similar to what was said to Adam: "Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat" <note>Genesis 2:16</note>. The inner material hidden within the fruit of the Tree of Knowledge that he ate is thus rectified. Just as the Priest is set apart for holiness and his garments are holy, he is likewise set apart to eat holy things.

So too, holy places are separated from one another: the Courtyard, the Tent of Meeting, and the Holy of Holies. Similarly, the labors of the Tabernacle are distinct. The sacrifices build the rectification on the Outer Altar, but the Incense <note>term: *Ketoret*</note> is the most beloved of all offerings. It "binds" <note>the Aramaic translation of 'bind' is 'katar', related to 'ketoret'</note> the upper will to the lower will. The spiritual life of the soul derives pleasure only from smell. Therefore, the incense is offered deep inside on the Golden Altar. Because of the great holiness of the Priest's body and garments, only communal incense may be offered there, never private incense, which would be "strange incense." No one is permitted to enter the innermost chamber—the Holy of Holies—not even Aaron the High Priest, except on the Day of Atonement, as it says in the portion of *Acharei Mot*: "that he come not at all times into the holy place."

Our Sages noted that while Aaron could not enter at all times, Moses could. This is because Moses’ physical matter was already pure, holy, and refined, like the "garments of light." When the House was filled with light, Moses was already there in that state. Although Aaron reached a high level through the rectification of the holy anointing oil, he did not reach the level of Moses, who had no "serpent's filth" in him.

This explains the Sages' question: "In what garment did Moses serve during the seven days of consecration?" They answered: "In a white tunic." At first glance, this seems like a trivial question about laundry, but the deeper meaning is: where did he get priestly garments? The questioner assumed one cannot perform the service without the official priestly garments. The answer "a white tunic" means he did not *need* the multi-colored priestly garments because Moses was not a "stranger" to the service, and his own "garment" was white—a hint at the "garments of light" mentioned before. He was so radiant, pure, and holy that he did not need garments of "honor," for honor itself was attached to him.

Returning to Aaron, the "Man of Kindness" <note>*Chesed*</note>: he is the rectification for Adam. Since "a world shall be built on kindness" and the secret of the supernal building involves the seven days of Creation, Aaron required seven "Days of Consecration" <note>term: *Miluim*</note> to be trained in holiness. Rabbi Isaac said: "It is written: 'Let there be light,' and the world was led by that light. The light of wisdom is sevenfold, like the light of those seven days." Rabbi Judah said: "These are the seven days of consecration, for on those days the world was established and returned to its perfection, and the moon was no longer diminished by the evil serpent."

Aaron was anointed with the "holy anointing oil," which points to the secret holiness of the supernal building from its root. According to the *Pardes* <note>a classic Kabbalistic work by Moshe Cordovero</note> in the "Gate of Appellations," the term "Oil" refers to the Divine flow of abundance. When the attribute of Kingship <note><term>Malchut</term></note> receives this abundance from the side of Kindness <note><term>Chesed</term></note>, it is called "Anointing Oil." This is because the Aramaic translation of "anointing" is *meshacha*, a term for greatness and kindness. When it receives from the side of Beauty <note><term>Tiferet</term></note>, it is called "Oil for Anointing" because *Tiferet* is the "Great Luminary." When it receives from the side of Strength <note><term>Gevurah</term></note>, it is called "Holy Anointing Oil" and it sanctifies the Levites. Because the flow comes from the side of Strength but is sweetened by Kindness, it is called "Holy Anointing Oil"—meaning the flow (*Oil*) is a special drawing down (*Anointing*) that combines the name of Kindness with the name of Holiness (*Gevurah*).

It is also called "crushed oil" from the side of the attribute of Foundation <note><term>Yesod</term></note>, because it "crushes" the olives to bring out the abundance and lower it to Kingship. It is known that human existence is refined through "crushing" <note>suffering or effort</note>. This crushing causes the flow (the olives) to be aroused. Thus, from the side of *Yesod*, it is called "pure olive oil, crushed for the light," for *Yesod* is called a "fresh olive tree." The "Oil" itself is the abundance flowing from Understanding <note><term>Binah</term></note> and rooted in Wisdom <note><term>Chokmah</term></note>, following the secret of the "Right Side."

Regarding the Priestly Garments, they are "garments of glory," hinting at the "garments of light." They are made "for glory and for beauty" <note>Exodus 28:2</note>. This represents the entire secret of the supernal building: the Divine Presence <note>term: *Shekhinah*</note>, specifically the attribute of Beauty <note>*Tiferet*</note> which includes the six directions and flows into Kingship <note>*Malchut*</note>.

Nachmanides <note>term: *Ramban*; a major medieval scholar</note> wrote: "According to the truth <note>a code phrase for Kabbalah</note>, 'for glory and for beauty' means Aaron shall serve in holy garments for the glory of God who dwells among them, and for the beauty of their strength. As it is written: 'For You are the beauty of their strength' <note>Psalm 89:18</note>... and 'Our holy and beautiful house where our fathers praised You' <note>Isaiah 64:10</note>." This refers to the attributes of Glory and Beauty. Israel is "beautified" through them. Even regarding the garments of the ordinary priests, it says "for glory and for beauty."

Furthermore, regarding the sacrifices, it is said: "they shall come up with acceptance on My altar, and I will glorify My beautiful house" <note>Isaiah 60:7</note>. Here, the Altar represents "Acceptance" and the Temple represents the "House of Beauty." These garments must be made with specific holy intent. That is why God said: "speak to all that are wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom" <note>Exodus 28:3</note>, so they would know the inner intention of what they were making. The Sages said: "the image of his [Aaron's] form was victorious before Me in the house of their war."

In the book *Tikunei HaZohar* <note>a foundational Kabbalistic text</note>, concerning the garments: there are four white garments and four golden garments. Together, they represent two Divine Names. The four white garments correspond to the secret of the Tetragrammaton <note>Y-H-W-H</note>, the Master of Mercy and Whiteness. The four golden garments correspond to the secret of the Name *Adonai*, of which it is said "from the Tabernacle..."

## The Tablets of the Covenant

The concept of nullification <note>original: "bitul," a legal concept where a small amount of a forbidden substance is neutralized by a larger amount of a permitted one</note> only applies when a substance is mixed with something of a different kind. Just as the evil angel Samael <note>In Jewish mysticism, the personification of the accuser or the "Satan"</note> answers "Amen" and thereby allows power to enter into the side of holiness, so too does the "Galbanum" <note>original: "Chelbenah," a foul-smelling resin used in the Temple incense</note> function within the mystery of the Incense. It is said that the "descendants of Haman studied Torah in public," and Mordechai is linked to the incense itself. As our Sages said: "Where is Mordechai found in the Torah? In the verse 'pure myrrh' <note>Exodus 30:23</note>, which is translated into Aramaic as *mira dachia* <note>A wordplay on the name Mor-de-chai</note>." 

This relates to the half-shekel coins; for if Israel had not pre-emptively given their shekels, Haman’s coins would have taken effect. Regarding Haman's entry into holiness, the Sages hinted at this with the obligation to drink on Purim "until one does not know" the difference <note>original: "ad d'lo yada," the famous Purim instruction</note> between "Cursed is Haman" and "Blessed is Mordechai." There is an investigation regarding the Galbanum in the Torah's incense—whether it was made for amusement or became sanctified. This is similar to the legal query in the Talmudic tractate Ketubot regarding whether certain biological matters are merely "deposited" or "absorbed." 

We return to the matter of the days of Purim: they shall never be nullified, only added upon. This is the secret of why God's Name and Throne are currently not "complete" <note>A mystical tradition based on Exodus 17:16, suggesting the world is fractured until evil is defeated</note>. Now the Name is, as it were, halved, but in the future, it will be full. Currently, we do not pronounce the Name as it is written; but in the future, the commandment to "Remember" <note>Exodus 17:14</note> will be fulfilled. This is the secret of the name *Adonai* <note>The name used in prayer in place of the four-letter Name</note>. When the task of blotting out Amalek <note>The biblical arch-enemy of Israel, from whom Haman descended</note> is finished, then His Name will be one. Purim, which is the wiping out of Haman, is a preview of that future perfection. 

Since Purim is only a preview and not the final completion, God’s Name is not mentioned in the Book of Esther except by hint, such as the initial letters of **"Let the King and Haman come today"** <note>Esther 5:4; in Hebrew, the first letters of "Yavo HaMelech VeHaman HaYom" spell the four-letter Name of God</note>. All this relates to the secret of "I am the first and I am the last." The numerical value <note>term: Gematria (assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters)</note> for the phrase "Cursed is Haman" equals 39, which is the same as the word for "Snake" <note>original: "Nachash"</note>. This is why it is said: "Cursed is he, and Blessed is Mordechai." 

The "Calculated Belt" of the Ephod <note>one of the priestly garments</note> atones for the sin of idolatry, which stems from Samael. The names of the patriarchs—Isaac and Jacob—are inscribed on the stones, suggesting they were ready to be "sown" with holiness. The Ineffable Name was not fully recorded there, but only as a "remembrance," which is why the text says, "This is My remembrance forever." The two shoulder pieces of the Ephod represent the letter *Vav*, and the five fingers of the hand represent the letter *Heh*—letters of God's Name. Currently, it is not complete; it is only revealed through hints. In the future, the secret of the Name will be fully revealed in the territory of the Tribe of Benjamin. May it be revealed speedily in our days, Amen Selah.

## The Way of Life: Ethical Reproofs

Regarding the command to "raise an eternal flame": This hints that the lighting of the lamp must never be missing. Even though, due to our sins, the Temple is destroyed, it is still a commandment to light a lamp in the Synagogue, which is called a "Miniature Sanctuary." It should be lit in the morning at the time of prayer, for prayer now stands in place of the sacrificial service in the Temple. It seems to me that this commandment of lighting a lamp in the Synagogue is:
<margin>Written in the great book *Menorat HaMaor* ("The Candelabrum of Light").</margin>

### And they shall make holy garments, etc.
Rabbi Menachem of Babylonia said: The reason for this commandment is that the Temple service requires intense focus <note>original: "kavanah"</note>. Wearing specific clothing for the service awakens the heart to think and to subject all one's mental faculties to the task. Just as physical clothing covers the nakedness of the body, these garments atone for the soul. The "holy garments" for Aaron your brother were for "honor and glory." A person should reflect on this when dressing: just as they cover the nakedness of the body, they should be stirred to cover the "nakedness of the soul."

to strengthen

</margin>

### The Breastplate shall not be loosened
...from the Ephod. The aforementioned Rabbi wrote that the reason for this is that anyone who appoints an unfit judge is as if they planted a pagan grove. The Breastplate <note>original: "Choshen," associated with judgment</note> atones for perverted justice, while the Ephod atones for idolatry. To hint at this connection, the Breastplate must be permanently fixed to the Ephod, to warn that idolatry is always a disgrace. They must be joined so that the Breastplate never slips.

### That the Robe shall not be torn
The aforementioned Rabbi wrote that the reason for this commandment is so the Priest shall place a strong wall around himself. He must not tear his garments because he is the intercessor for the holy people; therefore, no disgraceful word should exit his mouth. He is the one who "binds and sews," so his mouth must not be silent or diminished. Every person who serves God is like a priest, and he must sanctify his mouth with extra holiness.

### With the help of the One who gives strength, the portion of Tetzaveh is completed.
#### Given at the completion of the "Shovavim" <note>A period of spiritual repentance during the winter weeks</note>.

## The Portion of Ki Tisa
### His Name is beautiful, the number of the Children of Israel.

**The Lamp of Commandment:** 
Commandment 106 (of the 613): To give the Half-Shekel every year. 
107: For the Priest to sanctify (wash) his hands and feet for the service. 
108: The commandment regarding the High Priest’s anointing oil. 
109: That a non-priest shall not be anointed with the oil, and one shall not replicate its formula. 
111: Not to replicate the formula of the Incense to use for oneself. 
112: Not to eat or drink from the offerings of idolatry. 
113: To rest from working the land during the Sabbatical Year <note>original: "Shemittah"</note>. 
114: Not to eat meat with milk, as it says: "Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk." 

The *Sefer HaChinuch* <note>a 13th-century book categorizing the 613 commandments</note> writes on page 46: This verse prohibits both the eating of and deriving benefit from meat and milk. Do not find it difficult to understand why the Torah says "Do not cook" rather than "Do not eat." The answer is that this prohibition is unique compared to other forbidden foods. For other prohibitions, one is only liable if they eat the food in a normal manner of enjoyment. However, here, even if one consumes it in a way that is not normally considered "eating," if the body derives benefit from it, they are liable. The Torah uses the language of "cooking" to teach that the prohibition applies once the substances are cooked together, regardless of the manner of consumption. Even though the prohibition against cooking meat and milk is written three times in the Torah, it is to teach three distinct rules: the prohibition of cooking it, the prohibition of eating it, and the prohibition of deriving any benefit (such as selling it) from it. We do not count these as three separate commandments, because eating and benefiting are considered a single category. Usually, wherever the Torah says "Do not eat," it implies a prohibition on benefit as well. The Torah generally uses the word "eating" for all forms of benefit because eating is the most frequent and necessary pleasure for a person. As it is written, "And they beheld God, and they ate and drank" <note>Exodus 24:11</note>, meaning the Divine Presence was like food to them.

<meta>This page continues the author's exploration of the spiritual connections between the Torah portions of the wilderness journey, specifically moving from the aftermath of the Golden Calf in Ki Tisa to the construction of the Tabernacle and the laws of the Sabbath in Vayakhel and Pekudei.</meta>

->Written Torah: Sabbath and the Tabernacle<-

<margin>**The Matter of "And They Feared"**</margin> I have elaborated elsewhere on the thirteen attributes <note>Refers to the thirteen attributes of Divine Mercy revealed to Moses in Exodus 34:6-7.</note> as it is written: "whenever my children do this," meaning, whenever they clothe themselves in the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to become merciful, gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in kindness and truth, etc.
Regarding King Manasseh, our Sages of blessed memory said: see how great is the power of those who transgress. Before they sinned, they looked upon the face of the Divine Presence and were not afraid; but now, they cannot even look upon the face of the mediator <note>Referring to Moses, who acted as an intermediary between God and Israel.</note>. A person should take this to heart to purify and sanctify themselves, to cleanse the impurity of sins by turning away from evil and sanctifying themselves with holiness and doing good. And these are his words:

---

# With the help of the High and Exalted God, the portion of Ki Tisa is completed.
## Portions of Vayakhel and Pekudei
### This is the name by which it shall be called: Sabbath and the Tabernacle

<margin>**Lamp of the Commandment**</margin> Commandment 116 out of the 613 commandments: "You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings on the Sabbath day" (Exodus 35:3). Our Sages of blessed memory explained that this means the <term>Beth Din<gloss>Rabbinic court</gloss></term> should not carry out an execution by fire for one who has been sentenced, and the same applies to other forms of court-ordered execution. This is the language of the <term>Mekhilta<gloss>An early collection of legal interpretations on Exodus</gloss></term>: execution by fire was included in the general prohibition of work, but it was singled out to teach that just as execution by fire—one of the court's methods of execution—does not override the Sabbath, so too no other court executions override the Sabbath. Furthermore, our Sages said this verse teaches that "kindling a fire" was singled out to categorize it as a distinct labor <note>Meaning each of the 39 forbidden labors on Sabbath carries its own individual liability.</note>. Regarding the phrase "in all your dwellings," Rabbi Ila said in the name of Rabbi Yannai: "From here we learn that the courts shall not judge on the Sabbath," for they derived the prohibition of judging from the words "in all your dwellings."

<margin>**And Torah is Light**</margin> The inner meaning is that the Sabbath points toward the "World that is entirely Sabbath," which is the eternal reward where souls find rest and where their dwelling place is. This is the dwelling place of His Glory, may He be blessed. The lower Tabernacle <note>The physical Mishkan built in the desert.</note> was designed to correspond to the celestial one above, along with all its hints and symbols. Therefore, it says, "And Moses gathered (<term>Vayakhel</term>) the whole community of the Children of Israel," for every community of Israel has a portion in the World to Come, which is preserved by the Sabbath. Also, the community of Israel gathered there "as one man," which alludes to the secret of the <term>Shiur Qomah<gloss>The "Divine Stature" or mystical dimensions of the Divine presence</gloss></term>. The secret symbols of the Tabernacle were also tied to this mystery, as it says, "the Tabernacle was raised" (<term>hukam</term>), and the word <term>hukam</term> shares letters with <term>qomah</term> (stature), as I explained in the portion of Terumah. I also cited there the discussion of dimensions from the chapter "The Sound of the Footsteps," where the Sages mention "two thousand parasangs." I found in the writings of the <term>Arizal<gloss>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the foundational 16th-century kabbalist</gloss></term> that the Sabbath is hinted at in the verse "and the glory of the Lord filled the Tabernacle" (Exodus 40:34). When you calculate the numerical value of the word "Tabernacle" (<term>Mishkan</term>) with its hidden letters, it equals 236, which refers to the 236,000 parasangs of the Divine Stature. Thus, the Tabernacle becomes one with the Sabbath. The Sabbath in this world represents the "World that is entirely Sabbath," while the six days of work represent the "World of Action" meant for doing the will of their Creator regarding all matters of Torah and the Sabbath, leading to the reward in the World to Come. As it is written: "Today is for doing them, and tomorrow [the future world] is for receiving their reward." Therefore, the earthly courts are not to awaken any judgment or punishment on the Sabbath day, even for a commandment—for when Sabbath comes, rest comes.

Now, the matter of the connection between the Tabernacle and the Sabbath is something worthy of a lengthy explanation. Therefore, my children (may God protect them), I will record for you a treatise I wrote in my youth, which also contains insights into the portion of the Red Heifer and the portion of the New Moon, which usually occur during these weeks.

<margin>**Homily for Vayakhel**</margin> "And Moses gathered the whole community of the Children of Israel..." (Exodus 35:1). One might ask: why does it say "Children of Israel" here, while in the command for the Tabernacle's construction it says "from every man"? Furthermore, what is the meaning of "take from among you"? It has been written that the command for the Tabernacle from the mouth of the Holy One to Moses—namely, "they shall take for Me a contribution"—occurred before they made the Golden Calf. At that time, God said "take a contribution from every man," including the <term>Erev Rav<gloss>the "Mixed Multitude" of non-Israelites who left Egypt with the Hebrews</gloss></term>. However, Moses's command to Israel happened after the incident of the Calf, on the day after Yom Kippur. Since the corruption of the Calf was caused by the Mixed Multitude, Moses gathered specifically the "community of the Children of Israel" and said "take from among you" specifically—and not from the Mixed Multitude. However, Rashi disagrees with this chronology in the portion of Ki Tisa on the verse "and He gave to Moses when He finished speaking." This is also the view in the Midrash Tanchuma on the portion of Terumah. In truth, there is great wonder at Rashi's position where he tries to prove that "there is no chronological order in the Torah" and argues that Moses only gave the command on the day after Yom Kippur. While that is true, how do we know God's command to Moses wasn't before the Calf? Indeed, this is the opinion of the <term>Zohar<gloss>The foundational text of Jewish mysticism</gloss></term>. Regarding the proximity of the Sabbath to the Tabernacle: our Sages gave an explanation, but one must provide a reason why we are liable specifically for the types of labor that were performed in the Tabernacle. "Six days work shall be done..." (Exodus 35:2)—why all this? In the Mekhilta, it is answered: when the Children of Israel performed God's will, their work was done by others, which is why it says "work shall be done" <note>in the passive voice</note>. This is also answered by the Sages' teaching in Tractate Berakhot: because the early pietists were so holy, their Torah was preserved and their work was done for them. Therefore, you are warned that even now, your actions should cause work to be done as if by itself even during the weekdays. It should have said "on the seventh day," yet it says "on the day of the seventh" <note>a subtle grammatical point in the Hebrew text</note>. These two questions can be answered by referencing the Sages' statement: "One who is traveling in the desert and does not know when the Sabbath is..." He may do work on the seventh day for his survival and sanctify the seventh day of his own count. See the book *Kli Chemdah* on the portion of Ki Tisa. "This is the thing that the Lord commanded, saying..." (Exodus 35:4). It is asked why Moses needed to emphasize here that this was a Divine command more than with other commandments. It made sense when he appointed Aaron as High Priest; he needed to say it so people wouldn't think he was just honoring his brother. But here? It is explained in the Midrash and cited by the author of *Bachya* on the portion of Pekudei: Why is "Tabernacle" mentioned twice? To teach that the lower sanctuary corresponds exactly to the upper sanctuary. As it says: "the place for Your dwelling that You, Lord, have made." Do not read it as "place" (<term>makhon</term>) but as "corresponding" (<term>mkhuvan</term>). This Tabernacle corresponds to the creation of the world. In the creation of the world it is written, "Who stretches out the heavens like a curtain," and in the Tabernacle it says, "and he spread the [goats' hair] for a tent." It says, "stretching out the heavens like a veil." In the creation of the world it says, "let there be lights," and in the Tabernacle it says, "and you shall make a copper basin." In the creation of the world it says, "let there be lights," and in the Tabernacle, "and you shall make a Menorah." In creation, "and let birds fly," and in the Tabernacle, "the Cherubim shall spread their wings." In creation, "God created man," and in the Tabernacle, "bring near to you [Aaron]." In creation, "the heavens were finished," and in the Tabernacle, "all the work was finished." In creation, "God blessed the seventh day," and in the Tabernacle, "Moses blessed them" and "he sanctified it and all its vessels." In creation, "for on it He rested," and in the Tabernacle, "the cloud of the Lord was above." After the seventh day, it says "take from among you a contribution." There are many such comparisons. See the lengthy discourse in the Midrash Rabbah on the portion of Terumah where Rabbi Berechiah begins with: "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power..." Another interpretation of "they shall take for Me a contribution": Rabbi Berechiah opened with "Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power... for all that is in heaven and on earth." You find that everything the Holy One created above, He created below. Above there is "and birds fly," as it is written "and see the altar of Your holiness." There is the "thick cloud," and "Moses approached the thick cloud," and it is written "Can He judge through the thick cloud?" Below, Solomon said, "The Lord said He would dwell in the thick cloud." It is written, "I have surely built a house of habitation for You." Above, "Seraphim stand above Him." Below, "standing wood of acacia." Above, Cherubim, as it says "Who dwells between the Cherubim." Below, "and the Cherubim shall be..." Above, "and the wheels (Ophanim) were lifted up... alongside them." Below, "and the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel." Also, "behold, one wheel (Ophan) on the earth." Above, "the Lord is in His holy palace." Below, "and the palace of the Lord." Above, the hosts of angels descend. Below, "all the hosts of the Lord went out." Above, "let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters." Below, "the veil shall divide for you." Above, the Throne of the Lord. Below, "a throne of glory, on high from the beginning, the place of our sanctuary." Above, "and there were lights." Below, "two stones of onyx." Above, the counting of the stars. Below, "behold, you are today as the stars of the heaven for multitude." Above, "behold, those clothed in linen." Below, "a holy linen tunic." Above, and this...

<meta>This page continues the discussion regarding the spiritual journey of the Israelites, specifically focusing on Moses’ request for God’s direct presence rather than an angelic intermediary, and transitioning into the ethical requirements for communal leadership as exemplified by Bezalel.</meta>

<header>The Tablets of the Covenant</header>

The command was not entirely what was desired. Regarding the phrase "Go up from here," it should not be understood as a simple direction of ascent, but rather according to the first explanation written by **Rashi** <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent medieval commentator</note> on the words "Go, go up," which explains that the Land of Israel is spiritually higher than all other lands; therefore, the word "go up" is used. We can deduce that it was not God's full desire when He said, "Behold, I send an angel before you," for we desired that He Himself, in His own glory, should go with us. This is why Moses said: "And You have not let me know whom You will send with me," for this "letting me know" was not a true notification for me of who would accompany me. Rather, this prophecy referred to Joshua, to whom the angel later said, "Now I have come" <note>Referring to Joshua 5:14</note>. Since Moses was still the leader, the angel had no permission to come then. Even though our teacher Moses, peace be upon him, did not know then that Joshua would be the one to bring them in—thinking he himself would lead them—he nevertheless knew that by the words "Behold, I send an angel," they were being warned that they were destined to sin. For the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah<gloss>The indwelling presence of God</gloss></term> says to them, "I will not go up in your midst," as Rashi explains. Moses thought this might happen at some future time, perhaps when the Temple would be destroyed and rebuilt, that an angel would be sent. but while he was leading them, the Blessed Name should lead them Himself in His own glory. Therefore he said, "You have not let me know," for this "knowledge" is no knowledge to me. You said, "I have known you by name," meaning You considered me a "man among men" <note>original: "gavar begovrin"</note>; if so, why send an angel through another and not through me as well? Regarding this he said, "I have already said: I have known you by name," which refers to the **Explicit Name** <term>Shem HaMeforash<gloss>The four-letter name of God, Y-H-W-H</gloss></term>, as the Blessed Name said to the Patriarchs: "By My name 'Lord' I was not known to them." The matter of "knowing the Name" refers to the attachment to the name **Y-H-W-H**. The exodus from Egypt was on the condition that they would immediately enter the Land and possess the land which "the Lord seeks out." There, in the Holy Land, the name **Y-H-W-H** is firmly attached, as will be explained. 

And he also said, "I have found favor in Your eyes"—the word "also" is an addition to the matter. This refers to the special quality of "finding favor," which is that the attachment to the Name should not only be in the Land itself, but even before we arrive there—meaning, while we are traveling on the road, the attachment should be to He Himself and His glory. And the Blessed Name answered: "If I have truly found favor in Your eyes, let me know Your ways, that I may know You" through the knowledge of the Name even while we are traveling. Moses continued: "Consider that this nation is Your people," taking up the first language You used to say "behold," and to find favor with You. The Blessed Name replied: "My presence shall go," meaning the "resting" <note>dwelling of the Presence</note> will be in the Land of Israel itself, as it is written: "The Lord will be a resting place for you all around," meaning in the Land itself. Afterward, since the Blessed Name told Moses that His presence would be revealed to him in the Land of Israel itself, Moses wondered: what then is the advantage of Moses over Joshua? Will not Joshua also be the leader? Is not the Land of Israel "the portion of the Lord"? That is to say, even in the days of Joshua, although the Land is the Lord's portion, it is written that an angel would be there, as it says "for My name is within him." Even though the Name was given there, that was specifically in the **Holy Temple** <term>Beit HaMikdash<gloss>The Temple in Jerusalem</gloss></term>, but not throughout the whole Land. But if Moses were the leader, the Divine Presence would be everywhere in the Land. To this Moses said: "If Your presence does not go immediately," even on the journey, and not just as You said "My presence shall go" which implies the future—meaning in the Land—then how shall it be known? Even if I have found favor, and Joshua follows later, "How then shall it be known" that the Holy One, Blessed be He, values this journey too? "I will also do this thing... for you have found favor," to be with you in My essence and glory even on the road, so "I may know you by name," meaning as it will be in the Land of Israel. He prioritized "finding favor" on the road to "knowing the Name" in the Land, because the road comes before the arrival. 

Therefore Moses prayed on the road. It is known that prayer starts small and then increases. Thus he prayed first for the knowledge of the Name in the Land, and then added a request for "finding favor" on the road. This is the meaning of "And we shall be distinguished... from all the people on the face of the earth," referring to the lands of the nations. For our portion is the Name, even before we come to the Land. Everything revolves around the secret of the "Riding of the Name" upon Israel; as long as they do the will of the Place, even the Name is at peace and the Throne is at peace. The master of the guards is **Metatron** <note>A high-ranking angel in Jewish mysticism</note>, who is the "Face of the Ox," one of the four "Living Creatures" that carry the Throne. When Israel does the will of the Place, they carry the Throne through the fulfillment of the Torah and the commandments—that is, study and action. Then they are called "Man," as it is written: "You are called 'Man,'" and they are the chariot for "Man" <note>referring to the human form on the Divine Chariot</note>. Through the study of the Torah, they are the chariot of the **Ox**, for "much produce comes by the strength of the ox." Our Sages said: "A person should always place himself under the words of Torah like an ox to the yoke." From the perspective of action, they are like the **Lion** and the **Eagle**, as Judah ben Tema said: "Be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle." The **Tur** <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, author of the legal code Arba'ah Turim</note> explained this as referring to the heart and the eye, as it is written: "Do not explore after your heart and after your eyes." When Israel is refined, the "Lion" is established... [The text here discusses the transformation of the chariot faces based on Israel's behavior].

The matter of the **Ox** will be explained somewhat in the portion of the **Red Heifer** <term>Parah Adumah<gloss>A cow whose ashes were used for ritual purification</gloss></term>, which is usually read near the portion of Ki Tisa. I have already written that the Torah is represented by the Ox. But because of our many sins, the Torah has been diminished until the "time of the end," when "the earth shall be full of knowledge." Our Sages said that the entire Torah was spoken in the "male" tongue, but in exile, even though it is written "it shall not be forgotten from the mouth of his seed," there is a fear of it returning to a "female" state. This is the secret of the Red Heifer—that from the Ox (which is male), a Heifer (which is female) is made, to purify the impurity of death. When they received the Torah, they were free from death (which is the Accuser) and free from the nations, as it is written: "I said: You are angels, and all of you sons of the Most High; but indeed like men you shall die." When they sinned, the letters flew away, hinting at death and exile. This caused the light of redemption in Israel to be in the "female" tongue, like the "Song of the Sea" <note>In Hebrew, "Shirah" (song) is feminine</note>, whereas at the receiving of the Torah it was "male." After their corruption, there will be no "New Song" <note>"Shir" (song) in the masculine</note> until the future true redemption. This is the secret of "And the cows sang" <note>referring to the cows carrying the Ark in 1 Samuel 6:12</note>; the word used is an "androgynous" term, including both male and female language, hinting at the "Song of Songs" which contains both. This will be explained further in the portions of Vayakhel and Pekudei, in the discourse on the Red Heifer. See also the portion of Chukat at length regarding how the Red Heifer hints at the impurity of death, the service of idols, the Accuser, and how the nations taunt us regarding the matter of the Heifer. May it be speedily in our days that we sing a New Song. Amen.

## The Way of Life: Ethical Rebuke

<margin>
"See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur..." Open your eyes and see: one who merits to be a leader in Israel—how they must be full of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and they must also be worthy in the eyes of God and man.
</margin>

In the chapter "The One Who Sees" <note>Tractate Berakhot, page 55a</note>, Rabbi Yochanan said: We do not appoint a leader over the community unless we consult with the community, as it says: "And Moses said to the children of Israel: See, the Lord has called by name Bezalel." The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: "Is he worthy in your eyes?" Moses replied: "If he is worthy before You, he is certainly worthy before me." This "before You" requires explanation. Furthermore, if he is worthy before us, is it not even more obvious he is worthy before God? The explanation is that "worthiness" is divided into three categories. First: a worthy action, which is truly a new beginning that is proper. Second: sometimes an action is worthy in the eyes of Heaven, but the observer thinks it is unworthy due to a lack of knowledge or some other reason. Our Sages have already said: "A transgression for the sake of Heaven is greater than a commandment performed not for its own sake." These are two kinds of worthiness regarding revealed actions. There is a third: worthy intention for the sake of Heaven, and not so that people will call him "Rabbi" or the like. Regarding this, Moses said to the Holy One, Blessed be He: "Master of the Universe, if he is worthy before You—meaning in the third category, things hidden in the heart that could be concealed and not like what is revealed—then he is certainly worthy before the revealed world where I see his worthiness." And Israel said: "If he is worthy before the Holy One, Blessed be He, when he performs a good deed revealed before Him—at which time his hidden thoughts are like his revealed actions—and You testify that all his deeds are good, then the revealed things are an example of what is hidden." Sometimes an action seems unworthy, but You testify that all are worthy and it is we who are mistaken. The Holy One, Blessed be He, testifies that in every good thing he does, his hidden self is like his revealed self. In the chapter "The Flute" <note>Tractate Taanit</note>, Rabbi Yochanan said: There are three things the Holy One, Blessed be He, announces Himself: Famine, Abundance, and a Leader. We must understand why He announces these three specifically. We can find a reason for abundance, for the gift of rain is not in the hands of a messenger; four things are not handed to a messenger but remain in the hand of God Himself, as symbolized by the word "Maptechot" <note>Keys</note>. The reason is that a man's sustenance is as difficult as the splitting of the Red Sea, and the Red Sea could not be split by a messenger. But how do we explain the others? It appears to me that these three things sometimes seem wondrous in the eyes of the prophets. Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, announces them Himself. This is like the case of "invalid witnesses of the rabbis" who are "valid according to the Torah"—they require a public announcement. Regarding "Break the arm of the wicked" in a time of famine, Rabbi Alexandri said this refers to those who manipulate market prices... thus abundance is a wonder, and so is famine. The whole world is fed only for the sake of Chanina my son, while Chanina my son is satisfied with a small measure of carobs. A leader, too—sometimes it does not seem right in the eyes of men that this person should rise to greatness over another. Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, in His glory and essence, announces these three to let it be known that it is from Him, and He knows the reason. "And Moses spoke to the Lord, saying..." This "saying" is difficult. Rashi wrote what he wrote. The **Arizal** <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the great Kabbalist</note> wrote that even the "Head of the Exile" is appointed from Heaven, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, announces it in all the heavens—this is the meaning of "saying," meaning in all the heavens. May this speaking merit us to return our thoughts to the performance of commandments; one should let their thoughts roam through the mountains and valleys of wisdom and understanding... 

"And no man put on his ornaments." A person should strip away their physical actions and remember their sins, mourning and weeping, and sitting on the ground **and mourning** for the severe bans. One should wear sackcloth and ashes with crying and eulogy for having killed their own soul; perhaps God will have mercy. **And it was** that everyone who sought the Lord went out—the author of the **Baal HaTurim** <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher</note> said of blessed memory: From here we learn that a person must wander to a place of Torah. There is another sign for this matter in the words of our Sages: "Go and count..."

<meta>This page continues the author’s mystical exploration of the human soul and its relationship to the Sanctuary (Mishkan) and the cycles of time, specifically the Sabbath and the New Moon.
