# The Tablets of the Covenant

<margin>
And similarly, by way of a mystical hint, the secret of the name <term>SMTTC<note>original: סמטט"כ; likely a reference to a complex Name of God or an angelic cipher like Metatron</note></term> is that one can always direct their thoughts to cling to the realms above <term>SMC<note>original: סמ"כ; another mystical abbreviation</note></term> in the world of <term>Action<note>original: עשיה; Asiyah, the lowest of the four spiritual worlds</note></term>. As it is written, "we shall vow to occupy ourselves with that which is missing." They merited to hint at this through the language of the blessings, removing the <term>intermediaries<note>original: סרסוטים (Sarsutim); refers to distracting spiritual forces or agents</note></term> from within. Their kingdom then becomes a dwelling place, for at the time the Queen acts to cling to the heights, this is the "completion of the work." Understand this well.
</margin>

In the "Gate of Holiness," it is explained that the <term>Levels of the Soul<note>original: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah (נפש רוח נשמה)</note></term> correspond to the worlds of **Action**, **Formation**, and **Creation**. This is the secret of the creation of the world.

Similarly, in the Sanctuary: the outer "Heaven and Earth" correspond to **Action**. The "Separating Firmament" is the firmament above the heads of the <term>Living Creatures<note>original: חיות (Chayyot); the angelic beings described in Ezekiel's vision</note></term>, which is the secret of **Formation**. So too, the Veil (Parochet) represents the boundary: on one side is the *Nefesh* (lower soul), and on the other, it divides between the Holy and the Holy of Holies, which is the *Neshamah* (higher soul). The "Horns of the Altar" represent the upper secrets, the "pure marble stones" above the firmament. This is the secret of **Creation**, which is the secret of the *Neshamah*. Likewise, in the Sanctuary, the washing of the hands and feet signifies that every soul is comprised of the "ten supernal fingers," as mentioned in various sacred texts.

The matter of washing is the secret of immersion in the <term>River of Fire<note>original: נהר דינור (Nehar di-Nur); where souls are said to be purified</note></term. Afterward, the text mentions the holiness of the Sabbath and the completion of the work, hinting that at that time, three things are highlighted that are essential to the Sabbath—as a prototype of the **World to Come**:
1.  **Pleasantness**: A state of spiritual delight.
2.  **Holiness**: This pleasantness will be holy, without any "husks" or external impurities clinging to it. The "Left Side" <note>The source of harsh judgment or evil</note> will be subdued, and only the "Right Hand of the Lord" will perform valiantly.
3.  **Eternity**: These three are explicitly mentioned in the verse: "In Your right hand are **pleasantnesses** (1) **forever** (3)." The **blessing** mentioned is the pleasantness, as in "the pleasantness of the Lord." The **sanctification** is the aspect of the "Right Hand." And just as the Sanctuary was established on the day it was completed and never dismantled again, this hints at **Eternity**.

This explains the passage. At the beginning of the discourse, it says the Sanctuary of Solomon was aligned exactly with the one above, for this Sabbath is bound and hinted at in the "World that is entirely Sabbath." The "Testimony" mentioned at the end of the discourse refers to the "witnesses" within the holy vessels.

Now we shall explain the connection to the Torah portion *Vayakhel*. It is known that in the portion *Beshalach*, it says "a Sabbath-rest, a holy Sabbath," but in *Vayakhel*, it says "a holy Sabbath, a Sabbath-rest to the Lord." Regarding why "Holy" appears earlier in one and later in the other, the *Baal HaTurim* <note>Rabbi Jacob ben Asher, a famous medieval commentator</note> writes that it hints at adding from the "profane" to the "holy" both when the Sabbath begins and when it ends. However, the change in the phrasing "Sabbath-rest" still needs explanation. According to our approach, the "Preparation" comes before Sabbath, and the "Soul" follows the Sabbath. These are called "Sabbath-rest" (*Shabbaton*), meaning a "small Sabbath," similar to how the pupil of the eye is called *ishon* <note>a diminutive of 'ish' or man</note> because of its smallness.

The question I raised regarding the Tabernacle—how Moses completed it—is answered by the fact that the earthly Sanctuary is aligned with the heavenly one. The Sanctuary itself is the "Revealed" secret, while the vessels inside are the "Hidden" inner secret. From the perspective of the Blessed Creator, the **Hidden** comes first, and then the expansion and **Revelation** follow. But from our human perspective, the **Revealed** comes first, followed by the **Hidden**. Understand this.

This clarifies the matter of the Sabbath and the Sanctuary, which represent the World to Come and the Torah. All of this follows the secret of the soul's journey, as included in the verse, "I said, you are angels," and "One thing God has spoken, two have I heard." Now let us return to the discourse on the portion of the **Red Heifer** (*Parah*) and the hint regarding the **New Moon** (*Chodesh*).

<note>The author here refers the reader to a different section in the portion of Chukat for a lengthier explanation of the Red Heifer, as that is its primary location, and he wishes to avoid repetition.</note>

Regarding the secret of purifying the impure and defiling the pure: this relates to the "Heifer" and the "Calf," turning physical matter into spirit. We see this in the Talmud regarding King Saul: "Saul was a year old when he began to reign," meaning he was as untainted by sin as a one-year-old. When a "Heifer whose neck is broken" is brought to a place that cannot be tilled, it signifies that sin causes a lack of "fruit."

This was the greatness of Rabbi Eleazar, who had no peer. I will explain: Rabbi Eleazar represents "the Living God." In my opinion, the dispute in the Zohar between Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Yoshia regarding the principle that "The Torah is not in Heaven" means that for every commandment, there is a secret level of "clinging" (*devekut*) to the divine. One person may penetrate deeper than another, yet "both are the words of the Living God." The law is decided according to the majority because the legal status of a commandment depends on the collective "clinging" of the Jewish people. If all of Israel were on the level of Rabbi Eleazar, the law would follow him. For example, Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam <note>Famous medieval scholars</note> disagree on the order of the scrolls in Tefillin (phylacteries). It is not that one is "wrong," but rather that the human choice and the determination of the Sages define the reality on earth.

The level of Eleazar regarding the Red Heifer was awesome and great, encompassing both upper and lower worlds. Nevertheless, the law follows the Sages because the generations were not worthy of his level. This explains why Moses prayed that Eleazar (the son of Aaron) would be among his descendants, as he saw in him a reflection of his own light—the "shining face" of Moses.

-> Since we have spoken of the holiness of the Sabbath, we shall now speak of the holiness of the New Moon, which is the subject of the portion "The Month" (*Hachodesh*). <-
-> From the knowledge of the holiness of the New Moon, one adds to the knowledge of the holiness of the Sabbath. <-

## In the Midrash Yalkut
"This month shall be for you"—you count by it, but the nations of the world do not count by it. In the name of Rabbi Judah bar Ilai: The "Great One" counts by the "Great One," and the "Small One" counts by the "Small One." Esau, who is called "the Great," counts by the Sun, which is great. Jacob, who is called "the Small," counts by the Moon, which is small.

Rabbi Nachman said: This is a good sign. The Great One (the Sun) rules by day but not by night. So too, Esau the wicked rules in This World, but has no rule in the World to Come. The Small One (the Moon) is seen by day and night. So too, Jacob rules in both This World and the World to Come. Rabbi Nachman also said: As long as the light of the Great One shines, the light of the Small One is not recognized. Once the light of the Great One sets, the light of Jacob is revealed, as it is said: "Arise, shine!"

One might ask: what is the difference between these views? Furthermore, what extra advantage does the Sabbath give to Jacob over Esau? In the Talmud, darkness is compared to This World, yet here the World to Come is compared to the night? And why does Rabbi Nachman call this a "sign"?

## In the Haftarah
"Thus says the Lord: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut the six working days; but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened."
This indicates that **Inner Holiness** opens on the New Moon and the Sabbath. It does not mention the Festivals (Yom Tov). Elsewhere, the Bible asks, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither New Moon nor Sabbath," also omitting Festivals. Some commentators say Festivals are included logically, but why specify Sabbath? In the *Mordechai*, it is written that the wicked in Gehenna rest on Sabbath and the New Moon. On Festivals, they do not mention the "Charity of God" because of the honor of the Festival, so as not to publicize their punishment. Thus, there is a specific parallel between the New Moon and the Sabbath.

"You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy." Regarding the Exodus from Egypt, the Prophets and Sages compared the Holy One to a groom and the Assembly of Israel to a bride. This is the inner meaning of all the liturgical poems—the mutual elevation of God and Israel.

## And Behold
"This month shall be for you" is the first commandment. It is said the whole Torah was given in the "eight weeks" <note>referring to the time around Shavuot</note>. It is also taught that the Torah was given on the Sabbath. Here, the three foundations are revealed: The existence of God, the Torah, and Reward and Punishment. The Sabbath testifies to the creation of the world, and the creation testifies to the Creator. This will be fully revealed in the future, in the "World that is entirely Sabbath," when it will be said: "Behold, this is our God." This will be the eternal reward for those who do His will.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the laws of sacrifices, specifically focusing on the symbolic and mystical meanings behind the Sin Offering (Chatat) and Guilt Offering (Asham), the use of salt, and the philosophical debate regarding how physical offerings can create a spiritual connection with God.</meta>

# The Written Torah: Parashat Shelach

To rectify the commandment in a manner corresponding to the sin; therefore, his offering is a fire-offering or a goat. Regarding the reason the Guilt Offering <term>Asham; a sacrifice brought for specific transgressions such as theft or sacrilege</term> is a male, the Rabbi <note>Likely referring to the 13th-century scholar Nachmanides (Ramban)</note> of blessed memory wrote that because the Sin Offering <term>Chatat; an offering for unintentional sins that carry the penalty of being "cut off" from the spiritual source</term> is for those liable for "excision" <note>Karet; a spiritual penalty of being severed from the Jewish people</note>, it restores the soul to God who gave it. It is as if it is a "pleasing aroma," an "Ascending Offering" <term>Olah; a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire, symbolizing total devotion</term> for it rises higher than the Sin Offering. He explained regarding them the equivalence of the "Hidden Matter" of the community, whose blood is burned outside [the sanctuary], as I have already enlightened you concerning them.

Regarding the reason for the "pouring of the ash" <note>original: "shephek hadeshen"</note> that they shall burn, Rashi <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the preeminent 11th-century commentator</note> explained: also the goat of the Prince <note>Nasi; the tribal leader</note>, its secret is derived from the "goats" <note>Sa'irim; also meaning "demons" or "hairy ones"</note> which are used to remove the spirit of impurity. This is as our Rabbis of blessed memory said in the *Book of the Zohar*: "The goat only approaches from within to drive away the spirit of impurity, etc." However, the secret that appears from the opinion of the Rabbi [Nachmanides], of blessed memory, who wrote as follows: "The goat of the Prince is because he is the king who holds the power of judgment, and he fights the wars of God, and by his sword he shall live, in the manner of a goat." Regarding idolatry, the goat is for the Righteous One who holds the judgment. Behold, his offering is a goat to hint at his attribute, which fights the wars of the Great Name [God], and therefore it is a male.

The reason the Sin Offering involves seven sprinklings, as it is said, "and he shall sprinkle of the blood seven times before the Lord," you shall understand from the secret of the Seventh <note>A reference to the Sefirah of Malchut, the seventh of the lower emanations in Kabbalah</note>. When it says "before the Lord," it is possible that it hints to the "Face of Indignation." "Before the Lord" refers to the front of the Veil <note>The Parochet that separated the Holy from the Holy of Holies</note>. Thus far are his words.

The general principle is: the sacrifice rises to the Unique Name [Y-H-V-H], and it is offered upon the Altar Above, as it says, "They shall come up with acceptance on My altar, and I will glorify My glorious house."

"And on all your offerings you shall offer salt." Salt is the "Covenant of your God," for salt—which begins as water and afterward, through the power of fire, becomes hardened and made into salt—hints to the attribute of Royalty <term>Malchut; the final Sefirah, associated with the physical world and manifest authority</term>. For even though Queen Esther has a "thread of kindness" drawn over her—which is the secret of the "Upper Waters"—nevertheless, "the law of the kingdom is law," <note>original: "dina d'malchuta dina"; a legal principle meaning state law is binding, but here used kabbalistically to link the Kingdom/Malchut with the attribute of Judgment/Din</note> for she is the attribute of <margin>Powers</margin> Judgment. Her saltiness comes from the power of the burning fire. The "salt of the covenant" is the Union [of the divine attributes] through the "Foundation" <term>Yesod; the Sefirah representing the masculine creative force and the site of the covenant</term>, which is the "Sign of the Covenant" as is known.

Leaven and honey represent external forces. Leaven is the "harsh fermentation" [pride] and honey is the sweetness that comes from the power of desire. These are forbidden to be burned as incense because they are not within the secret of the *Korban* <term>Sacrifice; from the root K-R-V, meaning to "bring near" or unify</term>, which brings near and unifies. The sacrifice is to the Lord [Y-H-V-H] specifically, the letters of the Unique Name. Through the sacrifice, we are unified with Him, according to the secret of "And you who cleave unto the Lord your God."

Many philosophers wondered how an Israelite person could "cleave" to the Blessed One by means of a sacrifice. The "Companion" responded to the King of the Khazars <note>referring to Judah Halevi’s *Kuzari*</note> regarding this, saying that the cleaving of the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> with the nation of Israel is already found through the sacrifices offered in the Temple. This is similar to how you find the general soul connected with the body by means of the nutrients within it. Just as we do not know the reason for nourishment—how this lofty soul is sustained by these physical foods which are not of its nature, yet they agree and benefit—so too we do not know the reason for the "need" of the Divine Presence for these sacrifices. However, we find the cleaving of the Divine Presence with us through them. Thus far his words.

The author of *Akeidat Yitzchak* <note>Isaac Arama, a 15th-century philosopher</note> in Gate 57 wrote about this as follows: "Behold, it is clear that in addition to the fact that he [Halevi] did not explain the hidden matter... the parable does not resemble the subject. The difference between them is obvious: nourishment is a complete and publicized necessity for the creation of the body, which is essential for the standing and existence of the soul within it... This is not the case with sacrifices. They are not a necessity for the Divine Presence, nor a necessity for the nation so that the Divine Presence may dwell with them."

Instead of this, I say the matter is as follows: The [philosophers] maintain the health of the body through food, and in its health, the body has peace with its soul. So too with these sacrifices: through proper perspective, they give health and perfection to the collective of the nation and its individuals, so that the Divine attachment may be found among them without doubt. For the emanated and eternal soul [enters] the form of the perfect human through much effort, as it is said, "And man became a living soul." It is a precious soul, higher than the "vital spirit." Just as the body requires its nutrients, so too do these souls have distinct "nutrients" by which they are sustained within the body. While the vital soul is sustained by physical food and drink, this emanated and spiritual soul is only nourished by intellectual and conceptual matters. These are its "bread," just as the soul of our Master [Moses], peace be upon him, was nourished for forty days.

And we have already written there that it was not a matter of physical satiation... but in everything one eats and drinks, the soul has a beautiful portion set aside for it—whether it be a meal for a commandment <note>Seudat Mitzvah</note>, or by intending toward the commandments dependent on that meal, such as the kosher status of the foods, the distancing from prohibitions, and the study of the ways of the Torah. Or, by focusing on the blessings, or to strengthen the body to stand before God in the strength of Torah and service. For truly, these noble and spiritual intentions <margin>Body</margin> sustain the noble soul and maintain it, for they are "holy" and "from the holy things she shall eat." This is the meaning of "man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord."

Upon this very matter, the Divine Presence remains and cleaves to the collective of the Chosen Nation through the act of sacrifices. Not because they are "food" for the Divine Presence, nor for the nation, but because through their good intention and by offering them in a manner pleasing to the Desired One, they assist in perfecting their souls and readying their actions before the Blessed Name. Their good intention and great perfection become the necessary cause for the Divine Presence to be found among them, never to depart. As it says regarding sacrifices in general: "A pleasing aroma to the Lord"—a satisfaction of spirit before Me, for I commanded and My will was done. But when this perfect intention is removed from the sacrifices... the "bundle" is unraveled. Thus far his words.

The words of the author of *Akeidat Yitzchak* are correct, but one must give a reason to "sweeten" his words, just as salt sweetens food. It is this: the matter of the soul's attachment to the body through food was beautifully explained by the Divine Rabbi Isaac Luria <note>The Ari; the most influential 16th-century Kabbalist</note>, of blessed memory. The matter is that there is nothing that does not contain holiness. As our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "There is no blade of grass below that does not have a constellation <note>Mazzal</note> above that strikes it and says 'Grow!'" That "striking" is the abundance flowed into it, and from that power, it moves from potential to action. This flow is a spiritual thing that dwells as "life" within every food. Everything a person eats or drinks is a physical thing, but a spiritual thing is hidden within it as well; it is like a body and a soul.

Man, being both body and soul, eats and drinks: the body enjoys the physical aspect, and the soul <margin>Spirit</margin> enjoys the spiritual aspect within it. This is why it is written that the attachment of the body to the food and drink is through the verse "Man does not live by bread alone"—meaning, from the side of the bread alone as seen by the eye, which is the physical, but "by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord." When there is the "mouth of the Lord" within it—that is, He said "Let it be"—the "mouth of the Lord" caused it to have an "out-going." This spiritual flow is the cause for the soul's attachment to the body. So explained the aforementioned Rabbi.

And so I say as well regarding the attachment of the Holy One, blessed be He, to the nation of Israel through the sacrifices. For it is already known that everything in the lower world is evolved from the upper world, "high above high." The "outputs" of the lower world are: Inanimate, Vegetative, Animal, and Speaking <note>The four categories of creation in medieval Jewish philosophy</note>. These correspond to the four elements:
1.  **Inanimate** is the element of **Earth**.
2.  **Vegetative** is from the secret of **Water**, for the "hand of the rain" saturates the earth and causes it to give birth and grow.
3.  **Animal** is the element of **Air**, for "all that has the breath of life in it" depends on it. Without spirit and air, it dies.
4.  **Speaking** [Human] is the element of **Fire**, whose excellence comes from the soul, which is a spiritual light/fire, as it is written: "The soul of man is the lamp of God."

It is known that the root of the four elements is <margin>Soul</margin> Above, and above the above—"high above high." One might say they are the four camps of the Divine Presence: Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael.
*   **Michael** is the root of spiritual **Water**.
*   **Gabriel** is the root of spiritual **Fire**.
*   **Uriel** is the root of spiritual **Air**.
*   **Raphael** is the root of spiritual **Earth**.

These four spiritual elements evolve from four elements that are even higher and more spiritual, namely the four "Living Creatures" <note>Chayot; the angelic beings of Ezekiel's chariot</note>: the Lion, the Ox, the Human, and the Eagle. These evolve from the hidden spirituality of the "Four Legs of the Chariot" in the world of Emanation <term>Atzilut; the highest of the four spiritual worlds</term>. One could even say the four <margin>Living Creature</margin> letters of the Unique Name [Y-H-V-H] are the Root of the Root of the Roots of the four elements.
*   **Y** (Yod) is the element of **Water**.
*   **H** (Heh) is the element of **Spirit/Air**.
*   **V** (Vav) is the element of **Earth/Physicality**.
...as is known to the Sages of Truth <term>Kabbalists</term>.

There are thousands and tens of thousands of levels without measure until everything returns to its hidden Root. Then you will know and understand that "The Lord is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is none else." This means there is no existence other than Him, for everything is from Him, blessed be He.

Behold, the sacrifices consist of these four:
1.  From the **Inanimate**, there was the **Salt**: "On all your offerings you shall offer salt."
2.  From the **Vegetative**, there are the **Meal Offerings and Libations**.
3.  From the **Animal**, there are **Cattle, Sheep, Turtledoves, and Pigeons**.
4.  From the **Speaking**, there is the **Human** who meditates at the time of the sacrifice, awakening and offering his own soul. "When a soul <note>Nefesh</note> shall offer..." Also, sometimes he literally offers "the human" through the secret of reincarnation <term>Gilgul</term>, for the Blessed Name occasionally prepares for sacrifices those souls who have been reincarnated there. This is hinted at in the verse: "A man <note>Adam</note> who shall offer from among you."

Thus, in the offering, we find the matters of the lower existence being offered to the Higher One, to the Name Y-H-V, which is the spiritual source above. Then there is a connection between the Blessed One and us through the sacrifice. Let us return to the matter of the three purposes of the sacrifice: 1) For Atonement, 2) For Substitution, 3) For the sake of the Union of the Great and Awesome Name.

The verse "A man who shall offer from among you" refers to these three. Regarding **Atonement**, he must surrender his body and soul, humble himself, and perform an act to show that he was liable for [the four court-mandated deaths]: Stoning, Burning, Slaying, and Strangling. Through these, he shows the action of the sacrifice he brings, as if he is offering himself. Then it is "an offering to the Lord." This is why it says "A man who shall offer *from among you*"—that he offers himself through his will. But when he is not awakened to think this thought, and only performs the external action with the animal alone, this is not a "sacrifice to the Lord" for the sake of cleaving...

# Written Torah: Portion of Shlach
### Page 85

To correct our faults in a manner corresponding to the sin, we therefore bring a <term>Guilt Offering<note>original: "Asham"</note></term> or a male goat. Regarding the reason the Guilt Offering must be a male, the Rabbi <note>referring to Nachmanides, also known as Ramban</note> of blessed memory wrote that it is because the <term>Sin Offering<note>original: "Chatat"</note></term> is brought for sins carrying the penalty of spiritual excision <note>original: "Karet," a punishment where the soul is cut off from its divine source</note>, where the soul must return to the God who gave it. However, the Guilt Offering is not brought for sins of spiritual excision; it is as if to provide comfort. Because of this, it is like an <term>Ascending Offering<note>original: "Olah"</note></term>, which rises higher than the Sin Offering. The bull of the anointed priest and the bull brought for a communal oversight are burned outside the camp, as I have already enlightened you regarding them. Regarding the reason the ash deposit is also burned, Rashi explained that even the hair of the "Prince" <note>the leader or King</note> is removed through the goats, which serve to remove the spirit of impurity. This is as our Sages of blessed memory said in the **Zohar**: "The goat is only brought to drive away the spirit of impurity, etc."

However, what appears from the opinion of the Rabbi <note>Ramban</note> of blessed memory is as follows: "The goat of the Prince is brought because he is the King to whom judgment belongs, and he fights the wars of the Lord; he lives by his sword in the manner of a 'Sa'ir' <note>a wordplay on 'goat' and 'Esau/Seir,' the warrior</note>." Thus, his offering is a goat to hint at his attribute, which is fighting the wars of the Great Lord. Therefore, it is a male. As for the reason the blood of the Sin Offering is sprinkled seven times—as it is said, *'And he shall sprinkle of the blood seven times before the Lord'*—you may understand this from the secret of the sevens. Regarding the phrase *'before the Lord,'* it may hint at the 'Face of Wrath,' as *'before the Lord'* refers to the front of the Veil <note>the Parokhet in the Temple</note>. This concludes his words.

The general principle is that the sacrifice is offered to the Unique Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note>, and it is offered on the Altar Above, as it says: *'They shall come up with acceptance on My altar, and I will glorify My glorious house.'*

-> **"On all your offerings you shall offer salt."** <-

Salt is the "Covenant of your God," for salt begins as water and then, through the power of fire, it hardens and becomes salt. This hints at the attribute of <term>Kingship<note>original: "Malchut," the final emanation in Kabbalah</note></term>. Even though Queen Esther had a "thread of kindness" drawn over her—which is the secret of the "Upper Waters"—nevertheless, <note>original: "Dina d'Malchuta Dina"</note> "The law of the kingdom is law," for <note>original: "Adonai"</note> the Name of the Lord represents the attribute of Judgment, and its waters are salty from the power of the burning fire. The "Covenant of Salt" is the secret of Unification through the <term>Foundation<note>original: "Yesod," the emanation associated with the covenant of circumcision</note></term>, which is the sign of the covenant, as is known. 

As for other <insert>Sin</insert> offerings, they are transient and temporary. Leaven represents harsh fermentation, and honey represents the sweetness that comes from the power of desire; these are forbidden from being burned on the altar because they are not part of the secret of the "Sacrifice" <note>original: "Korban," from the root "to draw near"</note>, which brings one close and unifies. The sacrifice is for **the Lord** <note>Y-H-V-H</note>, the Unique Name; through the sacrifice, we unify ourselves with Him, according to the secret of *'And you who cling to the Lord your God.'*

Many philosophers have wondered how the Israelite nation could "cling" to the Blessed One through a sacrifice. The "Wise Companion" <note>the Jewish scholar in Judah Halevi's book, the *Kuzari*</note> answered the King of the Khazars on this point, saying that the attachment of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> to the nation of Israel is found through the medium of the sacrifices offered in His Holy Temple. This is similar to how you find the rational soul attached to the body by means of the food it consumes. Just as we do not know the exact reason for the union of the lofty soul with these physical foods—which are contrary to its nature—but we see that they are useful and necessary, so too we do not know the reason for the "need" of the Divine Presence for these sacrifices. However, we find through the knowledge of the Divine Presence that He is with us by means of them. 

The author of the *Akeidat Yitzchak* <note>Rabbi Isaac Arama</note> wrote in Chapter 57: "It is clear that in addition to what the philosopher explained... the analogy is not entirely identical. The difference is obvious: food is a recognized and well-known necessity for the health of the body, which is essential for the soul's survival within it... This is not the case with sacrifices; they are not a 'need' for the Divine Presence, nor a 'need' for the nation in the sense of physical survival, even though the Divine Presence and the attachment to God dwell among them because of them." 

He explains further: Just as the health of the body is completed through food, and in its health, it finds peace with its soul so that the soul clings to it, so too is the matter with these sacrifices. Through their proper provision, they give health and perfection to the nation as a whole, to its individuals, and its elite, so that the Divine attachment will undoubtedly be found among them. For it is known that the emanated soul strengthens itself within the perfected person through his great alacrity and effort—as it is said, *'And man became a living soul.'* This is a precious and lofty soul, higher than a mere biological or animalistic spirit. Just as they are distinct in their general foods, so too their specialized "foods" are what allow the soul to endure within the body. The biological soul, which is the primary messenger of the body, is nourished by physical food and drink. However, this emanated and spiritual soul is only sustained by intellectual and conceptual matters, for these are its "bread." This is how the soul of our Master <note>Moses</note>, peace be upon him, was sustained for forty days.

We have already written there that this was not a purely spiritual matter outside of his nature. Rather, in everything a person eats and drinks, the soul has a "beautiful portion" unique to it—if it is a meal for a commandment <note>a Seudat Mitzvah</note>, or if one intends to fulfill the laws of the meal, such as preparing the food properly, avoiding forbidden items according to the Torah, focusing on the blessings, or intending to strengthen the body so it may stand before God in the study of Torah and Divine service. Indeed, these honorable and spiritual intentions sustain the noble soul and preserve it, for they are "holy," and "of the holy things it shall eat." This is the meaning of: *'Man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord.'*

In this very manner, the Divine Presence remains attached to the Chosen Nation through the act of sacrifice—not because they are "food" for the Presence, but because when their intention is pure and they are offered in a pleasing and appropriate way, they help the person perfect their soul and rectify their deeds before God. This causes their refined intention and perfection to be the necessitating cause for the Divine Presence to be found among them, never to part. As it says regarding sacrifices in general: *'A pleasing aroma to the Lord'*—meaning, a satisfaction before Me, for I commanded and My will was done. But when the intention and the proper sign are removed from the sacrifices, the Divine Table is uprooted, and the "beloved connection" is severed.

The words of the author of the *Akeidah* are correct, but they need a "reason" to sweeten them, just as salt sweetens food. This "reason" is found in the words of the Divine <term>Ari<note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the father of modern Kabbalah</note></term> of blessed memory. The matter is this: there is nothing in existence that does not contain holiness. As our Sages said: "There is no blade of grass below that does not have a 'constellation' <note>original: "Mazal"</note> above telling it to grow." This "growth" is the flow of energy from the influencer to the influenced. This flow is a spiritual vitality that dwells within it. Thus, every food you eat and every drink you consume is a physical thing, but within it is hidden a spiritual spark. It is like a body and a soul. 

A human being, who is both body and soul, eats and drinks: the body enjoys the physical aspect, and the soul enjoys the spiritual aspect within it. This is the reason the soul clings to the body through food and drink. This is why the verse says, *'Man does not live by bread alone'*—meaning, not just from the visible, physical "bread"—*'but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord.'* Because the "mouth of the Lord" said "Let there be," that Divine word caused it to exist. This spiritual flow is the cause of the soul's attachment to the body. So explained the aforementioned Rabbi.

I also say: the attachment of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to the nation of Israel through sacrifices works the same way. It is known that everything in the lower world evolves from the upper world, "high above high." The components of the lower world are: Silent (Mineral), Growth (Vegetable), Living (Animal), and Speaking (Human). These correspond to the four elements: 
1. **Silent** is the element of Earth.
2. **Growth** is the secret of Water (for rain falls and saturates the earth, causing growth).
3. **Living** is the element of Air (everything that has the breath of life). Without this "airy spirit," it would die.
4. **Speaking** is Man, whose superiority comes from the Soul, which is the spiritual element of Fire (as it says, *'The soul of man is the lamp of God'*). 

It is known that these four elements have their roots above, and higher than high. They correspond to the four camps of the Divine Presence: **Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael**. 
*   **Michael** is the spiritual element of Water.
*   **Gabriel** is the spiritual element of Fire.
*   **Uriel** is the spiritual element of Air.
*   **Raphael** is the spiritual element of Earth.

These four spiritual elements evolve from four even higher and more spiritual elements, namely the four "Living Creatures" of the Chariot: the **Lion, Ox, Human, and Eagle**. These, in turn, evolve from the hidden "Four Legs of the Throne" in the world of Emanation <note>Atzilut</note>. Finally, the four letters of the **Unique Name** <note>Y-H-V-H</note> are the root of all roots for the four elements:

*   **H (Heh)** is the element of Earth.
(As is known to the scholars of Truth).

But the wicked are the opposite; the excision of the soul, etc. This is why the righteous turn the Attribute of Judgment into the Attribute of Mercy, and the wicked do the opposite. For the aspect of the soul and the body and the windows [of the soul] are this. Nevertheless, a single memory rises here and there. Therefore, the composition of matter and substance, the blind and the... hints at the teaching of Akavia and the teaching of our chapter regarding the ten miracles. 

Regarding the teaching of Akavia <note>from Pirkei Avot 3:1</note>: See in *Midrash Shmuel* why he teaches "all respond": one corresponding to the body and one corresponding to the soul, etc. See there. And with this, he answers "And to where are you going?" and "And to where" as in the beginning. For its meaning is also "nothingness." I mean to say, the soul in its coming is naked, as it says "The separation in the Gate of the Soul." But in its return, it says "Before whom are you destined to give an account," and it shall be "and it was light," dancing to ascend the soul's ascent in its eternity, as I have written elsewhere. And regarding the body, it says, "Before the King of Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He," for then He will judge all the kings of the earth, as I saw in the chapter "All are Kin," see there.

And through this, our Mishnah will be explained: "Ten miracles were performed for our ancestors in the Temple: 
1. No woman ever miscarried from the smell of the holy meat. 
2. The holy meat never spoiled. 
3. No fly was ever seen in the slaughterhouse. 
4. The High Priest never suffered a nocturnal emission on Yom Kippur. 
5. The rains never extinguished the fire of the wood-pile on the altar. 
6. The wind never overcame the pillar of smoke. 
7. No defect was ever found in the Omer, or in the Two Loaves, or in the Showbread. 
8. The people stood crowded together but prostrated themselves with ample space. 
9. No snake or scorpion ever caused harm in Jerusalem. 
10. No man ever said to his fellow, 'The place is too narrow for me to lodge in Jerusalem.'"

Thus far [the Mishnah]. And there is a difficulty: why does it say "for our ancestors"? It should have said... Granted, "ten miracles were performed for our ancestors in Egypt," meaning through the ten plagues from which they were saved when the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought them upon the Egyptians; see what *Midrash Shmuel* says there in the name of Rabbi Moshe Almosnino. Rather, the matter is that from these ten, one learns ten things, and the choice is in man's hand. They are considered against the five [types of] knowledge... the right hand against the three things of the Mishnah that Akavia mentioned: "From where did you come?", "To where are you going?", and "Before whom [are you destined to give an account]?" 

Now, one must make a repair <term>tikkun|Tikkun: a kabbalistic term for spiritual rectification or repair</term> against these... and then "before whom are you [destined to give an account]"... only "remembrance" is relevant as a repair. This makes eight. And so too in the body, similarly, there are eight. Therefore, our Mishnah begins with the physical <note>the body</note> and concludes with the praise of the soul.

**1. "No woman ever miscarried from the smell of the holy meat":** This is against the aspect of "From where did you come? From a tainted drop." And as it is brought in the Talmud, Tractate Yoma page 82b, regarding a pregnant woman who smelled [food on Yom Kippur] and they came before Rabbi. He said to them, "Go and whisper to her that it is Yom Kippur." They whispered to her, and she was quieted. He recited over [the fetus]: "Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you." From him emerged Rabbi Yochanan. Another pregnant woman smelled [food] and came before Rabbi Hanina. He said, "Whisper to her," and she was not quieted. He recited over [the fetus]: "The wicked are estranged from the womb" <note>Psalm 58:4</note>.

<margin>Luder:</margin>
This awakens the name "lowly" [meaning the body]. All "from the holy meat." And so it is written "from the holy meat" that is in her womb. 
**2. "The holy meat never spoiled":** This corresponds to "To where [are you going]? To a place of dust and worms, etc." On an ordinary day, it would rot, but the "holy meat"—the worm had no power over it. See Rabbi Elazar in the chapter *HaPoalim* regarding how many righteous people did not change [after death]. 

As he concludes, he opens the repair so that it does not smell, etc. 
**3. "No fly was ever seen in the slaughterhouse":** This refers to the lessening of bodily desires. For it says "Behold, he kills cattle and slaughters sheep." The "fly" is the Evil Inclination, as found in Berachot page 10b. But one who follows after superfluities... "and I will spread dung upon your festivals." The repair for "from where did you come" [from a tainted drop] is: 
**4. "No nocturnal emission occurred to the High Priest on Yom Kippur":** The secret of purity of thought in the brain, from where the seed originates. A person should be pure all his days, for every day is like Yom Kippur, as Rabbi Eliezer said to his disciples: "[Repent] one day [before your death]," etc. Then he is attached, and the filth of the lip is purified. 
**5. "The rains never extinguished the fire of the wood-pile":** This hints at the eternity of the judgment of the future. 

We shall clarify the matter of the soul and investigate according to the little we have drawn from holy inquiry. Spiritual creatures are not mentioned explicitly in the Torah, and there are many opinions on this, proven in the chapter *Avodat HaKodesh*, etc. In this, I will also investigate: why is it called the **Holy Tongue** <term>Lashon Kodesh|Lashon Kodesh: the Hebrew language, considered by mystics to be the essential language of creation</term>? Also, regarding the "handles of vessels" and the "small leg of the Throne"—it has no "hand" <note>a play on the word 'yad' meaning both hand and handle</note> that enlightens our eyes.

The attributes "Hand" and "Wave" known in the inquiries [of God], Blessed be He—all are answered with one solution based on the introduction to the **Pardes** <note>The "Orchard," a foundational kabbalistic work by Rabbi Moshe Cordovero</note>. Our language and letters are not merely conventional [agreements], but are "essences" <note>ontological realities</note>. Everything that we speak is drawn from the Holy Tongue, and this evolved from that—the matter of the names that Adam called [the animals]. It is found that the spirituality is the letters themselves. For example, "Rain" <note>Geshem</note> in truth refers to the "Higher Spiritual Flow," the ultimate spirituality. Afterward, it spreads in its likeness through all the worlds, in each world according to what it is, until in this physical world it is called "Rain" <note>Geshem</note> which falls down. This is a borrowed name, like the "handles <note>hands</note> of vessels," etc.

In this way... and he began with blessings... from the blessing in the rain from its own side, but it was only to mention the grain and the fruit. Delve into this. And return to our subject: "The fire of the wood-pile" refers to the higher fire, the secret of souls through... and the soul from its roots is the flow of the attachment of spirituality. One who does not merit it then will not be able to endure the abundance of the flow, for he cannot receive the abundance of the good... But the perfect one—"Many waters cannot extinguish the love." Delve into this now.

Regarding the five levels of the soul—three things and three repairs of the right hand:
**6. "The wind never overcame the pillar of smoke":** The aspect of "From where did you come?"—the soul comes from above the world of angels and spirits. The smoke connects the flesh with what is above; it is the [ascent of] souls. They were all standing as at the Standing at Sinai—a spiritual man who ascends. It is written: "And Mount Sinai was altogether in smoke." Then the angels were accusing, "Give [Your glory to the heavens]..." but "the wind did not overcome," etc.
**7. "No defect was found [in the Omer, etc.]":** Against the aspect of "To where are you going?" And here there is no [argument between] Sadducees and Rabbis regarding the Nefesh in the Ruach and the Ruach in the Neshamah... "For not by bread alone does man live, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord"—that is the nourishment. 
These three things mentioned... the Festival and the Sabbath. I mean to say: the Omer evolved from the Manna. "And the Omer, etc." and "they ate of the Manna on the morrow." They returned and descended on a weekday, a second portion for them on the Festival in the week, and the Showbread on the Sabbath. Thus are the levels of the soul, and this is guarded. One must ensure that "no defect is seen." 
**8. "Standing crowded [but prostrating with space]":** A repair of the heart... against "From where did you come."

# The Written Torah

The future and the source of the flow, and their fruit, are destined for us... the secret is that <term>matter will return to intellect</term><note>A philosophical and Kabbalistic concept suggesting that in the messianic future, physical substance will be refined and elevated to a purely spiritual or intellectual state.</note>. Behold, the Land of Israel, which the Lord seeks, provides spirits for the supernal land, for "all Israel [have a portion in the world to come]," as it is said, "Your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever." Behold, the <term>World to Come</term><note>Olam Ha-Ba</note> is called "Sabbath." The six years [of the agricultural cycle] correspond to "For in six days the Lord made [the heavens and the earth]," and so on until the Lord. The literal meaning of the <term>Sabbatical</term><note>Shmita</note> and <term>Jubilee</term><note>Yovel</note> years is for the sake of the holiness of the Sabbath... and until the Lord. This is a hint that the days of our years are seventy years; they are fifty from the age of twenty and onwards when one is held fully accountable.

Behold, seventy years allude to the six days of creation, with ten <term>Utterances</term><note>The ten sayings by which God created the world</note> for each day. When twenty are removed, fifty remain—seven times seven, for every seven rises to a "Sabbath of Sabbaths"... regarding the "aftergrowth of your harvest" [Leviticus 25:5], the *Zohar* and the commentators say... the river that goes out from Eden... and now "the river shall be parched and dry" [Isaiah 19:5]. See the *Zohar*, parashat Vayishlach... the story of the grapes that Eve squeezed... "And the Sabbath of the land shall be for food for you" [Leviticus 25:6]—he who toils on the eve of Sabbath shall eat on the Sabbath. "For you, and for your servant..." for distress saves many souls... and it is proven for the World to Come... just as with "another" and "Go forth" (*Lech Lecha*). Specifically: "If I am not for myself, who will be for me?" The seven Sabbaths [of years] correspond to the seven days of Creation. A person must awaken themselves. The fiftieth year is the "year of the seventy," and the "sounding of the shofar blast" before Israel. This is the custom when a person dies... the shofar goes out. And in the *Zohar* (III:12b), it says that on this day He shall atone—death atones for those who repent. "And you shall return every man to his possession," and "the spirit shall return to God." Regarding this, a person must always contemplate and not live "casually" (*keri*)... and consider himself a "sojourner" in the land, guarding eternity for the future. This is the meaning of "For you are strangers and sojourners with Me." This is difficult, but it can be explained: in the land, holiness leads to a permanent "dwelling," yet a person should not make their stay here "fixed." Warnings are given that "the land shall not be sold forever," unlike those mistaken ones who think their portion and their names are eternal in their own foolishness because they have wealth and a house. "Unless the Lord builds a house [the builders labor in vain]." This is "For you are strangers and sojourners with Me." It is difficult, but one should be attached to their Creator even in physical matters. This is "And you shall dwell on the land in safety." Afterward comes the spiritual reward: "If you walk in My statutes," which is the spiritual goal I alluded to above. Then matter shall return to intellect, and "you shall dwell safely in your land." May we also, all of us who are alive here today, merit the World to Come, God willing. "And he shall dwell on the land," not staying only overnight but dwelling in safety without fear—this is "and a land they envisioned." Speedily in our days, may we merit the dwelling. They announce before him the "pangs of the Messiah," for the Lord will grant rest to our exit from Babylon.
->The Messiah shall bring us to our land, and we shall no longer be mere overnight guests; the "generation or son of a generation" shall be established, and they shall eat. Amen.<-

## The Book of the Priestly Torah is completed with the help of the One who dwells in the heights.
### Chapter on the Way of Life: Ethical Rebuke from the entire Book of the Priestly Torah <note>Leviticus</note>

**"A man [Adam], when he brings an offering from among you"** [Leviticus 1:2]. I have already written: awaken the "Man" within us; it should be as if he is offering himself. He should think: "For the Lord, I bring this up." This is for a sin, a <term>Sin Offering</term><note>Chatat</note>, and "this is the law of the <term>Guilt Offering</term><note>Asham</note>." That is to say, what is done to the animal is the "Torah" [instruction] that the living being deserves to have done to it... as mentioned in the *Zohar* regarding sin. So too with the Sin Offering and the Guilt Offering. When he feels within himself that he is attached to the Creator, "this is the law of the <term>Peace Offerings</term><note>Shelamim</note>"—peace for the Altar, peace for the priesthood, and peace for the owners. Then the verse is fulfilled: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation," for the owners also eat just like the priests. Now, in our iniquities, when we have neither Altar nor priest, one should say the "Law of the Burnt Offering," the "Law of the Sin Offering," and the "Law of the Guilt Offering." One should occupy oneself with their laws, which is equivalent to bringing them. It should be done with perfection, with a broken heart within him, fulfilling: "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit." Furthermore, "occupying oneself" with the section of the sacrifices implies knowing their reason and secret. The sacrifice—especially when one fasts—is a "pleasing aroma," as brought in *Tola'at Yaakov* (Parashat Vayechi). The secret and hint of fasting is that it is an altar prepared for atonement for his sins. By reducing food and drink, one's fat and blood are diminished; he offers this in his thought and prayer before his God, and it is as pleasing before Him as the fat and limbs of a burnt offering. The "fire of the flame" is its foundation; it shall burn within him and not be extinguished, to consume and diminish his fat and blood. The secret of the truth is: just as there are "limbs" and matters and judgments above to consume the sacrifice from within the fire, so too there are limbs and known matters below in man. Their consumption of his fat and blood makes it heard—just as the smoke of the fire rises from the sacrifice, so the spirit of man goes out and ascends, and it is a "pleasing spirit to the Lord." All this occurs on the day of fasting. A man must direct his spirit and soul to all these paths and place himself before his God as if he were an altar of atonement. As we wrote in the previous chapter: the "laying of hands" (*semikhah*) on the sacrifice is through the power of the soul, spirit, breath, speech, memory, and prayer—not just for the sin he committed. Let it be for you a "Peace Altar" in all its matters and secrets. The fat, the blood, the fire, the smoke, and the aroma—all are a hint before the Lord. Just as this Altar brings near all the sacrifices in the world, so too when we [study], this Altar brings near his sacrifice... for the Torah is upon him for all his sins and all his guilt before the Lord. On this Altar, whether for a sin or a guilt offering, whether done in error or intentionally, he shall offer it... and all the limbs before the Lord shall be turned into smoke. And if a "Peace Offering" is his sacrifice in this place... he will find peace. It is a literal peace-sacrifice to atone for him before the Lord. Every sacrifice in the world can a man offer on this Altar, for this is a literal altar of atonement, to give life upon it and to offer all his limbs below to find the desires of Heaven. "Happy is the Altar... happy is the people whose God is the Lord." Thus far his words.

Regarding "not severing the head" of the bird-sin-offering, the Sage Rabbi Menachem the Babylonian <note>A 16th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote: The reason for this commandment is that the sinner damages the Creator of all... and not the "Face." Therefore, his sacrifice—which is his substitute, "a soul for a soul"—comes from the nape of the neck, since he was "stiff-necked." In the bird-sin-offering specifically, there is atonement, whereas in the bird-burnt-offering there is no confession. Therefore, in the bird-sin-offering, "he shall pinch its head at its nape but shall not divide it." On every sacrifice, "you shall offer salt." Rabbi Menachem the Babylonian (of blessed memory) said the reason for this commandment is as our Sages said: The Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the waters of the sea that they would be offered. He who brings a sacrifice must be [humble]... just as salt sweetens meat, so do sufferings [sweeten the person]. As our Sages said: "One rebuke in the heart of a man is better than a hundred lashes." Or, repentance is established like the covenant of salt.
->On all your sacrifices you shall offer salt. Thus far his words.<-

---

Regarding "not burning leaven or honey," the aforementioned Rabbi said the reason for this commandment is derived from the word "you shall burn" rather than "you shall offer." This teaches that with the sacrifice, one needs [proper] intention for it to be acceptable. As for leaven and honey—how is one drawn after them? They rise and elevate themselves by their nature [fermentation], but atonement depends on humility. Therefore, all meal offerings come as <term>Matzah</term><note>Unleavened bread, symbolizing humility</note>. The "burning" should not be made from what "rises"... and "burning" only occurs when "mist went up from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground" [Genesis 2:6]... those whose portion is before the Lord.

**"When a leader [Nasi] sins"** [Leviticus 4:22]. Happy is the generation whose leader pays attention... then surely the rest of the people will be awakened. There is a moral hint in the verse "the sin of the community" is "when a leader sins"—meaning, if the community sins, the leader is considered to have sinned if it was in his power to protest and he did not.

**"If a soul sins..."** and it is concealed, "or if his sin is made known to him." In the *Zohar*, it is written that there is an awakening in these verses. The intent is "or if his sin was [already] made known to him"—meaning he was already informed. <margin>In the image of the fetus</margin> From Heaven, before he comes into the world, he is reminded, as in "Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you." For there, they inform the person and show him a lamp burning over his head to guide him and teach him the ways of the Lord, and to adjure him to walk in the ways of God. As mentioned in the section: Rabbi Simlai lectured: "To what is the fetus in its mother's womb comparable?... A lamp is lit over its head, and it gazes from one end of the world to the other... and they swear to it and teach it the entire Torah, as it is said: 'He taught me and said to me,' etc. And it says: 'When His lamp shined over my head,' etc. It does not leave there until they adjure it, as it is said: 'For to Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.' What is the oath they adjure it? They say to it: 'Be righteous and be not wicked; and even if the whole world tells you that you are righteous, be in your own eyes as if you were wicked.' And know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is pure and His ministers are pure, and the soul He placed in you is pure. If you keep it in purity, well and good; if not, He will take it from you." Thus far. If so, man is already warned and taught before he comes into the world. Thus, when he transgresses, he should return from his sin. This is "or if his sin... was made known to him." Perhaps there is a support here: "If a soul sins, and hears the voice of an adjuration"—which refers to that aforementioned oath.

<meta>This page continues the enumeration of the 613 Commandments (Mitzvot), focusing on social justice, interpersonal ethics, and ritual prohibitions against pagan practices as found in the book of Leviticus.</meta>

<header>The Written Torah</header>

## 351. Not
to commit injustice in judgment, as it is said: "You shall do no injustice in judgment." The reason for this commandment is that one who commits injustice tips himself and the entire world toward the scale of guilt, while one who executes justice tips himself and the entire world toward the scale of merit. In the Jerusalem Talmud <note>The *Talmud Yerushalmi*, a collection of Rabbinic traditions compiled in the Land of Israel</note>, they asked Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta: "Why should we perform the judgment of the Torah?" and they said one should use the language of the Torah’s law. If you ask the governors <note>original: *Dokus*, likely referring to Roman administrative officials</note>, they would say that they are commanded to perform the law of the Torah as it was given at Sinai; and if one deviates from the law in a great matter, he is assuredly committing injustice in judgment.

## 352. Not
to honor a great person in judgment, as it is said: "nor shall you honor the person of the mighty." The reason for this commandment is so that the arguments of his fellow litigant are not suppressed out of intimidation; therefore, you shall not show honor. For you must honor the Face of the Greatest of all the great, the Creator of all, blessed be He, and the glory of the Ancient of Days who stands within the assembly of judges. If you show favoritism to a great man, you are casting doubt on the One who crowns the great. We have learned that we swear in a <term>Talmudic scholar</term> <note>Hebrew: *Talmid Chacham*</note> while seated, but we tell a common person to stand; however, if he does not sit, we do not worry about the prohibition of "honoring the great."

## 353. Not
to go about as a talebearer, as it is said: "You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people." The reason for this commandment is that gossip kills three people <note>The speaker, the listener, and the subject</note> and brings with it "all the powders of the merchant" <note>A poetic reference to the many varieties of gossip</note>. Onkelos <note>The famous 2nd-century translator of the Torah into Aramaic</note> translated this as "do not eat morsels of slander," hinting that people feed the talebearer so <gloss>(that he might increase)</gloss> his coming and going to speak evil. He used the word "morsels" <note>original: *kortzin*</note> just as we have learned "they nipped" <note>original: *kartzu*</note>, meaning in the context of slaughter <gloss>(see the chapter 'All the Offerings' in the tractate Menachot)</gloss>, for in every mention of gossip he speaks in a way that causes death, and people accept his words as if they are sweet to their tongue. However, it is permitted to speak <term>slander</term> <note>Hebrew: *Lashon Hara*, literally 'evil tongue'</note> regarding "masters of dispute" <note>people who cause communal strife</note>, even if the information is true. "You shall not go as a talebearer"—yet if by "talebearing" you can save someone, you must not "stand idly by the blood of your neighbor." The text says "do not go" to teach that even the act of walking toward it is forbidden, the opposite of <gloss>(and they went)</gloss> and they did, for the talebearer actively goes about to gossip. <gloss>(At the end of the tractate Pesachim, the one who reveals a secret receives his reward for the going and the doing.)</gloss>

## 354. Not
to hate your brother, as it is said: "You shall not hate your brother in your heart." The reason for this commandment is that because the hatred is in the heart, a person cannot guard himself against it; such a person possesses pride, which is an abomination to the Lord. But if he is a person who is not righteous, since he is a "servant of the heart" <note>motivated by his own desires</note>, you are certainly obligated to hate his deeds. "Baseless hatred" was the cause of our exile, as in "How does the city sit solitary" <note>The Book of Lamentations 1:1, beginning with *Eichah*</note>; the initials of *Eichah* <note>original: א"יכ"ה</note> hint that "Evil is He" <note>original: ר"ע ה"ו</note>. Since he is your brother, do not hate your brother in your heart.

## 355. Not
to stand idly by the blood of one's enemy, as it is said: "Neither shall you stand idly by the blood of your neighbor." The reason for this commandment is that all of Israel <gloss>(are guarantors)</gloss> for one another <gloss>(and see the commentary on the Torah in the chapter 'He who brings')</gloss>. This is hinted at because he brings his friend to a state of hanging <note>meaning, in danger</note>; if the Torah is strict about saving money, how much more so regarding the saving of a soul. If one sees another committing a transgression whereby he loses his world to come, he must save him. The verse says "do not pass over" so that you should not <gloss>(delay)</gloss> <gloss>(himself and not stand idle)</gloss>—since he is your "neighbor" in Torah and commandments. It also uses the language of a "statute," hinting that "your soul is in place of his soul" if you stand idly by the blood of your neighbor.

## 356. Not
to shame one's fellow, as it is said: "and you shall not bear sin because of him." The reason for this commandment is compared to one who pursues the blind and misleads him. If you do not rebuke him <gloss>(do not separate from him, do not charge him, and even more so in a way that he will not return from his evil way)</gloss>, you will carry his punishment on your own shoulders, for you are a guarantor of his debt. The Holy One desires for one to rebuke another gently so that he will accept it from him. If you cover for him, "an eye for an eye," you are sufficient to rebuke yourself first <note>meaning, self-correction precedes correcting others</note>. If in a place of rebuke one is permitted to "whiten his face" <note>to shame him publicly</note>, how much more so during a time of dispute; yet one is truly not permitted, so that you do not "bear sin because of him." Not to take revenge—see "Do not take vengeance."

## 357. Not
to bear a grudge, as it is said: "nor bear any grudge." The reason for this commandment is that it is not fitting to behave toward a holy person with a grudge kept in the heart <gloss>(to harbor it)</gloss> <gloss>(not to remember it because of the debt)</gloss>. If one remembers the sin, he is essentially taking revenge by not lending to him, just as he did not lend to him. It is forbidden for a scholar to forgive his own honor <note>when the Torah's honor is at stake</note>. Regarding that which Mar Zutra the Pious used to say when he got into bed—"I forgive and pardon all who have vexed me"—one could say he only forgave the pain of his body if someone cursed him, but he would not forgive the honor of the Torah. He did not keep it in his heart, for a <term>Talmudic scholar</term> who does not "avenge and guard a grudge like a snake" is not a true scholar. Perhaps the strictness only applied to monetary matters. It is fitting to accept an apology and to be "one who passes over his traits" <note>forgives slights</note>, for then all his sins will be passed over. It is forbidden to hand over a case to a court of law <note>to seek divine judgment against a fellow</note>. You also: "shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge."

## 358. Not to crossbreed animals, as it is said: "You shall not let your cattle gender with a diverse kind."

## 359. And not
to sow diverse seeds, as it is said: "you shall not sow your field with mingled seed." The reason for these commandments is that the Creator <gloss>(established everything in its forms and structures in the house of the world from the time of the constellations)</gloss> in His wisdom designed everything, each according to its essence, as is fitting for every thing and matter. Everything is manifest before Him, the Primordial One. It is written, for example, that species should not be mixed, lest the blessing of the perfection of all be diminished. These prohibitions exist so as not to mix and hinder that blessing. The verse concludes: "You shall keep my statutes: You shall not let your cattle gender with a diverse kind." Our Sages of blessed memory said that this refers to "diverse kinds" <note>Hebrew: *Kilayim*</note> to teach us that the reason is not to change the "engraving" of creation—every single species for itself. For even the smallest herb below has a "constellation" <note>Hebrew: *Mazal*</note> above that strikes it and says "Grow!" By mixing, one confuses the constellations. Therefore: "you shall not sow your field with mingled seed, nor let your cattle gender with a diverse kind."

## 360. Not to eat the fruit of a young tree <note>Hebrew: *Orlah*</note>, as it is said: "three years shall it be as uncircumcised unto you: it shall not be eaten." The reason is that during the first three years, the forces of impurity dominate the land and become "uncircumcised." One who benefits from the fruits born from that power is as if he benefits from the power of impurity called "uncircumcision," for they are their portion and lot. It must be removed and purged from the Vineyard of the Lord of Hosts. After three years, holiness and purity rest upon them. Do not wonder at this, for the law of the first three years relates to the "returning virginity" <gloss>(it shall be uncircumcised to you)</gloss> <gloss>(for they return after three years...)</gloss> <note>This gloss contains complex mystical and legal metaphors comparing the tree's growth to human development and purity laws.</note>

## 361. Not to practice divination, as it is said: "neither shall you use enchantment." The reason is that it is not fitting for Israel, who are the "essence" of the world, to say that everything happens by chance and not by Divine Providence, Heaven forbid. This includes those who use <term>Ov and Yidde’oni</term> <note>forms of necromancy or spiritism</note> to say, "The Lord has guided me." But "there is no divination in Jacob," for one who is blessed by the "Heel" <note>referring to Jacob/Israel</note> will not be interrupted. Therefore: "neither shall you use enchantment." <gloss>(Some say this refers to those who perform omens... such as when a piece of bread falls from his mouth, or a staff falls from his hand, he says 'I will not go today'... or if a fox passes by him... all this is included in the prohibition.)</gloss>

## 362. Not to practice sorcery <note>specifically interpreting times/clouds</note>, as it is said: "nor observe times." The reason is that all of one's trust should be in the Creator of all, blessed be He. This refers to one who looks at the clouds, performs illusions, or conducts his affairs only during specific hours and "seasons" <note>Hebrew: *onot*, from which 'observe times' is derived</note>. All this is included in "nor observe times," for the Creator of all does good or bad according to a person's deeds, not by the necessity of the hours.

## 363. Not to round the corners of the head, as it is said: "You shall not round the corners of your heads."

## 364. And not to destroy the corners of the beard, as it is said: "neither shall you mar the corners of your beard." The reason for this commandment is to distance oneself from the custom of idolatrous priests, who would mar the corners of their beards. A God-fearing person should be careful not to pass a razor under the throat at all, for sometimes it pulls the skin of the "corner" with it <gloss>(as mentioned by Maimonides and the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol)</gloss>. However, trimming with scissors is permitted. He who transgresses and does not repent—one sin drags another. "I will heal your backslidings." Therefore, do not round the corners of your head, so that you do not destroy the corners of your beard.

## 365. Not to make a tattoo, as it is said: "nor print any marks upon you." The reason is that it was the custom of pagan priests to mark the name of an idol upon <gloss>(their flesh)</gloss> <gloss>(it is forbidden to write even with ink... because it looks like a tattoo)</gloss> to publicize that they are its servants. They seal their own iniquity upon themselves. We, however, are hinted to the Creator of all, blessed be He, in our hearts and by the seal of the "Sign of the Holy Covenant" <note>Circumcision</note>. They make tattoos so that the forces of impurity will not distance themselves from them <gloss>(and they 'strike' and 'harden' like roosters...)</gloss>.

## 366. Not to perform the act of the *Ov* <note>a medium who calls up the dead</note>.

## 367. And not to perform the act of the *Yidde’oni* <note>a wizard/fortune teller</note>, as it is said: "Regard not them that have familiar spirits (*Ovot*), nor wizards (*Yidde’onim*)." The reason is that they imagine in their minds a creative force when they perform these "layings down" through the power of impurity to wake the dead. A spirit of impurity clothes them, and they tell the future—some of which comes true. *Ovot* is related to the "Fathers of Impurity" <note>Abot HaTumah</note>. It says "do not turn to them" rather than "do not do," meaning one should not even give them "face" <note>attention</note>, for "the Face of the Lord is their portion." One should stifle them, as it is forbidden to look at the face of a wicked person. The *Yidde’oni* is a bone of a beast whose name is *Yiddo*; one places it in his mouth and it speaks words of "truth," as it is found in the category of *Urim* <note>divine oracle</note> where impurity is more common. In the Jerusalem Talmud, it is said a person of the mountain... "Do not turn" neither to the *Ovot* nor to the *Yidde’onim*.

## 368. Not to commit injustice in judgment <note>referring specifically to weights and measures</note>, as it is said: "You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in meteyard [measures of length], etc." The reason for this commandment is that one who commits injustice in measures is equal to one who commits injustice in legal judgment. The one who commits injustice in measures destroys the world. The measurer is called a "judge." Since it says "you shall not do" rather than "you shall not judge," it implies an act of measurement. You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment.
