<meta>This page continues a deep mystical and philosophical exploration of the Torah portion regarding the Red Heifer (Parashat Parah). It focuses on the distinction between "statutes" (laws without apparent reason) and "judgments" (logical laws), specifically comparing the spiritual capacities of Moses and Rabbi Akiva.</meta>

### Written Torah — Homily for the Portion of the Red Heifer

To what is this matter comparable? To an actual angel, who is more of an angel in what he perceives of man, and perceives more of an angel than a man perceives of an angel. Yet, a man perceives a man more than he perceives an angel, and more than an angel perceives a man. This is a statute and a decree for the Master of the World. Rabbi Akiva's proof for this is: "A statute I have engraved, a decree I have decreed" <note>This refers to a famous Midrash where God explains that the laws of the Red Heifer are divine decrees that transcend human logic</note>. For Israel, this is a fixed statute in its place that does not budge. Rather, regarding all perceptions of the hidden realm, one has no permission to contemplate them—meaning, "do not seek out things that are too wondrous for you" <note>original: "be-mufla mimcha al tidrosh," a quote from Ben Sira often cited in the Talmud regarding the limits of human inquiry into the divine</note>. This is not to be understood according to its literal sense, as if one has no permission to wonder why He commanded something that has no reason. Rather, the matter follows what the commentators have written: that it is a statute (*chok*) for Israel, but a judgment (*mishpat*)—meaning the reason for the thing—for the God of Jacob. By the merit of the God of the heights, for the sake of Moses <note>referred to here as "the man of God"</note>, which is the aspect of His divinity above.

Afterward, Jacob hinted at this through the name of Akiva, with the additional letter *aleph* of "God" <note>The author is using gematria, or Jewish numerology, to link the names of Jacob and Akiva</note>. Behold, Moses and Akiva are equal in "small number" count, both totaling 12. For Moses is 8 and 4 <note>M=4, Sh=3, H=5 in small count, but the author uses a specific calculation here</note>. However, the superiority of Moses over Rabbi Akiva in the "large number" count is well known, involving the Name of 26 <note>the Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>, which is the sum of three Names revealed to Moses: the Name *Ehyeh* ("I Will Be"), the Name *YHWH* ("The Lord"), and the Name *Adonai* ("My Lord"). These three names and the "Small Count" also exist within the Name *YHWH* itself, in which Moses' prophecy is found, numbering 12. Furthermore, the superiority of Moses is 78. Our Sages of blessed memory said that 50 Gates of Understanding were given to Moses and Rabbi Akiva <note>Traditional Jewish thought suggests there are 50 levels of wisdom; Moses achieved 49</note>. These gates of understanding are drawn from the Divine Name of 72 (*Av*), originating from the attribute of Kindness (*Chesed*), with which he split the sea. When you remove the letter *aleph* for the sake of the 50 Gates, there remain 71 here. Our Sages said there are 70 "Sanhedrins" <note>referring to the 70 elders of the high court</note> with the Last One, and Moses is the Head over them, equal to them all, as stated in the first chapter of Berachot. Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is like Moses, except that one is "inner" and the other is "outer," as found in the Zohar. And the secret of "And he passed over" is the Name of 72, and 71 remains as explained. By these, the attribute of Moses was elevated. They said Rabbi Akiva was a "branch" of him, hinted at in his name: if you join the letters of Akiva (A-Q-I-B-A) you find the hint.

Let us return to the statement: "You did not lack for anything" <note>Deuteronomy 2:7</note>. This is to say that only the root of death within it—which is the "Samael" <note>an angelic name often associated with the accuser or the shadow side</note> and darkness within—is what defiles. Similarly, the physical waters do not purify; rather, their secret and their supernal root are what purify. They are "A statute I have engraved..." to prevent any questioning of My decree. It is written: "In this Torah," and "Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments." This means: from the commandments whose secret is known to you from the perspective of "to be known" and below, you shall believe in the hidden statutes. Thus, from the power of the decreed decrees, you shall come to the faith of the statute. Contemplate this.

Now we shall explain the essence of the four aforementioned levels. We find four expressions: 
1. The Torah of the Lord (*YHWH*).
2. The Torah of God (*Elohim*), as it is written: "And they read in the scroll, in the Torah of God, distinctly, and giving the sense."
3. The Torah of Truth.
4. The Torah of Man.

These are "two which are four" <note>a phrase from the Mishnah meaning two primary categories that expand into four</note>. The first two are hidden, and the second two are revealed. The hidden ones are the internal Names of *YHWH* and *Elohim*, the secret of the world of Emanation, the secret of "The Lord is One and His Name is One." *YHWH* is the hidden aspect. *Elohim*, in its value, is the secret of His revealed Name. Jethro said, "For the Lord is greater than all the gods (*elohim*)." It is written, "In order to tell My Name," hinting at the Name *YHWH*. And it is written, "And My Name is *YHWH*." And it is written, "And for all the signs and wonders which Moses performed"—the changing of nature comes from the side of *YHWH*. This is the first and internal matter.
2. *Elohim* is perfect knowledge, for "He knows my name," which is known to the enlightened among the Children of Israel. This is the "engraving." This is the hint at the beginning of the verse regarding the clarifications of "My Name." It is written: "Because he has set his love upon Me" (*be-chashak*), which are the vowel points *Cholam*, *Sheva*, and *Kametz*—the vowels of the Name *YHWH*. Sometimes *YHWH* appears with the vowels of *Elohim*, and so it is engraved. Understand this. This is the aspect of the hidden realms.

The revealed realms are two others:
3. The Torah of Truth: the commandments with their revealed, verified reasons for all.
4. The Torah of Man: the intellectual concepts.
Regarding these, the Blessings of the Torah hint—those said before reading and after reading. Before reading, they refer to the first two: "Who gave us His Torah" and "Blessed are You... Giver of the Torah." This is the revelation and attainment of the hidden. Afterward, the revealed ones: "Torah of Truth" and "Eternal Life." The explanation of these matters is that everything returns to one place, returning in its spirituality to the hidden. This is "The Torah of the Lord is perfect." This is the hint in the verse: "See, I have taught you statutes and judgments." The statutes are like the judgments in that they have a reason and are not "an empty thing"—and if they are empty, it is "from you" <note>a pun on a verse in Deuteronomy implying that if the Torah seems empty of meaning, the emptiness is in the person, not the text</note>. And the judgments are like statutes in that they are in the hidden level. Even simple matters that are called "judgments" return to the hidden level, as do the character traits (*middot*).

This is the plain meaning of what the commentators wrote regarding why our Holy Rabbi <note>Judah the Prince</note> began the Tractate *Avot* (Ethics of the Fathers) with "Moses received the Torah from Sinai." It is to inform us that even though the wise men of the nations authored 22 books on many character traits, do not say that these traits are not from Sinai. Therefore, he informs us: "Moses received." The matter is that there is a great difference. The philosophers attained character traits and habits from the perspective of human strength. But Moses received the Torah from Sinai; the traits are from the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as in the matter of "Walking in His ways"—just as He is merciful, so should you be. For our souls are a part of the Holy One, Blessed be He. By way of a hint: "The attribute of the Holy One is not like the attribute of flesh and blood." This means the philosophers understood traits from the side of man, who is flesh and blood. Therefore, they said that one who sees a wise man of the nations recites the blessing: "Blessed be He who gave of His wisdom to flesh and blood." But our traits are the attributes of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Thus, the two from the side of man are called "temporary life" (*chayei sha'ah*), while the ones from the side of the Holy One are called "eternal life" (*chayei olam*). This is "And He planted eternal life within us."

<column-break/>

**GLOSS**
From this, one can understand how to respond to those who complain about the high level of Moses. Why is it that the law (*halacha*) is not like Rabbi Akiva in all his disputes with his colleagues? They did not know or understand that this was due to his immense greatness; he was from a level above, in the spiritual depths, such that he could not establish his actions in the physical realm compared to that spirituality. The matter is even more internal. It is explained there what they said to him: "These and those are the words of the Living God." Its matter is explained with God's help in the homily for the portion of the Red Heifer. It is explained in Tractate Shevuot that influence is according to the readiness of the recipients to receive it. The law follows the majority to incline the path. Even though they "produced fruit" more than the supernal ones, there is a "sign of old age," for this is from the "children of the upper chamber." If the action had been for the community of Israel, the law would have been his. Since the "Kingship" (*Malchut*) which receives the influence from above is the receiver, and this was an act of his own to be a vessel for the spirit... but because the law is not so, it was not made a vessel for all.

Thus, the internal Divine Presence (*Shekhinah*) is found... and there is the secret of the statement: "The foundations of the pillars of the Lord are to give the kingdom as an inheritance to His son." And thus, the law was like Rabbi Akiva in all the disputes mentioned in the Gemara. All of this is in the spiritual level of his "crown," where Israel was. It is explained in the Midrash regarding the blessing: "He is in the Kingship." There are four: Eleazar and the Rabbi... it is explained in the *Tur*. It appeared from the heavens that he was told... as is explained. And this is what was said to him: "How? At the time of strength..." He said to him: "From strength shall the Menorah be made." And sometimes, as the staff was sunk and he descended, he went up and said, "My masters, it is written: 'it is hard' for him below." And because of this, it was difficult... He said to him, "And they shall descend." It was a stamp of fire, and He showed him the wrapping. And because it was difficult for him regarding the staff, there came to him a circuit of the moon in its orbit, and he should make it. He handed it over to Bezalel, and immediately the Menorah was made complete. He said, "How many afflictions!" And the Holy One showed it to him, "and I found it difficult in its thickness." But you were sent permission; you ascended by your own mind. In general, God created him; he stood in the Divine inspiration that the Holy One showed him—one step. And there it belongs because of Joseph in Babylon... from Rabbi Akiva... a support for life... Even though he was in Babylon, nevertheless, Rabbi Akiva's power was not diminished. On the contrary, this is a wonder: for in the strength of the physical wrapping, which was a vessel for the great spirituality of Rabbi Akiva, he was able to bring it into actuality. There in Babylon: for "the secret of the Lord is to those who fear Him" <note>original: "Sod Hashem Liyreyav," Psalm 25:14</note>. Not in the house... in the house... in the blood of Moses, which was water that lived in this for his merit.

# Written Torah: Sermon for the Portion of the Red Heifer

For the exchange of many sparks, one star heats and another cools; one illuminates from itself and another receives light; one moves swiftly and another slowly, and so on. Despite the multitude of stars, each one [corresponds to] the nature of man. Certainly, this was patterned with intention and will. This provides our response to the nations of the world <note>original: "Akum," referring to non-Jewish nations who questioned the logic of Jewish law</note> and those who hear and say that the commandment is without reason, a mere decree issued without purpose. Our response is that this is impossible; for if so, why would He decree contradictory things? Rather, it must be a "statute" <term>Chok: A commandment whose logical rationale is not revealed to human intellect</term>, the secret of the "Impression of the Will" which encompasses both a thing and its opposite. 

This explains the verse: *“Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people”* (Deuteronomy 4:6). It begins by saying, *“See, I have taught you statutes and judgments”*—just as judgments have an underlying reason, so too do the statutes. We learn the obscure from the explicit: they certainly exist to fulfill a hidden secret. *“Only a wise people,”* for it is not an empty thing for you; you have no right to question its reason. *“Do not seek what is too wondrous for you”* <note>A quote from Ben Sira, often cited in the Talmud</note>. When Israel holds fast to the Torah and righteous judgments, then all the nations praise them. 

Regarding this, the Midrash states: “This heifer is Israel.” “Red” is Israel, and so on. This means that Israel ascends through four parts, and then they are free from the nations and from the Accuser <note>The Satan</note>. But when influenced [by sin], then the nations and the four kingdoms count [their sins]. Also, in these four parts mentioned above, the secret of the Red Heifer completely removes the "Impression" of the gates of thought. To see this more clearly, look in the *Zohar* regarding the "man of the moment" <note>the person who led the scapegoat into the wilderness</note> whose sins are engraved. This is the secret of engraving and hewing—the secret of the "hewn souls," which is the secret of Levirate marriage and the reincarnation of souls. Diverse kinds (*Kilayim*) are revealed to the eyes as the secret of Action. Therefore, this portion is called *“the statute of the Torah.”* We find here the secret of the "Impression," the fixed statute that is the root of the entire Torah. The Red Heifer, according to the aforementioned Midrash, is a cow that conceived the impurity of a human corpse, as explained.

<note>Small font commentary block summarizing Rabbi Menachem the Babylonian and the Recanati</note>
(The following is the language of Rabbi Menachem the Babylonian, sections 137-138, regarding the reasons for the Red Heifer: Why is the reason for this mitzvah hidden? It is based on the foundation that the reason for the Red Heifer is to atone for the sin of the Golden Calf. He explains that its holiness is greater than what can be contained in our current state. It requires seven sprinklings and seven washings, and it remained a decree for all the days of our exile. The Midrash says that even King Solomon said: "I said I would be wise, but it is far from me." Know that even though one who touches a corpse is impure, the one who occupies himself with the purification process also becomes impure. This is the secret of how the pure becomes impure and the impure becomes pure. As it says, "When a man dies in a tent," the reason for this mitzvah is that the spirit of impurity hovers over the body, and the "waters of sprinkling" come to purify it. When the holy spirit departs, the external forces take hold. The Torah is the body of the world, just as the soul is the body of man. The ashes of the heifer mixed with living water have the power to restore the soul from the depths of impurity. One who touches the water of sprinkling is impure until evening, because this mitzvah pushes away the external thoughts to receive the mystery and memory of the matter. When those forces of impurity that are destined to be purified are removed from their shells, the one who touches the water must immerse until evening, and his merit is on the seventh day. ## **“Let us make man”** in our image. 
In thought, this refers to the "Chariot" and the Form. Ben Tema says: “Be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle, swift as a deer, and strong as a lion” (Ethics of the Fathers 5:20). He explains four things, paired as two: Boldness and Strength are one category, while Lightness and Swiftness are another. Therefore, by choice, one should be "strong as a lion" and "light as an eagle." These correspond to the heart and the eye, as it is said: *“And you shall not wander after your hearts and after your eyes”* (Numbers 15:39). These are the bridge to action. 

The "Ox" refers to the Torah, as the Sages said: “A man should always place himself under the words of Torah like an ox to the yoke.” It is also written: *“And much increase comes by the strength of the ox”* (Proverbs 14:4). The purification of stones follows the secret of the "Measure of the Stature" of the creation of man. Usually, the Torah is spoken of in masculine terms, implying dominion. "Freedom" (*Cherut*) refers to the redemption they experienced, and in the future, a "New Song" (*Shir Chadash*). 

But look, it writes *“This is the Torah”* (*Zot HaTorah*) in the feminine, because they used the "Ox" before it was prepared as the Chariot of the Torah. At that time, their strength was great. But now we have descended to the level of the "Ox" (masculine) and "Heifer" (feminine). This is the "New Song." The "Ox" and the "Heifer" represent the masculine and feminine aspects in the destruction, the ox and the labor. This is the secret of how relief was created after the Flood. Just as the labor of the heifer is for "Man" <note>humanity</note>, so too "You are called Man," and not the other nations. Now, in our many sins, the nations have freedom, and they are like the eagle or the lion coming out of its thicket. 

Now, in the aforementioned statement, he brought the Mishnah of those who engage in the Red Heifer: "From the beginning to the end, it defiles garments." This is difficult—does it not also purify the body from impurity? Rather, the hint is from the beginning of man—a "Clear Man" who "Lightly Sleeps"—until his end, from "Garments of Light" to "Garments of Skin" <note>A classic Hebrew wordplay: "Garments of Skin" (*Kotnot Or* with an Ayin) vs. "Garments of Light" (*Kotnot Or* with an Aleph), referring to humanity's state before and after the Fall</note>. The Torah itself is the inner part of the "Garments of Glory" for the soul. This is why it "defiles garments." It also hints that "these [Sages] declare impure and these declare pure"—both are the words of the Living God. It also hints that a Master of Torah who knows everything and yet sins is worse than an ignorant person who sins. This is "it defiles the pure." And it "purifies the impure" through the opening of repentance. As it says: "They have forsaken Me and did not keep My Torah—if only they had forsaken Me but kept My Torah, for the light within it would have returned them to the good." Regarding repentance: one who sins against his soul and afflicts himself with fasting when he has no strength for labor is considered a completely righteous person; in this, he "defiles the pure." But when he sins and has strength and afflicts himself, he "purifies the impure." The Nazirite, who accepted abstinence according to his righteousness, is called "holy," but when he exceeds what is necessary, he is called a "sinner." Therefore, in the first usage, he falls and returns, and is called a "sinner" or a "judge."

<column-break/>

## **The Secret** 
And why does the verse say *“This is the Torah: when a man dies in a tent”*? In the *Zohar*, page 149, it explains that because of the change in his world, his deeds are weighed, and he becomes impure because of the impurity that dwells within him. When a person is at rest, that desire [for sin] is gone. Therefore, a corpse does not convey impurity in a tent if he is from the nations, because they do not have the same level of merit and holiness. But the children of Israel, who in their lives were attached to the Holy Spirit and a deep soul, have a great secret. The general rule is that the impurity remains until the secret is doubled. The holiness of the "Vessels" <term>Kelim: Kabbalistic term for the physical or conceptual structures that hold Divine light</term> and the residue within them, and everything written about the scent and the flavor—this is for the heavenly bodies, so that an evil spirit does not enter. Through the perfection and prayer of the soul, the body is separated from the change during its holy life. 

The foundation of the body is like a garment for the soul. The corpse is impure because the soul has departed to a higher place, leaving the dust below. This is why the body is called "improper" in its death, and the body is exempt from the spirit. To what can the matter be compared? etc. End of quote.

# The Written Torah is for Blessing and Not for Curse

->For gladness and for joy, and the Ninth of Av <note>Tisha B'Av, the day of mourning for the destruction of the Temples</note> is called an "appointed time" <note>Hebrew: *Moed*</note> as it is written: "He has called an appointed time against me" <note>Lamentations 1:15</note>, because in the future it is destined to be a festival. Therefore, the Ninth of Av always falls on the same day of the week as the first day of Passover, the day Israel left Egypt, which is a precursor to the future redemption, as it is written: "As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt... I will show him marvelous things." <note>Micah 7:15</note> And there is a difficult question regarding the law found in the verse: "And it shall come to pass, that as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good... so the Lord will rejoice <note>Hebrew: *yasis*</note> to destroy you." <note>Deuteronomy 28:63</note> Our Sages, of blessed memory, asked: Does not the Holy One, blessed be He, suffer in the suffering of Israel? How then can it say He will "rejoice" over their destruction? They answered: He Himself does not rejoice, but He *causes others* to rejoice. Specifically, the text uses the word *yasis* <note>the causative form</note> rather than *yasush* <note>the simple form</note>. But this is difficult, as it is written: "So the Lord your God will rejoice (*yasis*) over you." This would imply He Himself rejoices! Why then are both terms used? We must say that *yasush* would mean even just one entity rejoices—God Himself—as it is written in the portion of *Nitzavim*: "For the Lord will again rejoice (*yashuv... la-shush*) over you for good, as He rejoiced over your fathers." <note>Deuteronomy 30:9</note> However, the word *yasis* has two meanings: sometimes it means "I will cause others to rejoice," and sometimes it refers to Himself. But we must investigate: why did the Torah use one word that has two different meanings? Based on what I have written, it works well, for these two meanings coincide, and the result is a blessing. This is the meaning of what is written: "If He has afflicted, He will also have compassion." <note>Lamentations 3:32</note> It should have said "and then He will have compassion," but rather, the affliction itself is the *cause* of the compassion. Through this, we can explain the Midrash on *Lamentations Rabbah*: "He has cut off in fierce anger all the horn of Israel." <note>Lamentations 2:3</note> There are ten horns: The horn of Abraham, as it is written: "a fruitful hill" <note>original: *keren ben shemen*—literally "a horn, the son of oil"</note>;<-

the horn of Isaac, as it is written: "caught in the thicket by his horns"; the horn of Joseph, as it is written: "his horns are like the horns of a wild ox"; the horn of Moses, for it is written: "the skin of his face shone" <note>Hebrew: *karan*, related to the word for horn</note>; the horn of the Torah, for it is written: "He had rays <note>horns</note> coming out of His hand"; the horn of the Priesthood, as it is written: "his horn shall be exalted with honor"; the horn of the Levites, as it is written: "All these were the sons of Heman the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn"; the horn of prophecy, for it is written: "my horn is exalted in the Lord"; the horn of the Holy Temple, as it is written: "from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me"; the horn of Israel, for it is written: "He has lifted up a horn for His people"; and some say the horn of the Messiah, as it is written: "He will give strength to His king and exalt the horn of His anointed." All of these were placed upon the heads of Israel, but when they sinned, these were taken from them, as it says: "He has cut off in fierce anger all the horn of Israel." These were then given to the nations of the world, as it is written <note>in Aramaic</note>: "And concerning the ten horns that were on its head... and the ten horns out of this kingdom are ten kings that shall arise." <note>Daniel 7:20-24</note> But when Israel performs repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, returns them to their place, as it is written: "All the horns of the wicked I will also cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted." <note>Psalm 75:11</note> When does the "Righteous One of the world" <note>God</note> return the horns He cut off? When the Holy One, blessed be He, exalts the horn of His Messiah. One might wonder: how could such holy power or the strength of the Levites be given to the nations? Do they have Levites or Priests among them? Rather, it means that through the "Laments" <note>the Book of Lamentations/Kinot</note> we reach these heights of light and eternity. Exile reminds us of God. Our Sages said that if Israel does not repent, the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman’s, and they are forced to repent and are redeemed. Regarding the verse "The punishment of your iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion," <note>Lamentations 4:22</note> Rabbi Helbo said: The removal of Pharaoh's signet ring in Egypt was better for Israel than forty years of prophecy in the desert, because the former led to redemption while the latter did not. Rabbi Simeon bar Yohai said: The removal of Ahasuerus's signet ring was better than the prophecies of the prophets, because it led to action. And the Rabbis said: The Book of Lamentations was better for Israel than forty years of Jeremiah's prophecies, because through it, Israel received their full compensation. Thus, sweetness emerges from the bitter matter. I have elaborated on this sermon elsewhere. This is why it is written: "And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon you, the blessing and the curse... and you shall call them to mind." <note>Deuteronomy 30:1</note> It is difficult: why mention the blessings? He should only mention the curses, for they are what cause repentance. Rather, the curse itself is the blessing, as it says: "the Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing for you." Even Balaam, who was prepared to curse them, ended up blessing them; the evil angel answered against his will. This change had to happen through Balaam because he was the prophet and the source for all the nations, just as Moses was the source for all the prophets of Israel. Our Sages said: "There arose not a prophet since in Israel like Moses"—but among the nations, one did arise, and that was Balaam. One might mistakenly think his level of knowledge was holy, but the Zohar warns about this:

"That wicked Balaam praised himself... he spoke the truth but praised himself in a hidden way. Anyone who heard him thought he was greater than all the world's prophets, as it is written: 'who hears the words of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High.' <note>Numbers 24:16</note> Who in the world would hear such things and not think there was no faithful prophet like him? And it was true! He did hear, and he did know. But that wicked man was referring to the levels of impurity he grasped. 'Hears the words of God' <note>original: *El*</note>—it does not say 'The God' <note>original: *Ha-El*</note>, for 'The God is perfect in His way,' but simply 'God' refers to 'another god' <note>an idol or impure force</note>, as in 'you shall not bow to another god.' He used a small word to hint to those who didn't know that he was great. 'Knows the knowledge of the Most High'—this refers to the levels of impurity that govern the expanses of the sea, forty minus one in number. The 'great one' of that filth who leads them is 'most high' over them. To this, that wicked one was attached... he stole the minds of people. 'Who sees the vision of the Almighty' <note>original: *Shaddai*</note>—one who hears this thinks he saw what no other saw. But this 'vision of Shaddai' was just a branch of the lower forces... he saw while 'fallen and with open eyes.'" Thus, the matter was not that he reached the level of Moses; rather, he spoke ambiguously so that listeners would think he possessed great providence and knowledge. When the Sages said "among the nations one did arise [like Moses]," they meant according to the listeners' perception of Balaam's words.

<column-break/>

<margin>Collected Notes</margin>
From what I have written, the Midrash on *Lamentations Rabbah* is clarified: "He has poured out His fury because of the multitude of her transgressions." Does this mean He can protect? The text says "because of the multitude of her transgressions." We must understand there is a difference between "sealing" (*la-hatom*) and "clearing away" (*le-va'er*). Clearing away is to remove, while sealing is to protect. In the context of the future, it is appropriate to "seal" so that the coming joy remains, but regarding the past, the "clearing" is the removal of sin. In the destruction of the Temple, we were cleared away so that the kingdom could be established over us. Some say the "punishment is accomplished" for all generations. This is because the suffering cleanses and covers the past. This leads to repentance, for when we remember our sins and see we have no helper, we realize we were caught in our iniquities. Also, on the Ninth of Av, the pride of the nations grew, and we were humiliated, as it says, "she has fallen wonderfully, she has no comforter." We feel that we lack the Temple and the sacrifices to atone for us. Woe to us for what we have lost! This is the "multitude of transgressions." It also hints that even if our merits have failed, our suffering remains. He says "transgressions" (*pesha'im*) and not "sinners" (*posh'im*), because the sins will be removed, and the spirit of purity will return. This is why the judgment is actually compassion.

<margin>Collected Notes</margin>
From this, we see that the first "redemptions" were called "blessing" and "curse," but the final one will be a complete "rejoicing." The pressure of the exile is what brings the return to God, and the "bitter" becomes the "sweet."

The essence of this writing is to clarify what our Sages said, that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the "Knower of Secrets," and all His ways are for the good of His people in the end of days.

<header>The Written Torah: The Way of Life and Ethical Rebuke</header>

“I have sinned, for I did not know” <note>Numbers 22:34</note>. Ostensibly, this is difficult to understand: if he did not know, then in what way did he sin? Rather, a person is held liable for those things which he *ought* to have known and understood, yet remained ignorant of. According to the words of our Sages, the Blessed Holy One gave man the intellect to contemplate and understand. Here too, Balaam should have understood that the donkey did not act for no reason. 
The core principle is that “a person is always forewarned” <note>original: "Adam mu’ad le’olam" — a legal principle meaning a human is always responsible for their actions, whether intentional or accidental</note>, whether awake or asleep. One must always contemplate, understand, and see to it that no evil occurs through them. 
“He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob...” <note>Numbers 23:21</note>. Regarding this verse, I have written at great length in the ethical section, explaining that a person should not think [sinful thoughts] in his heart even if they do not result in action. I wrote of this above in the section titled *Ten Sayings*, in the ninth article.

# **The Lamp of Commandment**
8. From our teacher, Rabbi Isaac <note>likely referring to the Sefer HaChinuch or a similar codifier</note>: The commandment of the laws of inheritance. 8a. The commandment of the daily offerings every day. 8b. The commandment of the additional offering (*Musaf*) for the Sabbath. 8c. The commandment of the offering for each and every New Moon. 8d. The commandment of the additional offering on the festival of Shavuot. 8e. The commandment of the Shofar on Rosh Hashanah. And there are seventy offerings for the other festivals mentioned in this portion, but they were already mentioned in the portion of *Emor*, and I have recorded them there.

# **The Torah is Light**
Blessed be He who formed man with wisdom—by which I mean that man was intended to be wise and perceptive, possessing a refined body and a divine soul, both bound together for good, clinging to life forever. For this purpose they were created. However, man corrupted this and the body became material <term>Chomer; physical matter susceptible to decay</term> due to the "ban of death" from the earth. There is no remedy for it now except through "shattering"—which is death. It will not be fully repaired until the future, when the Messiah comes, or when "the Lord rejoices in His works" and returns the world to its pristine brilliance. 

Our Sages hinted at this in Tractate Pesachim, in the chapter "The Woman": Rabbi Yochanan said that the gathering of the exiles is as great as the day on which heaven and earth were created, as it is said: "The children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and shall go up from the land; for great shall be the day of Jezreel" <note>Hosea 2:2</note>. And it is written: "And there was evening and there was morning, one day." The intention is that when the true, ultimate Unity occurs at the coming of our righteous Messiah, the creation will be renewed with a "new light" like the original light of creation. The body will be united with the soul, and even the earth—which is physical matter—will be refined and filled with knowledge. His life will be a true life from below, receiving abundance from above, living forever in both body and soul. 

At the time of creation, "man in his glory did not endure" <note>Psalm 49:13</note> and corrupted it, bringing death upon himself. However, the Blessed Holy One gave us a Torah of Truth through which we may merit the future. He gave us commandments that point toward this and leave an impression of this matter upon the eternity of the body, just like the soul. Currently, in these days, human perfection is found in the "species" and the "individual." In the species, it is from the perspective of the body, for "a generation goes and a generation comes" <note>Ecclesiastes 1:4</note>; the physical persists only as a species. But the soul persists in the specific individual, for every single soul is existent and eternal.

Regarding the laws of inheritance, they are called a "statute of judgment" <note>original: "Chukat Mishpat"</note>. Our Sages explained that although the Primordial Serpent caused sin and death, interrupting the continuity of physical bodies, nevertheless, that which remains in its place descends to the heir who inherits the rights of the house. The spiritual connection remains close, for the closeness of souls is not severed. This is the meaning of the verse: "If a man dies and has no son..." <note>Numbers 27:8</note>.

### **Afterward**
The Blessed Holy One commanded the daily offerings, which correspond to the cleaving of the soul and the spirit.

<columns>2</columns>
It is that which ascends on high; it ascends continually. It is an offering to the hand of God. He offers the letters of the Name <note>Y-H-V-H</note> and unifies them, and in this way, he binds his soul on high. Also, in the secret of reincarnation (*Gilgul*), there were many souls within the sacrifices, in the secret of the verse: "When a man (*Adam*) of you brings an offering..." <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. Regarding this, the hint is: "My offering, My bread for My fires." "My fires" (*Ishi*) refers to the "men" (*Anshei*) of the generation who are reincarnated in the sacrifice. Through this, their souls are softened. We explain the liturgy "and restore the service to the sanctuary... and the fire-offerings of Israel" accordingly. I have seen in the homilies of the Midrash that Michael, the Great Prince, offers the souls of Israel on high. However, this stems from the physical sacrifice below, as is known to the wise and the Kabbalists. 

There are five levels of the soul: *Nefesh* (Lowest soul), *Ruach* (Spirit), *Neshama* (Breath/Higher soul), *Chaya* (Living essence), and *Yechida* (Singularity/Unity).
- The level of *Nefesh* is attained on the New Moon and Intermediate Days of Festivals.
- The level of *Ruach* is attained on Festivals.
- The level of *Neshama* is attained on Yom Kippur.
- The level of *Chaya* is attained on the Sabbath.
- The level of *Yechida* is attained in the World to Come.
Therefore, there is an "additional" offering (*Musaf*). The Musaf of the New Moon, Festivals, Rosh Hashanah, and Yom Kippur are all one category—the beginning and end of judgment. The Musaf of the Sabbath consists of "two lambs," corresponding to "Remember" and "Observe" being spoken in a single utterance, pointing to the Sabbath of this world and the Sabbath of the World to Come, which is "entirely Sabbath." Afterward is the commandment of the Shofar on Rosh Hashanah, which is to confuse the Accuser <note>the Satan</note> and to awaken those who sleep. For the Angel of Death is the Accuser, and it is written: "On that day a great Shofar shall be blown."

<column-break/>

<meta>The following section contains significantly damaged or shorthand OCR text relating to the Sefer HaTikkunim and legal discussions of inheritance.</meta>

In the book of *Tikkunim* <note>Tikunei HaZohar</note>, it is written close to the literal meaning: When we look at the laws of inheritance, it mentions counting and judging in the matter of danger... "If he dies and has no son," and his inheritance passes to the "Crown" <term>Keter; the highest Kabbalistic emanation</term>. Herein is a hint regarding time and the secret of the rotation of souls... <unclear>various garbled legal terms</unclear>... 

Regarding the "two tablets"... <unclear>shorthand regarding heirs and the poor</unclear>... The Sages said: "If one says 'my son shall not inherit with his brothers,' or 'my daughter shall inherit me where there is a son,' he has said nothing, because he has conditioned against what is written in the Torah." However, if he gives it as a "gift" rather than an "inheritance," his words stand. This is because he cannot uproot the laws of the Torah regarding inheritance, but he has the power to give his property to whomever he wishes while alive.

Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says: If he says it regarding someone who is fit to inherit him, his words stand. But regarding one who is not fit to inherit him, his words do not stand.

<columns>1</columns>

The holy offerings in the secret of the *Musafim* (Additional Offerings) hint at the future. Regarding the New Moon, it is written: "This month shall be for you" <note>Exodus 12:2</note>. Israel counts by the moon. It says in the Midrash on the portion of *Bo* that the greatness of Israel is like the light of the moon. From Abraham our father until King Solomon, there were fifteen generations; then the light of the moon was at its full, and Solomon sat upon the throne of the Lord. From the fifteenth generation onward, the light of the moon began to diminish until the twenty-eighth generation, when it was completely blemished. Such were the generations from Solomon until Zedekiah, of whom it is written: "And the eyes of Zedekiah were blinded." 

However, in the future, "a new light shall shine upon Zion," and the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold. This is the secret of the New Moon offering. The Sabbath offering refers to the world that is "entirely Sabbath." The secret of Passover is that just as Israel was redeemed then, they are destined to be redeemed in Passover again, as it is written: "As in the days of your coming out of Egypt, I will show him wonders."

<header>The Written Torah — Ekev: The Consequence of Humility</header>

...upon them, but rather they replied to you: "Return Joshua." <note>Original: "השיבו נא לך את יהושע." A reference to the transition of leadership from Moses to Joshua.</note> In the portion of *Va’etchanan* (And I Besought), it says: "At that time, saying..." <note>Deuteronomy 3:23.</note> which means "Answer me," for "saying" can imply a request for a response. One might ask: God forbid, how could Moses speak so bluntly toward Heaven, as if to force a reply? Although it could be said, "Look what happened to him," for God did not answer him according to his desire and will. "Now you shall see..." <note>Exodus 6:1.</note> and he did not see the kings on high. The Holy One, blessed be He, did not send the healing immediately, but let him suffer for six days. Regarding the matter of "appointment," Moses thought his sons would inherit his greatness, but the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "Take Joshua." In *Va’etchanan*, it says, "The Lord did not listen to me." Truly, God forbid that one should suspect Moses of being disrespectful toward Heaven.

Therefore, it seems to me that the matter is this: Moses asked the Holy One, blessed be He, to explain a previous prophecy to him, as he had a doubt regarding its interpretation and wanted to study it to understand it well. This occurred when he said, "Let heavier work be laid upon the men," <note>Exodus 5:9.</note> or perhaps Moses was doubtful about the prophecy in retrospect when the Holy One, blessed be He, sent him to Pharaoh—whether the intent was for them to be redeemed immediately or after some time. This doubt was born from that increased burden of labor. Therefore, he said, "Answer me: are You redeeming them now?" Similarly, with Miriam, when the Holy One, blessed be He, called out suddenly, "Come out, you three," <note>Numbers 12:4.</note> He did not speak with Moses alone. Moses was doubtful as to why He called him, for there are two interpretations: First, that Aaron and Miriam were not prepared for prophecy as they were engaged in worldly matters <note>Specifically, marital relations, according to Rashi.</note>, so the prophecy had to be funneled through Moses. Second, that the Blessed Name did this to publicly admonish Aaron and Miriam in Moses’s presence, so they would be more humbled than if it were done in private, as a means of atonement for them. As the plain meaning of the verse says: "And the Lord renounced the punishment He said He would bring upon His people"—meaning once they received the words of rebuke, they were atoned for. But afterward, when Moses saw Miriam struck with leprosy, he asked the Holy One, blessed be He, to tell him why He had called him, and God answered. When God said, "Let her be shut out," and Miriam was not immediately forgiven, Moses understood the calling was not for the second reason, but for the first.

Regarding the <term>Kippur</term><note>Atonement</note>, he spoke of the "kindness of the Lord to Solomon." And regarding "These are the ordinances which you shall set before them"—this means "before their sages." If the interpretation of prophecy is that Moses is called "Godlike" <note>Exodus 7:1.</note> and Moses was ordained, and he would ordain another, and so on for all generations—or if the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints someone in every single generation—God answered him: "Set the <term>Karet</term><note>The penalty of 'cutting off' or a definitive ruling</note> in your hand." Similarly, in *Va’etchanan*, he imagined the vow [denying him entry to the Land] might be annulled, and he wanted to pray in retrospect regarding the oath of "Therefore you shall not bring..." Behold, Moses only sought to understand the matter clearly. How much more so should a common person like us not lean on our own understanding? "Appoint for yourself a teacher," <note>Pirkei Avot 1:6.</note> and one is obligated to study and review their learning constantly until it is clear. As it is written: "And you shall sharpen them" <note>Deuteronomy 6:7.</note>—that the words of Torah should be sharp in your mouth. All engagement with Torah and action should be for the sake of His Blessed Name, remembering the Creator always. As King David said: "I have set the Lord always before me." <note>Psalm 16:8.</note> And Moses warned them: "Know this day and take it to your heart, that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other." <note>Deuteronomy 4:39.</note>

By this we shall live and cleave to Him. Regarding this it says: "But you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today." <note>Deuteronomy 4:4.</note> This verse encompasses the whole Torah, the deeds, and the character traits. If a person conducts themselves in <term>Devekut</term><note>Mysterical cleaving or attachment</note> to the Blessed Name, everything is for the sake of His Name. Even when engaged in necessary physical needs, one should not move from this attachment. When engaged in business, one should think: "I am doing this business and I hope in the Lord for profit, for He is the one who gives. Through this, I will perform a commandment: I will support myself, my wife, and my children so they can serve the Lord, and I will give money to charity and for Torah study." Similarly, when eating or going to sleep, one should intend that their body be strong to engage in Torah and commandments. I have elaborated on this elsewhere. Thus, all the days of a person's life, they are constantly attached to the Blessed Name if they follow this path. Then they merit eternal attachment.

On this, our Master <note>Likely referring to the Zohar or a specific sage.</note> Rabbi Shimon said: "It is written, 'But you who cleave'—who are the holy people like Israel? It is written of them: 'Happy are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord.' <note>Deuteronomy 33:29.</note> Because their attachment to the Name of the Master of the world is such that in this world and the world to come, they are never separated from Him, from that 'bundle of bundles' in which the righteous are bound. For it says 'But you who cleave *in* the Lord'—not 'to' the Lord, but literally *in* the Lord." <note>Original Aramaic: "מאן עמא קדישא כישרא'... ואתם הדביקים בה' ולא אל ה' אלא בה' ממש." This highlights a mystical union where the soul is "inside" the Divine reality.</note> Understand that He called this name the "Bundle of Life," for there everything is bound. May it be His will that we merit this.

->With the help of Him who grants knowledge to man, I have finished the portion of Va’etchanan.<-

# The Written Torah: Portion of Ekev

->This is the name by which they shall call him: The Consequence of Humility<-

**The Candle of Commandment:** <note>Referring to the 613 Mitzvot (commandments) as enumerated by the Sefer HaChinuch or Maimonides.</note>
*   **Commandment 428:** Not to benefit from the plating of an idol or its ornaments. As it says: "You shall not covet the silver or gold on them." <note>Deuteronomy 7:25.</note>
*   **Commandment 429:** Not to benefit from anything offered to an idol or its accessories. As it says: "And you shall not bring an abomination into your house." <note>Deuteronomy 7:26.</note>
*   **Commandment 430:** To bless after eating. As it says: "And you shall eat and be satisfied and you shall bless..." <note>Deuteronomy 8:10.</note>
*   **Commandment 431:** To love the stranger. As it says: "And you shall love the stranger." <note>Deuteronomy 10:19.</note>
*   **Commandment 432:** To fear the Name. As it says: "The Lord your God you shall fear." <note>Deuteronomy 10:20.</note>
*   **Commandment 433:** To cleave to the Blessed One—meaning to associate and attach oneself to the Sages of the Torah. As it says: "And to Him you shall cleave." <note>Deuteronomy 10:20.</note>
*   **Commandment 434:** A commandment for anyone required to swear in a court of law to swear by the Name of the Lord.
*   **Commandment 435:** The commandment of prayer. As it says: "To serve Him with all your heart" <note>Deuteronomy 11:13.</note>—and prayer is the "service of the heart."

**The Torah Light:** "The end of the matter, all having been heard: Fear God..." <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13.</note> Behold, this commandment of fearing the Lord, as it says: "The Lord your God you shall fear, Him you shall serve, to Him you shall cleave, and by His name you shall swear," is a general commandment. It includes many matters, which is why the portion begins with it: "And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear..." The concept of the "Fear of Heaven" I have explained at length in my work *Ten Utterances*. Included in the fear of the Lord is the Unity of the Name and the Service of the Name. All the commandments mentioned in this portion are included here. The commandment to swear by the Name is to be a guardian of the Name, clothing oneself in His fear and swearing—or if a creator—swearing in truth like the Unity of the Name. One should love to turn away from evil and distance oneself from all idolatry, for the Lord our God is one Lord, and there is no other. One must be especially distant so as not to benefit from the plating of idols or their offerings. It says, "You shall not covet the silver and gold upon them and take it for yourself," because at the very moment of coveting, one is ready to take it; for the eye sees, the heart covets, and the physical tools complete the act. The moment of coveting is like the act of taking, for such is the law regarding idolatry: "to seize the heart of the house of Israel." So too, it says "You shall not bring an abomination *into* your house," rather than "to" your house—implying from the moment of bringing it, even if it is not yet literally inside the house.

Then comes the command to "do good," which is to love the stranger who has separated from idolatry. Strangers are beloved to the Creator of all, for He equated the love of them to the love of Himself. For it is written, "And you shall love the Lord your God," and it is written, "And you shall love the stranger." This is the "turning away from evil"—that one who was a Gentile enters into the portion of God's love through their holiness. Thus it arose in thought.

The commandment also came that we should attach ourselves to the Blessed One to "cleave to Him," which means the company of Sages, upon whom the spirit of purity rests. This is the opposite of idols and their accessories, upon which the spirit of impurity rests. By connecting to the Sages who know the Torah, the words of Torah do not receive impurity. This is included in the "Fear of the Name," as it is written: "The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever" <note>Psalm 19:10.</note>—meaning it stands forever in purity because words of Torah do not receive impurity. Service of the Lord in this regard depends on Prayer, which is "service in the heart." So too with all blessings of the Name. The "Grace after Meals" for food is a great thing, for the table is in the place of the [Temple] Service. The secret is eating in holiness and purity. It is like a sacrifice offered upon the Altar. I have elaborated on this in *The Light* under the letter *Kof* for *Kedushah* (Holiness). Regarding the holiness of eating, see there. If the food is eaten in holiness, it is transformed from blood into [the sustenance of] ministering angels. Just as food is the cause of existence for human beings, so too the angels and souls receive their "food" and existence from the Divine Presence (Shekhinah), as it says: "And You give life to them all." Eating for humans is a mirror of the sacrifices for the Supernal Forces.

This is the matter of the "elevation of eating" in the praise of the <term>Arizal</term><note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the 16th-century kabbalist.</note>. He explained the intentions corresponding to the four worlds, which is the Shekhinah. Like the gate of the Shekhinah, and the teeth generally represent the ten [Sefirot] of the secret of Atzilut (Emanation). Thus it is said that one needs ten things for eating:
1. To prepare the table with water and set it before the Great King. "And you shall eat and be satisfied... before the Lord your God."
2. Washing the hands before the meal.
3. Taking the right [vessel] in the left, and using the right to pour on the left, and washing up to the limit defined by the Sages.
4. One must raise their hands during the washing and join the two joints... at the time of washing.
5. The blessing over the washing of the hands.
6. To improve the table for the poor.
7. To recite the blessing of *HaMotzi* (the blessing over bread) and to...
8. To eat bread at his table without being a glutton or a swallower, for one is eating before the King.
9. One must have words of Torah at his table.
10. The final waters (*Mayim Acharonim*) are an obligation.
See the *Zohar*, for it elaborates on these matters according to the Secret...

### The Written Torah - Portion Ekev: On Humility

Everything will fall, even what he already possessed, as in the case of the "ant in the rice-store" <note>This refers to a Talmudic metaphor about loss or hidden treasures</note> which was a hidden storehouse for him. Now, Rav Ami and Rav Assi spoke regarding this verse; one expounded it, though they differed in this distinction just as Rav Huna and Rav Hisda disagreed regarding the word *Shibbolet* <note>original: "שבולת"; meaning an ear of grain</note>. Regarding this matter of the *Shibbolet*, it is said: "The pride of Ephraim." They said "Say *Shibbolet*," but he would say "*Sibbolet*" <note>A reference to Judges 12:6, where the Ephraimites' inability to pronounce the 'sh' sound betrayed them in battle</note>. You find the pride of Ephraim in the war of Gideon, and to Jephthah they said, "You are fugitives of Ephraim, Gilead in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh." Therefore, they could not speak the word *Shibbolet* <note>ear of grain</note>, but only *Sibbolet* <note>burden</note>, which equals 150 <note>This refers to the gematria (numerical value) of the word</note>. 

There is a further hint here according to the words of Rabbi Akiva, who said that Mount Sinai had five names, and from there hatred <note>A play on the word *Sinai* and *Sinah* (hatred)</note> descended to the nations of the world. Mount Sinai is also called *Sin*, like the male at the head of the journeys <note>Numbers 33</note>, which indicates hatred as mentioned. Now, the nations of the world are masters of pride, as found in the teaching on the verse "Not because you are more numerous than all the nations" <note>Deut. 7:7</note>; therefore, they said *Sibbolet* with a *Samekh* <note>The letter 'S' representing a "burden" or "lowliness" that they could not properly transform</note>, and contemplate this. 

There was a benefit that the Heavenly Voice came from the "Mountain of Humility" <note>Sinai</note>. And Ruth said, "Let me glean among the ears of grain (*shibbalim*)," and from her emerged David, who said, "But I am a worm" <note>Psalms 22:7</note>. Contemplate this: he received the Torah from Sinai, and the Torah only endures in those who are humble. Therefore, he merited the Supernal attachment and was forty days on the mountain, bringing peace to Israel and overturning hatred.

Regarding the matter of the eight places of pride that I mentioned, and the matter of the *Shibbolet* <note>ear of grain</note>: it is also stated there in the first chapter of Sotah <note>Sotah 5a</note>, "Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav: A Torah scholar must have in him one-eighth of an eighth [of pride]." Rav Huna the son of Rav Joshua said: "And it crowns him like the awn of an ear of grain (*shibbolta*)." 

Now, there are eight places [of pride] as explained. You already know that in many places, the letter *Aleph* is not counted in the sum. Therefore, it does not matter if he holds onto an eighth part, but rather that all are included together and they are "together at the head." Then each one is included in all of them; therefore, he should only hold onto a sixty-fourth part (an eighth of an eighth). If it is an eighth of an eighth, then he will fulfill the verse: "Be exceedingly humble of spirit." Then the *Shibbolet* will be crowned with the remaining pride. How so? Eight times eight equals sixty-four. When he has a measured amount of pride, he enters the state of "passing through" and then it is a "silent miracle." 

On this, there is a hint in the Psalm: "The fool says in his heart, there is no God." Elsewhere it is written: "They have all turned aside; they are together become corrupt; there is none that does good, no, not even one." This means when they are sixty-three, they are corrupt, or if "all turn aside" including the eighth. But it must be sixty-four as explained. Even this was only permitted to a Torah scholar so that he might compel those who would withhold good. Then he will have the portion of the *Aleph* <note>representing the One/God</note> which is not in the count, as explained. But if it is not for the sake of "doing good," then it is discarded. 

Let us return to our subject regarding these eight [expressions of humility in prayer]: 
1. **What are we?** against the sense of Hearing. As our Sages said: "If one makes another deaf, he must give him his entire value." 
2. **What is our life?** against Eating and Drinking, which is one's livelihood. 
3. **What is our kindness?** against the Eyes, as it says "Lest he show you grace in your eyes." 
4. **What is our righteousness?** against the Forehead. In the first chapter of Taanit (page 8), it says: "Righteousness looks down from heaven" regarding rain, which is an act of charity (*tzedakah*). Previously on page 6, Rav Shila said in the name of Rav Hamnuna: "Rain is only withheld because of the brazen-faced," as it is written, "The showers have been withheld... and you had a harlot’s forehead." Thus, the forehead is for the sake of righteousness. 
5. **What is our salvation?** against the Face, as it says: "Cause Your face to shine and we shall be saved." 
6. **What is our strength?** "One who is mighty in strength"—who is the mighty one? He who subdues his anger. 
7. **What is our power?** "Mighty like a lion" in the heart, not to have a heart of stone, which comes from the "broad heart" of pride. 
8. **What shall we say before You?** against the "tongue that speaks great things."

Regarding these, the verse says: "What does the Lord require of you?"—to be considered as "What" <note>original: "מה"; i.e., as nothing</note> in all these. All this is the humility of this world. But for the future: "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden" in the Treasury of Honor. Afterwards, it says "He asks of you," meaning He has the legal status of a "borrower" (*sho'el*). A borrower is liable even for accidents; thus the Holy One, blessed be He, pays the reward in the future. 

The phrase "to love Him with all your heart and all your soul" mentions these two perfections so they may exist eternally in the secret of "Jeshurun and Israel." Nevertheless, it also hints at the perfection of wealth in the following verse, "To observe... which I command you today," for this is only practiced "today" <note>in this life</note>. This is why it says "for your own good" specifically. "Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens"—those five have no "good" <note>in the material sense</note> but eight corresponding ones in the future. 

It is known in the secret of the fifty gates of understanding, which is the secret of the first *He* of the Name [YHVH]. The letter *Yod* equals ten, and combining five times ten equals fifty. This is "Behold, to the Lord your God," meaning all your actions should be for the sake of Heaven, for Him alone. This is "And He is," for they have no other "turning" or partner like pride. All should be for Him alone. "The heavens and the heavens of heavens" are the secret of the eternal Jeshurun and Israel. "The earth and all that is in it" is this world. Both together are the secret of "Grace" (*Chen*). 

"Only in your fathers did He delight (*heshak*)..." <note>Deut 10:15</note>. It is known that the name *Yod-Daled-Yod* <note>a mystical name</note> is vocalized with a *Cholam* and a *Kamatz* <note>Vowel marks</note>. Just as the hand (*Kaf*) is in "He delighted in you," so is the Name that is in you—meaning you are permitted to mention it, which is *Adonai*, also vocalized with the vowels of *Heshak*. Our Sages have already said: "Wherever you find His greatness, you find His humility." This is the hint in these vowel points. 

He who knows he is below hints at the "heel" (*ekev*) to the sole, to be created under his feet. The vowel *Sheva*, even though it is below, shows the light that is above it. The matter of humility is that he should consider every man to be better than himself. See *Duties of the Heart*, the "Gate of Submission," chapter 5. Our Sages said: "Be exceedingly, exceedingly humble of spirit." Maimonides elaborated on this, writing that in all traits, the middle path is good, but in humility, one must go to the furthest extreme. Therefore they said "exceedingly, exceedingly." This is why the *Sheva* vowel comes in place of a *Chirik* to show the sweetness of the light. It is written "God rested in this world," and then "as it is today." The *Cholam* and *Kamatz* hint at the world to come, the secret of Jeshurun and Israel, which rises upwards. The *Kamatz* represents "I dwell with the contrite" who are below, but it will be the secret of the *Kamatz* <note>from the root 'to close' or 'gather'</note> which is a great light beyond measure, the secret of the Hidden Light, the "heavens of heavens." 

Know that for Kabbalists, the entire Name [of God] is vocalized with *Kamatz* in the crown (*Keter*). Regarding humility, after the firstborn comes the one who pursues him. As it says, "The pride of man shall bring him low." The hint comes from the Mishnah: "The end of man is the worm." If one is a master of pride, his "horn" is raised, and then the *Kamatz* becomes a *Chirik* <note>A lower vowel point</note>, and the "raised" becomes "rot" (*rimmah*). The "horn" (*keren*) is reversed and becomes "pierced" (*neker*), like worms boring through. 

But regarding the fathers, "He delighted in your fathers"—"And I am dust and ashes." The vowel below is the secret of the *Sheva*. Isaac is an elevation in the secret of the *Chirik*, for "he lived in his life." It is written "The God of Isaac." Jacob is in the secret of his names Jeshurun and Israel, "an inheritance without boundaries." Thus the secret of *Heshak* is explained. This Name equals 65, the numerical value of *Adonai*. See Rashi on Portion Phinehas: "The few..."—God chose the few of all nations because there were 65 families. It is mentioned "in their seed after them" more than all the nations. 

I say that due to the greatness of this virtue of humility, our predecessors established the daily liturgy: "A man should always be God-fearing in secret... Sovereign of all Worlds... What are we? What is our life?" We have explained these eight expressions. Since it has come to hand, we shall explain the entire text by the good hand of God upon me. "A man should always be God-fearing in secret"—meaning even in secret. Or, he should hide his deeds as much as possible and do everything for the sake of "walking secretly with God," and not for any ulterior motive. See *Duties of the Heart* in the "Gate of Unification of Action." You will find there that the Evil Inclination first incites one not to do God's commandments at all. If it cannot, it entices him to do them in front of people for fame and glory. If it still cannot, it says the opposite: "Hide your deeds so they don't praise you," [using pride in one's own secrecy as a trap]. 

Furthermore: "One should be God-fearing in secret in his deeds," yet "acknowledging the truth." He should not abandon the way of truth because of this, since his intention is for Heaven. "Sovereign of the Worlds"—this title hints at His greatness, for He is the Great Ruler over all; there is no number to the worlds, high above high, the Cause of Causes. And we are dust, gall, shame, filth, and worms. Even though we are crushed, "Not because of our righteousness do we lay our supplications before You." This is what the Sages said: "Any Torah scholar who is not confident in being answered like Joshua is forbidden to fall [on his face in prayer]..."

Abaye and Rava would pray... "Not because of our righteousness, but because of Your abundant mercy," as it is written, "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy"—freely. "What are we? What is our life?" I have already explained. "What are we"—if I am for myself, what am I? "What is our life"—it is written, "which a man shall do and live by them," excluding the wicked who even in their lives are called dead. Even our life—what is it sufficient for, to be attached to the Sovereign of the Worlds?

# The Written Torah — On the Consequence of Humility

<column-break/>

->Not a literally new Torah, Heaven forbid, but rather that its letters will be combined in a different manner than they were previously,<-
prior to being given, as explained in the introduction of the Ramban <note>Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman, a 13th-century scholar</note> to the Five Books of Moses. God [originally] had the world with Him, and then He gave it [the Torah]. However, it says "He gave," meaning He will not give it again in the future. Now, He has given the "Body" of the Torah, which consists of the essence of the 613 commandments <note>original: "Taryag Mitzvot"</note>.

<column-break/>

The Torah that is now in our hands—but in the future there will be a "New Torah."
That is, the 613 commandments. There is also a third part called the "Garment," which consists of upright character traits and virtuous qualities, and those who learn from the stories of the Torah how to act. And what
are they? The Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings. The Torah is the highest level, the Prophets are below it, and the Writings are below them, which are in the category of the "Garment." The Writings were written through Divine Inspiration <note>original: "Ruach HaKodesh"</note>, as it is written: "And Esther clothed herself in royalty," and our Sages of blessed memory said: "She clothed herself in Divine Inspiration." Regarding this, the verse concludes: "But let him who boasts boast in this: that he understands and knows Me" <note>Jeremiah 9:23</note>. This refers to the parts of the Torah. And behold, the threefold nature of wealth is tripled in the Writings, and then the language is adjusted to answer the question I raised. It is written in the Torah regarding the understanding of the soul:
"The Lord your God, the God..." <note>Deut. 10:17</note> which refers to the parts of the Torah. And behold, the threefold nature of wealth is tripled in the Writings, and then the language is adjusted to answer the question I raised. It is written in the Torah regarding the understanding of the soul:
"The Lord your God," etc. He transcends the heights of the world and there is no way to perceive Him—we only perceive Him through His actions, namely: "The Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome" <note>A phrase from the Amidah prayer and Deut. 10:17</note>.
Regarding anyone who is arrogant: if he is a prophet, his prophecy departs; if he is a wise man, his wisdom departs. And so they said in the Midrash regarding the pious. And so you find
regarding the greatest of prophets <note>Moses</note>, because he concluded the matter by saying "Bring the case to me" <note>Deut. 1:17</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed him that even the eye of a prophet has limits: "And Moses brought
their judgment before the Lord" <note>Numbers 27:5; Moses had to ask God because he didn't know the law regarding the daughters of Zelophehad</note>. And this is the meaning of "He who shows no favoritism and takes no bribe." God said to him: "A person should always occupy himself with Torah even if it is not for its own sake <note>original: "shelo lishmah"</note>, for through doing it not for its own sake,
he will come to do it for its own sake." Do not err in interpreting this to mean that the Holy One, Blessed be He, assists him in reaching the sincere level because he occupied himself with it [insincerely]; for regarding this, "He takes no bribe." This action [insincere study] is not [inherently] a good
deed, for God hates pride. Rather, God acts such that one should occupy himself with it even if it is not for its own sake, because one finds written within the Torah that it is a great sin
to study not for its own sake; and this awakens him to study for its own sake. But the act of Torah study when done with an insincere motive is itself a sin. And with this, the difficulty raised by the Tosafot <note>Medieval Talmudic commentators</note> is resolved.
And whoever knows all this recognizes His greatness, may He be blessed, and in Him is found His humility. Just as He watches over the orphan and the widow, so too it is regarding the many
eternal things, about which it is said: "Your eyes shall behold your Teacher," for in the future they will learn Torah from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Behold, a father is obligated to teach his son; so too the Holy One, Blessed be He, is
a Father. And now, as in the Writings, there is no Father <note>meaning, a lack of direct revelation</note>. But in the future: "I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness," which refers to the Torah that was given as a bride. And now we are in faithfulness.
And so too the fixing of a place for Torah, as seen in the first chapter of Berakhot: "The Lord shall be one," and it was taught in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Whoever fixes a place for his Torah, his enemies fall beneath him."
And we are now "strangers" in the land, but in the future "you shall dwell with Me." And the matter of "bread and a garment" <note>Deut. 10:18</note> contains a hint that in the future the earth will produce fine rolls and silken clothes,
as our Sages of blessed memory said. "Two sons of building" refers to the perfection of the years and the perfection of the body, and this is the "Image of God." And this is what the Lord said, "High and exalted," and as it were, "Upon the throne as
the appearance of a man" <note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>. And our Sages said: "The righteous resemble the Form of their Creator." "With the contrite and lowly of spirit" <note>Isaiah 57:15</note>—I have written elsewhere in the name of the Ari, of blessed memory <note>Rabbi Isaac Luria, the great Kabbalist</note>, the secret of the word *Daka* <note>original: "דכא"; meaning contrite or crushed</note>:
A proud person is a [broken] vessel. It is said: "A beautiful dwelling, [beautiful vessels, and a beautiful wife expand a man's mind]." A beautiful dwelling is the Heart; beautiful vessels are the tools of action; a beautiful wife is the Soul. And these are the initials of D-K-A: **D**welling (*Dirah*), **K**elim (*Vessels*), **A**shah (*Woman*).
The body is a clean branch. It is tripled in the Writings against the perfection of wealth, which corresponds to Spirit, Body, and Soul. And behold, conversely, it was raised to the "stork" <note>A play on the Hebrew word for stork, *Chasida*, and the word for pious, *Chasid*</note>, for
the storehouses are in the firmament called *Aravot*, as seen in the chapter "One may not expound," where the treasures of blessing are stored. And it is written in the Torah "Father," and "Addition," and "Judgment"...
to have mercy on them, and there is no pride. So shall be His humility, as we have merited: "the orphan and the widow." Moses saw such great closeness before Him by his power
[above] the ministering angels. And this is "God in His holy habitation," as seen there in the chapter "One may not expound," that He occupies Himself with the praise of the "What" <note>referring to Israel</note> who say song at night and
during the day because of the honor of Israel. And so these three places of atonement, which hint at humility, are based on the aforementioned: "And it shall be a consequence (*Ekev*)." "The consequence of humility" <note>Proverbs 22:4</note> refers to
the perfection of the body, for no creature had a body as exalted as Adam the First, for his heel (*ekev*) darkened the sun, etc. Yet despite all this, his name is Adam: *Efer* (Dust), *Dam* (Blood), *Marah* (Gall/Bitterness), which indicates
humility. "Lest you eat and are satisfied," etc., speaks of wealth. "For the Lord your God," etc., speaks of the thought and the perfection of the Torah. And since we have explained this—and this
is "For the Lord your God," etc.—its explanation "And now, Israel," is according to its context. Especially since the pious Rabbi David commanded that the section on humility be read every day. It has
several fine points and unifications. And now, let this be upon the people according to humility, with God's help. "And now, Israel, what does the Lord ask of you?" <note>Deut. 10:12</note> It means:
from you, that which is not a matter of humility, as Moses said: "And what are we?" Then you will merit that which is hinted at in the name "Israel." "But to fear..." Our Sages said: "Is fear a
small thing?" Yes, it was a small thing for Moses. And I also wrote above regarding the "consequence of humility" and "fear of the Lord." And Israel gave "What" (*Mah*) instead of "One hundred" (*Me'ah*). And it is difficult to write the
matter, for the word "What" (*Mah*) has two meanings from one extreme to the other. It can be interpreted as a language of emptiness and insignificance, such as "How (*Mah*) great is Your goodness," and on the other hand, a language of
"And we are what (*Mah*)?" "What (*Mah*) is man that You are mindful of him?" Behold, in the matter of prayer, we need Him to purify us to be alone in His holiness—"How (*Mah*) manifold are Your works!" And it is good to say when one falls
in His sight and in His fear. And this is the intent: those one hundred [blessings] must be in the category of "What," and this is "But to fear." For "But" (*Ki im*) is the acronym of "Another" (*Achar*)...
they said "And they gave 'What'." "And now, Israel, what (*Mah*) the Lord asks of you," which is the attribute of "What," which is from the attributes... in the category of "What," "But to fear." That is, and this is to fear, to fear
Heaven. Then pride will be removed. And according to what is in the chapter "One who died," page 19: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: "One who finds diverse seeds (*Kilayim*)... until: there is no wisdom, no understanding, and no
counsel against the Lord." In any place where there is a desecration of God's name, one does not give honor to a teacher. And so they said regarding the poverty of a Torah scholar... And now,
what is written, what is the weight of humility? The arrangers of the prayer service arranged for us eight "Whats": "What are we? What is our life? What..." etc. The meaning is the longing for humility. And humility is seen in eight places in the
head:
1. The **Thought** that spreads in the heart and causes the heart to be haughty. But "a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise."
2. A **Brazen Forehead**.
3. **Haughty Eyes**, but it should be a "Good Eye" that guards the sight.
4. **Broad Ears** that listen to falsehood.
5. The **Nose**, which is the source of anger stemming from pride. But it is fitting for him [to be patient].
6. A **Tongue** that speaks grandiosely. But "guard your tongue [from evil]."
7. The **Taste**; and it is written: "Lest you eat and are satisfied," etc. But there must be the trait of contentment stemming from humility.
8. A **Furious Face**, but they should be
silent and patient. And all these are in the head. And this is the matter of "with a heavy head," so that one's head does not rise, and one should not walk with a straight [arrogant] posture, for our Sages said this "pushes away
the Divine Presence," measure for measure, for it is the opposite of the "consequence of humility." And regarding this path of "fear of the Lord," which is called "successful wisdom,"
in [Tractate] Sotah, Rav Ezra expounded—sometimes it was said in the name of Rabbi Ami and sometimes in the name of Rabbi Assi: "Any person who has arrogance in him will eventually be diminished, as it says: 'They are exalted [for a little while, then they are gone].'
He cannot change the world, for the verse says: 'and they are no more.' And if he repents, he is gathered from the world in his time, as it says: 'they are gathered in like all others,' like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, regarding whom 'all, from all, with all' is written.
If not: 'like the head of an ear of grain (*Shibbolet*) they are cut off.'" Rav Huna and Rav Hisda [disagreed]: one said like the chaff of the grain, and the other said like the ear of grain itself.
What is the meaning of this statement? This nation... Rabbi Ami... This is always...
The person is compared to an ear of grain. A woman is the "soil of the world" and the woman... And in the chapter "The Worker," Rabbi Hanina bar Papa expounded:
"You winnow my path and my lying down," etc. This teaches that a person is not formed from the whole drop [of seed], but only from the clearest part of it. The school of Rabbi Ishmael taught: It is a parable of a man who winnows in the threshing floor...
And so they are destined to stand in their garments, by a logical inference from a grain of wheat. Just as an ear of grain has an inner part and outer husks, so too in man. And the "head of the ear of grain" is
the man. And a man must be in the place of the ear of grain, which is the earth, as it is written: "And my soul shall be like dust to all." And if not, "like the head of an ear of grain they are cut off."
Behold, such-a-one lives... He who pursues greatness, greatness flees from him, and the "head of the ear of grain is cut off." And the other holds that this is the plain meaning, that they will not return...
in this.
